title: PR #401 silently drops the win32 skip on the mini image-preview tests whose teardown crashes the Windows runner
body:
## Finding

Open PR #401 (`feat(tui): name the asking subagent in the permission prompt`, Jules, fixes #389) contains an unrelated test change that re-enables the mini image-preview tests on Windows, even though the comment directly above them says they must stay off Windows.

In `packages/tui/test/mini/footer.view.test.tsx` the PR changes:

```diff
-test.skipIf(process.platform === "win32").each([
+test.each([
```

The two comment lines immediately above that call are unchanged by the PR and still read (verified at PR head `1bac6afee736a872f77fa6d46d739d1dd3ade81e`, and on current main):

```ts
// OpenTUI image teardown crashes Bun 1.3.14's Windows test runner after the assertions pass.
// Keep the native preview coverage on Linux while the attachment behavior remains covered on both platforms below.
```

Nothing in the PR body, the single commit message (`1bac6afe`, "feat(tui): name the asking subagent in the permission prompt"), or the #389 scope mentions Windows, image preview, or a Bun/OpenTUI teardown fix. The PR's actual test changes for its feature are elsewhere in the same file (adding a `subagents` fixture and expecting `From My Subagent`) and in `session-nested-asks.test.tsx`. The `skipIf` removal rides along silently.

## Evidence

- PR: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/401 — OPEN, MERGEABLE / CLEAN at review time (2026-10-24), 1 commit `1bac6afee736a872f77fa6d46d739d1dd3ade81e`, 5 files.
- Diff hunk: `packages/tui/test/mini/footer.view.test.tsx` — `test.skipIf(process.platform === "win32").each([` → `test.each([` for the parametrized test `"mini pastes, previews, submits, and recalls an image ($width x $height, mono=$mono, preview=$preview)"`.
- Current main still has the guard: `packages/tui/test/mini/footer.view.test.tsx:253` is `test.skipIf(process.platform === "win32").each([`, with the teardown-crash comment at lines 251–252.
- Dedup: issue searches for "image teardown", "win32 footer preview teardown", and "skipIf" return no open issue tracking this (only closed, unrelated #92 / #178).

## Why it matters

If #401 merges as-is, the four native-preview parametrizations run on Windows again, where — per the in-repo comment that this PR leaves in place — OpenTUI image teardown crashes Bun 1.3.14's Windows test runner after the assertions pass. That turns an unrelated TUI permission-prompt feature into a Windows CI regression, and leaves the code and its own explanatory comment contradicting each other for the next reader.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In PR #401 (or a follow-up if #401 has already merged), restore `test.skipIf(process.platform === "win32")` for the image-preview parametrized test in `packages/tui/test/mini/footer.view.test.tsx`, OR — if the Windows teardown crash is genuinely fixed — update/remove the stale comment in the same change and cite the evidence (Bun/OpenTUI version or fix) that makes the coverage safe on Windows.
- [ ] The permission-prompt changes from #401 keep passing their tests (`From My Subagent` footer case and the nested-asks session case) with no change in scope.
- [ ] No other unrelated test-guard changes ride along in the fix.

title: fix(schema): ModelAlias throws AliasMaxDepthError for a chain that settles exactly at the limit — 9-hop chain rejected, effective limit is 8
body:
## Problem

`ModelAlias.resolveRef` throws `AliasMaxDepthError` for an alias chain that successfully settles exactly on the depth limit. The post-loop check cannot distinguish "the loop settled and broke out" from "the loop ran out of depth", so a legitimate chain one hop shorter than the apparent limit already fails.

## Evidence (verified 2026-10-24 on main 58dd3fbe58)

File: `packages/schema/src/model-alias.ts`
- `MAX_DEPTH = 10` (line 32); loop is `while (depth < MAX_DEPTH)` (line 61), incrementing `depth` at the top of every iteration — including the final iteration that merely confirms the settled `provider/model` and `break`s.
- After the loop, line 153 unconditionally throws when `depth >= MAX_DEPTH`, even when the loop exited via `break` with a fully resolved reference.

Reproduction (Bun, importing `packages/core/src/model-alias.ts`; global model aliases `a0 -> a1 -> ... -> a(n-1) -> openai/gpt-4o`, i.e. `n` expansion hops):

| Hops | Result |
|---|---|
| 5 | `"openai/gpt-4o"` |
| 8 | `"openai/gpt-4o"` |
| 9 | THROWS `AliasMaxDepthError: Max alias resolution depth exceeded for: a0` |
| 10, 11 | THROWS `AliasMaxDepthError` (expected for 10+; the 9-hop case is the defect) |

A 9-hop chain needs 9 expansion iterations plus 1 settling iteration = depth 10, hits the post-loop check, and is rejected despite having resolved. The effective usable limit is therefore 8 hops, not the documented-by-constant 10, and the error message misreports a resolved chain as a runaway one.

## Why it matters

Alias chains are how users layer naming (team alias -> provider alias -> concrete model). A chain that is within the intended limit fails with an error that claims the opposite, and the failure boundary (8 usable hops) matches neither the constant nor any documented limit, so users cannot predict whether a config will work without counting loop iterations including the invisible settling pass.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A chain that settles within `MAX_DEPTH` total loop iterations resolves instead of throwing — in particular the verified 9-hop chain above returns `openai/gpt-4o`.
- [ ] A chain that genuinely never settles within the limit (cycle-free but longer than the limit, and cycles longer than the visited-set catches) still throws `AliasMaxDepthError`; cycle detection (`AliasCycleError`) is unchanged.
- [ ] The fix distinguishes settled-vs-exhausted loop exit (e.g. track settlement explicitly) rather than just raising `MAX_DEPTH`, so the boundary stays exactly at the constant.
- [ ] New tests in `packages/core/test/model-alias.test.ts` cover the boundary: the largest chain that should resolve, and the smallest that should throw. Existing tests (including test 13, chained expansion) still pass.
- [ ] Dedup checked 2026-10-24: no open or closed issue mentions `AliasMaxDepth` / max-depth alias behaviour.

Single-repo: `ModelAlias` lives only in this repo's schema/core packages.

title: fix(schema): ModelAlias alias path accepts invalid variants the no-alias parser rejects — empty variant dropped, second # kept
body:
## Problem

`ModelAlias.resolve` / `resolveRef` validates a model reference differently depending on whether any aliases are configured. With no aliases it uses `parseRefString`, which rejects an empty variant and a variant containing a second `#`. With aliases present it takes the loop path in `resolveRef`, which accepts both — silently dropping an empty variant and keeping a `#` inside the variant verbatim.

## Evidence (verified 2026-10-24 on main 58dd3fbe58)

File: `packages/schema/src/model-alias.ts`
- No-alias path delegates to `parseRefString` (line 53), whose check at line 233 throws when `variant` is empty or contains `#`.
- Alias path (lines 57-169) records `explicitVariant` from the first `#` (lines 72-73) with no equivalent validation, and builds the final ref from it at line 169 onward.

Reproduction (Bun, importing `packages/core/src/model-alias.ts`, aliases = `{ models: { flash: "openai/gpt-4o" }, variants: { high: "xhigh" } }`):

| Input | No aliases | With aliases |
|---|---|---|
| `openai/gpt-4o#` | THROWS `Invalid model reference: openai/gpt-4o#` | returns `"openai/gpt-4o"` (empty variant silently dropped) |
| `openai/gpt-4o#high#extra` | THROWS `Invalid model reference: openai/gpt-4o#high#extra` | returns `"openai/gpt-4o#high#extra"` (second `#` kept in the variant) |

## Why it matters

The same malformed reference is an error for one user and silently accepted for another, purely because the second user configured an unrelated alias. The double-`#` form produces a `ResolvedRef.variant` of `high#extra` and a canonical `ref` no other parser in the repo accepts, so it will fail later — further from the cause — or be passed to a provider as a variant name that can never match. The empty-variant form hides a typo (`model#` for `model#high`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With aliases configured, `openai/gpt-4o#` throws the same invalid-reference error as the no-alias path.
- [ ] With aliases configured, `openai/gpt-4o#high#extra` throws the same invalid-reference error as the no-alias path.
- [ ] Validation also covers a variant that arrives via an alias target (e.g. a model alias expanding to `provider/model#` or `provider/model#a#b`), not only a variant typed in the original input.
- [ ] New tests in `packages/core/test/model-alias.test.ts` cover both shapes on the alias path; all existing model-alias tests still pass.
- [ ] Dedup checked 2026-10-24: no open or closed issue tracks this validation parity gap (#391 is about a bare-alias variant being dropped by ModelResolver, a different code path).

Single-repo: `ModelAlias` lives only in this repo's schema/core packages.

title: feat(tui): name the asking subagent in the permission prompt — follow-up PR #384 left behind
body:
## Finding

PR #384 fixed #124 in the app: the root session's permission and question docks now name the subagent that asked ("From <title>", falling back to "From subagent"). Its scope notes explicitly left the same gap in the TUI as a follow-up:

> "The TUI permission prompt has the same gap (noted on #124); it is left for a follow-up — this PR covers the app docks per the issue's acceptance criteria."

That follow-up was never filed (issue searches for "TUI permission subagent", "permission prompt subagent", and in:title TUI return only the unrelated #78), and the gap is still live on current main. This issue tracks it, the same way #78 tracks the follow-up PR #64 left behind.

## Evidence

- PR: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/384 (commit 6a9fcf260c5025e662243c15ddb2f7cc01d8e63e, merged as 0a101b77ba60ef2bda0f4a458ca458f70c241952), scope notes quoted above.
- #124's body documents the TUI side: child-session permissions surface in the viewed (root) session's TUI, and the prompt header is just "Permission required" — the user cannot tell whether the root agent or a subagent is asking.
- Current main 977ff074e14536344e9aa36170143983e23bb534, `packages/tui/src/routes/session/permission.tsx`:
  - line 120: `const session = createMemo(() => data.session.get(props.request.sessionID))` — the requesting session is already loaded (currently used only for the `parentID` reject check at line 249); its title is available but never shown.
  - lines 204 and 219: the header and prompt title are the bare literal `Permission required`, regardless of which session asked.
  - line 269: `permissionSemanticLabel` likewise names only the action/title of the tool, never the session.
- Same generic title in the mini permission footer: `packages/tui/src/mini/footer.permission.tsx:185` returns `"Permission required"` with no source session.

## Why it matters

In the TUI a user can be asked to approve a shell command, edit, or external-directory access issued by a nested subagent while viewing the root session, with no indication of which agent is asking — exactly the ambiguity #124 called out for the app ("the user cannot tell whether the root agent or a subagent is asking before approving"). Approving the wrong agent's request is a real footgun; the app fix proves the label is cheap to compute from data the prompt already has.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a permission request's `sessionID` differs from the viewed session, the TUI permission prompt (`packages/tui/src/routes/session/permission.tsx`) names the asking session (its title when loaded, a generic "subagent" fallback when not), mirroring PR #384's app behaviour.
- [ ] A request from the viewed session itself renders exactly as today (no label).
- [ ] The mini permission footer (`packages/tui/src/mini/footer.permission.tsx`) is checked for the same gap and either gains the label or an explicit note on this issue records why it does not need one.
- [ ] Covered by a test or story that renders a child-session request in a parent session's prompt and asserts the label, and a same-session request asserting no label.

title: fix(core): PR #382's bare-alias fix never reaches the session runner — SessionRunnerModel still expands "flash/" and the run fails Model unavailable
body:
## Finding

PR #382 (`fix(cli,core): resolve bare model aliases through the server path`, OPEN, head `ffa98aac43bd`) fixes bare model aliases only in `ModelResolver.resolve`. The path a CLI session actually runs through — `SessionRunnerModel.resolve` in `packages/core/src/session/runner/model.ts` — still builds the alias-expansion string as `` `${target.providerID}/${target.id}` `` (lines 96–98 on current main `b8831f7197`), so a bare-alias target `{ providerID: "flash", id: "" }` becomes the string `"flash/"`. That consumer is byte-identical in PR #382's head: the PR does not touch the file.

## Evidence

- PR #382's CLI side (`packages/cli/src/session-target.ts:100-102` on the PR head) now passes a slash-less reference through as `{ providerID: resolved, id: "" }`, and `packages/cli/src/run/run.ts` (`parseRunModel`) forwards it as `{ providerID: "flash", modelID: "" }`; `packages/server` contains no `ModelResolver` use, so nothing expands it before the session runs.
- `SessionRunnerModel.resolve` (`packages/core/src/session/runner/model.ts:96-110` on main) builds `refStr = "flash/"`, calls `ModelAlias.resolveRef`, and swallows the throw in `catch {}`. Verified empirically with bun against current main's `packages/schema/src/model-alias.ts`: `resolveRef(aliases, "flash/")` throws `Invalid model reference after alias resolution: flash/` (the trailing-slash guard at model-alias.ts:163-164), while `resolveRef(aliases, "flash")` — the string PR #382 makes `ModelResolver.resolve` build (model-resolver.ts:609 on the PR head) — correctly returns `deepseek/deepseek-chat#high`.
- The unexpanded target then matches no catalog model, so the run fails at runner/model.ts:113 with `ModelUnavailableError` — the user sees `Model unavailable: flash/` instead of the alias expanding. The same applies to `mini` (session-target) sessions and to a bare alias with a variant (`"flash/#high"` throws the same way).
- The only other `ModelResolver.resolve(requested)` caller is the one-off `Generate.text` service (`packages/core/src/generate.ts:41`), which is not the session run path.
- PR #382's added test (`packages/core/test/config/aliases-normalize.test.ts`) exercises the config seam plus `ModelAlias.resolve` — code the PR does not change. Neither changed consumer (`parseSessionTargetModel`'s new passthrough, `ModelResolver.resolve`'s new refStr branch) and not the runner consumer has a test with an empty-id target. The PR body notes no live CLI run could be completed, so this gap was not caught.
- The behaviour is promised in the docs added by PR #379 (`services/www/src/docs/content/models.mdx`: "`opencode run -m flash` — passes through your configured default model behavior plus aliases", with a `flash` global alias in the example config).

## Why it matters

Bare aliases are the headline use of the #379 alias feature (`-m flash`). As PR #382 stands, merging it closes the CLI parse error but the session still fails server-side with a confusing `Model unavailable: flash/` message, and the PR's test gives false confidence that the end-to-end path works.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SessionRunnerModel.resolve` expands a `{ providerID: <bare alias>, id: "" }` target (with and without a variant) through the configured aliases, sharing the empty-id ref-string construction with `ModelResolver.resolve` instead of duplicating a divergent one.
- [ ] A test drives the session-runner resolution (or an equivalent end-to-end seam) with an empty-id bare-alias target and a config defining that alias, and asserts the resolved catalog model — not just `ModelAlias.resolve` in isolation.
- [ ] A bare name that is neither an alias nor a real model produces one clear error naming the original user input (not `flash/`).
- [ ] Existing model-resolver / model-alias / aliases-normalize tests still pass.

Found by pr-diff-review reviewing PRs #379, #381, #382, #383 in developing-today/opencode (2026-10-24 run). Cross-checked against current main `b8831f7197` via local clone, `git ls-remote`, and the GitHub MCP connector; `SessionRunnerModel` exists only in this repo (git grep over the code / openchamber / nix clones is empty), so this is a single-repo issue.

title: fix(core): a failed Console reload drops the policy refusal, re-enabling a refused instance's catalog copy
body:
## Finding

PR #373 (merged, merge commit be06d5d5953a259feb31b0ee1134cc7d35fdaff7) refuses a Console instance whose organization sends policies: `load()` in `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/opencode.ts` returns `{ ...next, config: undefined, mcp: undefined, refused: true }` (line 253 on current main), and the provider transform disables that instance's own catalog copy only while `snapshot.refused` is set (line 376):

```ts
if (snapshot.refused && providers.get(ids.providerID))
  providers.update(ids.providerID, (provider) => {
    provider.activation = "disabled"
  })
```

That refusal does not survive a failed reload. `load()`'s error fallback (line 267) rebuilds the snapshot from the previous one but drops the flag:

```ts
return IntegrationConnection.key(connection) === IntegrationConnection.key(snapshot.connection)
  ? { config: snapshot.config, connection, organization: snapshot.organization, mcp: snapshot.mcp }
  : { config: undefined, connection, organization: undefined, mcp: undefined }
```

`check()` re-runs `load()` every minute (line 536) and on inference 401/403, and `apply()` (line 483) replaces the snapshot and reloads providers whenever it differs — and a snapshot with `refused: true` differs from one without it. So one transient Console fetch failure (network error, 5xx, malformed body) for the same connection re-runs the provider transforms with `snapshot.refused === undefined`, the disable at line 376 no longer applies, and the refused instance's catalog copy (`opencode.work`, added by `ProviderInstancePlugin`) becomes available again — serving that organization without its policies, exactly the outcome commit 5840b5b ("fix(core): disable a refused Console instance's own catalog copy") was added to prevent. The next successful load re-refuses it, so the exposure window is from the first failed load until the next successful one, and it reopens on every later failure.

## Why it matters

The policy refusal is a security boundary: `ManagedPolicy` holds one organization's statements, so a second org's providers must never run unenforced (PR #373 body). A routine network blip silently lifts that boundary for the refused account's own catalog copy, with no status change the user would notice (the connection status stays whatever it was unless the error is a well-formed Console error).

## Evidence

- PR: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/373 (commits d2423253, 3874ddfe, 5840b5b7)
- `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/opencode.ts:253` — refusal sets `refused: true`
- `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/opencode.ts:267` — same-connection failure fallback omits `refused`
- `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/opencode.ts:376` — catalog copy disabled only when `snapshot.refused`
- `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/opencode.ts:483,536` — `apply()` on any snapshot difference; `check()` every minute
- Existing test `provider-opencode.test.ts` "refuses a second Console account whose organization sends policies" covers only the initial refusal; no test fails a subsequent load.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The same-connection failure fallback in `load()` preserves `refused` from the previous snapshot (or the refusal is otherwise stable across failed reloads).
- [ ] A regression test extends the refusal scenario: after the initial refusal, a failing Console fetch for the same connection leaves `opencode.work` unavailable (`providers.available()` still excludes it) and the integration status still `needs_auth`.
- [ ] Behavior for the main connection is unchanged: a failed load still keeps its last config so organization policy is not lifted.

title: fix(script): doc-env-var guard counts a documented variable as read when only a longer sibling name appears (OPENCODE_CONFIG vs OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR)
body:
## Finding

PR #357 (merged 2026-10-24T00:13:20Z, merge commit `9abb995bcee65b92be0eef8d10efd14fdfe61c16`; guard commit `a45a04f9741f2e295592570a6753a6e26194887a`) added `script/check-doc-env-vars.ts` to fail CI when `cli.mdx` documents an `OPENCODE_*` variable that nothing outside the docs reads. Its reader check, `gitHasReader` (`script/check-doc-env-vars.ts:35-56` on current main, verified via `gh api` contents), runs:

```
git grep -q -F <name> -- . :(exclude)packages/web/src/content/docs :(exclude)script/check-doc-env-vars.ts :(exclude)script/check-doc-env-vars.test.ts
```

`-F` without `-w` (or any boundary anchoring) is a plain substring search, while the extractor it feeds (`documentedVars`, same file:25-27) is boundary-exact (`\bOPENCODE_[A-Z0-9_]+\b`). So a documented variable counts as "read" when only a longer sibling name that has it as a prefix appears in the tree.

Two of the 15 variables documented in `cli.mdx` on current main (verified via `gh api`: the guard's own count of 15 is exact) have exactly this shape:

- `OPENCODE_CONFIG` is a prefix of `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` and `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`
- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE` is a prefix of `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS`

If the last exact reader of either variable were removed, the guard would stay green on the sibling names alone — the precise silent-no-op regression the guard was built to catch (#116, and the #103/#105/#114 chain before it).

## Evidence (reproduced this run)

Controlled repro with the guard's exact git invocation, in a scratch git repo whose only committed file contains `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` and `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS` and no exact occurrence of either shorter name (scratch removed after):

- `git grep -q -F OPENCODE_CONFIG -- . :(exclude)packages/web/src/content/docs …` → exit 0 (guard: has a reader)
- `git grep -q -F OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE -- . …` → exit 0 (guard: has a reader)
- Same commands with `-w` added → exit 1 for both (correctly: no exact reader)
- Sanity: `-w -F OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` → exit 0 (exact longer names still match with `-w`)

`gitHasReader` also has no test coverage: `script/check-doc-env-vars.test.ts` imports only `documentedVars` and `deadVars`, so the matching semantics of the one function that talks to git are untested.

## Why it matters

The guard is now a CI step in `.github/workflows/test.yml` ("Check documented env vars have readers"). A guard that cannot fail for two of the fifteen names it watches gives false confidence for the most central name on the list (`OPENCODE_CONFIG` itself). The fix is small; the test gap is the reason it shipped.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `gitHasReader` (or its replacement) matches whole variable names only — e.g. `git grep -w`, or an equivalent boundary-aware pattern — so `OPENCODE_CONFIG` is not satisfied by `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`/`OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, and `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE` is not satisfied by `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS`.
- [ ] A regression test exercises the reader matching itself (integration against a temporary git repo, or a factored pure matcher): prefix-sibling-only tree reports both shorter names as dead; a tree with an exact occurrence still reports them as read. Legitimate occurrence shapes that must keep counting as readers should be pinned by the test (e.g. `OPENCODE_CONFIG=…`, quoted `"OPENCODE_CONFIG"`, `${OPENCODE_CONFIG}`).
- [ ] Guard still passes on current main (all 15 documented variables have exact readers) and still fails listing the twelve dead variables when run against the pre-#357 `cli.mdx` (the PR's original ablation).

Single-repo: the guard script and the docs it watches live only in this repo; no copy exists in developing-today/code, developing-today/openchamber, or dezren39/nix.

title: fix(gui-extensions): WSL discovery still returns a banner line ending in the managed suffix when discoverScript prints nothing — frame the discovery output
body:
## Finding

PR #342 (https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/342, commit `12cd6af1b899c15ba6c0b5ee3468cce4ff72f67b`, merge `a97969cdc039af22387417f20cd99e5844363465`) narrowed `parseDiscoveredCli` to lines ending in `/.opencode/bin/opencode`. That closes #340 for banner paths outside the managed location, but the residual case is the same shape as #340: when `discoverScript()` prints nothing — the managed CLI is not installed — a login-shell banner/MOTD/profile line that itself ends in the managed suffix is still returned as the discovered CLI. The parser's own comment (`packages/gui-extensions/src/wsl/runtime.ts:88-100`) states the underlying problem: "No ordering rule can tell such a banner line from the script's own line when the script prints nothing". A suffix rule has the same limitation — it can only distinguish banner lines that do *not* look exactly like the one path the script can print.

## Evidence (verified on current main `b82506e82bd2b02ef0a3b5610a5b2986320e4993`)

- `packages/gui-extensions/src/wsl/runtime.ts:100` (on main): `.findLast((line) => line.startsWith("/") && line.endsWith("/.opencode/bin/opencode")) ?? null`
- `packages/gui-extensions/src/wsl/remote-cli.ts:14-19` (on main): `discoverScript()` prints the path with `printf '\n%s\n' "$cli"` — a leading newline puts it on its own line, but there is no framing marker (unlike `versionScript` in the same file, which frames its output with `OPENCODE_CLI_VERSION_BEGIN`/`END` for exactly this reason, and unlike the SSH registration frame `OPENCODE_SSH_REGISTRATION_BEGIN`/`END`).
- Reproduction with the real functions and the real `discoverScript` through `sh`, mirroring PR #342's own `runDiscoverScriptWithoutCli` harness (empty `HOME` = no CLI installed):
  - `parseDiscoveredCli("/home/other/.opencode/bin/opencode\n")` returns `"/home/other/.opencode/bin/opencode"` instead of `null`
  - Real-script run, no CLI installed, preceding output `/home/other/.opencode/bin/opencode\n`: parsed result is `"/home/other/.opencode/bin/opencode"`; with no preceding output the same harness correctly returns `null`.
- PR #342's new tests cover only banner paths that do *not* end in the managed suffix (`/opt/old-opencode/bin/opencode`, `/usr/local/bin/opencode`, `/opt/opencode` — `packages/gui-extensions/src/wsl/runtime.test.ts`); no test covers a banner line ending in `/.opencode/bin/opencode`.
- Baseline this run: focused `bun test src/wsl/runtime.test.ts src/wsl/remote-cli.test.ts` passes 20 / 1 skip / 0 fail on main, so this is an uncovered case, not a test regression.

## Why it matters

`resolveCli` (`runtime.ts:377`) feeds `inspectCli` in `packages/gui-extensions/src/wsl/servers.ts:92` (reports a CLI present and reads a version from the banner-named path) and `startWslSidecar` in `packages/gui-extensions/src/wsl/sidecar.ts:31` — which throws `error.opencodeNotInstalled` only when discovery returns `null`, and otherwise `exec`s the returned path as the server binary. A banner-advertised managed-suffix path (e.g. a profile/MOTD line naming another install location) therefore turns the not-installed case into a present-CLI report and an attempt to execute whatever binary sits at that banner-named path, instead of the clean not-installed flow. This is the remaining instance of the banner-invention class that #265/#272/#276 (parseVersion, fixed by framing), #334/#340 (this parser) have been closing one narrowing at a time; framing closes it for good rather than narrowing it further.

Scope: WSL only. The SSH `discoverScript`'s output path is consumed inside the remote script itself (`$cli`), not parsed from stdout, and SSH registration output is already framed — no SSH change is implied. `parseDiscoveredCli`/`discoverScript` (WSL) exist only in this repo (grep of code/openchamber/nix clones: no hits) — no cross-repo port owed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `discoverScript()` frames its output (e.g. BEGIN/END markers on their own lines, following the `versionScript` pattern in the same file, including the marker-gluing cases fixed for the version frame), and `parseDiscoveredCli` accepts only a framed path.
- [ ] With no CLI installed, preceding login-shell output that is a line ending in `/.opencode/bin/opencode` (including the exact `$HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode` spelling for a different/empty HOME) returns `null` — verified through the real `discoverScript` harness, terminated and unterminated preceding output.
- [ ] The real discovered path is still returned when it follows banner output, including banner output with no trailing newline.
- [ ] Ablation: with the parser/script change reverted, the new banner-suffix tests fail; restored, the focused wsl tests and the full gui-extensions suite pass, and package typecheck is clean.

title: fix(gui-extensions): WSL parseDiscoveredCli still returns a banner path when discoverScript prints nothing
body:
## Summary

PR #335 (commit 6d79aa5d234c6ed0bb01c9dae4e1f6dbd7b9d310, merged 2026-10-23) changed `parseDiscoveredCli` in `packages/gui-extensions/src/wsl/runtime.ts` (lines 88-100 on current main c61f5ac316) from `.find(...)` to `.findLast(...)`. That fixes a path-shaped banner line *preceding* the discovered path, but the residual case remains: when `discoverScript()` prints nothing — the managed CLI is not installed — a banner/MOTD/profile line that is itself an absolute path ending in `/opencode` is still returned as the discovered CLI.

## Evidence

The WSL `discoverScript()` (`packages/gui-extensions/src/wsl/remote-cli.ts:14-19`) can only ever print `$HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode` — that is the single path it tests with `[ -x ... ]` and prints. Any other returned path did not come from the script.

Verified on current main (c61f5ac316) with the real function under Bun:

```ts
parseDiscoveredCli("/opt/old-opencode/bin/opencode\n")
// => "/opt/old-opencode/bin/opencode"   ← banner-only; script printed nothing, should be null

parseDiscoveredCli("")
// => null   ← control

parseDiscoveredCli("/home/alice/.opencode/bin/opencode\n")
// => "/home/alice/.opencode/bin/opencode"   ← control
```

Issue #334 itself noted this option: "Optionally also require the `/.opencode/bin/opencode` suffix, since that is the only path the script can print; the ordering fix alone is sufficient" — for the banner-before-real case. The banner-only case is not covered by #334's acceptance criteria and has no regression test: `runtime.test.ts` covers banner text lines returning null, but no path-shaped banner line on its own.

## Why it matters

`resolveCli` (runtime.ts:375-377) feeds this result to:
- `servers.ts:92-97` `inspectCli`, which reports a CLI as present and reads its version instead of reporting it missing; and
- `sidecar.ts:31-50` `startWslSidecar`, which does `exec <resolved-path> serve --hostname 0.0.0.0 ...` — so instead of throwing `error.opencodeNotInstalled`, it tries to execute a binary named only by login-shell banner output, while the managed CLI is in fact not installed.

This is the same class of defect `parseVersion` in the same package solved with BEGIN/END framing markers (its comment: no ordering rule can tell a banner line from the script's own line when the script prints nothing). For WSL discovery a simpler rule is available because the script's output shape is fixed.

## Suggested fix

Either:
- require the returned line to end with `/.opencode/bin/opencode` (the only suffix `discoverScript()` can print), in addition to the current last-match ordering; or
- frame the discovery output with markers like `versionScript`/`parseVersion` and only accept lines inside the frame.

## Acceptance criteria

- `parseDiscoveredCli("/opt/old-opencode/bin/opencode\n")` returns `null` (banner-only output, script printed nothing), with a regression test in `packages/gui-extensions/src/wsl/runtime.test.ts` — ideally also through the real `discoverScript` with no CLI installed and path-shaped preceding output.
- Existing behaviours preserved: a real discovered `$HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode` is returned, including when a differently-shaped path banner line precedes it (PR #335's case); empty and non-path output return `null`.
- WSL gui-extensions suite and typecheck pass.

Single-repo: `parseDiscoveredCli` / the WSL `discoverScript` exist only in developing-today/opencode (per #334's cross-repo grep; no copy in developing-today/code, developing-today/openchamber, or dezren39/nix).

title: fix(gui-extensions): WSL parseDiscoveredCli returns the first path-shaped line — a banner line that is an absolute /opencode path beats the discovered CLI
body:
fix(gui-extensions): WSL parseDiscoveredCli returns the first path-shaped line — a banner line that is an absolute /opencode path beats the discovered CLI

## Summary

`parseDiscoveredCli` (`packages/gui-extensions/src/wsl/runtime.ts:88-98`) returns the **first** line of login-shell output that starts with `/` and ends with `/opencode`. The transport is a login shell (`sh -lc`), so a banner, MOTD or profile echo can precede the script's own output — and if any such line is itself an absolute path ending in `/opencode`, discovery returns that path instead of the one `discoverScript()` actually found.

This is a different defect from #290 (gluing onto unterminated preceding output; fixed by the script's leading newline). A newline-terminated banner line is unaffected by that fix: it is a complete line, and `.find` takes it before the script's line is ever considered.

## Evidence (verified on main 132eaa7705 with the real function under Bun)

```ts
parseDiscoveredCli("/opt/old-opencode/bin/opencode\n/home/alice/.opencode/bin/opencode\n")
// => "/opt/old-opencode/bin/opencode"   ← banner's path, not the discovered one

parseDiscoveredCli("\n/home/alice/.opencode/bin/opencode\n")
// => "/home/alice/.opencode/bin/opencode"   ← control

parseDiscoveredCli("Welcome\n")
// => null   ← control
```

The result is provably wrong, not just racy: the WSL `discoverScript()` (`packages/gui-extensions/src/wsl/remote-cli.ts:14-19`) can only ever print `$HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode` — that is the single path it tests and prints. Any returned path that is not that path did not come from the script.

## Why it matters

`resolveCli` (runtime.ts, `createWslRuntime`) feeds this result to the WSL extension as the CLI to run. A distro whose profile/MOTD echoes an opencode path (e.g. a setup hint, a stale second install under `/opt` or `/usr/local`, or a `which opencode`-style diagnostic line) makes the extension resolve — and execute — the wrong binary, or a path that is not the managed install at all, while the managed CLI sits undiscovered.

The sibling readers on the same transports all take the **last** candidate for exactly this reason: `parseVersion` returns `versions.at(-1)` (both remote-cli copies), `parseProbeAnswer` returns `.at(-1)` (runtime.ts:78-86), and SSH's `parseRegistration` uses `findLast` (ssh/bootstrap.ts:43). `parseDiscoveredCli` is the one remaining first-match reader. Its existing test (runtime.test.ts:61-69) covers banner *text* lines but no path-shaped banner line.

## Suggested fix

Take the last matching line instead of the first (`.findLast(...)`), matching the sibling readers' convention — the script's own line is printed after any banner, so it is the last path-shaped line. Optionally also require the `/.opencode/bin/opencode` suffix, since that is the only path the script can print; the ordering fix alone is sufficient and stays closest to the existing pattern.

## Acceptance criteria

- `parseDiscoveredCli` returns the discovered `$HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode` when a path-shaped banner line (an absolute path ending in `/opencode`) precedes it, with a regression test in `packages/gui-extensions/src/wsl/runtime.test.ts`.
- Existing behaviours preserved: clean output, banner text lines, empty output and non-path output still return the path / `null` as today (existing tests pass).
- WSL gui-extensions suite and typecheck pass.

Single-repo: `parseDiscoveredCli` has no copy in developing-today/code, developing-today/openchamber or dezren39/nix (grep-verified this run; #290's cross-repo note records the same for the WSL discovery read).

title: feat(app): permission and question docks don't say which subagent asked
body:
## Finding

Since PR #60 (merged as 1585d2b91e), the root session's docks show pending permission requests and questions from subagents at any depth, including ones raised before the app loaded. Neither dock says which session asked.

- The permission dock's header is "Permission required".
- The question dock's header is "Question", or "Question n of m".

That is the same whether the request came from the viewed session or from a grandchild. With several subagents running, the user can't tell which one wants to run the command or is asking.

## Evidence (main 5214f4d8ae)

- `packages/app/src/session/requests/model.ts:26-36` loads permissions and forms for every session in the viewed tree (`sessionTreeIDs(data.session.list(), id)`).
- `packages/app/src/session/requests/session-permission-dock.tsx:25-34`: the header is the warning icon and `language.t("notification.permission.title")` ("Permission required", `packages/app/src/runtime/i18n/en.ts:498`). The request's `sessionID` is never shown.
- `packages/app/src/session/requests/session-question-dock.tsx`: the header shows `summary()` (546-556), which is `session.question.title` ("Question", `en.ts:570`) or `session.question.progress` (127-132).
- Both docks are mounted in `packages/app/src/session/composer/session-composer-region.tsx:43-51`.

OpenChamber labels a docked request from a descendant "From subagent" (`chat.questionCard.fromSubagent`, developing-today/openchamber `packages/ui/src/lib/i18n/messages/en.ts:2493`).

The TUI's permission prompt header has the same gap: "Permission required" plus the tool's title (`packages/tui/src/routes/session/permission.tsx:200-214`). I haven't checked the rest of the TUI root view for attribution. This issue covers the app; the TUI can be fixed alongside it or tracked separately.

## Acceptance criteria

- A dock showing a request from a session other than the viewed one names that session, for example "From <subagent title>". The title comes from `data.session.get(request.sessionID)`, with a fallback when it isn't loaded.
- A request from the viewed session itself looks as it does today.
- New copy is an i18n key in `packages/app/src/runtime/i18n/en.ts` only, per `packages/app/AGENTS.md:30-31`; other locales fall back to English.
- An e2e test asserts the label for a subagent's request and its absence for the viewed session's own. "answers a subagent's permission from the root session after a fresh load" (`packages/app/e2e/regression/session-request-docks.spec.ts:212`) already sets up the first case.

title: feat(app): running menu inside a nested subagent lists only its parent's subtree, not the root's
body:
## Finding

The session header's running menu takes its owner from the viewed session's **parent**. PR #60 (merged as 1585d2b91e) made the menu nest running subagents at any depth below that owner, but kept the owner rule.

- Inside a direct child, the parent is the root, so the menu shows the whole tree.
- From depth 2 on, it doesn't. Viewing a grandchild G (root R → child C → G), the owner is C. The menu lists C's running subagents and everything below them, but not R's other running subagents or anything below those.

The rule predates nesting. It was written on 2026-10-05 (3a861ff8b0e), when a subagent's parent was always the root; subagents can launch subagents since PR #39 (2026-10-18). The agent that implemented #60 raised this as an open question, and the PR kept the parent rule without recording a decision.

## Evidence (main 5214f4d8ae)

- `packages/app/src/session/requests/model.ts:95-102`: the comment `// Inside a subagent, running work is the parent's, so the header lists its siblings.`, then `owner = data.session.get(id)?.parentID ?? id`. `createSessionBackground({ sessionID: owner, ... })` follows at 104-110.
- `model.ts:169` exposes `running: { sessionID: owner, ... tasks: running.tasks }`. `packages/app/src/session/screen.tsx:347-351` and `packages/app/src/session/timeline/message-timeline.tsx:435-439` pass those to `SessionRunningMenu` as `owner` and `tasks`.
- `packages/app/src/session/header/session-running-menu.tsx:80-86` builds the nested tree with `runningSessions({ sessionID: props.owner, ... })`, so nothing outside the owner's subtree can appear.
- `packages/app/src/session/requests/background.ts`: the owner's running subagents come from sessions whose `parentID` is the owner (100-118), and subagent calls still starting come from the owner's messages (line 21).

## Options

1. **Use the root as the owner.** `data.session.root(id)` already exists and the app uses it (`shell/layout/project-avatar-state.ts:72`, `shell/notifications/notification.tsx:179`). Every session in a tree would then show the same menu. The root's messages would need loading when a deep subagent is viewed: today `session/timeline/controller.tsx:310-317` loads only the direct parent's messages, and only when the child's task description is missing and those messages aren't loaded yet.
2. **Keep the parent as the owner**, and record why, for example that the menu is about the work around the viewed session. The comment at `model.ts:95` should then describe the scope at depth 2 and below.

Either way, the background-related lists at `model.ts:112-114` are unaffected. They are gated to the top-level session, where parent-or-self and root are the same session.

## Acceptance criteria

- A decision recorded here or in the PR that closes this issue.
- With option 1:
  - A grandchild view's running menu lists the root's running subagents nested at any depth.
  - Opening a row and the stop button still work.
  - An e2e test next to "nests running subagents at any depth under the subagent that started them" (`packages/app/e2e/regression/timeline-stream.spec.ts:1405`) covers a grandchild view.
- With option 2: the comment at `model.ts:95` matches the behavior at depth 2 and below.

title: docs: troubleshooting.mdx says the desktop app uses OPENCODE_PORT for its local server — nothing reads it
body:
## Problem

The English troubleshooting guide tells users debugging a desktop "Connection Failed" dialog to check `OPENCODE_PORT`:

- `packages/web/src/content/docs/troubleshooting.mdx:132` — "If you have `OPENCODE_PORT` set in your environment, the desktop app will try to use that port for the local server."
- `:134` — "Unset `OPENCODE_PORT` (or pick a free port) and restart."

**Nothing in this repo reads `OPENCODE_PORT`.** A user who follows this section will unset (or change) a variable that has no effect, while the actual port sources — the `server.port` config covered in the section directly above (:126-128), or the desktop sidecar's own choice — go unexamined for the case the guide attributes to the env var.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `0bb248b075`)

- `git grep OPENCODE_PORT` over the full tree returns hits **only in the docs** (the English page above and its translations). No reader in `packages/desktop`, `packages/cli`, `packages/server`, or anywhere else; no setter either.
- How the desktop's local server port is actually chosen in v2: `packages/desktop/src/main/service/background-service.ts:51-57` — the sidecar is spawned with an explicit `--port` (a fixed `0x0c0c` in the isolated case, with a comment explaining a fixed port makes a second contender fail to bind); the CLI/server path takes its port from the `server` config section, which is exactly what the troubleshooting section above this one tells users to remove.
- Dedup: this variable is not part of the cli.mdx env tables, so the audits in #103/#105/#114 (scoped to `cli.mdx`/`tools.mdx`) never covered it; issue searches for `OPENCODE_PORT` return no existing issue.

## Why it matters

Troubleshooting docs are read by users who are already stuck. A step that cannot change anything burns the one restart cycle the user is willing to try, and misattributes the cause: a port clash from a stale `OPENCODE_PORT` is presented as a live possibility in v2 when the variable is v1 residue.

## Acceptance criteria

Pick one direction and apply it consistently:

1. **Align the docs with v2**: remove the `OPENCODE_PORT` passage from `troubleshooting.mdx` (English source; translations follow the usual docs-locale-sync flow), keeping the working advice (the `server.port`/`server.hostname` config section above it). Or:
2. **Implement it**: make the desktop read `OPENCODE_PORT` when choosing its local server port, with a test showing the spawned server binds the requested port.

Filed-only: implement-vs-remove needs a maintainer decision (mirroring #103/#105), so no fix is attempted here. Single-repo: the guide and the desktop app live only in this repo.

title: docs: eleven remaining OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_* variables in the cli.mdx Experimental table are read nowhere
body:
## Problem

The Experimental table in `packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx` (lines 718–734) promises a set of `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_*` switches. Four of them (plus the umbrella) are tracked in #105, two rows belong to the desktop-setter finding in #115, and one was #104 — but **eleven rows remain that nothing in this repo reads**, so a user who sets any of them silently gets no effect:

| Variable | Docs promise (cli.mdx) | Readers in code |
|---|---|---|
| `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLE_COPY_ON_SELECT` | :720 "Disable copy on select in TUI" | none — copy-on-select survives only as a legacy config key migrated in `packages/cli/src/config/migrate.ts:45-53` (`terminal.copy_on_select`) |
| `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX` | :722 "Max output tokens for LLM responses" | none |
| `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_OXFMT` | :724 "Enable oxfmt formatter" | none |
| `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_EXA` | :727 "Enable experimental Exa features" | none (distinct from `OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA` in #105) |
| `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_LSP_TY` | :728 "Enable TY LSP for python files" | none |
| `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_PLAN_MODE` | :729 "Enable plan mode" | none |
| `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_EVENT_SYSTEM` | :730 "Enable experimental event system" | none |
| `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_NATIVE_LLM` | :731 "Enable native LLM request path" | none |
| `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_PARALLEL` | :732 "Enable parallel web search execution" | none (distinct from `OPENCODE_ENABLE_PARALLEL` in #105) |
| `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_SCOUT` | :733 "Enable Scout subagent" | none |
| `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_WORKSPACES` | :734 "Enable workspace support" | none |

## Evidence (verified this run, main `0bb248b075`)

- Method, same as #105/#114: `git grep <VAR>` over the full tree excluding `packages/web/src/content/docs/**` returns **zero hits** for every variable above — no reader, no setter, no test.
- #105's body explicitly scoped itself to four variables and noted "the rest of the `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_*` table (cli.mdx:718-734) is in the same state" — this issue is that remainder, minus the rows now covered elsewhere: `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL` + `BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` + `LSP_TOOL` (#105), `ICON_DISCOVERY` + `FILEWATCHER` (#115), `DISABLE_FILEWATCHER` (#104, resolved).
- Dedup: searches for these names across open and closed issues return only #105 and #114; neither lists any of the eleven above.

## Why it matters

Same silent-no-op shape as #103/#105/#114, in the table users treat as the canonical switch list for experimental features. Several rows (`PLAN_MODE`, `WORKSPACES`, `SCOUT`, `NATIVE_LLM`) read as major feature gates, so a user can reasonably believe they have enabled a feature that v2 either ships unconditionally, gates through config, or does not have. Fixing the whole remainder at once ends the one-variable-at-a-time drip (#103, #104, #105, #108, #114, #115).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For **each** variable above, a recorded decision: implement the documented behaviour in v2, map it onto its v2 config equivalent in the docs, or remove the row from the docs (English source; translations follow the usual docs-locale-sync flow).
- [ ] Afterwards, every row of the cli.mdx Experimental table either has a reader in the tree or is explicitly marked as a v1 removal.
- [ ] Ideally: the lightweight guard #114 asks for (a test or script that fails when a variable documented in the cli.mdx env tables has no reader) covers this table too, so the next dead variable is caught at PR time.

Filed-only: the implement-vs-remove choice is per-variable and needs a maintainer decision (as with #105), so no fix is attempted here. Single-repo: these docs and the v2 codebase they describe live only in this repo.

title: fix(desktop): OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_ICON_DISCOVERY / OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_FILEWATCHER are set on every launch but read nowhere
body:
## Summary

The desktop app sets `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_ICON_DISCOVERY="true"` and `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_FILEWATCHER="true"` into its environment on every launch, intending to enable icon discovery and the file watcher for the servers it spawns — but nothing in this codebase reads either variable. Both are silent no-ops in production code, the same failure shape as #108 (`OPENCODE_DISABLE_EMBEDDED_WEB_UI`), except here the docs also promise both variables to users.

## Evidence (all on main `0bb248b075`)

The only setters, and no readers:

- `packages/desktop/src/main/lifecycle/environment.ts:29-30` — `preferApplicationEnvironment` does `Object.assign(process.env, { OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_ICON_DISCOVERY: "true", OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_FILEWATCHER: "true", OPENCODE_CLIENT: "desktop" })`, so the values are inherited by every server the desktop spawns.
- Repo-wide `git grep` for each name returns **only that setter line** outside the docs (the docs rows are `packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx:719` and `:723`). No reader exists in `packages/cli`, `packages/server`, `packages/core`, or anywhere else.

The filewatcher is actually controlled by different names, and is on by default:

- `packages/cli/src/server-process.ts:146` — `filewatcher: !truthy(process.env.OPENCODE_FILEWATCHER_DISABLE ?? process.env.OPENCODE_DISABLE_FILEWATCHER)`. The watcher defaults to enabled and can only be *disabled* via those two names; setting `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_FILEWATCHER=true` cannot change anything. (The related dead name `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLE_FILEWATCHER` was #104, fixed by renaming that setter to `OPENCODE_DISABLE_FILEWATCHER`.)
- Icon discovery: no reader and no icon-discovery feature was found in `packages/server` or `packages/core` — the variable names a v1 feature that does not exist in v2 under any name.

## Why it matters

Anyone reading `environment.ts` as the list of what the desktop turns on for its servers is misled: neither entry does anything. The filewatcher entry is worse than dead — it invites the belief that watching is opt-in via this variable, when in fact it is default-on and governed by the `OPENCODE_FILEWATCHER_DISABLE` / `OPENCODE_DISABLE_FILEWATCHER` names, so a future attempt to control it from the desktop through this variable would silently fail. Users following the cli.mdx Experimental table hit the same wall from the other side.

## Acceptance criteria

Pick one direction per variable and apply it consistently:

1. **Implement it**: read the variable at the owning boundary (server-process `fs.filewatcher` selection for the watcher; wherever icon discovery would live, if the feature is intended to exist in v2), with a test showing setting it changes behaviour. Or:
2. **Remove the dead setters**: drop both entries from `environment.ts:29-30`, and remove or correct the matching cli.mdx Experimental-table rows (719, 723) so the docs no longer promise them.

Either way, afterwards no launch-time setter in the desktop lifecycle should name a variable nothing reads (the standard #108's acceptance asks for), and the docs should not list either variable as a working enable switch unless a reader exists.

Filed-only: the implement-vs-remove choice needs a maintainer decision (mirroring #108), so no fix is attempted here. Single-repo: this desktop lifecycle code exists only in this repo.

title: docs: eleven more OPENCODE_* variables in the cli.mdx env table are read nowhere — DISABLE_PRUNE, DISABLE_AUTOCOMPACT, PERMISSION, TUI_CONFIG and seven others

This is the same docs-vs-v2 drift as #103 (`OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME`), #104 (`OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLE_FILEWATCHER`) and #105 (`OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA` et al.), but none of those issues cover the variables below; each was checked against open and recently closed issues before filing.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `20d3a79bd7`)

| Variable | Docs promise | Readers in code |
|---|---|---|
| `OPENCODE_TUI_CONFIG` | cli.mdx:680 "Path to TUI config file" | none — v2 resolves TUI config from the main config (`resolve(yield* config.get(), …)` in `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/mini.ts`); there is no separate TUI file path |
| `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PRUNE` | cli.mdx:685 "Disable pruning of old data" | none |
| `OPENCODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE` | cli.mdx:686 "Disable automatic terminal title updates" | none — v2 equivalent is the TUI config key `terminal.title` (`packages/tui/src/config/index.tsx`, "Update the terminal window title") |
| `OPENCODE_PERMISSION` | cli.mdx:687 "Inlined json permissions config" | none in code — the only occurrences are *setters* in `.github/workflows/review.yml:61`, `.github/workflows/opencode.yml:43`, `.github/workflows/duplicate-issues.yml:59,194` |
| `OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS` | cli.mdx:688 "Disable default plugins" | none |
| `OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD` | cli.mdx:689 and `lsp.mdx:54` "disable automatic LSP server downloads by setting … to `true`" | none — v2 LSP config (`packages/schema/src/config/lsp.ts`) is per-server `disabled`, with no global download toggle |
| `OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_MODELS` | cli.mdx:690 "Enable experimental models" | none |
| `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOCOMPACT` | cli.mdx:691 "Disable automatic context compaction" | none — v2 equivalent is the config key `compaction.auto` (`packages/schema/src/config/compaction.ts:11`, handled in `packages/core/src/config/normalize.ts`) |
| `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT` | cli.mdx:693 "Disable reading `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`" | none — `packages/cli/src/server-process.ts` gates `.claude` roots only on `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE` / `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS`, with the comment ".claude is only read for skills, so both flags gate the same roots" |
| `OPENCODE_DISABLE_MOUSE` | cli.mdx:696 "Disable mouse capture in the TUI" | none — v2 equivalent is the TUI config key `mouse` (`packages/tui/src/config/index.tsx`, "Enable terminal mouse capture") |
| `OPENCODE_FAKE_VCS` | cli.mdx:697 "Fake VCS provider for testing purposes" | none |

Method: `grep -rn <VAR>` over the full tree (all file types, excluding `node_modules`), filtering out `packages/web/src/content/docs/**` and `services/www` docs. Every variable above returns only its docs rows (and, for `OPENCODE_PERMISSION`, the workflow setters listed).

## Why it matters

- Silent no-ops are worse than missing features: a user who sets `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOCOMPACT`, `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PRUNE` or `OPENCODE_PERMISSION` believes they have changed behaviour — in the permission case, restricted it — and nothing tells them otherwise.
- The table is the canonical env-var reference; every dead row erodes trust in the rows that do work and generates support confusion.
- This keeps recurring one variable at a time (#103, #104, #105, #108); fixing the whole remaining table at once, ideally with a guard, ends the drip.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For **each** variable above, a recorded decision: implement the documented behaviour in v2, map it onto the v2 config equivalent, or remove the row from the docs (English source; translations follow the usual flow).
- [ ] Where a v2 config equivalent already exists (at minimum: `compaction.auto`, TUI `mouse`, TUI `terminal.title`), the docs either point to it or the env var is wired to it — not left as a silent no-op.
- [ ] `lsp.mdx:54` is corrected together with the cli.mdx row for `OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD`.
- [ ] The `OPENCODE_PERMISSION` workflow setters are reconciled with the decision (kept only if something in the delivery path actually reads the variable).
- [ ] Ideally: a lightweight guard (test or script, in the spirit of the existing docs/CI checks) that fails when a variable documented in the cli.mdx env table has no reader in the tree, so the next dead variable is caught at PR time instead of by audit.

Filed-only: the implement-vs-remove choice is per-variable and needs a maintainer decision (as with #105), so no fix is attempted here.

title: fix(desktop): OPENCODE_DISABLE_EMBEDDED_WEB_UI is set on every launch but read nowhere — desktop servers serve the embedded web UI anyway
body:
## Summary

The desktop app sets `OPENCODE_DISABLE_EMBEDDED_WEB_UI="true"` on every launch, intending its server not to serve the embedded web UI — but nothing in this codebase reads that variable. Every server the desktop starts therefore serves the full embedded web UI anyway. It is a silent no-op in production code, the same failure shape as #104, except here no correctly-named alternative exists.

## Evidence (all on main `4e948420ce`)

The only setter, and no reader:

- `packages/desktop/src/main/lifecycle/configure.ts:21` — `process.env.OPENCODE_DISABLE_EMBEDDED_WEB_UI = "true"` inside `configureApplication()`, which `packages/desktop/src/main/index.ts:15` calls synchronously at every desktop launch, before anything else.
- Repo-wide `git grep OPENCODE_DISABLE_EMBEDDED_WEB_UI` returns **only that one line** — no reader in `packages/cli`, `packages/server`, `packages/core`, or anywhere else, and the variable is not promised in the docs either (so the docs audit in #105, which scopes to variables named in `cli.mdx`/`tools.mdx`, does not cover it).

The server path that should honor it, and does not:

- `packages/cli/src/server-process.ts:101` — every server start unconditionally builds `WebUi.handler()` as its transform; the surrounding code reads many other `OPENCODE_*` variables from the same inherited environment (e.g. `OPENCODE_CLIENT` at line 106, the `OPENCODE_DISABLE_*` family at lines 123–150), just never this one.
- `packages/cli/src/services/web-ui.ts:7-29` — the handler serves UI assets for every non-API path (`/api`, `/auth/`, `/openapi.json` are passed through; everything else goes to `serveUI`, which falls back to `index.html`), with no environment check.
- `packages/cli/src/app-assets.ts:12-22` — `load()` likewise has no disable check; in a non-local build it even *fails* when the embedded assets are missing, so a desktop build cannot shed them either.

The desktop does not need the server's UI:

- `packages/desktop/src/main/windows/scheme.ts:20` — packaged windows load the renderer via the custom renderer protocol (`${rendererProtocol}://${rendererHost}/…`); line 15's dev path loads the dev URL. Neither goes through the server's embedded web UI, which is presumably why `configure.ts` tried to disable it.

## Why it matters

A desktop-spawned server listens on a real port and, per the comment in `web-ui.ts`, serves the web shell *before* API authentication so a browser gets the sign-in screen. The desktop author's one-line defence against that surface — set at the earliest possible moment in startup — does nothing, and nothing warns about it. Either the desktop is carrying an unnecessary unauthenticated-before-login UI surface on every install, or the setter is v1 dead weight misleading anyone who reads `configure.ts` as a list of things the desktop actually turns off.

## Acceptance criteria

Pick one direction and apply it consistently:

1. **Implement it**: read `OPENCODE_DISABLE_EMBEDDED_WEB_UI` at the owning boundary (the `WebUi.handler` / server-process transform selection, or `app-assets.load`) so a server started with it set does not serve UI assets or `index.html` for non-API paths (404 is fine), while `/api`, `/auth/` and `/openapi.json` behaviour is unchanged. Add a test showing the handler's behaviour with the variable set vs unset. Or:
2. **Remove it**: delete the dead setter from `configure.ts` and record (in the PR or a comment here) that desktop servers intentionally serve the embedded web UI.

Either way, afterwards a repo-wide grep should show the setter matched by a reader, or no setter at all.

Related: #104 (same silent-no-op shape, but there a correctly-named reader already existed, so the fix was mechanical — here it does not), #103 / #105 (docs-promised variables; this one is set in code and promised nowhere).

Found by the new-issue-creator job, verifying repo-wide grep counts and the desktop → server-process → web-ui chain on current main.

title: docs: OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA / OPENCODE_ENABLE_PARALLEL / OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS / OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_LSP_TOOL are promised but read nowhere
body:
## Summary

Beyond the username case in #103, several more environment variables the English docs promise are read nowhere in this v2 codebase, so setting them silently does nothing: the web-search enable flags (`OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA`, `OPENCODE_ENABLE_PARALLEL`), the shell-timeout variable (`OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`), the LSP-tool gate (`OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_LSP_TOOL`, and the `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL` umbrella the docs pair it with). Each has a working v2 replacement the docs never mention.

## Evidence (all on main `2d302d6718`)

Docs promising the variables:

- `packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx:699-700` — env table: `OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA` "Enable Exa web search tools", `OPENCODE_ENABLE_PARALLEL` "Enable Parallel web search tools".
- `packages/web/src/content/docs/tools.mdx:239-246` — "This tool is only available when using the OpenCode or OpenCode Go provider, or when either the `OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA` or `OPENCODE_ENABLE_PARALLEL` environment variable is set…", with `OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA=1 opencode` / `OPENCODE_ENABLE_PARALLEL=1 opencode` examples.
- `packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx:721` — `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` "Default timeout for bash commands in ms".
- `packages/web/src/content/docs/tools.mdx:154-159` — the lsp tool "is only available when `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_LSP_TOOL=true` (or `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL=true`)".
- `packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx:718-734` — the rest of the `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_*` table (output-token max, oxfmt, plan mode, scout, workspaces, …) is in the same state; this issue scopes to the four above, the audit method below covers the rest.

Nothing reads them:

- `git grep` for each of `OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA`, `OPENCODE_ENABLE_PARALLEL`, `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_LSP_TOOL` across the repo excluding `packages/web` returns **zero** hits. `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL` itself is only ever *set* (desktop `environment.ts:29-30`, WSL sidecar), never read.

The v2 mechanisms that replaced them:

- Web search: providers are registered unconditionally — `packages/core/src/plugin/websearch/exa.ts:26-40` and `parallel.ts` register via `ctx.websearch.transform`, credentials come from the integration's env method (`EXA_API_KEY`, exa.ts:37), and selection/default is the `websearch` config (`packages/core/src/config/plugin/websearch.ts:12-16`) plus the tool's provider-selection flow (`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/websearch.ts`). No env gate exists.
- Shell timeout: `experimental.shell_timeout` config, read fresh at execute time in `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/shell.ts:119` (implemented for #13 item 3).
- The audit method: for every `OPENCODE_*` name in the cli.mdx env tables, `git grep <name> -- ':!packages/web'` — a documented variable should have at least one reader outside the docs.

## Why it matters

A user who follows tools.mdx and runs `OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA=1 opencode` to get web search on a non-OpenCode provider gets no error and no effect — the same silent-failure shape as #103, in a feature-gating (not just cosmetic) setting. The shell-timeout case is worse: the v1 variable and the v2 config have the same purpose, so users reasonably keep setting the documented one.

## Acceptance criteria

Pick one direction per variable and apply it consistently (mirroring #103):

1. **Implement it**: read the variable at the owning boundary (web-search provider registration / shell tool / lsp tool) with a test showing setting it changes behaviour. Or:
2. **Align the docs with v2**: remove the dead-variable claims from `cli.mdx` and `tools.mdx`, and document the working replacement instead (`websearch` config + `EXA_API_KEY`/integration credentials for search; `experimental.shell_timeout` for the shell timeout; whatever actually gates the lsp tool, or remove that claim).

Either way, afterwards every `OPENCODE_*` variable named in the English `cli.mdx`/`tools.mdx` should have a reader in code, or be explicitly marked as a v1 removal. Translations under `packages/web/src/content/docs/<locale>/` carry the same claims and should follow the English fix (the docs-locale-sync workflow propagates English changes).

Filed separately from the functional wrong-name bug in the test workflow / WSL sidecar, which has a mechanical fix.

title: docs: OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME is promised but never read — basic-auth username is hardcoded to 'opencode'
body:
## Summary

The docs promise that the basic-auth username for `serve`/`web` can be overridden with `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` (default `opencode`). In this v2 codebase nothing reads that variable: the username is hardcoded to `opencode` on both the server and client sides, so setting the variable silently does nothing. A test even sets it, which makes the dead variable look supported.

## Evidence (all on main `2d302d6718`)

Docs promising the override:

- `packages/web/src/content/docs/server.mdx:39` — "The username defaults to `opencode`, or set `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` to override it. This applies to both `opencode serve` and `opencode web`."
- `packages/web/src/content/docs/web.mdx:89` — "The username defaults to `opencode` but can be changed with `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME`."
- `packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx:702` — env table: "`OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` | Override basic auth username (default `opencode`)".
- `packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx:126` and `:378` — `--username`/`-u` flag rows: "Basic auth username (defaults to `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` or `opencode`)" (no such flag exists in `packages/cli/src/commands/commands.ts`).

Code hardcoding `opencode` and never reading the variable:

- `packages/server/src/auth.ts:19-21` — `Config.configLayer` accepts only a password and forces `username: "opencode"`; `authorized()` (line ~31) rejects any other username.
- `packages/server/src/process.ts:233` — `ServerAuth.Config.of({ password: ..., username: "opencode" })`.
- `packages/cli/src/env.ts:3-13` — the module that declares itself "Every environment variable the CLI reads, in one place" defines `password` (`OPENCODE_PASSWORD` / `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`) and no username.
- `packages/cli/src/services/server-connection.ts:28` — client auth for an explicit `--server` hardcodes `username: "opencode"`, so this CLI also cannot authenticate to a server that expects a different username.
- `packages/cli/src/services/standalone.ts:53` — standalone server auth hardcodes `username: "opencode"`.
- Repo-wide grep: `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` appears only in docs/translations and in `packages/cli/test/standalone.test.ts:11`, which sets it to `"custom"` and then asserts only HTTP 200 — the variable has no effect on the run, so the test gives false confidence that it is honored.

Corroboration that the fixed username is the deliberate v2 behavior: developing-today/openchamber `packages/vscode/src/opencode.ts:95` comments "OpenCode 2 accepts only the `opencode` username; OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME is ignored." (The variable was a v1 feature; the docs are v1 leftovers.)

## Why it matters

A user who follows the docs and sets `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` gets no error and no effect — the exact silent-failure shape that erodes trust in a security setting. Either the setting should work, or the docs and the misleading test should stop claiming it does.

## Acceptance criteria

Pick one direction and apply it consistently:

1. **Implement it**: read `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` in `packages/cli/src/env.ts`, thread it through the server auth config (`packages/server/src/auth.ts` / `process.ts`), the standalone service, and the `--server` client auth; add a test that a non-default username actually authenticates and the default one fails (and vice versa). Or:
2. **Align docs and test with the deliberate v2 behavior**: remove the override claims from `server.mdx`, `web.mdx`, and `cli.mdx` (env table and the `--username` rows), state plainly that the username is always `opencode`, and drop the unused `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` from `packages/cli/test/standalone.test.ts`.

Either way, a grep for `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` afterwards should find it only where it is genuinely honored (direction 1) or nowhere outside a "v1 removed" note (direction 2).
