body:
## Summary

`SpeechStream.headerUsage` — the shared parser that turns a speech provider's usage header into reported `MediaUsage` — accepts any finite `Number(...)`: a blank header manufactures a usage of 0, a negative header reports negative usage, and hex/exponent spellings are reinterpreted (`0x10` → 16, `1e3` → 1000). Its two callers report the result as the call's billed usage: Deepgram's `dg-char-count` (`packages/ai/src/protocols/deepgram-speech.ts:118`, type `characters`) and ElevenLabs' `character-cost` (`packages/ai/src/protocols/elevenlabs-speech.ts:180`, type `credits`, with the comment at `:179` noting it is billed credits, not a character count).

## Evidence

`packages/ai/src/protocols/utils/speech-stream.ts:106-110`:

```ts
export const headerUsage = (type: "characters" | "credits", value: string | undefined): MediaUsage | undefined => {
  const amount = Number(value)
  if (!Number.isFinite(amount)) return undefined
  return type === "credits" ? { type, credits: amount } : { type, characters: amount }
}
```

`Number("") === 0` and `Number("   ") === 0`, both finite, so an empty-valued header — which gateways/proxies do emit — is indistinguishable from an authored `"0"`; and nothing rejects a negative amount, which no character count or credit cost can be.

Verified on main `771d1bd0cc` via a bun probe on the LAPTOP importing the real module's exported `headerUsage` (`speech-stream.ts` md5 `b927177d1563b6db9199c0180508e382`, byte-identical on both checkouts; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-28-0235/probe.ts`, removed after):

| Input | Result | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `""` | `{type: "characters", characters: 0}` | `undefined` — no usage reported |
| `"   "` | `{type: "characters", characters: 0}` | `undefined` |
| `"-5"` | `{type: "characters", characters: -5}` (and `credits: -5` for the credits type) | `undefined` |
| `"1e3"` | `{characters: 1000}` | `undefined` — not a plain count spelling |
| `"0x10"` | `{characters: 16}` | `undefined` |
| `"42"` (control) | `{characters: 42}` | 42 ✓ |
| `"0"` (control) | `{characters: 0}` | 0 ✓ (an authored zero is a real zero) |
| `"abc"` (control) | `undefined` | `undefined` ✓ |
| absent (control) | `undefined` | `undefined` ✓ |

## Why it matters

- The returned usage is what the speech finish event reports as the call's consumption (`SpeechStream.finish`, `speech-stream.ts:84-103`). A blank header therefore records a confidently wrong "this call used 0 characters / cost 0 credits" instead of "usage unknown", which is exactly the distinction cost displays and accounting rely on — the same harm as the blank-pricing case fixed for Modal in #678.
- A negative value is worse: negative credits/characters flowing into any summed usage total silently subtract from real usage.
- The function's own contract already has the right fallback — `undefined` for a value that is not a usable amount (the `"abc"` and absent controls take it). Blank, negative, and wrong-notation values escape it only because `Number()`'s grammar and range are wider than a count's.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Blank or whitespace-only header values return `undefined` (no usage), for both `characters` and `credits`.
- [ ] Negative amounts return `undefined`; an authored `"0"` still returns a zero usage.
- [ ] Values outside a plain non-negative decimal grammar (at minimum `0x10` and `1e3`) return `undefined` rather than a reinterpreted amount.
- [ ] Plain values are unchanged: `"42"` → 42, `"0"` → 0.
- [ ] Regression tests cover blank, negative, hex, and exponent inputs plus the plain controls, in the speech protocol tests under `packages/ai/test/`.

body:
## Summary

`WebSearch`'s 429 cooldown parser uses bare `Number(...)`, so a `retry-after` header that is neither RFC 9110 delay-seconds (`1*DIGIT`) nor an HTTP-date is reinterpreted in another notation: `retry-after: 1e3` sidelines the provider for 1,000,000 ms (16.7 minutes) and `retry-after: 0x10` for 16 seconds, instead of taking the parser's own 60-second fallback for unusable values. This is the same grammar hole #682 covers in `RequestExecutor` (`packages/ai/src/route/executor.ts`); `cooldownMillis` in `packages/core/src/websearch.ts` is a separate parser with its own fallback that #682's fix does not reach.

## Evidence

`packages/core/src/websearch.ts:215-221` (the cooldown is set at `:204` on a 429 in `random` selection mode, and `randomProvider` at `:160-172` excludes the provider until it expires):

```ts
function cooldownMillis(value: string | undefined, now: number) {
  if (!value?.trim()) return 60_000
  const seconds = Number(value)
  if (Number.isFinite(seconds)) return seconds >= 0 ? seconds * 1000 : 60_000
  const date = Date.parse(value)
  return Number.isFinite(date) ? Math.max(0, date - now) : 60_000
}
```

The blank case is already handled (first line, the #677 pattern), and negatives already fall back — notation is the remaining hole: hex/exponent strings pass `Number.isFinite` and return before the HTTP-date branch or the 60 s fallback is ever considered.

Verified on main `771d1bd0cc` via a bun probe on the LAPTOP running the function's verbatim body (the function is module-private; `websearch.ts` md5 `76bf041b0ba345521fa2fd1c49f1fbc3`, byte-identical on both checkouts; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-28-0235/probe.ts`, removed after):

| `retry-after` | Result | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `"1e3"` | `1000000` ms | `60000` — not delay-seconds, not a date, so the unusable-value fallback |
| `"0x10"` | `16000` ms | `60000` |
| `"7"` (control) | `7000` | 7000 ✓ |
| `" 12 "` (control) | `12000` | 12000 ✓ |
| `"-5"` (control) | `60000` | 60000 ✓ |
| `"garbage"` (control) | `60000` | 60000 ✓ |
| HTTP-date 90 s ahead (control) | `90000` | 90000 ✓ |
| absent / `""` (control) | `60000` | 60000 ✓ |

## Why it matters

- In `random` web-search mode a 429 from one provider sets its cooldown from this header, and the provider is excluded from selection until the cooldown expires. An invented 16.7-minute cooldown shrinks the available provider pool far beyond anything the provider asked for; with few providers configured, repeated malformed headers can leave every provider cooling down and searches failing with the stored error.
- The parser already defines the right behaviour for values it cannot use — the 60-second fallback the `"garbage"` and negative controls take. Hex/exponent spellings are the only class that escapes it, because `Number()` accepts a grammar HTTP does not.
- Header values arrive verbatim from provider/gateway responses; a gateway that emits a non-standard numeric spelling is exactly the untrusted-input case this fallback exists for.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `retry-after` values that are not plain unsigned decimal integers and not HTTP-dates take the 60-second fallback — at minimum the hex (`0x10`) and exponent (`1e3`) forms.
- [ ] Authored plain values are unchanged: `"0"`, `"7"`, `" 12 "`, negative-to-fallback, and HTTP-date forms behave as today.
- [ ] Regression tests cover `1e3` and `0x10` plus the plain-value and HTTP-date controls (the cooldown is observable through the `WebSearch` service's provider exclusion in `packages/core/test/plugin/websearch.test.ts`, or by exporting the parser for a unit test — the test shape is the fixer's choice).
- [ ] The fix states the accepted grammar in a comment at the parse site, as #682 requires for the executor parser.

body:
## Summary

`RequestExecutor`'s retry-after parsing uses bare `Number(...)`, so header values that are neither RFC 9110 delay-seconds (1*DIGIT) nor an HTTP-date are reinterpreted as numbers in another notation: `retry-after: 1e3` becomes a 1,000,000 ms wait (16.7 minutes) and `retry-after: 0x10` becomes 16 seconds. The same loose grammar applies to the non-standard `retry-after-ms` header (`0x10` → 16 ms, `1e3` → 1,000 ms). A provider or gateway emitting a malformed header gets an invented wait instead of the parser's own fallback for unusable values (no instruction / the next source).

This is the remainder of #677, which fixed the blank-value case in the same function: the blank check does not touch notation, so hex/exponent forms still pass `Number.isFinite` and return before any validity check.

## Evidence

`packages/ai/src/route/executor.ts:23-36`:

```ts
const retryAfterMs = (headers: Record<string, string>) => {
  const millis = Number(headers["retry-after-ms"])
  if (Number.isFinite(millis)) return Math.max(0, millis)
  const value = headers["retry-after"]
  if (!value) return undefined
  const seconds = Number(value)
  if (Number.isFinite(seconds)) return Math.max(0, seconds * 1000)
  const date = Date.parse(value)
  ...
```

Verified on main `7001736e73` via a laptop bun probe importing the real module through the exported `responseRateLimit` (route-time-windows worktree; its `executor.ts` is byte-identical to main, md5 `69e35222661119713cd1db08d8d7eb93`; probe removed after, tree clean):

| Headers | Result | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `{"retry-after": "1e3"}` | `{retryAfterMs: 1000000}` | `undefined` — not delay-seconds, not a date |
| `{"retry-after": "0x10"}` | `{retryAfterMs: 16000}` | `undefined` |
| `{"retry-after-ms": "1e3"}` | `{retryAfterMs: 1000}` | `undefined` (or the `retry-after` value, if present) |
| `{"retry-after-ms": "0x10"}` | `{retryAfterMs: 16}` | `undefined` (or fall through) |
| `{"retry-after": "10"}` (control) | `{retryAfterMs: 10000}` | 10000 ✓ |
| `{"retry-after": "garbage"}` (control) | `undefined` | `undefined` ✓ |

Note the asymmetry the controls show: a plainly unparseable value already falls back to `undefined`, while a value that is only parseable in the wrong notation is honoured at face value.

## Why it matters

- `retryAfterMs` drives the wait before the next attempt and classifies the failure as a rate limit (`packages/ai/src/provider-error.ts:283,299`; `packages/core/src/session/runner/retry.ts` clamps it, and `model-route.ts` cooldown derives from it). An invented 16.7-minute wait stalls a session far beyond anything the provider asked for; an invented 16 ms `retry-after-ms` does the opposite, discarding a real wait the same response may carry in `retry-after`.
- On the success path `responseRateLimit` feeds the route observer's rate-limit snapshot (`packages/core/src/model-route-log.ts`), so the invented value is also recorded as the provider's stated limit state.
- The fleet has already decided this grammar question elsewhere: `McpxDiagnose` documents that its accepted grammar is `Number()`'s by explicit design (mcpx-diagnose.ts, with tests); HTTP delay-seconds has a defined grammar (RFC 9110 §10.2.3: `1*DIGIT`), and this parser already implements the fallback for values outside it — it just never reaches the fallback for hex/exponent spellings.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `retry-after` values that are not plain unsigned decimal integers and not HTTP-dates yield no instruction (`undefined` from the parser; `responseRateLimit` returns `undefined` when nothing else is present) — at minimum the hex (`0x10`) and exponent (`1e3`) forms.
- [ ] `retry-after-ms` values outside a plain decimal grammar fall through to `retry-after`, as blank values do after #677.
- [ ] Authored plain values are unchanged: `"0"`, `"250"` (ms), `"10"` (s), and HTTP-date forms behave as today, including the existing pinned tests in `packages/ai/test/executor.test.ts`.
- [ ] Regression tests cover `1e3` and `0x10` for both headers, plus the plain-value controls.
- [ ] The fix states the accepted grammar in a comment at the parse site, so the next reader does not have to re-derive it.

body:
## Summary

`Form.validateFields` — the create-time validation that `Form.create`/`ask` run before a form is stored — checks only `when` references. It never checks a field's own constraints against each other, so a form whose bounds contradict themselves is created successfully and can then never be answered: every possible answer fails `validateAnswer`. The same gap accepts a string field whose `pattern` is not a compilable regex; the authoring error only surfaces at answer time, where it is reported as an answer failure ("Form field has invalid pattern") for every value the user tries.

## Evidence

`packages/core/src/form.ts`:

- `validateFields` (lines ~313-336) validates duplicate keys and `when` references only — the header comment states its purpose: "Rejecting these at creation surfaces authoring mistakes to the caller instead of silently never matching." No bound or pattern check exists.
- `validateField` (lines ~356-395) enforces the bounds per answer: string `minLength`/`maxLength`, number `minimum`/`maximum`, multiselect `minItems`/`maxItems`, and compiles `pattern` with `new RegExp(...)` inside a try/catch that returns `Form field has invalid pattern: <key>` — at answer time, against the answerer.

Verified on main `7001736e73` via a laptop bun probe importing the real module (`route-time-windows` worktree, whose `form.ts` differs from main only inside `isDateTime` — the #656/#666 code, untouched by this probe; probe removed after, tree clean):

| Field definition | `validateFields` (create) | `validateAnswer` |
|---|---|---|
| string `minLength: 10, maxLength: 5` | `undefined` (accepted) | len 3 → "too short", len 7 → "too short", len 12 → "too long" — no length can pass |
| number `minimum: 10, maximum: 5` | `undefined` (accepted) | 3 → "too small", 7 → "too small", 12 → "too large" — no value can pass |
| multiselect `minItems: 3, maxItems: 1` | `undefined` (accepted) | 1 item → "Too few", 2 → "Too few", 3 → "Too many" — no selection can pass |
| string `pattern: "["` | `undefined` (accepted) | any value → "Form field has invalid pattern: p" |
| control: string `minLength: 2, maxLength: 5` | `undefined` | `"abc"` → `undefined` ✓ |

## Why it matters

- Forms are how agents ask the user questions (elicitation). An unsatisfiable form hangs the interaction: `Form.ask` waits on the deferred until cancel/close, and the user is shown a question no answer can settle, with errors that blame their answers ("too short" / "too long" for the same field).
- The invalid-pattern case actively misattributes the fault: the field author wrote a broken regex, but every answer is rejected as if the answer were wrong, so the failure reads as user error in logs and UIs.
- `validateFields` already exists precisely to catch authoring mistakes at creation (#601 extended it for `when` references); bounds coherence and pattern compilability are the same class of authoring mistake, checked nowhere.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `validateFields` rejects a string field with `minLength > maxLength`, a number/integer field with `minimum > maximum`, and a multiselect field with `minItems > maxItems`, with an error naming the field key.
- [ ] `validateFields` rejects a string field whose `pattern` does not compile as a RegExp, at creation time (the answer-time "invalid pattern" answer error remains only as defense-in-depth, if kept).
- [ ] Coherent definitions are unchanged: equal bounds (`minLength == maxLength`, `minimum == maximum`, `minItems == maxItems`) still create, and one-sided bounds still create.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/core/test/form.test.ts` cover each inverted pair, the invalid pattern, and an equal-bounds control.

body:
## Summary

`ModalModels`' price conversion accepts blank and negative pricing from the remote `/models` payload: a blank string becomes a cost of 0 and a negative value becomes a negative cost, in both cases silently replacing the catalog template's known cost. Omitting a price keeps the template cost (that behaviour is pinned by an existing test) — a present-but-invalid price is worse than an absent one.

## Evidence

`packages/core/src/modal/models.ts:85-89`:

```ts
function price(value: string | number | undefined, fallback: Money.USDPerMillionTokens) {
  if (value === undefined) return fallback
  const parsed = Number(value) * 1_000_000
  return Number.isFinite(parsed) ? Money.USDPerMillionTokens.make(parsed) : fallback
}
```

The schema admits any string for `pricing.prompt` / `completion` / `input_cache_read` (`models.ts:25-31`), `Number("") === 0` is finite, and no lower bound is checked — while the sibling `limit()` helper in the same file (`:91-94`) does reject out-of-range values (`parsed >= 0`) and falls back.

Verified on main `8cd052358a` via a bun probe on the laptop calling the exported `ModalModels.derive` (temporary test in the `route-time-windows` worktree, whose `modal/models.ts` is byte-identical to main, md5 `be297a36af07f259622f19225f5e3d7b`; probe removed after, tree clean). Template cost: input 5, output 10, cache.read 1, cache.write 2 (USD per million tokens):

| Remote pricing | Resulting cost | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `prompt: ""`, `completion: "  "`, `input_cache_read: ""` | input 0, output 0, cache.read 0 | template 5 / 10 / 1 (as when omitted) |
| `prompt: "-0.000003"`, `completion: -0.000004` | input **-3**, output **-4** | template 5 / 10 |
| `prompt: "abc"` (control) | input 5 (fallback) | 5 ✓ |
| `prompt: "0.000001"` (control) | input 1 | 1 ✓ |
| pricing omitted (pinned, `models.test.ts:102-126`) | template kept | ✓ |

## Why it matters

- The derived `Model.Info` cost is what cost accounting and the session header report. A negative per-token price makes recorded spend decrease as tokens are consumed; a blank-turned-0 makes a paid model report as free. Both corrupt the same numbers the route/usage tooling exists to keep honest.
- The payload is remote data from the Modal proxy endpoint (`load()` fetches `${baseURL}/models` and decodes each item tolerantly, `models.ts:52-71`): a proxy that emits `""` for an unknown price — a common convention — erases a cost the bundled catalog already knows, instead of leaving it in place like an omitted field does.
- An authored price of exactly `"0"` is a legitimate free model and must keep working; the defect is blank (no digits at all) and negative values, not zero.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Blank or whitespace-only pricing strings fall back to the template/default cost, like an omitted or non-numeric value.
- [ ] Negative pricing (string or number) falls back instead of producing a negative `Money.USDPerMillionTokens` cost.
- [ ] An authored `0` / `"0"` still yields a zero cost, and valid positive string/number pricing is unchanged.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/core/test/modal/models.test.ts` cover blank and negative pricing against a priced template, beside the existing omitted-pricing test.

body:
## Summary

`RequestExecutor`'s retry-after parsing reads a blank `retry-after-ms` header as 0 ms — and because that branch returns before looking at `retry-after`, a blank millisecond header silently discards a valid seconds (or HTTP-date) instruction the same response carries. A blank `retry-after` of only whitespace does the same. The provider's stated wait becomes an immediate retry.

## Evidence

`packages/ai/src/route/executor.ts:23-36`:

```ts
const retryAfterMs = (headers: Record<string, string>) => {
  const millis = Number(headers["retry-after-ms"])
  if (Number.isFinite(millis)) return Math.max(0, millis)

  const value = headers["retry-after"]
  if (!value) return undefined

  const seconds = Number(value)
  if (Number.isFinite(seconds)) return Math.max(0, seconds * 1000)
  ...
```

`Number("") === 0` and `Number("  ") === 0`, both finite, so a blank value is indistinguishable from an authored `"0"` (which existing tests pin as a real 0 — `packages/ai/test/executor.test.ts:461-546`).

Verified on main `8cd052358a` via a bun probe on the laptop importing the real module through the exported `responseRateLimit` (temporary test in the `route-time-windows` worktree, whose `executor.ts` is byte-identical to main, md5 `69e35222661119713cd1db08d8d7eb93`; probe removed after, tree clean):

| Headers | Result | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `{"retry-after-ms": "", "retry-after": "7"}` | `{retryAfterMs: 0}` | `{retryAfterMs: 7000}` |
| `{"retry-after-ms": "  ", "retry-after": "7"}` | `{retryAfterMs: 0}` | `{retryAfterMs: 7000}` |
| `{"retry-after": " "}` | `{retryAfterMs: 0}` | `undefined` (no usable instruction) |
| `{"retry-after-ms": ""}` alone | `{retryAfterMs: 0}` | `undefined` (cf. no headers → `undefined`) |
| `{"retry-after-ms": "250"}` (control) | `{retryAfterMs: 250}` | 250 ✓ |
| `{"retry-after-ms": "0"}` (control) | `{retryAfterMs: 0}` | 0 ✓ |
| `{"retry-after": "7"}` (control) | `{retryAfterMs: 7000}` | 7000 ✓ |

## Why it matters

- `retryAfterMs` classifies the failure as a rate limit and drives the wait before the next attempt (`packages/ai/src/provider-error.ts:283,299`; media polling raises its gap from it, `packages/ai/src/route/media.ts:147-159`). A discarded 7 s instruction means an immediate retry against a provider that just said it is rate-limited — the exact hammering the header exists to prevent.
- On the success path, `responseRateLimit` feeds the route observer's rate-limit snapshot (`packages/core/src/model-route-log.ts:155`), so a blank header also manufactures a `retryAfterMs: 0` snapshot where the response advertised no usable wait.
- This is the same blank-`Number()` hole fixed for rate-limit `remaining` in #672 (`model-route-limits.ts` now drops blank values at its parse site); the executor's parser was outside that fix. Header values reach this function verbatim from provider responses (`executor.ts:42-68` copies them through), and proxies/gateways do emit empty-valued headers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A blank or whitespace-only `retry-after-ms` is treated as absent: parsing falls through to `retry-after`, and to `undefined` when that is also absent/unusable.
- [ ] A blank or whitespace-only `retry-after` is treated as absent (no manufactured `retryAfterMs: 0`, and `responseRateLimit` returns `undefined` when nothing else is present).
- [ ] An authored `"0"` still yields `retryAfterMs: 0` (existing pinned behaviour), and valid millisecond, seconds, and HTTP-date forms are unchanged.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/ai/test/response-hook.test.ts` (or `executor.test.ts`) cover blank-ms-over-valid-seconds, whitespace-only `retry-after`, and the `"0"` control.

title: fix(core): ModelUsage.dayReports loses or corrupts a provider whose id collides with Object.prototype — '__proto__' vanishes, 'constructor' reports NaN

body:
## Problem

`ModelUsage.dayReports` (`packages/core/src/model-usage.ts:246-255`) accumulates each day's per-provider share in a plain object literal keyed by provider ID:

```ts
const providers: Record<string, { requests: number; metered: number; costUsd: number }> = {}
for (const row of dayRows) {
  const current = providers[row.providerID] ?? { requests: 0, metered: 0, costUsd: 0 }
  providers[row.providerID] = { requests: current.requests + row.requests, ... }
}
```

Provider IDs are user-chosen keys (custom providers are defined by name in config) and reach this function from the recorded route history. Any ID that collides with an `Object.prototype` member corrupts the report:

- **`__proto__`** — the read returns the prototype (not the zero record), and the assignment sets the object's prototype instead of an own property: the provider **vanishes** from the report entirely.
- **`constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`, …** — the read returns the inherited member (a function, not `undefined`), so `current.requests` is `undefined` and the provider's share becomes **NaN** (serialised as `null`).

The day totals stay correct (they are summed from the row array, not the record), so the corruption is silent: the per-provider breakdown — the part of the `route_usage` day report that answers "which provider did this day use" — drops or NaNs one provider's share with no error anywhere.

This is the same collision class the codebase already fixed for config alias resolution in #538, which moved user-keyed copies to `Object.fromEntries`; this accumulator was not part of that audit.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `45e00c8f48`)

Laptop bun probe importing the real `ModelUsage` module (probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-27-2335/probe.ts`; `model-usage.ts` md5 `cf82532048c7fea28a8257223eb47878`, byte-identical on both checkouts):

- Input rows for one day: `anthropic` (3 requests), `__proto__` (7 requests), `constructor` (5 requests), each 15 metered tokens / $1.
- Output `providers` JSON: `{"anthropic":{"requests":3,"metered":15,"costUsd":1},"constructor":{"requests":null,"metered":null,"costUsd":null}}` — `__proto__` absent (own keys are exactly `["anthropic", "constructor"]`), `constructor`'s numbers are NaN.
- Output day total: `requests: 15` — correct, which is why nothing downstream notices.

Existing tests (`packages/core/test/model-usage.test.ts`, "days group by date and keep each provider's share") cover only `openai`/`anthropic` IDs.

## Acceptance criteria

- `dayReports` reports a correct own entry for provider IDs `__proto__`, `constructor`, and `toString` (requests/metered/cost summed across that provider's rows for the day, including multiple rows with the same colliding ID).
- Ordinary provider IDs produce exactly the same reports as before, and the returned `providers` value serialises with `JSON.stringify` including the colliding IDs.
- The fix uses a prototype-safe construction (e.g. accumulate in a `Map` and/or build the record with `Object.fromEntries`, as #538 did) rather than blocklisting names.
- Regression tests in `packages/core/test/model-usage.test.ts` beside the existing day-grouping test; CI green.

title: fix(core): rate-limit windows read a blank remaining header as 0 — an empty value holds the target back like a spent window

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Problem

`ModelRouteLimits.windows()` parses a rate-limit window's `remaining` value with `Number(raw)` (`packages/core/src/model-route-limits.ts`, in `windows`). For an unparseable value such as `"lots"` that yields `NaN`, and the window is dropped — the existing test suite pins exactly that: `remaining: "lots"` produces no hold (`packages/core/test/model-route-limits.test.ts`, the `holdUntil` case expecting `0`).

But `Number("")` and `Number("  ")` are `0`, not `NaN`. An empty or whitespace-only `remaining` header value is therefore read as a window with **zero remaining**, and `holdUntil` treats the target as spent:

- with a stated reset, the target is held back until that reset;
- with no reset, it is held for the unknown-reset minute;
- the hold is capped only by `MAX_WINDOW_MS` (24h), so a blank value with a far-future reset can sideline a target for up to a day.

## Where the values come from

The `remaining` record is copied verbatim from provider response headers in `packages/ai/src/route/executor.ts` (`rateLimitDetails`: `x-ratelimit-remaining-*` and `anthropic-ratelimit-*-remaining`), flows through `ModelRouteLimits.snapshot` (called from `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts` on LLM failures), and is consumed by `ModelRoute.observeRateLimit` / `limitedUntil`, which is what actually keeps the target out of rotation. Empty header values are legal HTTP and are exactly what a proxy/gateway in front of a provider can emit; the parser's contract is that header values "stay as the provider wrote them", so the numeric interpretation is the layer that must not invent a zero.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `45e00c8f48`)

Laptop bun probe importing the real `ModelRouteLimits` module (probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-27-2335/probe.ts`; `model-route-limits.ts` md5 `2b01f63349b19c4a58b5ee436f9a1724`, byte-identical on both checkouts):

- `snapshot({ remaining: { requests: "" }, limit: { requests: "100" }, reset: { requests: "60s" } }, at)` → `windows()` returns `[{ name: "requests", remaining: 0, limit: 100, resetAt: at + 60000 }]` and `holdUntil(...)` returns `at + 60000` — a hold, from a blank value.
- `snapshot({ remaining: { requests: "  " } }, at)` (no reset) → `windows()` returns `[{ remaining: 0 }]` and `holdUntil` returns `at + 60000` via the empty-window/unknown-reset path.
- Control (already pinned by tests): `remaining: "lots"` → window dropped, `holdUntil` returns `0`; `remaining: "0"` → hold (intended, a genuinely spent window).

So the same "no usable number" input is treated two opposite ways depending on whether it is alphabetic (ignored) or blank (zero remaining, target sidelined).

## Why it matters

A single response carrying a blank `remaining` header silently removes a healthy target from rotation — up to 24h when the same response states a distant reset. The failure looks like a quota wall in the route history, not like a parsing artefact, so it would be diagnosed as a provider problem.

## Acceptance criteria

- `windows()` treats an empty or whitespace-only `remaining` value the same way it treats a non-numeric one: the window is not reported as having `remaining: 0` (dropping the window, consistent with the `NaN` path, is the expected shape).
- `holdUntil` returns `0` for a snapshot whose only window(s) have blank `remaining` values, with or without a stated reset.
- A genuine `"0"` remaining still produces the spent-window hold, and ordinary numeric strings parse exactly as before.
- Regression tests in `packages/core/test/model-route-limits.test.ts` beside the existing `"lots"` case, covering blank and whitespace-only `remaining` (with and without a reset); CI green.

title: fix(core): ModelRouteOverrides.parse drops a malformed until and keeps the override — an expiring instruction becomes permanent on its schedule

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Summary

`ModelRouteOverrides.parse` silently drops a present-but-malformed `until` when the entry also carries a schedule — the override becomes a permanent recurring one instead of expiring. The same malformed `until` on an entry *without* a schedule drops the whole entry, so the parser treats the identical bad value two opposite ways depending on an unrelated field.

## Evidence (verified on main `205db4ec10`)

`packages/core/src/model-route-overrides.ts:66-71`:

```ts
const hasUntil = typeof until === "number" && Number.isFinite(until)
if (!hasUntil && schedule === undefined) return []
```

A non-number / non-finite `until` is folded into "no until". With a schedule present the entry survives with `until` omitted (`parse` builds the entry at :92-103, spreading `until` only when `hasUntil`).

Verified via a bun probe on the laptop importing the real module (temporary bun test in the `1643-666-hour24-datetime` worktree, removed after; `model-route-overrides.ts` md5 `27cc94f7df44ec5a471e12979040f24b`, byte-identical on both checkouts), parsing at `now = 2026-10-27T12:00:00Z`:

| entry | result |
|---|---|
| `schedule: {}`, `until: "tomorrow"` | **kept, `until` omitted** |
| `schedule: {}`, `until: null` | **kept, `until` omitted** |
| `schedule: {}`, `until: now + 1 day` (control) | kept, `until` preserved |
| `schedule: {}`, no `until` (control) | kept, recurring — intended |
| no schedule, `until: "tomorrow"` | dropped entirely |

And `ModelRouteOverrides.applies(entry, {providerID:"openai", id:"gpt-x"}, 2100-01-01)` returns `true` for both malformed-`until` entries, while the valid-`until` control correctly returns `false`. A hand-edited or interpreter-written expiry typo (`"tomorrow"`, an ISO string, `null`) therefore converts an expiring `avoid`/`prefer` into one that applies forever on its schedule.

## Why it matters

This is the widening shape the parser already rejects in its neighbouring dimensions: malformed scope lists drop the entry (#536, comment at :49-52 — "emptying it would widen the entry") and a malformed schedule drops the entry (#570, comment at :60-65 — "keeping the entry would drop its time restriction"). The expiry dimension was missed: dropping a malformed `until` widens the entry in time exactly as dropping a malformed schedule did. An `avoid` that was meant to lapse can suppress a target indefinitely; a `prefer` can keep lifting one forever.

## Acceptance criteria

- `parse` drops an entry whose `until` field is present (`!== undefined`) but is not a finite number — regardless of whether a schedule is present.
- Entries with a valid numeric `until`, and schedule-only entries with no `until` field at all (the intentional recurring form, pinned in the existing tests), parse exactly as before.
- Regression tests in `packages/core/test/model-route-overrides.test.ts` next to the #570 malformed-schedule cases: string / null / non-finite `until` with a schedule drops the entry; the valid controls survive.
- CI green.

title: fix(core): date-time validators accept hour 24 — '2026-01-01T24:00:00Z' passes Form validation and parseAbsoluteTime but denotes Jan 2

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

The calendar checks added for #656/#609 round-trip only the **date** part of an ISO date-time. The **time** part has the same rollover hole at exactly one value: hour `24`. V8 parses `2026-01-01T24:00:00Z` as `2026-01-02T00:00:00.000Z` instead of rejecting it, the written date (`2026-01-01`) round-trips fine, and both validators accept a value that denotes a different day than the one written. RFC 3339 `date-time` (the Form format) does not permit hour 24 at all (`time-hour = 00-23`).

Verified on main `205db4ec10` with a laptop probe running the verbatim function bodies (minutes/seconds of 60+ are correctly `Invalid` in V8 — hour 24 is the only overflowing component):

```
2026-01-01T24:00:00Z       | isDateTime: true  | parseAbsoluteTime: 2026-01-02T00:00:00.000Z
2026-12-31T24:00:00Z       | isDateTime: true  | parseAbsoluteTime: 2027-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
2026-01-01T24:00:00+05:00  | isDateTime: true  | parseAbsoluteTime: 2026-01-01T19:00:00.000Z  (Jan 2 00:00 at +05:00)
2026-02-28T24:00:00Z       | isDateTime: true  | parseAbsoluteTime: 2026-03-01T00:00:00.000Z
2026-02-30T10:00:00Z       | isDateTime: false | parseAbsoluteTime: undefined   (date part already guarded)
```

## Evidence

- `packages/core/src/form.ts:374-389` — `isDateTime` execs `/^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})/` and round-trips only Y/M/D; used by `validateField` for `format: "date-time"` (line 334). A form answer of `2026-01-01T24:00:00Z` is accepted as a Jan 1 date-time while every downstream `new Date(value)` reads it as Jan 2.
- `packages/core/src/model-route-limits.ts:54-68` — `parseAbsoluteTime` makes the identical date-only check. It is the shared parser for the quota-reset surface: `resetMs`/`resetAtFromMessage` (same file), `ModelRouteTuning.parseQuotaReset` (model-route-tuning.ts:169), `QuotaSnapshot` explicit `resetAt` (quota-snapshot.ts:63), and `MessagingTemplate.parseTime` (messaging/template.ts:521). A provider message or plan `resetAt` of `…T24:00:00Z` silently becomes a reset a day later than written. The `ABSOLUTE_TIME` capture (model-route-limits.ts:90) admits `\d{2}:\d{2}` times, so `24:00` reaches the parser.

## Why it matters

This is the remaining cell of the rollover matrix the fleet has been closing one parser at a time (#471, #502, #609, #647, #655, #656): every sibling now rejects calendar-invalid **dates**, but a time component that rolls the instant into the next day still passes both copies of the check. For forms it accepts an answer outside the field's declared RFC 3339 format; for quota resets it fabricates a reset instant a day late from a value the author wrote as end-of-day.

## Acceptance criteria

- `Form.validateAnswer` rejects `2026-01-01T24:00:00Z` (and the `+05:00` / year-boundary forms) for a `date-time` field, with tests alongside the #658 cases in `packages/core/test/form.test.ts`.
- `ModelRouteLimits.parseAbsoluteTime` returns `undefined` for hour-24 ISO values, with tests alongside the #609/#627 cases in `packages/core/test/model-route-limits.test.ts`; consumers (`parseQuotaReset`, `QuotaSnapshot`, `MessagingTemplate.parseTime`) inherit the rejection.
- Valid boundary times still pass: `T23:59:59Z`, `T00:00:00Z`, leap-day `2024-02-29T24:00:00Z` is rejected (hour), while `2024-02-29T23:59:59Z` passes.
- Fix approach is the filer's choice (extend the round-trip to the time components in both copies, or reject hour > 23 when an ISO time part is present), but both copies must agree — they are kept in sync by hand today.

title: fix(core): a prefer override's factor/weight of 0 is silently dropped — the target gets the default ×3 lift instead

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`ModelRouteOverrides.parse` (packages/core/src/model-route-overrides.ts:79-84) silently drops a `prefer` override's `factor` or `weight` when the value is not positive and finite:

```ts
const factor =
  typeof factorValue === "number" && Number.isFinite(factorValue) && factorValue > 0 ? factorValue : undefined
const weight =
  typeof weightValue === "number" && Number.isFinite(weightValue) && weightValue > 0 ? weightValue : undefined
```

Dropping the field does not neutralize the override — it arms its strongest default. In `tracedWeightOf` (packages/core/src/model-route.ts:795-796), a `prefer` override with no `weight` applies `item.factor ?? PREFERRED_FACTOR`, and `PREFERRED_FACTOR` is **3** (model-route.ts:727). So an override file entry written as `factor: 0` — the lightest possible preference, or simply an invalid value — takes effect as a **×3 lift** for the target, the exact opposite of what was written. The same applies to `weight: 0` and to negative or non-finite values (a JSON `1e999` parses to `Infinity` and is dropped the same way).

This contradicts the house rule this very file already follows twice: a present-but-malformed dimension drops the *entry*, never widens it — malformed scope lists drop the entry (#536, `malformedList` at :46-48) and a present-but-unreadable schedule drops the entry (#570, :62-66). It also contradicts the sibling config surface: in the schema, the same two fields on scheduled weight rules are `PositiveFinite` (`Schema.Finite.check(Schema.isGreaterThan(0))`, packages/schema/src/config/model-routes.ts:11, used at :156-163 and :191-197) — zero is invalid input there, not a silent synonym for "no preference stated". The overrides file is plain JSON parsed by hand with no schema, so this parser is the only validation those values ever get.

## Evidence (verified on main 41c8a35f60, 2026-10-27)

Bun probe on the laptop importing the real modules via a temporary `bun test` in packages/core (worktree `~/git/fleet/1591-656-form-datetime`; model-route-overrides.ts md5 `27cc94f7df44ec5a471e12979040f24b` and model-route.ts md5 `50e894cb925426152504c11a75600d61`, byte-identical on the sandbox and laptop checkouts; probe file removed after the run):

`ModelRouteOverrides.parse` on a `prefer` override for provider `anthropic` with a valid `until`:

| written value | parsed override carries | end-to-end `ModelRoute.weightFactor(target)` |
|---|---|---|
| `factor: 0` | *(field absent)* | **3** |
| `factor: -1` | *(field absent)* | — (same dropped-field path) |
| `weight: 0` | *(field absent)* | **3** |
| `factor: 0.5` | `factor: 0.5` (correct control) | 0.5 |
| `weight: 0.25` | `weight: 0.25` (correct control) | — |

The end-to-end rows write the override through the real file store (`setFilePath` to a temp `route-overrides.json`) and read the weight through the real `ModelRoute.weightFactor`, so the ×3 is the value selection actually uses, not just a parse artifact.

Existing tests (packages/core/test/model-route-overrides.test.ts) pin the absent-field default (×3 at :113-116) and valid factors/weights (0.5, 1/3, 0.25, 0.2), but never a present-but-invalid `factor` or `weight`.

## Why it matters

Route overrides are the user's direct word on routing ("a user's word outranks the route's level", model-route-overrides.ts:22-23), stored in a hand-editable JSON file shared with OpenChamber. A typo'd or zero value in that file currently does not make the preference disappear or apply as written — it applies as the maximum default preference for a target the author may have been trying to mute. Silent inversion of an explicit instruction is worse than either honouring it or rejecting it.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `prefer` override whose `factor` or `weight` is present but not positive-finite (0, negative, `Infinity` via `1e999`) must NOT fall back to `PREFERRED_FACTOR`. Triage picks one contract and pins it: either (a) drop the entry, matching the #536/#570 drop-don't-widen precedent in the same parser and the schema's `PositiveFinite` for the same fields — the filer's recommendation — or (b) honour 0 as a real zero weight/factor.
- An override with `factor` and `weight` genuinely absent keeps today's behaviour exactly: `prefer` lifts by `PREFERRED_FACTOR` (existing test at model-route-overrides.test.ts:113-116 stays green).
- Valid values are unchanged: `factor: 0.5`, `weight: 0.25`, etc. parse and apply as today.
- New regression tests in packages/core/test/model-route-overrides.test.ts cover at least `factor: 0` and `weight: 0` at the parse level, plus one end-to-end `weightFactor` assertion showing the ×3 default no longer fires for a present-but-invalid value.
- Whichever contract is chosen is stated in a comment at the guard site, so the next reader can tell the dropped-field fallback was considered.

body:
# Finding (pr-diff-review lane B, PR #596)

PR #596 (OPEN, head `4c0f8c5a`, for #560) changes the public Protocol HttpApi — a new `Provider.InfoWithModels` schema and new endpoint descriptions in `packages/protocol/src/groups/provider.ts` — but **does not regenerate any of the checked-in OpenAPI documents**, so the published API documentation keeps describing `/api/provider` and `/api/provider/:id` as returning plain `Provider.Info` with no `models`.

## Evidence

- PR #596 file list: `packages/client/**` (generated), `packages/core/src/provider.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/groups/provider.ts`, `packages/server/src/handlers/provider.ts`, `packages/server/test/provider.test.ts`. No `openapi.json` anywhere.
- The generation chain exists and is checked:
  - `packages/protocol/script/generate-openapi.ts` builds `packages/protocol/openapi.json` from `OpenApi.fromApi(ClientApi)` and its `--check` mode fails when the file differs (`packages/protocol/package.json`: `check:generated`).
  - `services/www/script/generate-openapi.ts:3-4` copies `packages/protocol/openapi.json` to `services/www/openapi.json` and `services/www/public/openapi.json`; the www AGENTS.md requires `public/openapi.json` to stay generated from the protocol document, and `test.yml` runs www `check:generated` in CI.
- Precedent in the same review batch: PR #597, which changed model-route schema annotations, regenerated all three documents (`packages/protocol/openapi.json`, `services/www/openapi.json`, `services/www/public/openapi.json`).
- Because the PR adds a new annotated schema (`Provider.InfoWithModels`) and rewrites both endpoint descriptions, the generated document necessarily changes; the checked-in documents on the PR head therefore do not match the protocol the PR defines.

## Why it matters

The whole point of #560 is that API consumers discover models through `/api/provider`. If the OpenAPI documents are not regenerated, the published contract those consumers code against still shows no `models` field — the same discovery gap, one layer up — and the protocol `check:generated` gate fails as soon as anyone runs it.

## Acceptance criteria

- PR #596 (or a successor) regenerates `packages/protocol/openapi.json` via `bun run generate` in `packages/protocol`, and `services/www/openapi.json` + `services/www/public/openapi.json` via the www generate step.
- The regenerated documents contain the `Provider.InfoWithModels` schema and show `models` on both provider endpoint responses.
- `bun run check:generated` passes in both `packages/protocol` and `services/www`.

body:
## Problem

Form string fields with `format: "date-time"` accept calendar-invalid dates. In packages/core/src/form.ts:

```ts
function isDate(value: string) {
  if (!/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(value)) return false
  const date = new Date(`${value}T00:00:00.000Z`)
  return !Number.isNaN(date.getTime()) && date.toISOString().slice(0, 10) === value
}

function isDateTime(value: string) {
  return !Number.isNaN(new Date(value).getTime())
}
```

The sibling `date` format (form.ts:368-372) round-trips the components, so `2026-02-30` is correctly rejected there. `isDateTime` (form.ts:374-376) only checks that `new Date(value)` is not `NaN` — and `Date` parsing silently rolls day overflow into the next month, so a `date-time` answer of **2026-02-30T10:00:00Z** passes validation (`validateField`, form.ts:334) even though that instant does not exist. Whatever consumes the answer then parses a different day than the one that was entered.

## Evidence (verified on main 4a50304a73, 2026-10-28)

Bun probe on the laptop running the real `validateAnswer` from `@opencode/core/form` via a temporary `bun test` in packages/core (removed after; probe kept at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-27-resetdt/probe.ts`; form.ts md5 `6cf0564198d0426874cb5daeb8505dfc`, byte-identical on both checkouts). For a required string field with `format: "date-time"`, `validateAnswer` returned `undefined` (accepted) for:

- `2026-02-30T10:00:00Z` — Feb 30 does not exist (rolls to Mar 2)
- `2026-02-29T10:00:00Z` — 2026 is not a leap year (rolls to Mar 1)
- `2026-04-31T10:00:00Z` — April has 30 days (rolls to May 1)

Controls behaved correctly:

- `2026-01-01T25:00:00Z` and `2026-01-01T10:60:00Z` — rejected (time overflow is `NaN`, unlike day overflow: the asymmetry is exactly the calendar-day component)
- `2024-02-29T10:00:00Z` (leap year) and `2026-01-15T10:30:00Z` — accepted
- `not-a-date` — rejected
- The same values under `format: "date"`: `2026-02-30` rejected, `2024-02-29` accepted

Also observed, left for triage rather than asserted as part of this bug: `isDateTime` accepts non-ISO forms such as `Jan 5 2026` and `2026/01/15 10:30`, because it imposes no shape at all. Whether `date-time` should require ISO 8601 shape is a separate contract question; this issue is only about calendar-invalid ISO dates being accepted.

Existing tests (packages/core/test/form.test.ts) cover URI format validation but have no `date` / `date-time` format cases at all.

## Why it matters

Form answers are user/model-supplied structured data that downstream code trusts as validated: a field declared `date-time` is the system's promise that the value is a real instant. Accepting Feb 30 silently shifts the instant by days when anything re-parses it — the same rollover class fixed for the quota-reset parsers in #609 and for `MessagingTemplate.parseTime` in #647, and already guarded for this file's own `date` format.

## Acceptance criteria

- `validateAnswer` rejects calendar-invalid `date-time` values — at least `2026-02-30T…`, `2026-02-29T…` in a non-leap year, and `2026-04-31T…` — with `Expected date-time for form field: <key>`.
- Valid values keep passing, including leap-day `2024-02-29T…`, ordinary ISO date-times with offsets, and the currently accepted time-overflow rejections stay rejected.
- The check round-trips the date components (the technique `isDate` in the same file and `ModelRouteLimits.parseAbsoluteTime` already use), applied only when the value carries an ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` date part so non-ISO leniency is not silently changed by this fix.
- New tests in packages/core/test/form.test.ts cover `date-time` calendar-invalid and leap-valid cases, and pin the existing `date` format behaviour alongside them.

title: fix(core): QuotaSnapshot explicit resetAt rolls calendar-invalid dates over — '2026-02-30' becomes a Mar 2 reset

labels.name: effort/s

body:
## Problem

`QuotaSnapshot.resetAtOf` (packages/core/src/quota-snapshot.ts:60-65) parses an explicit `resetAt` with a bare `Date.parse`:

```ts
if (window.resetAt !== undefined) {
  const parsed = Date.parse(window.resetAt)
  if (Number.isFinite(parsed)) return parsed
}
```

`Date.parse` silently rolls calendar-overflow days into the next month instead of returning `NaN`, so a recorded reset of **2026-02-30** is reported to every snapshot consumer as a reset on **2026-03-02** — a date nobody recorded. The function's own contract (quota-snapshot.ts:53-56) says an explicit `resetAt` "is returned as recorded"; a rolled date is not the recorded one.

This is the one branch of this function not yet hardened: #629 fixed the `daily HH:MM UTC` branch in the same function (out-of-range components now yield `null`), and #609 added the shared calendar check `ModelRouteLimits.parseAbsoluteTime` (model-route-limits.ts:48-70) for the quota-reset parsers — but `resetAtOf`'s explicit-`resetAt` branch uses neither.

## Evidence (verified on main 4a50304a73, 2026-10-28)

Bun probe on the laptop importing the real module via a temporary `bun test` in packages/core (probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-27-resetdt/probe.ts`; quota-snapshot.ts md5 `1a4046aba6343fa067efec333c60f003`, byte-identical on the sandbox and laptop checkouts). With `now = 2026-10-27T12:00:00Z`, `QuotaSnapshot.derive` returned:

| recorded `resetAt` | snapshot `resetAt` |
|---|---|
| `2026-02-30T00:00:00.000Z` | **2026-03-02** (rolled) |
| `2026-02-29T00:00:00.000Z` (2026 is not a leap year) | **2026-03-01** (rolled) |
| `2026-04-31T12:00:00.000Z` | **2026-05-01** (rolled) |
| `2025-02-29T00:00:00Z` | **2025-03-01** (rolled) |
| `2026-10-27T25:00:00.000Z` | `null` (time overflow is NaN — the asymmetry: day overflow rolls, time overflow does not) |
| `2026-10-27T17:00:00.000Z` | 2026-10-27T17:00Z (correct control) |
| `2024-02-29T00:00:00.000Z` (leap year) | 2024-02-29 (correct control) |
| `not-a-date` | `null` (correct control) |

Existing tests (packages/core/test/quota-snapshot.test.ts:94-145) pin explicit valid and past `resetAt` values and the daily-rule out-of-range cases from #629, but never a calendar-invalid explicit `resetAt`.

## Why it matters

QuotaSnapshot is the shared quota signal for placement/routing consumers (design #587). A fabricated reset instant means consumers judge staleness and headroom against a reset that was never stated — the same failure class #609 fixed for the message parsers, in the one consumer those parsers feed. `resetAt` is a free-form `Schema.String` on the plan window (model-plan.ts), so nothing upstream rejects a calendar-invalid value before it reaches this branch.

## Acceptance criteria

- A calendar-invalid explicit `resetAt` (e.g. `2026-02-30`, `2026-02-29` in a non-leap year, `2026-04-31`) yields `resetAt: null` from `QuotaSnapshot.derive` — never a rolled-over date. (If triage prefers falling through to a valid `daily` resetRule on the same window instead, state that in the fix and pin it with a test.)
- The fix reuses the in-repo calendar check (`ModelRouteLimits.parseAbsoluteTime`, model-route-limits.ts:54) or an equivalent component round-trip, rather than adding a third copy of the logic.
- Valid explicit values keep working exactly as today, including a past `resetAt` returned as recorded (existing test at quota-snapshot.test.ts:137-145 stays green) and the leap-day control `2024-02-29`.
- New regression tests in packages/core/test/quota-snapshot.test.ts cover at least Feb 30, Feb 29 in a non-leap year, and Apr 31 as explicit `resetAt` values.
- The daily-rule branch behaviour from #629 is unchanged.

body:
## Bug

`getFilenameTruncated` in `packages/util/src/path.ts` (lines 21–29) returns nearly the whole filename when `maxLength` is 0 or negative, instead of an empty (or at most `maxLength`-character) result.

The fallback branch is:

```ts
const available = maxLength - extension.length - 1
if (available <= 0) return filename.slice(0, maxLength - 1) + "…"
```

With `maxLength = 0`, `maxLength - 1` is `-1`, and `slice(0, -1)` keeps everything except the last character — the exact `slice(-0)`-family trap its sibling in the same file already guards against: `truncateMiddle` (lines 31–40) returns `""` for `maxLength <= 0` with a comment explaining why, after issue #574 fixed the same class of bug in the truncate family. `getFilenameTruncated` never got the equivalent guard.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Probe run with bun on the laptop importing the real module (probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-27-filename-trunc/probe.ts`; `packages/util/src/path.ts` md5 `22e21e727d25094bb184bea54bf8ca23`, byte-identical on the sandbox and laptop checkouts; sandbox main `d29aa1df71`):

| call | result | length |
|---|---|---|
| `getFilenameTruncated("/repo/long-component-name.tsx", 0)` | `"long-component-name.ts…"` | 23 |
| `getFilenameTruncated("/repo/long-component-name.tsx", -1)` | `"long-component-name.t…"` | 22 |
| `getFilenameTruncated("/repo/long-component-name.tsx", -5)` | `"long-component-na…"` | 18 |
| `getFilenameTruncated("/repo/README", 0)` | `"READM…"` | 6 |
| `getFilenameTruncated("/repo/a.txt", 0)` | `"a.tx…"` | 5 |
| control: `…, 1` / `2` / `3` / `5` / `14` / `16` / `20` | exact-length results | 1 / 2 / 3 / 5 / 14 / 16 / 20 |
| control: `truncateMiddle("abcdefghijklmnop", 0)` | `""` | 0 |

Existing tests (`packages/util/src/path.test.ts`) pin `getFilenameTruncated` only at `maxLength = 16` and pin `truncateMiddle` at widths 0–2; no test covers `getFilenameTruncated` at 0 or below.

## Why it matters

The function's contract is "the filename in at most `maxLength` characters" — the one live caller (`packages/session-ui/src/message/comment-card.tsx:66`) passes a fixed 14 today, so this is a latent contract break rather than a live visual bug: any future caller that derives the width from a container size (the pattern that produced #574's live caller, which clamps with `Math.max(1, width())`) can feed 0 and get a 23-character string in a 0-character slot. The sibling function in the same file documents and tests the correct behavior; this one silently diverges.

## Acceptance criteria

- `getFilenameTruncated(path, 0)` returns `""`, and negative `maxLength` never returns a string longer than the `maxLength = 0` result.
- For every `maxLength >= 0`, the returned string's length is at most `maxLength` (including when an extension is present, absent, or longer than `maxLength`).
- New tests in `packages/util/src/path.test.ts` cover widths 0, 1, and 2 for `getFilenameTruncated`, mirroring the existing `truncateMiddle` width tests.
- Existing behavior at normal widths is unchanged (the pinned 16-character case and the rest of `path.test.ts` stay green).

body:
## Finding

`MessagingTemplate.parseTime` (packages/core/src/messaging/template.ts:504) falls back to a bare `Date.parse(input)` at :516-517 and returns the result unless it is `NaN`. `Date.parse` silently rolls calendar-invalid ISO dates into the next month instead of returning `NaN`, so a mistyped `since`/`until` is silently read as a different day instead of producing the `Invalid time` error every caller raises for an unparseable value.

Verified this run on main `b2b2caf2e9` via a bun probe on the laptop importing the real module (probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-27-parsetime-caldate/probe.ts`, per the no-sandbox-probes rule; template.ts md5 `1f0e9df23038be2f95b25b847410ede4`, byte-identical on the sandbox and laptop checkouts), with `now = 2026-10-27T00:00:00Z`:

| Input | Result | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `2026-02-30` | `2026-03-02T00:00:00Z` | undefined |
| `2026-02-29` (2026 is not a leap year) | `2026-03-01T00:00:00Z` | undefined |
| `2026-04-31` | `2026-05-01T00:00:00Z` | undefined |
| `2025-02-29T00:00:00Z` | `2025-03-01T00:00:00Z` | undefined |
| `2026-13-01` | undefined | undefined ✓ (asymmetry: month overflow is NaN, day overflow rolls) |
| `2024-02-29` (leap-valid control) | `2024-02-29T00:00:00Z` | unchanged ✓ |
| `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z` (control) | `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z` | unchanged ✓ |
| `2h` (relative control) | `now - 2h` | unchanged ✓ |

## Why it matters

- All four callers — packages/core/src/messaging.ts:769-774, :823-824, :1752-1753, :1826-1827 — treat `undefined` as the only failure signal (`Invalid time: <input>`). A rolled date therefore never errors: it silently sets a `time_created >= / <=` bound one or two days away from what the user asked for, returning an empty or shifted message/log window with no hint the date was invalid.
- The repo already decided this exact question for the other date parsers: #609 fixed the quota-reset parsers, and `ModelRouteLimits.parseAbsoluteTime` (packages/core/src/model-route-limits.ts:48-70) now round-trips ISO components through a real calendar date, with a doc comment stating "Date.parse silently rolls overflow days such as Feb 30 into the next month instead of returning NaN". `parseTime` is the remaining parser on a user-facing surface that never got the same check. (Not a duplicate of #609 — that issue's sites are `model-route-limits.ts` / `model-route-tuning.ts`; not a duplicate of #592 — that was this function's bare-epoch scaling, now fixed.)
- Existing tests (packages/core/test/messaging-template.test.ts:61-83) cover the epoch forms, one valid ISO timestamp, and a relative form — no calendar-invalid case, which is why the rollover survived the #592 fix in the same function.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parseTime` returns `undefined` for calendar-invalid ISO dates — at minimum `2026-02-30`, `2026-02-29`, `2026-04-31`, and `2025-02-29T00:00:00Z` — so the messaging callers raise `Invalid time` instead of silently querying the rolled-over day.
- [ ] Valid forms are unchanged: leap-valid `2024-02-29`, date-only and full ISO timestamps (including zone offsets), the relative forms (`90s`, `15m`, `2h`, `3d`, `1w`), and the 10-digit seconds / 13-digit milliseconds bare epochs from #592.
- [ ] The fix mirrors or reuses the established round-trip check (`ModelRouteLimits.parseAbsoluteTime`, or the same component round-trip applied locally when the input is ISO-shaped); triage decides and pins what happens to non-ISO `Date.parse` forms (e.g. `Jan 5 2026`) — either they keep parsing or they are rejected, but a test pins the decision either way.
- [ ] New regression tests in packages/core/test/messaging-template.test.ts pin the invalid-date cases and the valid controls; all existing messaging-template tests pass.

## Finding

PR #597 (merged, refs #240) moved most `packages/schema/src/config/model-routes.ts` field descriptions to annotate **before** `.pipe(optional)`, so they reach the generated JSON schema / OpenAPI document. It left a remainder behind — in the same file, still on current main (`e730a6784c97e872ac2df4d0bbd216b9bef94892`):

| Field | Location on main | In generated OpenAPI? |
|---|---|---|
| `Route.autonomy` | `model-routes.ts:220` — `Schema.Literals([...]).pipe(optional).annotate({...})` | **missing** |
| `Route.selection` | `model-routes.ts:224` — same pattern | **missing** |
| `Route.weights` | `model-routes.ts:~230` — `.pipe(optional).annotate({...})` | **missing** |
| `Route.schedules` | `model-routes.ts:234` — `Schema.Array(Schedule).pipe(optional).annotate({...})` | **missing** |
| `TargetObject.defaultVariant` | `model-routes.ts:22` — `Schema.String.pipe(optional).annotate({...})` | **missing** (Target inline object in `Config.ModelRoute.Target`) |
| `TargetObject.variants` | `model-routes.ts:25` — same pattern | **missing** |
| `TargetObject.until` | `model-routes.ts:29` — `PositiveInt.pipe(optional).annotate({...})` | **missing** |

Verified by reading `packages/protocol/openapi.json` on current main: `Config.ModelRoute.RouteEncoded` properties `autonomy`, `selection`, `weights`, `schedules` carry no `description`, while the fields #597 did fix (`budgets`, `hedgeAfterMs`, `attempts`, Schedule/GlobalSchedule/Window/Health fields) do; the `Config.ModelRoute.Target` inline object properties `defaultVariant`, `variants`, `until` likewise carry no description.

## Why this is a #240 remainder, not a new style nit

- #240's acceptance criteria explicitly listed route `schedules` (and target `defaultVariant`/`until`); #240 is CLOSED, but those items were not actually moved by #597.
- #597's own regression test (`packages/schema/test/config.test.ts`, "every documented field carries its description in the encoded JSON schema") covers `Route: ["budgets", "hedgeAfterMs", "attempts"]` only — it omits `schedules`, `autonomy`, `selection`, `weights`, and does not cover `TargetObject` at all, which is why the gap survived CI.
- #240's text said #233 had already moved `autonomy`/`selection`/`weights`; on current main they are back in (or never left) the outside-`optional` form, and their descriptions are absent from the OpenAPI document either way.

## Why it matters

These are some of the most consequential route fields (autonomy level, selection mode, weighted ratios, scheduled weight changes, and a target's variant remap / expiry). Editors and the OpenAPI document show nothing for them, while sibling fields are documented — exactly the inconsistency #240 set out to eliminate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In `packages/schema/src/config/model-routes.ts`, `autonomy`, `selection`, `weights`, `schedules` on `Route` and `defaultVariant`, `variants`, `until` on `TargetObject` annotate before `.pipe(optional)`.

- [ ] Extend the #597 regression test's field lists to include these fields (including a TargetObject case), so a future field added in the outside-`optional` form fails the test.
- [ ] Note for triage: `git grep "pipe(optional).annotate" packages/schema/src/` shows the same pattern in other schema files (e.g. `config.ts`, `config/messaging.ts`, `messaging.ts`). Those files were outside #240's scope; triage should say explicitly whether they are in scope for this issue or filed separately, rather than silently expanding it.

body:
## Request: time-windowed weights / ordering for model routes

Several plan meters are time-varying. Verified example: DeepSeek's peak/off-peak pricing passes through OpenCode Go (and is reflected in ClinePass's reference rates for DeepSeek models) — DeepSeek usage deducts at double rate during peak windows (Mon–Fri 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC; = 20:00–23:00 and 01:00–05:00 America/Chicago). Static route weights cannot express "prefer this leaf off-peak, deprioritize it at peak."

### Motivating design (2026-10-27 pool review)

The planned `background` tier is an ordered chain whose first and third stages are the same leaves separated only by the clock:

1. `deepseek-flash` on all doors except ClinePass — at off-peak rates
2. `mimo-flash` (any door)
3. `deepseek-flash` again — accepting peak rates rather than failing

Without clock-aware ordering, stages 1 and 3 collapse into one and the tier burns peak rates before falling to MiMo.

### Proposed shape

Allow a target (or route) to carry an optional time window that scales its weight or gates its position:

```jsonc
{ "model": "opencode-route/deepseek-flash-plan#high",
  "weight": 3,
  "window": { "peak": "deepseek", "scale": 0.5 } }
```

Requirements:

1. Named, reusable window definitions (e.g. `deepseek-peak`) with explicit timezone and weekday rules — windows belong to the meter, not the model.
2. Window evaluation must be visible: the resolved-route dump (see #637) should show the effective weight/order at a given time.
3. No behavior change for routes without windows.
4. Composes with quota-state demotion: a quota-exhausted leaf stays demoted regardless of window; a window never resurrects it.

Related: #637 (exclusion expressions) — the two features share the "pool definition as intent, not inventory" goal but are independent.

## Acceptance criteria

- A route/target can carry an optional time window referencing a named, reusable window definition with explicit timezone and weekday rules (windows belong to the meter, not the model).
- Inside the window the target's effective weight/order reflects the configured scale or gating; outside it, normal ordering applies — the motivating `background` tier resolves deepseek-flash (all doors except ClinePass) ahead of mimo-flash off-peak and behind it at peak rates.
- Routes without windows behave exactly as before (no behavior change).
- Window scaling never overrides quota-state demotion: a quota-exhausted leaf stays demoted regardless of window.
- The resolved-route dump shows the effective weight/order at a given time, including window effects.

title: fix(core): QuotaSnapshot daily reset rule rolls out-of-range times over — 'daily 25:99 UTC' yields a fabricated reset instead of null

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: priority/low

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Problem

`QuotaSnapshot.resetAtOf` (`packages/core/src/quota-snapshot.ts:56-71`, shipped in #588 / PR #615) derives the next reset from a `daily HH:MM UTC` reset rule, but it never range-checks the captured hour/minute. Out-of-range components are silently rolled over by `Date.setUTCHours`, so a malformed rule yields a **fabricated** reset instant instead of the documented `null` — the module's own contract says anything that does not yield a single derivable instant "yields null rather than a guess" (`quota-snapshot.ts:53-56`), and the snapshot doc promises a reset time only "when the window's reset data yields one".

## Evidence (verified on main e73d850df8)

- The rule is matched with `/^daily (\d{1,2}):(\d{2}) UTC$/` (`quota-snapshot.ts:63`) — `\d{1,2}` admits hours 24-99 and `\d{2}` admits minutes 60-99 — and the captures go straight into `at.setUTCHours(Number(daily[1]), Number(daily[2]), 0, 0)` (`:65-66`), which rolls overflow into the next hour/day.
- Nothing upstream validates the rule: `QuotaWindow.resetRule` is a free-form `Schema.String` (`packages/core/src/model-plan.ts:36`), the plan-info tool passes quota windows through, and `resetAtOf` is the only place a daily rule is parsed.
- Laptop probe (real module imported from the laptop checkout; `quota-snapshot.ts` md5 `c01dba5bc0a185bfcdc93b6c622f0849`, byte-identical to sandbox main; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-27-1335/probe.ts`, per the no-sandbox-probes rule), at `now = 2026-10-27T12:00:00Z`:
  - `daily 25:99 UTC` → resetAt `2026-10-28T02:39:00Z` (both components rolled)
  - `daily 12:60 UTC` → resetAt `2026-10-27T13:00:00Z` (minute overflow becomes the next hour)
  - Controls behave: `daily 23:59 UTC` → `2026-10-27T23:59:00Z`; `daily 00:00 UTC` → `2026-10-28T00:00:00Z`
- The existing tests (`packages/core/test/quota-snapshot.test.ts:94-122`) cover only a well-formed daily rule and the rolling/null cases — no out-of-range component case.

## Why it matters

Snapshots are the single quota signal the #587 design gives every consumer (#566 placement gating, #567 time-based weighting, #568 burn-rate all build on this module). A mistyped or model-written rule like `daily 12:60 UTC` (the rules are recorded by models via the plan tools, per the plan-tracking skill) does not fail visibly — it produces a plausible-looking reset time an hour (or, for `25:99`, a day) away from anything the user wrote, and downstream consumers will schedule around a reset that does not exist. The failure mode the module was written to avoid is exactly this: a guessed number presented as a reading.

## Adjacent observation for triage (verified, contract call left to triage)

An explicit `resetAt` in the past is returned as-is (`quota-snapshot.ts:59-62`): probe with `resetAt: "2026-10-20T00:00:00.000Z"` at the same `now` returned that past instant, although the `Snapshot.resetAt` doc calls it "the next reset". Decide and pin whether a past explicit `resetAt` stays (a record of the last stated reset) or becomes `null`; not part of the fix below unless triage says so.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A daily rule whose hour is > 23 or whose minute is > 59 yields `resetAt: null` (no rollover): e.g. `daily 25:99 UTC`, `daily 12:60 UTC`, `daily 24:30 UTC` at any `now`.
- [ ] Well-formed daily rules are unchanged, including the next-occurrence behaviour when today's time has passed, and single-digit hours (`daily 9:05 UTC`).
- [ ] The explicit-`resetAt` and rolling/free-text paths are unchanged; the past-explicit-`resetAt` question above is decided and pinned by a test either way.
- [ ] New regression tests in `packages/core/test/quota-snapshot.test.ts` pin the out-of-range cases; all existing quota-snapshot tests pass.

title: fix(core): route_stats weightLayers reports the oldest selection in the window, not the most recent — memberOf overwrites while iterating newest-first decisions

labels.name: task/small-fix
