labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`ModelRouteOverrides.parse` silently drops a malformed `schedule` on a stored override and keeps the override itself — as long as the entry also carries a valid `until`. The override then applies at **all times** until it expires, instead of only inside its scheduled window.

`packages/core/src/model-route-overrides.ts:60-62`:

```ts
const schedule = ModelRouteSchedule.parse(field(item, "schedule"))
const hasUntil = typeof until === "number" && Number.isFinite(until)
if (!hasUntil && schedule === undefined) return []
```

`ModelRouteSchedule.parse` returns `undefined` both when the `schedule` field is absent **and** when it is present but unreadable (bad time, bad timezone, unreadable day list). `parse` in `model-route-overrides.ts` cannot tell the two apart, and when `hasUntil` is true the entry is kept with `schedule: undefined`. `applies()` (`model-route-overrides.ts:113-125`) then has no schedule to check, so the override is in force at every instant.

This contradicts the schedule module's own stated contract (`packages/core/src/model-route-schedule.ts:12-15`): parse "rejects an object it cannot read, so a typo makes a rule disappear rather than apply at the wrong time." Here the typo makes the rule apply at *every* time. It is the same widening shape as #536 (a malformed scope list emptying into "everything"), one dimension over: a malformed time scope widening into "always".

The asymmetry confirms it is accidental: the *same* malformed schedule on an entry **without** `until` drops the entry (the `!hasUntil && schedule === undefined` branch) — so identical file content is either dropped or made always-on depending on whether an unrelated field is present.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `c007c53436`)

Temporary bun probe importing the real module (probe + output kept in the goal's hidden files, `probe-2026-10-27-0335/`):

- `parse` of `{ id, action: "avoid", providers: ["openai"], until: now+3600000, schedule: { start: "25:00", end: "17:00" } }` returned **1 entry with `schedule: undefined`**, and `applies(entry, { providerID: "openai", id: "gpt-5" }, now)` returned **true** — the "avoid openai" instruction is active outside any window.
- Control, well-formed future schedule (`{ from: now+86400000, until: now+90000000 }`) + same `until`: entry kept **with** its schedule, `applies(...)` at `now` returned **false**.
- Control, no `schedule` field at all: entry kept, `applies(...)` true (correct — no time restriction was requested).
- Control, malformed schedule (`{ timezone: "Not/AZone" }`) **without** `until`: **0 entries** — dropped, as it should be in both cases.

## Why it matters

Route overrides are operator/agent instructions like "avoid provider X during peak hours" or "prefer Y on weekdays". A single typo in the schedule (a `25:00` start, a misspelled timezone) silently converts a time-boxed instruction into an always-on one for the whole `until` lifetime — an `avoid` can take a provider out of rotation around the clock, with no error anywhere. The file is also written by other surfaces (OpenChamber reads/writes the same store), so hand edits and cross-surface writes are realistic sources of a malformed window.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ModelRouteOverrides.parse` drops an entry whose `schedule` field is present but does not parse (present-but-unreadable is distinguished from absent), regardless of whether the entry has a valid `until`.
- [ ] Entries with no `schedule` field, and entries with a well-formed schedule, parse exactly as before.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/core/test/model-route-overrides.test.ts` cover: malformed schedule + valid `until` → entry dropped; malformed schedule without `until` → entry dropped; well-formed schedule + `until` → entry kept with its schedule and `applies` respects the window.
- [ ] `bun test test/model-route-overrides.test.ts` from `packages/core` passes.

title: Time-based model/provider weighting: peak/off-peak profiles and temporary priority windows

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: New feature or capability request

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

body:
## Problem

Model/provider priority in OpenCode is static config. But the *value* of a pool changes with the clock:

- Off-peak, we want a cheap, deep pool (e.g. DeepSeek) at **very high priority** — burn it freely while nothing else competes.
- During peak hours, that same pool should drop in priority or be **disabled entirely**, reserving capacity and attention for the work that matters then.

And sometimes the change isn't recurring — it's a **one-off window**: a provider runs a deal for the next 2 days, and for exactly that window that model should be top usage priority, then automatically revert.

None of this is expressible today without hand-editing config on a schedule.

## Desired behavior

1. **Time-of-day / day-of-week weight profiles**: per model/provider, weights (and enable/disable) can vary by local time window. Example: DeepSeek weight very high 23:00–07:00, low or disabled 09:00–17:00.
2. **Temporary priority ranges**: a boost with an explicit **start and end** (absolute timestamps). Inside the range the model/provider is raised to a configured weight / top priority; at the end it reverts automatically — no manual cleanup, no forgotten boosts.
3. **Composition rules**: temporary ranges override recurring profiles; recurring profiles override the static base weight. The *effective* weight at any moment must be inspectable (a command or log line that answers "why is this model ranked here right now?").
4. Everything is per-model/per-provider, individually disable-able, and expressed in config — changing a weight or toggling a profile must not require code changes.

## Config sketch

```yaml
schedules:
  - target: deepseek            # provider or model
    windows:
      - days: [mon, tue, wed, thu, fri]
        from: "23:00"
        to: "07:00"
        weight: 10
      - days: [mon, tue, wed, thu, fri]
        from: "09:00"
        to: "17:00"
        enabled: false
boosts:
  - target: some-provider/some-model
    from: "2026-11-01T00:00:00-05:00"
    to: "2026-11-03T00:00:00-05:00"
    weight: 100                   # top usage priority for the deal window
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Effective weight/enabled state for a target changes as configured when a window boundary passes, with no restart required (or, if a restart is required, that is explicit and documented).
- [ ] A temporary boost applies at its start, and the target's weight returns to its profile/base value at its end, verified by test with a fake clock.
- [ ] Precedence (boost > profile > base) is implemented and tested, including overlapping windows.
- [ ] An inspection surface (CLI/log/status) reports the current effective weight and which rule produced it.
- [ ] Timezone handling is explicit (config declares the timezone; no silent UTC/local ambiguity).
- [ ] Disabling the scheduling feature entirely restores static behavior.

## Context

Companion to #566 (quota-% × session-type placement filtering): schedules change *weights over time*; #566 gates *placement by remaining quota*. Both feed the same selection path and should share the weight model.

body:
## Problem

`activityCalendar` (packages/util/src/activity-calendar.ts:19) builds its intensity quantile set from **every** value in the activity map — including days completely outside the requested `[from, to)` range. One out-of-range big day demotes every in-range day: the busiest day of the displayed period no longer reaches the top level (4).

The module's own test contract is "keeps intensity relative to the requested range when older weeks are clipped" (activity-calendar.test.ts:117) — days inside the range but in clipped-out weeks correctly still count. Days outside the range itself are a different case and should not count; nothing documents or tests them counting.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 58d2a8277f)

Temporary bun probe importing the real module (kept in the goal's hidden files, `probe-2026-10-27-0052/out-cal.log`), range Mon 2026-10-19 → Mon 2026-10-26 local, in-range activity 10 steps (Oct 20) and 5 steps (Oct 21), plus one out-of-range day 2020-01-01 with 100000 steps:

```
[{"date":"2026-10-20","steps":10,"level":3},{"date":"2026-10-21","steps":5,"level":2}]
```

Without the out-of-range day the same input gives level 4 for Oct 20 (the range's maximum) — the 2020 day alone demotes it to 3.

Root cause: activity-calendar.ts:19 `const levels = [...new Set([...values.values()]...)]` — `values` is the unfiltered activity map; the `[from, to]` ordinals computed on lines 12-13 are only applied per-cell at line 30, never to the level set.

Callers: packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/stats.ts:172 and packages/tui/src/feature-plugins/system/stats.tsx:47 pass their stats activity with a range — any activity rows outside that range (wider query window, stale rows) silently skew the heatmap.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The level quantile set is built only from activity days whose date falls inside the requested `[from, to)` range; days in clipped-out weeks **inside** the range still count (existing test at activity-calendar.test.ts:117 keeps passing unchanged).
- [ ] New regression test: an out-of-range high-activity day does not change any in-range day's level (the probe case above: Oct 20 → level 4, Oct 21 → level 2, with and without the 2020 outlier).
- [ ] `bun test src/activity-calendar.test.ts` from packages/util passes.


## Acceptance criteria

- `activityCalendar` builds its intensity quantile set only from days inside the requested `[from, to)` range; days inside the range but in clipped-out weeks still count, per the existing test contract.
- The probe case (in-range 10/5 steps plus a 100000-step day in 2020) yields level 4 for the in-range maximum.
- Regression tests cover an out-of-range high-value day and keep the existing clipped-weeks test passing.
- No other consumer of the activity map changes behavior.

body:
## Problem

`retry()` (packages/util/src/retry.ts:34-52) trusts `options.attempts` blindly. With `attempts: 0` (or negative), the loop body never runs, the operation is **never called**, and the function falls through to `throw lastError` — where `lastError` is still `undefined`. The caller receives a thrown `undefined`: no Error, no message, no stack, and no hint that the operation never executed.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 58d2a8277f)

Temporary bun probe importing the real module (kept in the goal's hidden files, `probe-2026-10-27-0052/out-retry.log`):

```
attempts:0 threw: undefined (not an Error) calls 0
attempts:-1 threw: undefined (not an Error)
attempts:1 threw: Error: boom   (control — the real error propagates)
```

Root cause: retry.ts:35 `const attempts = options.attempts ?? 3` accepts 0/negative verbatim; the `for (let attempt = 0; attempt < attempts; ...)` loop is skipped; line 51 `throw lastError` throws the uninitialized `undefined`.

Current in-repo callers (app global-sync bootstrap) use the default, so this is a latent footgun in a shared utility rather than a live outage — any future caller computing attempts (e.g. from config or a retry budget) and landing on 0 gets an undebuggable failure instead of one real attempt.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `retry` with `attempts <= 0` behaves as `attempts: 1`: the operation runs exactly once and its result or real error propagates (never a thrown `undefined`).
- [ ] Regression tests in packages/util/src/retry.test.ts cover attempts 0 and negative, plus the unchanged default path.
- [ ] `bun test src/retry.test.ts` from packages/util passes.


## Acceptance criteria

- `retry()` with `attempts: 0` or a negative value either performs exactly one attempt or throws a real `Error` naming the invalid attempts value — it never throws `undefined`.
- The operation is never silently skipped: a probe/test with attempts 0/-1 shows the chosen behavior explicitly.
- Regression tests cover attempts 0, negative, and 1 (control: the real error propagates unchanged).
- Existing callers (app global-sync bootstrap, default attempts) are unaffected; the util test suite passes.

title: fix(schema): Identifier sortable prefix wrapped on 2026-08-14 — ascending/descending IDs now misorder across the 2^36 ms boundary

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: app/schema
labels.description: Package: schema (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Problem

`Identifier.create` (packages/schema/src/identifier.ts:16-30) packs `BigInt(timestamp) * 0x1000n + BigInt(counter)` — about 53 bits at current timestamps — but emits only the **low 48 bits** as the sortable hex prefix (shifts 40 down to 0, 6 bytes). The discarded high bits make the prefix wrap every 2^36 ms (~2.18 years). The most recent wrap was **2026-08-14T11:19:55Z** (timestamp 26 × 2^36), so ordering has been broken across that boundary ever since:

- An ID minted now sorts **before** an ID minted a year ago under `ascending()` — the opposite of its contract.
- An ID minted now sorts **after** an ID minted a year ago under `descending()` — also inverted.
- Within one era ordering still works (same-ms prefixes verified strictly increasing), which is why no test caught it: there are no tests for this module at all.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 58d2a8277f)

Temporary bun probe importing the real module (`create(false|true, ts)`), probe + output kept in the goal's hidden files (`probe-2026-10-27-0052/`):

```
ascending now   17bf34a93001  yearAgo a24421e93001  now>old? false
descending now  e840cb56cffe  yearAgo 5dbbde16cffe  now<old? false
same-ms ascending prefixes [17bf34a93001, 17bf34a93002, 17bf34a93003] strictly increasing? true
```

Arithmetic check: prefix(26×2^36 − 1000) = `ffffffc18001`, prefix(26×2^36 + 1000) = `0000003e8001` — the prefix wraps to zero at the boundary.

## Impact

These IDs are the chronological sort key for core records:

- `SessionID.create` uses `descending()` (packages/schema/src/session-id.ts) — sessions created after 2026-08-14 sort as *older* than sessions created in the year before it wherever sessions are ordered by ID.
- Event IDs use `ascending()` (packages/schema/src/event.ts: `evt_` + ascending()) — event-log ordering/cursors that compare IDs across the wrap boundary misorder.
- The same helpers back credential, form, integration, permission, pty, shell, workspace and session-message IDs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ascending()` IDs are strictly lexicographically increasing for increasing timestamps across the 2^36-ms boundary (and `descending()` strictly decreasing), pinned by new tests in packages/schema/test that mint IDs at explicit timestamps on both sides of a wrap boundary.
- [ ] The fix states what happens to IDs already minted (they keep their 26-char shape; cross-era misordering for pre-fix IDs is either corrected or explicitly documented as accepted).
- [ ] ID shape stays 26 chars with the same alphabet, and same-millisecond monotonicity (counter) is preserved; consider whether >4096 IDs in one millisecond spilling into the next millisecond's prefix space needs a guard while this is open.
- [ ] `bun test` for packages/schema passes.

title: fix(core): route context cap (PR #554) is bypassed for compaction when targets carry limit.input — auto-compaction uses the uncapped input window

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Finding

PR #554 (merged, closes #553) added the per-route context cap, but it caps only `limit.context`. When every target of a route carries a `limit.input` — the normal case for catalog models, whose `limit` is built from models.dev as `{ context, input, output }` (`packages/core/src/models-dev.ts`) — the route's presented `limit.input` is still the uncapped minimum across targets, and auto-compaction sizes itself from `limit.input` in preference to `limit.context`. Sessions on a capped route therefore do **not** compact at the cap, which is the exact behaviour #553 asked for ("sessions on THIS route compact at 100k", for a pool that is much cheaper below 100k context).

## Evidence

- PR: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/554 (commit `9b0ed6c803`), verified verbatim on current main (`58d2a8277f74`).
- `packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts:109-112` (current main):
  - `context: route.limit?.context !== undefined ? Math.min(route.limit.context, leafContext) : leafContext` — capped.
  - `input: Math.min(...expanded.map((target) => target.model.limit.input!))` — **not** capped, and present whenever every target defines an input limit.
- `packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts:966`: `calculateCeiling` computes `const window = limit.input || limit.context`; that ceiling drives both the auto-compaction trigger (`due(...)`, compaction.ts:213) and the compaction budget (compaction.ts:223). With an uncapped `input` present, the capped `context` is never consulted for compaction timing.
- The schema description added by #554 (`packages/schema/src/config/model-routes.ts`) promises the cap "compacts them earlier than the targets would" — true only in the configuration its test exercises.
- Test gap in #554: the new location-layer test (`packages/core/test/location-layer.test.ts`, "presents a route's configured context cap as its model limit") defines both targets with `limit: { context: ... }` only — no `input` — so the uncapped-input path is never exercised.

## Why it matters

The motivating use case is a `luna-haiku-100k` route whose members are much cheaper below 100k context. If those targets carry input limits (catalog models do), a session on the capped route can grow to the targets' uncapped input window (~the full model window) before auto-compaction fires, silently defeating the pricing-tier/compaction point the route was configured for. The route *displays* the capped context (tooltip/accounting use `limit.context`), so nothing looks wrong while compaction ignores the cap.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A route with `limit.context: 100000` whose targets define both `context` and `input` limits presents an effective compaction window at the cap (e.g. its presented `limit.input` is also capped, or `calculateCeiling` takes the cap into account) — verified by a test, not just by reading `limit.context`.
- [ ] Regression test: extend the #554 location-layer test (or add a sibling) with targets that carry `input` limits, asserting the capped route's presented limits and/or the compaction ceiling derived from them.
- [ ] Uncapped and over-capped routes behave exactly as before (cap never raises any presented limit above a target's own).
- [ ] Existing model-routes / location-layer / compaction suites still pass.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #554 against current main; the queue triage task should verify the finding against current main before any fix.

title: fix(core): ModelPlan.daysSince returns -1 for a timestamp an hour in the future — floor makes the day count asymmetric

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: status/needs-triage
labels.description: Not yet triaged; needs a first look

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Problem

`ModelPlan.daysSince` floors the elapsed time, which is asymmetric around now: a date one hour in the *past* reports 0 whole days, but a date one hour in the *future* reports −1. A `verifiedAt` recorded slightly ahead of the reader's clock (clock skew between machines, a timezone slipped into a hand-recorded date — the plan store is shared JSON that OpenChamber also writes) therefore displays as "−1 days" in plan info instead of 0.

## Evidence (verified on main e4abe251d5, temporary bun probe, removed after; `now` = 2026-10-26T12:00:00Z)

- `daysSince(now − 1 hour)` → `0`
- `daysSince(now + 1 hour)` → **`-1`**
- `daysSince("garbage")` → `null`; `daysSince(undefined)` → `null` (the documented unusable-date behavior — unaffected by this issue)

Code — `packages/core/src/model-plan.ts:318-322`:

```ts
export const daysSince = (date: string | undefined, now: number) => {
  if (date === undefined) return null
  const at = Date.parse(date)
  return Number.isNaN(at) ? null : Math.floor((now - at) / 86_400_000)
}
```

`Math.floor` rounds toward −∞, so any future offset, however small, crosses into −1, while a past offset must reach a full 24 hours to count 1. The consumer is `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/plan-info.ts:67`, which renders `verified <date> (<daysSince> …)` for every plan.

## Fix (narrow)

Clamp the result at 0 — a date in the future is "0 days since" for a *since* counter (truncating toward zero would give the same result for every input and is equally acceptable; pick one and document it). Past behavior is unchanged for all inputs.

## Acceptance criteria

- `daysSince` returns `0` for any timestamp in the future (1 hour or 10 days ahead), and unchanged values for past timestamps (1 hour ago → 0, 25 hours ago → 1).
- `null` behavior for `undefined`/unparseable input is unchanged.
- Regression tests in `packages/core/test/model-plan.test.ts`; `bun test test/model-plan.test.ts` from `packages/core` passes.

title: fix(core): ModelPlan.readNotes with an unparseable since silently returns zero notes — NaN comparison empties the result

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Problem

`ModelPlan.readNotes` treats an unparseable `since` filter as a filter that matches nothing: every note is silently excluded and the caller gets an empty list with `skipped: 0` — indistinguishable from "there are no notes". The same file's `daysSince` follows the opposite convention for an unusable date (returns `null`, "no usable date"), so the store's two date-reading helpers disagree on how a bad date behaves.

## Evidence (verified on main e4abe251d5, temporary bun probe with a scratch data dir, removed after; the dir held one valid note dated 2026-10-20)

- `readNotes({}, dir)` → 1 note
- `readNotes({ since: "2026-01-01" }, dir)` → 1 note
- `readNotes({ since: "not-a-date" }, dir)` → **0 notes**, `skipped: 0`

Code — `packages/core/src/model-plan.ts:305-312`:

```ts
const since = filter.since === undefined ? undefined : Date.parse(filter.since)
...
.filter((note) => since === undefined || Date.parse(note.at) >= since)
```

`Date.parse("not-a-date")` is `NaN`; `since` is then a number that is not `undefined`, and `Date.parse(note.at) >= NaN` is false for every note, so the filter empties the result instead of signalling the bad input. (The same comparison also silently drops any stored note whose `at` fails to parse whenever a `since` is given — those notes are not counted in `skipped` either, although `skipped` exists precisely to surface damaged note data.)

## Why it matters

`readNotes` backs the plan-info tooling that reports what the user has recorded about their plans. A mistyped or malformed `since` (a free-form string in `NoteFilter`) currently reads as "no notes match", which can lead a reader — human or model — to conclude the user never recorded anything and act on that. A loud failure, or an explicitly documented ignore-the-filter behavior, is strictly better than a plausible-looking empty result; the current behavior is neither.

## Acceptance criteria

- A decided, documented behavior for an unparseable `since`: either it throws a clear error naming the bad value, or it is ignored *and* that choice is documented on `readNotes`/`NoteFilter` — it must not silently return zero notes as if the filter matched nothing.
- Notes whose stored `at` does not parse are handled deliberately when a `since` filter is present (counted in `skipped`, or the chosen behavior is documented and tested).
- Regression tests in `packages/core/test/model-plan.test.ts` for a garbage `since` (and a valid `since` still filtering as before); `bun test test/model-plan.test.ts` from `packages/core` passes.

title: fix(core): config {file:...} in a trailing // comment is still read and substituted — the comment guard only covers comments that start the line

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Problem

`ConfigVariable.substitute` skips a `{file:...}` reference that sits in a `//` comment only when the comment starts the line. When the comment trails code on the same line, the reference is treated as live: the file is read from disk and its (escaped) contents are inlined into the comment text. A commented-out secret reference on a code line therefore still performs the file read — and logs a "missing or unreadable" warning when the file is absent — even though the author commented it out.

## Evidence (verified on main e4abe251d5, temporary bun probe with the FSUtil node layer, removed after; scratch config dir with `secret.txt` containing `SECRET_CONTENT`)

- Trailing comment: text `{ "key": "value" // note {file:secret.txt} }` → output **contains `SECRET_CONTENT`** (the file was read and substituted into the comment).
- Full-line comment control: text `{ // note {file:secret.txt} \n "key": "value" }` → output does **not** contain `SECRET_CONTENT`; the token is preserved verbatim.

Code — `packages/core/src/config/variable.ts:56-64` (`substituteFiles`):

```ts
const lineStart = text.lastIndexOf("\n", index - 1) + 1
const prefix = text.slice(lineStart, index).trimStart()
if (prefix.startsWith("//")) {
  out += token
  cursor = index + token.length
  continue
}
```

The skip test only asks whether the trimmed line *prefix* begins with `//`, i.e. whether the comment is the first thing on the line. A `//` that appears anywhere before the token on the same line (outside a string) is not detected.

Related: #547 covers `{env:...}` being substituted inside `//` comments (the env pass has no comment handling at all). This issue is the separate `{file:...}` path, whose comment guard exists but only covers comment-at-line-start. A fix here should be careful not to regress the string case: a `{file:...}` inside a quoted string value that happens to contain `//` earlier on the line (e.g. a URL `"https://…"`) is live config and must still substitute — comment detection needs to be string-aware, e.g. by scanning the line with the JSONC tokenizer rather than a raw `//` search.

## Why it matters

Commenting out a config line is the normal way to disable a secret reference. Today, doing that on a line that also carries live config silently keeps the read alive: the file is opened on every config load, a stale reference produces warning noise (and the escaped file content lands in the parsed text's comment), and the behavior differs from the full-line comment case an author would reasonably expect to behave the same.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `{file:...}` token inside a `//` comment is left verbatim whether the comment starts the line or trails code on the same line; no file read is attempted for it (no missing-file warning).
- A `{file:...}` token in a live string value still substitutes, including on a line whose string contains `//` (e.g. a URL) before the token.
- Tests in `packages/core/test/config/config.test.ts` (or the variable-substitution test file) cover trailing-comment, full-line-comment, and `//`-in-string cases; existing substitution tests pass.

title: fix(core): ModelRouteSchedule.parse accepts start == end, a window that can never be active — from/until rejects the same empty range

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Problem

`ModelRouteSchedule.parse` accepts a window whose `start` equals its `end`, but `active` can never return true for it — the rule silently never applies, at any time of day. The same function rejects the analogous empty range for the epoch bounds, so the two range checks disagree.

## Evidence (verified on main e4abe251d5, temporary bun probe, removed after)

- `parse({ start: "09:00", end: "09:00" })` → `{ start: "09:00", end: "09:00" }` (accepted)
- `active(thatWindow, t)` → `false` for every hour of a sample day (00:00–23:00 UTC steps)
- `parse({ from: 1000, until: 1000 })` → `undefined` (rejected); `parse({ from: 2000, until: 1000 })` → `undefined`

Code:

- `packages/core/src/model-route-schedule.ts:216-232` — `start`/`end` are normalized and stored with no relation check.
- `packages/core/src/model-route-schedule.ts:248` — `if (result.from !== undefined && result.until !== undefined && result.from >= result.until) return undefined` — the epoch bounds reject an empty/inverted range.
- `packages/core/src/model-route-schedule.ts:264` — `minuteMatches`: `if (start === end) return false` — an equal start/end is defined as never active.

## Why it matters

The module header promises the opposite failure mode: "a typo makes a rule disappear rather than apply at the wrong time." A window with equal start/end (an easy typo, or an editor emitting a zero-length window) instead parses fine and is stored canonically, and the routing rule then never fires — with no error anywhere. The operator believes a scheduled weight/skip is in force when it is not.

## Acceptance criteria

- A decided, documented behavior for `start === end` at parse time, consistent with the `from`/`until` rule (recommended: `parse` returns `undefined` for equal start/end, since `active` already defines that shape as never-active and an all-day window is already expressed by omitting both fields).
- Regression tests in `packages/core/test/model-route-schedule.test.ts` covering equal start/end (and confirming a normal same-day and a wrapping window still parse and activate as before).
- `bun test test/model-route-schedule.test.ts` from `packages/core` passes.

title: model-routes: let a route cap the context limit it presents (pools that must stay under a context cliff)
body:
Wanted for pool design (Drew, 2026-10-26): a Luna+Haiku pool whose members are much cheaper below 100k context. A route's presented limit is currently always the minimum across its targets, and the targets are shared with other pools — so there is no way to declare 'sessions on THIS route compact at 100k'.

Feature: an optional per-route context cap in the route config. The route model presents min(cap, targets' minimum) as its context limit, so compaction and context accounting for sessions on the route use the cap. A cap above the targets' minimum changes nothing.

Implementation follows in a PR from the pool-remap work: schema field on Config.ModelRoute.Route, applied where the plugin builds the route's Model.Info, with a location-layer test (capped, uncapped, and over-capped routes).

title: fix(core): route_usage silently omits plan quota windows that have no windowHours — monthly/reset-rule windows never appear

body:
## Problem

`route_usage` silently omits every plan quota window that has no `windowHours`, even though such windows are valid, are shown by `plan_info`, and the reporting code downstream is written to handle them. A plan whose limit is recorded as a count plus a reset rule — e.g. `{ name: "monthly", unit: "requests", limit: 1000, resetRule: "resets on the 1st" }` — never appears in `route_usage` output at all: not in the plan reports, and not in per-session window shares.

- `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/route-usage.ts:82-84` — the windows list is built with `window.windowHours === undefined ? [] : [{ plan, window }]`, dropping the window before any report is made. The same filtered list feeds both the plan reports (:139-143) and `ModelUsage.sessionReports`' window shares (:124-132).
- `windowHours` is optional in the schema: `packages/core/src/model-plan.ts:31-39` (`QuotaWindow.windowHours: Schema.optional(...)`), and `plan_info` renders windows without it (`tool/plugin/plan-info.ts:63`, `window.windowHours === undefined ? "" : ...`).
- Downstream support for the case exists but is unreachable from this tool: `ModelUsage.windowReport` maps `windowHours: window.windowHours ?? null` (`model-usage.ts:253-266`), and route-usage's own `describe()` has a `plan.windowHours === null ? "" : " (Xh)"` branch (`route-usage.ts:166`) that can never fire today.

## Evidence (verified this run on main 5c72116653)

Temporary `bun test` in `packages/core` (removed after), using the same store/collect harness as `test/route-usage-tool.test.ts` — a plan with two quotas, written via `ModelPlan.upsertPlan`/`writeStore` to a temp data dir, then `RouteUsageTool.collect({ hours: 24 }, undefined, { dataDir, now })`:

- Quotas on the plan: `{ name: "monthly", unit: "requests", limit: 1000, resetRule: "resets on the 1st" }` and `{ name: "5-hour", unit: "requests", limit: 100, windowHours: 5 }`
- `report.plans` contained exactly one entry — the `5-hour` window. The `monthly` window (limit and reset rule included) was absent.

## Why it matters

The tool's own description promises "each plan's quota windows with the share used in its last window". For plans recorded by reset rule rather than a rolling hour count — the natural shape for monthly subscription quotas, and the shape `ModelPlan.guidance` steers recorders toward when a number cannot be expressed in hours — the window is invisible, so a user or agent asking "how much of my monthly window is gone" gets an answer that silently excludes the window they asked about. The limit and reset rule are known and reportable even when a rolling-hours usage figure is not.

## Acceptance criteria

- `RouteUsageTool.collect` reports every quota window of every matching plan, including windows with no `windowHours`.
- For a window with no `windowHours`, the report carries its name, unit, limit and reset rule, with usage presented as unknown (`used`/`percent`/`remaining` null — the presentation the tool already uses when no database is attached), unless a well-defined usage window is chosen and documented instead.
- Per-session window shares behave consistently with the plan reports for such windows (listed with unknown use, or omitted by a documented rule — not silently filtered in one place only).
- A test in the style of `test/route-usage-tool.test.ts` covers a plan whose quota has a limit and reset rule but no `windowHours`; existing route-usage tests still pass.

title: fix(core): route-log observer marks every tagged failure retryable — Authentication and QuotaExceeded rows contradict the runner's retryable column

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

Attempt rows written through `ModelRouteLog.observer` store a `retryable` value that does not mean retryable: it is true for **every** failure whose `AIError.reason` carries a `_tag`, including failure classes the canonical classifier says must never be retried. The same `route_attempt.retryable` column is written correctly by the session runner, so the history contradicts itself depending on which path recorded the attempt.

- `packages/core/src/model-route-log.ts:207-210` — `isRetryableHint` returns `reason.reason?._tag !== undefined`.
- `packages/core/src/model-route-log.ts:122` — `observer.done()` stores `retryable: result.failure ? isRetryableHint(result.failure) : undefined`.
- Canonical classifier: `packages/ai/src/provider-error.ts:81-106` — `isRetryable` returns **false** for `Authentication`, `QuotaExceeded`, `ContentPolicy`, `InvalidRequest` (and for `Transport` with rejected delivery), true for `RateLimit` / `ProviderInternal` / `UnknownProvider` / qualifying `Transport`.
- The runner path uses the canonical one: `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts:404` — `retryable: failed ? SessionRunnerRetry.isRetryable(llmFailure) : undefined` (`SessionRunnerRetry` re-exports `@opencode/ai`'s `isRetryable`, `session/runner/retry.ts:3,14`).
- Observer callers are the background calls: session title (`session/title.ts:63`), generate (`session/generate.ts:72`), and compaction (`session/compaction.ts:543`) — so exactly the attempts those paths record are the mislabelled ones.

## Evidence (verified this run on main 5c72116653)

Temporary `bun test` in `packages/core` (capturing rows via `ModelRouteLog.setSink`, removed after):

- `observer.done("failure", { failure: new AIError({ reason: new AuthenticationError(...) }) })` → stored `retryable = true`; canonical `isRetryable(failure) = false`; `error_tag = Authentication`
- Same with `QuotaExceededError` → stored `retryable = true`; canonical `false`; `error_tag = QuotaExceeded`
- Control, `RateLimitError` → stored `retryable = true`; canonical `true` (agrees only by accident — every tagged reason stores true)
- Control, a plain `Error` failure → stored `retryable = false` (no `reason._tag` to find)

## Why it matters

`route_attempt` is the routing history that tuning, route stats, and any agent reading the log reason over. A column that says an authentication or quota failure was "retryable" on title/generate/compaction attempts but "not retryable" on runner attempts for the identical failure class makes the record untrustworthy for exactly the questions it exists to answer (should this target have been retried / rotated?). The mislabelling is systematic, not rare: it affects 100% of tagged non-retryable failures on the observer paths.

## Acceptance criteria

- `observer.done()` stores the canonical retryability for an `AIError` failure (delegate to `@opencode/ai`'s `isRetryable`, as the runner does), so `Authentication` and `QuotaExceeded` failures store `retryable = false` and `RateLimit` stores `true`.
- A non-`AIError` failure's stored value is a deliberate, documented choice (false or undefined), not an accident of shape.
- Tests in `packages/core` cover at least the Authentication/QuotaExceeded (false) and RateLimit (true) observer cases; existing `model-route-log.test.ts` tests still pass.
- No change to which attempts are recorded, their outcomes, or the error fields (`failureFields`) stored alongside.

title: fix(core): route-usage target split corrupts slash-less targets — provider loses its last char, model keeps the whole string (model-usage + route-usage)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

The route-usage reporting splits a target string `"provider/model"` with `indexOf("/")` in two places, and both corrupt a target that contains no slash (`indexOf` returns -1):

- `packages/core/src/model-usage.ts` — `targetReports` (lines 147-156): `providerID: target.slice(0, slash)`, `modelID: target.slice(slash + 1)`.
- `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/route-usage.ts` — `splitTarget` (lines 47-50): the identical two lines, used to filter configured targets and session targets against the tool's `provider`/`model` inputs.

For a slash-less target, `slice(0, -1)` drops the last character of the provider and `slice(0)` keeps the whole string as the model: the report invents a provider that does not exist, and the `route_usage` filter compares against the mangled pair, so the target can never match a provider filter and is silently misreported instead of degrading cleanly.

## Evidence (verified on main 5c72116653)

Temporary bun probe against the pure function (removed after):

```
ModelUsage.targetReports([], ["gpt-5"], [], new Map())
→ [{ target: "gpt-5", providerID: "gpt-", modelID: "gpt-5", requests: 0, ... }]
```

Configured targets reach this code from pool configuration via `ModelRouteReview.configured(route).targets` (route-usage.ts:57-59, 102-109): a bare or aliased entry that reaches the pool without a provider prefix — a typo'd pool entry is exactly the case the report's `configured-not-reached` state exists to surface — is mangled instead of shown as-is.

## Why it matters

`route_usage` is the diagnostic tool for "why didn't this target run". A malformed pool entry is one of the things it exists to reveal (its own docs list "a typo" as a usual cause of `configured-not-reached`). Corrupting the provider/model split hides that entry behind a nonsense provider name and breaks provider/model filtering for it.

## Acceptance criteria

- Decide and pin one behaviour for slash-less targets (e.g. whole string is the model id with an empty provider, or the entry is reported verbatim with both fields derived consistently) and apply it in **both** split sites so they cannot drift again — ideally one shared helper.
- Normal `provider/model` targets (including model ids containing further slashes) split exactly as today: first slash wins.
- New tests cover a slash-less configured target in `targetReports` and, if the helper is shared, its use from route-usage filtering.
- Relevant package tests pass (`bun test` for the touched test files from `packages/core`).

title: fix(core): config {env:...} is substituted inside // comments — {file:...} is skipped there, and a newline in the value breaks out of the comment

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`ConfigVariable.substitute` (`packages/core/src/config/variable.ts`) treats the two reference kinds inconsistently around `//` comments in JSONC config text:

- `{file:...}` references on a comment line are deliberately **skipped**: `substituteFiles` (variable.ts:48-56) checks the line prefix and leaves the token untouched. There is a test pinning this: "Ignored reference: {file:.}" (`packages/core/test/config/config.test.ts:1419`).
- `{env:...}` references are substituted **everywhere**, including inside comments: the env pass (variable.ts:24-34) is a single global `replace(/\{env:([^}]+)\}/g, ...)` with no comment awareness.

## Evidence (verified on main 5c72116653)

Temporary bun probe (same harness as config.test.ts, removed after):

```
text:  {\n  // note: {env:PROBE_NOTE}\n  "a": 1\n}
env:   PROBE_NOTE = "injected"
result: {\n  // note: injected\n  "a": 1\n}
```

## Why it matters

A comment is where a config author pastes an example or disables a line — the one place substitution must not happen. Worse, the substituted value is inserted raw in the unescaped pass: an env value containing a newline ends the comment, and the rest of the value becomes live config text the author never wrote. The file-reference path already established the intended semantics (comment lines are ignored); the env path just never got the same guard.

## Acceptance criteria

- `{env:...}` (including the `:-` fallback form) on a `//` comment line is left untouched, matching the existing `{file:...}` behaviour; references on lines with code before the token behave as today (decide and pin with a test if a trailing-comment case is ambiguous).
- Substitution elsewhere is unchanged, including the parse-repair escaping pass.
- New regression tests in `packages/core/test/config/config.test.ts`: an env reference inside a comment stays literal, including a value containing a newline; a normal env reference still expands.
- `bun test test/config/config.test.ts` from `packages/core` passes.

title: fix(core): config env substitution re-scans its output for {file:...} — env values can read arbitrary local files into config

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: status/needs-triage
labels.description: Not yet triaged; needs a first look

labels.description: Needs a user-look: Muse reviews first and handles what it can

labels.name: source/creator

labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`ConfigVariable.substitute` (`packages/core/src/config/variable.ts`) runs environment substitution first and then scans the **resulting** text for `{file:...}` references:

- `substitute` (variable.ts:22-34) computes `env(false)` over the whole config text, then calls `substituteFiles(input, env(false))`.
- `substituteFiles` (variable.ts:36-86) expands every `{file:path}` match in that already-substituted text.

So text that arrives from an environment variable is treated as if the config author had written it. An env value containing `{file:...}` is expanded as a file read, leaking arbitrary local file contents into the loaded config.

## Evidence (verified on main 5c72116653)

Temporary bun probe (test harness identical to `packages/core/test/config/config.test.ts`, removed after):

```
text:  { "v": "{env:LEAK}" }
env:   LEAK = "{file:secret.txt}"   (secret.txt in the config dir contains TOPSECRET)
result: { "v": "TOPSECRET" }
```

The reverse direction does not chain (env pass runs first, so `{env:...}` inside a file's contents stays literal), which shows the chaining is an accident of pass order, not a designed feature.

## Why it matters

Config text is authored by the user; environment values are not held to the same trust. Env values reach this code from process env inherited by plugins/MCP servers, CI variables, and shell exports the user did not write for this config. Any of them can silently pull local files (keys, tokens) into config values — which then flow to providers, MCP servers, and logs. File references should only be honoured where the config author wrote them.

## Acceptance criteria

- `{file:...}` is expanded only when it appears in the original config text, never inside text produced by an `{env:...}` substitution (including the `:-` fallback path, which is part of the token, and the escaped second pass at variable.ts:33).
- Existing behaviour is otherwise unchanged: `{env:VAR}`, `{env:VAR:-fallback}`, `{file:path}` (relative, `~/`, absolute), missing-file → empty with a warning, and the parse-repair escaping pass all keep working.
- New regression tests in `packages/core/test/config/config.test.ts`: an env value containing `{file:...}` stays literal in the output; a config-authored `{file:...}` still expands.
- `bun test test/config/config.test.ts` from `packages/core` passes.

title: fix(core): ModelPlan.slug can return a trailing dash — the 64-char slice runs after the trim

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`ModelPlan.slug` (`packages/core/src/model-plan.ts:176-182`) builds a plan id by lowercasing, collapsing non-alphanumerics to `-`, trimming leading/trailing dashes, and **then** slicing to 64 chars:

```ts
value.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-").replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "").slice(0, 64)
```

The slice runs after the trim, so a name whose 64th character lands on a separator returns an id ending in `-` — violating the helper's own invariant, and the result is stored as a plan `id` by `upsertPlan`.

## Evidence (verified on main 61c35a0228)

Temporary bun probe (removed after):

```
ModelPlan.slug("a".repeat(63) + " b c")  ===>  "aaaa…aaa-"   (64 chars, trailing dash)
```

## Acceptance criteria

- `slug` never returns a string with a leading or trailing `-`, including for inputs longer than 64 chars.
- Ids of 64 chars or fewer are unchanged; the 64-char cap still holds.
- Regression test in `packages/core/test/model-plan.test.ts` covers the boundary case above; existing model-plan tests pass (`bun test test/model-plan.test.ts` from `packages/core`).

## Suggested fix

Trim again after slicing (or slice before the final trim): `.slice(0, 64).replace(/-+$/g, "")` as the last step.

title: fix(core): ModelPlan.readNotes limit 0 returns every note — slice(-0) breaks the newest-N contract

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`ModelPlan.readNotes` (`packages/core/src/model-plan.ts:310`) documents its `limit` as "keeping the newest `limit`", implemented as `matching.slice(-filter.limit)`. That breaks at the edges of the range:

- `limit: 0` → `slice(-0)` is `slice(0)`, so it returns **every** matching note instead of none.
- `limit: -1` → `slice(1)`, so it returns all but the **oldest** note instead of an empty/invalid result.

## Evidence (verified on main 61c35a0228)

Temporary bun probe (removed after) against a scratch data dir with two notes added via `ModelPlan.addNote`:

```
limit0:   2        (expected 0)
limit1:   second   (correct — newest 1)
limitNeg: 1        (slice(1): dropped the oldest, kept the newest)
```

The one in-repo tool caller (`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/plan-info.ts:49`) happens to validate its model-facing `limit` to 1..500 before calling, so the tool path is shielded today — but `readNotes` is the shared store API (the plan store is explicitly a plain-JSON file other tools/readers share), and its stated contract is wrong for any direct caller passing 0 or a negative value. A caller asking for "no notes" silently gets the full history.

## Acceptance criteria

- `readNotes({ limit: 0 })` returns zero notes; a negative limit returns zero notes (or is clamped to 0), never a positive slice from the wrong end.
- Positive limits keep current behavior (newest N, oldest first).
- Regression tests in `packages/core/test/model-plan.test.ts` cover limit 0 and a negative limit; existing model-plan tests pass (`bun test test/model-plan.test.ts` from `packages/core`).

## Suggested fix

Guard the slice in `readNotes`: when `limit !== undefined`, use `limit <= 0 ? [] : matching.slice(-limit)` (or clamp once at the top of the function).

title: fix(core): captured provider error bodies leak common credential shapes — redactBody only covers Bearer, key-fields and sk/pk/rk keys

labels.name: kind/security

labels.name: source/creator

labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`ModelRouteLog.failureFields` stores a provider error body (opt-in via `experimental.model_route_log`) after scrubbing it with `redactBody` (`packages/core/src/model-route-log.ts:221-228`). The scrubber only covers three shapes:

- `Bearer <token>`
- key-like fields (`api_key`, `authorization`, `access_token`, `token`, `secret`, `password`) followed by `:` or `=`
- `(sk|pk|rk)[-_]<8+ chars>`

Every other common credential shape passes through verbatim and is persisted (capped at 2,000 chars) into the route-attempt history.

## Evidence (verified on main 61c35a0228)

Temporary bun probe (removed after) calling `ModelRouteLog.failureFields({ body }, { captureBody: true })` and checking whether the full token survives in `error_body`:

| Shape | Result |
|---|---|
| `ghp_…` (GitHub PAT) | LEAKED verbatim |
| `github_pat_…` (fine-grained PAT) | LEAKED verbatim |
| `AKIA…` (AWS access key id) | LEAKED verbatim |
| `xoxb-…` (Slack token) | LEAKED verbatim |
| `AIza…` (Google API key) | LEAKED verbatim |
| JWT (`eyJ….….…`) | LEAKED verbatim |
| `Basic <base64 user:password>` | LEAKED verbatim |
| `https://user:password@host/…` (URL userinfo) | LEAKED verbatim |
| `Bearer …`, `sk-proj-…`, `"api_key": "…"` | redacted (existing coverage) |

Provider error bodies routinely echo request context and upstream messages, so any of these shapes appearing in an upstream error is written to disk in the clear — exactly what the opt-in + redaction design is meant to prevent.

## Acceptance criteria

- `redactBody` also redacts, at minimum: GitHub tokens (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghu_`, `ghs_`, `ghr_`, `github_pat_`), AWS access key ids (`AKIA`/`ASIA` + 16), Slack tokens (`xox[baprs]-…`), Google API keys (`AIza…`), JWTs (`eyJ…` three-segment), HTTP Basic credentials (`Basic <base64>`), and passwords in URL userinfo (`scheme://user:pass@host`).
- New cases are covered in `packages/core/test/model-route-log.test.ts` alongside the existing redaction test (~line 441), asserting the token does not appear in `error_body`.
- Existing behavior is unchanged for non-secret body text (no over-redaction of ordinary words/numbers), and the existing `model-route-log` tests pass (`bun test test/model-route-log.test.ts` from `packages/core`).

## Suggested fix

Extend the `redactBody` replace chain in `packages/core/src/model-route-log.ts` with one pattern per shape above, following the existing `[REDACTED]` replacement style. Keep it a heuristic — the goal is covering the well-known published token formats, not parsing the body.

labels.name: effort/s

labels.name: meta/enriched

body:
Found during the 2026-10-26 pool effort audit (ladders verified against the serve-resolved model list).

**Mismatch between three parts of the routing code:**

1. `config/plugin/model-routes.ts` `routeVariants()` (~line 352): a route-level variant is offered when every target can produce it "either natively or through its variantMap" — maps count as producible.
2. `model-resolver.ts` (~line 495) comment: "the route only offers variants every target can produce one of those two ways" — same design intent.
3. But expansion in `config/plugin/model-routes.ts` `visit()` (~line 265) prunes a leaf with `if (variant && !model.variants.some((item) => item.id === variant)) continue` — **native names only; the target's `spec.variants` map is never consulted on this path.**

**Consequence:** when a tier pins a variant in config (the normal way pools select effort, e.g. `scout` → `opencode-route/deepseek-flash#medium`), every leaf lacking that name natively is silently dropped from the route — even if its target spec declares a remap (`variants: { medium: "high" }`). Concrete case: ClinePass DeepSeek/GLM ladders have no `medium` (none/low/high/max), so scout's flash and GLM routes run OpenDesign-only despite maps being the documented remedy. The resolver's runtime-requested-variant path does honor maps; only the config-pinned expansion path ignores them, and nothing validates the difference (the OpenChamber pool validator also does not check that a pinned variant exists on the addressed leaves).

**Asked fix (either):**
- Preferred: expansion consults the target's variantMap before pruning — a leaf that can produce the requested variant via a map survives, with the mapped variant as its resolved variant (mirroring the resolver's semantics).
- Or, if pinned-strictness is intended: make `routeVariants()` and the resolver comment agree with expansion, and add validation so a pinned variant that prunes leaves is loud instead of silent.

Config-side workaround in use meanwhile (developing-today/code pool remap, 2026-10-26): tiers address pools only at rungs every leaf has natively.
## Acceptance criteria
- Route expansion treats a variant as producible when a target can produce it natively OR through its `variantMap`, matching the `routeVariants()` offer rule and the resolver's stated design intent.
- A config-pinned variant that is only reachable via a target's variantMap no longer prunes the leaf (regression test covers the scout/tier-pinned case from this issue).
- Leaves are still pruned when no target can produce the variant either way.
- Existing model-routes / model-resolver tests pass.

`resolveEntryModels` and `resolveRouteTargets` in `packages/core/src/config/normalize.ts` copy entries into a plain object with `res[k] = ...`. For a key named `__proto__` that assignment sets the object's prototype instead of adding an entry, so a command, agent or pool named `__proto__` disappears from the normalized config without a diagnostic.

It shows up as a flaky failure of `ConfigNormalize > preserves arbitrary JSON-round-tripped native configuration` in `packages/core/test/config/normalization.test.ts`: the arbitrary config sometimes has a `__proto__` key, and the expected value keeps it while the normalized one does not. Building those maps with `Object.fromEntries` or `Object.defineProperty`, as the other normalizer maps do, would keep the entry. Found while merging main into #233; that PR does not touch these functions.

- `resolveEntryModels` and `resolveRouteTargets` in `packages/core/src/config/normalize.ts` preserve an entry literally named `__proto__` as data (e.g. via `Object.fromEntries`/`Object.defineProperty`), instead of mutating the result's prototype.

title: fix(core): an unparseable first date shadows a later valid reset time in both quota-reset parsers

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Problem

Both quota-reset message parsers stop at the **first** absolute date their pattern matches. If that first date is unparseable (e.g. month 13), the parser gives up on absolute times entirely — it never looks at a later, valid reset date in the same message, and falls through to the relative branch / `undefined`.

Verified on main `c792e04fe0` (2026-10-26, temporary bun probe in `packages/core`, removed after), `at = Date.UTC(2026,0,1,14)`:

- `parseQuotaReset("quota reset at 2026-13-01, back at 2026-01-02T00:00:00Z", at)` → `undefined`
- `resetAtFromMessage("quota reset at 2026-13-01, back at 2026-01-02T00:00:00Z", at)` → `undefined`
- `parseQuotaReset("quota reset at not-a-date 2026-01-02T00:00:00Z", at)` → `undefined` (same for `resetAtFromMessage`)
- Control: `parseQuotaReset("quota resets at 2026-01-02T00:00:00Z", at)` → `2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` (same for `resetAtFromMessage`)

Expected: the valid stated reset `2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` is returned; an invalid first candidate should not shadow it.

## Evidence

- `packages/core/src/model-route-limits.ts:80-84` — `resetAtFromMessage` does a single `ABSOLUTE_TIME.exec(...)`, and `if (!Number.isNaN(date)) return date` — on NaN it falls out of the absolute branch to the relative regex instead of trying the next absolute match.
- `packages/core/src/model-route-tuning.ts:162-169` — `parseQuotaReset` has the identical single-exec / NaN-fallthrough shape.
- Consumers affected: `predict` (model-route-tuning.ts:137), `noteAdjustments` (:211), and the session runner's retry hint via `retryHintFromMessage` (model-route-limits.ts:93-96, used at `session/runner/step.ts:141`) — a shadowed reset means no skip/hold and an immediate retry into an exhausted quota.

## Why it matters

Provider messages and user notes are free text; a message that mentions an earlier (possibly malformed or merely illustrative) date before the real reset is exactly the kind of input these forgiving parsers exist for — every other branch degrades gracefully. Silently returning no reset converts a stated "come back tomorrow" into an immediate retry.

## Acceptance criteria

- Both parsers return `2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` for the two probe messages above.
- A message whose only absolute date is invalid still returns `undefined` from the absolute branch (relative branch behaviour unchanged).
- `parseQuotaReset`'s quota-keyword gate unchanged.
- New tests in `packages/core/test/model-route-limits.test.ts` and `packages/core/test/model-route-tuning.test.ts`; `bun test test/model-route-limits.test.ts test/model-route-tuning.test.ts` from `packages/core` passes.

## Suggested fix

Iterate absolute-pattern matches (global regex / `matchAll`) and return the first candidate that `Date.parse` accepts, in both functions — or deduplicate onto one shared implementation (see #532, the keyword-set divergence in the same pair of parsers; the two fixes are independent but touch the same lines, so coordinate if both are in flight). Related: #526 (relative forms in the same parsers).

title: fix(core): the two quota-reset message parsers disagree on absolute-time keywords — "expires at"/"try again at" vs "available at"

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

body:
## Problem

The repo has two parsers for the same job — reading an absolute quota/limit reset time out of a provider message — and they accept different keyword sets, so the same message yields a reset instant from one and `undefined` from the other.

Verified on main `c792e04fe0` (2026-10-26, temporary bun probe in `packages/core`, removed after), `at = Date.UTC(2026,0,1,14)`:

| Message | `ModelRouteTuning.parseQuotaReset` | `ModelRouteLimits.resetAtFromMessage` |
|---|---|---|
| `quota expires at 2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` | `undefined` | `2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` |
| `quota retry at 2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` | `undefined` | `2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` |
| `quota wait until 2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` | `undefined` | `2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` |
| `quota exhausted; try again at 2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` | `undefined` | `2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` |
| `quota available at 2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` | `2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` | `undefined` |
| `quota resets at 2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` (control) | `2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` | `2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` |

## Evidence

- `packages/core/src/model-route-tuning.ts:162-166` — `parseQuotaReset` absolute pattern keywords: `reset|resume|back|available|return`.
- `packages/core/src/model-route-limits.ts:65-66` — `resetAtFromMessage`'s `ABSOLUTE_TIME` keywords: `retry|try again|wait|back|resume|reset|returns?|until|expires?(?: at)?` — no `available`.
- Production consumers use the limits parser (`model-route-tuning.ts:137` predict, `:211` noteAdjustments, `session/runner/step.ts:141` retry hint), while `parseQuotaReset` is exported and unit-tested as a public entry point (`packages/core/test/model-route-tuning.test.ts:122`) — so which answer a caller gets depends on which door they happened to import, and fixes applied to one parser (e.g. #523's short-form fix, #526's relative forms) do not automatically reach the other.

## Why it matters

A provider that writes "expires at …" or "try again at …" is honoured by the runner's retry hint but invisible to anything calling `parseQuotaReset`, and vice-versa for "available at …". This is the same drift pattern that produced #523 and #526 in the relative branch; the absolute branch has the same duplication with a different, keyword-shaped symptom.

## Acceptance criteria

- For every message in the table above, both parsers return the same instant (the union of both keyword sets, or one parser delegating to the other).
- `parseQuotaReset`'s quota-keyword gate is unchanged: a non-quota message such as `try in 5 minutes` / `back at <date>` with no quota/limit wording still returns `undefined` from `parseQuotaReset` (existing test at model-route-tuning.test.ts:137).
- Existing absolute/relative tests in both `model-route-limits.test.ts` and `model-route-tuning.test.ts` still pass, plus new paired cases covering `expires at`, `try again at`, `wait until`, and `available at` for both functions.
- `bun test test/model-route-limits.test.ts test/model-route-tuning.test.ts` from `packages/core` passes.

## Suggested fix

Extract one shared absolute-time pattern (or have `parseQuotaReset` call `resetAtFromMessage` after its quota gate) so the keyword set lives in exactly one place. Related: #526 (relative decimal/compound forms, same two parsers), #523 (closed, relative short form).

title: fix(core): ModelRouteSchedule.parse rejects zero-padded weekday strings — "06" loses the whole window while daysOfMonth accepts "01"

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal

body:
## Problem

`ModelRouteSchedule.parse` rejects a whole schedule window when a weekday is written as a zero-padded numeric string, even though the same zero-padded form is accepted for days of the month.

Verified on main `c792e04fe0` (2026-10-26, temporary bun probe in `packages/core`, removed after):

- `parse({ daysOfWeek: ["06"] })` → `undefined` (window rejected entirely)
- `parse({ daysOfWeek: ["6"] })` → `{ daysOfWeek: [6] }`
- `parse({ daysOfWeek: [" 6 "] })` → `{ daysOfWeek: [6] }`
- `parse({ daysOfMonth: ["01"] })` → `{ daysOfMonth: [1] }` (zero-padded accepted here)

## Evidence

- `packages/core/src/model-route-schedule.ts:60-66` — `dayOfWeek` tests the trimmed string against `/^[0-6]$/`, exactly one digit, so `"06"` and `"00"` can never match.
- `packages/core/src/model-route-schedule.ts:69-74` — `dayOfMonth` instead uses `/^-?\d+$/` and `Number(...)`, so `"01"` parses fine.
- `packages/core/src/model-route-schedule.ts:199-202` — any unreadable `daysOfWeek` entry rejects the whole window (by design, per the mixed-list rule), so this one spelling makes the entire rule disappear rather than just that day.

## Why it matters

`parse` is the friendly-form normalizer: it accepts day names, `"tues"`/`"thurs"`, single-digit hours/minutes (`"9:5"`), and zero-padded month days. A config or interpreter output that writes Saturday as `"06"` (the form a zero-padding formatter naturally emits) silently loses the whole routing window — the exact "typo makes a rule disappear" failure the header warns about, triggered by a spelling that is unambiguous.

## Acceptance criteria

- `parse({ daysOfWeek: ["06"] })` returns `{ daysOfWeek: [6] }` and `parse({ daysOfWeek: ["00"] })` returns `{ daysOfWeek: [0] }`.
- Out-of-range zero-padded forms still reject the window: `"07"`, `"42"` → `undefined`.
- Existing behaviour unchanged: names, `"6"`, whitespace-trimmed forms, mixed-list rejection (`["mon", "frieday"]` → `undefined`).
- Targeted tests added in `packages/core/test/model-route-schedule.test.ts` for the zero-padded forms; `bun test test/model-route-schedule.test.ts` from `packages/core` passes.

## Suggested fix

Widen the numeric-string check in `dayOfWeek` to allow an optional leading zero (e.g. `/^0?[0-6]$/`), keeping the 0–6 range validation in one place. Related but distinct: #527 (daysOfMonth sorting), #528 (seconds digit count in `minutesOf`).

title: fix(core): route governance judges a wildcard target's literal pattern — expanded models escape the check, and expired/disabled targets are still judged (PR #512)

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

body:
# fix(core): route governance judges a wildcard target's literal pattern — expanded models escape the check, and expired/disabled targets are still judged (PR #512)

## Finding

`routeTargets` in `packages/core/src/session/model-governance.ts` builds ONE `Model.Ref` per route target using the target selection's literal model id, and judges that ref. The runtime never runs that literal ref when the target is a pattern, and it drops some targets entirely:

- The model-routes plugin expansion (`packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts`, `expand` + `matchingModels`) expands a target model id containing a `*` pattern into every matching catalog model, and skips targets that are expired (`spec.until` passed, :261), whose model is disabled (`!model.enabled`, :263), or whose fixed variant the model doesn't offer.
- Governance therefore judges a literal pattern id that never runs, while the actually-expanded models escape the route-target check: an excluded-model bypass for wildcard targets, and over-deny for expired/disabled targets (governance can deny a route over a target the runtime would never run, and can fail an allowed-list check on a dropped target).

This is the target-set divergence noted as a REVIEW-FINDING by the pr-diff-review job on 2026-10-26 (from PR #512), verified and filed by the issue sweep. It is related to #519 (governance judging `defaultVariant`/remap variants the runtime drops) but distinct: #519 is about the *variant* of a single concrete target; this issue is about *which models/targets* are judged at all.

## Evidence

Verified on current main `c792e04fe0`:

- Wildcard targets are valid, reachable config: `ConfigModel.ModelID` (`packages/schema/src/config/model.ts:11`) is `/^[^\s#/]+(?:\/[^\s#/]+)*$/u` — `*` is not excluded — and route tuning docs use patterns as targets (`deepseek/*`, `openai/gpt-6-*`; `packages/schema/src/config/model-routes.ts:152`). `Model.Ref.parse` (used by `ConfigModel.Selection` parsing) accepts a `*` in the model id.
- Plugin expansion: `model-routes.ts:262` iterates `matchingModels(ref.id, ...)`; `matchingModels` (:311) converts a pattern containing `*` into a regexp over the provider's catalog and returns every matching model; expired targets are skipped at :261 and disabled models at :263.
- Governance: `routeTargets` (model-governance.ts, ~:166-215) constructs `{ id: Model.ID.make(selection.model), providerID }` once per target — the literal pattern — and never reads `until` or any enabled flag, so a pattern target is judged as one pseudo-ref and dropped targets are judged as live ones.
- Dedup: searches for "wildcard route target governance" and "routeTargets" return only #519 (variant filtering, distinct) and closed #506 (variant remaps). No open or closed issue covers the target-set divergence.

## Acceptance criteria

- Governance judges a route's targets as the set the runtime will actually run: either `assertAllowed` consumes the plugin's expanded/filtered target list for the route, or `routeTargets` expands wildcard targets against the same catalog the plugin uses and drops expired/disabled targets the same way.
- A wildcard target whose expansion includes an excluded model denies the route (no bypass via the literal pattern).
- An expired (`until` passed) or disabled target does not by itself deny or fail the route.
- Regression tests in `packages/core/test/session/model-governance.test.ts` cover at least: (a) wildcard target expanding to an excluded model denies; (b) wildcard target expanding only to allowed models passes; (c) an expired target is not judged.
- Existing route governance tests (#506/#512 variant tests, plain targets) still pass.

Filed by issue-sweep-rotating 2026-10-26 (random pick 1, item 2), from the pr-diff-review REVIEW-FINDING recorded 2026-10-26.

body:
## Problem

`ModelRouteSchedule.minutesOf` accepts one- or two-digit hours and minutes but requires exactly two digits for seconds, so a hand-written time with a single-digit second makes `parse` reject the entire window.

- `packages/core/src/model-route-schedule.ts:80-88` — `minutesOf` matches `/^(\d{1,2}):(\d{1,2})(?::(\d{2}))?$/`: hours `\d{1,2}`, minutes `\d{1,2}`, seconds `\d{2}` only.
- The doc comment at :79 advertises the friendly forms: `"9:30", "09:30", "23:59", "9:5" or "9:30:15"` — single-digit minutes ("9:5") are explicitly in, single-digit seconds are inexplicably out.

## Evidence (verified this run on main c792e04fe0)

Probe run as a temporary `bun test` in `packages/core`, then removed:

- `ModelRouteSchedule.minutesOf("9:5")` → `545`
- `ModelRouteSchedule.minutesOf("9:30:15")` → `570`
- `ModelRouteSchedule.minutesOf("9:30:5")` → `undefined`
- `ModelRouteSchedule.parse({ start: "9:30:5" })` → `undefined` (the whole window is rejected, so the routing rule silently disappears — the header at model-route-schedule.ts:13-16 reserves that behaviour for a window it "cannot read")

## Why it matters

"9:30:5" is a readable time in exactly the friendly style this parser exists to accept, and seconds are truncated anyway ("Seconds round down", :79 — `parse({ start: "9:30:59" })` → `"09:30"` in the existing tests). Rejecting the whole window over one missing leading zero turns a trivially recoverable spelling into a silently dropped routing rule. This is the same minutesOf surface #517/#518 just fixed for out-of-range seconds (60-99); the digit-count asymmetry is the remaining inconsistency in that regex.

## Acceptance criteria

- `ModelRouteSchedule.minutesOf("9:30:5")` returns `570`, and `parse({ start: "9:30:5" })` returns `{ start: "09:30" }`.
- Range checking is unchanged: "9:30:60" and "9:30:99" still return `undefined`, and all existing cases in `packages/core/test/model-route-schedule.test.ts` keep passing.
- A regression test for the single-digit-seconds form is added to `packages/core/test/model-route-schedule.test.ts`.
- Tests run from `packages/core` (`bun test test/model-route-schedule.test.ts`).

body:
## Problem

`ModelRouteSchedule.parse` normalizes `daysOfWeek` to a sorted canonical list but leaves `daysOfMonth` in input order, so the same window parses to different canonical values depending on how the author happened to order the list.

- `packages/core/src/model-route-schedule.ts:203` — daysOfWeek: `const days = [...new Set(parsed as number[])].sort((left, right) => left - right)`
- `packages/core/src/model-route-schedule.ts:212` — daysOfMonth: `const days = [...new Set(parsed as number[])]` (dedupe only, no sort)

The file header (model-route-schedule.ts:13) promises "`parse` normalizes the friendly forms … to this shape" — one canonical shape. `describe()` (:293-295) also prints the days-of-month list in stored order, so two spellings of the same window describe differently.

## Evidence (verified this run on main c792e04fe0)

Probe run as a temporary `bun test` in `packages/core`, then removed:

- `ModelRouteSchedule.parse({ daysOfMonth: [15, 1, 15] })` → `{ daysOfMonth: [15, 1] }`
- `ModelRouteSchedule.parse({ daysOfWeek: [5, 1, 5] })` → `{ daysOfWeek: [1, 5] }`

## Why it matters

Anything that compares, snapshots, hashes, or displays a parsed window (config round-trips, editor UIs showing a rule back to its author via `describe`, tests) sees two different values for one identical window. The daysOfWeek branch already established the sorted-canonical precedent in the same function; daysOfMonth is the one list that was left out.

## Acceptance criteria

- `parse({ daysOfMonth: [15, 1, 15] })` returns the days in one deterministic canonical order, and `parse({ daysOfMonth: [1, 15] })` returns the identical value.
- The `-1` ("last day") sentinel keeps the position the existing test pins: `parse({ daysOfMonth: ["1", 15, -1] })` must still return `{ daysOfMonth: [1, 15, -1] }` (model-route-schedule.test.ts:14) — i.e. numeric days ascending with `-1` last, not a raw numeric sort that would put `-1` first.
- `active()` behaviour is unchanged (matching is order-insensitive today); all existing tests in `packages/core/test/model-route-schedule.test.ts` pass, plus a new case covering out-of-order input.
- Tests run from `packages/core` (`bun test test/model-route-schedule.test.ts`).

title: fix(core): relative quota resets with decimal or compound amounts are misread — "in 1.5 hours" ignored, "in 1 hour 30 minutes" read as 1 hour

labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal
