body:
### Context & Background
In OpenCode upstream commit `a3f7f42ac9` (`feat(core): continue responses after output token limits (#53876)`) and commit `044d8b7d2e` (`feat(ai): continue split Gemini responses (#55056)`), OpenCode added automatic multi-turn continuations: when an LLM truncates output because it reaches its maximum generation limit (`finish_reason: length` or `max_tokens`), the core runner automatically requests a continuation to complete the generation seamlessly.

In our fork (`developing-today/opencode`), every LLM call produces a discrete record in `route_attempt` with `tokens_input`, `tokens_output`, `tokens_reasoning`, and `cost_usd`. When a response requires multiple continuation requests, logging each continuation as an isolated attempt creates fragmented records that disconnect the full cost of the assistant turn.

### Feature Objective
Enhance `route_attempt` and our usage metrics store to stitch continuation requests together into a unified turn attempt:
1. Link continuation attempts to the primary root request via a `continuation_of` or `parent_attempt_id` reference.
2. Provide aggregated cost and token rollups for multi-segment responses so that total turn cost and duration are accurately reflected.

---

### Technical Specifications

#### 1. Schema Enhancement
- Add a new migration in `packages/core/src/database/migration/` (e.g. `20261017000000_route_attempt_continuation.ts`):
  ```sql
  ALTER TABLE `route_attempt` ADD `continuation_of` integer;
  ALTER TABLE `route_attempt` ADD `continuation_index` integer DEFAULT 0;
  CREATE INDEX `route_attempt_continuation_idx` ON `route_attempt` (`continuation_of`);
  ```

#### 2. Continuation Tracking in LLM Runner
- In `packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts`:
  - When a completion finishes with `finish_reason: length` and initiates a continuation:
  - Pass the parent attempt ID to the subsequent continuation request.
  - Set `continuation_index` incrementally (0 for initial, 1 for first continuation, etc.).
  - Calculate `cost_usd` for the incremental tokens of each chunk.

#### 3. Metrics Rollup Queries
- In `packages/core/src/model-usage.ts` and `packages/core/src/model-route-log/sql.ts`:
  - When querying turn attempts, provide a helper `getTurnAttemptMetrics(rootAttemptId)` that sums:
    - Total input tokens (excluding duplicate cached prefixes where applicable)
    - Total output tokens across all continuation chunks
    - Total `cost_usd`
    - Total response time (from start of chunk 0 to end of last chunk)

---

### Key Files & References
- `packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts`: Output token limit detection, response continuation loop
- `packages/core/src/database/schema.gen.ts`: `route_attempt` table
- `packages/core/src/model-usage.ts`: Attempt metrics aggregation and reporting
- `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/route-usage.ts`: `route_usage` inspection tool

### Acceptance Criteria
1. When an LLM response triggers automatic continuation, the follow-up requests record `continuation_of` pointing to the initial attempt.
2. `route_usage` and session cost aggregations correctly tally all continuation chunks into the total turn cost.
3. If a continuation fails, the initial partial output and failure reason are logged accurately.
4. Unit tests in `packages/core/test/` verify continuation linking and aggregated token/cost calculation.

body:
### Context & Background
In OpenCode upstream commit `d78267503d` (`feat(plugin): expose credential.activate to server plugins (#52797)`), upstream added a server-side API allowing plugins to programmatically activate and switch stored credentials for any provider.

In our fork (`developing-today/opencode`), we implemented intelligent model routing with tier awareness (`cheap`, `standard`, `frontier`), quota tracking, rate limit monitoring, and automated fallback. However, currently when a credential hits a 429 rate limit or its usage window is exhausted, routing can only failover to a different model or provider, or ask the user to switch accounts manually.

### Feature Objective
Implement automatic credential failover within our routing engine: when a request fails with an HTTP 429 or quota limit, rather than immediately degrading to a lower-tier model or prompting the user, the router should check for secondary stored credentials for the same provider, activate the next available credential via `credential.activate`, and retry the request seamlessly within the same turn.

---

### Technical Specifications

#### 1. Credential Inventory & Status Detection
- Upstream provides `server.credential.list()` and `server.credential.activate(id)` or plugin hooks under `packages/plugin/src/` and `packages/core/src/`.
- In our routing controller (`packages/core/src/model-route.ts` / `packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts`):
  - Inspect configured credentials for the target provider (e.g. `anthropic`, `openai`, `google`).
  - Track rate-limit backoff timers or quota windows per credential ID.

#### 2. Automatic Failover Sequence in Runner
- In `packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts` / `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts`:
  - When an LLM request returns an error tagged with 429 (`error_status === 429` or error message contains rate-limit/quota exhaustion):
  - Check if alternative credentials exist for `provider_id`.
  - If an alternative valid credential is found:
    1. Call `credential.activate(nextCredentialId)`.
    2. Record a failover note in `route_attempt` (`failed_over_to` or metadata indicating credential switch).
    3. Re-issue the request without interrupting the user turn.
  - If no alternative credential exists, fall back to the existing route fallback chain (alternate provider or prompt user).

#### 3. Quota Cooldown & Cooldown Window Expiration
- Maintain in-memory and persistent cooldown timestamps for credentials that hit rate limits (e.g. using `route_health` in `packages/core/src/model-route-log/sql.ts`).
- Avoid switching back to a cooled-down credential until its window has reset (or after standard exponential backoff).

---

### Key Files & References
- `packages/plugin/src/effect/plugin.ts` & `packages/plugin/src/promise/plugin.ts`: `credential.activate` interface
- `packages/core/src/model-route.ts`: Model route resolution, target selection, and fallback lists
- `packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts`: Request dispatch, error handling, retry loops
- `packages/core/src/database/schema.gen.ts`: `route_attempt` and `route_health` tables

### Acceptance Criteria
1. When multiple credentials exist for a provider and the active one receives a 429, the router activates an alternate credential without failing the turn.
2. The retry attempt successfully completes and records `failed_over_to: "credential:<id>"` in `route_attempt`.
3. If all credentials for the provider are exhausted, the router proceeds to the next provider in the route definition or triggers standard error handling.
4. Unit tests in `packages/core/test/` verify credential failover behavior with mocked provider responses.

body:
# fix(script): publish-winget GitHub API fetches have no deadline — a stalled api.github.com hangs the release publish step

Filed 2026-11-01 by new-issue-creator-opencode. Main: 99a3387394.

## Evidence

- `script/publish-winget.ts:207-217` — every GitHub API call in the script routes through the `github()` helper, which calls `fetch(\`https://api.github.com${route}\`, {...})` with **no `signal`, no `AbortSignal.timeout`, no deadline of any kind** (grep for `AbortSignal|signal` in the file: only the helper definition, no timeout anywhere).
- 10 call sites ride on that helper: `:139` (contents check), `:143-144` (fork create), `:146-147` (pulls list), `:154` (ref), `:155` (commit), `:156-157` (tree create), `:171-172` (commit create), `:177` (ref create), `:182-184` (ref PATCH on retry), `:193-194` (PR create).
- `script/publish-winget.ts:219-222` — `json()` reads bodies via `response.text()` (error path) / `response.json()` with no byte bound.
- Caller: `script/publish.ts:133` runs `bun ./script/publish-winget.ts` as part of the release publish flow, so this runs unattended in CI. The publish workflow jobs carry 30–90 minute `timeout-minutes` caps (`.github/workflows/publish.yml`), so a stalled GitHub API response burns the entire job cap instead of failing fast.
- This is the sibling the just-merged #1329 fix missed: `script/update-artifact.ts` got named per-operation deadlines (`REQUEST_TIMEOUTS`, `withDeadline`) at HEAD 99a3387394; `publish-winget.ts` performs the same class of release-pipeline API calls with none.
- Not covered by the bounded-http gate: `script/check-bounded-http.ts` SCAN_ROOTS covers `packages/*/src` and `services/*/src`; its scope note (#1256) deliberately leaves root `script/` out — root release scripts rely on per-site fixes like #1275 / #1329. This filing follows that precedent; it does not ask to extend the gate.

## Why it matters

The winget publish step is a sequential chain of ~10 GitHub API calls. Any one of them stalling (GitHub API degradation, network stall) hangs the release publish job until the workflow cap kills it, with no error naming the stalled operation — the exact failure mode #1329 fixed for update-artifact.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The `github()` helper in `script/publish-winget.ts` carries an explicit named deadline (e.g. an `AbortSignal.timeout` constant in the style of `update-artifact.ts`'s `REQUEST_TIMEOUTS`) that also bounds the `json()` body reads.
- [ ] A stalled GitHub API endpoint fails the script fast with an error naming the operation/route, instead of hanging until the workflow job cap.
- [ ] Existing behavior unchanged for answered responses: fork reuse, 422 ref-PATCH retry path, and PR creation all work as before.
- [ ] A test or scripted probe demonstrates the deadline aborting a stalled response.

body:
## Evidence

On main `35c411c1ee`, `script/update-artifact.ts` makes three outbound
fetches, none with a `signal`/timeout (grep for `timeout|AbortSignal` in
the file: no hits), and two read bodies unbounded:

- `:25` — GitHub OIDC token request:
  `fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: ... } })`, body read via
  `tokenResponse.json()` at `:27` with no cap.
- `:32-47` — the publish POST to `https://opencode.ai/update/api/publish`,
  retried up to 3 times **only on a returned 5xx**; a stalled endpoint
  never returns, so the retry loop never engages. The error path at `:47`
  reads `await response.text()` unbounded.
- `:101` — Cloudflare token verify inside `credentials()`:
  `fetch(.../tokens/verify, ...)`, body read via `response.json()` at
  `:105` with no cap.

Callers are the release pipeline: `packages/cli/script/publish.ts:91,116,123`,
`packages/cli/script/publish-aur.ts:93`, `packages/cli/script/publish-homebrew.ts:114`,
`packages/desktop/scripts/publish.ts:25`. These run inside the publish
workflows, so a single stalled endpoint burns the whole (now-capped) job
instead of failing fast with a named deadline — and on a local/manual
publish run it hangs indefinitely.

This is the one root-`script/` fetch site the bounded-http work has not
reached: the gate (`script/check-bounded-http.ts`) scans `packages/*/src`
and `services/*/src` only, and the sibling script fetch in
`script/release.ts` was already fixed/filed as #1275 (npm registry latest
doc, no timeout + unbounded `res.json()` — CLOSED). #1275's fix pattern
(named deadline constant + `AbortSignal.timeout`) is the model here.
`script/stats.ts` is a manual analytics script and is explicitly out of
scope for this issue.

Dedup: search 2026-11-01 for `update-artifact` finds no issue covering
these fetches (hits are the unrelated updater/services items #1031,
#1137, #141).

## Why it matters

- The publish path is how every release ships; its failure mode today is
  "hang until the workflow job cap kills everything" rather than a fast,
  diagnosable deadline error naming the stalled endpoint.
- The 3-attempt retry on the publish POST gives a false sense of
  resilience: it only handles *answered* failures, not stalls — the exact
  failure a deadline exists for.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three fetches in `script/update-artifact.ts` (OIDC token,
      publish POST, Cloudflare verify) carry an explicit named deadline
      (e.g. an `AbortSignal.timeout` constant, following #1275's pattern).
- [ ] The deadline also bounds the body reads (`tokenResponse.json()`,
      publish error-path `response.text()`, verify `response.json()`) —
      a deadline on headers alone does not settle a stalled body.
- [ ] A stalled endpoint now fails with an error naming the operation
      within the deadline, and the publish POST's existing 5xx retry
      behaviour is unchanged for answered failures.

title: fix(gui-extensions): browser file-URL policy throws URIError on malformed percent-encoding instead of refusing the URL

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/gui-extensions
labels.description: Package: gui-extensions (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Evidence

On main `35c411c1ee`, `packages/gui-extensions/src/browser/policy.ts:19-25`:

```ts
function canonicalPath(input: string) {
  const value = decodeURIComponent(input)
    .replaceAll("\\", "/")
    .replace(/^\/([A-Za-z]:\/)/, "$1")
  ...
}
```

`decodeURIComponent` is called with no guard, on two attacker/page-controlled
inputs inside `fileURLWithin` (policy.ts:36-44): the `pathname` of a parsed
file URL, and each allowed root. A file URL whose path contains a malformed
percent sequence — a bare `%` (a plausible real filename, e.g. `100%.html`),
an invalid hex escape (`%zz`), or a truncated UTF-8 sequence (`%E0%A4%A`) —
makes `fileURLWithin` **throw `URIError: URI malformed`** instead of
returning a boolean.

Verified this run with a laptop probe
(`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-gui-policy-decode`, exact copy of the
policy.ts:19-44 logic, node):

```
OK    true  file:///home/me/repo/out/index.html            (control: inside)
OK    false file:///home/me/.aws/credentials               (control: outside)
THROW URIError: URI malformed | file:///home/me/repo/100%.html
THROW URIError: URI malformed | file:///home/me/repo/%zz.html
THROW URIError: URI malformed | file:///home/me/repo/%E0%A4%A.html
OK    false file:///home/me/repo/out/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/.aws/credentials  (pinned traversal test)
THROW URIError: URI malformed | root path itself containing a bare %
```

The throw escapes into every caller, all of which are fail-closed security
guards that assume a boolean answer:

- `packages/gui-extensions/src/browser/pane.ts:119` — Electron
  `webRequest.onBeforeRequest` for `file://*/*`:
  `callback({ cancel: !fileURLWithin(details.url, entry.fileRoots) })`.
  On a throw the callback is **never invoked**, so the subresource request
  is left pending instead of being cancelled.
- `packages/gui-extensions/src/browser/chromium.ts:386-395` — the
  `will-frame-navigate` / `will-redirect` guard: the throw aborts the guard
  before `event.preventDefault()` and before the refusal is published.
- `policy.ts:54-97` — `allowedDestination` → `refusal` → `normalizeURL`:
  a typed address with malformed encoding surfaces a raw `URIError`
  instead of the documented refusal error.

The same package already has the correct pattern:
`packages/gui-extensions/src/file/resolve-link.ts:132-138`
(`decodePathSafely` wraps `decodeURIComponent` in try/catch). `policy.ts`
is the unguarded outlier. `policy.test.ts` pins encoded traversal
(`%2e%2e`, line 29) but has no malformed-encoding case.

Dedup: no open or closed issue mentions `fileURLWithin`, `canonicalPath`,
or a gui-extensions `URIError` (search 2026-11-01; the only URIError hit is
#1323, the console locale cookie, a different package and input).

## Why it matters

- This is a security-policy function: its contract is "answer yes/no for
  any URL a page or user presents". Throwing breaks that contract in the
  two Electron guard seats — one leaves a request hanging (callback never
  fires), the other skips the explicit block-and-report path.
- The trigger is not exotic: any web page or workspace file can link to a
  file URL with a bare `%` in the name, and a workspace directory whose
  own name contains `%` makes *every* check throw.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `fileURLWithin` / `allowedDestination` / `refusal` never throw on
      malformed percent-encoding in the URL or in a root; malformed input
      is refused (fail-closed, returns false / the workspace refusal).
- [ ] `policy.test.ts` gains cases: bare `%`, `%zz`, and truncated UTF-8
      in the file URL, plus a root containing a bare `%`; the existing
      `%2e%2e` traversal cases still return false and the inside/outside
      controls still pass.
- [ ] `bun test src/browser/policy.test.ts` passes from
      `packages/gui-extensions`.

# fix(ci): test.yml's ci-fix job has no timeout-minutes — per-job gap the file-level check cannot see (#61 rule)

## Evidence

On main `91410958d4`, `.github/workflows/test.yml:491-503`:

```yaml
  ci-fix:
    needs: [unit, build, e2e]
    if: failure()
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      issues: read
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: developing-today/code/.github/actions/pm-dispatch-ci-fix@main
        continue-on-error: true
```

The job has **no job-level `timeout-minutes`**, so a hang in the dispatch
action runs to the GitHub Actions default of 360 minutes. The job was added
in `a8dfb81801` ("ci: add dispatch agents workflow + ci-fix hook (#979)")
without a cap.

#61 established the rule that every job in every workflow carries a
`timeout-minutes` cap, and #1184 fixed the same regression in
branch-cleanup.yml. Both were verified at file level — but test.yml *does*
contain `timeout-minutes` (on other jobs and on steps), so a file-level
`grep -L` check passes while this one job is uncapped.

Verified this run by parsing every workflow under `.github/workflows/`
and checking each runnable job individually: across all 28 workflow files,
`ci-fix` in test.yml is the **only** runnable job with no job-level
`timeout-minutes` (the jobs in agents.yml are reusable-workflow callers,
which cannot take the key). Comparable single-purpose dispatch jobs are
capped: notify-discord.yml's job at 10, branch-cleanup.yml's at 30.

## Why it matters

- The job fires exactly when CI is already failing (`if: failure()`); a
  stuck dispatch would squat a runner for up to 6 hours on top of a red
  pipeline, and `continue-on-error: true` does not bound how long the step
  itself can hang.
- The gap is invisible to the verification method used for #61/#1184, so
  the rule can keep regressing one job at a time inside otherwise-capped
  files.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ci-fix` in `.github/workflows/test.yml` has a job-level
      `timeout-minutes` (10 matches the comparable notify-discord dispatch
      job; any small explicit cap is fine).
- [ ] A per-job scan of all workflows (parse YAML, check every runnable
      job) shows no remaining job without a job-level cap.
- [ ] Nice-to-have: the per-job check is scripted somewhere durable (a
      script test or CI step) so the #61 rule is enforced per job, not
      per file.

## Summary

Console locale resolution (`packages/console/app/src/lib/language.ts`) mishandles two adversarial inputs on the per-request hot path:

1. **`fromDocsPathname` reads `DOCS_LOCALE` through the prototype chain** — it tests membership with the `in` operator (`language.ts:193`), so a docs URL whose locale segment is `constructor` or `__proto__` resolves to an inherited member (the `Object` constructor function / `Object.prototype`) instead of `null`, and that non-string value escapes as the request's "locale".
2. **`localeFromCookieHeader` throws `URIError` on a malformed `oc_locale` cookie** — it calls `decodeURIComponent(raw)` unguarded (`language.ts:313`), so a cookie value with an invalid percent sequence (`%`, `%zz`, `%E0%A4%A`) throws instead of falling back, and `localeFromRequest` propagates the throw to every caller.

This is the console sibling of #851 (fixed for `packages/web`); the check:proto-reads gate scans only `packages/core/src`, so the console copy has no regression net.

## Evidence (main 305000712d, reproduced against the real module)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-console-language/probe.ts` importing `packages/console/app/src/lib/language.ts` from the laptop clone at the same HEAD:

```
control /docs/de/intro: "de"
control /docs/en/intro: "en"
proto /docs/constructor/intro: function function Object() { [native code] }
proto /docs/__proto__/intro: object [object Object]
control cookie en: "en"
cookie %: THREW URIError URI error
cookie %zz: THREW URIError URI error
cookie %E0%A4%A: THREW URIError URI error
localeFromRequest proto docs path: function function Object() { [native code] }
localeFromRequest bad cookie THREW URIError URI error
```

Code:

- `language.ts:188-195` — `fromDocsPathname`: `if (!(value in DOCS_LOCALE)) return null; return DOCS_LOCALE[value …]`. `DOCS_LOCALE` (language.ts:116) is a plain object literal, so `"constructor" in DOCS_LOCALE` and `"__proto__" in DOCS_LOCALE` are `true` via inheritance. (All-lowercase prototype names are the reachable ones: the segment is lowercased first, so `toString`/`hasOwnProperty` become `tostring`/`hasownproperty` and miss.)
- `language.ts:303-314` — `localeFromCookieHeader`: `return parseLocale(decodeURIComponent(raw))` with no try/catch. Compare `packages/web/src/i18n/locales.ts` `parse()`, which wraps `decodeURIComponent` in try/catch and returns `null`.
- Hot path: `localeFromRequest` is called per request from `entry-server.tsx:13` (SSR), `lib/stats-proxy.ts:16`, `lib/enterprise.ts:98`, `routes/docs/index.ts:10`, `routes/docs/[...path].ts:15`, `routes/s/[id].ts:10`; `localeFromCookieHeader` also from `routes/t/[...path].tsx:12` and client-side `context/language.tsx:28`. None of the call sites catch.
- Downstream of the prototype escape: `tag(locale)` (`language.ts:221-223`, `TAG[locale]`) and `i18n(locale)` receive a function/object, yielding `undefined`/garbage language tags instead of the `en` fallback — the #851 failure shape, in the console tree.

Dedup: #851 covered `packages/web` only; #1309/#1316 covered Accept-Language q-values in this same file's sibling function. No open or closed issue covers `fromDocsPathname`, `DOCS_LOCALE`, or the cookie decode.

## Why it matters

- A single crafted link (`/docs/constructor/…`) makes locale resolution return a function as the locale for that request — garbage `accept-language` tags forwarded by the docs/share proxies and broken i18n lookups, instead of a clean fallback.
- A malformed `oc_locale` cookie (corrupted, hand-edited, or set by another app on the domain — the app itself sets it for a year) turns every console page load for that visitor into an unhandled `URIError` until the cookie is cleared.

## Acceptance criteria

- `fromDocsPathname` uses an own-property check (`Object.hasOwn`) so `constructor`/`__proto__` segments return `null`; legitimate segments (`de`, `en`, `pt-br`, …) unchanged.
- `localeFromCookieHeader` returns `null` (no throw) for malformed percent-encoded cookie values, falling back to Accept-Language / `en` via `localeFromRequest`.
- Regression tests in `packages/console/app/src/lib/language.test.ts` cover both: prototype-named docs segments and malformed cookie values, plus the existing controls.
- `bun test src/lib/language.test.ts` (console app) passes.

## Summary

The config docs teach only the deprecated flat routing keys. Since #1140 (PR #1311, merged 2026-11-01) the canonical shape is `experimental.routes.*` and every flat `model_route*` key is annotated deprecated in the schema — but `packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx` never mentions the nested shape, and its key list is incomplete even for the flat family.

## Evidence (main 305000712d)

- `packages/schema/src/config/experimental.ts:65-67` — `routes` is annotated: "Routing config in its canonical nested shape: model routes, provider routes, windows, schedules, tuning, log and settings. The flat model_routes / provider_routes / model_route_* keys below are deprecated spellings of these keys and normalize into them."
- `packages/schema/src/config/experimental.ts:69-96` — each flat key is annotated "Deprecated: use experimental.routes.models / .providers / .schedules / .windows / .tuning / .log / .settings" (seven flat keys: `model_routes`, `provider_routes`, `model_route_schedules`, `model_route_windows`, `model_route_tuning`, `model_route_log`, `model_route_settings`).
- `packages/core/src/config/normalize.ts:502-507` — "the canonical shape is `experimental.routes.*`; the flat … keys are the deprecated spellings … when both spellings name the same key, the nested value wins and the conflict is diagnosed, per key."
- `packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx:580` — "Use the `model_route*` options under `experimental` to define named routes…" — the nested shape is not mentioned anywhere in the section (or the page).
- `packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx:582-588` — "This family has five keys" lists only `model_routes`, `model_route_windows`, `model_route_schedules`, `model_route_tuning`, `model_route_log`. It omits `provider_routes` and `model_route_settings` entirely, so two live config keys (and their nested forms `routes.providers` / `routes.settings`) are undiscoverable from the docs.
- Every example in the section (config.mdx:594, 617, 650, 681, 703, 732, 755, 777) uses the deprecated flat spellings.

Dedup: #866 (closed) documented the flat family before the nesting existed; #1140 (closed) changed schema/core only and included no docs update. No open issue covers documenting the nested shape.

## Why it matters

Users copying the docs write config in spellings the schema itself calls deprecated, and cannot discover `provider_routes` / `model_route_settings` or the nested-wins precedence rule at all. The routing family is this fork's headline feature; its docs should teach the canonical shape.

## Acceptance criteria

- The Model routes section of `packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx` presents `experimental.routes` as the canonical shape, with at least one full nested example covering models, providers, windows, schedules, tuning, log and settings.
- The flat keys are documented as deprecated-but-accepted spellings that normalize into the nested shape, including the per-key rule that the nested value wins on conflict (with a diagnostic).
- The key list is complete: all seven keys, including `provider_routes` and `model_route_settings`.
- `bun run script/check-doc-env-vars.ts` still passes; English page only (locale trees follow the docs-locale-sync flow).

body:
# fix(plugin-github): comment update/delete guard reads the mutation tables through the prototype chain — a server-supplied __typename of "__proto__"/"constructor" passes as a comment type

## Summary

In the GitHub plugin's comment-update tool, the node type returned by the GitHub API decides which edit/delete GraphQL mutation runs. The lookup is a bare bracket read on two plain-object tables, so it walks the prototype chain: the guard that is supposed to reject non-comment node types accepts any `__typename` that names an inherited `Object.prototype` member (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, `valueOf`, …) and proceeds — past authorization — to call the GraphQL client with a non-string "mutation" (an object or a function). This is the prototype-chain read class the repo audited in #833 and built `check:proto-reads` / `ownValue`/`ownOr` / `Object.hasOwn` guards against — but that gate scans only `packages/core/src` (its proposed extension in #919 covers `packages/ai` only), so this package's server-data reads are outside the net.

## Evidence (main 9c99d58ace)

- `packages/plugin-github/src/issue.ts:224-235` — `commentNode` fetches the node with `NODE_TYPE_QUERY` from the configured GitHub host (github.com or a GHES host, `packages/plugin-github/src/client.ts:314-327`); `node.__typename` is server response data, typed as a plain string in `CommentNode`.
- `packages/plugin-github/src/issue.ts:238-250` — `EDIT_MUTATIONS` / `DELETE_MUTATIONS` are plain object literals (`Record<string, string>`) with exactly three own keys: `IssueComment`, `DiscussionComment`, `PullRequestReviewComment`.
- `packages/plugin-github/src/issue.ts:681-685`:
  ```ts
  const edit = EDIT_MUTATIONS[node.__typename]
  const remove = DELETE_MUTATIONS[node.__typename]
  if (!edit || !remove)
    return yield* new GitHubClient.Error({ kind: "validation", message: `${input.id} is a ${node.__typename}, not a comment this tool can change.` })
  ```
  For a prototype-named type both reads return inherited truthy values, the validation error never fires, authorization runs (`GitHubShared.authorize(..., "comment_update", ...)`), and then `api.graphql(remove, …)` (:688) or `api.graphql(edit, …)` (:691) is called with the inherited object/function as the query.
- Downstream, `packages/plugin-github/src/client.ts:231-233` passes the value to `isMutation(query)` (:344, a regex `.test`, which string-coerces an object to `"[object Object]"` → treated as an idempotent read) and serializes it as the JSON `query` field — `Object.prototype` serializes to `{}`, a function is dropped entirely — so the host gets a garbage GraphQL POST and the user gets a confusing server/GraphQL error instead of the designed validation message.

## Reproduction (laptop probe, this run)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-plugin-github-proto/proto.ts` recreates the two tables verbatim and runs the exact guard expression:

- `IssueComment` → accepted, edit/remove are strings (correct).
- `Repository` (a genuine non-comment type) → rejected, both reads `undefined` (correct).
- `__proto__` → **accepted**, `typeof edit === "object"`; `constructor`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, `valueOf` → **accepted**, `typeof edit === "function"`. In every one of these cases the code proceeds to `api.graphql(<non-string>, …)`.
- Control with the repo's blessed guard (`Object.hasOwn`, as used at `packages/ai/src/utils/media-type.ts:53`): all prototype names correctly report `false`, `IssueComment` reports `true`.

## Why it matters

The `__typename` is data from a remote server the plugin does not control (any configured GHES host, a compromised or buggy endpoint, or a future GitHub type that collides with a prototype name). The check at :683 is the only thing standing between that data and an authorized write operation; a read that can be satisfied by the prototype chain makes the check answer a different question than it asks — the exact failure mode of the #833 class. Today the blast radius is a bogus API call and a misleading error after an unnecessary authorization prompt, but the same shape in a table whose values are invoked or spread would be worse, and nothing in CI watches this package for the class.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The mutation-table reads at `packages/plugin-github/src/issue.ts:681-682` only resolve own properties (e.g. `Object.hasOwn` guards, matching the pattern at `packages/ai/src/utils/media-type.ts:53`, or an equivalent own-key helper), so a `__typename` of `__proto__`/`constructor`/`toString`/`hasOwnProperty`/`valueOf` produces the existing validation error (`… is a <type>, not a comment this tool can change.`) and no GraphQL call is made.
- [ ] A regression test in `packages/plugin-github/test/issue.test.ts` (fixture harness already covers comment update with a `DiscussionComment` node) drives comment update/delete against a node whose `__typename` is a prototype name and asserts the validation error and that no mutation request was sent; the three real comment types still edit/delete as before.
- [ ] The other server-data table reads in the same package found during the fix are dispositioned (guarded, or noted on this issue as safe with the reason — e.g. schema-validated literal-union tool inputs such as `DEFAULT_REPLY[response.reason]` are caller-typed, not server data; `MEDIA[path.extname(...)]` at explore.ts:1439 takes a local file path).
- [ ] `bun test` for `packages/plugin-github` passes and the package typechecks.

## Dedup

- `gh search issues 'proto-reads'` / the #833 follow-up set: the gate (`script/check-proto-reads.ts:37`) scans `packages/core/src` only; #912/#919 (open, via stale-pr #1301) propose adding `packages/ai/src` and disposition its hits — neither mentions `packages/plugin-github` or `__typename`.
- `gh search issues 'plugin-github prototype'` and `'__typename mutation'` → no matching open or closed issue.
- Cross-repo: the plugin exists only in developing-today/opencode; no SET-REMAINDER owed to the other repos.

# fix(ci): check:numeric-boundaries does not scan packages/plugin-github — GitHub API header and Copilot-text conversions escape the regression net

## Summary

`script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` (design #992 phase 3, gate #995) requires every bare `Number(...)` / `parseInt(...)` / `parseFloat(...)` conversion in its scan roots to carry an allowlist disposition, so a new bare conversion on externally supplied input fails CI until a human dispositions it. The gate has been extended root-by-root to every network-boundary surface — `packages/server` (#1294), console + function (#1302), services workers (#1308) — but one network-boundary package is still outside: `packages/plugin-github`, the GitHub API client / Copilot review-loop plugin. It is already in scope for the sibling bounded-http gate (`script/check-bounded-http.ts:74` lists `packages/plugin-github/src`), so its exclusion from the numeric gate is an inconsistency, not a stated decision. Its bare conversions run on GitHub API response headers, Link-header pagination URLs, and parsed Copilot review text.

## Evidence (main 9c99d58ace, gate patterns P-A/P-B/P-C applied to the unscanned root)

`script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts:49-60`: SCAN_ROOTS lists 10 roots (core, ai, cli, server, console/app, console/function, function, services/changelog, services/files, services/update) — no `packages/plugin-github/src`.

17 hits in `packages/plugin-github/src`, none dispositioned in `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt` (grep count for the package there: 0). All spot-read this run:

Upstream GitHub API response headers (server-supplied, the exact class dispositioned for console in #1302):
- `packages/plugin-github/src/client.ts:415` — `Number(input.headers["x-ratelimit-reset"])` in the rate-limit error path; spot-read: guarded at use by `Number.isFinite(reset) && reset > 0` (:418-420), undispositioned.
- `packages/plugin-github/src/client.ts:416` — `Number(input.headers["retry-after"])`; same isFinite/>0 guard at use. Note the core route executor parses Retry-After with a strict `1*DIGIT` grammar (`packages/ai/src/route/executor.ts:23`); an HTTP-date form here silently becomes NaN and falls through — probably acceptable for a hint string, but that is a disposition to record, not assume.
- `packages/plugin-github/src/client.ts:474` — `Number(response.headers["content-length"])` (declared download size); guarded at use by `Number.isFinite(declared) && declared > maxBytes` before the early-fail, undispositioned.

Upstream pagination Link header:
- `packages/plugin-github/src/review.ts:333` — `Number(new URL(last).searchParams.get("page"))` on GitHub's Link header URL; a missing `page` param gives `Number(null) = 0` and garbage gives NaN — both fall through the `page > 1` check today, undispositioned.

Copilot review text (untrusted reviewer output parsed by regex):
- `packages/plugin-github/src/copilot.ts:61` — `Number(generatedMatch[1])` where the regex admits `(\d+)` or `no` (the `no` branch is handled before the conversion).
- `packages/plugin-github/src/copilot.ts:119-120, 142-143, 159` — line/endLine/commentID from `(\d+)` regex captures in Copilot finding locations and `discussion_r(\d+)` links.
- `packages/plugin-github/src/copilot.ts:233` — the local `number()` helper (`Number(value)`), called at :58-59 on `(\d+)` captures for open/resolved finding counts.

Caller-supplied identifiers:
- `packages/plugin-github/src/review.ts:1912` — `Number(response.id.slice("alert:".length))`: the item ID comes from the tool caller and is NOT digit-guarded — `Number("abc")` is NaN and is interpolated into the `/code-scanning/alerts/${alertNumber}` API path. Benign (a 404-class API error) but it is the one hit in this set with no guard at the site; triage should disposition it explicitly or guard it.
- `packages/plugin-github/src/actions.ts:101, 107` and `packages/plugin-github/src/repo.ts:64, 68, 74` — run/job/PR numbers, all behind `/^\d+$/` tests or `(\d+)` regex captures (safe by construction, still needs the recorded disposition if the root is scanned).

## Why it matters

This is the same gap class as #1294/#1302/#1308, on the one remaining package that talks to an external API and parses untrusted text from it. The bounded-http gate already treats plugin-github as in-scope production surface; the numeric gate does not. Until it does, a new bare conversion on a GitHub header, a pagination URL, or Copilot output lands with no CI signal and no recorded disposition — and the one unguarded hit (review.ts:1912) shows the inventory is not purely theoretical.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SCAN_ROOTS` in `script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` covers `packages/plugin-github/src` (or a documented decision on this issue for deliberately excluding it, reconciling with its inclusion in check:bounded-http).
- [ ] Every one of the 17 hits is dispositioned in `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt` (converted through a #993 primitive, safe by construction with the reason, or inventoried baseline per design #992).
- [ ] The gate exits 0 on main and `script/check-numeric-boundaries.test.ts` covers the new root the way the #1294/#1302/#1308 changes covered theirs (the current test pins the exact SCAN_ROOTS list, so it must be updated deliberately).
- [ ] The unguarded `alert:` ID conversion at review.ts:1912 is either guarded in the same change or split out as a linked follow-up — not silently allowlisted without a note.

## Dedup

- `gh search issues 'check-numeric-boundaries'` → #992 (design, open), #995 (closed), #1294 (closed, server only), #1302 (closed, console+function), #1308 (closed, services). No open or closed issue covers `packages/plugin-github`.
- `gh search issues 'numeric plugin-github'` → no results.
- Cross-repo: the gate and this package exist only in developing-today/opencode; no SET-REMAINDER owed to the other repos.

body:
## Problem

The docs site's locale middleware serves a language the client explicitly refused with `q=0`, and a malformed `q` value poisons its sort — the exact bug class fixed for the console in #1309, in a second, unfixed copy of the same Accept-Language parsing logic.

## Evidence (main `07eab62f38`)

`packages/web/src/middleware.ts`, `localeFromAcceptLanguage` (lines 52–84):

- Line 66: `q: q ? Number.parseFloat(q) : 1` — no finiteness check, so `q=abc` becomes `NaN` and the comparator at line 73 (`b.q - a.q`) returns `NaN`, which sort treats as `0`: the refused/malformed entry keeps its original position instead of sorting last.
- Lines 76–80: the parsed items are mapped to locales and the first match is returned — there is no refusal skip, so an entry with an explicit finite `q=0` (or `q=0.0`, or negative) is still served if it is the first matching locale.
- Lines 86–97 (`onRequest`): the result drives a real user-visible redirect — a `/docs` or `/docs/` request is 302-redirected to `/docs/<locale>/` (with an `oc_locale` cookie) based on this function.

The console's copy was fixed in #1309 (PR #1312, merged): `packages/console/app/src/lib/language.ts` `detectFromAcceptLanguage` (lines 267–303) now treats a malformed `q` as 0-weight last-resort and an explicit finite `q<=0` as a refusal that is never served. The web middleware copy predates / escaped that fix.

### Reproduction (laptop probe, this run)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-web-accept-language/probe.ts` on the laptop runs the middleware's function verbatim (with `matchLocale` stubbed to the real mapping in `packages/web/src/i18n/locales.ts` for the tested tags):

| Accept-Language | Result | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `fr;q=0` | `fr` | `root` — fr was refused |
| `fr;q=0, de;q=0` | `fr` | `root` — both refused |
| `de;q=0.0, es;q=0` | `de` | `root` — both refused |
| `fr;q=0, de;q=0.5` | `de` | `de` (control, passes) |
| `fr` | `fr` | `fr` (control, passes) |
| `fr;q=abc, de;q=0.5` | `fr` | `de` (or fr only as last resort) — NaN must not poison the sort |

No test covers this function: `packages/web` has `src/i18n/locales.test.ts`, `src/lib/share-data.test.ts`, and `src/pages/s/_share-model-param.test.ts`, but nothing for the middleware's Accept-Language handling, and `localeFromAcceptLanguage` is not exported.

## Why it matters

`q=0` in Accept-Language means "not acceptable" (RFC 9110 §12.4.2). A user (or a crawler / privacy tool) that explicitly refuses a language is nonetheless redirected into that language's docs and handed a one-year `oc_locale` cookie pinning the refused choice. Browsers rarely send `q=0` for their top language, which is why this survives unnoticed — but the console copy was judged worth fixing in #1309, and the two copies disagreeing means the docs site's behavior depends on which surface a visitor hits.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An explicit finite `q<=0` language is never served by `localeFromAcceptLanguage`: parsing falls through to the next accepted language, or to `root` (no redirect) when none is accepted.
- [ ] A malformed `q` value is treated as a 0-weight last-resort offer (mirroring #1309's pinned console semantics), never as `NaN` in the sort comparator.
- [ ] Normal headers behave exactly as before (controls: bare language defaults to `q=1`; higher-`q` accepted language wins).
- [ ] Tests cover the refused, all-refused, malformed-`q`, and control cases and pass in the `packages/web` test suite (export the helper or extract it the way `packages/web/src/pages/s/_share-model-param.test.ts` isolates its logic, if the Astro middleware import blocks direct testing).

## Related

- #1309 — the console fix this mirrors (`detectFromAcceptLanguage`, `packages/console/app/src/lib/language.ts`)
- #1302 — malformed-`q` NaN-poisoning disposition for the console/function packages

body:
## Finding (from a PR review comment, never addressed)

The main-broken race-loser reconcile in `.github/workflows/main-broken.yml` does not preserve inherited run links when reconciliation happens in stages.

Reviewer **chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]** (Codex, P2) on PR #1046, 2026-10-31T02:04:44Z, at `.github/workflows/main-broken.yml:261`:
https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1046#discussion_r4429914877

> "Preserve inherited run links when reconciling a former survivor. With three concurrent watchers for the same Breakage-ID, one reconciliation can close #12 into #11 while the lower-numbered #10 is still awaiting its label step. Once #10 is labeled, its reconciliation sees only #10 and #11, closes #11, and copies only the first run URL from #11's body. The run from #12 exists only in #11's reconciliation comments, so it never reaches the final survivor #10, even though all watchers succeed. Reading only the body therefore breaks the promised preservation of every run link when reconciliation happens in stages. Preserve inherited run links from previous reconciliation comments as well before closing a former survivor."

(Issue numbers #10/#11/#12 in the quote are the reviewer's example.)

## No-response evidence

- PR #1046 is MERGED, and the inline thread contains only the Codex comment — no reply from the author or any maintainer (verified via the REST review-comments list and a GraphQL `reviewThreads` read: one thread, `isResolved: false`, one comment).
- No fix followed it: the merged reconcile is the version that reads only the loser body (see below).

## Still live on current main

Verified 2026-11-01 against `origin/main` (`3ea95031d05786f5423348af72f287b3cb656b1f`), `.github/workflows/main-broken.yml`:

- The reconcile loop derives the loser run solely from the loser issue's body: `LOSER_BODY=$(gh issue view "$LOSER" ... --json body)` then `LOSER_RUN=$(printf '%s' "$LOSER_BODY" | grep -o 'https://github.com/[^ ]*/actions/runs/[0-9]*' | head -1)`.
- The comment it posts on the survivor carries only that single `LOSER_RUN` plus the reconciling run — so a run link that a previous reconcile left in a comment on the loser (not its body) is dropped when that loser is itself closed into an earlier survivor.
- Dedupe: searched open and closed issues for "former survivor", "inherited run links", "reconciliation comments", "main-broken reconcile", and PR #1046. The only match is the origin issue #1037 (closed; it tracked the unserialized lookup-then-create problem, not this run-link preservation gap). No issue covers this finding.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When closing a loser, the reconcile collects run links from the loser's body AND from its prior reconcile comments (agent-note:v1 reconcile comments), and forwards every distinct run link to the survivor.
- [ ] A staged three-watcher scenario (A closed into B, then B closed into C) leaves every run link on the final survivor — pinned by a test or a scripted fixture of the reconcile step.
- [ ] Or: a documented decision on this issue recording that staged-reconcile run-link loss is accepted, with the reasoning.

Found by the pr-comment-review job: unaddressed PR review comment, PR #1046.

body:
# fix(console): detectFromAcceptLanguage serves a language the client explicitly refused with q=0

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode, 2026-11-01.

## Evidence (main 5a74a72f31, verified by code read this run)

`packages/console/app/src/lib/language.ts:266-297` — `detectFromAcceptLanguage(header)`:

1. Parses each `Accept-Language` item's `q` value (default 1; malformed → 0, per the #1302 fix at :280-285).
2. Sorts items by descending `q` (:288).
3. Returns the first item whose language `match()`es a known locale (:291-295).

The loop never excludes `q=0` items. Per RFC 9110 §12.4.2, `q=0` means "not acceptable" — the client is explicitly refusing that language. Consequences on current main:

- `Accept-Language: fr;q=0` → items `[{fr, 0}]` → returns `"fr"`. The one language the client refused is the one served.
- `Accept-Language: fr;q=0, de;q=0` → returns `"fr"` (sort is stable, both 0) instead of the `"en"` fallback.
- A negative q (`fr;q=-1`, `Number.parseFloat` → -1, finite) is likewise only sorted last, still served when it is the sole match.

The sibling parser in the same app gets this right: `prefersMarkdown` in `packages/console/app/src/lib/content-negotiation.ts:16` requires `markdown > 0`, so a `text/markdown;q=0` refusal is honored there.

The existing tests (`packages/console/app/src/lib/language.test.ts`) cover highest-q selection and the malformed-q NaN case from #1302, but no `q=0` case.

## Why it matters

Locale detection runs on console requests (`localeFromRequest`, language.ts:324). A client — browser language settings can produce explicit `q=0` entries, and API/headless clients commonly send a single refused or low tag — can be served a UI language it explicitly marked not acceptable, with no fallback to the site default. It is also a correctness inconsistency between the app's two content-negotiation parsers.

## Acceptance criteria

- `detectFromAcceptLanguage` never returns a locale whose item has `q <= 0`; such items are treated as absent (the same treatment malformed-q already effectively gets when a positive-q alternative exists).
- If every offered language is refused or unmatched, the existing `"en"` fallback is returned.
- New tests in `packages/console/app/src/lib/language.test.ts`: sole refused language (`fr;q=0` → `"en"`), refused + acceptable mix (`fr;q=0, de;q=0.5` → `"de"`), and the all-refused case.
- Existing language/content-negotiation tests still pass.

# fix(ci): check:numeric-boundaries does not scan services/* — the public Cloudflare workers' client/upstream conversions escape the regression net

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode, 2026-11-01. Sibling of #1294 (packages/server, closed/fixed) and #1302 (console + function packages, closed/fixed) — same gate, next unscanned production surface.

## Evidence (main 5a74a72f31, verified this run)

`script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts:47-55` — `SCAN_ROOTS` is exactly:

```
packages/core/src, packages/ai/src, packages/cli/src, packages/server/src,
packages/console/app/src, packages/console/function/src, packages/function/src
```

No `services/*` root is scanned. The bounded-http gate (#1256) was extended to `services/*/src` for exactly this reason — deployed production code — but the numeric gate never got the same extension.

The services are public production workers, not local tooling (the bounded-http gate's stated reason for excluding root `script/` does not apply):

- `services/files/wrangler.jsonc:11,16` — routes `opencode.ai/files/*` (public file serving)
- `services/update/wrangler.jsonc:15-25` — routes `update.opencode.ai`, `opencode.ai/update*`
- `services/changelog/src/index.ts` — serves the changelog, fetching an upstream `SOURCE_URL`

Gate-pattern hits (`\bNumber\(`, `\bparseInt\(`, `\bparseFloat\(`) in the unscanned service trees — 6 total, every one spot-read this run, all currently guarded at the site but none dispositioned in any allowlist, so a future unguarded conversion in these trees fails nothing:

| Site | Input | Current guard |
|---|---|---|
| `services/files/src/index.ts:113` | client `Range` header (`bytes[1]`/`bytes[2]`) | regex `^bytes=(\d*)-(\d*)$` restricts to digits |
| `services/files/src/index.ts:114` | client `Range` header end | same regex + `Math.min(..., object.size - 1)` |
| `services/update/src/index.ts:270` | admin form field `duration_hours` | `Number.isFinite(duration)` + range checks at :274-278 |
| `services/update/src/index.ts:307` | query string `?page=` | `Number.isSafeInteger(requestedPage) && requestedPage > 0` at :308 |
| `services/changelog/src/index.ts:32` | upstream `Content-Length` header | `Number.isFinite(declared)` check before use |
| `services/changelog/src/index.ts:87` | own cached `FETCHED_AT` header | subtraction result compared against freshness window; NaN would make the comparison false (stale copy served until cache expiry — worth an explicit disposition) |

## Why it matters

#1294 and #1302 established the pattern: each production surface that parses client- or upstream-supplied numbers gets scanned, and every existing hit gets an explicit disposition so the *next* bare conversion is caught by CI instead of by an incident. The services are the remaining unscanned production surface — the files worker parses a client-supplied `Range` header on a public route, which is precisely the class this gate exists for (#992).

## Acceptance criteria

- `SCAN_ROOTS` in `script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` includes `services/changelog/src`, `services/files/src`, `services/update/src` (and `services/www/src` if it gains `.ts` sources — it currently has none matching).
- Every hit in the new roots is dispositioned in `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt` (guarded-at-the-site with the reason, as in the table above), or converted through the #993 primitives where a disposition shows the guard is insufficient.
- `script/check-numeric-boundaries.test.ts` covers the services roots the way the #1302 change covered console/function (collected roots actually scanned).
- `bun run check:numeric-boundaries` (or the script directly) exits 0 on main after the change, with no stale allowlist entries.

body:
## Finding

The SSH bootstrap fallback download (packages/gui-extensions/src/ssh/bootstrap.ts, from PR #1011) bounds its download with `ARCHIVE_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT = "180 seconds"` twice in sequence — once on the request, once on the body read — so the effective worst case is ~360 seconds, not the single 180-second bound the code states.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1011 "fix(gui-extensions): bound SSH bootstrap fallback download (size cap + timeout)", merged, merge commit 3247ec70fe99475216cc0e069aafbca5f0186748 (final head bcb43825f6).
- bootstrap.ts:65-66 on current main afb79448bd2b0027d739ae0ba1aed0905340e6f2: `// Comparable to the primary path's curl --max-time 180 bound.` / `export const ARCHIVE_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT = "180 seconds"`.
- bootstrap.ts:181: the fallback's `http.get(url)` is wrapped in `Effect.timeout(ARCHIVE_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT)` — this bounds only the phase that produces the response (headers).
- bootstrap.ts:191-192: `collectArchive(response)` is then wrapped in a second, fresh `Effect.timeout(ARCHIVE_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT)` for the body phase. The two budgets are sequential and additive: a server that answers headers at ~179s and then slow-drips the body gets a further ~180s.
- Contrast: the primary path's bound really is a total — remote-cli.ts:127 `curl --max-time 180` caps the whole transfer. The fallback therefore does not deliver the "comparable" bound its comment promises.
- No test pins any timeout for this download: PR #1011's new tests in bootstrap.test.ts cover collectArchive's size cap (declared-length and in-flight) only.

## Why it matters

The fallback exists for when the primary install path has already failed; a hostile or broken mirror can hold a desktop bootstrap at the "uploading" stage roughly twice as long as the documented bound before the download is abandoned. The size cap (256 MiB) is unaffected — this is a duration-bound composition defect, not an unbounded read.

## Acceptance criteria

- One overall deadline covers the fallback download end to end (request + body), comparable to the primary path's `--max-time 180` total, OR the constant/comment is corrected to state honestly that the bound is per-phase (~360s worst case) with the reasoning recorded.
- A regression test pins the chosen semantics with a stalled/slow body (e.g. headers arrive promptly, body stalls: the download fails at the single stated deadline, not at deadline × 2).
- Existing bootstrap tests stay green; the 256 MiB size cap behaviour is unchanged.

Dedupe: #1006 (closed) was the origin issue for the size cap + a timeout; it did not cover the two budgets composing. #1091 (open) covers a different download (desktop extension archive manager). #1281 (closed) covered the primary path's missing size cap, not this duration composition.

body:
# fix(ci): check:numeric-boundaries still misses the console and function packages — client- and upstream-supplied conversions escape the regression net

## Summary

`script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` (design #992 phase 3, gate #995) requires every bare `Number(...)` / `parseInt(...)` / `parseFloat(...)` conversion in its scan roots to carry an allowlist disposition, so a new bare conversion on externally supplied input fails CI until a human dispositions it. #1294 extended the net to `packages/server/src` ("the network-boundary package", fixed by PR #1297). Two more network-boundary trees are still outside the net: the console web app (public API routes, webhooks, download proxy, GitHub/stats/account integrations) and the function package (API + Discord relay). Their bare conversions on client- and upstream-supplied strings are invisible to the gate today.

## Evidence (main 5882947330, gate patterns P-A/P-B/P-C applied to the unscanned roots)

`script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts:44`:

```ts
export const SCAN_ROOTS: string[] = ["packages/core/src", "packages/ai/src", "packages/cli/src", "packages/server/src"]
```

11 hits in the unscanned roots, none dispositioned anywhere:

Client-supplied headers (raw request input):

- `packages/console/app/src/lib/content-negotiation.ts:8` — `Number(quality.slice(2))` on the client `Accept` header's `q=` value (shared by the console proxy and the stats app, per the file header). `q=abc` → `NaN`; the `markdown >= html` comparison then silently answers false.
- `packages/console/app/src/lib/language.ts:282` — `Number.parseFloat(q)` on the client `Accept-Language` header; a malformed `q` yields `NaN`, which poisons the `.sort((a, b) => b.q - a.q)` comparator (NaN comparisons make ordering unspecified).

Webhook / event payloads:

- `packages/console/app/src/routes/honeycomb/webhook.ts:50` — `Number(item.result)` on the Honeycomb payload (zod union `number | string`); spot-read: the result is guarded by `Number.isFinite` at the use site, but nothing records that disposition.
- `packages/console/function/src/log-processor.ts:33` — `parseInt(event.event.request.headers["content-length"] ?? "0")` on a CloudFront event header; a non-numeric value records `NaN` as `request_length` in the analytics record.

Upstream response headers (same declared-length shape dispositioned for server in #1297):

- `packages/console/app/src/lib/github.ts:14` — `Number(response.headers.get("content-length"))` (GitHub API response)
- `packages/console/app/src/lib/github.ts:79` — `Number.parseInt(linkHeader.match(/&page=(\d+)>; rel="last"/)?.at(1) ?? "0")` (GitHub Link pagination header)
- `packages/console/app/src/lib/stats-proxy.ts:106` — `Number(response.headers.get("content-length"))`
- `packages/console/app/src/lib/console-account.ts:23` — `Number(response.headers.get("content-length"))`
- `packages/console/app/src/routes/download/[channel]/[platform].ts:47` — `Number(response.headers.get("content-length"))`
- `packages/function/src/discord.ts:19` — `Number(response.headers.get("content-length"))`

Internal/UI (still needs a disposition entry if the root is scanned):

- `packages/console/app/src/component/spotlight.tsx:66` — `parseInt(m[1], 16)` ×3 on a regex-matched hex color.

## Why it matters

This is the exact gap class #1294 filed for server: the gate's purpose is that no bare conversion on external input exists without a recorded disposition. Console serves the public opencode.ai surface — its `Accept`/`Accept-Language` parsers run on every proxied request, and a malformed quality value currently degrades to silent `NaN` behavior instead of a deliberate answer. Each hit above is probably safe-by-construction or guarded (as all 7 server hits turned out to be), but "probably" is what the allowlist exists to replace with a recorded disposition, and any *new* bare conversion in these trees currently lands with no CI signal at all.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SCAN_ROOTS` in `script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` covers `packages/console/app/src`, `packages/console/function/src`, and `packages/function/src` (or a documented decision on the issue for any root deliberately excluded, e.g. UI components).
- [ ] Every hit in the newly scanned roots is dispositioned in `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt` (converted through a #993 primitive, safe by construction with the reason, or inventoried baseline per design #992).
- [ ] The gate exits 0 on main and the gate's own tests (`script/check-numeric-boundaries.test.ts`) cover the new roots the way PR #1297 covered server.
- [ ] Any hit the triage judges a real bug (e.g. NaN handling in the header parsers) is either fixed in the same change or split out as a linked follow-up issue — not silently allowlisted.

## Dedup

- #1294 (closed, fixed by PR #1297) covered `packages/server/src` only; its body and PR do not mention console or function.
- `gh search issues 'numeric console'` → no results; `'check-numeric-boundaries'` → #992 (design, open), #995 (closed), #1294 (closed). No open issue covers these roots.
- Cross-repo: the gate and these packages exist only in developing-today/opencode; no SET-REMAINDER owed to the other repos.

title: fix(cli): plugin add/remove config temp files are not created exclusively (writeFile without the wx flag) — #1291 residual in the sibling writers

body:
## Finding

#1291 established that the CLI config writers must create their temp files exclusively (`writeFile` with the `wx` flag) — and filed it for `mcp add` only. The two sibling writers have the identical non-exclusive write, verified on current main.

Evidence (verified 2026-11-01 on main `f88ee5845b`):

- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/plugin/add.ts:80-82`:
  ```ts
  const temporary = destination + ".tmp-" + process.pid + "-" + randomUUID()
  await writeFile(temporary, updated.endsWith("\n") ? updated : updated + "\n", { mode })
  await rename(temporary, destination)
  ```
- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/plugin/remove.ts:72-74`: the same three lines (temp name at :72, `writeFile(..., { mode })` at :73, `rename` at :74).
- No `flag` is passed in either, so `writeFile` defaults to `"w"`: a file already present at the temp path is truncated, and the `mode` option is ignored for an existing file — the exact residual CodeRabbit raised and #1291 filed for `writeMcpConfig` (`packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/mcp/add.ts:82-83`).
- The plugin writers' own comment says they "Match the sibling mcp add writer" — they match its flawed half too. The one writer that already does this correctly is `uninstall.ts`, which opens its temp file with `flag: "wx"` (noted in #1291).

## Why it matters

These writers rewrite the user's global opencode config — the same file `mcp add` writes, which can hold remote-MCP Authorization headers and other provider configuration. If a world-readable file already exists at the generated temp path, the non-exclusive write truncates it and writes the config into it with its permissions unchanged, for the window until the rename — the exposure #1291 describes for `mcp add`. The unique temp name makes collision unlikely; exclusive creation is what makes it impossible, and it is the standard the repo has already adopted for the other writers.

Dedup (searched 2026-11-01): #1291 covers `writeMcpConfig` only; #1056 (closed) covered the plugin writers' shared `.tmp` name, symlink handling and mode widening — not exclusive creation. No open or closed issue covers `wx` for the plugin writers.

## Acceptance criteria

- The temp files in both plugin writers (`plugin/add.ts`, `plugin/remove.ts`) are created exclusively (e.g. `writeFile(..., { mode, flag: "wx" })`), so an existing file at the temp path causes a failure rather than being truncated; a regression test pins that a pre-existing file at the temp path is left byte-for-byte intact (mirroring #1291's acceptance for `mcp add`).
- The existing guarantees stay intact: realpath/symlink preservation, unique temp name, existing-config mode preservation (`existing.mode & 0o600`, fresh config `0o600`); existing CLI tests stay green.
- If #1291's fix lands first as a shared helper, use it here rather than duplicating the pattern a third time — and vice versa.
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why exclusive creation is not required given the unique temp name (the same escape hatch #1291 offers).

## Finding

`check:numeric-boundaries` — the regression net for bare string→number conversions (design #992, phase 3 in #995) — scans only three packages, and the one package that parses client-supplied strings for a living is not among them.

Evidence (verified 2026-11-01 on main `f88ee5845b`):

- `script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts:43`: `SCAN_ROOTS = ["packages/core/src", "packages/ai/src", "packages/cli/src"]` (header at lines 13–14 says the same). The gate is wired into CI at `.github/workflows/test.yml` (`bun run check:numeric-boundaries`).
- `packages/server/src` — the HTTP server — converts client-supplied values with bare `Number(...)` at exactly 7 sites (counted this run by replicating the gate's own `scanSource`: patterns `\bNumber\s*\(`, `\bparseInt\s*\(`, `\bparseFloat\s*\(`, comment-only lines skipped, `.ts`/`.tsx`):
  - `packages/server/src/auth.ts:50` — `Number(parts[0])`, the expiry field of a client-presented session token
  - `packages/server/src/event-feed.ts:89` — `Number(digits)`, the `Last-Event-ID` replay cursor
  - `packages/server/src/handlers/fs.ts:133,137,138` — `Number(match[...])` on the HTTP `Range` header
  - `packages/server/src/handlers/persistent-pty.ts:119` — `Number(url.searchParams.get("cursor") ?? "0")`, WebSocket connect query
  - `packages/server/src/handlers/pty.ts:172` — `Number(parsedCursor)`, same query parameter

## This is a net gap, not a live-bug claim

All 7 sites were spot-read this run and are currently guarded at the site (`Number.isSafeInteger` checks at `auth.ts:51`, `persistent-pty.ts:121`, `pty.ts:173–176`; `\d+`/`\d*` regex pre-validation at `event-feed.ts:88` and `fs.ts:130`). The problem is that none of them is dispositioned anywhere: the gate cannot see this package at all, so the *next* bare conversion added to the server — on an auth token, a cursor, or a range header — merges with no gate failure and no human disposition. That is exactly the failure mode #995 built the net to prevent in the packages it does scan.

Precedents for expanding a gate root-by-root: #1256 extended `check:bounded-http` to `services/*/src` for the same reason (merged in PR #1274), and PR #919 (open) extends `check:proto-reads` to `packages/ai`. For scale: the gate's patterns match 223 lines across all unscanned `src` roots (counted this run) — this issue deliberately scopes to `packages/server/src` (7 hits) as the network-boundary package; other roots are separate follow-ups if wanted, not part of this change.

Dedup: searched open/all issues for "numeric-boundaries" on 2026-11-01 — #992 (design, open), #995 (the net, closed); no issue covers the server root.

## Acceptance criteria

- `SCAN_ROOTS` in `script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` includes `packages/server/src`, and the header comment is updated to match.
- Every current server hit (7 at filing) is listed in `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt` with a per-site disposition naming its guard (e.g. safe by construction: `Number.isSafeInteger` check follows), or converted through a #993 primitive if a disposition finds one that is not actually guarded.
- A script test pins the server root's presence in `SCAN_ROOTS` (the #1256 services expansion added the equivalent traversal test for bounded-http), the script's tests pass, and `bun run check:numeric-boundaries` exits 0 on the result.
- No production behaviour changes unless a disposition uncovers an unguarded conversion; if one does, it is fixed or split out and linked here.

- Original comment: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/978#discussion_r4422916363 (`packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/mcp/add.ts:73` at review time)
- Residual follow-up: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/978#discussion_r4422993986
- No-response evidence: the follow-up is the last comment in the thread; GraphQL `reviewThreads` for PR #978 (checked 2026-11-01) shows the thread `isResolved=false`, and no reply or fix followed it. (The sibling findings on the same PR — symlink preservation, unique temp name, mode preservation — were all fixed in-thread; this residual was not.)
- Not already tracked: searched open/all issues for "writeMcpConfig" / "wx exclusive" / "exclusive temporary" / "mcp add temporary" on 2026-11-01 — #977 (parent, closed) and #1056 (plugin writers, closed) match on other writers; no issue covers exclusive creation in `writeMcpConfig`. Note the sibling writer in `uninstall.ts` already opens its temp file with `flag: "wx"` — `mcp add` is the inconsistent one.

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-01, main `ecc162deef`)

`writeMcpConfig` in `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/mcp/add.ts:82-84`:

```ts
const temporary = destination + ".tmp-" + process.pid + "-" + randomUUID()
await writeFile(temporary, applyEdits(text, edits), { mode })
await rename(temporary, destination)
```

No `flag` is passed, so `writeFile` defaults to `"w"`: if a file already exists at the generated path it is truncated (and `mode` is ignored for an existing file). Exclusive creation is not enforced, exactly as the reviewer flagged.

## Acceptance criteria

- The temp file in `writeMcpConfig` is created exclusively (e.g. `writeFile(..., { mode, flag: "wx" })`), so an existing file at the temp path causes a failure rather than being truncated; a regression test pins that a pre-existing file at the temp path is left byte-for-byte intact.
- The existing guarantees stay intact: realpath/symlink preservation, unique temp name, existing-config mode preservation (`existing.mode & 0o600`, fresh config `0o600`); existing CLI tests stay green.
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why exclusive creation is not required given the unique temp name.

body:
## Finding (from PR review, unaddressed)

On PR #990, CodeRabbit raised a Major that was never fixed and never replied to:

> **Preserve ownership before replacing the target.** — If uninstall runs with a different effective user or group from the shell file's owner, `fs.rename(temp, target)` installs the temporary file's ownership. `fs.chmod` restores only its mode. A privileged uninstall can therefore leave a user's shell file owned by root, even though the previous direct write retained ownership. Capture the target's owner and group, apply them to the temporary file before rename, and fail without replacing the target if ownership cannot be preserved. The linked issue explicitly requires preservation of ownership as well as permissions.
> — coderabbitai[bot], 2026-10-30T13:09:30Z

Evidence:
- PR: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/990 (merged)
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/990#discussion_r4423949311 (`packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/uninstall.ts:162` at review time)
- No-response evidence: the review thread has no replies at all (GraphQL `reviewThreads` for PR #990, checked 2026-11-01: the thread is `isResolved=false` with the finding as its only comment), and no commit after the comment addressed ownership — the later fixes on the PR covered only the temp file's exclusive creation and its creation mode.
- Not already tracked: the parent issue #988 ("uninstall rewrites shell config files in place") is CLOSED, but its acceptance criteria explicitly included "the file's existing permissions/ownership are preserved" — the ownership half was never implemented (see below), so no open issue covers this remainder. Searched open/all issues for "uninstall ownership" / "ownership shell config" / "chown" on 2026-11-01: only #988 matches.

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-01, main `ecc162deef`)

`writeShellConfig` in `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/uninstall.ts:155-184` still preserves only the mode:

- `fs.stat(target)` is mapped to `info.mode` only (line ~163-166) — uid/gid are never read.
- The temp file is opened exclusively (`flag: "wx", mode: 0o600`, line 176), chmodded to the target's mode (line 180), and renamed over the target (line 181). There is no `chown` anywhere in the file.

So a privileged uninstall (e.g. under `sudo`) still leaves the user's `.bashrc`/`.zshrc` owned by the effective user/group of the uninstall process, exactly as the reviewer flagged.

## Acceptance criteria

- The shell-config rewrite preserves the target file's ownership: capture the target's uid/gid and apply them to the temp file before the rename; if ownership cannot be preserved, fail without replacing the target.
- Existing behaviour is unchanged otherwise: symlink resolution, exclusive temp creation at `0o600`, and mode preservation all stay as they are, with regression coverage for the ownership case (e.g. a test that stubs a differing owner or at least pins the chown-before-rename call).
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why ownership preservation is not required.

body:
# fix(script): both regression-gate collectors build repo-relative paths with OS separators — the bounded-http services test fails on Windows CI and allowlist keys would never match there

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-01 on main `23b2e8e659`)

test.yml run 41311427708 on main head `23b2e8e659`: basic unit (windows)
failed exactly one test —

```
(fail) services scan roots (#1256) > collect walks a services tree on disk
       and reports hits under their repo-relative path
```

Root cause, `script/check-bounded-http.ts:177-183` (`collect`):

```ts
const path = join(dir, entry.name)
...
hits.push(...scanSource(path.slice(root.length + 1), readFileSync(path, "utf8")))
```

`join()` produces OS-native separators, so on Windows the "repo-relative"
path handed to `scanSource` is `services\www\src\pages\install.astro`,
while the test (check-bounded-http.test.ts:89) — and every allowlist key —
uses forward slashes. On a Windows run of the actual gate, every hit's file
key would mismatch its allowlist entry the same way: all hits unlisted, all
entries stale.

`script/check-proto-reads.ts:97-103` has the identical construction
(`path.slice(root.length + 1)` on a `join()` result). It has not failed CI
only because its test file has no on-disk `collect` test; the latent bug is
the same. (The real gates run Linux-only in CI — `if: runner.os == 'Linux'`
in test.yml — which is why this surfaces through the unit test instead.)

## Fix shape

Normalize the sliced relative path to POSIX separators in both collectors
(e.g. split on `sep` / replace `\\` with `/`, or compute it with
`relative()` + a posix join), and add an on-disk collect test to
`script/check-proto-reads.test.ts` mirroring the bounded-http one so both
collectors are pinned to emit `packages/core/src/...`-style keys.

## Why it matters

These two gates are the regression nets for the unbounded-HTTP (#1127) and
prototype-chain-read (#865) classes. Their allowlist keys are path-shaped;
a separator-mismatched key set silently turns the gate into noise on any
non-Linux runner — and the Windows unit-test job is red on main today
because of it, polluting the CI signal alongside the Linux gate failures.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `collect` in `script/check-bounded-http.ts` and
      `script/check-proto-reads.ts` emits forward-slash repo-relative paths
      regardless of platform separators.
- [ ] The failing Windows test "collect walks a services tree on disk…"
      passes (test.yml basic unit (windows) green for this file).
- [ ] `script/check-proto-reads.test.ts` gains an equivalent on-disk
      collect test.
- [ ] Linux gate behavior unchanged: `bun run check:bounded-http` and
      `bun run check:proto-reads` produce identical hit sets before/after
      (modulo separately-tracked allowlist dispositions).
