body:
# test(core): add a deterministic per-field guard that every config schema field survives normalization — the Arbitrary round-trip missed the provider_routes drop that reached production

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-01 on main `23b2e8e659`)

`packages/core/src/config/normalize.ts` rebuilds the config document key by
key (`normalizeExperimental` at line 461ff, the `nativeAtomic` table at
lines 218–232, and per-section helpers). A schema field that nobody adds to
the rebuild is **silently dropped** — no diagnostic, no error.

This exact omission has now bitten twice in the routing surface alone:

- `experimental.provider_routes` (added by #1134) was never added to
  `normalizeExperimental`; every normalized config silently lost its provider
  route groups. It reached production: on 2026-11-01, collapsing the GPT
  routes to a single provider route produced zero group decisions across
  ~40 minutes / 374 decisions, and the seats vanished with no candidate, no
  exclusion entry, and no warning (fix commit `5436247665`, PR #1277).
- `experimental.model_route_settings` (#1142) was dropped by the same
  omission; invisible only because its defaults equal the old hardcoded
  constants.

The existing guard did not catch either: `packages/core/test/config/normalization.test.ts`
has a property test, "preserves arbitrary JSON-round-tripped native
configuration" (line ~144), which runs `Arbitrary.schema(Info)` for only
100 runs. The schema is almost entirely optional and deeply nested, so a
given run rarely populates any specific field — and the test file's own
history proves the gap: the property test has existed since 2026-10-17
(commit `1fc489d878`), `provider_routes` entered the schema later (#1132),
and the drop still shipped. The regression tests added by #1277
(normalization.test.ts lines 960 and 992) pin those two fields by name —
the next new field gets no such protection unless someone remembers.

## Proposal

Add a deterministic guard test in
`packages/core/test/config/normalization.test.ts` (or a sibling file) that
enumerates the schema itself — e.g. `Object.keys(Config.Info.fields)` and
`Object.keys(ConfigExperimental.Info.fields)` — and, for **every** field,
asserts a normalization round-trip with that field populated by a minimal
schema-valid value (generated per-field via `Arbitrary` on the single field
schema, or a maintained minimal-fixture table keyed by field name, failing
loudly when a new field has no fixture). Fields with intentional transforms
(legacy migrations, `experimental.policies` → top-level `policies`,
`experimental.aliases` → top-level `aliases`, malformed-note filtering) are
asserted at their documented destination, reusing the existing
`withoutEmptyCompatibilityContainers` / `withoutMalformedNotes` adjustments
where they already encode the intent.

## Why it matters

Config normalization sits under every config read in the fork; its failure
mode is the worst kind — a user's setting silently does nothing. The routing
features are actively growing new experimental fields (#1132–#1142 in the
last weeks), so the hand-maintained rebuild list will keep drifting from
the schema until the schema itself drives the test.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test enumerates all `Config.Info` top-level fields and all
      `ConfigExperimental.Info` fields from the schema (not a hand-copied
      list) and asserts each survives `ConfigNormalize.normalize` +
      decode, at its documented destination for intentionally-moved fields.
- [ ] The test fails when run against a normalize.ts with one handled field
      deliberately removed (mutation-checked during development, e.g.
      against the pre-#1277 tree or a temporary local removal).
- [ ] Existing normalization tests still pass; the two #1277 per-field
      regression tests may stay or be subsumed.
- [ ] Runs in the normal `packages/core` test suite (no new CI wiring).

title: provider_routes: group never candidated after config collapse — GPT pair invisible past health-expiry under the group shape; explicit routes serve immediately (rollback evidence, #1134)
body:
## Summary

After the fleet config collapsed the three explicit ordered routes (`openai-plan-terra` / `openai-plan-sol` / `openai-plan-luna`) into a single `experimental.provider_routes` group — `"openai-plan": { providers: ["openai.alternate", "openai"], selection: "ordered" }` with seats `openai-plan/<model>` (developing-today/code commit `3f40508e`) — the group never appeared in any route decision: zero decisions with `route_id='openai-plan'`, zero mentions of `openai-plan` in the candidates/detail/chosen of any decision, and zero GPT attempts — including ~40 minutes during which both providers' health exclusions had already expired. Rolling back to the explicit routes restored candidacy within seconds, and the pair has served cleanly since. Server build in both shapes: `opencode-2.0.30+855ec25` (contains PR #1134 and PR #1142).

## Timeline (2026-11-01, America/Chicago; evidence from the route ledger `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` on the fleet laptop)

- 05:07:10 — `route_health`: `openai`/`gpt-6-luna` failure cooldown-starts (untils escalating to 05:39:10).
- 05:08:55 — `openai.alternate`/`gpt-6-luna` quota-gated (until 05:38:55) + cooldown-start (until 05:23:55).
- ~05:09–05:10 — collapse committed in developing-today/code (`3f40508e`).
- 05:11:53 — server restarted onto the `855ec25` build (pid 3535723) with the collapsed config live.
- 05:11:53–05:52:23 (collapsed config in force): 374 `luna-plan` decisions, candidating only `opencode-go/gpt-6-luna`; zero decisions with `route_id='openai-plan'`; zero decisions of any route mentioning `openai-plan` in candidates/detail/chosen; zero `route_attempt` rows for `openai` / `openai.alternate`. Both exclusions expired inside this window (alternate gate 05:38:55, main bench 05:39:10) with no change in candidacy.
- 05:52:23 — rollback restore written to the live config file (the still-running server hot-reloaded it; the same restore was committed and pushed in developing-today/code as `7e20d9757`).
- 05:53:37 — `route_health` rows 3626/3627: cooldown-end "expired" for both credentials; first `openai-plan-luna` decision since the collapse; 10 attempts on `openai.alternate`/`gpt-6-luna` within 19 s, all failure `QuotaExceeded` 429 "The usage limit has been reached" (attempt ids 57718–57727, route `workhorse`). No `openai` (main) attempts in that burst.
- ~05:58:35 — server restarted cleanly on the restored config (pid 207044, same `855ec25` build).
- 06:00:16–06:08:48 — 268 `openai-plan-luna` decisions; `luna-plan` candidacy included the nested route in 268/268 decisions; attempts: `openai.alternate` 3× `QuotaExceeded` at 06:00:17 (then quota-gated until 06:30:17 + cooldown-starts, health rows 3628–3631), `openai` (main) **257 successes** (06:00:18–06:08:38) + 2 Transport timeouts. 1,084 decisions total in the window.

## Discrimination result

The rollback was run as a controlled comparison: same server build, same accounts, same health state — only the config shape changed. Under the group shape the pair was invisible past health expiry; under the explicit shape it candidated immediately and serves (alternate correctly benched on genuine 429s, main carrying the traffic). Conclusion: the defect is in the provider-route group path, not in health state. The fleet remains on the explicit routes; the collapse is **not** being re-applied.

## Notes / scope

- Only the luna path was exercised by live traffic in these windows. However, terra-plan/sol-plan seat the group directly as `openai-plan/<model>`, and no decision of any route mentioned the group post-collapse — the invisibility is not specific to referencing the group through a nested route.
- Alternate's 429s are genuine (that account is at its usage limit) and are not part of this bug: under the explicit shape they bench correctly and traffic falls through to main.

## Hypothesis (unverified — for the investigator)

The group appears to contribute no candidates at decision time, as if group expansion yields an empty ready set regardless of member health — e.g., the group's ready-set computation consults health/quota state keyed differently than per concrete provider/model/credential, or group targets are dropped during route-target expansion before candidacy is recorded. The total absence from decision records (not even an "excluded" entry) suggests the group never reaches the candidacy stage at all.

## Ask

Investigate why an `experimental.provider_routes` group referenced as `openai-plan/<model>` produces zero candidacy, and add a regression test that would catch a provider-route group silently vanishing from route decisions. The fleet will re-attempt the collapse once a fix is deployed and verified.

# fix(ci): check:bounded-http gate is red on main — install.astro allowlist entry went stale when the #1246 fix changed the fetch line

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-01 on main `23b2e8e659`)

`bun run check:bounded-http` exits 1 on current main:

```
Unlisted bounded-http candidate at services/www/src/pages/install.astro:14:
  const response = await fetch("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opencode/dev/install", {
Stale allowlist entry (the line no longer matches a sweep pattern):
  services/www/src/pages/install.astro :: const response = await fetch("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opencode/dev/install")
```

The allowlist entry at `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt:207` still
carries the pre-fix line text and the disposition "tracked by #1246:
… no deadline". But #1246 is fixed and closed: PR #1273 (merge `c21982ea7d`)
rewrote the fetch in `services/www/src/pages/install.astro:14-16` as a
multi-line call carrying `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(INSTALL_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS)`
(`INSTALL_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`, line 12). The #1256 services-scan work
(PR #1274, merged `f8b8d52ae6`, issue closed) recorded the old single-line
shape, so the entry no longer matches the line it dispositions.

In CI the failure is currently masked: test.yml runs the proto-reads check
before the bounded-http check, and the proto-reads step is already failing on
main (separate issue), so the bounded-http step does not get to report. Run
locally, the gate is red on its own.

## Why it matters

The bounded-http gate (#1129, design #1127) is the regression net for the
unbounded outbound HTTP class. A stale entry plus an undispositioned hit
means the gate cannot go green even though the underlying fetch is now
correctly bounded — the net is down for every services/ and packages/ tree
it scans, and the "tracked by #1246" disposition now points at a closed
issue for a site that is in fact bounded at the site.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The `services/www/src/pages/install.astro` allowlist entry matches the
      current line text (ending `, {`) and its disposition reads
      bounded-at-the-site, naming `AbortSignal.timeout(INSTALL_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000)`
      and noting the body is streamed through via `response.body`, not buffered.
- [ ] `bun run check:bounded-http` exits 0 on the resulting tree.
- [ ] No change to `services/www/src/pages/install.astro` behavior.

title: fix(gui-extensions): primary SSH remote download (stageBinary) has no size cap — curl/wget bound time only, unlike the fallback's 256 MiB cap (#1011)

body:
## Finding (from PR diff review of #1011)

PR #1011 bounded the SSH bootstrap **fallback** download with `MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES = 256 MiB` and a 180-second timeout. Its own merged comment states the remaining gap plainly — and the gap is still live on current main:

`packages/gui-extensions/src/ssh/bootstrap.ts:60-64` (current main, verified 2026-11-01 via two independent `gh api` reads):

> Legitimate CLI archives are tens of megabytes, so this generous ceiling costs a normal install nothing; it stops a buggy or hostile mirror from making the desktop process buffer an archive without limit. **The primary remote path (remote-cli.ts stageBinary) caps only time (curl --max-time 180), never size, so the fallback needs its own bound.**

## Evidence — current main

`packages/gui-extensions/src/ssh/remote-cli.ts:120-128`, `stageBinary()` (the primary path: the remote host downloads the archive itself):

```sh
url=…
if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 180 "$url" -o "$stage/archive.tgz"
else
  wget -T 180 -O "$stage/archive.tgz" "$url"
fi
tar -xzf "$stage/archive.tgz" -C "$stage"
```

- Neither branch bounds the downloaded size: no `--max-filesize` (curl), no size guard at all (wget).
- The same archive, fetched by the fallback path in the same feature, is capped at 256 MiB (`MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES`, bootstrap.ts). The two paths disagree about the bound for the identical artifact.
- The #1006 fix packet (queue task 3913's predecessor triage) explicitly scoped the primary path out ("The primary remote-download path (curl --max-time 180) — unchanged"), so this is a known leftover, not a duplicate of #1006 (closed) or #923 (four different paths).

Dedupe (2026-11-01): `gh issue list --state all` searches for "stageBinary size", "remote-cli download cap", "max-filesize", and "SSH archive download" returned no issue covering the primary path's size bound. Open #1091 is the desktop extension-archive timeout — a different path.

## Why it matters

The 180-second time bound is not a size bound: on a fast link a buggy or hostile mirror (the URL host is the npm registry / mirror infrastructure, and redirects are followed with `-L`) can write many gigabytes into the remote host's staging directory within 180 s before `tar` ever runs — filling the remote disk of the very machine the user is bootstrapping. The fallback path was capped for exactly this class of risk; the primary path — the one used whenever the remote can download at all — was not.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `stageBinary`'s download enforces a stated size cap consistent with the fallback's `MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES` (256 MiB) for the same archive, on **both** the curl branch (e.g. `--max-filesize`) and the wget branch (wget has no `--max-filesize`; use an equivalent guard that fails before extraction — and if the guard can only check after download, say so in a comment and keep the staged file from being extracted when over cap).
- [ ] An over-cap download fails the install with a clear error and the staged archive is not extracted (`tar` never runs on it); the existing `trap 'rm -rf "$stage"' EXIT` cleanup still applies.
- [ ] Normal archives (tens of MB) install exactly as today on both branches.
- [ ] Tests pin the generated install script's size bound for both branches (following the existing `remote-cli` / `bootstrap.test.ts` conventions for script assertions).

Source: pr-diff-review of PR #1011 (merged, fixes #1006), finding verified against current main 2026-11-01.

body:
## Summary

The Node-build script downloads the Node.js archive and its `SHASUMS256.txt` with **no timeout on either fetch** — a stalled or slow-dripping nodejs.org (or mirror/proxy) hangs the Node build indefinitely. The archive body is also buffered whole via `response.arrayBuffer()` and the sums via `response.text()`, with no byte bound. Integrity is verified (SHA256, unlike the Bun path in #1159), but a verified download that never finishes still wedges the build.

## Evidence (verified on main `c21982ea7d`, 2026-11-01)

- `packages/cli/script/build-node.ts:207` — `const [response, sums] = await Promise.all([fetch(\`${base}/${filename}\`), fetch(\`${base}/SHASUMS256.txt\`)])`: neither fetch carries a `signal`/deadline.
- `packages/cli/script/build-node.ts:211` — `const data = new Uint8Array(await response.arrayBuffer())` buffers the whole archive; `:212` `(await sums.text())` reads the checksums unbounded.
- Real sizes measured 2026-11-01: `node-v26.4.0-linux-x64.tar.gz` Content-Length **61,519,918 bytes** (~59 MiB, buffered whole in memory by design of the current code); `SHASUMS256.txt` 2,943 bytes.
- This is the residual #1159 did not cover: #1159 cites this file (`build-node.ts:207-216`) only as the integrity *contrast* for the Bun download in `build.ts` — its acceptance criteria touch `build.ts` only, and nothing in it asks for a deadline here.
- Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-script-buildnode/probe.ts` (Bun, local servers, the `Promise.all([fetch(archive), fetch(sums)])` + `arrayBuffer()`/`text()` shape copied from `:207-212` with only the URLs pointed at localhost): stalled archive leg → **STILL-PENDING >6s** (the sums leg had already resolved; `Promise.all` never settles). Control with `AbortSignal.timeout(3000)` → **REJECTED TimeoutError after 3001ms**.
- The site sits outside the bounded-http gate's scan roots (`script/check-bounded-http.ts` SCAN_ROOTS cover `packages/*/src` only — cf. open #1256 for the same escape class under `services/`), so no regression net will catch a reversion or prompt the fix.

## Why it matters

`resolveTargetNode()` (build-node.ts:184) runs on the Node build path whenever a cross-target Node must be downloaded (cache miss / no `.verified` marker). A network stall there hangs the build with no error and no progress — the failure only surfaces as a CI job-timeout kill, indistinguishable from a slow compile. The repo's own pattern for download paths is a named deadline (e.g. updater `AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)`, models fetchers 3-5s, #1168's script fix at 30s).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both fetches at `build-node.ts:207` carry a named deadline constant sized for a ~59 MiB archive on a slow link (state the value and rationale at the site; a headers-only deadline plus a streaming/overall bound is acceptable if reasoned).
- [ ] The checksum comparison and `.verified` marker behavior are unchanged: a tampered or truncated archive still fails with `Checksum mismatch` before extraction.
- [ ] A scripted check covers: stalled archive leg rejects at the deadline instead of hanging; stalled sums leg likewise; a normal download still verifies and extracts.
- [ ] Consider dispositioning this script surface in the bounded-http allowlist (or in #1256's widened scan) so the deadline cannot silently regress.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues 2026-11-01 for `build-node`, Node-archive download and timeout terms: no filing covers a deadline for this download. #1159 (open) covers `build.ts`'s Bun archive integrity + timeout and cites this file only as the verified-integrity contrast; #1256 (open) covers `services/` escaping the bounded-http scan, not `packages/cli/script/`.

body:
## Summary

`@opencode/script` resolves the next release version at import time by fetching the npm registry's `latest` document with **no timeout and an unbounded `res.json()` read**. This module is imported by the build and publish scripts of ~20 packages, so a stalled or slow-dripping registry (or any proxy in front of it) hangs every latest-channel build/publish that reaches version resolution, indefinitely and with no error.

## Evidence (verified on main `c21982ea7d`, 2026-11-01)

- `packages/script/src/index.ts:41-46` — the `VERSION` top-level await: `fetch("https://registry.npmjs.org/@opencode%2fcli/latest")` with no `signal`, then `.then((res) => res.json())` — a direct unbounded body read. It runs whenever `OPENCODE_VERSION` is unset and the channel is not a preview (the normal latest-channel publish path).
- Blast radius: `grep` for `@opencode/script` importers hits `packages/{ai,cli,client,codemode,core,plugin,plugin-browser,plugin-github,protocol,schema,sdk,server,simulation,theme,ui,util}/script/publish.ts` plus `packages/cli/script/build.ts`, `build-node.ts`, `publish-aur.ts`, `publish-homebrew.ts` and `packages/desktop/scripts/prepare.ts` — version resolution is on the critical path of all of them.
- The bounded-http regression net already inventories this exact site as a remaining surface (`script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt`: `packages/script/src/index.ts :: const version = await fetch(...) :: no signal in the call options — unbounded outbound fetch, remaining surface under design #1127`, and the matching `return res.json()` entry), but no issue tracks fixing it — the allowlist is an inventory, not a fix. Sibling script surfaces got their own issues and fixes (#1168 models-snapshot script, #1159 release build downloads); this one has none.
- Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-script-buildnode/probe.ts` (Bun, local servers, fetch shape copied verbatim from `index.ts:41-46` with only the URL pointed at localhost): stall server (accepts, never responds) → **STILL-PENDING >6s**; drip server (headers + 1 byte/sec) → **STILL-PENDING >6s**; a 32 MiB streamed body was consumed whole before the JSON parse was even attempted. Control with `AbortSignal.timeout(3000)` on the identical shape → **REJECTED TimeoutError after 3008ms**.
- Real document size measured 2026-11-01: `GET https://registry.npmjs.org/@opencode%2fcli/latest` = **2,451 bytes** — a small cap loses nothing.

## Why it matters

Version resolution is a top-level await: when it hangs, the importing build/publish script hangs before doing any work, with no timeout error to diagnose — the same failure class the repo has been closing site-by-site under design #1127 (e.g. #1168, the models-snapshot script, fixed with a 30s deadline + 32 MiB cap). A publish pipeline stuck on a registry stall burns CI time until the job-level timeout kills it and gives no signal about which step died.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The registry fetch in `packages/script/src/index.ts` carries a named deadline constant (e.g. `AbortSignal.timeout`, precedent: 30s in `packages/core/script/update-models-snapshot.ts`) so a stalled/dripping registry fails fast with a clear error naming the version-resolution step.
- [ ] The body is read through a bounded reader with a named cap sized generously above the real ~2.5 KB document (precedent caps: 32 MiB in #1168; even 1 MiB is ~400x headroom) instead of direct `res.json()`.
- [ ] A scripted check or test covers: stall rejects at the deadline, oversized body fails the cap, and a normal `latest` document still resolves and bumps the version as today.
- [ ] The two `packages/script/src/index.ts` entries in `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` are updated to the bounded disposition.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues 2026-11-01 for `packages/script`, `Script.version`, npm-registry and version-fetch terms: no filing covers this site. #1168 is `packages/core/script/update-models-snapshot.ts`; #1159 is `packages/cli/script/build.ts`/`build-node.ts`; the #1127/#1129 design and gate inventory the site but track no fix for it.

body:
# fix(ci): check:bounded-http scans only packages/*/src — services/ outbound fetches escape the regression net entirely

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-01 on main `87af482138`)

- `script/check-bounded-http.ts` `SCAN_ROOTS` (lines ~57-91) lists 34 roots, every one of them `packages/<pkg>/src`. The repo's other production TypeScript/Astro trees are absent: `services/changelog/src`, `services/files/src`, `services/update/src`, `services/www/src` (and the root `script/` tree).
- Outbound fetch / body-read sites in `services/` today that the gate has never inventoried (grep `fetch(|.text()|.json()|.arrayBuffer()` over `services/*/src`, 2026-11-01):
  - `services/www/src/pages/install.astro:4` — `fetch("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opencode/dev/install")`, no signal at all (filed separately this run);
  - `services/changelog/src/index.ts:24,29` — fetch with a 5s signal but `response.text()` with no byte cap (filed separately this run);
  - `services/www/src/docs/layouts/DocsLayout.astro:106,108` — browser-side same-origin fetch + `response.text()` for copy-as-markdown (needs a disposition: browser/local read, not necessarily a fix);
  - `services/update/src/index.ts:425` — inbound `request.json()` (inbound read; needs a disposition, the gate's allowlist already has an inbound/local category);
  - `services/files/src/index.ts` / `services/update/src/index.ts:45` — worker `fetch` handlers (inbound, not outbound call sites).
- This is the same failure shape as #912 (check:proto-reads missing `packages/ai`): a gate that covers most of the tree reads as "the class is netted" while a whole subtree keeps producing the exact bugs the gate exists to catch — the bounded-http family has produced 60+ per-site issues, and the two `services/` sites above survived precisely because they were never scanned.

## Why it matters

The gate's allowlist is the fleet's inventory of remaining unbounded surfaces under design #1127. An inventory that silently omits a production subtree (public install route + public changelog worker) makes "gate green" mean less than everyone reading it thinks it means.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SCAN_ROOTS` (or an equivalent mechanism) covers the `services/*/src` trees, including `.astro` files (already a scanned extension for `packages/web`).
- [ ] Every new hit from the expanded scan is dispositioned in `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt`: bounded-at-the-site, inbound/local/browser read with the reason, or tracked by an issue (the two outbound sites filed this run are linked from their entries).
- [ ] `script/check-bounded-http.test.ts` gains a case proving a fetch in a `services/` tree is scanned (a fixture hit outside `packages/` fails the gate until dispositioned).
- [ ] The root `script/` tree is either added the same way or explicitly documented in the gate header as out of scope with the reason (maintainer-only tooling), so the boundary is a decision, not an accident.

body:
# fix(changelog): changelog worker refresh reads the upstream body unbounded — the 5s deadline bounds duration, not bytes

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-01 on main `87af482138`)

`services/changelog/src/index.ts:23-29` (`refresh()`):

```ts
const response = await fetch(SOURCE_URL, {
  headers: { "User-Agent": "opencode-changelog" },
  signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000),
}).catch(() => undefined)
if (!response?.ok) return
const markdown = await response.text()
```

- The fetch has a 5s deadline, but `response.text()` has **no byte cap**: the whole body is buffered into memory, then duplicated into the Workers Cache via `cache.put(new Response(markdown, …))` (`index.ts:30-39`).
- `refresh()` is on the request path whenever the colo cache is empty (`loadSource`, `index.ts:44-49`: `if (!cached) return refresh(cache)`), not only in background revalidation.
- Laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-services-fetch/probe.mjs`, Node, same fetch+`text()` shape vs a local fast endless body): the 5s signal fired on time (**REJECTED TimeoutError after 5020ms**) but the process RSS grew **+557 MB** inside that window — duration was bounded, bytes were not.
- The real `CHANGELOG.md` is small today; the bound being missing means a compromised/bloated upstream (the URL is a mutable `dev` branch on another org's repo) or a fast hostile mirror can OOM the worker on a cold cache.
- Outside the bounded-http regression net: `script/check-bounded-http.ts` `SCAN_ROOTS` covers only `packages/*/src` (companion gate-gap issue filed separately). Same duration-not-bytes pattern as #1158 (console CRM lookup).

## Why it matters

"Has a timeout" reads as bounded, but a deadline alone does not bound memory: at line rate, five seconds is hundreds of megabytes. The fix pattern is already settled in this repo — read through a bounded reader with a named cap sized to the real document (the changelog is markdown measured in KB–low MB).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `refresh()` reads the body through a bounded read with a named cap (e.g. `CHANGELOG_MAX_BYTES`) sized with headroom over the real `CHANGELOG.md`, refusing (and not caching) an over-cap body.
- [ ] Over-cap / endless upstream → refresh returns without caching, and a cold-cache request still settles as the existing 503 error page rather than OOM/hang.
- [ ] A test or documented probe covers: normal changelog → cached and served; endless/oversized body → refused with bounded memory.
- [ ] The site is dispositioned in `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` once the gate covers `services/` — or noted as pending that gate extension.

# fix(www): /install proxy fetch has no deadline — a stalled upstream hangs the install-script route indefinitely

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-01 on main `87af482138`)

`services/www/src/pages/install.astro:4` (whole route, `prerender = false`, so this runs per request):

```ts
const response = await fetch("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opencode/dev/install")
```

- No `signal` / deadline of any kind on the fetch, and no status check before the upstream body is streamed back to the caller with the upstream status (`install.astro:5-12`).
- This is the route behind the public install script (the `curl …/install | bash` entry point): every request's lifetime is whatever raw.githubusercontent.com feels like doing that day.
- Laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-services-fetch/probe.mjs`, Node, replicating the exact fetch shape against a local server):
  - upstream that never sends headers → fetch **STILL-PENDING after 6s** (no bound at all — it would wait forever);
  - upstream that sends headers then drips 1 byte/sec → body read **STILL-PENDING after 6s**;
  - control: the same fetch with `AbortSignal.timeout(3000)` → **REJECTED TimeoutError**, as expected.
- The site is outside the bounded-http regression net: `script/check-bounded-http.ts` `SCAN_ROOTS` covers only `packages/*/src`, so this fetch was never inventoried (companion gate-gap issue filed separately).

## Why it matters

A stalled or slow-dripping GitHub raw endpoint turns into hung /install requests with no diagnostic — the first-run experience for new users — and each hung request holds a worker/render slot until the platform gives up on it. Every sibling proxy in this repo learned the deadline lesson already (console `/s` proxy, stats proxy, inference proxy #1186); this route is the same shape and was simply never in the inventory.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The install fetch carries a named-constant deadline (e.g. `AbortSignal.timeout(INSTALL_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS)`), sized for a small script fetch (seconds, not minutes).
- [ ] A stalled upstream settles as an error response (5xx) after the deadline instead of hanging; a healthy upstream is proxied unchanged (status, headers, streamed body).
- [ ] A test or documented probe covers: stall → deadline error; healthy upstream → body/status pass-through.
- [ ] The site is dispositioned in `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` (bounded-at-the-site) once the gate covers `services/` — or noted as pending that gate extension.

body:
## Problem

The `check:bounded-http` regression gate (#1129, design #1127 phase 3) is **red on current main**: its allowlist (`script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt`) drifted from the code when PR #1161 rewrote the `opencode api` fetch helpers for #1144 and added their tests. The gate runs in CI (`test.yml`: "Check bounded-http calls are dispositioned" → `bun run check:bounded-http`), so every main CI run currently fails this step and — worse — the net stops catching *new* unbounded calls while it is red.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `324b75e663`)

Re-ran the gate's exact scan logic (the two sweep patterns + occurrence-aware allowlist parsing from `script/check-bounded-http.ts`) over all 34 scan roots: **188 candidate hits, 7 unlisted, 4 stale entries** — the gate exits 1.

Unlisted hits (no allowlist disposition):

- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/api.ts:35` — `const response = await fetch(new URL("/openapi.json", endpoint.url), {`
- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/api.ts:40` — `return (await response.json()) as OpenApi`
- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/api.ts:56` — `const response = await fetch(new URL(request.path, endpoint.url), {`
- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/api.ts:62` — `const output = await response.text()`
- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/api.test.ts:64` and `:114` — `fetch() {` (the `Bun.serve` test-handler definitions for the stall tests)
- `packages/console/app/src/lib/aws.test.ts:45` — `body: await request.clone().text(),` (inside the test's mock `fetch` handler added by PR #1157 for #1143)

Stale entries (line no longer exists — all four are the pre-#1161 `api.ts` lines):

- `api.ts :: fetch(new URL(request.path, endpoint.url), {`
- `api.ts :: const output = yield* Effect.promise(() => response.text())`
- `api.ts :: const response = await fetch(new URL("/openapi.json", endpoint.url), { headers: Service.headers(endpoint) })`
- `api.ts :: return resolveOperation((await response.json()) as OpenApi, input[0], params)`

Cause: PR #1161 (merged, fixes #1144) extracted `fetchOpenApi` (`api.ts:32-45`, `OPENAPI_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`) and `fetchApi` (`api.ts:47-71`, `API_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 600_000`), both composing `AbortSignal.timeout(...)` into the fetch and covering the body read under the same deadline (file comments `api.ts:18-29`), without updating the allowlist. The same drift event's `console-account.ts` entry was repaired in PR #1162; the `api.ts` / `api.test.ts` / `aws.test.ts` families were missed. This drift was first recorded as an unfiled FINDING by a queue lane (task 5022) — this issue is that filing.

Dedup: searches for `bounded-http allowlist` / `allowlist drift` return only #1129 (the gate itself, closed) and the per-site fetch issues; no open or closed issue covers the current red gate. Open PR #989 ("stream opencode api response body") also touches `api.ts` — if it lands first, re-run the gate and disposition its final lines instead; the two changes must not both rewrite the same allowlist entries blind.

## Why it matters

A red regression net is worse than no net: CI signal for the whole bounded-by-default contract (#1127) is lost, real new unbounded calls hide in the noise, and contributors learn to ignore the step. The underlying production code is already bounded (#1144) — this is purely the inventory failing to keep up with two merged fixes, exactly the rot the gate's stale-entry check exists to catch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bun run check:bounded-http` exits 0 on main; `bun test script/check-bounded-http.test.ts` still passes.
- [ ] The 4 stale `api.ts` entries are replaced with dispositions for the current lines that name the actual bound (`fetchOpenApi`: `AbortSignal.timeout(OPENAPI_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS)`; `fetchApi`: `AbortSignal.timeout(API_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS)`, one deadline covering fetch + body read per `api.ts:18-29`) — body-read entries worded honestly about time-bound vs byte-cap.
- [ ] `api.test.ts:64,114` and `aws.test.ts:45` are dispositioned as test-file handler/mock reads, matching the allowlist's existing test-file wording.
- [ ] No production behavior change (allowlist-only, plus test-file dispositions). If the refresh uncovers a genuinely unbounded production site, file it separately and disposition it as a tracked remaining surface — do not fix it inside this change.
- [ ] Coordinate with open PR #989 if it merges first (re-run the gate; do not duplicate or conflict with its allowlist lines).

title: fix(console): inference proxy fetch has no deadline — a stalled inference backend hangs every Zen/Go route instead of settling as 503

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
## Problem

`proxyInference` in `packages/console/app/src/lib/inference-proxy.ts` — the single proxy behind **every** Zen and Go inference route (`/zen/v1/*`, `/zen/go/v1/*`: chat completions, responses, messages, systemone, models, usage) — fetches the new-inference service with **no deadline of any kind**. If the inference backend accepts the connection and stalls before (or while) returning response headers, the console request hangs indefinitely; the existing `.catch(() => undefined)` → 503 path only fires when the fetch *rejects*, and a stalled fetch never rejects.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `775632b96a`)

- `inference-proxy.ts:57-59`: `Resource.INFERENCE.fetch(forwarded, { redirect: "manual" })` — no `signal`, no timeout option; `grep -n timeout` on the file returns nothing. The bounded-http regression-net allowlist (`script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt`) dispositions this exact line as a "remaining surface in this inventory under design #1127" — with **no tracking issue named**, unlike its sibling entries (#1097 Salesforce, #1098 openapi route, #1081 theme loader), which each name an owner.
- Every sibling console proxy bounds its upstream fetch with a named constant: `packages/console/app/src/routes/s/[id].ts` exports `PROXY_TIMEOUT_MS = 8_000` and passes `AbortSignal.timeout(...)`; `packages/console/app/src/lib/stats-proxy.ts` exports `STATS_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 8_000` the same way and settles a stall as a 502.
- Callers (all deadline-free by construction): `packages/console/app/src/routes/zen/v1/{chat/completions,responses,messages,systemone,models}.ts`, `zen/v1/models/[model].ts`, and the six `zen/go/v1/*` equivalents — each is a 5-line wrapper over `proxyInference`.
- Dedup: `gh` searches for `proxyInference`, `inference-proxy`, `inference proxy no timeout`, `zen proxy` across open + closed issues return no issue covering this fetch's missing deadline.

## Why it matters

This is the public front door for Zen/Go inference traffic. A wedged inference backend currently converts into wedged console requests with no diagnostic and no 503 — clients retry against a proxy that never answers, and the failure mode is indistinguishable from a console outage. The codebase has already settled the pattern (named timeout constant + settle-as-5xx) in both sibling proxies; this one was left out, and #1127's inventory tracks it without an owner.

## Design note (why this is triage-sized, not a blind 8s copy)

A total-body deadline would be wrong here: streaming completions legitimately run for minutes. The bound needed is on **time-to-response-headers** (abort if the upstream hasn't started answering within the deadline; once headers arrive, the streamed body proceeds unbounded), plus the non-streaming routes (models, usage) can take the plain sibling-style deadline. The PR should state which shape it implements per route class.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `proxyInference` passes a deadline signal to the inference fetch, via a named exported constant in the sibling style (`PROXY_TIMEOUT_MS` / `STATS_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` precedent).
- [ ] A stall before response headers settles as the existing 503 "Inference routing is unavailable" response (or an equally explicit 5xx) instead of hanging.
- [ ] Streaming responses that have started are **not** cut off by the new deadline (test or documented probe demonstrates a slow-streaming body completing past the headers deadline).
- [ ] A unit test in the style of `stats-proxy.test.ts` covers: upstream stall → 503, upstream error → 503, healthy upstream → proxied response unchanged (including the 404→400 rewrite).
- [ ] The `check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` entry for `inference-proxy.ts` is updated to "bounded at the site" (or removed if the checker no longer flags the line).

body:
## Problem

`.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml`'s only job (`cleanup`) has **no `timeout-minutes`** — it is the one runnable job in the repo that regressed the rule closed by #61 ("CI: add timeout-minutes caps to every job in every workflow", closed 2026-10-19).

## Evidence (verified this run, main `775632b96a`)

- `grep -L timeout-minutes .github/workflows/*.yml` matches exactly two files: `agents.yml` (a thin reusable-workflow caller — caller jobs cannot take `timeout-minutes`; the callee owns its caps) and `branch-cleanup.yml` (a regular `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` job with steps). The other 27 workflow files all carry at least one cap.
- `branch-cleanup.yml` was added 2026-10-27 in `680d6af57c` ("ci: add stale-branch cleanup workflow") — eight days **after** #61 closed, so the new workflow never got the cap the repo had just standardized.
- The job is exactly the kind that can hang: `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0`, a full `git fetch --prune` of every branch ref, two `gh pr list --limit 1000` calls, a per-branch `git log`/`git merge-base` loop over all remote branches, and up to 50 `git push origin --delete` calls. With no cap, a stalled fetch/API/push runs to GitHub's 360-minute default instead of failing in minutes.
- Precedent values in sibling scheduled housekeeping workflows: `stats.yml` 15, `jules-daily-upstream-sync.yml` 30, `notify-discord.yml` 10, `repo-sweeper.yml` 90.

## Why it matters

A daily scheduled job (cron `17 14 * * *`) that can silently burn a 6-hour runner slot on a network stall, delaying its own next runs and hiding a real failure (auth expiry, API stall) behind a timeout nobody chose. #61 already decided this repo's policy; this is the one job that slipped past it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cleanup` job in `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml` carries an explicit `timeout-minutes` (suggested 30, matching `jules-daily-upstream-sync.yml`; justify any other value in the PR).
- [ ] No other behavior change to the workflow (triggers, permissions, dry-run latch, deletion logic untouched).
- [ ] The PR notes that `agents.yml` was checked and is exempt-by-construction (reusable-workflow caller), so the repo is back to "every runnable job capped" per #61.

## Problem

The public share page builds its social-card (`og:image`) URL from the set of models used in the shared session — but the zero-model case falls into the "many models" branch and produces a nonsense parameter:

- `packages/web/src/pages/s/[id].astro:83-91` — `models` is populated only from messages with `role === "assistant"` and a truthy `modelID`.
- `packages/web/src/pages/s/[id].astro:98-104` — `modelParam` handles `length === 1` and `length === 2` explicitly; every other length takes the else branch: `` `${modelsArray[0]} & ${modelsArray.length - 1} others` ``.
- For `length === 0` that evaluates to **`undefined & -1 others`** (URL-encoded: `undefined%20%26%20-1%20others`), which is interpolated into the `ogImage` URL at `:106` and emitted as the `og:image` / `twitter:image` meta content at `:134`/`:141`.

A shared session whose messages carry no assistant `modelID` — an empty or user-only session, or assistant messages without a recorded model — therefore advertises a social card keyed to a model literally named "undefined & -1 others".

## Evidence (verified this run, main `5e2ab97bc56729b69f78493d41c294725f2f9b00`)

- File read in full on current main: the `models` set, the ternary chain, and the `ogImage` interpolation are exactly as quoted above (lines 83–106).
- Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-share-modelparam/probe.ts` replicating the exact ternary logic:
  - zero models (`{m1:{role:"user"}}`), empty messages (`{}`), and assistant-without-`modelID` all produce `undefined%20%26%20-1%20others`.
  - Control cases are correct: one model → `gpt-x`; three models → `m1%20%26%202%20others`.
- Dedup: `gh` searches for `share_data`, `social card`, `og image models others share` return no open or closed issue covering this parameter bug. Related but distinct: #1179 covers this same page's unbounded `share_data` fetch/body read — a different defect in the same file; this issue is only the model-parameter construction.

## Why it matters

`/s/<id>` is the public link users send each other; its social card is what renders in chat/social previews. For any share with no recorded assistant model, the preview is generated from a garbage model label — a visible correctness papercut on a public, unauthenticated page, and the "-1 others" arithmetic shows the zero case was never exercised.

## Acceptance criteria

- Rendering (or a unit-level extraction of the parameter logic) for a share with zero recorded models produces a sane `model` parameter (omitted, empty, or a neutral label) — never the string `undefined` and never a negative count.
- The 1-model, 2-model, and ≥3-model outputs are unchanged from current behavior.
- A test or recorded probe covers all four cases (0, 1, 2, ≥3 models) with the outputs shown.
- No change to the `share_data` fetch itself (that is #1179's scope).

body:
## Problem

The public share page's server-side frontmatter fetches the session payload with **no deadline and no body cap**:

- `packages/web/src/pages/s/[id].astro:70` — `const res = await fetch(\`${apiUrl}/share_data?id=${id}\`)` with no `signal` in the call options.
- `packages/web/src/pages/s/[id].astro:71` — `const data = (await res.json()) as { ... }` buffers the whole body unbounded; there is also no `res.ok`/status check, so a non-JSON upstream error body surfaces as an unhandled parse throw (500) instead of a controlled response.

This runs on every render of `/s/<id>` on the docs/web server with `apiUrl` from `VITE_API_URL` (`:8`). A stalled or slow-dripping share API hangs the page render indefinitely (one hung render per request, no deadline anywhere in the chain), and an oversized or endless body is buffered whole in the web server's memory.

The repo's own bounded-http regression net already inventories this exact site: `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` dispositions both lines as a *remaining surface* under design #1127 ("no signal in the call options - unbounded outbound fetch (Astro frontmatter, server-side)" and "direct response body read not through a bounded/excerpt reader") — but unlike its sibling remaining surfaces (#1098 console openapi route, #1097 Salesforce, #1081 theme loader), no tracking issue owns this one. This issue is that tracking issue.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `93ec446835`)

- File read in full on current main: line 70 fetch has no signal; line 71 `res.json()` is the only read; no status check before the read; the only downstream guard is `if (!data.info)` → 404 (`:76-81`), which runs *after* the unbounded buffer.
- Allowlist dispositions quoted above (`script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt`, tail entries for `packages/web/src/pages/s/[id].astro`) — the checker added Astro sources to its sweep in c897dda446 (#1129) and this is the one remaining undispositioned-to-an-issue surface it lists for `packages/web`.
- Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-share-page/probe.ts` replicating the exact call shape (`fetch(url)` with no signal, then `await res.json()`) against local servers:
  - stall server (accepts, never responds): fetch **still pending at 6 s**, killed by the probe `timeout` (rc=124) — no deadline.
  - endless/oversized server (64 × 1 MiB chunks): `res.json()` consumed the **entire 64 MiB stream** before failing only at final parse (1328 ms) — the read never caps.
- Dedup: `gh` searches for `share_data`, `Astro share`, `web share_data unbounded` return no open or closed issue covering this page; #1127 is the design parent, #1098/#1097/#1081 are the sibling surfaces with their own issues.

## Why it matters

`/s/<id>` is the public face of session sharing — the link users send each other. Its only upstream call is unbounded in both time and bytes: a degraded share API turns into hung renders and worker pile-up on the web server, and a bad body is a memory-amplification surface on a public, unauthenticated route. Every other inventoried surface from the same sweep already has an owner; this one is the leftover.

## Acceptance criteria

- The `share_data` fetch runs under a named deadline (e.g. `AbortSignal.timeout(...)`) that also covers the body read; a stall produces a controlled error response (not a hung render) naming the deadline.
- The body is read through a bounded reader with a named byte cap sized with stated headroom over a real shared-session payload (measure one and state it); an over-cap body fails closed with a controlled response.
- A non-OK upstream status or non-JSON body produces a controlled response (e.g. the existing 404 path or a 502), not an unhandled throw.
- The two allowlist entries for this file are updated to "bounded at the site" naming the bound, and `bun run script/check-bounded-http.ts` passes.
- Verification recorded on the issue: stall server, oversized-body server, and a real share id render against the fixed page.

title: Pre-push hook typecheck fails on @opencode/core at main

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

body:
## Problem

The husky pre-push hook in this repo runs the monorepo typecheck (~3.5 min). Against the primary checkout's **current main**, the typecheck fails on `@opencode/core` — so any push from a checkout at current main is blocked by the hook.

## Evidence

Reproduced on 2026-11-01 during a worktree-rescue operation that pushed a series of historical branches (all plain fast-forward / new-branch pushes, all accepted by GitHub). The first two pushes died on this hook; the remaining pushes had to use `--no-verify` to bypass the **local hook only** — no remote protection was involved.

The failure is **branch-independent and pre-existing**: the branches being pushed were historical (their content passed CI in its PR era); the hook fails because of the state of `@opencode/core` typecheck at current main, not because of anything on the pushed branches.

## Impact

- Pushes from a main-based checkout fail locally for an unrelated reason, which trains exactly the wrong habit: routine `--no-verify`.
- CI signal and local-push signal diverge — CI can be green while the local hook is red.

## Reproduction

From a checkout of this repo at current main, attempt any push (a trivial new branch is enough) and watch the pre-push hook fail on `@opencode/core#typecheck`. The exact failure output can be reproduced with a no-op push.

## Ask

Fix the `@opencode/core` typecheck errors at main (or, if the errors are a known transient, scope the hook so a failure unrelated to the pushed branches doesn't block the push).

title: fix(core): models-snapshot refresh script fetches api.json with no timeout and no body cap — response.text() unbounded, body written straight into the committed snapshot

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: area/ci
labels.description: CI, workflows, and build infrastructure

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

The bundled models.dev snapshot refresh script fetches the catalog with **no deadline and no body cap**, then writes whatever it buffered to the committed snapshot:

- `packages/core/script/update-models-snapshot.ts:8` — `const response = await fetch(\`${source}/api.json\`)` with no `signal`.
- `packages/core/script/update-models-snapshot.ts:13` — `const text = await response.text()` buffers the whole body unbounded.
- `packages/core/script/update-models-snapshot.ts:20-21` — the only guard is a floor on provider count (≥100 keys parse); there is no size ceiling before `Bun.write(target, text)` commits the body as `packages/core/src/models-dev/snapshot.txt`.

`source` is operator-controlled (`OPENCODE_MODELS_URL`, :7), and the script runs unattended twice daily in the `models-snapshot` workflow (`.github/workflows/models-snapshot.yml`, cron `0 0,12 * * *`, job timeout 30 min) and locally via `packages/core/package.json`'s `update-models-snapshot`. A stalled endpoint burns the full 30-minute job timeout on every scheduled run; an endless or oversized body is buffered whole in memory, and any oversized-but-parseable body with ≥100 providers would be written and committed as the boot-time catalog floor.

The runtime counterpart of this same fetch was already bounded for size (#1078: the app catalog fetch reading `api.json` unbounded), and the sibling refresh-adjacent fetches in core are deadline+cap pairs — this script is the uncovered surface.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `57e7f7cadb`)

- Script read in full (24 lines): no `AbortSignal`, no byte cap, no maximum-size check anywhere.
- Real catalog measured this run (laptop, real `https://models.opencode.ai/api.json` via the unmodified script): **235 providers, 5,963,733 bytes** written — so a generous named cap (e.g. 32 MiB) has >5× headroom.
- Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-import-post/` running the **unmodified script copied from current main** (md5 `c00c7f0fc3253543b0df92369f1928c9`, identical in sandbox clone, laptop clone, and probe copy) with `OPENCODE_MODELS_URL` pointed at local servers:
  - stall server (accepts, never responds): script **still pending at 6 s**, killed by the probe's `timeout` (rc=124) — no fetch deadline.
  - endless server (1 MiB chunk every 50 ms): script **still buffering at 6 s**, killed by `timeout` (rc=124) — `response.text()` never caps or errors.
- Dedup: #109 (closed) made the workflow run on this fork; #156 (closed) added its concurrency queue; #1078 (closed) bounded the runtime catalog fetch. No open or closed issue covers the refresh script's own fetch.

## Why it matters

This is the supply path for the bundled catalog snapshot that boots every install when no cache exists. Its failure modes are silent waste (a stalled upstream stalls a twice-daily workflow for its full timeout, indefinitely, with no actionable error) and unbounded memory/commit surface on the one script in the repo that writes a fetched body straight into the tree.

## Acceptance criteria

- The fetch runs under a named deadline (e.g. `AbortSignal.timeout(...)`) that also covers the body read, and a stall produces a clear non-zero exit naming the source URL and the deadline.
- The body is read with a named byte cap sized with stated headroom over the real catalog (~6 MiB today; e.g. 32 MiB), and an over-cap body fails before any write to `snapshot.txt`.
- The existing ≥100-provider floor guard is preserved; a failed refresh leaves the previous snapshot untouched.
- Verification recorded on the issue: stall server, endless-body server, and a real-catalog run (byte count + provider count) against the fixed script.

title: fix(cli): session import's server POST has no timeout and reads its response unbounded — remote leg is bounded (#1115), the server leg in the same handler is not

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/cli
labels.description: Package: cli (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`opencode session import` bounds its remote-source fetch — one 600 s deadline covering the fetch and a 256 MiB bounded body read (`fetchRemote`, the #1115 fix) — but the very next step in the same handler, the POST that delivers the session to the server, has **no deadline at all and reads its response unbounded**:

- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/session/import.ts:62-71` — `fetch(new URL("/api/experimental/session/import", server.endpoint.url), { method: "POST", … })` with no `signal`.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/session/import.ts:77-79` — `response.text()` with no byte cap (contrast `readBoundedResponseBody` used at :32 for the remote leg).

The `--server` endpoint is arbitrary (the same premise as #1144/#987): a stalled or slow-dripping server hangs the import forever, after the source data was already fetched successfully; a hostile or broken server can also stream an endless response body into `response.text()`.

There is a second unbounded call in the same flow: the generated client's `client.location.get(...)` at :57-61 goes through `packages/client/src/promise/generated/client.ts:376` (`fetch(prepared.url, prepared.init)`), whose init carries no default deadline either. The POST is the primary gap; triage should decide whether the location lookup is in scope or a follow-up.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `57e7f7cadb`)

- Code read in full: the handler's remote leg (:28-34) composes `AbortSignal.timeout(SESSION_IMPORT_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS)` + `readBoundedResponseBody(response, MAX_SESSION_TRANSFER_BYTES, signal)`; the server POST leg (:62-79) composes neither.
- Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-import-post/probe.mjs` replicating the exact POST pattern (no signal, then `response.text()`):
  - stall-headers server: **still pending after 5 s** (no RESOLVED/REJECTED at the 5 s mark).
  - drip-body server (1 byte/s): `response.text()` **still pending after 5 s**.
  - Control (`control.mjs`, same endpoints with `AbortSignal.timeout(3000)` covering fetch + body read): **REJECTED after 3011 ms** (stall) and **3014 ms** (drip) with `TimeoutError`.
- Dedup: #942 (closed) covered the remote leg's size cap; #1115 (closed) covered the remote leg's deadline; #1144 (closed) and #987 (open) cover the `opencode api` handler's fetches/body. No open or closed issue covers the import handler's server POST leg or its `response.text()`.

## Why it matters

The import command's robustness work (#942, #1115) left the final hop unguarded, so the user-visible behaviour — "import hangs forever against a bad server" — survives both fixes. The endpoint is user-supplied, so the bad-server case is a misconfigured or wedged server, not an exotic attacker.

## Acceptance criteria

- The POST to `/api/experimental/session/import` runs under a named deadline sized for a legitimately large transfer (the remote leg's 600 s precedent in the same file is the natural value, or a stated alternative), composed so the deadline also covers the response-body read.
- The success response body is read through a bounded reader (e.g. `readBoundedResponseBody` from `packages/cli/src/util/io.ts`) with a named cap sized for a `Session.Info` JSON payload, instead of bare `response.text()`.
- A deadline expiry produces an error that names the import endpoint/deadline, not a raw `TimeoutError`.
- Regression tests (pattern of `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/api.test.ts` / the import tests): stall-headers and drip-body servers fail at the deadline; a normal small JSON response imports successfully.
- Triage decides explicitly whether `client.location.get` (:57) is bounded in the same change or filed as a follow-up, and records the decision on this issue.

title: fix(console): console-account CRM lookup reads its JSON body unbounded — 3s timeout bounds duration, not bytes (response.json() with no cap)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/console
labels.description: Package: console (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

`lookupConsoleAccount` in the console app bounds its CRM lookup in **time** (3s) but not in **size**: the response body is read with `await response.json()` and no byte cap, so a misbehaving or compromised lookup endpoint can make the enterprise-form request buffer an arbitrarily large body — as much as the connection can deliver inside the 3s window.

## Evidence (verified on main `7918a1bcfe`, 2026-10-31)

- `packages/console/app/src/lib/console-account.ts:13-17` — `fetch(Resource.CONSOLE_CRM_LOOKUP_URL.value, { method: "POST", ..., signal: AbortSignal.timeout(3000) })`: a deadline exists.
- `packages/console/app/src/lib/console-account.ts:20` — `z.object({ account: consoleAccountSchema.nullable() }).parse(await response.json())`: the whole body is buffered and parsed with no declared-length pre-check and no streamed cap. The valid response is a tiny struct (`id` ≤255 chars, email, nullable name, datetime — `console-account.ts:4-9`), so the legitimate body is well under a few KiB.
- Sole production caller: `packages/console/app/src/lib/enterprise.ts:121` — `handleEnterpriseRequest` awaits this lookup on the public enterprise-form path (degrading to `account=undefined` only when the promise *rejects*; an oversized body must first be buffered and fail/complete parsing).
- Contrast in the same app, same week: `packages/console/app/src/lib/github.ts` and `changelog.ts` read GitHub bodies through a streamed capped reader (1–8 MiB caps), and `packages/console/app/src/routes/download/[channel]/[platform].ts` caps release metadata at 1 MiB. This lookup is the remaining uncapped JSON read in the enterprise flow. (The #1143 triage packet's scope note called this lookup "already bounded at 3s" — that bounds duration only, not bytes; this issue is the size half.)

## Reproduction (laptop probe)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-console-account/probe.mjs` (Node 24, local HTTP server, client replicating the exact `console-account.ts:13-20` pattern — `fetch` with `AbortSignal.timeout(3000)` then `await response.json()`):

- `/huge` — server returns a 32 MiB JSON body (`{"account":null,"pad":"x"×33554432}`) at local speed: **RESOLVED in 563 ms, pad length 33,554,432, RSS 244 MiB** — the entire body was buffered and parsed well inside the deadline.
- `/endless` — server drips the body indefinitely: **REJECTED at 3008 ms with TimeoutError** — confirming the deadline bounds duration; it does not bound bytes delivered within the window.

On a fast datacenter link (console worker ↔ CRM endpoint), the 3s window admits far more than 32 MiB.

## Why it matters

The enterprise form is a public endpoint; its handler should not be able to allocate unbounded memory on the word of one upstream response. Every neighbouring console fetch has now been given a named byte cap for exactly this failure mode — this is the residual gap in that set, not a new class of concern.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `lookupConsoleAccount` reads the lookup response through a bounded reader with a named byte cap sized for the schema (the account struct is <1 KiB; house precedent for tiny JSON is 64 KiB–1 MiB), failing the lookup (→ caller's existing `account=undefined` degradation) on an over-cap body instead of buffering it.
- [ ] Declared `content-length` over the cap is rejected before reading, and a streamed/chunked body is cut at the cap (no `response.json()` on the raw response).
- [ ] Regression tests in the console app (following `salesforce.test.ts` / `enterprise.test.ts` patterns): normal small response parses; declared-oversize and streamed-oversize responses fail bounded; timeout behaviour unchanged.
- [ ] No behaviour change for legitimate responses: `ConsoleAccount | null` result and the `enterprise.ts:121` degradation path are unchanged.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `console-account`, `CRM`, `lookupConsoleAccount` (2026-10-31): no filing covers this call. #1097 is the Salesforce login/lead fetches (different service, same flow); #1143 is the SES `sendEmail` fetch (no body read at all). This is the CRM lookup's size bound only.

body:
## Problem

Neither fetch in the `opencode api` handler has a deadline:

- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/api.ts:38-44` — the main request: `fetch(new URL(request.path, endpoint.url), { method, headers, body })` with **no `signal`**; `response.text()` at `:45` then waits for the body however long it takes.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/api.ts:74-76` — the operation-by-name path first fetches the spec: `fetch(new URL("/openapi.json", endpoint.url), { headers })`, again **no `signal`**, then `await response.json()`.

The `--server` endpoint is arbitrary (`packages/cli/src/services/server-connection.ts` uses it verbatim — a shared, standing, or remote server, per #987), so a server that accepts the connection and then stalls — or a network path that black-holes — hangs the CLI **forever with no output and no error**, in a command whose whole purpose is scripting/debugging against possibly-unhealthy servers.

## Relationship to #987 (not a duplicate)

#987 covers the **size** axis for these same two calls: `response.text()` / `response.json()` buffer whole bodies, and its acceptance asks for streaming or a byte cap. A streaming/capped fix does not bound **time**: a stalled server sends no bytes at all, so nothing streams and no cap ever trips. This is the same size-vs-time split the fleet has filed separately before — #942 capped the session-import body and #1115 was filed as its residual for the missing time bound. #987's acceptance criteria contain no deadline for either fetch.

## Evidence (verified this run, main ec099f1c15)

- Code read: `api.ts:38-45` and `api.ts:74-76` — neither init carries a `signal`; no timeout exists anywhere in the handler.
- Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-cli-api-timeout` (exact call shapes against a local server that accepts and never responds):
  - Main-request shape: `STILL-PENDING after 5000ms`.
  - `/openapi.json` shape (fetch + `response.json()`): `STILL-PENDING after 5000ms`.
  - Control: the same lookup with `AbortSignal.timeout(3000)` rejects `TimeoutError` at 3013ms.
- Dedup: `gh` search (open + closed) for the `api` handler timeout returns only #987, whose scope is body size (see above).

## Why it matters

`opencode api` is routinely pointed at long-lived shared servers, including by scripts and fleet automation. A hung server currently means a hung CLI process that never returns — automation waits on it indefinitely and a human gets no diagnostic at all. The `/openapi.json` lookup is a metadata GET that should complete in seconds; the main request needs a deadline policy that respects legitimately long operations (see acceptance).

## Acceptance criteria

- The `/openapi.json` fetch in `resolveRequest` carries a timeout via a named constant (house precedent: `AbortSignal.timeout(...)`), so a stalled server fails the lookup with a clear error instead of hanging the CLI.
- The main request fetch also gains a considered deadline policy: either a generous named deadline that cannot cut off legitimately long-running operations the CLI is used for, or an explicit, documented decision (in the fix) on why the main request differs — silence is not an outcome. If a deadline is applied, the resulting error message names the timeout rather than surfacing a raw abort.
- #987's scope is untouched: this issue does not re-decide body streaming/caps, and the two fixes must compose (deadline signal and bounded/streamed body read on the same calls).
- Regression coverage for: stalled server on the spec lookup (times out with a clear error), stalled server on the main request (per the chosen policy), normal operation resolution and raw requests (existing `api.test.ts` cases stay green).

body:
## Problem

The console's AWS SES send has no deadline:

- `packages/console/app/src/lib/aws.ts:12` — `sendEmail()` calls `client.fetch("https://email.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/v2/email/outbound-emails", { method, headers, body })` (aws4fetch `AwsClient`) with **no `signal`** and no other timeout. A stalled or slow-dripping SES endpoint holds the call open indefinitely.
- Sole caller: `packages/console/app/src/lib/enterprise.ts:127-140` — `handleEnterpriseRequest` awaits `sendEmail(...)` inside a `Promise.all` (`:119`), so one hung SES call pins the **entire enterprise-form request** forever, even though the sibling calls in the same `Promise.all` are bounded or degradable (Salesforce is bounded after #1097; the result also gates the `!lead && !mail && !octopus` failure decision at `:142`, so the request can neither succeed nor fail while SES hangs).

The response body is never read (`res.ok` / `res.statusText` only, `aws.ts:37`), so this is a time bound only — no body cap is needed.

This is a distinct service/file from #1111 (EmailOctopus subscribe fetches, including the `subscribe()` call in the same `enterprise.ts` file) and #1097 (Salesforce).

## Evidence (verified this run, main ec099f1c15)

- Code read: `aws.ts:6-38` — the `client.fetch` init contains `method`, `headers`, `body` only; no `signal` anywhere in the file. `enterprise.ts:119-141` — `sendEmail` is awaited in `Promise.all` with no surrounding timeout or race.
- Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-ses-send-email` (real `aws4fetch` `AwsClient` from the console app's own `node_modules`, exact `aws.ts` call shape against a local server that accepts and never responds):
  - No-signal (aws.ts shape): `STILL-PENDING after 5000ms`.
  - Control: the same call with `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(3000)` rejects `TimeoutError` after 3016ms — proving aws4fetch passes a signal through to the underlying fetch, so the fix works through this client.
- Dedup: `gh` search (open + closed) for `SES` / `sendEmail` / `aws` in this repo returns no filing covering this call; #1111 is EmailOctopus and #1097 is Salesforce, both different services in the same enterprise flow.

## Why it matters

The enterprise contact form is a public endpoint. One stalled SES response pins its server request (and the worker slot serving it) indefinitely; repeated stalls accumulate pinned requests. Every other third-party call in this flow has been bounded one by one (#1097 Salesforce, #1111 EmailOctopus) — this is the remaining unbounded one, and it sits in the `Promise.all` that decides the whole submission.

## Acceptance criteria

- `sendEmail()` in `packages/console/app/src/lib/aws.ts` carries a timeout via a named constant (house precedent: `AbortSignal.timeout(...)`, in line with the 3–8s bounds used by the neighbouring console calls), so a stalled SES endpoint rejects instead of hanging.
- On timeout, the enterprise flow's existing degradation keeps working: `handleEnterpriseRequest` logs the failure and treats `mail` as `false` (the `.then(() => true, err => false)` arm), and the request still completes on the strength of the lead/octopus results.
- Success behaviour unchanged: a prompt SES 2xx still resolves `sendEmail` and `mail` is `true`.
- Regression coverage for: stalled SES endpoint (times out), normal send (unchanged). Inventory the console app's existing test conventions for `enterprise.ts` handlers (e.g. `salesforce.test.ts` / `console-signup.test.ts` patterns) as the home for this.

body:
Drew's directive (2026-10-31): "make constants into experimental config defaulted to current values."

## Problem

The model-route machinery's tuning constants are hardcoded in `packages/core/src/model-route.ts`. The per-route `health` block covers only the two bench bases (60s failure / 900s quota). Everything else — the bench ladder's shape, quota demotion, the quota gate, escalation, the network-suspect heuristic, continuity hedging, the user-preference default — is a literal or an entry in `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`, for which a code-level `ModelRoute.configure()` hook exists but **no config key feeds it** (grep-verified: `configure()` is called only from tests). Operators cannot tune any of it without a code change and a rebuild.

## Constants inventory (all in `packages/core/src/model-route.ts` unless noted)

New config home for every row: `experimental.model_route_settings`, grouped so the block can later move under `experimental.routes.settings` with a mechanical path change when the staged nesting (#1140) lands.

### bench — the cooldown ladder

| Symbol / locus | Current value | New key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_COOLDOWN_MS` (:344) | 86_400_000 (24h) | `bench.maxCooldownMs` |
| backoff multiplier, inline `2 **` in `bench()` (:378) | 2 | `bench.multiplier` |
| retry-after floor, inline `Math.max(·, 1_000)` (:377) | 1_000 | `bench.retryAfterMinMs` |
| failure-base cap, inline in `policy()` (:197) | 3_600_000 (1h) | `bench.cooldownCapMs` |
| quota-base cap, inline in `policy()` (:198) | 86_400_000 (24h) | `bench.quotaCooldownCapMs` |

### demotion — quota-error demotion

| Symbol / locus | Current value | New key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DEFAULT_SETTINGS.quota.demoteAfter` (in `Settings`, no config feeder) | 3 | `demotion.after` |
| `DEFAULT_SETTINGS.quota.windowMs` | 14_400_000 (4h) | `demotion.windowMs` |
| `DEMOTED_FACTOR` (:1134) | 0.01 | `demotion.factor` |

### quotaGate — exhaustion gates from quota snapshots / attempt reports

| Symbol / locus | Current value | New key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `QUOTA_GATE_MAX_MS` (:597) | 2_592_000_000 (30d) | `quotaGate.maxMs` |
| `QUOTA_GATE_FALLBACK_MS` (:601) | 1_800_000 (30m) | `quotaGate.fallbackMs` |
| `shouldFeedQuota` default ttl (:589) | 60_000 | `quotaGate.feedTtlMs` |

### escalation — racing the next target after give-ups

| Symbol / locus | Current value | New key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DEFAULT_SETTINGS.escalation.enabled` (no config feeder) | true | `escalation.enabled` |
| `DEFAULT_SETTINGS.escalation.afterGiveUps` | 2 | `escalation.afterGiveUps` |
| `OUTCOME_WINDOW` (:254) — outcomes the give-up count reads | 5 | `escalation.outcomeWindow` |

### network — network-suspect forgiveness / provider-wide demotion

| Symbol / locus | Current value | New key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NETWORK_WINDOW_MS` (:313) | 30_000 | `network.windowMs` |
| `NETWORK_PROVIDERS` (:314) | 3 | `network.providers` |
| `PROVIDER_MODELS` (:315) | 2 | `network.providerModels` |

### continuity — hedging back to a failover origin

| Symbol / locus | Current value | New key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ORIGIN_HEDGE_REQUESTS` (:1612) | 2 | `continuity.hedgeRequests` |

### overrides — user preference default

| Symbol / locus | Current value | New key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PREFERRED_FACTOR` (:1137) | 3 | `overrides.preferredFactor` |

## Deliberately left hardcoded

- **Backoff exponent cap (30)** in `bench()` — an arithmetic overflow guard, not a knob: 2^30 × 1ms ≈ 12.4 days already exceeds the 24h bench cap, so the cap always binds first.
- **State memory bounds** — `HEALTH_LIMIT` 2_000, `SESSION_LIMIT` 5_000, `CONTINUITY_LIMIT` 5_000: LRU caps on process-local maps. Resource-safety invariants, not routing policy.
- **Event buffer caps** — `recentFailures` ring at 200, quota-event history at 50 (`recordQuota`): bounded-memory invariants sized as headroom over the thresholds they serve. The schema therefore caps `demotion.after` at 50, so a configured threshold can never exceed the retained history.
- **Usage-accounting internals** — `BUCKET_MS` 6_000, `DAY_MS` 86_400_000, the 60s last-minute usage window: ledger bucketing granularity/retention, not failover policy.
- **Relational clamps in `policy()`** (`slowThreshold ≤ sampleWindow`; `sampleWindow ≤ 50` mirrors the schema's `SampleCount`) — consistency clamps tied to the schema, not standalone values.

Same property, noted as follow-up (out of scope here): `model-route-limits.ts` (`MAX_WINDOW_MS` 24h, `UNKNOWN_RESET_MS` 60s — burst rate-limit holds) and `model-route-tuning.ts` (`MAX_QUOTA_RESET_MS`, which mirrors `quotaGate.maxMs` and should stay in step with it).

## Design

- Schema: a `Settings` class in `packages/schema/src/config/model-routes.ts` with grouped sub-objects (`bench` / `demotion` / `quotaGate` / `escalation` / `network` / `continuity` / `overrides`), every field optional and annotated with its default; registered as `experimental.model_route_settings` in `packages/schema/src/config/experimental.ts`. The grouped shape survives either schema outcome: it works flat today, parallel to `model_routes`, and moves under `experimental.routes.settings` mechanically when #1140 lands.
- Validation rejects nonsense: durations are positive ints bounded at 90 days; `bench.multiplier` ≥ 1 (below 1 successive benches would shrink); `demotion.factor` in (0, 1] (0 would zero a weight; above 1 a quota error would *promote*); `demotion.after` ≤ 50 (retained-history cap, above); `network.providers` ≥ 2 (1 would forgive every lone failure as a network fault); counts are positive ints.
- Wiring: the model-routes config plugin registers a lazy settings reader on `ModelRoute` (the `ModelRouteLog.onCaptureErrorBodies` precedent), so config reloads are honored without a restart. `demotion.after` / `demotion.windowMs` and `escalation.enabled` / `afterGiveUps` feed the pre-existing `Settings` / `configure()` store; the rest feed a new `Constants` store with `configureConstants()` / `currentConstants()` mirroring `configure()` / `currentSettings()`.
- Precedence: compiled defaults ← programmatic `configure()` / `configureConstants()` ← config. Per-route `health` bases still override locally for their route; the bench caps (now `bench.cooldownCapMs` / `bench.quotaCooldownCapMs`) bound those local values exactly as the hardcoded caps do today.

## Acceptance

- With no `model_route_settings` in config, behavior is bit-for-bit current behavior: the existing model-route test family passes **unchanged** (no edits to existing expectations), and new tests assert the resolved defaults equal the current constant values.
- New tests show config overrides change behavior: demotion factor, bench max cap, quota-gate fallback (plus defaults + validation coverage).
- Typecheck clean; the routing skill doc (`routing-config.md`) documents the block.


## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A new `experimental.model_route_settings` config block feeds every inventoried constant in `packages/core/src/model-route.ts`, grouped as specified in the body.
- [ ] With no config set, behavior is byte-for-byte the current defaults (existing route tests pass unmodified).
- [ ] Setting a value in config observably changes the corresponding machinery constant without a code change.
