# fix(cli): updater release check buffers the whole response body — `response.json()` with no size cap in `Updater.release`

## Evidence (verified this run, on main `18e33f84ec`)

`packages/cli/src/services/updater.ts:275-322` (`release()`, used by `latest()`, `check()`, `upgrade()`, and the automatic update check in `run()`): the release metadata is fetched from `https://formulae.brew.sh/api/formula/opencode.json` (brew/core) or `https://opencode.ai/update/api/<channel>/<artifact>/<distribution>` (all other methods), and the body is read with `response.json()` at line 309:

```ts
const response = yield* Effect.tryPromise({
  try: (signal) =>
    fetch(core ? "https://formulae.brew.sh/api/formula/opencode.json" : `https://opencode.ai/update/api/...`, {
      signal: AbortSignal.any([signal, AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)]),
    }),
  ...
})
...
const data = yield* Effect.tryPromise({ try: () => response.json(), ... })
```

The 10-second timeout bounds time, not bytes — a fast or compromised endpoint delivers arbitrarily much inside it. There is no size cap, no declared-length pre-check, and no streaming bound anywhere on this path. The real payload is a few hundred bytes (`{version, metadata.package}` or `{versions.stable}`).

The codebase already has the bounded primitive for native fetch responses: `readBoundedResponseText` in `packages/core/src/tool/http-body.ts:39` (declared-length pre-check + in-flight stream bound). This site was missed by the sibling caps (#960, #1017, #1018, #1023, #1025, #1026, #1029).

### Laptop probe (real service, this run)

Probe modeled on the repo's own `packages/cli/test/updater-install.test.ts` harness (real `Updater.Service`/`Updater.layer`, temp `Global`, global `fetch` stubbed like the fixture does), saved at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-30-updater-release-cap/probe-updater-cap.test.ts`, run on the laptop against main `18e33f84ec`:

- The stub fetch returned a **streamed** 50 MiB body (chunked `ReadableStream`, no `content-length`, valid JSON with a 50 MiB `pad` field) — so a declared-length check alone would not have caught it.
- Result: `updater.latest("npm")` returned `2.3.4` — the whole body was buffered and parsed; process **RSS +101 MiB** for a metadata document that is normally a few hundred bytes.

## Why it matters

- This is an **automatic** path: `run()` performs the update check without the user invoking `opencode upgrade`, so every CLI start that checks for updates fetches this body. A compromised or misbehaving update endpoint (or a MITM on a network where TLS verification is bypassed by a corporate proxy) OOMs the CLI process — all sessions in it — with a single response.
- It is the same defect class the fleet has been closing path by path; this is the CLI updater's turn.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `release()` in `packages/cli/src/services/updater.ts` reads the body through a bounded path (e.g. `readBoundedResponseText` from core's `tool/http-body.ts`, or an equivalent local bounded read) with a named, documented cap sized for release metadata (the real payloads are well under a few KiB; anything in the 64 KiB–1 MiB range is generous); a declared over-cap `content-length` is rejected before consuming, and a streamed/chunked over-cap body is rejected in flight.
- [ ] An over-cap body surfaces as the existing `UpgradeError` "Could not read the OpenCode update information" path — the update check fails soft exactly as it does today for unreadable bodies, never crashes or hangs the CLI.
- [ ] Tests in `packages/cli/test/` (extending the `updater-install.test.ts` fixture pattern, whose fetch stub is already in place) pin: a normal small body still resolves the version/package; an over-cap declared body and an over-cap streamed body both fail with `UpgradeError`.
- [ ] Verification via CI or laptop test run — no builds on the sandbox.

# fix(core): provider OAuth token/device/discovery responses are read with `response.json()`/`response.text()` and no size cap — the #960/#1017 bound never reached the auth helpers

## Evidence (verified this run, on main `2932c4d6c0`)

Four provider auth modules in `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/` read token, device-code, and discovery responses by buffering the whole body, with no size cap:

| Site | Read | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `chatgpt.ts:505-510` (`request<A>`) | `response.json()` | token exchange + refresh (`:398`, `:417`) |
| `openai.ts:410-415` (`request<A>`) | `response.json()` | device code, token exchange + refresh (`:204`, `:380`, `:394`) |
| `openai.ts:230` | `response.json()` | device poll success body |
| `github-copilot.ts:482-487` (`request`) | `response.json()` | device code + token exchange; URLs are built from the user-entered GitHub Enterprise domain (`:98-103`) |
| `github-copilot.ts:451-465` (`discoverCopilotApiEndpoint`) | `response.json()` | `/copilot_internal/user` lookup, run automatically at load for credentials that stored no endpoint (`:221`); only a 10 s timeout bounds it — time, not bytes |
| `xai.ts:208-209` (`decode`) | `response.json()` | device + token responses |
| `xai.ts:162`, `:192` | `response.text()` | error bodies, embedded in the failure message path |

The bounded primitive already exists and is already imported by one of these very files: `readBoundedResponseText` from `packages/core/src/tool/http-body.ts`, used at `github-copilot.ts:553` for the utility-title call (#960, with its named 64 KiB cap at `:506-515`). The Copilot **model-list** loader was capped under #1017 and MCP OAuth discovery under #1019 — the auth helpers in the same modules were missed. Token/device/discovery payloads are small JSON structs (hundreds of bytes to a few KiB), so a tight named cap per site is safe, exactly as #960 reasoned.

### Laptop probe (real module, this run)

Probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-30-oauth-body/probe.ts`, run against main `2932c4d6c0`, calling the exported `discoverCopilotApiEndpoint` with a stub `fetch` returning a **streamed** 50 MiB JSON body (chunked, no `content-length`):

- Result: endpoint returned successfully (`https://api.business.githubcopilot.com`), process **RSS +101 MiB** — the whole body was buffered and parsed before the schema decode discarded the padding.

The three private `request()`/`decode()` helpers share the identical one-line read pattern, so the same behaviour follows from the code for them; the probe pins the exported site.

Related audit pointers (same class, Effect HttpClient side — not in this issue's scope): `gitlab.ts:415`, `poe.ts:145`, `snowflake-cortex.ts:66` read error bodies via `response.text`, and the GitLab/Poe/Snowflake token success paths use `HttpClientResponse.schemaBodyJson`, which also buffers whole. File separately if triage confirms.

## Why it matters

- These are credential-flow responses: a compromised or misbehaving issuer — or, for Copilot, the user-entered Enterprise host — can OOM the client during login, token refresh, or (for discovery) automatic credential load, with a body the code then discards almost all of.
- The fleet has been closing this exact class file by file (#923, #960, #1017, #1018, #1019, #1023, #1025); leaving the auth helpers unbounded means the highest-trust flows are the last ones capped.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each site in the table reads its body through a bounded path (`readBoundedResponseText` or equivalent) with a named, documented cap sized for token/device/discovery payloads; a declared over-cap `content-length` is rejected before consuming, and a streamed/chunked over-cap body is rejected in flight.
- [ ] Over-cap responses fail the same way an unreadable/invalid response does today (auth fails with the existing error shape, discovery returns its current failure/fallback) — no partial JSON is decoded, and no over-cap error text is embedded in messages (xAI sites).
- [ ] Tests pin, for at least the shared helpers / discovery path: a small body behaves exactly as today (endpoints/tokens decoded unchanged) and an over-cap declared + streamed body is rejected.
- [ ] Verification via CI or laptop test run — no builds on the sandbox.

# fix(core): remote instruction URLs are fetched with no body size cap — `response.text` buffers the whole body into model context

## Evidence (verified this run, on main `2932c4d6c0`)

`packages/core/src/config/plugin/instruction.ts:138-156` (`ConfigInstructionPlugin.reconfigure`): every `http(s)://` entry in the config `instructions` array is fetched at config load with the Effect HttpClient, and the body is read with `response.text` (line 146):

```ts
HttpClientRequest.get(url).pipe(
  http.execute,
  Effect.flatMap((response) => response.text),
  Effect.timeout("5 seconds"),
  Effect.map((content) => new InstructionDiscovery.File({ path: url, content })),
```

The 5-second timeout bounds time, not bytes — a fast server delivers arbitrarily much inside it. There is no size cap anywhere on this path: the fetched string becomes an `InstructionDiscovery.File` whose content is rendered into the model's instruction context.

The codebase already has the right primitive for exactly this shape: `collectBoundedResponseBody` in `packages/core/src/tool/http-body.ts:4-31` (Effect HttpClient response, declared-length pre-check + in-flight stream bound), used by the bounded fetch paths fixed under #923. This site was missed.

### Laptop probe (real module, this run)

Probe test modeled on the repo's own `packages/core/test/instruction-discovery.test.ts` harness (injected HttpClient via `respond`/`HttpClientResponse.fromWeb`, real `ConfigInstructionPlugin` + `InstructionDiscovery`), saved at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-30-remote-instructions/probe.test.ts`, run on the laptop against main `2932c4d6c0`:

- The stub server returned a **streamed** 50 MiB body (chunked, no `content-length`, so a declared-length check alone would not have caught it).
- Result: the full body was loaded as instruction content — rendered initial instruction text length **52,428,856** chars, process **RSS +250 MiB** (the string is copied through the hash/render pipeline, so memory amplification is worse than the wire size).

## Why it matters

- `instructions` URLs are config-controlled: a project or shared config can point at any `http(s)` URL (docs encourage remote instruction files). A compromised, misconfigured, or just unexpectedly huge endpoint OOMs the client at config load — before any model call — or silently floods the model's context with megabytes of "instructions", burning the token budget on every session.
- Every sibling remote-body path has been capped one by one (#923 downloads, #1017 model lists, #1019 MCP OAuth discovery, #1023 mcpx daemon, #1018 service probe); this is the same class on an automatic, config-load path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The remote-instruction fetch in `instruction.ts` reads the body through a bounded path (e.g. `collectBoundedResponseBody` from `tool/http-body.ts`) with a named, documented cap sized for instruction files; a declared over-cap `content-length` is rejected before consuming, and a streamed/chunked over-cap body is rejected in flight.
- [ ] An over-cap (or otherwise unreadable) body keeps the current failure semantics: the fetch failure is logged as a warning and the last good copy is kept / the URL is skipped — config load never fails and no partial over-cap content enters the instruction set.
- [ ] Tests in `packages/core/test/instruction-discovery.test.ts` (or a sibling) pin: a small remote body still loads verbatim; an over-cap declared body and an over-cap streamed body are both skipped with the rest of the instruction set intact.
- [ ] Verification via CI or laptop test run — no builds on the sandbox.

body:
## Problem

`SessionStore.list` passes its limit to drizzle untouched — the one paging method in `packages/core/src/session/store.ts` that the #981/#983 store-boundary normalisation did not cover:

- store.ts:148: `input.limit === undefined ? query.all() : query.limit(input.limit).all()` — no truncation, floor, or finiteness check.
- `Session.list` (packages/core/src/session.ts:539-541) forwards its input to `store.list` unchanged, so the whole `Session` service surface has the same hole.
- In the same file, `messages` was fixed at the store boundary by #983: store.ts:61-66 (`messagesLimit`: non-finite → 50, else floored and clamped to [1, 200], with a comment stating the policy). `list` has no equivalent.

The guarded doors stay guarded — this is not a re-file of #935/#951: the plugin door normalises through `sessionListLimit` (`packages/core/src/plugin/session-list.ts:41`, the #951 fix) and the HTTP door decodes via protocol + `?? DefaultSessionsLimit` (`packages/server/src/handlers/session.ts:70`). What remains is the service boundary itself, for any direct `Session.list`/`SessionStore.list` caller (in-process consumers, future callers, JS callers) — exactly the boundary #981 fixed for `messages` while `list`, two methods away in the same file, was left raw.

## Verified behaviour (laptop probe, main `1c7f4d41ad`)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-30-session-list-limit/probe.ts` — bun:sqlite (the store's driver) `SELECT ... LIMIT ?` over 5 rows, the semantics store.ts:148 reaches through drizzle:

- control `LIMIT 2` → 2 rows.
- `LIMIT -5` / `-1` → **all 5 rows** (SQLite treats a negative LIMIT as unlimited) — a negative limit silently widens the query to every session.
- `LIMIT 0` → 0 rows.
- `LIMIT 1.5` / `NaN` / `Infinity` → `SQLiteError: datatype mismatch` — the read defects (surfaced as `orDie` at store.ts:148-150) instead of returning a page or a typed error.

## Why it matters

A session list is the fleet's most-enumerated collection; a negative limit from any non-schema caller silently returns every session, and a fractional/non-finite one kills the read with an opaque defect. The fix pattern already exists in the same file (`messagesLimit`) and in the plugin layer (`sessionListLimit`, deliberately ceiling-free because the HTTP surface applies none) — `list` is the inconsistent outlier.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SessionStore.list` normalises a present limit at the store boundary (the `Session.list` surface inherits it): fractional → truncated, zero/negative → floored to 1, non-finite → a documented policy (treated as absent, or the handler default) — a present limit never reaches drizzle raw.
- [ ] An absent limit keeps today's behaviour exactly (unbounded query, used by internal callers such as `Session.remove` child enumeration); no ceiling is introduced (mirrors `sessionListLimit`'s documented no-ceiling choice).
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/core/test/session-store.test.ts` (or the existing store test file) call `SessionStore.list`/`Session.list` directly with limit in {-5, -1, 0, 0.5, 1.5, NaN, Infinity} and pin the normalised behaviour; existing list/messages tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] Plugin (`sessionListLimit`) and HTTP handler behaviour are unchanged.

# fix(gui-extensions): SSH bootstrap fallback downloads the CLI archive with response.arrayBuffer — no size cap, no timeout

## Evidence (verified on main `1c7f4d41ad`, 2026-10-30, by line-level reading)

When the remote host cannot download the CLI archive itself, SSH bootstrap falls back to downloading it locally and uploading it over SSH stdin:

- `packages/gui-extensions/src/ssh/bootstrap.ts:130` — `http.get(url)` with no timeout applied to the request.
- `packages/gui-extensions/src/ssh/bootstrap.ts:139` — `const archive = new Uint8Array(yield* response.arrayBuffer …)`: the whole response body is buffered into memory with **no size cap, no `content-length` pre-check, and no streaming bound**. The bytes are then handed to the remote install script (`bootstrap.ts:141-152`, source type `"archive"`), which extracts them (`tar -xzf`) and runs the extracted binary's `--version` check on the remote host (`packages/gui-extensions/src/ssh/remote-cli.ts`, `stageBinary`/`verifyScript`).
- The URL is the npm registry tarball built by `RemoteCli.archiveUrl` (`remote-cli.ts:87-94`, validated target + version) — a fixed host, but the body is still network-controlled (registry mirror / proxy / compromised endpoint), and there is no integrity check between download and remote extraction either.

The asymmetry inside the same feature shows the bound is expected: the primary remote-download path is time-bounded (`curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 180`, `remote-cli.ts:125`), and `RemoteCli.latestBeta` applies `Effect.timeout("30 seconds")` to its registry read (`remote-cli.ts:143`). The local fallback has neither a time bound nor a size bound.

This is a fifth unbounded-download path of the #923 class, in a package #923 did not cover (its four paths were media, skill files, the ripgrep archive, and CodeMode fetch). Dedup: `gh` search (open + closed) for "bootstrap arrayBuffer", "ssh archive download cap", and "ResponseTooLarge" returned nothing; #923's body scopes itself to its four named paths.

## Why it matters

A stalled response hangs SSH connect indefinitely in the "downloading/uploading" stage, and an oversized or endless body grows the desktop process's memory without limit while it is buffered whole — before the archive is ever handed to the remote host, which would extract and execute whatever arrived. The legitimate tarballs are tens of megabytes, so a generous named cap costs nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The fallback download enforces a stated size cap (named constant with a comment justifying it for a CLI tarball): a declared `content-length` above the cap fails before the body is read, and a streamed/chunked body is bounded in flight, failing with an `SshFailure("install", …)`-style error instead of buffering past the cap.
- [ ] The fallback download carries a timeout comparable to the primary path's 180 s bound.
- [ ] Normal archives download, upload, and install exactly as today; the remote-download primary path is unchanged.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/gui-extensions/src/ssh/` (following `bootstrap.test.ts`/`remote-cli.test.ts` conventions) pin the over-cap behaviour for declared-length and streamed bodies.
- [ ] Out of scope: the four #923 paths, `latestBeta` (already time-bounded and schema-decoded), and any change to `archiveUrl` validation.

Phase 1 of design #992 (one numeric contract at the service boundary). Design doc: `files/designs/opencode-numeric-boundary-contract.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace.

## Task

Add `packages/core/src/util/number.ts` (alongside `record.ts`, the #865 shared guard) exporting the normalisation primitives the per-site numeric fixes have converged on, with policy choices as named parameters:

- `pageLimit(value, { default, max? })` — absent/non-finite → default; else trunc, floor 1, optional ceiling.
- `pageOffset(value)` — absent/non-finite → 0; else trunc, floor 0.
- `boundedCount(value, { default, max })` — positive integer with documented ceiling (the Messaging `chars` shape).
- `serverSeconds(value, { fallback, max, oversized: "fallback" | "clamp" })` — non-positive/non-finite → fallback; oversized → the named policy.
- `timeoutMs(value, { fallback, max })` — max defaults to 2^31-1 ms (the setTimeout cliff, #972).

Then re-implement the existing paging helpers on `pageLimit`, behaviour bit-identical: `sessionListLimit` (`packages/core/src/plugin/session-list.ts:41`, re-export preserving its name/signature — deliberately NO ceiling), `branchListLimit` (`packages/core/src/plugin/vcs/branch-list.ts:20`, ceiling 100; `packages/server` imports it by name), and the inline limit spelling in `KV.scan` (`packages/core/src/kv.ts:61`).

Module header states the admission rule: a function joins only when two or more boundary sites share its exact policy shape.

## Acceptance

- [ ] One table-driven conformance test suite covers every primitive over the shared edge table: undefined, NaN, +Infinity, -Infinity, negative, zero, fractional (incl. a value in (0,1)), exactly-at-bound, one-over-bound, unit-confused oversized (e.g. seconds value in milliseconds).
- [ ] All existing tests for session-list, branch-list and kv pass UNCHANGED (they are the behaviour contract).
- [ ] No new limits, defaults or ceilings introduced — every value comes from the existing helpers/handlers.

title: fix(core): Messaging log chars and grep context are never validated — NaN chars replaces entry text with a garbage marker, fractional context defects the read

body:
## Problem

The Messaging service's `log` read never validates two of its numeric inputs — `chars` (maximum characters per entry) and `context` (entries of context around grep matches) — even though the contract schema promises `PositiveInt` for `chars` and `NonNegativeInt` for `context` (`packages/schema/src/messaging.ts:392,384`). Sibling issues #948 and #953 cover the same service's `limit` and `offset`; neither covers `chars` or `context`, which fail in different ways:

| Input reaching the service | Result (verified this run) |
|---|---|
| `chars: -5` on a 100-char entry | `clip` returns 95 characters — the "maximum" is ignored and the entry's last 5 chars are silently dropped instead of the entry being clipped to a small page |
| `chars: NaN` | `clip` returns the literal string ` …[NaN chars]… ` as the entry's entire text — the real content is replaced by a garbage marker |
| `chars` with no ceiling (e.g. `1e9`) | Every entry is returned unclipped, defeating the per-entry cap the parameter exists to enforce (defaults are 500 / 4000 for `pull`) |
| grep `context: 1.5` | The context-selection loop iterates fractional indices (`index ± 1.5`, stepping by 1), `all[fractional]` is `undefined`, and the output stage throws `TypeError` on `entry.text` — the whole `log` call defects |
| grep `context: -1` or `NaN` | Silently behaves like `context: 0` — no error, no diagnostic, the requested context is just dropped |

Verified on main `294f03032e` (code read) plus a laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-30-msg-log-chars-context/probe.mjs`) running the verbatim `clip()` body and the verbatim grep selection loop: controls pass (`chars: 500` returns the entry intact; `context: 0` returns just the hit; `context: 1` returns hit ± 1 entry).

## Evidence (file:line, main 294f03032e)

- `packages/core/src/messaging.ts:1835` — `log()`: `const chars = input.chars ?? (op === "pull" ? 4000 : 500)` — no floor, no ceiling, no finiteness check; `chars` feeds `MessagingLog.clip(entry.text, chars)` in the output stage at `:1848`.
- `packages/core/src/messaging/log.ts:165-180` — `clip(text, chars)`: its arithmetic (`Math.ceil(chars * 0.7)`, `text.slice(0, chars)`, the marker-length loop) assumes a positive finite integer; negative/NaN inputs produce the wrong-end and garbage-marker results above. (#577 fixed `clip` exceeding its budget at small *positive* limits; unvalidated inputs reaching it are a different gap.)
- `packages/core/src/messaging.ts:1874-1879` — grep: `const context = input.context ?? 0`, then `for (let near = Math.max(0, index - context); near <= Math.min(all.length - 1, index + context); near++)` — a fractional `context` makes `near` fractional, so `selected` gains fractional keys and `all[near]` is `undefined` when entries are materialised at `:1881-1883`.
- `packages/core/src/plugin/host.ts:457` — the plugin host passes `log` input straight to the service (`log: (input) => messaging.log(input)`), with no schema decode in front of it — the same unvalidated entry path as #948/#953.
- `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/messaging.ts:181,185` — the built-in messaging tool protects `chars` (`Count` = positive int) but declares `context` as bare `Schema.Int`, so a negative `context` is actively accepted by the tool layer while fractional values are stopped there and only arrive via the plugin host.
- Contrast: `packages/core/src/kv.ts:61` shows the house pattern for a service-level numeric input — floor + clamp to a range plus an explicit NaN case.

Dedup: searched open and closed issues for "messaging log chars", "messaging clip", "log context fractional" — the only hits are #577 (clip budget at small positive limits, closed), #948 (`limit` only) and #953 (`offset` only). None covers `chars` or `context` validation.

## Why it matters

- `log` is how sessions read each other's transcripts. A `chars: NaN` silently replaces an entry's content with a `NaN chars` marker — the caller receives plausible-looking output with the actual message destroyed.
- A fractional grep `context` — easy for a caller computing context from a ratio — doesn't degrade; it throws a `TypeError` that defects the whole log call.
- An unbounded `chars` removes the only per-entry size guard on a read that can return whole transcripts, so one request can materialise far more text than the defaults intend.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Messaging service normalises `chars` and `context` at its boundary in `log()`: `chars` becomes a positive integer within a documented ceiling (NaN treated as absent/default, matching the #948 approach for `limit`); `context` becomes a non-negative integer (floored, NaN treated as 0/absent).
- [ ] `clip` is no longer reachable with a negative, fractional, or non-finite `chars` from the service, and the grep selection loop only ever indexes `all` with integers.
- [ ] The built-in messaging tool's `context` field (`tool/plugin/messaging.ts`) matches the contract (`NonNegativeInt`-equivalent) instead of bare `Schema.Int`.
- [ ] Tests in `packages/core/test` (messaging / messaging-log tests) pin: `chars: -5` and `chars: NaN` no longer produce wrong-end or garbage-marker output; grep `context: 1.5` returns the hit with integer context instead of throwing; `context: -1` behaves as the documented normalised value.
- [ ] Valid inputs behave exactly as today: default `chars` (500, 4000 for `pull`), positive integer `chars`, and `context: 0` / positive integer context.

# fix(cli): session import buffers a remote URL's whole body with no size cap — `session import https://…` reads response.text() unbounded before any validation

## Evidence (verified on main `3a1c3a0c78`, 2026-10-29, by line-level reading)

`packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/session/import.ts:17-25`: when the import source starts with `http://`/`https://`, the handler does

```ts
fetch(input.file).then((response) => {
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(...)
  return response.text()
})
```

The whole response body is buffered into a single string with **no size cap, no `content-length` pre-check, and no streaming bound**, and only afterwards is it schema-decoded (`import.ts:26`, `SessionTransfer.Data`). `fetch` follows redirects, so the effective host is not necessarily the host in the pasted URL.

This path is **not** one of the four download paths in #923 (media assets, skill files, ripgrep archive, CodeMode fetch), and it is not in #923's out-of-scope list either (own outbound request bodies, local-file reads) — the local-file branch of this same handler (`readFile`, `import.ts:24`) is the user's own file and is out of scope here; the remote branch is a response body from a server the user does not control.

## Why it matters

Importing a session from a URL is the share-link flow: the URL is exactly the kind of thing another person hands you. A hostile, compromised, or merely mistaken endpoint (or a redirect to one) serving a multi-GB body — or a slow endless stream, which `response.text()` also never bounds in time-to-cap terms — OOMs or hangs the CLI before the schema decode that would have rejected ordinary garbage gets a chance to run. The house already has the bounded pattern for untrusted bodies: the webfetch tool streams through `collectBoundedResponseBody` (`packages/core/src/tool/http-body.ts:4`) with a declared-length pre-check and a per-chunk cap, `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` = 5 MB (`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/webfetch.ts:13,78-81`), and #923 is extending that discipline to the core/ai download paths. The CLI's one remote-body read was left out of both sweeps.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The remote (`http(s)://`) branch of session import enforces a stated size cap while reading (declared `content-length` over the cap fails before the body is read where available; a streamed/chunked body is cut off at the cap), failing with a clear "session data too large" style error instead of buffering past it.
- [ ] The cap is a named constant with a comment justifying the size for session exports (legitimate exports must pass comfortably — if real exports can exceed a few MB, say what the observed/expected range is and size the cap to it).
- [ ] Local-file imports behave exactly as today; a normal-sized remote import behaves exactly as today (including the existing non-OK status error).
- [ ] A regression test pins the over-cap behaviour for the remote branch (oversized declared length and/or oversized streamed body), following the CLI package's existing test conventions; if the handler's structure makes that impractical, the bounded read is factored into a testable helper and the test pins the helper.
- [ ] Out of scope: the four #923 paths, the local-file branch, and the second `response.text()` at `import.ts:56-59` (a response from the user's own configured server, behind the import POST — note it in passing if the same helper makes bounding it free, but it is not required here).

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode, 2026-10-29 run. Cross-reference: #923 (the four core/ai unbounded download paths; this is a fifth, in the CLI, that set did not list).

body:
## Finding

PR #766 exposed `session.list` to v2 plugins, mirroring the HTTP `session.list` endpoint — but the plugin host never applies the endpoint's default page size. A plugin that calls `ctx.session.list({ parentID })` (the exact shape in the PR's own README example) with no `limit` gets **every matching session in the database**, not the newest 50 the API documents.

## Evidence

- PR: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/766 (merged, commits 2f5f7b6b / a2f4968e / 075d054d)
- Current main `2de87eac7562f4d9793cfd15abb11fed9d870eba`:
  - `packages/core/src/plugin/host.ts:610` — `sessions.list(sessionListInput(filter, query.limit, decoded?.anchor))` passes the caller's limit through untouched.
  - `packages/core/src/plugin/host.ts:745` — inside `sessionListInput`, `const bounded = limit` is a no-op rename; nothing bounds or defaults the value (the variable name shows the intent was there).
  - `packages/core/src/session/store.ts:135` — the store runs `input.limit === undefined ? query.all() : query.limit(input.limit)`, i.e. an undefined limit is an unbounded full-table read.
  - `packages/server/src/handlers/session.ts:29,72` — the HTTP handler the plugin mirrors applies `limit: ctx.query.limit ?? DefaultSessionsLimit` with `DefaultSessionsLimit = 50`.
  - `packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts` (limit field) — documented contract: "Maximum number of sessions to return. Defaults to the newest 50 sessions."
- PR #766's tests (`packages/core/test/plugin/session-list.test.ts`) list 1–2 sessions per case, so the missing default is invisible to them.

## Why it matters

- The documented pagination contract is broken on the plugin surface: the first "page" is the whole table, so `cursor.next` pagination (the README pattern) degenerates — page 1 returns everything and page 2 is empty.
- On a long-lived install the session table grows indefinitely; every no-limit plugin `list()` call materialises all of it in memory, where the HTTP path caps at 50.
- The two surfaces of the same endpoint now disagree silently, the same divergence class PR #766 set out to eliminate for cursors (it mirrored the HTTP codec precisely, but not the HTTP default).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Plugin `session.list` with no `limit` returns at most the same default page size as the HTTP handler (50), or the divergence is explicitly documented in the plugin API docs with the unbounded behaviour called out.
- [ ] A test in `packages/core/test/plugin/session-list.test.ts` (or the store tests) creates more sessions than the default page size and pins that a no-limit plugin list returns exactly the default page plus a `cursor.next` that reaches the remainder.
- [ ] Explicit `limit` behaviour (including values above the default) is unchanged.

# fix(core,ai): four download paths buffer whole response bodies with no size cap — media assets, skill files, the ripgrep archive and CodeMode fetch

## Evidence (verified on main `61b359a25b`, 2026-10-29, by line-level reading of every path below; no global HttpClient body cap exists in `packages/util` or `packages/ai/src/route/transport`)

Each of these reads a remote response body **whole into memory** with no size limit, no `content-length` pre-check, and no streaming bound:

1. **Media assets (provider-controlled URL)** — `packages/ai/src/media.ts:243-266` `download()` does `response.arrayBuffer` on `source.url`. The URL can come straight from a provider response: `packages/ai/src/protocols/anthropic-messages.ts:710,719` builds `{ type: "url", url: rawString }` sources from raw provider output. A provider (or a compromised/mitm'd endpoint) returning a URL to a multi-GB body OOMs the host process while "reading media".
2. **Skill discovery files (remote index-controlled)** — `packages/core/src/skill/discovery.ts:78-90` `download()` does `response.arrayBuffer` then writes the bytes. File URLs and the file list come from the remote skill index fetched in `pull()` (`discovery.ts:94-105`); the index body itself is also decoded unbounded via `schemaBodyJson`. Skill sources are user-configured remote indexes (`packages/core/src/config/plugin/skill.ts:91,109`), i.e. third-party servers.
3. **Ripgrep archive** — `packages/core/src/ripgrep/binary.ts:106-114`: `response.arrayBuffer`, then the bytes are written to disk and extracted. Fixed GitHub Releases URL, so the lowest-risk member, but there is still no size or integrity check between download and extraction: a truncated/oversized/wrong body is only discovered as a tar failure (or succeeds as a wrong binary).
4. **CodeMode `fetch`** — `packages/core/src/codemode/web.ts:16-27`: the fetch exposed to model-written CodeMode programs does `await response.bytes()` with only a 30 s timeout (`TIMEOUT_MS`). Thirty seconds of a fast connection is gigabytes; the executing program is model-generated, so the URL is effectively model-chosen.

## Why it matters

The house already has the bounded pattern and uses it exactly where a body is untrusted: the webfetch tool streams through `collectBoundedResponseBody` (`packages/core/src/tool/http-body.ts`, declared-size pre-check + per-chunk cap) with `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` = 5 MB (`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/webfetch.ts:13,80-81`). These four paths predate or bypass that helper, so the largest, least-trusted bodies in the system are the ones with no bound. One bad body takes down the whole opencode process (all sessions), not just the requesting feature.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the four paths enforces a stated per-path size cap (media, skill file, ripgrep archive, CodeMode fetch), failing with a clear "response too large" style error instead of buffering past the cap; a declared `content-length` above the cap fails before the body is read where the client exposes it.
- [ ] Caps are named constants with a comment justifying the size for that path, in the spirit of `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`; streaming/chunked bodies without a declared length are also bounded (not just the header check).
- [ ] Normal-sized bodies behave exactly as today (ripgrep archive ~ a few MB, typical skill files, typical media assets all pass).
- [ ] Regression tests pin the over-cap behaviour for at least the media and skill download paths (oversized declared length and oversized streamed body), following each package's existing test conventions.
- [ ] Out of scope: the already-bounded webfetch path, request bodies the process itself constructs (`aisdk.ts`, `model-request.ts` — own outbound payloads), and local-file reads (`persistent-pty/binary.bun.ts` — a local path, not a response).

title: Antigravity door: tool-carrying sessions 400 on function_declarations schema (paths.items missing field)
body:
Found 2026-11-03 during the dead-provider removal verification (code PRs #5081/#5084), pre-existing and unrelated to that change: the full path (route definitions, antigravity-direct provider block, overlay catalog, agents, tools) is leaf-identical before and after the config change.

## Symptom
Sessions routed to the design personas (design-code-pro, design-code-flash) resolve correctly to their antigravity-direct Gemini leaves and reach the upstream, which returns HTTP 400 on the session tool schema:

    GenerateContentRequest.tools[0].function_declarations[17].parameters.properties[paths].items: missing field

So tool-carrying sessions through the Antigravity door currently fail at the upstream on schema translation, while the door itself is up and reachable (the request gets far enough to be schema-rejected).

## Evidence

## Suspected area
Tool-schema translation for the Gemini GenerateContentRequest shape in the antigravity path (the fork provider and/or the door): a `paths` array property is emitted without the `items` field Gemini requires.

body:
## Finding (from PR review, never addressed)

On PR #1359 (fix(core): skip malformed V1 migration data URLs), CodeRabbit raised a **Major / Data Integrity** finding that was neither fixed nor responded to:

- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1359#discussion_r4438785826
- Reviewer: `coderabbitai[bot]`, 2026-11-02T03:56:26Z
- Location (PR diff): `packages/core/src/database/v1-migration.bun.ts:1079` (`decodeFilePayload`)

Reviewer's point, in their terms: **"Decode non-base64 data URLs as bytes."** `decodeURIComponent` decodes percent escapes as Unicode and throws for valid binary octets such as `%FF`. The catch then causes `transformSession` to omit the attachment, and the committed migration cursor prevents an automatic retry. They asked for a byte-preserving decoder that converts each `%HH` escape directly to one byte, encodes unescaped literal Unicode as UTF-8, and rejects malformed escapes, leaving the base64 path unchanged.

In other words: a *valid* non-base64 data URL carrying binary content (e.g. `data:application/octet-stream,%FF%00...`) is misclassified as a malformed data URL and the attachment is silently dropped during the V1 migration. The sibling closed issues #1358 (malformed non-base64 URL wedging the migration) and #1360 (malformed base64 silently stored as garbage) cover malformed payloads — neither covers valid percent-encoded binary payloads being lost.

## No-response evidence

- GraphQL `reviewThreads` for PR #1359: the thread containing comment r4438785826 is **unresolved**, with the single CodeRabbit comment and no replies.
- PR #1359 has a single commit, `3545784a4` (2026-11-02T03:48:28Z), which **predates** the comment (03:56:26Z). No fix commit followed; the PR merged as-is.
- No issue tracks this residual mode (searched open + closed issues 2026-11-03 for `decodeURIComponent`, `non-base64`, `data URL migration attachment`, `1359` — only #1358/#1360, the malformed-payload siblings).

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-03)

`packages/core/src/database/v1-migration.bun.ts` on main:

- Line 1058: non-base64 payloads route to `decodeFilePayload(payload)`.
- Lines 1084–1090: `decodeFilePayload` is still
  ```ts
  function decodeFilePayload(payload: string) {
    try {
      return Buffer.from(decodeURIComponent(payload)).toString("base64")
    } catch {
      return undefined
    }
  }
  ```
  `decodeURIComponent("%FF")` throws a URIError, so `decodeFilePayload` returns `undefined`, `migrateFile` takes the `invalid-data-url` path, and the attachment is replaced by the unavailable placeholder — for a payload that is a perfectly valid data URL.

## Acceptance criteria

- Non-base64 data-URL payloads are decoded byte-preservingly: each valid `%HH` escape becomes exactly one byte; unescaped literal Unicode is encoded as UTF-8; malformed escapes still take the `invalid-data-url` path.
- A regression test migrates a file part whose non-base64 data URL contains a binary percent-escape (e.g. `%FF`) and asserts the stored attachment bytes match the escaped bytes (not the unavailable placeholder).
- Existing malformed-payload behavior from #1358/#1360 (invalid-data-url marking, canonical base64 validation) is unchanged.
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why dropping such attachments is intended.

body:
# fix(desktop): renderer path guard rejects in-root files whose name starts with `..`

## Summary

`resolveRendererPath` (the desktop renderer's path-traversal guard) rejects any
resolved file whose path relative to the renderer root starts with the string
`..` — including files that are **inside** the root whose own name merely
begins with two dots (e.g. a top-level asset named `..foo.js`). The check
conflates "name starts with `..`" with "path escapes the root".

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-03 at origin/main 3e483a8cafd816f4defe64cd71b1029249dc9e9f)

`packages/desktop/src/main/windows/renderer-path.ts:10-13`:

```ts
const file = path.resolve(rendererRoot, `.${decodeURIComponent(pathname)}`)
const relative = path.relative(rendererRoot, file)
if (relative.startsWith("..") || path.isAbsolute(relative)) {
  return { kind: "rejected", file, response: new Response("Not found", { status: 404 }) }
}
```

Reproduction on the laptop probe at that head
(`bun -e` importing `resolveRendererPath` from the file above):

| pathname | result | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/..foo/bar.js` | `{"kind":"rejected", ...}` (404) | `resolved` — the file is inside the root |
| `/assets/..foo.js` | `{"kind":"resolved", ...}` | `resolved` ✓ (only the top-level case is broken) |
| `/../secrets` | `{"kind":"rejected", ...}` | `rejected` ✓ |
| `/assets/app.js` | `{"kind":"resolved", ...}` | `resolved` ✓ |

So the guard is imprecise exactly at the root level: `path.relative` returns
`..foo/bar.js` for an in-root file, and `startsWith("..")` treats it as an
escape. The existing tests (`packages/desktop/src/main/windows/renderer-path.test.ts`)
cover malformed encodings, a valid asset, and one traversal (`/%2e%2e/secrets`)
— no in-root `..`-prefixed name case.

Caller: `packages/desktop/src/main/windows/protocol.ts:88` — a `rejected`
result is served as 404, so such an asset would silently never load.

## Why it matters

This helper is the renderer's only traversal boundary; its predicate should
mean exactly "escapes the root", in both directions. Today it over-rejects
(a correctness bug: a legitimately bundled asset whose name starts with `..`
at the top level 404s with no diagnostic beyond a rejected-path log line),
and the imprecision invites future edits that loosen the wrong side of the
check. The precise predicate is the standard one: escape means
`relative === ".."`, or `relative` starts with `".." + path.sep`, or
`relative` is absolute.

## Acceptance criteria

- `resolveRendererPath(root, "/..foo/bar.js")` (and `/..foo.js`) returns
  `resolved` with the in-root file path.
- Traversal still rejected: `/../secrets`, `/%2e%2e/secrets`, `/assets/../../secrets`,
  and a `..` segment that lands exactly on the parent (`/assets/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/x`)
  all return `rejected` with the 404 response.
- New regression tests in `renderer-path.test.ts` pin both directions
  (in-root `..`-prefixed name resolves; exact-parent and multi-segment
  escapes reject), including on the separator form the platform produces.
- `cd packages/desktop && bun test` stays green (169 tests at the filing head:
  168 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail).
- No behaviour change for malformed encodings (still `malformed` → 404).

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues 2026-11-03 for `renderer-path`,
`renderer path traversal`: no existing filing covers this guard or the
`..`-prefix false positive.

title: services.opencode: a module with a single enable for the standing serve server
body:
Companion to the mcpx daemon modules (code#4801 chain, landed 2026-11-03). Drew's design extension (2026-11-03): each level of the chain offers an option that handles its service creation as a single enable switch, cascading upward — set services.openchamber.enable = true and all three services (mcpx, opencode, openchamber) are created, with no consumer-side reaching into package overrides/unwrapped.

This repo's slice: author services.opencode platform modules (nixosModules / homeManagerModules / darwinModules.opencode, sitting beside the mcpx re-exports from #1502) that run the standing server as a user service:
- services.opencode.enable (the single switch), .package (default: this flake's opencode build), .port (default 13420, the standing server's port), .hostname, .environment / extra settings.
- The service runs opencode serve in its --service mode (publishes its per-start password to ~/.local/state/opencode/service-prod.json — the file OpenChamber's module reads at start; never anything secret in the store).
- systemd user unit on NixOS/home-manager-Linux; launchd user agent on darwin (home-manager + nix-darwin flavors), mirroring the mcpx modules' shapes and restart semantics.
- The module also enables the daemon below it by default: services.mcpx.enable = lib.mkDefault true (the fork's opencode talks to the mcpx daemon; the mcpx module is already re-exported here).
- The OPENCODE_DB / TMPDIR pins that dezren39/nix currently applies via a consumer-side package wrapper belong here as service environment (options or fixed env in the unit), so service consumers stop wrapping the package themselves.

Verification: eval each platform module; a config with only services.opencode.enable = true renders the serve unit/agent with the right command, port, and the mcpx enable cascading.

body:
## Problem

`packages/protocol`'s `check:generated` is not run by any workflow — and `packages/protocol/openapi.json` is the source document the wired www check copies verbatim, so drift in the protocol document itself passes every wired gate.

## Evidence (verified this run, 2026-11-03, clean laptop probe at ae4b9776f85c)

- `packages/protocol/package.json:25` defines `"check:generated": "bun run script/generate-openapi.ts --check"`, which regenerates the OpenAPI document from `ClientApi` (`packages/protocol/script/generate-openapi.ts`) and fails if `packages/protocol/openapi.json` differs.
- No workflow runs it: `grep -rn "packages/protocol" .github/workflows/` returns nothing, and `.github/workflows/test.yml` wires `check:generated` only for `packages/client` ("Check generated client") and `services/www` ("Check generated documentation").
- The check is currently green: `bun run check:generated` in `packages/protocol` exits 0 at ae4b9776f85c. This is a wiring gap, not a current drift.
- Why the wired checks cannot catch this drift: `services/www/script/generate-openapi.ts:3` sets its source to `packages/protocol/openapi.json` and the www `generate`/`check:generated` only copy/compare that file — they never regenerate from the API. If `packages/protocol/openapi.json` drifts from `ClientApi`, the www copies faithfully propagate the stale document and their check stays green; the client check covers the client transport, not this document.
- This pipeline drifts repeatedly in practice: #660 (protocol HttpApi shape changed, no documents regenerated), #829 and #1498 (www copies stale), #1493 (client stale). Every one of those was caught by a wired check or by hand; a protocol-side drift has no net at all.

## Why it matters

`packages/protocol/openapi.json` is the canonical OpenAPI document for the server API (www publishes copies of it). The one check that verifies it against the actual `ClientApi` definition runs nowhere in CI, so the next protocol change that forgets to regenerate lands silently — and the downstream wired checks certify the stale document as current.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A CI step runs `bun run check:generated` in `packages/protocol` alongside the existing client/www generated checks in `.github/workflows/test.yml` (Linux), or an equivalent wired location.
- [ ] `bun run check:workflows` still passes after the workflow change.
- [ ] The new step is verified to fail when `packages/protocol/openapi.json` is deliberately made stale (or the step's command is shown to be the package's own check, which exits 1 on a stale document per `script/generate-openapi.ts`).

## Generated client is stale on main — `check:generated` red (route `system` field + completions 404/503 statuses missing from the committed client)

Verified 2026-11-03 on a clean laptop primary at main `e21f70672a3f16323a73bdd3abda374a2fde21ec`:

```
cd packages/client && bun run check:generated
# exits 1 — regeneration rewrites two committed files:
#   packages/client/src/promise/generated/client.ts  (12 lines changed)
#   packages/client/src/promise/generated/types.ts   (1 line added)
```

The same check passes for `packages/protocol` (`bun run check:generated` clean), so the protocol/OpenAPI layer is current and only the client generation step was skipped.

### The drift, item by item

1. **Route `system` prompt missing from client types.** `packages/schema/src/config/model-routes.ts:272` declares `system: Schema.String` ("System prompt this route carries…", persona routes #1413), added by commit `a7bfbbcdcd` (feat(routes): routes carry a system prompt + façade route failover). That commit updated the schema and `packages/protocol/openapi.json`, but the regenerated client type was never committed:

   ```diff
   export type ConfigModelRoutes = {
     [x: string]: {
       name?: string
   +   system?: string
       targets: Array<ConfigModelRouteTarget>;
   ```

   Effect: a client consumer cannot set or read a route's system prompt through the typed promise client even though the schema and the server accept it.

2. **Completions `/v1/models` endpoints under-declare their error statuses.** `packages/protocol/src/groups/completions.ts:16,30,44` declare `error: [InvalidRequestError, ServiceUnavailableError, LocationNotFoundError]` for the three models endpoints, and the committed `packages/protocol/openapi.json` lists responses `200/400/401/404/503` for `GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{id}` and `GET /v1/models/{provider}/{model}` (changed in commit `830a62735a`, fix(facade): advertise configured model_routes at /v1/models). The committed generated client still declares only `[400, 401]` for all three:

   ```diff
   -          { method: "GET", path: `/v1/models`, successStatus: 200, declaredStatuses: [400, 401], empty: false },
   +          { method: "GET", path: `/v1/models`, successStatus: 200, declaredStatuses: [400, 401, 404, 503], empty: false },
   ```

   (same change for `/v1/models/${id}` and `/v1/models/${provider}/${model}`.) Effect: the generated transport does not declare the 404 (unknown model id — the endpoints' own docs promise "Unknown ids answer 404") or 503 responses these endpoints can return.

The committed generated client was last regenerated in `a10f00161e` (#1410), before both source changes.

### Why CI did not catch it

`.github/workflows/test.yml` does have a "Check generated client" step (line 284, `working-directory: packages/client`), but it sits in the `unit` job *after* the "Run unit tests" step (line 248) with no `if: always()`, so any unit-test failure earlier in that job skips it — and the unit suite has been red on main for unrelated reasons (#1484). This is the sixth recurrence of this exact class (#450, #483, #676, #813, #1365 were the same failure with different fields). Triage should confirm the masking mechanism; if step ordering is it, moving the generated checks ahead of (or independent of) the unit-test step is part of the durable fix.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cd packages/client && bun run check:generated` exits 0 on main (regenerated `client.ts`/`types.ts` committed; regeneration produces no further diff).
- [ ] Client types expose `ConfigModelRoutes` entries with `system?: string`; the three `/v1/models` calls declare `[400, 401, 404, 503]`.
- [ ] `packages/client` tests pass; no hand-edits inside generated files (output of `bun run generate` only).
- [ ] The masking mechanism is identified on this issue; if it is the test.yml step ordering, the generated-client/documentation checks no longer sit behind the unit-test step in the same job (or the recurrence is otherwise explained and dispositioned).

# fix(ai): check:numeric-boundaries red on main — Antigravity token-refresh content-length parse (PR #1474) has no gate disposition

## Summary

`bun run check:numeric-boundaries` fails on current main (`e520ea5982`) with a new, undispositioned candidate introduced by the merged fix for #1469 (PR #1474, commit `aac38b202b`). This is distinct from #1477, which covers the other current candidate (`packages/core/src/systemone.ts:200`); fixing #1477 alone will not make the gate green.

## Evidence (verified this run, two sources)

Gate run on the laptop primary at main `e520ea5982`:

```
$ bun run check:numeric-boundaries
Unlisted numeric-boundary candidate at packages/ai/src/providers/antigravity-auth.ts:186:
  const parsedSize = contentLength ? Number.parseInt(contentLength, 10) : undefined
  Convert it through the shared primitives (packages/core/src/util/number.ts, #993), or add its disposition to script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt.
Unlisted numeric-boundary candidate at packages/core/src/systemone.ts:200:   <- already filed as #1477
error: script "check:numeric-boundaries" exited with code 1
```

- `packages/ai/src/providers/antigravity-auth.ts:185-189` (also read back via `gh api` raw contents, identical bytes):

```ts
const contentLength = response.headers["content-length"]
const parsedSize = contentLength ? Number.parseInt(contentLength, 10) : undefined
const declaredSize =
  parsedSize !== undefined && Number.isSafeInteger(parsedSize) && parsedSize >= 0 ? parsedSize : undefined
if (declaredSize !== undefined && declaredSize > TOKEN_REFRESH_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES) return yield* Effect.fail(tooLarge())
```

- `grep antigravity script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt` → 0 entries (also 0 via the GitHub API copy of the allowlist).
- `git log -S 'Number.parseInt(contentLength'` → introduced in `aac38b202b` "fix(ai): bound Antigravity token-refresh fetch (#1469) (#1474)".
- Dedup: open/recently-closed search for "numeric-boundaries antigravity" / "antigravity-auth" returns no issue covering this candidate; #1477 names only the systemone conversion.

## Why it matters

- The regression net (#995, design #992) exists so every bare string→number conversion on externally supplied input carries an explicit disposition. Right now the gate is red on main for a second, untracked reason, which trains everyone to ignore it — and red-gate noise is exactly how the next genuinely unsafe conversion slips in.
- The conversion itself is largely defended downstream (safe-integer + non-negative check, `> TOKEN_REFRESH_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` (64 KiB) early fail at :189, and the streamed body is independently capped in `readBoundedTokenResponse`), so this is probably *safe by construction* — but `Number.parseInt` still truncates trailing garbage (`"123abc"` → 123, per the gate's own header rationale), so the disposition should be a conscious call, not silence: either record the safe-by-construction reason in the allowlist, or tighten the parse (e.g. accept only an all-digits header) / route it through a shared primitive.
- The header is remote-server-controlled (the OAuth token endpoint response), i.e. exactly the externally supplied input class the net was built for.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `antigravity-auth.ts:186` is dispositioned: allowlist entry with the safe-by-construction reasoning, OR the parse is tightened/converted so no bare `parseInt` on the header remains.
- [ ] `bun run check:numeric-boundaries` no longer lists the antigravity-auth candidate (the gate may still list the systemone candidate until #1477 lands; after both, the gate exits 0).
- [ ] Existing Antigravity tests still pass: `packages/ai` `bun test test/provider/antigravity-auth.test.ts test/provider/antigravity.test.ts` (17 pass at `e520ea5982`), including the oversize/stalled refresh cases from #1469.
- [ ] No behavior change to the 64 KiB cap or the 15 s refresh deadline from #1474.

body:
Filed from PR #1479 review disposition (task 6715, #1478). The title-generation probe-claim settlement landed in #1479; CodeRabbit's review of that PR surfaced the same claim-release class in other resolution consumers and paths, which were out of #1478's packet scope (title path only; runner claim semantics explicitly excluded). Collecting them here so they are tracked, not lost:

1. Compaction: `session/compaction.ts` resolves the compaction model (spending a due bench probe claim) and can return `NOTHING_TO_COMPACT` / fail before any request runs without releasing the claim (PR #1479 thread 4450763474).
2. Resolver load failure: when a picked target fails to load in `model-resolver.ts`, `ModelRoute.failed` without a credential clears only the target-scope claim; the credential-scope claim from the same pick stays set (thread 4450763483).
3. Runner failover: the runner settles only the serving credential; when `routing.probeClaim` names a different (snapshot) credential, that claim stays outstanding, including after failover replaces `routing` (thread 4450763521).
4. Title target-scope claim on credential failure: `ModelRoute.failed` with a credentialID benches only the credential; whether the target-scope claim from the same resolution also needs release should be decided together with (3) so title and runner settlement stay mirrored (thread 4450763510).
5. Title interruption during request preparation: stream interruption already releases via `SessionTitle.attempt` settlement, but interruption during `context.request.title` preparation runs no settlement (thread 4450763519).
6. Claim ownership token: `releaseBenchProbe` identifies a claim by its millisecond `claimedAt`; two resolutions in the same millisecond share the value, so a stale release could clear a newer claim. A unique claim token would remove the collision class (thread 4450763491).
7. Title timing: `startedAt` in `SessionTitle.attempt` is taken before plugin-hook preparation, so preparation time counts toward firstTokenMs/responseMs samples (thread 4450763499).

Each item should be verified against current main before fixing; several may already be covered by bench expiry semantics by design.

_agent-note:v1 — agent: repo-worker-opencode, task 6715, PR #1479 review disposition_

## Acceptance criteria

- Bench probe claims are released on every non-title exit path (error, timeout, early return), not only the title path.
- A leaked claim can no longer wedge subsequent bench probes for the same resource.
- Tests cover at least one non-title exit path releasing the claim.

body:
# fix(ci): agents.yml sets timeout-minutes on a reusable-workflow caller job — workflow fails at startup, and check:workflows cannot see it

## Evidence (verified on main `eeebf4143d`, 2026-11-02)

`.github/workflows/agents.yml:44-46` — the repo's only job-level reusable-workflow call now carries a key GitHub does not allow on a caller job:

```yaml
jobs:
  scheduled:
    uses: developing-today/code/.github/workflows/pm-scheduled.yml@main
    timeout-minutes: 60
```

Added by commit `fb06892c2d` ("ci: add job timeouts to agents.yml", PR #1480, merged as `eeebf4143d` minutes before this filing).

GitHub's reusable-workflow reference is explicit about the caller job's allowed keywords: "When you call a reusable workflow, you can only use the following keywords in the job containing the call: `jobs.<job_id>.name`, `uses`, `with`, `secrets`, `strategy`, `needs`, `if`, `concurrency`, `permissions`, `cache-mode`" (docs.github.com, "Reusing workflow configurations"). `timeout-minutes` is not among them — a caller job has no steps of its own, so there is nothing for it to time out; the called workflow owns its jobs' timeouts.

Observed behavior since the change:

- Actions run `41566885724` (push, head `eeebf4143d`, `.github/workflows/agents.yml`): conclusion **failure**, and the run's jobs list is **empty** — the workflow never started a job. `gh run view` reports: "This run likely failed because of a workflow file issue."
- The scheduled agent dispatches this workflow exists for (bolt / palette / suggestions slots, per the file's own header) therefore do not run at all on this revision.

The repo's own gate cannot catch this class:

- `bun run check:workflows` on the same main exits **0** ("All 29 workflows … follow the workflow policies").
- `script/check-workflows.ts` (`workflowViolations`) skips caller jobs entirely: `if ("uses" in job) continue`. Its header even documents why the exemption exists — "the caller cannot set `timeout-minutes` on such a job" — but the gate only *exempts* caller jobs from the timeout requirement; it never flags a forbidden key placed on one. test.yml runs this gate on every push to main, so CI is green on a workflow file GitHub rejects at startup.
- `agents.yml` is the only workflow in the repo with a job-level `uses:` (grep over `.github/workflows/*.yml`), so today this blind spot has exactly one live instance — this one.

Related: #1406 (the workflow-policy gate this extends), #970 (prior startup-failure class in this repo's workflows), #61 / #1326 / #1184 (the timeout-minutes convention that motivated the change — it applies to jobs with steps, not to caller jobs).

## Why it matters

A well-intentioned timeout sweep silently disabled the repo's scheduled-agent dispatcher: the workflow fails validation before any job exists, so there is no failing job to alert on — the runs just read "failure" with an empty jobs list. And the policy gate built in #1406 to keep workflow files valid-by-construction is blind to exactly the key-placement error that caused it, so the same mistake can recur in any future caller workflow.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.github/workflows/agents.yml`: the `scheduled` caller job no longer sets `timeout-minutes` (or any other key outside GitHub's caller-job allowlist); if a dispatch timeout is wanted, it is set on the jobs inside the called workflow (`developing-today/code` `pm-scheduled.yml`), not here.
- [ ] A `workflow_dispatch` (or push) run of `agents.yml` on the fixed revision starts jobs instead of failing at startup with an empty jobs list.
- [ ] `script/check-workflows.ts` flags non-allowlisted keys on reusable-workflow caller jobs (at minimum `timeout-minutes`, `runs-on`, `steps`, `env`, `defaults`), with coverage in `script/check-workflows.test.ts`; the gate fails on the pre-fix `agents.yml` and passes on the fixed tree.
- [ ] `bun run check:workflows` passes on the fixed tree, and no other workflow's caller jobs (if any appear) regress.

body:
## Finding (from PR review, never addressed)

Title generation can spend a bench's sole half-open probe claim on a model that is never attempted, and the title path never settles a claim it does spend — so a recovered route leaf stays excluded from normal selection until the bench expires, potentially many hours later.

Codex (P2), 2026-11-01T17:06:49Z, on PR #1305: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1305#discussion_r4436566906 — "Claim bench probes only for requests that will report an outcome" (`packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts:716`): `SessionContext.selectTitle` resolves the session's primary model before selecting a preferred title model; if the preferred model succeeds, the primary is never attempted. Even when the primary is used, `SessionTitle.attempt` records usage but never calls `ModelRoute.completed` or `ModelRoute.failed`. Defer the claim to actual request execution, or ensure every resolution consumer releases or settles its claim.

## No-response evidence

- PR #1305 (fix(core): half-open probe at quota reset and active benches in route stats, #1123) had a single commit (645378c63f, 2026-11-01T17:03:08Z) and merged 2026-11-01T17:06:07Z; the Codex review of that head posted at 17:06:49Z with no reply.
- The review thread is unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads`, checked 2026-11-03) and contains only the Codex comment.

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-03 via `gh api` raw reads)

- `packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts` on main (:844-850): resolution spends the claim when selection picks a target — `ModelRoute.claimBenchProbe(target, undefined, now)` (and per-credential) inside the resolve path; the tentative-admission comment at :779-785 confirms claims are spent at resolution, not at request execution.
- `packages/core/src/session/context.ts` on main (:106-133): `selectTitle` still resolves the primary first, then resolves a preferred title model — two resolutions per title generation, each able to spend a probe claim, while at most one model is ever attempted.
- `packages/core/src/session/title.ts` on main (:50-125): `SessionTitle.attempt` records usage (`ModelRoute.recordRequest`, usage events) but never calls `ModelRoute.completed`/`ModelRoute.failed` or any claim release/settlement.

## Acceptance criteria

- A probe claim is spent only for a request that actually executes and reports an outcome, or every resolution consumer (title generation included) releases/settles claims for models it does not attempt.
- A regression test covers title generation resolving a primary and a preferred model after a quota reset: the unattempted model's bench is not left with a probe in flight.
- Or: a documented decision on this issue.

Found by the pr-comment-review job from an unaddressed PR review comment.

body:
## Problem

`bun script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` exits 1 on clean main `d96751c983156833a148aab264a453f0554270ba` with exactly one unlisted candidate, in the new systemone (Clef façade) file:

```
Unlisted numeric-boundary candidate at packages/core/src/systemone.ts:200:
  const configured = Number(process.env.CLEF_PROXY_DATA_PATH_TIMEOUT_MS)
```

The code (packages/core/src/systemone.ts:199-202):

```ts
const dataPathTimeoutMs = () => {
  const configured = Number(process.env.CLEF_PROXY_DATA_PATH_TIMEOUT_MS)
  return Number.isSafeInteger(configured) && configured > 0 ? configured : 30_000
}
```

## Why it is a bug, not just a missing disposition

The comment above the function (lines ~195-198) calls this "the door's single deadline covering the upstream fetch AND the response-body read (30s…)". The value feeds `Effect.timeoutOrElse({ duration: dataPathTimeoutMs(), … })` at systemone.ts:247-251.

The check rejects NaN / non-integers / non-positives (those fall back to 30_000), but there is **no upper bound**: any positive safe integer passes. `CLEF_PROXY_DATA_PATH_TIMEOUT_MS=86400000000` (1000 days) — or any value up to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` — is accepted, which effectively disables the deadline the comment promises: a stalled or slow-dripping Cloudflare gateway upstream then hangs the systemone data path for that long instead of timing out at a sane bound.

The shared primitive for exactly this exists in the same package: `timeoutMs(value, { fallback, max? })` in `packages/core/src/util/number.ts:83` — non-finite/non-positive → fallback, otherwise truncated and clamped to `max` (defaulting to the `SET_TIMEOUT_MAX_MS` timer cliff, #993). This site bypasses it with a hand-rolled check that omits the clamp half of the contract.

`grep` of `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt` shows no entry for systemone.ts.

## Why it matters

- `check:numeric-boundaries` is red on main — every PR inherits the failing gate and the net stops catching new bare conversions (precedent for this failure mode: #995/#1294 were filed to build/extend this net).
- An operator-set (fleet-inherited, per the comment: "the door's env override is honored under its own name so a fleet-wide setting keeps working") timeout value can silently remove the only deadline on this data path; the body read is byte-capped at 5 MiB (line 204) but nothing else bounds time.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `dataPathTimeoutMs` converts through the shared primitive (`timeoutMs` from `packages/core/src/util/number.ts`) or an equivalent that clamps to a named maximum, preserving: unset/invalid/non-positive → 30_000 fallback, and the env name `CLEF_PROXY_DATA_PATH_TIMEOUT_MS` unchanged
- [ ] A regression test (in `packages/core/test/systemone.test.ts` or a sibling) covers an oversized env value being clamped/falling back, plus the normal override case
- [ ] `bun script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` exits 0 on main; if any allowlist entry is added it states the conversion used, not a bare exemption
- [ ] No change to the 5 MiB body cap or the 504 timeout error mapping at systemone.ts:255-260

Related: #992 (design), #993/#995 (primitives + this net), #1077 (the same timer-cliff class for MCP timeouts). Deduped against open and recently closed issues this run — the open numeric items (#994, #996) cover other sites.

title: fix(console): inference proxy drops the incoming request signal — a client disconnect no longer cancels the upstream fetch (#1187)

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
## Finding

PR #1187 added a headers deadline to `proxyInference` by passing an explicit `signal: controller.signal` to the inference service-binding fetch. That explicit signal **replaces** the signal the forwarded request already carried: `forwarded = new Request(destination, request)` inherits the incoming request's signal, and a `fetch(input, init)` call uses `init.signal` when one is given. Before #1187 the call was `.fetch(forwarded, { redirect: "manual" })`, so a client disconnect aborted the upstream fetch; after #1187 it no longer does. A disconnected client's upstream inference call now runs until the headers deadline — up to 300 s on generation POSTs (`INFERENCE_GENERATION_HEADERS_TIMEOUT_MS`) — spending upstream generation/billing for nobody.

CodeRabbit raised exactly this as a Major on PR #1187 (comment 4435158406, 2026-11-01T09:55:34Z) and, after the generation-deadline fix landed, replied on the final head (comment 4435322001, 2026-11-01T10:56:43Z): "This thread concerns a separate issue: incoming request cancellation… Combine both signals… This finding remains open." The PR merged (87af48213825828e666b5fe23d23eea07a9a10cd) without the composition, and the thread was marked resolved without the change.

## Evidence

- PR #1187: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1187 (merged 2026-11-01T11:30:33Z, head 7fba8c9c8f17ddac4bae99a04c211b23a495aa18)
- CodeRabbit Major: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1187#discussion_r4435158406 ; rebuttal on the final head: comment 4435322001 ("This finding remains open")
- Current main d96751c983156833a148aab264a453f0554270ba, `packages/console/app/src/lib/inference-proxy.ts` (~:65-72): the fetch still runs as `.fetch(forwarded, { redirect: "manual", signal: controller.signal })` — no composition with `request.signal` anywhere in the file.
- Pre-#1187 call (parent of the PR's first head): `.fetch(forwarded, { redirect: "manual" })` — cancellation propagated through the forwarded Request's inherited signal.

## Why it matters

Every Zen/Go route goes through this proxy. Client disconnects are routine (users close tabs, CLIs are Ctrl-C'd, load balancers time out); each one now leaves the upstream inference service generating — and billing — for up to 5 minutes with no consumer, and holds the worker-side fetch open for the same window. It is a regression in cancellation behavior introduced by a PR whose purpose was bounding, i.e. the bound it added silently removed the bound that already existed.

## Acceptance criteria

- `proxyInference` composes the incoming request signal with the headers-deadline controller signal (e.g. `AbortSignal.any([request.signal, controller.signal])`, or an equivalent listener) so an incoming abort cancels the upstream fetch at any point before headers arrive, on both GET lookup and generation POST routes.
- The headers deadlines behave exactly as today when the incoming request does not abort: pre-headers stall settles as the existing 503, generation POSTs keep the 300 s headers bound, and a started streaming body is not cut.
- New regression test in `packages/console/app/src/lib/inference-proxy.test.ts`: aborting the incoming request aborts the signal observed by the mocked INFERENCE binding before the deadline (the existing suite's mock already captures `init.signal`).
- Existing inference-proxy tests pass; the `check:bounded-http` allowlist disposition for `inference-proxy.ts` is refreshed if the call line changes.

body:
# fix(ai): Antigravity token refresh fetch has no deadline, response body unbounded — check:bounded-http is red on main

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode, 2026-11-02. Verified on main `0d94cb4a2bb0af2746edf0da80eb35ef2b4ccd39`.

## Evidence

The Antigravity credential bridge added in PR #1457 (commit `a11475960a`, for #1414) refreshes the agy CLI's OAuth access token in `packages/ai/src/providers/antigravity-auth.ts`:

- `:174` — `refresh()` calls `fetch("https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token", { method: "POST", headers, body })` with **no `signal`** — no deadline of any kind. A stalled or slow-dripping token endpoint hangs the refresh forever; `loadToken()`'s shared `inflight` promise then blocks every subsequent Antigravity auth attempt in the process.
- `:179` — `const text = await response.text()` reads the **whole response body unbounded** before the status check / `JSON.parse`. A hostile or broken endpoint (or a MITM'd connection) can stream an arbitrarily large body into memory.

This is exactly the class design #1127 ("bounded by default") and the `check:bounded-http` regression gate (#1129) exist to catch — and the gate catches it:

```
$ bun run script/check-bounded-http.ts   # on clean main 2d717bae63, laptop
Unlisted bounded-http candidate at packages/ai/src/providers/antigravity-auth.ts:174:
  const response = await fetch("https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token", {
Unlisted bounded-http candidate at packages/ai/src/providers/antigravity-auth.ts:179:
  const text = await response.text()
GATE_EXIT:1
```

These are the only two unlisted candidates in the repo — `packages/ai/src` is in the gate's `SCAN_ROOTS` (`script/check-bounded-http.ts`), and there is no allowlist entry for this file. So the gate is red on main until this site is bounded at the site (the correct fix) — an allowlist disposition of "unbounded, tracked here" would green the gate but leave the hang/memory bug in place; the site fix is small and preferred.

## Precedent / how to bound it

- Sibling OAuth token flows in core use the bounded pair, e.g. `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/chatgpt.ts:554-558`: fetch with a composed `signal`, body via `readBoundedResponseText(response, oauthMaxResponseBytes, …)`.
- The dependency-free helpers live in `packages/util/src/http-body.ts` (`deadlineSignal`, `readBoundedResponseText`, `readExcerptResponseText`). Note `@opencode/ai` does **not** currently depend on `@opencode/util` (its workspace deps are `@opencode/http-recorder` and `@opencode/schema`), so the fix either adds that workspace dependency or follows the #1373 http-recorder precedent of a small local conforming bounded reader. The error path only needs the first 200 chars (`text.slice(0, 200)` at :180) — excerpt semantics fit the non-200 branch; the 200 branch parses a small JSON token document, so a modest cap (token responses are ~1 KB; cf. the 1 MiB caps used for other OAuth JSON reads, or smaller) suffices.
- The same file already bounds its other external read correctly: the keyring `execFile` at :85 carries `timeout: 15_000, maxBuffer: 1 << 20` — the fetch is the outlier.

## Why it matters

1. **Availability:** this is on the auth path for the new antigravity-direct provider (#1414). One stalled token endpoint wedges Antigravity auth process-wide (shared `inflight`), with no timeout to recover.
2. **Memory safety:** unbounded `.text()` on a network response is the exact failure the #1127 contract and 60+ prior per-site issues eliminated everywhere else.
3. **CI:** `check:bounded-http` is red on main right now; every subsequent PR inherits the red gate and the signal value of the regression net erodes (cf. #1188, the last allowlist-drift red-gate incident).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The token-refresh `fetch` in `packages/ai/src/providers/antigravity-auth.ts` carries a deadline (e.g. `deadlineSignal` / `AbortSignal.timeout` with a named constant consistent with the file's existing 15s keyring timeout class).
- [ ] The response body is read through a bounded or excerpt reader with a named byte cap; an oversize body fails (or truncates, for the error excerpt) instead of buffering unboundedly.
- [ ] `bun run script/check-bounded-http.ts` exits 0 on the resulting tree with **no** new "unbounded" allowlist disposition for this file.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/antigravity.test.ts` (or a sibling test file) cover: refresh succeeds against a stubbed token endpoint, and an oversize / stalled response is rejected by the cap/deadline rather than buffered/hung.
- [ ] Existing antigravity provider tests pass; the keyring read path (:85) is unchanged.

Dedup: title/keyword search over open + closed issues for "antigravity-auth", "antigravity token", and "bounded-http" found no issue covering this site — #1436 (github/ tree scan gap), #1385/#1386/#1388 (other unbounded surfaces), and #1188 (closed, api.ts allowlist drift) are distinct. #1418 is an unrelated main-broken watch-job failure at a different head SHA.
