## Finding

Issue #1151 (OPEN, a step of the OpenAI-façade design from PR #1156) is scoped to add a **new** demotion config key — `experimental.model_route_demotion {threshold, window_ms}` with defaults 3 / 14400000, wired into `ModelRoute.configure({quota})`. That config surface **already exists**: PR #1142 (merged 2026-10-31, merge commit 855ec25f53e2b2a28ef2ffe2ceac396db2bfc753, closing issue #1141) shipped quota demotion as config in `experimental.model_route_settings.demotion`.

Implementing issue #1151 as written would leave **two config keys controlling the same demotion threshold and window**, with no stated precedence — an operator setting one would silently not get the behaviour the other implies.

## Evidence

- Current main (ac3e374eb79203452f0c13513adaf7542870f564), `packages/schema/src/config/model-routes.ts:383-397`: `Settings.Demotion` class — `after` ("Quota errors within the window that demote a target… Defaults to 3", capped at 50), `windowMs` ("How long a quota error counts toward demotion. Defaults to 14400000 (4h)"), `factor` (defaults to 0.01). Same class is seated as `demotion` in the route `Settings` at model-routes.ts:474 ("Quota-error demotion").
- PR #1142's body: `DEFAULT_SETTINGS.quota.demoteAfter` → `demotion.after` (default 3) and `DEFAULT_SETTINGS.quota.windowMs` → `demotion.windowMs` (default 14_400_000), feeding the existing Settings store via `ModelRoute.onSettingsConfig`.
- Issue #1151's scope text proposes the identical pair under a different name and shape: `experimental.model_route_demotion {threshold, window_ms}` (defaults 3 / 14400000) wired into `ModelRoute.configure({quota})`.
- The design PR #1156 (merged 2026-11-01, merge commit 775632b96ae79fd1231b9acf80fe96edcb9ca094) §6 describes demotion-as-config as "replacing both hardcoded copies (route proxy lines 86-87 and the in-process defaults, same values)" — but PR #1142 had already replaced the in-process defaults copy the day before the design merged, so that premise is stale.
- Issue #1140 (CLOSED) additionally nested routing config under `experimental.routes.*` with a compat shim for the flat keys, so issue #1151's flat top-level key location is stale on placement as well as on duplication.
- Dedupe: issue searches for `model_route_demotion` / `model_route_settings` (all states, 2026-11-02) return issues #1141/#1142/#1151/#1423/#1424 and docs issue #1322 — none names this duplication conflict.

## What is still genuinely open in issue #1151

Only the parts PR #1142 did not do: demotion counts read from the `route_attempt` ledger within the window (in-process map as hot cache only), and façade traffic sharing the same demotion behaviour as session traffic. Those should be re-scoped onto the existing `model_route_settings.demotion` settings (in their current nested location), not a second key.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Issue #1151 is re-scoped (title/body) to the ledger-backed counting + façade-sharing work only, referencing the existing demotion settings as the single config source — or closed as partially duplicate with a successor issue carrying only that remainder.
- [ ] No second demotion config key (`model_route_demotion` or equivalent) is added; any new wiring reads the existing `demotion.after` / `demotion.windowMs` settings.
- [ ] The façade design spec (`specs/2026-11-01T04-10-00Z_design_openai-facades.md`, §6/§11 step 5) is corrected to point at the shipped settings instead of describing demotion-as-config as unbuilt.
- [ ] A test or docs note pins which single config location controls demotion threshold/window for both session and façade traffic.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #1142 and PR #1156 (batch PRs #1118–#1156, 2026-11-02).

# fix(core): two policy consumers still process-global after the #1423 Location scoping — tuning quota ceiling and threshold-derived balance holds

Follow-up to #1423 / PR #1432, filed from Codex re-review findings on PR #1432's merged-with-main head `2c3016a3ad` (findings 4448854587 and 4448854593). PR #1432 scopes the model_route_settings reader per Location; these two consumers sit outside that reader's reach and were deliberately NOT folded into #1432 (each needs its own design pass and tests) — they are tracked here so #1432 can land.

## Finding 1 — scheduled tuning ignores the Location's quotaGate ceiling
`ModelRouteTuning.quotaResetCeilingMs()` calls `currentConstants()` without a Location, and `review()` predictions and note adjustments use that helper without an override. With two active Locations configuring `quotaGate.maxMs` to one hour, a provider message or tuning note stating a reset in three days installs a three-day skip instead of the configured one-hour maximum once the second Location registers.
Fix shape: thread the owning Location (or its resolved ceiling) from the model-routes plugin into the tuning schedule and review paths.

## Finding 2 — threshold-derived balance holds are not Location-scoped
Locations A and B share a credential but configure `balanceDeadThreshold` to 1 and 0.1 respectively. A observing a balance of 0.5 creates a `balanceHold` in the process-global, credential-keyed `credentialQuota` map; B's `credentialQuotaBlocked()` then returns an indefinite block before consulting B's threshold, even though that balance is usable under B's policy, and feeding the same balance through B cannot correct it (`observeCredentialQuotaState()` returns early unless the held balance increases or its grant changes).
Fix shape: keep policy-derived holds Location-scoped, or preserve enough provenance to evaluate them under the judging Location's policy — without weakening genuine attempt-reported exhaustion holds.

## Acceptance
- Tuning schedule/review paths judge quota-reset ceilings with the owning Location's `quotaGate.maxMs`.
- A balance hold created under one Location's `balanceDeadThreshold` does not block a Location whose threshold admits the balance; attempt-reported exhaustion holds keep their current force.
- Regression tests: two Locations with divergent `quotaGate.maxMs` / `balanceDeadThreshold` each observe only their own policy (mirroring the #1423 test shapes in `packages/core/test/model-route.test.ts`).

## Acceptance criteria
- The tuning quota ceiling is resolved per Location: two Locations with different `quotaGate.maxMs` values each get their own ceiling applied in schedule and review paths.
- Threshold-derived balance holds are Location-scoped: one Location's hold never blocks another Location sharing the credential.
- Tests cover both two-Location divergence scenarios from the findings; the #1423 scoping behaviour is unchanged.

# fix(core): embeddings door sorts backend vectors by index but never validates the index set — duplicate or out-of-range indices silently misassign vectors to inputs

## Evidence (verified this run)

Verified on laptop primary `~/git/opencode` at main `648e9bf1bdf93e570fd459d72b471d283917e636` (fast-forwarded this run).

- `packages/core/src/embeddings.ts:292-299` — the embeddings service (`Embeddings.layer`, added in commit `54e0b333ec`, the embeddings door #1146 wave A1) validates the backend response in exactly three ways: the entry count equals the input count (`:292`), the entries are sorted by their `index` field (`.toSorted(...)` at `:298`), and each vector's length equals the expected dimension (`:301-304`).
- It never checks that the returned indices are exactly the set `0..inputs.length-1`, each exactly once. A backend that returns the right count with duplicate or out-of-range indices — e.g. indices `[1, 1, 2]` or `[0, 1, 99]` for three inputs — passes every check, and the door returns the vectors positionally after the sort: one input's vector is silently duplicated/lost, or a vector the backend labelled for a different position is handed back as another input's embedding.
- The introducing commit message states the contract this misses: "The backend response is validated (count, order, vector length == the registered or requested dimension) so a misbehaving backend fails loudly instead of returning wrong-shaped vectors." Sorting is not order validation — with a duplicated index there is no correct order to sort into.
- Test gap: `packages/core/test/embeddings.test.ts` covers the happy path against a stub backend (which always returns well-formed sequential indices, `:146-149`), a supported-`dimensions` pass-through, and the wrong-dimension failure — there is no test for a malformed index set (duplicate, missing, or out-of-range), and no count-mismatch test either.
- Dedup: title/keyword search over open and closed issues (`embeddings index`, `embeddings backend validation`) found only #1079 (closed; unbounded body reads in the separate messaging embedding client) — no issue covers index-set validation in the door's `Embeddings` service.

## Why it matters

Embeddings are positional data: the vector at position *i* is only meaningful as the embedding of input *i*. A misbehaving or partially-failing local backend (the registered backend is a local Snowflake embedder at `127.0.0.1:18752`) that returns a malformed index set currently produces silently wrong search/index data downstream instead of the loud failure the door was designed to give — the worst failure mode for an embeddings pipeline, because nothing downstream can detect the misassignment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Embeddings` service rejects a backend response whose indices are not exactly `0..inputs.length-1`, each exactly once (duplicate, missing, or out-of-range index fails with a clear error naming the problem), before any vector is returned.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/core/test/embeddings.test.ts` with a stub backend returning (a) a duplicated index, (b) an out-of-range index — both fail loudly; the existing happy-path, dimensions, and wrong-dimension tests still pass.
- [ ] The count-mismatch failure at `:292` also gains a test if it does not already have one.

body:
The mandatory attestation case of the #1152 parity suite FAILS, recorded here as the muse door's Wave C blocker.

Recorded door behaviour (developing-today/code bin/muse-proxy.mjs + its tests):
- Meta's direct Responses path rejects tool lists naming shell/bash with 403 client_attestation_denied (verified live 2026-10-30).
- The door renames shell→run_command and bash→terminal upstream (tool definitions, history function_call items, tool_choice) and translates returned calls back, so the caller sees its own names and a normal 200.
- If the upstream still 403s (fingerprint moved), the chat front falls back to the CLI door and the caller STILL gets a 200 completion.

Façade behaviour (design §9.1 rule, verified by the parity suite): tool names are preserved verbatim through parse and rendering — never renamed, dropped, or synthesized — and there is no CLI door behind the façade. The same request sent to the muse provider therefore draws the 403 and surfaces as a provider failure (failover to a different route candidate, or the 502 envelope), NOT a 200 from the muse target.

This divergence is deliberate per §9.1, but #1152's acceptance rule is that the merged proxy be the same; by that rule the attestation case is a parity failure. The muse front retirement (#1155) is gated on Drew accepting the §9.1 rule as the replacement behaviour, or the muse provider gaining door-side aliasing. Evidence: packages/core/test/facade-parity.test.ts (attestation describe block) and packages/server/test/facade-parity.test.ts (shell/bash tools reach generation verbatim over HTTP).

## Acceptance criteria

- The façade reproduces the muse door's attestation behaviour: shell/bash tool lists are renamed upstream (definitions, history function_call items, tool_choice) and returned calls are translated back to the caller's names, with a normal 200.
- On a persistent upstream 403 (client_attestation_denied), the caller still receives a 200 completion via the CLI-door fallback, matching the door.
- The #1152 parity suite's mandatory attestation case passes against the façade; this is the Wave C gate for #1155, so the pass is recorded there.

Found by the #1152 parity suite (door vs façade replay pairs).

Design §2 (specs/2026-11-01T04-10-00Z_design_openai-facades.md) promises the error mapping: 429 quota/rate-limit with the provider's reset hint preserved in the message, because caller retry logic keys on it.

Recorded door behaviour (developing-today/code bin/):
- muse-proxy: an upstream 429 is passed through verbatim on both fronts (status 429, upstream error body as-is; door test: "upstream 429 passes through and never falls back to exec").
- opencode-route-proxy: exhausted candidates answer 502 {error:{message: "leaf HTTP 429: …", type: "proxy_error"}} — status parity with the façade, but only by accident of its failover shape.
- codex-proxy: no quota shape at all (generic 500 execution failure).

Façade today: packages/server/src/handlers/completions.ts maps every non-selection Generate error to 502 {error:{message, type:"server_error"}}. The provider message (and any reset hint inside it) survives, but the 429 status does not — a caller migrating from the muse door and keying retries on 429 silently changes behaviour.

Parity evidence: packages/server/test/facade-parity.test.ts ("quota failure, non-streaming…") and packages/core/test/facade-parity.test.ts (muse + codex quota cases).

Fix direction: surface quota/rate-limit failures from generation as a distinguishable error so the handler can answer 429 with the hint preserved in the message (and keep failover semantics: a 429 is only the final answer once candidates are exhausted). Blocks Wave C repointing for quota-sensitive muse callers; recorded on #1152.

## Acceptance criteria

- A quota/rate-limit failure surfaces from the façade as HTTP 429 with the provider's reset hint preserved in the message, per design §2 — not as 502 server_error.
- Caller retry behaviour keyed on 429 + reset hint works unchanged against the façade.
- A parity/regression test pins the mapping for the quota case (and distinguishes it from genuine upstream 5xx, which keeps its own mapping).

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

Codex (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]) raised a P2 on PR #1374 — "Track temp ownership immediately after exclusive creation":

> If `writeFileString` creates the temporary file but then fails while writing it (for example, due to ENOSPC or a quota limit), the success-only `Effect.tap` never sets `created`. The error handler consequently skips removal, leaving a partial cassette behind; the previous unconditional cleanup removed it. Open the file exclusively first, mark ownership once that succeeds, and then write through the scoped handle, as `FSUtil.writeAtomic` does, so write failures are cleaned up without deleting another writer's collision file.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1374 (https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1374), merged 2026-11-02T08:49:07Z
- Review comment: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1374#discussion_r4440398774 — chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-02T08:49:12Z, on `packages/http-recorder/src/cassette/store.ts:177`
- No-response evidence: the review thread is unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads` checked this run: `isResolved: false`), the thread contains only Codex's comment (no replies), and the PR's only commit (`55fb4ec3fc`, 2026-11-02T08:47:02Z) predates the comment — no fix commit followed it.
- Still live on current main (verified this run via `gh api` raw read of `packages/http-recorder/src/cassette/store.ts` on main):
  - line 172: `let created = false`
  - line 173: `yield* fs.writeFileString(temporary, formatCassette(cassette), { flag: "wx", mode: 0o600 }).pipe(`
  - `created = true` is set only in the success-path `Effect.tap`, and the `Effect.onError` handler (line 181) removes the temp only when `created` is set — so a write that creates the file and then fails (ENOSPC, quota) still leaves a partial `.tmp` cassette behind.
- Not already tracked: issue searches for the cassette store temp-file cleanup / `writeFileString` partial temp returned no covering issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- Temp ownership is recorded as soon as exclusive creation succeeds (e.g. open exclusively first, mark ownership, then write through the scoped handle, mirroring `FSUtil.writeAtomic`), so a mid-write failure removes the partial temp.
- Cleanup still never deletes another writer's file on a `wx` collision.
- A regression test covers a write failure after creation (partial temp removed) and the collision case (other writer's file untouched).
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue.

# fix(ci): check:bounded-http does not scan the nested script trees — packages/console/app/script and packages/plugins/figma/script escape the regression net (#1394's class)

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-02 on main 401ba065a1)

`script/check-bounded-http.ts` header (lines 15-16, 99-100) claims the gate scans "every script tree (root `script/`, each package script/scripts tree, and `services/www/script`)" and "every packages/*/script and packages/*/scripts ... where present". The implementation is a hardcoded `SCAN_ROOTS` list (script/check-bounded-http.ts:82-127), and it misses the two nested-package script trees that exist on main:

- `packages/console/app/script` (console is a multi-package tree: `packages/console/app/src` and `packages/console/function/src` ARE in the src roots, but `console/app/script` is not in the script roots)
- `packages/plugins/figma/script` (the whole `packages/plugins/*` nesting level is absent from SCAN_ROOTS)

Hits that escape the gate today (pattern-matched per the gate's own P-A/P-B):

- `packages/console/app/script/dev-enterprise.ts:77` — `const response = await fetch(accountUrl, { ... signal: AbortSignal.timeout(8000) })`: the fetch carries a deadline but has never been dispositioned in `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt`.
- `packages/console/app/script/dev-enterprise.ts:84` — `... .parse(await response.json()).account`: response body read via bare `.json()` — deadline bounds duration, not bytes; exactly the read shape the gate exists to disposition.
- `packages/console/app/script/dev-enterprise.ts:38,40` — `new Response(child.stdout).text()` / `new Response(child.stderr).text()`: P-B chained reads, undispositioned (local subprocess streams — a disposition, not necessarily a fix).
- `packages/console/app/script/dev-enterprise.ts:50` — `async fetch(request) {` matches P-A textually (handler definition, needs a disposition if the tree is scanned).
- `packages/plugins/figma/script/sync-skills.ts` — no current P-A/P-B hits; the tree is simply outside the net, so the next fetch/read added there escapes silently.

Gate run this run: `bun run script/check-bounded-http.ts` → exit 0, "All 354 bounded-http candidates in 62 scan roots are dispositioned" — green while the above sites are unscanned.

Same failure class as #1394 (script trees escaped because the gate didn't scan them), #1256 (services/), #1361/#1369 (proto-reads trees), #1318 (numeric-boundaries tree): a hardcoded root list drifting from the tree it claims to cover.

## Why it matters

The bounded-http gate is the regression net for the "bounded by default" contract (#1127). Every prior escape (#1394: 153 hits across 24 script roots) was found by audit, not by the gate. A root list that claims full coverage but is hardcoded will keep drifting as packages nest (console/*, plugins/* are the current shape of that drift). The undispositioned `response.json()` in dev-enterprise.ts is low-risk (localhost dev tool, 8s deadline), but the gate's value is that no site is invisible — today these are.

## Acceptance criteria

- `packages/console/app/script` and `packages/plugins/figma/script` are in the bounded-http scan (roots derived from the filesystem, or the hardcoded list completed AND a test/guard that fails when a script/scripts tree exists on disk but is not scanned).
- Every hit in the newly scanned trees is dispositioned in `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` (bounded-at-site, local/inbound read with reason, or tracked).
- The header comment's coverage claim matches the implementation.

body:
## Finding

PR #1142 made the quota gate's ceiling configurable (`quotaGate.maxMs`) but left the sibling ceilings it must stay in step with as hardcoded constants — a follow-up the PR itself named as out of scope, which was never filed.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1142 (merged 855ec25f5, implements #1141), PR body section "Deliberately left hardcoded" / "Noted follow-up (out of scope)": "`model-route-limits.ts` `MAX_WINDOW_MS` / `UNKNOWN_RESET_MS`, and `model-route-tuning.ts` `MAX_QUOTA_RESET_MS` (kept in step with `quotaGate.maxMs` by hand today)".
- Verified on current main 401ba065a1:
  - `packages/core/src/model-route-tuning.ts:37`: `export const MAX_QUOTA_RESET_MS = 30 * 86_400_000`, used as the prediction ceiling at lines 150, 186, 200, 243 — independent of the configured `quotaGate.maxMs`.
  - `packages/core/src/model-route.ts:1178`: the gate code comments that its cap "mirrors ModelRouteTuning.MAX_QUOTA_RESET_MS" — the mirror is by convention only.
  - `packages/core/src/model-route-limits.ts:172-174`: `MAX_WINDOW_MS = 86_400_000`, `UNKNOWN_RESET_MS = 60_000`, likewise outside the settings block.
- Dedupe: no open or closed issue covers wiring these constants to `model_route_settings` (searches for MAX_QUOTA_RESET_MS / UNKNOWN_RESET_MS / "kept in step" return only #1141, #933, #1266, none of which covers this).

## Why it matters

Setting `quotaGate.maxMs` away from 30 days now silently desynchronizes the system: the gate honors the configured ceiling while tuning predictions and limit windows keep the old 30-day/24h constants, so predicted resets and actual gate holds disagree — the exact hand-sync hazard #1142's configurability was meant to remove.

## Acceptance criteria

- `ModelRouteTuning`'s reset ceiling derives from the same configured value as the quota gate (or a clearly-named sibling settings field), and the limits constants are either wired to settings or explicitly re-documented as invariants with the reasoning recorded in code.
- The "mirrors" comment at model-route.ts:1178 is replaced by an actual shared source of truth (no by-hand mirror remains).
- Regression tests: a non-default `quotaGate.maxMs` changes tuning's prediction ceiling accordingly; default configuration behaves exactly as today.

body:
## Finding

The `experimental.model_route_settings` reader is a single module-global, so route machinery settings are not scoped to the Location (project) whose config supplied them: the last model-routes plugin activation wins for every Location in the process.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1142 (merged 855ec25f5) added `ModelRoute.onSettingsConfig`, mirroring the lazy-reader pattern, with the model-routes config plugin registering `() => settingsConfig(configuredSettings(loaded.entries))` from its own Location's config entries.
- Codex P1 on PR #1142 (2026-11-01T03:43:12Z, thread unresolved, no reply): "Scope the route settings reader to its Location" — every `activeSettings()` / `currentConstants()` call uses the one global reader with no Location identifier, so opening another project changes an existing project's escalation, cooldown, and weighting behavior; a Location with no settings block replaces the reader with one returning undefined, silently reverting the other Location to defaults.
- Verified still present on current main 401ba065a1, `packages/core/src/model-route.ts:781-787`: `let readSettingsConfig: (() => SettingsConfig | undefined) | undefined` and `onSettingsConfig` assigns it unconditionally; consumers at lines 792 and 2460 read the same global.

## Why it matters

Route settings govern failure behavior (bench ladders, quota gates, escalation) for live traffic. Cross-Location leakage means one project's config — or merely opening a second project — rewrites another project's failure handling with no log line and no config change in the affected project, the hardest class of routing surprise to diagnose.

## Acceptance criteria

- Settings resolution is keyed by Location (or the reader is carried through the Location-scoped service/graph the other route state uses), so each Location's machinery reads its own config; a Location without a settings block gets defaults without disturbing any other Location.
- Regression test: two Location graphs with different `model_route_settings` (e.g. different `escalation.afterGiveUps` / bench multiplier) each observe only their own values, in either activation order.
- Single-Location behavior is unchanged; the model-route and config test suites pass.

title: fix(core): bench exponent cap of 30 freezes cooldown growth far below maxCooldownMs when multiplier < 2 (#1142)

body:
## Finding

The bench ladder's backoff exponent is still capped at 30, an invariant that was invisible when the multiplier was hardcoded to 2 but silently freezes cooldown growth far below the configured maximum once `bench.multiplier` is configurable below 2.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1142 (merged 855ec25f5) turned the bench constants into `experimental.model_route_settings` config (#1141), including `bench.multiplier` (schema: finite, >= 1) and `bench.maxCooldownMs` (default 86_400_000, 24h).
- Codex P2 on PR #1142 (2026-11-01T03:43:12Z, thread unresolved, no reply): with `bench.multiplier: 1.1` and a 60s base, the cooldown freezes at ~17.45 minutes after the 31st consecutive failure and never grows again, despite the 24h configured maximum.
- Verified still present on current main 401ba065a1, `packages/core/src/model-route.ts:421`: `Math.min(base * ladder.multiplier ** Math.min(state.consecutiveFailures - 1, 30), ladder.maxCooldownMs)`. Arithmetic check: 60_000 x 1.1^30 = ~1_046_940 ms (~17.45 min) — the exponent cap binds for every failure after the 31st, so `maxCooldownMs` is unreachable for any multiplier whose 30th power times the base is below it. The PR body lists the exponent cap 30 among "deliberately left hardcoded" invariants on the reasoning that "2^30 x a 1ms base already exceeds the 24h cap" — true only for multiplier 2, the value that stopped being fixed in the same PR.

## Why it matters

An operator who sets a gentler multiplier (a supported, schema-valid choice) to stretch benches toward a long maximum gets a ladder that stalls at a fraction of the intended ceiling: a persistently failing target is retried far more often than configured, indefinitely.

## Acceptance criteria

- The saturation point is derived from the configured multiplier and `maxCooldownMs` (or the exponent is uncapped with an overflow-safe formulation), so for any valid multiplier > 1 the ladder keeps growing until `maxCooldownMs` binds.
- Multiplier exactly 1 keeps its documented behavior (every bench at base).
- Regression tests: multiplier 1.1 / 60s base benches keep increasing past the 31st consecutive failure and eventually reach the configured cap; default multiplier 2 behavior is unchanged; the model-route test suite passes.

title: fix(core): round-robin tiers compare computed weights with exact float equality — equal tiers split and a member starves (#1124)

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core

body:
## Finding

Round-robin priority tiers are compared with exact floating-point equality, so mathematically equal tier weights computed through different paths split into separate tiers and the lower one is starved while the upper tier has any ready member.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1124 (merged 6aae7cc05) made round-robin `weights` priority tiers (#1122).
- Codex P2 on PR #1124 (2026-11-01T01:32:50Z, thread unresolved, no reply): "Normalize computed weights before comparing priority tiers" — an equal-weight round-robin parent containing a three-leaf nested group and a direct leaf, under a global schedule factor of 0.1, gives the group weight `(0.1 + 0.1 + 0.1) / 3 = 0.10000000000000002` via `factor()` (an average over leaves) versus `0.1` for the direct leaf; the group becomes the sole top tier and the leaf receives no draws.
- Verified still present on current main 401ba065a1, `packages/core/src/model-route.ts`: group tier weight is `base * factor(child.node, rules, nodePath, "adjustment")` (average of leaf adjustments, ~line 2157), leaf tier weight is `traces[position]?.adjustment` directly, `byTier` sorts by raw subtraction, and `topTier` (line 2175-2182) filters with `tier.weight === head.weight` (line 2180) — no rounding, epsilon, or normalization anywhere in tier construction or comparison.

## Why it matters

Tiering is the mechanism pools use to burn preferred plans first (weights like 3/2/1 and schedule factors like 0.1 are the fleet's real configuration shapes). A one-ulp difference silently converting an equal partner into a fallback means traffic, quota burn, and cost land on the wrong accounts indefinitely, with decision records showing a plausible-looking tier split.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tier keys are normalized before comparison (e.g. rounded to a documented precision) so weights that are equal up to floating-point computation noise form one tier, for both leaf and group candidates, in `byTier` ordering and `topTier` membership.
- Regression test reproducing the Codex example: a three-leaf group and a direct leaf at mathematically equal adjusted weight under a 0.1 schedule factor rotate evenly as one tier.
- Genuinely distinct weights (2 vs 1, demoted vs live) keep today's ordering exactly; the model-route test suite passes.

title: fix(core): provider-route member validation keeps '*' and 'opencode-route' — a provider route can dispatch outside its membership (#1134)

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage

body:
## Finding

`configuredProviderRoutes` retains non-concrete members that the expansion then treats as real dispatch targets, so a provider route can serve through providers outside its declared membership — contradicting its own validation warning ("it contributes no leaves").

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1134 (merged 668386358), `packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts`.
- Two unresolved bot findings on PR #1134, both verified still present on current main 401ba065a1:
  1. Codex P2 (2026-11-01T02:22:51Z): a member `"*"` is kept with the "names no known provider; it contributes no leaves" warning (`configuredProviderRoutes`, line 346ff on main). But expansion builds the group's route from the member list, and a target with `ref.providerID === "*"` hits the door-set branch in `expand` (main model-routes.ts line 658-662), expanding across **every** catalog provider offering the model. A provider route declared as `providers: ["openai", "*"]` can therefore dispatch to providers that were never members.
  2. CodeRabbit Minor (2026-11-01T03:32:45Z, model-routes.ts:332 in the PR): the nesting guard runs only when `!knownProviders.has(member)`. The second caller (main line 194) passes `models.provider.list()`, which by then includes `opencode-route` (the routes provider added by the provider transform), so a member naming `opencode-route` is treated as a known concrete provider and kept instead of being dropped as a nesting attempt — the two callers validate the same config differently.
- Current main code (line ~365): `if (!knownProviders.has(member) && (member === ModelRoute.PROVIDER_ID || declared.has(member)))` — drop-with-warning; otherwise unknown members are pushed after the "contributes no leaves" warning.

## Why it matters

Provider routes exist to pin *which* accounts/providers may serve a model. A wildcard member silently widening the pool to every provider defeats that pin (unexpected providers, unexpected cost/credential use), and the log line actively misleads an operator into believing the member is inert. The caller-dependent `opencode-route` case means the same config file validates differently depending on which transform asks first.

## Acceptance criteria

- `"*"` and `opencode-route` (ModelRoute.PROVIDER_ID) are always rejected as provider-route members with a warning, regardless of the caller's known-provider set; likewise any member naming another declared provider route.
- A member that names no known provider keeps today's warn-and-keep behavior only if it can never act as a pattern/door-set at expansion; otherwise it is dropped.
- Regression tests cover: `providers: ["openai", "*"]` never expands beyond `openai`; `providers: ["opencode-route", "openai"]` drops the routes-provider member from both call paths; valid member lists expand exactly as before.

title: fix(core): model governance does not expand provider routes — concrete-provider policies are bypassed or misapplied (#1134)

body:
## Finding

Model governance (`ModelGovernance.assertAllowed` / `routeTargets`) does not expand provider routes, so a route target naming a provider route is judged literally — as if `openai-plan` were itself a provider — and agent/session model policies are bypassed or misapplied for every model the provider route actually serves.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1134 (merged 668386358) introduced provider routes (`experimental.provider_routes`): a target `openai-plan/gpt-6.1-terra` expands at runtime to the members' concrete leaves.
- Codex P1 on PR #1134 (2026-11-01T02:22:51Z, thread unresolved, no reply): "Expand synthetic members in model governance as well" — a parent policy excluding `openai/*` permits a route targeting `openai-plan/m` even when its serving member is `openai/m`; conversely an allowlist naming the concrete members rejects the same route.
- Verified still present on current main 401ba065a1: `packages/core/src/session/model-governance.ts` `routeTargets` (line 204ff) recurses into `opencode-route` targets, expands door-set (`*`) targets over the catalog (line 282) and glob targets via `matchingModels`, but has no provider-route handling — `catalog?.get(selection.providerID)` for a provider-route id is undefined, so the target falls through to the literal ref (`known === undefined ? [literal] : ...`, ~line 293).

## Why it matters

Governance is the enforcement layer for which models an agent/subagent may use. Any policy written against concrete providers (exclusions like `openai/*`, or allowlists) silently stops binding the moment a pool is expressed through a provider route — exactly the configuration provider routes encourage. The inverse case (allowlist rejects a legitimate provider-route target) breaks working setups with a misleading denial.

## Acceptance criteria

- `routeTargets` expands a provider-route target into the concrete member leaves for that model (using the configured provider routes + catalog, mirroring the runtime expansion in the model-routes plugin), so exclusion and allowlist policies judge the providers that will actually serve.
- Regression tests: (a) an exclusion of a member provider denies a route whose provider route can serve through that member; (b) an allowlist of the concrete members permits the provider-route target; (c) a provider route whose members are all excluded is denied.
- Behavior for routes with no provider-route targets is unchanged (existing governance tests pass).

body:
## Problem

Two workflow policies in this repo are enforced by nothing but memory:

1. **No-PR-trigger policy** (Drew, 2026-11-02; commit `0c4ea315ed`, PR #1401): "CI never runs on pull requests; workflows run on push to main, on schedule, or by manual dispatch." That change only added `workflow_dispatch` to the four workflows that lacked it — it added no check that the policy stays true.
2. **Per-job `timeout-minutes` rule** (#61): already regressed twice and caught manually both times — #1326 (test.yml's ci-fix job, "per-job gap the file-level check cannot see") and #1184 (branch-cleanup job, "the one runnable job that regressed #61's cap rule").

The repo's other house rules all have regression gates for exactly this reason (`script/check-bounded-http.ts`, `check-proto-reads.ts`, `check-numeric-boundaries.ts`, `check-doc-env-vars.ts`, wired as steps in `.github/workflows/test.yml` — "or the class regrows one call at a time"). None of them looks at `.github/workflows/` at all: `grep -rn "timeout-minutes|workflow_dispatch|pull_request" script/*.ts` returns no hits.

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-02 on main `424c8d6f18`)

All 29 workflows currently comply — this is a missing regression net, not a live violation:

- 0 workflows declare a `pull_request` or `pull_request_target` trigger.
- 29/29 workflows declare `workflow_dispatch`.
- 0 non-reusable jobs are missing `timeout-minutes` (jobs with `uses:` excluded — reusable-workflow caller jobs cannot take the key, cf. #1326's agents.yml note).

A new or edited workflow that adds a PR trigger, omits `workflow_dispatch`, or omits a job timeout would pass every existing gate and ship silently.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new gate in the house shape — `script/check-workflows.ts` + `script/check-workflows.test.ts` + a `check:workflows` package.json script + test.yml steps mirroring the other gates — fails (exit 1, naming workflow + job/rule) when any workflow:
  - declares a `pull_request` or `pull_request_target` trigger,
  - lacks `workflow_dispatch`, or
  - has a job without `timeout-minutes` (jobs using a reusable workflow via `uses:` exempt).
- [ ] The gate passes clean on the current 29 workflows.
- [ ] Trigger matching is exact-key: `pull_request_review_comment` (opencode.yml) and `issue_comment` are comment triggers, not PR CI triggers — the #1401 policy commit counted the repo as compliant with those present, and the gate must not flag them.
- [ ] The YAML handling copes with the real files: `on:` is boolean-true under YAML 1.1 parsers, and triggers appear in string, list, and map forms across the 29 files (tests pin at least the map and list forms plus the `on:` quirk).
- [ ] Gate tests cover one synthetic violation of each rule and the compliant-tree case.

Out of scope (possible follow-on dispositions, not this gate unless triage disagrees): concurrency `queue: max` rules (#151/#156/#179 family) and top-level `permissions:` (#118).

Related: #1401 (policy), #61 / #1326 / #1184 (timeout rule and its manual catches), #1127 / #865 / #995 (the gate pattern this follows).

title: OpenAI-compatible completions door for external harnesses (OpenClaw direct to OpenCode)
body:
## Problem

OpenClaw (external agent harness) currently reaches fleet route models through a standalone proxy (code-repo `opencode-route-proxy`, :18750) that re-implements route/provider resolution outside OpenCode — including provider endpoint resolution, which it gets wrong for credential-backed providers (developing-today/code#4444: the GPT pair resolved to the PAYG platform door instead of the credential-backed Codex backend).

Ruling (Drew, 2026-11-02): OpenClaw should talk directly to OpenCode. The standalone re-implementation is the architectural mistake.

## What exists

`POST /api/experimental/generate` (Generate.Service) already runs one stateless generation through the server's own ModelResolver + LLM layer — route models resolve in-process, no session is stored. But it accepts only a single `prompt` string and returns only text: it cannot serve an external harness that speaks the OpenAI chat-completions wire format (message history, tools, streaming).

## Proposal

Add an OpenAI-compatible completions door to the server, backed by the same in-process machinery:

- `POST /v1/chat/completions` — accepts the OpenAI payload (`model` = a route ref such as `opencode-route/workhorse` or a bare route id, `messages`, `tools`, `tool_choice`, `stream`), resolves the model through ModelResolver (in-process model_routes/provider_routes resolution + provider layer), runs one provider completion via the LLM client, and returns the OpenAI wire shape (JSON, or SSE chunks terminated by `[DONE]` when streaming). No session is created or stored (a fresh attribution id is minted per call, as Generate does).
- `GET /v1/models` — the route models the door serves.
- Server auth applies as for every other route (no new unauthenticated surface).

Consumers: OpenClaw repoints its `opencode-route` provider from :18750 to this door once deployed; the standalone proxy then has no remaining production consumer and can be retired (tracked from the code repo side).

## Acceptance

- Tests: wire-shape tests for non-streaming + streaming completions and the models list, with the completion service faked (pattern: packages/server/test/generate.test.ts).
- A route model that resolves to a plan-backed leaf completes through the fork's own provider wiring (the case the standalone proxy could never serve).

body:
## Problem

`opencode auth import` buffers its entire input unbounded on **both** input branches before any validation runs:

- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/auth/import.ts:19` — `file ? readFile(file, "utf8") : readStdin()`: the file branch is a plain `readFile` with no size pre-check, and the stdin branch goes through `readStdin()`.
- `packages/cli/src/util/io.ts:3-6` — `readStdin()` is `text(process.stdin)` from `node:stream/consumers`, which concatenates the whole stream with no cap.
- `import.ts:20` — the buffered string then feeds `Schema.fromJsonString(Schema.Array(Credential.Entry))`, so the input must fit in a single JS string before the schema ever sees it.

## Why it matters

This is the same shape the session-import handler already fixed: `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/session/import.ts:14-36` caps its transfer at 256 MiB (`readLocal` stat pre-check for files, `readBoundedResponseBody` for remote), with the in-file rationale that past the ~512 MiB engine string ceiling an unbounded read dies with an opaque `RangeError`/OOM instead of a clear too-large error (#942, #1398, #1115).

Auth exports are small — `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/auth/export.ts:22` writes one JSON array of credentials — so a generous cap rejects nothing legitimate. Today, piping the wrong (huge/binary) file into `opencode auth import`, or pointing it at an oversized file, hangs on memory and then fails opaquely instead of failing fast with a clear error.

Severity: low (local CLI, user's own input), robustness/paper-cut class — filed for parity with the session-import bound.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The file branch rejects an over-cap file with a clear "too large" error before buffering it whole (stat pre-check, mirroring session import's `readLocal`).
- [ ] The stdin branch reads through a bounded reader that fails with the same clear error once the cap is exceeded, instead of `node:stream/consumers` `text()` unbounded.
- [ ] The cap is sized generously above real credential exports (kilobytes–low megabytes) and named/documented in the handler like `MAX_SESSION_TRANSFER_BYTES` is.
- [ ] Normal file and stdin imports behave exactly as today; a regression test pins the over-cap behaviour for at least one branch (both preferred) following the CLI package's existing test conventions (`packages/cli/test/import-export.test.ts`, `packages/cli/test/auth.test.ts`).

Evidence verified on main `424c8d6f18`. Dedup: title/keyword search over open + closed issues found no coverage of auth-import input bounding (#435 is a different, closed bug; #942/#1398/#1115 are session import only).

body:
## Problem

PR #1391 (merged, closing #1388) added `createRunFetch` in `packages/cli/src/run/fetch.ts`: non-streaming `opencode run` requests get a 30s deadline, while the event stream (`/api/event`) and the session idle wait (`/api/experimental/session/<id>/wait`) are exempted. The exemption is an **exact full-pathname match**:

```ts
// packages/cli/src/run/fetch.ts:5-6 (verified on current main after the #1391 merge e937b724)
const pathname = new URL(request instanceof Request ? request.url : request).pathname
if (pathname === "/api/event" || /^\/api\/experimental\/session\/[^/]+\/wait$/.test(pathname))
```

When the configured server URL carries a **path prefix** (e.g. `--server https://host/ws/abc`), the generated client preserves that prefix, so the long-lived requests arrive as `/ws/abc/api/event` and `/ws/abc/api/experimental/session/<id>/wait`. Neither matches the exemption, so both receive the 30s deadline: runs against a prefixed server longer than 30 seconds lose their event stream and wait-until-idle behavior — the exact long-lived behavior #1388 set out to preserve.

## Origin

- Codex P2 on PR #1391, review comment 4442798908 (2026-11-02T13:14:38Z), head `1e41d82d87`: "Preserve long-lived exemptions for prefixed server URLs" — thread left unresolved when PR #1391 was merged at 2026-11-02T15:15:57Z.
- CodeRabbit raised the same finding independently (comment 4442830715, Major).
- This follow-up was filed by the queue worker (lane A shift, task 6225) after re-verifying the finding against current main — it is NOT fixed on main today.

## Acceptance criteria

- Long-lived route exemption matches `/api/event` and `/api/experimental/session/<id>/wait` **relative to the configured base URL / its path prefix**, so prefixed servers keep the unbounded event stream and session wait.
- Non-streaming requests through a prefixed server still carry the 30s deadline (no regression of #1388's bound).
- Tests in `packages/cli/test/run/fetch.test.ts` (or its successor) cover prefixed URLs for both the exempt long-lived routes and a bounded non-streaming route; existing 3 fetch tests still pass.
- `bun run check:bounded-http` still passes.

Distinct from #1385 (generated promise-client transport default deadline).

body:
## Problem

In `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/session/import.ts`, the session-import handler bounds every ingress leg except one:

- `:19` — `MAX_SESSION_TRANSFER_BYTES = 256 * 1024 * 1024`, sized (comment at `:14-18`) from 514 real session exports: median 0.38 MiB, p90 7.55 MiB, 97.9% under 256 MiB — and because "the ~512 MiB engine string ceiling makes an unbounded `response.text()` fail with an opaque RangeError just above this".
- `:28-33` — the remote (`http(s)://`) branch enforces that cap via `readBoundedResponseBody`, with a 600 s deadline (#942, #1115).
- `:54-84` — the import POST leg is likewise bounded (600 s deadline, 1 MiB response cap).
- `:96-97` — the local-file branch is plain `readFile(input.file, "utf8")`: no size pre-check, no cap. Its result feeds the same `Schema.fromJsonString(SessionTransfer.Data)` decode at `:99`.

## Why it matters

The same transfer document is bounded or unbounded purely by transport. A >256 MiB export fetched over HTTP fails fast with a clear "too large" error; the same file on disk is buffered whole, and past the ~512 MiB string ceiling the local import dies with an opaque `RangeError` (or OOM pressure) instead of the clear error the cap was created to produce. About 2.1% of the real exports in the #942 triage exceed 256 MiB, so this is a real tail, not a theoretical one. Session export files are also the share/hand-off format, so the file on disk is not necessarily one the user produced themselves.

## Dedup note

#942 (closed) covered only the remote branch and explicitly scoped the local branch out — that scoping predates the #942 fix landing the cap, its sizing rationale, and the string-ceiling evidence in this same file. No open or closed issue covers the local branch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The local-file branch rejects a file larger than `MAX_SESSION_TRANSFER_BYTES` with a clear "session data too large"-style error before buffering it whole (e.g. a stat size pre-check, or a factored `readLocal`-style helper mirroring `fetchRemote`).
- [ ] A normal-sized local import behaves exactly as today (existing file-import tests in `packages/cli/test/import-export.test.ts` still pass).
- [ ] A regression test pins the over-cap local-file behaviour, following the CLI package's existing test conventions (the remote branch's over-cap tests in the same file are the pattern).
- [ ] No behaviour change to the remote branch, the location lookup, or the import POST.

Verified on main `78c48b5068` (2026-11-02) by line-level reading. Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode.

body:
## Problem

The bounded-http regression gate (`script/check-bounded-http.ts`, the #1129 net for design #1127) scans only `*/src` trees. Every build/release/CI script tree escapes it, and that unscanned population is exactly where the unbounded-fetch bugs keep being found one at a time.

## Evidence (verified on main `5d3780ea0b`, 2026-11-02)

- `script/check-bounded-http.ts:56` — `SCAN_ROOTS` lists 39 roots, every one a `packages/*/src`, `services/*/src`, or `packages/console/{app,function}/src` tree. No `script/` (repo root), no `packages/*/script`, no `packages/*/scripts` root appears.
- `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` — 0 entries whose file is under a script tree (grep `^(script/|packages/[^/]+/scripts?/)` = 0), so no script-tree hit is dispositioned either.
- Gate-pattern replication (the gate's own `PATTERNS` from `check-bounded-http.ts`: `fetch(`, argument-less `.text()/.json()/.arrayBuffer()` reads, comment-only lines skipped) over the 24 script roots present in the tree (`script/`, 22 `packages/*/script(s)`, `services/www/script`) = **153 hits across 73 files**, none dispositioned. Top files: `script/check-bounded-http.test.ts` 19 (gate's own fixtures), `packages/cli/script/service-smoke.ts` 15, `packages/sdk/script/verify-package.ts` 8, `packages/desktop/scripts/finalize-latest-json.ts` 6, `packages/core/script/migration.ts` 5.
- Most hits are dispositionable local reads (`Bun.file(...).text()`, `` $`...`.text() ``, subprocess stdout) — the allowlist already dispositions the same shapes in src trees. But the population also contains genuinely unbounded network sites that no gate will ever catch a regression in, e.g.:
  - `packages/ai/script/recording-cost-report.ts:219` — `fetch(MODELS_DEV_URL)` (`https://models.opencode.ai/api.json`) with no signal/deadline, body read via unbounded `.json()`.
  - `packages/desktop/scripts/finalize-latest-json.ts:38` — GitHub release fetch with no deadline; `:58` unbounded `.json()`; `:133` asset fetch with no deadline; `:146` `await res.arrayBuffer()` buffers a whole desktop release asset in memory before `Bun.write`.
  - `packages/cli/script/build.ts:252`/`:269` — tracked individually by #1159, but still not gate-dispositioned.
- The pattern's cost is already measured: every top-level `script/` fetch bug was filed as its own issue after escaping this gate — #1275 (release version resolution), #1329/#1333 (update-artifact), #1332/#1336 (publish-winget), #1337 (stats.ts), #1344 (GitHub closers). #1256 extended this same gate to `services/` when its fetches escaped the same way; the script trees are the remaining unscanned population.

## Why it matters

`check:bounded-http` is the regression net that is supposed to make the bounded-by-default contract (#1127) self-enforcing: a new unbounded `fetch(` in a scanned tree fails CI until it is bounded or dispositioned. In the script trees — the code that runs release publishing, version resolution, and CI automation, often against api.github.com and registries with a token in env — a new unbounded fetch lands silently, and the fleet keeps paying one issue + one fix per site.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SCAN_ROOTS` in `script/check-bounded-http.ts` (or an equivalent mechanism) covers the repo's script trees: root `script/`, every `packages/*/script` and `packages/*/scripts`, and `services/*/script` where present.
- [ ] Every hit in the newly scanned trees is dispositioned in `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt`: bounded at the site (naming the bound), a local/inbound/non-response read (with the reason), or a remaining surface naming its tracking issue (e.g. `build.ts` → #1159, `stats.ts` → #1337) — following the allowlist's existing format.
- [ ] The two spot-read unbounded network sites above (`recording-cost-report.ts:219`, `finalize-latest-json.ts:38/58/133/146`) are either bounded in the same pass or filed as their own tracked issues and named in their dispositions; they do not get a bare "remaining surface" disposition with no owner.
- [ ] `script/check-bounded-http.test.ts` covers the new roots (a hit in a script tree is reported unlisted until dispositioned), and `bun run check:bounded-http` passes on the result.
- [ ] No production runtime behavior changes in this pass beyond any site explicitly bounded under the previous criterion.

Dedup: searched open + closed issues for `check:bounded-http` gate coverage (2026-11-02): #1129 built the gate (src trees), #1256 extended it to `services/`; #1369/#1371 are the sibling extensions for the proto-reads and numeric-boundaries gates. No issue covers the bounded-http gate's script trees.

body:
Origin: Codex P2 review finding on PR #1384 (merged 2026-11-02 as f7b4c02dab), thread on packages/core/src/model-route.ts (line 622 at head 4794119cf5), left unresolved at merge. Verified still present on current main by queue task 6188 (lane A, 2026-11-02).

## Problem

`poolQuotaExhausted` (packages/core/src/model-route.ts, ~line 609) pulls a pool once **two distinct leaves** are quota-out, but `quotaOut` (~line 546) counts a leaf as out when its serving credential is quota-gated (`credentialQuotaBlocked`) or its provider is quota-gated. Those gates are **shared evidence**: for a nested route containing `provider-a/model-1`, `provider-a/model-2`, and a healthy `provider-b/model-3`, one quota failure on provider A's active credential gates both A leaves through the same credential gate. The loop counts them as two distinct leaf failures and declares the whole pool exhausted, so the resolver hard-excludes the healthy B leaf (including from the all-full last resort) even though no second independent quota source has failed. The credential-less provider gate has the same flaw.

## Fix direction (from the Codex finding)

Deduplicate shared quota-gate evidence, or track distinct leaf failures, before applying the `POOL_QUOTA_LEAVES` threshold: leaves that are out only because of the same credential/provider gate count as one signal; genuinely independent leaf quota benches still count separately.

## Acceptance

- A pool where two leaves share one gated credential/provider and a third leaf is healthy is NOT declared pool-exhausted from that single gate; the healthy leaf stays selectable (including last resort).
- Two leaves with independent quota benches (distinct credentials/gates) still exhaust the pool (existing PR3 tests keep passing).
- New regression test beside packages/core/test/model-route.test.ts pool-shaped tests demonstrating the shared-gate case.
- packages/core model-route + model-resolver suites pass; typecheck clean.

Part of the #1014 PR3 follow-up set; does not reopen #1014's other routed packets.

## Acceptance criteria
- A pool where two leaves share one gated credential/provider and a third leaf is healthy is NOT declared pool-exhausted from that single gate; the healthy leaf stays selectable, including from the all-full last resort.
- Two leaves with independent quota benches (distinct credentials/gates) still exhaust the pool; existing PR3 tests keep passing.
- A new regression test beside `packages/core/test/model-route.test.ts` pool-shaped tests demonstrates the shared-gate case.
- packages/core model-route and model-resolver suites pass; typecheck is clean.

body:
## Problem

`opencode run`'s client fetch wrapper disables Bun's fetch deadline for **every** request, not just the event stream that motivated it: a server that accepts the connection and then stalls — headers arrive (or never do), then silence — hangs the run forever, before or during prompt admission, with no error to act on.

This is a remaining surface under design #1127 ("bounded by default"), dispositioned as untracked in the bounded-http allowlist; no issue owns it.

## Evidence (verified on main `cfc35c69ee`, 2026-11-02)

- `packages/cli/src/run/run.ts:92-98` — `execute()` creates the run client with a custom fetch: `fetch(request, { ...init, timeout: false })`. The comment at line 95 gives the motive: Bun's default five-minute deadline terminates the event stream used by long-running sessions. The wrapper applies to every request through this client, not just the stream.
- Only the event stream needs that carve-out: `packages/cli/src/run/noninteractive.ts:78` subscribes via `client.event.subscribe({ signal: controller.signal })` — long-lived by design.
- Non-streaming calls go through the same deadline-free client, none with a timer:
  - `packages/cli/src/run/run.ts:100` — `resolveSessionTarget(...)` (session create/get, plus the `model.default` lookup in its prepare callback).
  - `packages/cli/src/run/run.ts:141-146` — `client.session.update(...)` to set the session title.
  - `packages/cli/src/run/noninteractive.ts:716-726` — `client.session.prompt(...)` (admission): its `admission` AbortController (line 715) is aborted only on interrupt/cleanup (lines 683, 731), never on a timer.
- `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt:58` dispositions this exact line as "no signal in the call options — unbounded outbound fetch, remaining surface in this inventory under design #1127" with **no tracking issue named**.

Distinct from neighbours: #1385 is the generated promise-client transport's missing default deadline (a different layer — this caller additionally strips Bun's own idle backstop, and the stream carve-out decision lives here); #1144 (closed) covered the separate `opencode api` command; #193 is an undiagnosed local in-process hang investigation, not the attached-server stall.

## Why it matters

`opencode run` is the scripted/headless face of the CLI — exactly the context (CI, automation, attached `--server` runs) where a silent infinite hang is worst: no UI, no error, no timeout for a supervisor to act on short of killing the process. A wedged or network-stalled server turns session setup or prompt admission into that hang, in the class design #1127 exists to eliminate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Non-streaming requests made by `opencode run` (session target resolution, session update, prompt admission, interrupt) carry a bounded deadline; a stalled server surfaces a transport/timeout error instead of hanging forever.
- [ ] The event subscription (`event.subscribe`) keeps working for long-running sessions — no request deadline kills a healthy stream (an explicit per-request carve-out for the stream, not a client-wide `timeout: false`).
- [ ] A test with a stalled server (accepts, then silence) fails the affected non-streaming call with a timeout error instead of hanging; a long-lived event-stream test still passes.
- [ ] The `packages/cli/src/run/run.ts` entry in `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` is re-dispositioned naming the bound/carve-out, and `bun run check:bounded-http` passes.

body:
## Problem

The shared OAuth callback page's bootstrap script POSTs the authorization result to the local server's token endpoint with **no deadline**, and reads a non-OK response body with an **unbounded `res.text()`**. If the local server stalls mid-callback, the page never succeeds and never fails — the user sits on a dead "connecting" page and the OAuth flow silently never completes. Both sites are dispositioned in the bounded-http allowlist as untracked remaining surfaces under design #1127; no issue owns them.

## Evidence (verified on main `cfc35c69ee`, 2026-11-02)

- `packages/core/src/oauth/page.ts:127` (inside `bootstrapScript`): `fetch(TOKEN_URL,{method:"POST",headers:{"Content-Type":"application/json"},body:JSON.stringify(body)})` — no `signal` in the call options. `TOKEN_URL` is same-origin (`window.location.origin` + the token path, line 116), so the risk is not a hostile remote — it is the local server stalling during the one POST the whole flow depends on.
- `packages/core/src/oauth/page.ts:128`: on a non-OK response, `res.text()` is read whole and thrown as the error text shown on the page — no byte cap.
- The page is the shared callback surface for every browser OAuth flow in core: `packages/core/src/mcp/oauth.ts:23`, `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/gitlab.ts:15`, `snowflake-cortex.ts:10`, `digitalocean.ts:11`, `poe.ts:7`, `openai.ts:11`, and `chatgpt.ts:15` all import `OauthCallbackPage` from this module.
- `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` dispositions both lines as "remaining surface in this inventory under design #1127" with **no tracking issue named**; the gate itself passes (all 194 candidates dispositioned), so the sites are known-but-unowned.
- Not covered by the sibling OAuth filings: #1029 and #1049 concern server-side provider token/error body reads (gitlab/poe/snowflake plugin code and MCP OAuth token errors) — neither names this browser page's POST or its error read. Title/keyword dedup search for "oauth/page" and "callback page" over open and closed issues returned nothing.

## Why it matters

This page is the last step of every "connect a provider" browser flow. A stall here has the worst failure shape: no error, no timeout, no retry affordance — the user cannot tell whether authorization worked, and the token POST may or may not have landed. Every other leg of these flows has been bounded under #1127; the page that completes them is the residual.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The bootstrap script's token POST carries a deadline (e.g. `AbortSignal.timeout(...)` composed into the fetch) so a stalled server resolves to the page's existing `fail(...)` path with a visible error instead of hanging forever.
- [ ] The non-OK error body read is byte-capped (excerpt-style: enough for a useful error message, not the whole body) before it is thrown/displayed.
- [ ] Success-path behavior is unchanged: a prompt OK response still shows success and auto-closes; a provider `error` in the callback still shows the failure card.
- [ ] A test renders the bootstrap page/script and exercises the deadline + capped-read behavior (or an equivalent script-level test in `packages/core`).
- [ ] The two `packages/core/src/oauth/page.ts` entries in `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` are re-dispositioned as bounded at the site, and `bun run check:bounded-http` passes.

body:
## Problem

The promise client's generated transport has **no default deadline**: a request whose caller passes no `signal` hangs forever when the server stalls — response headers arrive (or never do), then silence, or a body that slow-drips under the byte cap. The byte caps cannot save it: they only trip as bytes arrive, so a stalled or slow-dripping body never completes and never errors.

This is a remaining surface under design #1127 ("bounded by default"), dispositioned as untracked in the bounded-http allowlist; unlike the sibling sites filed so far (#1078, #1381, #1382), no issue owns it.

## Evidence (verified on main `cfc35c69ee`, 2026-11-02)

- `packages/client/src/promise/generated/client.ts:361` — the transport's only deadline source is the caller: `signal: requestOptions?.signal`. `ClientOptions` (same file, ~line 307) offers `baseUrl` / `fetch` / `headers` only — no timeout option and no default.
- `packages/client/src/promise/generated/client.ts:376` — `execute()` calls `fetch(prepared.url, prepared.init)` with that possibly-absent signal.
- Body reads are byte-capped but deadline-free: `json()` (line ~2624; `maxJsonBodyBytes` 16 MiB) and `binary()` (line ~2696; `maxBinaryBodyBytes` 256 MiB) loop on `reader.read()` with no timer — the caps bound memory, not time.
- In-repo callers rely on the transport: `packages/cli/src/acp/` consumes `@opencode/client` and `packages/cli/src/acp/client.ts` passes no `signal` anywhere (grep: no matches), so ordinary ACP-layer requests have no deadline at all.
- The package's own convention is per-call deadlines everywhere else: `packages/client/src/service-probe.ts:63` composes `AbortSignal.timeout(timeout)` for the `/api/info` probe; `packages/client/src/pty-handoff.ts:29,36` pass `AbortSignal.timeout(timeout)`. Only the generated transport lacks a floor.
- `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` dispositions all three generated-client sites ("no signal in the call options — unbounded outbound fetch, remaining surface in this inventory under design #1127"; two direct body reads likewise) with **no tracking issue named**.
- The file is generated: `packages/client/package.json` `generate` runs `script/build.ts` over `@opencode/httpapi-codegen`, and `check:generated` enforces the committed output matches — so the fix belongs in the codegen/template, not in a hand-edit of the generated file.

The SSE/event path is explicitly out of scope for a plain default deadline: `packages/client/src/promise/client.ts:12-14` wires `event.subscribe` with a caller signal, and long-lived streams must not be killed by a request deadline (an activity-based bound is a separate design choice).

## Why it matters

The promise client is the plain-JS face of the client package (CLI ACP layer today, external consumers tomorrow). A wedged or network-stalled server turns any ordinary call — session list, config get, prompt — into a silent infinite hang with no error to act on, in the exact class design #1127 exists to eliminate. Every other transport in the same package already carries a deadline.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Non-SSE requests made through the promise client carry a bounded default deadline when the caller supplies no signal; a caller-supplied signal still composes/wins.
- [ ] A test with a stalled server (headers then silence) and a slow-drip body under the byte cap fails the request with a transport/timeout error instead of hanging.
- [ ] SSE/event subscription behavior is unchanged (no default request deadline kills a healthy long-lived stream).
- [ ] The change lands in the `@opencode/httpapi-codegen` output source; the regenerated client is committed and `check:generated` passes in `packages/client`.
- [ ] The three `packages/client/src/promise/generated/client.ts` entries in `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` are re-dispositioned as bounded at the site (naming the bound), and `bun run check:bounded-http` passes.

body:
## Problem

In `packages/stats/core/src/r2-sql.ts`, `fetchRows` bounds its R2 SQL query in time and rows but reads the response body with a bare `response.text()` — the whole JSON body is buffered with no byte cap before `decodeResponse` parses it.

- The request itself is deadline-bound: `AbortSignal.timeout(R2_SQL_TIMEOUT_MS)` (15 min, line 5) composed with the caller's signal (lines 102–122).
- The query carries `LIMIT ${R2_SQL_MAX_ROWS}` (10,000 rows, line 4) — that bounds row **count**, not bytes. Row width is data-dependent, and a malfunctioning or unexpected upstream response (error payloads, API shape changes) is not bound by the LIMIT at all.
- The repo's own bounded-http inventory already flags this exact line as remaining work: `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt:185` dispositions it as "direct response body read not through a bounded/excerpt reader — remaining surface in this inventory under design #1127" — with no tracking issue, unlike its tracked neighbours (#1097, #1098, #1081).

Under design #1127 ("bounded by default"), the read should go through a bounded reader with a cap sized to the legitimate worst case (10,000 rows of stats data), so an oversized response fails as a clear `R2SqlQueryError` instead of buffering unbounded in the stats sync.

## Evidence (main `52ac2c2852`)

- `packages/stats/core/src/r2-sql.ts:131–136` — `try: () => response.text()` with no cap.
- `packages/stats/core/src/r2-sql.ts:4–5` — `R2_SQL_MAX_ROWS = 10_000`, `R2_SQL_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000` (the existing bounds this read lacks a byte-side counterpart for).
- `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt:185` — the gate's own "remaining surface" disposition for this line, untracked.
- Dedup: searched open + closed issues for r2-sql / R2 SQL — #1082 (closed) covers the stats **catalog** fetches in other files; no issue covers this read.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The R2 SQL response body is read through a bounded reader (e.g. `readBoundedResponseText` from `@opencode/util/http-body`, or the core `collectBoundedResponseBody`) with a named byte-cap constant in `r2-sql.ts`, sized and justified against the 10,000-row limit.
- [ ] An oversized response fails as an `R2SqlQueryError` naming the cap, through the existing error path — no partial parse.
- [ ] Normal-sized responses decode exactly as before (existing stats-core tests pass; add a test with an oversized body if the package's test setup allows).
- [ ] The bounded-http allowlist entry for this line is updated to the bounded disposition.

body:
Follow-up implementation issue for #1014 (routed by triage task 6187, 2026-11-02; the umbrella #1014 stays open — this issue owns only the two deferred CodeRabbit findings below, ported from #1014 comment 6561987451, not a re-file of the umbrella).

## Items (deferred from PR #1190 review, recorded on #1014 comment 6561987451)

1. **Stale balance holds when a balance plan is deleted or reclassified** (PR #1190 thread, `packages/core/src/model-route.ts` ~779 in that diff): `refreshQuotaGate` returns early when no relevant plan/eligible window remains, so `quota:<provider>` / `quota-credential:<id>` adjustments from a deleted or reclassified balance plan can persist indefinitely; a `windowHours` reclassification also makes `releasesHold` reject the snapshot. Fix: clear the stale balance hold when no balance grant remains, replacing it with the remaining window's normal timed gate when one exists, while preserving the hold for a still-applicable depleted balance plan.
2. **Balance-exhaustion classification breadth** (PR #1190 thread, `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts` ~455 in that diff): generic exhaustion text (e.g. a plain HTTP 429 "You have reached your rate limit") can enter the balance-exhaustion branch when the prior snapshot has `balance === true`, installing an increase-only hold with no expiry. Fix: keep the broad match for entering the quota-failure path, but require an explicitly credit/balance-specific match (or QuotaExceeded) for the balance-exhaustion classification unless the provider contract establishes the text reports credits. (Note: issue #1340 covers a different quota-gate defect from PR #1028 — not this classification item.)

## Acceptance
- Both items fixed with dedicated tests (they change hold-release/classification semantics, which is why they were deferred from #1190 rather than fixed in its merge).
- A hold for a still-applicable depleted balance plan is preserved (no regression to PR1 balance gating, #1190 merged 3739116d85).
- Generic 429 rate-limit text alone no longer installs an increase-only, no-expiry balance hold.
- Do not close #1014 from this issue's PR; link it.

body:
# fix(core): skill discovery index.json is still read unbounded — schemaBodyJson with no byte cap and no deadline (#923 residual)

## Evidence (verified this run on main `a940b080d2`)

`SkillDiscovery.pull` fetches the remote skill catalog's `index.json` and decodes the whole body with no size bound and no deadline:

- `packages/core/src/skill/discovery.ts:112-121` — `HttpClientRequest.get(index)` → `http.execute` → `HttpClientResponse.schemaBodyJson(Index)`. No `collectBoundedResponseBody`, no `Effect.timeout`. The `http` client at `discovery.ts:78-85` is only `retryTransient(times: 2)` + `filterStatusOk`; the underlying client is the plain `FetchHttpClient.layer` (`packages/util/src/effect/app-node-platform.ts:11`), which imposes neither a body cap nor a timeout.
- The same file bounds every file the index points at, precisely because the source is untrusted: `discovery.ts:14-19` — "Skill files are markdown and reference text fetched from a remote, third-party index, so the body is untrusted", `MAX_SKILL_FILE_BYTES = 5 MiB`, enforced in `download()` via `collectBoundedResponseBody` (`discovery.ts:91-97`). The index is the first and most attacker-controlled body on this path (skill sources are user-configured remote indexes, `packages/core/src/config/plugin/skill.ts`), yet it is the one body with no bound.
- This is a residual of #923: its body explicitly named this site ("the index body itself is also decoded unbounded via `schemaBodyJson`"), but the fix (commit `16377328b9`) only converted `download()` to `collectBoundedResponseBody`; `pull()`'s index decode was left as-is and #923 closed.
- Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-02-skill-index` (run on the laptop against the repo's own effect@4.0.1): `HttpClientResponse.schemaBodyJson(Index)` happily decoded a streamed (no content-length) 3,688,902-byte index with 200,000 skill entries — it buffers and parses the entire body before schema validation, so neither a declared-length pre-check nor any streaming bound ever engages.
- Tests pin the file cap but not the index: `packages/core/test/skill-discovery.test.ts:190-225` rejects skill files over `MAX_SKILL_FILE_BYTES` (declared and streamed); the fixture serves `index.json` from `state.skills` with no oversized-index case.

## Why it matters

A malicious or broken skill index (or a MITM'd plain-HTTP one) can stream an arbitrarily large JSON body into the opencode process: memory exhaustion while buffering/parsing takes down every session, not just the skill pull, and a stalled index response hangs the pull indefinitely because the fetch has no deadline either. The house pattern for exactly this shape already exists in the same file and in `packages/core/src/messaging/embedding.ts:738-740` (collect bounded bytes first, then decode the bounded bytes instead of `schemaBodyJson` on the raw response).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The `index.json` body in `SkillDiscovery.pull` is read through a named byte cap (e.g. `MAX_SKILL_INDEX_BYTES`, justified in a comment — an index is a list of names/paths, far smaller than a 5 MiB skill file), using `collectBoundedResponseBody` or the equivalent bounded reader; both a declared `content-length` over the cap and an undeclared streamed body over the cap fail the pull (log + return `[]`, matching the current failure disposition) instead of decoding.
- [ ] The index fetch gets a stated deadline (named constant, in the spirit of `WellKnown`'s 15s `requestTimeout` at `packages/core/src/wellknown.ts:63`), so a stalled index cannot hang the pull forever.
- [ ] Normal-sized indexes behave exactly as today (all existing `skill-discovery.test.ts` cases pass unchanged).
- [ ] New tests in `packages/core/test/skill-discovery.test.ts` pin the over-cap index behavior for declared and streamed bodies, mirroring the existing oversized-file test.
- [ ] Out of scope: the already-bounded skill-file downloads, and any change to the `Index` schema or the on-disk cache layout.

body:
## Finding

Dependabot PRs **#1075** (glob 13.0.5 → 14.0.2) and **#1076** (minimatch 10.2.5 → 11.0.1) both bump `packages/util` and both arrive **package.json-only — no `bun.lock` change** — so neither can merge as-is: CI's frozen-lockfile install fails when `package.json` and `bun.lock` disagree. This is the recurring class from #196 / #480, arriving again as a split pair.

The two PRs are one unit of work, not two:

- Both edit adjacent lines of the same file (`packages/util/package.json`: glob line 57, minimatch line 59), so landing one strands/conflicts the other.
- glob 14 itself moves to minimatch 11 (per the #1075 changelog: "Use minimatch 11"), so the pair should land together with a single regenerated `bun.lock`, not as two sequential half-states.

## Evidence

- PR #1075 — https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1075 — head `8271cc5d2d45b5792d82ac08c2835932d20afcd6`, OPEN, files: only `packages/util/package.json` (+1/−1).
- PR #1076 — https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1076 — head `33a77611297778e7a793f412cd836ce93f9b87d7`, OPEN, files: only `packages/util/package.json` (+1/−1).
- Current `main` (`a940b080d2c74621568e38290e56a9b4040cb543`, verified 2026-11-02) still pins `"glob": "13.0.5"` (`packages/util/package.json:57`) and `"minimatch": "10.2.5"` (`packages/util/package.json:59`), and `bun.lock` matches those pins — the bumps exist nowhere but the two stranded PRs.
- Precedent: merged dependabot PRs in this repo (e.g. #475/#476/#493/#494) all carried `bun.lock` + `package.json`; package.json-only arrivals were filed and rescued under #196, #257 (split pair), #480, #497, #498.
- Major-bump surface is small: the only in-repo consumer is `packages/util/src/glob.ts` — `glob`/`globSync` (lines 24–28) and `minimatch(filepath, pattern, { dot: true })` (line 32). None of the APIs removed in glob 14 / minimatch 11 (`makeRe`, `AST`, `Pattern#isRegExp`, `GlobWalker` set returns) are used there, but the matching-semantics changes (empty trailing portion, `**` partial matching) need a test pass, not a blind merge.

## Why it matters

glob 14 / minimatch 11 remove the RegExp-based pattern matching that made patterns ReDoS-able; leaving the pair stranded leaves `packages/util` on the old matching engine indefinitely, and two open PRs editing the same two lines rot against each other and against `main`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One consolidated change lands both bumps together (one PR rescued/superseded, the other closed as superseded with a pointer), with `bun.lock` regenerated so `package.json` and the lockfile agree.
- [ ] `packages/util` tests pass in CI on the consolidated PR, including the `Glob.scan` / `Glob.scanSync` / `Glob.match` paths in `packages/util/src/glob.ts`.
- [ ] No other package's glob/minimatch pins are changed in the same pass.
- [ ] Both #1075 and #1076 are closed/merged with a comment pointing at the consolidating PR.

Filed by pr-diff-review lane B (source PRs #1075 + #1076 reviewed 2026-11-02).
