body:
## Summary

The HTTP cassette store's file writer is the one remaining temp+rename site dispositioned in #1348's closing note as "migrate to FSUtil.writeAtomic in a follow-up under #1345" — but no implementation issue exists for it, the writer still does not conform to the #1345 atomic-replace contract on main, and the migration as stated cannot be taken without a dependency decision (below). This issue tracks closing the gap, by whichever route the triage decides.

## Evidence (main `d29a36e1b0`, verified this run)

`packages/http-recorder/src/cassette/store.ts:138-142` (the `fileSystem` layer's `append`):

- L138: temp is `${target}.${crypto.randomUUID()}.tmp`
- L139: `fs.writeFileString(temporary, formatCassette(cassette))` — no options: the temp is **not created exclusively** (no `wx` flag) and not at mode `0600`.
- L140: `fs.rename(temporary, target)` — **single attempt, no retry**.
- L142: failures go through `Effect.orDie`, so a transient rename failure becomes a defect that crashes the recording session.

The contract it should meet (design #1345, phase 1 #1346) is `packages/util/src/fs-util.ts`: `writeAtomic` (L202) creates its temp exclusively (`wx`) at `0600` beside the target, and `renameWithRetry` (L181-200, delays 10/25/50/100 ms) retries transient `EPERM`/`EACCES`/`EBUSY` rename errors — exactly the class a Windows reader holding the cassette open produces, and the class the desktop/core/tui sync writers were conformed for in #1348.

## Why "just call FSUtil.writeAtomic" needs a decision

- `packages/http-recorder/package.json` has **no `@opencode/util` dependency** — only `@effect/platform-node-shared` plus peer `effect`. It is a standalone published leaf package (it ships a `verify:package` script) consumed by `@opencode/ai` and `@opencode/core`.
- `packages/util/package.json` has no `http-recorder` dependency either, so there is no cycle — but importing `FSUtil` would pull `@opencode/util`'s full dependency tree (arborist, npm config, OpenTelemetry exporters, …) into the published recorder package.
- The cassette layer currently requires only `FileSystem.FileSystem` (e.g. `packages/http-recorder/test/support.ts:35` provides `fileSystem({ directory })` + `NodeFileSystem.layer`). `FSUtil.Service` is a separate service its consumers do not provide.

Phase 3 (#1348) set the precedent for writers that cannot consume the primitive: a **conforming local copy** tested against the same contract rows. That route — exclusive temp creation + private mode + rename-with-retry inside `store.ts` — keeps the package leaf-shaped. Adding the dependency is the alternative; either is acceptable if the choice and its reason are recorded here.

## Why it matters

Cassettes are the recorded fixtures the AI/core test suites replay. A transient rename failure (antivirus/reader lock on Windows, the exact failure the contract's retry exists for) currently kills a recording run as an unhandled defect instead of being absorbed, and the non-exclusive, default-mode temp is the same contract deviation #1348 closed in the three sibling writers. The disposition in #1348's closing note names this as owed work; without an issue it sits silently.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `append` in `packages/http-recorder/src/cassette/store.ts` creates its temp file exclusively (`wx`) at mode `0600` (or a waiver with reason is recorded on this issue).
- [ ] The rename over the target retries transient `EPERM`/`EACCES`/`EBUSY` failures with bounded backoff equivalent to the contract's (10/25/50/100 ms), instead of dying on the first failure.
- [ ] The route taken — local conforming copy vs `@opencode/util` dependency — is recorded on this issue with its reason; if the dependency route is taken, `verify:package` for `@opencode/http-recorder` still passes and the layer's provided-services contract for existing consumers is unchanged or migrated.
- [ ] Secret-redaction behaviour (`failIfUnsafe` before any write) and the append lock's ordering are unchanged.

body:
## Problem

`check:numeric-boundaries` (design #992's regression net for the bare string→number conversion class) scans only 11 production trees. The other production trees have no net at all, so a new bare `Number(...)` / `parseInt(...)` / `parseFloat(...)` on an externally supplied string can land there undetected — the exact regrowth the gate exists to prevent.

Per-tree extensions have landed one at a time (#1294 server, #1302 console+function, #1308 services, #1318 plugin-github, all closed). This filing is the remaining-trees counterpart, in the same shape as #1369 for the proto-reads gate.

## Evidence (verified on main `d29a36e1b0`, 2026-11-02)

- `script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` `SCAN_ROOTS` lists 11 roots: `packages/core/src`, `packages/ai/src`, `packages/cli/src`, `packages/server/src`, `packages/console/app/src`, `packages/console/function/src`, `packages/function/src`, `services/changelog/src`, `services/files/src`, `services/update/src`, `packages/plugin-github/src`. `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt` has **0 entries** for any other tree.
- Replicating the gate's exact patterns (P-A `\bNumber\s*\(`, P-B `\bparseInt\s*\(`, P-C `\bparseFloat\s*\(`, scanned extensions `.ts`/`.tsx`, comment-only lines skipped, as in `scanSource`) over the remaining production trees yields **182 hits across 19 trees**: tui 38, stats/app 26, app 14, stats/core 14, ui 13, gui-extensions 12, merman 12, desktop 10, util 10, codemode 9, session-ui 9, client 4, httpapi-codegen 2, script 2, simulation 2, web 2, plugin-browser 1, schema 1, theme 1. The remaining trees with 0 hits today (http-recorder, latex, plugin, protocol, sdk, stats/server, services/www) cost nothing to include and prevent silent regrowth there.
- Contrast: `check:bounded-http`'s `SCAN_ROOTS` already covers every one of these trees — the numeric gate is the outlier.
- Spot-reads of externally supplied values (all guarded / safe-by-construction, none dispositioned — the gate cannot tell them apart from a bare unguarded conversion):
  - `packages/desktop/src/main/extension/assets.ts:54-55` — `Number(match[...])` on the request `Range` header (regex `\d*` constrained, range-checked after).
  - `packages/client/src/service-probe.ts:111` — `Number(response.headers.get("content-length"))` on an upstream response, finite-checked.
  - `packages/app/src/composer/prompt.ts:48` — `Number(value)` in `positiveLine` after a `/^\d+$/` test, on URL `start`/`end` query params.
  - `packages/tui/src/editor.ts:46` — `parseEditorPort`: `Number(value)` after `/^\d+$/`, range-checked 1–65535.
  - `packages/gui-extensions/src/ssh/bootstrap.ts:79` and `packages/codemode/src/openapi/runtime.ts:299` — `Number.parseInt(content-length, 10)` with `Number.isSafeInteger` guards.
  - `packages/web/src/lib/accept-language.ts:17` — `Number.parseFloat(q)` on the client `Accept-Language` header, finite-checked.

## Why it matters

The #992 class is silent misbehaviour, not a crash: `parseInt("12abc")` truncates, `Number("")` is 0, a NaN poisons a comparator or a cap. The trees left out include network- and input-facing surfaces (desktop extension Range handling, client service probing, gui-extensions downloads, codemode OpenAPI responses, stats, tui, app) — the same shapes the landed per-tree extensions dispositioned elsewhere. Until the gate scans them, every hit is unreviewed inventory and every new hit is invisible.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` scans every production `packages/*/src` and `services/*/src` tree (including the console and stats subtrees) in addition to its existing roots; `script/check-numeric-boundaries.test.ts` is updated and green.
- [ ] Every current hit in the newly scanned trees is dispositioned: converted through the #993 primitives, guarded at the site, or allowlisted with a specific reason per existing allowlist conventions. Any live bug found while dispositioning is filed as its own issue and cross-linked, not allowlisted away.
- [ ] `bun run check:numeric-boundaries` passes on the resulting tree.
- [ ] No behaviour change to any hit dispositioned as safe/internal.

title: http-body tests: collect streamed-oversize test cannot detect a read-all-before-reject regression

body:
## Finding (from a PR review comment, never addressed)

The streamed-oversize test for `collectBoundedResponseBody` cannot detect the regression the helper exists to prevent: a collector that consumes the entire stream before rejecting an oversized body would still pass.

Reviewer **coderabbitai[bot]** (CodeRabbit, Nitpick · Trivial · Maintainability & Code Quality), 2026-10-31T10:50:39Z, in its review of PR #1069, on `packages/core/test/http-body.test.ts:57-60`:
https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1069#pullrequestreview-5722419537

> "Track chunk consumption in the collect streamed-oversize test. The test at lines 57-60 passes three 512-byte chunks with a 1024-byte cap. The third chunk is the first to exceed the cap, and no chunk follows it. The test asserts only the rejection. A regression that reads every chunk before it rejects would pass this test. The text-helper test already checks this with a `pulled` counter. Apply the same pattern here: add a fourth 512-byte chunk after the oversized chunk, count the chunks that `fakeResponse` pulls from its stream, and after rejection assert that the count is below the total number of chunks. The trailing chunk alone does not detect the regression. The counter is required."

Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1069 — "test(core): add direct tests for tool/http-body bounded-body helpers (#1068)"

This is a missing test for a specific failure mode — in-flight rejection is the bounded collector's core contract (it is what keeps memory bounded against a hostile or broken server) — not a style preference.

## No-response evidence

- PR #1069 has a single commit, `bf2ef3a746` (2026-10-31T10:42:32Z), which **predates** the review (10:50:39Z); no fix commit followed, and the PR merged as-is.
- No reply to the review exists on the PR (no inline replies; conversation contains only the Codex no-findings summary and the CodeRabbit summary).
- No issue tracks it (searched 2026-11-02: "http-body", "collectBoundedResponseBody", "chunk consumption", "bounded-body", "1069" — parent issue #1068 is closed by this PR; the other hits are production unbounded-read issues, not this test gap).

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-02)

`packages/core/test/http-body.test.ts` (blob `fd1e60f8e8dc80e88724b74652e1b3c1b8997ba2`, identical in the local clone and via the GitHub contents API), test "rejects a streamed oversized body in flight" in `describe("collectBoundedResponseBody (#1068)")`:

```ts
const chunk = new Uint8Array(512)
await expect(collect(fakeResponse([chunk, chunk, chunk]), 1024)).rejects.toThrow("response body too large")
```

Three chunks, the third is the first over the cap, nothing follows it, and the only assertion is the rejection — exactly as the review described. The sibling `readBoundedResponseText` streamed-oversize test in the same file already uses the `pulled` counter pattern the review points to.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The collect streamed-oversize test adds a chunk after the first oversized chunk and counts stream pulls (via the existing `fakeResponse` `onStream`/an equivalent counter), asserting consumption stopped below the total after rejection.
- [ ] The strengthened test fails against a read-all-then-reject variant of the collector and passes against current production code.
- [ ] Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why the coverage is unnecessary.

# fix(client): generated client stale on main — check:generated red (quotaGate.balanceDeadThreshold missing from committed types)

## Evidence (verified this run, main fd690f6c7e)

Running the repo's own generated-client check on a clean checkout of main fails:

```
$ cd packages/client && bun run check:generated
# = bun run generate && git diff --exit-code -- src/promise/generated src/effect/generated src/effect/api
error: script "check:generated" exited with code 1
```

Regeneration produces exactly this uncommitted drift in `packages/client/src/promise/generated/types.ts` (2 hunks, 2 lines):

```diff
-              quotaGate?: { maxMs?: number; fallbackMs?: number; feedTtlMs?: number }
+              quotaGate?: { maxMs?: number; fallbackMs?: number; feedTtlMs?: number; balanceDeadThreshold?: number }
```

(same change in both `ConfigEntry` quotaGate occurrences, ~lines 2841 and ~2910 of the generated file.)

The field is real and live in the source of truth:

- `packages/schema/src/config/model-routes.ts:411` — `balanceDeadThreshold: Schema.Finite.check(Schema.isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(0))` in the quotaGate schema.
- `packages/core/src/model-route.ts:2223,2248` — the constant is part of `quotaGate` constants, defaulted from `QuotaSnapshot.DEFAULT_BALANCE_DEAD_THRESHOLD`.
- `packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts:494,500` — consumed when deriving quota snapshots.

The schema change landed without regenerating the client, so the committed generated types are stale. (`services/www`'s `check:generated` was also run this run and passes — this drift is client-only.)

## Why it matters

- The committed generated types are what SDK consumers compile against: `quotaGate.balanceDeadThreshold` is a real, documented-by-schema config knob that the typed client cannot express.
- `check:generated` is a CI step in `.github/workflows/test.yml` ("Check generated client"); a red-on-main gate trains everyone to ignore it and hides the next drift. This is the same class as #450, #483, #676 (client) and #829 (www) — each was a distinct field drift, fixed by regenerating.

## Acceptance criteria

- `bun run generate` in `packages/client` is run and the regenerated output committed; the only change is the `balanceDeadThreshold` addition above (any further drift found is reported on this issue, not silently bundled).
- `cd packages/client && bun run check:generated` exits 0 on the resulting tree.
- No hand-edits to generated files beyond what the generator produces; no schema or core changes.

title: fix(core): v1 migration silently converts malformed base64 data-URL attachments into empty/corrupted files instead of marking them unavailable

body:
## Problem

The V1→V2 migration's file-part handler validates the **non-base64** data-URL branch but not the **base64** branch. A legacy file part whose `;base64` payload contains garbage is silently converted into an empty or garbage-stripped file and stored as a valid migrated attachment, instead of taking the `invalid-data-url` path #1358 added (which renders the attachment as `[Attachment unavailable after migration: …]`).

## Evidence (verified on main `adb82331d1`, this run)

- `packages/core/src/database/v1-migration.bun.ts:1058-1059` — the base64 branch is a bare re-encode with no validation:
  ```ts
  const data = header.endsWith(";base64")
    ? Buffer.from(payload, "base64").toString("base64")
    : decodeFilePayload(payload)
  ```
  `Buffer.from(str, "base64")` never throws on a string and silently **ignores characters outside the base64 alphabet**, so `data` is never `undefined` and the `invalid-data-url` return at `:1061` is unreachable for this branch.
- Contrast the sibling branch in the same function: `decodeFilePayload` (`:1074-1080`) catches the `URIError` from `decodeURIComponent` and returns `undefined` → `invalid-data-url` (the #1358 fix, PR #1359).
- Contrast the live ingestion path: `packages/core/src/session/prompt.ts:222-223` rejects non-canonical base64 outright (`bytes.toString("base64") !== payload` → `AttachmentError`).
- Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-v1-migration-base64` (replicates the `:1058-1059` expression verbatim; `migrateFile` is not exported), Bun:
  | payload | migration result (`data`) | prompt.ts |
  |---|---|---|
  | `aGk=` | `aGk=` ✓ | ok |
  | `!!!` | `""` — empty file stored as valid | REJECTED |
  | `====` | `""` — empty file stored as valid | REJECTED |
  | `aGk=####` | `aGk=` — garbage silently dropped | REJECTED |
  | `aG!k=` | `aGk=` — garbage silently dropped | REJECTED |
  | `aGk` (unpadded) | `aGk=` — normalized | REJECTED |
- Downstream, stored `file.data` is trusted as valid base64 with no further check (`packages/core/src/session/runner/to-llm-message.ts:43,62`, `packages/core/src/messaging/log.ts:59`), so the corrupted/empty bytes propagate as the user's attachment content.
- Test gap: `packages/core/test/v1-migration.test.ts:220-227` pins the malformed percent-encoded case (#1358) and a valid base64 case, but has no malformed-base64 case.

## Why it matters

Migration is one-shot and effectively irreversible for the migrated session: a corrupt legacy attachment becomes a plausible-looking empty/truncated file in V2 instead of the explicit "unavailable" placeholder, so neither the user nor any later diagnostic can tell data was lost. #1358 established the fail-closed disposition for exactly this function; the base64 branch — the common case for real attachments — missed it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `;base64` payload containing characters outside the base64 alphabet (e.g. `!!!`, `aG!k=`, `aGk=####`) takes the `invalid-data-url` path and migrates as the unavailable placeholder, never as a stored file.
- [ ] Canonical payloads (`aGk=`, `aGVsbG8gd29ybGQ=`) migrate byte-identical to today.
- [ ] Unpadded / whitespace-bearing payload handling is decided explicitly and pinned by a test (normalize-and-keep or invalid — either is acceptable, silence is not).
- [ ] New cases in `packages/core/test/v1-migration.test.ts` next to the #1358 cases cover the above.

body:
# fix(core): v1 migration throws URIError on a malformed non-base64 data-URL attachment — one legacy file part wedges the whole migration at the same session forever

## Evidence (verified this run, main `3177e78a84`)

- `packages/core/src/database/v1-migration.bun.ts:1047` (`migrateFile`, defined :1039): the non-base64 branch is `Buffer.from(decodeURIComponent(payload)).toString("base64")` — unguarded. Any legacy `SessionV1.FilePart` whose `data:` URL payload is not valid percent-encoding (a bare `%`, `%zz`, a truncated `%E0%A4%A`) throws `URIError`.
- The migration's own design is skip-and-warn for bad legacy rows: `transformSession` (:222) pushes `invalid-message` / `invalid-part` / `orphan-part` warnings (:232/:243/:259) and continues. `migrateFile` bypasses that — it is called from the user-message projection at :322 (`files.flatMap((part) => migrateFile(part))`) with no try/catch anywhere in `transformSession`.
- The throw is not contained per session: `run()` calls `transformSession` at :637 inside the per-session transaction, which is piped through `Effect.orDie` (:671, and `run()` itself at :698). The layer (:505) forks `run()` and records `runtimeState = { status: "error" }` on failure. The migration cursor is written inside the same transaction, so the defect rolls it back — the next start retries the **same** session, fails the same way, and every session after it never migrates.
- Laptop probe (real code, not a replica) — `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-v1-migration-decode/probe.ts`, importing `V1Migration.transformSession` from the laptop clone at the same HEAD, run with bun from `packages/core`:
  - control `data:text/plain,hello%20world` → OK, attachment `aGVsbG8gd29ybGQ=`, no warnings
  - control `data:text/plain;base64,aGk=` → OK, attachment `aGk=`
  - `data:text/plain,100% coverage` → **THREW `URIError: URI error`**
  - `data:text/plain,%zz` → **THREW `URIError: URI error`**
- Existing tests (`packages/core/test/v1-migration.test.ts`, "maps embedded files…") cover a valid encoded payload (`hello%20world`) and base64 only — no malformed-payload case.
- Dedup: `gh search issues` for `migration decodeURIComponent`, `v1-migration migrateFile`, `migration data URL attachment`, and open/closed list scan — no existing issue covers this. The live sibling decoder in `packages/core/src/session/prompt.ts` (`decodeDataURL`, :213) already wraps the same decode in `Effect.try` → `AttachmentError`; only the migration copy is unguarded.

## Why it matters

The v1→v2 migration runs at startup for every user upgrading with a legacy database. A single malformed attachment — exactly the kind of corrupt legacy data a migration exists to survive — permanently wedges the migration in an error state: no later session migrates, and every restart re-fails at the same cursor with only a generic "V1 migration failed" log. The fix should follow the migration's established disposition for bad rows (skip with a warning), not invent a new one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A legacy file part with a malformed non-base64 data-URL payload (`100% coverage`, `%zz`, truncated `%E0%A4%A`) no longer throws out of `transformSession`; the attachment is skipped and a warning (consistent with the existing `Warning` reasons) is recorded, or the message migrates with the attachment dropped and the skip is logged.
- [ ] The rest of the session (text and other parts) and subsequent sessions migrate normally after such a part.
- [ ] Valid payloads migrate byte-identically to today: percent-encoded (`hello%20world` → `aGVsbG8gd29ybGQ=`) and base64 (`aGk=`) controls unchanged.
- [ ] New test(s) in `packages/core/test/v1-migration.test.ts` cover at least one malformed non-base64 payload alongside the existing controls.
- [ ] No change to the live prompt-path decoder (`session/prompt.ts decodeDataURL`) or to base64 handling.

body:
## Problem

A malformed percent-encoded `oc://extensions/<id>/<path>` request settles as a **500 with an error-level report** instead of a 404, because the extension asset handler decodes the path with an unguarded `decodeURIComponent`.

## Evidence (main `3177e78a84`, verified this run)

- `packages/desktop/src/main/extension/assets.ts:32`, in `extensionAsset`:
  ```ts
  const [id, ...rest] = url.pathname.slice(1).split("/").map(decodeURIComponent)
  ```
  There is no try/catch in the function, so a malformed segment throws `URIError: URI malformed` before any lookup happens.
- Wiring: `packages/desktop/src/main/extension/index.ts:50` — `setExtensionAssets((request, url) => extensionAsset(storage.db, request, url))`.
- The throw is caught one layer up in `packages/desktop/src/main/windows/protocol.ts` (extension-host branch of `serve()`), which does `report("error", "extension asset error", …)` and returns `new Response(null, { status: 500 })`. A bad URL from a renderer/extension is client input, not a server failure.
- Contrast in the same protocol handler, on current main: the renderer branch returns **404** for malformed paths via `resolveRendererPath` (`packages/desktop/src/main/windows/renderer-path.ts`, fixed for #1349 / PR #1350) and reports at warning level. The two hosts of the same `oc://` protocol now disagree on what a malformed path means.
- There is no test file for `assets.ts` (the extension folder has `lifecycle.test.ts`, `manager.test.ts`, `storage.test.ts` only).

### Reproduction (laptop probe)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-extension-assets-decode` (laptop, replicating the assets.ts:32 decode and the protocol.ts catch-to-500 wrapper):

- `oc://extensions/my-ext/assets/app%2ejs` → 200, `id=my-ext`, `path=assets/app.js` (valid control decodes correctly)
- `oc://extensions/%zz/app.js` → 500, `URIError: URI malformed`
- `oc://extensions/my-ext/%E0%A4%A` → 500, `URIError: URI malformed`
- `oc://extensions/my-ext/assets/%` → 500, `URIError: URI malformed`

Note on #1349: its queue packet scoped this site out as "covered by its caller's catch". This issue does not claim a crash — it is about that catch's disposition: 500 + error telemetry for malformed client input, inconsistent with the renderer branch's 404.

## Why it matters

- Error-level reports for malformed URLs pollute the desktop error signal with non-errors and can mask real extension-asset failures.
- Extensions/renderers that retry or surface status codes treat 500 (server fault, retryable) differently from 404 (no such asset, terminal).
- The unguarded decode is the same pattern the repo has been fixing fail-closed elsewhere (#1328, #1349); this is the remaining `oc://` host that was left inconsistent.

## Acceptance criteria

- A malformed percent-encoded extension id or path segment settles as a 404 response from `extensionAsset` (or an equivalent fail-closed result), never as a thrown `URIError` reaching the protocol layer's 500 catch.
- No error-level `extension asset error` report is emitted for malformed encodings (warning or silent 404, matching the renderer branch's disposition).
- Valid percent-encoded ids/paths decode and serve exactly as before, including byte-range handling.
- A new unit test for `extensionAsset` covers malformed encodings (`%zz`, `%E0%A4%A`, trailing `%`) and a valid encoded control.

body:
## Problem

The desktop renderer's custom-protocol handler decodes the request path with an unguarded `decodeURIComponent`, outside any `try`/`catch`:

`packages/desktop/src/main/windows/protocol.ts:88` (on main `4b4f4673ab`), in `serve()`:

```ts
const file = path.resolve(rendererRoot, `.${decodeURIComponent(url.pathname)}`)
```

- The only `try` in `serve()` starts at `:97`, *after* the decode and the traversal check — it covers only the `net.fetch` at `:99`.
- The caller, `registerRendererProtocol` (`:56-65`), wraps `serve()` in `try { … } finally { inflight--; served++ }` — a `finally`, not a `catch`. A `URIError` from the decode therefore rejects the Electron `protocol.handle` callback outright instead of settling as an HTTP response, unlike the extension-host branch in the same function (`:72-80`), which catches and returns a 500.

## Reproduction (laptop probe, `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-desktop-protocol-decode`)

```
"/%E0%A4%A"      -> THROWS URIError URI malformed
"/%zz"           -> THROWS URIError URI malformed
"/assets/%"      -> THROWS URIError URI malformed
"/index.html"    -> "/index.html"          (control)
"/assets/app%2ejs" -> "/assets/app.js"     (control)
```

Any renderer asset request whose URL path carries a malformed percent escape — a stray `%` in a filename, a truncated UTF-8 sequence — hits this path, because asset URLs are built from file paths.

## Why it matters

This is the same throw-instead-of-refuse defect fixed for the sibling file-URL policy in #1328, and the house pattern elsewhere is fail-closed: `services/files` returns 400 on a bad decode (`services/files/src/index.ts:29-34`), the server location decoder catches and falls back (`packages/server/src/location.ts:82-88`). The renderer protocol is the outlier: one malformed asset path takes down the request with an unhandled rejection in the main process instead of the 404 the handler already returns for rejected hosts and traversal attempts.

- [ ] A malformed percent-encoded renderer path settles as a response (404, matching the handler's rejected-host / rejected-path responses), never as a rejected `protocol.handle` callback

- [ ] A unit test covers the malformed cases (`%E0%A4%A`, `%zz`, trailing `%`) plus the valid controls — there is currently no test file for `protocol.ts`
- [ ] The extension-host branch behavior is unchanged

## Phase 1 of design #1345 — the atomic-replace primitive in `@opencode/util`

Design #1345 (doc: `files/designs/opencode-atomic-replace-contract.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace) states one atomic-replace contract for user-owned files. Today there is no such primitive: `FSUtil` (`packages/util/src/fs-util.ts`) offers `writeWithDirs` and `writeJson`, both in-place, and at least ten writers hand-roll temp+rename with divergent rules.

### Scope

Add to `FSUtil` in `packages/util/src/fs-util.ts`:

- `writeAtomic(path, content, options?)` implementing the design's rules 1–6: temp file in the same directory as the **resolved** target (symlinks resolved via the existing `resolve`/`realPath` behaviour first), temp name unique per invocation (pid + random), created **exclusively** (`wx`) at mode `0o600`, rename over the target with retry on transient Windows codes (EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY, delays 10/25/50/100 ms — the schedule the three existing `renameSyncWithRetry` copies share), and on any failure the temp is removed, the original error propagates, and the target is left byte-identical.
- Mode as a named option: `modePolicy: "preserve"` (existing file keeps its exact mode; fresh file gets `freshMode`, defaulting to `0o600`) or `"owner-capped"` (existing mode `& 0o600`; fresh `0o600`) — the two policies the existing writers already embody. A write never widens permissions.
- An explicit `preserveOwnership` option (rule 7) carrying uninstall's chown-before-rename behaviour (#1290), off by default.
- `writeJsonAtomic(path, data, options?)` built on `writeAtomic` (JSON.stringify with the same formatting `writeJson` uses today).

### Conformance suite (the shared probe matrix)

One table-driven suite in `packages/util` covering, at minimum: round-trip replace of an existing file; fresh create under both mode policies; existing mode under both policies (including a read-only `0o400` file staying `0o400` under `preserve`); symlinked target — link preserved, content lands on the real file; temp-name collision refused by `wx` rather than overwritten; rename retry succeeding on an injected transient EPERM; a failing write leaving the target byte-identical with no temp file left behind.

### Acceptance

- [ ] `FSUtil.writeAtomic` / `writeJsonAtomic` land in `packages/util` with the contract above; no call site migrates in this issue (phases 2–3 do that).
- [ ] The conformance suite passes and every matrix row above is a test.
- [ ] `bun run check` from the repo root passes, or pre-existing base-branch failures are named in the closing note; tests run from package directories, never the repo root.

body:
## Design: Replace it whole, or not at all — one atomic-replace contract for user-owned files

**Design doc:** `files/designs/opencode-atomic-replace-contract.md` in the goal workspace (keep-the-four-repos-healthy) — problem, evidence, alternatives, risks, and open questions in full. Grounded on main `4b4f4673ab`.

### Problem

At least thirteen filings in this repo are one shape — a user-owned file rewritten by truncating it in place, or an atomic rewrite whose hand-rolled mechanism missed one rule: #85, #99, #924, #977, #988, #1056, #1067, #1073, #1290, #1291, #1295 (all closed), and two still open: #998 (core `Config.update` rewrites the global config in place) and #1005 (desktop `saveFile` writes the user's chosen file in place). The fixes are not converging: #1067 is titled "#1056 residual", #1073 "the one writer #1067/#1070 missed", #1295 "#1291 residual in the sibling writers", #1290 "#988 acceptance unmet". Each fix stated the rules in a comment at one site ("Match the sibling config writers: …") and the next residual was found in a sibling. This pass's predecessor (2026-10-31) named this family the runner-up candidate: "revisit next pass if #998-class residuals keep spawning" — #1291/#1295/#1290 are exactly those residuals, and #998/#1005 are still open.

### Current state

- **No shared primitive:** `FSUtil` (`packages/util/src/fs-util.ts`) — the Effect filesystem core/cli already use — offers `writeWithDirs` and `writeJson`, both in-place. Nothing in `@opencode/util` does temp+rename.
- **At least ten private implementations, divergent on every axis:** temp name (unique pid+UUID in the cli config family and tui · pid+random hex in uninstall · `Math.random()` in core `model-plan.ts`/`model-route-overrides.ts` · **fixed `${file}.tmp`** in desktop `atomic-write.ts` · fixed `${file}.${id}.tmp` in cli `service-registration.ts`); exclusive `wx` creation (mcp/plugin/uninstall yes post-#1291/#1295, the cli config writers and everyone else no); symlink resolution (cli family + uninstall yes, desktop/tui/core sync no); mode policy (existing `& 0o600` in the cli family · exact preserve in uninstall, whose comment notes the other writers "hardcode 0o600" · unstated in desktop/tui/core); ownership preservation (uninstall only, #1290); temp cleanup on failure (migrate/desktop/tui/core yes, cli `config/config.ts` + `service-config.ts` no).
- **Three verbatim copies of `renameSyncWithRetry`** (core `model-plan.ts`, core `model-route-overrides.ts`, desktop `atomic-write.ts`, each commented "kept in sync with" another) plus an async twin in tui — while every cli Effect writer renames with no retry at all, despite #99 being the precedent.
- **No writer fsyncs** — today's de-facto contract is atomicity (no partial file is ever observed), not power-loss durability. Named an open question, not silently settled here.
- Dedupe: `kind/design` here is #587/#800/#992/#1127 only; #992 governs numeric values, #1127 outbound HTTP bodies, openchamber #976 is the sibling design in that repo's layer. Searches for symlink/atomic returned only per-site fixes — no shared design or epic covers file replacement.

### The contract (proposal)

1. **Replace, never truncate** — temp file in the same directory as the resolved target, rename over it; the target is never opened for writing.
2. **Resolve first** — a symlinked target is resolved before the temp is placed, so the rename lands on the real file and the link survives.
3. **The temp is private and unique** — pid + random name, created exclusively (`wx`) at mode `0o600`; concurrent writers cannot consume each other's rename source, secret-bearing content is never briefly world-readable.
4. **Mode is a named policy:** `preserve` (existing file keeps its exact mode; fresh file gets the caller's stated default) or `owner-capped` (existing `& 0o600`, fresh `0o600` — the cli config family's current behaviour for secret-bearing configs). A write never widens permissions; a third policy needs a design, not a comment.
5. **Rename retries the transient Windows codes** — EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY on the house schedule (10/25/50/100 ms) all existing copies already share.
6. **Failure leaves no trace** — temp removed, original error propagates, target byte-identical.
7. **Ownership preserved where preserved today** (uninstall's chown-before-rename) via an explicit option; generalising it is an open question.

One implementation per layer (the #1127 rule): the Effect home is `FSUtil` in `@opencode/util` (already a dependency of core and cli); the sync writers (core stores, desktop Electron main) cannot consume an Effect API, so they become *conforming copies* — same contract, same shared probe matrix as tests, "kept in sync" comments replaced by a pointer to the contract. Read-modify-write locking (`Flock`, permits) stays at call sites — atomic replace makes a write indivisible, it does not serialise writers.

Alternatives (per-site status quo; one implementation forced on every layer; fsync-everything now) and why they lose are in the design doc.

### Phases

- **Phase 1 (filed as a sub-issue):** `FSUtil.writeAtomic` / `writeJsonAtomic` in `packages/util` implementing rules 1–6 (ownership as an option), plus one table-driven conformance suite over the shared probe matrix (round-trip replace, fresh create under both mode policies, existing mode under both, symlink preserved, `wx` collision refused, injected-EPERM rename retry, failure leaves target intact and no temp). No call-site migrations.
- **Phase 2 (filed as a sub-issue, plus one adopted instance):** the cli Effect writers migrate onto the primitive behaviour-identical — `config/config.ts`, `config/migrate.ts`, `services/service-config.ts`, `services/service-registration.ts`, `mcp/add.ts`, `plugin/add.ts`, `plugin/remove.ts`, uninstall's `writeShellConfig` (ownership via the option). Core's instance is already filed: **#998 is adopted as phase 2's core instance**, linked as a sub-issue, keeping its own queue lifecycle; its fix routes through the primitive once phase 1 lands.
- **Phase 3 (filed as a sub-issue, plus one adopted instance):** the sync layer conforms — desktop `atomic-write.ts` gains a unique exclusively-created temp (rules 3+6) with tests extended from the shared matrix; core `model-plan.ts` / `model-route-overrides.ts` and tui `writeJsonAtomic` checked against the matrix, gaps closed or explicitly waived on the phase issue. **#1005 is adopted as phase 3's desktop instance**, linked as a sub-issue, keeping its own queue lifecycle; its fix routes `saveFile` through the conformed helper. The phase closes with a disposition list for the remaining private sites (http-recorder cassette store, desktop-cli, pty binary, skill/embedding staging): conform, migrate, or leave-with-reason.

### Open questions (in the doc, not filed as issues)

fsync durability per file class (needs a cost measurement); ownership preservation as a general rule vs a shell-rc special case; a `check:atomic-writes` ratchet in the #1129 shape (revisit once the private-writer list shrinks); service-registration's fixed temp name (phase 2 answers it for that site).

🤖 Filed by the repo-design-architect job. No Drew decision needed — mechanism consolidation only; mode policies name the behaviours the writers already have, and no call site's file content changes.
<!-- agent-note:v1 agent=repo-design-architect state=filed at=2026-11-01T19:33:00Z -->

## Acceptance criteria

- The contract is specified once (FSUtil.writeAtomic semantics: temp-write, fsync, rename, directory fsync, cleanup on failure) and the conformance probe suite exists that every writer migration must pass.
- The still-open in-place writers named in the design (issue #998 core `Config.update`, issue #1005 desktop `saveFile`) are migrated onto the contract or explicitly excepted with a reason.
- Each phase child (issues #1346, #1347, #1348 and successors) lands with the conformance probes green in CI; no writer keeps a hand-rolled atomic mechanism after its migration phase.

body:
## Problem

The two daily GitHub housekeeping scripts that comment on and **close** issues and PRs make every GitHub API call with no deadline, and read response bodies unbounded:

**`script/github/close-issues.ts`** (on main `4b4f4673ab`):
- `:45` comment `POST` fetch — no `signal` in the init
- `:52` close `PATCH` fetch — no `signal`
- `:67` list pager fetch — no `signal`; `:73` `(await res.json())` buffers the whole page unbounded
- The pager is `while (true)`; there is no `AbortSignal` anywhere in the file

**`script/github/close-prs.ts`**:
- `:296` `githubRequest()` fetch — no `signal`. Its retry loop (up to 10 attempts, sleeps up to 300s) only engages *after a response arrives*; a stalled or slow-dripping `api.github.com` connection never returns, so the retries never help
- `:275` `ensureCleanupLabel()` fetch — no `signal`, and it bypasses `githubRequest` entirely
- `:251` `(await response.json())` in `graphql()` unbounded; `:306` `await response.text()` error-body read unbounded

## Where they run

`.github/workflows/repo-sweeper.yml:176` runs `bun script/github/close-issues.ts` in the daily 02:00 UTC window and `:186` runs `bun script/github/close-prs.ts --execute` in the daily 22:00 UTC window. The shared `sweep` job's `timeout-minutes: 90` (`repo-sweeper.yml:57`) — shared with every other sweeper step — is the only bound: one stalled fetch can burn the whole job window and starve the steps scheduled after the closers.

## Why it matters

Same class as #1329 / #1332 / #1337 (script fetches with no deadline), but these two were missed by that series and they perform destructive writes (closing issues/PRs). The bounded-http gate (`script/check-bounded-http.ts`) explicitly scopes root `script/` out, so these sites have no regression net either — the per-site fix is the established pattern for this tree.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every `fetch()` in `script/github/close-issues.ts` and `script/github/close-prs.ts` carries a named deadline constant via `AbortSignal.timeout(...)` (or an equivalent composed signal), sized for the GitHub API (the sibling script fixes used 30s-class constants)
- [ ] Response bodies are read through a bounded reader or capped: the pager/`graphql()` `.json()` reads and the `githubRequest` error-body `.text()` read cannot buffer an unbounded body
- [ ] Retry behavior in `githubRequest` is preserved: a deadline expiry is treated as a retryable failure where the existing status-based logic would retry, and the label-existence check in `ensureCleanupLabel` keeps its 404 semantics
- [ ] A stalled-server test (headers or body never arrive) proves each script path settles with a deadline error instead of hanging — following the test pattern in `packages/script/test/` / `script/*.test.ts`
- [ ] Dry-run behavior of `close-prs.ts` (the default) is unchanged apart from the bounds

body:
## Finding

For a quota window with a fixed reset rule (e.g. `resetRule: "daily 00:00 UTC"`), the proactive gate feed reads usage over a rolling `windowHours` lookback instead of the current quota period. Just after the reset, usage from the end of the previous period still counts, so a provider that was full at 23:55 derives a known-full snapshot at 00:05 — with `resetAt` already advanced to the *following* midnight — and is re-gated for almost another full period despite having reset.

This is Codex P2 finding 4429477406 on PR #1028, merged without a fix or a reply (the PR's final Codex state is `has_unresolved_findings: true`). The sibling P1 from the same review was filed as #1106 and fixed by PR #1113; this P2 was never filed.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1028 "fix(core): feed current quota reads into route candidacy gate (#984)", merged, head c9aeff9c578aa00f37698bd219a1cfb24d1d093a. Codex finding: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1028#discussion_r4429477406
- Current main 51c4457109774c9d7063b5e861ed1ef62c6783d1, packages/core/src/quota-snapshot.ts:132-137: `usageSince` returns `now - window.windowHours * 3_600_000` for every windowed quota — it never looks at the window's `resetRule`/`resetAt`, so the lookback always straddles the period boundary. (Its only period-aware branch is the non-windowed credit-balance case, which starts at the grant's creation.)
- The feed sums `ModelRouteLog.targetUsage(db, usageSince(plan, window, now))` rows into the window's totals (model-resolver.ts:462-467), and `QuotaSnapshot.derive`/`resetAtOf` (quota-snapshot.ts:69-85) advances a daily rule's `resetAt` to the next occurrence — so the post-midnight known-full snapshot carries a reset almost a full period in the future, and `isKnownFull` (reset still ahead, percent ≥ 100) keeps the gate armed until then.
- Worked example (from the finding): 100 requests at 23:55 against a 100-request daily limit; at 00:05 the rolling 24h totals still include them, percent = 100, resetAt = next midnight → provider gated for ~24h of a period in which it has used nothing.

## Why it matters

Daily-reset quotas are the common shape for the providers this gate manages (#984 names cline-pass, commandcode, go). Every provider that legitimately exhausts a daily window near the end of its period risks being held out for a second, phantom period — halving its availability — and the health log records it as quota exhaustion, so the mis-gate is invisible in normal operation.

## Acceptance criteria

- For windows whose reset is derivable (daily rule or explicit `resetAt`), the feed's usage read starts at the current period's start (the most recent reset instant), not at `now - windowHours`; rolling windows without a fixed reset keep the rolling lookback.
- A regression test pins the boundary: usage timestamped just before a daily reset does not count toward the new period's snapshot, and usage just after it does.
- Existing quota-snapshot / model-resolver / route-usage suites stay green.

Dedupe: searched open + closed issues 2026-11-01 for "fixed-reset", "quota period", "daily reset quota usage previous period", and the finding's title — no existing issue covers this. #1106 (closed) covered only the sibling Codex P1; #1033 (closed) was about burn-rate sample bucketing, not the gate feed's lookback.

## Finding

When no window of a provider is known-full, `QuotaSnapshot.gatingSnapshot` falls back to the FIRST snapshot of the pool — which may be an unknown snapshot (a window with no `windowHours`/limit derives percent `null`) — even when a later window's snapshot is known and below its limit. Both gate observers reject an unknown update whenever prior gate state exists, so a gate that was armed by the known window is never cleared by the fresh below-limit reading.

This is Codex P2 finding 4429477398 on PR #1028, merged without a fix or a reply (the PR's final Codex state is `has_unresolved_findings: true`). The sibling P1 from the same review was filed as #1106 and fixed by PR #1113; this P2 was never filed. The fallback shape survives unchanged in today's `gatingSnapshot`.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1028 "fix(core): feed current quota reads into route candidacy gate (#984)", merged, head c9aeff9c578aa00f37698bd219a1cfb24d1d093a. Codex finding: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1028#discussion_r4429477398
- Current main 51c4457109774c9d7063b5e861ed1ef62c6783d1, packages/core/src/quota-snapshot.ts:170: `return deadBalance ?? latestFull ?? pool.find((snapshot) => snapshot.balance) ?? pool[0]` — no preference for a *known* snapshot in the non-full fallback. Pool order is plan-then-window order from `deriveAll` (quota-snapshot.ts:174-182).
- packages/core/src/model-route.ts:831 (credential path) and :929 (provider path): `if (previous && !QuotaSnapshot.known(snapshot)) return` — an unknown snapshot delivered by the feed is dropped whenever the target is already gated, so the stale gate state stands.
- Scenario from the finding: window 1 has no limit/windowHours (unknown snapshot, pool[0]); window 2 is a rolling window with a null reset. Window 2 arms the gate at 100%; after usage drops, the feed delivers window 1's unknown snapshot, the observers reject it, and — with no reset to expire it — the credential/provider can remain blocked indefinitely. The half-open probe work (#1305) only helps gates that have a known reset time.

## Why it matters

A provider that recovered its headroom stays out of rotation not because any reading says it is full, but because the feed picked the wrong representative snapshot. For null-reset windows there is no timed expiry to rescue it; the route silently loses a healthy provider until process restart or an unrelated state reset.

## Acceptance criteria

- `gatingSnapshot`'s non-full fallback prefers a known snapshot (e.g. the first known one, or the freshest known) over an unknown `pool[0]`; an unknown snapshot is chosen only when every snapshot in the pool is unknown.
- A regression test pins the multi-window case: window 1 unknown, window 2 known-full arms the gate, then window 2 known-below-limit clears it (provider and credential observers).
- Existing quota-snapshot / model-route suites stay green, including the dead-balance and latest-full precedence tests.

Dedupe: searched open + closed issues 2026-11-01 for "gatingSnapshot unknown", "known snapshot", "multi-window gate", and the finding's title — no existing issue covers this. #1106 (closed) covered only the sibling Codex P1.

body:
## Finding

The proactive quota gate feed derives gating snapshots from every plan stored for a provider — including plans whose status is `expired` or `cancelled`, which the plan store deliberately retains as history. A retained plan with a smaller windowed quota can produce the selected known-full snapshot and gate a provider whose current (active) plan still has capacity.

This is Codex P2 finding 4429477391 on PR #1028, merged without a fix or a reply (the PR's final Codex state is `has_unresolved_findings: true`). The sibling P1 from the same review was filed as #1106 and fixed by PR #1113; this P2 was never filed.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1028 "fix(core): feed current quota reads into route candidacy gate (#984)", merged, head c9aeff9c578aa00f37698bd219a1cfb24d1d093a. Codex finding: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1028#discussion_r4429477391
- Current main 51c4457109774c9d7063b5e861ed1ef62c6783d1, packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts:450: `relevantPlans = plans.filter((plan) => targetProviders.has(plan.providerID))` — no status filter. `ModelPlan.readStore` (model-plan.ts:112) returns the whole store; plan `status` is one of `active | expired | cancelled | unknown` (model-plan.ts:20).
- Totals are per-provider (scoped per credential after #1113), not per-plan: the same usage rows are derived against every plan of the provider (model-resolver.ts:462-510), so an old plan's smaller limit yields a higher percent for the same usage.
- The expired-plan mitigation that exists today covers only credit balances: packages/core/src/quota-snapshot.ts:122 spreads `expired` into a snapshot only when `balance` is true, and `gatingSnapshot` (quota-snapshot.ts:152-171) only excludes plans whose *balance* snapshot is expired. A windowed snapshot from an expired/cancelled plan carries no expired marker, is never excluded from the pool, and `isKnownFull` (percent ≥ 100 with a future reset) lets it win as `latestFull`.

## Why it matters

Plans accumulate: a provider whose user replaced a small plan with a bigger one keeps the old plan in the store as history. The gate can then bench the whole provider (or a credential) at the old plan's limit while the current plan has headroom — a self-inflicted outage of that route until the old plan's stated reset, with the health log attributing it to quota exhaustion.

## Acceptance criteria

- Gate derivation in the candidacy feed considers only plans applicable now (active status, not past `expiresOn`), for windowed and balance windows alike — or expired/cancelled plans' snapshots are excluded inside `gatingSnapshot` whenever a live plan of the same provider contributes a snapshot.
- A regression test with an expired small plan alongside an active larger plan for one provider shows the provider is NOT gated at the old plan's limit, and a test shows an expired plan still gates when it is the provider's only plan (nothing live to prefer), if that remains the intended semantics — either way the chosen semantics is pinned by a test.
- Existing model-route / quota-snapshot / model-resolver suites stay green.

Dedupe: searched open + closed issues 2026-11-01 for "expired plan quota gate", "historical plans", "gatingSnapshot", and the finding's title — no existing issue covers this. #1106 (closed) covered only the sibling Codex P1. The balance half of this shape was mitigated by the later balance-gate work (#1014 / #1190 line); the windowed half above is what remains.

body:
## Finding

The proactive quota gate feed from PR #1028 is throttled by a single process-global timestamp, but each feed only feeds the providers of the route that happened to win the throttle. When different routes resolve within the same 60-second window, the first resolution consumes the allowance and every later route's providers go unrefreshed — a regularly requested route can keep other routes' exhausted providers ungated (or stale-gated) indefinitely.

This is Codex P2 finding 4429477383 on PR #1028, merged without a fix or a reply (the PR's final Codex state is `has_unresolved_findings: true`). The sibling P1 from the same review was filed as #1106 and fixed by PR #1113; this P2 was never filed.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1028 "fix(core): feed current quota reads into route candidacy gate (#984)", merged, head c9aeff9c578aa00f37698bd219a1cfb24d1d093a. Codex finding: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1028#discussion_r4429477383
- Current main 51c4457109774c9d7063b5e861ed1ef62c6783d1, packages/core/src/model-route.ts:997-1007: a single module-level `lastQuotaFeedAt`; `shouldFeedQuota(now)` returns false for every caller within `feedTtlMs` (60s) of the last successful feed, regardless of which providers that feed covered.
- packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts:442: `refreshQuotaGate` returns immediately when `shouldFeedQuota(now)` is false; when it does run (lines 449-510) it derives snapshots only for `targetProviders` — the providers of the targets in this one resolution — and feeds only those targets (plus held credentials of those same providers).
- No other caller feeds the gate: `shouldFeedQuota` / `observeProviderQuota` / `observeCredentialQuota` have no other production call sites (grep of packages/core/src on main).

## Why it matters

The proactive gate is the mechanism that keeps quota-exhausted providers out of candidacy before a 429 (#984). A provider that belongs only to routes resolved after another route consumed the minute's feed is never proactively gated while traffic keeps the popular route resolving at least once a minute — it stays in rotation, takes requests, and 429s, which is exactly the failure the gate exists to prevent. The same starvation also delays re-admission reads for gated providers on quiet routes.

## Acceptance criteria

- The feed throttle is scoped to what was actually refreshed (e.g. keyed by provider/credential set), OR derived snapshots are cached and applied to every resolution regardless of which call refreshed them, so one route's refresh cannot starve another route's providers.
- A regression test resolves two routes with disjoint providers back-to-back inside one TTL window and shows both providers' quota snapshots reach the gate.
- Existing model-route / model-resolver / quota suites stay green; the 60s per-provider refresh cost bound is preserved (no unthrottled DB read per resolution).

Dedupe: searched open + closed issues 2026-11-01 for `shouldFeedQuota`, "quota feed", "quota gate throttle", and the finding's title — no existing issue covers this. #1106 (closed) covered only the sibling Codex P1 (credential-scope attribution), fixed by #1113. #984 (closed) is the origin feature issue.

body:
## Problem

`script/stats.ts` — run daily in CI by `.github/workflows/stats.yml` — makes all three of its outbound fetches with no deadline and reads both JSON responses with unbounded `response.json()`. It is the remaining CI-run script that has not been given the per-call bounds its siblings received (#1275, #1329/#1333, #1332/#1335).

## Evidence (verified on main `51c4457109`)

- `script/stats.ts:11-24` — PostHog event POST: `fetch("https://us.i.posthog.com/i/v0/e/", {...})` with no `signal`. The `.catch(() => null)` settles network errors, but a stalled connection never settles, so the send can hang indefinitely.
- `script/stats.ts:57` — npm downloads: `fetch(\`https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/range/2020-01-01:${endYear}-12-31/${packageName}\`)` with no `signal`; `await response.json()` (:62) buffers the whole range document uncapped.
- `script/stats.ts:78` — GitHub releases pager: `fetch(url)` with no `signal` inside an unbounded `while (true)` pagination loop (:73-95); `await response.json()` (:83) buffers every page whole. A stalled page hangs the run.
- `.github/workflows/stats.yml:35` runs `bun script/stats.ts` on a daily cron (:12-13). The only existing bound is the job-level `timeout-minutes: 15` (:26) — it kills a hung run after the full window and does nothing for body size.
- The bounded-http gate does not cover this file: its scope note (#1256, `script/check-bounded-http.ts:43-44`) excludes the root `script/` tree, so nothing catches this mechanically.
- Sibling pattern: `packages/script/src/registry.ts` bounds the registry fetch at 8s + 1 MiB (#1275); `script/update-artifact.ts` and `script/publish-winget-github.ts` now carry deadlines (and update-artifact a byte cap).

## Why it matters

A stalled PostHog, npm, or GitHub connection turns the daily stats job into a 15-minute burn before the job timeout kills it, and an oversized or slow-dripping JSON body is buffered whole in CI memory. Every other CI-run script in this repo has been bounded per-call for exactly this failure class; stats.ts is the leftover.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three fetches in `script/stats.ts` carry a named per-request deadline (e.g. `AbortSignal.timeout(...)`, tens of seconds, in the style of the sibling scripts).
- [ ] The two `response.json()` reads (npm downloads, GitHub releases pages) go through a bounded read: declared-length pre-check plus a streaming cap, or an equivalent capped reader with a named limit.
- [ ] Current failure semantics preserved: npm failure warns and returns 0 (:59-68), GitHub failure throws (:79-81), PostHog failure stays non-fatal (:21).
- [ ] The pagination loop still terminates on a short/empty page, and a deadline abort on any page settles as the GitHub-failure error, not a silent partial result.

body:
## Problem

`script/publish-winget-github.ts` (created by PR #1335 to fix #1332) bounds every WinGet GitHub API request with a 30s deadline, but its response body reader is not byte-bound — the same gap #1334 closed for `script/update-artifact.ts` the same day.

## Evidence (verified on main `51c4457109`)

- `script/publish-winget-github.ts:63-93` — `readResponseBody` streams chunks and accumulates them in memory. It maintains a byte counter (`size += result.value.byteLength`, :82) but never compares `size` to any limit: no cap constant, no declared `content-length` pre-check, no cancel-on-overflow.
- `script/publish-winget-github.ts:36-50` — `json()` reads every response through this reader, and on a non-OK status the full body text is embedded in the thrown error (:41), so an oversized error body is also buffered whole (and copied into CI logs).
- Callers: `script/publish-winget.ts:141-202` — fork, pulls, git ref/commit/tree, commit, refs, and PR-creation responses all flow through `github.json(...)`.
- The intended pattern already exists twice in this tree: `script/update-artifact.ts:27` `UPDATE_ARTIFACT_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES = 1024 * 1024` with a declared-length pre-check (:193-195) and a streaming cap with reader cancel (:208-210), added by #1334; and `packages/script/src/registry.ts:34-52` (#1275). The winget module was split out one hour earlier in #1335 and did not get the cap.
- `packages/script/test/publish-winget-github.test.ts` pins only the deadline (stalled body cancelled at 25ms) and a 422-retry parse path. No over-cap test exists.

## Why it matters

The deadline bounds duration, not bytes (the #1158/#1333 distinction). These GitHub API responses are small, schema-known JSON, but a fast, broken, or intercepted endpoint can deliver arbitrarily many bytes inside the 30s window and grow the release job's memory unboundedly — the exact failure #1334 closed for the sibling module.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `readResponseBody` in `script/publish-winget-github.ts` enforces a named byte cap (1 MiB, matching `UPDATE_ARTIFACT_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` / `MAX_REGISTRY_DOC_BYTES`): a declared `content-length` over the cap fails fast, and a streamed body over the cap cancels the reader and throws an error naming the operation and the cap.
- [ ] The non-OK error path no longer embeds an unbounded body in the thrown error (the cap bounds it, or the excerpt is truncated to a named limit).
- [ ] Legitimate responses at/under the cap are unaffected, including the 422-ref retry flow pinned by the existing test.
- [ ] A new test in `packages/script/test/publish-winget-github.test.ts` feeds an over-cap body through the `fetchImpl` seam and asserts rejection; existing tests still pass.

# fix(script): update-artifact response bodies are deadline-bound but not byte-bound — readResponseBody accumulates without a cap

Filed 2026-11-01 by new-issue-creator-opencode. Main: 99a3387394. Residual of #1329 (closed, fixed at HEAD).

## Evidence

- `script/update-artifact.ts:184-209` — `readResponseBody()` (added by the #1329 fix) streams the body chunk-by-chunk and accumulates every chunk into memory: it maintains a running `size` counter (`:192 size += result.value.byteLength`) but **never compares it to any limit**. There is no `MAX`/cap constant anywhere in the file (grep `cap|MAX|byte`: only the size accounting itself).
- All three release-pipeline responses flow through it: the GitHub OIDC token JSON (`readResponseJson`, publish path), the publish POST error-path text (`readResponseText`), and the Cloudflare token-verify JSON (`credentials()`).
- The #1329 deadlines (10s OIDC / 30s publish / 10s verify) bound *duration*, not *bytes* — the same distinction #1158 filed for the console CRM lookup ("3s timeout bounds duration, not bytes") and #1250 fixed for the changelog worker with a 1 MiB capped reader. A fast or misbehaving endpoint can stream far more than these small JSON responses will ever legitimately be within the deadline window, growing CI runner memory until the deadline or OOM.
- Test seam already exists: `packages/script/test/update-artifact.test.ts` drives `publish()`/`credentials` paths through the injectable `fetchImpl` + `timeouts` options, so an oversized-body case can be pinned without network.

## Why it matters

These are three small, schema-known JSON responses (a token, an ack, a verify result). An explicit byte cap turns an unbounded memory sink in the release pipeline into a fast, named failure, completing the bounding #1329 started (it bounded time; the body reader it introduced counts bytes but never enforces them).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `readResponseBody` enforces a named byte cap (sized generously for the OIDC/publish/verify JSON payloads, e.g. 1 MiB in the style of #1250's `CHANGELOG_MAX_BYTES`): exceeding it cancels the reader and throws an error naming the operation and the cap.
- [ ] Legitimate responses at/under the cap are unaffected; the publish 5xx retry behavior is unchanged.
- [ ] A test in `packages/script/test/update-artifact.test.ts` feeds an over-cap body through the `fetchImpl` seam and asserts rejection; existing update-artifact tests still pass.

title: fix(cli): release build downloads the Bun compiler archive with no integrity check — unverified executable becomes the shipped opencode runtime

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/cli
labels.description: Package: cli (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

When `BUN_COMPILE_RELEASE` is set, the CLI release build downloads a per-target Bun archive from GitHub, unzips it, and uses the extracted executable as the compiler/runtime for the shipped `opencode` binary — with **no integrity verification, no timeout, and no size bound** on the download. The sibling build script in the same directory verifies the Node archive's SHA256 before extracting it; the Bun path verifies nothing.

## Evidence (verified on main `7918a1bcfe`, 2026-10-31)

- `packages/cli/script/build.ts:228-262` — `compileExecutable()`: resolves the asset URL via `compileReleaseAssets()`, then at `:252` `fetch(url, { headers: { Accept: "application/octet-stream", ... } })` — no `signal`/timeout; at `:259` streams `response.body` chunk-by-chunk to the archive file with no byte cap; at `:261` `unzip -oq` extracts it; the extracted path is returned as the executable. No hash, checksum, or signature is computed or compared anywhere in the function (the only `sha256` in `build.ts` is for the unrelated opencode-pty binary, `:127`).
- `packages/cli/script/build.ts:154,179` — the returned `executablePath` is passed to `Bun.build({ compile: { executablePath } })`: the downloaded executable is not a throwaway tool, it becomes the runtime embedded in the shipped CLI binary for that target.
- `packages/cli/script/build.ts:266-272` — `compileReleaseAssets()` also fetches the GitHub release-metadata document with no timeout and reads it with unbounded `response.json()`.
- Contrast, same directory: `packages/cli/script/build-node.ts:207-216` downloads `SHASUMS256.txt` alongside the Node archive, extracts the expected digest for the exact filename, and throws `Checksum mismatch` before extracting; `:228` writes a `.verified` marker. Contrast, runtime code: `packages/core/src/ripgrep/binary.ts` pins per-platform SHA256 digests and verifies the ripgrep archive before install (fixed in #1137) — the repo's stated pattern is verify-before-execute for downloaded executables.
- Feasibility verified: Bun releases publish `SHASUMS256.txt` covering every asset this function downloads (laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-bun-build/probe.mjs` against release `bun-v1.3.5`: HTTP 200, 22 entries, including digests for `bun-linux-x64.zip`, `bun-darwin-aarch64.zip`, and `bun-windows-x64.zip`) — a `build-node.ts`-style check needs no new infrastructure, and the GitHub API asset objects `compileReleaseAssets` already consumes also carry per-asset digests.

## Why it matters

This is the supply-chain path for release binaries: a corrupted or substituted archive (compromised release asset, broken mirror/proxy, partial-then-resumed bad bytes that still unzip) is silently compiled into the shipped `opencode` executable for every user of that target. The failure mode the repo already accepted as worth fixing for ripgrep (#1137) and already implements for Node in the adjacent script applies here with higher stakes — the artifact is the product itself. The missing timeout/size bound on both fetches additionally lets a stalled release build hang or fill disk indefinitely.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `compileExecutable()` verifies the downloaded Bun archive's SHA256 against the release's `SHASUMS256.txt` entry (or the GitHub API asset digest) **before** `unzip`, and fails the build with a clear checksum-mismatch error on any mismatch or missing entry — mirroring `build-node.ts:207-216`.
- [ ] Both fetches in `build.ts`'s compile path (release metadata and archive) carry a named timeout; the archive stream is not left unbounded in time (a size bound is optional if the checksum gate lands, since a verified digest bounds integrity, but the download must not hang forever).
- [ ] The cached-executable fast path (`Bun.file(executable).exists()` return) only reuses an executable that was verified when downloaded (e.g. a `.verified` marker like `build-node.ts:228`, or re-verification).
- [ ] A test or scripted check covers: correct digest passes, tampered archive fails before extraction, missing SHASUMS entry fails closed.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `compileExecutable`, `BUN_COMPILE_RELEASE`, `SHASUMS`, and build-script checksum terms (2026-10-31): no filing covers the Bun download in `packages/cli/script/build.ts`. #1137 was the ripgrep archive in `packages/core` (runtime, now fixed); #1006/#1091 are desktop/gui-extensions download paths. This is the release-build Bun compiler download only.

body:
# Auto-apply config file changes: audit, gaps, and the fix

## Question

When an operator edits `opencode.json` / `opencode.jsonc` (or the global config) while the server is running, which properties take effect automatically, which need a manual reload (`SIGHUP`, `opencode reload`, `client.location.reload`), and which need a restart? The goal: **a file edit should be live for new work with no reload call, no restart, and no polling.**

## How it works today (audit of `main`, 2026-10-31)

The machinery is mostly already here:

- The Config service (`packages/core/src/config.ts`) is per-Location. Discovery (`config/discovery.ts`) covers the system dir, global config dir, macOS MDM plist, ancestor `opencode.json`/`opencode.jsonc` files, `.opencode` dirs, and `.claude`/`.agents` compat roots.
- `ConfigWatch.plan` (`config/watch.ts`) watches **every** discovery root — including roots that don't exist yet, via parent-directory entries watches — through the Watcher service (`filesystem/watcher.ts`, `@parcel/watcher` with a `node:fs.watch` fallback).
- Watch events feed a 100 ms-debounced reload (`config.ts:383`). A reload re-reads and re-normalizes all documents; if the result is deep-equal to the current entries nothing is published. Otherwise it publishes `config.updated` with the list of changed top-level **sections** (`changedSections`).
- Domain plugins subscribe per section via `config/plugin/entry-observer.ts`: on `config.updated`, a plugin refreshes its captured entries and runs its domain reload **only when one of its sections changed**.
- The manual reload paths (SIGHUP at `packages/cli/src/server-process.ts:275`, server `reload:` at `packages/server/src/process.ts:150` publishing `Config.ReloadRequested` at `config.ts:31`) drive exactly the same reload the watcher drives. Reload is an escape hatch, not a separate mechanism.
- In-flight sessions are not pinned to stale config: runners resolve model/agent per step from domain state, so the next step of a running session picks up new config. A session with an explicitly pinned model keeps that pin (by design).

## Per-property verdicts

| Property | Today | Mechanism / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `experimental.model_routes` (routes) | ✅ auto | `config/plugin/model-routes.ts` observes `experimental` → provider + tool reload |
| `agents`, `permissions` (+ `agent/*.md` files) | ✅ auto | `config/plugin/agent.ts` sections + agent-md changes feed |
| `providers` (definitions, options) | ✅ auto | `config/plugin/provider.ts` → integration + provider reload |
| `disabled_providers` | ✅ auto | Normalized into `policies` provider.use deny rules (`config/normalize.ts:433`); `config/plugin/policy.ts` observes `policies`/`experimental` → provider/mcp/skill reload; denied providers are removed by transform. **The Oct 2026 operational note "reload does not apply disabled_providers" is outdated on current main** — verified by test (remove + restore on disk edit, no reload call). |
| Plugin-registered models | ✅ auto | Rebuilt when plugins re-activate (supervisor watches `plugins`/`policies`/`experimental`) |
| `mcp` | ✅ auto | MCP plugin observes `mcp` |
| `commands` | ✅ auto | observes `commands` |
| `skills` | ✅ auto | observes `skills` + directory changes rescan |
| `instructions` | ✅ auto | refreshes on any `config.updated` |
| `formatter`, `shell`, `snapshot`, `tool_output`, `websearch`, `references`, `worktree`, `media`, `compaction`, watcher policy, messaging | ✅ auto | per-section entry observers |
| Aliases, several `experimental` knobs | ✅ auto | read fresh from `entries()` at each use (e.g. `session/runner/model.ts`) |
| **`model` (default model)** | ❌ **stale until restart/manual reload** | Consumed by the provider transform and the `models.default` catalog value, but **no observer listed section `model`**, so a model-only edit never invalidated anything. |
| **`default_agent`** | ❌ **stale until restart/manual reload** | Consumed by the agent transform (`config/plugin/agent.ts:88`); its triggers were sections `[agents, permissions]` + the agent-md feed only. |
| `lsp` | ⚠️ inert | Normalized (`config/normalize.ts`) but has **no runtime consumer in core**, so there is nothing to hot-apply to. Needs a consumer first; out of scope here. |
| `username`, `share`, `update`, `enterprise` | ⚠️ startup-level | No hot consumer; read at startup. Named here for completeness. |
| macOS MDM plist | ❌ not watched | Discovery reads it (`config/discovery.ts:34-38`) but `ConfigWatch.plan` does not include the plist path, so MDM changes need SIGHUP/restart. |
| Remote wellknown manifest | 🔁 polls (by design) | Refreshed on a 10-minute timer (`config.ts`) — remote state, not a local file. Plugin-update checks poll every 24 h. These are the only polls in the system; local files are purely event-driven. |
| workerd / `fs.filewatcher=false` | ⚠️ watcher off by design | `packages/server/src/routes.ts` disables watching where no filesystem watcher exists; manual reload remains the path there. |

## Design

No new mechanism is needed — the watch → debounce → section-diff → per-domain invalidation pipeline already exists and is event-driven end to end (no polling, no re-reads while files are quiet). The work is closing the invalidation gaps:

1. **`model`**: the provider plugin observes section `model` in addition to `providers`, so a default-model edit re-derives provider/catalog state and `models.default`.
2. **`default_agent`**: the agent plugin treats `default_agent` like `agents`/`permissions` for reload notification.
3. **MDM plist**: add the discovery plist paths to `ConfigWatch.plan` so managed-preference changes are watched like every other root. (Follow-up; macOS-only.)
4. Everything else already auto-applies; `lsp` stays inert until it has a runtime consumer.

Reload stays as an escape hatch (and the only path where the watcher is disabled), but for file edits it becomes unnecessary.

## Tests

`packages/core/test/config/auto-apply.test.ts` (new) proves, against the live watcher pipeline with no reload call anywhere:

- editing `model` in the config file updates the resolved default model;
- editing `default_agent` updates the resolved default agent;
- editing `disabled_providers` removes and then restores a provider;
- a rewrite that changes nothing publishes no `config.updated`;
- with a watcher backend that never emits, a file write is **not** picked up — the service serves cached entries and never re-reads (watch-driven, not polling).

The first two tests fail on unpatched `main` and pass with the fix.


## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Editing `model` in a watched config file updates the resolved default model for new work with no reload call and no restart.
- [ ] Editing `default_agent` updates the resolved default agent the same way.
- [ ] The tests named in the Tests section exist and pass (including the no-op-rewrite and never-emitting-watcher cases).
- [ ] The named follow-ups are dispositioned on this issue: macOS MDM plist watching (follow-up) and `lsp` (inert until it has a runtime consumer).

## Repo snapshot

- **Commits:** 21,521 on `main` — first commit 2025-03-21, last 2026-10-31
- **Visibility:** public — **fork** of dezren39/opencode, tracking the anomalyco upstream
- **Fresh clone of `main`:** ~449.0 MB pack (GitHub repo size 453 MB) — tip is 8,810 files / 142 MB
- **Local clone:** 1.6 GB `.git` (local worktree/branch refs and loose objects; local-only bloat)

Very little, and what exists is mostly upstream's, not ours:

- models-dev `snapshot.txt` churn — 283 MB uncompressed → **~10 MB packed** (the only strip candidate; stripping it would take a fresh clone from 449.0 MB to ~438.9 MB, saving 2%)
- `bun.lock` churn — 1.13 GB uncompressed across versions, delta-packed small
- The remaining top blobs are legitimate upstream product assets (lander mp4s, `vc_redist.x64.exe`, fonts)

## Verdict: NEVER rewrite history

This repo is a fork tracking the anomalyco upstream. **Rewriting its history severs upstream sync permanently** — that alone ends the discussion, before counting the 15 open PRs a rewrite would orphan and the ~10 MB (2%) it would save. The 449 MB fresh-clone size is real product history, not junk.

## Already done

- Nothing required. This issue exists so the measurement — and the never-rewrite rule for this fork — is on record.

## Open questions

- None. Local-clone bloat (1.6 GB local vs 453 MB repo) is fixable with local `git gc` + stale-ref cleanup whenever convenient; deferred by Drew's choice ("locally is fine for now", 2026-10-31).

## Standing forward-hygiene rules

- **Never rewrite fork history**; upstream sync is worth more than any pack saving.
- In our own commits: no build outputs, binaries, or log files added at the tip; gitignore scratch classes (scratch/output dirs, dumps, `*.err`/`*.out`).
- Runtime state files belong outside repos (`~/.local/state/`) per the pm-aggregator precedent.
- Re-run the hygiene census quarterly, or sooner if junk classes appear at the tip in our own commits. Fleet tracking issue: filed in developing-today/code ("Standard task: per-repo hygiene census + cleanup documentation").

## Acceptance criteria

- The measured census for this repo is on record in this issue, including the never-rewrite verdict for this fork.
- No history rewrite is performed on this fork under any future cleanup without a new decision superseding the recorded verdict.
- Forward hygiene: no build outputs, binaries, or log files are committed at the tip in our own commits.

title: fix(console): Salesforce login and lead fetches have no timeout — login() and createLead() hang the enterprise form forever, only salesforceRequest's inner call is bounded (8s, same file)
