body:
## Problem

The console Salesforce client's auth and lead-creation fetches have **no timeout at all** — in the same file whose third fetch path bounds itself:

- `packages/console/app/src/lib/salesforce.ts:64` — `login()` fetches `${url}/services/oauth2/token` with **no `signal`**. A Salesforce instance that accepts the connection and never responds leaves the promise pending forever.
- `packages/console/app/src/lib/salesforce.ts:121` — `createLead()` fetches `${auth.url}/services/data/v59.0/sobjects/Lead` with **no `signal`** either — and it first awaits the unbounded `login()`.
- `packages/console/app/src/lib/salesforce.ts:75,135` — on a non-OK status both paths log `await res.text()`, buffering the **whole error body with no size cap** (the success path at `:79` likewise reads `res.json()` unbounded).
- Contrast, same file: `packages/console/app/src/lib/salesforce.ts:152-156` — the `salesforceRequest()` helper's fetch carries `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(8000)`. So console-signup syncs bound their data calls at 8 s, but the `login()` they all depend on (`salesforceRequest()` itself awaits `login()` first) and the enterprise lead path have no bound at all. Across all of `packages/console/app/src`, these and `lib/console-account.ts:17` (`AbortSignal.timeout(3000)`) are the only `AbortSignal` uses.

## Verification (this run, laptop probes with the real module)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-salesforce-openapi/` (laptop), importing the real `createLead` / `salesforceRequest` from `packages/console/app/src/lib/salesforce.ts` (code identical on main `4208bef54a` and `12f411d167` — the intervening commits touch only ROADMAP.md and the models snapshot):

- **Lead endpoint never responds (real `fetch`, local `Bun.serve` token endpoint + never-responding lead endpoint, `SST_RESOURCE_*` set as in `salesforce.test.ts`):** `PROBE createLead real-fetch lead-endpoint-never-responds: STILL-PENDING` — still pending after 5 s, with no deadline at which it would settle.
- **Control, same server, same file:** `PROBE salesforceRequest query-never-responds CONTROL: REJECTED(8006ms) TimeoutError` — the `salesforceRequest` path aborts at its 8 s timeout, proving the bound exists in-file and only `login()`/`createLead()` lack it.
- **Token endpoint returns 500 with a paced endless body (stubbed `globalThis.fetch`):** `PROBE createLead token-500-endless: STILL-PENDING bytesEnqueued=64487424` — `login()`'s error-path `res.text()` consumed 64,487,424 bytes in 5 s and was still going.
- **Token body never delivers:** `PROBE createLead token-hang: STILL-PENDING`.

## Why it matters

`createLead()` is on the public enterprise inquiry path: `packages/console/app/src/lib/enterprise.ts` `handleEnterpriseRequest` awaits it in a `Promise.all` alongside the notification email and the mailing-list subscribe, so one stalled Salesforce endpoint hangs the whole `/api/enterprise` submission indefinitely — the visitor's form never resolves, and the other two completed side effects are never reported. `login()` is also the shared first step of `salesforceRequest()`, so even the nominally 8 s-bounded console-signup sync inherits the unbounded auth call. There is no fallback to reach: `.catch()` handlers on both fetches only fire on rejection, and a hang never rejects.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both fetches in `salesforce.ts` (`login()` token POST, `createLead()` lead POST) carry a named timeout constant consistent with the in-file precedent (8 s in `salesforceRequest()`; console range 3–8 s), so a stalled Salesforce endpoint settles as a failed auth / failed lead (`login()` returns undefined, `createLead()` returns false) instead of hanging.
- [ ] The error-body reads at `:75`/`:135` (and the token success read at `:79`) are bounded by a named cap appropriate for a Salesforce JSON response, enforced while reading, not after buffering.
- [ ] Happy path unchanged: the existing `salesforce.test.ts` lead-mapping test and the enterprise handler test still pass; a rejected/timed-out fetch keeps today's `console.error` + undefined/false behaviour.
- [ ] Regression coverage in `packages/console/app/src/lib/salesforce.test.ts` (which already runs the real module against a local `Bun.serve` fake Salesforce): a never-responding token endpoint and a never-responding lead endpoint each settle within the chosen bound.
- [ ] Out of scope: `salesforceRequest()`'s existing 8 s timeout and its `response.json()` (a follow-up if wanted); `lib/console-account.ts` (already 3 s-bounded in time); the EmailOctopus subscribes and SES send in the enterprise flow (separate surfaces).

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode, 2026-10-31 run. Same no-timeout class as #1083/#1089/#1090, different surface (CRM client, not a route or metadata query).

body:
## Problem

`ModelsDev.fetchApi` reads the models catalog with Effect `HttpClientResponse.text` and **no size cap at all** — the only bound is a 10-second timeout. The catalog source is configurable (`ModelsDev.Options.url`, `models-dev.ts:269-275,337`), so a custom, compromised, or misbehaving source can stream an arbitrarily large body that is buffered whole into memory, then JSON-decoded, digest-hashed, and offered to the KV cache — on the automatic startup/refresh path, not a user-initiated download.

This is the unbounded-body class the house has been closing path by path (#923, #1007, #1017, #1029, #1061), on a surface none of those cover: Copilot/Modal model lists got 4 MiB caps in #1017, but the main catalog fetch — the largest legitimate JSON body in the system — has none.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `8dab871ace`)

- `packages/core/src/models-dev.ts:346-353` — `fetchApi`: `HttpClientRequest.get(`${source}/api.json`)` → `http.execute` → `Effect.flatMap((res) => res.text)` → `Effect.timeout("10 seconds")`. No `content-length` pre-check, no streaming bound, no named cap anywhere in the file (grep for `MAX|maxBytes|bound` in `models-dev.ts`: no hits).
- `packages/core/src/models-dev.ts:337` — `const source = options?.url || defaultSource`: the URL is a configuration input, not a hard-coded trusted endpoint only.
- `packages/core/src/models-dev.ts:379-381,413-420` — both callers (`fetchAndWrite`, `refresh`) pass the whole text to `decodeCatalog(text)` and `writeCache(text)` / `bodyDigest(text)`, so an oversized body is buffered, parsed, hashed, and cache-written, never rejected early.
- Scale context from the file itself (`models-dev.ts:364-368`): the real `api.json` "passed 2 MB in Aug 2026" and already outgrows some KV value limits — a generous cap (the 16 MiB generated-client precedent in #1007, or the 4 MiB model-list precedent in #1017 scaled up) loses nothing legitimate.
- Test check: `packages/core/test/models.test.ts` exercises `fetchApi` via a mock client (e.g. `:390,454` assert the `/api.json` URL) but has no oversized-body case.
- Laptop probe this run (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-unbounded-catalog-embedding/probe.mjs`, Node): a local server streaming a 32 MiB chunked body (no `content-length`) was buffered whole by the same `.text()` primitive in 477 ms — far inside the 10 s timeout, so the timeout is not an effective bound on a fast connection.

Dedup: `gh issue list --search 'models-dev unbounded / ModelsDev text / catalog fetch'` (all states) — no hit for this fetch; #1017 covers only the Copilot/Modal `/models` loaders, #1025/#1029/#1049 cover other endpoints.

## Why it matters

The catalog refresh runs automatically and periodically for every instance. One bad source response — hostile custom source, a CDN error page of unbounded size, a misconfigured mirror — OOMs or stalls the whole process (all sessions) instead of failing one refresh cleanly and keeping the bundled/cached catalog, which the code already treats as the boot-time floor.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `fetchApi` reads the catalog body through a bounded path (`collectBoundedResponseBody` from `packages/core/src/tool/http-body.ts`, or equivalent) with a named, documented cap sized for the real catalog's growth (multi-MB today; justify the chosen value in a comment).
- [ ] A declared `content-length` above the cap fails before the body is read, and a chunked/undeclared body is bounded in flight — not buffered whole and checked afterwards.
- [ ] An over-cap response fails the refresh/fetch cleanly (existing fallback to cache/bundled snapshot behaviour is preserved) instead of reaching `decodeCatalog`/`writeCache`.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/core/test/models.test.ts` (or a sibling): a normal catalog still loads, and an over-cap body (declared and streamed variants) is rejected.

title: fix(core): provider OAuth token and error responses are read unbounded with HttpClientResponse.text/schemaBodyJson in gitlab/poe/snowflake

body:
## Evidence (verified during #1026 triage)

Three provider auth modules in `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/` that use Effect's `HttpClient` read OAuth token success bodies and error responses with no size cap:

| Site | Read | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `gitlab.ts:415` | `response.text` | OAuth error response body, decoded to error string |
| `gitlab.ts:420` | `HttpClientResponse.schemaBodyJson(Token)` | OAuth token exchange success body |
| `poe.ts:145` | `response.text` | OAuth error response body, decoded to error string |
| `poe.ts:155` | `HttpClientResponse.schemaBodyJson(Token)` | OAuth token exchange success body |
| `snowflake-cortex.ts:66` | `response.text` | OAuth error response body embedded into error message |
| `snowflake-cortex.ts:68` | `HttpClientResponse.schemaBodyJson(Token)` | OAuth token exchange success body |

Both `response.text` and `HttpClientResponse.schemaBodyJson` on an Effect `HttpClientResponse` buffer the stream without bounds.

The bounding primitive for Effect `HttpClientResponse` already exists in `packages/core/src/tool/http-body.ts`: `collectBoundedResponseBody`.

## Why it matters
A misbehaving or malicious endpoint (or user-entered self-hosted GitLab instance / Snowflake account) can stream unbounded data, exhausting client memory during login or token refresh.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each listed site reads its body through a bounded path (`collectBoundedResponseBody` or equivalent) with a named, documented cap (e.g. 64 KiB).
- [ ] Over-cap declared or streamed responses fail cleanly before buffering unbounded payloads.
- [ ] Provider auth tests verify bounded behaviour for small and over-cap payloads.

body:
Drew's directive (2026-10-30): ensure that OpenCode — and OpenChamber where it surfaces routes/models — removes a model/target from rotation when it repeatedly returns errors, for an increasing amount of time per recurrence, or until the time the error is expected to be resolved when that is known.

## Error classes in scope (all of them)
- Rate limit (429, with or without Retry-After)
- Billing / funds (402, insufficient credits, payment-required class)
- Quota exhaustion (usage-limit errors naming a reset time)
- Auth/attestation failures
- Upstream 5xx and timeouts / first-token failures
- Any other repeated provider error class

## Required behavior
1. Repeated errors of any class take the model/target out of rotation — not retried on a fixed short interval forever.
2. The removal duration ESCALATES with recurrence (increasing backoff), capped sensibly.
3. When the error carries an expected resolution time (quota reset, Retry-After), the removal lasts until that time instead — and the target is restored automatically when it passes (or when a fresh quota read shows headroom).
4. Restoration is automatic and probed, not permanent: a recovered model re-enters rotation without operator action.
5. The behavior is consistent across both surfaces: the OpenCode router (packages/core model-route) and any OpenChamber-side model/route handling, so a model removed in one is not immediately re-offered by the other.

## Existing partial coverage to verify against (do not duplicate blindly)
- #823 (closed): route health cooldown escalation.
- #870 (closed): rate-limit holds threaded through the credential dimension.
- #984 + PR #991 (merged): quota-exhausted pools gated until their stated reset.

## Acceptance criteria
- An audit table (in the PR or a linked comment) listing each error class above × where its removal/escalation/reset behavior lives, with the gaps found.
- Every gap closed: billing errors and non-quota repeated errors escalate like quota/rate-limit ones; openchamber surface checked and aligned.
- Tests demonstrating: repeated 402s remove the target with escalating cooldown; a quota error naming a reset restores the target at the reset; a recovered target re-enters rotation.

body:
# fix(desktop): DesktopFiles.saveFile writes the user's chosen file in place — a failed write destroys the previous version, unlike the package's own atomic writes

## Summary

The desktop main process's `saveFile` — the save-dialog path used when the app or a
GUI extension saves a file for the user — writes with a plain truncating
`fs.writeFile` directly to the destination. If the write fails partway (disk full,
file-size limit, I/O error), the file that was there before is already truncated and
partially overwritten: the user loses the previous version *and* doesn't get the new
one. The same package already has an atomic write helper (temp file beside the
destination + rename, temp cleaned on failure) and uses it for its own settings and
window-state files — the user's files are the ones that don't get the protection.

## Evidence (main `195bdae185d92ef377bee7a54ad6bc77e96b10da`)

- `packages/desktop/src/main/files/index.ts:73-86` — `saveFile`: after
  `dialog.showSaveDialog`, `yield* fs.writeFile(result.filePath, new
  TextEncoder().encode(content))`. Effect's FileSystem `writeFile` is Node's
  `fs.writeFile` with the default `w` flag: the destination is truncated on open,
  before any bytes land.
- `packages/desktop/src/main/atomic-write.ts:36-52` — the package's own
  `writeFileSyncAtomic(file, content)`: writes `${file}.tmp` beside the destination,
  renames over it with `renameSyncWithRetry` (Windows EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY retries),
  and removes the temp and rethrows on failure. Its callers are the app's own state:
  `packages/desktop/src/main/storage/store.ts:37` (desktop store) and
  `packages/desktop/src/main/windows/window-state.ts:108` (window state). It has its
  own test file (`atomic-write.test.ts`).
- Reachability: IPC `FilesSaveFile` (`packages/desktop/src/main/ipc-handlers/files.ts:27`,
  `Effect.orDie` — a failed write surfaces as a defect after the damage is done),
  exposed to the renderer as `platform.saveFile`
  (`packages/desktop/src/renderer/platform/files.ts:61-62`) and used by GUI extensions
  to save files (`packages/app/src/runtime/extension/host-apis.tsx:222`:
  `platform.saveFile({ defaultPath: file.name }, file.content)`). The save dialog
  happily targets an existing file (with the OS overwrite prompt), so the destroyed
  previous version is the normal case, not an edge case.
- The fleet's CLI/core surfaces fixed exactly this shape repeatedly — config writes
  (#998), shell-config rewrites on uninstall (#988, closed), `mcp add` (#977, closed),
  route-overrides (#924, closed) — always temp-file + rename. The desktop save path
  is the remaining in-place writer of a user-owned file.

## Reproduction (laptop probe, `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-30-desktop-savefile/probe.mjs`)

The probe mirrors `saveFile`'s write (`fs.promises.writeFile(path, bytes)`, default
flag) against an existing file, with the process under a 1-block file-size limit
(`ulimit -f 1`) so the write fails deterministically partway:

```
before: ORIGINAL-CONTENT size: 16
write failed as expected: EFBIG
after: size: 1024 originalIntact: false
```

The failed save left 1024 bytes of the new content in place of the original 16-byte
file — both versions lost. With temp+rename, the same failure leaves the original
file byte-identical and only a temp file to clean up.

## Why it matters

A save dialog is a promise: until the new content is safely on disk, the old file is
the user's only copy. Disk-full and quota failures are exactly when users save
exports/backups of their work (extension-saved files, session exports), and those
are the writes that currently corrupt the pre-existing file they target. The fix is
small because the package already owns and tests the atomic helper.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `DesktopFiles.saveFile` writes atomically: content lands in a temp file in the
      destination's directory and is renamed over the destination only once fully
      written (reusing `writeFileSyncAtomic` from `../atomic-write`, or an async
      equivalent following the same pattern including the Windows rename retries),
      so a failed or interrupted write leaves any pre-existing destination file
      byte-identical and no `.tmp` litter behind.
- [ ] Successful-save behaviour is unchanged: the dialog flow, cancellation
      (`false` when cancelled), return values, and the `FilesSaveFile` IPC contract
      stay as they are; saving to a new path and overwriting an existing file both
      still work.
- [ ] The overwrite case keeps the destination's usability: if preserving the
      existing file's permissions across the rename is not automatic, the chosen
      behaviour is stated in the code (the current in-place write preserves mode;
      a bare rename does not).
- [ ] A regression test (alongside `packages/desktop/src/main/atomic-write.test.ts`
      or a new files test) pins: a write that fails partway leaves the previous
      destination content intact, and a successful save replaces it completely.
- [ ] Existing desktop tests stay green.

body:
# fix(core,schema): Worktree.create name is never validated — a name with `../` segments creates (and later removes) a worktree outside the managed worktree directory

## Summary

`Worktree.create` builds the new worktree's directory as `path.join(directory, name)`
with no validation of `name` at any door. A name containing `../` segments escapes
the managed worktree parent directory: the git strategy checks the repository out at
the escaped path, the escaped directory is recorded as a managed worktree, the
project's start command runs there, and a later `worktree remove` deletes it. Every
caller-facing schema accepts such a name — the service schema takes any string, and
the model's own `worktree_create` tool checks only that the name is non-empty after
trimming.

## Evidence (main `195bdae185d92ef377bee7a54ad6bc77e96b10da`)

- `packages/core/src/worktree.ts:211-218` — `const name = input.name ?? Slug.create()`,
  then `worktreeDirectory = path.join(directory, name)`; the collision loop only
  re-checks existence and appends `-<suffix>` to the same unchecked name. Nothing
  requires the result to stay inside `directory`, or `name` to be a single segment.
- `packages/schema/src/worktree.ts:19` — `CreateInput.name` is a plain
  `Schema.String` (no trim, no non-empty, no segment check). This schema is the HTTP
  payload: `packages/protocol/src/groups/worktree.ts:37-38` (`worktree.create`
  payload is `Worktree.CreateInput`) and `packages/server/src/handlers/worktree.ts:17`
  passes `ctx.payload` straight to `worktrees.create`.
- `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/opencode.ts:31-33,156-162` — the model's pinned
  `worktree_create` tool: its `name` is `Schema.Trim.check(Schema.isNonEmpty())` and
  nothing else, and its execute passes `input.name` to `ctx.worktree.create`. A model
  (or a prompt injection that steers it) can name a worktree `../../outside`.
- `packages/core/src/plugin/host.ts:588` — the plugin host exposes the same
  `worktrees.create(input, …)` to plugins with the same unchecked name.
- `packages/core/src/worktree.ts:227,236-242` — the result is canonicalised and
  stored as a managed worktree (strategy recorded), and the project's
  `commands.start` runs with `cwd: result.directory` — i.e. in the escaped directory.
  `Worktree.remove` (same file) later removes any stored directory by strategy, so
  the escaped directory is also deletable through the managed path.
- `packages/core/src/git.ts:1243-1255` — the git strategy runs
  `git worktree add --detach -- <directory> HEAD`; git places no containment check on
  the destination (verified below).

Contrast: the default name is `Slug.create()` (`packages/core/src/util/slug.ts`) —
always a single `adjective-noun` segment — and every test name in
`packages/core/test/worktree.test.ts` is a single segment. A single-segment name is
clearly the intended contract; it is just never enforced. The sibling input
`directory` is different by design: it is documented in the schema as the
caller-chosen *parent* directory, so its absoluteness is intentional — `name` is the
part that is supposed to live under it.

## Reproduction (laptop probes, `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-30-worktree-name/`)

1. `probe.mjs` replicates the exact `path.join(directory, name)` from
   `worktree.ts:213` with the managed parent
   `/home/user/.local/share/opencode/worktree/abc123`:

   | name | joined | inside parent |
   |---|---|---|
   | `brave-otter` (control) | `…/abc123/brave-otter` | yes |
   | `../escape` | `…/worktree/escape` | **no** |
   | `../../escape` | `…/opencode/escape` | **no** |
   | `x/../../escape2` | `…/worktree/escape2` | **no** |
   | `a/b` | `…/abc123/a/b` | nested (not a single segment) |
   | `.` / `` (empty) | the parent itself | collides, diverted to `.-2` / `-2` by the suffix loop |

2. `git-probe.sh` runs the git strategy's exact argv
   (`git worktree add --detach -- <escaped> HEAD`) in a scratch repo on the laptop:
   exit 0, the worktree is registered at the escaped path
   (`/tmp/wtprobe.*/managed/escape`, a sibling of the managed parent `abc123`, which
   stayed empty), and the checkout (`file.txt`) lands there. Cleaned up afterwards.

So `worktree_create` / `POST worktree.create` with `name: "../escape"` (when that
path does not yet exist) creates and registers a real worktree outside the managed
root today. On Windows the same applies to `..\` segments, which `path.join` treats
as separators there.

## Why it matters

Worktrees are supposed to be contained, enumerable, and safely removable as a set.
An escaping name breaks all three: the checkout (plus the project's start command)
lands in a directory the user never designated for worktrees — e.g. a sibling state
directory — it is recorded as managed, and the managed remove path can later delete
a directory outside the worktree root. The reachable doors include the model-facing
tool, so the name is not only operator input.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A worktree `name` must be a single path segment at every door: the service
      (`Worktree.create`) rejects — with a named error, before any directory is
      created or git is invoked — names that are empty/blank, `.` or `..`, or contain
      `/` or `\` (or a NUL), and the `Worktree.CreateInput` schema states the same
      contract so the HTTP door fails validation instead of reaching the service.
- [ ] Defence in depth at the service: after joining (and after each suffix-loop
      step), the destination is verified to be directly inside the parent
      `directory`; a destination outside it is rejected rather than created.
- [ ] Valid behaviour is unchanged: slug-generated default names, ordinary names
      (`task`, `selected-clone`), and the existing collision suffixing (`name-2`,
      `name-3`, …) work exactly as today, and the caller-chosen parent `directory`
      input keeps its documented meaning.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/core/test/worktree.test.ts` (which already calls
      the service directly through its fixture) pin: `../escape`, `../../escape`,
      `a/b`, `..`, `.`, and an empty/blank name are all rejected and create nothing
      on disk; a normal name still creates inside the parent.
- [ ] Existing worktree tests stay green.

body:
## Finding

PR #814 fixed #236 for routes that have at least one definition-visible target, and documented a residual in its own body ("Known residual") that was never filed as an issue: **a route whose targets are ALL transform-created models is never built at all, and the retarget transform cannot create it afterwards.**

## Evidence

- Source PR: #814 (merged, commit `8dc0c24f`), body section "Known residual (documented on `retargetDefinition`)": "a route whose targets were *all* transform-created is never built by the provider transform, and model edits cannot create the route provider — such a route still needs a definition-visible target (a glob or a catalog sibling) to exist before it can be retargeted."
- Current main `195bdae1`, `packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts`:
  - `:165` — the provider transform returns early when the expansion produced no route models (`if (models.length === 0) return`), and the routes provider is only added for routes that expanded against provider definitions.
  - `:187` — the post-group model transform iterates `models.list(ModelRoute.PROVIDER_ID)`, i.e. only route models that already exist; it rewrites stored definitions in place and cannot create a new route model/provider.
  - `:560-563` — the `retargetDefinition` doc comment still states the residual verbatim: "A route the provider transform never built — one whose targets were all transform-created — cannot be created here: model edits cannot create a provider, so such a route still needs a definition-visible target (a glob or a catalog sibling) to exist before it can be retargeted."
- Dedupe: searched open + closed issues for the residual ("transform-created", "retargetDefinition", "definition-visible") — the only hits are #236 itself (closed by #814), #869/#871 (door-set retarget follow-ups, closed), and #238 (open; distinct — a pool whose matching keys select no models *disappears with no diagnostic*; that is the diagnostic for empty expansion, not a mechanism for building an all-transform-created route).

## Why it matters

A user can write a perfectly valid route that names only Azure-style deployment models created by a model transform — precisely the motivating case of #236 — and the route silently does not exist: no route model, no error at config load, and nothing the retarget pass can do later. #236 reads as fixed, but its hardest sub-case is still unreachable, discoverable only by reading a doc comment in the plugin source.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A route whose targets are all transform-created models becomes selectable after model transforms run (e.g. the route provider/route models are created or deferred until transform-created ids are known), OR the limitation is made loud: a config-load diagnostic naming the route and the reason, so the failure is not silent.
- [ ] A regression test in `packages/core/test/model-route-transform-models.test.ts` (or a sibling suite) covers the all-transform-created-targets route, alongside the existing mixed-route cases from #814.
- [ ] If the diagnostic route is chosen instead of full support, the `retargetDefinition` doc comment and any user-facing route docs are updated to match, and this issue records why full support was not chosen.
- [ ] Relationship to #238 is recorded on completion: if the fix also gives empty-expansion routes a diagnostic, note it there; the two issues are not duplicates.

body:
# fix(core): Shell timeout duration is never normalised at the service boundary — a negative or NaN duration kills the command instantly, Infinity silently disables the timeout

## Summary

`Shell.create` and `Shell.timeout` pass their `duration`/`timeout` number straight to
`Effect.sleep(Duration.millis(duration))` with no normalisation. With the repo's own
Effect runtime, a negative or NaN duration completes the sleep **immediately**, so the
timeout fiber runs `finish("timeout", …)` and kills a just-started command as
"timed out" at ~0 ms. An infinite (or absurdly large) duration never fires, silently
disabling a timeout the caller believes is set — the only documented way to disable a
shell timeout is `0`.

## Evidence (main `195bdae185d92ef377bee7a54ad6bc77e96b10da`)

- `packages/core/src/shell.ts:413-431` — `command.timeout = (duration) => …` checks only
  `duration === 0`, then forks `Effect.sleep(Duration.millis(duration))` →
  `finish("timeout", undefined, handle.kill({ forceKillAfter: 3s }))`. It is invoked as
  `command.timeout(invocation.timeout)` at `shell.ts:431`.
- `packages/core/src/shell.ts:210-215` — the public `Shell.timeout(id, duration)` service
  method forwards `duration: number` to `command.timeout` untouched.
- `packages/core/src/shell.ts:285,297` — `create` builds
  `invocation.timeout = input.timeout ?? 0` and then runs plugin hooks:
  `hooks.trigger("shell", "create.before", invocation)`. `ShellCreateBefore.timeout` is a
  mutable plain `number` (`packages/plugin/src/effect/shell.ts:3-9`); any plugin's
  `create.before` hook can rewrite it (in-tree hook users: `tool/plugin/mcpx.ts:332`,
  `tool/plugin/mcpx-subagent.ts:152`), and the tool-plugin's own `prepare` returns
  `invocation.timeout` unchecked (`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/shell.ts:146,175`).
  The schemas that do exist (`NonNegativeInt` in the tool input and the protocol
  `CreateInput`) guard only those two doors, have no ceiling, and do not cover the
  service or the hook path — the same host-bypass pattern #992 documents
  (`plugin/host.ts:457`).
- Sibling in the same file is already fixed: `Shell.output` paging was normalised at the
  service boundary in #964 / PR #967 (`outputCursor`/`outputLimit` in `shell.ts`). The
  timeout duration in the same service never got the same treatment.

## Reproduction (laptop probe, repo's own Effect 4.0.1)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-30-shell-timeout/probe.ts` on the laptop — forks
`Effect.sleep(Duration.millis(duration))` exactly as `command.timeout` does and records
when/if it fires within 600 ms:

| duration | result |
|---|---|
| `200` (control) | fired at 212 ms, Success |
| `-5` | **fired at 0 ms, Success** → command killed as timeout immediately |
| `-1` (the common "no timeout" sentinel in other APIs) | **fired at 0 ms, Success** |
| `NaN` | **fired at 0 ms, Success** |
| `Infinity` | never fired in 600 ms → timeout silently disabled |
| `3e9` (~34.7 days) | never fired in 600 ms (no timer-overflow inversion in Effect — it simply becomes an effectively-unbounded wait) |
| `1.5` | fired at 2 ms (fractional is harmless) |

So in the real service: `Shell.create({ timeout: -1 })`, a `create.before` hook that
sets `invocation.timeout = -1`/`NaN`, or a direct `Shell.timeout(id, -1)` kills the
command instantly with status `timeout`; `Infinity` or a unit-confused oversized value
(e.g. seconds supplied as milliseconds ×1000 beyond any intent) leaves a runaway command
with no working timeout.

## Why it matters

Shell commands are the agent's most destructive tool surface. A timeout that fires at
0 ms makes commands fail confusingly (`Command exceeded timeout of -1 ms`), and a
timeout that silently never fires removes the only bound on a hung foreground command.
The values arrive from exactly the untrusted-at-the-service-boundary sources the recent
service-boundary fixes (#964, #965, #980, #981) were filed for: plugin hooks mutate the
invocation in-process with no decode, and direct service callers bypass the schemas.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Shell.create` (post-hook `invocation.timeout`) and `Shell.timeout` normalise the
      duration at the service boundary, in one shared place (the `command.timeout`
      funnel or a small helper beside it): negative and NaN durations never reach
      `Effect.sleep` as an immediate timeout — they are treated as `0` (disabled, the
      documented sentinel) or rejected with a named error; the chosen policy is stated
      in the code and pinned by tests.
- [ ] Non-finite (`Infinity`) and oversized durations cannot silently masquerade as a
      set timeout: they normalise to the same documented disabled state, or to a stated
      ceiling consistent with the house timeout bound (2³¹−1 ms, #972), with the choice
      documented.
- [ ] Valid behaviour is unchanged: `0` disables, a positive finite duration fires
      after that many milliseconds, fractional durations behave as today (≈floor/round
      to whole ms), and re-setting a timeout via `Shell.timeout` still replaces the
      previous fiber.
- [ ] Regression tests at the service level (direct `Shell` calls / hook-mutated
      invocation, not only schema-decoded tool input) pin: negative, NaN, Infinity, a
      very large finite value, `0`, and a normal positive duration.
- [ ] Existing shell tests stay green (`packages/core/test/tool-shell.test.ts` and the
      shell service tests).

title: fix(core): Config.update rewrites the global config in place — non-atomic truncation of opencode.jsonc, fresh file created with default permissions

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: priority/normal

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

Core `Config.update` — the write behind the desktop settings shell picker — rewrites the user's **global opencode config file in place, non-atomically**:

```ts
// packages/core/src/config.ts:434-451 (main 195bdae185)
const update = Effect.fn("Config.update")(
  function* (patch: Patch) {
    const directory = initial.global ?? AbsolutePath.make(globalService.config)
    const candidates = ConfigDiscovery.names.map((name) => path.join(directory, name))
    const filepath =
      (yield* Effect.filter(candidates, fs.isFile)).at(-1) ?? path.join(directory, "opencode.jsonc")
    const text = (yield* fs.readFileStringSafe(filepath)) ?? "{}\n"
    const updated = yield* Effect.try({ try: () => applyEdits(text, modify(text, ["shell"], ...)), ... })
    yield* fs.writeWithDirs(filepath, updated.endsWith("\n") ? updated : `${updated}\n`)
```

`FSUtil.writeWithDirs` (`packages/util/src/fs-util.ts:138-155`) is a direct `fs.writeFileString(path, content)` to the target path — it truncates the existing file and writes into the same inode. There is no temporary file, no rename, and no mode argument is passed at this call site, so a config file **created** by this path also gets default (umask) permissions.

Reachability: `packages/app/src/settings/general/controllers.ts:63` — changing the shell in desktop Settings calls `sdk.api.config.update({ shell })`, which lands here. The target is the last existing global config candidate, or a freshly created `opencode.jsonc`.

## Why it matters

- An interrupted write — crash, kill, power loss, full disk — leaves the user's **entire global config truncated or partially written**: every provider, MCP server, permission and routing setting in that file, not just the `shell` key this call meant to change. The next startup then parses a broken config.
- The house pattern everywhere else is temp file in the same directory + rename: CLI `packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:41-47` (with mode `0o600`), `config/migrate.ts:27`, `services/service-registration.ts:39`, and the atomic rewrites landed for route-overrides (#924), `mcp add` (#977/#978) and uninstall's shell-config rewrite (#988/#990). Core `Config.update` is a remaining in-place writer of a user-owned config file.
- Global config files are also commonly **symlinks** (dotfiles repos, Nix/home-manager managed configs): a naive temp+rename over the link path would replace the symlink with a regular file. The #990 fix (`writeShellConfig` in `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/uninstall.ts`) already solved exactly this shape — write beside the *resolved* target, rename over the target, preserve the target's existing mode — and its tests pin symlink + mode preservation.

## Evidence

- `packages/core/src/config.ts:451` — `yield* fs.writeWithDirs(filepath, ...)` with no mode, on main `195bdae185`.
- `packages/util/src/fs-util.ts:138-155` — `writeWithDirs` implementation: direct `writeFileString`/`writeFile` to the target path; `chmod` only when a mode argument is supplied (this call site supplies none).
- Contrast: `packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:41-47` — temp `file + ".tmp"`, `writeFileString(temp, text, { mode: 0o600 })`, `rename(temp, file)`.
- Caller: `packages/app/src/settings/general/controllers.ts:59-63` (shell picker → `sdk.api.config.update`).
- No test covers `Config.update`'s write path: `packages/core/test/config/` contains changed-sections / entry-observer / policy tests, none exercising `update` against a real file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The global-config rewrite is crash-safe: the on-disk config is never a partially written version (temp file in the same directory + rename, or an equivalently atomic mechanism; on Windows the rename follows the house EPERM-retry precedent from #99 if applicable).
- [ ] A symlinked config file still resolves to the same target after an update, and an existing file's permissions are preserved; a newly created config does not end up with looser permissions than the CLI writer's `0o600` precedent.
- [ ] Behaviour is otherwise unchanged: same candidate selection (last existing config name, else `opencode.jsonc`), same JSONC edit (only the `shell` key, formatting options unchanged), same reload signalling after a successful write.
- [ ] Regression coverage exists for the write path: round-trip update of an existing config, creation when none exists, symlink preservation, and mode preservation; existing core config tests stay green.

title: fix(core): quota-reset relative parsers disagree on compact units — tuning parser misses '6d 13h'/'3h', both miss '30m'/'30min'

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

The two relative quota-reset message parsers disagree on compact units, and both miss the compact minute unit entirely — so a provider that states its reset compactly is honoured by one door and silently ignored by the other(s).

Verified on main `195bdae185` (post-#991) with a laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-30-creator-reset-units`, real `model-route-limits.ts` imported by bun + verbatim-spliced `parseQuotaReset` from the real `model-route-tuning.ts`; controls pass):

| message | `ModelRouteLimits.resetAtFromMessage` | `ModelRouteTuning.parseQuotaReset` | expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| `your quota resets in 6d 13h` | now + 565200000 | **undefined** | now + 565200000 |
| `quota exhausted, resets in 3h` | now + 10800000 | **undefined** | now + 10800000 |
| `quota resets in 2d` | now + 172800000 | **undefined** | now + 172800000 |
| `quota resets in 30m` | **undefined** | **undefined** | now + 1800000 |
| `quota resets in 30min` | **undefined** | **undefined** | now + 1800000 |
| `quota resets in 45s` | now + 45000 | now + 45000 | control ✓ |
| `quota resets in 1 hour 30 minutes` | now + 5400000 | now + 5400000 | control ✓ |
| `come back in 5 deals` | undefined | undefined | control ✓ (no false positive) |

## Evidence

- `packages/core/src/model-route-limits.ts:120-122` — #991 extended `RELATIVE_PART`/`RELATIVE_PARTS` with the compact letter units `h` and `d`, and `model-route-limits.test.ts` now pins `resets in 6d 13h`. The unit set is `second|minute|hour|day|sec|h|d|s` — no `m`/`min` for minutes, even though the sibling header-duration parser in the same file accepts `m` (`UNITS` at `model-route-limits.ts:37-43`; the `Snapshot` doc cites durations such as `"6m0s"`).
- `packages/core/src/model-route-tuning.ts:186-199` — `parseQuotaReset` carries its own copy of the relative grammar, still at the pre-#991 unit set `second|minute|hour|day|sec|s`: no `h`, no `d`. Its comment says "The relative form mirrors ModelRouteLimits", and `model-route-limits.ts:110-112` states the pairing rule for the absolute branch: "a message honoured by one door must be honoured by the other". The relative branch now violates that rule — the same drift class #532 fixed for absolute-time keywords.
- Consumers: `resetAtFromMessage` feeds the runner's `failureHint` (`packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts:149`), the new #984 quota gate (`step.ts:448-455`), the tuning review's predictions (`model-route-tuning.ts:146`) and note adjustments (`model-route-tuning.ts:235`). A missed parse means: no retry hint, the #984 gate falls back to the flat 30-minute hold instead of the stated reset, and no tuning prediction.

## Why it matters

Providers do state resets compactly (`resets in 6d 13h` was #991's own motivating example). Since #991, whether that statement is honoured depends on which parser a given consumer happens to call, and the most common compact minute spellings (`30m`, `30min`) are honoured by neither — a pool that stated a 90-minute reset gets retried after the 30-minute fallback and collects fresh 429s, or a tuning prediction is never made.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both parsers accept the same relative-unit grammar, including compact `h`/`d` (tuning parity with #991) and `m`/`min`/`mins` for minutes in both.
- [ ] The unit grammar lives in one place (shared from `model-route-limits`), or paired tests pin the two copies to identical results over a shared case table — the drift cannot recur silently.
- [ ] Guard cases still return undefined: `in 5 deals`, `in 2 homes` (the `(?![a-z])` word-head guard keeps working for the new units, e.g. `in 5 marks` states no wait).
- [ ] Compound compact sequences sum: `in 1h30m` or `in 1h 30m` reads as 90 minutes if the grammar admits it; otherwise the limitation is explicit in a test.
- [ ] Existing tests in `model-route-limits.test.ts` and `model-route-tuning.test.ts` keep passing.

title: design(core): one numeric contract at the service boundary — shared normalisation primitives for limits, durations and timeouts

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core

labels.name: effort/l
labels.description: Large: multi-day or open-ended; expect staged check-ins

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

labels.name: meta/epic
labels.description: Epic / cross-repo tracker

labels.name: kind/design
labels.description: A design proposal (design-architect): multi-step, phased, decision-bearing

labels.name: source/design-architect
labels.description: Filed by the repo design architect job

body:
**One-line summary:** the ~40 per-site numeric-validation fixes of 2026-10-27→30 (poisoned limits, offsets, `expires_in`, poll intervals, timeouts) each re-derived the same guard locally and the policies have diverged — this design states one contract: shared normalisation primitives in `packages/core/src/util/number.ts`, the existing helpers migrated onto them with behaviour unchanged, and a `check:numeric-boundaries` regression net modelled on `check:proto-reads`.

Design doc: `files/designs/opencode-numeric-boundary-contract.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace (central register: `files/potential-projects.md`).

## Problem in one paragraph

Numbers arriving from outside a service (plugin callers, query strings, OAuth servers, provider responses, config, env) are `undefined` / `NaN` / ±Infinity / negative / fractional / unit-confused, and JS defaults for them are hostile in repeating ways: negative SQLite `LIMIT` = unlimited (#981, #948, #951), `slice(-0.5)` = everything (#904, #733), fractional `git --unified=` or array indices defect the call (#980, #947, #957), oversized timeouts fire in ~1 ms and oversized `expires_in` disables refresh for weeks (#972, #879), un floored poll intervals busy-poll (#880). The fleet fixed these one site at a time; the shared layer was never designed — unlike the prototype-chain class, which got audit #833 → shared guard #865 → `check:proto-reads`.

## Evidence of divergence (main `195bdae185`)

- Three functions named `expiresInSeconds`, three contracts: shared `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/expires.ts:29`; a private copy in `packages/core/src/mcp/oauth.ts:250` the shared module never absorbed; a same-named *string-parsing* variant in `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/digitalocean.ts:48`.
- One file, two policies for server durations: oversized token lifetime → fallback (`expiresInSeconds`), oversized device lifetime → clamp (`deviceLifetimeSeconds`, expires.ts:45). No record of intent.
- Paging helpers per surface: `sessionListLimit` (plugin/session-list.ts:41, no ceiling), `branchListLimit` (plugin/vcs/branch-list.ts:20, ceiling 100), and a third inline spelling in `KV.scan` (kv.ts:61) that #957's evidence calls "the house pattern" — folklore, not a module.
- Schemas promise `PositiveInt`/`NonNegativeInt` (packages/schema/src/messaging.ts:384,392) but the plugin host bypasses decode (plugin/host.ts:457), so service-boundary normalisation is the load-bearing layer.
- Still-open instances: #935 (session.list default page), #957 (Messaging chars/context) — both in flight/claimed; cited as evidence, NOT adopted by this design.
- `packages/core/src/util/` already hosts the shared guards (`record.ts` from #865) — there is no `number.ts`.

## Proposal

1. **`packages/core/src/util/number.ts`** — named primitives, policies as parameters: `pageLimit(value, {default, max?})`, `pageOffset(value)`, `boundedCount(value, {default, max})`, `serverSeconds(value, {fallback, max, oversized: "fallback"|"clamp"})`, `timeoutMs(value, {fallback, max})` (ceiling defaults to the 2³¹−1 ms setTimeout cliff, #972). One table-driven conformance suite over the shared edge table (undefined/NaN/±Infinity/negative/zero/fractional/at-bound/over-bound/unit-confused).
2. **Existing helpers become wrappers, then disappear** — behaviour bit-identical, existing per-site tests stay and must pass unchanged; any site a primitive cannot reproduce exactly is recorded as a named exception in the module.
3. **`check:numeric-boundaries`** — a script + allowlist modelled on `check:proto-reads`, scanning for bare `Number(`/`parseInt(`/`parseFloat(` in `packages/core/src`, `packages/ai/src` AND `packages/cli/src` from day one (#912 is the lesson of starting one package short).

Out of scope: calendar-date parsing (sibling family, #798 et al. — different primitive); schema/host enforcement (open question in the doc); any new limits/defaults/ceilings (every value comes from an existing handler, helper or landed fix).

## Phased breakdown

1. **Phase 1 — primitives + paging migration** (filed as sub-issue, enqueued): the util module + conformance tests; `sessionListLimit`, `branchListLimit`, `KV.scan` re-implemented on `pageLimit`.
2. **Phase 2 — duration de-duplication** (filed as sub-issue, enqueued): delete the `mcp/oauth.ts` and DigitalOcean `expiresInSeconds` duplicates for `serverSeconds`; `expires.ts`'s pair become call sites with `oversized` named per site.
3. **Phase 3 — the net** (filed as sub-issue, enqueued): `script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` + allowlist + tests, wired as `check:numeric-boundaries`.

Open questions (in the doc, not filed): host-side schema decode as defence in depth; a strict string→int parser (reject-vs-fallback differs per surface, #874/#875); whether `packages/ai` may depend on core's util.

title: fix(cli): opencode api buffers the whole response body — response.text() is unbounded against an arbitrary --server

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: user/review

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/cli
labels.description: Package: cli (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

The `opencode api` command buffers the **entire response body in memory** before printing anything:

```ts
// packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/api.ts:42-47 (main 56321bbd1a)
const response = yield* Effect.tryPromise(() => fetch(new URL(request.path, endpoint.url), { ... }))
const output = yield* Effect.promise(() => response.text())
if (output) process.stdout.write(output + ...)
```

The operation-by-name path does the same for the OpenAPI document:

```ts
// packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/api.ts:74-77
const response = await fetch(new URL("/openapi.json", endpoint.url), { ... })
return resolveOperation((await response.json()) as OpenApi, input[0], params)
```

## Why the body size is not under the CLI's control

- The target server is arbitrary: `--server` is used verbatim as the endpoint URL (`packages/cli/src/services/server-connection.ts:25-41`), so the server can be a shared, standing, or remote server — not just the local managed one.
- The raw request form (`api.ts` `rawRequest`) accepts any method + path, so a caller can request endpoints whose bodies are as large as the underlying data: the server's `fs.read` handler streams arbitrary file bytes (`packages/server/src/handlers/fs.ts` `serveFile`, with Range support precisely because files can be large), and session/message/export-style reads scale with the stored history.
- `response.text()` resolves only when the body ends: a huge body is fully resident in the CLI's memory before a byte reaches stdout, and an endless/slow body hangs the command with no output at all. There is no cap, no streaming, and no timeout on this read.

## The in-repo precedent

Core tools never buffer a remote body whole: `packages/core/src/tool/http-body.ts` provides `collectBoundedResponseBody` (used by webfetch, capped at `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`), and the unbounded-body class has already been filed/fixed for sibling surfaces — #923 (four core/ai download paths), #942 (CLI session import remote body), #960 (Copilot utilityTitle). The CLI `api` handler is a separate, uncovered path: it is not one of #923's four paths and is not the session-import path of #942.

## Why it matters

`opencode api` is the scripting/debugging door into a server, routinely pointed at long-lived shared servers. One large response (a big file read, a large session export) can OOM or indefinitely hang a small CLI process that only needed to relay bytes to stdout — streaming makes the memory cost independent of the body size.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The response body is streamed to stdout (or collected under a stated byte cap with a clear error when exceeded), so CLI memory no longer scales with response size.
- [ ] Existing behaviour is preserved: non-OK responses still set exit code 1 and print `HTTP <status> <statusText>` to stderr; the trailing-EOL handling for printed output is preserved or its change is pinned by a test.
- [ ] The `/openapi.json` fetch in `resolveRequest` is likewise bounded or streamed, with a clear failure on an oversize/unparseable document.
- [ ] Regression coverage: a test drives the handler (or its extracted body-handling seam) against a fake/chunked large response and shows bounded handling; the existing `api.test.ts` cases (operation resolution, raw requests) stay green.

body:
## Problem

The prototype-chain regression gate (`bun run check:proto-reads`, `script/check-proto-reads.ts`) scans **only `packages/core/src`**, so the package where this bug class has bitten most often recently — `packages/ai` — has no regression net at all. Every `packages/ai` instance so far was found by hand, one at a time.

## Evidence (verified on main `427f20399e`, this run)

- `script/check-proto-reads.ts:27` — `export const SCAN_ROOT = "packages/core/src"` (singular root, used at `:83`); the CI step in `.github/workflows/test.yml` ("Check prototype-chain reads are dispositioned") therefore covers core only.
- `script/check-proto-reads.allowlist.txt` contains **0** entries for `packages/ai` (50 lines, all core).
- Replicating the gate's exact two sweep patterns (P-A uppercase-table read, P-C bracket read with `??`) over `packages/ai/src` (`.ts`, same as the gate's collector) yields **28 hits across 17 files**, none dispositioned. The hit list includes the exact sites of four separately-filed bugs:
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/media-type.ts:52,69` — #906 (media-type tables)
  - `packages/ai/src/protocols/deepgram-speech.ts:50,75`, `cartesia-speech.ts:81`, `elevenlabs-speech.ts:99` — #907 (speech format tables)
  - `packages/ai/src/protocols/open-responses.ts:954` — #908 (item-ID prefix)
  - `packages/ai/src/protocols/anthropic-messages.ts:1211` — #856 (server-tool-result names, fixed)
- Other hits are a mix of shapes the core allowlist already knows how to disposition, e.g. regex-constrained keys (`MONTH_NUMBERS[...toLowerCase()]` at `packages/ai/src/route/executor.ts:50,53` and `packages/ai/src/protocols/replicate-images.ts:142,145` — safe by construction, same disposition as the identical core lines), internal state maps (`packages/ai/src/schema/events.ts:594,602`), and at least one unexamined table read (`PCM_CODECS[codec]` at `packages/ai/src/protocols/elevenlabs-speech.ts:173`, codec derived from a split format string).

## Why it matters

The gate exists (#865, follow-up to the #833 audit) precisely so this class "cannot silently regrow one bare read at a time" — but that guarantee currently stops at the core package boundary. `packages/ai` parses untrusted provider responses all day; it is the highest-risk surface for prototype-named keys (`constructor`, `__proto__`, `toString` arriving as provider-supplied type/format strings). #906/#907/#908 were all filed within one day of each other by manual hunting; the next one should fail CI instead.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `script/check-proto-reads.ts` scans `packages/ai/src` in addition to `packages/core/src` (multi-root scan; the gate's unit tests in `script/check-proto-reads.test.ts` updated/kept green).
- [ ] Every one of the 28 current `packages/ai` hits is dispositioned: guarded at the site (own-key read), or allowlisted with a specific disposition (safe by construction with the reason / internal-only keys / tracked by an open issue, per the existing allowlist conventions). Hits that are live bugs get their own issue filed and cross-linked rather than a silent allowlist entry.
- [ ] `bun run check:proto-reads` passes on the resulting tree, and the CI step comment in `.github/workflows/test.yml` no longer describes the scan as core-only.
- [ ] No behavior change to any hit dispositioned as safe/internal.

Scope note: extending the same scan to the remaining packages (`packages/app`, `packages/tui`, `packages/client` also produce pattern hits) is explicitly out of scope here — those are DOM/client surfaces with different key provenance; file separately if wanted.

title: feat(routes): date-aware route windows — specific dates / holiday exclusions (DeepSeek peak suspends on Chinese public holidays)

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: New feature or capability request

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: queue/queued
labels.description: Has a queued task in the Supabase agent queue

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

body:
## Summary

Route windows (`experimental.model_route_windows`, shipped under #639 / PR #649) cannot express specific calendar dates, date ranges, or holiday calendars, and a target gate cannot exclude one named window from another. That makes at least one real provider clock — DeepSeek's peak/off-peak pricing — impossible to encode correctly: its peak windows are suspended in full on Chinese public holidays.

## Motivating case: DeepSeek's verified peak/off-peak rules

From DeepSeek's own pricing page, https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing/ (read 2026-10-29), footnote (2), verbatim:

> "(2) Off-peak rates are half of the peak rates. Peak hours are 01:00 - 04:00 and 06:00 - 10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday, excluding Chinese public holidays. All other hours are off-peak, including weekends and Chinese public holidays in full."

The change log (https://api-docs.deepseek.com/updates/, entry dated 2026-08-13) adds that peak/off-peak pricing took effect "at 16:00 (UTC Time) on August 16, 2026", "with off-peak prices set at half of the peak-hour prices".

So the rule has three parts:

1. Peak = Mon–Fri 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC — encodable today.
2. Weekends are off-peak in full — encodable today (windows are Mon–Fri only).
3. Chinese public holidays are off-peak **in full**, even when they fall Mon–Fri — **not encodable today**. DeepSeek does not enumerate the dates on its own pages; they are the annually published PRC State Council holiday arrangement (2026 example, published 2025-11-04: New Year Jan 1–3, Spring Festival Feb 15–23, Qingming Apr 4–6, Labour Day May 1–5, Dragon Boat Jun 19–21, Mid-Autumn Sep 25–27, National Day Oct 1–7). Weekday dates inside those blocks were incorrectly treated as peak by our config — e.g. National Day 2026 fell Thu Oct 1, Fri Oct 2, Mon Oct 5, Tue Oct 6, Wed Oct 7.

Note the asymmetry a holiday-calendar feature must preserve: per DeepSeek's text, weekends are off-peak "in full", so Chinese make-up workdays (weekend days officially worked to bridge a holiday block, e.g. Sat Oct 10, 2026) do **not** become peak. The needed operation is date **exclusion** from the peak windows, not a working-day calendar that flips weekends on.

## Why the current schema cannot express this

`packages/schema/src/config/model-routes.ts`, `Window` class — the complete field list is:

- `daysOfWeek` — recurring weekdays
- `daysOfMonth` — days of the month (1–31, or -1 = last day); recurs **every** month: there is no month or year field
- `start` / `end` — one daily time range
- `timezone`
- `from` / `until` — single epoch-ms bounds on the whole window ("before/after which the window never applies")

`packages/schema/test/config.test.ts` pins exactly that field list: `["daysOfWeek", "daysOfMonth", "start", "end", "timezone", "from", "until"]`. The runtime evaluator (`packages/core/src/model-route-schedule.ts`, `dayMatches` / `active`) matches only day-of-week and day-of-month, plus the single `from`/`until` bounds.

And the gate itself (`Target.window` in the same schema file) is a single window name, or `{ name, invert: true }` — no boolean composition, so a target cannot be gated on "window A AND NOT window B", and a named window cannot declare "except these dates".

`from`/`until` + `daysOfMonth` can be contorted to name one specific date in one specific month for one window, but it cannot subtract that date from a recurring peak window, cannot express a multi-day block crossing a month boundary, and fragments into 16+ windows for a single year's holidays with no way to compose them into the background route's single inverted Flash gate.

## Requested

Date-aware windows, in whatever shape fits the schema's style, e.g. one or more of:

- A `dates` field on `Window`: explicit calendar dates and/or date ranges (in the window's timezone) on which the window is active — and/or an `excludeDates` field listing dates/ranges on which it is not.
- Gate/window composition sufficient for "peak AND NOT holiday": e.g. a window referencing exception windows, or a target gate accepting an exclusion.
- Support for a named holiday calendar (a named window that is just a list of dates) so one `chinese-public-holidays-<year>` window can be reused as the exclusion for both peak windows.

## Current workaround

developing-today/code's `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` keeps the two Mon–Fri peak windows as the closest correct approximation (peak times and weekend treatment are exactly right; only the holiday exclusion is missing) and carries a comment naming this gap. Cost of the gap: on weekday Chinese public holidays the background route leads with MiMo and treats DeepSeek Flash as peak-priced (2x deduction on the pass-through plans) when it is actually off-peak — lost value, never overspend.


## Acceptance criteria

- The route-window schema can express specific calendar dates and date ranges (in the window's timezone), as active-on dates and/or as excluded dates, without fragmenting one holiday set into per-day recurring windows.
- Gate/window composition expresses "peak AND NOT holiday": a target gate or window can subtract an exception window (or equivalent), so the two DeepSeek Mon–Fri peak windows can exclude Chinese public holidays in full.
- A named holiday-calendar window (e.g. `chinese-public-holidays-<year>` — a window that is just a list of dates) can be defined once and reused as the exclusion for multiple windows.
- Tests cover: a weekday holiday suspends the peak window for the whole day; a multi-day exclusion range crossing a month boundary; weekend and ordinary-weekday behaviour unchanged from today's windows.
- The developing-today/code `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` peak-window config is updated to use the holiday exclusion (and its workaround comment removed), or that follow-up is filed and linked here before closure.

title: Token display overstates usage for session-backed proxy providers — surface cache/delta or trim resent context

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: user/review
labels.description: Needs a user-look: Muse reviews first and handles what it can

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/l
labels.description: Large: multi-day or open-ended; expect staged check-ins

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

labels.name: meta/protocol-gap
labels.description: An agent touched this without the required agent-note comment or labels; needs review of why

body:
## Problem

For session-backed providers (the local CLI proxies: commandcode via ACP, muse-proxy, codex-proxy, agy-proxy), OpenCode's per-message token record shows the FULL resent context as fresh input on every turn and reports `cache.read = 0`, even when the downstream session served almost everything from cache. The display therefore overstates real usage for exactly the providers where the warm-session work (developing-today/code#480) is cutting cost, and any quota/failover decision made from these numbers is made from wrong data.

## Evidence (2026-10-24, verified live)

End-to-end verification session `ses_e914921a9ffeickeigSWt8x9Pr` on the sandbox server, provider `commandcode`, model `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, two turns against the resident-ACP commandcode proxy:

- Turn 1 assistant message (`msg_16eb6e0c3001Ntlxn2l6w7J4DV`): tokens `{input: 26103, output: 3, cache: {read: 0, write: 0}}`
- Turn 2 assistant message (`msg_16eb93165001ZSOEC17Hs5PA5O`): tokens `{input: 26129, output: 56, cache: {read: 0, write: 0}}`

Turn 2 was a delta turn against a persistent cmd session: the proxy sent ~32 chars of new content downstream (vs an 18,899-char full history) and ACP usage reported ~99% of replayed context as cache-read. None of that is visible in OpenCode's record — both turns read as ~26.1k fresh input.

Same shape on the other CLI proxies: the muse route carries ~27k tokens of CLI session scaffolding per call, all displayed as fresh input every turn.

## Why it matters

- The user tracks token usage and makes provider/quota decisions from OpenCode's numbers (plan allowances, failover choices in the keeper's registry). Systematically overstating proxy-provider usage skews those decisions.
- As warm-session proxies land (code#480), the gap between displayed and real usage grows — the better the caching works, the more wrong the display looks by comparison (it never improves).

## Fix options (either, or both)

1. **Display/accounting fix:** when a provider response carries usage that distinguishes cache reads (or the proxy reports ACP/session usage), ingest it into the message token record (`cache.read`) and show net figures in the UI, so a cached turn reads as mostly cache, not fresh input.
2. **Bake the trimming into OpenCode:** for providers known to be session-backed (a provider capability flag), OpenCode itself sends delta-only context after the first turn instead of resending the full history, and accounts tokens accordingly — moving the optimization from per-proxy hacks into the client.

## Acceptance criteria

- A two-turn conversation against a session-backed proxy provider shows turn 2 with the bulk of its context under cache read (or a materially reduced input figure), matching the proxy's own usage report within a reasonable tolerance.
- Non-proxy providers' token records are unchanged.
- The chosen approach is noted on code#480 so the proxy program and the client stay in agreement about who owns trimming.

Related: #9 (prompt cache optimization across model pools) — adjacent, not the same problem: #9 is about routing for cache hits; this is about the token record/display being wrong for session-backed providers, and optionally moving trimming into the client.

body:
## Problem

`opencode run` hangs indefinitely on a headless Linux machine (NixOS-style sandbox, no desktop). This needs a real investigation — the CLI is unusable there while the server works fine.

## Observed behavior (opencode 1.18.31, this fork)

- `opencode run` loads the config, logs `all LSPs are disabled` / `init`, then produces **zero output forever** (observed 75–170s before timeout kill; no error, no partial stream).
- Reproduces with: any provider (Cloudflare gateway, OpenCode Go, built-in Codex OAuth), with and without `--pure`, with `OPENCODE_MCPX_DAEMON=0`, from both a persistent home dir and tmpfs, with both authenticated and unauthenticated egress proxy forms.
- The **server** (`opencode serve --pure`, same binary, same config, same flags, same env) answers the same providers via its HTTP API in seconds — sessions, messages, tool calls all work.

## Ruled out

Network/proxy credentials, provider auth, cwd/git discovery, plugins (hangs with `--pure` too), the mcpx daemon.

## What to investigate

- What does the `run` path do after init that `serve` does not? (session creation, snapshot/git work, event subscription, TUI-less output plumbing)
- Does `run` wait on something that never fires headless (stdin/TTY detection, an event that only the server path emits, a watcher)?
- Add diagnostics: verbose logging should show the last step before the stall.

## Acceptance

- Root cause identified and fixed, or a documented workaround + the blocking component named.
- `opencode run` completes a one-shot prompt headless on Linux with the full user config.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Root cause identified and named (the component/step the `run` path waits on headless), or a documented workaround with the blocking component named.
- [ ] `opencode run` completes a one-shot prompt on headless Linux with the full user config (not only `--pure`).
- [ ] Verbose logging shows the step sequence up to completion, so a future stall is diagnosable from logs alone.

body:
### Context & Background
In OpenCode upstream commit `69a71426ce` (`feat(core): configure Anthropic cache breakpoints with compatibility.cacheFormat (#54945)`), upstream introduced `compatibility.cacheFormat` for Anthropic and AWS Bedrock models to control how prompt caching breakpoints are structured and placed.

In our fork (`developing-today/opencode`), model routes (`experimental.model_routes`) balance requests across pools of models according to tiers (`cheap`, `standard`, `frontier`). Prompt cache read hits (`tokens_cache_read`) provide up to 90% cost savings compared to base prompt tokens (tracked in our `route_attempt` table). However, currently cache configuration is not unified across routed pools, causing cache fragmentation or missed breakpoint opportunities when requests cycle through different models in a pool.

### Feature Objective
Introduce cache format optimization into model route definitions:
1. Allow model routes to declare cache format strategies (`compatibility.cacheFormat`) to maximize prompt caching efficiency.
2. Track and report cache savings ($ saved via cache hits) in `route_stats` and `route_usage`.

---

### Technical Specifications

#### 1. Route Schema Support for Cache Optimization
- In `packages/schema/src/config/model-routes.ts` and `packages/core/src/model-route.ts`:
  - Add optional `cache_format` setting to route target definitions:
    ```jsonc
    "experimental": {
      "model_routes": {
        "frontier_pool": {
          "mode": "ordered",
          "tier": "frontier",
          "cache_format": "anthropic-breakpoints",
          "targets": [
            { "provider": "anthropic", "model": "claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022", "cache_format": "anthropic-breakpoints" },
            { "provider": "bedrock", "model": "anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet", "cache_format": "bedrock-converse" }
          ]
        }
      }
    }
    ```

#### 2. Cache Format Application in Provider Adapter
- When resolving the target model in `packages/core/src/session/runner/model.ts`:
  - Ensure the resolved route target injects the appropriate `compatibility.cacheFormat` into the request options before invoking the provider transport.
  - Verify that Anthropic cache breakpoints (`cache_control: { type: "ephemeral" }`) are preserved when switching between supported targets in the same pool.

#### 3. Cache Savings Metrics in `route_usage` & `route_stats`
- In `packages/core/src/model-usage.ts` and `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/route-usage.ts`:
  - Compute `cost_saved_usd` based on difference between base input pricing and cached read pricing:
    ```
    savings = tokens_cache_read * (price_input - price_cache_read)
    ```
  - Display cache hit ratio and total USD saved in `route_usage` tool output.

---

### Key Files & References
- `packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts`: Route schema and normalization
- `packages/core/src/session/runner/model.ts`: Route resolution and model options injection
- `packages/core/src/model-usage.ts`: Usage tracking, token pricing, and cost calculations
- `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/route-usage.ts`: Usage reporting tool

### Acceptance Criteria
1. Route targets can specify cache format preferences that are applied to outgoing LLM requests.
2. `route_attempt` records non-zero `tokens_cache_read` when prompt caching is active.
3. `route_usage` reports total USD savings achieved through cache hits.
4. Unit tests in `packages/core/test/` verify cache format propagation and savings calculations.

body:
# fix(cli): sharp-stub build guard passes when only one of its two rewrites applies — a respelled sharp import silently restores the #1727 packaged-binary failure

## Summary

Verified on `origin/main` `3342e1ddeb`: the `sharpStubPlugin` in `packages/cli/script/build.ts` (added by PR #1786 fixing #1727) claims to fail the build loudly when its transformers-bundle rewrites stop matching upstream, but its guard only catches the case where **both** rewrites fail, or where a `requireFromHere("onnxruntime-node")` call survives. If upstream respells the sharp import — a routine bundle formatting change, e.g. `import sharp from 'sharp';` with single quotes — the sharp rewrite silently becomes a no-op, the onnxruntime rewrite succeeds, the guard passes, and the compiled binary ships with the real `sharp` import again: exactly the #1727 failure mode (sharp's native binding cannot be located from inside `$bunfs`, so even **text** embeddings die at import in the packaged binary), with no build error anywhere.

## Evidence

`packages/cli/script/build.ts:157-178` (at `3342e1ddeb`):

```ts
const transformed = source
  .replace('import sharp from "sharp";', stub)
  .replace('requireFromHere("onnxruntime-node")', 'require("onnxruntime-node")')
if (transformed === source || transformed.includes('requireFromHere("onnxruntime-node")'))
  throw new Error("Failed to rewrite the transformers sharp/onnxruntime-node loaders")
```

- `transformed === source` is true only when **both** `.replace` calls are no-ops.
- The `includes(...)` check only inspects the onnxruntime rewrite.
- Nothing asserts the sharp import is gone or that the stub is present. (`String.replace` also replaces only the first occurrence, so the sharp side has no leftover check equivalent to the onnxruntime side's.)

Laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-creator-opencode-sharp/probe.mjs`, node, replicating the exact transform + guard from `build.ts`):

- Case A (current upstream spelling `import sharp from "sharp";` + `requireFromHere("onnxruntime-node")`): transform succeeds, sharp stubbed = true.
- Case B (sharp import respelled with single quotes, onnxruntime call unchanged): **guard passes (no throw); real sharp import still present = true.**

Dedup: `gh issue list --search "sharp rewrite build"` / `"transformers stub"` return only closed #1615 and #1727 and open #1554/#1146 — no open issue covers this guard. The sibling Node-bundle rewrites in `packages/cli/vite.node.config.ts:55,109,187` each perform a **single** rewrite guarded by `transformed === code`, so they do not share this partial-application flaw; this issue is only about the two-rewrite Bun plugin.

## Why it matters

#1727 was a three-layer packaging failure that kept the packaged server's default embeddings backend from ever running, and this plugin is the layer that keeps layer (2) from recurring. Its own comment says the rewrite must fail loudly ("Failed to rewrite…"). As written, the most likely upstream drift — a quote/formatting respell of one import string in a regenerated transformers bundle — defeats exactly one rewrite and passes the guard, so the regression would only be discovered the way #1727 was: by running the packaged binary and watching text embeddings fail.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each rewrite is asserted independently: the build throws when the sharp import was not replaced (stub absent / sharp import still present), and throws when any `requireFromHere("onnxruntime-node")` remains — a partial application can no longer pass.
- [ ] The current upstream bundle spelling still builds: both rewrites apply and the guard passes on the unmodified transformers dist bundle.
- [ ] A regression test or scripted probe covers the partial-application case (respelled sharp import with a working onnxruntime rewrite must throw), in the spirit of the repo's testing doctrine: the oracle is "both rewrites applied, or the build fails".
- [ ] No change to the stub's behavior, the onnxruntime rewrite target, or any runtime code — build-script guard only.

body:
## Summary

The ClinePass quota provider (`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/cline-pass.ts`) builds its windows record by unconditional assignment — `windows[kind.key] = ...` (cline-pass.ts:86) — so when the usage-limits response carries two entries of the same `type`, the later entry silently overwrites the earlier one. That is the opposite of the convention the suite adopted in #1750 for opendesign coding-plan windows ("duplicate durations keep the first entry instead of silently overwriting"). The mapping is also entirely unpinned: `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` never imports cline-pass, and the parse logic is embedded in `fetchForKey` rather than an exported pure function (it is still testable end-to-end via the injectable `fetchImpl`, as the probe below shows).

## Evidence (verified this run, main 4b9febff80)

Probe on the laptop (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-cline-pass/probe.ts`) calling `provider.fetchQuotaForCredential` with a stubbed `fetchImpl` returning:

```json
{ "data": { "limits": [
  { "type": "five_hour", "percentUsed": 10, "resetsAt": "2026-11-06T00:00:00Z" },
  { "type": "five_hour", "percentUsed": 90, "resetsAt": "2026-11-06T01:00:00Z" },
  { "type": "weekly",    "percentUsed": "42", "resetsAt": "2026-11-12T00:00:00Z" },
  { "type": "weekly",    "percentUsed": 7,  "resetsAt": "2026-11-13T00:00:00Z" },
  { "type": "monthly",   "percentUsed": 55, "resetsAt": "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z" }
] } }
```

Published windows: `5h` → 90% used (the 10% entry silently dropped), `weekly` → 7% used (the `"42"` entry silently dropped), `monthly` → 55%. No error, no log, no indication a duplicate ever existed. Whether first-wins or last-wins is correct for Cline's wire is currently an undocumented accident of loop order; #1750 already settled the house convention as keep-first for the identical shape in opendesign.

## Why it matters

ClinePass is one of the plan pools the fork rotates across. If Cline ever returns split or repeated limit entries (per-model splits, plan migrations), the published usage flips to whichever entry happens to sort last, with nothing recording that a choice was made. The parser also has no test pinning its string/number `percentUsed` handling, unknown-type skipping, or the empty-windows "No quota data in response" path — the same unpinned-parser gap #1725 / #1750 closed for the other providers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Duplicate `type` entries keep the first entry, per the #1750 convention (or a different disposition is chosen and documented in the code + this issue's closing note).
- [ ] The limits→windows mapping is pinned in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` (via `fetchQuotaForCredential` with a stubbed `fetchImpl`, or an extracted pure parser): happy path for all three window kinds, numeric-string `percentUsed`, missing `percentUsed` (entry skipped), unknown `type` (skipped), duplicate `type`, and the all-invalid → "No quota data in response" result.
- [ ] Existing quota suite stays green; gate state not regressed (the three quota-era gates already red on main belong to #1724 — do not conflate).
