# fix(ai): commandcode + claude-code auth bridges accept whitespace-only credentials — a blank env var shadows commandcode's valid login file, and both bridges send `Bearer <spaces>`

Verified 2026-11-05 on main `23d68ea41451eea55dde7ce5fd59dc0e218a8801` (laptop primary, fresh fetch/ff), with a probe run on the laptop (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-auth-whitespace/probe.ts`) driving the real exported resolvers from all three new direct-provider auth bridges against injectable sources.

## Evidence

The three bridges landed together (PR #1749, #6117) but disagree on blank handling. `vibe-auth.ts` trims every source and treats a blank as absent (`resolveApiKey`: `env[API_KEY_ENV_VAR]?.trim()`, file and keyring values likewise, vibe-auth.ts:146-160). The other two check only `length > 0`:

- `packages/ai/src/providers/commandcode-auth.ts:80` — the env loop returns the first env var with `value.length > 0`; whitespace passes.
- `packages/ai/src/providers/commandcode-auth.ts:57` — `parseAuthFile` returns any `apiKey` string with `length > 0`; whitespace passes.
- `packages/ai/src/providers/claude-code-auth.ts:78` — `parseCredentialsFile` accepts any non-empty `accessToken`; whitespace passes.
- `packages/ai/src/providers/claude-code-auth.ts:113` — the env fallback accepts any non-empty `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; whitespace passes.

Probe results (real resolvers, injected sources):

- commandcode, env `COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY="   "` + auth.json holding a valid key → resolver returns `"   "` — **the blank env var shadows the valid login file** (env is tier 1, the file is tier 2, and the resolver returns the first hit) — and `cliHeaders` then produces `authorization: "Bearer    "`. The request fails upstream as an auth error against a credential that was never real, while the machine's actual login sits unused in the file below it.
- commandcode, `parseAuthFile({"apiKey": "  "})` → returns `"  "`.
- commandcode, env `""` + valid file → correctly falls through to the file key (empty string is the only blank that works today).
- claude-code, credentials file with `accessToken: "   "` → accepted as a credentials-file credential; env `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN="   "` with no file → accepted as an environment credential.
- vibe, env `MISTRAL_API_KEY="   "` + `.env` file holding a valid key → correctly falls through and returns the file key. This is the behavior the other two bridges should match.

Neither auth test file pins any of this: `grep -c whitespace/trim` over `packages/ai/test/provider/commandcode-auth.test.ts` and `packages/ai/test/provider/claude-code-auth.test.ts` returns 0 for both.

This is the blank-value class the fleet has fixed repeatedly elsewhere (#677 blank retry-after header, #874 blank env var, #1741 blank quota fields) arriving in the newest credential code — with a worse failure shape than usual in the commandcode case, because the blank value doesn't just misread, it *wins* over a valid credential in a lower tier. It is a sibling of #1752's trap (a bad file credential blocking the env source in claude-code), not a duplicate: #1752 is about an expired-but-real token and the expiry check; this one is about values that are not tokens at all, in both bridges.

## Why it matters

These bridges spend the user's real CLI logins. A stray blank env var (an exported-but-empty variable in a shell profile, a CI secret wired but unset, a templated `.env`) silently breaks the commandcode provider despite a healthy `cmd login` on the same machine, and the failure surfaces as an opaque upstream 401 rather than the bridges' own not-signed-in guidance, which names exactly what to fix. Blank-acceptance also defeats the bridges' documented resolution contract ("first credential a source can produce" — a whitespace string is not a credential a source produced).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In `commandcode-auth.ts` and `claude-code-auth.ts`, every resolved credential source (env vars, auth/credentials file fields) trims its value and treats blank-after-trim as absent, matching `vibe-auth.ts`; the returned credential is the trimmed value.
- [ ] A whitespace-only `COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY` / `COMMANDCODE_API_KEY` no longer shadows a valid `~/.commandcode/auth.json` key; a whitespace-only file `apiKey` reads as "no credential there".
- [ ] A whitespace-only claude-code file `accessToken` reads as "no credential there" (so resolution reaches the env tier, per the existing malformed-file fall-through), and a whitespace-only `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` reads as absent.
- [ ] Explicit static config overrides (`apiKey` / `accessToken` provider options, documented as tests/offline inputs) are out of scope and unchanged.
- [ ] New tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/commandcode-auth.test.ts` and `packages/ai/test/provider/claude-code-auth.test.ts` pin: whitespace env + valid file → file key; whitespace file value → absent/fall-through; whitespace env token (claude) → absent; padded real values (`"  key  "`) resolve to the trimmed key (oracle: vibe-auth's established trim-and-fall-through behavior).
- [ ] Existing commandcode-auth / claude-code-auth / vibe-auth tests still pass.

# fix(ai): codex quota windows keyed only by derived duration label — a missing or shared limit_window_seconds silently drops one window, and an empty window object mints a phantom all-null window

Verified 2026-11-05 on main `23d68ea41451eea55dde7ce5fd59dc0e218a8801` (laptop primary, fresh fetch/ff), with a probe run on the laptop (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-codex-quota/probe.ts`) driving the real `provider.fetchQuota` from `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/codex.ts` against a mocked ChatGPT `wham/usage` response.

## Evidence

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/codex.ts:104` and `:112` publish the primary and secondary rate-limit windows into a plain record keyed **only** by the derived duration label:

```ts
windows[resolveWindowLabel(windowSeconds)] = toUsageWindow({ ... }) // primary, :104
windows[resolveWindowLabel(windowSeconds)] = toUsageWindow({ ... }) // secondary, :112
```

`resolveWindowLabel` (`packages/ai/src/quota/utils.ts:64`) returns `"tokens"` for a null/zero duration, `"5h"` for 18000, `"weekly"` for 604800, etc. — it has no notion of which window it is labelling. The two windows therefore share a key whenever their durations collide, and the secondary silently overwrites the primary.

Probe results (mocked payload → published `usage.windows`):

- Baseline (primary 18000s/10%, secondary 604800s/80%): both windows published (`5h`, `weekly`) — correct.
- **Both windows missing `limit_window_seconds`** (primary 10%, secondary 80%): only ONE window survives — `tokens: { usedPercent: 80, ... }`. The primary's 10% is silently lost; the result still reports `ok: true`.
- **Both windows at 18000s**: same loss — only `5h: { usedPercent: 80 }` survives.
- **`primary_window: {}` (empty object)**: a phantom window is minted — `tokens: { usedPercent: null, remainingPercent: null, windowSeconds: null, resetAt: null, ... }` — and the result is `ok: true` with a window that carries no data at all.
- Primary with `limit_window_seconds` + `reset_at` but **no `used_percent`**: publishes a `5h` window whose `usedPercent`/`remainingPercent` are both null.

There is no test net for any of this: `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` contains no Codex describe/block at all (grep for `codex`/`Codex` in that file returns nothing), while sibling providers (mistral, meta, turso, groq, command-code) are pinned there. This is the same unpinned-parser class as #1725/#1750, with a live data-loss bug inside it.

## Why it matters

Quota windows drive placement and exhaustion decisions (design #587: one quota signal, three consumers). A dropped primary window means the fleet sees only the looser/looser-looking limit; a phantom all-null window means a provider with no usable rate-limit data still presents a window downstream consumers must guess at. Both failures are silent — `ok: true` either way — so nothing downstream can tell data was lost.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Primary and secondary windows can never overwrite each other: when their derived labels collide (equal durations, or either duration missing), both windows are published under distinct, stable keys (the fix names the keying scheme — e.g. primary/secondary-qualified keys — and records what downstream consumers see for the normal 5h/weekly case, which must not change).
- [ ] A window object carrying no usable data (no `used_percent`, no duration, no reset) does not mint a published window; if neither window has usable data, the result follows the sibling providers' no-data contract (cf. cline-pass/deepseek: `ok: false`, "No quota data in response") or the issue records why a different contract is right for Codex.
- [ ] A window with a duration/reset but no `used_percent` is dispositioned explicitly (kept with null percent, or dropped) — not left as an accident of the current code.

body:
## Problem

The Command Code protocol's usage mapper drops two fields the gateway already sends in the `finish` event's `totalUsage`, so the canonical `Usage` the session layer consumes is wrong on both:

- `packages/ai/src/protocols/commandcode.ts` — `WireUsage` (the `totalUsage` struct) types only `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, and `inputTokenDetails`; the wire's top-level `totalTokens` and `reasoningTokens` decode only through the StructWithRest record, untyped.
- Same file, `mapUsage`: `Usage` is built with no `reasoningTokens` field at all, and `totalTokens: ProviderShared.totalTokens(inputTokens, outputTokens, undefined)` — the provider-supplied total is never passed, even though the shared policy (`packages/ai/src/protocols/shared.ts`, `totalTokens` doc) states "The provider-supplied total is the source of truth when present".
- The module's own header comment records that these fields are real on the wire: live-captured 2026-11-05 `totalUsage` carries `totalTokens` / `reasoningTokens` (and the live-capture regression test in `packages/ai/test/provider/commandcode.test.ts` includes `totalTokens: 7920, reasoningTokens: 20` in its fixture — but asserts only `inputTokens` and `cacheReadInputTokens`, so the drop is unpinned).

Every sibling protocol that receives these fields maps them (e.g. `openai-chat.ts` maps `reasoningTokens` and passes `usage.total_tokens` into `totalTokens(...)`; likewise open-responses, antigravity, gemini, mistral, bedrock). Command Code is the outlier.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probe at main `87c145300f`)

Probe: laptop worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-creator-opencode-1210`, `packages/ai/test/provider/probe-usage.test.ts` (bun 1.4.4, `LLMClient.generate` + `fixedResponse` NDJSON, the same harness as `commandcode.test.ts`):

- Stream: `text-delta` + `finish` with `totalUsage: { inputTokens: 100, outputTokens: 50, totalTokens: 999, reasoningTokens: 20, inputTokenDetails: { cacheReadTokens: 10, cacheWriteTokens: 5 } }`
- Resulting `Usage`: `totalTokens: 150` (the computed sum — the provider's 999 ignored), `reasoningTokens: undefined` (the wire's 20 dropped; it survives only inside the raw `providerMetadata` spread).

## Why it matters

`Usage.reasoningTokens` feeds `Usage.visibleOutputTokens` (`packages/ai/src/schema/events.ts`: output minus reasoning) — with reasoning dropped, every Command Code turn overstates its visible output and loses the reasoning/output split that token display and cost accounting read (cf. #394). And when the gateway's reported total ever diverges from input+output, the published total silently contradicts the provider's own accounting, against the shared `totalTokens` policy every other route follows. The provider merged 2026-11-05 in PR #1749 as the tool-call-correct native replacement for the retired CLI bridge (code#6117); its usage surface should meet the same contract as its siblings.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `finish` event whose `totalUsage` carries `reasoningTokens` produces a `Usage` with that `reasoningTokens` value (and `visibleOutputTokens` reflects it).
- [ ] A `finish` event whose `totalUsage` carries `totalTokens` produces a `Usage` whose `totalTokens` is the provider-supplied value, per the shared policy in `shared.ts`; when the wire omits it, the input+output fallback still applies.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/commandcode.test.ts` pin both mappings (including a case where the provider total differs from input+output, so the fixture coincidence in the live-capture test — 7860+60=7920 — cannot mask it).
- [ ] The existing commandcode provider/protocol tests still pass.

body:
## Problem

The Command Code stream parser neither validates nor fails on malformed `tool-call` events — it silently drops nameless calls and emits id-less calls with colliding empty ids:

- `packages/ai/src/protocols/commandcode.ts:575-579` — the `tool-call` case reads `const name = event.toolName ?? ""` and `const id = event.toolCallId ?? ""`, and the only guard is `if (name)`: a call with no name is skipped entirely (no event, no error), and a call with no id is emitted with `id: ""`.
- This is the one silent path in a module whose stated contract is fail-loud: a stream ending without a finish event is a hard error (same file, `onHalt`), and invalid string tool input is a hard error via `ProviderShared.parseToolInput` — never a silent repair.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probe at main `24784651b6`)

Probe: laptop worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-creator-opencode-1055`, `packages/ai/test/provider/probe-toolcall.test.ts` (bun 1.4.4, `LLMClient.generate` + `fixedResponse` NDJSON streams, the same harness as `packages/ai/test/provider/commandcode.test.ts`):

- `{type:"tool-call", toolCallId:"call_x", input:{a:1}}` (no `toolName`) followed by `finish: "tool-calls"` → **Success with 0 tool calls** and finish normalized `tool-calls` — an internally inconsistent response: the turn claims tool calls that do not exist anywhere in it, and the model's requested action has vanished without a trace.
- Two `{type:"tool-call", toolName:"get_weather", input:{...}}` events with no `toolCallId` → both emitted with `id: ""` — two distinct calls sharing one empty id.

## Why it matters

Tool-call identity is how the session layer pairs calls with their results. A dropped call ends the turn as though the model never asked for the tool (the work simply never happens, with no error anywhere), and duplicate empty ids cross-wire results between distinct calls. The provider was merged today (PR #1749, commit `c6acfa2a86`) as the tool-call-correct replacement for the retired CLI bridge (code#6117) — silent loss on this surface is exactly the failure class it exists to eliminate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `tool-call` event missing `toolName` or `toolCallId` fails the stream with a provider error naming the malformed event (consistent with the file's fail-loud contract), or is given an explicitly stated, test-pinned disposition — silence is not an acceptable outcome.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/commandcode.test.ts` cover: nameless tool-call, id-less tool-call, and two id-less tool-calls in one stream.
- [ ] A response can no longer report a `tool-calls` finish while containing zero tool calls due to a dropped event.
- [ ] The existing commandcode provider/protocol tests still pass.

## Problem

The Command Code protocol's finish-reason mapper rewrites two of the fork's canonical finish reasons to `stop`, and an aborted stream completes as a normal stop:

- `packages/ai/src/protocols/commandcode.ts:446-461` — `mapFinishReason` handles only the tool spellings (`tool_use`/`tool-calls`/`tool_calls`) and `length`/`max_tokens`; every other raw value falls through to `"stop"`.
- The fork's own vocabulary, `packages/schema/src/llm.ts:5`, is `["stop", "length", "tool-calls", "content-filter", "error", "unknown"]` — so a gateway finish carrying `content-filter` or `error` is a first-class outcome this mapper erases.
- `packages/ai/src/protocols/commandcode.ts:653` — `onHalt` answers an `abort` event with `finishEvents(state, "abort")`, which the same mapper normalizes to `"stop"`: a gateway-aborted turn returns success with its partial text and a clean-stop finish.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probe at main `24784651b6`)

Probe: laptop worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-creator-opencode-1055`, `packages/ai/test/provider/probe-finish.test.ts` (bun 1.4.4, `LLMClient.generate` + `fixedResponse` NDJSON streams, the same harness as `packages/ai/test/provider/commandcode.test.ts`):

- `finish` with `finishReason: "content-filter"` → `finishReason.normalized = "stop"` (raw preserved as `content-filter`)
- `finish` with `finishReason: "error"` → `normalized = "stop"` (raw `error`)
- `finish` with `finishReason: "stop"` / `"length"` / `"tool_calls"` → `stop` / `length` / `tool-calls` (correct)
- `{type:"abort"}` then end-of-stream → **Success**, `normalized = "stop"`, raw `abort`, partial text presented as the completed response

## Why it matters

Downstream layers key real behavior off the normalized finish reason, not the raw string: content-policy handling exists precisely for content-filter finishes (#1620, #1084), and error-vs-stop outcomes feed attempt accounting and model-removal logic (#1014). A Command Code turn that was filtered, errored, or aborted is currently indistinguishable from a clean completion — partial text is presented as the finished answer and none of the policy/error paths can ever trigger for this provider (merged today in PR #1749, commit `c6acfa2a86`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `finish` event with `finishReason: "content-filter"` normalizes to `"content-filter"`, and one with `"error"` normalizes to `"error"`; genuinely unrecognized spellings map to `"unknown"` (or are explicitly dispositioned in a test) rather than silently becoming `"stop"`.
- [ ] A stream terminated by an `abort` event does not report `normalized: "stop"` — it maps to a stated non-stop reason (or fails), with the decision recorded on this issue.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/commandcode.test.ts` cover all three cases (content-filter finish, error finish, abort-then-EOF).
- [ ] The existing commandcode provider/protocol tests still pass.

# fix(ai): claude-code provider — an expired credentials-file token traps auth even when a valid CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is set; the env source is only reached when the file is missing or malformed

New surface from PR #1749 (commit `c6acfa2a86`, merged 2026-11-05): `packages/ai/src/providers/claude-code-auth.ts`.

The module documents a resolution order (header comment, lines 22-29):

0. explicit config (`auth` override, then static `accessToken`)
1. `~/.claude/.credentials.json` (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` override)
2. environment `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`

and `resolveCredential` implements "file first, env second" — a file that is missing or malformed falls through to the env token (pinned by the test "the env token is the fallback when the file has no credential", `packages/ai/test/provider/claude-code-auth.test.ts:48`).

The expired case does not fall through. `resolveCredential` returns the expired file credential (it does not check expiry), and the expiry check lives afterwards in `loadCredentialEffect` (claude-code-auth.ts, the `expiresAt <= now` branch), which fails the whole auth with the expired message — the env source is never consulted.

## Verified behavior (laptop probe, main 8185486080)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-creator-opencode-1535/probe-claude-auth2.ts`, using the module's own injectable sources, mirroring the existing test harness:

- File blob `{ accessToken: "tok-expired", expiresAt: 1000 }`, `now: () => 2000`, env `{ CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: "tok-env-valid" }` → auth **fails** with "The Claude Code OAuth credential in ~/.claude/.credentials.json expired at … Run `claude` and complete the sign-in to renew it" — the valid env token is never tried.
- Same setup with a malformed file (`"not json"`) → resolves to the env token.
- Same setup with a live file token → file token wins (correct, pinned).

So three file states — missing, malformed, expired — behave inconsistently: two fall through to the documented second source, one traps.

## Why it matters

`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is the CLI's own headless token variable — the source a headless/fleet deployment is most likely to actually maintain. On any machine where Claude Code was once signed in interactively and that login has since expired (the normal state of a headless box weeks later), setting the env token does not restore the provider: every claude-code request fails closed with instructions to run an interactive sign-in the operator may have deliberately replaced with the env token. The fail-closed design (code#6117) was about not refreshing the CLI's token and not falling back to the CLI or an API key — the env OAuth token is neither; it is the module's own documented source 2.

## Decision needed / acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide the intended precedence: (a) an expired file credential falls through to the env token (expiry = "no usable credential there", like malformed), or (b) fail-closed-on-expired is deliberate even with an env token present — in which case the header comment's resolution order and the error message must say so (the message should name that an env token is set but was not used, if that is the ruling).
- [ ] If (a): `claudeCodeAuth` with an expired file credential and a valid `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` succeeds with the env token as Bearer; the expired message still fires when no env token exists (existing test unchanged).
- [ ] If (b): a test pins expired-file + valid-env → expired failure, and the module header documents the trap.
- [ ] Either way: a regression test in `packages/ai/test/provider/claude-code-auth.test.ts` covers the expired-file + env-token combination (today only expired-file + empty-env is pinned), and the existing claude-code auth tests still pass.

# test(ai): the quota suite still pins none of claude / meta-billing / opendesign's pure parsers — and three of them demonstrably drop or invent windows on plausible payload shapes

Sibling of #1725 (which covers opencode-go's three parsers and openrouter's reset math). The same gap remains for the other exported pure parsers in `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/`, re-exported from `packages/ai/src/quota/index.ts:21-26`:

- `toClaudeUsage` — `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/claude.ts:166`
- `parseBillingBanner` — `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/meta.ts:105`
- `parseCodingPlanWindows` — `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/opendesign.ts:78`
- `normalizeOpenDesignCredential` — `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/opendesign.ts:49`

`grep` across `packages/ai/test/` and `packages/core/test/` returns zero references to any of the four (verified this run on main `8185486080`). `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins mistral, meta subscription, turso, groq, command-code and the `toNumber` blank-string cases — none of these four.

## Verified fragile behaviors (laptop probe, main 8185486080)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-creator-opencode-1535/probe-quota-parsers.ts` on the laptop, importing the real modules.

1. **`parseBillingBanner` rejects numeric strings that every sibling parser accepts.** `parseBillingBanner({ remaining_minor_units: 12345, currency: "USD" })` → `123.45`, but `parseBillingBanner({ remaining_minor_units: "12345", currency: "USD" })` → `null`. The function hand-rolls a `typeof minor !== "number"` check (meta.ts:106-109) instead of the module's shared `toNumber` (utils.ts), which accepts numeric strings — the exact lesson of #1741 (providers send string-typed numbers; the quota suite now pins that for command-code/opencode-go/meta-subscription). A string-typed banner silently nulls the Meta billing cross-check credits.
2. **`toClaudeUsage` discards the legacy windows whenever `limits` is non-empty.** With `limits: [{ kind: "weekly_scoped", … }]` plus populated legacy `five_hour`/`seven_day` fields, the result is `windows: {}` — the session and weekly windows vanish, because the legacy branch is an `else` of `limits.length > 0` (claude.ts:175-215). A payload whose limits list contains only scoped or unrecognized kinds loses data the payload itself carries.
3. **`parseCodingPlanWindows` publishes a window for a zero limit.** `{ durationSeconds: 18000, limitCredits: 0, remainingCredits: 0 }` yields a `5h` window with `usedPercent: null` and `valueLabel: "0 / 0 credits"` (opendesign.ts:92-99 publishes whenever either percent or label exists via `toUsageWindow`). Compare command-code's pinned behavior: a zero monthly balance is a real 100%-used window (#1744 tests), not a null-percent label-only window. Duplicate `durationSeconds` entries also silently overwrite (last wins, no note).

`normalizeOpenDesignCredential` showed no defect in the probe (bare token correctly prefixed with the session-cookie name; a full `better-auth…` cookie passed through) — it is included for pinning, not as a defect claim.

## Why it matters

These parsers feed the same quota surfaces as the #1722/#1741/#1744/#1746 line of bugs: every one of those was a pure-parser shape assumption that only surfaced in production payloads. The four parsers above are the remaining unpinned surface of the same module, and two of them already demonstrably diverge from the module's own conventions on plausible payload shapes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` (or a sibling test file) pins all four parsers: happy path, missing/malformed fields, string-typed numbers, and the null/empty conventions the rest of the module follows.
- [ ] `parseBillingBanner` accepts numeric-string `remaining_minor_units` via the shared `toNumber` (or the strictness is documented as deliberate, with a test pinning the rejection).
- [ ] `toClaudeUsage` with a non-empty `limits` array that yields no session/weekly window still surfaces legacy `five_hour`/`seven_day` windows (or the exclusivity is documented and pinned by test).
- [ ] `parseCodingPlanWindows` zero-limit behavior matches the module convention (a pinned test states which), and duplicate-duration handling is pinned.
- [ ] Existing quota tests still pass (`bun test test/quota.test.ts` in packages/ai) and `bunx tsgo --noEmit` for packages/ai is clean.

# fix(ai): Command Code quota publishes purchasedCredits as a quota window — contradicting the module's own READ RULE that it is never a quota figure

Verified 2026-11-05 on origin/main `fba8bcca0b` (laptop primary, clean), probe at `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-creator-opencode-0815/probe.ts` on the laptop (bun, run against the real parser).

## The contradiction

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/command-code.ts:18-21` states the rule the port was made under:

```
 * Command Code quota — ported from the OpenChamber quota module
 * (providers/command-code.js). Per Drew's quota READ RULE (2026-11-01)
 * Command Code reads report the PLAN windows; the top-up balance
 * (purchasedCredits) is never a quota figure.
```

The same file's parser then does exactly what the rule forbids — `parseCommandCodeCredits` (command-code.ts:74-81) publishes both top-up-style balances as windows in the quota result:

```ts
for (const [label, field] of [
  ["purchased_credits", "purchasedCredits"],
  ["free_credits", "freeCredits"],
] as const) {
  const value = toNumber(credits?.[field])
  if (value !== null) windows[label] = toBalanceWindow(value)
}
```

## Reproduced (probe, payload-shaped, against the real parser)

`parseCommandCodeCredits({ credits: { purchasedCredits: 40 } })` → a `purchased_credits` window (`usedPercent: null`, `valueLabel: "40"`) in the returned WindowMap. The CLI renderer (`packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/quota.ts:358-367`) renders every window in that map as a quota line, so `opencode quota` presents the top-up balance as a quota window named `purchased_credits 40` — precisely the reading the READ RULE prohibits. Any other consumer of the WindowMap (quota-aware routing snapshots) inherits the same figure with no marker distinguishing it from a plan window beyond the name.

## Why it matters

The READ RULE exists so a purchased top-up is never mistaken for plan quota: a balance that only decreases when spent, with no reset and no cap, presented as a window invites exactly the misreading the rule was written to prevent (headroom that is actually a wallet). Either the code or the stated rule is wrong; today both ship in the same file, so the next porter cannot tell which to follow. The `free_credits` window has the same shape and should be dispositioned in the same pass — the rule names only `purchasedCredits`, so free credits may be a deliberate exception, but that exception is currently undocumented.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Code and the module header agree: either `purchased_credits` (and, per the same reasoning, dispositioned `free_credits`) no longer appears in the quota WindowMap, or the header is amended to state the exception and why a balance window is not a quota figure.
- [ ] If the windows are removed: a payload carrying only `purchasedCredits` yields no windows (and the provider's "could not be parsed" path still behaves for genuinely empty payloads).
- [ ] Tests in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` (or a wired sibling) pin the dispositioned behavior for `purchasedCredits` and `freeCredits`.
- [ ] Existing quota tests still pass under the ai package test command; ai typecheck clean.

# fix(ai): Command Code quota monthly window vanishes when remaining credits exceed the hard-coded 10 included — an over-limit payload reads as "could not be parsed"

Verified 2026-11-05 on origin/main `fba8bcca0b` (laptop primary, clean), probe at `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-creator-opencode-0815/probe.ts` on the laptop (bun, run against the real parser).

## The bug

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/command-code.ts:62-72` — `parseCommandCodeCredits` only publishes the monthly window when the remaining balance falls inside the assumed included range:

```ts
export const MONTHLY_INCLUDED_CREDITS = 10
const monthlyRemaining = toNumber(credits?.monthlyCredits)
if (monthlyRemaining !== null && monthlyRemaining >= 0 && monthlyRemaining <= MONTHLY_INCLUDED_CREDITS) {
  const monthlyUsed = MONTHLY_INCLUDED_CREDITS - monthlyRemaining
  windows.monthly = toUsageWindow({ usedPercent: ..., valueLabel: `${monthlyUsed} / 10`, ... })
}
```

Any remaining balance **above** the hard-coded 10 (a plan change, a promo/rollover grant, a higher included tier, an upstream field whose meaning is total rather than remaining) drops the window entirely — no window, no error, no clamp.

## Reproduced (probe, payload-shaped, against the real parser)

- `parseCommandCodeCredits({ credits: { monthlyCredits: 5 } })` → `monthly` window, `usedPercent: 50`, label `"5 / 10"` ✓
- `parseCommandCodeCredits({ credits: { monthlyCredits: 10 } })` → `monthly` window, `usedPercent: 0` ✓
- `parseCommandCodeCredits({ credits: { monthlyCredits: 25 } })` → **`{}` — no windows at all**
- `parseCommandCodeCredits({ credits: { monthlyCredits: 25 }, windowLimits: { fiveHour: { used: 1, cap: 4, resetAt: 1893456000 } } })` → only the `5h` window; monthly silently absent
- Downstream: when the monthly credit is the only data in the payload, `fetchCommandCodeUsage` (command-code.ts) throws `"Command Code usage data could not be parsed"` on a perfectly parseable payload, and the provider reports a hard failure instead of a healthy 0%-used month.

## Why it matters

This is the same failure shape the repo just fixed for Turso in #1743 ("publish over-limit windows above 100 percent", merged PR #1743): a value outside the assumed range must be published truthfully (here: 0% used, with the real remaining figure visible), never dropped. A dropped monthly window reads downstream as "no quota data" — the `opencode quota` display loses the provider's headline window and quota-aware consumers reason from an absence. The hard-coded `MONTHLY_INCLUDED_CREDITS = 10` makes the trigger more likely over time, not less: the first plan that includes more than 10 monthly credits breaks the read.

Negative remaining (`monthlyCredits: -3`) also drops the window in the probe; that is nonsense data and dropping it is defensible — the acceptance below only requires the over-included case to publish.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parseCommandCodeCredits` with `monthlyCredits` above `MONTHLY_INCLUDED_CREDITS` publishes a `monthly` window with `usedPercent: 0` and a value label that shows the real remaining figure (not a fabricated "0 / 10" that hides it).
- [ ] In-range behavior is unchanged: 5 → 50% used, label "5 / 10"; 10 → 0% used.
- [ ] A payload whose only data is an over-included monthly credit no longer makes `fetchCommandCodeUsage` throw "could not be parsed".
- [ ] Tests in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` (or a wired sibling) pin the over-included case alongside the in-range cases.
- [ ] Existing quota tests still pass under the ai package test command; ai typecheck clean.

# fix(ai): quota `toNumber` coerces empty strings to 0 — an empty upstream field reports a pool 100% used (or 0% used)

Verified 2026-11-05 on origin/main `b318603c68` (laptop primary, clean), probe at `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-creator-opencode-1235/` on the laptop (`probe.ts`, `probe2.ts`, bun 1.4.4, run twice with identical results).

## The bug

`packages/ai/src/quota/utils.ts:26-31` — the shared numeric parser for the whole quota suite:

```ts
export const toNumber = (value: JsonValue | undefined): number | null => {
  if (typeof value === "number" && Number.isFinite(value)) return value
  if (typeof value === "string") {
    const parsed = Number(value)
    return Number.isFinite(parsed) ? parsed : null
  }
  return null
}
```

`Number("") === 0` and `Number("  ") === 0`, both finite — so an **empty or whitespace-only string is parsed as a real zero**, not as "no value" (`null`). Probe: `toNumber("") = 0`, `toNumber("  ") = 0`, `toNumber("12") = 12`.

`toNumber` is the front door for ~25 call sites across 9 quota providers (codex `used_percent`/`balance`/spend limits, claude percents + money, deepseek balances, opencode-go percent/balance/`expires`, opendesign credits, command-code credits, antigravity `activeIndex`, meta key-endpoint percent). Every one of them inherits the flaw.

## Reproduced consequences (probe, payload-shaped)

- `parseCommandCodeCredits({ credits: { monthlyCredits: "" } })` → monthly window **`usedPercent: 100`, label "10 / 10"** — an empty field reports the Command Code monthly pool **fully exhausted**. Quota-aware routing and the `opencode quota` display both reason from this.
- `parseOpenCodeGoUsage({ usage: { rolling: { percent: "", resetsAt: 1893456000 } } })` → a kept `5h` window with **`usedPercent: 0`** — an empty field reports a pool **completely untouched** (false headroom, the opposite error).
- Same shape elsewhere by construction: codex `credits.balance: ""` → a real $0 balance; opencode-go `expires: ""` → expiry 0 (1970).

Providers do emit empty strings for unset fields (that is why sibling helpers exist: `asNonEmptyString` in the same file treats `""`/blank as absent, and cline-pass's caller already guards its percent through it). `toNumber` is the one parser that does not.

## The duplicate

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/meta.ts:73-77` carries a local `num` helper with the identical `Number(value)` body and the identical flaw: `window_weighted_used: ""` parses to 0 and passes `parseSubscriptionQuota`'s null gate (:84-89), minting windows from empty fields. One fix should land in the shared helper and the duplicate should delegate to it.

## Why it matters

These numbers feed the quota display and quota-aware routing (#587/#566 consumers): a false 100% steers sessions away from a live pool; a false 0% steers them into a walled one. Both errors are silent — the window looks well-formed either way. The fix is one guard in one shared function, plus pinning tests in the pattern #1722/#1725 established.

Out of scope (checked, already safe): groq's `headerNumber` (groq.ts:55-59 guards `!raw` first; its regex parser cannot match an empty capture), cline-pass's percent (goes through `asNonEmptyString` first).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `toNumber` returns `null` for empty and whitespace-only strings (and still parses `"12"`, `" 12 "`, numeric strings with signs/decimals as before).
- [ ] meta.ts's local `num` delegates to the shared `toNumber` (or is otherwise fixed identically) — no second copy of the flaw.
- [ ] Tests in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` (or a wired sibling) pin: `toNumber("")`/`toNumber(" ")` → null; `parseCommandCodeCredits` with `monthlyCredits: ""` produces no monthly window; `parseOpenCodeGoUsage` with `percent: ""` produces no window for that field.
- [ ] Existing quota tests still pass under the ai package test command; ai typecheck clean.

# fix(ai): DeepSeek models behind multi-family gateways get the wrong max-tokens field and a `store` flag — #1731's family classifier omits deepseek

Follow-up to #1706 (closed by PR #1731). #1706's own survey named DeepSeek as one of the families fronted by the multi-family gateways (cline-pass, opendesign, opencode-go), but the family classifier PR #1731 added covers only GLM / Kimi / Gemini, so DeepSeek models behind those gateways still get the generic defaults instead of the direct-DeepSeek decisions.

## Evidence (main 736273ebe5, PR #1731 merge)

`packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts`:

- `detectModelFamily` (:696-704) — `type ModelFamily = "glm" | "kimi" | "gemini"`; no deepseek.
- `detectMaxTokensField` (:710-717) — family glm/kimi short-circuit to `max_tokens`; DeepSeek reaches `max_tokens` only via `p === "deepseek"` or a `deepseek.com` baseURL, neither of which holds behind a gateway. The function's own comment (:706-709) states DeepSeek "still require[s] `max_tokens`".
- `detectSupportsStore` (:747-764) — the direct-DeepSeek case is in the non-standard set (`isDeepSeek`, :764) so direct requests omit `store`; the family short-circuit (:751) covers only the three recognized families, so a gateway DeepSeek model gets `supportsStore = true`.
- Precedent in the same file: `requireReasoning` (:571-575) already detects DeepSeek by model id (`modelID.includes("deepseek")`), because the direct/gateway distinction was already known to matter there.

## Reproduction (laptop probe, this run)

Probe test through the same `compileRequest` harness PR #1731's tests use (`packages/ai/test/provider/openai-chat.test.ts`), comparing the direct `deepseek` provider (`https://api.deepseek.com/v1`) against cline-pass / opendesign / opencode-go (gateway baseURL), generation `maxTokens: 20`, one tool:

| model id | direct deepseek | behind each of the 3 gateways |
|---|---|---|
| `deepseek-chat` | `max_tokens`, no `store` | `max_completion_tokens`, `store` present |
| `deepseek/deepseek-chat` | `max_tokens`, no `store` | `max_completion_tokens`, `store` present |
| `deepseek-v3.2` | `max_tokens`, no `store` | `max_completion_tokens`, `store` present |
| `deepseek-reasoner` | `max_tokens`, no `store` | `max_completion_tokens`, `store` present |

All 12 gateway combinations diverge from direct on both fields; `strict` already matches (true both ways).

## Why it matters

A DeepSeek model seated behind opencode-go / cline-pass / opendesign is sent `max_completion_tokens` — the field the codebase itself says DeepSeek does not use in place of `max_tokens` — so the caller's token cap can be silently ignored or rejected upstream, and it carries a `store` flag the direct route deliberately withholds from a non-standard endpoint. This is exactly the #1706 failure mode ("the same model gets different wire behavior depending on which door it entered through"), left for one of the families #1706 enumerated.

## Acceptance criteria

- `detectModelFamily` recognizes DeepSeek model ids with the same anchoring discipline as the existing families (whole id segment: start of id or the segment after a `/` vendor prefix; case-insensitive; ids merely embedding the name inside a larger segment, e.g. `not-deepseek-chat`, are not the family).
- Behind cline-pass / opendesign / opencode-go, DeepSeek ids compile to the direct-DeepSeek body for the affected fields: `max_tokens`, no `store`; explicit `compatibility` overrides still win, including explicit values that contradict the family default.
- Regression tests extend PR #1731's gateway-parity test in `packages/ai/test/provider/openai-chat.test.ts` with DeepSeek ids (bare, vendor-prefixed, versioned, reasoner) asserting gateway bodies equal the direct body on the pinned fields.
- No behavior change for the direct `deepseek` provider or for non-DeepSeek models behind gateways (existing openai-chat / openai-compatible-chat suites green).

# fix(cli): `opencode quota <valid> <unknown>` discards the valid providers' results — one bad name returns before anything is rendered

Found by reading on main `255fa099f2` (laptop primary, 2026-11-05). Quota subcommand surface (#1718 / PRs #1722, #1728); distinct from #1729 (timeout/omission under load) and #1733 (config-facts discovery scope).

## Evidence

`packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/quota.ts:371-389` (handler, named-provider branch):

```ts
for (const name of requested) {
  const resolved = resolveQuotaProviderName(ctx, name)
  if (!resolved) {
    process.stderr.write(`Unknown provider: ${name}${EOL}`)
    process.exitCode = 1
    return                       // ← discards everything fetched so far
  }
  if (groups.some((group) => group.providerId === resolved)) continue
  const results = yield* Effect.promise(() => fetchProviderWithTimeout(ctx, resolved))
  groups.push({ providerId: resolved, results })
}
// rendering happens only after the loop (:385-389) — never reached on the return above
```

## Observed behavior (by construction)

- `opencode quota claude bogus`: claude is fetched (a real provider call, up to the 30s budget), then `bogus` fails resolution and the handler returns — claude's results are **never printed**, in text or `--json` mode. Names after the bad one are never resolved or fetched either.
- In `--json` mode stdout is left completely empty: a machine consumer gets no parseable output at all, only a stderr line and exit 1 — for a typo in one name out of several. This is the subcommand the fleet quota gatherer drives (developing-today/code#6125); #1729's contract for this surface is "a result or an error result, never silence" — a mixed valid/invalid invocation currently produces silence for the valid half.

Exit code 1 for an unknown name is correct and should stay; discarding the successfully fetched groups is the defect.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A mixed invocation renders every resolvable provider's results (text and `--json`), reports each unknown name on stderr, and exits 1 — no fetched group is discarded, and names after an unknown one are still processed.
- [ ] An invocation with only unknown names keeps today's shape: stderr line(s), no stdout results, exit 1.
- [ ] A regression test covers the mixed case (e.g. one resolvable + one unknown name yields the resolvable provider's rows on stdout, the unknown name on stderr, exit code 1).
- [ ] The all-valid and no-argument paths are unchanged; existing quota tests stay green.

# fix(cli): `opencode quota` config-facts read never walks ancestors or the system directory — disabled/instance facts diverge from the runtime's merged config

Found by reading on main `255fa099f2` (laptop primary, 2026-11-05). Follow-up surface of the quota subcommand (#1718 / PRs #1722, #1728); distinct from #1729 (timeout/omission/discovery-cost) and #1730 (docs).

## Evidence

The quota handler assembles its `QuotaContext` config facts with its own hand-rolled candidate list — `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/quota.ts:180-188` (`readConfigFacts`, consumed at `:254` by `buildQuotaContext`):

```ts
addCandidates(global.config)
if (process.env.OPENCODE_CONFIG) files.push(process.env.OPENCODE_CONFIG)
addCandidates(process.cwd())
addCandidates(join(process.cwd(), ".opencode"))
```

That is the whole discovery: the global config dir, `$OPENCODE_CONFIG`, the current directory, and `cwd/.opencode`. The two facts it extracts — `disabled_providers` and provider instances (`instanceOf`, `handlers/quota.ts:190-230`) — therefore only ever come from those four locations.

The runtime's merged config for the same directory is built by `ConfigDiscovery` (`packages/core/src/config/discovery.ts:59-105`), which:

- includes the **platform system directory** (`/etc/opencode`, `%ProgramData%\opencode`, `/Library/Application Support/opencode` — `discovery.ts:28-33`, `:71`) ahead of the global directory, and core loads those managed settings **last so they override everything** (`packages/core/src/config.ts:287-292`);
- **walks up from the location directory** (`fs.up`, `discovery.ts:80`), collecting `opencode.json`/`opencode.jsonc` and `.opencode` directories from **every ancestor**, and loads all discovered project roots (`config.ts:314-317`).

The quota handler never opens any of those files.

## Observed divergence (by construction, from the two code paths)

- Run `opencode quota` from a **subdirectory** of a project (e.g. `packages/app/` under a repo whose root `opencode.jsonc` disables a provider or defines a provider instance): the runtime honours the root config; the quota listing does not — it fetches a provider the runtime has disabled, and provider instances defined at the root never appear as instance rows.
- A `disabled_providers` entry that exists **only in the system directory** (managed/managed-settings config) is invisible to the quota subcommand even though it outranks every other layer at runtime.

This is the standalone/no-server path's only source of config facts (credentials fall back to the local store in the same handler), so there is no second source that corrects it.

## Why it matters

`opencode quota` is the fork's single source for quota info (developing-today/code#6125); the fleet's quota gatherer and Drew's own checks run it from varying working directories. A listing whose disabled/instance facts silently depend on which directory it was launched from contradicts the runtime it reports on: disabled providers get probed (wasted calls against walled pools), and instance rows vanish — the same "provider vanished" failure shape #1729's contract exists to prevent, from a different cause.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `opencode quota`'s config facts match the runtime's merged config for the invocation directory: ancestor project configs (walking up, with a bound comparable to core discovery — do not reintroduce the unbounded-discovery cost profiled in #1729 defect 3) and the system config directory are read, or the handler reuses `ConfigDiscovery` / the core config entries instead of its own candidate list.
- [ ] A regression test pins it: with `disabled_providers` and an `instanceOf` instance defined only in a parent directory's config, a quota context built from a child directory reports the provider disabled and the instance present; same for a system-directory-only disable.
- [ ] Behaviour from the repo root and from the global-config-only case is unchanged (existing quota tests stay green).
- [ ] The fix states explicitly how it interacts with #1729 defect 3 (bounded discovery when `OPENCODE_CONFIG_PATH` is unset): the walk is bounded and a slow/absent layer degrades to a result, never a hang.

## Finding

PR #1559 (native in-process embeddings backend, step 2 of #1554) recorded a loader-path requirement and made it a precondition for the step-3 flip:

> The native bindings this loads (onnxruntime-node's `.node`, and sharp's, which transformers loads transitively) need **libstdc++ (`libstdc++.so.6`) and zlib (`libz.so.1`) on the process loader path**. … **The packaged server's nix closure must provide libstdc++/libz on the loader path before step 3 flips the registration to native.**

Step 3 has now flipped the registration (PR #1690, merged 2026-11-05), but the packaged nix closure still does not provide either library, and no open issue tracks this packaging item (#1689 step 4 covers sidecar retirement / HTTP-path removal / docs only).

## Evidence (verified on current main `13ab3dc5c2d51fa35ff0273e18f5ef647eca83db`, 2026-11-05)

- `packages/core/src/embeddings.ts` (~line 132): `EMBEDDING_MODELS[0]` registration is `backend: { kind: "native-onnx", snapshotEnv: "LOCAL_EMBED_SNAPSHOT", … }` — the native backend is now the default for the local model.
- `packages/core/src/embeddings-native.ts` header (Packaging note) still states in the present tense: "the packaged server's nix closure must provide them" (libstdc++ / libz).
- `nix/opencode.nix:99`: the packaged binary's wrapper sets `--prefix LD_LIBRARY_PATH : ${lib.makeLibraryPath [ wayland ]}` on Linux — wayland only; no `stdenv.cc.cc.lib` (libstdc++), no `zlib`.
- `flake.nix` (~line 87): `stdenv.cc.cc.lib` appears only in the **devShell** `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (for @parcel/watcher) — that does not reach the packaged server. No nix file under `nix/` mentions libstdc++, zlib, or onnx.
- PR #1690's verification was a laptop dev-shell run ("`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` per embeddings-native.ts header") with the sidecar stopped — the packaged binary was not exercised. In a bare environment the failure mode per #1559 is loud but total for embeddings: `Embeddings.UnavailableError: libstdc++.so.6: cannot open shared object file`.

Source PRs: #1559 (merge `adc454beeb`, the finding) and #1690 (the flip). This is a pr-diff-review finding from reviewing #1559's diff/body against current main.

## Why it matters

The default embeddings registration now depends on native bindings whose loader requirements the shipped package does not satisfy. Anyone running the packaged `opencode` (the nix build is the fleet's deployment route) risks embeddings failing on first use — after the :18752 sidecar is retired in step 4 (#1689), there will be no fallback path left.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The packaged nix build (`nix/opencode.nix`) is exercised end-to-end for embeddings: the built `opencode` binary answers an embeddings round-trip (index + query) with the model snapshot present, with no dev-shell `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and no :18752 sidecar running — OR the failure is reproduced and recorded here.
- [ ] If it fails: the wrapper/closure provides libstdc++ (`stdenv.cc.cc.lib`) and zlib on the loader path (e.g. added to the `wrapProgram` `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` in `nix/opencode.nix`), and the round-trip above passes with the built binary.
- [ ] The packaging note in `packages/core/src/embeddings-native.ts` is updated to match the resolved state.

title: Switchboard slice: embedded Vibe route registered disabled-by-default beside vibe-direct; parity acceptance + cutover criteria
body:
Part of the Vibe-embedding epic (ACP-hosted `vibe-acp`). Depends on the runtime, permission-bridge, auth, and usage children.

## Scope — production-shaped slice, switchboard rules

- Register the embedded Vibe route in the deployed config (developing-today/code `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`) **alongside** `vibe-direct`, following the provider switchboard rule: definitions are never deleted; enablement is a flag (`disabled_providers`). The embedded route ships **disabled by default**.
- `vibe-direct` stays the live route until cutover criteria are met. Nothing about tonight's working route changes in this slice.

## Parity acceptance (before any enablement)

- A fixed battery of representative prompts (plain chat, file-read reasoning, bash tool use, multi-turn continuation, a denied-permission case) runs through **both** routes; transcripts + usage compared. Embedded route must show: same model identity (`mistral-vibe-cli-latest` family), tool calls actually executed by the real agent, usage attributed (see usage child), no capability the shim has that the embedded route lacks (and the reverse noted — embedded gains the agent's own tools/skills/subagents by construction).
- Failure behavior: `vibe-acp` process death mid-turn surfaces as a session error, not a hang (the standing lesson from provider stalls).

## Cutover criteria (Drew's word required)

1. Parity battery green.
2. Usage reconciliation green for a mixed-traffic day (usage child acceptance).
3. Auth acceptance green (keyring-only path, rotation proven).
4. Then: enable embedded as the first leg of the mistral route, shim demoted to fallback — one flag flip, reversible.
5. Shim retirement is a separate later decision after a clean burn period; its definition stays in the tree per switchboard rules until Drew orders removal.

title: Embedded Vibe usage attribution: ACP usage → quota gatherer with call_source=vibe_code parity

## Scope

- ACP gives usage in two places (observed 2026-11-05): the `session/prompt` response (`usage: {totalTokens, inputTokens, outputTokens, cachedReadTokens}` — spike turn: 16,864 total) and streaming `session/update` `usage_update` notifications (`used`/`size` context window + `_meta` steps, prompt/completion/cached tokens).

Adjacent: developing-today-forks/openchamber#1630 (browser-derived usage figures) and developing-today/code#6087 (aggregator display exemption).

title: Embedded Vibe auth: keyring credential (ai.mistral.vibe) lifecycle + refresh for the hosted process — no browser cookies
body:
Part of the Vibe-embedding epic (ACP-hosted `vibe-acp`).

## Rule (Drew, standing, 2026-11-05)

No provider may depend on a non-renewing browser cookie. Anything browser-born must have auto-renew built in (auto-renewing cookie or long-lived token with its own refresh). The embedded Vibe path must ride the **keyring/OAuth credential with its own refresh** — never the Mistral console session.

## Current facts

- The credential lives in the OS keyring as service `ai.mistral.vibe` (username `MISTRAL_API_KEY`), landed by the one-time `vibe --setup` sign-in (2026-11-04). The `vibe-direct` shim already resolves it via the binary's own order (config → env → `~/.vibe/.env` → keyring).
- ACP `initialize` advertises one auth method: `browser-auth` ("Sign in through Mistral AI Studio"). With the keyring credential present, the 2026-11-05 spike needed **no** `authenticate` call — `session/new` and the turn just worked.
- Mistral docs: "Vibe stores the key in your OS keyring, or in `~/.vibe/.env` when no keyring is available, and reuses it across sessions." (https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/use-vibe-in-other-ides)

## Scope

- The hosted `vibe-acp` process resolves the same keyring credential (same user/session context — keyring access needs the user session bus; the service/supervision design must guarantee it, as tonight's runs did via the laptop user session).
- Detect credential expiry/revocation from ACP errors and surface it as a named, actionable state (re-run of the one-time sign-in), never as a silent provider failure or a fallback to console cookies.
- Prove rotation: replace the keyring entry (the RustDesk-drift lesson — stored credentials drift) and show the hosted process picks up the new value without code or config changes.

## Acceptance

- Embedded turns succeed with only the keyring credential present (no browser session, no console cookies anywhere in the path — verified by running with the browser closed/logged out of the console).
- A deliberately invalidated keyring entry produces the named re-auth state in the UI/logs, and restoring a valid entry recovers without restart of anything else.

title: ACP permission + mode bridge: request_permission → fork approvals; ask/accept-edits/auto-approve + model/effort config options
body:
Part of the Vibe-embedding epic (ACP-hosted `vibe-acp`).

## Scope

Bridge ACP's host-delegated control surface into the fork's own UX and policy:

- `session/request_permission`: when the agent asks, surface the tool call + its options (`allow_once`, `allow_always`, `reject_once`, `reject_always` as offered) through the fork's approval flow; return the user's selection as the outcome. Timeouts/cancel must resolve as rejection, never silent approval.
- Session modes as first-class session config: `ask` (approval for tool executions), `accept-edits` (auto-approve file edits only — the agent's default), `auto-approve` (approve everything). Expose via `session/set_mode` and/or the `mode` config option the agent advertises in `session/new`.
- Model + effort config options: surface the agent's `model` select (tonight: `mistral-medium-3.5`, alias `mistral-vibe-cli-latest`) and reasoning-effort select (`off`/`high` observed) as settable session options, mapped to the fork's variant system.

## Open verification from the spike

The 2026-11-05 spike turn ran under the default `accept-edits` mode and its bash call executed with **zero** permission requests — expected for edits, but the bash-under-accept-edits behavior needs a pinned answer: run the same turn in `ask` mode and prove the `session/request_permission` round-trip fires and is honored (deny path included: a rejected command must not execute).

## Acceptance

- In `ask` mode, a bash tool call produces exactly one permission request; allow → executes; deny → does not execute and the agent is told.
- Switching mode/model/effort mid-session takes effect on the next turn and is reflected in the session record.

title: ACP client runtime: host vibe-acp from the fork (lifecycle, streaming, session mapping)
body:
Part of the Vibe-embedding epic (ACP-hosted `vibe-acp` as successor to the `vibe-direct` wire emulation).

## Scope

Build the fork's ACP client runtime for `vibe-acp`:

- Spawn and supervise the `vibe-acp` process (stdio, JSON-RPC 2.0, ACP protocol v1) per host/workspace, with lifecycle management (start on demand, reap on idle/exit, restart on crash with session state preserved by the agent under `~/.vibe`).
- Implement the client side of: `initialize`, `session/new`, `session/prompt`, `session/cancel`, `session/load` (agent advertises `loadSession: true`), `session/list` / `session/fork` / `session/close`.
- Map fork sessions ↔ ACP sessions 1:1; stream `session/update` notifications (agent message/thought chunks, tool calls and their updates) into the fork's session event model.
- Prompt capabilities the agent advertises: text, image, embeddedContext.

## Spike proof this builds on

2026-11-05, laptop amd-6: a 211-line stdlib Python host drove a real turn end-to-end (session `48475654-f48c-f816-04aa-56fd06364bd4`, tool call executed, usage in the prompt response). Artifacts: `~/work/spikes/vibe-acp-embed-2026-11-05/` on the laptop.

## Acceptance

- A fork session can be created against the runtime and driven through a multi-step tool-using turn with streaming output visible in the fork, indistinguishable in shape from a native provider session.
- Killing the `vibe-acp` process mid-session and restarting it loses no conversation state (session/load resumes).
- Runtime never touches the `vibe-direct` path; both coexist.

title: Epic: embed Mistral Vibe as a hosted ACP agent (vibe-acp) — successor to the vibe-direct wire emulation
body:
## Direction

Drew (2026-11-05): "eventually vibe direct needs to be embedded per that project" — Vibe's end state in our stack is **embedded the way Mistral's own project intends**: the real `vibe` agent hosted by the fork, not wire-emulated by it.

## Current state — the shim

`vibe-direct` today is a wire-protocol provider in `packages/ai` (`packages/ai/src/providers/vibe.ts` + `vibe-auth.ts`, landed in #1653):

- Reuses the MistralChat route against `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` (the same wire the binary uses), rebranded to provider id `vibe`, with Vibe's model presets and request defaults (temperature 1.0, reasoning_effort "high").
- Stamps requests with the binary's attribution (`metadata.call_source = "vibe_code"`).
- Resolves the credential the way the binary does: config → env `MISTRAL_API_KEY` → `~/.vibe/.env` → OS keyring (service `ai.mistral.vibe`).
- The #1653 commit says it plainly: **"No vibe subprocess, no ACP host."** It emulates the binary's requests; the binary's agent (tools, skills, subagents, session semantics) is not in the loop.

Deployed route (developing-today/code `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`): model `mistral-vibe-cli-latest`, providers `["vibe-direct", "mistral"]`, vibe-direct attempted first.

## Vibe's intended embedding surface (primary sources)

Mistral documents ACP as the embedding path:

- "Vibe implements the **Agent Client Protocol (ACP)** and is published in the ACP registry… If your client has no agent registry, install the CLI and point the client at the `vibe-acp` command it installs." — https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/use-vibe-in-other-ides
- "One agent, three surfaces… They share the same engine, configuration, and customization layer (agents, skills, MCP servers)" + ACP for other clients — https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/choose-cli-vscode-web-sessions
- ACP registry id: `mistral-vibe`; ACP command: `vibe-acp`.

Installed on the laptop (vibe 3.1.0, verified 2026-11-05): three entrypoints —

- `vibe` — interactive CLI + headless programmatic mode (`-p/--prompt`, `--output json|streaming`, `--output-dir` writes `export.json` with token usage/cost).
- `vibe-acp` — "Run Mistral Vibe in ACP mode": JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, protocol v1.
- `vibe-app-server` — an app-server surface ("Unified Harness connections", `--multiplex`) — noted for the design record; ACP is the documented, registry-published path and the one this epic builds on.

What the host provides over ACP (observed live, see spike): the client spawns `vibe-acp`, drives `initialize` → `session/new` → `session/prompt`; the agent streams `session/update` (message chunks, tool calls, usage updates), delegates approvals back via `session/request_permission`, and exposes session modes (`ask` / `accept-edits` / `auto-approve`) and config options (model, reasoning effort) for the host to present and set. Session state (journal, resume) stays the agent's, under `~/.vibe`.

## Spike result (2026-11-05, laptop amd-6) — PROVEN

A minimal ACP host (211-line Python client, stdlib only) drove **one real end-to-end turn** through `vibe-acp` on the Vibe plan credential:

- `initialize` → protocolVersion 1, agent `@mistralai/mistral-vibe` 3.1.0; capabilities: loadSession, prompt image + embeddedContext, session list/fork/close. No `authenticate` call needed — the keyring credential was already live.
- `session/new` → session `48475654-f48c-f816-04aa-56fd06364bd4`; model config option `mistral-medium-3.5` (the model behind alias `mistral-vibe-cli-latest`), effort `high`, default mode `accept-edits`.
- `session/prompt` (instructed to run `echo VIBE-EMBED-SPIKE-OK` via its bash tool) → tool call `bash: echo VIBE-EMBED-SPIKE-OK`, reply exactly `MARKER=VIBE-EMBED-SPIKE-OK`, `stopReason: end_turn`, **usage: 16,864 total tokens (16,643 in / 221 out, 3,072 cached read)** in the prompt response, plus streaming `usage_update` notifications.
- Artifacts on the laptop: `~/work/spikes/vibe-acp-embed-2026-11-05/` (`acp_client.py`, `transcript.jsonl`, `summary.json`, `run.log`).

The embedded contract works tonight, unmodified, on the plan credential — no console cookies involved.

## Target architecture

The fork hosts `vibe-acp` as an embedded agent runtime: a session in the fork maps to an ACP session in a supervised `vibe-acp` process; prompts/streaming/tool calls flow over ACP; host approvals answer `session/request_permission`; modes + model/effort surface as session config; usage lands in the quota pipeline with `call_source=vibe_code` parity. The embedded route registers switchboard-style beside `vibe-direct` (definition present, enablement a flag) and the shim retires only after parity acceptance.

**Auth rule (Drew, standing):** the embedded path rides the keyring/OAuth credential with its own refresh — never a browser console cookie. Anything browser-born in any provider must have auto-renew built in; Vibe's keyring credential already satisfies this and the design must keep it that way.

## Children

- [ ] ACP client runtime: host `vibe-acp` (lifecycle, streaming, session mapping)
- [ ] Permission + mode bridge (`session/request_permission` → fork approvals; modes/model/effort config options)
- [ ] Embedded auth: keyring credential lifecycle + refresh for the hosted process
- [ ] Usage attribution: ACP usage → quota gatherer, `vibe_code` parity (adjacent: developing-today-forks/openchamber#1630)
- [ ] Switchboard slice: embedded route disabled-by-default beside `vibe-direct`; parity acceptance + cutover criteria

Design note: `~/workspace/scratch/vibe-embed-2026-11-05/design.md` (fleet scratch, 2026-11-05).

body:
# Multi-family gateways (cline-pass, opendesign, opencode-go) get zero per-family tool adaptation — detectors key on provider id/baseURL, not the model family

From the 2026-11-05 tool-call audit (`~/workspace/scratch/toolcall-audit-2026-11-04/code-inventory.md` §7A, §12–§14).

cline-pass, opendesign, and opencode-go are all multi-family gateways: one provider id fronts GLM, Kimi, DeepSeek, MiniMax, Claude, Gemini and more. But every dialect adaptation in the fork's OpenAI Chat protocol is keyed on **provider id or baseURL**, so behind a gateway none of it fires:

- ZAI `tool_stream:true` is added only when the provider/baseURL looks like ZAI (`detectZaiToolStream`, openai-chat.ts) — GLM models reached via `cline-pass` / `opendesign` / `opencode-go` never get it.
- Gemini thought-signature custody (`extra_content.google.thought_signature` decode + replay in openai-chat.ts) depends on the gateway forwarding `extra_content` verbatim — nothing verifies or repairs this per gateway.
- Moonshot/Kimi reasoning-details handling and strict-mode detection (`detectSupportsStrictMode`) take generic defaults for these ids; `strict:false` is sent to gateways that forward to strict validators.
- Parallel-call recovery in the chat protocol is heuristic (index → id → batch position → latest). If a gateway strips both `index` and `id` on later parallel deltas, arguments can concatenate onto the wrong call. No fixture pins any of these gateways' actual delta shapes.
- opencode-go compounds it: its dialect is **catalog data** (per-model pinned `api` URL + package from models.dev). A catalog refresh can flip a model's dialect (chat ↔ messages ↔ responses) with no code review, silently changing its tool-call handling.

## Ask

1. Key the compatibility detectors on the **model family** (model id) as well as provider/baseURL, so GLM/Kimi/Gemini models get their adaptations behind any gateway.
2. Recorded-fixture tests for the seated models behind each gateway (delta shapes, parallel calls, signature forwarding), so gateway behavior changes are caught as test failures instead of session failures.
3. For opencode-go: a pinned expectation per seated Go model (package + api family) asserted in tests, so a catalog refresh that changes a dialect shows up as a deliberate diff.

# opencode-route: mid-session leaf switching is dialect-unsafe for Gemini-family leaves (thought signatures strand)

From the 2026-11-05 tool-call audit (`~/workspace/scratch/toolcall-audit-2026-11-04/code-inventory.md` §10 + §3).

The façade has no wire of its own: each step resolves one leaf and the leaf's protocol lowers the request; if a later step (retry, hedge, cooldown failover) resolves to a **different leaf**, the whole history — including tool calls minted under the previous leaf — is re-lowered by the new leaf's protocol. `providerMetadata` is namespaced by the originating provider key, so dialect attachments do not transfer:

- Tool calls minted by a chat-protocol leaf carry no `antigravity` thought signature. When an Antigravity leaf later replays that history, its replay path falls back to Google's `skip_thought_signature_validator` sentinel **for the first unsigned call only**; subsequent unsigned (e.g. parallel) calls get nothing — Gemini 3 may reject the replay with a 400.
- The reverse directions degrade silently rather than failing: Gemini-via-OpenAI `extra_content` signatures are invisible to the Antigravity leaf; Responses `itemId`s are dropped by chat leaves; Mistral's 9-char hashed ids re-hash idempotently.

The resolver gates target selection on quota/context/health only — never on "this leaf can faithfully replay the session's existing tool history" (§10-G2).

## Ask

- Prefer stickiness for sessions whose history contains signature-bearing (or signature-needing) tool calls: once a session has Gemini-family tool history, keep it on a Gemini-family leaf unless that leaf is walled/down (session affinity exists in the resolver — extend its keying to dialect custody).
- Or synthesize/preserve signatures at the route layer so custody survives a switch.
- Add a route-level test: session with parallel tool calls minted on a chat leaf, next step forced to antigravity-direct, replays without a signature 400. (Today there is no route-level tool-call test at all — tool behavior is tested per-protocol only.)

# antigravity-direct: every prompt 404s NOT_FOUND (gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-3-flash) — provider down for plain prompts

Found live by the 2026-11-05 tool-call audit against the laptop standing server (build v2.0.30+7774bf0, which includes the #1550 fix commits b6cde1778f / d896d82157 / 2249412cea).

Every prompt to `antigravity-direct` models `gemini-2.5-flash` and `gemini-3-flash` (both from the provider's own served catalog) failed identically, streaming and non-streaming:

```
provider.invalid-request, HTTP 404
{"error":{"code":404,"message":"Requested entity was not found.","status":"NOT_FOUND"}}
```

Auth was accepted (not 401, not quota) — the request reaches the v1internal endpoint and something in it names an entity that does not exist: wire model-id construction (`<id>-<effort>`), the `aicode-consumers` project, or a skipped loadCodeAssist/discovery step are the leading suspects; upstream endpoint rotation is also possible. Raw captures: `~/workspace/scratch/toolcall-audit-2026-11-04/live/antigravity-gemini-single.json`, `native-antigravity-single.json`, `native-antigravity-parallel.json`; protocol map in the same dir's `code-inventory.md` §3. Compare against the retired known-good door (`bin/antigravity-direct.mjs` in developing-today/code) and #1550 (the Claude-leaf 400 — possibly a shared root cause in request construction).

A diagnosis + fix lane is running (2026-11-05); this issue is the tracking home. Acceptance: a plain prompt and a tool-call round-trip succeed on a Gemini model through the standing server after the fix deploys, with a fixture test pinning the accepted request shape.

# v2 server does not load `.opencode/tool/*.ts` custom tools at all

Found by the 2026-11-05 tool-call audit (live tests against the laptop standing server, build v2.0.30+7774bf0). Full evidence: `~/workspace/scratch/toolcall-audit-2026-11-04/live-tests.md` + `live/diag*.json` in the same scratch dir.

## What was proven (three independent ways)

1. A custom tool built exactly per the documented pattern (`.opencode/tool/echotest.ts`, `@opencode-ai/plugin` `tool()` helper, project `package.json` pinning the plugin package, placed before first session creation in a fresh project dir) never appears: the code-mode catalog `search({query:"echotest"})` returns 0 items.
2. A direct `tools.echotest({...})` call returns `Unknown tool 'echotest'`.
3. The **production** global tool `session-identity` (`~/.config/opencode/tool/session-identity.ts`) is equally absent from the catalog — this is not a scratch-dir artifact.
4. Re-registering the same tool as a project plugin (`.opencode/plugin/echotest.ts`) also does not surface it.

In this build, all tool use funnels through code mode (`execute` / `mcpx_discover` / `mcpx_project`) plus projected MCP tools (callable as native `<namespace>_<tool>` once projected). If that funnel is the intended v2 end state, the `.opencode/tool` loading path should fail loudly (or the docs/config surface should say it is retired) instead of silently ignoring user tools. If it is a regression, the loader needs restoring.

## Acceptance

- Either: custom tools from `.opencode/tool/*.ts` (project + global config dirs) load and are callable in v2 sessions, with a regression test; or: an explicit design decision recorded here that v2 retires them, plus a startup warning naming each ignored tool file so nothing is dropped silently.
- The production `session-identity` tool is the canary: whichever way this resolves, its absence must stop being silent.

## Problem

`packages/app/e2e/performance/timeline-stability/fixture.test.ts` — the unit test that validates the timeline fixture validators (`validateTimelineMessages`, `validateTimelineEvent` from `packages/app/e2e/utils/timeline`) that every timeline-stability Playwright spec builds its oracle data on — runs in no script and no workflow. It is verified nowhere.

## Evidence (verified on origin/main 7a9e5810a695825ab3f61b4f78590417376631c2, laptop probe worktree, 2026-11-05)

- `fixture.test.ts:1` imports `describe, expect, test` from `bun:test` — it is a Bun unit test, not a Playwright spec.
- `packages/app/e2e/performance/timeline-stability/playwright.config.ts:6` sets `testMatch: "**/*.spec.ts"`, so the suite's own Playwright config deliberately excludes it.
- `packages/app/package.json:21` — the `test` chain (what CI runs via `bun turbo test` in `.github/workflows/test.yml`) is `test:unit && test:browser && test:icons`:
  - `:22` `test:unit` scopes Bun to `./src` — fixture is under `e2e/`.
  - `:23` `test:browser` scopes Bun to `./test-browser`.
  - `:24` `test:icons` names only `./vite.icons.test.ts` (the #1695 fix).
- The two scripts that touch this area still miss it: `:34` `test:stability`'s Bun step names only `./e2e/performance/unit/visual-stability.test.ts`; `:35` `test:bench`'s Bun step names only the `./e2e/performance/unit` directory. Neither `test:stability` nor `test:bench` is referenced by any workflow (grep of `.github/workflows/*.yml` is empty) — and the `e2e/performance/unit` benchmarks being manual is documented intent (`e2e/performance/README.md`), which does not extend to this deterministic fixture-validation unit test.
- Direct run with dependencies installed (Bun 1.4.4): `bun test ./e2e/performance/timeline-stability/fixture.test.ts` → **4 pass / 0 fail, 10 expect() calls, ~660 ms** — the test is sound and fast; it is simply never executed. `bun run test:unit` in the same checkout ran 564 tests across 108 files with zero hits for `fixture.test`.

## Why it matters

The timeline-stability specs assert layout/continuity contracts against fixture timelines. If the fixture builders/validators drift (e.g. a malformed event shape starts passing validation), the specs' oracle data silently degrades and the suite can pass against fixtures that no longer represent real SDK values — the exact failure `fixture.test.ts` exists to catch ("rejects malformed SDK values at runtime"). Same unwired-test class as #1695 (fixed) and #1611 (open, script/ tree).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/app`'s `test` chain (directly or via a named sub-script, following the `test:icons` precedent from #1695) executes `e2e/performance/timeline-stability/fixture.test.ts`.
- [ ] The wired run passes on current main (4 tests).
- [ ] Negative control: deliberately breaking a validator expectation makes the wired run fail.
- [ ] No change to the Playwright `testMatch` (specs only) and no change to the documented manual status of the `e2e/performance/unit` benchmarks.

# fix(ci): packages/app/vite.icons.test.ts runs in no script or workflow — the PWA/channel icon regression net is verified nowhere

Verified on main `77454801fa498e04f0aa00661ff47da8db21a1c7` (2026-11-04, laptop worktree of origin/main).

## Evidence

- `packages/app/vite.icons.test.ts` holds 7 tests ("bundles {dev,beta,prod,local} app icons", "serves {dev,beta,prod} app icons", 142 expect() calls) guarding the channel-specific favicon/PWA icon pipeline in `packages/app/vite.icons.ts` (used by `packages/app/vite.config.ts:5`). The file's history is a chain of icon regressions fixed upstream: channel-specific favicons (#45543), maskable PWA icons (#46434), PWA installability (#53905).
- It is run by nothing:
  - `packages/app/package.json:21` — `"test": "bun run test:unit && bun run test:browser"` is the only test entry point turbo/CI invokes.
  - `packages/app/package.json:22` — `test:unit` runs `bun test … ./src` only (108 test files under `src/`).
  - `packages/app/package.json:23` — `test:browser` runs `bun test … ./test-browser` only (40 files).
  - `packages/app/bunfig.toml:2` — `[test] root = "./src"`, so even a bare `bun test` in the package discovers only `src/`.
  - No workflow in `.github/workflows/` and no package script references `vite.icons.test` (repo-wide grep; the only reference is the `vite.config.ts` import of the non-test module).
- Empirical, this run (laptop worktree at origin/main):
  - `bun run test:unit` in `packages/app`: "Ran 564 tests across 108 files" — exactly the `src/` set; `vite.icons` appears 0 times in the output.
  - `bun test ./vite.icons.test.ts` run directly: **7 pass / 0 fail** — the suite is healthy; only the wiring is missing. A future icon regression (wrong channel asset, missing maskable icon, broken serve path) would merge unnoticed, exactly the failure class #1611 tracks for `script/gate-harness.test.ts`.

## Why it matters

The icons under test are the installed-PWA / browser-tab identity of the web app per release channel. Three separate upstream fixes were needed in this area; the regression net written for them silently stopped counting when the package's test roots were split into `./src` + `./test-browser`, leaving the package-root test file orphaned.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `vite.icons.test.ts` is executed by the package's standard test path (`packages/app` `test` script, and therefore by `bun turbo test` in `.github/workflows/test.yml`, both `--affected` and full runs) or by an explicit step in `test.yml` — following the #1611 wiring precedent.
- [ ] The wiring does not force the file through the `test:unit` Solid/happydom preload conditions it does not need; a dedicated script (e.g. `test:icons`) chained into `test` is acceptable.
- [ ] Verified: the wired command reports the 7 icon tests running (not just passing overall), and a deliberately broken icon asset turns it red.
- [ ] No other package-root test file in `packages/app` remains outside every test script (audit `find packages/app -name '*.test.*'` against the script globs as part of the fix).
