# test(core): variant invariant fails on main — @opencode/ai/providers/vibe spells no reasoning variants (#1653 follow-up)

## Evidence (verified this run at origin/main 2659023e73)

The bundled-package invariant in `packages/core/test/variant.test.ts:520-526` fails on current main:

```
test("spells reasoning variants for every bundled native package", () => {
  const supports: Variant.Support[] = [{ type: "toggle" }, { type: "effort" }, { type: "budget_tokens" }]
  const missing = Array.from(Provider.builtinPackages).filter(
    (packageName) => Variant.resolve(model(packageName, "test-model", 32_000), supports).length === 0,
  )
  expect(missing).toEqual([])
})
```

Solo run on a clean laptop worktree of origin/main (2659023e73636f7e241b12ac78d1a4c97cb93770):

```
$ bun test test/variant.test.ts   # packages/core
18 pass / 1 fail — missing = ["@opencode/ai/providers/vibe"]
```

Full core suite in the same worktree: 8167 pass / 6 fail; the other 5 failures are environment-bound and unrelated (preload `OPENCODE_TEST_HOME` is set by the `packages/core/script/test.ts:42` runner, not by bare `bun test`; the 4 native-embeddings parity tests need the real HF snapshot + `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` — the laptop cache holds a 360K stub snapshot).

## Root cause

- `packages/core/src/provider.ts:133` registers `@opencode/ai/providers/vibe` in `Provider.builtinPackages` (added by 3613696384, PR #1653).
- `Variant.resolve` (`packages/core/src/variant.ts:28-38`) looks the model's package up in the `PROTOCOLS` table (`packages/core/src/variant.ts:624`); there is no vibe entry, so it returns `[]` for every vibe model.
- The vibe provider reuses the MistralChat protocol unchanged (`packages/ai/src/providers/vibe.ts:1-17`: "differs from the plain `mistral` provider only in branding, model presets/defaults, the attribution stamp, and credential resolution"), and its default preset declares `defaults: { reasoningEffort: "high" }` — reasoning effort is a first-class vibe feature. The `mistral` package itself maps to `openaiChat` in the same table (`variant.ts:664`), which spells effort as `settings: { reasoningEffort }`.
- Precedent: #1471 (CLOSED) was this exact class for antigravity; fixed by adding the `PROTOCOLS` entry + a pinning test (6dac29ea53, PR #1483).

## Why it matters

Vibe models expose no reasoning variants at all: users cannot select or change reasoning effort for vibe models in the picker/TUI even though the provider's own default preset is built around `reasoningEffort: "high"`, and the core invariant that guards every bundled package stays red on main.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Variant.resolve` returns the Mistral-parity effort variants for `@opencode/ai/providers/vibe` models (same spelling as the `mistral` package, which shares the MistralChat protocol), or a dedicated vibe protocol spelling with a stated reason it must differ.
- [ ] A pinning test mirroring "spells Antigravity variants as thinking levels" covers the vibe package's spelled variants.
- [ ] `bun test test/variant.test.ts` in packages/core is fully green, including the bundled-package invariant.
- [ ] No behavior change for any other package's variants.

# fix(ci): bounded-http + numeric gates red on main — the #1098 and #1646 fixes landed without gate dispositions (openapi.json.ts, services/files)

## Summary

Verified on `origin/main` `b6481d9b18227e4ba242023691cd4df3a00fca35` (laptop archive probe, gates run with `bun run check:*`; sites re-verified by `gh api` raw reads at the same SHA): `check:bounded-http` and `check:numeric-boundaries` each exit 1 with NEW findings no open issue lists, all introduced by the 2026-11-05T01:55Z merge batch — PR #1608 (fixing #1098, bounded openapi.json route) and PR #1649 (fixing #1646, files worker Range handling + its first tests). `check:workflows`, `check:gates`, and `check:proto-reads` are GREEN at the same SHA. Closed #1540 covered this class for different sites; its sites do not appear in the current output.

## Evidence

`check:bounded-http` at `b6481d9b18` — 9 unlisted candidates + 2 stale entries, nothing else:

- `packages/console/app/src/routes/openapi.json.ts:12` — `const response = await fetch(OPENAPI_URL, { signal })` (the #1098 fix's new fetch line), plus BOTH stale entries for this file (the old `const response = await fetch(` and `const json = await response.json()` lines no longer exist).
- `services/files/src/index.test.ts:41,47,54,61,73,80,87,93` — the new test file from PR #1649: the `worker.fetch(...)` helper call (:41) and `await response.text()` assertions on its in-process responses.

`check:numeric-boundaries` at `b6481d9b18` — 3 unlisted candidates + 2 stale entries, nothing else:

- `packages/console/app/src/routes/openapi.json.ts:26` — `const declared = Number(response.headers.get("content-length"))` (the #1098 fix's cap pre-check).
- `services/files/src/index.ts:110` and `:111` — `Number(bytes[1])` / `Number(bytes[2])` (PR #1649's rewritten Range parse), plus BOTH stale entries for this file (the old `const offset = bytes[1] ? Number(bytes[1]) …` and `const end = bytes[1] && bytes[2] ? …` lines were replaced by :121-122, which use the already-parsed `first`/`last`).

Every site is safe by construction — no behavior change is needed, only dispositions:

- openapi.json.ts: the fetch carries `AbortSignal.timeout(OPENAPI_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 8_000)` (:11-12) and the body is read through `readCappedJson`'s capped reader (`OPENAPI_MAX_BYTES = 4 MiB`, :24-58); the `Number(content-length)` at :26 is `Number.isFinite`-guarded (:27) and only compared against that cap.
- files index.ts:110-111: the values come from the `/^bytes=(\d*)-(\d*)$/` regex (:105, digits only) and are clamped against `object.size` before any use (:121-123).
- files index.test.ts: the responses come from the worker's own `fetch` handler driven in-process against a mocked R2 with a 10-byte fixture — there is no network and no unbounded body.

## Why it matters

This is the recurring drift class (#1514, #1540, #1606, #1607, #1655): a correct fix lands, its lines change, and the exact-text allowlists are left with undispositioned candidates plus stale entries, so both gates stay red on main. A red gate is exactly how the next genuine unbounded fetch or bare numeric conversion hides in the noise.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt`: disposition for `openapi.json.ts:12` (deadline + capped reader) and for the `services/files/src/index.test.ts` sites (in-process test responses, mocked R2 fixture); the 2 stale openapi.json.ts entries removed.
- [ ] `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt`: dispositions for `openapi.json.ts:26` (isFinite-guarded, cap comparison only) and `services/files/src/index.ts:110-111` (regex digits only, clamped to object.size); the 2 stale files entries removed.
- [ ] `bun run check:bounded-http` and `bun run check:numeric-boundaries` both exit 0 on main.
- [ ] No behavior change to `openapi.json.ts`, `services/files/src/index.ts`, or its tests.

## Phase 1 of design #1684 — disposition tables + one fidelity corpus for the three schema translators

Design #1684 (doc: `files/designs/opencode-schema-projection-fidelity.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace) states one fidelity contract for the provider tool-schema projections in `packages/ai`: every keyword, in every translator, has exactly one named disposition — **preserved**, **approximated (named, with direction: widening or narrowing)**, or **refused** — and never silent, never inverted, never contradicted. This phase builds the contract's enforcement artifact: the tables and the corpus that asserts them. **No production behaviour changes.**

### Scope

- **Disposition tables** for the three translators, checked in where their tests live (a table fixture/module the corpus consumes — name per repo convention):
  - antigravity `convertSchema`/`convertSchemaNode` (`packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts`),
  - `GeminiJsonSchema.normalize` (`packages/ai/src/protocols/utils/gemini-json-schema.ts`),
  - `ToolSchemaProjection.moonshot` (`packages/ai/src/protocols/utils/tool-schema.ts`).
- Each table covers: every keyword appearing in the repo's built-in tool schemas, plus every keyword shape exercised by the family fixes #1548/#1550/#1556/#1573/#1585/#1667 (boolean subschemas, multi-valued `type`, `allOf`/`not`-only roots, ARRAY without items, mutually recursive `$defs`, draft-04 bounds, draft-07 tuples).
- **One shared corpus** in `packages/ai/test/` (extending or alongside the existing per-translator suites `tool-schema-projection.test.ts`, `gemini-json-schema.test.ts`, `provider/antigravity.test.ts`): every table row runs through its translator and the projected shape is asserted against the table. The oracle is the table itself (the model of each translator's intended semantics) — name it as such in the test file's header comment.
- Rows whose current behaviour is **known-lossy** are recorded in the table as known-lossy and linked: antigravity `const` → #1557 (open), Moonshot `prefixItems` with `items` present → #1574 (open). The corpus asserts the table including those rows' current projected shapes, so each site's fix flips exactly one row to its conforming disposition.
- Approximations that already exist and were probed against live endpoints are recorded as named approximations, not changed: Gemini loop-cut to `{}` (#1585's `cutDefCycles` semantics), antigravity anyOf→oneOf fold for Anthropic targets (#1550), Moonshot `prefixItems` fold when `items` is absent, `objectRoot`'s object-root forcing in `tool-schema.ts`.

### Out of scope

- Any change to translator production code (the #1557/#1574 fixes are those issues' own work, adopted as design #1684 phase 2).
- Built-in-schema meta-validation (#1668, design phase 3, its own lifecycle).
- Other protocol schema paths (bedrock, OpenAI-compatible, gateway sanitizers) — design phase 4, deliberately unfiled.

### Acceptance

- [ ] A disposition table exists for each of the three named translators, covering the keyword set above, with every row one of preserved / approximated-named-with-direction / refused / known-lossy-with-issue-link.
- [ ] The shared corpus runs every table row through its translator and passes on current main, with known-lossy rows asserted as their current (lossy) projections and clearly marked.
- [ ] The corpus fails if a translator's projection for a table keyword changes without the table changing (spot-provable by flipping one row in review).
- [ ] No production files under `packages/ai/src/` change.
- [ ] Existing ai suites still pass: `bun test` for `packages/ai/test/tool-schema-projection.test.ts`, `gemini-json-schema.test.ts`, and `provider/antigravity.test.ts` (via CI per fleet policy).

body:
## Problem

One malformed (or unreadable) custom theme file rejects the **entire** custom-theme discovery — every valid custom theme in every config directory is lost for the session.

`packages/tui/src/theme/discovery.ts:17` (on main `618de2888fcf`):

```ts
result[path.basename(file, ".json")] = JSON.parse(await readFile(file, "utf8")) as unknown
```

There is no per-file error isolation: `readFile` failures and `JSON.parse` failures propagate out of the sequential loops in `discoverThemes` (only the `readdir` at :8-11 is guarded, and only for `ENOENT`).

## Verified reproduction (laptop probe, origin/main 618de2888fcf, run twice with identical results)

Probe importing `discoverThemes` verbatim from the main tree, with two directories each holding one valid theme:

- Control (all valid): resolves `{"good-a":{"source":"a"},"good-b":{"source":"b"}}`
- After adding one file `a/themes/broken.json` containing `{ not json`: **REJECTED** — `SyntaxError: JSON Parse error: Expected '}'` at `discovery.ts:17`. Neither valid theme is returned, including the one in the untouched second directory.

## Why it matters — both callers degrade badly

- Main TUI (`packages/tui/src/context/theme.tsx:160-166`): `syncCustomThemes()` catches the rejection with `.catch(() => setStore("active", "opencode"))` — one bad file not only drops all custom themes, it silently overrides the user's configured theme selection back to the built-in `opencode` theme.
- Mini TUI (`packages/tui/src/mini/theme.ts:312`): `themeSource()` awaits `discoverThemes(...)` with no local guard; the rejection propagates to the caller's fallback, again losing every custom theme (including the requested one, even when the requested theme's own file is perfectly valid).

Custom themes are user-owned files in `themes/` directories (global config + project `.opencode/`); a typo in one JSON file — the most likely state of a theme a user is actively editing — should cost that one theme, not all of them plus the user's selection. Sibling user-state parsers in the same package already isolate per-entry failures (e.g. `parsePromptStash` in `packages/tui/src/prompt/stash.tsx` skips bad lines; `parsePromptInfo` in `history.tsx` validates shape).

## Acceptance criteria

- `discoverThemes` resolves (does not reject) when an individual theme file is malformed JSON or unreadable; that file is skipped and all other valid themes, in all directories, are still returned with the existing directory-precedence behavior intact.
- The skipped file's failure is diagnosable (named in a warning/log or otherwise surfaced — not silently swallowed without trace, if a suitable channel exists in the TUI; at minimum the behavior is pinned by tests).
- New tests in `packages/tui/test/theme.test.ts` next to the existing `discoverThemes` precedence tests (~:126-150): malformed file in the first directory does not lose valid themes from either directory; malformed file that would shadow a valid same-named theme does not take the valid one down with it (decide and pin whether the earlier valid entry survives).
- Existing theme tests pass.

Oracle: the existing `discoverThemes` precedence tests plus per-entry isolation precedent in the sibling TUI parsers (`stash.tsx`/`history.tsx`).

# fix(ai): vibe default model sends both temperature and top_p when the caller sets topP — preset temperature defeats the binary's top_p suppression

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode, 2026-11-04 run. Parent: #1653 (vibe provider, landed via PR #1661 at main 7774bf07e8).

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probe of origin/main 7774bf07e8)

`packages/ai/src/providers/vibe.ts:74-75` documents the binary's rule:

> temperature 1.0 (top_p is then suppressed — Mistral rejects both)

The preset-default logic does not honor that rule when the caller supplies `topP`:

- `vibe.ts` `withPresetDefaults` merges the preset's `temperature: 1.0` UNDER the caller's generation config — it only checks whether the caller set `temperature`, never whether the caller set `topP`.
- `packages/ai/src/protocols/mistral-chat.ts:416` then lowers both fields verbatim: `temperature: request.generation?.temperature, top_p: request.generation?.topP`.

Reproduced on the laptop (probe of origin/main 7774bf07e8, `compileRequest` on `Vibe.configure({ apiKey, generation: { topP: 0.9 } }).model("mistral-vibe-cli-latest")`):

```json
{"model":"mistral-vibe-cli-latest","messages":[...],"stream":true,"temperature":1,"top_p":0.9,"reasoning_effort":"high"}
```

The wire body carries both fields — exactly the combination the file's own comment says Mistral rejects. The existing test (`packages/ai/test/provider/vibe.test.ts:38`, "temperature 1.0, thinking high, no top_p") only covers the no-caller-generation case, so this interaction has no regression net.

## Why it matters

Any caller that configures `topP` for the default Vibe model (a normal generation setting, e.g. from user/session config) gets a request the upstream rejects — the provider's headline default model fails for a configuration the binary itself handles by suppressing top_p. This is the fork's newest provider surface (landed today in PR #1661); the gap is in the seam between preset defaults and caller config.

## Acceptance criteria

- Compiling a request for the default model (`mistral-vibe-cli-latest` or its alias `mistral-medium-3.5`) with a caller-supplied `topP` and no caller-supplied `temperature` produces a body that does NOT carry both `temperature` and `top_p` (the preset temperature yields to the caller's explicit topP, consistent with "preset defaults sit under caller config"; or top_p is suppressed with the precedence documented in code — pick one and document it).
- A regression test in `packages/ai/test/provider/vibe.test.ts` pins the caller-topP case alongside the existing default case.
- Existing vibe tests still pass; plain `mistral` provider behavior is unchanged unless the fix is deliberately placed in the shared MistralChat lowering (if so, say why in the PR).

body:
# fix(ci): main-broken and test.yml still use remote pm-dispatch actions — #1519's staging failure, already observed killing main-broken (#1418)

## Summary

Two workflows still load pm-dispatch actions in the remote form
`uses: developing-today/code/.github/actions/...@main` — the exact form the
fleet already proved dies in "Set up job" and migrated away from in the other
two workflows. One of the two has already failed this way in production.

## Evidence (verified on main `e4abd8c375902c350dcaadfc08abd4d84360029a`, laptop probe grep + `gh api` raw read, two independent reads)

Remote refs still present:

- `.github/workflows/main-broken.yml:187` — `uses: developing-today/code/.github/actions/pm-dispatch-queue@main` ("Queue a new main-broken issue via pm-dispatch")
- `.github/workflows/main-broken.yml:204` — `uses: developing-today/code/.github/actions/pm-dispatch-queue@main` ("Attach a fresh task to the existing main-broken issue via pm-dispatch")
- `.github/workflows/test.yml:527` — `uses: developing-today/code/.github/actions/pm-dispatch-ci-fix@main` (the `ci-fix` job's only step)

The migrated pattern (the fix to mirror):

- `.github/workflows/agents.yml:67-72` checks `developing-today/code` out at
  `.pm-central` (`persist-credentials: false`) and loads
  `./.pm-central/.github/actions/pm-dispatch-task` (:159/:167/:175); its
  comment (:61-65) records why: "the remote form is what fails with the
  `_staging` archive error", and the checkout path matters because
  pm-dispatch-task's nested steps load pm-dispatch-start / pm-dispatch-queue
  from that same `.pm-central` path.
- `.github/workflows/jules-daily-upstream-sync.yml:57-67,128` was migrated the
  same way by PR #1671 for #1519; its comment (:48-56) quotes the failure:
  the runner's action-download staging for that repo fails in "Set up job"
  ("Could not find file .../_staging/code-<sha>/archive"; runs 41629732319,
  41797627927, 41824863958 all died before any step ran).

This is not hypothetical for main-broken: open issue #1418 (main-broken run
41487561227, 2026-11-02) failed in exactly this way — its log excerpt shows
the `watch` job dying in "Set up job" while downloading
`developing-today/code@main`:

```
##[error]Could not find file '/home/runner/work/_actions/_temp_.../_staging/code-5c49f480735ab006b64c675182fb0828645bae2d/archive'.
```

Because action downloads happen at job setup, when staging fails the whole
`watch` job dies before the filing logic runs — main-broken cannot file or
queue its own failure. For test.yml the failure is additionally invisible:
the `ci-fix` step carries `continue-on-error: true`, so a staging death is
masked and the ci-fix dispatch silently never happens.

Post-migration proof the local form loads: #1672's run of the migrated
jules workflow reached the dispatch step itself (failed later on an
unrelated pm-dispatch HTTP 502, tracked there) — the actions loaded fine.

`bun run check:workflows` is green on current main, so no existing gate
rejects the remote form.

## Why it matters

- main-broken is the fleet's failure-filing path for this repo: when it dies
  at setup, main CI failures produce no issue and no queued remediation task
  (that is how #1418's breakage round sat since 2026-11-02).
- test.yml's ci-fix dispatch is the automatic remediation path for every
  other test failure; its staging failure is silent by construction.
- The fix pattern is already proven twice in this same repo (agents.yml,
  jules-daily-upstream-sync.yml via #1671/#1519) — this is the un-migrated
  remainder, not a new design.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.github/workflows/main-broken.yml` loads pm-dispatch-queue from a
      local `.pm-central` checkout of `developing-today/code` (mirroring
      agents.yml:67-72 / jules-daily-upstream-sync.yml:57-62, including
      `persist-credentials: false`), at both current call sites (:187, :204).
- [ ] `.github/workflows/test.yml`'s `ci-fix` job does the same for
      pm-dispatch-ci-fix (:527); first confirm pm-dispatch-ci-fix's nested
      step loading contract (whether it loads sibling actions from the
      checkout path, as pm-dispatch-task does) and use the path it expects.
- [ ] No `uses: developing-today/code/.github/actions/...` remote refs remain
      anywhere under `.github/workflows/` (grep-verifiable).
- [ ] `bun run check:workflows` exits 0; consider extending that gate (or its
      tests) to reject remote pm-dispatch action refs so a future workflow
      cannot reintroduce the form — if the gate change is declined, say why
      on this issue.
- [ ] Cross-link #1418 (the observed main-broken staging death) and #1519
      (the original failure + fix) from the fixing PR.

## Related

- #1519 (closed by PR #1671): the original Daily Upstream Sync staging
  failure and the .pm-central fix pattern.
- #1418 (open): main-broken run killed by this exact staging error.
- #1672 (open, different failure): migrated workflow reaching dispatch —
  proof the local form loads.

The task 9458 triage verdict (2026-11-04, on #1550) audited the in-repo translation layer and found it clean, and recorded the follow-up this issue files: **nobody has ever meta-validated the actual built-in tool schemas** — as translated for Anthropic targets — against the draft 2020-12 meta-schema. Until that test exists, the offender in `tools.5` cannot be named: if a built-in schema is the invalid one, the test names it; if every built-in schema validates, the offender is proven external (MCP/plugin tool) and #1550's remaining step is only the route-ledger payload pull.

## Evidence (origin/main `6a35d3a284`, checked 2026-11-04)

- No such test exists: a grep across `packages/` for a 2020-12 meta-schema validation of tool schemas finds only schema *generation* sites — `packages/core/src/tool/runtime.ts:169-170` emits schemas with `target: "draft-2020-12"` — and a fixture `$schema` string in `packages/ai/test/provider/antigravity.test.ts:44`. Nothing validates the emitted schemas against the meta-schema they claim to target.
- The built-in tool set is enumerable: `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/*.ts` (read, edit, shell, grep, glob, patch, skill, question, subagent, …), each producing its `inputSchema` through `definition()` in `packages/core/src/tool/runtime.ts`; `packages/core/test/tool-schema.test.ts` already tests those definitions shape-by-shape but never meta-validates them.
- Both Anthropic-bound translations are in scope: `packages/ai/src/protocols/anthropic-messages.ts:550` passes `input_schema: tool.inputSchema` verbatim, and the Antigravity protocol's `convertSchema` (`packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts`, `anthropic` flag) re-serializes proto Schemas into Anthropic `input_schema`s for Claude leaves — the exact path that 400'd in #1550.
- Oracle (per the repo's testing doctrine, AGENTS.md 2026-11-04): the official JSON Schema draft 2020-12 meta-schema itself — validation success/failure per named tool is decidable, no hand-written expectations.

## Acceptance criteria

- A test enumerates every built-in tool (the `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/` set), takes each tool's generated `inputSchema`, applies the Anthropic-bound translation(s), and validates each result against the draft 2020-12 meta-schema.
- A validation failure names the offending tool and the meta-schema violation (the test output identifies `tools.N` candidates instead of a bare pass/fail).
- The test runs in an existing package test suite (core or ai) with no network access — the meta-schema is vendored or embedded as a fixture.
- The result is recorded on #1550 either way: the named built-in offender, or the explicit "built-ins clean — offender is external" verdict that unblocks the payload-pull step.

title: fix(ai): antigravity convertSchema forces type OBJECT onto allOf/not-only roots — a string allOf root becomes unsatisfiable, a not root is narrowed to objects

labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`convertSchema` in `packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts` (origin/main `6a35d3a284`) forces `type: "OBJECT"` onto any converted root whose `type` is undefined and which carries no `anyOf`/`oneOf` — including roots that describe themselves through `allOf` or `not` composition:

```ts
export const convertSchema = (schema: unknown, anthropic = false) => {
  if (schema === false) return { not: {} }
  const converted = convertSchemaNode(resolveSchemaRefs(isRecord(schema) ? schema : {}), anthropic)
  // A branch-only root (a multi-valued type union, #1556, or the node's own
  // anyOf/oneOf composition) describes itself; forcing OBJECT onto it would
  // narrow the union back to objects only.
  if (converted.type === undefined && converted.anyOf === undefined && converted.oneOf === undefined)
    converted.type = "OBJECT"
  return converted
}
```

The guard implements the comment's own rationale for `anyOf`/`oneOf` roots but not for `allOf`/`not` roots, which describe themselves in exactly the same way.

## Evidence (laptop probe, verbatim extraction, 2026-11-04)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-04-creator-opencode-1335/probe.ts` on the laptop — lines 90–267 of `packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts` at origin/main `6a35d3a284` extracted verbatim and run under bun (identical output with `anthropic` true and false):

- `{ allOf: [{ type: "string", minLength: 2 }] }` → `{"allOf":[{"minLength":2,"type":"STRING"}],"type":"OBJECT"}` — the conjunction is now unsatisfiable: no value is both a string and an object, so the parameter can never validate.
- `{ not: { type: "string" } }` → `{"not":{"type":"STRING"},"type":"OBJECT"}` — "anything except a string" is narrowed to "any object except a string": numbers, booleans, arrays and null are silently excluded.

Roots composed with `allOf` are a realistic tool-schema shape (raw/MCP `jsonSchema` tools commonly wrap parameters in `allOf: [{ $ref: … }]`; `resolveSchemaRefs` inlines the refs but leaves the `allOf` wrapper in place), and a root whose branches are not all objects — or a `not`-only root — is corrupted by the forced OBJECT instead of being passed through self-describing.

## Why it matters

This is the same class as #1556/#1573 in the same function: a silent semantic rewrite of a tool's declared parameter schema on the Antigravity wire. The model is told a parameter is an object (or can never be satisfied) when the tool declared something else, with no error anywhere — the failure only shows up as refused or mis-shaped tool calls upstream.

## Acceptance criteria

- `convertSchema` does not add `type: "OBJECT"` to a root that carries `allOf` or `not` (with no `type` of its own), for both Gemini and Anthropic targets.
- Plain roots still default to OBJECT exactly as today: `{}`, `{ properties: … }`, and `{ description: … }` conversions are byte-identical to before.
- New tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/antigravity.test.ts` cover: an `allOf`-only root (object and non-object branches), a `not`-only root, and the existing OBJECT-default cases.
- Existing antigravity `convertSchema` tests (#1548 ARRAY items, #1550 anyOf fold, #1556 type unions, #1573 boolean schemas) still pass.

body:
## Problem

`parseFrecency` (`packages/tui/src/prompt/frecency.tsx:12-32`) trusts every
JSON-parseable line of `frecency.jsonl` to be a well-shaped `FrecencyEntry`.
Its neighbours do not: `parsePromptInfo` (history.tsx) and
`parsePromptStash` (stash.tsx) validate shape (`typeof text === "string"`,
`Array.isArray(pasted)`, `typeof timestamp === "number"`) before accepting a
parsed line. `parseFrecency` casts `JSON.parse(line) as FrecencyEntry` and
only filters out lines whose parse *threw*.

## Evidence (verified this run, origin/main b306dc264f; function text extracted verbatim and run under bun on the laptop)

- A line containing `null` (valid JSON) makes `parseFrecency` **throw**:
  `null is not an object (evaluating 'entry.path')` — the `.reduce` at
  frecency.tsx:24-27 dereferences `entry.path` outside the per-line try/catch.
  The only call site (frecency.tsx:44, the provider's `onMount`) catches
  errors from `readText` but not from `parseFrecency`, so one such line
  kills the whole frecency load for that TUI session (unhandled rejection
  in `onMount`) — every valid entry in the file is lost with it.
- Wrong-shape lines pass through as entries: `123` → `[123]`, `"hello"` →
  `["hello"]`, `[1,2]` → `[[1,2]]`, `{path: 42, frequency: "x", lastOpen: "y"}`
  passes verbatim. The provider then builds store data from `entry.path`
  (key becomes `"undefined"` / `42`) and **rewrites the file from these
  entries** (frecency.tsx:52-53), persisting the garbage.
- `{path: "/a"}` (missing `frequency`/`lastOpen`) is accepted;
  `calculateFrecency` (frecency.tsx:35-38) then returns `NaN` for that file
  (`undefined / (1 + (now - undefined)/86400000)`), poisoning frecency
  ordering in the file picker.
- Existing test coverage misses the class: `packages/tui/test/prompt/jsonl.test.ts`
  covers an unparseable `"broken"` line for both stash and frecency, but no
  valid-JSON/wrong-shape line — exactly the gap the stash parser was already
  hardened against.

How a bad line gets there: the file is append-written across TUI versions
and concurrent sessions; a torn or foreign line that happens to be valid
JSON (a bare `null`, a number) is all it takes. The stash/history files in
the same directory already treat this as expected corruption.

## Fix shape

Validate each parsed line the way `parsePromptInfo` does — record with a
string `path` and finite numeric `frequency`/`lastOpen` — and drop anything
else, so `parseFrecency` never throws and never returns a non-entry.

## Acceptance criteria

- `parseFrecency` returns only entries with `typeof path === "string"` and
  finite numeric `frequency` and `lastOpen`; it never throws for any input
  text, including lines containing `null`, numbers, strings, arrays, or
  objects with missing/wrong-typed fields.
- New tests in `packages/tui/test/prompt/jsonl.test.ts` cover those
  wrong-shape lines for frecency (mirroring the existing corruption test).
- Existing frecency/stash JSONL tests still pass; no behavior change for
  well-formed files (latest-per-path dedupe and the 1000-entry cap intact).

# fix(ci): check:bounded-http + check:numeric-boundaries red for httpapi-codegen template — PR #1640's AbortSignal.timeout guard orphaned both allowlist dispositions

## Summary

Verified on `origin/main` 61caa59beb (laptop archive probe, gates run with `bun script/check-*.ts`): `check:bounded-http` and `check:numeric-boundaries` each exit 1 with a NEW finding no open issue lists — `packages/httpapi-codegen/src/index.ts:961`, the giant generated-client template string — plus that line's now-stale entry in each gate's allowlist. Every other candidate/stale entry in both gates is tracked by open issue #1540 (api.ts:70/:121/:113, v1-migration.bun.ts:1105, model-route-tuning + api.ts stale entries) or issue #1625 (prompt.ts:253).

## Evidence

- Commit 38d7de638c (PR #1640, fixing #1562) added two lines inside the template at `packages/httpapi-codegen/src/index.ts:961` — the comment `// Runtimes without AbortSignal.timeout get no client deadline rather than a throw… (#1562)` and the guard `if (typeof AbortSignal.timeout !== "function") return requestOptions ?? {}` in the generated `withDeadline` — and regenerated `packages/client/src/promise/generated/client.ts` to match. Because both allowlists key the template's disposition to the template line's exact text, the edit orphaned both entries at once.
- `bun script/check-bounded-http.ts` at 61caa59beb: unlisted candidate `packages/httpapi-codegen/src/index.ts:961` + stale allowlist entry for the same line (other hits = #1540's api.ts set only).
- `bun script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` at 61caa59beb: unlisted candidate `packages/httpapi-codegen/src/index.ts:961` + stale allowlist entry for the same line (other hits = #1540's api.ts:113 / v1-migration.bun.ts:1105 / model-route-tuning stale, and #1625's prompt.ts:253).
- `check:workflows` and `check:proto-reads` are GREEN at the same SHA.
- The template content itself is safe by construction, same as when it was dispositioned under closed issue #1514: the generated `json()` guards `Number(response.headers.get("content-length"))` with `Number.isFinite` + the 16 MiB `maxJsonBodyBytes` cap, body reads are streamed with byte caps, and non-SSE requests carry the composed `AbortSignal.timeout` deadline. No behavior change is needed — this is a re-sync of the two dispositions to the new template text.

## Why it matters

This is the third time a legitimate template edit has silently orphaned this line's gate dispositions (#1510 via #1514, now #1640). Until the entries are re-synced, both gates stay red on main beyond the tracked #1540/#1625 sets — and a red gate is exactly how the next genuine unbounded fetch or bare numeric conversion hides in the noise.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` and `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt` entries for `packages/httpapi-codegen/src/index.ts` (the :961 template line) match the current template text, with the disposition reasons updated to mention the #1640 `AbortSignal.timeout` guard where relevant; the stale pre-#1640 entries are gone.
- [ ] `bun script/check-bounded-http.ts` and `bun script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` report no `httpapi-codegen` finding (remaining red is #1540/#1625 scope only).
- [ ] No behavior change to the generated client, the codegen template's runtime semantics, or any other file's gate status.

body:
**Design correction (2026-11-04, Drew):** the original ACP-client-host design on this issue is withdrawn. Drew: "the other direct providers do not use acp they emulate exactly how the binary works." This issue now specifies a native wire-protocol provider, like `antigravity` and `mistral` in `packages/ai`. No `vibe` subprocess, no ACP host, no `vibe-acp`.

## What to build

A provider package `@opencode/ai/providers/vibe` (provider id `vibe`) in this repo:

- `packages/ai/src/providers/vibe.ts` — the package (mirrors `providers/mistral.ts`: same `MistralChat` protocol route, same endpoint), registered in `providers/index.ts` and in the `builtins` map in `packages/core/src/provider.ts`.
- `packages/ai/src/providers/vibe-auth.ts` — the credential resolver (mirrors `providers/antigravity-auth.ts`: `secret-tool` lookup, in-memory cache + `invalidate()`, `MissingCredentialError` when absent).
- Users select it like the other direct providers: declare provider `vibe` in opencode config with `npm: "@opencode/ai/providers/vibe"` and the models below (models.dev carries no `vibe` entry; same contract as `antigravity`).

## Wire spec — verified from the installed mistral-vibe 3.1.0 source on amd-6

Package: `~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/` (+ `mistralai_vibe_local_harness/`).

### Completion request (the only call the provider makes)

- `POST https://api.mistral.ai/v1/chat/completions`, streamed (SSE), via the official `mistralai` SDK: `Mistral(api_key, server_url = api_base minus any /vN suffix)`; vibe's preset `api_base` is `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` — identical to this repo's `MistralChat.DEFAULT_BASE_URL`, so the existing `MistralChat` protocol route is reused unchanged.
- Headers: `Authorization: Bearer <key>` is the ONLY auth header on the API-key path. No tenant/workspace/org headers exist anywhere in the binary. Provider `extra_headers` default empty; `x-affinity: <id>` appears only when a session affinity id exists (not applicable here).
- Body: `model` (route model id), `messages`, `temperature` (top_p omitted when temperature is set — Mistral rejects both), `reasoning_effort` when the model reasons (off is sent only to known-reasoning models), `max_tokens` when capped, `tools` + `parallel_tool_calls: true` when tools are present. Usage comes from the stream's usage object (prompt/completion/total + cached input tokens) — the route's existing usage mapping covers this.

### Models (Vibe's own presets)

Default: `mistral-vibe-cli-latest` (alias `mistral-medium-3.5`, "Mistral Medium 3.5"), temperature 1.0, thinking `high` (levels off/high), context 262144, image input, cost in/out/cache-read 1.5 / 7.5 / 0.15 per M tokens.
Selectable: `mistral-medium-latest`, `mistral-large-latest`, `mistral-small-latest`, `codestral-latest`, `ministral-14b-latest`, `ministral-8b-latest`, `ministral-3b-latest`. (Vibe's third-party GLM presets ride a different provider preset and stay out of scope; the `zai` provider covers them.)

### Credential resolution — mirror the binary exactly

The binary's `resolve_api_key_with_origin` order (first hit wins):

1. Explicit provider config (`apiKey` / custom `auth`) — fork-level override for tests and offline use, mirroring `antigravity`'s Config.
2. Environment `MISTRAL_API_KEY` — the binary's process env already includes `~/.vibe/.env` values (loaded under the real env; real env wins), so the resolver checks env `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, then the `~/.vibe/.env` dotenv file itself (0600; the binary writes it only when no keyring backend exists).
3. OS keyring: `secret-tool lookup service ai.mistral.vibe username MISTRAL_API_KEY`; legacy service `vibe` as fallback (the binary migrates legacy entries forward). The browser sign-in (`vibe --setup`, PKCE against console.mistral.ai) stores a plain workspace API key there — sent as Bearer verbatim; no refresh, no exchange (unlike antigravity's OAuth JSON).

Keyring read mechanism (must work from this repo's TS runtime on amd-6): exec `secret-tool` located via `SECRET_TOOL_PATH` -> PATH -> `/nix/store` scan for libsecret (the `antigravity-auth` pattern). Python `keyring` is broken on amd-6 (kwalletd6 owns org.freedesktop.secrets and its Secret Service cannot do the DH session python-secretstorage mandates; gnome-keyring runs pkcs11-only) — do not use it. `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` defaults to `unix:path=/run/user/<uid>/bus` when unset; 15s timeout; any failure = credential absent, never a hang.

### Out of scope (the binary's first-party side calls, not the provider's)

- Model catalog `GET {api_base}/model-catalog?surface=vibe-code` (fail-open, cached) and `GET https://console.mistral.ai/api/vibe/whoami` — the provider ships Vibe's preset table in code instead.
- The experimental OIDC sign-in (`VIBE_CLI_OIDC_ENABLED=1`, issuer auth.mistral.ai, keyring bundle under service `ai.mistral.vibe.oidc`) — the default browser sign-in provisions an API key; OIDC is not the shipped flow.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests: resolution order (config > env > .env file > keyring primary > keyring legacy; absent everywhere -> the not-signed-in error) and request shaping (endpoint, Bearer-only auth, default model carries temperature 1.0 + `reasoning_effort: "high"`, caller-supplied values win).
- Live: after the one-time desktop sign-in lands the keyring credential, an opencode session using provider `vibe` completes a real task end-to-end with no `vibe` process involved.
- Not signed in: any `vibe` request fails fast with a clear error naming the missing credential and the fix (run `vibe --setup` once, or set `MISTRAL_API_KEY`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Provider package `@opencode/ai/providers/vibe` (id `vibe`) exists in `packages/ai/src/providers/vibe.ts`, mirroring the `MistralChat` protocol route and endpoint — no `vibe` subprocess, no ACP host.
- [ ] `vibe-auth.ts` resolves credentials like the other direct providers (secret-tool lookup, in-memory cache + `invalidate()`, `MissingCredentialError` when absent).
- [ ] Provider is registered in `providers/index.ts` and the `builtins` map in `packages/core/src/provider.ts`, and is selectable via config as specified in the body.
- [ ] PR #1661 (already open, implementing this issue) is shepherded to merge or superseded by an equivalent PR that closes this issue.

title: fix(providers): cloudflare-ai-gateway credential fails upstream auth (code 10000), blocking clef classifications

body:
## Defect

Every Clef classification request currently fails at the Cloudflare upstream with an authentication error, on BOTH the (now retired) standalone door and the server facade — the failure is in the shared credential, not in either front.

Live evidence (2026-11-04, after the #1627 facade redeploy): the recorded clef classifier probe (the exact body in `packages/core/test/facade-parity.test.ts`) sent to `POST http://127.0.0.1:13420/v1/systemone` on the deployed +63c50ee server and to the then-still-running door at `:18742` returned **byte-identical** responses:

```
HTTP 401
{"error":"Cloudflare Workers AI Clef execution failed","details":{"result":null,"success":false,"errors":[{"code":10000,"message":"Authentication error"}],"messages":[]}}
```

The facade side ledgered the attempt (`route_attempt` id 232756, provider `cloudflare-ai-gateway`, model `@cf/cloudflare/clef-flash`, session_id NULL, outcome failure). The same envelope was already observed in the #1638 scratch proof, so the condition predates the facade migration; the migration is behaviour-preserving through it (parity proven), but no classification can complete until the credential is repaired.

## Scope

- Identify which credential the `cloudflare-ai-gateway` route presents upstream (server credential store entry + the Cloudflare env top-up the wrapper performs) and why Cloudflare rejects it with code 10000 (expired/revoked token, wrong account/gateway pairing, or a token minted for a different surface).
- Repair or re-mint it through the normal credential path (never in repo files), then prove one real classification end-to-end: the recorded probe against the facade returns the typed probability answer shape (cf. the 2026-11-02 live door capture in the parity test) instead of the 401 envelope.
- Note in the fix evidence whether the OpenChamber Jev classifier (the consumer, repointed to the facade under #1410) resumes classifying unaided.

Filed from the #1146 sequence: #1410's repoint + door retirement completed behind this defect; this issue is the remaining blocker for actual classification traffic.

body:
## Problem

The public files worker (`services/files/src/index.ts`, the R2-backed worker serving release binaries and videos at `opencode.ai/files/*`) answers **416** for Range requests whose byte-range-set is *invalid* — a spec with `first-byte-pos > last-byte-pos` (e.g. `Range: bytes=5-3`) or a suffix range with zero length (e.g. `Range: bytes=-0`). Both the HTTP spec and this service's own documented contract say such a header must be **ignored**, serving the full `200` response:

- **RFC 9110 §14.2:** a byte-range-set containing a spec with first-byte-pos greater than last-byte-pos, or a suffix-byte-range-spec with a zero suffix-length, is invalid, and a recipient **SHOULD ignore the Range header field**.
- **`services/files/README.md:63-65`:** "Unsupported or malformed range formats fall back to a full response."
- **`services/files/src/index.ts:104` (the code's own comment):** "Ignore unsupported/malformed and multipart ranges; a full 200 is valid."

The genuinely-unsatisfiable case (`bytes=50-` on a 10-byte object) correctly returns 416 — that part must not change.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probe of origin/main `63c50eec0d`)

Probe: the worker's `fetch` handler driven directly on the laptop with a mocked R2 bucket (10-byte object `hello.txt`, etag `"abc123"`) and a stubbed Cache API. Full probe output:

| Request | Result | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| plain GET | 200, 10 bytes | 200 ✓ |
| `Range: bytes=2-4` | 206, `bytes 2-4/10` | 206 ✓ |
| `Range: bytes=-3` | 206, `bytes 7-9/10` | 206 ✓ |
| `Range: bytes=-0` | **416** | 200 full body (invalid set → ignore) ✗ |
| `Range: bytes=5-3` | **416** | 200 full body (invalid set → ignore) ✗ |
| `Range: bytes=50-` | 416 | 416 ✓ (truly unsatisfiable) |
| `Range: bytes=0-1,3-4` | 200 full body | 200 ✓ (multipart ignored, per :104) |
| `If-None-Match: "abc123"` / weak form | 304 | 304 ✓ |
| `If-Match` mismatch | 412 | 412 ✓ |
| malformed `%FF` key | 400 | 400 ✓ |
| POST | 405 | 405 ✓ |

Code path (`services/files/src/index.ts:105-122`): the regex `/^bytes=(\d*)-(\d*)$/` accepts both cases; for `-0`, `(bytes[1] || bytes[2])` passes on the string `"0"`, `offset` computes to `object.size` and `end` to `size - 1`, so the `offset >= object.size || end < offset` check at `:115` fires the 416 at `:118`. Same check fires for `5-3`. Neither case is distinguished from a truly unsatisfiable range.

## Why it matters

This worker serves the release binaries (`bin/<version>/opencode-*.tar.gz` per the README) and media that download resumption and video seeking depend on. A client that emits a zero-length suffix probe or a clamped inverted range (both seen from HTTP client libraries computing ranges from content lengths) gets a hard 416 error instead of the file — against the documented contract of this very service. The class is invisible today because **the worker has no tests at all**: `services/files/` contains no `*.test.*` file and its `package.json` has no `test` script (only build/dev/deploy/typecheck), so `turbo test` skips it and `deploy-files.yml` runs only the typecheck. The conditional/range/cache logic (~163 lines, hand-rolled) has no regression net — sibling services (changelog, update) both have test scripts and suites.

## Acceptance criteria

Oracle: RFC 9110 §14.1–14.2 range/conditional semantics plus the README contract quoted above.

- [ ] `Range: bytes=-0` and `Range: bytes=5-3` (and equivalents: any spec with first > last, any zero-length suffix) return **200 with the full body and no `Content-Range`**, matching the multipart/unsupported fallback.
- [ ] Genuinely unsatisfiable ranges (`bytes=50-` beyond EOF, `bytes=10-` on a 10-byte object) still return **416** with `Content-Range: bytes */<size>`.
- [ ] Valid single ranges, suffix ranges, `If-Range`, and the conditional headers (`If-Match` 412, `If-None-Match` 304, `If-Modified-Since`) behave exactly as in the probe table above.
- [ ] A test suite for the worker exists and runs in CI (e.g. `services/files/src/index.test.ts` with a `test` script in `services/files/package.json` so `turbo test` picks the package up), covering at minimum the probe table: plain/HEAD, valid range, suffix range, invalid range sets (this issue), unsatisfiable range, multipart fallback, conditional 304/412, malformed key 400, missing key 404, wrong method 405.
- [ ] `bun typecheck` in `services/files` still passes.

## Dedup / related

- `gh search issues` for "files service", "services/files", "R2 range", "conditional request" (open + closed): no issue covers this worker's range handling or its missing tests. Nearest neighbours are gate-coverage issues for services trees (#1256, #1308, both closed — bounded-http/numeric scans, not behavior tests) and #143 (console/stats test wiring, closed).
- Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode, 2026-11-04 run; verification in a laptop archive probe of origin/main `63c50eec0d27139b6ebdc57ed85d4d3ace35b5b3` (probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-04-creator-opencode-1635` on the laptop).

title: antigravity: client-secret extraction (first GOCSPX match) stale for agy 1.4.11 — refresh fails invalid_client
body:
# antigravity: OAuth client-secret extraction (first GOCSPX match) is stale for agy 1.4.11 — refresh fails invalid_client

Found 2026-11-04 during the #1414 native repoint verification (deploy-gated sequence on #1146).

## Symptom

With the native provider live (config repoint merged in code), the first call failed:

    route_attempt 227773 | antigravity-direct | gemini-3.8-flash | failure
    provider.auth: Antigravity keyring credential unavailable: token endpoint HTTP 401:
    invalid_client — "The provided client secret is invalid."

The door (bin/antigravity-direct.mjs in developing-today/code, same extraction design) fails identically on :18751, so this is a shared extraction defect, not a provider wiring defect.

## Root cause (verified live against Google's token endpoint)

binaryIntel() in packages/ai/src/providers/antigravity-auth.ts takes the FIRST match of /GOCSPX-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}/ and slices 35 chars, per the layout of the agy binary it was verified against. That layout changed:

- agy 1.4.8 (nix build): 2 GOCSPX runs, lengths [70, 40]. run0[:35] is the 70-char concatenated pair's first half — token endpoint answers invalid_grant for a bogus grant (= client secret ACCEPTED).
- agy 1.4.11 (~/.gemini/bin/agy, self-updated 2026-10-30): 3 runs, lengths [40, 43, 40]. run0[:35] -> invalid_client (rejected). **run1[:35] -> invalid_grant (accepted)**. run2[:35] -> invalid_client.

So in the 1.4.11 binary the pairing secret is the SECOND run's first 35 chars; the first-match heuristic picks a decoy/other-client secret. Probe method note: with an intentionally bogus refresh_token, Google answers invalid_client when the secret is wrong and invalid_grant when the secret is right — a safe oracle that never touches the real grant.

## Impact

Any consumer refreshing through this extraction is down whenever the stored access token expires: the native provider AND the remaining door. Lane traffic survived until the stored token aged out (last success 2026-11-04 09:00 UTC); the 05:47 CST reboot stopped the CLI from refreshing it, and every refresh since has hit invalid_client.

## Interim workaround (applied live, 2026-11-04)

AGY_BIN=/run/current-system/sw/bin/agy on the opencode.service unit (drop-in), so extraction reads the 1.4.8 binary whose layout the heuristic matches. Verified: route_attempt 227942, antigravity-direct/gemini-3.8-flash, success through the native provider; the same AGY_BIN drop-in restored the door (chat completion via :18751 OK).

## Fix direction

Do not trust position: collect ALL candidate secrets (each run's [:35], plus [35:70] for >=70-char runs, deduped), and on a token-endpoint invalid_client response try the next candidate (cache the winner in memory). Add a test with both binary layouts (1.4.8-style 70-char pair first; 1.4.11-style decoy first, pairing secret second). The door carries the same logic in code's bin/antigravity-direct.mjs but retires under #1414; the fork fix is the durable one.

# Facade routes are in the OpenAPI spec but not served by opencode serve (SPA/405)

Found during the #1146 deploy-gated sequence on generation 528 (2026-11-04). The #1146 facades answer in tests, but the deployed serve listener does not route them:

## Evidence (running server, 127.0.0.1:13420, build 2.0.30+4175c63, pid 616146)

- GET /openapi.json (basic auth) lists all facade paths: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/embeddings, /v1/messages, /v1/systemone, /v1/models, /v1/models/{id}, /v1/models/{provider}/{model} (140 paths total).
- GET /v1/models (with and without basic auth, with x-opencode-directory header) returns 200 with the web UI SPA HTML, not the models JSON.
- POST /v1/chat/completions and POST /v1/responses (with/without auth, with directory header and ?directory= query) return 405 with empty body.
- /api/* endpoints on the same listener work normally with the same auth (e.g. GET /api/credential returns data).
- The binary contains the completions group (server.completions, completions.models strings present).

## Reproduced on the pinned build too

A scratch instance of the pinned build (opencode-2.0.30+ae5d592, the flake.lock opencode_2 rev ae5d592093) on a scratch port/HOME/DB behaves identically: SPA HTML for GET /v1/models, 405 for POST /v1/chat/completions. So this is not a stale-build artifact: at both revs, packages/server/src/handlers.ts registers CompletionsHandler and routes.ts mounts HttpApiBuilder.layer(Api) unconditionally, yet the serve listener does not route the group. The OpenAPI is generated from the Api definition, which is why the spec advertises routes the listener does not serve. Suspect the serve entry router composition (UI catch-all shadowing the API router for GET, no fall-through for POST), while the fetch-handler entry used in tests serves the API only — worth checking where serve composes its router versus ServerFetch.make.

## Impact

Blocks the #1146 migration legs that repoint callers to the facade: #1410 (clef to /v1/systemone), #1153 (route-proxy retirement + OpenClaw rewire proof), the #1155 live attestation probe, and the facade leg of the #1154 Gate 1 verification window. Session traffic is unaffected.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every route advertised in the OpenAPI spec is either served by `opencode serve` or removed from the spec
- The facade /v1/* behavior (SPA fallback / 405) is intentional and documented for any route kept in the spec
- A test or scripted check compares spec routes against served routes

## Problem

`bun run check:numeric-boundaries` is red on main for one candidate no open issue lists: the byte-wise data-URL decoder merged today in PR #1623 (commit `edb8a2f3e4`, fixing #1539) added `packages/core/src/session/prompt.ts:253`:

```ts
bytes.push(parseInt(hex, 16))
```

in `decodePercentPayload`, without a disposition in `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt`.

The conversion is safe by construction — `hex` is validated by `/^[0-9a-fA-F]{2}$/` on the preceding line (`prompt.ts:251`), so the value is provably 0–255. This is exactly the pattern already dispositioned for the mirrored decoder in `packages/core/src/database/v1-migration.bun.ts:1105` under #1540: the prompt.ts comment itself notes the algorithm is mirrored from that module (#1529). PR #1623 copied the algorithm but not its gate disposition.

## Evidence (verified at origin/main `16f52006edeeb032c91b0e431556931fec9f94e9`, laptop archive probe)

- `bun script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` → exit 1. Unlisted candidates: `api.ts:113`, `v1-migration.bun.ts:1105` (both #1540), `digitalocean.ts:58`, `expires.ts:33`, `expires.ts:48`, `httpapi-codegen/src/index.ts:961` (all #1514), and **`prompt.ts:253` (new — in neither issue)**. The 6 stale entries are likewise all #1514/#1540 scope.
- `bun script/check-bounded-http.ts` → exit 1 with only #1540's `api.ts:70`/`:121` + its 2 stale entries; `check:workflows` and `check:proto-reads` are green at the same SHA.
- Raw read of `prompt.ts:238-257` at that SHA: `decodePercentPayload` regex-validates each `%HH` escape before `parseInt(hex, 16)`; malformed escapes throw `Invalid data URL`.
- `grep prompt.ts script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt` shows only the two pre-existing baseline entries (:85/:86) — no entry for the `parseInt(hex, 16)` line.
- Dedup: `gh issue list --search` for `prompt.ts numeric-boundaries`, `decodePercentPayload`, and `1539 numeric` returns nothing; full gate output compared line-by-line against the #1514 and #1540 issue bodies.

## Why it matters

The numeric-boundaries gate is the regression net for bare numeric conversions (#992/#993). It is already red for the tracked #1514/#1540 sets; every additional undispositioned site that lands behind that noise makes the next genuine bare conversion easier to miss — this is the same drift pattern as #1514, #1540, #1606 and #1607, now repeated by #1623 within hours of merging.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `prompt.ts:253` carries a disposition in `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt` keyed to its current line text, stating the safe-by-construction reason (hex regex-validated `/^[0-9a-fA-F]{2}$/` immediately before the parse, value provably 0–255 — mirroring the #1540 disposition for `v1-migration.bun.ts:1105`), or the line is converted through the shared primitives in `packages/core/src/util/number.ts` (#993).
- [ ] `bun script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` at the then-current main reports no `prompt.ts` finding (remaining red is #1514/#1540 scope only).
- [ ] `bun test script/check-numeric-boundaries.test.ts` still passes (or the gate's own tests, wherever wired).
- [ ] No behavior change to `decodePercentPayload` / data-URL attachment decoding (#1539's fix stands as merged).

Related: #1539 / PR #1623 (the change that introduced the site), #1529 / #1540 (the mirrored migration decoder and its disposition), #1514 (the already-tracked remainder of this gate's red), #992/#993.

body:
## Problem

The Workspace service's idle janitor only ever sees workspaces that the current process has connected to. After a restart, persisted workspace rows with live bindings are invisible to it — nothing at boot reconciles them — so their backing resources are never idle-suspended (and the promised ~23h safety snapshot rotation does not exist at all) until someone happens to provision/connect that exact workspace ID again.

The code itself promises this in a later PR that has not landed:

`packages/core/src/workspace.ts:358-359` (at main `a6bc4dca06faa872d83f1b65b00c4f7cd6dbd6a5`):

```
// TODO(workspace-plan): add the boot janitor and ~23h safety snapshot rotation in a later PR.
// TODO(workspace-plan): make cold wake interruptible with a re-pin loop against janitor races.
```

## Evidence (verified this run, pinned reads at `a6bc4dca`)

- The janitor loop (`workspace.ts:190-222`, repeated on `Schedule.spaced(pollInterval ?? 1 minute)` at `:222`) iterates only `[...connections.entries()]` (`:194`) — the in-memory `connections` map, which is empty at process start and only gains entries via `open()` on provision/connect.
- Every `WorkspaceTable` access in the tree is by-ID (`find` `:96`, `saveBinding` `:105`, updates `:184`/`:211`, create select `:228-230`, insert `:244-247`, delete `:347`); there is no scan of persisted rows anywhere, and no boot-time reconciliation pass in the layer.
- `grep -rn "janitor" packages/ --include="*.ts"` returns only the two TODO lines; `grep -rn "snapshot" packages/core/src/workspace/ packages/core/src/environment/` returns nothing — the safety snapshot rotation is entirely unimplemented, not just unscheduled.
- `packages/core/test/workspace.test.ts` (33 tests) pins the in-process lifecycle — including "persists the workspace lifecycle and reconnects after idle suspension" (`:330`) with a fake driver recording `suspendForIdle` — but has no boot/restart scenario: no test builds the layer over pre-existing persisted rows (grep for boot/restart/reconcile in the test file: no matches).

## Why it matters

Workspaces back real (potentially billed / resource-holding) driver resources. A server restart — deploy, crash, upgrade — silently orphans every persisted, bound workspace that nobody reconnects to: it is never suspended for idleness, never snapshotted, and its row's `last_used_at` goes stale with no process responsible for it. The longer the deployment runs between restarts, the more this looks like a slow resource leak that only manual `destroy` calls can clean up. The TODO's second line compounds it: cold wake is not interruptible against janitor races, so a boot janitor added naively could race wakes — the two TODOs need to be designed together.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On layer startup (boot), the Workspace service scans persisted `WorkspaceTable` rows and reconciles them: rows with a binding whose `last_used_at` is beyond the idle threshold are driven through the same `suspendForIdle` path the poll loop uses (respecting the per-workspace lock and the deliberate racing-spawn semantics documented at `workspace.ts:206`); rows with no binding are left untouched.
- [ ] Boot reconciliation is safe against a concurrent provision/connect of the same workspace (no double-suspend, no suspend of an active connection) — the cold-wake re-pin concern in the `:359` TODO is addressed or explicitly documented as out of scope with reasoning.
- [ ] The ~23h safety snapshot rotation from the `:358` TODO is either implemented (driver capability + rotation cadence + retention) or split into its own follow-up issue with the TODO updated to point at it — the TODO must not silently survive another "later PR".
- [ ] New tests in `packages/core/test/workspace.test.ts` style (fake driver, persisted rows seeded before layer construction): (a) a stale bound row is suspended at boot without any connect; (b) a fresh bound row is left alone; (c) a boot scan racing a connect does not suspend the active workspace.
- [ ] Existing workspace tests still pass.

## Dedup / related

- `gh search issues` for "janitor", "boot janitor", "safety snapshot", "workspace-plan": no matches in any state. "workspace idle suspend" returns only #1110 (server fs endpoints auth, unrelated) and #374 (local-first epic — possible parent, but it names no janitor work; link as related if the epic owner wants it attached natively).
- Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode, 2026-11-04 run; verification in a detached laptop probe worktree at `dc3613c185` plus pinned `gh api` reads at `a6bc4dca` (the compare `dc3613c185...a6bc4dca` touches only `session/runner/step.ts` + its test, so the workspace evidence is unchanged at current main).

body:
# fix(core): a content-filter finish strands the attempt's half-open probe claim — #1602 released claims only on the ContentPolicy error path

## Summary

PR #1602 (for #1084) taught the session runner to isolate content-policy rejections from route health. Its second commit released any half-open bench probe claim an attempt carried when the attempt ended in a `ContentPolicy` **error**, because a policy rejection bypasses the health accounting (`ModelRoute.failed()` / `ModelRoute.completed()`) that normally settles the claim — an outstanding claim strands the target's route recovery (`probeDue` stays false) until the bench expires.

The same refusal delivered as a **finish reason** (`content-filter`) was handled for the attempt log (recorded as outcome `failure` with `error_tag: ContentPolicy`) but not for the probe claim: on that path no code settles the claim, so a benched target whose probe attempt is answered with a content-filter finish stays unrecoverable until bench expiry — the exact stranding #1602 set out to remove, one delivery shape over.

## Evidence (verified at `origin/main` d5f62962d3c640921b28eb3e9b0e6cf8f1f6b848, pinned `gh api` raw reads of both files)

- `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts:506` — `policyFinish = !failed && recorded.finish?.finish === "content-filter"`; on this path `llmFailure` is `undefined` (the stream did not fail).
- `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts:599-605` — the probe-claim release added by #1602 is gated on `policyFailure` (`llmFailure?.reason._tag === "ContentPolicy"`), so it never fires for `policyFinish`.
- `packages/core/src/session/runner/publish-llm-event.ts:588-589` — a `content-filter` finish sets `providerFailed = true` on the publisher record.
- `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts:729-735` — `ModelRoute.completed(...)` (the other claim settler, which receives `input.model.routing.probeClaim`) requires `!record.failure && !record.providerFailed`, so it is not called for a content-filter finish either.
- The health-accounting call `ModelRoute.failed(...)` (step.ts:~610-625) requires `llmFailure`, so it is also skipped — correctly for health, but it means no settler runs at all.
- The only other `releaseBenchProbe` in step.ts (~:839) covers a different claim: a hedge candidate whose *preparation* failed (#1486) — not the primary attempt's claim.
- Test coverage: `packages/core/test/session-runner.test.ts` pins the error path (scenarios at :1225 and :1270) and the finish path's message projection (:5738), but no scenario combines a probe claim with a policy outcome of either shape; nothing asserts claim settlement on a content-filter finish.

## Why it matters

Bench probes are how a benched target earns its way back into rotation. A probe attempt is a real request to the provider, and a provider can answer it with a content-filter finish (safety/refusal finish reasons normalize to `content-filter`). When that happens today, the claim is stranded: the target cannot be probed again until the bench expires, extending an outage the routing layer had already decided the target might have recovered from — silently, since the attempt row looks correctly recorded as a policy rejection.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A session-runner scenario: a probe-claimed attempt whose stream finishes with reason `content-filter` settles the claim (the target becomes probe-eligible again / `releaseBenchProbe` is invoked with the attempt's claim), mirroring the #1602 error-path behavior.
- [ ] The content-filter finish still records outcome `failure` + `error_tag: ContentPolicy`, still counts in `policyRejections` and never in `failures` (model-route-log), and still does not call `ModelRoute.failed()` or `ModelRoute.completed()` for health.
- [ ] Existing #1602 scenarios (session-runner.test.ts :1225/:1270, model-route-log tests) still pass; no behavior change for non-probe attempts.

## Related

- #1084 (closed) / PR #1602 — the fix this follows up; its commit "release half-open probe claims on content-policy rejection" covers the error path only.
- #1486 (closed) — probe-claim release gaps in other consumers (compaction, resolver load failure, runner failover preparation); this is the remaining runner path.

# fix(cli): Node bundle crashes at startup on every command — onnxruntime-node's native binding is dynamically required inside the Rollup bundle

## Summary

The Node distribution built from current main cannot start at all. `packages/cli/script/build-node.ts` bundles the CLI into `dist-node/opencode.mjs` (Rollup), and since the native embeddings backend landed (#1554 step 2, commit b56245df9b), the bundle dies during module initialisation:

```
$ node dist-node/opencode.mjs --version
Error: Could not dynamically require "../bin/napi-v6/linux/x64/onnxruntime_binding.node". Please configure the dynamicRequireTargets or/and ignoreDynamicRequires option of @rollup/plugin-commonjs appropriately for this require call to work.
    at commonjsRequire (file:///.../packages/cli/dist-node/opencode.mjs:772:103559)
    at requireBinding (.../opencode.mjs:4693:141667)
    at requireBackend (.../opencode.mjs:4693:142720)
    at requireDist (.../opencode.mjs:4693:145773)
Node.js v26.4.0   (exit 1)
```

Verified on `origin/main` 57d2870e301e (laptop probe; bundle built by the repo's own `script/build-node.ts --bundle-only --skip-install`, run with the test-pinned Node v26.4.0 from `packages/cli/.cache/node/`). `--version` never executes — the crash is at import time, so **every** command in the Node build is dead on arrival.

## Root cause chain

- #1554 step 2 (b56245df9b) added `onnxruntime-node: 1.31.1` to `packages/core/package.json:136` and `packages/core/src/embeddings-native.ts`, which loads it lazily: `const ort = await import("onnxruntime-node")` (embeddings-native.ts:106).
- Under Bun (the primary runtime) the dynamic import resolves the real package from node_modules, so the server works.
- Under the Rollup Node bundle, onnxruntime-node is inlined; its own dist loader (`requireDist` → `requireBackend` → `requireBinding`) performs a dynamic `require()` of the platform binding path `../bin/napi-v6/linux/x64/onnxruntime_binding.node`, which @rollup/plugin-commonjs cannot resolve — hence the startup throw.
- `packages/cli/script/build-node.ts` has no externals / dynamicRequireTargets handling for onnxruntime-node (or sharp, which @huggingface/transformers loads transitively — embeddings-native.ts:46's packaging note covers the Nix server closure and libstdc++, but never the Node bundle).
- The lazy `await import()` in embeddings-native does not save the bundle: onnxruntime-node's package entry is pulled into the module graph and its binding require runs at bundle initialisation, before any embed call.

## Test evidence

`packages/cli` suite at 57d2870e301e (laptop probe, `bun test --timeout 30000`): the only 2 failures are the two Node-bundle tests in `test/serve-handover.test.ts`, both failing because the bundle they spawn crashes on startup:

- `(fail) node: a successor takes over a supervisor's socket with no refused connection and no failed request [140938.36ms]` — stack at `ensureNodeBundle (serve-handover.test.ts:378)`, underlying error = the build-node run reporting the bundled node exiting status 1 with the dynamic-require error above.
- `(fail) node: control: without a supervisor's socket, the same restart refuses connections [60098.08ms]`

The Bun-runtime handover tests in the same file pass; 241+ other cli tests passed in the same run.

## Why it matters

The Node bundle is the non-Bun distribution of the CLI (the serve-handover machinery and its tests exist precisely for it). Right now it is 100% broken on main — not a degraded feature, a binary that cannot print its version. The embeddings work (#1554) is mid-flight with more steps queued, so the bundle breakage will only get harder to unwind the longer it sits; and because the failing tests take 60–140 s each to fail, the red is expensive noise in every cli suite run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `node dist-node/opencode.mjs --version` (bundle built from main via `script/build-node.ts`) exits 0 and prints a version, on Linux x64 at minimum.
- [ ] Both Node tests in `packages/cli/test/serve-handover.test.ts` pass; the rest of the cli suite stays green.
- [ ] The Bun runtime path is unchanged: native embeddings still load lazily on first embed call under Bun (no eager native load at server boot), and #1583/#1567 behaviour is untouched.
- [ ] The chosen mechanism (e.g. externalising onnxruntime-node + sharp in build-node.ts with the binding shipped/resolved beside the bundle, dynamicRequireTargets/ignoreDynamicRequires configuration, or excluding the native backend from the Node bundle behind its registry flag) is written down in build-node.ts or the packaging notes in embeddings-native.ts, so the next native dependency does not re-break the bundle silently.
- [ ] A fast guard exists so this fails in seconds, not 140 s: e.g. the node-bundle smoke (build + `--version`) runs as its own cheap test/step rather than only inside the handover tests.

## Related

- #1554 (embeddings bake-in epic — the change that introduced the regression), #1583 / #1567 (native-backend behaviour, separate), #1300 / #777 (serve handover race — different failure, same test file), #442 / #435 (earlier Node-build breakage class).

# fix(www): services/www OpenAPI copies stale again — PR #1596's fix was generated against a pre-merge protocol file, check:generated red on main

## Summary

Verified on `origin/main` `57d2870e30` (laptop archive probe): `bun run check:generated` in `services/www` exits 1 — "Generated OpenAPI documents are stale." This is the third recurrence of this drift (#1498 → #1593 → now), and this time the fix itself landed stale: PR #1596 (the fix for #1593) regenerated the www copies on its branch, but commit `913ec58c38` ("chore(protocol): regenerate openapi after main merge (description drift)") landed on main before the merge, and the merged result pairs the newer protocol file with the branch's older www copies.

## Evidence

- `services/www/script/generate-openapi.ts` is a pure copy check: `services/www/openapi.json` and `services/www/public/openapi.json` must byte-match `packages/protocol/openapi.json`.
- At `57d2870e30`: protocol md5 `04a72370077463230d9d69b7aab2f048`, both www copies md5 `26bc5fffe8681469571f121baa2a06be` (the two www copies match each other).
- The content diff is exactly 2 lines (16328 and 16551), the same description in two schema spots: protocol reads "Give-ups among a target's recent outcomes that mark it unsteady and start escalation. **Cannot exceed the outcome window, because the count reads only the retained outcomes in that window.** Defaults to 2." — the bolded sentence is missing from both www copies.
- The mismatch already exists at the #1596 merge commit itself (`00d606762e`): `git log 59f3f9c1aa..origin/main -- packages/protocol/openapi.json` shows `913ec58c38` changed the protocol file after the www fix branch (`59f3f9c1aa`) was generated, and no commit since has touched `services/www/openapi.json`.
- Dedup: #1593 is CLOSED (fixed by #1596). #1560 is a different artifact (packages/protocol's own openapi.json vs its schema source) — related, cross-linked, not this. No open issue lists the www copies' current drift.

## Why it matters

The www check is the only guard keeping the published OpenAPI documents in sync with the protocol package. It has now gone red three times by the same mechanism — a protocol regen lands (or a fix branch goes stale against one) and nothing re-runs the www copy step. Each red day trains contributors to ignore `check:generated`, and the docs site serves a spec that disagrees with the shipped protocol.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `services/www/openapi.json` and `services/www/public/openapi.json` regenerated from `packages/protocol/openapi.json` (`bun run generate` in `services/www`); `bun run check:generated` exits 0 on main.
- [ ] No other content changes — the diff is the 2 description lines above.
- [ ] Triage note: consider whether the recurrence (three filings: #1498, #1593, this) warrants folding the www copy into the protocol regen path or the gate-registry work (#1525/#1527) rather than a fourth manual regen — record the decision on this issue; the regen itself is the small fix and does not wait for it.

## Related

- #1593 (closed) — previous occurrence, fixed by PR #1596
- #1560 — protocol's own OpenAPI generation drift (different check)
- #1525 / #1527 — gate harness / gate registry design that may own the durable fix

# fix(ci): check:numeric-boundaries — salesforce.ts:16 content-length parse from the #1097 fix never got a disposition

## Summary

Verified on `origin/main` `ef9139835e` (laptop archive probe, `bun script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` exits 1). Every undispositioned candidate in the current output is already tracked — api.ts:113 and v1-migration.bun.ts:1105 by #1540, digitalocean.ts:58 / expires.ts:33 / expires.ts:48 and the httpapi-codegen template by #1514 — except one:

## Evidence

Unlisted numeric-boundary candidate at `packages/console/app/src/lib/salesforce.ts:16`:

```ts
const declared = Number(response.headers.get("content-length"))
```

This is in `readCappedBody()`: the very next line guards it with `Number.isFinite(declared) && declared > SALESFORCE_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`, cancels the body, and throws — and the streamed read below enforces the same 1 MiB cap in flight. The parse is safe by construction (a missing header yields `Number(null) = 0`; a non-numeric header yields NaN, which fails the isFinite check and falls through to the capped streamed read).

The line was introduced by the #1097 fix, which added careful bounded-http dispositions for this file's fetches (`script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` :91–94) but no numeric-boundaries disposition for the content-length parse it added. `grep salesforce script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt` returns nothing.

## Why it matters

The numeric-boundaries net (#992/#993) only works if every bare conversion carries a current disposition. This is one overlooked line from an otherwise exemplary bounded-HTTP fix; left undispositioned it adds one more permanent red line to a gate that is already red for #1514/#1540 reasons, which is exactly how the next genuine bare conversion hides in the noise.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/console/app/src/lib/salesforce.ts:16` carries a disposition in `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt` stating the safe-by-construction reason (isFinite guard + 1 MiB cap with body cancel; streamed read enforces the cap regardless) — or the parse is converted through the shared primitives in `packages/core/src/util/number.ts` (#993).
- [ ] After the change, `bun script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` reports no salesforce.ts finding (remaining red is #1514/#1540 scope only).
- [ ] No behavior change to `readCappedBody` or the Salesforce fetches.

Related: #1097 (closed — the fix that introduced the line), #1514 / #1540 (the already-tracked remainder of this gate's red), #992 / #993 (numeric-boundaries design and primitives).
