# fix(ci): check:bounded-http red for cli/script/build.ts — the Bun-archive verification rewrite (de19ec16f5) orphaned the #1159 dispositions and left 4 undispositioned sites

## Summary

Verified on `origin/main` `ef9139835e` (laptop archive probe, `bun script/check-bounded-http.ts` exits 1). The gate's red breaks down as: api.ts:70/:121 + two stale api.ts entries = open #1540's scope, plus a NEW set in `packages/cli/script/build.ts` that no open issue lists.

## Evidence — new build.ts findings at ef9139835e

Unlisted bounded-http candidates:

- `packages/cli/script/build.ts:258` — `fetch(checksumsUrl, { headers, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(BUN_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS) })`
- `packages/cli/script/build.ts:259` — `fetch(url, { headers, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(BUN_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS) })`
- `packages/cli/script/build.ts:264` — `const [data, checksums] = await Promise.all([response.arrayBuffer(), checksumsResponse.text()])`
- `packages/cli/script/build.ts:277` — `const pending = fetch(\`https://api.github.com/repos/oven-sh/bun/releases/tags/${release}?...\`, {` (the deadline signal is on the following line, so the sweep's first-line key no longer matches the old disposition)

Stale allowlist entries (script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt):

- the `const response = await fetch(url, {` entry (:272) and the `const pending = fetch(...)` entry (:273) no longer match any sweep pattern — de19ec16f5 restructured both fetches.
- Worse, the surviving disposition text is now factually wrong: :272/:273 describe these fetches as "with no deadline, tracked by #1159", but de19ec16f5 (2026-11-03, "fix(cli): verify Bun compiler archive before use") added `AbortSignal.timeout(BUN_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS)` to both, and #1159 is closed. The :274 `response.json()` disposition still matches its line but also cites the closed #1159 as its tracker.

## Remaining genuine surface

The downloads are now deadline-bounded and the archive is SHA-256-verified against SHASUMS256.txt before use (de19ec16f5), but the body reads at :264 are still uncapped in flight: `response.arrayBuffer()` buffers the whole Bun archive and `checksumsResponse.text()` buffers the whole checksums file, bounded only by the deadline. The archive is consumed whole (verify + unzip), so a disposition stating the deadline + verify-before-use reasoning may be the right remedy rather than a streaming rewrite — that call is triage's.

## Why it matters

check:bounded-http is the regression net for the bounded-http bug class (#1127 family). Dispositions that describe the opposite of the current code ("no deadline" for a fetch that has one, tracking by a closed issue) train readers to distrust the allowlist, and the four undispositioned sites hide the next real finding behind gate red that everyone assumes is #1540's.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The two stale build.ts entries are removed from `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt`; the surviving :274 `response.json()` disposition is re-keyed/reworded so it no longer cites closed #1159 as its tracker.
- [ ] Each of build.ts:258, :259, :264, :277 is either bounded at the site or dispositioned with text that accurately describes the current code (AbortSignal.timeout deadline; archive verified against SHASUMS256.txt before use; whole-archive read is by design, if that is the verdict).
- [ ] After the change, `bun script/check-bounded-http.ts` reports no build.ts findings (remaining red is #1540's api.ts scope only).
- [ ] No behavior change to the Bun download/verify flow in `packages/cli/script/build.ts`.

Related: #1159 (closed — original bounded-download issue for this file), #1394 / #1425 (script-tree scan that brought this file into the gate), de19ec16f5 (the rewrite), #1540 (the api.ts remainder of this gate's red), #1127 (bounded-by-default design).

# fix(ci): check:proto-reads red for embeddings-native truncateVector — one undispositioned site landed with the native embeddings backend

## Problem

`bun script/check-proto-reads.ts` exits 1 on clean `origin/main` `775b70088219c5aa21c86595d79ac6b89feea173` (verified this run in a laptop archive probe of that SHA, and the site re-verified by a raw `gh api` read at the same SHA). Of the four unlisted candidates the gate reports, three are already tracked by #1476 (`generate.ts:171`, `systemone.ts:235`, `muse-attestation.ts:90`) and the one stale allowlist entry (`model-route-tuning.ts` unit line) is already tracked by #1540. The remaining site is new and listed by neither issue:

```
Unlisted prototype-chain read candidate at packages/core/src/embeddings-native.ts:139:
  for (let index = 0; index < dimensions; index++) sliced[index] = full[index] ?? 0
```

## Origin

`packages/core/src/embeddings-native.ts` was added 2026-11-03 by commit `b56245df9b` ("feat(core): native in-process embeddings backend behind the registry (#1554 step 2)") — after #1476 was filed (2026-11-02, against main `d96751c983`), so its sweep of `packages/core/src` could not have listed this file. #1476's acceptance criteria include "gate exits 0 on main", so this site must be dispositioned either there or here; it is filed separately, following the #1540 precedent of tracking merge-wave gate drift in its own issue rather than silently expanding an earlier issue's site list.

## Site analysis (disposition-shaped, not a live prototype bug)

- `full` is a fresh plain array built at the only call site, `embeddings-native.ts:174`: `Array.from(data.subarray(rowIndex * input.nativeDimensions, (rowIndex + 1) * input.nativeDimensions))`, where `data` is the ONNX `Float32Array` output.
- The read key `index` is a numeric loop variable bounded by `dimensions`, and the branch is only reached when `dimensions < nativeDimensions` (lines 135–137 return/throw otherwise). The key is never a caller-controlled string, so the harmful prototype-chain form behind #833/#865/#916/#1085 (attacker-named keys like `toString`/`constructor` on a plain record) is not reachable here.
- A short `data` array makes `full[index]` yield `undefined` → `?? 0`; that short-output behavior is the output-width validation gap already tracked by #1583 and is explicitly out of scope here.

So the expected remedy is an accurate allowlist disposition in `script/check-proto-reads.allowlist.txt` stating the safe-by-construction reason above (or an equivalent guard if triage prefers code over disposition).

## Why it matters

The proto-reads gate is the regression net for the prototype-chain read class. While it stays red for an undispositioned site, the next real instance can land unnoticed behind the noise — the same drift pattern as #1514 and #1540, one merge wave later.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/core/src/embeddings-native.ts:139` is dispositioned in `script/check-proto-reads.allowlist.txt` with the safe-by-construction reason (fresh `Array.from` numeric array, numeric bounded loop index, no caller-controlled key), or guarded at the site
- [ ] After #1476 and #1540 also land, `bun script/check-proto-reads.ts` reports no unlisted candidate for `embeddings-native.ts` and no new stale entries
- [ ] No behavior change to `truncateVector` or the native embeddings path (the width-validation behavior stays #1583's scope)

Related: #1476 (the gate's other three core sites), #1540 (the stale tuning entry), #1583 (output-width validation in the same file), #1369 (proto-reads coverage of the remaining trees).

# fix(www): services/www OpenAPI copies stale again — protocol regenerated by PR #1587 without regenerating www, check:generated red on main

## Summary

`packages/protocol/openapi.json` was regenerated in PR #1587 (session-create `directory` query parameter + new description text) and already carried the `hidden` model field added after PR #1547, but the two verbatim copies under `services/www` were not regenerated. `services/www`'s `check:generated` therefore fails on current main: the published www API documentation is missing the `directory` parameter, the updated session-create description, and the `hidden` field.

This is a recurrence of #1498 (same copies, previous drift wave, fixed by regeneration in PR #1499). The drift source this time is #1587, which updated `packages/protocol/openapi.json` and the generated clients but not the www copies.

## Evidence (verified on origin/main `cbdb6a24e86c4869a204591c812844cb1948ce97`, 2026-11-03)

- `services/www/script/generate-openapi.ts:3-4` copies `packages/protocol/openapi.json` verbatim to `services/www/openapi.json` and `services/www/public/openapi.json`.
- Checksums differ: both www copies are identical to each other (`md5 905c898b0fe3c35b15987d439047ff3d`) and both differ from `packages/protocol/openapi.json` (`md5 6d320ecc2334fab09fade2bc06156f2b`).
- Running the check on a clean tree of origin/main (laptop probe):
  `cd services/www && bun script/generate-openapi.ts --check` → exit 1, "Generated OpenAPI documents are stale. Run `bun run generate` from services/www."
- Diff (www copy vs protocol source) includes:
  - session create: www has `"parameters": []`; protocol adds the optional `directory` query parameter (`AbsolutePath | null`).
  - session create description: protocol adds the payload-precedence / directory-vs-parentID wording from #1587; www still has the old text.
  - `hidden` boolean properties present in protocol, absent in www (the #1560-era protocol drift, now landed in protocol but never propagated to www).
- Dedup: open-issue scan for openapi/www finds only #1560 (the protocol-side staleness — protocol itself now carries both changes) and #1098 (unrelated console fetch bounds). #1498 covered the previous drift instance and is closed.

## Why it matters

The www site serves these copies as the public API reference. Right now the published docs omit a real session-create parameter (`directory`, shipped in #1587 / issue #1570) and a real model field (`hidden`), so API consumers reading the docs cannot discover behavior the server actually implements. Because the test workflow that contains the wired `Check generated documentation` step (`test.yml`, unit job) is not currently running on main, the red check surfaces nowhere — each protocol regeneration can silently strand the www copies again, as it now has twice (#1498, this issue).

## Acceptance criteria

- `services/www/openapi.json` and `services/www/public/openapi.json` are byte-identical to `packages/protocol/openapi.json` on main.
- `bun run check:generated` from `services/www` exits 0 on main.
- The regenerated copies include the session-create `directory` query parameter and the `hidden` model field.
- No other files change (regeneration of the www OpenAPI copies only; the CLI schema half of `bun run generate` is out of scope unless it also proves stale, in which case note it on this issue rather than bundling silently).

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode, verified this run against origin/main `cbdb6a24e86c4869a204591c812844cb1948ce97`.

# fix(schema): route windows accept `from` >= `until` — a window that can never be active decodes cleanly and disagrees with the runtime parser

## Summary

`Config.ModelRoute.Window` carries epoch bounds `from` ("Epoch milliseconds before which the window never applies") and `until` ("Epoch milliseconds after which the window never applies"). Setting `from` >= `until` describes a window that can never be active, but the config schema accepts it with no error or diagnostic. The runtime window parser in core *does* reject exactly this combination — by silently dropping the window — so the two layers disagree: config that validates is later discarded (or, where the parsed form is not used, simply never matches), and a target or schedule gated on that window silently never applies (or, with an inverted gate, always applies).

## Evidence (verified on origin/main `cbdb6a24e8`, 2026-11-03)

Schema — `packages/schema/src/config/model-routes.ts`, `Window` class: `from` and `until` are plain optional `PositiveInt` fields; no cross-field check.

Decode probe (laptop, `Schema.decodeUnknownSync(ConfigModelRoutes.Window)`, mirroring `packages/schema/test/config.test.ts`):

- `{ from: 2000, until: 1000 }` → **ACCEPTED**
- Control `{ from: 1000, until: 2000 }` → ACCEPTED (correct)

Runtime disagreement — `packages/core/src/model-route-schedule.ts`:

- The parser rejects the combination outright: line 333, `if (result.from !== undefined && result.until !== undefined && result.from >= result.until) return undefined` — the window is dropped, with no diagnostic surfaced to the operator.
- `active()` (lines 407–408) can never return true for such a window in any case: `now < from` and `now >= until` cover every instant when `from >= until`.

So one layer says the config is valid, the other says the window does not exist, and neither tells the operator. A mistyped bound (e.g. transposed digits in an epoch-ms value) turns a peak-hours window, a holiday exclusion calendar, or a target eligibility gate off forever, silently.

## Why it matters

Windows gate target eligibility (`window` on route targets, including `{ name, invert: true }` forms — an inverted gate on a never-active window is *always* open), schedule applicability, and `excludeWindows` holiday calendars. A silently dead window misroutes traffic in exactly the time-bound cases the operator configured it for, and the schema/runtime disagreement means the failure mode depends on which code path reads the window.

## Acceptance criteria

- Decoding a `Window` with `from >= until` (both set) fails at config decode with a clear error naming the bounds — matching, at the schema layer, the invariant the runtime parser already enforces (same remedy shape as the #1163 / PR #1578 `Escalation` cross-field check in the same file).
- Windows with only one bound set, or with `from < until`, decode and behave exactly as today.
- New tests in `packages/schema/test/config.test.ts`: `from > until` and `from == until` rejected; one-sided and ordered bounds accepted.
- The decode rejection and the runtime parser's drop agree (no config the schema accepts is silently dropped by `ModelRouteSchedule.parse` for this reason).

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode, verified this run against origin/main `cbdb6a24e8`.

# fix(schema): route schedules accept both `factor` and `weight` (and neither) — "exactly one" is documented but never enforced

## Summary

`Config.ModelRoute.Schedule` documents that exactly one of `factor` and `weight` is expected, but nothing enforces it — at schema decode, in config normalization, or in the core weight interpreter. A schedule with both set silently discards `factor`; a schedule with neither set matches its window and targets and then changes nothing. The operator believes a weight change is in force (or scaled as written) and routing silently does something else. The same pair, with the same gap, exists on `GlobalSchedule`.

## Evidence (verified on origin/main `cbdb6a24e8`, 2026-11-03)

Schema — `packages/schema/src/config/model-routes.ts`:

- `Schedule.factor` is annotated: "Multiplies the target's configured weight while the window is active. … Exactly one of factor and weight is expected." Both `factor` and `weight` are plain `optional` fields; there is no `.check` / cross-field filter on `Schedule` or on `GlobalSchedule` (which carries the same pair).

Decode probe (laptop, `Schema.decodeUnknownSync`, mirroring `packages/schema/test/config.test.ts`):

- Route with `schedules: [{ when: {}, factor: 2, weight: 5 }]` → **ACCEPTED**
- Route with `schedules: [{ when: {} }]` (neither) → **ACCEPTED**
- `GlobalSchedule` with `{ when: {}, factor: 2, weight: 5 }` → **ACCEPTED**; with `{ when: {} }` → **ACCEPTED**
- Control: factor-only schedule → ACCEPTED (correct)

Runtime consequence — `packages/core/src/model-route.ts`, `scheduled()` (lines 2455–2463):

```ts
if (rule.weight !== undefined) weight = rule.weight
else if (rule.factor !== undefined) weight *= rule.factor
```

- Both set: `weight` wins and `factor` is silently ignored — a schedule written to *scale* instead *replaces* the weight (or the operator's later `factor` edit has no effect).
- Neither set: the rule matches its window/targets and applies nothing — a silently inert schedule.

The internal `WeightRule` struct in the same file (lines 81–90) also carries both fields as plain optionals, and `packages/core/src/config/normalize.ts` emits no diagnostic for either combination.

## Why this shape of fix

This is the same class of gap as #1163, fixed in PR #1578 by adding a decode-time cross-field check to `Escalation` in this very file (`EscalationClass.check(Schema.makeFilter(...))`, with defaults applied so one-sided overrides are checked too). Cross-field invariants the fields cannot state alone belong at decode, with a clear error — not as a silent precedence rule or a silent no-op at interpretation time.

## Acceptance criteria

- Decoding a `Schedule` or `GlobalSchedule` with **both** `factor` and `weight` set fails with an error naming the exactly-one rule.
- Decoding a `Schedule` or `GlobalSchedule` with **neither** set fails the same way (a schedule that changes nothing is a configuration error, not a rule).
- Schedules with exactly one of the two fields decode and behave exactly as today (weight replaces, factor scales).
- New tests in `packages/schema/test/config.test.ts` covering both/neither/exactly-one for both classes, mirroring the #1163 boundary tests.
- If any field description text changes, the generated OpenAPI/JSON-schema artifacts are regenerated in the same change (see #1560 for the protocol staleness this otherwise adds to).

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode, verified this run against origin/main `cbdb6a24e8`.

## Finding (from PR review)

Codex (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]) raised this P2 finding on open PR #1473 and it was never fixed or replied to:

- PR: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1473 — "fix(core): let due bench probes recover quota-exhausted pools" (OPEN)
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1473#discussion_r4449550443 (2026-11-03T00:50:22Z, on `packages/core/src/model-route.ts`)
- Essence: "When a benched leaf learns an early reset and subsequently receives a known-full snapshot with a later reset (or acquires a balance hold), `probeDue()` becomes true at the earlier reset even though its independent quota gate still blocks recovery. `armBenchProbe()` deliberately retains the earliest reset, so this condition is possible through the existing quota observers. Unconditionally removing that leaf from the count makes a three-leaf pool with two quota-out members appear recovered, allowing the resolver to select the untried third member rather than the outside fallback, even though neither exhausted member can actually probe. Only carve out a due probe when its independent quota gate also permits admission; otherwise the pool's hard exclusion is lifted prematurely."

## No-response evidence

- The review thread contains only the Codex comment; no reply followed it (reviewThreads check 2026-11-04: thread unresolved, sole author chatgpt-codex-connector).
- The PR's only commit (aee912ad6f, 2026-11-03T00:46:48Z) predates the comment (2026-11-03T00:50:22Z); no fix commit followed it. The comment is over 24 hours old on a still-open PR (grace rule met).

## Still live on the PR head (verified 2026-11-04 by gh api raw read at aee912ad6f)

`packages/core/src/model-route.ts`:
- `armBenchProbe` (~line 480) retains the earliest reset: `if (state.benchQuotaResetAt !== undefined && state.benchQuotaResetAt <= resetAt) return`.
- `probeDueState` (~line 488) judges due-ness from `benchQuotaResetAt` alone; it does not consult the leaf's independent quota gate (balance hold / later known-full snapshot reset).
- `poolQuotaExhausted` (~line 660): `if (probeDue(target, credentialID, now)) continue` — a due-probe leaf is removed from the exhaustion count unconditionally, so a 3-leaf pool with 2 quota-out leaves can drop below the `POOL_QUOTA_LEAVES` threshold and lose its hard exclusion even when the due leaf's own quota gate still blocks admission.

Related but distinct: issue #1390 tracks the inverse defect (pool exclusion defeating due probes); this finding is about the carve-out over-lifting exclusion. It is not covered by #1390.

## Acceptance criteria

- `poolQuotaExhausted` only carves out a due-probe leaf when that leaf's independent quota gate also permits admission (no active balance hold, no later known-full snapshot reset still ahead); otherwise the leaf keeps counting toward pool exhaustion.
- A regression test covers the scenario: benched leaf with an early bench reset plus a later independent quota block, in a pool at the exhaustion threshold — the pool stays excluded and the resolver takes the outside fallback.
- Or: the finding is resolved on this issue by a documented decision with reasoning recorded.

# fix(ai): Gemini schema normalize only cuts single-def `$ref` loops — mutually recursive `$defs` through required properties reach Gemini uncut

## Summary

`GeminiJsonSchema.normalize` (`packages/ai/src/protocols/utils/gemini-json-schema.ts`) is supposed to make tool schemas safe for Gemini's `parametersJsonSchema`: per the module's own comment (lines 45–46), "Gemini accepts a recursive `$ref` only when the loop passes through an optional property or potentially empty array `items`", and `cutLoops` replaces other self-references with an unconstrained schema `{}`.

The cutting only ever tracks **one target at a time**: `normalize` (lines 63–76) runs one pass per `$defs`/`definitions` entry with that entry's own target (`#/$defs/<name>`), plus one pass for the root target `#`. `cutLoops` walks the literal schema tree and never resolves a `$ref` into another def's body — so a cycle that spans **two or more defs** is invisible to every pass. A mutually recursive pair whose steps all pass through required properties (or `items` with `minItems > 0`) is sent to Gemini exactly as written, in precisely the shape the module exists to prevent.

## Evidence (verified on `origin/main` ae5d592093, laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-03-gemini-mutual`, `GeminiJsonSchema.normalize` run under bun)

Control — direct self-loop through a required property is cut, as intended:

- Input `$defs.node.properties.child = { $ref: "#/$defs/node" }`, `required: ["child"]`
- Output: `child` becomes `{}`.

Bug — mutual recursion, every step required, survives intact:

- Input: `$defs.A = { properties: { b: { $ref: "#/$defs/B" } }, required: ["b"] }`, `$defs.B = { properties: { a: { $ref: "#/$defs/A" } }, required: ["a"] }`, root `properties.root = { $ref: "#/$defs/A" }`
- Output is byte-for-byte the same cycle: A still requires a B, B still requires an A. No step in the cycle passes through an optional property or a potentially empty `items`, so by the module's stated rule Gemini does not accept this shape.

Control — the same mutual pair with the A→B step optional is (correctly) kept, because the loop can terminate:

- `A` without `required: ["b"]` → output keeps both refs. Any fix must preserve this case (and the `items`/`minItems` analogue).

The same gap applies to cycles of length ≥ 2 through `definitions` (same code path), and to mixed cycles where the inter-def steps are `items` with `minItems > 0`.

## Why it matters

This projection runs on every Gemini-family tool schema (`ToolSchemaProjection.gemini`, selected in `packages/ai/src/protocols/utils/tool-schema.ts:49` and applied to all tools before a request is built). Tools with recursive data models (trees, nested comments, ASTs, org charts) commonly split the recursion across two named defs; when every link is required, the uncut cycle reaches Gemini unaltered — the class of schema the normalizer was written to keep off the wire — instead of degrading to the unconstrained-`{}` fallback the single-def case gets.

## Acceptance criteria

- `GeminiJsonSchema.normalize` cuts (replaces with `{}`) at least one `$ref` in any cycle whose steps never pass through an optional property or a potentially empty `items` — including cycles spanning two or more `$defs`/`definitions` entries.
- Cycles that DO pass through an optional property or a potentially empty `items` at any step are preserved unchanged (existing controls above keep passing).
- Existing single-def and root-`#` loop behavior is unchanged.
- New unit tests in `packages/ai` (e.g. alongside `test/tool-schema-projection.test.ts`) cover: mutual A↔B required (cut), mutual A↔B with one optional step (kept), and a 3-def required cycle (cut).

# fix(core): ModelResolver bare-alias tests red on main — #1547's `models.all()` call has no implementation in the test's Model mock

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-03 at origin/main `ae5d592093`)

`packages/core` test file `test/session-runner-model.test.ts`, run through the package's own test entry:

```
cd packages/core && bun run script/test.ts test/session-runner-model.test.ts
→ 5 pass / 2 fail
(fail) ModelResolver bare aliases > expands a bare-alias target that carries its own variant
(fail) ModelResolver bare aliases > expands a bare-alias target without a variant to the alias target's variant

UnimplementedError: @opencode/Model: Unimplemented method "all"
  at packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts:1226
  at ModelResolver.resolve (test/session-runner-model.test.ts:121)
```

Root cause:

- `abd9ca42e0` ("fix(core): keep hidden models execution-eligible and reveal them on exact-name picker search (#230)", merged via PR #1547) changed `ModelResolver.resolve` to compute alias precedence against the full model list: `model-resolver.ts:1226` — `const availableModels = (yield* models.all()).filter((model) => model.enabled)`.
- The test's resolver layer (`test/session-runner-model.test.ts`, the `Layer.mock(Model.Service, …)` in the `resolver` layer) implements only `get` and `available`. `Layer.mock` throws `UnimplementedError` for any other method, so both `ModelResolver bare aliases` tests die before asserting anything. The sibling `SessionRunnerModel bare aliases` tests pass because that path receives its catalog through a callback instead.

Bisection (same command, laptop probe of each tree):

- `f61305aa1b` (parent of `abd9ca42e0`): **7 pass / 0 fail**
- `abd9ca42e0` and current main `ae5d592093`: **5 pass / 2 fail**

Full core suite on main for context: 8131 pass / 11 fail — the other 9 are already tracked (#1484 ×2, #1551, #1552, and 4 native-embeddings tests that need the libstdc++ loader path documented on #1554) or preload-env artifacts of bypassing `script/test.ts`. These 2 are the only untracked red.

## Why it matters

These are the only tests covering bare-alias expansion through `ModelResolver.resolve` itself — the #391 semantics that a user's explicit variant wins over the alias target's variant. Since #1547 they have asserted nothing: alias precedence (a real model keeps precedence over an alias, hidden or not — the exact behavior #1547 added) can regress silently while the suite looks "only known-red". A red-on-main test file also trains every subsequent run to ignore failures in this file.

## Acceptance criteria

- `bun run script/test.ts test/session-runner-model.test.ts` from `packages/core` passes 7/7 on main.
- The fix keeps #230/#1547 semantics intact: alias precedence is still judged against the full enabled model list (including picker-hidden models), not narrowed back to the picker-visible `available()` set.
- The mock's `all()` returns entries in the real `Model.Service.all` shape (with `enabled`, `providerID`, `id`) so the resolver's `exists` check is genuinely exercised — including at least the catalog model the alias points at.
- Full `packages/core` suite loses exactly these 2 failures and gains no new ones.

# fix(core): native embeddings never validate the ONNX output width — a graph whose `sentence_embedding` width differs from the registration silently misassigns vectors

## Problem

The native in-process embeddings backend (`packages/core/src/embeddings-native.ts`, #1554 step 2) slices the model's flat output buffer by the *registered* `nativeDimensions` without ever checking that the graph actually produced that many floats per input:

- `embedNative` (embeddings-native.ts, the `model.run(...)` result handling): `data` is used unchecked; each row is `data.subarray(rowIndex * nativeDimensions, (rowIndex + 1) * nativeDimensions)`.
- `truncateVector` builds its result from `full[index] ?? 0`, so a short row is silently zero-padded to the requested length.
- The caller's guard in `packages/core/src/embeddings.ts` (native branch, ~:305-312) only checks each returned vector's `length` — which the slicing/padding above makes pass even when the underlying rows are wrong.

The HTTP backend path validates the analogous invariants (count, per-vector length, and — since #1449 / PR #1571 — the exact index set). The native path validates none of the output-shape invariants.

## Verified (laptop probe, origin/main 68ccd202b4)

Probe test in a scratch copy of `packages/core`, with `onnxruntime-node` and `@huggingface/transformers` mocked (fake snapshot dir with `tokenizer.json` + graph file present), tokenizer returning 2 ids per input:

1. Graph outputs **8-wide** vectors, registration claims `nativeDimensions: 4`, inputs `["a", "bb"]`, graph data = `1..16`:
   - Returned vectors: `[[1,2,3,4],[5,6,7,8]]`
   - The second input's true vector is `[9..16]`; it silently received the **tail of the first input's vector**. Both returned vectors have length 4, so the `embeddings.ts` length check passes.
2. Graph outputs **2-wide** vectors, registration claims 4:
   - Returned vectors: `[[0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5],[]]` — row 0 is two inputs' data concatenated, row 1 is fabricated/empty; with a Matryoshka `dimensions` request, `truncateVector`'s `?? 0` fill manufactures right-length zero-padded vectors instead of failing.

A registration/graph mismatch (wrong snapshot paired with a registration, a re-exported graph with a different output width, a future model swap in step 3 of #1554) therefore corrupts embeddings silently instead of failing loudly — the same failure class #1449 fixed for the HTTP backend.

## Why it matters

- Embeddings feed semantic indexing/search; silently wrong vectors degrade results with no error anywhere.
- Step 3 of #1554 flips registrations to the native backend — this is exactly the moment a snapshot/registration mismatch becomes likely.
- The module's own header stresses "reject loudly, never silently" semantics everywhere else (context limit, missing snapshot files); the output shape is the one unchecked invariant.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `embedNative` validates the model output before slicing: the returned tensor's total length (or its dims) must equal `inputs.length * nativeDimensions`; any mismatch throws an error naming the expected and actual widths
- [ ] Regression tests (mocked `onnxruntime-node` / `@huggingface/transformers`, no real model artifact needed): wider-than-registered output rejects; narrower-than-registered output rejects; correct-width output returns per-row vectors unchanged
- [ ] Existing native parity tests and the HTTP-backend embeddings tests still pass
- [ ] No behavior change when the graph width matches the registration

Related: #1449 (HTTP index-set validation, same class), #1554 (native backend epic), #1567 (native load-cache poisoning — distinct).

body:
## Finding

The main-broken race-loser reconcile in `.github/workflows/main-broken.yml` ends with a status echo that lost its survivor issue number:

```bash
echo "this run created loser #$CREATED -- its links were forwarded to # above"
```

The `#` is followed by nothing — the `$SURVIVOR` reference the line carried before PR #1315 is gone, so the workflow log no longer says which issue the created loser's run links were forwarded to. When several reconciles run, that log line is the only place the created-loser → survivor pairing is recorded outside the issue comments themselves.

## Evidence

- Introduced by PR #1315 (fix(ci): preserve inherited run links in main-broken reconcile (#1314)), commit `18215ebe6` ("fix(ci): reconcile adjacent run links and stage comments"). The PR's diff changes the line from `... forwarded to #$SURVIVOR above` to `... forwarded to # above`.
- Still present on current main: `.github/workflows/main-broken.yml:288` (verified 2026-11-03 against the `main` branch head via the contents API).
- PR #1315's regression test (`script/main-broken-reconcile.test.ts`) executes only the shell between the `RUN-LINKS-BEGIN`/`RUN-LINKS-END` markers; this echo sits after `RUN-LINKS-END`, outside the pinned region, which is why the test suite did not catch the regression.

## Why it matters

The main-broken watcher is the fleet's signal that main is broken. Its reconcile log is an audit trail for which duplicate was closed into which survivor; a line that names the loser but not the survivor forces a reader to reconstruct the pairing from issue comments across several issues.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The closing echo in `.github/workflows/main-broken.yml` names the survivor again (restores the `$SURVIVOR` interpolation dropped in PR #1315).
- [ ] The pinned-region test in `script/main-broken-reconcile.test.ts` (or an equivalent check) covers this final status line — e.g. the tested shell region is extended, or a fixture asserts the CREATED-branch echo contains the survivor number — so the line cannot silently lose the reference again.
- [ ] No other reconcile behaviour changes (run-link collection, dedupe, survivor/loser comment bodies stay as PR #1315 left them).

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #1315 (batch PR #1298–#1324, developing-today/opencode).

body:
## Failure mode

The `opencode-node_modules` fixed-output derivation (nix/node_modules.nix, hash recorded in nix/hashes.json) silently rots when the flake-lock follows-graph moves the toolchain: the recorded `outputHash` was stamped under one nixpkgs/bun, and after `nixpkgs` began following the fleet pin (7572064620, 2026-11-02 — landed on main *after* the last x86_64-linux stamp in 2ec20071af), `bun install` under bun 1.4.4 produces a different — but fully deterministic — node_modules tree for a byte-identical `bun.lock`/`package.json`. Nothing fails until someone actually builds the package, which in practice means the fleet NixOS switch discovers it.

## Instance: 2026-11-03 fleet switch failure

```
error: hash mismatch in fixed-output derivation '/nix/store/22bgylscwqq0yy7fp4jv5npdy0af7w73-opencode-node_modules-2.0.30+e57af29.drv':
         specified: sha256-/LjrX3eMVnwjXBmNU69z/VkwuBdhA2o2Ajp0VaSmP+8=
            got:    sha256-MDhMpRl2bCwfsocwx8gWtLfKsdd/p2BO+CRvYWGZxIc=
```
(switch-20261103-164658.log lines 1177-1180; SWITCH_EXIT=1, generation unchanged.)

## Determinism evidence

The "got" hash `sha256-MDhMpRl2bCwfsocwx8gWtLfKsdd/p2BO+CRvYWGZxIc=` was reproduced identically in three independent builds: the failed switch build (fork e57af29 via the code flake) and two consecutive laptop builds of `.#opencode.node_modules` at fork main 68ccd20. This is a stale stamp, not install nondeterminism — the fix is restamping, and the recurrence risk is any future toolchain move via the follows-graph (fleet nixpkgs pin bumps) invalidating the stamp again without touching bun.lock.

## Notes

- Only x86_64-linux was rebuilt and restamped; aarch64-linux / aarch64-darwin stamps were not re-verified (no builder available) and may be stale in the same way.
- A guard worth considering: a CI job or flake check that builds `.#opencode.node_modules` when flake.lock / hashes.json changes, so rot surfaces on the PR that moves the toolchain instead of at switch time.

## Acceptance criteria
- After a follows-graph move of the bun toolchain, the recorded `opencode-node_modules` outputHash in nix/hashes.json either still matches or is re-stamped in the same change that moves the toolchain — a fleet switch no longer discovers the rot.
- A guard exists (CI check, switch preflight, or documented stamp step) that fails loudly when `bun install` output under the pinned toolchain diverges from the recorded hash for a byte-identical bun.lock/package.json.
- The 2026-11-03 failure instance (specified sha256-/LjrX3eMVnwjXBmNU69z/VkwuBdhA2o2Ajp0VaSmP+8= vs got sha256-MDhMpRl2bCwfsocwx8gWtLfKsdd/p2BO+CRvYWGZxIc=) is dispositioned: hash re-stamped under bun 1.4.4 or the toolchain pin adjusted, with the choice recorded on this issue.

# fix(ai): moonshot tool-schema projection drops `prefixItems` when `items` is also present — position constraints are silently replaced

## Summary

In `packages/ai/src/protocols/utils/tool-schema.ts`, `moonshotNode` translates 2020-12 tuple schemas for Moonshot/Kimi targets. When a node carries `prefixItems` alone, the positions are folded into an `items` anyOf (the function's tested approximation). But when a node carries **both** `prefixItems` and `items` — the standard 2020-12 way to say "these positions have these types, the rest have that type" — the `prefixItems` branch returns `[]` (tool-schema.ts:31-34, `if ("items" in schema) return []`) and the positions vanish. The surviving `items` schema then applies to *every* element, including position 0, so the projected schema does not merely lose the position constraint — it contradicts it.

## Evidence (verified this run against origin/main e57af295bb, laptop probe tree)

Probe importing the real module (`ToolSchemaProjection.moonshot`):

- Input: `{type:"object", properties:{ pair:{ type:"array", prefixItems:[{type:"string"}], items:{type:"integer"} } }}`
- Output: `{"type":"object","properties":{"pair":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"integer"}}}}` — element 0, required to be a string by the source schema, is now declared an integer like every other element.
- Control, `prefixItems` alone: `[{type:"string"},{type:"integer"}]` → `items:{anyOf:[{type:"string"},{type:"integer"}]}` — the fold the both-present case skips.

Existing coverage (`packages/ai/test/tool-schema-projection.test.ts`): the tuple test (~line 199) covers an `items` array alone and `prefixItems` alone, never the two together — this combination is untested, unlike the neighboring deliberate behaviors in the same function (the `$ref`-sibling strip at tool-schema.ts:25 is intentional and pinned by that same test; it is explicitly out of scope here).

## Why it matters

`ToolSchemaProjection` runs on every tool schema for Kimi/Moonshot models, including models reached through gateways and OpenAI-compatible endpoints (model-name selection in `modelCompatibility`). Fixed-shape tuple parameters (coordinate pairs with a trailing free list, [name, ...values] shapes) are exactly the schemas that carry both keywords. Today those tools are advertised to the model with a wrong element type for their leading positions — the model generates arguments the tool then rejects, or the provider validates against a schema the tool never declared.

## Acceptance criteria

- A node carrying both `prefixItems` and `items` projects to a schema that keeps every prefix position's constraint reachable (e.g. fold the prefix branches together with the `items` schema into the same anyOf the prefixItems-only path already produces), instead of discarding `prefixItems`.
- `prefixItems`-only and `items`-only (array and schema forms) projections are byte-identical to today.
- A regression test in `packages/ai/test/tool-schema-projection.test.ts` covers the both-present combination, including a single-element `prefixItems`.
- The deliberate `$ref`-sibling strip and the `unevaluatedItems` drop are unchanged.

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode (fleet role map: developing-today/code#2131; implementation #2152). Probe tree: laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-03-creator3` at origin/main e57af295bb.

# fix(ai): antigravity convertSchema inverts boolean `false` subschemas — a never-valid schema is sent upstream as unconstrained

## Summary

`convertSchema` in `packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts` treats every non-record node as an empty schema. A JSON Schema boolean `false` subschema — which means *no value is valid* — therefore comes out as `{}` — *every value is valid*. The conversion silently inverts the constraint instead of dropping a field (the allowlist's usual, safe failure mode).

## Evidence (verified this run against origin/main e57af295bb, laptop probe tree)

`convertSchemaNode` opens with (`packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts`, in `convertSchemaNode`):

```ts
if (!isRecord(node)) return {}
```

so any boolean node becomes `{}`. Probe output (`bun`, calling the exported `convertSchema`):

- `properties: { extra: false, name: {type:"string"} }` → `{"properties":{"extra":{},"name":{"type":"STRING"}},"type":"OBJECT","required":["name"]}` — a property the client schema forbids outright is offered upstream as a free-form parameter.
- `{type:"array", items: false}` → `{"items":{},"type":"ARRAY"}` — an array that may hold no elements is sent as an array of anything (and now also satisfies the #1548 synthesized-items shape, so nothing downstream notices).
- `properties: { v: { anyOf: [{type:"string"}, false] } }` → `anyOf: [{"type":"STRING"}, {}]` — an `anyOf` with a `{}` branch is always satisfied, so the whole property becomes unconstrained, not just the dead branch.
- Top-level `false` → `{"type":"OBJECT"}` — a never-valid tool input becomes an unconstrained object input.

`resolveSchemaRefs` has the same shape: its `walk` returns non-record nodes unchanged, so `false` survives ref resolution intact and is only inverted at conversion — the fix belongs in the converter (and its tests), not the resolver.

## Why it matters

Boolean schemas are how generators express "never": zod/Effect-derived tool schemas emit `false` for never-typed fields, and hand-written MCP tool schemas use `items: false` / `additionalProperties`-style never positions. Inverting never → anything means the model is told it may pass values the tool contract forbids, and the failure surfaces (if at all) as a tool-side validation error far from the cause. Sibling filings cover other silent losses in this same converter (#1556 type-union collapse, #1557 dropped `const`); this one is worse in kind, not degree: it reverses meaning rather than narrowing it.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `false` subschema never reaches the wire as `{}`. Choose and document one faithful encoding — e.g. a proto-expressible never (`not: {}` is in the converter's own `SCHEMA_FIELDS` allowlist), dropping the containing property/branch with the property also removed from `required`, or a loud conversion error for shapes that cannot be represented — applied consistently at property, `items`/`prefixItems`, `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf` branch, and root positions.
- A `true` subschema continues to convert to `{}` (unconstrained is its correct meaning).
- Tests in the antigravity protocol suite cover: `false` property, `items: false`, an `anyOf` containing `false`, top-level `false`, and `true` in the same positions as a regression guard.
- No behavior change for record schemas: the existing antigravity test suite passes unchanged.

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode (fleet role map: developing-today/code#2131; implementation #2152). Probe tree: laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-03-creator3` at origin/main e57af295bb.

body:
## Bug

`POST /api/session?directory=/some/dir` silently ignores the `directory` query parameter and creates the session at the server process's working directory. A caller that believes it scoped the session to a work directory gets a tool-enabled session running somewhere else — in the original report, the account home directory, where the session wrote a file before the cause was spotted.

Origin record (with the original benchmark report): https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/1360 — this issue is the implementation home for the fix; the code issue stays open as the record until this lands.

## Evidence at current main (e57af295bb, verified 2026-11-03)

- `packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts` — `HttpApiEndpoint.post("session.create", "/api/session", …)` declares **no query schema at all**; the payload carries an optional `location` and nothing else. The `directory` parameter is not declared, so it is dropped without a signal.
- `packages/server/src/handlers/session.ts` — the `session.create` handler builds the session with `location: ctx.payload.location ?? { directory: AbsolutePath.make(process.cwd()) }`: no payload location → the server's cwd, silently.
- The parity gap is visible in the same file: `session.list`'s `SessionsQuery` **does** declare `directory: AbsolutePath.pipe(Schema.optional)` — a caller reasonably expects create to accept what list accepts.

## Fix (preference order from the origin issue)

1. Honor `?directory=` on session create, for parity with the body's `location` (declare `directory` in the endpoint's query schema; when present it selects the location directory, with the body's `location` taking precedence if both are given — or reject the combination loudly).
2. Or return a 400 when a `directory` parameter is supplied that the endpoint will not honor.

The one unacceptable behavior is the current one: silent fallback to the server's home/cwd.

## Acceptance criteria

- No API path can produce a session in an unintended directory without an explicit, visible signal.
- A server regression test creates a session with the query param and asserts the session's location (or the 400).
- The silent fallback is gone: an ineffective `directory` param can no longer pass unnoticed.

body:
## Summary

The native in-process embeddings backend (#1559, step 2 of #1554) caches the model-load promise forever — including when the load **fails**. One failed first load permanently bricks the native backend for the life of the server process, and every later call replays the original error even after the underlying problem is fixed on disk.

## Evidence

`packages/core/src/embeddings-native.ts:94-128` (origin/main `3bd4efaaf8`):

```ts
const loadedModels = new Map<string, Promise<LoadedModel>>()

const loadModel = (snapshotDir: string, onnxFile: string): Promise<LoadedModel> => {
  const key = `${snapshotDir}\n${onnxFile}`
  const existing = loadedModels.get(key)
  if (existing) return existing
  const pending = (async (): Promise<LoadedModel> => { ... })()
  loadedModels.set(key, pending)
  return pending
}
```

The rejected promise is never evicted, so a transient first-load failure (snapshot still syncing, tokenizer.json not yet written, a briefly-missing graph file) is final.

Reproduced this run on the laptop against a clean `git archive` of origin/main, driving `embedNative` directly with a temp snapshot dir (no model artifact needed — both failures occur before any native binding loads):

```
call1 (empty snapshot dir)
  => native-onnx embeddings backend: no tokenizer.json in model snapshot /tmp/embed-snap-XXXXXX
# tokenizer.json then created in that same directory; graph still missing
call2 (tokenizer.json now present, graph still missing)
  => native-onnx embeddings backend: no tokenizer.json in model snapshot /tmp/embed-snap-XXXXXX   ← stale cached error
```

Expected call2 behavior: the load is retried and fails at the *next* real problem — `no ONNX graph at <dir>/onnx/model_int8.onnx` — or succeeds once the snapshot is complete.

## Why it matters

Step 3 of #1554 flips a registration to `native-onnx` deliberately. The first embed call after that flip is exactly when a snapshot problem is most likely (wrong path, partial HF download). Today that first failure is unrecoverable without a server restart, and the error message actively misleads: it names a file that may already exist by the time anyone reads the log. The HTTP sidecar this replaces has no equivalent failure mode — a fixed sidecar serves the very next request.

## Acceptance criteria

- A failed load is evicted from `loadedModels` (only if the map still holds that same promise), so the next `embedNative` call retries the load from disk.
- A successful load stays cached and shared exactly as today (one load per (snapshot, graph) pair; concurrent first calls still share one load).
- Regression test that needs no model artifact and no native bindings: first call against a snapshot dir missing `tokenizer.json` fails with the tokenizer error; after `tokenizer.json` is created in that dir, a second call fails with the *graph* error (proving the retry reached the next check) instead of replaying the tokenizer error. `packages/core/test/embeddings-native.test.ts` is the natural home — outside the snapshot-gated parity describe, since CI has no model file.
- Existing embeddings suites stay green: `packages/core/test/embeddings-native.test.ts`, `packages/core/test/embeddings.test.ts`.

Part of the #1554 native-embeddings series; found by the new-issue-creator sweep while verifying #1559 on main.

body:
## Problem

`packages/app`'s unit suite is red on main: 762 pass / 11 fail. All 11 failures are in two files — `src/runtime/server/health.test.ts` (3) and `src/runtime/server/image.test.ts` (8) — and all turn on `AbortSignal` handling since the generated client started composing a default 120s deadline into every non-SSE request.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probes, bisected)

- Clean `origin/main` `2fe726dc75`, `bun run test:unit` in `packages/app`: **762 pass / 11 fail** (773 tests), reproduced twice. Both files also fail solo (health 5 pass / 3 fail; image 33 pass / 8 fail) — not test pollution.
- Bisection: at commit `568c66d921^` (parent) the two files are **49 pass / 0 fail**; at `568c66d921` itself they are **38 pass / 11 fail**. That commit is "fix(client): compose a default 120s deadline into generated promise transport" — it updated the client package's own tests (`packages/client/test/promise-deadline.test.ts`, `solid-data.test.ts`) but not the app-level tests that observe signals through the client.
- Failure shapes:
  - `health.test.ts` "uses provided abort signal": expects the fetch to receive the caller's signal object (`expect(signal).toBe(abort.signal)`); it now receives the client's `AbortSignal.any([caller, deadline])` composition.
  - `health.test.ts` "allows slow servers thirty seconds by default": expects the health check's own 30s timeout to have aborted the request (`expect(aborted).toBe(true)` → received `false`) — this one is behavioral, not just identity: under composition, which signal actually fires needs re-verifying, because the health layer's 30s bound is the tighter, intentional one.
  - `image.test.ts`: all 8 `readLocalImage` success cases expect `requests[0].init.signal` to be the caller's signal; all receive the composed signal instead. The URL/location/auth assertions in the same tests pass.

## Why it matters

The app suite is one of the wired CI suites; a permanently red suite trains everyone to ignore it, and the next real regression in server health checks or local image reading lands invisibly. One of the 11 (the 30s health timeout) may also be a real behavior change under signal composition, not just a stale assertion — that needs a verdict, not a blanket test rewrite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A stated verdict for the 30s health-check case: the health layer's timeout still aborts an in-flight request under the client's deadline composition (fix the composition/health layer if it does not; fix the test's observation point if it does)
- [ ] `health.test.ts` and `image.test.ts` updated to assert the composed-signal contract (abort propagation and deadline behavior) rather than signal identity where identity is no longer the contract — or the client preserves caller-signal identity when no deadline composition is needed, with the choice stated in the PR
- [ ] `bun run test:unit` in `packages/app` green on main (773+ tests, 0 fail)
- [ ] `packages/client` tests (incl. `promise-deadline.test.ts`) still green — the 120s client deadline itself is intentional (#1385) and stays

Related: commit `568c66d921`, #1385 (client deadline). Distinct from #1522 (console-app mock pollution — different package, different mechanism; these files fail solo). Deduped against open and recently closed issues this run — no existing issue covers the app suite's signal-test failures.

## Problem

`packages/protocol`'s checked-in OpenAPI document is stale on main: `bun run check:generated` exits 1. The `hidden` field added by the hidden-models work (#230, merged in PR #1547) is in the schemas and in the regenerated client, but was never regenerated into `packages/protocol/openapi.json` — so the source document every consumer copies from does not describe a field the API actually returns.

## Evidence (verified this run on clean `origin/main` `2fe726dc75`, laptop probe tree)

- `packages/schema/src/model.ts` — `Info.hidden: Schema.Boolean.pipe(optional)` ("Picker-hidden but still routable (#230)"), plus the matching addition in `packages/schema/src/config/provider.ts` (both in PR #1547's diff).
- `packages/client/src/promise/generated/types.ts` WAS regenerated in the same PR (+2 lines) — the protocol document was the one generated artifact missed.
- In the probe: `bun run check:generated` in `packages/protocol` → "Generated OpenAPI document is stale." (exit 1). `services/www`'s `check:generated` passes only because it copies the protocol document verbatim (`services/www/script/generate-openapi.ts:3`), so both stay consistently stale.
- Running `bun run generate` in `packages/protocol` produces exactly this drift and nothing else (8 diff lines): a `"hidden": { "type": "boolean" }` property added next to `enabled` in the model Info schema, and the same property in the nested provider-config model schema.

## Why it matters

`packages/protocol/openapi.json` is the source OpenAPI document: the www docs copy it verbatim and external consumers (editor/IDE integrations, API clients) read the model shape from it. Right now it says a model record has no `hidden` field, one merge after the field shipped — the same drift class as #1493 (client) and #1498 (www), in the one artifact those fixes' source feeds from. #1500 wired this check into CI precisely so this would be caught; the document itself still needs the regen.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/protocol/openapi.json` regenerated (`bun run generate` in `packages/protocol`); the only change is the two `hidden` boolean properties from #1547
- [ ] `services/www` documents regenerated afterwards so its copies match (`bun script/generate-openapi.ts` in `services/www`), and `check:generated` exits 0 in both `packages/protocol` and `services/www`
- [ ] `packages/client` `check:generated` still exits 0 (no further client drift introduced)

Related: #230 / PR #1547 (introduced the field), #1493, #1498, #1500 (same drift class in sibling artifacts). Deduped against open and recently closed issues this run — #1500 covered wiring this check, #1498 covered the www copy; neither covers the protocol document's current drift.

body:
## Problem

`convertSchema` in `packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts` silently collapses a multi-valued JSON Schema `type` union to its first member. A tool parameter declared `type: ["string", "integer"]` is sent upstream as `STRING` only — the integer alternative is lost for both Gemini and Anthropic (Claude) targets.

## Evidence (verified this run on clean main `974ca6c76d`, laptop probe importing the real module)

`packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts:199-203`:

```ts
if (Array.isArray(node.type)) {
  const types = node.type.filter((entry): entry is string => typeof entry === "string")
  if (types.includes("null")) nullable = true
  const concrete = types.filter((entry) => entry !== "null")
  if (concrete.length) out.type = concrete[0].toUpperCase()
}
```

Every concrete member after the first is discarded, and no `anyOf`/`oneOf` branch is emitted. Probe output (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-03-creator2/probe.ts` on the laptop, module imported from main):

```
convertSchema({type:"object",properties:{mode:{type:["string","integer"]}}})
  -> {"properties":{"mode":{"type":"STRING"}},"type":"OBJECT"}
convertSchema(same, anthropic=true)
  -> {"properties":{"mode":{"type":"STRING"}},"type":"OBJECT"}
convertSchema({type:["string","integer"]})            // root level
  -> {"type":"STRING"}
convertSchema({type:"object",properties:{mode:{type:["string","null"]}}})
  -> {"properties":{"mode":{"type":"STRING","nullable":true}},"type":"OBJECT"}   // null case works
```

The single-`null` case is correct and is pinned by a test (`packages/ai/test/provider/antigravity.test.ts:48` uses `type: ["string", "null"]`). There is no test for a multi-concrete-type union.

## Why it matters

The proto Schema's `type` is a single enum, so a union cannot be represented as-is — but this same function already has the faithful machinery: #1550 folds `anyOf` into `oneOf` branches for Anthropic targets and passes `anyOf` through for Gemini (antigravity.ts:173-184). A union type is exactly a branch set, one branch per concrete type.

Union-typed parameters are common in real tool schemas (an id that is a string or an integer, a value that is a number or a boolean). Today the model is told the parameter accepts only the first type: on Anthropic targets the re-serialized `input_schema` then misdescribes the tool, and integer/boolean values a caller legitimately supplies are outside the declared schema. This is the same silent-constraint-loss class as #1548 (bare array → missing `items`) and #1550 (`anyOf` mishandling), in the same converter.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `type` array with two or more concrete (non-`null`) members converts to one branch per concrete type — `anyOf` for Gemini targets, `oneOf` for Anthropic targets (consistent with the #1550 fold) — with the node's remaining applicable keywords (description, enum, numeric bounds, items/properties per branch type, etc.) preserved rather than dropped.
- [ ] `"null"` in the array still produces `nullable: true` alongside the branches; `["string", "null"]` output is byte-identical to today (STRING + nullable).
- [ ] Single-member and plain-string `type` behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/antigravity.test.ts`: multi-type union at a property and at the root, for both targets; the `["string","null"]` case stays pinned.
- [ ] `bun test` in `packages/ai` green (1894 pass / 0 fail at main `974ca6c76d` before the change).

Related: #1548, #1550 (same converter, same class). Deduped against open and recently closed issues this run — no existing issue covers multi-valued `type` unions or `convertSchema` type handling beyond the `anyOf` fold.

# fix(core): a balance-held credential is released when its dead grant is re-observed alive with less money — no increase required (the provider-scope path holds)

## Summary

Verified on clean `origin/main` `aa32898362268557918810393abc681dba90b416` (laptop probe, canonical runner `bun run script/test.ts` in `packages/core`): `test/model-route-credential.test.ts` fails deterministically — 31 pass / 1 fail, solo and in the full core suite.

Failing test: `ModelRoute balance-hold grants + credential restart baseline (#1014 Codex pass) > a funded replacement grant releases a credential balance hold without beating the dead grant's leftover` (`packages/core/test/model-route-credential.test.ts:486-…`).

## The sequence the test pins

1. Observe credential `cred-grant` with a dead grant (balance-shaped, `expired: true`, remaining 10) at t=10_000 → `credentialQuotaBlocked("cred-grant", 10_000)` is `{ until: null }` (balance hold armed). ✅ passes
2. Re-observe the **same grant alive again but not increased** (`expired: false`, remaining **5**) at t=20_000 → the test expects the hold to stand: `credentialQuotaBlocked("cred-grant", 20_000)` should still be `{ until: null }`. ❌ **Returns `undefined` — the credential is fully unblocked.** (assertion at test line 495)
3. A genuinely *different* grant with less money is then fed as a funded replacement (the release the test's title describes) — never reached, step 2 already diverged.

The provider-scope sibling test immediately below in the same describe block ("a funded replacement grant releases a *provider* balance hold without beating the dead grant's leftover") **passes**: on the provider path, a below-baseline live re-read keeps the hold ("Above the dead threshold but not above the benched balance: no increase, no release") and only a genuine increase — or a genuinely different grant — releases it. The credential path (`observeCredentialQuotaState`, `packages/core/src/model-route.ts:1294`, via `observeCredentialQuota` at :1426; hold release judged by `releasesHold` / `grantReclassified` / `grantIdentity` in the same surface) treats the expired→alive flip of the same grant as a replacement/reclassification and drops the hold without any increase over the benched balance.

## Why it matters

The balance hold is the mechanism that keeps a balance-exhausted credential out of rotation until a fresh balance *increase* is observed (#1014/#984). If a routine re-read of the same grant — alive again on paper but with *less* money than when it was benched — silently releases the hold, the router re-admits a credential that is broker than when it was held, burning real attempts against a dead balance and defeating the increase-only release rule the provider path enforces. The durable baseline is also cleared on this path, so a restart does not restore the hold either.

Repro (laptop, clean tree of origin/main):

```
cd packages/core && bun run script/test.ts test/model-route-credential.test.ts
# 31 pass / 1 fail — expect(ModelRoute.credentialQuotaBlocked("cred-grant", 20_000)).toEqual({ until: null })
# received undefined, at test/model-route-credential.test.ts:495
```

(Note: run through the package runner `script/test.ts`; raw `bun test` uses a 5 s default timeout and no test-home isolation, which produces unrelated artifacts.)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bun run script/test.ts test/model-route-credential.test.ts` passes in full on main, including the funded-replacement-grant test's step 2 (same grant alive, remaining 5 < benched 10 → hold stands) and step 3 (a genuinely different funded grant releases without beating the dead grant's leftover).
- [ ] The provider-scope sibling tests in the same file and the balance-hold restart-baseline tests (#1014 fix pass block) stay green — credential and provider scopes judge the same sequence the same way.
- [ ] The durable credential baseline is not cleared by a non-releasing re-observation (a restart after step 2 restores the still-armed hold).

Related: #1014 (balance holds + restart baseline), #984 (credential quota gate), #1461 (Location-scoped balance-hold judging), #1380 (grant reclassification).

# fix(core): failureHint reads a retry-after out of the transport timeout's own duration text — a plain Timeout failure is treated as rate-limited

## Summary

Verified on clean `origin/main` `aa32898362268557918810393abc681dba90b416` (laptop probe, canonical runner `bun run script/test.ts` in `packages/core`): `test/session-step-failure.test.ts` fails deterministically — 14 pass / 1 fail, solo and in the full core suite.

Failing test: `SessionStep.failureHint > an ordinary provider failure may carry a retry-after and is never a quota` (`packages/core/test/session-step-failure.test.ts:59-80`).

The third case feeds a `TransportError` with `code: "Timeout"` and message `"No response output within 1000ms"` and expects `{ retryAfterMs: undefined, quota: false, auth: false, network: false }`. The code returns `retryAfterMs: 1000`.

## Mechanism

- `failureHint` (`packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts:136-160`) derives `retryAfterMs` as `reason.retryAfterMs ?? reason.rateLimit?.retryAfterMs ?? ModelRouteLimits.retryHintFromMessage(reason.message ?? reason.body, Date.now())`.
- `retryHintFromMessage` (`packages/core/src/model-route-limits.ts:175-178`) delegates to `resetAtFromMessage` (`:159-169`), whose relative-duration scan (`relativeMs`) parses a duration out of arbitrary message text. The timeout message's own `"1000ms"` — the client's statement of how long *it* waited for output — parses as a provider-stated retry-after of 1000 ms.
- The same function already knows this message shape is special: its `network` classifier explicitly excludes `reason.code === "Timeout" && reason.message?.startsWith("No response output within ")` (step.ts, `network:` field). The retry-after scrape has no equivalent exclusion.

## Why it matters

`failureHint`'s `retryAfterMs` is load-bearing in two places: `isRateLimited` in the same file treats any failure with a defined `retryAfterMs` as rate-limited ("moving on beats waiting"), and `ModelRoute.failed` consumes the hint to hold the target (model-route.ts:461 area). A plain transport timeout — the provider said nothing about waiting — therefore gets rate-limit treatment and a spurious 1 s hold derived from the client's own timeout budget, and the misclassification scales with the configured output timeout (a 30 s timeout would read as a 30 s retry-after). The test pins the intended contract: an ordinary failure may carry a retry-after only when the provider actually stated one.

Repro (laptop, clean tree of origin/main):

```
cd packages/core && bun run script/test.ts test/session-step-failure.test.ts
# 14 pass / 1 fail — expect(received).toEqual(expected): retryAfterMs expected undefined, received 1000
# at test/session-step-failure.test.ts:78
```

(Note: run through the package runner `script/test.ts`; raw `bun test` uses a 5 s default timeout and no test-home isolation, which produces unrelated artifacts.)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bun run script/test.ts test/session-step-failure.test.ts` passes in full on main.
- [ ] A `TransportError` with `code: "Timeout"` whose message states the client's own wait ("No response output within Nms") yields `retryAfterMs: undefined` from `failureHint`, while a provider message that genuinely states a wait ("retry after 5s", an absolute reset time) still yields a hint — the existing passing cases in the same test stay green.
- [ ] No regression in the sibling classifications in the same file (quota / auth / network) or in `packages/core` model-route tests.

Related: #1380 (retry-after / quota classification discipline), #1484 (the other two core tests red on main — different mechanism, Location-scoped demotion).

title: fix(core): unknown keys directly under experimental.routes are silently dropped — no diagnostic for a typo'd nested routing key (#1311)

body:
## Finding

PR #1311 (merged, head `ac3302b5e3`, merge `ca81b0b221`) made `experimental.routes.*` the canonical routing-config shape and folds both spellings in `packages/core/src/config/normalize.ts`. Unknown keys **inside** the `tuning` and `log` blocks are diagnosed at whichever path the user wrote — but unknown keys **directly under `experimental.routes`** are silently dropped, with no diagnostic at all.

Verified live on current main `468023f2acdcd8c3b74d699de16f6711ca06981d`:

- `packages/core/src/config/normalize.ts:517-588` — `routeSources` reads only the seven known nested keys (`models`, `providers`, `schedules`, `windows`, `tuning`, `log`, `settings`) out of `routesInput`. Nothing ever enumerates the other keys of the `routes` object.
- The only `unknownKeys(...)` calls in the file are at `:539` (tuning value) and `:548` (log value). The helper itself (`:1022-1030`) states the house rule: "The decode drops keys a block does not know; for these blocks each one is reported by name."
- Because `:588` emits `result.routes = routes` whenever `routesInput !== undefined`, a config like `experimental.routes: { modles: { pool: { targets: [...] } } }` (typo) normalizes to an **empty** routes block: the entire routing config vanishes and the user is told nothing. A malformed entry inside a known key, by contrast, IS diagnosed (pinned by `packages/core/test/config/nested-routes.test.ts`, "a malformed nested entry is dropped with a nested-path diagnostic"), and an unknown key inside `routes.tuning` is diagnosed as `{kind: "invalid", path: ["experimental","routes","tuning","intervall"], message: "omitted unknown setting"}` (same test file). The container one level up is the only un-diagnosed layer of the new shape.

## Why it matters

The flat→nested migration is exactly when these typos happen: a user hand-editing their deployed config from `model_routes` to `routes.models` who misnames one key loses all routing — pools, windows, schedules, settings — silently, where the pre-migration flat spellings at least failed entry-by-entry with diagnostics for the blocks the normalizer reports on. PR #1311's stated design goal was diagnostics parity at whichever path the user wrote; the container level was missed.

Secondary observation for triage: `routes.settings` is decoded with `decodeEncoded` and no `unknownKeys` call (`:572-575`), so unknown keys inside `settings` are also silently dropped. The flat `model_route_settings` had the same gap, so this half is parity, not a regression — worth deciding in the same pass.

## Acceptance criteria

- An unknown key directly under `experimental.routes` produces a diagnostic `{kind: "invalid", path: ["experimental", "routes", <key>], message: "omitted unknown setting"}` (e.g. via `unknownKeys(routesInput, ConfigExperimental.Routes.fields, ["experimental", "routes"], diagnostics)`), while known keys in the same block still fold normally.
- A test in `packages/core/test/config/nested-routes.test.ts` mirrors the existing tuning test: a typo'd container key (e.g. `modles`) is diagnosed at its nested path and does not disturb the folding of valid sibling keys.
- Triage decides the `routes.settings` unknown-key gap in the same pass (fix it the same way, or record why settings stays exempt).

## Evidence / dedupe

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1311 (closes #1140); follow-on reader issues it filed (code#3889, openchamber#1270) do not cover normalizer diagnostics.
- Deduped 2026-11-03 against open + closed issues: searches for `experimental.routes`, `"unknown setting" routes`, `routes unknown key diagnostic`, `experimental.routes typo` return only #1140 (closed parent), #1322 (closed; docs teaching flat keys — different problem), #238 (open; a model pool whose matching keys select no models — different mechanism), #1464 (unrelated). No covering issue.

Filed by pr-diff-review lane B (agent-note:v1; Agent: pr-diff-review-b; state: filed).

# fix(ci): lint:effect-patterns drifted 32 → 33 — the api.ts streaming rewrite added a JSON.parse cast at api.ts:164 that #1496's disposition list does not cover

## Summary

Verified on `origin/main` 468023f2acdcd8c3b74d699de16f6711ca06981d (laptop probe, `bun install` + `bun run lint:effect-patterns`): the ast-grep scan now reports **33 errors**, one more than the 32 filed in #1496 earlier today. The rule breakdown is identical to #1496's except `no-json-parse-cast`, which went 5 → 6:

- 20 × `no-star-import` (unchanged)
- **6 × `no-json-parse-cast` (was 5)**
- 4 × `no-effect-die-string` (unchanged)
- 3 × `no-import-alias` (unchanged)

## The new site

- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/api.ts:164` — `return JSON.parse(text) as OpenApi` in the OpenAPI-document loader added by the api.ts streaming rewrite (commit db0f7bfe76, "fix(cli): stream opencode api response body instead of buffering it whole", for #987; the same rewrite whose bounded-http/numeric drift is filed as #1540).

Verified absent at #1496's verification commit: `git show ae4b9776f85c:packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/api.ts` contains no `JSON.parse` at all; the line is present at 76c4902638 and at current `origin/main`. The other five `no-json-parse-cast` sites are exactly #1496's (codemode/web.ts:89, completions.ts:53, aisdk.ts:950, chatgpt.ts:556, openai.ts:430).

The read itself is now properly bounded (the text comes from `readBoundedText` under `maxOpenApiBytes`, api.ts:~158), so this is a rule-conformance / disposition question, not a new unbounded read: parse the document through an Effect Schema decode, or record why this whole-document parse is an accepted exception in whatever disposition mechanism #1496 establishes.

## Why it matters

#1496 is the issue that will disposition the original 32 and decide how this gate gets its regression net. If this 33rd site is not on anyone's list, it survives that cleanup unexamined — the same drift-behind-a-red-gate pattern as #1514 and #1540, one gate over. Filing it separately keeps #1496's scope frozen at its verified 32 while making sure the new site gets an explicit disposition.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] api.ts:164's `JSON.parse(text) as OpenApi` is either converted to a Schema-based decode of the OpenAPI document or explicitly dispositioned (with the bounded-read reason stated) in the mechanism #1496 lands.
- [ ] `bun run lint:effect-patterns` reports no hit at api.ts:164, and the total count is back to #1496's baseline of 32 (or lower as #1496 lands).
- [ ] No behavior change to the `opencode api` OpenAPI loading path (same documents load, same errors on malformed JSON).

Related: #1496 (the 32 + the unwired-gate question), #1540 (the same rewrite's bounded-http/numeric drift), #987 (the streaming rewrite's issue).

# fix(ci): three gates red on main from today's merge wave — #1404's api.ts rewrite, #1531's byte decoder and #1532's parser unification left new undispositioned sites and stale allowlist entries

## Summary

Verified on `origin/main` 76c4902638 (laptop probe, gates run with `bun script/check-*.ts`): `check:bounded-http`, `check:numeric-boundaries`, and `check:proto-reads` each exit 1. Part of each red is already tracked (#1476 proto sites, #1477 systemone, #1514 expires/digitalocean/codegen). This issue covers only the NEW drift introduced by today's merges, which none of those issues list:

## New undispositioned sites

- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/api.ts:70` — `streamResponseBody`'s no-body fallback: `const text = await response.text()` collects the whole body with no byte cap (the function's own doc comment says the previous whole-body read "buffered an arbitrary, server-sized body — and hung on an endless one"). The fetch carries an `AbortSignal.timeout` deadline (api.ts:149/:182), so it is time-bounded, but the streaming path's byte-unboundedness is exactly what PR #1404 removed everywhere else in this file. Bounded-http gate hit.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/api.ts:121` — `readBoundedText`'s no-body fallback reads `response.text()` whole, then checks the byte count after the fact; in-flight it is uncapped (the streamed branch at :124+ is properly capped). Bounded-http gate hit.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/api.ts:113` — `Number.parseInt(contentLength, 10)`; the result is guarded by `Number.isSafeInteger(...) && >= 0` on the next line, so it is safe by construction and needs a numeric-gate disposition (or conversion through the shared primitives).
- `packages/core/src/database/v1-migration.bun.ts:1105` — `bytes.push(parseInt(hex, 16))` in the byte-wise decoder added by PR #1531 (issue #1529); `hex` is regex-validated `/^[0-9a-fA-F]{2}$/` on :1103, so the value is provably 0–255 — safe by construction, needs a numeric-gate disposition.

## Stale allowlist entries (lines rewritten by the same merges)

- bounded-http allowlist :53/:55 — `return (await response.json()) as OpenApi` and `const output = await response.text()` in api.ts no longer exist (PR #1404 rewrote both reads).
- numeric allowlist :63 and proto-reads allowlist :26 — `packages/core/src/model-route-tuning.ts :: total += Number(amount) * (unit[name] ?? 1_000)`; PR #1532 (commit 5331ad9c81, quota-reset relative-unit unification) replaced that line, so both entries are stale in two different gates.

## Why it matters

These gates are the regression nets for the bounded-http and numeric-boundary bug classes. Every day they sit red on main, new undispositioned sites can land unnoticed behind the noise — this is the same drift pattern as #1514, one merge wave later. The api.ts:70 fallback is also a genuine (if exotic-path) return of the unbounded-read behavior #1404 set out to remove.

## Acceptance criteria
