# fix(core): session prompt rejects valid non-base64 data-URL attachments — decodeDataURL percent-decodes as UTF-8 text, so binary payloads (%FF) fail the whole prompt

## Summary

The live session-prompt attachment path decodes non-base64 `data:` URLs with `decodeURIComponent`, which interprets percent-escapes as UTF-8 text and throws on valid binary octets. A valid non-base64 data-URL attachment (e.g. `data:application/octet-stream,%FF%00%41`) therefore fails with `Invalid attachment data URL` — and because attachment materialization is on the prompt path, the whole prompt fails. The V1 migration decoder had exactly this bug and was fixed byte-wise in #1529 / PR #1531; the live path was not.

Verified on `origin/main` 657c84e66f; re-verified this run on `origin/main` 76c4902638 (prompt.ts:221 unchanged, probe re-run: %FF%00%41 still throws URIError).

## Evidence

- `packages/core/src/session/prompt.ts:213` — `decodeDataURL(uri, label)`; `:221` — the non-base64 branch is `return Buffer.from(decodeURIComponent(payload))`.
- `packages/core/src/session/prompt.ts:102` — `materializeAttachment` calls `decodeDataURL` for every `data:` attachment; `:56` — attachments are materialized via `Effect.forEach(input.files, materializeAttachment, …)` in the prompt flow, so one rejected attachment fails the prompt submission with `AttachmentError`.
- Probe (this run, laptop, executing the actual `decodeDataURL` source extracted from prompt.ts at 657c84e66f, with only the Effect/AttachmentError shell stubbed):
  - `data:application/octet-stream,%FF%00%41` → **AttachmentError "Invalid attachment data URL: inline attachment"** (should be bytes `[0xFF, 0x00, 0x41]`)
  - `data:text/plain,caf%C3%A9 %E2%82%AC` → OK, correct UTF-8 bytes
  - `data:text/plain,hello` → OK
  - `data:text/plain;base64,aGk=` → OK (`hi`); `data:text/plain;base64,not-base64` → correctly rejected (canonical-base64 round-trip check)
- The fixed sibling: `packages/core/src/database/v1-migration.bun.ts:1084` `decodeFilePayload` decodes byte-wise — "Each %HH escape becomes exactly one byte; unescaped literal text is encoded as UTF-8; a malformed escape is invalid" — with the regression test in `packages/core/test/v1-migration.test.ts` ("keeps valid binary percent-escapes in non-base64 data URLs as bytes (#1529)": `%FF%00%41` is stored as base64 `/wBB`, no warning). Its comment even notes the base64 canonical check is "the check prompt.ts applies to live attachments" — the two decoders are meant to share semantics, and now diverge on the non-base64 branch.
- Test gap: every data-URL case in `packages/core/test/session-prompt.test.ts` is base64 (e.g. lines 323, 477, 495, 519, 542); there is no non-base64 prompt-attachment test at all.

## Why it matters

Non-base64 data URLs are a supported attachment encoding in this codebase's data model — the migration decoder accepts and preserves them. Any client (SDK, API consumer, import path) that submits an inline binary attachment percent-encoded rather than base64-encoded gets its entire prompt rejected with a misleading "invalid data URL" error, even though the URL is valid and the same attachment survives a V1 migration intact. The two decoders disagreeing on what is a valid attachment is also a standing trap for the next change to either one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `decodeDataURL` in `packages/core/src/session/prompt.ts` decodes non-base64 payloads byte-wise with the same semantics as the migration's `decodeFilePayload`: each `%HH` escape becomes exactly one byte, unescaped literal text is encoded as UTF-8, a malformed escape (e.g. a lone `%`) stays an `AttachmentError`.
- [ ] The canonical-base64 validation for `;base64` payloads is unchanged (non-canonical payloads still rejected).
- [ ] New tests in `packages/core/test/session-prompt.test.ts` cover: a binary percent-escaped non-base64 attachment (`%FF%00%41` → bytes FF 00 41), a UTF-8 percent-escaped text attachment round-tripping, and a malformed escape still erroring.
- [ ] Consider sharing one decoder between prompt.ts and v1-migration.bun.ts (or record on this issue why they stay parallel implementations with mirrored tests).

Related: #1529 / PR #1531 (same bug class, migration decoder — fixed), #1360 / #1358 (migration data-URL hardening).

# fix(ci): pr-standards workflow can never run — its only trigger is workflow_dispatch, but both jobs dereference context.payload.pull_request

## Summary

`.github/workflows/pr-standards.yml` checks PR standards, but on `origin/main` 3cb0dcfa7e its only trigger is `workflow_dispatch`, and both of its jobs immediately dereference `context.payload.pull_request` — which is undefined for a dispatch event, so a manual run crashes before checking anything. It has silently done nothing since its real trigger disappeared.

## Evidence

- `.github/workflows/pr-standards.yml:7-8` — `on:` contains only `workflow_dispatch:`.
- `:22` and `:179` — both jobs begin `const pr = context.payload.pull_request;` followed by `const login = pr.user.login;` (:23, :180). For `workflow_dispatch`, `context.payload` carries `inputs`, not `pull_request`, so `pr` is `undefined` and `pr.user` throws a TypeError in the github-script step.
- `:4` — even the concurrency group is written for PR events: `${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}`.
- Actions API: the workflow has 1,196 historical runs, all with event `pull_request_target`, and the most recent run is 2026-10-30 — i.e. it used to run on PRs, the trigger was replaced, and it has not run since.
- No other workflow covers PR standards: a trigger scan of all 29 workflows on main found no `pull_request` trigger anywhere in the repo (see also #1533 for the PR-tier workflows).

## Why it matters

A standards gate the fleet believes is watching PRs (description-template sections and author checks, per the script at :218) has been dead for days with no signal: the workflow neither runs on PRs nor can succeed when dispatched manually. Dead automation that looks alive is worse than none — it hides exactly the drift it was meant to catch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Triage decides: restore a PR trigger (the historical `pull_request_target`, with an explicit safety review — the script only reads PR metadata and comments, no PR-head checkout — or `pull_request`), **or** retire the workflow file and any docs that reference it.
- [ ] If restored: a run on a real PR completes (link the run) and both jobs execute their checks.
- [ ] If retired: no dangling references to pr-standards remain in docs/workflows.
- [ ] Consider folding this into the trigger-vs-policy regression net proposed in #1533 so a workflow whose script requires a payload its triggers never supply fails a gate.

Related: #1533 (PR-tier workflows have no pull_request trigger).

# fix(ci): the documented PR tier never runs — check, test and nix-eval have no pull_request trigger

## Summary

`.github/ci-policy.md` defines a fast PR tier as this repo's **merge requirement**, but none of the three PR-tier workflows triggers on `pull_request`, so the tier never runs on a PR. Verified on `origin/main` 3cb0dcfa7e.

## Evidence

Policy (`.github/ci-policy.md`):

- :23-25 — "Merge requirement: the basic-validation (PR) tier only."
- :31-38 — the tier's checks are `basic typecheck` (workflow `check`), `basic affected packages` and `basic unit (<os>)` (workflow `test`), and `e2e (<os>)` (workflow `test`) — "the aggregator only on PRs: it reports green when the e2e suite is tier-skipped, so the name stays stable for branch rules".
- :46-47 — "`check` … runs on every PR and on push to `main`. Unchanged by the tier split."
- :54-55 — "The branch-required `e2e (<os>)` check names still report on PRs via the aggregator job".
- nix-eval is likewise documented as "PR tier: paths-gated to nix inputs".

Reality (triggers at the top of each workflow on main):

- `.github/workflows/check.yml` — `on:` is `push` (branches: [main]) + `workflow_dispatch` only.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` — `on:` is `push` + `workflow_dispatch` + `schedule` only. The file still carries PR-tier machinery that can now never fire: `TURBO_SCM_BASE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && … }}` (lines 263, 281, 352), job gates `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'` (lines 302, 375), and `fetch-depth: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 2 || 0 }}` (line 325).
- `.github/workflows/nix-eval.yml` — `on:` is `push` (branches: [main]) + `workflow_dispatch` only; no paths-gated PR trigger.
- A scan of all 29 workflows on main found **no** workflow with a `pull_request` trigger at all (the only PR-event trigger in the repo is `pull_request_review_comment` in `opencode.yml`).
- Recent `test.yml` runs via the Actions API are all `push` events.

## Why it matters

The checks named as the merge requirement never report on PRs. Either branch protection does not actually require them (so PRs merge with zero basic validation — no typecheck, no affected unit tests — and the first signal is a red main owned by the remediation chain), or the policy document describes a pipeline that no longer exists and misleads every contributor and agent that reads it. This is the trigger-level parent of #1508 (one dead step inside `check.yml`); fixing #1508's step alone still leaves the step unreachable on PRs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Triage decides the intended shape: restore `pull_request` triggers on `check`, `test` and `nix-eval` matching ci-policy.md (including the paths gate for nix-eval and the aggregator-reports-on-PRs behavior for `e2e (<os>)`), **or** correct ci-policy.md to describe the push-only reality and remove the dead PR-tier conditionals from test.yml.
- [ ] Whichever shape is chosen, the `basic *` check names documented as the merge requirement demonstrably report on a test PR (link the run), or the policy no longer names them as requirements.
- [ ] A regression net exists so trigger-vs-policy drift fails loudly (e.g. the check:workflows gate or the gate-wiring meta-check in #1527 asserts each workflow named in ci-policy.md carries the triggers the policy claims).

Related: #1508 (dead lint:changed step inside check.yml), #1525/#1527 (gate wiring meta-check design).

## Finding (from PR review, never addressed)

On PR #1343 (fix(script): add stats.ts fetch deadlines and bounded JSON reads, fixing #1337), CodeRabbit's follow-up review asked for one specific missing regression test, and it was never added or responded to:

- Review: https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/1343#pullrequestreview-5731286341
- Reviewer: `coderabbitai[bot]`, 2026-11-02T01:40:06Z, state COMMENTED
- Location: `packages/script/test/stats.test.ts:73-112`

Reviewer's point, in their terms: **"Add a test for a stalled later releases page."** The releases deadline tests stall only the first request. A regression that returns the accumulated releases after a later-page abort would pass them. The parent issue (#1337) requires that any-page abort reject, so they asked for a case where page 1 is full and page 2 stalls, asserting the fetch rejects rather than returning the partial result.

## No-response evidence

- PR #1343 has no inline review threads (GraphQL `reviewThreads` is empty) and no reply to the review anywhere on the PR; the only other comments are the Codex summary (no findings) and the CodeRabbit walkthrough.
- The PR merged with the test suite as written; no follow-up commit added the case.

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-03)

`packages/script/test/stats.test.ts` on main:

- Line 88: `a stalled releases page settles at its deadline as an error, not a partial result` uses `stalledFetch` for **every** call, so the stall happens on page 1.
- Line 73: `releases pagination terminates on a short page` covers a full page followed by a short page, but nothing stalls.
- No test returns a full first page and then stalls/aborts on page 2, so a regression in `script/stats.ts`'s `fetchReleases` that resolved with the accumulated page-1 releases on a later-page abort would pass the whole suite.

Dedupe (2026-11-03): searched open + closed issues for the stats stall/pagination test gap — parent #1337 is closed by PR #1343 and does not track this residual test; no other issue covers it.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add a test in `packages/script/test/stats.test.ts`: page 1 returns a full page (100 releases), page 2 stalls past its deadline; `fetchReleases` must reject (and the page-2 signal must be aborted), not resolve with the 100 accumulated releases.
- The test fails against an implementation that returns partial results on a later-page abort.
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why first-page-only stall coverage is sufficient.

## Phase 3 of design #1525 — the gate registry and the wiring meta-check

Design #1525 (doc: `files/designs/opencode-gate-integrity-harness.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace), rule 3: a gate that runs nowhere is a silent gap, and this repo has found three by hand — `lint:effect-patterns` in no workflow and 32 violations red (#1496), `check.yml`'s `lint:changed` step gated on an event the workflow never receives (#1508), and `packages/protocol`'s `check:generated` unwired until #1500. Nothing enumerates the checks this repo promises run, so absence from CI is only ever discovered by a human grepping workflows.

**Blocked by (their fixes stay theirs):** #1508 and #1496 must be dispositioned before the meta-check can go green on main — #1508 by running `lint:changed` on push (its own stated fix), #1496 by wiring `lint:effect-patterns` after its 32 sites are dispositioned. This issue does not absorb either fix.

**Depends on:** phase 1 of #1525 (the shared harness — the registry is harness data).

### Scope

- A gate registry in the harness: one entry per promised check — name, the `package.json` script (or package + script for per-package gates), and its owning workflow. Initial membership: the five root `check:*` gates (`check:proto-reads`, `check:bounded-http`, `check:numeric-boundaries`, `check:workflows`, `check:doc-env-vars`), the root `lint:*` scans (`lint`, `lint:changed`, `lint:effect-patterns`, `lint:effect-simplifications`), `test:lint-rules`, and per-package `check:generated` (client, www, protocol).
- A meta-check (in `check:workflows` or a sibling `check:gates` — the design doc leaves the home open; record the choice and why in the PR) that fails when:
  - a `check:*` or `lint:*` script exists in the root `package.json`, or a `check:generated` script exists in any package `package.json`, but has no registry entry;
  - a registered gate's command appears in no workflow file;
  - a registered gate's workflow step is unreachable: a step-level `if:` equality on `github.event_name` names an event that is not among the workflow's triggers (parsed the way `check:workflows`' `triggerNames` already parses them — step-level equalities only, not expressions that merely mention an event; test.yml's graceful-degradation expressions per #1508's survey must not false-positive).
- The meta-check is itself wired in test.yml alongside the other gates, and registered (it is its own first self-test).
- Unit tests pin each failure shape with fixture workflows/package.json snippets, including the #1508 shape verbatim as a fixture.

### Acceptance

- [ ] The registry exists as harness data and covers the initial membership above.
- [ ] The meta-check fails on each of the three shapes (unregistered script, registered-but-unwired, unreachable step) with a message naming the gate and the shape; fixtures pin all three.
- [ ] On main with #1508 and #1496 dispositioned, the meta-check passes and is wired in test.yml.
- [ ] No existing gate's patterns, scope, allowlist, or workflow step changes in this issue beyond adding the meta-check step itself.

🤖 Filed by the repo-design-architect job as phase 3 of design #1525.
<!-- agent-note:v1 agent=repo-design-architect state=filed at=2026-11-03T14:04:47Z -->

## Acceptance criteria

- A gate registry exists in the shared harness (#1526's deliverable): one entry per promised check — name, package.json script (or package + script), owning workflow — covering at minimum the five root check:* gates, the root lint:* scans, and test:lint-rules named in this issue.
- The wiring meta-check fails CI when a promised gate is unregistered, unwired (no workflow runs it), or unreachable (its workflow step is gated on an event the workflow never receives — the #1508 shape).
- The meta-check is green on main once #1508 and #1496 are dispositioned (their fixes stay theirs, per the issue), and a deliberately unwired fixture gate makes it fail (the gate proves itself).

## Phase 1 of design #1525 — the shared gate harness

Design #1525 (doc: `files/designs/opencode-gate-integrity-harness.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace) states that the repo's three allowlist regression gates — `script/check-proto-reads.ts`, `script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts`, `script/check-bounded-http.ts` — must share one machinery implementation instead of three near-verbatim copies that have already drifted into bugs (#1506: numeric's `collect` kept the Windows-broken `path.slice(...)` construction PR #1289 removed from the other two; the `parseAllowlist` ` :: `-in-text divergence from #1394; proto's missing comment-skip).

### Scope

- Extract the machinery the three gates share into one module under `script/` (name it per repo convention, e.g. `script/gate-harness.ts`): tree walking / `collect` (repo-relative hit keys built with `relative(root, path).split(sep).join("/")`, exported), `scanSource` (comment-only lines skipped), `parseAllowlist` (occurrence-aware, hit text = everything between the file field and the last ` :: ` field), `unlistedHits`, `staleEntries`, and the on-disk tree-inventory helpers bounded-http already has (`scriptTreesOnDisk` shape).
- Re-express each of the three gates as a declaration over the harness: its `PATTERNS`, its scan roots, its scanned extensions, its `ALLOWLIST_PATH`, and its per-hit remediation text. Gate entry points, `package.json` script names, and test.yml wiring do not change.
- **Behaviour-identical:** patterns, scan roots, extensions, allowlist files and their contents are unchanged. The single intentional change is numeric-boundaries' hit keys becoming POSIX (from the shared `collect`) — byte-identical on Linux, and it satisfies #1506's acceptance by construction (exported `collect` + the on-disk collect test living in the harness suite; note this on #1506 rather than closing it — it keeps its own lifecycle).
- The gates' existing unit tests keep passing; where a test targeted a gate's private copy of the machinery, it moves to the harness suite (one on-disk collect test, one allowlist-accounting suite) and each gate keeps a smoke test that its declaration loads and its current hit set is dispositioned.

### Acceptance

- [ ] One shared harness module under `script/`; the three gates contain no private copies of `collect`/`scanSource`/`parseAllowlist`/`unlistedHits`/`staleEntries`.
- [ ] For each gate, the sorted hit-key set on current main is byte-identical before and after the change (record the counts and a hash/diff in the closing note).
- [ ] `bun run check:proto-reads`, `bun run check:numeric-boundaries`, and `bun run check:bounded-http` all exit with the same result on current main as before the change (green except hits already filed under other issues, named in the closing note if any).
- [ ] The harness's on-disk collect test asserts forward-slash hit keys from a temp tree (the #1289 proto-reads test, generalised).
- [ ] No scan root, pattern, extension list, or allowlist entry changes in this issue — scope/coverage changes are design #1525 phase 2 (#1494) and the per-tree expansion issues, not this phase.

# fix(test): console-app suite fails as a whole — process-wide `mock.module` registrations for `@opencode/console-resource` pollute sibling test files

## Evidence (verified this run on clean origin/main `3e483a8caf`, laptop probe worktree)

Running the package's own test command fails, deterministically, while every
failing file passes on its own:

- `cd packages/console/app && bun test` → **103 pass / 4 fail / 1 error**
  (107 tests, 18 files), reproduced identically in two consecutive runs.
- Solo runs all pass: `salesforce.test.ts` 2/0, `emailoctopus.test.ts` 2/0,
  `stats-proxy.test.ts` 5/0, `aws.test.ts` 4/0.
- Sibling suites are green: `packages/stats/app` 23/0, `packages/stats/core` 48/0,
  `packages/desktop` 168 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail.

Failures in the full-suite run:

1. `src/lib/salesforce.test.ts` — "a fake entry keeps the visitor message…"
   throws `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating
   'Resource.SALESFORCE_INSTANCE_URL.value')` at `src/lib/salesforce.ts:54`
   (via `createLead`, `salesforce.ts:118`).
2. `src/lib/emailoctopus.test.ts` — both tests throw the same way on
   `Resource.EMAILOCTOPUS_API_KEY.value` at `src/lib/emailoctopus.ts:10`.
3. `src/lib/stats-proxy.test.ts` — file-level error, tests never run:
   `SyntaxError: Export named 'waitUntil' not found in module
   'packages/console/resource/resource.node.ts'`.

## Root cause

Bun's `mock.module` is **process-wide** (the suite already knows this:
`src/lib/aws.test.ts:3-19` documents it and builds a merging Proxy fixture to
cope). The files register incompatible mocks for the same module,
`@opencode/console-resource`:

- `console-account.test.ts:6` — `Resource` with only `CONSOLE_CRM_*` entries,
  no `waitUntil` export.
- `inference-proxy.test.ts:8` — `Resource` with only `ConsoleMigration` /
  `INFERENCE`, no `waitUntil` export.
- `stats-proxy.test.ts:3` — its own mock *with* `waitUntil`, which loses when
  another file's mock is registered first → the named-export check fails
  against the winning mock (hence the SyntaxError naming the real file).
- `salesforce.test.ts` / `emailoctopus.test.ts` — no mock at all; they set
  `SST_RESOURCE_*` env vars and rely on the real `resource.node.ts`, so a
  winning mock leaves `Resource.SALESFORCE_*` / `Resource.EMAILOCTOPUS_*`
  undefined.

Pair-level repros (each pair fails, each file passes solo):

- `bun test src/lib/console-account.test.ts src/lib/stats-proxy.test.ts`
  → 1 fail / 1 error.
- `bun test src/lib/inference-proxy.test.ts src/lib/emailoctopus.test.ts`
  → 2 fail.

## Why it matters

`@opencode/console-app#test` is a turbo task (`turbo.json`) and CI runs
`bun turbo test` (`.github/workflows/test.yml`, unit-tests step), so the
console suite's red state is either failing CI or being ignored — either way
the bounded-http regression tests for the Salesforce / EmailOctopus /
stats-proxy paths (the #1097/#1111/#1104 fix series) currently provide no
trustworthy signal when run the way CI runs them. It also makes any new
console test file a lottery ticket: adding a file can flip unrelated suites.

Related (not duplicates): #143 (closed) wired these suites into turbo;
#1097 (open) is the salesforce timeout fix whose tests are among the victims.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cd packages/console/app && bun test` exits 0 with all 18 files'
      tests executing (no file-level errors), repeatedly and regardless of
      file ordering.
- [ ] One shared, complete `@opencode/console-resource` test fixture (every
      `Resource.*` key any suite needs, plus `waitUntil`) — e.g. the
      Proxy-fixture pattern `aws.test.ts` already uses, hoisted to a shared
      preload/helper — instead of per-file partial mocks.
- [ ] `salesforce.test.ts` and `emailoctopus.test.ts` no longer depend on
      winning/losing a process-wide mock race for their `SST_RESOURCE_*`
      env pattern.
- [ ] No test deleted or weakened to reach green; solo-file runs still pass.

body:
## Problem

`check:numeric-boundaries` does not scan any script tree, so the bare string→number conversion class it exists to net (design #992, gate #995) regrows invisibly in the release / publish / CI tooling — the exact trees `check:bounded-http` was extended to cover in #1394 for the sibling reason: those scripts run against api.github.com and registries with a token in env, and every script-tree bug in that class escaped precisely because the gate did not scan them.

## Evidence (verified this run at origin/main `260082fb145cdd5587815365211fccb6be52d436`)

- `script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts:44` — `SCAN_ROOTS` lists only production `src` trees (`packages/*/src`, `services/*/src`); no `script/` or `packages/*/script(s)` root appears, and unlike `check-bounded-http` (`script/check-bounded-http.ts:242` `scriptTreesOnDisk`, `:266` `unscannedScriptTrees`, failing `main()`), the numeric gate has no on-disk script-tree guard, so the omission is silent.
- Re-running the gate's own sweep patterns (`\bNumber\s*\(`, `\bparseInt\s*\(`, `\bparseFloat\s*\(`) over the script trees (root `script/`, every package `script`/`scripts` tree, `.ts`/`.tsx` only, comment-only lines skipped, probe run on the laptop against `origin/main`) finds **56 hits**: 13 are the gate's own test fixtures (`script/check-numeric-boundaries.test.ts`) and **43 are production script code across 19 files**, none of them dispositioned in `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt`.
- The undispositioned hits include the exact shapes this gate dispositions in `src` trees:
  - Response-header parses: `script/github/close-issues.ts:136`, `script/github/close-prs.ts:386`, `script/publish-winget-github.ts:82`, `script/stats.ts:88`, `script/update-artifact.ts:192` — all `Number(response.headers.get("content-length"))` (compare #1487, the same parse in `packages/ai/src`).
  - Upstream-header arithmetic: `script/github/close-prs.ts:339` `Number(retryAfter) * 1000` and `:341` `Number(reset) * 1000 - Date.now()` — a non-numeric or huge `retry-after` / `x-ratelimit-reset` header yields `NaN` (retry silently skipped) or an unbounded sleep in the rate-limit retry loop.
  - Env / CLI-argument conversions with no validation: `packages/core/script/wellknown-server.ts:2` `Number(process.env.PORT ?? 8787)`, `packages/console/app/script/dev-enterprise.ts:49` `Number(process.env.ENTERPRISE_DEV_PORT || 3101)`, `packages/desktop/scripts/bench-startup.ts:70-76`.
  - Remainder (regex-capture and local-output parses, likely safe-by-construction dispositions): `script/profile-typecheck.ts` (7), `script/stats.ts:229-231`, `script/mcpx-cleanup.ts:114`, `packages/core/script/benchmark-*.ts` (11), `packages/desktop/scripts/finalize-latest-yml.ts` / `publish.ts` (4), `packages/session-ui/script/generate-session-progress-indicator.ts:23`.

## Why it matters

The gate's purpose is that a new bare conversion fails CI until a human dispositions it. In the script trees a new conversion — including one on an upstream-supplied header or an env var, the two inputs this class is about — currently fails nothing, is listed nowhere, and the initial allowlist (the gate's remaining-work inventory) silently understates the class by 43 sites.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` scans the script trees (root `script/` plus every package `script`/`scripts` tree), reusing or mirroring `check-bounded-http`'s `scriptTreesOnDisk` inventory so the two gates agree on what a script tree is.
- [ ] Every hit in the newly scanned trees is dispositioned in `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt` (converted through the #993 primitives, safe-by-construction with the reason, or tracked) — including the gate's own test-fixture self-matches, as `check:bounded-http` does.
- [ ] The gate fails when a package script tree exists on disk but is not scanned (the `unscannedScriptTrees` drift guard, as in `check:bounded-http`), so the list cannot silently drift again. (The `src`-tree half of that guard is #1494; this issue is the script-tree scan itself.)
- [ ] `bun test script/check-numeric-boundaries.test.ts` covers the new roots / drift guard, and `bun run check:numeric-boundaries` is green on main with the expanded scope.

Related: #995 (the gate), #1394 / #1425 (bounded-http's script-tree extension and its drift guard — the precedent), #1494 (src-tree drift guard for both gates), #1514 (current allowlist drift in the scanned trees).

body:
## Problem

`bun run check:numeric-boundaries` is red on main (verified at `5bae9ad8b0e5`, 2026-11-03) with **5 stale allowlist entries and 5 unlisted candidates**. One unlisted candidate is already tracked by #1477 (`packages/core/src/systemone.ts:200`). The other 9 findings are new drift from two merges that landed today, neither of which updated `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt`:

- **PR #1507** (merge `9917026037`, `a1e4f5984f` — the #994 phase-2 collapse of the `expiresInSeconds` duplicates onto `serverSeconds`) rewrote the very lines the allowlist dispositions key on.
- **PR #1510** (merge `94939076d9`, `568c66d921` — the #1385 default 120s deadline in the generated promise client) changed the httpapi-codegen client template (`requestTimeout` / `ClientOptions`), so the template's allowlist entry no longer matches verbatim.

The gate's own test suite passes (`bun test check-numeric-boundaries.test.ts` — 11 pass / 0 fail at the same commit), so this is allowlist drift, not a gate bug. The gate is wired in CI (`test.yml` runs `bun run check:numeric-boundaries`), and it was already red for #1477 — these merges added 9 more findings on top, which is exactly how a red gate trains everyone to ignore it.

## Evidence (all at main `5bae9ad8b0e5`, clean laptop probe clone)

Stale allowlist entries (line no longer matches a sweep pattern):

1. `packages/core/src/mcp/oauth.ts :: const seconds = Number(value)` — the private copy was deleted by #1507; `oauth.ts:288` now calls `serverSeconds(...)` directly and has no unlisted hit.
2. `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/digitalocean.ts :: return /^\d+$/.test(text) ? Math.min(Number.parseInt(text, 10), …` — replaced by `digitalocean.ts:58`.
3. `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/expires.ts :: const seconds = Number(value)` — **two** entries (the old file had two occurrences); both gone.
4. `packages/httpapi-codegen/src/index.ts :: return \`import type { ${imports.join(", ")} …` — the giant template-string entry; the template changed in #1510 (new `requestTimeout` doc + `defaultRequestTimeoutMs` + `withDeadline`).

Unlisted candidates (excluding #1477's `systemone.ts:200`):

5. `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/expires.ts:33` — `return serverSeconds(Number(value), { fallback, max: MAX_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS, oversized: "fallback" })`
6. `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/expires.ts:48` — `return serverSeconds(Number(value), { fallback, max: MAX_DEVICE_LIFETIME_SECONDS, oversized: "clamp" })`
7. `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/digitalocean.ts:58` — `return serverSeconds(Number.parseInt(text, 10), { fallback: 0, max: MAX_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS, oversized: "clamp" })`, reached only after the `/^\d+$/` spelling check at :57.
8. `packages/httpapi-codegen/src/index.ts:961` — the regenerated template text (contains `Number(response.headers.get("content-length"))` guarded by `Number.isFinite` + the 16 MiB cap, and the `requestTimeout` `Number.isFinite` validation from #1510).

## Why it matters

The numeric-boundaries net (design #992, phase 3 #995) only works if every bare conversion carries a current disposition. #1507 was the net's own phase-2 migration — the conversions now genuinely go through the `serverSeconds` primitive — but because the allowlist keys on exact line text, the migration simultaneously (a) orphaned its old baseline entries and (b) left the new, blessed call sites undispositioned. Left alone, the next bare conversion hides in a gate that is already red for 10 reasons.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The 5 stale entries above are removed from `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt`.
- [ ] Each new call site (items 5–8) carries a disposition entry keyed to its current line text, stating why it is safe (conversion through the `serverSeconds` primitive with fallback/max for items 5–7; the template's guarded `content-length` parse + finite-checked `requestTimeout` for item 8) — or the gate's sweep is taught to recognise a conversion wrapped in a #993 primitive call, with the gate's tests updated accordingly.
- [ ] After the change, `bun run check:numeric-boundaries` reports **only** the pre-existing #1477 `systemone.ts:200` finding (no stale entries, no other unlisted candidates) at the then-current main.
- [ ] `bun test check-numeric-boundaries.test.ts` (in `script/`) still passes.
- [ ] No production behaviour changes: this is allowlist/gate bookkeeping for the already-merged #1507/#1510 code, unless the sweep-recognition route is chosen.

Related: #1477 (the remaining systemone finding), #994 / PR #1507, #1385 / PR #1510, #992, #1506 (the same gate's collector bug — different defect).

body:
# fix(ci): check.yml's lint:changed step can never run — warn-level anti-slop gate for GUI files runs nowhere

Verified 2026-11-03 by new-issue-creator-opencode on clean laptop probe
~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-03-creator2 at origin/main 9679be7a1d67.
(Laptop primary ~/git/opencode is diverged — local keeper snapshot
59e192c13f ahead 1 / behind 6 — left untouched; all reads in the probe.)

## Evidence

- `.github/workflows/check.yml:8-11` — triggers are only `push` (branches:
  [main]) and `workflow_dispatch`. There is no `pull_request` trigger.
- `.github/workflows/check.yml:42,45` — the "Lint changed files" step is
  gated `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` and runs
  `bun run lint:changed HEAD^1`. The condition can never be true for any
  event this workflow runs on, so the step has never executed in CI.
  It was born dead: check.yml was introduced in PR #1303 (merge commit
  9c99d58ace1b, 2026-11-01) already in this shape.
- `grep -rn "lint:changed" .github/workflows/` returns exactly that one
  step — no other workflow runs it. test.yml runs
  lint:effect-simplifications and the check:* gates, not lint:changed.
- `script/lint-changed.ts:1-2` (header): it is the ONLY enforcement of the
  warn-level anti-slop oxlint rules for GUI packages (app, desktop,
  gui-extensions, ui, session-ui): "Fails when a GUI package file this
  branch adds or edits has any oxlint problem, including warn-level rules
  (anti-slop)". check.yml:39-40 states the same purpose.
- The first step of check.yml (`bun run check` = root lint + typecheck)
  does NOT cover it: root `oxlint` exits 0 on warn-level diagnostics.
  Verified empirically in the probe (after `bun install --frozen-lockfile`):
  a scratch file `packages/ui/src/__oxprobe__.ts` containing
  `[1,2,3].filter(...).map(...)` (anti-slop/no-array-filter-map, warn):
  - `bunx oxlint packages/ui/src/__oxprobe__.ts` → "Found 1 warning and
    0 errors", exit 0.
  - `bun script/lint-changed.ts HEAD` → prints the diagnostic,
    "lint:changed: 1 problem(s) in 1 of 1 changed files", exit 1.
  Scratch file removed afterwards; probe tree clean.
- House policy bans PR triggers (the check:workflows gate enforces
  "no PR triggers" — and indeed `bun script/check-workflows.ts` passes
  on all 29 workflows at 9679be7a1d67, blind to this dead-step class),
  so "just add a pull_request trigger" contradicts #118/#1406 policy.
  The checkout already uses fetch-depth: 2 with a comment about HEAD^1
  being the base — a push-to-main run with base HEAD^1 would diff exactly
  the merged change, so running the step on push is mechanically sound.
- check.yml is the only workflow with a step-level
  `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` gate (surveyed all workflows'
  event_name uses; test.yml's are expressions/outputs that degrade
  gracefully on push, not whole-gate step kills).

## Why it matters

The anti-slop warn rules exist to keep GUI files clean at touch time
("a change that touches a file leaves the whole file clean"). Since
2026-11-01 that guarantee has been enforced nowhere: warn-level problems
in touched GUI files merge silently, and the step's presence in check.yml
makes the coverage look real. Every other script gate in this repo that
was found unwired (#1496, #1500) turned out to be hiding exactly this
kind of silent gap.

## Acceptance criteria

- The lint:changed enforcement actually executes in CI on an event the
  workflow triggers on (e.g. the step runs on push to main with base
  HEAD^1, or the gate moves to a main-tier job in test.yml), OR the step
  and script are deliberately removed with the decision recorded — no
  dead step remains.
- Demonstrated: a change introducing a warn-level anti-slop diagnostic in
  a GUI package file fails the chosen CI path; a clean change passes.
- `bun run check:workflows` still passes; no `pull_request` trigger is
  added (house no-PR-trigger policy).
- Bonus/optional: extend check:workflows (or another gate) to flag a
  step-level event_name condition that no trigger of the same workflow
  can satisfy.

Dedup: open+closed search 2026-11-03 for "lint-changed", "lint:changed",
"anti-slop", "check.yml" — no hits for this dead step. #37 and #171 are
different never-run mechanisms (branch targets / repo-name gate), both
closed. Sibling unwired-gate filings: #1496 (lint:effect-patterns),
#1500 (protocol check:generated, fixed by PR #1501).

## Problem

`check:workflows` — the gate built by #1406 to turn workflow policy from convention into a regression net — does not check `permissions:`. #118 fixed the instances (six workflows declared no permissions and fell back to the repo-default `GITHUB_TOKEN`), but no gate prevents the next workflow from landing the same way: a new or edited workflow with no `permissions:` at workflow or job level passes every wired check while its token silently inherits the repo defaults.

## Evidence (verified this run, 2026-11-03, clean laptop probe worktree at origin/main d370a2972b)

- The gate's own header (`script/check-workflows.ts:1-35`) lists exactly three policies: no `pull_request`/`pull_request_target` triggers, `workflow_dispatch` declared, and `timeout-minutes` on every non-reusable job (plus the reusable-caller key allowlist). `permissions` appears in that file only once, as an allowed key on reusable-workflow caller jobs (`script/check-workflows.ts:54`) — never as a requirement.
- The gate is green today: `bun script/check-workflows.ts` exits 0 with "All 29 workflows in .github/workflows follow the workflow policies".
- Current state is clean, so this is a net gap, not a live exposure: every one of the 29 workflow files declares `permissions:` at least once (top-level or job-level; verified by grep over `.github/workflows/*.yml` — e.g. `check.yml` top-level `contents: read`, `review.yml` job-level `contents: read` + `pull-requests: write`, `stats.yml` job-level `contents: write`).
- The class has already regressed once by hand: #118 ("six workflows declare no permissions — GITHUB_TOKEN falls back to repo defaults") was caught and fixed manually, exactly how the timeout policy regressed twice before #1406 gated it (#1326, #1184, cited in the gate's own header).

## Why it matters

This fork's workflows hold write tokens on purpose (`contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`, `id-token: write` in several). The one workflow that forgets to declare permissions does not fail closed — it runs with whatever the repo default grants, and nothing in CI notices. The repo's established pattern for exactly this situation is a gate policy (#1406, #1481, #1494, #1500); permissions is the remaining #118-class policy still enforced by convention only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `script/check-workflows.ts` fails a workflow in which any job would run without an applicable `permissions:` declaration (workflow-level or job-level), with reusable-workflow caller jobs handled consistently with the existing caller-key policy.
- [ ] `script/check-workflows.test.ts` gains fixture coverage: a workflow with no permissions anywhere fails, a job-level-only declaration passes, a workflow-level-only declaration passes.
- [ ] The gate stays green on the current 29 workflows (`bun script/check-workflows.ts` exits 0) and `bun run check:workflows` remains the wired CI entry.

## `lint:effect-patterns` is red on main (32 errors) and nothing runs it — the main ast-grep rules have no regression net

Verified 2026-11-03 by running the scan in a clean clone of main `ae4b9776f85c` and reading the CI wiring.

### Evidence

- Root `package.json:23` defines the scan: `lint:effect-patterns` = `ast-grep scan -c script/ast-grep/sgconfig.yml packages/util/src packages/core/src packages/server/src packages/protocol/src packages/cli/src`. Run on clean main it exits with **32 error-level diagnostics**:
  - 20 × `no-star-import`, 5 × `no-json-parse-cast`, 4 × die with `new Error(...)`, 3 × `no-import-alias`.
  - 13 of the star imports are in the vendored drizzle tree (`packages/core/src/database/drizzle/**`), whose files carry `/* oxlint-disable */` but no ast-grep suppression or config exclusion.
  - The other 19 are first-party sites, e.g. `packages/server/src/handlers/completions.ts:53` (JSON.parse cast), `packages/server/src/inherited-socket.ts:2` (import alias), `packages/core/src/mcp/client.ts:13`, `packages/core/src/messaging.ts:8`, `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/openai.ts:430`, `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/chatgpt.ts:556`, `packages/core/src/workspace.ts:158`, `packages/core/src/tool/runtime.ts:47`, `packages/core/src/aisdk.ts:950`, `packages/util/src/cross-spawn-spawner.ts:2-3`, `packages/util/src/effect/app-node-platform.ts:3-4`, `packages/util/src/observability.ts:3`.
- Nothing runs the scan: `grep` over `.github/workflows/` finds `lint:effect-patterns` nowhere. `test.yml` runs the rule *tests* (`test:lint-rules`, wired for #153) and the *simplifications* scan (`lint:effect-simplifications`, which is green on main), and `check.yml:45` runs only `lint:changed`. The root `lint` script is `oxlint && ast-grep scan -c script/ast-grep/gui-extensions/sgconfig.yml && bun script/sdk-docs.ts` — the gui-extensions config, not the main rules.
- So the main rules (no star imports, no JSON.parse casts, no aliased value imports, no `die(new Error)`) are enforced only when someone happens to run the script by hand, and main has already drifted 32 violations deep — the same unwired-net failure shape as #153 (rule tests) and #1406 (workflow policies), except here the drift has already happened.

### Why it matters

These rules encode house Effect style that reviewers rely on (Schema decoding over unchecked JSON casts is a correctness rule, not cosmetics — a cast at `completions.ts:53` accepts any shape the peer sends). Every new violation that lands while the scan is unwired raises the cost of ever wiring it, which is how a lint rule quietly dies: the longer the drift, the more likely the eventual fix is to delete the rule instead of the violations.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every one of the 32 current diagnostics is dispositioned: first-party sites fixed to comply, or individually suppressed with a reason at the site; the vendored `packages/core/src/database/drizzle/**` tree is excluded via ast-grep config (or suppressed) with the vendoring rationale recorded, mirroring its existing `/* oxlint-disable */` treatment.
- [ ] `bun run lint:effect-patterns` exits 0 on main after the dispositions.
- [ ] The scan is wired somewhere it actually runs on change — a `test.yml` step alongside `lint:effect-simplifications` (Linux) is the natural home — so a new violation fails CI.
- [ ] The rule test suites stay green: `bun run test:lint-rules` and `bun run test:effect-simplification-rules` pass, and no rule is weakened to make the scan pass.

## The bounded-http and numeric-boundaries gates have no src-tree drift guard — a new package `src` tree silently escapes both regression nets

Verified 2026-11-03 by reading both gates on main `e21f70672a3f16323a73bdd3abda374a2fde21ec` and inventorying the trees on disk.

### Evidence

- `script/check-bounded-http.ts` hardcodes its 38 `src` roots in `SCAN_ROOTS` (lines 62–99). Its only on-disk drift guard is `scriptTreesOnDisk` / `unscannedScriptTrees` (lines 242–266), which inventories **`script`/`scripts` trees only** — the guard added for #1425, whose comment says the script list "cannot drift again". The `src` list has no equivalent: a new `packages/<new>/src` (or `services/<new>/src`) tree is never scanned and the gate still prints "All … candidates … are dispositioned".
- `script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` hardcodes the same 38 `src` roots in `SCAN_ROOTS` (lines 44–83) and its `main()` (lines ~170–185) only iterates that list — there is **no on-disk inventory at all**, for any tree kind.
- Today the lists happen to be complete: `find packages services -type d -name src` returns exactly the 38 listed roots (34 under `packages/`, 4 under `services/`), and both gates are green on main except the already-filed hits (#1476 proto, #1477 numeric). The gap is the missing guard, not a current unscanned tree.
- The hand-maintained-list failure mode is this repo's most repeated gate bug: bounded-http missed services (#1256) and then the script trees (#1394, #1425); numeric-boundaries missed server (#1294), console/function (#1302), services (#1308), plugin-github (#1318), and "the remaining production trees" (#1371) in successive filings. Each was fixed by extending the list by hand; only the script trees ever got a drift guard.

### Why it matters

Both gates exist so that two bug classes — unbounded outbound HTTP (#1127) and bare numeric conversions at boundaries (#992/#993) — cannot regrow one call at a time. A new package is exactly when new calls of both classes arrive, and it is the one moment neither gate is watching: the first fetch or `Number(...)` in a new `src` tree lands with no disposition, no allowlist entry, and no failing check, and is only found by a later manual sweep (the pattern behind every issue cited above).

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `check:bounded-http` fails with a clear "unscanned src tree on disk" message when a `packages/*/src` or `services/*/src` tree exists that is not in its `SCAN_ROOTS` (mirroring `unscannedScriptTrees`), with a unit test in `script/check-bounded-http.test.ts` pinning the failure.
- [ ] `check:numeric-boundaries` gains the same src-tree drift guard and a pinning test in `script/check-numeric-boundaries.test.ts`.
- [ ] Both gates still pass on current main (the on-disk inventory equals the listed roots — verified at filing).
- [ ] The guard follows the `scriptTreesOnDisk` precedent for what counts as a tree (package-owned `src` directories; no node_modules, no false positives from asset/skill folders).

# fix(core): demoted() ignores the judging Location's settings demotion — two #1423 model-route tests fail on main

Verified on main `eeebf4143d6c227d3d5ecd728e94e8cbf1b33a6f` (laptop primary, 2026-11-02).

## Reproduction

```
cd packages/core && bun test test/model-route.test.ts
→ 119 pass, 2 fail
```

Failing tests (both added for the #1423 Location-scoping work):

1. `behavior consumers judge with their own Location's settings, not the unscoped fallback (#1423)` — `packages/core/test/model-route.test.ts:1807`, failing assertion at `:1827`: two quota failures recorded, Location A configured with settings `demotion: { after: 2 }`, Location B with `after: 9`; `ModelRoute.demoted(target, now + 10, undefined, "/loc/a")` returns `false`, expected `true`.
2. `quota-event and network histories retain the union of Location windows (#1423)` — `test/model-route.test.ts:1939`, failing assertion at `:1955`: A judges by settings `demotion: { after: 2, windowMs: 60_000 }`, B by `windowMs: 1_000`; `demoted(target, now + 2_000, undefined, "/loc/a")` returns `false`, expected `true`.

Reproduced twice in a row this run; fleet lanes have been carrying these as "pre-existing #1423 failures" in PR verification notes (e.g. on PR #1479 / PR #1483 work) without a tracking issue.

## Root cause (code evidence)

- `packages/core/src/model-route.ts:946-953` — `demotionPolicy(location)` resolves the per-Location `model_route_demotion` config (`demotionConfig(location)`), but its fallback layer is `activeSettings().quota` at `:948`: **`activeSettings()` is called without the `location` argument**, so the judging Location's `experimental.routes.settings` demotion (`demotion.after` → `quota.demoteAfter`, `demotion.windowMs` → `quota.windowMs`, mapped at `model-route.ts:883-884`) is never consulted. With two or more Locations registered, the unscoped settings read returns the compiled defaults (threshold 3, window 4h — `model-route.ts:781`), so a Location that configured `demotion.after: 2` in its routes settings is judged by threshold 3. The single-Location case accidentally works, because the unscoped read follows the sole registered reader.
- `packages/core/src/model-route.ts:1006` — `retainedQuotaWindowMs()`, the settings-based union of demotion windows, is **defined but never called** (its only occurrence in the file is its definition; it is the known pre-existing `TS6133` in the core typecheck). `recordQuota` at `:1015` prunes the shared quota-event history using only `retainedDemotionWindow()` at `:960`, the union over the `model_route_demotion` readers — a Location whose wide demotion window comes from its routes settings does not extend retention. Contrast `retainedNetworkWindowMs()` at `:373`, which correctly unions over the settings readers for the network history.
- The model-routes plugin registers both readers per Location (`packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts:60` settings, `:69` demotion), so in production a Location that sets only the canonical routes-settings demotion (the shape #1464 established as canonical, with `model_route_demotion` re-scoped as the duplicate) silently gets default demotion behaviour whenever a second Location is open.

## Why it matters

Quota demotion decides when a failing target drops to last-resort in route order. A project that tuned `demotion.after`/`windowMs` in its routes settings gets the compiled defaults instead — with no log line and no config error — exactly the cross-Location surprise class #1423 was filed to eliminate. Main's own regression tests for this have been red since the #1437 demotion-as-config layer landed over the #1423 settings layer, and the red suite is being normalised as "pre-existing" in lane verification notes, which masks future regressions in the same file.

## Not this issue

- #1461 / #1463 cover two *other* process-global consumers (tuning quota ceiling, threshold-derived balance holds) — not `demoted()`/`demotionPolicy()`.
- #1151 (re-scoped per #1464) is the ledger/façade remainder of the demotion work, not this fallback wiring.

## Acceptance criteria

- `bun test test/model-route.test.ts` in `packages/core` passes fully on main (121/121), including the two tests named above and the #1151 demotion-policy suite (a Location's `model_route_demotion` config still takes precedence over its routes-settings demotion, field by field).
- `demotionPolicy(location)` judges a Location that configured only routes-settings demotion by that Location's `after`/`windowMs`, in a multi-Location process.
- Quota-event retention covers the widest demotion window from *both* config layers (settings readers and demotion readers); the dead `retainedQuotaWindowMs` is either wired in or removed, and the core typecheck no longer reports `TS6133` for it.
- Single-Location and unconfigured behaviour is unchanged (defaults: threshold 3, window 4h).

body:
## Problem

`bun script/check-proto-reads.ts` exits 1 on clean main `d96751c983156833a148aab264a453f0554270ba` with exactly three unlisted candidates, all in façade-wave files merged in the last two days. One of them is a genuine prototype-chain bug, not just a missing disposition.

Gate output (run on the laptop primary, clean main, this run):

```
Unlisted prototype-chain read candidate at packages/core/src/generate.ts:171:
  if (typeof path === "string" && !path.endsWith(DOOR_PATHS[dialect])) return undefined
Unlisted prototype-chain read candidate at packages/core/src/systemone.ts:227:
  const gatewayBase = (process.env[GATEWAY_BASE_ENV] ?? DEFAULT_GATEWAY_BASE).replace(/\/+$/, "")
Unlisted prototype-chain read candidate at packages/core/src/muse-attestation.ts:90:
  const alias = ALIASES[name]
```

## The real bug: `packages/core/src/muse-attestation.ts:90`

`ALIASES` is a plain object literal (`{ shell: "run_command", bash: "terminal" }`) and `name` comes from the tool names in a caller's request (`plan(toolNames(...))`, called from `packages/core/src/generate.ts:398`). A bare `ALIASES[name]` walks the prototype chain.

Verified with a probe on the laptop (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-02-proto/probe.ts`, importing the real module from main):

- `plan(["toString"])` → forward map `toString -> function toString() { [native code] }` (typeof `function`, not a string)
- `plan(["constructor"])` → forward map `constructor -> function Object() { [native code] }`
- `plan(["hasOwnProperty"])` and `plan(["__proto__"])` likewise produce non-string "aliases"

Downstream, `aliasEntry` / `aliasRawBody` do `plan.forward.get(name)!` and write that value back as a tool's `name` (`muse-attestation.ts:115-116, 221-222`), so a request carrying a tool named `toString`/`constructor` gets its tool renamed to a function object instead of being left alone. This is the same class as #833/#865/#916/#1085 — which is exactly why the gate exists.

## The other two sites look safe by construction (disposition, not a guard)

- `generate.ts:171` `DOOR_PATHS[dialect]`: `dialect` is the closed union `Dialect = "chat" | "responses" | "messages"`, and line 168 already returns early unless `NATIVE_DIALECTS.get(String(route.protocol)) === dialect` — the map only yields those three values, so by line 171 the key is proven to be an own key. Needs an accurate allowlist disposition saying so (or an `ownValue` guard if preferred).
- `systemone.ts:227` `process.env[GATEWAY_BASE_ENV]`: the key is the module constant `GATEWAY_BASE_ENV = "OPENCODE_SYSTEMONE_GATEWAY_BASE"` (line ~204), never caller-controlled. Needs an allowlist disposition saying so.

Neither site is allowlisted today (`grep` of `script/check-proto-reads.allowlist.txt` for `generate.ts` / `systemone` / `muse-attestation`: no entries).

## Why it matters

- The regression net for the prototype-chain class is red on main, so every new PR inherits a failing gate and the next real instance can land unnoticed (precedent: closed #1282, the same gate red on main after a merge wave).
- The muse-attestation site is reachable with caller-supplied tool names through the façade path in `generate.ts`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `MuseAttestation.plan` uses an own-property read (`ownValue`/`ownOr` from `packages/core/src/util/record.ts`, or an equivalent `Object.hasOwn` guard) so tool names `toString`, `constructor`, `hasOwnProperty`, `__proto__` produce no alias entry
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/core/test/muse-attestation.test.ts`: prototype-named tools are left unaliased; `shell`/`bash` aliasing and the collision guard are unchanged
- [ ] `generate.ts:171` and `systemone.ts:227` are dispositioned in `script/check-proto-reads.allowlist.txt` with the safe-by-construction reasons above (or guarded at the site)
- [ ] `bun script/check-proto-reads.ts` exits 0 on main with no stale allowlist entries
- [ ] No behavior change for the legitimate `shell`/`bash` aliasing path

Related: #833, #865, #1085, #1282 (same gate, prior wave), #1369/#1361/#912 (gate *coverage* of other trees — distinct from this red-on-main finding in the already-scanned `packages/core/src` tree). Deduped against open and recently closed issues this run.

Part of #1146 (generic OpenAI façades on the server; design: specs/2026-11-01T04-10-00Z_design_openai-facades.md §8 — fronts AND backends fold into the fork's provider machinery; Drew's 2026-11-02 clarification: per provider the façade passes through or proxies as needed, and special tokens like the direct providers' must be handled).

## Door (backend face — the one the design catalog predates)
`bin/antigravity-direct.mjs` (developing-today/code), port 18751, `antigravity-direct.service` active/running. Since 2026-10-30 this is the fleet's SINGLE Antigravity door: it replaced agy-proxy (:18743) and antigravity-ls-proxy (:18745). It speaks the agy CLI's own wire protocol directly — keyring OAuth credential (Secret Service, service "gemini" / username "antigravity"), the CLI's embedded OAuth client for refresh, and its exact `v1internal` envelope to daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com — with no spawned CLI and no language server. It exists because no stock provider speaks that wire.

## Consumers (verified 2026-11-02)
- Deployed opencode.jsonc: `antigravity-direct` provider baseURL :18751 — the plan seats (gemini-4-argon etc.) route through it; routes seat antigravity leaves in workhorse and elsewhere.
- Drew ordered Antigravity OUT of the primary/workhorse path 2026-10-31, but the provider remains a live leaf door — verify current route seats before scoping.

## Work — fold the wire protocol into the fork as a provider
1. Inventory the door's special handling from source: keyring credential read + refresh ownership (who refreshes when the fork owns it — the standing server already owns credential refresh for other providers; the keyring lives in the user session), the v1internal envelope shapes (stream + non-stream), tool-call translation to/from the wire, model id mapping, error/quota shapes (per-model sub-window 429s are a known behaviour — DeepSeek-style sub-windows were observed on this door's models).
2. Implement as an in-fork provider (provider implementation inside the fork's provider machinery, per Drew: "the proxy logic becomes provider implementation"), reusing the fork's credential store / refresh patterns where they fit; where the keyring source cannot move, name the exact bridge the provider uses and why.
3. Parity suite against the live door (chat non-stream/stream, tool calls, a quota-shaped failure) before any seat moves.
4. Repoint the provider config from :18751 to the in-fork provider; live-verify route seats that use Antigravity leaves; observe zero traffic on :18751 for a stated window; then remove the unit + `bin/antigravity-direct.mjs` from developing-today/code via merged PR + switch.
5. NEVER FUNDS / quota discipline unchanged: this door is plan-backed (Antigravity plan); no API-key fallback may appear in the fold.

If the wire protocol cannot be preserved faithfully in-fork yet, this door does NOT retire — record the precise gap here and on #1146 and move on (quirk loss is a regression, per the program guardrails).

<!-- agent-note:v1 agent=proxy-fold-coordinator state=filed at=2026-11-02T16:55:00Z -->

## Acceptance criteria

- The antigravity-direct (18751) wire protocol is reachable through the in-fork provider façade with no proxy process in the path.
- Existing antigravity-direct behaviors exercised through the façade match the proxied behavior (auth, streaming, error mapping).

title: fix(core): skill file downloads have no deadline — byte-capped but a stalled or slow-dripping source hangs skill pull forever (#1376 sibling)

body:
## Problem

In `packages/core/src/skill/discovery.ts`, the per-file download path (`download()`, lines 98–122) is byte-capped but has **no deadline**. Its sibling in the same file — the `index.json` fetch — got both a byte cap and a 15-second deadline in #1376 (PR #1377). The file downloads were left with the cap only (#923's scope).

A skill source server that accepts the connection and then stalls, or slow-drips body bytes, hangs the download indefinitely:

- `download()` pipes the request through `collectBoundedResponseBody` (`packages/core/src/tool/http-body.ts`), which bounds bytes only — it contains no timeout/deadline logic.
- The `HttpClient` used by the service (discovery.ts:89–96) is wrapped only with `retryTransient` + `filterStatusOk`; its layer is the plain `FetchHttpClient.layer` (`packages/util/src/effect/app-node-platform.ts:11`). No client-level deadline exists, and `retryTransient` never fires for a response that simply never completes.
- `pull()` runs the downloads with `Effect.forEach` in both the unversioned branch and the versioned staging branch, so one stalled file blocks publication of the whole skill; `pull` is called during plugin/skill loading (`packages/core/src/config/plugin/skill.ts:23`).

This is the same failure shape as #1115 (session import fetch, fixed) and #1091 (desktop extension download, open): size-capped, time-unbounded.

## Evidence (main `52ac2c2852`)

- `packages/core/src/skill/discovery.ts:31` — `const indexFetchTimeout = "15 seconds"` is defined for the index fetch only.
- `packages/core/src/skill/discovery.ts:140` — index fetch carries `Effect.timeout(indexFetchTimeout)`.
- `packages/core/src/skill/discovery.ts:98–122` — `download()` has no `Effect.timeout` (grep the function: no timeout/deadline).
- `packages/core/src/tool/http-body.ts` — `collectBoundedResponseBody` enforces the byte cap only.
- Dedup: searched open + closed issues for skill-download deadline/timeout — #1376 covers the index fetch only; no issue covers the per-file downloads.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A skill file download that stalls or drips past a named deadline fails with a clear error (logged via the existing `Effect.catch` path in `download()`, returning `false` like other download failures), instead of hanging `pull()` forever.
- [ ] The deadline is a named constant in `discovery.ts`, in the same style as `indexFetchTimeout`; the value is justified in a comment (files can be up to `MAX_SKILL_FILE_BYTES` = 5 MiB, so the deadline should account for size, or be paired with a minimum-throughput expectation).
- [ ] A test in `packages/core/test/skill-discovery.test.ts` proves a non-completing download settles as a failed download under a test clock / short deadline, and that normal downloads are unaffected.
- [ ] The bounded-http gate disposition for the discovery download site is updated if its allowlist text changes.

Design contract: #1127 (bounded by default — every outbound call carries a deadline and a cap).

body:
## Problem

`script/check-proto-reads.ts:31` scans exactly one tree:

```ts
export const SCAN_ROOT = "packages/core/src"
```

The gate is the regression net for the prototype-chain dictionary-read class (#865, follow-up to the #833 audit): a bare `record[key]` read walks the prototype chain, so an externally supplied key like `"constructor"` resolves to an inherited member and a `?? fallback` never fires. Two extensions are already tracked — #912 (packages/ai, PR #919) and #1361 (packages/plugin-github) — and #912 explicitly scopes every other package out. Every other production tree remains unscanned, and the class has already bitten in unscanned trees: latex (#937), web (#851), console (#1323).

## Evidence (main 6eb53396b5, verified this run)

Replicating the gate's exact three patterns (P-A / P-C / P-D) over the remaining `packages/*/src` trees (plus the console/stats subtrees; `services/*` and server/sdk/plugin/web/function return 0) yields **194 hits across 17 trees, none dispositioned** — the allowlist has zero entries for any of them:

| tree | hits | tree | hits |
|---|---|---|---|
| packages/merman/src | 77 | packages/stats/app/src | 6 |
| packages/tui/src | 25 | packages/desktop/src | 5 |
| packages/client/src | 24 | packages/latex/src | 5 |
| packages/gui-extensions/src | 16 | packages/cli/src | 4 |
| packages/app/src | 11 | packages/console/app/src | 4 |
| packages/stats/core/src | 9 | packages/codemode/src, packages/theme/src | 2 each |
| | | packages/httpapi-codegen/src, packages/plugin-browser/src, packages/ui/src, packages/util/src | 1 each |

Control: the same replication over `packages/core/src` returns 45 hits, all allowlisted — the replication matches the gate.

Spot-reads of the dangerous shape (externally influenced key, `??` fallback that can never fire):

- `packages/stats/core/src/domain/model-normalization.ts:50` — `MODEL_NAME_ALIASES[resolved.toLowerCase()] ?? resolved`; model names are provider-supplied, so a model named `constructor` returns the Object constructor instead of its name — the exact shape of #1085.
- `packages/stats/core/src/domain/home.ts:1142` — `aliases[slug] ?? slug`; `:1087` — `known[normalized] ?? …`.
- `packages/latex/src/parser.ts:609` — `negated[value] ?? …` over parsed document input; #937 already fixed this same class in this package's parser command tables, and this table sits outside the net.
- `packages/merman/src/core/geometry.ts:135/139/143/147` — `DIRECTION_AXIS[direction]`, `DIRECTION_SIGN[direction]`, `DIRECTION_SIDE[direction]`, `OPPOSITE_SIDE[side]`, keyed by direction strings parsed from user-authored diagram text.
- `packages/tui/src/mini/theme.ts:315` — `custom[name] ?? allThemes()[name] ?? …`, where `name` comes from user theme config.

Many hits are plainly dispositionable (numeric-index reads; dot-prefixed extension keys like `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/local-attachment.ts:22`; server-generated session IDs in `packages/client/src/solid/data.ts`) — but today none of that is recorded, so the next bare read in any of these trees lands silently.

## Why it matters

The fleet has fixed this bug class at least nine times (#792, #851, #906, #907, #908, #916, #937, #1085, #1319, #1323). The net that prevents recurrence covers one tree, with two more in flight. Until the remaining production trees are scanned and dispositioned, each new table read in them is an unguarded recurrence risk — including in packages that parse untrusted input (latex, merman) or consume provider-supplied strings (stats).

## Acceptance criteria

- `script/check-proto-reads.ts` scans every production `packages/*/src` tree (including the console and stats subtrees) in addition to its existing root(s), coordinated with #912's multi-root conversion and #1361 so the three efforts compose instead of colliding; gate unit tests updated and green.
- Every current hit in the newly scanned trees is dispositioned: guarded at the site (e.g. `ownValue`/`ownOr` from `packages/core/src/util/record.ts` or `Object.hasOwn`), or allowlisted with a specific per-entry reason per existing conventions.
- Any hit that is a live bug (externally influenced key reaching a table read with behavioral effect) is filed as its own issue and cross-linked, not allowlisted away.
- `bun run check:proto-reads` passes on the resulting tree.
- No behavior change to any hit dispositioned as safe/internal.

## Scope notes

- Out of scope: packages/ai (#912) and packages/plugin-github (#1361) — this issue covers the trees neither of those touches; landing order should follow #912's SCAN_ROOTS conversion.
- Cross-references: #865, #833, #912, #1361, #1085, #937.

title: fix(core,schema): escalation afterGiveUps above outcomeWindow is silently inert — threshold can never be reached over the retained window

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
## Problem

`experimental.model_route_settings.escalation` (added in #1141) accepts a combination that can never do anything: **`afterGiveUps` greater than `outcomeWindow` silently disables escalation entirely**, with no validation error, no clamp, and no diagnostic.

The two fields are validated only independently, each as a count up to 50:

```ts
// packages/schema/src/config/model-routes.ts — Escalation class
afterGiveUps: SampleCount   // PositiveInt, <= 50; "Defaults to 2"
outcomeWindow: SampleCount  // PositiveInt, <= 50; "Defaults to 5"
```

## Why the combination is unreachable (verified on main `c3a4b4ee87`)

```ts
// packages/core/src/model-route.ts:273-274 — outcomes are retained only for the window
const pushOutcome = (outcomes, answered) =>
  [...outcomes, answered].slice(-currentConstants().escalation.outcomeWindow)

// packages/core/src/model-route.ts:574-580 — the count can never exceed the window
export const giveUps = (target, credentialID?) =>
  (state?.outcomes ?? []).filter((answered) => !answered).length   // <= outcomeWindow, always
export const steady = (target, credentialID?) =>
  giveUps(target, credentialID) < activeSettings().escalation.afterGiveUps
export const escalates = (target, credentialID?) =>
  activeSettings().escalation.enabled && !steady(target, credentialID)
```

If `afterGiveUps > outcomeWindow`, then `giveUps <= outcomeWindow < afterGiveUps` for every possible history, so `steady` is always true and `escalates` always false. Example accepted today: `{ escalation: { afterGiveUps: 10, outcomeWindow: 5 } }` — or even `{ afterGiveUps: 6 }` alone, since the default window is 5.

## Verification (laptop probe, this run)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-escalation-window/probe.mjs` on the laptop, replicating the three functions above verbatim:

- default `after=2, window=5`, 5 failures → `giveUps=5, steady=false, escalates=true` (control: works)
- config `after=10, window=5`, 20 failures → `retained=5, giveUps=5, steady=true, escalates=false`
- config `after=6, window=5`, 100 failures → `retained=5, giveUps=5, steady=true, escalates=false`
- config `after=50, window=50`, 50 failures → `escalates=true` (the threshold is reachable only when `afterGiveUps <= outcomeWindow`)

The schema test suite pins the individual bounds but not the relationship: `packages/schema/test/config.test.ts` rejects `afterGiveUps: 51` and `outcomeWindow: 0`, and accepts `afterGiveUps: 4, outcomeWindow: 8` — no case with `afterGiveUps > outcomeWindow`.

## The in-repo precedents this misses

- **Demotion, same settings block:** `demotion.after` is capped at 50 with the explicit rationale (schema description): *"Capped at 50, the number of quota events retained per target, so a threshold can never be set beyond what is counted."* The escalation threshold has exactly the same shape — a threshold over a retained, windowed count — but its retaining bound is the configurable `outcomeWindow`, not a fixed 50, so a fixed cap cannot express it.
- **Route health policy:** `packages/core/src/model-route.ts:211` clamps at runtime: `slowThreshold: Math.min(input?.slowThreshold ?? ..., sampleWindow)` — a threshold is never allowed to exceed the window it counts over.

## Why it matters

Escalation is the mechanism that races the next target when the current one keeps giving up. A user who raises `afterGiveUps` to make escalation less trigger-happy (e.g. 10, leaving the window at its default 5) instead turns it off completely — the opposite failure mode, and a silent one: config loads, no warning, routes just never race. This is the new (#1141) config surface, so the gap is cheapest to close now, before the nested-config migration in #1140 builds on these fields.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A settings value with `afterGiveUps > outcomeWindow` can no longer be silently inert: either config decoding rejects it with a clear error, or the effective threshold is clamped to the window (the `slowThreshold` precedent) with the clamp visible in docs/descriptions — one behaviour, chosen and stated in the PR.
- [ ] The chosen behaviour also covers the programmatic seams (`ModelRoute.configure` / `configureConstants` in `model-route.ts`), not only the schema decode, or the PR explains why those seams are exempt.
- [ ] Regression coverage: a schema/config test pins `afterGiveUps > outcomeWindow` (rejected or clamped), and a core test shows a target with a full window of give-ups escalates at the effective threshold; the existing `afterGiveUps: 4, outcomeWindow: 8` round-trip and defaults (2 / 5) stay green.
- [ ] Field descriptions for `afterGiveUps` / `outcomeWindow` state the relationship (threshold must not exceed the window it counts over).

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `escalation afterGiveUps outcomeWindow` and `model_route_settings` (2026-11-01): the only hits are #1141 (the feature itself, closed/merged) and #1140 (open, config nesting — a different change). No filing covers this cross-field invariant.

title: fix(function): token exchange builds a fresh JWKS set per request — jose's JWKS cache never warms, every exchange fetches GitHub's JWKS live

labels.name: kind/performance

body:
## Problem

The GitHub App token-exchange handler in `packages/function/src/api.ts` builds a brand-new jose remote JWK set on every request:

- `packages/function/src/api.ts:272` — inside `POST /exchange_github_app_token`: `const JWKS = createRemoteJWKSet(new URL(JWKS_URL))`, then `jwtVerify(token, JWKS, ...)` at `:275`.

`createRemoteJWKSet` is designed to be created **once** and reused: each instance keeps its own in-memory JWKS cache (jose default cache max-age 10 minutes, with key-rotation handling on unknown `kid`). A fresh instance per request means the cache is always cold, so **every** token exchange performs a live HTTPS fetch of `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com/.well-known/jwks` before verification can start. That adds a full cross-network round trip to every `opencode github run` token exchange, and couples the endpoint's availability and latency to GitHub's JWKS endpoint on every single call instead of at most once per cache window.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 05b37bd71f)

- Code read: `packages/function/src/api.ts:260-283` — the `JWKS` set is constructed inside the request handler; there is no module-level JWK set anywhere in the file (only other fetch/JWKS references are the import at `:4` and this handler).
- Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-jwks-per-request/probe.mjs` (local JWKS HTTP server counting requests, real `jose` from `packages/function/node_modules`, real signed RS256 token with the handler's issuer/audience):
  - Pattern A (fresh `createRemoteJWKSet` per verify, the current code shape): 3 verifies → **3 JWKS HTTP fetches**.
  - Pattern B (one shared module-level set): 3 verifies → **1 JWKS HTTP fetch**.
- Dedup: `gh` search (open + closed) for `jwks` / `createRemoteJWKSet` / `exchange_github` returns no filing covering this handler.

## Why it matters

`/exchange_github_app_token` sits on the hot path of the GitHub Action integration — every action run starts with this exchange. The per-request JWKS fetch is pure overhead (latency on every run) and an unnecessary availability coupling: a slow or briefly unreachable JWKS endpoint fails or stalls exchanges that a warm cache would have served locally. It also discards jose's built-in rotation behavior, which only works across requests when the set (and its cache) survives between them.

## Acceptance criteria

- The remote JWK set for the GitHub Actions issuer is created once at module scope in `packages/function/src/api.ts` (or an equivalent lazily-initialized singleton) and reused by every `/exchange_github_app_token` request; no `createRemoteJWKSet` call remains inside a request handler.
- Verification semantics unchanged: same issuer, same audience (`opencode-github-action`), invalid/expired tokens still return 403, and a token signed with an unknown `kid` still triggers jose's cache-refresh path (key rotation keeps working).
- Regression coverage: a test or probe demonstrating that two sequential verifications against a counting JWKS endpoint produce exactly one JWKS fetch, and that a rotated key (new `kid`) still verifies after refresh.
- The PAT exchange route (`/exchange_github_app_token_with_pat`) is untouched.

title: fix(console): openapi.json route fetches the upstream spec with no timeout and no body cap — response.json() buffers unbounded and a non-OK upstream body is served as the spec
