body:
## Problem

The console site's `/openapi.json` route fetches its upstream spec with **no timeout and no size cap**:

- `packages/console/app/src/routes/openapi.json.ts:2-4` — `GET` awaits `fetch("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opencode/refs/heads/dev/packages/protocol/openapi.json")` with **no `signal`** — a stalled raw.githubusercontent.com leaves the route handler pending indefinitely; the handler has no fallback and no error path at all (no status check, no catch).
- `packages/console/app/src/routes/openapi.json.ts:5` — the body is read with `await response.json()`, buffering the whole response before parsing. The served document is a generated OpenAPI spec (normally well under a few MB); nothing bounds what a compromised or misbehaving upstream can make the console server buffer per request, and a non-200 upstream body is parsed and returned as if it were the spec.

## Verification (this run, laptop probes with the real handler)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-salesforce-openapi/` (laptop, `probe.ts` case 5 + `probe3.ts`), importing the real `GET` from `packages/console/app/src/routes/openapi.json.ts` (code identical on main `4208bef54a` and `12f411d167`) with `globalThis.fetch` stubbed:

- **Hang:** fetch returns 200 with a body stream that never delivers and never closes. Result: `PROBE openapi.json GET hang: STILL-PENDING` — `GET` still pending after 5 s, with no deadline at which it would settle.
- **Unbounded (clean rerun, `probe3.ts`):** fetch returns 200 with a paced endless body (256 KiB every 20 ms). Result: `PROBE openapi.json GET endless-body: STILL-PENDING bytesEnqueued=64487424` — 64,487,424 bytes handed to the buffering `response.json()` read in 5 s, still pending, never rejected.

## Why it matters

`/openapi.json` is a public console route serving the API spec. Today a stalled upstream stalls every request to it (no timeout, no error response), and an oversized upstream response buffers without limit in the console server process, once per request. Sibling console surfaces already bound at least their time — `lib/console-account.ts:17` uses `AbortSignal.timeout(3000)`, `lib/salesforce.ts:156` uses `AbortSignal.timeout(8000)`, the changelog loader's chosen bound in #1083 is 8 s — this route is an outlier with neither a time nor a size bound and not even an upstream-status check. It is a different surface from #1083 (changelog loader), #1089 (download redirect route), and #1090 (GitHub metadata queries): this is the raw.githubusercontent.com spec fetch behind `/openapi.json`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The upstream fetch in `GET` carries a named timeout constant (console precedent range 3–8 s), so a stalled upstream settles the handler with an error response instead of hanging the route.
- [ ] The spec body is read through a bounded read with a named cap constant sized for the generated spec document (declared `content-length` over the cap fails fast where available; a streamed body is cut off at the cap), failing as an error response rather than buffering without limit.
- [ ] A non-OK upstream status is not parsed-and-served as the spec: it produces an error response (or a documented passthrough) instead of `return json` on an error body.
- [ ] Happy path unchanged: a normal spec response is still parsed and returned as the route's JSON.
- [ ] A regression test pins the over-cap, never-resolving, and non-OK behaviours for `GET` (the handler is a plain exported function, directly callable with a stubbed `globalThis.fetch`), following the console app's existing test conventions.
- [ ] Out of scope: the changelog loader (#1083), the download redirect route (#1089), the console/stats GitHub metadata fetches (#1090), and the docs/stats proxy routes (which stream `response.body` through rather than buffering).

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode, 2026-10-31 run. Same no-timeout/no-cap class as #1083/#1089/#1090, different surface.

title: ensure(router): content-policy (censor) rejections must not count toward model removal, demotion, or disable in routes

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: effort/l
labels.description: Large: multi-day or open-ended; expect staged check-ins

labels.name: kind/enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

body:
Drew's directive (2026-10-31): ensure that a content-policy ("censor") rejection can never take a healthy model out of rotation in the wider route system.

## The risk

opencode#1014 mandates that repeated errors of ANY class remove a model/target from rotation for escalating time. opencode#984 (landed) auto-disables providers at 100% quota. The route system also has automatic quota demotion (>=3 quota errors in 4h -> weight x0.01), route-health cooldowns (#823), and rate-limit holds (#870).

A content-policy rejection is a property of the REQUEST, not of model or provider health. If it is counted like a quota/rate-limit/upstream failure:

- One censored prompt — or one session doing legitimate work that trips a filter (security research, reverse engineering, adult/creative writing, controversial topics) — can demote or disable a healthy leaf for EVERY other session sharing the route.
- Escalating removal makes it worse over time: the more edgy-but-legitimate work a session does, the more of the fleet's healthy capacity silently disappears.
- The failure is invisible as censorship: it presents as "model unavailable", so nobody learns the provider is censoring the workload.

## Required behavior

1. Content-policy / safety rejections are classified as their OWN error class, distinct from quota, rate-limit, billing, auth, and upstream classes. Shapes to cover (verify against each seated provider):
   - OpenAI-compatible: `content_policy` / `content_filter` error codes and types, incl. 400/403 variants carrying them.
   - Anthropic-style: refusal `stop_reason` and refusal-category responses.
   - Provider-specific safety blocks surfaced as errors (e.g. Gemini safety-block finish reasons mapped to errors, Azure content-filter errors).
   - In-band refusals (HTTP 200 with refusal text): at minimum audit and document whether these are detectable; they currently look like success.
2. This class NEVER increments failure, demotion, removal, or disable counters — no route-health cooldown, no quota demotion, no #984-style gating, no #1014 escalation. Repeated rejections (test: 10 in a row) leave the target fully in rotation for other requests/sessions.
3. This class is NOT retried against the same model for the same request (pointless — the same prompt will be rejected again). The request fails over instead; the uncensored-fallback investigation is the companion topic in developing-today/code (filed 2026-10-31, cross-linked below).
4. This class IS logged and counted in telemetry as its own class (per provider/model), so censorship frequency is measurable — excluded from health counters, not invisible.

## Audit required

Table every counter/removal mechanism x this error class: quota demotion, route-health cooldown (#823), rate-limit holds (#870), quota auto-disable (#984/#991), the #1014 any-class removal as it lands, and any OpenChamber-side route handling. Each cell: excluded (with the code location) or gap (with fix).

## Acceptance criteria

- Audit table (PR or linked comment) covering the mechanisms above.
- Tests: repeated content-policy rejections leave the target in rotation at full weight; quota/429/402 classes still demote/disable exactly as before; a rejection on one session does not change route state observed by another session.
- Telemetry: censor-rejection counts visible per provider/model, separate from error/health counts.

Companion: the uncensored-fallback (Sable) investigation in developing-today/code — what a censored request should fail over TO. This issue is only about never poisoning route health.

title: fix(ui,gui-extensions): two renderer remote-JSON fetches have no timeout — theme loader fetch has no signal at all, whats-new only a teardown signal (#1061 residual)

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage

labels.name: effort/s

body:
## Summary

The two renderer remote-JSON fetches that #1061 / PR #1062 bounded by **size** still have **no time bound at all** — the size-cap half of the fix landed, the timeout half (#1019's pattern: "no timeout and no body size cap") was never applied to either site:

1. **Theme loader** — `packages/ui/src/theme/loader.ts:130-138`: `loadThemeFromUrl` calls bare `fetch(url)` with **no signal whatsoever**, then streams the body through the bounded reader from #1062. A server that accepts the connection and never responds leaves the promise pending forever; a server that drip-feeds bytes under the 1 MiB cap (e.g. 100 bytes every 2 s) also holds it forever — the bounded reader caps total bytes, not elapsed time.
2. **What's-new changelog** — `packages/gui-extensions/src/updater/whats-new.tsx:65`: `fetch(CHANGELOG_URL, { signal: ctx.signal, … })` — the only signal is the extension-setup lifecycle signal, which aborts on teardown, not on a deadline. A stalled `https://opencode.ai/changelog.json` (whats-new.tsx:9) leaves the fetch pending for the life of the process: the `.catch(() => undefined)` never fires, `markSeen()` is never reached through this path, and every start retries into the same hang.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `8dab871ace`)

Code:

- `packages/ui/src/theme/loader.ts:131` — `const response = await fetch(url)`; no `AbortSignal.timeout`, no caller-supplied signal in the signature (`loadThemeFromUrl(url: string)`), and `readBoundedThemeText` (loader.ts:92-128) has no deadline logic. Repo-wide grep: this is the only bare remote `fetch(` in `packages/ui/src`.
- `packages/gui-extensions/src/updater/whats-new.tsx:65` — signal is `ctx.signal` only (setup context); compare the hardened sibling in the same package, `packages/gui-extensions/src/wsl/sidecar.ts:140-145`, whose health probe uses `AbortSignal.timeout(3000)`.
- House precedent everywhere else: Copilot models `AbortSignal.timeout(5_000)`, Modal models `AbortSignal.timeout(3_000)`, ModelsDev catalog 10 s, CodeMode web fetch 30 s, MCP OAuth discovery 5 s (#1019). These two renderer fetches are the outliers.
- Existing tests pin only the size cap: `packages/ui/src/theme/loader.test.ts` (#1061 describe block) covers normal / declared-oversized / streamed-oversized; no test uses a never-resolving or slow-drip response. The whats-new reader tests (PR #1064) likewise pin size only.

Reproduction (laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-theme-timeout/probe.ts`, bun, importing the **real** `loadThemeFromUrl` from the laptop checkout at the same main, raced against a 6 s marker):

```
HANG: STILL-PENDING after 6010ms
DRIP: STILL-PENDING after 6003ms
```

HANG = a local server that accepts the connection and never sends anything. DRIP = headers plus a small first chunk, then 100 bytes every 2 s (would take ~3 hours to reach the 1 MiB cap). Both leave the real loader pending indefinitely; there is no code path that ever settles either promise.

## Why it matters

A custom theme URL is user-supplied configuration, and the changelog URL is a single remote host — either can stall without being down (captive portals, proxies that hold connections, a slow-drip origin). Today that failure mode is indistinguishable from success-in-progress: the caller awaits forever, no error surfaces, no fallback theme/changelog behaviour runs, and the pending fetch (plus its reader loop) is held for the process lifetime. Every other remote fetch in the repo already carries a named timeout; these two were only half-fixed by #1062.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `loadThemeFromUrl` fetches with a named timeout constant (e.g. `AbortSignal.timeout(themeTimeoutMs)`, justified in a comment like the existing `themeMaxResponseBytes` note); a response that has not completed — headers plus bounded body read — within the deadline rejects with a clear error instead of pending forever.
- [ ] The whats-new changelog fetch gets the same treatment: a named timeout combined with `ctx.signal` (e.g. `AbortSignal.any([ctx.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(…)])`), so a stalled changelog settles through the existing `.catch(() => undefined)` path and leaves the update for the next start, as a failed request already does.
- [ ] Regression tests pin the deadline for at least the theme loader, following `loader.test.ts` conventions: a never-resolving fake fetch (or a fetch that only settles on abort) rejects promptly; existing size-cap tests stay green.
- [ ] Normal behaviour unchanged: a prompt, normal-sized theme/changelog loads exactly as today; `bun run test` + typecheck for `packages/ui` (and `packages/gui-extensions` if touched) green on laptop or CI.

Out of scope: the size caps themselves (#1061/#1062, landed), local `blob:`/`data:` fetches (app drafts, word-images — not remote), and fetches that already carry a timeout.

title: fix(schema,core): MCP timeouts have no upper bound — a value over ~24.8 days clamps to ~1ms in the SDK timer and every MCP call times out instantly (#972 residual)

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage

body:
## Problem

MCP per-server timeout settings (`timeout.startup`, `timeout.catalog`, `timeout.execution`) accept any positive integer with **no upper bound**, and the values are passed verbatim to the MCP SDK, whose request/connect timers are raw `setTimeout`. A value above 2^31−1 ms (~24.8 days) inverts its meaning: `setTimeout` clamps it to ~1 ms, so every MCP connect / catalog / tool call to that server times out almost immediately — the user asked for "effectively forever" and got "effectively never". This is the #972 overflow class on a surface #972 did not cover (provider HTTP timeouts were bounded there; MCP timeouts were not).

## Evidence (verified this run, main `8dab871acea4`)

- `packages/schema/src/mcp.ts:7-18` — `TimeoutConfig`: `startup` / `catalog` / `execution` are all bare `PositiveInt` (`Schema.Int.check(Schema.isGreaterThan(0))`, `packages/schema/src/schema.ts:3`): finiteness/integer are enforced, magnitude is not. `3000000000` (34.7 days) decodes cleanly.
- `packages/core/src/config/normalize.ts:266-276` — the legacy `experimental.mcp_timeout` is decoded with the same bare `PositiveInt` and copied into `timeout.catalog` + `timeout.execution`, so the legacy global knob has the identical hole.
- `packages/core/src/mcp/client.ts:222` — `client.connect(transport, { timeout: config.timeout?.startup ?? DEFAULT_STARTUP_TIMEOUT, signal })`: the raw config value goes straight into the SDK connect options.
- `packages/core/src/mcp/client.ts:324-325,368-384` — `catalog` / `execution` objects (`{ timeout: … }`) are passed verbatim as SDK request options for `readResource`, `getPrompt`, and tool calls.
- The MCP SDK (`@modelcontextprotocol/client` 2.3.0, inspected in the laptop clone's installed tree) implements request timeouts with raw `setTimeout`.
- Runtime semantics re-verified this run on the laptop (Node): `setTimeout(fn, 3000000000)` prints `TimeoutOverflowWarning: 3000000000 does not fit into a 32-bit signed integer. Timeout duration was set to 1.` and the callback fired after ~5 ms instead of 34.7 days. Bun follows the same clamp (documented in #972's verification).

Defaults for scale: startup/catalog default to 30 s and execution to 12 h (`packages/core/src/mcp/client.ts:34-36`), so a legitimate value never needs to approach 2^31−1 ms; a cap at or below that boundary loses nothing real.

## Why it matters

MCP timeouts are exactly the knobs users crank up for slow local servers ("give it an hour / a day"). A ms-vs-seconds confusion or a "make it huge" value (e.g. `86400000` intended as seconds = 1000 days in ms) silently makes the server unusable — every call fails instantly with a timeout error that points at the server, not the config — instead of being clamped or rejected at decode with a clear diagnostic.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Mcp.TimeoutConfig` fields (and the legacy `experimental.mcp_timeout` decode in `config/normalize.ts`) enforce a stated upper bound at or below 2^31−1 ms (a named constant with a comment, in the spirit of the bounded timeout introduced for #972), so an oversized value fails decode with a config diagnostic naming the field instead of reaching a timer.
- [ ] Alternatively/additionally, the values are clamped at the `mcp/client.ts` consumption boundary — but decode-time rejection is preferred for consistency with config diagnostics elsewhere; whichever is chosen, no code path can hand a >2^31−1 ms value to the SDK.
- [ ] Values at/above the old defaults and up to the cap behave exactly as today (in particular, the 12 h execution default and multi-hour user values still work).
- [ ] Regression tests: schema/normalize decode rejects (or the client clamps) `2**31` and a ≫2^31−1 value for each of startup/catalog/execution and for legacy `mcp_timeout`; a value just under the cap is accepted.

body:
## Evidence (verified this run on main `506321740d0e2df2b76705bb0d94cad08da11cd3`)

Two remote **error-body** reads still buffer the whole response with `clone().text()` and no size cap. Both decode only a small JSON error struct, and both endpoints are remote / user-configured:

| Site | Read | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/core/src/mcp/oauth.ts:82` | `parseErrorResponse(await response.clone().text())` in `loggedFetch` | OAuth error body from an MCP server's token endpoint, on a failed `refresh_token` / `authorization_code` grant; only `error?.code` / `error?.message` are logged |
| `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/snowflake-cortex.ts:229` | `decodeError(yield* Effect.promise(() => event.response.clone().text()))` in the session `http.response` hook | Snowflake provider 400 response body; `decodeError` (`snowflake-cortex.ts:32-36`) parses only `{message?, error?}` and the hook only checks whether the message contains "conversation complete" |

Distinct from already-tracked work:

- #1019 capped the MCP OAuth **discovery** fetch in this same file — `mcp/oauth.ts` already imports `readBoundedResponseText` (`:26`) and caps discovery at `CONFIGURED_DISCOVERY_MAX_BYTES = 64 * 1024` (`:39`, used `:141`) — but the `loggedFetch` error path at `:82` was not covered.
- #1029 covers the Snowflake **token exchange** reads (`snowflake-cortex.ts:66` `response.text`, `:68` `schemaBodyJson`) via Effect `HttpClient`; the `:229` site is the separate session `http.response` hook on model responses and is not listed there.
- A grep for `clone().text()` across `packages/*/src` returns exactly these two remote-response sites plus `github-copilot.ts:372`, which clones the client's **own outgoing request** (locally constructed) and is out of scope.

Test coverage check: `packages/core/test/mcp-oauth.test.ts:649-687` pins the discovery cap only — nothing bounds the `loggedFetch` error read; `packages/core/test/plugin/provider-snowflake-cortex.test.ts` has no test for the 400-response hook / "conversation complete" path.

## Why it matters

A misbehaving or malicious MCP server (user-configured URL) or Snowflake endpoint can return an arbitrarily large error body on exactly the paths meant to handle failures, buffering it whole into memory during token refresh/exchange or a model call. The bounded primitive for native fetch responses already exists in the same package — `readBoundedResponseText` in `packages/core/src/tool/http-body.ts` — and one of the two files already imports it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `mcp/oauth.ts:82` reads the OAuth error body through a bounded path (`readBoundedResponseText` or equivalent) with a named, documented cap (the file's existing 64 KiB discovery cap is the natural precedent); over-cap bodies degrade to "no parsed error" (the current `orElseSucceed(() => undefined)` behaviour) instead of buffering unbounded.
- [ ] `snowflake-cortex.ts:229` reads the 400 response body through a bounded path with a named, documented cap; over-cap bodies simply do not match the "conversation complete" check.
- [ ] Tests verify bounded behaviour for both paths: a small error body still parses (MCP error code/message logged; Snowflake "conversation complete" still rewritten to the synthetic stop response), and an over-cap body does not.
- [ ] No change to the outgoing-request clone in `github-copilot.ts:372` or to the token-exchange reads tracked in #1029.

body:
## Finding

PR #801 added the non-ISO calendar check (`namedDateParts`: "Feb 30 2026", "30 Feb 2026", "2026/02/30", non-ISO hour-24) identically to six copies of the checked date parser, but the new named-form behavior is pinned by tests in **core only**. The ai, tui, and cli copies have no test that exercises a single named-form spelling, so a future edit that diverges one of those copies regresses silently.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #801 (merged, commit `24511d3b`, for #798). Its body states: "The ai/tui/cli copies are byte-identical logic and are covered by CI for their packages." CI runs each package's existing tests — but no existing test in ai/tui/cli passes a named-form date to these parsers.
- Current main `195bdae1` — the copies:
  - `packages/ai/src/route/executor.ts:44` — `namedDateParts` (used by `parseHttpDate`)
  - `packages/ai/src/protocols/replicate-images.ts:136` — `namedDateParts` (used by `parseCompletedAt`)
  - `packages/tui/src/util/form.ts:164` — `namedDateParts` (used by `validDateTime`)
  - `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/auth/form.ts:206` — `namedDateParts` (used by `validDateTime`)
- Test coverage on current main (grep over all test trees for the named spellings):
  - Named forms ("Feb 30 2026", "30 Feb 2026", "2026/02/30", "Feb 30 2026 24:00") appear ONLY in `packages/core/test/form.test.ts` and `packages/core/test/model-route-limits.test.ts`.
  - ai: `packages/ai/test/provider/replicate-images.test.ts` pins only ISO invalid forms ("2026-02-30T10:00:00Z", "2026-04-31T10:00:00Z"); `packages/ai/test/response-hook.test.ts` pins only ISO retry-after forms (#713 cases).
  - tui: `packages/tui/test/util/form.test.ts:69-70` pins only ISO invalid date-times.
  - cli: `packages/cli/test/auth-form.test.ts` date-time cases pin only ISO invalid forms ("2026-02-30T10:00:00Z", "2025-02-29T10:00:00Z", hour-24 ISO).
- Dedupe: no open or recently closed issue covers tests for the #801 copies (the #798 issue is closed; its tests landed core-only).

## Why it matters

The six copies are deliberately duplicated logic — the fleet's own history in this area (#717/#779/#785/#798) is a chain of one copy being fixed while another kept the bug. Untested copies are exactly how the next divergence ships: the named-form check is the only thing standing between a provider's "Feb 30" Retry-After / completed_at and a rolled-over Mar 2 instant in ai, and between a user-typed named date and acceptance in tui/cli forms.

body:
# fix(cli,server): stats --days over 3720 always fails server-side, and the error says the range "must end after it starts"

## Summary

`opencode stats --days N` accepts any non-negative integer, but every `N >= 3721` is guaranteed to fail: the CLI builds a range wider than the stats service's maximum span, the service rejects it, and the server handler then reports a message that describes a different problem — so the user is told their range "must end after it starts" when it plainly does.

## Evidence (main `195bdae185`)

- CLI flag has no upper bound — `packages/cli/src/commands/commands.ts:329-333`: `days: Flag.Int("days")` with schema only `Schema.Int.check(Schema.isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(0))` (contrast the sibling `year` flag at :334-338, bounded 1970–9999, and `limit` at :348-352, bounded below).
- The handler turns days into a range with no cap — `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/stats.ts:148-157` (`statsRange`): `from` is local midnight `Math.max(0, input.days - 1)` days ago, `to` is now + 1 ms, and the pair is sent to `client.session.stats`.
- The service rejects any span over 3720 days — `packages/core/src/session/stats.ts:80-97`: `Window = 31 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1_000`, `MaxSpan = 120 * Window` (= 3720 days), and `SessionStats.get` fails with `InvalidRangeError` when `to - from > MaxSpan` (the bound added for #959, so one request cannot run millions of sequential window scans).
- The server mislabels the failure — `packages/server/src/handlers/session.ts:113-124`: every `SessionStats.get` error is mapped to `InvalidRequestError({ message: "Stats range must end after it starts" })`, whether the actual cause was `from >= to` or the span cap.

## Verification (laptop probe, this run)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-30-stats-days/probe.ts` (laptop, repo at `195bdae185`) extracts the real `Window`/`MaxSpan` constants and the real `statsRange` formula from the source files and evaluates the boundary at three times of day:

- `--days 3720`: span 3719.00–3720.00 days → accepted at 00:01, 12:35 and 23:59.
- `--days 3721`: span 3720.00–3721.00 days → `InvalidRangeError` at all three times (from is midnight 3720 days ago and `to` is now + 1 ms, so the span always exceeds 3720 days).
- `--days 4000` and `--days 100000`: always `InvalidRangeError`.

So 3720 is the largest `--days` value that can ever succeed, and the failure mode for anything larger is a misleading server error after a round trip, not a flag error.

## Why it matters

- A documented flag silently has a hard ceiling roughly a tenth of the values a user might plausibly try for long-range stats ("show me the last 5000 days" / lifetime-ish queries on a long-lived install), and `--all` is the only workaround — there is no hint of that.
- The error message actively misdiagnoses the problem: users and agents debugging it will check their range ordering, which was never wrong.
- This is the CLI/server half of the #959 contract: the service bound was added deliberately, but neither of its two callers' surfaces (flag schema, handler error mapping) was updated to match.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `opencode stats --days 3721` (and anything larger) fails at the CLI with a clear message naming the maximum usable days (3720, or a rounder documented cap at or below it), instead of reaching the server.
- [ ] The `session.stats` handler distinguishes the two `InvalidRangeError` causes: a reversed/empty range keeps the "must end after it starts" message; an over-wide span reports that the range is too wide (and ideally the maximum span).
- [ ] `--days 3720`, `--days 365`, `--days 0`, `--year` and `--all` behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] Tests cover the boundary: stats handler/flag tests for 3720 vs 3721 (or the chosen cap), and a server handler test for the two distinct error messages.

## Problem

The standing laptop OpenCode server on 127.0.0.1:13420 accepts session creation but its prompt POST never progresses: observed hanging for over 15 minutes producing nothing. This is a server-side stall, not a provider failure — no error is returned and no output is produced.

## Evidence (OpenClaw-vs-OpenCode comparison, 2026-10-29 early morning CDT, tracked on developing-today/code#2171)

During setup of the five-fixture comparison, two OpenCode surfaces were tried and found non-viable:

- `opencode run` (CLI) blocks indefinitely without creating a session (two attempts killed) — already tracked in #193.
- The standing server on 127.0.0.1:13420 accepted a session, but its prompt POST hung >15 min producing nothing. One F1 prompt POST died with that server; the fixture was then executed once, to completion, on the working route.

Workaround used for the whole comparison: the OpenChamber-managed OpenCode instance on 127.0.0.1:36183, agent `build`, route `opencode-route/workhorse` — all five fixtures completed there. So the same binary/config family serves prompts fine via the managed instance while the standing server's prompt route stalls.

## Impact

This blocks the fleet's standard session route: any session driven through the standing server's prompt POST stalls silently. All comparison work had to be routed around it to the managed instance. A stall with no error and no output is also invisible to callers — there is nothing to retry against.

## What to investigate

- What the standing server's prompt POST path waits on after session creation that the managed instance's path does not (event subscription, watcher, session attach, directory scope handling).
- Whether the stall reproduces with a fresh session on the same server today, and whether server logs show the prompt request arriving at all.
- Whether a prompt timeout / progress signal is owed so a stalled prompt surfaces as an error instead of hanging forever.

## Acceptance

- Root cause identified and fixed, or a documented workaround with the blocking component named.
- A prompt POST to the standing server completes (or fails loudly) instead of hanging >15 min.

## Acceptance criteria

- The hang is reproduced against the standing server on 127.0.0.1:13420 (session created, prompt POST stalls) and the stall point is identified (server log / stack evidence linked here) — or the server is shown healthy under the same repro and the issue is closed with that evidence.
- A prompt POST to the standing server completes (or errors visibly) within a bounded time in a verification run; indefinite silent hangs are the failure being closed.

title: fix(core): DigitalOcean OAuth callback server reads its token POST body unbounded — no byte cap on the one inbound callback body in core

labels.name: kind/security

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Problem

The DigitalOcean browser-OAuth callback server reads its token POST body **unbounded**: every chunk is pushed onto an array and concatenated at `end`, with no byte cap and no declared-size pre-check. It is the only OAuth callback server in core that accepts a POST body at all — every sibling callback (chatgpt, openai, mcp/oauth) takes its code from the GET query string — and every other body read in these flows has been bounded under design #1127. This inbound surface was left behind.

The legitimate body is tiny and machine-generated: the shared callback page's bootstrap script POSTs a JSON object built from the URL hash (token, expiry, state) — a few hundred bytes. Anything larger is not a real callback.

## Evidence (verified on main `8b5ed112e5`, 2026-11-07)

- `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/digitalocean.ts:87-90` — the token-path handler:
  - line 88: `request.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => chunks.push(chunk))` — no running total, no limit.
  - line 90: at `end`, `Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8")` is decoded — the whole body is buffered in memory first.
- Probe (laptop worktree of current main, temporary test using the existing `provider-digitalocean.test.ts` fixture harness, removed after the run): a token POST with a 3,000,001-character token (3,000,061-byte JSON body) returned **200 in 71 ms** and the credential was saved with the full 3,000,001-character token. A bounded reader (the fleet's usual 64 KiB–1 MiB caps) would have rejected it long before decode.
- Precedents the fix should follow, all already in tree:
  - `packages/core/src/oauth/page.ts:117` — the callback page itself caps its error excerpt at 65,536 bytes (`ERROR_EXCERPT_MAX_BYTES`) after #1386.
  - `packages/core/src/tool/http-body.ts` — `collectBoundedResponseBody`: declared-size pre-check + per-chunk running bound.
  - #1893 / #1862 — outbound token-exchange reads capped at 1 MiB for the same reason: an unbounded body is a memory-exhaustion surface.
- Dedup: title/keyword search over open and closed issues for "digitalocean" + callback/unbounded returned #771/#899 (expires_in grammar/bound — different site, closed), #994 (expires refactor, closed), and #1386 (the callback *page's* outbound POST deadline + error read — the browser side, closed/fixed). No issue owns the server-side body read in `digitalocean.ts`.

## Why it matters

The server listens on the fixed loopback port 1456 for the whole login attempt. While it is up, any local process — or any web page that can POST to localhost — can stream an arbitrarily large body at it: the process buffers all of it before responding, so a multi-GB drip exhausts memory in the user's OpenCode process, and a body that never ends also never resolves or fails the login Deferred (the attempt hangs with no error). One cap at the single inbound handler closes both.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The token POST handler enforces a byte cap on the accumulated body (suggested 64 KiB, matching the callback page's own excerpt cap — a legitimate callback body is a few hundred bytes), counting bytes as chunks arrive, not after `Buffer.concat`.
- [ ] An over-cap body fails the login attempt with a clear error and an HTTP error response to the poster, and the listener is released so a fresh login attempt can start (mirroring the existing invalid-callback tests).
- [ ] Normal callbacks are unchanged: the existing success, 30-day-fallback, and invalid-body tests in `packages/core/test/plugin/provider-digitalocean.test.ts` still pass.
- [ ] A regression test posts an over-cap body and pins the rejection.
- [ ] `bun run check:bounded-http` disposition: if the gate's scanner covers inbound server reads, the site is dispositioned as bounded; if not, say so on the issue rather than editing the allowlist blindly.

title: fix(ai): moonshot tool-schema projection rewrites literal enum/default/const values as schemas — structured values are corrupted

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: priority/normal

labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: area/typescript
labels.description: TypeScript code area

body:
## Bug

`ToolSchemaProjection.moonshot` (`packages/ai/src/protocols/utils/tool-schema.ts`, `moonshotNode`) recurses into **every** key of a schema node — including the value keys `enum`, `default`, `const`, and `examples`, whose contents are literal data, not schemas. A structured literal whose object values happen to carry schema-shaped keys is rewritten as if it were a schema:

- an `items` array inside a literal is folded by the Moonshot tuple rule (`tupleItemsSchema`) into `{ anyOf: [...] }`,
- a literal carrying `$ref` is cut down to `{ $ref }` alone (sibling data silently dropped) via the node's `$ref` early return,
- a literal `prefixItems` is renamed/folded into `items`.

Both sibling schema walkers in the same package explicitly exempt value keys for exactly this reason: `gemini-json-schema.ts` (`VALUES = {const, default, enum, examples, dependentRequired}`, applied in `normalizeNode`, `cutLoops`, and `collectDefRefs`) and antigravity's `convertSchemaNode` (`SCHEMA_VALUE_KEYS = {enum, default, example}`). The moonshot walker has no equivalent guard.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `4fd5c5520b`)

Probe `probe-moonshot-values.ts`, laptop probe worktree `probe-2026-11-07-creator-1335` (`packages/ai`), calling `ToolSchemaProjection.moonshot` directly:

| input (property `v`) | output |
|---|---|
| `{ enum: [{ items: ["a", "b"] }] }` | `{ type: "object", enum: [{ items: { anyOf: ["a", "b"] } }] }` — literal array rewritten |
| `{ enum: [{ $ref: "#/x", extra: 1 }] }` | `{ type: "object", enum: [{ $ref: "#/x" }] }` — `extra: 1` silently dropped |
| `{ enum: [{ prefixItems: [{ type: "string" }], note: "keep" }] }` | `{ enum: [{ items: { type: "string" }, note: "keep" }] }` — literal key renamed |
| `{ type: "object", default: { items: [1, 2, 3] } }` | `default: { items: { anyOf: [1, 2, 3] } }` |
| `{ const: { items: ["x"] } }` | `const: { items: "x" }` |

Controls unchanged: scalar enums (`enum: ["a", "b"]` → type derived, values verbatim), a real tuple schema (`items: [{type: string}, {type: number}]` → folded `anyOf`, the intended #1574 behavior), and a plain string schema.

## Why it matters

The projection runs on every tool schema sent to Moonshot/Kimi models (`ToolSchemaProjection.tools`, applied to every request). A tool whose parameter legitimately enumerates or defaults to structured values — config objects, payload templates, fixed shapes — is sent upstream with its allowed/default values corrupted: the model is told the enum contains shapes that were never allowed, and real allowed values disappear. This is the value/invariant half of the fidelity contract tracked by design #1684; the antigravity half of the same class was #1557.

## Acceptance criteria

- `moonshotNode` returns the contents of `const`, `default`, `enum`, and `examples` verbatim (matching the sibling walkers' value-key sets), at every nesting level.
- New tests in `packages/ai/test/tool-schema-projection.test.ts` pin: structured enum values with `items`/`prefixItems`/`$ref`-shaped keys pass through unchanged; structured `default` and `const` values pass through unchanged; the existing scalar-enum type derivation and the #1574 tuple fold are unchanged.
- Existing `tool-schema-projection` and `tool-schema-fidelity-corpus` suites pass; `packages/ai` typecheck clean.

title: fix(ai): antigravity convertSchema still forces OBJECT onto constraint-only roots — minItems/minLength/minimum roots are narrowed to objects and their constraints stranded (#1901 remainder)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/ai

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: area/typescript
labels.description: TypeScript code area

body:
## Summary

`convertSchema` in the antigravity protocol still forces `type: "OBJECT"` onto roots whose only keywords constrain a **non-object** type — an array root described only by `minItems`/`maxItems`, a string root described only by `minLength`/`maxLength`/`pattern`, or a number root described only by `minimum`/`maximum`. The forced OBJECT narrows the schema to objects only (excluding every value the constraints were written for) and strands the constraint keyword on a type it can never apply to. This is the #1667 / #1901 defect pattern, one keyword family past the guard those fixes built.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probe worktree `probe-2026-11-07-creator-1235` at main aca6992391)

- `packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts:286-315` — `convertSchema` applies the OBJECT default when `converted` has no `type` and none of `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf`/`not`/`enum`/`items`/`prefixItems`. The constraint keywords `minItems`, `maxItems`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `minimum`, `maximum` are not in the guard list, although each constrains exactly one non-object type (arrays, strings, numbers respectively) — the same reasoning #1901 recorded for `items`/`prefixItems` ("its element keywords constrain arrays only, so a forced OBJECT strands them on a root they can never reach").
- Probe `packages/ai/probe-schema-root.ts` (worktree above, run with bun against the real `convertSchema`, both Gemini and Anthropic targets — identical results):
  - `{minItems: 2}` → `{"minItems":2,"type":"OBJECT"}`; `{maxItems: 3}` → `{"maxItems":3,"type":"OBJECT"}`
  - `{minLength: 2}` → `{"minLength":2,"type":"OBJECT"}`; `{pattern: "^a+$"}` → `{"pattern":"^a+$","type":"OBJECT"}`
  - `{minimum: 5}` → `{"minimum":5,"type":"OBJECT"}`; `{minimum: 5, maximum: 9}` → `{"minimum":5,"maximum":9,"type":"OBJECT"}`
  - Controls unchanged, as pinned by #1667/#1901: `{enum:["a","b"]}` → no type; `{items:{type:"string"}}` → no type; a plain object schema → `type:"OBJECT"`; `{}` → `type:"OBJECT"`; `{minProperties: 1}` (an object keyword) → `type:"OBJECT"`.
  - Non-root nodes are unaffected: a nested `{minItems: 2}` property keeps no forced type — the defect is only the root default in `convertSchema`, not `convertSchemaNode`.
- Baseline: `bun test test/provider/antigravity.test.ts` on the same worktree at aca6992391 — 25 pass / 0 fail.

## Why it matters

- A constraint-only root is how a caller says "an array of at least 2", "a string of at least 2 chars", or "a number ≥ 5" without restating the type. After conversion the upstream model is told the parameter is an object with an inapplicable keyword: valid calls (arrays/strings/numbers) are outside the declared type, and the constraint itself is dead. On the Anthropic re-serialization path (#1550) the same narrowed schema is what gets validated.
- #1667 (allOf/not roots) and #1901 (enum/items/prefixItems roots) established the rule and the fix shape — a root that describes itself takes no OBJECT default. The guard list simply was not extended to the single-type constraint keywords, so the rule is currently applied inconsistently across keyword families.

## Acceptance criteria

- `convertSchema` (both targets) leaves a root carrying any of `minItems`, `maxItems`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `minimum`, or `maximum` — with no type/branch/enum/items keyword — without a forced `type`, mirroring the #1901 guard; the constraint keywords themselves pass through unchanged.
- Object-keyword roots are unchanged: `{minProperties: 1}`, `{}`, and ordinary object schemas still get `type: "OBJECT"`; all #1667/#1901 controls keep their current outputs.
- Tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/antigravity.test.ts` pin the new roots (array/string/number constraint-only, both targets) alongside the existing controls; the ai provider/protocol suites stay green and ai typecheck passes.

## Related

- #1667 (allOf/not roots, closed), #1901 (enum/items/prefixItems roots, closed), #1557 (const dropping — a different defect in the same converter), #1926 (type-union branch merging, open), #1684 (the fidelity-contract design this converter family answers to).

## The defect

`packages/ai/src/quota/index.ts`, `listConfiguredQuotaProviders` (:84-145):

- The function's own docstring (:76-83) promises: "Providers turned off in config (`disabled_providers`) are left out unless `includeDisabled` is set."
- Every credential provider honours that: the configured list is filtered through `isProviderDisabled` (:98-103), and instance ids are skipped when disabled (:107).
- The built-in turso fetcher does not: after being skipped in the configured loop (:90, `continue`), it is appended unconditionally at :142-143 — `visible.push(turso.providerId)` — with no disabled check and no `includeDisabled` check.
- `fetchAllQuota` (:325-335) fetches every id the listing returns, so a disabled turso is still fetched on every default `opencode quota` run: its fetch resolves a Bitwarden secret (spawning `bws`) and calls the Turso API (turso.ts:184-195).
- The same module's catalogue disagrees with the listing: `listQuotaProviderCatalogue` marks turso `disabled: true` via `isProviderDisabled` (:161) while the listing simultaneously includes it.

The CLI assembles `disabledProviders` verbatim from the merged config's `disabled_providers` entries (`packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/quota.ts:241-260`), so putting `turso` in `disabled_providers` is exactly the user action this path silently ignores.

## Runtime probe (laptop worktree, `probe-turso-disabled.ts`, kept in the worktree)

Driving the real exported functions with an empty credential set:

- Control (nothing disabled): listing `["antigravity","turso"]`, catalogue `turso.disabled=false`.
- `disabledProviders = {"turso"}`: listing `["antigravity","turso"]` — unchanged — while catalogue `turso.disabled=true`. The listing and the catalogue contradict each other on the same context.
- `disabledProviders = {"turso"}` with `includeDisabled: true`: listing identical again — the flag that is supposed to govern disabled providers has no effect on this row either way.

## Why it matters

`disabled_providers` is the one switch a user has to stop a quota read — for turso that read is not free: it spawns a secrets-manager child process and makes authenticated API calls on every default quota run. A disable that is honoured by every provider except the one built-in fetcher is a silent no-op on exactly the row the user cannot remove any other way, and the listing/catalogue contradiction means downstream consumers cannot agree on whether the row is off.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One explicit disposition, recorded in the closing note: either the listing honours the disabled filter for turso like every other provider (left out unless `includeDisabled`), or turso's exemption is deliberate and the docstring at index.ts:76-83 plus the catalogue's `disabled` flag are corrected so the three surfaces agree.
- [ ] If the filter is honoured: with `turso` disabled and `includeDisabled` unset, `fetchAllQuota` performs no turso fetch (no `bws` spawn, no Turso API call); with `includeDisabled: true` the row returns.
- [ ] `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins the turso-disabled listing case (and the `includeDisabled` case under the chosen disposition); no existing test pins this today.
- [ ] Existing quota suite stays green; the 13-provider registry inventory (rule 7) is unchanged.

The turso over-100% publish disposition (code#6227) is about window figures, not listing inclusion.

# fix(ai): claude quota spend toAmount trusts the wire exponent — exponent 999 publishes "$0.00 / $0.00" for a real $5/$10 spend, exponent -2 inflates it 100x

Verified 2026-11-07 on origin/main `cfc5e3d82c` (merge of PR #1916), in a laptop worktree (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-06-creator-2335`, kept).

## The defect

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/claude.ts`, `toAmount` (:128-133):

```ts
const minor = toNumber(money?.amount_minor)
if (minor === null) return null
const exponent = toNumber(money?.exponent) ?? 2
return minor / 10 ** exponent
```

The divisor exponent is taken from the wire with no range validation at all. Money exponents are a tiny closed set in practice (ISO 4217 currency exponents are 0-3; Anthropic's payload uses 2). An out-of-range exponent silently rescales a real amount into a false one instead of reading as absent:

- A large exponent underflows the amount to zero — a real spend publishes as `$0.00`, the most misleading value a quota label can carry (it reads as "nothing spent").
- A negative exponent multiplies the amount — a $5 spend publishes as `$500.00`.

Every other numeric field in this quota module is range-checked at the boundary (percents clamped, timestamps null on non-positive, zero/negative limits read as no-data #1799/#1750, negative banner amounts read as null). The exponent — the one field that scales all the others — is the exception. Disposition of the amount's SIGN is a separate issue (negative `amount_minor` publishing raw); this issue is only the exponent's range.

## Runtime probe (laptop worktree, `probe-claude-spend.ts`, kept in the worktree)

Driving the real exported `toClaudeUsage` with `spend: { enabled: true, percent: 50, used: {...}, limit: {...} }`:

- `used { amount_minor: 500, exponent: 999 }`, `limit { amount_minor: 1000, exponent: 999 }` → `extra_usage` window, `valueLabel: "$0.00 / $0.00"` (the real $5.00 / $10.00 spend erased to zero).
- `used { amount_minor: 5, exponent: -2 }`, `limit { amount_minor: 10, exponent: -2 }` → `valueLabel: "$500.00 / $1000.00"` (100x inflation).
- Control `exponent: 2` → `"$5.00 / $10.00"` (correct, unchanged).

## Why it matters

The `extra_usage` label is the paid-overage signal for a Claude subscription. A corrupted exponent — a buggy or mimicking gateway, a payload shape change — currently converts directly into a fabricated spend figure with no trace: either a false zero (headroom that does not exist, the failure mode the window contract exists to prevent) or a 100x overstatement. Reading an implausible exponent as absent costs nothing: the percent figure on the same window still publishes, and a spend object with no other figure falls to the no-data contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An `exponent` outside one explicit, recorded valid range (the ISO 4217 0-3 range is the natural choice; the chosen range and its rationale are recorded in the closing note) makes `toAmount` read that money object as absent (null), consistent with the module's other boundary dispositions.
- [ ] In-range exponents (0, 2, 3) and the absent-exponent default of 2 are unchanged (`$5.00 / $10.00` control).
- [ ] A spend window whose percent is valid still publishes on the percent when its amounts read as absent.
- [ ] `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins the over-range, negative-exponent, and in-range control cases in the claude spend coverage.
- [ ] Existing quota suite stays green.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues this run for claude spend / exponent / `amount_minor`: no covering issue. No test in quota.test.ts exercises the claude spend path's exponent at all. The negative-amount disposition for the same function is filed separately this run (sign and scale are different defects with different fixes); #1913 (open, OpenRouter negative spend) and #1799 (closed, zero-limit) are different providers/fields.

# fix(ai): claude quota extra-usage spend publishes negative amounts — "$-5.00 / $10.00", and a negative-only payload still returns ok:true

Verified 2026-11-07 on origin/main `cfc5e3d82c` (merge of PR #1916), in a laptop worktree (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-06-creator-2335`, kept).

## The defect

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/claude.ts`:

- `toAmount` (:128-133) converts a money object with `minor / 10 ** exponent` and no sign check — a negative `amount_minor` yields a negative amount.
- The spend block (:206-213) formats that amount straight into the `extra_usage` window's label via `formatSpendLabel` (:136-142). The window's `usedPercent` comes from the separate wire `spend.percent` (clamped), so nothing cross-checks the label's sign.
- `addWindow` (:156-166) publishes the window whenever a percent OR a valueLabel exists — so a spend object whose only figure is a negative amount still mints an `extra_usage` window, and `fetchQuota` then returns `ok: true` (the #1915 no-data contract only fires when windows AND models are both empty).

A negative spend/limit is a figure that cannot exist. Sibling code in this same quota module treats it as absent: meta's `parseBillingBanner` maps a negative `remaining_minor_units` to null (pinned by test), turso's `numNonNegative`, opencode-go's `toMicroCents` (rejects `< 0`), and command-code's `monthlyRemaining >= 0` gate (#1744) all read a negative amount as no data. OpenRouter's identical unlimited-path defect was filed as #1913. The claude spend path is the remaining raw-negative money label.

## Runtime probe (laptop worktree, `probe-claude-spend.ts`, kept in the worktree)

Driving the real exported `toClaudeUsage`:

- `{ spend: { enabled: true, percent: 50, used: { amount_minor: -500, exponent: 2, currency: "USD" }, limit: { amount_minor: 1000, exponent: 2, currency: "USD" } } }` → `extra_usage` window, `valueLabel: "$-5.00 / $10.00"`.
- Same with the limit negative (`amount_minor: -1000`) → `valueLabel: "$5.00 / $-10.00"`.
- `{ spend: { enabled: true, used: { amount_minor: -500, exponent: 2, currency: "USD" } } }` (no percent, no limit) → `extra_usage` window with `usedPercent: null` and `valueLabel: "$-5.00"` — the negative amount is the window's ONLY figure, so through `fetchQuota` this payload alone publishes `ok: true`.
- Controls: positive `{ amount_minor: 500 } / { amount_minor: 1000 }` → `"$5.00 / $10.00"` (correct); zero used → `"$0.00 / $10.00"` (correct); `{ spend: { enabled: true } }` with no figures → no window (correct, unchanged).

## Why it matters

The `extra_usage` window is the paid-overage signal for a Claude subscription: downstream consumers read its label as money actually spent against a real limit. A negative spend is impossible wire data (a billing glitch, a refund/adjustment spelled as spend, a mimicking gateway); publishing it as `ok: true` quota data — in the negative-only case as the provider's sole result, defeating the #1915 no-data contract in spirit — teaches consumers a figure that cannot be true, in the one shape (money amounts) where this fleet has repeatedly chosen "bad data reads as absent" over fabrication.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A negative `amount_minor` on `spend.used` or `spend.limit` gets one explicit disposition — read as absent (the meta `parseBillingBanner` precedent in this same module) is the sibling-consistent choice; any other disposition is chosen and recorded in the closing note.
- [ ] A spend payload whose only figure is a negative amount publishes no `extra_usage` window, so through `fetchQuota` it reaches the existing "No quota data in response" contract when nothing else is usable.
- [ ] Positive and zero amounts are unchanged (`$5.00 / $10.00`, `$0.00 / $10.00` controls), and a valid percent-only spend window still publishes.
- [ ] `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins the negative-used, negative-limit, and negative-only cases beside the existing claude describes (the spend path currently has no tests at all).
- [ ] Existing quota suite stays green.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues this run for claude spend / negative amount / `amount_minor`: no covering issue. #1913 (open) is OpenRouter's unlimited-path `usage_monthly`, a different provider and field; #1915 (closed) is the figure-less-200 no-data contract for limits/legacy windows and does not touch the spend block; #1882 (open) is codex `spend_control`, a different provider. # fix(ai): antigravity quota summary path publishes figure-less buckets as all-null-percent windows

Verified 2026-11-06 on origin/main `10f305865f` (merge of PR #1732), in a laptop worktree (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-06-creator-2235/wt`, kept).

## The defect

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/antigravity.ts`, `parseBucket` (~:271-307) — the summary path, distinct from the per-model fallback filed as #1912:

```ts
const remainingFraction = toNumber(record?.remainingFraction)
const remainingPercent = remainingFraction !== null ? Math.round(remainingFraction * 100) : null
const usedPercent = remainingPercent !== null ? Math.min(100, Math.max(0, 100 - remainingPercent)) : null
...
return { label, seconds, remainingFraction, window: toUsageWindow({ usedPercent, windowSeconds: seconds, resetAt }) }
```

Once the bucket's window string is recognized (`5h` / `weekly` / `daily`), the bucket publishes its window **unconditionally** — including when `remainingFraction` is absent, so `usedPercent` and `remainingPercent` are both null and the window carries no quota figure at all: only a duration and a reset the payload happened to include. `transformSummary` (~:322-330) stores that window in the group's windows (keep-first), and `transformModels`' matched-group branch (~:356-375) then republishes it as every matched model's window set.

That is the phantom-window shape window-contract rule 4 in `packages/ai/src/quota/types.ts` forbids ("No figure, no window — an empty/all-null/zero-limit window-shaped object publishes no window"), and the reset-only spelling two siblings disposition explicitly:

- codex (#1762): "a duration/reset with no percent is dispositioned the same way (dropped, not published with a null percent)".
- meta key-endpoint (#1907): figure-less objects dropped instead of publishing all-null windows beside real ones.

#1768's fix taught this path to propagate a missing fraction as null instead of inventing 1-as-fully-remaining — but null propagation into a published window is still publication: the window exists, with a fabricated kind (the recognized string) and no figure.

## Runtime probe (laptop worktree, `probe-creator.ts`, kept in the worktree)

Driving the real exported `parseBucket` / `transformSummary` / `transformModels`:

- `parseBucket({ window: "5h", resetTime: "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z" })` (reset + kind, no fraction) → a `5h` window with `usedPercent: null, remainingPercent: null, windowSeconds: 18000` and the reset populated.
- `transformSummary({ groups: [{ displayName: "Gemini", buckets: [{ window: "5h", resetTime: … }] }] })` → the group's windows carry that same all-null-percent `5h` window, and it becomes the group's `bucket5h`.
- `transformModels({ models: { "gemini-x": {} } }, <that group>)` → `"gemini-x"` inherits the phantom `5h` window verbatim.
- Control `parseBucket({ window: "5h", remainingFraction: 0.5, resetTime: … })` → real window, 50% used / 50% remaining (correct, unchanged).
- Control `parseBucket({})` → `null` (an unrecognized/absent window string is already skipped, per #1768 — only the recognized-but-figure-less case slips through).

Because `fetchWithCandidates` returns `ok: true` whenever at least one model entry exists, a summary whose buckets are all figure-less reads as a successful quota read whose every model carries an all-null-percent window.

## Why it matters

The summary path is the primary path — it serves every model that matches a group, which is the normal case; the #1912 fallback only serves unmatched models. A figure-less bucket (an upstream shape change, a bucket reported before its first figure, a new window kind spelled with a familiar string) currently manufactures a window per group and per model from a reset timestamp alone, telling downstream consumers a 5-hour/weekly window exists with unknown usage instead of the honest absence. It also feeds the weekly-constrained ordering in `transformModels`, whose comparisons the code itself says require the fractions to actually be present (#1768 comment, ~:357-362).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A bucket whose `remainingFraction` carries no usable figure publishes no window (the `parseBucket`-returns-null disposition, matching its unrecognized-kind case, is the precedent — or another single disposition, chosen and recorded in the closing note).
- [ ] `transformSummary` groups built only from figure-less buckets carry no windows from those buckets, and matched models inherit none.
- [ ] The real-figure control is unchanged: a present `remainingFraction` still publishes its window with the existing label derivation and keep-first collision behaviour.
- [ ] `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins: reset-only bucket, figure-less summary group, matched-model inheritance, and the real-fraction control.
- [ ] Existing quota suite stays green; the per-model fallback path is #1912's scope and is unchanged by this fix.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for "antigravity parseBucket", "antigravity summary phantom", and "antigravity transformModels" this run: no covering issue. #1912 (open) is the per-model **fallback** branch and explicitly scopes the summary-group path out ("the summary-group path is unchanged"). #1768 (closed) covered bucket labelling, keep-first, and missing-fraction-as-1 in this path; it did not cover a recognized bucket with no fraction still publishing a window. #1909 (open) is only about the stale inventory rows.

# fix(ai): claude quota returns ok:true with empty windows for a 200 payload carrying no usable quota data

Verified 2026-11-06 on origin/main `10f305865f` (merge of PR #1732), in a laptop worktree (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-06-creator-2235/wt`, kept).

## The defect

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/claude.ts`, `provider.fetchQuota` (~:265-280): after a 200 response, the result of `toClaudeUsage(payload)` is published unconditionally:

```ts
const { windows, models } = toClaudeUsage(payload)
const usage = Object.keys(models).length > 0 ? { windows, models } : { windows }
return withMetadata(buildResult({ providerId, providerName, ok: true, configured: true, usage, ... }), credential)
```

There is no empty check. `toClaudeUsage`'s own guard (`addWindow`: a window needs a percent or a value label) correctly produces **no** windows for a figure-less payload — and the provider then reports that empty set as a successful quota read: `ok: true, configured: true, usage: { windows: {} }`, no error.

Claude is the only one of the 13 quota providers that does this. Every sibling implements the no-data contract on the same shape:

- codex (~:176-185), with the contract stated in its comment: "No usable quota or credit data at all: the sibling providers' no-data contract (ClinePass/DeepSeek/OpenRouter), not ok:true with empty windows (#1762)" → `ok: false`, error `"No quota data in response"`.
- cline-pass (~:97-105), deepseek (~:100), openrouter (~:91-119), turso (~:213), opencode-go (throws "usage data could not be parsed"), command-code (same throw), groq (its `no-quota-surface` error class), opendesign (throws on unparseable windows), mistral (console read with no budgets is a `no-data` failure), meta (~:248-258: no windows + not subs-active → `ok: false`, failureClass `no-data`).
- antigravity (~:437): `ok: false` when `transformModels` yields no model entries.

## Runtime probe (laptop worktree, `probe-creator.ts`, kept in the worktree)

Driving the real `provider.fetchQuota` with a stubbed fetch and an env credential:

- `{}` → `ok: true, configured: true, usage: { windows: {} }` — a successful read of nothing.
- `{ limits: [] }` → identical `ok: true` with empty windows.
- `{ limits: [{ kind: "session", resets_at: "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z" }] }` (a limit entry with a reset but no percent — no figure) → identical `ok: true` with empty windows.
- Control `{ five_hour: { utilization: 10, resets_at: "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z" } }` → `ok: true` with the real `5h` window at 10% used (correct, unchanged).

## Why it matters

`ok: true` is the signal downstream consumers (the aggregator gatherer, the dashboard, quota-aware placement) act on: an empty-but-successful Claude row reads as "the account was read and has no limits" instead of the honest "the read carried no quota data" — a wire-shape change, a partial Anthropic response, or a new account type silently becomes a healthy-looking empty picture, and the failure is invisible precisely because nothing errors. The sibling fleet settled this exact question in #1762: no usable data is an error row, not a success.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A 200 payload from which `toClaudeUsage` derives no windows and no models returns the sibling no-data contract: `ok: false`, `configured: true`, error `"No quota data in response"` (still carrying the credential metadata via `withMetadata`).
- [ ] Payloads with any real window (limits, legacy `five_hour`/`seven_day`, spend) or any model-scoped window are unchanged, byte-for-byte.
- [ ] `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins the provider-level cases: empty object, empty `limits`, figure-less limit entry, and the real-figure control.
- [ ] Existing quota suite stays green.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for "claude quota no-data / empty / ok:true" this run: no covering issue. #1781 (open) is the claude duplicate-limits overwrite — a different defect in the same transform. #1762 (closed) established the no-data contract for codex and named the sibling set; claude was not in its fix scope.

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/openrouter.ts`, the unlimited path (`limit === null`, ~:126-132): the monthly window's only figure is `usage_monthly`, read via the shared `toNumber` — which accepts any finite number, including negatives — and formatted straight into the label:

```ts
valueLabel = `$${formatMoney(usageMonthly)} spent`
```

Nothing checks the sign. A negative `usage_monthly` — a spend figure that cannot exist — publishes as a successful quota read whose window claims the account has spent a negative amount of money. The provider's own neighbouring code already treats impossible figures as no data: a zero/negative **limit** returns the no-data contract (#1799, window-contract rule 4). The spend figure on the unlimited path is the one figure in this provider with no sign check at all.

Sibling parsers guard the same shape: turso's `numNonNegative`, opencode-go's `toMicroCents` (rejects `< 0`), and command-code's `monthlyRemaining >= 0` gate (#1744) all read a negative amount as absent. OpenRouter's limited path is also safe by construction — its label derives from `used = max(0, limit − limit_remaining)` and its over-limit shape is pinned publish-truthfully by the quota suite (`$120.00 / $100.00` at a clamped 100%). Only the unlimited path's raw spend escapes.

## Runtime probe (laptop worktree, `probe-antigravity.ts`, kept in the worktree)

Driving the real `provider.fetchQuota` with a stubbed fetch (the test suite's own harness shape):

- Control (existing test, #1799 describe): `{ limit: 0, limit_remaining: -5, usage_monthly: 5 }` → no-data error — the negative *remaining* on a zero limit is already dispositioned; only a negative *spend on the unlimited path* slips through.

## Why it matters

On the unlimited path this label is the provider's entire quota signal — there is no percent and no limit to cross-check it against. A negative spend is impossible wire data (a billing reset glitch, a credits/refund adjustment spelled as spend, a gateway mimicking the `/key` shape with a signed balance); publishing it as `ok: true` quota data teaches downstream consumers a figure that cannot be true, in the one shape (credits/spend balance) where this fleet has repeatedly chosen "bad data reads as absent" over fabrication.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A negative `usage_monthly` on the unlimited path gets one explicit disposition — read as absent (so a payload with no other figure returns the existing "No quota data in response" contract) is the sibling-consistent choice; any other disposition is chosen and recorded in the closing note.

- [ ] The limited path is unchanged, including its pinned publish-truthfully over-limit shape.
- [ ] `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins the negative-spend case beside the existing #1799 openrouter describe.
- [ ] Existing quota suite stays green.

body:
# fix(ai): antigravity quota transformModels fallback publishes a phantom all-null "5h" window for models with no quota figure

Verified 2026-11-06 on origin/main `529cf7fa05` (merge of PR #1908), in a laptop worktree (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-06-creator-2135`, kept).

## The defect

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/antigravity.ts`, `transformModels` (the per-model fallback branch, ~:376-398): when a model has no matched summary group, the branch builds a window from the model's own `quotaInfo` — but it publishes that window **unconditionally**, even when `quotaInfo` carries no quota figure at all:

- `remainingFraction` missing → `usedPercent: null` (correctly propagated as unknown, per #1768).
- `resetTime` missing → `resetAt: null`, and the label derivation falls through to the default: label `"5h"`, `windowSeconds: 18000` — a duration and a window kind the payload never sent.
- The result is assigned as `transformed[name] = { windows: { "5h": <all-null window> } }` with no figure check.

That is exactly the phantom-window shape the window contract exists to forbid — rule 4 in `packages/ai/src/quota/types.ts` ("No figure, no window — an empty/all-null/zero-limit window-shaped object publishes no window") — and the shape two sibling providers already disposition explicitly:

- codex (#1762): "a window without a usable used_percent carries no quota figure, so it is dropped… a duration/reset with no percent is dispositioned the same way (dropped, not published with a null percent)".
- meta key-endpoint (#1907, fixed this week): figure-less `subs_usage` objects dropped instead of publishing phantom all-null windows beside real ones.

Antigravity's summary path learned the #1768 lessons (unknown buckets skipped, missing fraction = null), but the per-model fallback path — the path taken by every model when the summary carries no usable group for it — never got the figure check.

## Runtime probe (laptop worktree, `probe-antigravity.ts`, kept in the worktree)

Driving the real exported `transformModels` with an empty summary-group list:

- `{ models: { "gemini-x": {} } }` → `"gemini-x": { windows: { "5h": { usedPercent: null, remainingPercent: null, windowSeconds: 18000, resetAfterSeconds: null, resetAt: null, resetAtFormatted: null } } }` — a phantom 5h window minted from **no data at all**.
- `{ models: { "gemini-x": { quotaInfo: {} } } }` → identical phantom 5h all-null window.
- `{ models: { "gemini-x": { quotaInfo: { resetTime: "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z" } } } }` (reset only, no fraction) → a `"weekly"` window with `usedPercent: null` — the label/duration are fabricated from the reset distance alone (>36h → weekly), the reset-only spelling codex #1762 drops.
- Control `{ quotaInfo: { remainingFraction: 0.5, resetTime: … } }` → real window: `usedPercent: 50, remainingPercent: 50` under `"5h"` (correct, unchanged).

Because `fetchWithCandidates` returns `ok: true` whenever `transformModels` yields at least one model entry, a models payload whose entries all lack `quotaInfo` reads as a successful quota read full of all-null windows.

## Why it matters

These per-model windows are the antigravity provider's whole published usage (`usage: { windows: {}, models }`). A phantom window tells downstream consumers (the aggregator, the dashboard, quota-aware placement) that a 5-hour window exists with unknown usage, instead of the honest answer — this model carries no quota figure. It also fabricates the window's *kind*: the same figure-less model is labelled `5h`, `daily`, or `weekly` purely by how far away an unrelated reset timestamp sits, or by default when there is none.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A model whose fallback `quotaInfo` carries no usable `remainingFraction` publishes no window (the model entry is omitted, or carries empty windows — one disposition, chosen and recorded in the closing note; the codex #1762 / meta #1907 drop-the-window disposition is the precedent).
- [ ] A reset-only `quotaInfo` (reset present, fraction absent) likewise publishes no window — no label is derived from a reset alone.
- [ ] The real-figure control is unchanged: a present `remainingFraction` still publishes its window with the existing label derivation (5h/daily/weekly by reset distance).
- [ ] `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins: model with no `quotaInfo`, model with empty `quotaInfo`, reset-only `quotaInfo`, and the real-fraction control.
- [ ] Existing quota suite stays green; the summary-group path (`transformSummary` / matched-group branch) is unchanged.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for "antigravity transformModels", "antigravity phantom window", and "antigravity quotaInfo" this run: no covering issue. #1768 (closed) covered bucket labelling / keep-first / missing-fraction-as-1 in the summary path; it did not cover the fallback branch publishing a window with no figure. #1909 (open) is only about the stale inventory rows for #1768/#1785.

## Problem

The quota window-contract parser inventory (`packages/ai/src/quota/types.ts`, the contract's own record of which parsers are conforming vs known-lossy) still marks two parsers as KNOWN-LOSSY for issues that are **closed-completed and fixed on main**, and the shared probe matrix header in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` repeats the stale claim. The inventory's own rule (types.ts, and the matrix header at quota.test.ts:1079-1085) is that a parser's issue "flips" its row when it lands — for these two, the flip never happened, so the contract's oracle now misdirects anyone extending or auditing the parsers.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 529cf7fa05)

- **antigravity row** (types.ts:64-67): says the transforms `parseBucket` / `transformSummary` / `transformModels` "are module-private" and marks the parser "KNOWN-LOSSY: #1768". In fact all three are exported (`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/antigravity.ts:272,310,343`), `quota.test.ts` imports them (line 9), issue #1768 is CLOSED (COMPLETED, 2026-11-06T11:34:28Z), and the dedicated describe "antigravity quota bucket labelling (#1768)" (quota.test.ts:1420) pins the fixed behaviours: unrecognized window strings skipped, same-label collisions keep-first, missing remainingFraction propagates as null.
- **mistral row** (types.ts:97-99): "KNOWN-LOSSY: #1785 (usedPercent clamped while usedAmount is derived from the raw percentage...)". In fact `parseBudget` derives `usedAmount` from the clamped percent (`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/mistral.ts:75-78`), issue #1785 is CLOSED (COMPLETED, 2026-11-06T11:29:46Z; fix 8b601e1bc3 via PR #1836), and quota.test.ts:81-91 pins "clamps over-100 usage consistently for percent and amount" plus the negative case.
- **matrix header** (quota.test.ts:~1079-1085): lists antigravity (#1768) and "mistral field consistency (#1785)" among the parsers that "are NOT asserted as conforming" and "live in the types.ts inventory as known-lossy until their own issues land and flip their rows".
- Control rows verified still accurate this run: claude #1781 OPEN, meta #1777 OPEN, opencode-go/openrouter #1725 OPEN — those rows stay lossy.

## Why it matters

The inventory is the contract's index (window contract rule 7): producers and reviewers deciding where quota-parser risk remains read these rows first. Two stale lossy marks hide two now-conforming parsers from the shared-matrix conformance set, overstate the remaining #1794 work, and understate regression risk — a future change that re-breaks mistral field consistency or antigravity bucket labelling would look "already known-lossy" instead of like a regression.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] types.ts inventory: antigravity row corrected (transforms exported, #1768 disposition recorded as landed/conforming) and mistral row flipped to conforming (#1785 landed), with wording matching the current code.
- [ ] quota.test.ts shared-matrix header no longer lists #1768 / #1785 as known-lossy-not-asserted.
- [ ] Triage decides the rule-7 pinning shape and records it in the header: either mistral + antigravity cases join the shared probe matrix, or the header names their dedicated describes (#1768 / mistral-budget describes) as their pins.
- [ ] No production behaviour changes; quota suite green.

body:
## Problem

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/meta.ts` — `keyUsageResult` (the Meta key-endpoint cross-check, module-private) publishes a window for every `subs_usage.window` / `subs_usage.weekly` **object that is present**, even when the object carries no usable figure at all. An empty window object mints a phantom all-null window, violating window-contract rule 4 (types.ts: "No figure, no window — an empty/all-null/zero-limit window-shaped object publishes no window") and diverging from the codex #1762 disposition for the identical shape ("a window without a usable used_percent carries no quota figure, so it is dropped — an empty window object used to mint a phantom all-null window") and from claude's `addWindow` guard (`percent === null && !valueLabel` → no window).

## Evidence (verified this run, main 69016eaca8)

Probe `probe-meta-keyusage.ts` in laptop worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-06-meta-keyusage/wt` (detached origin/main), driving the real `provider.fetchQuota` with a stubbed key-endpoint response and an unreachable CDP base (portal path fails closed, key endpoint answers):

- `subs_usage: { window: {}, weekly: { used_percent: 25, resets_at: 1893456000 } }` → `ok: true` with **two** windows: a phantom `rolling` window (`usedPercent: null, remainingPercent: null, windowSeconds: null, resetAt: null`, no label) beside the real `weekly` window. The CLI renderer prints this as `rolling: unknown` next to real data.
- `subs_usage: { window: {}, weekly: {} }` → `ok: true` with two all-null windows and no figure anywhere — the result's own no-data branch (`Object.keys(windows).length === 0` → `no-data` failure / post-roll empty state) is bypassed because the phantom keys make the map non-empty.
- Control, both windows carrying `used_percent` → both publish normally (unchanged by the fix).

Site: meta.ts `keyUsageResult` — the `rolling` block adds `windows[...]` unconditionally when `asObject(subsUsage?.window)` is non-null; the `weekly` block does the same. `toUsedPercent` already returns `null` for a missing/unusable percent; the result is never checked.

## Why it matters

The key endpoint is the cross-check/fallback for the portal read (session-expired and portal-failure paths): a phantom window there reads as a real (empty) rolling window to the CLI renderer and to downstream quota consumers that group windows by provider, and an all-phantom answer masquerades as a successful quota read instead of the honest no-data/post-roll states the same function already implements.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `subs_usage` window object with no usable `used_percent` publishes no window (per window: a missing-figure rolling window drops while a real weekly window still publishes, and vice versa).
- [ ] When neither window carries a figure, the existing dispositions apply unchanged: `is_subs_active !== true` → the `no-data` failure; active → the post-roll empty state.
- [ ] Windows carrying a figure publish byte-for-byte as today (percent clamping, duration-derived key, reset handling unchanged; the #1777 key-collision behaviour is out of scope).
- [ ] Tests in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` drive `provider.fetchQuota` for the key-endpoint path (empty window + real weekly, both empty, control) and pass; ai typecheck clean.
