body:
# fix(ai): five quota providers accept blank credentials — a whitespace key/token counts as configured and is sent as `Bearer ` + spaces

## Summary

Five of the thirteen quota providers read their credential with a raw
truthiness check instead of the fleet's blank-credential rule
(`asNonEmptyString`). A stored credential whose key/token is whitespace
only (`"   "`) therefore:

1. reports `isConfigured === true` in the `opencode quota` listing,
2. is sent on the wire as `Authorization: Bearer    ` (Bearer + spaces),
3. and the upstream 401 is misreported as an expired/revoked real
   credential ("Session expired — please re-authenticate …"), sending
   the user to re-authenticate a credential that was never there.

An empty-string key is handled correctly ("Not configured"); only
whitespace slips through — exactly the gap the blank-credential rule
closed for the auth bridges in #1763 and antigravity-auth in #1765.
Those fixes scoped to the provider auth bridges; the quota providers
were never swept.

## Evidence (main 22c0a6ddbee1)

Raw reads (no `asNonEmptyString`):

- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/deepseek.ts:34` — `isConfigured: … Boolean(entry?.key)`; `:38` — `const apiKey = entry?.key`
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/groq.ts:84` — `isConfigured: … Boolean(getAuthEntry(…)?.key)`; `:87` — `const apiKey = entry?.key`
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/mistral.ts:204` — `fetchForEntry`: `const apiKey = entry?.key` (covers `fetchQuotaForCredential`, which passes the row through the same function); `:230` — `isConfigured: … Boolean(…?.key)`
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/openrouter.ts:50` — `isConfigured: … Boolean(…?.key)`; `:53` — `const apiKey = entry?.key`
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/codex.ts:38` — `const accessToken = entry?.access ?? entry?.token`; `:202-203` — `entryWithToken` gates `isConfigured` on the same raw values

Conforming siblings (the rule already applied in this same package):

- `meta.ts:345,349` — `asNonEmptyString(entry?.access) ?? asNonEmptyString(entry?.key)`
- `cline-pass.ts` — `keyOf` is `asNonEmptyString(entry?.key)`
- `command-code.ts` — `getApiKey` via `asNonEmptyString`
- `opencode-go.ts` — `readKey` via `asNonEmptyString`
- `antigravity.ts` / `claude.ts` resolve credentials through their auth
  bridges, which #1763/#1765 already hardened.

## Reproduction (laptop probe, worktree of origin/main 22c0a6ddbee1)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-06-creator-0435/probe-blank-key.ts` +
`probe-blank-codex.ts` — each provider driven with a one-row credential
context (`active: true`, value key/access as shown) and a stub
`fetchImpl` that records the Authorization header and returns 401:

| provider | key/access | isConfigured | fetch calls | Authorization sent | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| deepseek | `"   "` | **true** | 1 | `"Bearer    "` | configured=true, "Session expired — please re-authenticate with DeepSeek" |
| deepseek | `""` | false | 0 | — | "Not configured" ✓ |
| deepseek | `"sk-real"` | true | 1 | `"Bearer sk-real"` | configured=true, "Session expired …" |
| groq | `"   "` | **true** | 1 | `"Bearer    "` | configured=true, "Invalid or revoked API key …" |
| groq | `""` | false | 0 | — | "Not configured" ✓ |
| openrouter | `"   "` | **true** | 1 | `"Bearer    "` | configured=true, "Session expired — please re-authenticate with OpenRouter" |
| openrouter | `""` | false | 0 | — | "Not configured" ✓ |
| codex | access `"   "` | **true** | 1 | `"Bearer    "` | configured=true, "Session expired — please re-authenticate with OpenAI" |
| codex | access `""` | false | 0 | — | "Not configured" ✓ |
| mistral | `"   "` | **true** | (console path first) | — | `fetchQuota` proceeds as configured instead of "Not configured" |
| mistral | `""` | false | 0 | — | "Not configured" ✓ |

The whitespace row is indistinguishable downstream from a real revoked
credential — that is the harm: the quota listing claims the provider is
configured, and the error directs the user at re-authentication rather
than at the blank stored value.

## Why it matters

- The quota surface is the fleet's pool-visibility layer; a phantom
  "configured" provider with a misleading expiry error corrupts the
  diagnosis path every other quota issue in this repo exists to keep
  honest.
- The blank-credential rule is established fleet doctrine (#1763,
  #1765); these five providers are the remaining unswept readers in
  `packages/ai/src/quota`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] deepseek, groq, mistral, openrouter: key reads (both
      `isConfigured` and the fetch path, including
      `fetchQuotaForCredential` where present) go through
      `asNonEmptyString` — a whitespace-only key behaves exactly like
      an absent key: `isConfigured === false`, `fetchQuota` returns
      `configured: false` / "Not configured", and no fetch is issued.
- [ ] codex: the same rule for `access`/`token` in
      `fetchQuotaForEntry`, `entryWithToken`, and the instance-folding
      `isConfigured` path.
- [ ] A stored key with surrounding whitespace and real content (e.g.
      `"  sk-real  "`) is treated the way the conforming siblings treat
      it (trimmed via `asNonEmptyString`), not sent verbatim.
- [ ] `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins the whitespace case for the
      affected providers (whitespace → not configured, no fetch;
      control: real key → fetch issued).
- [ ] No behavior change for non-blank credentials; existing quota
      suite green.

title: Provider availability: one state machine for quota / rate-limit / unknown / infra stops
body:
## Provider availability: one state machine for quota / rate-limit / unknown / infra stops (Drew, 2026-11-06)

Drew's spec, verbatim intent:

> make a system to show available providers that aren't errored or showing max quota or empty api balance. make providers stop trying when quota burned until it shows an increase, stop rate limit until retry after, block provider for increasing times if errors unknown. if its erroring because it can't route like our dns or the opencode server is having issues or something it shouldn't be exactly same, should wait until [the path] starts working again etc

And the binding design principle: **plan seats are never removed/re-added around quota walls.** Config is the standing design; availability is a dynamic routing-layer state. `commandcode` sits in `disabled_providers` today only because this system was missing — the router kept trying an erroring provider, throwing errors and adding delay even when calls ultimately succeeded. **Seamlessness is the core acceptance property: a stopped provider costs a session ~nothing.**

This generalizes the #1806 defect family (it does not duplicate it: #1806 tracks the resolver cascade — sticky pin, pool-level tried-set, worst-credential judging; this issue is the availability/classification layer underneath, plus the two #1806 secondaries that live here: the flat cooldown ignoring the provider-stated reset, and the AG-vs-Mistral classification split).

## What already exists (built on, not rebuilt)

- Benches (`model-route.ts` `bench()`): escalating ladder per consecutive failure; a stated retry-after is believed as-is; quota benches bounded by a trustworthy window reset with a single half-open probe at the reset (#1123, #1486).
- Quota gates: per-credential and per-provider gates fed by the quota subsystem (the single quota source); **balance holds are increase-only with no expiry** (#1014, #1380); known-full snapshots gate until their reset; re-admission on a not-full reading is logged (`quota-readmitted`).
- Rate-limit window holds from response headers (`ModelRouteLimits` snapshots; #870).
- Correlated-transport forgiveness (`networkSuspect`): transport failures across unrelated providers clear each other's benches (#1034).
- `route_health` / `route_attempt` ledgers and the `route-stats` tool, which already exposes `activeBenches` (stopped targets with reason + until).

## Gaps this design closes

1. **Classification split (#1806 secondary).** The identical condition — window quota exhausted — classifies as `QuotaExceeded` (quota bench) for Mistral but `RateLimit`/retryable for Antigravity, whose reset is stated only in message text ("Individual quota reached… Resets in 81h35m49s"). The hint layer must recognize a quota statement in text, and bind the stated reset to the bench.
2. **No infra class.** A DNS failure (`ENOTFOUND`), a refused connection (`ECONNREFUSED`), or a dead local service is not a provider being unhealthy: the request never reached an API, it says nothing about quota or balance, and it must not escalate the provider's error standing. Today it rides the same bench ladder as a provider 500.
3. **Quota benches don't hear the quota feed.** Gates re-admit on a measured increase; benches only wait out their timer/reset. Drew's rule — *stop until it shows an increase* — must apply to benches too: a fresh, known, not-full quota reading for the scope releases quota-class benches early.
4. **The availability surface is partial.** `activeBenches` shows benches only. A provider stopped by a balance hold, a quota gate, a rate-limit window hold, or (new) an infra hold is invisible in the readout. Drew asked for one surface: *which providers are available, which are stopped, why, until when, and what resumes them.*

## The availability state machine

Per provider / credential / target (finest scope that carries evidence wins; a leaf is unavailable when any scope that binds it is stopped):

| State | Entered by | Router behavior | Resume rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| **available** | — (default; also every release below) | candidate normally | — |
| **quota-stopped** | `QuotaExceeded` tag, or a quota statement in error text (window exhaustion wording); known-full quota snapshot | not a candidate; attempts trend to zero | **measured increase**: a fresh known quota reading for the scope shows headroom (not-full) — or the window's stated reset passes (one half-open probe at the reset, full release on probe success) |
| **balance-stopped** | balance-exhaustion evidence only (`QuotaExceeded` tag or credit/balance-specific text — #1380's bar) | not a candidate, **no expiry** | measured balance **increase** over the benched baseline (existing increase-only hold) |
| **ratelimit-stopped** | HTTP 429 / `RateLimit` without quota evidence; provider rate-limit window snapshots | not a candidate | the provider-stated **retry-after** timestamp (header, details, or message text), believed as-is, never multiplied |
| **unknown-blocked** | any other failure (5xx, unrecognized errors) | not a candidate | **escalating** timer: base bench × multiplier per consecutive failure, capped; a success resets the count |
| **infra-held** | transport path failures whose OS code proves the request never reached an API: `ENOTFOUND` / `EAI_AGAIN` (DNS), `ECONNREFUSED` (dead local service / proxy) | not a candidate (sessions fail over silently) | **path-health**: short fixed cadence holds (30s → 60s → 120s → 240s, cap 5 min); first success on the target clears the hold. Infra failures **never** increment the unknown-error escalation count, never plant quota/balance evidence, never gate a pool |
| **auth-stopped** | 401/403, org-disabled credential | not a candidate | long bench (existing): it cannot heal by itself; resumes on timer or credential change |

Classification precedence on one failure: balance evidence → balance-stopped (plus quota bench accounting) · quota tag/text → quota-stopped · retry-after present → ratelimit-stopped · infra code → infra-held · auth → auth-stopped · else unknown-blocked. A stated retry-after on a quota failure is believed for the bench length, but the bench stays quota-class and bound by the stated reset.

Stale-read doctrine (standing): a failed or stale quota read never idles a pool and never releases a stop — releases require a *known, fresh* reading.

## Availability surface

**`ModelRoute.availability(now)`** in `packages/core/src/model-route.ts`, merging every stop in force — benches, quota gates, balance holds, rate-limit window holds, infra holds — into one list of `{ providerID, modelID?, credentialID?, class, reason, until?, resume }` where `resume ∈ reset | increase | retry-after | timer | path`. It is exposed through the existing **`route-stats` tool** output (new `availability` field beside `benches`) — the surface the fleet already reads — rather than a new silo. Absence from the list = available. The effective stop for a leaf is the latest `until` among its entries (a balance hold has no `until`: it is stopped until an increase is measured).

## Acceptance (harness scenarios, mock-provider fixtures)

1. Quota burn (AG-shaped text wall and Mistral-shaped tag) classifies identically as quota; the bench binds the stated reset; attempts to the walled member trend to zero while blocked.
2. A fresh not-full quota reading releases a quota bench **before** its reset; a stale/unknown reading releases nothing.
3. A 429 with retry-after resumes at the retry-after, not before, and the wait is never multiplied.
4. Unknown errors escalate: successive benches grow by the ladder multiplier; a success resets the count.
5. **Seamlessness:** a pool with one permanently erroring member serves every step on its sibling; after the first bench, attempts to the bad member stay at zero while it is stopped; the session sees no error.
6. A DNS failure fails over, holds as infra on the short cadence, and leaves the target's unknown-error count and quota standing untouched; the next success after the hold clears it.
7. A balance hold still releases only on a measured increase (regression guard for #1014).

## Proving case

`commandcode` comes out of `disabled_providers` only when the seamlessness acceptance is demonstrable: harness scenarios green **and** a driven live session against a deliberately failing leaf completing on siblings with attempts-to-the-bad-leaf trending to zero. Prepared as a config PR in developing-today/code with the evidence attached; merged only if both legs pass.

Related: #1806 (resolver cascade family), #1014 / #1380 (balance holds), #1123 / #1486 (reset-bound benches + probes), #870 (rate-limit windows), #1034 (transport forgiveness), PR #1807 (mock harness).

## Audit follow-up — fleet edits inside the shared protocol of official providers

Source: 2026-11-06 provider audit (Audit A: official provider files). **Every official provider file is clean** — no fleet-authored changes in `providers/openai.ts`, `mistral.ts`, `deepseek.ts`, `groq.ts`, `openrouter.ts`, `meta.ts`, `openai-compatible.ts`. The one material breach of the "don't edit official providers" doctrine is one layer down, in the shared protocol those providers lower through.

### The finding: `packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts`

Two fleet commits change wire behavior for **every** consumer of the OpenAI Chat protocol — official `openai`, `deepseek`, `groq`, `openrouter`, `meta` (chat), and the fork `openai-compatible` (which effectively serves the `opendesign` / `cline-pass` / `opencode-go.*` doors after the native-rewrite layer):

- `46c691ef5f` (2026-11-05, #1706) — adds `detectModelFamily()` (glm/kimi/gemini by model-ID segment), threads `modelID` into `detectMaxTokensField` / `detectSupportsStore` / `detectSupportsStrictMode` / `detectZaiToolStream`.
- `94ec4190e4` (2026-11-05, #1737) — extends it with a `deepseek` family (`max_tokens`, no `store`).

Stated motivation is the fleet's multi-family gateway doors. But the detection also fires on direct official-provider traffic with matching model ids, and it will conflict on every upstream sync.

### Fix shape

The protocol already honors explicit per-model `compatibility` overrides *after* detection ("Explicit `compatibility` overrides are applied after detection and always win" — the commit's own comment). Move the gateway family defaults to where they belong:

- per-model `compatibility` entries on the gateway doors (`cline-pass`, `opendesign`, `opencode-go` catalog entries in `opencode.jsonc` / models.dev overlay), **or**
- a fleet-owned wrapper around the compatible provider for those doors.

Then revert the detection commits' behavior changes from the shared protocol (keeping any purely additive, behavior-neutral helpers if upstream-shaped).

### Secondary shared-file fleet edits (lower severity — same principle, tracked here)

- `protocols/open-responses.ts` — `f64bbc14a7` (#908/#910): own-property guard on item-ID prefixes.
- `protocols/utils/responses-hosted-tools.ts` — `c523a00fe7` (#927/#928): prototype-name guard.
- `protocols/anthropic-messages.ts` + `route/client.ts` + `route/transport/http.ts` + `schema/options.ts` — `715c29a069` (#1146) native-shape pass-through fast path; `5315572131` (#856) in anthropic-messages. (Serves the fleet `claude-code` provider; official `anthropic` is not fleet-used.)
- `protocols/utils/tool-schema.ts` — `bd60fed2b8` (#1574); `protocols/utils/gemini-json-schema.ts` — `42b9794461` (#1585). Shared schema utils, motivated by antigravity/moonshot.
- Verified clean by contrast: `protocols/mistral-chat.ts`.

These guards are close to behavior-preserving, but they are still fleet edits in upstream files and will surface as sync conflicts; each should either move to a fleet-owned location or be proposed upstream.

## Acceptance criteria
- Fleet model-family detection no longer lives in the shared `packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts` protocol layer, OR a written decision on this issue records why the protocol layer is the accepted home.
- Official providers' wire behavior is unchanged for non-fleet model IDs (existing protocol tests pass; any behavior delta is enumerated on this issue).
- The gateway-door compatibility configuration carries the family detection for the fleet doors that need it (opendesign / cline-pass / opencode-go).

title: fix(ai): agy GOCSPX scan can collect a truncated prefix at chunk boundaries — #1642's 'never truncated' guarantee fails for stable-boundary straddles

labels.name: task/triage

body:
## Finding

The chunked GOCSPX scan added by PR #1642 in packages/ai/src/providers/antigravity-auth.ts can add a truncated prefix of a secret run as a candidate, contradicting its own comment — a run that straddles the "stable region" boundary is matched truncated first, and only later matched whole. No test exercises a run straddling a chunk boundary.

## Evidence

- PR: #1642 "fix(ai): antigravity secret extraction tries all GOCSPX candidates (#1633)", merged 2026-11-04T17:33:15Z, merge commit 94c44617fb77, head 9070d628e652.
- Current main 4d2d9bf989a5, antigravity-auth.ts (blob b3145bb6f1b8, unchanged since the PR): :154 the scan reads the binary in 1 MiB chunks; :163-165 `collect` matches on `stable = text.slice(0, -256)` for non-flush calls; :171-177 the loop sets `carry = text.slice(-256)` and flushes the carry at EOF.
- The comment at :158-162 claims matches are collected from the stable region "so a run split across a chunk boundary is matched whole, never as a truncated prefix". That holds only for a run that starts inside the last 256 chars. A run that starts at least 17 chars before the stable boundary (7 for `GOCSPX-` + the regex's `{10,}` minimum) and ends after it is matched by `matchAll(/GOCSPX-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}/g)` in truncated form and added to `runs` in that form; the whole run is added only on the next chunk's pass, after the truncated one in scan order.
- Candidate derivation (:~185-190) slices each run to its first 35 chars: a truncated run of 17-34 chars yields a bogus short candidate distinct from the real one, so the first refresh in a process spends an extra token-endpoint attempt on a candidate that can only be rejected `invalid_client` before trying the real secret (the winner cache masks this on later refreshes).
- Test gap: the #1633 tests in packages/ai/test/provider/antigravity-auth.test.ts use small single-chunk fixture binaries; no fixture places a GOCSPX run across a 1 MiB chunk boundary (or across the stable/carry boundary), so the claimed guarantee is untested.

## Why it matters

The scan's correctness claim is false for exactly the boundary case it was written to handle. The practical cost today is one wasted `invalid_client` round-trip on a first refresh whenever a run straddles a boundary, plus a candidate list that does not match the documented invariant — and a future change that trusts the invariant (e.g. stopping at the first candidate, or capping candidate count) would turn the truncated entry into a real extraction failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test with a fixture binary whose GOCSPX run straddles a chunk/stable boundary (at several start offsets, including 17-34 chars of the run inside the stable region) asserts the candidate set contains the whole run and no truncated prefix.
- [ ] `collect` no longer emits a match that ends exactly at the stable-region boundary (or an equivalent fix), and the :158-162 comment matches the implemented guarantee.
- [ ] Existing antigravity-auth candidate tests (#1633 layouts, non-invalid_client no-cycle) keep passing.

title: fix(ai): command-code quota windows split their out-of-range disposition — percent clamped, label raw; non-positive resetAt published as a 1969/1970 date

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
## Problem

`parseCommandCodeCredits` (`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/command-code.ts`) applies the out-of-range disposition to only half of each `windowLimits` window, and publishes non-positive `resetAt` values as real dates. The window contract in `packages/ai/src/quota/types.ts` (design #1794) requires the opposite on both counts:

- Rule 5: "A window's fields agree — derived fields are computed from the published (post-disposition) values; the out-of-range disposition (clamp vs publish-truthfully) is the provider's stated choice, applied to the whole window, never split."
- Rule 3: "Missing is null, and nulls the field — never a number… An absent reset is an honest null `resetAt` on the window."

Yet the types.ts inventory lists command-code as "Conforming", and the shared probe matrix (#1795) pins its rule-3 absent-reset case but no out-of-range `windowLimits` case — so the defects below are unpinned.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probe at origin/main `4d2d9bf989`)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-06-commandcode/probe.ts` against the real `parseCommandCodeCredits` in worktree `probe-2026-11-06-creator-0335`:

- Negative used — `{ windowLimits: { fiveHour: { used: -5, cap: 10, resetAt: 1893456000 } } }` → `usedPercent: 0, remainingPercent: 100, valueLabel: "-5 / 10"`. The percent is clamped but the label publishes the raw negative figure: the window disagrees with itself (the #1785 mistral defect, in this provider's `windowLimits` loop at command-code.ts:85-90). The monthly path in the same function guards `monthlyRemaining >= 0` (command-code.ts:63); the `windowLimits` loop has no `used >= 0` guard at all.
- Over-cap used — `{ used: 15, cap: 10 }` → `usedPercent: 100` but `valueLabel: "15 / 10"`. Same split: clamped percent, truthful label. (Turso's stated publish-truthfully choice publishes both raw; a clamp choice must clamp both.)
- Negative reset — `{ weekly: { used: 5, cap: 10, resetAt: -5000 } }` → `resetAt: -5000000`, `resetAtFormatted: "Wed, Dec 31, 4:36 PM"` (1969). The local seconds→ms conversion at command-code.ts:89 (`resetAt < 1_000_000_000_000 ? resetAt * 1000 : resetAt`) never rejects non-positive values.
- Zero reset — `resetAt: 0` → `resetAt: 0`, formatted as the epoch (Dec 31, 1969 local) instead of the honest `null` the absent-reset case correctly publishes.
- Control — `{ used: 5, cap: 10, resetAt: 1893456000 }` → `usedPercent: 50`, `resetAt: 1893456000000`, label `"5 / 10"` (correct).

## Why it matters

Quota windows drive pool gating and the dashboard/`opencode quota` rendering. A window whose percent says 0% while its label says "-5 / 10" (or 100% vs "15 / 10") presents two contradictory truths to every consumer, and a 1969/1970 reset date renders as a real reset time. These are exactly the payload-anomaly shapes the contract and the #1793 groq strictness fix exist to keep out of published quota state; command-code's `windowLimits` loop is the remaining unguarded one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One stated disposition for `windowLimits` windows, applied to the whole window: a negative `used` publishes no contradictory figure (no window, or a window whose percent and label agree), and an over-cap `used` has percent and label in agreement (both clamped or both truthful).
- [ ] A non-positive `resetAt` (0 or negative, seconds or ms spelling) publishes `resetAt: null` (with null derived reset fields), never an epoch/1969 date; a valid positive reset is unchanged.
- [ ] Probe-matrix cases in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pin all three shapes for `parseCommandCodeCredits` (negative used, over-cap used, non-positive resetAt), and the types.ts inventory row for command-code reflects the outcome.
- [ ] Existing quota tests still pass, including the #1744 monthly over-included and rule-3 absent-reset cases.

title: fix(ai): antigravity union ARRAY branch can never carry prefixItems — #1629's else-if is unreachable

body:
## Finding

In `convertSchemaNode` (packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts), the multi-valued type-union branch added by PR #1629 can never carry `prefixItems` into the ARRAY branch — the `else if` that would do it is unreachable — and no test pins a type union with `prefixItems`.

## Evidence

- PR: #1629 "fix(ai): emit one branch per member for multi-valued type unions in antigravity convertSchema (#1556)", merged 2026-11-04T14:45:23Z, merge commit 2afce66b77f8, head 6f3730f22f8b.
- Current main 4d2d9bf989a5, antigravity.ts:187-193 — before the branch construction, the node munging synthesises `items`: `if (prefixItems !== undefined && items === undefined) items = {}`. So whenever `prefixItems` is present, `items` is always defined.
- antigravity.ts:233-235 — consequently `out.items` is set whenever `out.prefixItems` is set.
- antigravity.ts:255-256 — the ARRAY branch then reads: `if (out.items !== undefined) branch.items = out.items; else if (out.prefixItems !== undefined) branch.prefixItems = out.prefixItems`. The `else if` can never execute: its condition implies `out.items !== undefined`. The comment at :249-252 says the ARRAY branch carries "the node's items/prefixItems", but a prefixItems-only node (e.g. `{type:["array","string"], prefixItems:[{type:"string"}]}`) produces an ARRAY branch holding only the synthesised unconstrained `items: {}`, and a node with both `items` and `prefixItems` produces an ARRAY branch holding only `items` — the same drop class as the moonshot fix #1574 (closed), in the branch this PR introduced.
- Test gap: the #1629 test in packages/ai/test/provider/antigravity.test.ts covers an ARRAY branch with `items` only; no case has a unioned ARRAY member with `prefixItems` (alone or with `items`).

## Why it matters

Either the tuple constraint silently fails to reach the ARRAY branch the wire validates (the branch is the unit the #1548 items requirement applies to, per the code's own comment), or the outer node's retained `prefixItems` is the intended carrier and the branch code + comment misdescribe the semantics — in which case the dead path invites a future editor to "fix" the wrong thing. Triage should settle which, then pin it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Triage verdict on issue: confirm whether the ARRAY branch must carry `prefixItems` itself, with the wire/proto evidence recorded.
- [ ] If it must: the branch carries `prefixItems` alongside `items` (and the synthesis at :193 no longer pre-empts it); tests pin unioned ARRAY with prefixItems-only and with items+prefixItems, for Gemini (anyOf) and Anthropic (oneOf) targets.
- [ ] If the outer node is the carrier: remove the unreachable `else if`, correct the :249-252 comment, and add a test pinning that a unioned ARRAY node's `prefixItems` survives conversion at the node level.
- [ ] Existing antigravity convertSchema tests keep passing.

Related (not duplicates): #1556 (the union bug #1629 fixed), #1574 (moonshot translator's prefixItems drop — different translator, non-union path), #1684 (umbrella fidelity-contract design for the translators; this is one concrete dead path inside it).

title: claude-code provider: Anthropic third-party gate fingerprints OpenCode's env instruction ('Is directory a git repo') — main sessions billed to extra usage
body:
## Anthropic third-party gate classifies OpenCode as a third-party app on the claude-code provider (env-instruction fingerprint)

**Provider:** `claude-code` (#6117 native wire emulation) · **Evidence:** fleet laptop, 2026-11-06, deployed binary `2.0.30+1add729`, Claude Code CLI credential (subscription OAuth).

### Symptom
Every real OpenCode session request through the claude-code provider is refused by Anthropic:

```
HTTP 400 invalid_request_error
"Third-party apps now draw from your extra usage, not your plan limits. Add more at claude.ai/settings/usage and keep going."
```

while the SAME credential succeeds for: the real `claude` CLI, minimal prompts in the provider's exact wire shape, and even captured OpenCode requests with one system-prompt line removed (below). Title-generation requests (no env instruction) pass; main session requests fail.

### Isolation (all against `POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`, provider's captured wire shape)
Wire capture of the deployed binary (local forwarding proxy) showed the main session request carries system blocks: [0] claude-code identity, [1] OpenCode harness prompt, [2] model info, [3] Code Mode catalog + skills + date + `<env>` block, [4] worktree note, [5] session note. Bisecting the captured body against the live API:

- Dropping block [3] → 200. Dropping block [1] instead → still 400.
- Within block [3], the sole load-bearing trigger is the environment instruction emitted by `packages/core/src/instructions/builtins.ts:43`:
  `  Is directory a git repo: yes|no`
  in the `<env>` block that follows `Today's date: …` / "Here is some useful information about the environment you are running in:" / `Working directory:` / `Workspace root folder:`.
- Full captured body with ONLY that one line removed → **200, correct reply text**. Same body with the value flipped (`no`→`yes` or `yes`→`no`) → still 400. Every other env line (Working directory, Workspace root folder, Platform, the /tmp guidance line) individually passes; the git-repo line alone or in pairs passes — it fires only in the complete env block, i.e. Anthropic's classifier fingerprints the env block by that anchor line.
- A Claude-Code-shaped prompt (large system prompt + real tool definitions) in the identical wire shape → 200. The gate is content classification, not headers/UA/betas (swapping `User-Agent` between `opencode/…` and `claude-cli/2.1.306` changes nothing).

### Reading
Anthropic's third-party detection for subscription OAuth keys on the harness's own env instruction: any client whose system prompt contains OpenCode's `<env>` block is classified "third-party app" and billed to extra usage (which this account does not have funded) instead of plan limits. The native claude-code emulation reproduces the CLI's wire faithfully — the request is rejected because of what OUR harness puts in the prompt, not because of the provider's protocol shape.

### Options
1. **Per-provider instruction shaping:** when the target provider is claude-code, omit (or rephrase) the `Is directory a git repo` line — or the whole `<env>` block — from builtin instructions. Verified sufficient at the API level (removal → 200 with the rest of the harness prompt, Code Mode catalog, and tools intact). Cost: the model loses one env fact on this provider only.
2. **Fund extra usage** at claude.ai/settings/usage (account-side; Drew's call, changes billing for ALL third-party-classified traffic).
3. Accept the provider as title-gen/small-prompt-only — not viable; main sessions are the point.

Option 1 looks like a one-line change in `builtins.ts` gated on provider, or an instruction-layer filter in the session runner for the claude-code provider id. Filing for the design call; the API-level fix is proven.

title: fix(ai): codex quota isConfigured counts inactive credentials — provider lists as configured while fetchQuota reports Not configured

body:
## Problem

The Codex quota provider's `isConfigured` disagrees with its own `fetchQuota` when the only Codex/OpenAI credential is **inactive**. `isConfigured` returns `true`, so `listConfiguredQuotaProviders` lists Codex as a configured provider — but `fetchQuota` then returns `configured: false` / "Not configured". Every other quota provider judges configuration through `projectAuth(ctx)`, which projects only active credential rows (`packages/ai/src/quota/utils.ts:217-218`); Codex alone has two extra branches that read raw credential rows and ignore the `active` flag.

## Evidence (verified this run on origin/main `f318c1ae1c`, laptop probe importing the real module)

Sites in `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/codex.ts`:

- `:217` — the instance loop finds the instance's credential row with no `active` check, while `fetchQuota`'s own instance loop at `:232` requires `r.active`.
- `:220-222` — a fallback `ctx.credentials.some(...)` over raw rows with no `active` check, and no counterpart in `fetchQuota` at all (`fetchQuota` only consults `projectAuth` plus active instance rows).

Probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-06-codex-isconfigured/probe.ts` on the laptop, module imported from main; fetch stubbed to throw so no network is touched):

```
A inactive direct row:   isConfigured = true
A fetchQuota = {"ok":false,"configured":false,"error":"Not configured"}
B inactive instance row: isConfigured = true
B fetchQuota = {"ok":false,"configured":false,"error":"Not configured"}
C active direct row:     isConfigured = true,  fetchQuota configured = true (proceeds to fetch)
D no credentials:        isConfigured = false, fetchQuota configured = false
```

## Why it matters

`listConfiguredQuotaProviders` (`packages/ai/src/quota/index.ts:92`) is built from `isConfigured`, and its contract is "providers with a usable credential". A deactivated OpenAI credential (the store's way of parking an account) leaves Codex listed as configured while every fetch reports "Not configured" — a self-contradictory provider state in `opencode quota` output, and a divergence from the active-only convention all twelve sibling providers follow. The single-row paths in `index.ts` force `active: true` before calling `isConfigured`, so they are unaffected; the divergence is specific to Codex's two raw-row branches.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With only an inactive direct-alias credential present, `isConfigured` returns `false` (matching `fetchQuota`'s `configured: false`).
- [ ] With only an inactive instance credential present, `isConfigured` returns `false`.
- [ ] Active direct and active instance credentials still read as configured (no regression to the folding behavior).
- [ ] Regression tests in the quota test suite pinning the inactive-direct and inactive-instance cases.
- [ ] `bun test` for `packages/ai` quota tests green.

Deduped against open and recently closed issues this run — no existing issue covers Codex `isConfigured` or inactive-credential handling in the quota providers.

title: fix(ai): vibe-auth resolution is silent about which tier won — an env MISTRAL_API_KEY shadows the keyring sign-in key and reroutes billing with no diagnostic

body:
## Summary

`vibe-auth`'s credential resolution is silent about which tier won. When an environment `MISTRAL_API_KEY` (or a `~/.vibe/.env` entry) is present, it shadows the OS-keyring sign-in key that `vibe --setup` provisioned — and because billing follows the KEY, not the `call_source` stamp (verified empirically 2026-11-06, see the `vibe.ts` header comment), vibe-direct then silently spends a different budget than the sign-in intended. Nothing in the resolution path records or surfaces the winning tier: the resolver returns a bare string and the module has no logging. This exact shadowing burned the account API pool on 2026-11-05 and walled the mistral-plan route (root cause on #1653); the only mitigation so far is a config fix in another repo (developing-today/code#6460) that removes the env var from one deployment. Any other host or env that legitimately sets `MISTRAL_API_KEY` — the plain `mistral` provider reads the same variable (`providers/mistral.ts:31`) — re-creates the silent reroute.

## Evidence (verified this run, origin/main 8cf16377a7)

Sites in `packages/ai/src/providers/vibe-auth.ts`:

- `resolveApiKey` (vibe-auth.ts:144-147) returns the env value on first hit: `const fromEnv = env[API_KEY_ENV_VAR]?.trim(); if (fromEnv) return fromEnv`. The keyring tiers (services `ai.mistral.vibe` / legacy `vibe`) are only consulted when env and `~/.vibe/.env` both miss.
- The return type is `Promise<string>` — a bare credential with no origin/tier metadata, so no caller can know (or log) which tier supplied it. The result is then cached process-wide (`cached`, vibe-auth.ts:167-184), so the silent choice persists for the process lifetime.
- The module contains no logging at all (no logger import, no `console.*`): the winning tier is observable nowhere — not in logs, not in the error surface, not in any return value.

Probe (run on the laptop against origin/main 8cf16377a7, `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-06-vibe-shadow/probe2.ts`, injected `CredentialSources`):

- env `{ MISTRAL_API_KEY: "marker-from-env-tier" }` + keyring returning `"marker-from-keyring-tier"` → winner: `marker-from-env-tier` (env shadows the sign-in key, silently).
- Control, env `{}` + same keyring → winner: `marker-from-keyring-tier`.

The tier ORDER is intentional and pinned — `packages/ai/test/provider/vibe-auth.test.ts` ("environment wins over the .env file and the keyring") mirrors the binary's `resolve_api_key_with_origin`. This issue is not about changing precedence; it is that a billing-critical precedence outcome has zero observability. The existing suite asserts WHICH key wins and never asserts anything about a diagnostic, because none exists.

Distinct from #1763 (closed): that fixed whitespace-only credentials in the commandcode/claude-code bridges. Distinct from #1653 (closed): that built the provider and recorded the incident's root cause; its fix surface was the provider itself plus the code#6460 config change, not a runtime diagnostic in the resolver.

## Why it matters

The failure mode is silent money misrouting: vibe-direct keeps working — requests succeed, the stamp looks right — while every call bills the wrong budget, discovered only when a pool walls or a bill arrives. The 2026-11-05 incident is the proof of cost. A one-line diagnostic at resolution time (winning tier named, credential value never logged) converts the next occurrence from a post-mortem into a log line an operator (or the quota/pool monitors) can act on immediately. This is the same "no diagnostic" class the fleet already treats as file-worthy (#238: a pool that selects no models "disappears with no diagnostic").

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When resolution succeeds via a non-keyring tier (env or `~/.vibe/.env`) while a keyring sign-in entry also exists, an observable diagnostic is emitted naming the winning tier (and that a keyring entry was shadowed) — the credential value is never logged, in whole or part.
- [ ] The diagnostic route follows the repo's existing logging/observability conventions for the ai package; the disposition (where the signal lands and its exact shape) is recorded in the closing note.
- [ ] `packages/ai/test/provider/vibe-auth.test.ts` pins: env-shadows-keyring emits the diagnostic; keyring-wins emits no shadow diagnostic; env-wins-with-no-keyring-entry does not claim a shadow. Tier precedence itself is unchanged (existing tests pass unmodified).
- [ ] Existing vibe-auth and ai package suites stay green; gate state not regressed (the three quota-era gates already red on main belong to #1724 — do not conflate).

body:
## Summary

The Mistral quota budget parser reads each budget's `currency` from the console payload — and then throws it away. The published window's `valueLabel` always uses a dollar sign, so a budget denominated in any other currency is reported as dollars.

## Evidence (verified this run, origin/main c81b9d816c)

Sites in `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/mistral.ts`:

- The wire payload carries a per-budget currency — the module's own header comment (mistral.ts:35-36) documents the shape: `api_budget: { usage_percentage, initial_budget, currency, reset_at }` (same for `vibe_budget`).
- `MistralBudgetWindow` declares the field (mistral.ts:65: `currency: string`), and `parseBudget` populates it (mistral.ts:79: `currency: asNonEmptyString(budget.currency) ?? "USD"`).
- Nothing ever reads it back. `budgetWindow` (mistral.ts:96-102) — the only place a Mistral budget becomes a published `QuotaWindow` — builds the label with a hardcoded dollar sign and never references `budget.currency`:

  ```ts
  valueLabel: `$${formatMoney(budget.usedAmount)} / $${formatMoney(budget.budgetAmount)}`
  ```

  A repo-wide search finds no other consumer of the parsed currency: `parseMistralBudget` is exported, but its `currency` field has no reader outside `parseBudget` itself, and `QuotaWindow` carries no currency field — the `valueLabel` is the only place the currency could surface, and it is fixed to `$`.

Traced example (deterministic from the code above): a payload with `api_budget: { usage_percentage: 25, initial_budget: 200, currency: "EUR" }` parses to `{ usedPercent: 25, usedAmount: 50, budgetAmount: 200, currency: "EUR" }` and publishes the window label `"$50.00 / $200.00"` — euro amounts labelled as dollars. The USD control traces correctly only because the hardcoded sign happens to match.

The existing test does not catch this: `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` ("mistral console budget mapping") uses only `currency: "USD"` payloads (the 2026-11-05 capture) and never asserts the parsed `currency` field or any rendered label.

## Why it matters

Mistral is a European provider and the console budget payload denominates each budget explicitly — a EUR-denominated workspace budget is the ordinary case for it, not an exotic one. The Mistral console read is the only quota surface for the Mistral/Vibe account (per the provider's header comment, no API-key usage endpoint exists), and the dollar label is the figure pool-rotation decisions read. A label that silently re-denominates the amount misstates spend by the exchange-rate factor while looking exact.

This is also a window-contract rule 5 problem (types.ts, #1794): a window's fields must agree — here the window's own parsed currency and its published label disagree. Sibling precedent in the same package: Claude's spend label respects the payload currency (`claude.ts:142-145,219`: `formatSpendLabel` prefixes `$` only for USD/absent and `${currency} ` otherwise), and DeepSeek's balance label switches symbol on CNY.

Distinct from #1785 (open): that issue is the clamp split inside the same parser (`usedPercent` clamped, `usedAmount` derived raw). This issue is the currency field parsed-then-discarded; either fix can land without the other, though both touch `budgetWindow`/`parseBudget`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A budget whose payload currency is not USD publishes a `valueLabel` denominated in that currency (e.g. the `EUR ` prefix form Claude uses, or a correct symbol), for both the api and vibe windows; USD and absent-currency budgets keep the current `$` label byte-for-byte.
- [ ] `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins: a non-USD budget's rendered label, the USD control, and the absent-currency default; the parsed `currency` field is asserted at least once.
- [ ] The disposition is recorded in the closing note (label format chosen for non-USD currencies), and the types.ts parser inventory's mistral row is updated if the fix changes its known-lossy list.
- [ ] Existing quota suite stays green; gate state not regressed (the three quota-era gates already red on main belong to #1724 — do not conflate).

# fix(ai): commandcode stream emits id-less and nameless tool-results — the #1756 fail-loudly guard covers tool-calls only

## Summary

`packages/ai/src/protocols/commandcode.ts` fails a stream loudly when a `tool-call` event arrives without its `toolName` or `toolCallId` (#1756: a nameless call used to vanish silently; an id-less call was emitted with a colliding empty id). The sibling `tool-result` event — the gateway's own server-executed results — has no such guard: its handler substitutes empty strings and emits the result anyway, so a malformed server tool-result enters the conversation with `id: ""` or `name: ""`, where it can never be matched to the tool-call it answers.

## Evidence (verified this run on origin/main c81b9d816c)

- Event schema (`commandcode.ts`, stream `Event` struct): `toolCallId: optionalNull(Schema.String)` and `toolName: optionalNull(Schema.String)` — both are optional on every stream event, so a `tool-result` with either missing decodes cleanly.
- The #1756 guard in `step` (comment at the `event.type === "tool-call"` check) rejects only `tool-call` events missing `toolName`/`toolCallId`, with a `ProviderShared.eventError` failure.
- The `tool-result` case in the same `step` switch does `LLMEvent.toolResult({ id: event.toolCallId ?? "", name: event.toolName ?? "", ... providerExecuted: true })` — no validation before the empty-string substitution (the file's only unguarded `?? ""` identity site).
- Laptop probe (worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-creator-2335`, `packages/ai/test/provider/probe-toolresult.test.ts`, run with `bun test` on the laptop, 3 pass): driving the real provider through `LLMClient.generate` with a stubbed NDJSON stream —
  - `{ type: "tool-result", toolName: "web_search", output: "sunny" }` (no `toolCallId`) + finish → **Success**, emitting `{"type":"tool-result","id":"","name":"web_search","providerExecuted":true}`.
  - `{ type: "tool-result", toolCallId: "srv_1", output: "sunny" }` (no `toolName`) + finish → **Success**, emitting `{"type":"tool-result","id":"srv_1","name":"",...}`.
  - Control with both fields present → Success with the real id/name preserved.
- Dedup: `gh` search for commandcode tool-result / empty id returns #1756 (tool-calls only, closed), #1760, and the #1708 audit umbrella — no open or closed issue covers stream `tool-result` identity. Cross-link: #1756, #1708.

## Why it matters

A provider-executed tool-result is matched to its call by id downstream; an empty id matches nothing (or, with two malformed results, everything collides on `""` — the exact failure #1756 named for tool-calls). The stream currently presents that malformed gateway output as a clean, successful turn instead of the protocol error it is, leaving a corrupt, unmatchable result in the session history. #1756 established the contract for this adapter — malformed tool identity fails the stream loudly because there is no safe fallback identity to invent; the sibling event type was left out of that fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- A stream `tool-result` event missing `toolCallId` or `toolName` fails the stream with the same class of loud protocol error #1756 uses for `tool-call` (naming the missing field), instead of emitting a tool-result with an empty id or name.
- A well-formed `tool-result` (both fields present) is emitted unchanged, provider-executed, as today.
- Regression tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/commandcode.test.ts` pin both missing-field cases next to the #1756 tool-call tests, and the existing commandcode suite stays green.
- No change to the request lowering, the tool-call guard, or the finish/abort mapping.

body:
# fix(ai): CDP quota reads can hang forever — the DevTools WebSocket client has no request timeout and no close handling

## Summary

`packages/ai/src/quota/cdp.ts`'s WebSocket client settles a request only when a reply with the matching id arrives. There is no per-request timeout and no `onclose`/`onerror` settlement after connect, so a wedged renderer (page hung, target crashed, socket silently dropped) leaves every pending `Runtime.evaluate` promise unsettled forever — and `cdpPageFetch` never returns, never throws, and never runs its cleanup.

## Evidence (verified this run on origin/main 7702b0d23e)

- `packages/ai/src/quota/cdp.ts` `connectWs`: `send` registers `pending.set(next, res)` and resolves only from `ws.onmessage`; `ws.onerror` is wired only to reject the *connect* promise; there is no `ws.onclose` handler and no timeout on `send`.
- `waitForPage`'s nominal 20s deadline is defeated by the same hang: its first `evaluate()` call awaits `send`, and a promise that never settles is not a rejection, so the `.catch(() => "")` + deadline loop never advances.
- `cdpPageFetch`'s `finally` (close the WS client; `GET /json/close/<createdId>` for a page this call created) only runs when the awaited `evaluate` settles — so a hung read also leaks the browser tab it created.
- The only consumer today, meta (`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/meta.ts:362`), awaits `cdpPageFetch` directly; the CLI's 30s race in `fetchProviderWithTimeout` abandons the promise but cannot settle it, close the socket, or close the created page — every timed-out meta read leaks both.
- Reproduction (laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-cdp-hang/probe.ts`): a fake CDP endpoint whose `/json/list` returns a page on the requested origin and whose WebSocket accepts `Runtime.evaluate` but never replies. `cdpPageFetch` was still pending after 35,000 ms — past `waitForPage`'s 20s deadline — while every HTTP step in the same file carries a 10s `AbortSignal.timeout`.

## Why it matters

Meta quota is read through this path on every `opencode quota` run that includes meta. A single wedged portal tab turns the read into a permanent hang for any consumer that does not race it, and into a slow tab/socket leak for the one that does. The file's own discipline elsewhere (10s HTTP timeouts, 20s page-wait deadline, 5s close timeout) shows bounded waits are the intended contract; the WS request path is the one unbounded hole.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `Runtime.evaluate` request that gets no reply settles (rejects) within a bounded time, and `cdpPageFetch` surfaces it as an error (the `cdp-unavailable:` class or a sibling), so `waitForPage`'s deadline logic works as written.
- A socket that closes or errors mid-request settles all pending requests instead of leaving them pending.
- The `finally` cleanup (client close + created-page close) demonstrably runs on the hang path.
- A regression test drives `cdpPageFetch` (or the WS client) against a never-replying fake endpoint and asserts settlement within the bound; existing quota tests stay green.

title: fix(ai): deepseek quota balance selection discards a positive balance — a non-USD/CNY balance is ignored, and a zero/negative USD entry wins over a positive one

body:
## Problem

DeepSeek quota's balance selection defeats its own positive-balance filter. `fetchQuota` first collects the `balance_infos` entries whose `total_balance` is > 0, and prefers a positive USD then CNY entry — but if neither preferred currency has a positive entry, it falls back to the **first USD/CNY entry of any sign** in the full list, and it never considers a positive balance in any other currency at all. Consequences, all verified below:

1. A sole positive balance in a non-USD/CNY currency is reported as **"No quota data in response"** (`ok: false`) — a funded account reads as broken.
2. A zero or negative USD entry **wins over** a positive balance in another currency, publishing `$0.00` (or even `$-5.00`) as the account's `credits_balance` while real money sits unused in the payload.

This contradicts the window contract's spirit (#1794: parse the window you were sent) and the provider's own two-step intent in code: the positive filter exists precisely so a spent/empty entry does not shadow a funded one.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `5fd613e46d`)

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/deepseek.ts`:

- :71-75 `positiveBalances` = entries with `toNumber(total_balance) > 0`.
- :77-82 selection chain: `positiveBalances.find(USD) ?? positiveBalances.find(CNY) ?? balanceInfos.find(USD) ?? balanceInfos.find(CNY) ?? null` — steps 3-4 search the **unfiltered** list, and no step ever returns a positive entry in another currency.
- :99-101 the label symbol is binary (`currency === "CNY" ? "¥" : "$"`), so a third-currency balance would also be mis-symbolled if it were ever selected.

Laptop probe (worktree of `origin/main` `5fd613e46d`, driving `provider.fetchQuota` with a stubbed fetch, probe kept at `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-creator-2135/probe2.ts` on the laptop):

- `[{currency:"EUR", total_balance:"100.00"}]` → `ok: false`, error `"No quota data in response"` — the €100 balance is invisible.
- `[{currency:"EUR", total_balance:"100.00"}, {currency:"USD", total_balance:"0.00"}]` → `ok: true`, `credits_balance` label `"$0.00"` — the zero USD entry shadows €100.
- `[{currency:"GBP", total_balance:"80"}, {currency:"USD", total_balance:"-5"}]` → `ok: true`, label `"$-5.00"` — a negative USD entry shadows £80.
- Control that works by construction: `[{currency:"USD", total_balance:"-5"}, {currency:"CNY", total_balance:"50"}]` → label `"¥50.00"` (the positive CNY entry is found at step 2).

Dedup: issue search for "deepseek currency balance" and "deepseek balance_infos" returned no issues; the #1795 inventory describes DeepSeek as fetch-only with "no figure to parse" and lists no known-lossy item for this selection logic.

## Why it matters

DeepSeek is a PAYG reserve pool (its balance is the thing being measured). Publishing `$0.00` / `$-5.00`, or a no-data error, for an account that holds a positive balance makes the quota row lie in the dangerous direction: tooling and humans reading the row conclude the reserve is empty or broken while funds exist in the payload that was actually sent.

## Acceptance criteria

- Selection prefers, in order: a positive USD entry, a positive CNY entry, **any other positive entry**, and only then falls back to a non-positive USD/CNY entry (or no-data) — a positive balance is never shadowed by a zero/negative one.
- A sole positive balance in a third currency publishes a `credits_balance` window whose label does not mis-symbol it as `$`/`¥` (use the currency code or its correct symbol; the choice is recorded in the closing note).
- The existing USD/CNY behaviours stay: USD preferred over CNY when both are positive; a genuinely empty/absent `balance_infos` still returns "No quota data in response".
- `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins the selection: third-currency-only positive, positive-third-currency vs zero-USD, and positive-third-currency vs negative-USD cases, driven through `provider.fetchQuota` with a stubbed fetch (the fetch-only style the #1795 inventory describes for DeepSeek).
- The #1795 parser inventory in `types.ts` is updated if the fix changes DeepSeek's row.

Related: #1794 (window contract), #1795 (parser inventory).

title: fix(ai): openrouter quota publishes a zero-limit window — $0.00 / $0.00 with null percent reads as headroom where there is no limit

body:
## Problem

OpenRouter quota publishes a window for a key whose `limit` is **0**: `usedPercent: null` with the value label `$0.00 / $0.00`, and the result is `ok: true`. A zero limit is no quota figure at all — the window reads as a live (empty) quota where the key in fact has no limit/headroom surface. This is exactly the symptom the window contract and a sibling provider already dispositioned:

- Window contract (#1794, `packages/ai/src/quota/types.ts` rule 4): "No figure, no window — an empty/all-null/**zero-limit** window-shaped object publishes no window; only quota figures are windows."
- OpenDesign precedent (#1750, comment in `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/opendesign.ts` `parseCodingPlanWindows`): a zero limit "used to publish a label-only window (usedPercent null, '0 / 0 credits') that reads as quota headroom where there is no plan" — and now publishes nothing.

OpenRouter was not given the same disposition. The #1795 inventory lists OpenRouter's only known-lossy item as #1725 (unpinned `resolveResetAt`); the zero-limit case is not covered there.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `5fd613e46d`)

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/openrouter.ts`:

- :105-106 `limit` / `limitRemaining` parsed via `toNumber`.
- :130-133 in the limited branch: `used = Math.max(0, limit - limitRemaining)`, `percent = limit > 0 ? (used / limit) * 100 : null` — for `limit === 0` the percent becomes `null` but the branch still builds a window.
- :149-152 the window is published unconditionally under the reset-derived key.

Laptop probe (worktree of `origin/main` `5fd613e46d`, driving `provider.fetchQuota` with a stubbed fetch, probe kept at `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-creator-2135/probe2.ts` on the laptop):

- `{limit: 0, limit_remaining: 0, usage_monthly: 0, limit_reset: "monthly"}` → `ok: true`, window `monthly: { usedPercent: null, remainingPercent: null, valueLabel: "$0.00 / $0.00", windowSeconds: 2592000, resetAt: <next month> }`
- `{limit: 0, limit_remaining: -5, usage_monthly: 5, limit_reset: "monthly"}` → `ok: true`, window `monthly: { usedPercent: null, valueLabel: "$5.00 / $0.00" }` — spent money against a zero limit, still no percent and no error.
- Controls behave: `{limit: 100, limit_remaining: -20}` → `usedPercent: 100`, label `$120.00 / $100.00`; `{limit: 100, limit_remaining: 150}` → `usedPercent: 0`, label `$0.00 / $100.00`.

## Why it matters

The `opencode quota` listing and downstream consumers (aggregator/dashboard) treat an `ok: true` window as a real quota surface. A zero-limit key (revoked, unpaid, or a free key with no purchased limit) currently shows a plausible monthly window with a reset date instead of the no-data/error row its siblings produce, masking exactly the state a user checks quota to discover.

## Acceptance criteria

- A payload with `limit: 0` publishes **no** limit window: if it is the only data, the result follows the sibling no-data contract (`ok: false`, "No quota data in response"), matching the OpenDesign zero-limit disposition (#1750) and contract rule 4.
- The unlimited path (`limit: null` with `usage_monthly` present) still publishes its monthly spent window unchanged.
- Normal and over-limit cases stay as probed above (100 / 150-remaining controls).
- `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins the zero-limit case (and the zero-limit-with-spend case) for OpenRouter, in the shared probe-matrix style from #1795.
- The #1795 parser inventory in `types.ts` is updated if the fix changes OpenRouter's known-lossy list.

Related: #1794 (window contract), #1725 (OpenRouter `resolveResetAt` pinning — separate), #1750 (OpenDesign zero-limit precedent).

body:
## Problem

`opencode quota` (human-readable mode) prints each window's `usedPercent` with raw JavaScript number interpolation — no rounding anywhere in the render path. Most quota providers compute the percent as an unrounded division, so ordinary usage prints with full float noise:

```
OpenCode Go (opencode-go)
  weekly: 33.33333333333333% used, resets Mon, Dec 31, 6:00 PM
```

## Evidence (verified this run on origin/main aa2fe24fe398, laptop probe importing the real modules)

Probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-quota-render/probe2.ts`, kept on the laptop) fed the real `parseConsoleGoUsage` (packages/ai/src/quota/providers/opencode-go.ts:81, `clampPercent((used / limit) * 100)`) a console meter of used 100 / limit 300 micro-cents and passed the result to the real `renderQuotaResults`:

```
parser windows: {"weekly":{"usedPercent":33.33333333333333, ...}}
rendered: "  weekly: 33.33333333333333% used, resets Mon, Dec 31, 6:00 PM"
```

The render sites interpolate the number verbatim:

- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/quota.ts` — window line: `${window.usedPercent}% used`
- same file, per-model parts: `${label} ${window.usedPercent}%`

Unrounded producers (grep on main): command-code.ts:67,87; groq.ts:108,120; meta.ts:91; opencode-go.ts:81; opendesign.ts:99; openrouter.ts:131 — all `(used / limit) * 100` with clamping only. Turso is the exception: it rounds via its `pct3` helper (turso.ts:47), so providers already disagree about percent precision. The existing CLI render tests (packages/cli/test/quota.test.ts:59-60) only use pre-rounded fixtures (4.66, 0.04), so the noise never shows in tests.

## Why it matters

This is the human-facing surface of the quota subcommand — the number a user reads to decide whether a pool is spent. Sixteen-digit floats are noise, they differ per provider for no reason, and the JSON shape (which should keep full precision for machines) is not the place to fix it: the render layer owns presentation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Human-readable quota output rounds percents to at most 2 decimal places, trailing zeros trimmed (33.33333333333333 → 33.33; 4.66 stays 4.66; 100 stays 100), in both the window lines and the per-model parts of `renderQuotaResults`.
- [ ] `--json` output is unchanged (full-precision numbers for machine consumers).
- [ ] Regression tests in packages/cli/test/quota.test.ts with an unrounded percent (e.g. 100/300) for a window line and a model part.
- [ ] packages/cli quota tests pass.

## Phase 1 of the quota-window design — the contract, the parser inventory, and the shared probe matrix

Design #1794 (filed this run by repo-design-architect; doc: `files/designs/opencode-quota-window-contract.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace) states one contract for the thirteen provider quota parsers in `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/`: identity is semantic and a derived label never erases a window; duplicates keep the first; missing is null and nulls the field, not the window; no figure, no window; a window's fields agree; unknown kinds are skipped, not renamed; every pure parser is pinned against the contract. This phase builds the contract's enforcement artifacts. **No production behaviour changes.**

### Scope

- **The contract, stated in the module:** the seven rules written where the parsers live — the header of `packages/ai/src/quota/types.ts` or a sibling doc-comment home, following the module's existing conventions (the #1746 READ RULE and #1741's `toNumber` comment are the local style).
- **A parser inventory** covering all 13 providers in the `quotaProviders` registry (`src/quota/index.ts`): for each, its pure parser(s) by exported name (e.g. `parseCodingPlanWindows`, `parseCommandCodeCredits`, `parseSubscriptionQuota`, `toClaudeUsage`, `parseGroqResetSeconds`) or an explicit "fetch-only — no pure parser" entry with the reason. Known-lossy rows are marked and linked: antigravity → #1768 (transforms module-private, zero coverage), meta collision sites → #1777, claude duplicates → #1781, mistral field consistency → #1785, opencode-go + openrouter → #1725.

body:
# fix(ai): groq quota header parsing accepts values it should reject — a negative remaining publishes "-5 / 100 requests remaining" at 100% used, and a partially-parsed reset duration publishes a wrong resetAt

## Summary

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/groq.ts` is the only quota provider with its
own local numeric parsers (`headerNumber`, `parseGroqResetSeconds`), and both
accept malformed wire values that every sibling parser rejects — publishing
wrong quota windows instead of treating the data as absent (the provider's
own honest-absence path, `no-quota-surface`).

Verified 2026-11-05 on main `aa2fe24fe3981756d37452191175e0416d3853ae`
(laptop worktree of origin/main) with a probe driving the real exported
`provider.fetchQuota` / `parseGroqResetSeconds`
(`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-groq-quota/probe.ts` on the laptop).

## Evidence

1. **Negative remaining counts are published as a spent window.**
   `headerNumber` (groq.ts:54-59) returns any finite `Number(raw)` — no
   lower bound. The window guards (groq.ts:105, :117) check only
   `limit > 0` and `remaining !== null`. Probe, headers
   `x-ratelimit-limit-requests: 100`, `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests: -5`:
   result `ok: true` with window
   `requests_daily: { usedPercent: 100, valueLabel: "-5 / 100 requests remaining" }`
   — the clamp at groq.ts:108 hides the impossibility in the percent while
   the label publishes the negative count verbatim. A negative remaining is
   not a count; the tokens window (groq.ts:115-125) has the identical flaw.

2. **Non-decimal spellings parse as counts.** `headerNumber` uses bare
   `Number()`: probe `x-ratelimit-limit-requests: 0x64` read as limit 100,
   and `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests: 1e1` read as remaining 10 (window
   published at 90% used). This is the exact class closed #711 fixed for
   core rate-limit headers (plain decimal only) and that
   `script/check-numeric-boundaries` exists to keep out. Note: the gate
   *disposition* for these two `Number()` sites (groq.ts:46, :57) is
   already tracked in open #1724 — this issue is the runtime behaviour,
   not the gate bookkeeping.

3. **`parseGroqResetSeconds` partially consumes malformed durations and
   publishes the truncated value as `resetAt`.** The regex
   (groq.ts:45) is unanchored and the loop sums whatever segments match;
   unconsumed input is never checked. Probe results from the real parser:
   - `"1h30"` → `3600` (the unitless `30` is dropped; the published
     `resetAt` is 30 minutes early — end-to-end probe: header
     `x-ratelimit-reset-requests: 1h30` produced `resetAfterSeconds: 3600`)
   - `"2m59.56"` → `120` (the unitless `59.56` tail is dropped)
   - `"59s trailing"` → `59` (trailing garbage accepted)
   - `"-30s"` → `30` (the sign is silently discarded)
   - `"1m1m"` → `120` (duplicate units summed)
   
   The parser's own contract for unparseable input is `null` (`"soon"` →
   `null`, `""` → `null`, groq.ts:40-42), which correctly yields
   `resetAt: null`; a partially-valid string is worse than an invalid one
   because it looks authoritative.

Checked and NOT claimed: blank header values are already absent —
`headerNumber`'s `if (!raw)` falsy check returns `null` for `""`, and
`Headers` normalises a whitespace-only value to `""`. The #1741
blank-is-zero failure does not reproduce here.

Existing tests pin none of this: `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts`
(groq describe, ~:192-200) covers only the happy-path durations
(`2m59.56s`, `7.66s`, `14h12m`), `null`, and `"soon"`.

## Why it matters

Groq's windows feed the same quota consumers as every other provider
(aggregator, dashboard, quota-aware placement). A garbage header from a
proxy or a future Groq spelling change currently degrades into a
confidently wrong answer — a pool shown 100% used with a negative
remaining count, or a reset time up to tens of minutes early — instead of
the provider's designed honest absence (`no-quota-surface`). Sibling
providers all route through the shared `toNumber` / clamp primitives in
`quota/utils.ts`; groq is the outlier.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `headerNumber` (or its replacement via the shared `quota/utils.ts`
      primitives) accepts only plain non-negative decimal counts: a
      negative, hex (`0x…`), or exponent (`1e…`) limit/remaining header
      reads as absent, so no window is minted from it (the result falls
      back to `no-quota-surface` when no valid window remains).
- [ ] `parseGroqResetSeconds` returns `null` unless the entire trimmed
      input is a well-formed duration (each segment number+unit, no
      sign, no duplicate-unit requirement beyond full consumption);
      valid spellings `2m59.56s`, `7.66s`, `14h12m` keep their current
      values.
- [ ] New tests in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pin: negative
      remaining → no window; hex limit / exponent remaining → no window;
      `1h30`, `2m59.56`, `59s trailing`, `-30s` → `null` reset (and a
      fetchQuota case showing `resetAt: null` for a malformed reset
      header with otherwise-valid limit/remaining).
- [ ] Existing groq/quota tests stay green; the #1724 gate disposition
      for groq.ts:46/:57 is resolved by whichever route the fix takes
      (conversion through shared primitives or an allowlist entry that
      now tells the truth).

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode; deduped against open/closed search
for "groq quota", "x-ratelimit", "parseGroqResetSeconds" and
"headerNumber" (2026-11-05): #1724 covers only the numeric-gate
disposition for these lines, #711/#672 are the core ModelRouteLimits
header path, #1741 is the shared `toNumber` — none covers this provider's
local parsers' runtime behaviour.

## Finding

PR #1617 stubbed `onnxruntime-node` and `sharp` out of the Node bundle (`packages/cli/vite.node.config.ts` `nativeStubPlugin`): module load succeeds, but any actual use throws "native bindings (onnxruntime-node/sharp) are unavailable in the Node bundle". That trade-off was safe when the PR landed because, in its own words, "the native-onnx embeddings backend is opt-in per registration … it becomes a backend only by the deliberate #1554 step-3 flip, which has not happened — every registered model uses the HTTP backend".

The step-3 flip has since happened (PR #1690), and nothing revisited the Node-bundle stub. On current main the default — and only — embedding registration is native-onnx, with no fallback to its HTTP registration data, so embeddings through the default model always throw the stub error under the Node bundle (the `dist-node` build), while the Bun build works.

## Evidence (verified on current main `aa2fe24fe3981756d37452191175e0416d3853ae`, 2026-11-05)

- `packages/core/src/embeddings.ts:131-141`: `EMBEDDING_MODELS[0]` carries `backend: { kind: "native-onnx", … }` (comment: "Step 3 flip (#1554, 2026-11-05)"), and `DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL = EMBEDDING_MODELS[0]`. Its HTTP registration data (`baseURL`/`baseURLEnv`) is retained only "for step 4"; the embed path at `embeddings.ts:307` branches on `backend.kind === "native-onnx"` and calls `embedNative` — there is no fallback to the HTTP path when the native call fails.
- `packages/core/src/embeddings-native.ts:124-133`: `embedNative` does `await import("onnxruntime-node")` and calls `ort.InferenceSession.create(...)` / `new ort.Tensor(...)` — exactly the entry points the Node-bundle stub makes throw.
- `packages/cli/vite.node.config.ts:81-141` (current main): `nativeStubPlugin` still resolves `onnxruntime-node` and `sharp` to throwing stubs and rewrites the transformers loaders to the same stub; `nativeStubGraphPlugin` still guards that arrangement. Its header comment still argues safety from the pre-flip premise.
- `packages/core/src/embeddings-native.ts:62-69` (the Node-bundle note #1617 added) still states in the present tense that "this backend is unavailable under Node and any use throws a clear error there" — written when no registration used the backend by default.
- Dedupe (2026-11-05): #1727/#1739/#1786 fixed the same flip's loader requirements for the packaged Bun/nix binary; #1554 (open) scopes the native bake-in to the Bun server runtime and its step 4 is sidecar retirement only; #1788/#1789 cover the sharp-stub build guard. No open or closed issue covers the Node bundle's embeddings path after the flip.

Source PRs: #1617 (merge `3f5b8200aa4b80a44ad6f79ff0c44614f3e17606`, the stub and its safety premise) and #1690 (the step-3 flip that invalidated the premise). Filed by pr-diff-review lane B reviewing PRs #1598–#1618.

## Why it matters

The Node bundle is a shipped build (its startup crash was worth fixing in #1615 precisely because every command died there). Since the flip, that build's embeddings door is dead for the default model — not degraded, but a guaranteed throw on first use — and the code comments in both files still assure the next reader the arrangement is safe. When #1554 step 4 retires the sidecar/HTTP path, there will be no embeddings path under Node at all unless this is decided deliberately.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide and record the Node bundle's embeddings contract: either the native backend works there (externalise `onnxruntime-node`/`sharp` instead of stubbing, with the platform binding resolved at runtime), or the embed path falls back to the registration's HTTP backend under Node, or native-onnx under Node is explicitly unsupported and the failure is a clear, documented unsupported-backend error at the embeddings surface (not a bundling stub throw).
- [ ] The Node bundle (`bun script/build-node.ts --bundle-only`, then the built `dist-node` artifact) is exercised for embeddings with the model snapshot present: an embeddings round-trip through the default model succeeds, or fails with the recorded contract's error.
- [ ] The stale safety comments are corrected: `vite.node.config.ts`'s `nativeStubPlugin` header and the Node-bundle note in `packages/core/src/embeddings-native.ts` no longer claim the backend is unused by default.
- [ ] A regression pin exists for the chosen contract (build-graph guard, stub/fallback unit test, or bundle smoke test), so a future registration flip cannot silently break a bundle again.

## Evidence

`bun script/check-bounded-http.ts` now reports **8** unlisted candidates. Seven are the set already tracked by #1724 (quota `cdp.ts` ×5, `turso.ts`, `utils.ts` — line numbers shifted). The eighth is new since the last creator sweep verified the 7-site set (2026-11-05T22:35Z run, main `6c0063ea9f`):

- `packages/cli/script/build.ts:161` — `const source = await Bun.file(args.path).text()`

`git log -S 'Bun.file(args.path)'` attributes the line to `6a78bec602` — PR #1786, the #1727 packaged-binary native-onnx fix merged 2026-11-05T22:50Z. It is the `sharpStubPlugin` `onLoad` hook: it reads the installed `@huggingface/transformers` dist bundle from disk so the build can rewrite the sharp and onnxruntime-node loaders (the rewrites PR #1789/#1788 then asserted individually).

The other three gates are unchanged from #1724's set: numeric-boundaries 4 unlisted, proto-reads 4 unlisted; `check:workflows`, `check:gates`, and `check:doc-env-vars` are green.

## Assessment

The read itself is disposition-class, not a bounded-by-default hole (#1127): it is a local filesystem read of an installed package file by a build plugin — not a network response body — the same class as the existing allowlist entries for `packages/http-recorder/script/build.ts` and `packages/simulation/script/build.ts` (`local file read via Bun.file (filesystem), not a network response body (#1394)`). What is missing is the written disposition the gate exists to force: while the gate stays red for an unrecorded reason, it cannot distinguish this known-harmless site from genuinely new drift.

Related: #1724 tracks the other seven bounded-http sites plus the numeric/proto sets and the turso/`readQuotaJson` substance; if that fix lands first and dispositions this site on its way to green, this issue closes with it. This issue exists so the post-#1724 drift is recorded now rather than silently absorbed into #1724's stale site list (the #1688 → #1724 pattern).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/cli/script/build.ts:161` no longer appears in `bun script/check-bounded-http.ts` output — dispositioned in `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` as a local `Bun.file` filesystem read (naming the #1727 sharp-stub plugin purpose), with no change to the plugin's behavior.

## Summary

The Mistral quota budget parser (`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/mistral.ts`, `parseBudget`, mistral.ts:70-82) clamps `usedPercent` into [0, 100] but derives `usedAmount` from the *unclamped* percentage, so the two fields of the same window disagree whenever the console reports a percentage outside [0, 100]. The published `valueLabel` is built from the amount (`budgetWindow`, mistral.ts:96-104: `$<usedAmount> / $<budgetAmount>`), so the quota row can show e.g. 100% used alongside "$150.00 / $100.00", or 0% used alongside "$-10.00 / $50.00".

## Evidence (verified this run, main 6c0063ea9f)

Probe on the laptop (worktree of origin/main) importing the exported `parseMistralBudget`:

- `usage_percentage: 150, initial_budget: 100` → `{ usedPercent: 100, usedAmount: 150, budgetAmount: 100 }` — percent clamped, amount not.
- `usage_percentage: -20, initial_budget: 50` → `{ usedPercent: 0, usedAmount: -10, budgetAmount: 50 }` — a negative dollar figure reaches `formatMoney` and the valueLabel.
- Control, `usage_percentage: 25, initial_budget: 100` → `{ usedPercent: 25, usedAmount: 25 }` — consistent, as expected.

Code: mistral.ts:76-77 — `usedPercent: Math.min(100, Math.max(0, usedPercent))` sits directly above `usedAmount: (usedPercent / 100) * budgetAmount`, where `usedPercent` is still the raw parsed value.

## Why it matters

The Mistral console read is the only quota surface for the Mistral/Vibe account (the provider's own header comment: no API-key usage endpoint exists). The dollar label is what a reader uses to judge spend against budget; a label that contradicts the window's own percentage — or shows negative dollars — erodes trust in the one number the pool-rotation decisions read. Note the deliberate contrast with Turso, where over-100% is a *published* real state (turso.ts, code#6227): Mistral's parser already made the opposite disposition (clamp the percent) — the amount simply doesn't follow it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `usedAmount` is derived consistently with the clamped `usedPercent` (or both fields publish the raw figure with the percent clamp removed — one disposition, applied to both, and recorded in the closing note; the current split disposition is the defect).
- [ ] `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` mistral describe pins: an over-100 percentage case and a negative percentage case, asserting percent and amount agree under the chosen disposition.
- [ ] Existing mistral cases (normal percentages, flat-payload fallback, empty payload) stay green.
