body:
## Summary

The v2 custom-tool adapter added for #1703 (`packages/core/src/config/plugin/tool.ts`) hands every v1 `.opencode/tool/*.ts` tool a fabricated abort signal that can never fire. `legacyContext()` (tool.ts:214-224) returns `abort: new AbortController().signal` — the controller is created inside the call, never stored anywhere, and nothing in the file (or anywhere else) ever calls `.abort()` on it. The signal a v1 tool receives is therefore `aborted === false` forever, by construction.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 6c0063ea9f)

- tool.ts:221 is the only `AbortController` in the file (grep-verified); the controller reference is discarded when `legacyContext` returns, so no code path can ever abort the signal.
- The execution wrapper that could have supplied a real signal ignores it: tool.ts:110-111 wraps the call in `Effect.tryPromise({ try: async () => definition.execute(input, legacyContext(location, context)), ... })` — Effect's `tryPromise` passes an `AbortSignal` (fired on fiber interruption) to its `try` callback, and this callback discards it.
- The v2 `Tool.Context` the adapter receives (packages/schema/src/tool.ts:14-20) carries no abort/signal field at all, while the promise-side `ToolContext` (packages/plugin/src/promise/tool.ts:11-14) does carry a real `signal: AbortSignal` — native promise tools get cancellation, adapted v1 tools do not.
- The #1703 commit message states the v1 context fields "(sessionID, messageID, agent, directory, worktree, abort) are adapted at the boundary" — abort is listed as adapted, but what is adapted is a stub.
- The pinning test's context probe (packages/core/test/config/tool.test.ts, `contextProbe`) asserts only sessionID, agent, and directory; `context.abort` is unpinned, so the stub passes the suite.

## Why it matters

Custom tools are a production surface again (#1703 restored them precisely because the production session-identity tool was silently dropped). A v1 tool written against the documented context shape will pass `context.abort` into `fetch`, a subprocess, or an abort listener: when the user interrupts the session or the tool call is cancelled, that work keeps running to completion — side effects included — while the runtime believes it was cancelled. A tool that *waits* on the abort signal (long-poll / watch patterns) can never observe cancellation at all. This is a silent fidelity break of exactly the kind #1703 set out to eliminate: the tool loads, appears in the catalog, executes — and one field of its context contract is fiction.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A v1 custom tool's `context.abort` fires when the tool execution is interrupted/cancelled (wire the `Effect.tryPromise` interruption signal, or an equivalent real source, into `legacyContext`) — or, if a real signal genuinely cannot be provided at this layer, the stub is removed/replaced with a loud load-time warning and the limitation is documented, so no tool author can mistake it for a working signal. The disposition is recorded in the closing note.
- [ ] `packages/core/test/config/tool.test.ts` pins the abort behavior: the context probe asserts `context.abort` is an `AbortSignal`, and an interruption case shows a tool observing the signal (or the documented-warning case is pinned instead).
- [ ] Existing custom-tool tests stay green (discovery, registration, catalog, execution, reload).

## Evidence (verified this run, main 4b9febff80)

Probe on the laptop (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-antigravity-quota/`, byte-identical copy of the source with only an export line appended — diff-verified identical) driving `transformSummary` / `parseBucket`:

1. **An unrecognized bucket overwrites the genuine 5h window with wrong data.** Group buckets `[{window:"FIVE_HOUR", remainingFraction:0.5}, {window:"MONTHLY", remainingFraction:0.9}]` produce a single `"5h"` window with `usedPercent: 10`, `windowSeconds: 18000`, and the *monthly* bucket's reset time (Dec 1). `parseBucket` (antigravity.ts:283-296) defaults `label = "5h"` / `FIVE_HOUR_WINDOW_SECONDS` when the window string matches neither week nor day keywords, and `transformSummary` (antigravity.ts:326) does `windows[parsed.label] = parsed.window` — last wins, no trace of the dropped bucket.
2. **Same-label collisions drop windows.** Buckets `[{window:"WEEKLY", remainingFraction:0.25}, {window:"7D", remainingFraction:0.75}]` both derive label `"weekly"`; the published window is the second one (25% used) and the first is silently gone. `bucket5h` / `bucketWeekly` are overwritten the same way (antigravity.ts:327-328). This is the defect class fixed for opendesign in #1750 ("duplicate durations keep the first entry instead of silently overwriting") and filed for codex in #1762 — antigravity has neither the fix nor the pins.
3. **A missing `remainingFraction` is treated as fully remaining for ordering.** `parseBucket` returns `remainingFraction: remainingFraction ?? 1` (antigravity.ts:295) while `usedPercent` is honestly `null`. That invented `1` feeds `transformModels`' weekly-constrained comparison (antigravity.ts:355-358), so window *ordering* is decided by data the wire never sent.

## Why it matters

Quota output drives pool-rotation decisions in this fork. A monthly (or any future/unrecognized) bucket silently relabelled as the 5h window publishes a confident, wrong used-percent with a mismatched reset time — worse than an honest absence (the groq provider's `no-quota-surface` precedent). Because the transforms are unexported, no test can pin any of this today.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Buckets whose window string is not recognized are not published under a fabricated `"5h"` label (skip them, or surface them under a distinct, honest label) — disposition chosen and recorded in the fix.
- [ ] Same-label bucket collisions follow the #1750 convention (keep the first entry) for `windows`, `bucket5h`, and `bucketWeekly`, instead of silent last-wins overwrite.
- [ ] A bucket with no `remainingFraction` does not participate in weekly-constrained ordering as if fully remaining (null/unknown propagates, or the comparison requires both fractions present).
- [ ] `parseBucket` / `transformSummary` / `transformModels` are exported and pinned in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts`: happy path per label, unrecognized window string, duplicate labels, missing `remainingFraction`, matching the probe cases above.
- [ ] Existing quota suite stays green; gate state not regressed (the three quota-era gates already red on main belong to #1724 — do not conflate).

# fix(ai): antigravity-auth does not apply the blank-credential rule — whitespace keyring tokens are accepted and sent

## Summary

The repo's auth bridges share one rule, stated verbatim in the #1763 fix
(commit `0dd051a394`, PR #1764): **"A blank value is no credential (the
vibe-auth rule): trim, and treat whitespace-only as absent."** `vibe-auth.ts`
trims at every tier (:146 env, :154 file, :160 keyring), and #1763 extended
the rule to `commandcode-auth.ts` and `claude-code-auth.ts` with tests.

`packages/ai/src/providers/antigravity-auth.ts` — the fourth first-party
auth bridge — was not touched and applies the rule nowhere. Verified by
reading on main `2981dfd838`:

## Evidence

1. **Whitespace-only refresh token passes the shape check and is POSTed.**
   `antigravity-auth.ts:115` — `if (!creds.token?.refresh_token) return
   reject(...)` rejects only missing/empty values. A refresh token of
   `"   "` passes, and `refresh()` sends it to
   `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token` as `refresh_token` (:252), where
   it fails as an opaque `invalid_grant` instead of being read as "no
   credential stored".

2. **Whitespace-only access token is cached and sent as a Bearer.**
   `loadToken` (:308): `if (creds.accessToken && creds.expiryMs -
   Date.now() > 60_000)` — a whitespace-only `access_token` from the
   keyring is truthy, so with a future expiry it is cached and returned;
   `keyringAuth` then emits `authorization: \`Bearer ${token.accessToken}\``
   (:335) — literally a Bearer token of spaces, the exact failure #1763's
   title names for the sibling bridges.

3. **Whitespace-only access token from the token endpoint is accepted.**
   `refresh()` (:274): `if (!parsed.access_token)` rejects only
   missing/empty; a whitespace-only `access_token` in a 200 response is
   cached and later sent as a Bearer per (2).

4. **No test pins any of this.** `packages/ai/test/provider/antigravity-auth.test.ts`
   covers only refresh bounding (#1469) and client-secret candidates
   (#1633); grep for `trim|whitespace|blank` in that file: 0 hits. The
   sibling bridges each gained explicit whitespace tests in #1763
   (`claude-code-auth.test.ts`, `commandcode-auth.test.ts`).

## Why it matters

The keyring entry is written by an external binary (agy) and read back
verbatim; a corrupted or placeholder entry currently degrades into a
confusing upstream auth failure (or a spaces-only Bearer) instead of the
bridge's own clear "credential unavailable / unexpected shape" errors.
Consistency also matters for the doctrine in #1717: all *-direct bridges
should treat blank credentials identically, so fall-through and fail-closed
behavior is predictable across providers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Keyring parsing treats whitespace-only `refresh_token` as an
      unexpected-shape/absent credential (same rejection path as a
      missing one), and trims stored tokens before use.
- [ ] A whitespace-only keyring `access_token` is never cached or sent;
      `loadToken` falls through to refresh.
- [ ] `refresh()` rejects a whitespace-only `access_token` in the token
      endpoint response (treated like "returned no access_token") and
      trims accepted tokens.
- [ ] New tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/antigravity-auth.test.ts`
      pin all three cases, mirroring the #1763 sibling tests; existing
      #1469/#1633 tests stay green.
- [ ] `bun run check:bounded-http` / gate state not regressed by the
      change (note: the three quota-era gates are already red on main
      under #1724 — do not conflate).

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode; sibling of closed #1763 (same rule,
bridge not covered there — deduped against open/closed search for
"blank credential whitespace" and "antigravity auth", 2026-11-05).

# docs(cli): the `opencode quota` subcommand is documented nowhere — no cli.mdx section, and neither of its env knobs is in the env table

Verified 2026-11-05 on origin/main `255fa099f2d2028df0ba6374596c136ab4dbd15c` (merge of PR #1728), in a laptop worktree, by direct reads (each grep run against the English docs tree):

## Evidence

- The command exists and is user-facing: `packages/cli/src/commands/commands.ts:360-375` — `Spec.make("quota", { description: "Show provider quota usage", … })` with a variadic `provider` argument ("Provider id, name, or alias (repeat for multiple)"), a `--json` flag, and an `--all` flag ("Include providers turned off in config (disabled_providers)").
- The handler is substantial and behavior-rich: `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/quota.ts:29-47` header — assembles quota from the running server's credential list with a read-only local credential-store fallback, skips disabled providers unless `--all`, always fetches named providers, and exits non-zero when a requested provider produced no successful result. None of this behavior is discoverable from the docs.
- `packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx` documents every other subcommand in its own `###` section (agent, attach, auth, github, mcp, models, run, serve, session, stats, export, import, web, acp, plugin, pr, db, debug, uninstall, upgrade — lines 55-660). There is no `quota` section, and `grep -n "quota" packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx` returns zero hits.
- Both env knobs are likewise undocumented: `OPENCODE_QUOTA_TIMEOUT_MS` (`packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/quota.ts:50`, default 30_000, accepted range 1..2_147_483_647) and `OPENCODE_QUOTA_CDP_URL` (`packages/ai/src/quota/cdp.ts:62`, default `http://127.0.0.1:19222`) appear in no English docs page (`grep -rn "OPENCODE_QUOTA" packages/web/src/content/docs services/www/src/docs/content` outside locale dirs: zero hits), including cli.mdx's Environment variables table (line 676+).
- The existing guard cannot catch this direction: `script/check-doc-env-vars.ts` fails only when a *documented* variable has no reader (docs→code). A whole subcommand plus its knobs landing with no docs at all (PRs #1722/#1728, ~4,700 lines of quota code) passes every gate — `check:doc-env-vars` is green on this main.

## Why it matters

Quota is this fork's headline surface — routes demote, gate, and fail over on quota readings (#587 design: one quota signal, three consumers), and the handler header calls `opencode quota` "the single source for quota info (code#6125)". A user who does not already know the command exists cannot find it: it is absent from the canonical CLI reference they copy from, and its two tuning knobs (timeout, CDP bridge URL) are discoverable only by reading source. This is the reverse of the #103-#116 dead-docs class the doc-env gate was built for, and it is currently ungated.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] cli.mdx gains a `### quota` section in the Commands list covering: the variadic provider argument (id/name/alias), `--json`, `--all` and the disabled-provider rule, where credentials come from (running server, local-store fallback), and the non-zero exit when a requested provider yields no successful result.
- [ ] cli.mdx's Environment variables table documents `OPENCODE_QUOTA_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 30000, valid range) and `OPENCODE_QUOTA_CDP_URL` (default `http://127.0.0.1:19222`, what the CDP bridge is for).
- [ ] The section's examples match the real output shape of the handler (verify against `opencode quota` / `opencode quota --json` on a configured machine, not invented output).
- [ ] Optional but welcome: note the reverse-direction gap (implemented-but-undocumented commands/knobs) on the doc-env gate — either extend `check:doc-env-vars` or record why the reverse check is not worth gating.

# fix(ci): three gates red on main — PR #1722's quota subcommand landed 16 undispositioned sites, and turso bypasses the PR's own bounded reader

Verified 2026-11-05 on origin/main `13ab3dc5c2d51fa35ff0273e18f5ef647eca83db` (merge of PR #1722, `3f98804cdd feat(ai): provider quota functions with opencode quota subcommand`), in a laptop worktree, each gate run twice with identical results. `check:workflows`, `check:gates`, and `check:doc-env-vars` are green; these three are red, and every flagged site is in a file PR #1722 added:

## check:bounded-http — 7 unlisted

- `packages/ai/src/quota/cdp.ts:44` + `:46` — `httpJson`: fetch carries `AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)` but the body is read with unbounded `response.json()`. Endpoint is the local CDP bridge (`cdpBaseOf`, default `http://127.0.0.1:19222`, cdp.ts:38-41) — disposition-class, but it must be written down.
- `packages/ai/src/quota/cdp.ts:160` + `:164` — a fetch expression evaluated *inside the browser page* via CDP (`credentials: "include"`, `await r.text()` unbounded, no signal). The gate's primitives cannot bound an in-page expression the usual way; disposition must say so explicitly.
- `packages/ai/src/quota/cdp.ts:190` — `/json/close/` fetch with a 5s timeout, body never read; disposition-class.
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/turso.ts:191` — **the substantive one.** `get()` fetches `https://api.turso.tech` with a 15s timeout and returns unbounded `response.json()` — it bypasses `readQuotaJson` (`packages/ai/src/quota/utils.ts:157`), the bounded reader the same PR introduced for exactly this purpose. Every other provider path that uses `readQuotaJson` gets the 1 MiB cap; turso's two calls (`/usage`, `/subscription`) get none.
- `packages/ai/src/quota/utils.ts:158` — `readQuotaJson` itself: `await response.text()` reads the *entire* body into memory and only then checks `text.length > QUOTA_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES`. The comment above it (utils.ts:150-155) claims "a hostile or misconfigured endpoint cannot grow memory inside the deadline" — as written it can, up to whatever arrives before the deadline; the cap is post-hoc, and `text.length` counts UTF-16 code units, not bytes. Disposition must either record this as accepted (bounded by the caller's deadline) or switch the helper to a streaming bounded read (`readBoundedResponseText`-style).

## check:numeric-boundaries — 5 unlisted

- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/groq.ts:46` `Number(match[1])` and `:57` `Number(raw)` — parses of upstream rate-limit header values.
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/meta.ts:74` `Number(value)`.
- `packages/ai/src/quota/utils.ts:23` `Number(value)`.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/quota.ts:44` `Number(process.env.OPENCODE_QUOTA_TIMEOUT_MS)` — an env var parse with no disposition; a non-numeric value yields `NaN` downstream unless the shared primitives/another guard reject it (verify and say which).

Each needs conversion through `packages/core/src/util/number.ts` (#993) or a written disposition, per the gate's own instruction.

## check:proto-reads — 4 unlisted

- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/antigravity.ts:193` — `archNames[process.arch]` (local constant keyed by runtime arch).
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/claude.ts:122` — `SOURCE_MAP[credential.source]` (key from a stored credential record).
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/openrouter.ts:135` — `PERIOD_SECONDS[data.limit_reset]` (key from upstream response JSON — the one genuinely untrusted key of the four; guard with `ownValue`/`ownOr` or disposition with that noted).
- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/quota.ts:166` — `providerConfig[id]` read/spread in the CLI config merge.

## Why it matters

This is the recurring pattern of #1540, #1514, #1655, #1660, and #1688: a large feature lands, the allowlist gates go red on main, and they stay red until a later sweep notices — during which window the gates cannot catch *new* drift. PR #1722 is ~4,700 new lines of quota code touching 13 provider endpoints; it deserves a clean gate state at landing, and the turso/`readQuotaJson` inconsistency is a real (if small) hole in the PR's own bounded-by-default contract (#1127).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bun run check:bounded-http`, `bun run check:numeric-boundaries`, and `bun run check:proto-reads` all exit 0 on main.
- [ ] turso's `get()` reads through `readQuotaJson` (or an equivalent bounded reader), or the issue records why its direct `response.json()` is accepted.
- [ ] The `readQuotaJson` disposition (or fix) addresses the read-then-check order and the chars-vs-bytes count explicitly — not a bare allowlist line.
- [ ] No allowlist entry is added for a site that is actually unbounded against a remote endpoint without a written justification in the allowlist entry itself.
- [ ] Gate test suites (`script/check-*.test.ts`) still pass.

Related: developing-today/code#6132 (Mistral probe), developing-today/code#6125 (direct-provider completeness).

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

CodeRabbit (coderabbitai[bot]) raised this finding as a follow-up in its review of merged PR #1605 and it was never fixed or responded to:

- PR: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/1605 — "fix(core): judge demotion by the judging Location's settings (#1484)" (MERGED 2026-11-04T08:00:35Z)
- Review: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/1605#pullrequestreview-5764816212 (coderabbitai[bot], 2026-11-04T07:32:44Z, COMMENTED; follow-up finding anchored at `packages/core/src/model-route.ts:1133-1135`)
- Essence: "**Keep quota events for a Location whose wider settings window registers later.** `recordQuota` prunes events with only the readers registered at that moment. A Location that registers later with a wider `demotion.windowMs` cannot recover events already pruned. Its demotion may lag until new quota errors accumulate. A fix needs a retention design change, not a localized edit." (Reviewer severity: Minor · Functional Correctness · Poor tradeoff.)

## No-response evidence

- The PR's only commit (9748389984, 2026-11-04T07:25:18Z) is the head CodeRabbit reviewed; the PR merged at 2026-11-04T08:00:35Z on that same head — no fix commit followed the review.
- The PR conversation contains only the Codex review summary (completed, `has_any_findings:false`, on a different aspect) and CodeRabbit's own summary comment. No comment replies to, acknowledges, or defers this follow-up finding, and there is no linked tracking issue for it.
- Dedupe (searched 2026-11-05, open + closed, by `recordQuota`, PR number 1605, and demotion-retention keywords): issue #1484 (closed, the PR's own issue) covers judging a Location by its own settings and unioning both config layers for *registered* readers; issue #1423 (closed) covers the per-Location settings readers. Neither covers live-recorded events pruned before a wider-window Location registers.

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-05 by two independent `gh api` raw reads)

`packages/core/src/model-route.ts`:

- `recordQuota` (lines 1183–1192): `retentionMs = retainedDemotionWindow()` and the stored events are filtered to `now - at <= retentionMs` at record time, then capped with `.slice(-50)`.
- `retainedDemotionWindow` (lines 1124–1139) unions only the readers registered at that moment (`demotionReaders` + `settingsReaders`); a Location whose graph activates later is not — and cannot be — in that union.
- Contrast with the restore path in the same file: `seedDemotion` (lines 2396–2405) deliberately replays ledger rows with `ModelRouteLog.MAX_DEMOTION_WINDOW_MS` (7,776,000,000 ms ≈ 90 days, `model-route-log.ts:501`) precisely because "a Location with a longer demotion window can activate after the restore, and pruning the replay against the then-current retention … would discard failures its policy still counts, unrecoverably". The live recording path has no equivalent protection, so in a long-running process the same loss happens for live events: they survive in the durable ledger but are gone from the in-memory `quotaEvents` cache until a restart re-seeds them, and `demoted()` for the later Location under-counts in the meantime.

## Acceptance criteria

- Live quota-event retention preserves events that a later-registering Location could still count under the widest supported demotion window (e.g. record with the `MAX_DEMOTION_WINDOW_MS` horizon, as `seedDemotion` already does), or another documented retention policy with the same guarantee; `demoted()` keeps applying each judging Location's own window over what is retained.
- A regression test covers the scenario: quota events recorded while only a narrow-window Location is registered still count toward demotion for a wider-window Location that registers afterwards, without a restart.
- Or: the finding is resolved on this issue by a documented decision with reasoning recorded (e.g. an argued case that later registration cannot occur in-process, or that restart reseeding bounds the impact acceptably).

## Finding

`convertSchema` in `packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts` still forces `type: "OBJECT"` onto a **format-only root** — the one remaining type-specific keyword in the proto vocabulary that the #1950 guard (landed by PR #1951) does not exempt. A root schema carrying only `format` (e.g. `{ format: "date-time" }` or `{ format: "int64" }`) describes a string/number parameter; the forced OBJECT both narrows it to objects only and strands the `format` on a type it can never apply to — exactly the #1901/#1950 defect, one keyword past that fix's guard list.

## Evidence

- PR #1951 (merged, merge commit `4fd5c5520bf10f81b57253ea53ce6b5fa8cd1e9e`): https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/1951 — fixed #1950 by extending the root OBJECT-default guard to `minItems`/`maxItems`, `minLength`/`maxLength`/`pattern`, `minimum`/`maximum`. `format` was not added.
- Current main `7191ad2a7446e3a2c1dceb8ab20a7a61c5428711` (verified via `gh api` x2), `packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts`:
  - `SCHEMA_FIELDS` (:120-125) includes `"format"` (:121), so a `format` key survives conversion (it passes through the node's fallthrough copy; it is not in the skip set and not value/map-keyed).
  - The OBJECT-default guard in `convertSchema` (:326-342) checks `type`/`anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf`/`not`/`enum`/`items`/`prefixItems`/`minItems`/`maxItems`/`minLength`/`maxLength`/`pattern`/`minimum`/`maximum` — `converted.format` is never checked, so at :342 a format-only converted root gets `type = "OBJECT"`.
  - The other proto-vocabulary keywords are all accounted for: object keywords (`properties`/`minProperties`/`maxProperties`) correctly keep the OBJECT default; `exclusiveMinimum`/`exclusiveMaximum` are folded into `minimum`/`maximum` by `convertSchemaNode` (:186-187), so they are covered indirectly. `format` is the only type-specific survivor not covered.
  - In the proto Schema vocabulary `format` applies only to primitive datatypes (string: `date-time`, `enum`; integer: `int32`, `int64`; number: `float`, `double`) — it is meaningless on an OBJECT.
- Probe (verbatim guard condition extracted from current main and evaluated, `probe-guard.mjs` in the lane evidence dir `pr-review-b-2026-11-09-1118/`): `{format:"date-time"}` → OBJECT forced: **true**; `{format:"int64"}` → **true**; control `{minLength:2}` (#1950-covered) → false; controls `{}` and `{minProperties:1}` → true (intended OBJECT default, unchanged).
- Test gap: PR #1951's new test (`convertSchema leaves constraint-only roots self-describing (#1950)` in `packages/ai/test/provider/antigravity.test.ts`) pins the seven constraint keywords and the `minProperties`/`{}` controls — no `format`-only case.
- Dedupe: issue searches for `convertSchema format OBJECT` and `format-only` return no covering issue; #1950 (CLOSED) covers only the constraint keywords above.

## Why it matters

Any tool whose root parameter schema is a bare formatted scalar (a date-time string, an int64, a float) sent through the Antigravity protocol is silently re-typed as an object parameter: the door receives a schema the model's argument can never satisfy as intended, and the format constraint is dead. It is the same silent-narrowing class this file has now fixed three times (#1901, #1950); the guard enumerates keywords, so any keyword missed stays broken until someone trips over it.

## Acceptance criteria

- `convertSchema({ format: "date-time" })` and `convertSchema({ format: "int64" })` (both targets, `anthropic` true/false) return the format with NO forced `type: "OBJECT"`.
- Controls unchanged: `{}` and `minProperties`-only roots still take the OBJECT default; all #1901/#1950 cases keep passing.
- A new case in `packages/ai/test/provider/antigravity.test.ts` pins format-only roots alongside the #1950 constraint-only cases.
- The fix comment/guard accounts for the full proto vocabulary in `SCHEMA_FIELDS`: every remaining field is either exempted, folded into an exempted field (exclusive bounds), an object keyword, or a pure annotation (`title`/`description`/`default`/`example`/`nullable`) — so the enumeration is closed, not one keyword longer.

body:
## Finding

`route_usage`'s `lastServing` readout (from PR #1929, which closed #1891) reports a **hedged race won by the hedge leg as a failover** — although no attempt failed. The readout's stated job is to answer "which leaf served my last step, and did it fail over"; for hedged turns it gives the wrong second answer, and the text output prints `attempted <primary> -> failed over, served by <hedge leg>`, sending anyone diagnosing routing to chase a failure that never happened.

## Evidence

- PR #1929 (merged): https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/1929 — merge on main `fef7d30735aee7204a9dd85010650a31db39788a` lineage.
- `packages/core/src/model-usage.ts` on current main (`fef7d30735`), `lastServing` (~:486-510): a turn is the group of attempts sharing the newest attempt's assistant message id; `served` is the group's latest `outcome === "success"` attempt; `failedOver` is computed as `attemptedLeaf !== leaf || failedOverTo !== null`. There is no check of the attempts' `hedged` flag or of the loser's `hedged-out` outcome.
- Hedged pairs are exactly the shape that trips this: `packages/core/src/model-route-log.ts:71-72` ("True for both legs of a hedged attempt") and `:641-642` — hedged rows share one assistant message, one leg records outcome `hedged-out` (the loser), the other `success` (the winner). When the later-started hedge leg wins, the earliest attempt (the primary) differs from the serving leaf, so `failedOver` comes out `true` with `failedOverTo: null`.
- The data needed to tell the two apart is already fetched and then dropped: `ModelRouteLog.sessionAttempts` selects `hedged` (model-route-log.ts ~:818) and `ServingAttemptRow` carries it (model-usage.ts ~:430), but `servingSteps` does not surface it and `lastServing` never reads it.
- Probe (verbatim `lastServing` body from main, type annotations stripped only; `probe-lastserving.mjs` in the lane evidence dir): a hedged pair — primary `openai/gpt-luna` started t=1000, outcome `hedged-out`, `hedged: true`; hedge leg `vibe/mistral` started t=1500, outcome `success`, `hedged: true`, same message id — returns `{ leaf: "vibe/mistral", attemptedLeaf: "openai/gpt-luna", failedOver: true, failedOverTo: null }`. A genuine failover control also returns `failedOver: true` (correct); a hedged race the primary wins returns `failedOver: false`.
- Test gap: the tests PR #1929 added (`packages/core/test/model-usage.test.ts`, "ModelUsage serving readout (#1891)") cover a true failover, a single-leaf turn, and an older turn's failover — no hedged pair in either win direction.

## Why it matters

Hedging is a standing route feature in this fork, so hedge-leg wins are routine, not exotic: every one of them makes the session's own serving readout claim a failover occurred. That corrupts exactly the signal #1891 built the readout for (post-hoc routing diagnosis: "did my last step fail over, and to what") and can send a session or an operator hunting a phantom provider failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- A turn whose non-serving attempts all ended `hedged-out` (a hedged race) is NOT reported as `failedOver` in `lastServing`, in either win direction; it is reported as hedged (a distinct flag/wording), or at minimum not as a failover.
- A genuine failover (an attempt with outcome `failure`/`timeout`, or a recorded `failed_over_to`) still reports `failedOver: true` — the existing #1891 tests keep passing.
- The per-step readout (`serving` / the text lines) distinguishes hedged legs from failed attempts (e.g. surfaces the already-selected `hedged` flag).
- New tests in `model-usage.test.ts` pin a hedged pair both ways (primary wins, hedge leg wins) against the real `lastServing`/`servingSteps`.

body:
## Problem

`truncate` in `packages/script/src/highlights.ts:54-59` cuts release-highlight titles and bodies at raw UTF-16 code-unit indexes (`value.slice(0, limit - 1)`, then optionally `cut.slice(0, space)`), with no surrogate-pair guard. When an astral character (e.g. an emoji) straddles the cut, the result ends in a lone high surrogate — ill-formed text that is then embedded verbatim into the release build as `OPENCODE_RELEASE_HIGHLIGHTS` JSON (`embed`, highlights.ts:62-68).

Reproduced this run on main `86da7064fd` with a probe against `parse()` (limits: title 60, body 300, highlights.ts:3):

- Title `"a"×58 + 😀 + " extra words…"`: parsed title is `"aaa…a\ud83d…"` — `title.isWellFormed()` is `false`, length 60.
- Body `"b"×298 + 😀 + " tail…"`: parsed body ends `"bb\ud83d…"`, `body.isWellFormed()` is `false`, length 300.
- `problems` is empty in both cases — the corruption is silent, despite the module's design of reporting formatting problems instead of failing the release.

## Why it matters

Release highlights are user-facing text shipped in the binary. A lone surrogate re-encodes as U+FFFD (or breaks strict JSON/UTF-8 consumers downstream) — a mangled emoji at exactly the truncation point, in exactly the text meant to showcase the release. The house rule is to never split a pair (core `Text.truncate` drops a straddling pair whole, `packages/core/src/util/text.ts`); this local helper predates / sits outside that contract. Note the design #2208 inventory in issue #2209 covers `packages/ai`, `packages/core`, `packages/util`, and `packages/tui` only — `packages/script` is not inventoried, so this site is not tracked by phases 1–3.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `truncate` in `packages/script/src/highlights.ts` never splits a surrogate pair: a straddling pair is dropped whole (the core `Text.truncate` disposition), for both the hard cut and the word-boundary cut.
- [ ] New pins in `packages/script/test/highlights.test.ts`: an astral character straddling the title limit and the body limit, asserting `isWellFormed()` and the exact expected output; non-straddling controls unchanged.
- [ ] Existing highlights suite stays green; length limits (60 / 300 including the ellipsis) are unchanged.

title: fix(ai): partial-json nested number fallback ignores Allow.NUM and trims at the last 'e' in the whole input — {"a":1e,"e":5} silently parses to {}

body:
## Problem

`parseNum` in `packages/ai/src/protocols/utils/partial-json.ts` has two defects in its nested-value branch (the branch taken for any number that is not the whole input — i.e. every number inside an object or array, which is the shape streaming tool-call arguments actually arrive in). Both were reproduced this run on main `86da7064fd` with a probe against the module (existing suite: 8 pass).

### 1. The exponent-trim fallback ignores `Allow.NUM` for nested numbers

The top-level branch (`index === 0`, partial-json.ts:243-258) guards the trim-at-`e` repair with `if (Allow.NUM & allow)`. The nested branch (partial-json.ts:261-272) applies the same repair unconditionally at :268. The `Allow` flags are documented and tested as independent controls over which partial value kinds are accepted (`controls partial collection values independently`, `distinguishes disallowed partial values from malformed values` in `packages/ai/test/partial-json.test.ts`), so a caller that withholds `Allow.NUM` gets different semantics depending on nesting depth:

| input | flags | result |
|---|---|---|
| `1e` | `Allow.ARR` (no NUM) | throws `MalformedJSON` |
| `[1e]` | `Allow.ARR` (no NUM) | `[1]` |
| `[1e]` | `0` (no flags at all) | `[1]` |
| `{"a":1e}` | `Allow.OBJ` (no NUM) | `{"a":1}` |
| `[1e]` | `Allow.ARR \| Allow.NUM` | `[1]` (correct) |
| `[12]` | `Allow.ARR` | `[12]` (control) |

### 2. The trim point is the last `e` in the whole input, not in the number token

Both branches compute the trim as `jsonString.substring(start, jsonString.lastIndexOf("e"))` (partial-json.ts:251 and :268) — searching the entire remaining input rather than the token that was just scanned (`start..index`). When any later key or string contains an `e`, the substring spans past the token, the decode fails, and the error propagates into the enclosing object parser, whose `Allow.OBJ` catch returns the object accumulated so far — silently discarding the malformed entry **and every valid entry after it**:

| input | flags | result |
|---|---|---|
| `{"a":1e,"e":5}` | `Allow.ALL` | `{}` — both entries lost |
| `{"e":5,"a":1e}` | `Allow.ALL` | `{"e":5,"a":1}` — same content, order flipped, parses |

## Why it matters

`parse` is the streaming tool-argument parser (`packages/ai/src/protocols/utils/tool-stream.ts:7,74`): partial tool inputs are parsed with it on every delta. Defect 2 means one exponent-truncated number early in an arguments object can silently empty the rest of the parsed arguments — order-dependent data loss with no error surface. Defect 1 means the `Allow` flag contract the module's own test suite pins for top-level values does not hold for the nested values that are the parser's main use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The nested-number exponent-trim repair runs only when `Allow.NUM` is set, matching the top-level branch; `[1e]` with no NUM flag throws/partial-fails the same way top-level `1e` does.
- [ ] The trim point is computed within the scanned token (`start..index`), never beyond it: `{"a":1e,"e":5}` under `Allow.ALL` yields `{"a":1,"e":5}`.
- [ ] New pins in `packages/ai/test/partial-json.test.ts` cover: nested `1e` with and without `Allow.NUM`, and the order-flipped object pair above.
- [ ] Existing partial-json suite stays green; no behaviour change for complete JSON or for the default `Allow.ALL` streaming path beyond the two fixes.

body:
# fix(script): NativeArch.verify accepts a universal Mach-O for either single arch — a fat x64+arm64 binary passes both the x64 and the arm64 gate

## Finding

`NativeArch.verify(file, arch)` in `script/native-arch.ts` is the release gate that keeps a wrong-architecture native image from shipping inside a per-arch build (its doc cites the 2.0.27 incident: an ARM64 Windows CLI embedding an x64 `rust_pty.dll`). Its stated contract is strict:

- `script/native-arch.ts:28` — "Fails unless `file` is a native image for `arch` and **every image embedded in it targets `arch` too**."
- `script/native-arch.ts:38` — the failure message itself: "`${file}` **must contain only `${arch}` code**, but has …"

The check does not implement that contract for universal (fat) Mach-O binaries:

- `script/native-arch.ts:35` — `const wrong = found.filter((image) => !image.arches.includes(arch))`

A fat image's `arches` is the list of ALL its slices (`fat()` at `script/native-arch.ts:88-102` collects every slice's cpu). `includes(arch)` asks "does this image contain the target arch anywhere", not "does it contain only the target arch". For thin PE/ELF/Mach-O images `arches` has exactly one entry, so the two readings coincide — but a universal Mach-O carrying both x64 and arm64 slices satisfies `includes` for **both** arches, so the same file passes the x64 gate and the arm64 gate while containing code for the other arch in both cases.

`NativeArch.verify` is called per-arch from three build paths, all of which build single-arch artifacts:

- `packages/cli/script/build.ts:257` — `NativeArch.verify(<per-target bin>, item.arch)`
- `packages/cli/script/build-node.ts:149` — `NativeArch.verify(output, target.arch)`
- `packages/desktop/electron-builder.config.ts:132` and `:158` — `NativeArch.verify(cli, arch)` / per-file verify in the desktop packager

If a universal binary (or a universal dylib embedded in a compiled executable — `images()` scans the whole file, including Bun-embedded libraries) ever reaches one of these per-arch outputs, the gate that exists to catch exactly that class of mistake reports success.

There is also no test file for this parser: `script/` has tests for check-bounded-http, check-gates, check-workflows, mcpx-cleanup, turbo-json and others, but nothing for `native-arch.ts` — the three-format hand-rolled binary parser behind the release gate is entirely unpinned.

## Evidence (probe, this run)

Probe `probe-creator.test.ts` run with `bun test` in a laptop worktree at main `e340f54ac284` (script/ directory), with synthetic binaries built byte-by-byte:

- `images(fat x64+arm64)` → `[{"offset":0,"format":"Mach-O","arches":["x64","arm64"],"end":176}]` — one universal image, thin slices correctly filtered out.
- `verify(fat, "arm64")` → **RESOLVED** (contract says it must throw: the file contains x64 code).
- `verify(fat, "x64")` → **RESOLVED** (same file passes the opposite gate too).
- Controls, all correct:
  - `verify(thin arm64, "arm64")` → RESOLVED; `verify(thin arm64, "x64")` → THREW "must contain only x64 code, but has Mach-O arm64 at byte 0".
  - `verify(thin x64, "arm64")` → THREW as documented.
  - arm64 ELF with an embedded x64 thin Mach-O → THREW (embedded-image detection works); clean arm64 ELF → RESOLVED.
- Secondary observation for triage scope: a 32-bit Mach-O (`\xce\xfa\xed\xfe`, cpu x86) is invisible to `images()` (returns `[]`) — fail-closed for a standalone file (verify throws "not a native executable"), but an embedded 32-bit image would be missed entirely. Whether 32-bit Mach-O is in scope for this gate is a triage call; the fat/`includes` defect above is not — it contradicts the documented contract on the gate's primary macOS surface.

Dedupe (this run): issue/PR searches for native-arch / NativeArch / universal / fat binary / verify arch return no existing item.

## Why it matters

This gate is the only automated check standing between a packaging mistake and a shipped wrong-arch binary — the failure mode it was written for is silent (a wrong-arch library "loads only on the machine that needs it, so it ships unnoticed"). A universal binary slipping into a per-arch release is precisely the kind of mistake the gate's doc promises to catch, and today it cannot: it waves the same file through both arch gates.

## Acceptance criteria

- `NativeArch.verify(file, "arm64")` rejects a file whose only native image is a universal Mach-O with x64+arm64 slices (and symmetrically for `"x64"`), with the existing "must contain only … code" error naming the fat image's arches — OR the contract is explicitly re-decided: if universal binaries are intentionally acceptable in some call path, the doc and the error message are rewritten to say so and the per-call-site disposition is recorded (the three call sites above are all per-arch today).
- The disposition for a fat image whose slices are all the target arch (e.g. arm64 + arm64e-style duplicates mapping to one arch name) is stated and pinned.
- A new `script/native-arch.test.ts` (following the sibling script tests) pins at minimum: thin PE/ELF/Mach-O accept + wrong-arch reject, embedded wrong-arch image reject, fat single-arch accept/reject per the decided contract, fat multi-arch behavior per the decided contract, and the non-native-file rejection.
- Triage records whether 32-bit Mach-O (and fat64) detection is in scope or a documented non-goal.

body:
## Problem

`session.export --sanitize` redacts transcript text, file data, tool input/output, and metadata, but `SessionTransfer.sanitizeMessage` preserves stored `SessionError` values unchanged:

- The assistant branch spreads `message` while only rewriting content/metadata (`packages/core/src/session/transfer.ts:264-289`), leaving `message.error` intact.
- Failed compactions spread `message` and only redact metadata (`:291-310`).
- Error tool states spread `state` and redact input/content/metadata, but not `state.error` (`:313-329`).
- Idle messages fall through to the generic spread at `:310`; their optional `error` field is part of `Session.Message.Idle` (`packages/schema/src/session-message.ts:289-295`).

`SessionError.Error` includes a string `message` and optional string `response.body` (`packages/schema/src/session-error.ts:7-11`). Those values can contain provider response text or other sensitive context. The CLI's `--sanitize` flag is described as redacting sensitive transcript and file data (`packages/cli/src/commands/commands.ts:487-489`) and is passed through to `session.export` (`packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/session/export.ts:74`), yet these error payloads remain verbatim. The existing sanitized-export assertion currently expects `Original error` to remain (`packages/core/test/session-create.test.ts:1500-1510`).

This is distinct from #541, which addressed redaction in model-route log capture; this issue is specifically the session-transfer export path.

## Why it matters

A user may share a supposedly sanitized export while it still contains arbitrary upstream error text, including echoed credentials, prompt excerpts, or local details. That undermines the privacy purpose of the sanitization option.

## Acceptance criteria

- With `sanitize: true`, redact non-empty `SessionError.message` and `response.body` values in assistant, failed-compaction, error-tool-state, and idle-message errors; preserve safe structure such as error type/status.
- Add `SessionTransfer.export` regression coverage with distinct sentinel values in both error fields across the error-bearing message variants, asserting no sentinel appears in the sanitized JSON.
- Confirm ordinary export (`sanitize: false`) continues to retain the original error payloads.

body:
# fix(script): raw-changelog classification — scoped conventional prefixes escape the exclusion filter, and /fix/i substring sends prefix/fixture commits to Bugfixes

## Summary

Two classification defects in `script/raw-changelog.ts` corrupt the changelog
input independently of which commits the pathspec admits: scoped
conventional-commit subjects are never excluded as test/chore/ci noise, and
the Bugfixes/Improvements split is a bare substring match on "fix".

## Evidence (verified this run; laptop primary @ e340f54ac284)

1. **Exclusion filter misses scoped prefixes.** Both `commits()`
   (`script/raw-changelog.ts:129`) and `contributors()` (:164) drop noise
   commits with `/^(ignore:|test:|chore:|ci:|release:)/i`. The colon must
   immediately follow the type word, so the scoped forms this repo actually
   uses — `test(ai):`, `test(console):`, `chore(ci):`, `ci(workflows):` —
   never match and are kept as notable changes (and credited in the
   contributors/thank-you list). Real subjects from this repo's history:
   - `test(ai): reclassify moonshot prefixItems corpus row to approximated/widening, guard known-lossy links (#1933)`
   - `test(console): one shared console-resource preload fixture (#1522)`
2. **Bugfix split is a substring match.** `type()` (:84-87) is
   `if (message.match(/fix/i)) return "Bugfixes"`. Any subject containing the
   letters `fix` anywhere classifies as a bugfix — `prefix`, `suffix`,
   `fixture`, `prefixItems`. 14 of the last 2000 subjects on main contain
   `prefix` or `suffix`. The `test(ai): … prefixItems …` subject above hits
   both defects at once: kept by the filter, then filed under Bugfixes.

## Why it matters

The changelog command's prompt treats the script output as pre-filtered and
pre-grouped; misclassified entries flow straight into release notes — test
and chore work presented as user-facing bug fixes — and the contributors
section credits noise commits. The errors are silent and systematic (every
scoped test/chore commit, every prefix/suffix/fixture subject).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The exclusion filter recognises scoped conventional prefixes
      (`test(scope):`, `chore(scope):`, `ci(scope):`, and the unscoped forms)
      in both `commits()` and `contributors()`.
- [ ] `type()` classifies by the conventional-commit type (a leading `fix`
      type, scoped or not), not by a substring anywhere in the subject:
      subjects mentioning prefix/suffix/fixture in prose land in
      Improvements (or are excluded per the filter), while `fix:` /
      `fix(scope):` subjects land in Bugfixes.
- [ ] The two example subjects above classify as excluded (test) and not
      Bugfixes respectively, pinned by a test or a documented manual check.

## Finding

The v1-dialect effort drop that PR #1872 fixed for muse-direct only is still unowned for every other native provider. Config variants written in the v1 dialect (`{options: {reasoning_effort: "xhigh"}}`) migrate to variant settings carrying the snake_case / nested spellings, and a native provider whose settings resolver reads only the flat camelCase `reasoningEffort` silently sends `reasoning: null` — the session runs at the wrong effort with no error anywhere. #1825's own record states this is fork-wide ("The same latent drop affects every native provider whose config variants use the v1 dialect — the `meta` provider block included. Flagged here as a fork-wide follow-up; this change fixes muse-direct only"), but the follow-up was never split into its own issue: it sits inside #1825, whose title and scope are now a different audit follow-up (secret-tool spawning), so nothing tracks the remaining providers.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1872 (MERGED 2026-11-06T18:45:57Z, merge f4514086e5f6) "muse-direct: native Meta wire provider (#1825)". Link: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/1872
- The fix's shape, from the PR diff, `packages/ai/src/providers/muse-direct.ts`: `fromSettings` normalizes `providerOptions.reasoningEffort ?? reasoning_effort ?? options?.reasoningEffort ?? options?.reasoning_effort` into the native `reasoningEffort` option, with a wire test ("v1-dialect effort settings normalize to reasoningEffort on the wire") covering all four spellings. No other provider received the normalization in that PR.
- #1825 (OPEN) body section "Effort parity defect — found in scratch, fixed in the same PR" records the root cause as fork-wide and the muse-direct-only scope explicitly. Verified 2026-11-09 by reading the issue body.
- Dedupe (2026-11-09, lane B): issue searches for "reasoning_effort", "reasoningEffort dropped variants", "effort parity", "reasoningEffort v1 dialect native provider" return only #1825 and the closed provider-emulation issues — no dedicated issue exists for the non-muse-direct providers.

## Why it matters

Effort is a routing/cost/quality control Drew sets deliberately per seat. A provider that silently drops it runs sessions at a default effort while the config says otherwise — the exact failure #1872 proved end-to-end for muse-direct (recorder capture showed `reasoning: null` for variant sessions). Until each remaining native provider is audited, nobody knows which seats are affected, and the flag on #1825 will keep being mistaken for tracking.

## Acceptance criteria

- An audit table (in this issue or a linked one) naming every native provider in `packages/ai/src/providers` whose settings path can receive variant effort, with its disposition: normalizes all four spellings (`reasoningEffort`, `reasoning_effort`, `options.reasoningEffort`, `options.reasoning_effort`), already conforming (with the test that proves it), or not effort-capable.
- Each provider found dropping the v1 spellings gains the same normalization muse-direct received, pinned by a wire/settings test in the muse-direct test's shape.
- #1825 is updated to point at this issue for the effort-parity remainder, so the flag stops living only in its body.

body:
<!-- agent-note:v1
Agent: pr-diff-review-b
state: filed
-->

## Finding

PR #1874 implemented #1858's package seating: the first config document declaring a provider's `package` seats it, and a later document declaring a *different* package for the same provider is conflicted — its contribution is supposed to be ignored. In the provider transform that actually builds the provider record, the conflict flag gates only `package` and `settings`. The conflicting document's `headers` and `body` are still merged into the seated provider, ungated — so a document that lost the package seat can still inject arbitrary request headers (including authorization-style headers) and body overlays into a provider it does not own. That is the hijack surface #1858 set out to close, left open on two of the request-shaping fields. The neighbouring ungated fields in the same block (`canonical`, `compatibility`, `name`) should be judged in the same pass — `canonical` in particular remaps provider identity and triggers the source-clone assignment above it.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1874 (MERGED 2026-11-06T18:18:19Z, merge 90453b467fcc) "fix(core): provider ownership hardening — package seating + unscoped baseURL rewrite warnings (#1858)". Link: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/1874
- Verified on current main e340f54ac2847afe7bed16ebcb5365a77875118e (contents API, read twice, byte-identical), `packages/core/src/config/plugin/provider.ts`:
  - `:113` `if (!conflict && item.package !== undefined) provider.package = item.package` — gated.
  - `:116-117` `if (!conflict && item.settings !== undefined) provider.settings = Provider.mergeOverlay(...)` — gated.
  - `:118` `if (item.headers !== undefined) provider.headers = Provider.mergeHeaders(provider.headers, item.headers)` — NOT gated.
  - `:119` `if (item.body !== undefined) provider.body = Provider.mergeOverlay(provider.body, item.body)` — NOT gated.
  - `:89` shows the pattern was applied deliberately elsewhere in the same function: the provider-baseURL set filters `!conflict`.
  - The seating computation itself (`configuredProviders`, :286-302 of the same file) and the startup warning (:28-38, "the conflicting document's settings for that provider are ignored") describe the conflicting document's contribution as ignored, with no headers/body carve-out.
- The sibling surface is clean: `foldSettings` in `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/configured.ts` folds settings only, and it is gated.
- Test gap, verified on main: `packages/core/test/plugin/provider-ownership.test.ts` (167 lines) covers `foldSettings` seating and the `model.request` baseURL warning only. Nothing exercises `configuredProviders` / the provider transform at all, so the ungated merge is neither pinned nor refuted by a test.
- Dedupe (2026-11-09, lane B): issue searches for "seating headers", "package seating conflict", "conflicting document", "headers body fold provider" return nothing; #1858 is CLOSED and its acceptance was settings/package folding. This residual is unfiled.

## Why it matters

#1858 exists because a config document that does not own a provider must not be able to steer its traffic. Settings and baseURL were closed; headers/body are the same class of steering (credentials and payload shape) on the same record, reachable by the same conflicting document. Leaving them ungated makes the seating guarantee read stronger than it is — the startup warning tells the user the conflicting document is ignored while its headers are on the wire.

## Acceptance criteria

- In the provider transform, a conflicted document's `headers` and `body` no longer merge into the seated provider (or an explicit, documented disposition states why headers/body are exempt, and the startup warning text is corrected to match reality).
- `canonical`, `compatibility`, and `name` in the same block are each explicitly gated or explicitly dispositioned in the same change.
- A test drives the real provider transform (not only `foldSettings`) with a seated provider plus a conflicting-package document carrying headers/body, and asserts the seated provider's headers/body are unchanged.
- Existing provider-ownership tests still pass; documents declaring no package (user config) fold headers/body exactly as before.

title: fix(core): lazy caches a synchronous initializer throw as undefined — loaded is set before fn() runs, so a transient load failure is never retried or rethrown and later calls return undefined as T

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`lazy` in `packages/core/src/util/lazy.ts:1-11` sets its `loaded` flag **before** calling the initializer:

```ts
return (): T => {
  if (loaded) return value as T
  loaded = true          // :7 — set before fn() runs
  value = fn()           // :8
  return value as T
}
```

If `fn()` throws synchronously, `loaded` stays `true` and `value` stays `undefined`. Every later call silently returns `undefined` cast to `T` — the failure is neither retried nor rethrown, and callers receive a value that violates the return type with no error anywhere.

There is **no test file for `lazy`** (`packages/core/test/util/` has error-summary, number, record, text, which, flock, git-executable — no lazy).

## Evidence (verified this run on main `9f4e222016f9`)

Sites:

- `packages/core/src/util/lazy.ts:7` — `loaded = true` precedes `value = fn()` at `:8`
- Callers: `packages/core/src/filesystem/watcher.ts:29` (native `@parcel/watcher` binding load — its initializer catches internally and returns `undefined`, so a cached-undefined is the intended shape there), `packages/core/src/pty.ts:16` (`lazy(() => import("#pty"))`), `packages/core/src/shell/parse.ts:392` (`lazy(initialize)` — tree-sitter parser/language load)

Probe `probe-lazy.test.ts`, laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-1835` @ `9f4e222016f9`, `packages/core` (3 pass):

- Initializer that throws on first call and would return `42` on second: first call throws; **second call returns `undefined`, does not throw, and the initializer is never called again** (`calls` stays 1)
- Controls correct: a successful initializer runs exactly once and caches; an initializer legitimately returning `undefined` also runs exactly once

Dedup: title/keyword search over open + closed issues for `lazy` returns no filing for this helper (only unrelated lazy-loading issues #95/#1615).

## Why it matters

`lazy` is the load-once guard for native/expensive initializers — the file watcher binding, the PTY implementation, and the shell parser. Its contract is "run once, replay the value"; the current ordering silently converts a transient synchronous load failure (a binding that is briefly unavailable, a parser asset that fails to resolve) into a permanent, type-lying `undefined` for the life of the process, with the original error visible only on the very first call — which may happen on a code path that discards it. The promise-returning callers (pty, shell parse) are mostly shielded today because an async initializer cannot throw synchronously, and the watcher caller self-catches — which is exactly why the disposition is a triage call: retry-on-next-call (set `loaded` only after success) vs cache-and-rethrow the same error, and whether a rejected cached promise deserves the same treatment, should be decided once for the helper rather than rediscovered per caller.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A synchronously throwing initializer is not permanently cached as `undefined`: a later call either retries the initializer or rethrows the original error (triage records the chosen disposition on this issue)
- [ ] New unit tests for `lazy` pin: success caches and runs once; a legitimately `undefined` result caches and runs once (watcher shape); the throwing-initializer disposition above; the promise-returning shape used by pty/shell-parse callers
- [ ] Existing callers' behavior is unchanged on the success path (`hasNativeBinding`, pty load, shell parser load)
- [ ] `packages/core` util test suites stay green

title: fix(ai): quota getAuthEntry reads through the prototype chain — a toString/constructor alias returns an inherited member instead of null, against the #865 own-property doctrine

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

body:
## Problem

`getAuthEntry` in `packages/ai/src/quota/utils.ts:301` looks a provider's credential entry up by alias with a bare prototype-chain read:

```ts
export const getAuthEntry = (auth: Record<string, QuotaAuthEntry>, aliases: string[]): QuotaAuthEntry | null => {
  for (const alias of aliases) {
    if (auth[alias]) return auth[alias]
  }
  return null
}
```

An alias that names an inherited member — `toString`, `constructor`, `valueOf` — returns that inherited member instead of `null`. This is exactly the read shape the repo's own dictionary doctrine forbids: `packages/core/src/util/record.ts` (#865, follow-up to the #833 audit) states that a bare `record[key]` read walks the prototype chain, so an externally influenced key resolves to an inherited member and a `?? fallback` never fires, and every such dictionary read goes through `ownValue`. The quota module hardened the *write* side of this same record in #2110/#2171 (`projectAuth` at `utils.ts:287` defines each entry with `Object.defineProperty` so a `__proto__` integration id lands as an own property) — the read side was left bare.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `bdf2bc83f6`)

Sites:

- `packages/ai/src/quota/utils.ts:301` — `getAuthEntry` bare `auth[alias]` read (twice: the truthiness test and the return)
- `packages/ai/src/quota/utils.ts:287` — `projectAuth` write side, already prototype-safe via `Object.defineProperty`
- `packages/core/src/util/record.ts:13` — `ownValue`, the house helper for exactly this read
- Callers: every quota provider's `isConfigured`/`fetchQuota` (groq.ts:85/:87, deepseek.ts:34/:38, meta.ts:377/:381, claude.ts:89, codex.ts:237/:253, opencode-go.ts:182–:193, command-code.ts, cline-pass.ts)

Probe `probe2-quota-utils.test.ts`, laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-1735` @ `bdf2bc83f6`, `packages/ai`:

- `getAuthEntry({}, ["toString"])` → the inherited `toString` function (truthy, returned as the "entry")
- `getAuthEntry({}, ["constructor"])` → the inherited `Object` constructor
- Control: `getAuthEntry({}, ["groq"])` → `null`, as expected

Dedup: title/keyword search over open + closed issues for `getAuthEntry` returns no filing for this read site (#1831, closed, is the blank-credential issue in the same providers — a different defect).

## Why it matters

Today the aliases are provider-module constants, so no live provider is misconfigured by this — the exposure is latent, and that is precisely when the #865 doctrine says to fix the read: the alias lists are the extension point every new quota provider copies (13 providers already call this helper), the auth record's keys come from credential-store rows (integration ids are store data, already treated as hostile on the write side), and a single future alias or store-driven lookup named like an `Object.prototype` member turns `isConfigured` checks and credential reads into reads of an inherited function — truthy, wrong-typed, and silent. The fix is small (own-property lookup, e.g. via the `ownValue` shape) and behavior-identical for every real alias.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `getAuthEntry` returns `null` for aliases that are not own properties of the auth record (`toString`, `constructor`, `valueOf`, `__proto__`, `hasOwnProperty`)
- [ ] An entry stored under a prototype-named integration id by `projectAuth` (e.g. a `__proto__` row, per #2110/#2171) still round-trips: `getAuthEntry` returns that own entry
- [ ] New unit tests pin both directions (inherited member not returned; own prototype-named entry returned)
- [ ] No behavior change for ordinary aliases across the 13 quota providers; `packages/ai` quota suite stays green

title: fix(util): parsePathLineSuffix consumes an out-of-range line suffix and drops it — path stripped with no selection, and the suffix grammar has no tests

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`parsePathLineSuffix` in `packages/util/src/path.ts:127` strips a trailing line suffix (`file.ts:42`, `file.ts#L42-L58`) and returns `{ path, selection }`. When the suffix's line numbers are **out of range** — line `0`, or above the `MAX_LINE_NUMBER` cap of 1,000,000 at `path.ts:97` — `toLineRange` (`path.ts:105`) returns `undefined`, but the suffix is still consumed: the result is the stripped path with `selection: undefined`.

That breaks the signal every consumer keys on. Consumers treat `parsed.path !== input` as "a line suffix was present":

- `packages/gui-extensions/src/file/resolve-link.ts` (`extractLineSelection`): `if (parsed.selection || parsed.path !== input)` returns the stripped path as a file link with no selection
- `packages/session-ui/src/components/markdown-image.ts:38` (`localLinkPath`): same `cited.path !== target` test
- `packages/session-ui/src/components/markdown-inline-code-kind.ts:34`: uses `.path` directly to classify inline code

So `file.ts:0` and `notes:1234567` silently lose their suffix and resolve as plain file references, and a non-path string like `tel:5551234` is mangled to `tel`. The function and its sibling `isLineRangeHash` have **no tests**: `packages/util/src/path.test.ts` never references either.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `bdf2bc83f6`)

Sites:

- `packages/util/src/path.ts:97` — `MAX_LINE_NUMBER = 1_000_000`
- `packages/util/src/path.ts:105` — `toLineRange` returns `undefined` for non-safe-integer, `< 1`, or `> MAX_LINE_NUMBER` inputs
- `packages/util/src/path.ts:127` — `parsePathLineSuffix` returns the stripped `path` with that `undefined` selection in both the hash and colon branches

Probe `probe1-path.test.ts`, laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-1735` @ `bdf2bc83f6`, `packages/util`:

- `"file.ts:0"` → `{path: "file.ts"}` (selection undefined, suffix consumed)
- `"file.ts:1000001"` → `{path: "file.ts"}`; `"notes:1234567"` → `{path: "notes"}`
- `"file.ts#L0"` → `{path: "file.ts"}`
- `"tel:5551234"` → `{path: "tel"}`
- Controls correct: `"file.ts:42"` → selection `{42,42}`; `"file.ts#L42-L58"` → `{42,58}`; `"a.ts:5-3"` → `{3,5}` (order normalized); `"C:5"` → untouched (drive guard)

Dedup: title/keyword search over open + closed issues for `parsePathLineSuffix` and "line suffix" returns no filing for this site.

## Why it matters

A cited line that cannot exist (0, or past the cap the module itself declares) should not be silently swallowed: the file opens with no selection and no trace that a citation was dropped, and the `path !== input` contract consumers rely on becomes ambiguous — it now means "a suffix-shaped tail was removed", not "a line reference was parsed". The clean disposition is to leave the input untouched when the range is invalid (so `path !== input` again means a valid suffix was consumed), but that changes what the three consumers see for malformed citations, so it is a triage call — pinned by tests either way.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An out-of-range suffix (line 0 or above 1,000,000, either `#L` or colon form) no longer produces a stripped path with an undefined selection: `parsePathLineSuffix` returns the input untouched, or triage records an explicit alternative disposition on this issue and pins that instead
- [ ] New unit tests pin the full suffix grammar: valid single/range/column forms in both spellings, reversed ranges, the drive-letter guard (`C:5`), and the out-of-range cases above
- [ ] The three consumers (resolve-link, markdown-image, markdown-inline-code-kind) behave as before for valid suffixes and plain paths
- [ ] Existing `packages/util` path suite stays green

title: fix(util): containsDirectory treats an empty parent as containing every absolute path — the workspace-scope containment family has no tests

body:
## Problem

`containsDirectory(parent, child)` in `packages/util/src/path.ts:64` decides whether `child` is `parent` or inside it, and the app/workspace layer uses it to scope sessions and directories to a workspace. An **empty parent contains every absolute path**:

- `comparablePath("")` returns `""` (no trailing-slash trim applies, not a drive, does not start with `/` after trimming)
- the containment test at `path.ts:71`-ish is `target === root || target.startsWith(root.endsWith("/") ? root : root + "/")` — with `root === ""` the prefix tested is `"/"`, so every absolute child path passes

The whole containment family — `comparablePath`, `containsDirectory`, `sameDirectory` — has **no tests anywhere**: `packages/util/src/path.test.ts` (97 lines) covers only the filename/truncation helpers and `encodeFilePath`, and no other test file references these functions.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `bdf2bc83f6`)

Sites:

- `packages/util/src/path.ts:52` — `comparablePath` (empty input returns `""`)
- `packages/util/src/path.ts:64` — `containsDirectory`; `:74` — `sameDirectory` built on it
- Consumers: `packages/app/src/workspaces/paths.ts:40` (sessions filtered by `containsDirectory(workspace, session.location.directory)`), `:105`/`:108` (active/in-workspace flags), `:117`/`:123` (directory-in-workspace checks); `packages/core/src/config/plugin/instruction.ts:253` (`sameDirectory`)

Probe `probe1-path.test.ts`, laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-1735` @ `bdf2bc83f6`, `packages/util`:

- `containsDirectory("", "/etc/passwd")` → `true`
- `containsDirectory("", "rel/path")` → `false` (the hole is specific to absolute children)
- Controls correct: `containsDirectory("/", "/etc")` → `true`; `containsDirectory("/a/b", "/a/bc")` → `false` (sibling prefix rejected); `sameDirectory("", "")` → `true`

Dedup: title/keyword search over open + closed issues for `containsDirectory`, `comparablePath`, `sameDirectory` returns no filing.

## Why it matters

These helpers are the workspace-scope boundary for the app: which sessions belong to a workspace, whether a directory counts as inside it, and which sandbox directories get filtered out all reduce to `containsDirectory`/`sameDirectory`. A project or workspace record whose directory is empty/unset (a non-git project, a partially migrated record) silently scopes to *everything absolute* instead of nothing — sessions and directories from unrelated roots read as belonging to that workspace. The disposition is a triage call (empty parent contains nothing vs empty input is a caller error to surface), and the untested Windows/UNC case-folding branches in the same functions need pins either way.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `containsDirectory("", child)` is `false` for every non-empty `child` (or triage records an explicit alternative disposition on this issue and pins that instead)
- [ ] `sameDirectory`/`comparablePath` empty-input behavior is pinned by tests consistent with the chosen disposition
- [ ] New unit tests cover the containment family: empty parent, root parent, sibling-prefix (`/a/b` vs `/a/bc`), trailing-slash parent, nested child, Windows drive and UNC case-insensitive comparisons
- [ ] Existing `packages/util` path suite stays green; no behavior change for non-empty parents

title: fix(ai): normalizeToolHistory collapses duplicate tool-call ids — the second call overwrites the first in the pending map, one missing result is never synthesized, and a real result is renamed to the wrong call

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/ai

labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`normalizeToolHistory` in `packages/ai/src/tool-history.ts` tracks unanswered tool calls in a plain id-keyed `Map` (:8, populated at :40 with `pending.set(part.id, part)`). When one assistant message carries two tool calls with the **same id** — which histories assembled from forks, merges, recorded sessions, or a provider that recycled an id can contain — the second call silently overwrites the first in the map. The repair layer then produces a history that is still count-mismatched, and misattributes a real result:

- With **no results at all**, only ONE `Tool result missing` error result is synthesized (for the second call, from `pending.values()` at :17) — the first call gets no result, so the 2-calls/1-result mismatch the function exists to repair survives normalization.
- With **one result per call**, the first call's real result is renamed to the second call's name: `normalizeToolMessage` (:68–:69) looks the result's id up in the map, gets the *second* call, deletes the entry, and `normalizeToolResult` rewrites the result's `name`/`namespace` to that call's identity (the function's own "a matching call is the complete tool identity" rule, applied to the wrong call). The second result then matches nothing and also ends up carrying the second call's name — both results read as the second call, and the first call's identity disappears from the tool history entirely.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `a5d85a2416`)

Sites:

- `packages/ai/src/tool-history.ts:8` — `const pending = new Map<string, ToolCallPart>()`
- `packages/ai/src/tool-history.ts:40` — `pending.set(part.id, part)` for every non-provider-executed tool-call part, no duplicate check
- `packages/ai/src/tool-history.ts:17` — missing results are synthesized from `pending.values()`, so a collapsed entry can only ever produce one
- `packages/ai/src/tool-history.ts:65–:69` — `normalizeToolMessage` resolves each result's call by id from the same map and deletes it
- `packages/ai/src/route/client.ts:274` — the live call site: `normalizeToolHistory(request.messages)` runs on every compiled request, so the collapsed history is what every protocol lowering sends

Probe `probe-creator.test.ts` + `probe2-creator.test.ts`, laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-1635` @ `a5d85a2416`, `packages/ai`:

- Calls `dup/a` + `dup/b`, no results → normalized history has exactly one synthesized result: `{id:"dup", name:"b", result:{type:"error", value:"Tool result missing"}}` — call `a` unanswered
- Calls `dup/a` + `dup/b`, results `dup/a="result-for-a"` and `dup/b="result-for-b"` → BOTH results come out named `"b"`; `"result-for-a"` is misattributed to call `b`, and no result carries call `a`'s identity
- Control: distinct ids `x/a` + `y/b` with only `x` answered → `x` keeps its real result and `y` gets the synthesized missing result, correctly named — the collapse is specific to duplicate ids
- Existing suite on the same tree: `test/tool-history.test.ts` — 8 pass / 0 fail; it contains no duplicate-id case (calls are keyed by distinct ids in every test)

Dedup: title/keyword search over open + recently closed issues for `normalizeToolHistory`, tool-history duplicates, and duplicate tool-call ids returns no filing for this site (#1756, closed, was the commandcode stream emitting id-less calls — a different layer).

## Why it matters

This function is the history-repair seam whose whole contract is "every non-provider-executed tool call leaves with exactly one result under its own identity" — protocol lowerings (Anthropic in particular) reject or misread histories where tool_use/tool_result counts and identities diverge. A duplicate id is exactly the kind of malformed history this layer is fed (forked/merged sessions, provider id reuse), and today it fails silently in both directions: an unanswered call stays unanswered, and a real result is silently renamed to a different call, corrupting which tool the model believes produced which output. The disposition is a triage call — e.g. track pending calls per occurrence (a queue per id) and synthesize/attribute per occurrence, or detect duplicates and give the later call a distinct synthesized identity — because it changes what malformed histories compile to.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two same-id tool calls in one assistant message each leave normalization with a result under their own identity (per-occurrence tracking), or triage records an explicit alternative disposition on this issue and pins that instead
- [ ] A real result is never renamed to a different call's name/namespace because another call shared its id
- [ ] With no results, the number of synthesized `Tool result missing` results equals the number of unanswered call occurrences
- [ ] New unit tests cover the probe cases (duplicate ids with zero, one, and two results) plus the distinct-id control; `packages/ai` tool-history suite stays green
- [ ] No behavior change for distinct-id histories: missing-result synthesis, empty-result normalization, held system/effort updates, and the identity fast path are unchanged

title: fix(ai): mergeJsonRecords drops a __proto__ key and re-prototypes the merged record — http.body/providerOptions overlays lose the key and shadow absent-key reads
