body:
## Problem

`mergeJsonRecords` in `packages/ai/src/schema/options.ts` (:9, merge loop :15–:19) builds its result as a plain `{}` and assigns each key with `result[key] = …`. A key named `__proto__` therefore never becomes an own property: the assignment invokes the `Object.prototype` setter instead. Verified consequences:

- A `__proto__` entry whose value is a record is **dropped from the merged record** (it never appears in `Object.keys` or `JSON.stringify` output) and instead **becomes the result object's prototype** — later reads of absent keys on the merged record resolve through the overlay-supplied prototype.
- A `__proto__` entry whose value is not a record (string, number) is **silently swallowed** (the setter ignores non-object values): the key just disappears.
- When `__proto__` is the only key being merged in, the result has zero own keys, so the function's empty-check returns `undefined` — the whole merge reads as "no data".
- The same applies one level down for nested records (the recursive merge at :19), and to `mergeProviderOptions` (:49), which is `mergeJsonRecords` under another name.

The sibling helper in the same file, `mergeStringRecords` (:31), builds via `Object.fromEntries` and does not have this problem — `mergeJsonRecords` is the inconsistent one. This is the same plain-object-assignment family as closed #2110 (quota model maps), at a site that filing did not cover.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `0f2f6f2cc5`)

Sites:

- `packages/ai/src/schema/options.ts:15` — `const result: Record<string, unknown> = {}`
- `packages/ai/src/schema/options.ts:19` — `result[key] = isRecord(result[key]) && isRecord(value) ? mergeJsonRecords(result[key], value) : value` (note `result["__proto__"]` also *reads* `Object.prototype`, which `isRecord` accepts as a record, so a record-valued `__proto__` takes the recursive-merge branch)
- `packages/ai/src/schema/options.ts:49` — `mergeProviderOptions` delegates to `mergeJsonRecords`
- `packages/ai/src/schema/options.ts:104` — HTTP option bodies are merged through the same function
- `packages/ai/src/route/transport/http.ts:50` — the live request path: `mergeJsonRecords(body, request.http.body) ?? {}` overlays the caller-supplied `http.body` onto every compiled JSON request body
- ~30 protocol call sites merge `request.providerOptions` / `request.http?.body` through this helper (openai-images, fal, bfl, deepgram, elevenlabs, cartesia, runway, zai, google-images, transcription/speech protocols, gateway-protocol, system-one)

Probe `probe-creator.test.ts`, laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-1535` @ `0f2f6f2cc5`, `packages/ai` (inputs via `JSON.parse`, the shape a parsed JSON body/config actually has):

- `mergeJsonRecords({model:"m"}, {"__proto__":{"polluted":"yes-merge"}})` → own keys `["model"]` only; `JSON.stringify` → `{"model":"m"}` (overlay key lost); `merged.polluted` reads `"yes-merge"` through the mutated prototype; global `({}).polluted` stays `undefined` (per-result prototype mutation, not global pollution)
- `mergeJsonRecords({}, {"__proto__":{"polluted":"solo"}})` → returns `undefined`
- `mergeJsonRecords({a:1}, {"__proto__":"str"})` → own keys `["a"]`, key silently gone
- Nested: `mergeJsonRecords({cfg:{x:1}}, {"cfg":{"__proto__":{"polluted":"nested"}}})` → `cfg` own keys `["x"]`, `cfg.polluted` reads `"nested"`, JSON drops it
- `mergeProviderOptions({openai:{a:1}}, {"__proto__":{"polluted":"po"}})` → own keys `["openai"]`, `merged.polluted` reads `"po"`
- Control: ordinary deep merge `{a:{x:1}} + {a:{y:2}}` → `{a:{x:1,y:2}}` behaves correctly
- Existing suites green on the same tree: `test/compile.test.ts` + `test/schema.test.ts` — 37 pass / 0 fail; no test in `packages/ai/test` mentions `__proto__` for this helper

## Why it matters

`http.body` overlays and `providerOptions` are caller/config-controlled JSON: a provider option, a gateway/native field, or a tool/provider parameter literally named `__proto__` is legal JSON and parseable config. Today such a key (a) silently never reaches the wire — the request body the provider receives is missing it, with no error anywhere — and (b) worse, a record-valued one re-prototypes the merged options/body object, so any subsequent `options.<absent-key>` read in compile/lowering code can return the overlay's value instead of `undefined`. The failure is silent in both directions. The fix shape is small and precedented in-file (build via `Object.fromEntries` / `Object.defineProperty` / a null-prototype result, as `mergeStringRecords` and the #2110 fix already do elsewhere), but which shape — and whether `__proto__` should round-trip as a normal key or be rejected — is a triage call because this helper sits under every protocol's body compilation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `mergeJsonRecords` (and therefore `mergeProviderOptions` and the http-body overlay) preserves a `__proto__` key as an ordinary own property that survives `Object.keys` and `JSON.stringify`, at the top level and nested — or triage records an explicit reject/strip disposition on this issue and pins that instead
- [ ] Merging a `__proto__` entry never changes the result object's prototype, and never makes an absent-key read return an overlay-supplied value
- [ ] A merge whose only incoming key is `__proto__` no longer returns `undefined` for a non-empty merge (under the preserve disposition)
- [ ] New unit tests cover the probe cases (record value, primitive value, solo key, nested, provider-options path) plus the ordinary deep-merge control; `packages/ai` compile/schema suites stay green
- [ ] No behavior change for ordinary keys: deep-merge of record values, `undefined`-value skipping, and the single-item fast path are unchanged

body:
## Problem

`isSessionExpiredStatus` in `packages/ai/src/quota/cdp.ts` (:332) classifies a CDP fetch outcome as session-expired when `result.status === 401 || result.status === 403 || result.url.includes("auth") || result.url.includes("login")`. The URL test is a raw substring match over the whole final URL, and both callers consult it **before** their success branch — so a successful HTTP 200 quota read whose final URL merely contains `auth` or `login` anywhere (a path segment like `/api/authorizations` or `/api/login-history`, a resource named `authors`, a query parameter) is reported as `session-expired` and the good data is discarded, with a message telling the user to re-login to a session that is not expired.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `e61c8e6891`)

Sites:

- `packages/ai/src/quota/cdp.ts:332` — the substring test; the helper's doc says only "Whether an HTTP outcome from a console read is the session-expired class"
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/meta.ts:406` — `if (quotaResult && isSessionExpiredStatus(quotaResult))` → `session-expired` failure, checked **before** the `quotaResult.status === 200` parse branch (~:412)
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/mistral.ts:165` — same check before the `result.status !== 200` http-error branch (~:171); a 200 with an `auth`-bearing URL returns `session-expired` ("Mistral console session expired — sign in to admin.mistral.ai again")

Probe `probe-creator.test.ts`, laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-2035` @ `e61c8e6891`, `packages/ai` — direct calls to the exported helper:

- `{status: 200, url: "https://admin.mistral.ai/api/authorizations"}` → `true` (misclassified)
- `{status: 200, url: "https://dev.meta.ai/api/login-history"}` → `true` (misclassified)
- `{status: 200, url: "https://console.example.com/authors/42"}` → `true` (misclassified)
- Controls behave: 401 and 403 → `true`; 200 at `…/api/portal/teams/t1/subscription-quota` → `false`; 500 at a plain URL → `false`; 200 redirected to `…/login?next=/billing` → `true` (the intended redirect-detection case)

No test pins this helper at all: `grep isSessionExpiredStatus packages/ai/test/` returns no hits.

## Why it matters

The failure mode is a false "session expired — re-login" on a healthy session: the quota read's data is thrown away and the user is sent to re-authenticate, which cannot fix anything because nothing expired. Substring URL heuristics drift as providers rename endpoints — an API path gaining an `auth`-named resource (authorizations, auth-tokens, login-history are all plausible console API names) silently flips that provider's quota producer into permanent session-expired. The redirect-to-login detection the URL test exists for is real (a bounced fetch lands on a 200 login page), so the fix is scoping the test, not deleting it — a triage call: e.g. only apply the URL test when the status is not a success, or match path segments (`/login`, `/auth/` boundaries) instead of raw substrings, and pin whichever semantics is chosen.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A 200 outcome is never classified `session-expired` solely because its URL contains `auth`/`login` substrings in a path segment, resource name, or query value — or triage records on this issue why a 200 must remain classifiable and scopes the match (segment-boundary) so `/api/authorizations`, `/api/login-history`, and `/authors/…` no longer match.
- [ ] The intended detections still classify as expired: 401, 403, and a landed-on login/auth page URL (redirect case), each pinned by a test.
- [ ] New unit tests for `isSessionExpiredStatus` cover the probe cases above (200 misclassifications + controls); Meta and Mistral quota suites stay green.
- [ ] No change to the `cdp-unavailable` classification or to per-path result shapes.

body:
## Problem

`cdpPageFetch` in `packages/ai/src/quota/cdp.ts` deliberately splits page-side JavaScript failures from transport failures: when the in-page fetch expression throws, `evaluate()` raises `page eval exception: …` and the `cdpPageFetch` catch rethrows it **unchanged** instead of wrapping it as `cdp-unavailable:` — the comment at the catch states the contract ("Page-eval exceptions keep their own class"). Callers classify on that split (e.g. Mistral's CDP branch maps thrown errors by class). **No committed test exercises the passthrough.** `packages/ai/test/cdp.test.ts` contains zero occurrences of `exceptionDetails` (grep-verified); its eight cases cover request timeout, close-mid-request, reply, stalled handshake (connect + page-fetch levels), resolver-derived paths, control paths, and the wedged-evaluate → `cdp-unavailable` path — every classification except the page-eval one.

A refactor that drops the prefix check in the catch (or the `exceptionDetails` check in `evaluate()`) would silently reclassify every page-side failure as `cdp-unavailable`, and the full suite would stay green.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `e61c8e6891`)

Sites, `packages/ai/src/quota/cdp.ts`:

- `evaluate()` (~:194-202) — `if (result.exceptionDetails) throw new Error("page eval exception: …")`
- `cdpPageFetch` catch (~:306-315) — `if (error.message.startsWith("page eval exception")) throw error`, otherwise wraps as `cdp-unavailable: CDP page fetch failed: …`; the `finally` still closes the client and any page this call created

Tests: `grep -c exceptionDetails packages/ai/test/cdp.test.ts` → 0. Existing suite: 8 pass on current main.

Probe `probe-creator.test.ts`, laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-2035` @ `e61c8e6891`, `packages/ai` (2 pass; existing `cdp.test.ts` 8 pass) — the passthrough **holds today**, so this is purely a missing pin:

- Fake CDP whose fetch evaluate replies with `exceptionDetails` → `cdpPageFetch` rejects with `page eval exception: {"text":"Error: boom in page",…}`, the message does **not** contain `cdp-unavailable`, and the `finally` cleanup still closes the created page (`closedPageIds == ["page-1"]`)

First recorded as a REVIEW-FINDING by pr-diff-review 2026-11-08 (from PR #1846, in the opencode backlog file); independently re-verified this run against current main with the probe above. The same finding's second half — post-connect `ws.onerror` settlement in `connectWs` — is likewise untested by direct code read (the close-mid-request case settles via `onclose`); triage may pin it too if a fake can trigger a post-open error event, but the eval-exception pin stands alone.

## Why it matters

The CDP quota producers (Meta portal, Mistral console) run inside the user's signed-in browser pages; page-side JS failures (a provider changing its page, an extension interfering, a CSP change) are a different operational signal from a dead browser — one says "the read logic broke", the other "the browser is unreachable". The classification split was written deliberately in the #1803/#1895 hardening series, whose other branches all got tests. Unpinned deliberate branches are the ones refactors lose.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new test in `packages/ai/test/cdp.test.ts` (fake-CDP `exceptionDetails` reply, following the existing fake's pattern) pins: `cdpPageFetch` rejects with the `page eval exception` prefix and the message is not wrapped as `cdp-unavailable`.
- [ ] The same test (or a sibling) pins that the `finally` cleanup still runs on this path — the page the call created is closed.
- [ ] Existing cdp tests stay green (8 tests); no change to the classification behavior, error message shapes, or caller handling.

body:
## Problem

`reportShadowedKeyring` in `packages/ai/src/providers/vibe-auth.ts` carries an explicit never-break-resolution guarantee — its doc comment (:162-166) states "Probe or sink failures never break resolution: observability must not become an auth outage", implemented by two separate swallow branches: a throwing `keyringLookup` abandons the probe (`:175-183`, catch → return) and a throwing `onShadowDiagnostic` sink is swallowed (`:184-187`, try/catch). **No committed test exercises either branch.** The shadow-diagnostic describe block in `packages/ai/test/provider/vibe-auth.test.ts` (:169-230) has four cases, all with well-behaved lookups and sinks; the word `throw` does not appear anywhere in the test file.

A refactor that drops either try/catch — or hoists the probe above the resolution it must never block — would convert a keyring-daemon hiccup or a broken warning sink into a Mistral authentication outage, and the full suite would stay green.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `ae96cba53c`)

Sites, `packages/ai/src/providers/vibe-auth.ts`:

- `:162-166` — the guarantee, stated in the doc comment on `reportShadowedKeyring`
- `:175-183` — the probe loop over `[KEYRING_SERVICE, LEGACY_KEYRING_SERVICE]` inside try/catch; a throw returns silently
- `:184-187` — the sink invocation inside its own try/catch
- `:198` / `:209` — the probe is awaited on both non-keyring win paths (`environment`, `dotenv-file`) before the winning key is returned, so an unswallowed throw would reject `resolveApiKey` itself

Tests: `packages/ai/test/provider/vibe-auth.test.ts` contains zero occurrences of `throw` (grep-verified); the shadow-diagnostic cases at :176-230 cover env-win, dotenv-win, keyring-win (no diagnostic), and no-entry (no diagnostic) only.

Probe `probe2-creator.test.ts`, laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-1335` @ `ae96cba53c`, `packages/ai` (5 pass; existing `vibe-auth.test.ts` 19 pass) — the guarantee **holds today** in every shape, so this is purely a missing pin:

- Throwing `keyringLookup` → `resolveApiKey` still resolves the environment key; no diagnostic emitted
- Throwing `onShadowDiagnostic` sink (with a real shadow present) → still resolves the environment key
- Throwing `keyringLookup` on the dotenv-file path → still resolves the file key
- Lookup throwing on the first (primary) service abandons the whole probe: the legacy service is never queried and no diagnostic fires — a semantic worth pinning deliberately, since a per-service catch would change it
- Control: non-throwing legacy-shadow case emits exactly one diagnostic

First recorded as a REVIEW-FINDING by pr-diff-review 2026-11-08 (from PR #1854, in the opencode backlog file); independently re-verified this run against current main with the probe above.

## Why it matters

This probe runs on the credential-resolution path for the Mistral vibe provider, in front of a real OS keyring (secret-tool) whose daemon can be absent, locked, or slow in exactly the headless/CI environments where a silent auth break is hardest to diagnose. The guarantee was written deliberately (#1809) after the shadow-diagnostic was added; unpinned deliberate guarantees are the ones refactors lose. The sibling guarantee style in this area — claude-code-auth's write/refresh failure handling — is heavily tested; this one is not.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/vibe-auth.test.ts` pin: a throwing `keyringLookup` still resolves the winning key on both the environment and dotenv-file paths, with no diagnostic emitted.
- [ ] A throwing `onShadowDiagnostic` sink still resolves the winning key (diagnostic attempted, failure swallowed).
- [ ] The first-service-throw semantics are pinned as implemented (whole probe abandoned, legacy service not queried) — or triage changes the implementation to a per-service catch and pins that instead, recording the decision on this issue.
- [ ] Existing vibe-auth tests stay green (19 tests); no change to the resolution order, the diagnostic payload, or the probed services.

title: fix(ai): claude-code sign-in callback accepts a code-only paste — the OAuth state check is skipped when the paste has no '#', and the sign-in's own state is substituted in the exchange

body:
## Problem

The claude-code provider's in-product OAuth sign-in callback (`beginClaudeCodeSignIn` in `packages/ai/src/providers/claude-code-auth.ts`) validates the pasted `code#state` value's state **only when the paste contains a `#`**. A paste of the authorization code alone — no separator, no state — skips the state check entirely and is exchanged, with the sign-in's **own** state substituted into the token-exchange body. The state parameter therefore does not bind the paste to this sign-in attempt whenever the separator is absent, which is exactly the case the check exists for.

The behavior is also internally inconsistent: a paste with a trailing separator and an empty state (`code#`) **is** rejected as a state mismatch, while the same paste with the separator removed (`code`) is accepted.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `ae96cba53c`)

Sites, `packages/ai/src/providers/claude-code-auth.ts`:

- `:376-377` — `separator = trimmed.indexOf("#")`; `pastedState = separator === -1 ? undefined : trimmed.slice(separator + 1).trim()`
- `:382-383` — the mismatch check is `if (pastedState !== undefined && pastedState !== state) throw …` — an absent state can never mismatch
- `:394` — the exchange body sends `state: pastedState ?? state`, substituting this sign-in's own state for the missing one
- `:86` / `SIGN_IN_INSTRUCTIONS` and the callback doc at `:349` both require pasting "the full code#state value"

Probe `probe-creator.test.ts`, laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-1335` @ `ae96cba53c`, `packages/ai` (stubbed fetch/filesystem, deterministic randomness; 4 pass, existing `claude-code-auth.test.ts` 42 pass):

- `callback("auth-code-1")` → **succeeds**: one token-exchange call, credential persisted and returned, and the exchange body's `state` equals the sign-in's own state taken from its authorize URL
- `callback("auth-code-1#wrong-state")` → rejects "state mismatch", zero exchange calls (control)
- `callback("auth-code-1#")` → rejects "state mismatch", zero exchange calls (contrast: empty state rejected, absent state accepted)
- `callback("auth-code-1#<correct state>")` → succeeds, one exchange call (control)

Existing tests (`packages/ai/test/provider/claude-code-auth.test.ts:365-372`) pin the empty paste and the wrong-state paste, but no test covers a code-only paste.

First recorded as a REVIEW-FINDING by pr-diff-review 2026-11-08 (from PR #1861, in the opencode backlog file); independently re-verified this run against current main with the probe above — the code is unchanged since that review.

## Why it matters

OAuth `state` is the CSRF/login-confusion binding between the authorize step and the callback: it proves the code being exchanged was issued for *this* sign-in attempt on *this* machine. PKCE still binds the code to the verifier held here, which bounds the impact (this is defense-in-depth, not a known exploitable hole) — but a check that silently evaporates when its separator is missing is worse than no check: the instructions, the error text, and the mismatch branch all tell the user and future maintainers that the full `code#state` is required and verified. A code obtained for a different sign-in attempt (or a different client flow using the same hosted callback page) can be pasted here without the state ever being compared, and nothing logs or errors.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A paste with no `#` separator (code only) fails with the named `ClaudeCodeSignInError` (malformed / missing-state wording) and makes **no** token-exchange call — the same disposition as a state mismatch — OR triage records an explicit decision that code-only pastes are deliberately accepted, in which case that acceptance is pinned by a test and the instructions/error text stop claiming the state is verified.
- [ ] The exchange body never substitutes a state the user did not paste: it sends the pasted state after it has been verified equal to the sign-in's state.
- [ ] New tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/claude-code-auth.test.ts` pin the code-only paste (and keep the `code#` empty-state, wrong-state, and correct-state cases green).
- [ ] No change to the PKCE flow, the authorize URL constants, the single-use inflight memo behavior (#1868), or credential persistence.

## Problem

`resolveTursoLimits` in `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/turso.ts` (added by PR #2153, merged 2026-11-08, to stop a Scaler org being divided by Starter limits) matches the subscription's plan name **exactly after lowercasing only** — no trimming — in both of its lookup paths, and `tursoWindows` takes the plan label verbatim. Any surrounding whitespace in either string silently defeats the fix and the org regresses to Starter denominators, reproducing the exact false over-limit figures PR #2153 was written to eliminate.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `7814932592`)

Probe `probe-creator.test.ts` + `probe2.test.ts`, laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-1435` @ `7814932592`, `packages/ai`:

- `resolveTursoLimits("Scaler", null).rowsRead` → `100000000000` (scaler static fallback — control, correct)
- `resolveTursoLimits(" scaler ", null).rowsRead` → `500000000` (Starter); `"scaler "` → `500000000`
- `tursoWindows(usage, { plan: " scaler " })` with `rows_read: 1_180_000_000` → rows-read `usedPercent` **236** — the identical false figure from the code#5468 incident (1.18B / 500M); the clean `"scaler"` label gives `1.18`.
- Dynamic path: `resolveTursoLimits("scaler ", plansDoc)` where the plans doc carries a `Scaler` entry with `rowsRead: 42_000_000_000` → `500000000` (neither the dynamic entry nor the static scaler row matches). Plans-side whitespace (`name: "Scaler "`, label `"scaler"`) → the dynamic 42B value is silently missed and only the static fallback masks it.
- A whitespace-only label `" "` is accepted as a plan label: `tursoWindows` at `turso.ts:157` hand-rolls `typeof planRaw === "string" && planRaw !== ""` instead of the shared `asNonEmptyString` helper (`packages/ai/src/quota/utils.ts`, which trims), so the published `planLabel` can be `" "`.

Sites:

- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/turso.ts:124` — static fallback lookup `TURSO_PLAN_LIMITS[planLabel.toLowerCase()]`, no trim
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/turso.ts:129-132` — dynamic match `plan.name.toLowerCase() !== wanted`, neither side trimmed
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/turso.ts:157` — plan label taken verbatim from `sub.plan ?? sub.name`

Contrast: sibling providers normalize plan labels through the shared trimmer — `claude.ts:74` `asNonEmptyString(oauth?.subscriptionType)`, `meta.ts:280` `asNonEmptyString(body.subs_tier_name)`. Turso is the outlier, and it is the one provider whose label is a lookup key rather than display text.

## Why it matters

PR #2153's stated guarantee is that "a non-Starter org can never silently regress to Starter denominators". The guarantee currently rests on the subscription and /plans endpoints returning byte-clean plan names forever. A padded name (proxy/gateway re-serialization, an API-side display-name change like `Scaler `, a hand-edited fixture) re-opens the 2026-11-08 incident shape — rows-read ~235%, storage ~213% false over-limit on a healthy org — with no error anywhere: the fallback is silent by design.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Plan-label matching in `resolveTursoLimits` is whitespace-insensitive on both sides: the subscription label and each plans-doc `name` are trimmed (and lowercased) before the static-table lookup and the dynamic match.
- [ ] `tursoWindows` derives its plan label via the shared `asNonEmptyString` (or equivalent trim), so a whitespace-only plan publishes no `planLabel` and resolves as unknown-plan.
- [ ] New tests in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pin: padded subscription label resolves Scaler limits statically and dynamically; padded plans-doc name still matches dynamically; whitespace-only label behaves as no label. Existing turso tests (exact-match dynamic, static fallback, starter/unknown) stay green.
- [ ] No change to the limit values, the per-field quota fallback, or the publish-over-100% disposition (code#6227).

title: fix(ai): sanitizeSurrogates silently drops entries when sanitized keys collide — distinct lone-surrogate keys collapse into one U+FFFD key

body:
## Summary

`sanitizeSurrogates` (`packages/ai/src/utils/sanitize.ts:10-12`) rebuilds every record by mapping each key through `toWellFormed()` and collecting the results with `Object.fromEntries`. `toWellFormed()` is many-to-one — every lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD — so two distinct keys that differ only in their lone surrogates (or a lone-surrogate key next to an existing U+FFFD key) collapse into one entry, and the earlier entries are silently dropped from the payload.

This sanitizer runs on outbound LLM/media request payloads, so the drop happens after the request was built and before it reaches the provider, with no error.

## Evidence

Probe `probe-ai.test.ts` (laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-1235` @ main `391e43eb36`, `packages/ai/`, against the real module):

- Input record with three own keys — `"\uD800a"` → 1, `"\uDC00a"` → 2, `"\uFFFDa"` → 3: `sanitizeSurrogates` returns a record with **1 key** (`"\uFFFDa"` → 3). Values 1 and 2 are gone.
- Control clean: a well-formed record (`{alpha: 1, beta: 2}`) round-trips with both keys and values intact.

Call sites: `packages/ai/src/route/client.ts:572` (the LLM request is rebuilt from the sanitized record) and `packages/ai/src/route/media.ts:371`; also `packages/ai/src/experimental/evaluation-client.ts:36`. Keys in these payloads include tool names, tool-argument property names, and provider option keys — surfaces where model- or provider-supplied strings with lone surrogates (from `\uD800`-style JSON escapes) are exactly the input this sanitizer exists to handle.

## Why it matters

The sanitizer's whole job is to make an ill-formed payload safe to send; silently deleting entries makes it unsafe in a different way — a tool's argument or a request option vanishes, and the resulting provider error (or subtly wrong call) names nothing about the real cause. It is the same loss class as #2110 (quota maps dropping a model named `__proto__`, fixed today in PR #2141), in a different module with a different mechanism: there, plain-object assignment swallowed one special key; here, a many-to-one key mapping plus `fromEntries` swallows any colliding keys.

## Acceptance criteria

- When sanitized keys would collide, no entry is silently lost: the disposition (collision-safe renaming, first-wins with a recorded signal, or another stated rule) is chosen in triage and pinned by a test using the `"\uD800a"` / `"\uDC00a"` / `"\uFFFDa"` triple above.
- Well-formed records round-trip unchanged (keys, values, order-insensitive equality), and nested records/arrays behave the same as at the top level — pinned by tests.
- The existing surrogate-value behavior is unchanged: string values and keys are still made well-formed (`toWellFormed` semantics for the surviving key).
- The audit note from triage states whether sibling rebuilds in the same payloads (e.g. other `fromEntries`/`Object.entries` maps on request shapes) share the hazard.

## Notes

- Filed by the new-issue-creator run; not self-solved: the collision disposition touches the outbound request contract, so it is a triage call, not a silent rename chosen by the filer.
- Dedup checked: no open or closed issue covers `sanitizeSurrogates`, key collisions after `toWellFormed`, or entry loss in the route payload sanitizer (title/keyword search over open + closed, 2026-11-08). #2110 is the quota-map sibling, cross-linked for the shared loss class only.

body:
## Summary

The AI media sniffer's MPEG frame-sync test (`packages/ai/src/utils/media-type.ts:52-53`) accepts any content whose first two bytes are `0xFF` followed by a byte with the top three bits set. A UTF-16LE text file begins with exactly that: its BOM is `FF FE`. The sniffer therefore publishes a UTF-16LE text file as `audio/mpeg`, and `fileMediaType` (line 89) lets that sniffed result override the file's own extension — a `notes.txt` saved as UTF-16LE comes back as audio.

## Evidence

Probe `probe-ai.test.ts` (laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-1235` @ main `391e43eb36`, `packages/ai/`, against the real module):

- UTF-16LE bytes for "Hello" (`FF FE 48 00 65 00 6C 00 6C 00 6F 00`): `detectMediaType` → `audio/mpeg`; `fileMediaType(bytes, "notes.txt")` → `audio/mpeg` (the `.txt` extension never gets a say).
- Controls clean: UTF-16BE ("Hello", `FE FF` BOM) → `undefined` (no false claim); a real MP3 frame header (`FF FB 90 64`) → `audio/mpeg`; the pinned frame-sync cases in `packages/ai/test/media.test.ts` (FF FB / FF F3 → mpeg, FF F1 → aac) are the behavior to preserve.

Site: `media-type.ts:53` — `bytes[0] === 0xff && (bytes[1] & 0xe0) === 0xe0`, with the layer bits (`bytes[1] & 0x06`) choosing AAC vs MPEG. `FE` passes: sync bits set, layer bits `11` ≠ `00`, so MPEG. Nothing downstream re-checks the claim: consumers are `Media.from`/`Media.bytes` (`packages/ai/src/media.ts:140`, `:323`, `:361`), the meta-responses protocol (`packages/ai/src/protocols/meta-responses.ts:130`), and `promise.ts:116` — the mislabelled type is what gets published to the provider.

## Why it matters

UTF-16LE is the default encoding of Windows PowerShell redirection and a common Notepad save format — precisely the text files a user on Windows might hand to a media-aware route. The content is then shipped to a provider as an audio file: transcription/generation routes reject it or, worse, process it as audio, and the real cause (a two-byte BOM) is invisible from the error. A two-byte sync test with no further header validation will keep collecting false positives from any format that starts `FF Ex`–`FF Fx`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A UTF-16LE (and UTF-16BE) text file is not detected as `audio/mpeg`/`audio/aac` — pinned by tests using BOM-led text bytes, including the `fileMediaType(bytes, "notes.txt")` path.
- The pinned true positives stay green: ID3-tagged MP3, raw frame-sync MP3 (`FF FB`, `FF F3`) and AAC ADTS (`FF F1`) cases in `packages/ai/test/media.test.ts`.
- The disposition (BOM exclusion vs fuller MPEG header validation — e.g. reserved bitrate/sampling values — vs extension precedence for known text types) is chosen in triage and stated on the issue.
- No other detector in the same file changes behavior for its pinned cases.

## Notes

- Filed by the new-issue-creator run; not self-solved: the right strengthening of a deliberately minimal frame-sync test is a triage call (it trades off headerless raw-audio detection the test was written for).
- Dedup checked: no open or closed issue covers the frame-sync test, UTF-16 BOMs, or `fileMediaType` extension precedence (title/keyword search over open + closed, 2026-11-08). #2127 (closed today) was the same file's `ftyp` branch — a different test, a different mechanism.

body:
## Summary

Core `Mime.detect` (`packages/core/src/mime.ts`) has no ISO-BMFF brand dispatch: its only `ftyp` handling (lines 12–15) recognizes the `avif`/`avis` major brands, and every other `ftyp` container falls through to the text/binary fallback. The AI package's sniffer got exactly this fix in #2127 (PR #2144, merged today: brand table `FTYP_BRANDS` in `packages/ai/src/utils/media-type.ts`); the core detector — the one prompt attachments and the read tool actually use — still has the pre-fix shape.

## Evidence

Probe `probe-core.test.ts` (laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-1235` @ main `391e43eb36`, `packages/core/`, against the real module), each input a 16-byte `ftyp` box (size + `ftyp` + major brand):

- brand `heic` → `application/octet-stream` (a HEIC photo is not recognized as an image at all)
- brand `M4A ` → `application/octet-stream` (an M4A audio file is not recognized as audio)
- brand `avif` → `image/avif` (the one brand family that is recognized)

Consumers and consequences:

- `packages/core/src/session/prompt.ts:116` — a HEIC photo attached to a prompt is published with mime `application/octet-stream`, so the provider receives an opaque binary file instead of an image (or rejects it), with no error pointing at the real cause.
- `packages/core/src/tool/read-filesystem.ts:21` — `MEDIA_MIMES` is `{image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp, application/pdf}`: even the formats core `detect` does recognize beyond that set (`image/avif`, `image/bmp`) are not ingestible as media by the read tool, so an AVIF file is handled as a binary/text read instead. Detector and ingest set disagree.

## Why it matters

HEIC is the default photo format on iPhones; M4A is a common voice-memo format. A user attaching either to a session in the core app gets a silently useless attachment. The fork already paid for this exact design once today — the AI sniffer's brand table (#2127 / PR #2144) is the model — the core detector just never received the same treatment, and its read-tool ingest set was never reconciled with what it can detect.

## Acceptance criteria

- `Mime.detect` dispatches on the `ftyp` major brand at least for the image/audio brands the AI sniffer now claims (`heic`/`heix` → `image/heic`, `mif1`/`msf1` → `image/heif`, `avif`/`avis` → `image/avif`, `M4A `/`M4B ` → `audio/mp4`), with tests pinning each brand and an unknown-brand control falling through to the existing fallback.
- The read tool's `MEDIA_MIMES` and the prompt path's handling are reconciled with the enlarged detection set in the same change (every newly detected media type is either ingestible or the gap is explicitly dispositioned on the issue).
- Unknown/other `ftyp` brands keep today's behavior unless triage dispositions them.
- Existing core suites that touch attachments stay green.

## Notes

- Filed by the new-issue-creator run; not self-solved: how much of the AI brand table to mirror, and whether the read tool should ingest HEIC/AVIF as media, are triage calls. Sibling of #2127 (the AI package's sniffer, closed via PR #2144) — same pattern, different package, different consumers; cross-linked rather than reopened because #2127's fix is merged and scoped to `packages/ai`.
- Dedup checked: no open or closed issue covers core `Mime.detect` `ftyp` handling, HEIC/HEIF/M4A detection in core, or `MEDIA_MIMES` reconciliation (title/keyword search over open + closed, 2026-11-08).

body:
## Summary

Core `Mime.detect` (`packages/core/src/mime.ts`) checks two image signatures that are plain ASCII prefixes before it ever reaches its text check, so a plain-text file whose first bytes spell those letters is published as an image:

- Line 7: any content starting with the two bytes `BM` returns `image/bmp`.
- Line 6: any content starting with the four bytes `GIF8` returns `image/gif`.

The `isText` fallback (line 16) is only reached when no signature matches, so it never gets to arbitrate these.

## Evidence

Probe `probe-core.test.ts` (laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-1235` @ main `391e43eb36`, `packages/core/`, against the real module):

- `Mime.detect("BM25 is a ranking function used by search engines.\n")` → `image/bmp`
- `Mime.detect("GIF89a is the format this document describes.\n")` → `image/gif`
- Controls clean: a real BMP header (with plausible size/DIB fields) → `image/bmp`; plain text not starting with those letters → `text/plain`; empty input → `text/plain`.

Consumers and consequences:

- `packages/core/src/session/prompt.ts:116` — attachment mime is `resolved.mime ?? Mime.detect(resolved.bytes)`; `:138` `normalizeImageAttachment` routes any `image/*` mime into the photon image pipeline, whose decode of a text file fails with `DecodeError`, surfaced as an `AttachmentError` — attaching a text file that starts with `BM` or `GIF8` fails the whole prompt.
- `packages/core/src/tool/read-filesystem.ts:137-138` — the read tool ingests whatever `Mime.detect` returns when it is in `MEDIA_MIMES` (`:21`, which includes `image/gif`): a text file starting with `GIF8` is returned as base64 `image/gif` media instead of readable text. (`image/bmp` is not in `MEDIA_MIMES`, so the two signatures fail differently — one more sign the signature set and the ingest set were never reconciled.)

There is no test file for `packages/core/src/mime.ts` at all.

## Why it matters

"BM" and "GIF8" are plausible starts of real text: a note about BM25 ranking, documentation about the GIF89a format, a changelog, a spec. Today the first breaks the user's prompt outright with an image decode error; the second silently feeds the model a base64 blob labelled as a GIF instead of the document's text. Content sniffing that can be triggered by ordinary prose needs signatures stronger than the prose itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- A plain-text file starting with `BM` or `GIF8` (but not a structurally valid BMP/GIF) is detected as `text/plain` — pinned by new tests for `packages/core/src/mime.ts`.
- A structurally real BMP (signature plus plausible header fields, e.g. the reserved/size/DIB fields a real encoder writes) and a real GIF (full `GIF87a`/`GIF89a` header) are still detected as `image/bmp` / `image/gif` — pinned by tests with realistic headers, not just the prefix bytes.
- The disposition for each weak signature (strengthen the check vs drop the format from `detect`) is chosen in triage and stated on the issue; whichever is chosen, the read tool and the prompt-attachment path behave the same for the same bytes.
- Existing core suites that touch attachments stay green (`packages/core` session-prompt / read-filesystem tests).

## Notes

- Filed by the new-issue-creator run; not self-solved: the strengthen-vs-drop disposition per signature, and the interplay with the read tool's `MEDIA_MIMES` set, is a triage call.
- Dedup checked: no open or closed issue covers core `Mime.detect`, BMP/GIF sniffing, or text-as-image misdetection (title/keyword search over open + closed, 2026-11-08). The AI package's separate sniffer is #2127's subject (closed, PR #2144) — this is the core package's own detector, with different consumers.

Agent: pr-diff-review-b

## Finding

Merged PR #1843 added a branch to the antigravity GOCSPX chunked scan that recovers a secret run when the stable region ends in the middle of the literal `GOCSPX-` prefix itself — and that branch has no committed test. Every committed boundary test starts the run at least 10 characters inside the stable region, so the literal is always whole inside it; no test splits the literal (fewer than 7 run characters inside).

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1843 (MERGED, merge 24a68f829ba2d1d8b21c8e60f591c8ba9637b9e7, commit 364515b02c534be4802c0fd40e2798ecc7594939), for #1822. PR link: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/1843
- The branch, in `packages/ai/src/providers/antigravity-auth.ts` (diff hunk @@ -187,21 +187,53, the `if (!flush && pending < 0)` block): `for (let k = Math.min(6, stable.length); k >= 1; k--) { if (stable.endsWith("GOCSPX-".slice(0, k))) … }` — it fires only when the stable region's tail is a proper prefix of `GOCSPX-` (k from 6 down to 1).
- The PR body says the case was verified by an external "probe replication … 11/11" — that probe is not in the repo.
- Verified on current main c54d11129ba4e44c30cfd87c16a8a188f0876361: `packages/ai/test/provider/antigravity-auth.test.ts`, describe `Antigravity GOCSPX stable-boundary recovery (#1822)` (line 253) has exactly four cases, all built with `boundaryRun(inside, …)` at inside = 20, 10, 20, plus a chunk-boundary control at 20. None uses inside < 7, and a grep of the test file finds no literal-split construction.
- Dedupe (2026-11-08): issue search for the stable-boundary scan returns only the parent #1822 (closed, the defect this PR fixed); no issue covers the missing test.

## Why it matters

#1822 exists because a truncated GOCSPX prefix was actually collected and sent as a client-secret candidate, failing refresh with invalid_client. The literal-split case is the thinnest slice of the same guarantee ("never truncated"): if the suffix-matching loop regresses (e.g. an off-by-one in the k range), a run starting 1–6 characters inside the stable region is collected truncated again, and no committed test would catch it.

## Acceptance criteria

- The (#1822) suite gains a case with the run starting fewer than 7 characters inside the stable region (e.g. `boundaryRun(3, …)`), asserting exactly one candidate attempt carrying the whole run, like the existing `expectWholeOnly` cases.
- Ideally boundary values k = 1 and k = 6 are both covered (run starting 1 and 6 characters inside).
- Existing four boundary cases keep passing unchanged.

<!-- agent-note:v1
Agent: pr-diff-review-b
state: filed
-->

## Finding

`writeCredential` in the claude-code provider writes the full OAuth credential blob to a temp file and renames it into place, but if the rename fails the credential-bearing temp file is never removed — it stays in the user's claude config directory indefinitely. The helper's own contract ("A failure leaves the original file untouched") is kept for the target file, but nothing cleans up the temp copy, which contains the access token AND the refresh token.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1861 (MERGED, merge ef4a9d21d87105dd1e233b666719168deabb7fe3, commit 32c52e7c67f3a9a4c270d14ac53411631b67aaa1) introduced `writeCredential` for the in-provider OAuth sign-in (#1852). PR link: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/1861
- Verified on current main c54d11129ba4e44c30cfd87c16a8a188f0876361 (read twice, parent + first-pass reviewer independently), `packages/ai/src/providers/claude-code-auth.ts:231-251`:
  - `:248` `const temp = \`${path}.tmp-${process.pid}-${suffix}\``
  - `:249` `await writeFile(temp, contents)` — contents is the serialized credentials file including `claudeAiOauth.accessToken` and `refreshToken` (buildCredentialsFileContents, :195-220)
  - `:250` `await renameFile(temp, path)` — no try/finally, no cleanup on throw.
  - A grep of the whole file on main finds no `unlink`, `rm(`, or remove call anywhere.
- The blast radius grew after #1861: the same helper is now THE write path for the refresh write-back (#1818, renewed by merged PR #2126), so a rename failure during a routine token refresh leaks the same temp file — with the freshly rotated refresh token in it.
- Existing tests do not cover it: `packages/ai/test/provider/claude-code-auth.test.ts` has a rename-throws test for the refresh path ("a write failure discards the rotated tokens, leaves the file byte-identical") but it asserts only the target file's contents; the in-memory harness's temp entry is never asserted absent. The sign-in path's write-failure test mocks `writeFile` itself throwing, so no temp file exists in that mock at all.
- Dedupe (2026-11-08): issue searches for writeCredential / credentials temp / rename return only #1818 and #1852 (the parent features, both closed); no issue covers temp-file cleanup.

## Why it matters

The temp file is mode 0600, so this is not a world-readable leak — but a long-lived plaintext copy of a refresh token outside the canonical credentials file defeats the rotation story: Anthropic rotates the refresh token on every exchange (#1818), yet a stale temp copy from a failed rename keeps an older (or the newest, if the rename of the newest write failed) token on disk in a file nothing ever reads, rotates, or deletes, in a directory other tooling syncs and backs up. Rename failures are exactly the cross-device/overlay-filesystem cases this atomic-write pattern is used in.

## Acceptance criteria

- `writeCredential` removes the temp file when `renameFile` (or any step after the temp write) throws — e.g. try/finally with a best-effort unlink that never masks the original error.
- The original error still propagates and the target file remains untouched on failure (existing contract).
- A test drives `renameFile` throwing after a successful temp write and asserts no temp entry remains (both the sign-in write and the refresh write-back path share the helper, so one helper-level test suffices).
- Success path unchanged: temp+rename, 0600, unrelated fields preserved (existing tests keep passing).

body:
## Summary

`Patch.derive` (the `apply_patch` update engine) misplaces a pure-addition update chunk that carries a `@@` change context: the context is looked up and validated, but its position is then discarded and the added lines are appended at end-of-file instead of at the anchored location.

## Evidence

Site: `packages/util/src/patch.ts`, `computeReplacements` (lines 311–322):

- Lines 314–318: when `chunk.changeContext` is set, the context is sought in the file and `lineIndex = context + 1` — a missing context throws (`Failed to find context '<ctx>' in <path>`), so the anchor is treated as load-bearing.
- Lines 320–321: the pure-addition branch (`chunk.oldLines.length === 0`) then ignores `lineIndex` entirely and pushes the replacement at `[lines.length, 0, chunk.newLines]` — end-of-file, unconditionally.

Probe (laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-1035` @ `84c5c14aa4`, `packages/core/test/probe-patch.test.ts`, 6 pass):

- Parse of `*** Update File: f.txt` + `@@ fn a` + `+inserted` yields one chunk `{ oldLines: [], newLines: ["inserted"], changeContext: "fn a" }`.
- `Patch.derive` of that chunk (directly and via the parsed patch) on `"fn a\nx\nfn b\ny\n"` returns `"fn a\nx\nfn b\ny\ninserted\n"` — appended after `y`, not after the `fn a` anchor.
- The same chunk anchored at `fn b` returns the identical EOF result — the two anchors are indistinguishable in the output.
- A pure-addition chunk with a nonexistent context **does** throw `Failed to find context 'nope' in f.txt` — the context is validated, then thrown away for placement.
- Controls clean: a context-free pure-addition chunk appends at EOF (the behavior pinned by `packages/core/test/patch.test.ts:245`, "appends a pure-addition chunk to a nonempty file"), and an anchored replacement chunk (`changeContext: "fn b"`) edits the correct occurrence. Existing suite baseline: `bun test test/patch.test.ts` 46 pass / 0 fail.

Consumers of `Patch.derive`: the apply-patch tool (`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/patch.ts:169`) and the ACP permission rebuild path (`packages/cli/src/acp/permission.ts:110` and `:159`).

## Why it matters

The `@@` header is how a patch author says *where* an insertion belongs. A chunk consisting of only `+` lines under a context header is the natural way to insert lines at a specific place in a file. Today such an insertion silently lands at the end of the file: the patch "succeeds", the file content is wrong in a way no error surfaces, and the misplaced lines can break the file (e.g. inserted code after a closing brace / export block) or quietly change its meaning. The context validation (throwing on a missing anchor) makes the silent misplacement worse — the caller is told the anchor matters, then it is ignored.

## Acceptance criteria

- A pure-addition chunk with a `changeContext` inserts its lines at the anchored position (immediately after the located context line, consistent with how anchored replacement chunks start searching at `context + 1`), or the chunk shape is explicitly rejected at parse/derive time with a clear error — one disposition, chosen in triage and pinned by tests either way.
- A test pins the anchored pure-addition case for at least two different anchors in the same file, with distinguishable results.
- The pinned context-free behavior is unchanged: a pure-addition chunk with no context still appends at end-of-file (`patch.test.ts:245` and the equal-offset insertion-order tests stay green).
- A missing context on a pure-addition chunk still fails loudly.
- Interplay with `*** End of File` pure-addition chunks and with multiple chunks (ordering / equal-offset insertion order) is considered and, where it changes, pinned by a test.
- Full `packages/core/test/patch.test.ts` suite passes.

## Notes

- Filed by the new-issue-creator run; not self-solved: the insert-at-anchor vs reject-the-shape disposition, and its interplay with the end-of-file marker and multi-chunk ordering, is a triage call.
- Dedup checked: no open or closed issue covers `Patch.derive` placement, pure-addition chunks, or `changeContext` (title/keyword search over open + closed, 2026-11-08).

body:
## Problem

`script/github/close-issues.ts` (the repo-sweeper's daily stale-issue closer) paginates the **open**-issue list with offset pages while closing items from that same list between page fetches. Every close removes an item from the list the next `page=` request offsets into, so the following page starts a full page-worth of items later in the shifted list: one whole page of stale issues is skipped for each page closed, and the run still finishes reporting success.

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-08, main `09b9ae340f`)

- `close-issues.ts:97` — `let page = 1`; the loop at `:101` fetches one page via `fetchIssuePage` (`:52`, `per_page=100&page=${page}`, `state=open&sort=updated&direction=asc`).
- `close-issues.ts:128-134` — after scanning the page, the loop closes every stale item on it (`closeIssue`, `:64`) and only then does `page++` and fetches the next offset page from the now-shorter open list.
- `close-issues.ts:122`/`:137` — the run reports `Closed N issues total` with no indication anything was skipped.

Probe (laptop, this run): the **real** script was run as `main` against a stubbed `fetch` serving a mutable fake GitHub API (250 stale, non-exempt open issues, all older than the 60-day cutoff), via `bun --preload stub-fetch.ts script/github/close-issues.ts` in the laptop primary at `09b9ae340f`:

- Closed: issues #1–#100 and #201–#250 — **150 total**, exactly what the script reported.
- Skipped, still open at exit: issues **#101–#200** — a full page. Page 1's closes shifted them onto page 1, so the `page=2` fetch landed on #201.
- Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-08-creator-0835/stub-fetch.ts` (laptop).

Contrast in the same directory: `close-prs.ts:170` calls `fetchOpenPullRequests` to collect **all** open PRs first, and only then comments/closes — it never paginates a list it is mutating.

## Why it matters

The closer is the daily stale-issue hygiene for this repo. On any day with more than 100 stale issues, roughly every second page is silently deferred a day (the skipped items are the next-oldest, so they are re-skipped in the same pattern whenever the backlog stays above one page), and the log line claims a complete sweep. It compounds the harm of open issue #2120 (same script, different defect): the items this loop does reach are closed, while a full page of equally stale items is never even examined.

## Relationship to #2120

Distinct defect, same file: #2120 is the missing PR filter in `fetchIssuePage`/`shouldSkip`; this is offset pagination over a mutating list in `main`. Fixing one does not fix the other. Both touch `close-issues.ts` — land them sequentially (or in one PR that states both), not in parallel branches.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The closer determines the full stale set (or a page-stable equivalent, e.g. re-fetching page 1 / collecting before closing) **before** closing any issue, so closing an item can never shift an unexamined item past the scan.
- [ ] The early stop is preserved: issues are scanned in `updated`-ascending order and the scan still stops at the first fresh (non-stale) issue; exempt-author skipping (#-team/agent/OWNER/MEMBER behaviour) is unchanged.
- [ ] A regression test drives the scan/close flow (extracting it from `main` if needed) against a fake fetch with >200 stale issues across 3 pages and asserts **all** of them are closed and none is skipped; the 250-issue probe scenario above closes 250/250.
- [ ] The final log line remains accurate for the new flow, and existing `script/github` tests still pass.

## Suggested direction

Mirror `close-prs.ts`: first pass collects the stale numbers page by page (stopping at the first fresh issue), second pass closes them. Keep `fetchIssuePage`/`closeIssue` signatures and the bounded-body/timeout behaviour from #1344 intact.

body:
## Problem

The DeepSeek quota fetcher's balance selection is asymmetric between its positive and zero fallbacks: a positive balance in a third currency (not USD/CNY) is selected, and a zero USD or CNY balance publishes as `$0.00` / `¥0.00` — but a zero balance in a third currency is never selected, so an account whose only balance row is e.g. EUR 0 reports `ok: false` with "No quota data in response" instead of publishing a zero balance.

This is the zero-row remainder of #1800 (which added the third-currency fallback to the positive chain) and #1928 (which pinned negative-only payloads as no-data).

## Evidence

Site: `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/deepseek.ts` — the `balanceInfo` selection chain. The positive chain has three steps (USD, CNY, then any other currency); the zero chain has only two (USD, then CNY), with no third-currency step, and then falls through to `null`.

Probe (laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-0735` @ `29f21dc7dd`, `packages/ai/test/probe-deepseek.test.ts`, bun test 4 pass — probe asserts observed behavior via the provider's own `fetchQuota` harness, mirroring the `deepseek quota mapping (#1800)` describe in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts`):

| Payload `balance_infos` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `[{ currency: "EUR", total_balance: 0 }]` | `ok: false`, error "No quota data in response", no window |
| `[{ currency: "GBP", total_balance: "0" }]` | `ok: false`, error "No quota data in response", no window |
| `[{ currency: "USD", total_balance: -5 }, { currency: "EUR", total_balance: 0 }]` | `ok: false`, error "No quota data in response", no window |
| `[{ currency: "USD", total_balance: 0 }]` (control) | `ok: true`, label `$0.00` |
| `[{ currency: "CNY", total_balance: 0 }]` (control) | `ok: true`, label `¥0.00` |
| `[{ currency: "EUR", total_balance: "100" }]` (control) | `ok: true`, label `EUR 100.00` |

Existing pins that make this a divergence, not a design choice: `quota.test.ts` pins "a positive third-currency balance wins over zero USD" and "a positive third-currency balance wins over negative USD" — so a third-currency row outranks both a zero USD row and a negative row when positive, yet is invisible when it is itself zero. And the negative-only pins (#1928: negative USD/CNY alone → no-data) rely on negative reading as absent, which makes the USD −5 + EUR 0 row above equivalent to EUR 0 alone.

## Why it matters

A drained third-currency DeepSeek account flips from a truthful `EUR 0.00` credits window to a provider error ("No quota data in response"), which reads as a broken integration rather than an empty balance — the exact publish-truthfully distinction the quota figure contract (#1942) draws. It also makes the row flicker: any positive top-up publishes, returning to exactly zero errors again.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A payload whose only balance row is a zero balance in a third currency publishes `ok: true` with a `credits_balance` window labelled e.g. `EUR 0.00`.
- [ ] A zero third-currency row wins over negative USD/CNY rows (mirroring the pinned positive-over-negative precedence); negative-only payloads still return the no-data error (#1928 pins unchanged).
- [ ] Zero USD still wins over zero third-currency, and zero CNY still wins over zero third-currency (USD → CNY → other order preserved in the zero chain, mirroring the positive chain).
- [ ] New tests in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` (deepseek mapping describe) cover the three cases above; the existing deepseek and quota figure-contract tests still pass.

body:
## Problem

`detectMediaType` in `packages/ai/src/utils/media-type.ts:20` treats **any** ISO-BMFF file as video:

```ts
if (bytes.length >= 12 && ascii(bytes, 4, 8) === "ftyp") return "video/mp4"
```

It never reads the major brand at bytes 8–12. That brand is what distinguishes the containers that share the `ftyp` box:

- `M4A ` / `M4B ` — audio-only MP4 → should be `audio/mp4`
- `avif` / `avis` — AVIF image → should be `image/avif`
- `heic` / `heix` / `mif1` (HEIF) — HEIC/HEIF image → should be `image/heic` / `image/heif`
- `isom` / `mp41` / `mp42` / `avc1` / `dash` etc. — genuine video MP4 → `video/mp4`
- `3gp*` — 3GPP video → `video/3gpp`

Because sniffing wins over the file extension (`fileMediaType`, `media-type.ts:57`: `detectMediaType(bytes) ?? extensionMediaType(path)`), even a correctly named `song.m4a` or `photo.avif` file is published with the wrong media type.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `87c05e11db`)

Probe `probe-media-ftyp.ts` (laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-08-creator-media-ftyp/`, run with `bun` against the real `packages/ai/src/utils/media-type.ts` on the laptop primary at `87c05e11db`), constructing 12-byte `ftyp` headers per brand:

```
M4A audio brand       detect= video/mp4  file= video/mp4   (path song.m4a)
M4B audiobook brand   detect= video/mp4  file= video/mp4   (path book.m4b)
avif image brand      detect= video/mp4  file= video/mp4   (path photo.avif)
heic image brand      detect= video/mp4  file= video/mp4   (path photo.heic)
isom video brand      detect= video/mp4  file= video/mp4   (path clip.mp4)  ← correct
mp42 video brand      detect= video/mp4  file= video/mp4   (path clip.mp4)  ← correct
```

Note the extension table cannot rescue the audio/image cases even where it knows them: `EXTENSIONS` in the same file has no `avif`/`heic` entry, and the sniff result pre-empts the `m4a → audio/mp4` entry that does exist.

## Why it matters

The sniffed type is authoritative at every call site:

- `packages/ai/src/media.ts:140` — bytes-source assets take `detectMediaType(...)` first
- `packages/ai/src/media.ts:323` — `Media.bytes` defaults to the sniffed type
- `packages/ai/src/media.ts:361` and `packages/ai/src/promise.ts:116` — file loads via `fileMediaType`
- `packages/ai/src/protocols/meta-responses.ts:130` — the sniffed type (or octet-stream) is what is sent on the wire

So an M4A voice note / audiobook or an iPhone HEIC / AVIF photo handed to a provider is labelled `video/mp4`: audio routes can reject or mishandle it, image routes never see it as an image, and downstream `mediaTypeExtension` / kind logic inherits the wrong kind. This is the media façade's own sniffing contract — the doc comment at `media-type.ts:8-9` promises the type "of a file's contents", and for these brands it returns a type the contents are not.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `detectMediaType` dispatches on the `ftyp` major brand (bytes 8–12): at minimum `M4A `/`M4B ` → `audio/mp4`, `avif`/`avis` → `image/avif`, `heic`/`heix` (and HEIF `mif1` if claimed) → the matching image type; genuine MP4 brands (`isom`, `mp41`, `mp42`, `avc1`, …) still → `video/mp4`.
- [ ] An unrecognized `ftyp` brand does **not** silently become `video/mp4` — it falls through to `undefined` (so `fileMediaType` can use the extension) or the chosen fallback is stated in the code comment and pinned by a test.
- [ ] `fileMediaType(m4aBytes, "song.m4a")` returns `audio/mp4` and `fileMediaType(avifBytes, "photo.avif")` returns `image/avif` (add `avif`/`heic` to `EXTENSIONS` if the brand dispatch does not already cover extension-only cases).
- [ ] Tests in `packages/ai/test/media.test.ts` pin each brand family above plus the unknown-brand case, alongside the existing magic-byte cases; existing media tests still pass.
- [ ] No other sniffer branch (PNG/JPEG/GIF/RIFF/EBML/frame-sync/…) changes behaviour.

Dedup: searched open + closed issues for `ftyp` / `detectMediaType` / media-type sniffing on 2026-11-08 — the only hit is closed #906 (prototype-chain lookups in the same file, fixed with `Object.hasOwn`); no open or closed issue covers the `ftyp` brand dispatch.

body:
## Problem

`script/github/close-issues.ts` — the repo-sweeper's daily stale-issue closer (02:00 UTC window in `.github/workflows/repo-sweeper.yml`) — treats pull requests as issues. It never distinguishes the PR items that GitHub's list-issues endpoint returns from real issues, so a stale PR that is not exempt will be commented on and closed **as an issue**, bypassing the separate PR closer's criteria entirely.

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-08, main `5aee3994c8`)

- `script/github/close-issues.ts:52-60` — `fetchIssuePage` calls `GET /repos/{repo}/issues?state=open&sort=updated&direction=asc&per_page=100&page=N` and returns the page cast to `Issue[]`. GitHub's list-issues endpoint returns pull requests as items carrying a `pull_request` field.
- `script/github/close-issues.ts:18-23` — the `Issue` type does not declare `pull_request` at all, so the distinction is invisible to the rest of the script.
- `script/github/close-issues.ts:47-50` — `shouldSkip` exempts only the agent login, TEAM_MEMBERS logins, and OWNER/MEMBER associations. There is no PR check.
- `script/github/close-issues.ts:105-115` (main loop) — every non-exempt item with `updated_at` older than the 60-day cutoff is pushed to `stale` and passed to `closeIssue`, with no PR check.
- `script/github/close-issues.ts:64-82` — `closeIssue` posts the issue message ("issues are automatically closed after 60 days of no activity…") and PATCHes `/issues/{num}` with `state: closed, state_reason: not_planned`, whatever the number actually is.
- Live read of the exact endpoint the script calls (`issues?state=open&sort=updated&direction=asc&per_page=100&page=1`, 2026-11-08): **29 of the first 100 items carry `pull_request != null`** — e.g. PR #777, PR #822, PR #233, and a run of PRs by `developing-today[bot]` whose `author_association` is `NONE` and whose login is in neither TEAM_MEMBERS nor the exempt agent login (`opencode-agent[bot]`), so `shouldSkip` returns **false** for them. Today none is 60 days stale, but any of them that sits untouched for 60 days will be closed by this script.
- Probe `probe-close-issues.test.ts` (laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-1135` @ `5aee3994c8`, `bun test` in `script/`): a fake page `[{number:41, pull_request:{…}}, {number:42}]` comes back from `fetchIssuePage` unfiltered (`PAGE_NUMBERS [41, 42]`, `PAGE_HAS_PULL_REQUEST_FIELD [true, false]`), and `closeIssue(41, …)` happily issues `POST …/issues/41/comments` + `PATCH …/issues/41`. 2 pass / 0 fail.
- The bypass: `script/github/close-prs.ts` is the PR closer, with deliberately different criteria — created more than 1 month ago, **fewer than 2 positive reactions** (`close-prs.ts:174`), the `automated-pr-cleanup` label, a PR-specific message, `--max-close` and a 20 s sleep between closes (sweeper passes `--threshold 2 --age-months 1 --sleep-ms 20000 --max-close 50 --execute`). A PR closed by `close-issues.ts` gets none of that: no reaction check, no cleanup label, no cap/sleep, and the wrong message and close reason.

Related: #1972 (the token-convention fix for this same script — its new guard test in `script/github/token.test.ts` scans the invoked scripts for token reads but says nothing about PR items), #1344 (bounded reads for the closer scripts, closed).

## Why it matters

The two closers encode two different policies Drew's repo actually runs: issues close on 60 days of inactivity; PRs close on age + community-reaction criteria with their own labelling and pacing. The issue closer silently overriding the PR policy means an unpopular-but-active-policy-exempt PR — today most plausibly a `developing-today[bot]` PR, which is not exempt in `shouldSkip` — can be closed as `not_planned` with a message telling its author to "open a new one", and no record that the PR cleanup ever considered it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `close-issues.ts` never comments on or closes an item carrying a `pull_request` field: PR items are excluded from the stale set (in `fetchIssuePage`, `shouldSkip`, or the main loop — one place, stated in a comment), and skipped PRs are logged as skipped, not silently counted as issues.
- [ ] The `Issue` type (or its replacement) reflects the endpoint's real shape, including the optional `pull_request` field, so the distinction stays visible to future edits.
- [ ] A test pins the behaviour with the module's oracle (the endpoint's documented/observed shape): a page mixing a stale non-exempt PR and a stale non-exempt issue selects/closes only the issue; existing exempt-author behaviour is unchanged. body:
## Summary

`parseDotEnv` in the Mistral Vibe credential bridge (`packages/ai/src/providers/vibe-auth.ts`) parses `~/.vibe/.env` line by line, so a **multiline quoted value** — legal dotenv, and the form both python-dotenv (the vibe binary's ecosystem) and Node's `dotenv` accept — is misparsed in two compounding ways:

1. The multiline value itself is truncated at the first newline and returned **with its opening quote still attached**.
2. Every following line of the quoted block is parsed as its own statement, so a `KEY=value` line *inside* the quoted value is **fabricated into a real key**. If that inner line names `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, the resolver picks it up as the credential (first-hit file tier, `vibe-auth.ts:205-207`) — a value the file's author wrote as data inside another variable becomes the API key sent to Mistral.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Site: `packages/ai/src/providers/vibe-auth.ts:67-91` (`parseDotEnv` splits on `/\r?\n/` at line 69 and parses each line independently; the quoted-value regex at line 77 is anchored to a single line).

Probe `probe-batch.test.ts`, laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-1055` @ `5aee3994c8` (current `main`), calling the real `parseDotEnv`:

| Input | Result | Expected (dotenv semantics) |
|---|---|---|
| `A="line1\nB=injected\nline3"\nC=real` | `{A: '"line1', B: 'injected', C: 'real'}` | `{A: 'line1\nB=injected\nline3', C: 'real'}` — no `B` key exists |
| `A="x\ny"` (literal backslash-n in source) | `{A: 'x\\ny'}` | `{A: 'x\ny'}` — double-quoted values expand `\n`/`\r` escapes in both python-dotenv and Node dotenv |
| `A=x\t# note` | `{A: 'x\t# note'}` | `{A: 'x'}` — an unquoted trailing comment preceded by a **tab** is not stripped; line 82 only searches for `" #"` (space-hash), so the comment text becomes part of the value (for the credential key: part of the API key, guaranteeing an auth failure) |
| `A="x" junk` | `{A: '"x" junk'}` | quoted value with non-comment trailing junk falls through to the unquoted branch and is returned verbatim, quotes included |

Controls that behave correctly (pinned by the existing suite / same probe): quoted values with `#` inside, quoted values with space-`#` trailing comments (`#1870`), single-quoted values, unquoted `x#y` (hash not a comment), CRLF and empty values.

Related but distinct: #1867 / PR #1870 fixed quotes-plus-trailing-comment on a single line. #1964 tracks removing the secret-tool/agy binary dependencies from this module's credential paths, not the parser grammar.

## Why it matters

This file is a credential file. The parser's job per its own header is to mirror the vibe binary's credential resolution so the provider "spends the exact credential the binary provisions". A hand-edited or tool-generated `.env` containing a multiline value (a common dotenv shape for certs/JSON blobs in *other* variables sharing the file) silently corrupts the parse: keys are invented, values are truncated, and in the worst case a fabricated `MISTRAL_API_KEY` line is what gets sent as the Bearer credential. The tab-comment case is the everyday version of the same class: a value quietly gains a `\t# note` suffix and auth fails with no hint why.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A multiline double- or single-quoted value parses as one value (newlines preserved); no key is ever produced from a line inside a quoted value — probe above becomes `{A: 'line1\nB=injected\nline3', C: 'real'}`.
- [ ] Double-quoted escape sequences (`\n`, `\r`, minimally) expand the way dotenv parsers define; single-quoted values stay literal.
- [ ] An unquoted trailing comment is stripped when `#` is preceded by any whitespace (space or tab), while `x#y` keeps its hash.
- [ ] A quoted value followed by non-comment junk has a defined, tested disposition (reject the line, or take the quoted value) — never the current verbatim quotes-plus-junk string.
- [ ] New tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/vibe-auth.test.ts` pin all of the above alongside the existing #1870 cases; the full `vibe-auth` suite passes.
- [ ] Disposition note: if full multiline support is judged out of scope for a "minimal" parser, the fallback must still be safe — an unterminated quote must not fabricate keys from the quoted block's lines (e.g. consume to the closing quote or drop the statement), and that choice is pinned by a test.

Agent: pr-diff-review-b

## Finding

Merged PR #1832's `SessionStep.failureHint` emits `quotaResetAtMs` present-but-undefined whenever a quota-class error states no reset in its text — directly contradicting the omitted-when-unset convention its own comment (added in the same PR) states.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1832 (MERGED, merge 6b178f665a53, commit 472d7b9a), `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts`.
- Verified on current main 2961e602aa011cd3c8dbefb51ec3708ca126c333 (read twice): step.ts:180-184 —
  - the comment: "Optional hint fields are omitted when unset, never present-but-undefined — the same convention the route policy follows."
  - the code directly under it: `...(quota ? { quotaResetAtMs: ModelRouteLimits.resetAtFromMessage(reason.message ?? reason.body, Date.now()) } : {})` — the key is included for EVERY quota hint, whatever the parser returns.
- `resetAtFromMessage` returns `number | undefined`: `packages/core/src/model-route-limits.ts:159-169` on main returns `undefined` when the message is absent or states no parseable absolute/relative reset. A tagged `QuotaExceeded` error with no reset text (the common shape) therefore yields a hint object where `"quotaResetAtMs" in hint === true` and `hint.quotaResetAtMs === undefined`.
- No runtime break today: the one consumer, `statedQuotaResetAt` in model-route.ts, guards with `!== undefined`. The defect is the convention violation itself plus the latent trap for any future consumer that enumerates keys, deep-equals hint objects, or serializes them.
- Dedupe (2026-11-08): issue search for "quotaResetAtMs" returns no issues; "present-but-undefined failureHint" returns only the parent incident #1806 and closed #1486, neither of which covers this.

## Why it matters

The comment states the convention because hint consumers in this codebase rely on key presence as the signal (the `infra` field in the same function follows it correctly, two lines below). A field that is present-but-undefined makes presence checks lie, and the next consumer written against the documented convention will misread every reset-less quota error as carrying a stated reset.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `failureHint` omits `quotaResetAtMs` entirely when `resetAtFromMessage` returns undefined, and sets it when a reset is stated.
- [ ] A test pins both shapes: a quota error with no reset text produces a hint with `"quotaResetAtMs" in hint === false`; the Antigravity-wall shape (reset stated in text) still produces the extracted `quotaResetAtMs`.
- [ ] Existing session-runner/step and model-route availability suites still pass.

<!-- agent-note:v1

## Finding

Merged PR #1837 (fix for #1768) silently dropped recognition of the `daily` window spelling in antigravity's quota `parseBucket`: a bucket whose window/bucketId string is `DAILY` (lowercased `daily`) is now skipped entirely, so its daily quota window is never published. Before #1837 that spelling was explicitly recognized.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1837 (MERGED, merge cbfaa84514a2, commit bc4cb956). Its diff to `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/antigravity.ts` changed the daily branch from `windowStr.includes("day") || windowStr.includes("daily")` to only `windowStr.includes("day")`, in the same hunk that added the new else-return-null for unrecognized windows.
- The two checks are NOT equivalent: `"daily"` does not contain the substring `"day"` (d-a-i-l-y — the letters d/a/y are never consecutive), so the removed `|| includes("daily")` was the only branch that matched the `daily` spelling.
- Verified on current main 2961e602aa011cd3c8dbefb51ec3708ca126c333 (file read twice via the contents API): `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/antigravity.ts:285-295` still reads week/7d → weekly, `includes("day")` → daily, five/5h/hour → 5h, else `return null`. A `daily` bucket therefore returns null and `transformSummary` skips it (`if (!parsed) continue`).
- PR #1837's new tests pin FIVE_HOUR, WEEKLY, MONTHLY (skipped) and 7D spellings, but no DAILY case — so the regression landed with every suite green.
- Dedupe (2026-11-08): issue searches for "parseBucket" and "antigravity daily bucket" return #1941 (OPEN, integer-quantized percents — different defect), closed #1917/#1912 (figure-less buckets) and closed #1768 (the original issue #1837 fixed). Nothing tracks the lost `daily` recognition.

## Why it matters

This is the mirror image of the #1768 bug #1837 set out to fix: instead of an unrecognized bucket fabricating a window, a recognized one now silently vanishes. Any antigravity payload that spells its daily window `DAILY`/`daily` (the spelling the pre-#1837 code deliberately handled) loses that window from the published quota read — the router and UI under-report the provider's daily headroom with no error anywhere.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parseBucket` recognizes the `daily` spelling again (window string AND bucketId spelling), publishing label `daily` with `DAILY_WINDOW_SECONDS`.
- [ ] A test in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins a `DAILY` bucket (and/or a `daily` bucketId) publishing its daily window, and fails on current main.
- [ ] Unrecognized spellings (e.g. MONTHLY) are still skipped, and the existing #1768 bucket tests still pass.

# fix(ai): quota model maps drop a model named `__proto__` — plain-object assignment keyed by payload model names (claude scoped windows, antigravity models)

## Summary

Two quota transforms build their per-model result maps with plain-object assignment keyed by **payload-supplied model names**, so a model named `__proto__` silently vanishes — and the assignment mutates the result object's prototype instead of adding an entry:

- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/claude.ts:201-203` — `toClaudeUsage`: for `weekly_scoped` limits, `const modelWindows = models[modelName]?.windows ?? {}` … `models[modelName] = { windows: modelWindows }`, where `modelName` is the payload's `scope.model.display_name`.
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/antigravity.ts:355` + `:380` / `:406` — `transformModels`: `for (const [modelName, rawData] of Object.entries(rawModels))` … `transformed[name] = { windows: … }`, where the keys are the payload's model names.

For `name === "__proto__"`, `obj[name] = value` invokes the prototype setter: no own property is created, `Object.keys` / `Object.entries` downstream never see the model, and the result object gains a phantom `windows` property through its new prototype. The fleet's prototype-chain programme (#833 audit and the `check:proto-reads` gate) guards **reads** through the chain; these are unguarded **writes** keyed by wire data, and they lose a whole model's quota windows.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `426c71b0d9`)

Probes `probe-proto.test.ts` / `probe-proto2.test.ts` (laptop worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-08-creator-0935` @ `426c71b0d9`, `bun test` in `packages/ai`; copies in the creator run dir `creator-2026-11-08-0335/`):

- Claude: `toClaudeUsage` with two `weekly_scoped` limits (display names `__proto__` at 42% and `Sonnet` at 7%) returns `Object.keys(models) === ["Sonnet"]` — the `__proto__` model's 7d window is gone. Control: a model named `constructor` at 11% survives (`models["constructor"].windows["7d"].usedPercent === 11`), so this is specifically the `__proto__` setter, not name handling in general.
- Antigravity (wire-faithful: payload built with `JSON.parse`, so `__proto__` arrives as an own property, exactly as `readQuotaJson` delivers it): raw model keys `["__proto__", "gemini-3"]` → `transformModels` returns keys `["gemini-3"]` only, and the returned object reads a phantom `.windows` through its mutated prototype.

## Why it matters

A quota read that silently drops one model misreports that model's windows everywhere the usage map is consumed (per-model quota rows, gating inputs). The name is provider-controlled wire data: a provider (or a gateway / façade in front of one) that introduces a model whose display name or id is `__proto__` — or any future collision of the same shape — loses its quota row with no error, and the prototype mutation can leak a stray `windows` read into unrelated lookups on the same object. The sibling disposition in this codebase is own-property discipline (#791, #819, #824, #862 and the burn-rate / snapshot `Object.hasOwn` guards); the model maps are the remaining write-side exception in the quota subsystem.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A model named `__proto__` survives as an own, enumerable entry in both transforms: claude `toClaudeUsage` scoped windows and antigravity `transformModels` (both the matched-group branch and the fallback `quotaInfo` branch), with its windows intact.
- [ ] The result objects' prototype is untouched (`Object.getPrototypeOf(result) === Object.prototype`) and no phantom `windows` property is readable on them.
- [ ] Tests pin the `__proto__` case for both providers (payloads constructed via `JSON.parse` so the key arrives as wire data does), with `constructor` / ordinary-name controls unchanged.
- [ ] Any other payload-keyed plain-object assignment in `packages/ai/src/quota/` found during the fix gets the same disposition or is named in the PR as safe-by-construction (fixed key set).
- [ ] `packages/ai` quota test suite passes.

## Related

- #833 (closed) — prototype-chain audit; its net and `script/check-proto-reads.ts` cover reads, not assignments.
- #538 (closed) — config alias resolution dropping a `__proto__` entry: same loss shape, different subsystem.
- #819 / #824 (closed) — quota-adjacent prototype-chain reads fixed with own-property guards.
