body:
# fix(core): failureHint extracts the stated quota reset from `message ?? body` — a reset stated only in the error body is classified as quota but never bound to the bench

## Summary

`SessionStep.failureHint` (`packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts:154`) classifies an error by scanning **both** text fields — `const text = \`${reason.message ?? ""} ${reason.body ?? ""}\`` feeds the quota test (`step.ts:171`) and the auth test — but it extracts the stated reset / retry-after from only **one** of them:

- `step.ts:178`: `ModelRouteLimits.retryHintFromMessage(reason.message ?? reason.body, Date.now())`
- `step.ts:183`: `ModelRouteLimits.resetAtFromMessage(reason.message ?? reason.body, Date.now())`

The `??` means: whenever a summary `message` exists (the normal case — `classifyProviderFailure` in `packages/ai/src/provider-error.ts:236` always builds errors with a message plus `body: input.rawBody`), the raw body is **never scanned** for a reset. That contradicts the function's own contract at `step.ts:148-153`: "A quota stated only in the error text classifies as quota too, **with the stated reset bound to the bench**." It also contradicts the error type's design: `ProviderFailure.rawBody` is documented in `provider-error.ts` as the "Raw wire payload, scanned for failure signals … that the summary message does not carry", and the classifier builds its scan text from `[input.message, body].join("\n")` (`provider-error.ts:246`) for exactly this reason.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `426c71b0d9`)

Probe `probe-failurehint.test.ts` (laptop worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-08-creator-0935` @ `426c71b0d9`, `bun test` in `packages/core`; copy in the creator run dir `creator-2026-11-08-0335/`):

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Control: `QuotaExceededError`, message `quota exhausted; reset at 2099-01-02T00:00:00Z` | `quota: true`, `quotaResetAtMs: 4070995200000` ✅ |
| `ProviderInternalError`, message `quota exhausted`, body `… reset at 2099-01-02T00:00:00Z` | `quota: true` (body scanned for classification), **`quotaResetAtMs: undefined`** ❌ |
| `ProviderInternalError`, message `rate limited`, body `try again in 30 minutes` | **`retryAfterMs: undefined`** (expected `1800000`) ❌ |
| Both fields state different resets | message's reset wins; body's is never considered |

Baseline: the existing `packages/core/test/session-step-failure.test.ts` suite passes on this main (16 pass) — no existing test constructs an error with a `body`, so the gap is unpinned.

## Why it matters

Providers commonly return a terse summary message while the reset time lives in the raw payload (JSON error bodies, `resets_at` fields, "try again in …" text). For those failures the route layer benches the target as quota — the long, serious class — but with **no stated reset bound**, so re-admission falls back to generic cooldown behaviour instead of the provider's own stated reset: targets can be retried long before the reset (hammering a walled pool) or held on the wrong schedule. This is the live step-runner path (`step.ts:512`, `step.ts:676`, and title generation at `packages/core/src/session/title.ts:184`), not a test-only helper.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `failureHint` extracts `retryAfterMs` and `quotaResetAtMs` from the same combined text it classifies on (message and body), so a reset stated only in `body` is bound to the bench.
- [ ] The #1551 guard is preserved: for a client `Transport`/`Timeout` failure, the client's own "No response output within …" duration text still yields no hint — extraction must not start reading a wait out of that message merely because scanning widened (state the disposition for a provider-stated wait in such an error's body).
- [ ] Ordering is stated and pinned: when both fields state a reset, which one wins (and a reset stated in the message must not be shadowed by unrelated body text that merely parses as a date).
- [ ] New tests in `packages/core/test/session-step-failure.test.ts` construct errors with a `body`: body-only absolute reset → `quotaResetAtMs`; body-only relative wait → `retryAfterMs`; message-only controls unchanged; the #1551 timeout cases unchanged.
- [ ] `packages/core` session-step / model-route test suites pass.

## Related

- #1551 (closed) — the timeout-text guard this change must preserve.
- #1806 (open) — quota-walled members and failover; stated resets are part of correct re-admission.
- Sibling parsers already scan combined text: `ModelRouteTuning.parseQuotaReset` / `ModelRouteLimits.resetAtFromMessage` take a single message argument — the divergence is at this call site, which holds two fields and only forwards one.

body:
## Summary

Every quota window published through the shared converter carries two formatted reset fields, and they are always the same string. `toUsageWindow` (`packages/ai/src/quota/utils.ts:113-137`) computes one `resetFormatted` value and assigns it to **both** `resetAtFormatted` (line 134) and `resetAfterFormatted` (line 135). The window's numeric fields keep the two concepts apart — `resetAt` is the absolute instant, `resetAfterSeconds` is the relative seconds-until-reset (`calculateResetAfterSeconds`, line 132) — but the formatted pair collapses them: `resetAfterFormatted` never contains a relative duration, for any provider, because every provider's windows are built by this one converter.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probe at `07b0352b45`)

Probe: `probe-creator.test.ts`, laptop worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-08-creator-0235` @ `07b0352b45`, `bun test` — 4 pass.

`toUsageWindow({ usedPercent: 50, resetAt: Date.now() + 3_600_000 })` returns:

```json
{ "resetAfterSeconds": 3600, "resetAtFormatted": "9:42 AM", "resetAfterFormatted": "9:42 AM" }
```

The relative field says "in one hour" numerically (3600) and "9:42 AM" textually — the absolute wall-clock time, duplicated. The end-to-end claude/meta windows in the same probe show the identical duplication on real parser output.

No test pins the non-null relationship: the only assertions on these fields (`packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts:609-610`) check that both are `null` when there is no reset, which passes under any assignment.

## Why it matters

`QuotaWindow` is the shape downstream consumers map unchanged (aggregator gatherer, dashboard, Supabase recording — `packages/ai/src/quota/types.ts:5-15`). A consumer that reads `resetAfterFormatted` for what its name and its numeric sibling say — a formatted relative wait, e.g. to render "resets in 1h" — silently renders an absolute time instead, and a consumer comparing the two formatted fields to distinguish "when" from "how long" cannot. Window contract rule 5 (#1794): a window's fields agree — derived fields are computed from the published values; here one derived field is computed from the *other concept's* value.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Triage disposition is recorded on this issue: either (a) `resetAfterFormatted` is derived from `resetAfterSeconds` as a human duration, or (b) the field is documented in `types.ts`/`utils.ts` as intentionally identical to `resetAtFormatted` (legacy shape), with the reason named.
- [ ] If (a): the format matches how the CLI already renders durations, and a past reset (0 seconds) and a null reset both have pinned behavior.
- [ ] A non-null test pins the two formatted fields' relationship (distinct under (a), explicitly identical under (b)) in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts`, alongside the existing null-case assertions.
- [ ] Full `packages/ai` quota test suite passes.

title: fix(ai): shared quota toNumber reinterprets hex/binary/octal/exponent strings — "0x64" publishes as 100, "1e2" as a spent claude window

body:
## Summary

The shared quota string-to-number converter `toNumber` (`packages/ai/src/quota/utils.ts:25`) parses string figures with a bare `Number(value)`. That reinterprets non-decimal spellings — hex, binary, octal, exponent, leading `+` — as numbers, so a malformed or hostile quota payload can fabricate a quota figure for **every** provider that parses through the shared converter (all 13 providers in the registry use it). Every sibling numeric surface in this repo that faced the same question adopted a plain-decimal grammar instead; this one boundary was never given one.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probe at `07b0352b45`)

Probe: `probe-creator.test.ts`, laptop worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-08-creator-0235` @ `07b0352b45`, `bun test` — 4 pass.

`toNumber` direct:

| input | result | plain-decimal reading |
|---|---|---|
| `"0x64"` | `100` | null (no figure) |
| `"0b1100100"` | `100` | null |
| `"0o144"` | `100` | null |
| `"1e3"` | `1000` | null |
| `"1e2"` | `100` | null |
| `"+42"` | `42` | disposition (see below) |
| `"42"` / `"4.5"` / `"-5"` | `42` / `4.5` / `-5` | unchanged (controls) |
| `""` / `"lots"` | `null` | already guarded (`#1741` blank-string rule) |

End-to-end through real parsers:

- `toClaudeUsage({ limits: [{ kind: "session", percent: "0x50", resets_at: 1798761600 }] })` publishes the `5h` window with `usedPercent: 80`; with `percent: "1e2"` it publishes `usedPercent: 100` — a fully-spent window fabricated from a spelling no provider sends.
- `parseSubscriptionQuota` with `window_weighted_used: "0x64"`, `window_weighted_limit: "100"` publishes a `5h` window at 100% used.

## Why this is the undispositioned gap, not a settled one

- The quota subsystem's own groq parser documents the house rule at `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/groq.ts:38-50` (#1793): string figures are "accepted only as a plain non-negative decimal … never via a bare `Number()`, which would also accept negatives, hex (0x64) and exponents (1e1)".
- Core's sibling rule: `PLAIN_COUNT = /^\d+(?:\.\d+)?$/` at `packages/core/src/model-route-limits.ts:209` (#711); the ai executor's retry-after grammars at `packages/ai/src/route/executor.ts:28-29`; websearch's cooldown (#686). Prior per-surface filings: #682, #686, #711, #715, #724, #771 — the shared quota converter is the remaining one.
- The numeric-boundaries gate allowlist (`script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt`) dispositions groq's `Number(text)` (line 10) explicitly because its text "has already matched a plain … decimal pattern … no sign, hex, or exponent", but dispositions this call (line 11) only as "accepts only JSON strings/numbers and rejects non-finite results" — true, and silent on spelling: a JSON string `"0x64"` passes that rationale and is still reinterpreted.

## Why it matters

Quota figures drive routing gates, skip/re-admission decisions, and the dashboard's published state. A fabricated 100%-used window (claude `"1e2"`, meta `"0x64"`) benches a healthy provider; a fabricated balance figure distorts spend reporting. The window contract (#1794) rule framing — a figure that cannot exist is not a figure (#1942) — is violated at the one converter every quota parser shares, so one fix covers the whole subsystem.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `toNumber` accepts only plain-decimal string spellings: optional leading `-`, digits, optional fraction (after the existing trim); hex/binary/octal/exponent spellings return `null`.
- [ ] Negative plain decimals keep parsing (`-5` → `-5`): negative balances/percents are real data published truthfully or clamped downstream (#1924/#1928 dispositions) — the grammar must not become groq's unsigned one blindly. The `+42` disposition (reject vs accept) is stated in the fix.
- [ ] Probe tests pin the spellings above at the `toNumber` level **and** end-to-end (claude percent, meta weighted used), with `"42"`/`"4.5"`/`"-5"`/`""` controls unchanged.
- [ ] `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt` line 11's rationale is updated to name the plain-decimal grammar, matching line 10's standard.
- [ ] Full `packages/ai` quota test suite passes.

body:
## Summary

The shared quota-reset relative-time grammar has no **week** unit, so a provider (or user note) that states a reset as "resets in 1 week" is read as stating no reset at all — and a compound phrase that contains a week component is silently truncated to the non-week part.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `07b0352b45`)

Grammar: `packages/core/src/model-route-limits.ts`

- `RELATIVE_PART` (line ~141) accepts only `second|minute|hour|day|sec|mins?|ms|h|d|m|s`; `RELATIVE_UNITS` (line ~144) has no week entry (a week is exactly `7 * 86_400_000` ms — no calendar ambiguity, unlike a month).
- This grammar is the single shared one for both doors (#996/#1532): `ModelRouteLimits.relativeMs` / `resetAtFromMessage` and `ModelRouteTuning.parseQuotaReset` (model-route-tuning.ts:216).

Probe `probe-week.test.ts`, laptop worktree `probe-2026-11-08-creator-0135` @ `07b0352b45`, `bun test` in `packages/core` (controls pass; week cases fail):

| message | result | expected |
|---|---|---|
| `quota resets in 7 days` | `now + 7d` ✅ control | `now + 7d` |
| `quota resets in 30m` / `in 1 hour 30 minutes` | ✅ controls | — |
| `quota resets in 5 deals` | `undefined` ✅ guard control | `undefined` |
| `weekly quota resets in 1 week` | `undefined` ❌ | `now + 7d` |
| `weekly quota resets in 2 weeks` | `undefined` ❌ | `now + 14d` |
| `weekly quota resets in 1 wk` | `undefined` ❌ | `now + 7d` |
| `quota resets in 1 week 2 days` | `undefined` ❌ | `now + 9d` |
| `quota resets in 2 days and 1 week` | `now + 2d` ❌ (week silently dropped) | `now + 9d` |
| tuning door: `quota limit reached, resets in 1 week` via `parseQuotaReset` | `undefined` ❌ | `now + 7d` |

## Why it matters

Consumers of the missing parse get no stated reset where the provider stated one:

- `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts:178,183` — `retryHintFromMessage` / `resetAtFromMessage` on a quota error: a weekly-limit error phrased in weeks falls back to the generic hold instead of the stated reset.
- `packages/core/src/model-route-tuning.ts:164` — `predict` reads the last error's stated reset the same way.
- `packages/core/src/model-route-tuning.ts:257` — `noteAdjustments`: a user's own note "back in 1 week" produces no skip adjustment at all.
- The compound truncation is worse than a miss: "in 2 days and 1 week" publishes a reset 7 days early, so the target is re-tried against a window that is still closed.

Weekly windows are a first-class shape in this fork (Claude/meta/codex weekly quota windows), so week phrasing in reset text is a realistic form, not an exotic one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The shared grammar in `model-route-limits.ts` accepts week forms (at minimum `week`/`weeks`; triage decides on `wk`/`wks`/`w`) at exactly 7 days per week, in both single and compound positions.
- [ ] `resetAtFromMessage("…resets in 1 week")` returns `now + 7 * 86_400_000`; `"in 2 days and 1 week"` and `"in 1 week 2 days"` both return `now + 9 * 86_400_000` — no silent truncation.
- [ ] Both doors stay in parity (#996): the paired case tables in `model-route-limits.test.ts` / `model-route-tuning.test.ts` gain the week cases for both entry points.
- [ ] Guards unchanged: `in 5 deals`-style non-units still parse to `undefined`, and a week unit cannot match the head of a following word.
- [ ] Existing ceilings still apply downstream (`parseQuotaReset` / `noteAdjustments` clamp as today).

Dedup: no open or closed issue covers a week unit in this grammar — #996/#1532 unified the existing units (seconds→days) across the two parsers and did not add weeks; search for `relativeMs` / week+reset returns only those.

## Finding

PR #1726 — the completed implementation of issue #1725 (payload-present OpenCode Go windows kept with nullable fields, plus the first tests for `parseOpenCodeGoUsage` / `parseConsoleGoUsage` / `parseConsoleBillingBalance` and for OpenRouter `resolveResetAt` calendar math) — is stale, conflicted, and now duplicated in flight, and no live record treats it as the work vehicle for #1725 anymore:

- The queue remainder for #1725 was triaged on 2026-11-08T04:08:47Z and enqueued as queue task 12745 (repo-health-opencode-pilot), scoped to exactly PR #1726's three items (pin the three opencode-go parsers; conform `parseOpenCodeGoUsage` to design #1794 rule 3 — keep the window, null the field; pin `resolveResetAt` reset math). The triage note never mentions PR #1726. The 2026-11-08T00:26:15Z routing note on #1725 likewise treats the issue as having no live work vehicle. If task 12745's worker starts cold, it re-implements PR #1726 from scratch and produces a competing PR for the same change.
- PR #1726 itself can no longer land as-is (evidence below), so "just merge it" is not available either. One vehicle has to be chosen and recorded, or the fleet runs both.

This is a consolidation finding (pr-diff-review, PR consolidation rule: a stale open PR whose fix is still needed, with a parallel work stream for the same set). The underlying quota work stays tracked by issue #1725 — this issue tracks only the PR/task collision.

## Evidence

- PR #1726 (OPEN): single commit `0f3e08da8c5a`, created 2026-11-05T09:08:23Z, `updated_at` unchanged since creation, no labels, no reviews, no comments. Its diff: `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/opencode-go.ts` (+5/−2, drop-on-null replaced with keep-window/null-field) and `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` (+113, the three parsers + `resolveResetAt` daily/weekly/monthly boundary tests).
- `gh api repos/developing-today-forks/opencode/pulls/1726` at review time: `mergeable: false`, `mergeable_state: "dirty"`, base `13ab3dc5c2d5` — the PR now has real merge conflicts against main.
- The work is still needed and not landed: on current main `07b0352b45d8f32f2557ffae4001b0139c1ccd1e`, `parseOpenCodeGoUsage` (`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/opencode-go.ts`) still drops any window whose `usedPercent` or `resetAt` is null.
- Two current-main tests pin the opposite disposition and fail under PR #1726's code as written (static proof from the code paths: post-#1742 `toNumber("") === null`, post-#1851 `toTimestamp(-5000) === null`, and PR #1726 keeps the window in both cases):
  - `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts:615` (PR #1742, #1741 describe): an empty `percent` field must mint **no** opencode-go window — `expect(parseOpenCodeGoUsage(payload)).toEqual({})`.
  - `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts:513` (PR #1851 era): a non-positive reset publishes **no** window ("existing drop-on-null behaviour … #1725 keeps the broader rule-3 call").
  Any revival of PR #1726 must disposition both pins deliberately (update them to the #1794 rule-3 disposition, or keep them and narrow the change), not discover them as surprise CI failures.
- Issue #1725 history: a 2026-11-05T17:32:11Z correction note on #1725 explicitly called PR #1726 "the live work for this issue"; the issue was then adopted as phase 3 of design #1794 (2026-11-06T01:45:26Z), and the Nov 8 routing/triage notes (00:26:15Z, 04:08:47Z) re-queued the remainder as task 12745 without reference to the PR. Dedupe: GitHub search for "1726" across this repo's issues returns only #1725 itself; no open issue covers the PR/task collision.

## Why it matters

The fleet has already paid for this exact failure mode (a fix implemented twice because the second work stream never saw the first — cf. the cross-repo one-issue-per-finding rule). PR #1726 holds reviewed-shape tests and the deliberate rule-3 disposition choice #1794 recommends; losing it silently wastes that work, while reviving it later — after task 12745 lands its own version — guarantees a conflicting duplicate PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One vehicle is chosen and recorded on both issue #1725 and PR #1726: either (a) PR #1726 is rebased onto current main, the two contrary test pins (quota.test.ts:615 and quota.test.ts:513) are dispositioned in the PR, and task 12745 is pointed at PR #1726 as its implementation; or (b) PR #1726 is closed as superseded by task 12745, with the closing note pointing at #1725 / task 12745 so its tests and disposition reasoning are harvested, not lost.

title: fix(core): quota gates never re-admit after a window roll — attempt-reported skip 'until' outlives its period (opendesign dark 33h)
body:
## Defect: attempt-reported quota gates never re-admit after a period roll (stale `until` outlives its window)

**Live incident (2026-11-07):** the `opendesign` provider sat at **zero attempts for ~33h** while its plan window was full and open. Chain of evidence:

- 2026-11-06 19:32Z: genuine exhaustion (402 `insufficient_balance`) → attempt-reported skip `quota:opendesign` planted with `until` = the reset stated then (**2026-11-10T12:02:21Z**), persisted as a `route_note` row.
- The provider's window **rolled** on 2026-11-07 10:52:34Z (new 7d window: 150,000/150,000 credits, reset 2026-11-14T10:52Z — verified via the quota gatherer). The old period ended; usage in the new period ≈ 0.
- But no mechanism re-judged the skip: the proactive plan-feed derives usage **only from the local `route_attempt` ledger** (`targetUsage` sums tokens per provider/model), and OpenDesign's recorded `cost_usd` is 0.0 across all 5,306 historical attempts, so any credits/usd accounting also reads empty. The gate's `actualResetAt` stayed latched to the old period.
- The skip only lapses at its stated `until` — i.e. the provider would have stayed dark until **Nov 10**, three days into a fresh window.
- **Escalation 2026-11-07 22:19 CST:** with workhorse-primary + workhorse-weighted emptied, workhorse = deepseek-flash-plan#high only; the pool-exhaustion verdict (2+ leaves with quota evidence, `poolQuotaExhausted`) compounded the outage — 30 no-candidate workhorse decisions — because cline-pass/commandcode/opendesign evidence counting has no per-period freshness either.

## Root causes (code evidence, `packages/core/src/model-route.ts` unless noted)

1. **Asymmetric adjustment lifecycle.** `removeAdjustment` exists (`model-route.ts:2623`) and the proactive path calls it on a not-full reading (line 1897), but in the entire production `route_note` history there is **not one `{"op":"remove"}` record** — every re-admission in practice happens by `until` lapse or restart-state quirks, never by an explicit reconciling remove. Attempt-reported skips (`observeQuotaFailure`, credential-less path) plant `until` + note and nothing ever re-judges them against a rolled window.
2. **Gate freshness is ledger-derived only.** `refreshQuotaGate` (`model-resolver.ts:451`) builds snapshots from `ModelPlan` store windows + `targetUsage` sums over `route_attempt`. A provider whose attempts carry no token/cost accounting for the gated unit — or whose plan record's `resetAt` is the *old* period's — can never produce the not-full snapshot that is the only designed release for a proactive gate; for attempt-reported skips there is no release path at all short of `until`.
3. **No period-roll invalidation.** Nothing compares a gate's `actualResetAt`/skip `until` against the provider's *current* window boundary. When the window rolls, the old reset is provably stale, yet the gate keeps it.

## Ask

- On each quota feed (or gate check), if a gate's stated reset is **older than the current window's period start** for that provider+window, treat the gate as stale: re-derive from current-period usage and re-admit when the current period is not full (log `quota-readmitted`).
- Give attempt-reported skips the same re-judgement: their `until` is the reset *as stated at plant time*; a window roll must re-open them for one probe (the half-open probe machinery, #1123/#1390, already exists for benches — extend the carve-out to pool-exhaustion evidence).
- Consider feeding the gate from the providers' own quota wires (the `opencode quota` CLI already emulates first-party usage endpoints per provider) as a cross-check when ledger-derived usage is empty for a provider that has recorded attempts — an empty-ledger reading for a busy provider is a data defect, not headroom evidence either way.

## Workaround applied live (2026-11-07)

Direct statement of the fresh period into the running server by a fleet lane session (`route_usage` read of the current window + explicit provider call): `opendesign/claude-haiku-5.5` attempt **succeeded 2026-11-08T04:32:10Z** (first since 2026-11-06 19:32Z), proving provider + credential healthy. NOTE: routed (pool) selection still shows the stale gate state in the long-running server process — full re-admission of the opendesign leaf in `deepseek-flash-plan` awaits this fix or a server restart cycle.

Related: #7073 (startup failover — different defect: sessions dying on first-candidate errors; this issue is gate staleness). Filed from the gate-fix lane under Drew's 2026-11-07 approval ("gate fixes only" + "so fucking fix it").

## Summary

#1966 added a `splitsPair` guard to `messaging/log.ts` `clip()`, and #1970 tracks the five unguarded cuts in `messaging.ts`. The same defect class survives at six more truncation sites outside the messaging modules, none of which uses the guard (it is still module-private to `messaging/log.ts:171`). Each site slices a string at a fixed UTF-16 code-unit budget; when an astral character (emoji, CJK ext, musical symbols — 2 code units) straddles the cut, the output ends with a lone high surrogate. The string is not well-formed: UTF-8 encoding replaces the lone surrogate with U+FFFD, so the corruption is persisted/shown verbatim wherever the text lands (DB rows, model context, embedding requests, error messages).

`session/compaction.ts`'s `truncateToolOutput` already shows the house-correct pattern ("Count code points so a surrogate pair is never split") — these six sites predate or missed that treatment.

## Sites (all on main 24200c35a4)

1. `packages/core/src/session/title.ts:35` — `truncate()`: `` `${value.slice(0, MAX_LENGTH - 3)}...` `` (MAX_LENGTH 100, cut at 97). Session titles are LLM-generated from user text, persisted, and shown in every session list/header.
2. `packages/core/src/codemode/catalog.ts:69` — description `firstLine.slice(0, DESCRIPTION_LIMIT - 3) + "..."` (DESCRIPTION_LIMIT 120, cut at 117). The catalog summary is inlined into the model's code-mode context.
3. `packages/core/src/messaging/embedding.ts:1022` — `text.slice(0, current.limit)` clips embedding inputs; a straddling pair sends a lone surrogate to the embedding provider in the request JSON.
4. `packages/core/src/session/runner/publish-llm-event.ts:670` — `inputExcerpt()`: `value.slice(0, INPUT_EXCERPT_LIMIT)`, surfaced in step-failure messages.
5. `packages/core/src/model-route-log.ts:279` — `redactBody(value.body).slice(0, 2_000)`, persisted as `error_body` in route-log rows.
6. `packages/core/src/ripgrep.ts:261` — match `text.slice(0, 2_000) + "..."` in search results returned to the model.

Checked and NOT included: `tool-output.ts:107` slices at a kept-lines boundary derived from whole lines of the same joined text, so the cut always lands at a line end and cannot straddle a pair; `messaging/log.ts` (fixed by #1966) and `messaging.ts` (tracked by #1970).

## Evidence (this run, laptop probe worktree `probe-2026-11-07-creator-2219` @ 24200c35a4)

- Real function: `CodeModeCatalog.summarize()` fed a tool whose description first line is 116×`a` + 😀 + 10×`b` (128 units) produced a listing line ending `aaaa\ud83d...` — `isWellFormed() === false`, and a UTF-8 encode/decode round-trip changes the string (lone surrogate → U+FFFD). Control with the pair fully before the cut: `isWellFormed() === true`.
- Title expression (verbatim from title.ts:35, module-private): 96×`a` + 😀 + 10×`b` → `isWellFormed() === false`, tail `aa\ud83d...`; control (pair at 95–96) clean.
- Embedding-clip expression (verbatim slice at limit 51 over 50×`x` + 😀 + …): `isWellFormed() === false`. Same result for a generic 2_000-unit excerpt cut.
- Probe files: `probe/probe-catalog.ts`, `probe/probe-surrogate.ts` in the probe worktree.

## Why it matters

Titles are the most user-visible surface here: an emoji-heavy first message can permanently store a mojibake title. The embedding clip is the only site whose corrupted output leaves the process in a provider request. The rest corrupt model-facing context and persisted diagnostics — the same harm #1966/#1970 were filed for, in the modules those two did not cover.

## Acceptance criteria

- The #1966 `splitsPair` guard (or an equivalent code-point-aware cut) is promoted to a shared home importable outside `messaging/` and applied at all six sites above (dropping the straddling pair whole, as #1966 does, is the established disposition).
- A test per site (or per shared helper plus one integration site) pins: pair straddling the cut → output `isWellFormed()` and contains no U+FFFD after UTF-8 round-trip; pair fully inside/outside the budget unchanged; plain-ASCII truncation byte-identical to today.
- Existing suites stay green: session-title, catalog, tool-schema/embedding, model-route-log, ripgrep tests in packages/core.

Related: #1966 (guard origin), #1970 (messaging.ts sibling set).

## Summary

#1966 fixed `MessagingLog.clip` (`packages/core/src/messaging/log.ts`) so none
of its cuts split a surrogate pair, and its fix comment states the house rule:
"A cut at `index` splits a surrogate pair … The house rule is to never split
a pair (messaging/search.ts, session compaction), so a straddling pair is
dropped whole instead" (log.ts:164-170 on main ce5b1d691c).

The parent module `packages/core/src/messaging.ts` still makes the same
unguarded code-unit cuts at five sites. An astral character (any code point
above U+FFFF — emoji, 𝄞, CJK ext.) straddling any of these budgets is split:
the kept text ends with a lone high surrogate. The result is not well-formed
(`isWellFormed() === false`) and re-encodes as U+FFFD the moment it is
serialized or displayed — the exact harm #1966 was filed for, in the module
that calls the fixed function.

## The five unguarded cuts (main ce5b1d691c)

- `messaging.ts:2250` — `render()`: the model-visible delivered message body.
  `` `${message.data.slice(0, DELIVERED_CHARS)}\n…[N more characters; …]` ``
  with `DELIVERED_CHARS = 8000` (messaging.ts:120). This is the text a
  receiving session actually reads, wrapped by `MessagingLog.escapeBody`
  (messaging.ts:2253), which escapes message tags only and does not repair
  lone surrogates. The `[N more characters]` count is also derived from the
  raw cut (`message.data.length - DELIVERED_CHARS`), so a boundary
  adjustment must recompute it.
- `messaging.ts:561` — `announce()`: the `Messaging.Event.Created` preview,
  `input.data.slice(0, 197)` + `"..."`, published globally on the bus.
- `messaging.ts:619` — the `TuiEvent.ToastShow` message for user delivery,
  `input.text.slice(0, 397)` + `"..."`.
- `messaging.ts:2221` — `firstLine()`: `line.slice(0, 97)` + `"..."`; feeds
  the synthetic-message description (messaging.ts:594) and `render()`'s
  description (messaging.ts:2254), so it reaches both UI and session
  transcripts.
- `messaging.ts:1071` — advanced-search rerank input:
  `content(item.row).slice(0, 600)` is the text handed to the rerank model.

## Repro (verified this run)

Probe `probe.mjs` in `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-07-creator-messaging-slices`
(laptop), evaluating each site's exact slice expression against a string
with U+1F600 placed straddling the cut (high surrogate at index cut-1, low
at cut). `render`/`firstLine` are module-private, so the probe drives the
literal expressions and budgets from the source above; the four
service-level sites share the same expression shape.

- All five cuts (197, 397, 600, 97, 8000): sliced text
  `isWellFormed() === false`, and a TextEncoder/TextDecoder round-trip
  contains U+FFFD.
- Guarded variant (drop the straddling pair whole, the #1966 disposition):
  well-formed at every cut.
- Control (pair fully inside the budget): well-formed — the defect is the
  boundary, not astral text itself.

Dedup: `gh search issues "surrogate"` returns only closed #1966 (log.ts
`clip`); no open or closed issue covers the messaging.ts sites.

## Why it matters

- The delivered body (2250) is the highest-stakes site: cross-session
  messages are this fork's coordination substrate, message text routinely
  carries emoji, and the mangled character is what the receiving session
  reads and may quote onward.
- The codebase treats pair-splitting as a defect wherever it has looked:
  `messaging/search.ts:17` ("one character, never two halves of a surrogate
  pair"), `session/compaction.ts:886` ("Count code points so a surrogate
  pair is never split"), and #1966 in the sibling log module. messaging.ts
  is the remaining unguarded cutter in the same subsystem.
- A shared guard already exists one module away: `splitsPair` in
  `messaging/log.ts` (module-private today). Exporting/reusing it keeps one
  disposition — drop the pair whole — instead of a fifth spelling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No truncation in `packages/core/src/messaging.ts` can return a lone
      surrogate: for any input, the preview (561), toast (619), rerank
      text (1071), `firstLine` (2221) and delivered body (2250) outputs
      are well-formed (`isWellFormed()`), with a straddling pair dropped
      whole — reusing the `splitsPair` guard from `messaging/log.ts`
      rather than a new spelling.
- [ ] The delivered body's `[N more characters]` count stays accurate
      when the boundary adjustment drops the straddling pair (count
      computed from the adjusted cut, as #1966's marker recount does).
- [ ] Regression tests pin each site (or the shared helper plus one
      service-level path per surface) with an astral character straddling
      the budget; oracle: well-formedness + the sibling no-split rule in
      search.ts/compaction.ts. Existing messaging suites stay green.

## Out of scope (observed siblings, separate disposition)

Same-shaped unguarded cuts exist in `packages/core/src/tool-output.ts:107`,
`packages/core/src/session/title.ts:35` and
`packages/core/src/codemode/catalog.ts:69`. They are different surfaces
(tool output bounding, session titles, codemode catalog); disposition them
separately rather than expanding this fix.

## Finding

Open PR #1779 — the only fix for the meta quota rolling/weekly window-key collision (#1777) — changes two lines and adds no test, despite its own body promising test coverage ("add test coverage for the weekly-length rolling duration collision case"). Neither collision site is pinned by any test on current main, so the fix can merge and later regress with every suite green.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1779 (OPEN, head a73202025608855117e9d25821f1408f193cd3e5, untouched since 2026-11-05T21:44:11Z, no labels). Its complete diff is 2 lines in `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/meta.ts` (prefixing the rolling window key with `rolling:` at the `parseSubscriptionQuota` site and the `keyUsageResult` site) — no test file is touched.
- Verified on current main 684598b1f3abf34a3eb7d8c1d0f4382e1fc3b826 (commits API, read twice): the collision is still live at both sites — `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/meta.ts:99` and `:233` both key the rolling window by `windowSeconds ? resolveWindowLabel(windowSeconds) : "rolling"` with no prefix, so a weekly-length (604800s) rolling window is overwritten by the literal `weekly` entry written immediately after.
- No existing test covers the collision: in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` at main, every `parseSubscriptionQuota` case uses `window_duration_secs: 18000` (the 5h shape), and the key-endpoint `subs_usage` describe (line 160) never sets `window_duration_mins`, so its rolling key is always `"rolling"`. No meta case uses a 604800s / 10080-minute rolling duration.
- The shared probe matrix landed by PR #1796 explicitly lists meta's collision sites as known-lossy under #1777 and does not assert them conforming, so the matrix does not catch this regression class either.
- Dedupe (2026-11-07): issue searches for "meta rolling weekly collision test" and "1779" return #1777 (the bug itself, OPEN), #1794 (design), and closed unrelated #1907/#1855 — nothing tracks the missing test coverage for the fix.

## Why it matters

#1777 is a silent data-loss bug (a published quota window is erased). Its fix landing untested means the next refactor of meta.ts window keying — an active area: #1849, #1855 and #1907 all changed meta.ts after PR #1779 opened — can reintroduce the overwrite undetected. The PR body already promised this coverage; it was never delivered.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test pins the portal site: `parseSubscriptionQuota` with `window_duration_secs: 604800` plus weekly figures publishes BOTH windows under distinct keys, each with its own usedPercent/resetAt.
- [ ] A test pins the key-endpoint site: `provider.fetchQuota` with `subs_usage.window.window_duration_mins: 10080` plus a weekly object publishes BOTH windows under distinct keys.
- [ ] Both tests fail against pre-fix main code and pass with PR #1779's change (mutation check).
- [ ] The tests land with PR #1779 or in a follow-up merged immediately after it; existing `packages/ai` quota tests still pass.

body:
# fix(core): messaging log clip() can split a surrogate pair at all three of its cuts — delivered log text starts or ends with a lone surrogate

## Summary

`MessagingLog.clip` (`packages/core/src/messaging/log.ts:165-180`) shortens a
log entry to a head + omission marker + tail with plain code-unit slices.
None of its three cuts avoids a surrogate-pair boundary, so an astral
character (any code point above U+FFFF — emoji, 𝄞, CJK ext.) that straddles
a cut is split: the kept text ends with a lone high surrogate or starts
with a lone low surrogate. The result is not well-formed text
(`isWellFormed() === false`) and the character re-encodes as U+FFFD the
moment the clipped entry is serialized or displayed.

`clip` is the delivery path for messaging log reads:
`packages/core/src/messaging.ts:1901` clips every entry returned by the
log service (per-entry budget normalised to 1..8000 chars by
`normalizeChars`, messaging.ts:127-136), so the corrupted text is what
sessions and users actually receive — not an internal diagnostic.

## The three unguarded cuts (main 684598b1f3)

- `log.ts:179` — head: `` `${text.slice(0, head)}${marker}...` `` can end
  on a lone high surrogate.
- `log.ts:179` — tail: `text.slice(-tail)` can start on a lone low
  surrogate.
- `log.ts:178` — the marker-too-big fallback `text.slice(0, chars)` can
  end on a lone high surrogate.

## Repro (verified this run)

Probe `probe-clip.ts` / `probe-clip3.ts` in laptop worktree
`probe-2026-11-07-creator-1935` (HEAD 684598b1f3 = current main), calling
the real `MessagingLog.clip` with U+1D11E (𝄞, D834 DD1E) placed at each
boundary:

- Head split: pad so the pair straddles the head cut, budgets 50 / 60 /
  100 → output head ends `...\ud834`, `isWellFormed() === false`.
- Tail split: text `a×300 + 𝄞` (pair at the very end), budgets 70–73 →
  output tail is exactly `\udd1e` (lone low surrogate),
  `isWellFormed() === false`.
- Fallback split: budget 10 with the pair straddling position 10 →
  output `"aaaaaaaaa\ud834"`, `isWellFormed() === false`.
- Control: pure-BMP text clips cleanly and well-formed at every budget.

Existing tests (`packages/core/test/messaging-log.test.ts:174-195`) pin
clip's length, marker-count accuracy and head/tail content — with BMP-only
fixtures, so no case exercises a pair at a boundary.

## Why it matters

- This codebase already treats pair-splitting as a defect everywhere it
  has looked: `packages/core/src/messaging/search.ts:17` ("a character
  outside the basic plane is one character, never two halves of a
  surrogate pair"), `packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts:886`
  ("Count code points so a surrogate pair is never split"), and the ai
  package sanitizes with `toWellFormed()` (`packages/ai/src/utils/sanitize.ts:5`).
  `clip` is the same shape of cut, unguarded.
- Log entries are message text written by sessions and users (emoji are
  routine there); a clipped read silently mangles exactly one character
  at the seam, and the mangled form is what gets quoted onward.
- Sibling history: #957 hardened this same function's budget inputs
  (NaN/fractional chars); the cut boundaries were not part of that pass.
  Same defect class as openchamber #1803 (its shared bounded-output
  accumulator), in this repo's own code.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `clip` never returns a string with a lone surrogate: for any input
      and any budget in the service's 1..8000 range, the output is
      well-formed (`isWellFormed()`), and a pair straddling a cut is
      dropped whole (never half-kept) at the head cut, the tail cut,
      and the marker-too-big fallback cut.
- [ ] The existing clip contract still holds: output length ≤ budget,
      and the omission marker's count stays accurate when a boundary
      adjustment shrinks the head or tail (marker recomputed from the
      adjusted lengths, as the current shrink loop does).
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/core/test/messaging-log.test.ts`
      pin all three boundaries with an astral character straddling each
      cut (oracle: well-formedness + the sibling no-split rule in
      search.ts/compaction.ts), and the existing messaging-log suite
      stays green.

## Out of scope (observed siblings, separate disposition)

Two inline diagnostic tails use the same unguarded tail slice —
`packages/core/src/mcp/stdio.ts:150` (MCP server stderr tail) and
`packages/core/src/messaging/embedding.ts:798` (llama-server stderr
tail). They feed error/log text only; disposition them separately rather
than expanding this fix.

## Remainder of #1825 — remove the binary dependencies from the antigravity + vibe credential paths

Filed as the routed implementation follow-up of #1825 (re-triage of queue task 10989, 2026-11-08). #1825 stays open as the audit record; this issue owns the implementation.

### Status of #1825's slices

- Narrow error-quality slice: DONE — PR #1844 merged (946b49c7): missing-binary errors now name `secret-tool` / the `agy` binary and the remedies.
- Architectural remainder: this issue. It was recorded BLOCKED on a design choice among (a)–(d); **Drew ruled on 2026-11-06** (https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/issues/1825#issuecomment-6686794578), ruling the OUTCOME instead of picking a mechanism:

> "ensure this will be the last time we have to run a binary Command for a provider"

No provider may depend on running a binary command for auth. Amending the doctrine to sanction these exceptions (option d) is ruled out as a standalone answer. Per-provider mechanics are the fleet's, under that constraint.

### Gap on current main (684598b1f3abf34a3eb7d8c1d0f4382e1fc3b826, verified x2 2026-11-08)

- `packages/ai/src/providers/antigravity-auth.ts:156-164` — every credential load `execFile`s `secret-tool lookup service gemini username antigravity` (15s timeout).
- `packages/ai/src/providers/antigravity-auth.ts:175-270` — `findAgyBinary()` + `binaryIntel()` extract OAuth client-secret candidates from the `agy` binary's bytes; `refresh()` (:316, :414) depends on them, so an expired token cannot refresh where the binary is absent.
- `packages/ai/src/providers/vibe-auth.ts:118-131` — tier-4 resolution `execFile`s `secret-tool lookup`. This is the deployed tier: the fleet config keeps `MISTRAL_API_KEY` out of the server env (#1653).
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/antigravity.ts:1,124` — imports `execFile` from `node:child_process` and `execFile`s `secret-tool` (graceful `null`).

### Chosen no-spawn route (specified in triage)

1. **Keyring reads move in-process** at all three sites: read the Secret Service keyring via a D-Bus client binding in-process (session bus, `org.freedesktop.secrets`), deleting every `child_process`/`execFile` use. If a D-Bus client proves infeasible in the Bun runtime, the fallback route is a provisioned credential-file tier read in place (the `claude-code`/`commandcode` pattern — file read only, zero spawns) made the deployed default, with the subprocess keyring tier removed. Either way: no child process is spawned.
2. **Antigravity refresh without the `agy` binary:** the OAuth client secret is provisioned at sign-in time into the provider's own credential store (credential-file field or env `ANTIGRAVITY_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`); `findAgyBinary`/`binaryIntel` byte extraction is removed from the refresh path.

# fix(ai): image routes double the version segment — BFL, Replicate and Stability baseURLs ending in /v1 or /v2beta post to /v1/v1/... and /v2beta/v2beta/...

## Summary

The image routes for Black Forest Labs, Replicate and Stability carry the
API version segment in the protocol PATH and compose the request URL by
plain concatenation, with no de-duplication. A provider configured with a
baseURL that ends in the version segment — the shape the image family's
own OpenAI, xAI, Google, Meta and Runway protocols require, and the shape
their tests use — renders a doubled version segment
(`.../v1/v1/flux-2-pro`, `.../v2beta/v2beta/stable-image/...`) that no
upstream accepts (404). This is the image-route sibling of #1956
(Anthropic Messages LLM route) and #1959 (Deepgram/ElevenLabs/AssemblyAI
speech/transcription routes); neither covers the image protocols.

## The inconsistent convention (all on main 6631ec3d42)

Version segment in PATH, base is the bare origin:

- `packages/ai/src/protocols/bfl-images.ts:13` — base
  `https://api.bfl.ai`, path (`:213`) `` `/v1/${request.model.id}` ``
- `packages/ai/src/protocols/replicate-images.ts:12` — base
  `https://api.replicate.com`, path (`:216-217`)
  `/v1/models/${id}/predictions` or `/v1/predictions`
- `packages/ai/src/protocols/stability-images.ts:12` — base
  `https://api.stability.ai`, generate path (`:207`)
  `/v2beta/stable-image/generate/${endpoint}`, upscale path (`:219`)
  `/v2beta/stable-image/upscale/creative`, poll path (`:13`, `:197-198`)
  `/v2beta/results/${id}`

Version segment in the BASE, path carries none:

- `packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-images.ts` — base
  `https://api.openai.com/v1`, path `/images/generations`
  (same split in `xai-images.ts`, `meta-images.ts:12`,
  `google-images.ts:12` base `.../v1beta`, `runway-video.ts:12` base
  `.../v1`, `zai-images.ts:9` base `.../api/paas/v4`)

Composition (no de-duplication anywhere on main): submit goes through
`Endpoint.render` (`packages/ai/src/route/endpoint.ts:58`, called from
`packages/ai/src/route/media.ts:372`), which is plain
`trimBaseUrl(baseURL) + path`; poll/follow-up URLs are built separately at
`packages/ai/src/route/media.ts:314` as `trimBaseUrl(baseURL) + path`,
and `trimBaseUrl` (`endpoint.ts:49`) strips trailing slashes only.

The family's own tests teach the version-in-base shape for the second
group — `packages/ai/test/image.test.ts:49,132,273,352` configure OpenAI,
xAI and Google image models with baseURLs ending in `/v1` resp.
`/v1beta` — while the version-in-path providers are configured bare
(`image.test.ts:896,936`). A user who configures BFL, Replicate or
Stability the same way as OpenAI silently gets the doubled path.

## Repro (verified this run)

Probe test `probe-image-version.test.ts` in laptop worktree
`probe-2026-11-07-creator-1835` (HEAD 6631ec3d42 = current main), using
the image test harness with a recording HTTP handler:

- BFL, `baseURL: "https://bfl.test/v1"` →
  `POST https://bfl.test/v1/v1/flux-2-pro`
  (bare control → `POST https://bfl.test/v1/flux-2-pro`, correct)
- Replicate (official model), `baseURL: "https://replicate.test/v1"` →
  `POST https://replicate.test/v1/v1/models/owner/model/predictions`
  (bare control → `POST https://replicate.test/v1/models/owner/model/predictions`, correct)
- Stability generate, `baseURL: "https://stability.test/v2beta"` →
  `POST https://stability.test/v2beta/v2beta/stable-image/generate/sd3`
  (bare control → `POST https://stability.test/v2beta/stable-image/generate/sd3`, correct)

By the same composition, the Stability upscale submit
(`/v2beta/stable-image/upscale/creative`) and the Stability results poll
(`/v2beta/results/<id>`, built at `media.ts:314`, not via
`Endpoint.render`) double identically; those two were verified by code
read, not by probe (the upscale start requires an image input, so its
submit URL was not captured).

## Relation to PR #1960 (open, fixes #1956)

PR #1960 adds a render-time de-duplication to `Endpoint.render` — but it
only handles a trailing `/v1` base against a `/v1...` path. If it merges
as-is it would cover the BFL and Replicate *submit* URLs above, and
nothing else in this issue:

- Stability's segment is `/v2beta`, not `/v1` — generate, upscale and
  results-poll URLs still double.
- Poll/follow-up URLs are composed at `media.ts:314`, bypassing
  `Endpoint.render` entirely — the Stability results poll doubles even
  for a hypothetical `/v1` protocol.

This issue is filed per the fleet rule that an open PR does not suppress
a filing; whoever dispositions #1960 should disposition this scope
question with it (extend the de-dup to the media composition and to
non-`/v1` segments, or scope it explicitly to #1956 and leave this issue
for the image/media remainder).

## Why it matters

- Image generation through these three providers 404s for anyone who
  configures them by analogy with the family's OpenAI/xAI/Google
  protocols — the version-in-base shape is the convention most of the
  family mandates, and nothing in the provider config docs or types
  warns that these three differ.
- The failure is silent at configure time: the model constructs fine and
  only the first real call fails, against a URL the user never sees
  unless they capture traffic.
- This is the third filing in the same recurrence class (#1956 LLM,
  #1959 speech/transcription): the convention (where the version segment
  lives) exists only per-protocol by implication, and each protocol
  family re-derives it differently. A route-layer fix that only handles
  `/v1` at `Endpoint.render` leaves the class open.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A BFL, Replicate or Stability image model configured with a
      baseURL ending in the protocol's version segment (`/v1`, resp.
      `/v2beta`) renders single-version URLs for submit and — for
      Stability — results-poll calls, or the configure path
      rejects/normalizes that shape with a test pinning the behaviour.
      Either disposition is acceptable; the doubled URL must be
      unreachable.
- [ ] Rendered URLs for the version-suffixed shape are pinned by tests
      for at least BFL (generate submit), Replicate (official-model
      submit) and Stability (generate submit + results poll), with the
      bare-baseURL controls unchanged.
- [ ] No change to the correct version-in-base protocols (OpenAI, xAI,
      Google, Meta, ZAI, Runway, Fal).
- [ ] The disposition is coordinated with PR #1960 / #1956 and #1959 so
      the three filings in this class converge on one convention,
      recorded where the next protocol author will see it (route/media
      or protocol header comment).
- [ ] Full `packages/ai` suite: no new failures beyond the baseline
      attributable to #1956 (whose 12 red tests PR #1960 addresses).

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `v1/v1`, `v2beta/v2beta`, `image
route`, `stability`, `replicate`, `black forest`, and `baseURL version`:
the only hits in this class are #1956 (Anthropic Messages LLM route
only), #1959 (speech/transcription media routes only — Deepgram,
ElevenLabs, AssemblyAI; its acceptance criteria name no image protocol),
closed #1813 (the earlier Anthropic default-endpoint instance), and open
PR #1960 (the `/v1`-only `Endpoint.render` fix for #1956, analysed
above). No filing covers the image protocols.

# fix(ai): Anthropic Messages route doubles /v1 — every provider baseURL ending in /v1 posts to /v1/v1/messages (12 ai tests red on main)

## Summary

The Anthropic Messages protocol route appends its PATH `/v1/messages` to the
configured baseURL with no de-duplication, so every provider whose baseURL
already ends in `/v1` produces `.../v1/v1/messages` at runtime — a URL no
Anthropic-compatible upstream accepts (404). This is the exact failure the
protocol file's own comment records from #6117 (claude-code provider), and it
has recurred at every baseURL-only call site that carries the version segment
itself instead of overriding the path.

## Evidence (verified on main 23a4f6ef82, laptop primary, this run)

Contract, `packages/ai/src/protocols/anthropic-messages.ts:37-46`:

- Comment: "The protocol's endpoint render appends PATH ("/messages") to this
  base, so the base is the API origin only — "https://api.anthropic.com/v1"
  here produced https://api.anthropic.com/v1/v1/messages at runtime
  (Anthropic 404), which broke every AnthropicMessages consumer that relied
  on the default (notably the claude-code provider, #6117)."
- `PATH = "/v1/messages"`; "Endpoint.render concatenates baseURL + path with
  no de-duplication … the version segment lives here exactly once."

Violating sites (baseURL ends in `/v1`, route path not overridden):

1. `packages/ai/src/providers/cloudflare-ai-gateway.ts:50,110,120` —
   passthrough segment `"anthropic/v1"` → baseURL
   `https://gateway.ai.cloudflare.com/v1/{account}/{gateway}/anthropic/v1`,
   render → `.../anthropic/v1/v1/messages`.
2. `packages/ai/src/providers/amazon-bedrock-mantle.ts:123` — baseURL factory
   `https://bedrock-mantle.${region}.api.aws/anthropic/v1`, render →
   `.../anthropic/v1/v1/messages`.
3. `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic-compatible.ts` (`compatibleRoute`,
   `configure`) — a user-supplied baseURL ending in `/v1` (the shape every
   Anthropic-compatible vendor documents) renders `.../v1/v1/messages`.
4. `packages/ai/src/providers/alibaba.ts:102` — default messages baseURL
   `https://${host}/apps/anthropic/v1`, endpoint overridden by baseURL only;
   same construction, no test currently pins its rendered URL.

Safe pattern already in-tree (path override): `minimax.ts:82`,
`moonshot.ts:86`, `zai-coding-plan.ts:45` use
`Endpoint.path("/messages", { baseURL: ".../anthropic/v1" })`.

## Repro

On the laptop primary at main 23a4f6ef82:

- `bun test` in `packages/ai`: **2293 pass, 12 fail**. Every failure is this
  class:
  - `Cloudflare > posts Claude and OpenAI models to the provider-native gateway endpoints`
    — received `https://gateway.ai.cloudflare.com/v1/test-account/default/anthropic/v1/v1/messages`,
    expected `.../anthropic/v1/messages` (test/provider/cloudflare.test.ts:129).
    The OpenAI responses URL in the same test is correct.
  - `Amazon Bedrock Mantle provider > uses the Mantle endpoint…` + 4
    `Bedrock Mantle Messages recorded` tests — received
    `https://bedrock-mantle.us-west-1.api.aws/anthropic/v1/v1/messages`.
  - `provider package entrypoints > maps Anthropic-compatible settings onto the executable model`
    — baseURL `https://messages.example.test/v1` rendered
    `https://messages.example.test/v1/v1/messages`, expected
    `https://messages.example.test/v1/messages` (test/provider-package.test.ts:264).
  - 3 `MiniMax M3 Anthropic-compatible recorded` + 2 `Cloudflare AI Gateway
    Claude Haiku 4.5 recorded` tests (same provider-package mapping path).
- Single-file reruns reproduce deterministically (cloudflare.test.ts,
  bedrock-mantle.test.ts, provider-package.test.ts).

## Why it matters

- Every Anthropic-model call through the Cloudflare AI Gateway native
  passthrough and through Amazon Bedrock Mantle's Messages route goes to a
  doubled path and 404s — these providers are broken for Claude models, not
  degraded.
- The generic `anthropic-compatible` package — the door for any vendor whose
  documented base URL ends in `/v1` — is broken for the standard documented
  shape.
- 12 red tests on main mask future regressions in the ai suite (test.yml is
  dispatch+nightly per #1927, so this does not surface per-PR).
- The #6117 comment shows this is a recurrence class: the convention lives in
  a comment, nothing enforces it, and each new provider re-derives it wrong.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All 12 failing tests above pass; full `packages/ai` suite green
      (2293+ pass, 0 fail) on the fix branch.
- [ ] Cloudflare gateway Anthropic passthrough renders
      `.../anthropic/v1/messages`; Bedrock Mantle messages renders
      `.../anthropic/v1/messages`; an anthropic-compatible baseURL ending in
      `/v1` renders `.../v1/messages`.
- [ ] Alibaba's messages route rendered URL is pinned by a test and correct
      against the DashScope `/apps/anthropic` convention (fix or explicit
      disposition in the PR).
- [ ] The fix addresses the class, not only the instances: either the route
      composition de-duplicates a trailing `/v1` on the baseURL, or every
      in-tree baseURL conforms to the bare-origin convention AND a test/lint
      pins that no AnthropicMessages consumer supplies a `/v1`-suffixed
      baseURL without a path override.
- [ ] No change to the correct OpenAI Responses/Chat compositions or to the
      safe Endpoint.path("/messages") providers (minimax, moonshot, zai).

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `v1/v1`, doubled/duplicate path,
bedrock-mantle, anthropic-compatible titles: no existing issue covers this.
#6117 (referenced in the code comment) covered the claude-code default-base
instance only. Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode, 2026-11-07.

## Summary

Every Command Code generate call made through the fork's protocol route sends the **server process's absolute cwd path and the sorted top-level listing of that directory** to `api.commandcode.ai` by default. This is a wire-emulation requirement (the gateway validates the config block), but the disclosure has never been dispositioned: nothing records whether the full path + listing are actually required, whether a minimized block passes the gateway, or that users/deployments are told this leaves the machine on every turn.

## Evidence (verified this run on laptop primary `~/git/opencode` at main c342ba5db7; file unchanged since fe9f61be50)

- `packages/ai/src/protocols/commandcode.ts:288-312` — `buildServerConfig()` builds the block from the server process: `workingDir = process.cwd()`, `structure` = `readdirSync(workingDir)` mapped to entry names, filtered to non-hidden and non-`node_modules`, sorted. Git fields take the hardcoded non-git fallback (`isGitRepo: false`, empty branch/status, `recentCommits: []`).
- `packages/ai/src/protocols/commandcode.ts:397` — `config: options.serverConfig ?? buildServerConfig()`: the locally built block is the default on every `/alpha/generate` request unless a deployment supplies the whole object via the `serverConfig` provider option.
- `packages/ai/src/protocols/commandcode.ts:22-30` (header comment) — the gateway validates all nine fields (a bare `{}` is a 400, probed live 2026-11-05). Presence is validated; whether an **empty `structure` array** or a **non-identifying `workingDir`** also passes has never been probed.
- `packages/ai/test/provider/commandcode.test.ts:84-91` — the test suite pins the current behavior (`config.workingDir` is `process.cwd()`, `structure` is an array), so the disclosure is load-bearing in tests, not incidental.

## Why it matters

- The server process's cwd is not necessarily the end user's project: for a shared/server deployment it is the deployment's own directory, and for a server started from `$HOME` the top-level listing of the user's home directory goes to a third-party API on every turn.
- The sibling fields show minimization was possible where the shape allowed it (git fields are inert fallbacks). The two identifying fields were carried at full fidelity without a recorded decision.
- Origin: flagged as a REVIEW-FINDING in the 2026-11-07 pr-diff-review of PR #1749 ("consciously accept or file") and left unfiled; #1946 covers a different defect from the same PR (threadId/permissionMode). This issue records the finding for an explicit disposition.

## Acceptance criteria

- Triage records ONE disposition on this issue:
  - (a) **Accept**: the full `workingDir` + `structure` are required (or the risk is accepted as-is) — the disclosure is then documented where a deployment/user can see it (provider docs and/or the header comment), naming exactly what is sent; or
  - (b) **Minimize**: probe the gateway with a minimized block (empty `structure`, non-identifying `workingDir`) and send the least it accepts, keeping all nine fields present; or

- Whichever disposition: tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/commandcode.test.ts` pin it (the cwd/structure expectations updated deliberately, not just relaxed), and the ai provider/protocol suites stay green.
- No change to the nine-field presence the gateway requires unless a live probe evidences the gateway accepting fewer.

## Finding

The commandcode protocol silently discards a caller-supplied non-UUID `threadId` and forwards any arbitrary string as `permissionMode`, with no test covering either option. This is the same class of silent downgrade PR #1749 explicitly fails closed on for `tool_choice` ("failing closed instead of silently downgrading it to auto").

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1749 (merged, merge commit 8185486080ab686d3a160f16deb5357f1199fda3, head c6acfa2a8661) introduced `packages/ai/src/protocols/commandcode.ts`.
- Verified present on current main fe9f61be507c74c94628fd07a5fdf8c724c7ef00 (read twice):
  - `packages/ai/src/protocols/commandcode.ts:402` — `threadId: options.threadId !== undefined && UUID_PATTERN.test(options.threadId) ? options.threadId : undefined` — a non-UUID threadId is silently dropped; a fresh thread starts and session continuity is lost with no error surface.
  - `packages/ai/src/protocols/commandcode.ts:111-112` — `permissionMode: Schema.optional(Schema.String)` with a comment documenting only `"standard" | "auto-accept" | "plan"`, and `:401` forwards `options.permissionMode ?? "standard"` unvalidated, so a typo surfaces only as an opaque gateway error.
- Tests: `packages/ai/test/provider/commandcode.test.ts` has no test referencing `threadId` (valid, invalid, or absent) or a `permissionMode` override (review of PR #1749's diff: 13 stream/lowering tests, none touch either option).
- Dedupe (2026-11-07): GitHub issue searches for "commandcode threadId" and "commandcode permissionMode" return no issues; no open or recently closed issue covers this.

## Why it matters

A typo'd or legacy-format thread id produces confusing context loss (a silently fresh conversation) instead of a local invalid-request error, and an invalid permissionMode fails remotely and opaquely. Both contradict the provider's own fail-closed doctrine established in the same PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A non-UUID `threadId` is rejected locally with a clear invalid-request error (or, if silent-drop is a deliberate disposition, it is documented in the option's doc comment and pinned by a test stating that disposition).
- [ ] `permissionMode` is validated against the documented set (`standard`, `auto-accept`, `plan`) at the schema/lowering layer; invalid values fail locally.
- [ ] New tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/commandcode.test.ts` cover: valid UUID threadId forwarded, invalid threadId disposition, valid permissionMode forwarded, invalid permissionMode rejected.

## Summary

PR #1944 (for #1823) renamed the fleet-built provider ids to leading-underscore ids — `claude-code → _claude`, `commandcode → _commandcode`, `antigravity → _antigravity`, `muse-direct → _muse`, `vibe → _vibe` — and its commit states the rule: "providerMetadataKey follows the id, incl. the antigravity protocol route defaults". The antigravity protocol route was updated, but the other two protocol-owned routes were missed: the bare exported routes for Claude Code and Command Code still carry the pre-rename provider id and providerMetadataKey, so the same wire protocol presents two different provider identities depending on which public entry point a caller composes from.

## Evidence (verified at main fe9f61be507c, 2026-11-07)

Sites:

- `packages/ai/src/protocols/claude-code-messages.ts:110-113` — `Route.make({ provider: "claude-code", providerMetadataKey: "claude-code", ... })`
- `packages/ai/src/protocols/commandcode.ts:732-735` — `Route.make({ provider: "commandcode", providerMetadataKey: "commandcode", ... })`
- Re-exported unchanged as the providers' public route surface: `packages/ai/src/providers/claude-code.ts:89` (`export const route = ClaudeCodeMessages.route`) and `packages/ai/src/providers/commandcode.ts:85` (`export const route = CommandCode.route`), each also in `routes`.

Probe (`probe-rename.ts`, laptop worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-07-creator-0835` of origin/main fe9f61be507c, run with bun against the package sources):

```
claude bare provider.route:        provider=claude-code  metadataKey=claude-code
claude protocol route:             provider=claude-code  metadataKey=claude-code
claude configured model.route:     provider=_claude      metadataKey=_claude
commandcode bare provider.route:   provider=commandcode  metadataKey=commandcode
commandcode protocol route:        provider=commandcode  metadataKey=commandcode
commandcode configured model.route: provider=_commandcode metadataKey=_commandcode
antigravity configured model.route: provider=_antigravity metadataKey=_antigravity
muse-direct configured model.route: provider=_muse       metadataKey=_muse
vibe exported route:               provider=_vibe        metadataKey=_vibe
vibe configured model.route:       provider=_vibe        metadataKey=_vibe
ids: _claude _commandcode _antigravity _muse _vibe
```

Why the configured models are correct today: `Route.with` in `packages/ai/src/route/client.ts:402-412` derives the metadata key from a changed `provider` patch, and both providers' `configuredRoute` passes `provider: id`. The bare routes have no such derivation applied — they are the defaults the rename commit updated for antigravity (`protocols/antigravity.ts` route now `_antigravity`/`_antigravity`) but not for these two.

## Why it matters

- The exported `route`/`routes` are the provider packages' public composition surface (every fleet provider exports them uniformly). A host, façade, or test composing from the bare route gets models whose provider id is the retired string and whose response/thinking metadata is stamped under the retired key (`anthropic-messages.ts` reads and writes `providerMetadata[route.providerMetadataKey]` for signatures, redacted data, server-tool results, and usage) — metadata written under `claude-code` is not read back by a configured `_claude` model, and vice versa.
- The rename's purpose (#1823) is that the leading underscore marks fleet-built providers everywhere the id appears; two of five renamed providers still present the old identity on one of their two surfaces, which is exactly the split the rename was meant to end.
- No test pins the bare-route identity for these two providers: the provider tests assert the configured model's provider only, so the split is invisible to the suite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Triage records the disposition: the two protocol routes follow the rename (provider + providerMetadataKey become `_claude` / `_commandcode`, matching the antigravity protocol route), or the bare protocol route is recorded as a deliberate separate namespace with its reason on this issue.
- [ ] If fixing: `ClaudeCode.route` / `ClaudeCodeMessages.route` and `Commandcode.route` / `CommandCode.route` report the renamed provider and metadata key, and the configured-model behaviour is unchanged (the `Route.with` derivation already yields the same values).
- [ ] Tests pin the bare-route identity for both providers (mirroring how the antigravity/muse-direct tests pin the configured route's `providerMetadataKey`), and the existing ai provider + protocol suites stay green.
- [ ] No other surface changes: quota ids/aliases/disabledBy pins from PR #1944, the CLI display strip, and the config-layer ids in core are out of scope.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for "providerMetadataKey", "metadata key", and "bare route" on 2026-11-07: no existing issue records this split. #1823 (still open, the naming-convention design) and PR #1944 (its rename implementation) are the origin; this is a follow-up gap in that implementation, not a duplicate of either.

# test(ai): quota figure contract — figure inventory + shared figure probe matrix for the 13 quota providers (design #1942, phase 1)

Phase 1 of design #1942 ("a figure that cannot exist is not a figure"). Design doc: `files/designs/opencode-quota-figure-contract.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace.

## Task

For the thirteen provider quota parsers in `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/`:

(a) State the design's six figure-contract rules where the parsers live — in `packages/ai/src/quota/types.ts` beside the window contract (#1794), in the module's existing comment style:
1. Impossible figures read as absent (zero is a real figure and publishes).
2. A pair is judged as a pair; the impossible-pair disposition is whole-window and named per provider in the inventory — never split between percent and label.
3. Scaling inputs are figures too (wire exponent/divisor/multiplier validated to its closed range before scaling; out-of-range reads the scaled figure as absent, sibling figures still publish).
4. Precision is part of the figure (rounding is a display act, never a parser act).
5. A result whose only figure is impossible is no result (the provider's existing no-data contract fires).
6. Every figure path is pinned against this contract. Named exception: turso's stated publish-truthfully over-100% disposition stands.

(b) Add a figure section to the *same* parser inventory in `types.ts` (not a second table): per provider, the figures it publishes (percent / money amount / balance / count) and each figure's named disposition for the impossible cases. Mark the known-lossy rows with links and do NOT assert them as conforming: deepseek negative balance → #1928, codex negative credits → #1924, claude negative spend → #1919, groq pair → #1897, opendesign pair → #1879, claude exponent → #1920, antigravity precision → #1941 (design phases 2–3 adopt those issues; they keep their own lifecycles).

(c) Add the shared figure probe matrix in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` (or a wired sibling): one case per rule (negative figure reads as absent; zero control publishes unchanged; impossible pair under one consistent disposition; out-of-range scaling input reads the scaled figure as absent; sub-percent precision preserved) run against the parsers that already conform — meta `parseBillingBanner` (negative minor → null), opencode-go `toMicroCents` (negative → null) and its balance path, command-code's clamp-both windows (#1821), turso's `numNonNegative` path — with the suite header naming the contract as the oracle.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The inventory's figure section covers all 13 registered providers with figures-published + named dispositions, and marks the seven known-lossy rows with links (#1928, #1924, #1919, #1897, #1879, #1920, #1941).
- [ ] The probe matrix passes on current main for the conforming parsers listed, with one named case per contract rule per parser family, and its header names the contract as the oracle.
- [ ] The matrix demonstrably fails if a conforming parser's figure disposition changes without the contract changing.

# design(ai): a figure that cannot exist is not a figure — one figure contract for the quota parsers' amounts, balances, counts and percents

Design doc: `files/designs/opencode-quota-figure-contract.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. Grounded on main `05702ca18d`. Filed by the repo design architect (2026-11-07 pass) after reading ROADMAP.md / TODO.md / planning, the central register (`files/potential-projects.md`), the `kind/design` list, and the quota sources on current main.

## Summary

#1794 stated the window contract — what a parser may put into `usage.windows`, under what key — and deliberately scoped balances out of windows (its rule 4). No design has ever stated the contract for the **figures themselves**: every number a quota parser publishes, in a window's percent fields, in a `valueLabel` amount / balance / count, and in the wire scalars that scale those numbers. In the two days since #1794 phase 1 landed (#1795), that unstated layer produced fifteen filings, seven still open:

- **Negative money publishes as a successful read** — deepseek #1928 (its own `> 0` filter bypassed by the unfiltered fallback: `"$-5.00"`, `ok: true`), codex #1924 (`"-5"` credits label), claude #1919 (`"$-5.00 / $10.00"`, negative-only payload mints the window); openrouter #1913 closed as the same defect.
- **Pairs are never judged as pairs** — groq #1897 (`"150 / 100 requests remaining"` beside 0% used / 100% remaining), opendesign #1879 (`"-50 / 100 credits"` at 100% used); codex #1882 closed as the same split.
- **A scaling input is trusted blindly** — claude #1920: `toAmount` divides by `10 ** exponent` with the wire exponent unvalidated (999 erases a real $5/$10 spend to `"$0.00 / $0.00"`; −2 inflates it 100×).
- **Precision is discarded at publication** — antigravity #1941: `Math.round(remainingFraction * 100)` at both conversion sites (99.9% used publishes as 100% / 0% remaining; 0.1% as 0%), while every sibling keeps the float percent and the CLI rounds only for display (#1797).
- **The shared layer was already rescued once** — #1904: `toUsageWindow` derived `remainingPercent` above 100%.

The precedents exist one provider at a time, exactly as the window rules did before #1794: meta `parseBillingBanner` returns null for `minor < 0`; opencode-go `toMicroCents` returns null for `amount < 0`; turso carries a private `numNonNegative`; command-code gates `monthlyRemaining >= 0` (#1744) and clamps percent *and* label from one figure (#1821); deepseek filters `total_balance > 0` (#1800). The shared layer (`packages/ai/src/quota/utils.ts`, read verbatim on current main) offers `toNumber` (negative included), `clampPercent` and `formatMoney` (formats a negative verbatim) — no amount reader, no pair check, no precision rule. Each open filing asks its fixer to re-derive the same dispositions alone, in one provider, again.

## The contract

**A figure that cannot exist is not a figure.** For every number a quota parser publishes — percent, amount, balance, count, in a field or in a `valueLabel` — and for every wire scalar that scales one:

1. **Impossible figures read as absent.** Negative money / balance / spend publishes as absent, never as a formatted label (meta / opencode-go / turso / command-code precedent, generalised). Zero is a real figure and publishes unchanged.
2. **A pair is judged as a pair.** `remaining ≤ limit` etc.: individual well-formedness is not enough. The disposition of an impossible pair is whole-window and *named per provider in the inventory* — read-as-absent, or clamp-with-the-real-figure-annotated (#1744's shape) — never split between percent (clamped) and label (raw). Extends #1794 rule 5 from derived fields to the raw pair.
3. **Scaling inputs are figures too.** An exponent / divisor / multiplier from the wire is validated against its closed range before it scales anything (money exponents: ISO 4217 0–3). Out of range reads the *scaled figure* as absent; sibling figures on the same window still publish.
4. **Precision is part of the figure.** A published percent keeps the wire's precision; rounding is a display act (CLI, #1797), never a parser act.
5. **A result whose only figure is impossible is no result.** Refusing impossible figures that empties a result fires the provider's existing no-data contract (`ok: false`) — #1915/#1762 extended from figure-less to impossible-only payloads.
6. **Every figure path is pinned against this contract.** One shared figure probe matrix (negative, zero control, impossible pair, out-of-range scaling input, sub-percent precision) per parser that publishes figures; the figure inventory rides the *same* `types.ts` table as the window inventory — not a second table to drift (#1939 is the warning).

Named exception: turso's publish-truthfully over-100% disposition (#1743) stands — a provider's *stated* disposition governs its out-of-range figures, as under window rule 5. The contract forbids unstated and split dispositions, not stated ones.

## Phases

- **Phase 1 (FILED, new)** — the contract stated in `packages/ai/src/quota/types.ts` beside the window contract; a figure section in the same parser inventory (figures published per provider + each figure's named disposition; known-lossy rows linked, not asserted); the shared figure probe matrix in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` over the already-conforming parsers (meta `parseBillingBanner`, opencode-go `toMicroCents` + balance path, command-code clamp-both, turso `numNonNegative` path). Tests/docs only, no production behaviour changes. Filed as a sub-issue of this design issue.
- **Phase 2 (ADOPTED)** — the negative-figure family lands: #1928 (deepseek), #1924 (codex), #1919 (claude). Already filed, scoped, probe-verified; each keeps its own queue lifecycle, linked as sub-issues, not re-enqueued.
- **Phase 3 (ADOPTED)** — pairs, scaling inputs, precision land: #1897 (groq pair), #1879 (opendesign pair), #1920 (claude exponent), #1941 (antigravity precision). Same terms as phase 2.
- **Phase 4 (NOT FILED)** — shared figure helpers in `utils.ts`; a scaling-input inventory across all 13 providers; a precision audit of every rounding site; the inventory-drift ratchet (shared question with #1794 phase 4 / #1939). Open questions in the design doc.

## Grounding

- `packages/ai/src/quota/utils.ts` — shared scalars only; no amount/pair/precision layer.
- `packages/ai/src/quota/types.ts` — window contract + parser inventory; balances scoped out by rule 4; inventory already drifting (#1939).
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/{deepseek,codex,claude,groq,opendesign,antigravity,meta,opencode-go,turso,command-code}.ts` — the per-provider precedents and violations cited above.
- Related: #1794 (window contract — producer sibling, composed not duplicated), #587 (consumers), #992 (core service-boundary numerics — different layer), #1939 (inventory drift — cited, not adopted).

## Acceptance criteria

- Phase 1 lands as filed: the figure contract is stated in `packages/ai/src/quota/types.ts` beside the window contract, the figure section rides the same `types.ts` inventory table as the window inventory (figures published per provider + each figure's named disposition), and the shared figure probe matrix (negative, zero control, impossible pair, out-of-range scaling input, sub-percent precision) runs in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` over the already-conforming parsers. Tests/docs only — no production behaviour changes in phase 1.
- Phases 2 and 3 proceed only through their already-filed sub-issues (#1928, #1924, #1919; #1897, #1879, #1920, #1941), each keeping its own queue lifecycle — no re-enqueueing from this design.
- No parser publishes an impossible figure (negative money/balance, impossible pair split between percent and label, out-of-range scaling input, parser-side percent rounding) once its adopting phase has landed, except under a provider's stated disposition (e.g. turso's publish-truthfully over-100% rule).
