# fix(ai): antigravity quota publishes integer-quantized percents — 99.9% used reads as 100% used / 0% remaining, 0.1% used reads as 0%

## Summary

The Antigravity quota provider (`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/antigravity.ts`) converts the wire's `remainingFraction` (a float, e.g. 0.999) to a percent by rounding to the nearest integer before deriving the window's `usedPercent`, at both conversion sites. Every sibling parser keeps the float percent (claude/codex use `clampPercent(toNumber(...))` unrounded; turso rounds to 3 decimals via `pct3`; the CLI renderer rounds only for display, #1797, because "providers compute usedPercent as an unrounded division"). Antigravity is the only parser that quantizes the published figure itself, so sub-percent usage is erased in both directions:

- a bucket 0.1% used (`remainingFraction: 0.999`) publishes `usedPercent: 0, remainingPercent: 100` — a pool with real usage reads as completely untouched;
- a bucket 99.9% used (`remainingFraction: 0.001`) publishes `usedPercent: 100, remainingPercent: 0` — a pool with headroom left reads as fully exhausted, the state placement/gating treats as a wall;
- a bucket 49.6% used (`remainingFraction: 0.504`) publishes `50 / 50`.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop primary at origin/main `05702ca18d4380326d8c0c10a10a2b100f39a6ee`)

Sites (both use the identical rounding conversion):

- `parseBucket` (the summary path), antigravity.ts:278-279: `const remainingPercent = remainingFraction !== null ? Math.round(remainingFraction * 100) : null`, then `usedPercent = clamp(100 - remainingPercent)`.
- `transformModels` fallback (per-model `quotaInfo`), antigravity.ts:393-394: the same two lines.

Probe on the laptop (worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-07-creator-0435`, script `probe-antigravity-rounding.ts`, kept; imports the real `parseBucket` / `transformModels` from the primary at the SHA above):

- `parseBucket({window: "FIVE_HOUR", remainingFraction: 0.999})` → `usedPercent=0 remainingPercent=100` (true used 0.1)
- `parseBucket(..., remainingFraction: 0.001)` → `usedPercent=100 remainingPercent=0` (true used 99.9)
- `parseBucket(..., remainingFraction: 0.504)` → `usedPercent=50 remainingPercent=50` (true used 49.6)
- controls: `0.5` → `50/50`, `0.25` → `75/25` (exact, unchanged)
- `transformModels` fallback with `quotaInfo.remainingFraction: 0.001` → window `{"5h": {usedPercent: 100, remainingPercent: 0, ...}}`; with `0.999` → `usedPercent: 0, remainingPercent: 100`.

Existing pins: `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` exercises antigravity fractions only at 0.5 / 0.25 / 0.75 / 0.0005 — values where integer rounding is either exact or not asserted on the published percent (the 0.0005 case asserts the weekly-constrained ordering, which reads the raw `remainingFraction` the bucket retains, not the published percent). No test pins a sub-percent published figure.

Note the transform's own weekly-constrained threshold (`weeklyFraction <= 0.001`, transformModels) operates on the raw fraction at sub-percent precision — the module itself treats sub-percent differences as meaningful for ordering, while the published window discards them.

Dedup: searched open + closed issues this run for antigravity rounding/percent topics — #1768 (label collisions / missing fraction), #1912 (fallback phantom window), #1917 (summary figure-less buckets) cover different defects in this same file; #1741 is the shared `toNumber` empty-string coercion, not this rounding. No open or closed issue records the quantization.

## Why it matters

Quota percents drive pool placement and exhaustion decisions, and the fleet's doctrine is to use pools all the way to 100% — the last percent is exactly where the decision matters. A window that reports 100% used / 0% remaining at 99.9% can wall the Antigravity pool early; a window that reports 0% used at 0.1% (or 49.6% as 50%) misstates the pool's state to every consumer of the quota row (aggregator, dashboard, routing weights). The fix is also the sibling-consistent one: publish the unrounded percent and let the renderer round for display (#1797).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both conversion sites (`parseBucket` and the `transformModels` fallback) publish the float percent derived from `remainingFraction` without integer rounding (clamping to 0-100 unchanged); `remainingPercent` derived by `toUsageWindow` then reflects the same figure.
- [ ] `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins sub-percent cases for both paths (e.g. 0.999 → 0.1% used, 0.001 → 99.9% used, 0.504 → 49.6% used) plus the existing round-fraction controls unchanged.
- [ ] The bucket's raw `remainingFraction` retention and the weekly-constrained ordering behaviour are unchanged; existing quota suite stays green; gate state not regressed.
- [ ] The window-contract inventory row for antigravity in `packages/ai/src/quota/types.ts` is updated if triage judges the row's "Conforming" verdict needs a mark while this is open (cf. #1939).

# docs(ai): quota window-contract inventory verdicts do not reflect the open known-lossy filings — six rows certify or omit parsers with live lossy issues, and turso's row has no verdict at all

## Summary

The quota window-contract parser inventory in `packages/ai/src/quota/types.ts` (the contract's own record, rule 7: "the inventory below stays complete") marks rows KNOWN-LOSSY for the lossy issues that are open against them — that is the established convention: claude's row cites open #1781, meta's row cites open #1777, opencode-go/openrouter cite open #1725. The lossy issues filed since then were never recorded, so six rows now certify (or silently omit) parsers that have live, open, verified lossy filings against exactly the behaviour the row describes, and one row carries no verdict at all. This is the opposite-direction sibling of closed #1909 (stale lossy marks after fixes landed); that issue is closed and does not cover these rows.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop primary at origin/main `5cd3c79fcf`)

- **antigravity** (types.ts:64-67): row says "Conforming". Open #1917 alleges the summary path (`transformSummary`, one of the three transforms this row certifies) publishes figure-less buckets as all-null-percent windows.
- **claude** (types.ts:69-72): row's only KNOWN-LOSSY mark is #1781 (duplicates). Open #1919 (extra-usage spend publishes negative amounts, ok:true on a negative-only payload) and open #1920 (spend `toAmount` trusts the wire exponent) are additional lossy cases in `toClaudeUsage`'s spend path, unrecorded.
- **codex** (types.ts:75-77): row says "Conforming (collision qualifiers and the phantom-window guard, #1762)". Open #1924 alleges the credits path in the same fetch publishes a negative balance as the `credits_balance` label and returns ok:true on a negative-only payload.
- **deepseek** (types.ts:84-86): row gives no verdict and states its only window "is a credits_balance label, which carries no figure to parse". Open #1928 shows the balance figure IS parsed and published: a negative-only payload returns "$-5.00" with ok:true — the row's premise is contradicted by the filed probe.
- **groq** (types.ts:87-89): row describes `parseGroqResetSeconds` but gives no verdict on the window construction from rate-limit headers. Open #1897 alleges that construction publishes a contradictory window ("150 / 100 requests remaining" beside 0% used / 100% remaining).
- **opendesign** (types.ts:108-110): row says "Conforming (keep-first, zero-limit publishes nothing, unknown durations skipped, #1750)". Open #1879 alleges `parseCodingPlanWindows` splits the window's fields (rule 5): percent clamped while the label publishes raw out-of-range remaining ("-50 / 100 credits", "150 / 100 credits").
- **turso** (types.ts:116-117): the row ends after naming `tursoWindows` — it is the only one of the 13 registry rows with neither a Conforming nor a KNOWN-LOSSY verdict, despite rule 7 requiring the inventory to stay complete and `tursoWindows` being an exported pure parser.

Control rows verified accurate this run: meta (#1777 open, marked), opencode-go and openrouter (#1725 open, marked), mistral and command-code (conforming, no open lossy filing found), cline-pass (conforming, #1769).

Dedup: searched open + closed issues this run for the inventory/verdict topic — closed #1909 covered only the mistral (#1785) / antigravity (#1768) stale-after-landing flips and is closed; no open issue records the rows above. Each underlying parser defect has its own open issue (cited); this issue is only about the contract's index agreeing with them.

## Why it matters

The inventory is where producers, reviewers, and the #1794 program decide where quota-parser risk remains. A row that says "Conforming" for a parser with a live verified lossy filing hides that risk exactly where people look for it, and the deepseek row's "no figure to parse" premise actively misdirects anyone triaging #1928's class. When those underlying issues land, their flips will also have no accurate baseline to flip from.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each row above is corrected to match the live state: the open lossy issue(s) recorded as KNOWN-LOSSY marks (the #1781/#1777/#1725 style), or — where triage judges a filing does not make the parser lossy under the contract — the row records that disposition and its reason in one line.
- [ ] turso's row gains an explicit verdict (conforming with its pin, or known-lossy with a link), so all 13 registry rows carry one.
- [ ] The deepseek row's "carries no figure to parse" wording is corrected regardless of the verdict chosen.
- [ ] No production behaviour changes; the shared probe matrix header in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` is updated only if a row's pinning claim changes; quota suite stays green.

title: fix(core): custom-tool override order is lexicographic by file path, not config priority — a project tool can lose to a global tool of the same name (#1748)

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage

labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Finding

Custom tools loaded by `ConfigToolPlugin` (PR #1748, for #1703) do not override each other in config priority order. `load()` collects the tool files from every config root in priority order, then sorts **all** file paths lexicographically (`items.flat().toSorted()`), so when a global tool and a project tool share a name, the winner is whichever file path sorts last — not the higher-priority (project) one.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1748 (merged, merge `326493e694de`, head `2cf384068a41`) — added `packages/core/src/config/plugin/tool.ts`.
- On current main (`8ba66b0545def36fbe8e55159e016603a84dee01`, verified twice via the commits API), `packages/core/src/config/plugin/tool.ts:158` still reads `Effect.map((items) => items.flat().toSorted())`, directly above the comment at :159-160: "Registration order is config priority order: later (project) tools override earlier (global) ones, and all of them override built-ins." The global sort discards the per-entry order the comment relies on.
- Registration is last-wins: `tool.ts:188` applies `loaded.tools` in order via `editor.add(tool)`, and the editor in `packages/core/src/tool.ts:183-190` implements `add` as `face(editor, tool).set(id, ...)` — a Map.set that overwrites any earlier registration of the same name.
- Laptop probe (Node, verbatim semantics: entries in priority order → flat → toSorted → Map.set): with the global config directory at `/home/u/xdg/opencode` (the location when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/home/u/xdg`, or an `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` under a late-sorting path) and a project root at `/home/u/proj/.opencode`, both defining `tool/foo.ts`, load order comes out `[project, global]` and the registry winner is the **global** `foo.ts` — the opposite of the documented project-over-global rule. With the default `~/.config/opencode` global path the sort happens to align with priority, which is why the defect is silent in the common layout.
- #1748's tests (`packages/core/test/config/tool.test.ts`) use a single config root, so cross-root override order is untested.

## Why it matters

Overriding a built-in or global tool with a project-local one is a documented custom-tools behavior, and the tool that wins is the code that executes in the session. A silent path-dependent inversion means a project can believe it has shadowed a tool while the global implementation is the one that actually runs — with no warning either way.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `load()` preserves config-entry priority order across roots (deterministic sorting, if kept, applies only within a single root's scan results).
- [ ] A regression test with two config roots whose paths sort opposite to their priority order proves the higher-priority root's same-named tool wins.
- [ ] Existing custom-tool tests (`packages/core/test/config/tool.test.ts`) still pass.

# fix(ai): meta quota portal read never uses the page's team — `teamIdOf`'s page-URL branch is dead, so every portal read targets the default team

## Evidence (verified this run on laptop primary at origin/main `9c02ef62d1`)

- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/meta.ts:56-64` — `teamIdOf(ctx, pageUrl)` first tries to read `team_id` from a page URL, then falls back to the `META_TEAM_ID` env var, then to the hard-coded `DEFAULT_TEAM_ID` (`"1073226932208501"`, meta.ts:52).
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/meta.ts:372` — the **only** call site in the repo is `teamIdOf(ctx, "")`. `new URL("")` throws, the `catch` at meta.ts:60-62 swallows it, and the page-URL branch can never produce a value. A repo-wide grep for `teamIdOf` returns exactly the definition and this one call.
- `packages/ai/src/quota/cdp.ts:28-31,246,303` — `cdpPageFetch` deliberately returns `pageUrl` in its outcome, documented as *"The URL of the page the fetches ran in (may carry a team_id parameter)"* — the exact input `teamIdOf`'s first branch was built to consume.
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/meta.ts:377-379` — `fetchQuota` reads only `outcome.results[...]` from the CDP outcome; `outcome.pageUrl` is never read anywhere (repo-wide grep: no consumer of `.pageUrl` outside cdp.ts itself).
- No test pins any of this: `grep -rn "team" packages/ai/test/` finds no meta-team, `META_TEAM_ID`, or default-team reference.

## Why it matters

The portal read is the system of record for Meta percentages (meta.ts header, code#6079/#6125). As written, every portal quota read targets the hard-coded default team unless the operator happens to set `META_TEAM_ID` — regardless of which team the laptop browser's signed-in dev.meta.ai page is actually on. If the portal session is ever on a different team (a second team, a team switch in the portal UI), the read silently targets the wrong team: either a no-data/http failure that masquerades as a portal problem, or — worse — another team's quota figures published as this account's. The dead branch also misleads maintainers: the code reads as if page-derived team selection works.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Team selection for the portal read is honest: either the page's `team_id` genuinely participates (e.g. discover the team from the already-open portal page / the `cdpPageFetch` outcome and use it, with env and default as fallbacks), or the dead page-URL branch and the unused `pageUrl` plumbing are removed and the env/default-only behaviour is documented at the call site.
- [ ] The chosen precedence (page vs `META_TEAM_ID` vs default) is stated in one place in the code and matches the implementation.
- [ ] A test pins the selection: a page URL carrying a non-default `team_id` produces portal paths for that team (or, under the removal route, a test pins that only env/default decide the team and no page-URL parameter remains).
- [ ] Existing quota tests still pass (`packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts`) and the ai package typecheck is clean.

# fix(ai): deepseek quota publishes a negative balance — the no-positive fallback bypasses its own >0 filter, so a negative-only payload returns "$-5.00" with ok:true

Verified 2026-11-07 on origin/main `9c02ef62d1`, in a laptop worktree (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-07-creator-0135`, kept).

## The defect

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/deepseek.ts`, the balance selection (:72-110):

- `positiveBalances` filters `total_balance > 0` (:74-77) — the #1800 selection rule.
- The fallback chain then re-reads the UNFILTERED list: `balanceInfos.find(currency === "USD") ?? balanceInfos.find(currency === "CNY")` (:85-86). When no positive balance exists, a negative USD/CNY entry is selected anyway.
- `totalBalance` is only null-checked (:89-103); a negative value flows to `formatMoney` and the label `` `$${formatMoney(totalBalance)}` `` (:105-110), publishing a `credits_balance` window with `ok: true`.

A negative balance is a figure that cannot exist as spendable credit. Sibling balance parsers in this same module read a negative amount as absent: meta's `parseBillingBanner` returns null for `minor < 0` (meta.ts), opencode-go's `toMicroCents` returns null for `amount < 0` (opencode-go.ts), turso's `numNonNegative`. The existing deepseek test "keeps the non-positive USD fallback when no positive balance exists" pins only ZERO (`total_balance: 0` → `"$0.00"`, quota.test.ts in the #1800 describe) — zero is a real empty account; negative is not, and no test exercises a negative-only payload.

## Runtime probe (laptop worktree, `probe-deepseek-negative.ts`, kept in the worktree)

Driving the real `provider.fetchQuota` with a mocked 200 fetch:

- `{balance_infos:[{currency:"USD", total_balance:"-5.00"}]}` → `ok:true`, sole window `credits_balance` label `"$-5.00"`.
- Same with numeric `-5` → `"$-5.00"`; `{currency:"CNY", total_balance:"-7"}` → `"¥-7.00"`, `ok:true`.
- Controls: `0` → `"$0.00"` (correct, pinned, must stay); `42` → `"$42.00"`; negative USD + positive EUR `10` → `"EUR 10.00"` (the #1800 positive-selection rule, correct and unchanged).

## Why it matters

The `credits_balance` window is the DeepSeek balance figure downstream pool decisions read. Publishing an impossible negative balance as a successful read — in the negative-only case as the provider's ONLY result, defeating the module's "No quota data in response" contract in spirit — teaches consumers a figure that cannot be true, in the money/balance shape where this module has repeatedly chosen "bad data reads as absent" over fabrication (cf. codex credits #1924, openrouter spend #1913, claude spend #1919 — each a different provider/file).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A negative-only `balance_infos` payload publishes no `credits_balance` window and reaches the existing "No quota data in response" error (ok:false), instead of `ok:true` with a negative label.
- [ ] Negative USD/CNY entries never publish a negative label in any mix; a positive entry in any currency still wins per #1800.
- [ ] Zero and positive balances are unchanged (`"$0.00"`, `"$42.00"` controls; the pinned zero-fallback test stays green).
- [ ] `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins the negative-only USD and CNY cases beside the existing deepseek #1800 describe.
- [ ] Existing quota suite stays green.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues this run for deepseek balance / negative: #1800 (closed) is deepseek's balance *selection* discarding a positive balance — it introduced the >0 filter whose fallback this issue is about, and its tests pin only the zero fallback. #1924 (open) is codex credits, #1913 openrouter spend, #1919 claude spend — different providers and files. No issue covers a negative-only deepseek payload.

## Finding

`.github/ci-policy.md` still describes a push-to-`main` CI tier, but PR #1635 (2026-11-04, per Drew's ruling: no commit- or PR-triggered CI — dispatch/placement, schedule, and `workflow_call` only) removed **every** `push:` trigger in the repo, and no workflow on current `main` has one. The policy file was reconciled to the push-to-main tier hours earlier by PR #1616 (for #1533) and never updated for the #1635 removal, so it now states the opposite of the enforced reality — the same failure #1533 was filed for, one policy change later.

Stale statements in `.github/ci-policy.md` on current `main` (`9c02ef62d1c8b91f54d2be7720c22f233e88860a`, read fresh via `gh api` contents this run):

- Intro: "merges to `main` get basic validation fast and then run everything"; "The tier split below therefore runs on push to `main`, on the nightly schedule, and by hand".
- Change-class table header: "fast tier (push to `main`)".
- Merge requirement: "validation lands with the push to `main`".
- "The full main-tier jobs (`build`, `e2e` suites) run in the same push-to-`main` runs, after the basic tier."
- Workflow mapping: "`check` … runs on push to `main` and on manual dispatch"; "`test` — … `build` and `e2e` additionally run on push to `main`, on manual dispatch, and on the nightly schedule"; "`nix-eval` — full evaluation on every push to `main` and on manual dispatch (the push trigger carries no paths filter…)".

Actual triggers on current `main` (every workflow's `on:` block read fresh this run):

- `check.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` only — no automatic run of any kind.
- `test.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` + nightly schedule (`0 3 * * *`) — no push.
- `nix-eval.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` only.
- No workflow in `.github/workflows/` (all 29 listed) contains a `push:` trigger; `main-broken.yml` runs on `workflow_run` + dispatch, `agents.yml`/`repo-sweeper.yml` on schedule + dispatch.

## Evidence

- Filed by pr-diff-review (2026-11-07 01:24 CST run) from its review of PR #1635 (merged, merge verified ancestor of current main via compare API) and PR #1616 (merged the same day, hours earlier).
- PR #1635 diff: removes the `push:` block from 16 workflows (`check`, `test`, `nix-eval`, `containers`, the `deploy-*` set, `publish*`, `storybook`, `docs-locale-sync`, `nix-hashes`) and touches nothing outside the `on:` blocks — `ci-policy.md` is not among its files.
- PR #1616 diff: rewrote `ci-policy.md` to the push-to-main framing quoted above (it correctly described reality between its merge and #1635's).
- Deduped this run: searches for `ci-policy dispatch`, `ci-policy push triggers`, `1635 ci-policy`, and `no push triggers policy` return #1533 (CLOSED — the original reconciliation this file already went through), #1932 (pr-standards dispatch input, distinct), and #1724 (gate-registry drift, distinct). Nothing tracks the post-#1635 staleness.

## Why it matters

The policy file is the repo's own answer to "what validates a merge and when does it run" — the question #1533, the workflow-policy gate (#1406), and the `main-broken` remediation chain all depend on. As written, it tells a reader that merges are automatically validated on push and that a red main is owned by remediation, when in fact `check` (typecheck + lint) and `nix-eval` have **no** automatic trigger at all and `test` auto-runs only nightly; everything else happens by dispatch/placement. Anyone triaging a red or never-ran main from this document will look for push runs that cannot exist.

## Acceptance criteria

- `ci-policy.md` describes the post-#1635 trigger reality: no `push`/`pull_request` triggers anywhere; CI runs via `workflow_dispatch`/placement, schedule, and `workflow_call`; the per-workflow mapping names each workflow's actual triggers (`check` dispatch-only, `test` dispatch + nightly, `nix-eval` dispatch-only, `main-broken` on `workflow_run`).
- The merge-requirement and remediation paragraphs no longer claim validation "lands with the push to `main`"; they state how a merge gets validated under the dispatch/placement model (and what, if anything, owns a red main now).
- No statement in the file attributes a trigger to a workflow that its `on:` block does not contain — verifiable by grepping every workflow's `on:` block against the file's claims (the workflow-policy gate's view).
- The historical no-PR-trigger rationale (#1401/#1406, fork-PR credential safety) stays intact — this is a reconciliation to the newer ruling, not a proposal to restore push or PR triggers.

title: fix(ai): antigravity convertSchema merges a multi-valued type union into the node's own anyOf/oneOf — conjunction becomes disjunction (constraints dropped on Gemini, valid calls rejected on Anthropic)

body:
## Finding

`convertSchema` in `packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts` merges the branches it creates for a multi-valued `type` union (PR #1629, for #1556) into the **same** `anyOf`/`oneOf` array that holds the node's own composition branches. In JSON Schema, a node's `type` and its `anyOf`/`oneOf` are conjunctive — an instance must satisfy **both**. After the merge, the converted proto schema holds one flat disjunction — an instance need satisfy only **one** branch from either set. Both directions break:

- **Gemini (`anyOf`) — widening / dropped constraints.** For a property `{ type: ["string", "integer"], anyOf: [{ type: "string", minLength: 5 }, { type: "integer", minimum: 10 }] }`, the converted schema is `anyOf: [{STRING, minLength 5}, {INTEGER, minimum 10}, {STRING}, {INTEGER}]`. The bare `{STRING}` branch admits `"ab"`, which the source schema rejects (a string must pass the `anyOf`, and neither branch accepts it). Tool-parameter constraints the author wrote are silently dropped.
- **Anthropic (`oneOf`) — valid calls rejected, plus widening.** `oneOf` is exactly-one. An instance that satisfies its type **and** exactly one own branch — valid in the source — now matches two merged branches and is rejected; an instance matching only a bare type branch (and no own branch) matches exactly one and is admitted, though the source rejects it.

## Evidence

- Filed by pr-diff-review (2026-11-07 01:24 CST run) from its review of PR #1629 (merged, merge commit `6f3730f22f8b` short / PR head; merge verified ancestor of current main `9c02ef62d1c8b91f54d2be7720c22f233e88860a` via compare API, status `behind`).
- PR #1629 diff, `packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts`: `if (anthropic) out.oneOf = [...(Array.isArray(out.oneOf) ? out.oneOf : []), ...branches]` / `else out.anyOf = [...(Array.isArray(out.anyOf) ? out.anyOf : []), ...branches]` — the type-union branches are appended into whichever array the node's own `anyOf`/`oneOf` handling (earlier in the same function) already emitted on that side.
- Verified on current main this run via a fresh `gh api` contents read of `packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts`: the merge is unchanged (the type-handling block still spreads the existing `out.anyOf`/`out.oneOf` and appends the union branches; the only post-#1629 change in this area is the ARRAY-branch `prefixItems` handling fixed under #1820).
- No test covers the combination: PR #1629's new test exercises a type union alone (property and root, both targets) and keyword preservation, but never a node carrying a multi-valued `type` **and** its own `anyOf`/`oneOf`. The translator fidelity corpus from PR #1723 (#1685, CLOSED) likewise dispositions "multi-valued type" and "anyOf" only as separate standalone shapes — the combined shape is not in the corpus.
- Deduped this run: searches for `convertSchema anyOf`, `antigravity anyOf type union conjunction`, `type union anyOf widens`, and `multi-valued anyOf merge` return #1556 (CLOSED, the union-collapse original), #1667/#1901 (OBJECT forcing, distinct), #1557 (const drop, distinct), #1820 (CLOSED, #1629's unreachable `prefixItems` else-if, distinct), and #1685 (CLOSED corpus, standalone shapes only). Nothing tracks the conjunction merge.

## Why it matters

This is the same fidelity class this repo has been fixing one shape at a time (#1556, #1573, #1667, #1820, #1901): the wire schema sent upstream diverges from the tool author's declared schema, silently. Here the divergence both loosens validation (Gemini admits values the tool schema forbids, so a model can emit arguments the tool then rejects or mishandles) and, on the Anthropic side, can reject calls that are valid under the declared schema (exactly-one miscount). Any tool whose parameter combines a type union with a composition keyword — a common shape for "string-or-number with per-form constraints" parameters — is affected today.

## Acceptance criteria

- A node carrying both a multi-valued `type` and its own `anyOf` (Gemini) converts to a schema that does **not** admit instances the source rejects: in the example above, `"ab"` and `5` are refused while `"abcde"` and `10` are admitted. (One faithful encoding is to keep the two branch sets conjunctive — e.g. the type branches under an `allOf` wrapper beside the node's own `anyOf` — but triage picks the shape the proto accepts.)
- The Anthropic (`oneOf`) conversion of the same combined shape neither rejects an instance that satisfies the type plus exactly one own branch, nor admits one that satisfies only a bare type branch.
- Regression tests pin both targets for the combined shape and name their oracle: JSON Schema conjunction semantics (an instance must satisfy `type` and the composition keyword independently).
- Existing behavior is preserved for the standalone shapes: a type union alone still emits one branch per member (#1556 tests stay green), a node's own `anyOf`/`oneOf` alone still folds as before (#1550), and the #1629 keyword-preservation cases stay green.
- The translator fidelity corpus (PR #1723) gains the combined shape with its disposition, so the approximation — if any remains — is recorded rather than silent.

# fix(ai): codex quota credits publishes a negative balance — "-5" as the credits_balance label, and a negative-only payload still returns ok:true

Verified 2026-11-07 on origin/main `27bd60d11c`, in a laptop worktree (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-07-creator-0035`, kept).

## The defect

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/codex.ts`, the credits block (:144-157):

- `const balance = toNumber(credits.balance)` (:145) — `toNumber` accepts any finite number, negative included.
- `const label = unlimited ? "Unlimited" : balance !== null ? String(balance) : null` (:147) — a negative balance becomes the window's label verbatim.
- The window publishes whenever `label !== null` (:149-156), and the no-data contract (:191-199) only fires when NO window exists — so a payload whose only figure is a negative balance returns `ok: true` with a single `credits_balance` window labelled `"-5"`.

A negative credits balance is a figure that cannot exist as spendable credit. Sibling balance parsers in this same quota module read a negative amount as absent: meta's `parseBillingBanner` returns null for `minor < 0` (meta.ts:121), opencode-go's `toMicroCents` returns null for `amount < 0` (opencode-go.ts:65), turso's `numNonNegative` (turso.ts:50-51), and deepseek's balance selection discards zero/negative entries (#1800). The codex credits path is the remaining raw-negative balance label.

## Runtime probe (laptop worktree, `probe-codex-credits.ts`, kept in the worktree)

Driving the real `provider.fetchQuota` with a mocked 200 fetch:

- `{ credits: { balance: -5 } }` → `ok: true`, sole window `credits_balance` with `valueLabel: "-5"`, all percents null.
- A real rate-limit window plus `{ credits: { balance: -5 } }` → the `5h` window is correct (10% used) and `credits_balance` still publishes `"-5"` beside it.
- Controls: `{ credits: { balance: 0 } }` → label `"0"`; `{ credits: { balance: 42 } }` → label `"42"` (both correct, unchanged by any non-negative guard).

## Why it matters

The `credits_balance` window is the Codex/ChatGPT credit figure downstream pool decisions read. Publishing an impossible negative balance as a successful quota read — in the negative-only case as the provider's ONLY result, defeating the #1762 no-data contract in spirit — teaches consumers a figure that cannot be true, in the one shape (money/balance amounts) where this module has repeatedly chosen "bad data reads as absent" over fabrication.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A negative `credits.balance` gets one explicit disposition — read as absent (the meta `parseBillingBanner` / opencode-go `toMicroCents` precedent in this same module) is the sibling-consistent choice; any other disposition is chosen and recorded in the closing note.
- [ ] A payload whose only figure is a negative balance publishes no `credits_balance` window, so it reaches the existing "No quota data in response" contract (#1762) when nothing else is usable.
- [ ] Zero and positive balances are unchanged (`"0"`, `"42"` controls), and the `unlimited` label path is unchanged.
- [ ] `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins the negative-balance and negative-only cases beside the existing codex describes.
- [ ] Existing quota suite stays green.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues this run for codex credits / balance / `credits_balance`: no covering issue. #1800 (closed) is deepseek's balance *selection* discarding a positive balance, a different provider and defect; #1919/#1920 (open) are claude spend amounts; #1913 (open) is openrouter's negative monthly spend. No quota.test.ts case exercises a negative codex credits balance.

body:
# fix(ai): muse-direct minted-key cache is process-global and ignores the credential source — a second source silently spends the first account's key

Verified 2026-11-06 on origin/main `2d11e0f649` (merge of PR #1896), in a laptop worktree (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-06-creator-1735`, kept). Gates this run: `check:workflows` and `check:doc-env-vars` GREEN; `check:bounded-http` 7 / `check:numeric-boundaries` 3 / `check:proto-reads` 4 RED = exactly #1724's set — no new drift.

## The defect

`packages/ai/src/providers/muse-direct-auth.ts` caches the minted inference key in module-global state that is never keyed to — or bypassed by — the credential source it was minted from:

- :180-181 — `let cached: KeyState | undefined` and `let inflight: Promise<string> | undefined` are module singletons.
- :190-193 `loadKey(sources)` — the cache is consulted **before** the credential file is read: `if (cached && now(sources) - cached.cachedAt < MINTED_KEY_TTL_MS) return Promise.resolve(cached.key)`. The `sources` argument (which selects the auth file via `authPath` / `MUSE_AUTH_PATH` / `readFile`, :66-77, and the exchange via `fetchFn` / `apiBase`) plays no part in the cache decision.
- `MuseDirect.configure({ sources })` builds one provider instance per source set (`packages/ai/src/providers/muse-direct.ts:96`), so two differently-sourced instances in one process share the cache.
- The sibling bridge solved exactly this: `vibe-auth.ts` `loadApiKey` bypasses the process cache whenever explicit sources are supplied ("Explicit sources (tests, embedding hosts) bypass the process cache"). muse-direct has no equivalent rule, and its own test suite works around the leak by calling `MuseDirectAuth.invalidate()` at the top of nearly every test in `packages/ai/test/provider/muse-direct.test.ts`.

## Runtime probe (laptop worktree, `probe-muse-cache.ts`, kept in the worktree)

Against the real `museDirectAuth({ sources }).apply(...)` with two stubbed source sets (A: account token A → exchange returns key A; B: account token B → exchange returns key B):

- Apply with sources A → `Bearer key-A`; A's file read 1×, A's exchange fetched 1×.
- Apply with sources B, **no invalidate** → `Bearer key-A`; B's file read **0×**, B's exchange fetched **0×** — B never even reads its own credential; it silently spends account A's plan with A's minted key.
- Control: after `MuseDirectAuth.invalidate()`, apply with sources B → `Bearer key-B`; B's file read 1×, exchange fetched 1× (correct).

## Why it matters

The minted key is account-scoped plan credit. Serving source A's key to a caller configured for source B bills the wrong Meta account, presents the wrong account's credential to the API, and makes a credential rotation (a different account written to the auth file, or a second configured instance) a silent no-op for up to the 10-minute `MINTED_KEY_TTL_MS` — the cache hit path does not even re-read the file, so there is no signal anything is stale. The 401 invalidation path (`invalidate()`, called by the transport on a rejected key) is the only escape, and a wrong-account key is not rejected — it is valid, just not the caller's.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A minted key is only ever served to the credential source it was minted from: the cache is keyed to the source identity, or explicit sources bypass the process cache (the vibe-auth precedent), or the cache moves into the per-instance auth closure — the route is recorded in the fix.
- [ ] Two `museDirectAuth` / `MuseDirect.configure` instances with different sources in one process each exchange and send their own key, with no cross-serving and no required `invalidate()` between them.
- [ ] A test pins the two-source case in `packages/ai/test/provider/muse-direct.test.ts` (B gets B's key without an invalidate; the single-source exchange-once/TTL behaviour and the 401 invalidate-and-retry test still pass).
- [ ] The single-source default path is unchanged: one exchange per TTL window, `invalidate()` still forces a re-exchange on 401.

Related: #1893 (the key-exchange response bound in the same module), #1868 (the sibling claude-code bridge's cached-failure fix — same cache-lifecycle class).

body:
## Finding

`githubActionsJWKSet(jwksURL, options?)` in `packages/function/src/github.ts` caches the shared remote JWK set in a module-level `Map` keyed **only by `jwksURL.href`** — the `options` argument is used only when the entry is first created and is silently ignored on every later call for the same URL:

```ts
const key = jwksURL.href
const existing = remoteJWKSetByURL.get(key)
if (existing) return existing
const created = createRemoteJWKSet(jwksURL, options)
```

So a second caller that passes different jose options (e.g. `cooldownDuration`, `cacheMaxAge`, `timeoutDuration`) for the same JWKS URL receives a set built with the first caller's options, with no error or warning. The options are security-relevant verification parameters for the GitHub Actions token exchange: a caller that deliberately tightened (or loosened) them would not get the behavior it asked for.

## Evidence

- Filed by pr-diff-review (2026-11-06 17:24 CST run) from its review of PR #1609 (merged, merge commit 27656e6f1620da56bbb3ac0a20d89ad64c1f5a9b, verified ancestor of current main 2d11e0f649436d6c4d20a64ce13fd7e0501bdd96 via compare API), which introduced the singleton to close issue #1112.
- PR #1609 diff, `packages/function/src/github.ts`: the cache key is `jwksURL.href` only; `options` appears only in the `createRemoteJWKSet(jwksURL, options)` creation call.
- Verified on current main this run via a fresh `gh api` contents read of `packages/function/src/github.ts`: the function is byte-for-byte the PR's version — key is URL-only, later-call options are dropped.
- The PR's own test illustrates the trap: `packages/function/test/github.test.ts` calls `githubActionsJWKSet(server.url, { cooldownDuration: 0 })` and comments that production uses jose's defaults via `api.ts` — that only holds because the two callers use different URLs. Any future same-URL caller with different options (another test against the production JWKS URL, or a second verification path in `api.ts`) silently inherits whichever options were passed first.

## Why it matters

This is a latent correctness trap on an auth-verification surface, not a live outage: today the only production caller (`packages/function/src/api.ts`) passes no options, so current behavior is correct by accident of call order. The exported signature promises per-call options; the implementation delivers first-caller-wins. The fix is small, but it should be a deliberate decision (key the cache by URL + options, or drop the options parameter and document that the set is built once with defaults) rather than a surprise discovered during a future token-verification change.

## Acceptance criteria

- Two calls to `githubActionsJWKSet` with the same URL but meaningfully different options no longer silently return a set built with the first call's options — either the cache distinguishes the options, or the API no longer accepts per-call options (single documented construction, with the test's `cooldownDuration: 0` need met another way, e.g. distinct test URLs as today).
- A regression test pins the chosen behavior (same-URL/different-options case) and names its oracle: the options the returned set was actually constructed with, or the documented single-construction contract.
- Existing behavior is preserved: the JWKS document is still fetched once across verifications for the production URL and still refreshes on an unknown `kid` (the #1112 regression test in `packages/function/test/github.test.ts` stays green).

# fix(ai): groq quota accepts remaining above the limit — "150 / 100 requests remaining" publishes beside 0% used / 100% remaining

Verified 2026-11-06 on origin/main `2d11e0f649` (merge of PR #1896), in a laptop worktree (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-06-creator-1635`, kept). Gates this run: `check:workflows` and `check:doc-env-vars` GREEN; `check:bounded-http` 7 / `check:numeric-boundaries` 3 / `check:proto-reads` 4 RED = exactly #1724's set — no new drift.

## The defect

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/groq.ts` builds both rate-limit windows from the `x-ratelimit-*` headers with a strict plain-count parser (#1793: non-negative decimals only — negatives, hex, and exponents read as absent), but neither window ever checks the pair against each other:

- :124-131 (requests): any `remainingRequests` is accepted when `limitRequests > 0`; :128 clamps the derived percent into [0, 100], and :131 publishes the **raw** remaining in the label: `` `${remainingRequests} / ${limitRequests} requests remaining` ``.
- :136-143 (tokens): the identical shape for `remainingTokens` / `limitTokens`.

A remaining count above its limit is an impossible pair — the same class of bad data #1793 made the parser reject in its other spellings ("bad data reads as absent"). Here it is instead published, and the window's fields contradict each other: the percent follows the clamp while the label follows the raw wire, and `toUsageWindow` derives `remainingPercent` from the clamped percent — the failure window-contract rule 5 in `packages/ai/src/quota/types.ts` ("derived fields are computed from the published (post-disposition) values; the out-of-range disposition … is applied to the whole window, never split") exists to prevent.

## Runtime probe (laptop worktree, `probe-groq.ts`, kept in the worktree)

Against the real `provider.fetchQuota` with a stubbed fetch (the test-suite's own harness shape):

- Headers `x-ratelimit-limit-requests: 100`, `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests: 150` → window **published**: `usedPercent: 0`, `remainingPercent: 100`, `valueLabel: "150 / 100 requests remaining"` — the label claims 150% of the limit remains beside fields saying 100%.
- Headers `x-ratelimit-limit-tokens: 10000`, `x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens: 12000` → window **published**: `usedPercent: 0`, `remainingPercent: 100`, `valueLabel: "12000 / 10000 tokens remaining"`.
- Control `limit-requests: 100`, `remaining-requests: 40` → `usedPercent: 60`, `remainingPercent: 40`, `valueLabel: "40 / 100 requests remaining"` (correct).

## Why it matters

These windows are the only quota surface Groq offers (no first-party usage endpoint exists — the module's own header comment), so a contradictory window is the whole signal for this provider in the `opencode quota` output and for quota-aware consumers. #1793 already established this parser's disposition for impossible values — reject them so bad data reads as absent — but only enumerated the negative/hex/exponent/reset-duration spellings; the remaining-above-limit pair slipped through because each value is individually a well-formed plain count.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A remaining count above its limit gets one explicit, whole-window disposition in both the requests and tokens windows — either the pair reads as absent (no window, per #1793's bad-data-reads-as-absent philosophy) or the remaining is clamped to the limit so percent, remainingPercent, and label all derive from the same published figure (the #1821 rule-5 shape). The choice is recorded in the fix and pinned by tests.
- [ ] No published groq window can carry a `valueLabel` claiming more remaining than the limit while its percent fields say otherwise.
- [ ] Tests pin both over-limit cases (requests and tokens) plus the in-range control in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts`; the existing groq tests (#1793 cases included) still pass.
- [ ] The types.ts parser inventory row for groq is updated if the fix changes its disposition description.

Related: #1793 (this parser's strictness fix), #1794 / rule 5 of the window contract in `packages/ai/src/quota/types.ts`, #1821 (whole-window clamp precedent).

## Finding

The `question` tool's description (`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/question.ts`) says: "Use this tool when you need to ask the user questions during execution" — with **no warning** that in a detached/subsessions context there may be no user watching, that the parent session is *not* notified, and that a foreground parent blocks with the child until an external actor answers.

## Workshop evidence

Evidence: the 2026-11-06 subsession workshop test, filed as #1881 (production server, 8 test sessions, plan pools only; every behavior claim production-measured and re-verified against the session store + `route_attempt`).

#1881 Q6: a child's `question` call stalled it and its foreground parent for 10+ minutes with zero notification; after the call errored, retry machinery resumed both and the child re-asked the identical question. This is the user-facing description that leads models into that trap.

## Desired

- Description warns plainly: in detached/background/subsessions contexts the form may never be seen; the parent is not notified; prefer recording the question and continuing with a stated default.
- Cross-reference the structural fixes filed alongside: the stall bug (very high priority), question escalation to the parent, and the API launch mode that disables `question` entirely — the description should name the disable mode once it exists so models can recognize and respect it.

## Acceptance sketch

- Updated description ships; a detached-context session reading its tool list can tell, from the description alone, not to call `question` blindly.

## Acceptance criteria

- The `question` tool description warns that in detached/subsessions contexts there may be no user watching, the parent is not notified, and a foreground parent blocks until an external actor answers.
- The description points at the detached-operation alternative (record the question, pick the documented default, continue).
- Wording lives in `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/question.ts` and matches the behavior verified in the workshop.

## Finding

Family prompts disagree about delegation itself, and selection is per-model — so the same route behaves differently depending on which leaf serves a step:

- `gpt.txt` / `gpt-astra.txt`: "Do not spawn subagents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for subagents, delegation, or parallel agent work."
- `meta.txt`: proactively encourages the `subagent` tool.
- `kimi.txt`: mentions it neutrally.
- **DeepSeek matches no family** in `packages/core/src/plugin/optimize.ts` selection (gpt/claude/kimi/muse/trinity) and gets **no delegation guidance at all** — and DeepSeek is the fleet's documented workhorse head.

## Workshop evidence

Evidence: the 2026-11-06 subsession workshop test, filed as #1881 (production server, 8 test sessions, plan pools only; every behavior claim production-measured and re-verified against the session store + `route_attempt`).

#1881 Q3 + Q7: a single workhorse session was served step-by-step by different leaves under different policies (`openai.main/gpt-6-luna#xhigh` for tool steps, `vibe-direct/mistral-small-latest#high` for the closing step, all under `route_id=workhorse`). Delegation behavior currently varies by leaf luck, not by design.

## Desired

- One consistent subsession policy across all family prompts (aligned with the base-prompt delegation block, filed separately) — no leaf-level veto on spawning when the task/AGENTS.md calls for delegation.
- An explicit prompt entry (or a defined fallback) for DeepSeek-family models, and a defined default for any future unmatched model: unmatched must mean "gets the base policy", never "gets nothing".

## Acceptance sketch

- Every family file carries the same delegation stance; optimize.ts selection has a DeepSeek entry or a documented fallback.
- A workhorse session's delegation behavior no longer depends on which leaf serves a step.

## Acceptance criteria

- All model-family prompts give consistent delegation guidance, or the differences are deliberate and documented in one place.
- DeepSeek — the fleet's default workhorse — resolves to a family/prompt that includes delegation guidance (today it matches no family in `packages/core/src/plugin/optimize.ts` selection and gets none).
- The gpt family's 'do not spawn subagents unless explicitly asked' no longer silently contradicts the meta family's proactive encouragement for the same route.

## Finding

The base system prompt (`packages/core/src/session/runner/prompt/system.txt`, 15 lines) mentions **none** of the subsession machinery: the `subagent` tool, nesting and the depth cap, directory/route inheritance, background completion semantics, cross-session messaging (`comms`), model-switch limits, or detached-operation rules. Every model gets whatever its family prompt happens to say — and family prompts contradict each other (filed separately).

## Workshop evidence

Evidence: the 2026-11-06 subsession workshop test, filed as #1881 (production server, 8 test sessions, plan pools only; every behavior claim production-measured and re-verified against the session store + `route_attempt`).

Full prompt audit in #1881 Q7. The machinery demonstrably works (Q1–Q4) — sessions succeed by tool-description luck, not by baseline instruction.

## Desired

A short delegation/messaging block in the base prompt (or a shared include every family inherits), covering at minimum:

- Subsessions exist (native `subagent` tool); nesting is allowed to the depth cap (`experimental.subagent_depth`, default 5).
- Children inherit the parent's directory and, without a `model` argument, the parent's model/route.
- Background completion arrives on its own as a synthetic turn — no polling/babysitting needed.
- Cross-session messaging is via `comms` in code mode.
- Sessions cannot change their own model (see the separate model-switch gap).
- **Detached sessions must not call the `question` tool** — record the question, pick the documented default, continue (see the very-high-priority stall bug, filed alongside).

## Acceptance sketch

- The block ships in the base prompt path and is present for a model from every family and for unmatched models.
- Prompt tests/snapshots updated; behavior spot-check: a fresh workhorse session can state the rules above unprompted.

## Acceptance criteria

- The base system prompt (`packages/core/src/session/runner/prompt/system.txt`) contains a short delegation/messaging block covering: the `subagent` tool, nesting/depth cap, directory+route inheritance, background completion semantics, `comms` messaging, model-switch limits, and detached-operation rules.
- The block is consistent with the family prompts (see issue #1888) and with tool descriptions (issues #1889, #1890).
- Kept short — a pointer block, not a manual.

title: gap: no in-session model switch — expose `Session.switchModel` in-session, or a switch-request path to the parent/launcher

body:
## Finding

A session cannot change its own model/route. The mechanism exists one level up — `Session.switchModel` in core, used by the command/API path (`POST /api/session/:id/model` → 204, next turn runs under the new route) — but **no in-session tool exposes it**, and nothing tells the session that.

## Workshop evidence

Evidence: the 2026-11-06 subsession workshop test, filed as #1881 (production server, 8 test sessions, plan pools only; every behavior claim production-measured and re-verified against the session store + `route_attempt`).

- Asked to switch itself to `opencode-route/speed`, the test session improvised in code mode with `tools.opencode.session_move({directory: "opencode-route/speed"})` — a *directory* move, not a model switch — got "Unable to move session", and honestly reported `SWITCH_METHOD: NONE_AVAILABLE` (#1881 Q5).
- The API switch itself is instant and clean; the gap is purely in-session reachability/discoverability.

## Options to decide between

1. **In-session switch tool** wrapping `Session.switchModel`, with the prompt-cache warning in its description (a switch invalidates the prompt cache for the new model — sessions should switch rarely and deliberately).
2. **Switch-request path:** the session emits a request its parent/launcher performs via the API (keeps the authority outside, makes the intent visible in the tree).
3. **Docs-only floor** (if both are rejected by design): base prompt + tool descriptions state plainly that sessions cannot change their own model and must ask their launcher — silence today produces improvisation against the wrong API.

## Acceptance sketch

- One of the options is implemented and documented; a session asked to switch itself either succeeds via the sanctioned path or answers with the documented procedure — never an improvised wrong-API call.
- Cache-invalidation consequence is stated wherever the mechanism is described.

## Acceptance criteria

- A session can either invoke an in-session model/route switch backed by the existing `Session.switchModel`, or has a documented switch-request path to its parent/launcher — and the tool/prompt surface says which.
- A session asked to switch no longer improvises with unrelated tools (the workshop's `session_move` directory attempt).
- Switch semantics (next-turn effect, cache loss) are stated where the capability is exposed.

body:
## Request (Drew, 2026-11-06)

Sessions launched through the API in a specific way — a flag/option on session create, e.g. a detached / non-interactive mode — should have the `question` tool **unavailable**: absent from the toolset, or hard-erroring with a clear "disabled in this mode" result the model can route around (record the question, pick the documented default, continue).

## Why

Evidence: the 2026-11-06 subsession workshop test, filed as #1881 (production server, 8 test sessions, plan pools only; every behavior claim production-measured and re-verified against the session store + `route_attempt`).

The workshop (#1881 Q6) proved a subsession's `question` call stalls the child and its foreground parent silently for 10+ minutes, and retry machinery can turn it into a re-ask loop. Detached fleet sessions run under a standing rule — never call `question`, record the question and keep working — but that rule currently lives only in launch-prompt text. A launch-mode guarantee makes it structural instead of instructional.

## Scope / design questions

- **Shape:** boolean/option on session create (e.g. `question: "disabled"` or a `detached` mode bundling related defaults) vs an agent-config default vs both (config default, per-session override).
- **Default posture:** off = today's behavior everywhere. Nothing changes for interactive/attached sessions unless the launcher opts in.
- **Semantics when called anyway** (tool restored by config merge, stale session, etc.): immediate tool error result naming the mode — never a form, never a block.
- **Interaction with permissions config:** how this composes with the existing tool-permission surface — is it a permission preset, a separate axis, or an override that wins over permissions? Decide and document.
- **Inheritance:** children of a disabled-mode session inherit the mode (a detached tree should not sprout an interactive leaf).
- Cross-ref: the stall bug (very high priority, filed alongside) and question escalation to the parent (filed alongside) — this mode is the third leg: prevent, escalate, or surface; all three are wanted.

## Acceptance sketch

- Session created with the mode on: `question` is absent from its tool list (or errors immediately with the mode named); children inherit it.
- Session created without it: behavior byte-identical to today.
- The mode is visible in session metadata so an orchestrator can verify a tree is detached-safe.

## Acceptance criteria

- An API launch option (detached / non-interactive mode) exists under which the `question` tool is absent from the toolset or hard-errors with a clear 'disabled in this mode' result.
- Sessions launched in this mode never block a foreground parent chain on an unanswerable form.
- Interactive launches are unaffected.

title: Workshop test: subsession machinery from a workhorse session — results and system-prompt suggestions

body:
**Date:** 2026-11-06 · **Surface:** laptop production OpenCode server (build 2.0.30+5e9b135f, fastlane drop-in), driven over the attach API. Sessions ran in a scratch worktree of developing-today/code; trivial tasks only (echo markers); plan-pool routes only; no PAYG. Prompt sources were read at fork main `93f5382` — one rev ahead of the deployed build; every *behavior* claim below is production-measured, file paths are where a fix would land.

**Sessions (8):** parent `ses_e5e4dbeab89ffe46hz8cRqBlw4` · ping child `ses_e5e4dbe9e4dffeWizUlwwUm39M` · nesting child `ses_e5e4dbc9e3fffeMb60xdJOxdBp` · grandchild `ses_e5e4dbc7a9bffeslsXpOLx6swS` · background child `ses_e5e4dba3ad9ffeU3Mi31lGq3rW` · question child `ses_e5e4db95f87ffeK76Av0XDWn2P` · messaging pair `ses_e5e4dbc04f3ffewG71bZwljs53` / `ses_e5e4dbc0516ffexNg6xfwuU22a`.

## Q1 — Does a workhorse session know it can launch subsessions, and how does it do it?

**Yes, immediately and unprompted.** The parent was told only "launch a subsession to print PING42" — no mechanism, no tool name. First turn, it called the native **`subagent` tool** (ordinary tool call; the tool is registered `codemode: false`, it is *not* reached through mcpx):

```json
{"agent": "build", "description": "Print exact ping", "prompt": "Use the shell to print exactly the string PING42 and nothing else...", "background": false}
```

Tool result: `<subagent sessionID="ses_e5e4dbe9e4dffeWizUlwwUm39M" state="completed">PING42</subagent>`. The child landed in the **parent's directory** (the worktree) and **inherited the parent's session model** (`opencode-route/workhorse`) because no `model` argument was passed. The parent waited synchronously (foreground is the default) and aggregated the result verbatim. The parent self-reports the mechanism as "functions.subagent".

## Q2 — Can a subsession launch its own subsession?

**Yes.** The nesting child launched a grandchild the same way (`subagent` tool, agent `build`), output `NEST7` relayed verbatim up both levels. Nothing — no prompt, tool, or error — claimed it couldn't. Depth cap is real but generous: `experimental.subagent_depth`, default 5 (`packages/core/src/session/subagent-depth.ts`), and the tool description itself says "A subagent may itself launch subagents, subject to the depth limit and to model governance".

## Q3 — Are defaults clear? What actually served?

- Child sessions **inherit the parent's route ref and directory** when `model` is not passed (observed in all 5 children). The launched sessions behave as if this is obvious; nothing in the tool result states it back.
- **Leaf ≠ head, and leaves vary per step.** Every session's declared model stayed `opencode-route/workhorse`, but `route_attempt` shows single turns served step-by-step by *different leaves*: e.g. the messaging pair's turns ran `openai.main/gpt-6-luna#xhigh` for the tool steps and `vibe-direct/mistral-small-latest#high` for the closing step — all under `route_id=workhorse`. After an API model switch (Q5), the `speed` route's first step hit `opencode-go.drewrypope/muse-spark-1.3-contributor#xhigh` → 429 (pool walled) and failed over to `vibe-direct/mistral-small-latest#high`, success. So: no drift of the *session's* model ref — but a session cannot tell which leaf served any given step, and prompt policy differs by leaf (see Q7). Launch prompts should state the intended route/head explicitly; the machinery will not confirm it back.

## Q4 — Cross-session messaging while running

**Works, both directions, via mcpx code mode.** Messaging is not a plain tool call in these transcripts: the sender first ran `mcpx_discover` (namespace `comms`; the first discover call errored, the retry succeeded), then the `execute` tool:

```js
tools.comms.msg({mode: "send", to: "ses_e5e4dbc0516ffexNg6xfwuU22a", text: "Token: TOK-987. Reply to me with the token reversed.", deliver: "wake"})
→ {"topic": "<sender>/bidi/<recipient>", "seq": 1, "delivered": [{"session": "<recipient>", "delivery": "wake"}]}
```

The woken recipient replied the same way (`789-KOT`), and the original sender, blocked in `tools.comms.msg({mode: "unread", wait: 120})`, received it inside the same turn and reported it. DM + wake + unread-with-wait is a complete request/response loop between two running sessions.

## Q5 — Can a session change its own model?

**Not from inside — the mechanism exists one level up.** Asked to switch itself to `opencode-route/speed`, the session improvised in code mode with `tools.opencode.session_move({directory: "opencode-route/speed"})` — that is a *directory* move, not a model switch — got "Unable to move session", and honestly reported `SWITCH_METHOD: NONE_AVAILABLE`. (`Session.switchModel` exists in core and is used by the command/API path — `packages/core/src/session/session.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts` `session.switchModel` — but no in-session tool exposes it.) The API switch is instant and clean: `POST /api/session/:id/model` → 204, the session's model ref became `opencode-route/speed`, and the next turn's attempts ran under `route_id=speed`. The cache caveat stands: a switch invalidates the prompt cache for the new model, so sessions should switch rarely and deliberately — today they can't switch at all, which makes the point moot until a tool exists.

## Q6 — Questions and errors in detached operation

**Errors: handled.** A background child told to `cat` a missing path hit an environment error (`cat: command not found`, exit 127 — the restricted shell profile). It did not stall or ask anyone; it reported the error verbatim as its final output. The parent, which had launched it `background=true` and ended its turn, received the completion **unprompted** as a synthetic turn (`<subagent sessionID="..." state="completed" ...>` + a follow-up assistant turn carrying the child's output). No babysitting needed for errors or for background completion.

**Questions: a hard stall — the one real hazard found.** A child instructed to use the `question` tool ("Which color?", options Red/Blue) called it and blocked: the tool call sat in `status=running` for 10+ minutes, the *parent's foreground `subagent` call blocked with it*, and **nothing notified anyone** — no message in the parent's transcript, no form on the parent session (`GET /api/session/<parent>/form` → `[]`). The form waits on the *child* session for an external actor (UI or API client).

**The stall degrades into a retry loop if left alone.** Somewhere in the following ~25 minutes the child's question call ended in `status=error` (operator probing of the form endpoints coincided with this window and its output was lost to a transport timeout, so whether the call timed out on its own is undetermined). The error propagated to the parent's `subagent` call (`status=error`), and the fleet's session-retry machinery then resumed both sessions automatically: the child got its task re-delivered as a fresh user message and **re-asked the identical question** (stall #2), while the parent relaunched the child through the `sessionID` continuation path. Unanswered, this loop can repeat — worse than a clean stall, since it burns turns producing nothing.

**An external answer unblocks everything instantly.** The pending form lives on the child (`GET /api/session/<child>/form` → `frm_…`, one field, key `q0`); `POST /api/session/<child>/form/<id>/reply` with `{"answer": {"q0": "Blue"}}` (answers are keyed by field key — a bare array is rejected with `Expected Form.Answer`, an array value with `Expected string for form field: q0`) returned 204; the child's `question` call completed (`User has answered your questions: "Which color?"="Blue"`), it printed `CHOSEN: Blue`, and the parent's `subagent` call returned and relayed it verbatim. Both sessions idle, outcome succeeded.

Detached design work must therefore treat the `question` tool as forbidden unless a watcher is assigned: record the question, pick the documented default, and continue.

## Q7 — Do the system prompts describe any of this?

Mostly no, and where they do, they contradict each other:

1. **Base prompt is silent.** `packages/core/src/session/runner/prompt/system.txt` (15 lines) mentions none of: the `subagent` tool, nesting, background mode/stop policies, messaging, or detached operation.
2. **Family prompts disagree about delegation itself.** `packages/core/src/plugin/system-prompt/gpt.txt` and `gpt-astra.txt`: "Do not spawn subagents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for subagents, delegation, or parallel agent work." `meta.txt` proactively encourages the `subagent` tool; `kimi.txt` mentions it neutrally. Selection is per-model (`packages/core/src/plugin/optimize.ts` matches gpt/claude/kimi/muse/trinity in the model id). **DeepSeek — the documented workhorse head — matches no family and gets no delegation guidance at all**, while a single workhorse session can be served by a GPT-policy leaf on one step and a no-policy leaf on the next (Q3). Delegation behavior currently varies by leaf luck, not by design.
3. **The fleet's own instruction file is stale.** developing-today/code `.opencode/instructions/subagents.md` (loaded via the global config's `instructions`) calls the tool the "Task tool" (its name is `subagent`), lists `plan` as a subagent type (mode `primary` — the tool rejects it: "cannot run as a subagent"; `build` works only because its mode is `all`), and says nothing about the depth limit, background/stopPolicy, model/directory inheritance, messaging, model switching, or the question stall.
4. **The `comms` namespace is undocumented.** `.opencode/instructions/mcpx.md`'s namespace table omits `comms` entirely; the sender had to discover it via `mcpx_discover` (first call errored). The `msg`/`topics`/`sessions` tool descriptions in `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/messaging.ts` are thorough — but sessions reach messaging through code mode, where discoverability is the weak link.
5. **The `question` tool's description invites the stall.** `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/question.ts`: "Use this tool when you need to ask the user questions during execution" — no warning that in a detached/subsession context there may be no user, that the parent is *not* notified, or that a foreground parent blocks with it.
6. **The `subagent` tool description is the best text in the system** (`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/subagent.ts`) — nesting, background, stop policies, continuation by sessionID are all there. Two gaps: it doesn't state that children inherit the parent's directory and (without a `model` arg) the parent's model/route; and it doesn't warn that a child's `question` call stalls the foreground call until an external actor answers.

## Suggestions

1. Add a short delegation/messaging block to the base system prompt (`system.txt` or a shared include): subsessions exist, nesting is allowed to the depth cap, children inherit directory + route unless overridden, background completion arrives on its own, messaging is via `comms` in code mode, and **detached sessions must not call the `question` tool** — record the question and continue with the stated default.
2. Reconcile the family prompts: replace the gpt/gpt-astra prohibition with the same delegation block (the fleet's standing doctrine is subagent-first; a leaf-level veto makes route behavior unpredictable).
3. Give DeepSeek-family models an explicit prompt entry in `optimize.ts` selection — the workhorse head should not be the one model with no guidance.
4. Fix the fleet instructions file: rename "Task tool" → `subagent`, drop `plan` from subagent types (or note mode rules), add the depth cap, inheritance, background/stopPolicy, `comms`, and the question-stall warning. (Fleet-side change, tracked here for visibility.)
5. Document the `comms` namespace in `mcpx.md`'s table, and consider registering `msg` as a plain tool as well as a code-mode projection so messaging doesn't depend on discovery.
6. Either expose an in-session model-switch tool (wrapping `Session.switchModel`, with the cache warning in its description) or state in the base prompt that sessions cannot change their own model and must ask their launcher to do it. Silence today produces improvisation with the wrong API (`session_move`).
7. Surface the serving leaf: include the resolved provider/model for the current step somewhere a session can see (e.g. in its context or a `sessions` tool field). A session asked "which model are you on" currently answers from its route ref or guesses.
8. Consider a question-relay: when a *child* session's `question` form goes unanswered for N minutes, surface it to the parent session (the parent is the natural answerer in detached trees) — or time the form out with a visible cancellation the child can handle. Today's behavior is a silent stall of the whole foreground chain that, once the call eventually errors, the retry machinery can turn into a re-ask loop.

*Test hygiene note: one intermediate tool output during this test returned a fabricated transcript (a wrong child session id and an invented successful answer). Every claim above was re-verified with independent reads of the session store and `route_attempt` before filing.*

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each system-prompt suggestion in the workshop results is dispositioned: adopted (with the prompt change landed or linked), declined with reasoning, or spun out as its own issue
- [ ] The disposition is recorded on this issue so the workshop findings do not sit as an unowned report

body:
# fix(ai): opendesign quota parseCodingPlanWindows publishes out-of-range remaining raw — "-50 / 100 credits" at 100% used, "150 / 100 credits" at 0% used

Verified 2026-11-06 on origin/main `90453b467f` (merge of PR #1874), in a laptop worktree (`~/git/probe-2026-11-06-creator-1235`, kept). Gates this run: `check:workflows`, `check:gates`, `check:doc-env-vars` GREEN; `check:bounded-http` 7 / `check:numeric-boundaries` 3 / `check:proto-reads` 4 RED = exactly #1724's set — no new drift.

## The defect

`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/opendesign.ts:78-107` (`parseCodingPlanWindows`) guards the limit (`limit <= 0` entries are dropped, :94 — the #1750 disposition) but never range-checks `remainingCredits`:

- :99 clamps the derived percent into [0, 100]: `Math.min(100, Math.max(0, (1 - remaining / limit) * 100))`
- :104 publishes the **raw** remaining in the label: `` `${remaining} / ${limit} credits` ``

Percent and label therefore derive from different figures and can contradict each other — the exact failure the window contract's rule 5 (whole-window clamp, #1821, implemented for command-code) exists to prevent: "percent and label derive from one clamped used figure, so they can never contradict each other."

## Runtime probe (laptop worktree, `probe-quota-caps.ts`, kept in the worktree)

Against the real `parseCodingPlanWindows` imported from main, one 5h window (`durationSeconds: 18000`, `limitCredits: 100`, `resetsAt: 1893456000`):

- `remainingCredits: -50` → window **published**: `usedPercent: 100`, `valueLabel: "-50 / 100 credits"` — a negative remaining balance rendered to the user.
- `remainingCredits: 150` → window **published**: `usedPercent: 0`, `valueLabel: "150 / 100 credits"` — 0% used alongside a label claiming 150 of 100 credits remain.
- Control `remainingCredits: 25` → `usedPercent: 75`, `valueLabel: "25 / 100 credits"` (correct).

## Why it matters

The label is the user-facing figure in the `opencode quota` output. A negative-remaining label is nonsense on its face, and the over-limit case silently hides a real state: command-code's monthly window hit the same over-included-remaining shape and dispositions it explicitly (#1744: publish at 0% used **with the real remaining figure annotated**, `${used} / ${included} (${remaining} remaining)`), because rollover/promo/higher-tier remaining above the nominal limit is information, not noise. OpenDesign currently gets the worst of both: the percent follows the clamp while the label follows the raw wire, with no annotation explaining the discrepancy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Percent and valueLabel derive from one consistent disposition of an out-of-range `remainingCredits` — they can never contradict (the #1821 rule-5 shape).
- [ ] Negative remaining never renders as a negative figure in the label (clamp to 0 remaining / 100% used, or an equally explicit disposition).
- [ ] Over-limit remaining follows an explicit disposition — the #1744 annotation shape (0% used with the real remaining named) or a clamped label — chosen in the fix and pinned by a test; not the current silent raw label.
- [ ] Tests pin all three cases (negative, over-limit, in-range control) for `parseCodingPlanWindows`; the existing quota suite still passes.

body:
## Finding

In `parseDotEnv` (packages/ai/src/providers/vibe-auth.ts, added by PR #1661), a quoted value that carries a trailing comment keeps its quote characters: `MISTRAL_API_KEY="abc123" # rotated` parses to the literal string `"abc123"` — quotes included. That value is then used verbatim as the Bearer credential, so the vibe provider authenticates with a corrupted key and the resolver never falls through to the keyring tiers.

## Evidence

- PR #1661 "feat(ai): vibe provider — native emulation of the Mistral Vibe binary (#1653)", merged 2026-11-05T00:30:03Z, merge commit `7774bf07e8c64eb18ee6ea84b10157b03519324a`, head `2428c887480296af2b6c734d48425905c933a499` — added `parseDotEnv` and the `~/.vibe/.env` resolution tier.
- Current main `384050a02672fce2abdad874a702e077b5374d57`, vibe-auth.ts:67-88 (unchanged since #1661): the quote-strip branch at :78-82 only fires when the value both starts AND ends with the same quote; a trailing comment makes the value end with the comment text, so control falls to the unquoted branch at :84-86, which strips the ` #…` comment but leaves the surrounding quotes in place.
- Reproduced by extracting `parseDotEnv` verbatim from current main and running it (bun):
  - `MISTRAL_API_KEY="abc123" # rotated 2026-11-01` → `"abc123"` (literal quotes retained)
  - `MISTRAL_API_KEY='abc123' # note` → `'abc123'` (same defect, single quotes)
  - Controls behave: `MISTRAL_API_KEY="abc #123"` → `abc #123` (quoted `#` content kept); `MISTRAL_API_KEY=abc123 # note` → `abc123` (unquoted comment stripped).
- vibe-auth.ts:207-210 (main): `resolveApiKey` takes `parseDotEnv(contents)[API_KEY_ENV_VAR]?.trim()` and returns it if non-empty — trimming does not remove the quotes, and because the tier "found" a value, the keyring services (`ai.mistral.vibe`, legacy `vibe`) are never consulted.
- Test gap: PR #1661's `parseDotEnv` tests in packages/ai/test/provider/vibe-auth.test.ts pin plain, quoted, exported, and unquoted-trailing-comment lines, but no quoted-value-with-trailing-comment line.

## Why it matters

The `~/.vibe/.env` tier exists for machines where the vibe binary had no keyring at sign-in; a hand edit or a dotenv tool that annotates a quoted value with a comment silently corrupts the credential. The failure mode is a 401 from Mistral with a key that looks correct everywhere it is displayed masked, and the working keyring credential that would have saved it is shadowed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parseDotEnv` returns `abc123` for both `MISTRAL_API_KEY="abc123" # comment` and `MISTRAL_API_KEY='abc123' # comment` (strip the trailing comment before, or independently of, quote removal), while quoted values containing ` #` keep their content.
- [ ] Regression tests in packages/ai/test/provider/vibe-auth.test.ts pin the quoted-plus-comment cases alongside the existing controls.
- [ ] Existing vibe-auth / vibe provider tests keep passing.
