body:
## Why

Providers classify clients by request shape — #1819 was Anthropic's third-party gate fingerprinting our env instruction line. The User-Agent is the same class of exposure: each fleet direct provider emulates a specific binary, so its requests must present that binary's identity, not OpenCode's.

Mechanism found by the audit: session requests carry the harness UA (`opencode/<channel>/<version>/cli`, from `App.useragent` in packages/core) in `request.http.headers`, and the transport (`packages/ai/src/route/transport/http.ts`) merges request headers OVER route headers. A provider identity set only in route headers therefore never reaches the wire; the stamp has to happen in the auth layer (`Headers.setAll`, applied after the merge) — the pattern antigravity and commandcode already used.

## Baseline — audited 2026-11-06

This table is the baseline for the weekly binary wire check (`weekly-binary-wire-check`, Mondays): it diffs the installed binaries and the fork against these rows and updates them.

| Provider | Reference binary (version audited) | Reference wire identity (captured) | Fork UA before | Fork UA after | UA version source in code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| claude-code | `claude` — Claude Code CLI 2.1.306 (`~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.306`) | `User-Agent: claude-cli/2.1.306 (external, sdk-cli)` in print mode (`(external, cli)` is the interactive entrypoint form); `x-app: cli`; `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`; long anthropic-beta list; plus X-Stainless-* SDK headers (see gaps) | `opencode/prod/2.0.30+1add729/cli` — the session UA won the transport merge; the route's `claude-cli/2.1.306 (external, cli)` never reached the wire | `claude-cli/2.1.306 (external, cli)` | Constant `CLI_USER_AGENT` in `packages/ai/src/protocols/claude-code-messages.ts`; re-stamped post-merge in `packages/ai/src/providers/claude-code-auth.ts` (both credential paths) |
| antigravity / antigravity-direct | `agy` — Antigravity CLI 1.5.0 (`~/.gemini/bin/agy`) | `User-Agent: antigravity/cli/1.5.0 (aidev_client; os_type=linux; arch=amd64; cl=1013440158; auth_method=consumer)` on `POST /v1internal:loadCodeAssist` | `antigravity/cli/1.4.11 (aidev_client; os_type=linux; arch=amd64; cl=1010154931; auth_method=consumer)` — stale fallback; the binary scan cannot match current builds (the UA is constructed at runtime, no literal exists in the binary) | `antigravity/cli/1.5.0 (aidev_client; os_type=linux; arch=amd64; cl=1013440158; auth_method=consumer)` | Constant `FALLBACK_UA` in `packages/ai/src/providers/antigravity-auth.ts` (exported). A runtime binary scan runs first; on current builds the fallback is the effective identity, so the constant must move with the installed CLI |
| vibe / vibe-direct | `vibe` — Mistral Vibe CLI 3.1.0 (uv tool install) | `User-Agent: Mistral-Vibe/3.1.0` on `POST /v1/chat/completions` (NOT the bundled mistralai SDK default, `speakeasy-sdk/python …`) | `opencode/prod/<ver>/cli` — no identity stamped anywhere | `Mistral-Vibe/3.1.0` | Constant `CLI_USER_AGENT` in `packages/ai/src/providers/vibe-auth.ts` (exported) |
| commandcode | `commandcode` — Command Code CLI 1.74.1 | `User-Agent: cli`; `x-command-code-version: 1.74.1`; `x-cli-environment: production` | identical — already exact, no change | identical | Constant `CLI_VERSION` in `packages/ai/src/providers/commandcode-auth.ts` (`cliHeaders()`; a `cliVersion` override exists) |
| meta (fork-native) | none — first-party API surface (`api.meta.ai`), no emulated consumer binary | — | no UA stamped | no UA stamped (unchanged) | — |
| muse-direct | config-only provider id; the upstream leg is executed by muse-proxy / the Muse CLI, outside fork code | not established (no fork-side wire) | — | — | — |

## Verification

- Wire capture, claude-code **before**: isolated instance of the deployed binary (2.0.30+1add729), session pinned to `claude-code/claude-haiku-5-5`, provider baseURL pointed at a local capture listener: `POST /messages` with `User-Agent: opencode/prod/2.0.30+1add729/cli`.
- Wire capture, claude-code **after**: isolated from-source instance of the fixed code, same setup: `POST /v1/messages` with `User-Agent: claude-cli/2.1.306 (external, cli)`, `x-app: cli`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`, full anthropic-beta list.
- Reference captures: `claude -p` with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` pointed at the listener; `vibe -p` with a capture provider in an isolated `VIBE_HOME`; `agy --print` through a local CONNECT MITM with a self-signed CA.
- Unit tests assert the stamped UA through auth application with a session UA present (claude-code-auth, vibe-auth, antigravity-auth test files); the full packages/ai suite shows no new failures (2165 pass; the 12 failures are pre-existing on main: Bedrock Mantle / Cloudflare / MiniMax recorded suites).

## Known gaps / notes for the weekly check

- claude-code: the real CLI also sends `X-Stainless-*` headers (language/runtime/OS/arch, SDK package version 0.128.0). The fork does not send them; previously established as not gated on. Track here whether that changes.
- Version drift is the standing risk: every UA above embeds a client version held in a named constant (last column). When an installed binary moves, its constant must move; the weekly check exists to catch exactly that.
- Quota-provider UAs are a separate surface (e.g. antigravity quota uses `antigravity/2.24.0 <platform>` in `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/antigravity.ts`) and are NOT covered by this baseline.
- Related: #1819 (env-line fingerprinting — same exposure class).

Fix PR: to be linked.

## Acceptance criteria
- Each fleet direct provider's requests present the User-Agent of the binary it emulates, not the harness UA (`opencode/<channel>/<version>/cli`).
- The transport header-merge order no longer lets session/request headers silently override a provider's identity headers (or the override is explicit, tested, and documented on this issue).
- Regression coverage asserts the on-the-wire User-Agent for at least one direct provider end-to-end (route + transport).

title: claude-code provider: no OAuth renewal — emulation depends on the real CLI keeping ~/.claude/.credentials.json fresh

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: source/human
labels.description: Filed directly by a human

labels.name: priority/low

body:
## Gap: claude-code provider does not perform the Claude Code binary's OAuth renewal

**Provider:** `packages/ai/src/providers/claude-code-auth.ts` (#6117 native wire emulation)

### What the binary does
The Claude Code CLI renews its claude.ai OAuth login itself: when the access token in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` approaches/passes expiry, the CLI exchanges the stored `refreshToken` at Anthropic's OAuth token endpoint (`POST https://console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token`, `grant_type=refresh_token`, the Claude Code OAuth client identity) and writes the rotated credential back to the same file. Fleet-observed cadence: the file's `expiresAt` advances in ~8h steps as the CLI runs (e.g. 2026-11-06: 08:19 CST → 09:19 CST after CLI use).

### What the emulation does
Read-only by deliberate design. `claude-code-auth.ts` lines 34–40 (header) state it plainly:

> "The credential is read IN PLACE, fresh per request, never copied into the fork's credential store, never written back, and never logged. This provider deliberately does NOT refresh the token: the refresh token is the CLI's, a refresh here would rotate it out from under the CLI, and renewal of an expired login is the interactive `claude` sign-in. An expired credential therefore fails LOUDLY … instead of silently degrading."

`parseCredentialsFile` does not even read `refreshToken` out of the blob (only `accessToken` + `expiresAt`); an expired file credential falls through to `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` if set (#1752), else fails with `expiredMessage` ("this provider does not refresh the CLI's login. Run `claude`…").

### Why this is a gap vs the binary
- The provider's liveness silently depends on the real CLI being run interactively often enough to keep the shared file fresh. A laptop where nobody runs `claude` for >8h has a dead claude-code provider even though a valid refresh token sits in the same file.
- The in-repo precedent solves the identical problem safely: `antigravity-auth.ts` performs the CLI's own refresh exchange in memory only, noting Google's client does not rotate the refresh token, "so refreshing here never invalidates the CLI's stored credential". Anthropic's OAuth behavior for the Claude Code client needs the same determination: if the token endpoint does NOT rotate the refresh token (or the rotated pair can be written back to the credentials file atomically, mirroring the CLI), the emulation can renew without racing the CLI.
- Quota side already half-knows: `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/claude.ts` parses `refreshToken` out of the same blob (line 79) but never uses it; on 401/403 it reports "Claude session expired. Open Claude Code to sign in again."

### Suggested shape (mirrors antigravity-auth)
1. Parse `refreshToken` in `parseCredentialsFile`.
2. On expired (or near-expiry) file credential, attempt ONE in-memory refresh against the OAuth token endpoint with the Claude Code client identity; use the returned access token for the request; never log tokens.
3. Decide write-back vs memory-only from Anthropic's actual rotation behavior (probe: refresh once, then check whether the CLI still functions with the file's original refresh token). If rotation invalidates the file's token, write the rotated pair back to `~/.claude/.credentials.json` atomically (0600 preserved) exactly as the CLI would.
4. Keep the fail-loud behavior when refresh itself fails.

### Evidence gathered 2026-11-06 (fleet laptop)
- Credential file: `claudeAiOauth`, scopes include `user:inference` + `user:sessions:claude_code`, refresh token present, `expiresAt` observed advancing after real-CLI runs.
- The provider's inference wire shape is otherwise verified live (200s from `api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` in the provider's exact shape); renewal is the one lifecycle piece of the binary the emulation does not cover.

## Acceptance criteria
- The provider's behavior when the CLI credential passes expiry with no live CLI renewal is explicit and observable: either the emulation performs the refresh-token exchange itself (with the rotation hazard addressed in writing), or the failure surfaces as a named, actionable error (expired credential, run the CLI to renew) instead of an opaque auth failure.
- The read-in-place, never-logged credential discipline is preserved by any change.
- Coverage exists for the expired-credential path.

body:
## Summary

The Claude quota transform (`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/claude.ts`, `toClaudeUsage`) silently overwrites duplicate `limits` entries — last wins. `addWindow` assigns `target[key] = ...` unconditionally (claude.ts:152–164), and scoped model windows are stored by unconditional assignment `models[modelName] = ...` (claude.ts:185). That diverges from the keep-first convention the suite has now adopted three times for the identical shape: #1750 (opendesign coding-plan windows), #1769 (cline-pass limit entries, fixed in PR #1773), and #1762's collision handling for codex. Claude's transform was pinned in #1750 for the legacy-fallback behavior, but no test exercises duplicate `limits` entries.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 32fc03baef)

Probe on the laptop (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-claude-quota/probe.ts`, kept) importing `toClaudeUsage`:

- CASE1 — limits `[session 20% (reset 2026-12-01), session 80% (reset 2026-12-02), weekly_all 30%, weekly_all 70%]`: published `5h` = 80% with the second reset, `7d` = 70% — both first entries silently dropped.
- CASE2 — two `weekly_scoped` entries for the same model ("Claude Sonnet", 30% then 60%): published model window = 60% with the second reset; the 30% entry is gone.
- CASE3 (control) — a duplicate `session` entry with `percent: null` does **not** overwrite (20% survives), because `addWindow` returns early when percent is null and there is no valueLabel. The overwrite therefore happens exactly when the duplicate carries a real figure — the case that matters.

## Why it matters

Claude is a plan pool the fork rotates across. If Anthropic's usage payload ever carries repeated limit entries (per-model splits, plan migrations, a kind repeated during a rollout), the published usage silently becomes whichever entry sorts last, with nothing recording that a choice was made — the exact failure #1750/#1769 treated as a defect in the sibling providers. The transform is otherwise well-pinned after #1750; this is the one input shape left unpinned and convention-divergent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Duplicate `limits` entries keep the first entry per kind (and per model for `weekly_scoped`), per the #1750 convention — or a different disposition is chosen and documented in the code + this issue's closing note. The legacy-fallback precedence from #1750 (limits-produced windows win over `five_hour`/`seven_day`) is unchanged.
- [ ] `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins: duplicate `session`, duplicate `weekly_all`, duplicate `weekly_scoped` for one model, two different models' scoped entries both surviving, and the null-percent duplicate control (first entry survives).
- [ ] Existing quota suite stays green; gate state not regressed (the three quota-era gates already red on main belong to #1724 — do not conflate).

body:
## Summary

The Meta quota provider (`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/meta.ts`) keys its rolling window only by a label derived from the window's duration, then writes the weekly window under the literal key `weekly` in the same record — so when the rolling window's duration is one week, the two distinct windows collide and the rolling window is silently lost. This is the same derived-label collision class fixed for codex in #1762, in a provider whose parser was supposedly pinned by #1750 (its tests only ever use a 18000s rolling duration).

Two sites share the pattern:

- `parseSubscriptionQuota` (meta.ts:96–106): the object literal is `{ [windowSeconds ? resolveWindowLabel(windowSeconds) : "rolling"]: <rolling window>, weekly: <weekly window> }`. `resolveWindowLabel` (quota/utils.ts:64–72) returns `"weekly"` for 604800s, so the literal `weekly` entry overwrites the rolling entry.
- `keyUsageResult` (meta.ts:219–232, the key-endpoint fallback): `windows[resolveWindowLabel(window_duration_mins * 60)] = <rolling>` followed by `windows.weekly = <weekly>` — a rolling duration of 10080 minutes collides identically. This function is not exported, so it has no direct test seam today.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 32fc03baef)

Probe on the laptop (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-meta-quota/probe.ts`, kept) importing `parseSubscriptionQuota` from the laptop primary:

- CASE1 — `window_duration_secs: 604800`, rolling 100/1000 (10% used, reset 1793552400), weekly 900/1000 (90% used, reset 1793980800): published keys are exactly `[ "weekly" ]`, with `usedPercent 90` — the rolling 10% window is gone, with no error or trace.
- CASE2 (control) — `window_duration_secs: 18000`, same figures: keys `[ "5h", "weekly" ]`, 5h at 10%, weekly at 90%.
- CASE3 (control) — `window_duration_secs: 86400`: keys `[ "1d", "weekly" ]`, both windows present.

So the loss is specific to the derived label equalling `weekly`. The portal's current proven payload uses 18000s (see the fixture comment in quota.test.ts), which is why this has not fired live yet — but the parser deliberately derives the key from an upstream-supplied duration instead of the window's semantic role, so a plan/tier whose rolling window is a week (or any upstream duration change) silently degrades the published quota to one window. Meta is the Muse High Usage pool — the sole-door pool the fleet's placement decisions read — so a silently missing window is a placement-grade data loss, not a cosmetic one.

Existing pins: `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` ("meta portal subscription-quota mapping") covers only 18000s durations; no case exercises a weekly-length rolling duration for either site.

## Why it matters

Quota windows drive pool placement and exhaustion decisions. A collision here does not produce a wrong percentage — it erases a whole window, and the surviving `weekly` window carries the weekly figure under the correct-looking key, so nothing downstream can tell data was lost. #1762 established that derived-label keying must not be able to drop a window; meta is the remaining provider with that exact construction, in two places.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both meta mapping sites (`parseSubscriptionQuota` and `keyUsageResult`) publish the rolling and weekly windows under distinct keys for every rolling duration, including 604800s / 10080 minutes — e.g. a semantic rolling key, or collision disambiguation in the style of #1762's fix; the chosen keying is documented in code.
- [ ] `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` pins the collision case (weekly-length rolling duration, distinct rolling/weekly figures and resets, both windows survive with their own values) plus the existing 18000s shape unchanged.
- [ ] `keyUsageResult` gains a test seam (export or equivalent) if needed to pin the second site, or the closing note records how that site was verified.
- [ ] Existing quota suite stays green; gate state not regressed (the bounded-http / numeric / proto gates already red on main belong to #1724 — do not conflate).

title: fix(ci): check:workflows never validates job-level permissions content — caller jobs bypass the #1503 policy entirely, excepted jobs unchecked

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: area/ci
labels.description: CI, workflows, and build infrastructure

labels.name: app/script
labels.description: Package: script (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Finding

The permissions policy PR #1594 added to `check:workflows` (for #1503) validates only the **top-level** `permissions:` block. No job-level `permissions:` block ever has its content checked against the policy — and reusable-workflow caller jobs are not even gated on having a block:

- In `script/check-workflows.ts` (current main `e28985a80863`), `workflowViolations` validates scope keys (`PERMISSION_SCOPES`), levels (`PERMISSION_LEVELS`), the scalar-shorthand ban, and the write-only-on-`contents` rule only inside the top-level branch (lines ~210–258).
- Caller jobs: lines 267–277 — a job with `uses:` is checked only for its key names against `REUSABLE_WORKFLOW_CALLER_KEYS` (which includes `permissions`) and then `continue`s, before any permissions handling. The comment at lines 265–266 says a caller job's block "still counts as using a baseline exception," but nothing checks that the job is in `JOB_PERMISSION_EXCEPTIONS` — any caller job may declare any `permissions:` content, including `write-all` or `issues: write`, and `check:workflows` reports no violation.
- Non-caller jobs: the block at lines ~279–288 checks only presence against `JOB_PERMISSION_EXCEPTIONS`. A baselined exception job (e.g. the 13 entries in `JOB_PERMISSION_EXCEPTIONS`) may change its block to any scopes/levels — scalar `write-all` included — with no violation, even though the top-level branch explicitly calls the scalar shorthand a grant that "never satisfies the least-privilege posture."

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1594 (merged 2026-11-04T07:19:40Z, merge commit `53f06c2ead835`, commits `006592843a06`, `70bd31b26c3f`) — its body states the policy as "every workflow must declare a top-level `permissions:` mapping in the least-privilege posture" with scope/level/write rules; the job-level content path was not implemented.
- Current main verification (this run): re-read `script/check-workflows.ts` at main `e28985a80863` twice — the caller branch still `continue`s at line 277 ahead of the `no-job-level-permissions` check, and no code path calls the scope/level/write validation on a job-level value. `PERMISSION_SCOPES` / `PERMISSION_LEVELS` / `WRITE_PERMITTED_SCOPES` are referenced only for the top-level block.
- Live posture today is conformant by inspection (e.g. `agents.yml`'s job-level block mirrors its top level), so this is a gate hole, not a live over-grant: the next caller or exception job that widens its block is invisible to the gate #1503 created to catch exactly this class (#118: GITHUB_TOKEN falling back to broader grants than intended).
- Dedupe: searched open + closed issues for `caller permissions`, `job-level permissions`, `check-workflows` (2026-11-05). #1503 (closed) is the parent policy; open PR #1504 is the superseded weaker variant whose closure is tracked by open #1654 — neither covers validating job-level content in the landed policy. #1654 does not mention this gap.

## Why it matters

The #1503 policy's value is that a broader-than-intended GITHUB_TOKEN grant cannot land silently. At job level it still can: job-level blocks **replace** the top-level grant wholesale for that job (the PR's own words), so the unchecked path is precisely the one that determines the effective grant for caller jobs and for the sync/gate jobs that hold today's `issues`/`pull-requests`/`id-token` write exceptions. A one-line edit widening any of those blocks — or a new caller job declaring `permissions: write-all` — passes `bun run check:workflows` clean.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `workflowViolations` applies the same content validation to every job-level `permissions:` value it permits (caller jobs and `JOB_PERMISSION_EXCEPTIONS` jobs): mapping form only (no `write-all`/`read-all` scalar), scope keys in `PERMISSION_SCOPES`, levels in `PERMISSION_LEVELS`.
- [ ] Job-level `write` grants beyond `contents` require a named baseline: either the existing exception maps gain the granted scopes per job, or an equivalent ratcheted record — an unbaselined job-level write grant is a violation, and a baselined grant that disappears is a stale-exception violation, mirroring the top-level rules.
- [ ] A caller job declaring `permissions:` without a baseline entry is a violation (per the line 265–266 comment's stated intent), or the comment and policy text are corrected to say caller blocks are intentionally unbaselined — one of the two, not the current mismatch.
- [ ] Tests in `script/check-workflows.test.ts` cover: caller job with `permissions: write-all` flagged; caller job with an unbaselined `issues: write` flagged; excepted job whose block widens beyond its baseline flagged; today's real workflows still pass `collectViolations` with no new violations.

title: fix(ci): gate drift guard walks only packages/ and services/ — sdks/vscode/src, github/script and sdks/vscode/script already escape all three allowlist gates

body:
## Finding

The src/script tree drift guard added by PR #1575 (for #1494) and carried into the shared harness by PR #1586 only walks two top-level directories, so package trees anywhere else escape every allowlist gate undetected — and three already do.

In `script/gate-harness.ts` (current main `e28985a80863`), `treesOnDisk` at line 138 walks only:

```ts
for (const top of ["packages", "services"]) if (existsSync(join(root, top))) walk(join(root, top))
```

That walk feeds `srcTreesOnDisk` / `scriptTreesOnDisk` / `unscannedSrcTrees` / `unscannedScriptTrees` for all three gates (`check-bounded-http`, `check-numeric-boundaries`, `check-proto-reads`). A tree outside `packages/` and `services/` is therefore invisible to the guard, so the gates' own completeness tests pass while the tree is in no `SCAN_ROOTS` list.

## Evidence

- Source PRs: #1575 (merged 2026-11-04T01:59:12Z, merge commit `35fef7480ff1`, commit `0116e7eb36ab` — added `srcTreesOnDisk` with the same two-top walk in both gate files) and #1586 (merged 2026-11-04T07:52:29Z, merge commit `6fd843601291` — generalised the same walk into `script/gate-harness.ts` `treesOnDisk`, unchanged on current main at line 138).
- Already escaping on current main (git tree of `main` @ `e28985a80863`, verified this run):
  - `sdks/vscode/src` — a package src tree by the guard's own definition (its parent `sdks/vscode/package.json` exists; the tree holds `extension.ts`, a `.ts` file in the gates' scanned extensions). It appears in **no** gate's `SCAN_ROOTS` (the lists in `script/check-bounded-http.ts`, `script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts`, `script/check-proto-reads.ts` cover only `packages/*` and `services/*` src trees).
  - `github/script` — a package script tree (parent `github/package.json` exists; holds `publish` and `release`). Not in `check-bounded-http`'s `SCAN_ROOTS` (which lists root `script`, `packages/*/script(s)`, `services/www/script` only) and undiscoverable by `scriptTreesOnDisk`.
  - `sdks/vscode/script` — same shape (parent `sdks/vscode/package.json` exists; holds `publish` and `release`); likewise unscanned and undiscoverable.
- Checked and correctly excluded: `nix/scripts` — no `package.json` at `nix/` or at the tree itself, so it does not meet the guard's package-tree definition; this finding is only about trees that meet the definition but sit under other top-level directories.
- Dedupe: searched open + closed issues for `unscanned`, `treesOnDisk`, `"sdks/vscode"`, `"github/script"` (2026-11-05). #1494 (closed) created the guard for `packages/`+`services/`; #1611 (open) is about `gate-harness.test.ts` not running in any workflow — a different gap. Nothing covers the top-level walk blind spot or the three escaped trees.

## Why it matters

#1494 existed because a new package's src tree "would silently escape the gates while both reported success." That exact failure is already live for the VS Code extension package: `sdks/vscode/src/extension.ts` gets no bounded-http, numeric-boundary, or proto-read scanning, and the drift guard structurally cannot notice any future tree created under `sdks/`, `github/`, or any new top-level directory. The guard's green test ("no src tree on disk in this repo is unscanned") is self-consistent with its own blind spot.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `treesOnDisk` in `script/gate-harness.ts` discovers package-owned src/script trees under every top-level directory that can hold a package (at minimum `sdks/` and `github/`), or walks the repo root with the existing exclusions (node_modules, non-package folders) instead of a fixed top list.
- [ ] `sdks/vscode/src`, `github/script`, and `sdks/vscode/script` are either added to the relevant gates' `SCAN_ROOTS` with their hits dispositioned in the allowlists, or explicitly excluded with a named disposition in the harness/gate source.
- [ ] Regression tests in `script/gate-harness.test.ts` (or the gate test files) plant a package tree under a non-`packages/`/non-`services/` top (e.g. `sdks/<pkg>/src` with a parent `package.json`) and assert it is reported by `unscannedSrcTrees`/`unscannedScriptTrees`; the real-repo completeness checks pass.
- [ ] All three gates' hit sets for the previously scanned roots are unchanged (byte-identical before/after, as in #1586's verification).

body:
## Finding (filed by the pr-diff-review job, 2026-11-05 09:24 CST run)

Open PR #1473 — "fix(core): let due bench probes recover quota-exhausted pools" — is the only implementation of issue #1390, and it is stranded: CONFLICTING/DIRTY against current main and untouched since 2026-11-03, while #1390 stays open and the defect stays live on main.

## Evidence

- PR #1473: OPEN, created 2026-11-03T00:48:21Z, last updated 2026-11-03T00:50:26Z, head `aee912ad6`. Merge state verified twice this run: `gh pr view` reports mergeable=CONFLICTING / mergeStateStatus=DIRTY; the REST pulls endpoint agrees.
- Issue #1390: OPEN — "pool quota exclusion defeats due bench probes — probe-eligible leaves stay excluded until the escalated cooldown expires".
- Current main `8185486080ab686d3a160f16deb5357f1199fda3` does NOT contain the fix:
  - `packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts`: the pool-exclusion branches (lines ~809–824) still read `else if (isPoolExhausted)` and `!isPoolExhausted` with no due-probe carve-out (`poolProbe` does not exist on main).
  - `packages/core/src/model-route.ts`: `poolQuotaExhausted` (line ~741) counts a leaf's quota evidence via `quotaEvidence(...)` with no `probeDue` carve-out, so a due half-open probe still counts toward the pool threshold that excludes it.
- Conflict warning for whoever rebases: PR #1473's diff also deletes `retainedQuotaWindowMs` as "dead code" (the TS6133 cleanup). On current main that helper no longer exists in that form — the #1484 retention fix (issue #1484, CLOSED) landed refactored: `retainedDemotionWindow()` now unions both config layers (demotion readers + settings readers). A rebase must drop/redo that hunk against main's current shape, not resurrect the old deletion or re-break #1484's retention union.

## Why it matters

The due bench probe is the pool's half-open recovery path. While the pool verdict counts the due probe itself as exhaustion evidence, a quota-exhausted pool cannot recover until the escalated cooldown expires — exactly the failure #1390 records (a PR #1384 Codex P2 that was never addressed). The finished, test-carrying fix exists only in this conflicting PR, and every day main moves, the rebase gets harder.

## Acceptance criteria

- PR #1473 is rebased onto current main and mergeable (not CONFLICTING/DIRTY), or closed as superseded by a fresh PR carrying the same change.
- On the resulting branch: `poolQuotaExhausted` does not count a leaf whose bench probe is due (claimed / not-yet-due benches still count), and the resolver's ready + last-resort pool exclusion admits a leaf whose own probe is due — matching PR #1473's original change.
- The PR's regression tests pass on the final head: the model-route pool test ("due bench probes do not pull their pool; claimed and not-yet-due benches still do") and the model-resolver recovery test ("lets a due half-open probe recover a quota-exhausted pool").
- Main's current #1484 shape is preserved: `demotionPolicy` still falls back to `activeSettings(location).quota` and `retainedDemotionWindow()` still unions both config layers.
- Issue #1390 is closed by the landing PR; this issue closes when PR #1473 (or its superseding PR) lands.

# quota: harden the subcommand against slow providers (30s cap + silent omission)

Follow-up to #1718 / PR #1722, found during the single-source E2E (developing-today/code#6125), 2026-11-05.

Two defects in one live gatherer tick driven by the built binary (v2.0.30+quota):

1. **mistral read hit the 30s handler cap under concurrent load** — `Quota fetch timed out after 30000ms`. The provider alone returns ok in ~8.9s and the raw CDP budget fetch in ~7.2s; under the full listing's concurrency the CDP-backed read exceeds 30s. A CDP-backed quota read needs a larger budget: raise the per-provider timeout for the mistral/console read (or globally to 60s) so a slow-but-working provider is not indistinguishable from a dead one.
2. **A provider result was omitted entirely instead of error-rowed.** The same tick's listing JSON contained no deepseek result at all (13 runs expected from 14 listing results + 2 explicit asks; deepseek absent), while an earlier standalone run returned deepseek ok. Whatever the cause (an internal deadline cutting the tail is the suspect), the contract must be: every configured provider emits a result object every run — an error result when it cannot answer — never silence. The gatherer cannot retain last-known rows (#1268) for a provider the subcommand never mentions, so an omission reads downstream as "provider vanished".

Acceptance: a full listing under load emits one result per configured provider + credential (error rows included); mistral's console budget read completes within its budget on the standing laptop.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A full `opencode quota` listing under load emits exactly one result object per configured provider + credential — an error row when a provider cannot answer, never a silent omission.
- [ ] The mistral/console (CDP-backed) read completes within its per-provider budget on the standing laptop (budget raised for CDP-backed reads, e.g. 60s, or an equivalent fix).
- [ ] A regression test or recorded live tick demonstrates both: no missing provider rows, and a slow provider resolving as a result (ok or error), not a timeout-shaped absence.

# test(ai): PR #1722's quota suite pins 4 of its pure parsers — opencode-go's three parsers and openrouter's reset math have none, and opencode-go silently drops windows its siblings would keep

Verified 2026-11-05 on origin/main `13ab3dc5c2d51fa35ff0273e18f5ef647eca83db` (PR #1722, quota subcommand). `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` (7 tests, all passing on the laptop) pins exactly four pure parsers against captured live payloads: `parseMistralBudget` (mistral), `parseSubscriptionQuota` (meta), `tursoWindows` (turso), `parseGroqResetSeconds` (groq). That is the PR's own established pattern — exported pure parser + payload-shaped test, including the pinned semantic "a payload without budgets maps to nulls, never zeros".

The same PR exports more pure parsers that no test touches (grep over `packages/ai/test/` and `packages/cli/test/` for their names: 0 hits):

## opencode-go — three exported parsers, zero tests (`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/opencode-go.ts`)

- `parseOpenCodeGoUsage` (:48-61), `parseConsoleGoUsage` (:69-84), `parseConsoleBillingBalance` (:86-90) — payload→WindowMap conversions for a provider this fork's routing actually leans on.
- Concrete unpinned behavior: at :57 a window is **dropped entirely** when `usedPercent === null || resetAt === null`. A payload entry with a valid percent but a missing/unparseable `resetsAt` vanishes — no window at all — where sibling mappers in the same PR keep the window and report the missing field as null (deepseek's `credits_balance` window is built with `resetAt: null`; codex's `credits`/`credits_balance` windows likewise). Whether dropping is right for opencode-go is a decision; today it is an accident of implementation that no test records. `fetchOpenCodeGoUsage` (:110-112) then converts an all-dropped map into a thrown "usage data could not be parsed", so one field's absence turns a partial answer into a provider error.
- `parseConsoleGoUsage` (:80) requires limit AND used AND resetAt, and computes `(used / limit) * 100` from micro-cents — unit or field-name drift upstream silently zeroes the provider's windows (empty map → error path above), with no fixture to catch it.

## openrouter — reset date math, zero tests (`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/openrouter.ts`)

- `resolveResetAt` (:32-44) computes daily/weekly/monthly reset instants in UTC. The weekly branch (:38-41) resolves to the next Monday UTC via `d + ((8 - dow) % 7 || 7)` — an assumption about OpenRouter's reset weekday and timezone that appears nowhere else (no comment, no test, no captured payload). On a Monday it jumps a full 7 days. If the assumption is wrong, every openrouter window's reset time is wrong by days, and quota-aware routing (#587/#566 consumers) reasons from it.
- The monthly branch (:42) and daily branch (:37) are likewise unpinned at month/year boundaries (Dec 31 → Jan 1, Jan 31 → Mar 1 via `Date.UTC(y, m + 1, 1)` overflow semantics).

## Why it matters

These parsers are the quota signal's front door: their outputs feed the `opencode quota` display and the route/quota consumers. The PR proved the testing pattern on four parsers; the untested remainder includes the provider (opencode-go) whose payloads are most likely to drift, and date math of exactly the class this repo has been bitten by before (#655: calendar-invalid reset dates rolling over; #933: reset parsing without a ceiling). A fixture per parser costs little now, while the payload shapes are fresh; reconstructing them after a silent upstream drift is the expensive version.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` (or a sibling test file wired into the ai package test script) covers `parseOpenCodeGoUsage`, `parseConsoleGoUsage`, and `parseConsoleBillingBalance` with payload-shaped fixtures, including the missing-field cases.
- [ ] The window-drop behavior at opencode-go.ts:57 is either pinned by a test that names it as intended, or changed to the sibling pattern (keep the window, null the missing field) with a test for the new behavior — the issue/PR records which was chosen and why.
- [ ] `resolveResetAt` is pinned for daily/weekly/monthly at day, week, month, and year boundaries, with the weekly reset-weekday assumption stated in a comment or test name (and corrected if the pin shows it wrong).
- [ ] All new tests pass under the ai package's existing test command; the 7 existing quota tests still pass.

# fix(ai): antigravity WIRE_COMPLETE_MODELS is a static snapshot of a live upstream catalog — the next wire-complete model silently 404s again (#1704 recurrence)

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-05 on main d91f5a4964, the merge of PR #1716)

PR #1716 fixed #1704 by teaching `resolveModelAndEffort` not to append an effort suffix to wire-complete model ids. The classification is a hardcoded set:

- `packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts:82-92` — `WIRE_COMPLETE_MODELS` holds exactly 9 ids (gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.5-flash-lite, gemini-2.5-flash-thinking, gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-3-flash, gemini-3.1-flash-image, gemini-3.1-flash-lite, gemini-3.5-flash-lite, gemini-3.8-flash-tiered).
- `packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts:101` — every other model id gets `-<effort>` appended: `WIRE_COMPLETE_MODELS.has(model) ? model : \`${model}-${resolved}\``.
- The set was transcribed from a one-time live probe of the upstream `v1internal:fetchAvailableModels` catalog (26 keys, daily- and prod cloudcode-pa, 2026-11-05) — that catalog exists in this repo only as a comment (`antigravity.ts:62-81`) and in PR #1716's commit message. `grep -rn fetchAvailableModels packages/ai/src` returns only the comment: the provider never fetches or validates against the catalog at runtime.
- `packages/ai/test/provider/antigravity.test.ts:114-149` pins the behavior by example (4 of the 9 set members, plus suffix-healing) but no test or fixture asserts the set against the probed catalog, so nothing fails when the set and the catalog drift apart.

## Why it matters

The upstream catalog is live and changes (models are added/renamed by Google, not by this repo). The first time a user selects a wire-complete model that shipped upstream after 2026-11-05 — or a renamed one — `resolveModelAndEffort` appends `-medium` (or the chosen effort), minting an entity that does not exist upstream, and `streamGenerateContent` answers 404 NOT_FOUND. That is exactly the #1704 failure mode ("provider down for plain prompts"), recurring silently with no test, gate, or probe positioned to catch it before a user does. The effort-family side has the symmetric risk: an effort family upstream starts keying bare would be suffixed into a 404 the same way.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The wire-complete classification is checked against a recorded catalog fixture: a test in `packages/ai/test/provider/antigravity.test.ts` (or a sibling) holds the probed 26-key catalog (both endpoints, dated) as data and asserts every key is classified correctly — bare keys resolve bare, effort-family keys resolve to a catalog key — so a set edit without a catalog re-probe fails loudly.
- [ ] A documented refresh path exists (script or probe note in the fixture header): how to re-probe `fetchAvailableModels` on daily- and prod cloudcode-pa and update the fixture + set together.
- [ ] OR, instead of the fixture: classification is derived at runtime from a `fetchAvailableModels` call where auth is available, with the static set kept only as an offline fallback — and a test covers the fallback classification against the fixture.
- [ ] Existing antigravity tests stay green (`bun test test/provider/antigravity.test.ts` in packages/ai), including the suffix-healing cases from PR #1716.

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode, 2026-11-05 run (verified by reading the code at main d91f5a4964 in a laptop worktree; all 6 root check:* gates green at that SHA). Related: #1704 (the bug this classification fixed), PR #1716.

## Finding

Open PR #1459 (`fix(github): bound action HTTP calls and scan the tree`, head `b153e2296ec6a6f2e4594796d06010817582e287`) is **CONFLICTING / DIRTY against current main** and has not been updated since 2026-11-02, while the fix it carries is still needed: its origin issue #1436 is still OPEN, and the unbounded fetches it bounds are still present verbatim on current main.

This is a pr-shepherd finding from the pr-diff-review job: PR #1459 needs to be rebased / reworked onto current main (or superseded by a fresh PR carrying the same change) — not left conflicting while #1436 stays open.

## Evidence

- PR #1459 state, verified twice this run (2026-11-05 ~01:24 CST): `gh pr view` reports `mergeable: CONFLICTING`, `mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`; an independent `gh api …/pulls/1459` read reports `mergeable: false`, `mergeable_state: dirty`. Last update: `2026-11-02T23:08:51Z`.
- Origin issue #1436 (`fix(ci): check:bounded-http does not scan the github/ tree …`) is still OPEN.
- Current main `github/index.ts` (blob `e8acd9a9cef3c7cdd41093612430e0938f212100` at review time) still contains the unbounded sites PR #1459 was written to bound: the token-exchange fetches at lines 377 and 386, unbounded `response.json()` reads at lines 395 and 399, the attachment download fetch at line 465, and the token-revoke fetch at line 1063 — none carries an `AbortSignal` deadline or a byte-capped body read.
- PR #1459's own diff (4 files) is the fix that is stranded: `github/index.ts` (30s token-exchange deadlines + 64KB capped JSON reads, 60s / streamed 10MB attachment download, 10s token-revoke deadline), `script/check-bounded-http.ts` (adds `github` to `SCAN_ROOTS`), its allowlist dispositions, and gate tests.
- Main has moved on in the same gate area since PR #1459 was opened — e.g. PR #1575 (src-tree drift guards for the bounded-http gate) and PR #1586 (one shared harness for the three allowlist gates) merged — which is the likely source of the conflicts in the `script/check-bounded-http*` files; the `github/index.ts` half may apply more cleanly, but the PR as a whole cannot merge as-is.
- Dedupe: a search for open issues naming PR #1459 found no existing shepherd / stale-PR issue; issue #1436 tracks the underlying gate gap, not the stranded PR.

## Why it matters

The published GitHub Action's outbound calls still have no deadline and read response bodies unbounded — exactly the hang / memory risk the repo's bounded-http policy exists to prevent, and the gate still does not scan the `github/` tree, so new unbounded sites there would not be caught either. A conflicting PR gives the appearance of coverage while nothing can land.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PR #1459 is rebased onto current main with its conflicts resolved (preserving both the PR's `github/` dispositions and main's later gate changes, incl. the shared allowlist-gate harness from PR #1586), **or** it is closed as superseded by a fresh PR carrying the same bounded-http change for the `github/` tree.
- [ ] On the resulting branch, `bun run script/check-bounded-http.ts` exits 0 with the `github/` tree scanned, and the gate tests in `script/check-bounded-http.test.ts` pass.
- [ ] Issue #1436 is closed by the landing PR (it already carries `Closes #1436` intent), or a comment on issue #1436 records why it remains open.
- [ ] Whichever PR lands, the token-exchange, attachment-download, and token-revoke fetches in `github/index.ts` carry deadlines and byte-capped body reads on main.

# fix(ci): Solid test suites break on Bun ≥1.4.3 — `jsxDEV` not found in solid-js production build; CONTRIBUTING's "Bun 1.3 or newer" is false for tests

## Evidence (verified this run, on origin/main `561e5304e0cd24d9838ea72e9f5a6364b163028e`)

The repo pins `bun@1.4.2` (`package.json` `packageManager`), and CI enforces the pin via `bun-version-file: package.json` (`.github/workflows/test.yml:53`, `.github/actions/setup-bun/action.yml`) — so CI is green. But anyone running the tests with a newer Bun — which `CONTRIBUTING.md:25` explicitly invites ("OpenCode requires Bun 1.3 or newer") — gets a cryptic module error in every Solid-JSX package and no usable test verdict:

```
SyntaxError: Export named 'jsxDEV' not found in module
'…/node_modules/solid-js/dist/solid.js'
```

Reproduced in a clean laptop worktree of `origin/main` (`bun install` from the lockfile), same tree, three Bun versions:

| Bun | `packages/ui` (`bun test src`) | `packages/session-ui` | `packages/app` (`test:unit`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.4.2 (pinned) | 156 pass / 0 fail | — | — |
| 1.4.3 | `src/context/i18n.test.ts`: 1 fail / 1 error (jsxDEV) | — | — |
| 1.4.4 | 3 files error (i18n, scroll-view, segmented-control), 124 pass / 3 fail | 1 file errors (`markdown-solid.test.tsx`), 247 pass / 1 fail | 35 errors, all jsxDEV |

Non-Solid suites are unaffected on 1.4.4 (ai 1933 pass, tui 1521 pass, codemode 1418 pass, core-adjacent packages green) — the break is specific to test files whose import graph pulls in `.tsx` compiled against `solid-js`.

## Root cause (as far as verified)

- Bun ≥1.4.3's test transpiler emits `jsxDEV` imports (`solid-js/jsx-dev-runtime`) for JSX in test-loaded modules.
- `solid-js@1.9.15`'s `package.json` exports map `./jsx-dev-runtime` to `./dist/solid.js` — the **production** build, which does not export `jsxDEV` (the dev build `dist/dev.js`, which does, is only reachable via the `development` export condition). The repo's own `patches/solid-js@1.9.15.patch` does not touch this mapping.
- The affected packages' test scripts (`packages/ui/package.json`: `"test": "bun test src --only-failures"`, `packages/session-ui/package.json`: `"test": "bun test src --only-failures"`) set no conditions/preload that would resolve the development build, unlike `packages/app`'s `--conditions=solid` unit script — and even app's suites fail on 1.4.4, so conditions alone are not the whole story.

## Why it matters

- The documented contributor floor ("1.3 or newer") and the actually-working toolchain (exactly 1.4.2) disagree; the failure mode is a misleading `SyntaxError` deep in `node_modules`, not a version check — a new contributor (or a fleet machine whose distro bumps Bun, as this run's laptop did: nix-provided 1.4.4) burns time rediscovering that the toolchain, not the code, is broken, and Solid packages silently lose their local test verdict.
- The pin is a single point of fragility: the next intentional Bun bump will hit this on day one, in CI, with no prior warning.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide and implement one direction: (a) make the Solid test suites pass on current Bun (e.g. resolve the `development` condition / `jsx-dev-runtime` to the dev build in the affected packages' test setup, or extend the solid-js patch), or (b) enforce the pinned Bun version for local test runs with a clear early error (and correct `CONTRIBUTING.md` to state the exact pin).
- [ ] Whichever direction: `packages/ui`, `packages/session-ui`, and `packages/app` unit suites run to a real verdict on the Bun version the repo claims to support, verified by running them.
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s Bun requirement matches reality after the change.
- [ ] No regression on the pinned toolchain: the same suites still pass under `bun@1.4.2` / in CI.

# fix(schema): route Window string fields accept values the runtime parser rejects — one bad `dates`/`start`/`timezone` string silently drops the whole window

## Summary

`Config.ModelRoute.Window`'s string fields carry documented formats but no schema validation: `dates`/`excludeDates` are plain `Schema.Array(Schema.String)`, and `start`, `end`, and `timezone` are plain `Schema.String`. The runtime parser in core enforces those formats strictly — and rejects the **entire window** when any one entry is unreadable. So config that validates cleanly at decode is later discarded wholesale, with no diagnostic: a typo in one holiday date, a `"9am"` start, or a misspelled timezone silently disables every rule gated on that window (or, for an inverted gate, leaves it always open). This is the same schema/runtime disagreement class as #1590 (`from >= until`), for the string fields #1590 does not cover.

## Evidence (verified on origin/main `e4abd8c375`, 2026-11-04)

Schema — `packages/schema/src/config/model-routes.ts`, `Window` class:

- `dates` / `excludeDates`: `Schema.Array(Schema.String)` — documented as `"YYYY-MM-DD"` or an inclusive `"YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM-DD"` range, but any string decodes.
- `start` / `end`: `Schema.String` — documented as `"HH:mm"`, but any string decodes.
- `timezone`: `Schema.String` — documented as an IANA name, but any string decodes.
- Contrast in the same file: `WindowName` and the `RouteID` pattern *are* schema-validated (`Schema.isPattern(/^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._-]{0,127}$/)`), and `DayOfWeek`/`DayOfMonth` are constrained unions — the string fields above are the unvalidated remainder.

Runtime disagreement — `packages/core/src/model-route-schedule.ts`, `parse()`:

- `dateEntry` (lines 101–110): an entry must match the date grammar, be a real calendar date (`isRealDate`), and a range's end must not precede its start; anything else returns `undefined`.
- Lines 280–288: if **any** `dates`/`excludeDates` entry is unreadable (or the list is empty), `parse` returns `undefined` — the whole window is dropped, not just the bad entry.
- `minutesOf`/`normalizeTime` (lines 122–137) + lines 301–314: a `start`/`end` that is not a valid time of day (hour > 23, minute > 59, or unparseable like `"9am"`) drops the whole window.
- Lines 317–322 + `timezoneName` (lines 159–162): a `timezone` the runtime's `Intl` does not know drops the whole window.
- Line 336: `start === end` (after normalization) also drops the window — the schema accepts equal bounds, e.g. `start: "09:00", end: "09:00"`, and even differently-written equal bounds such as `start: "9:00", end: "09:00"`.

Decode side: `packages/schema/test/config.test.ts` shows the established pattern for this exact remedy — cross-field/format checks on the schema classes with decode tests (the #1163 `Escalation` check, the #1589 `Schedule`/`GlobalSchedule` exactly-one check, #1590's acceptance criteria for `from`/`until`).

## Why it matters

Windows gate route-target eligibility, schedule applicability, and `excludeWindows` holiday calendars. The failure mode is maximally silent and maximally broad: one bad character in one entry does not just lose that entry, it deletes the entire window at runtime while the config layer reports the file as valid — so a peak-hours window, a holiday exclusion, or an inverted eligibility gate misbehaves with no error anywhere. Operators currently can only discover it by noticing routing behavior change.

## Acceptance criteria

- Decoding a `Window` fails at config decode with a clear error naming the field/entry when: a `dates`/`excludeDates` entry is not `"YYYY-MM-DD"` or `"YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM-DD"` with real calendar dates and a non-reversed range; `start`/`end` is not a valid time of day the runtime parser accepts; `start` and `end` normalize to the same minute; or `timezone` is not a timezone name the runtime accepts. The schema's accepted grammar must match the runtime's (`dateEntry`, `normalizeTime`, `timezoneName` in core are the oracle) — no config the schema accepts is silently dropped by `ModelRouteSchedule.parse` for these reasons.
- Valid windows decode exactly as today, including runtime-accepted spellings (e.g. `"9:30"`), one-sided time bounds, and an omitted timezone.
- New tests in `packages/schema/test/config.test.ts`, mirroring the #1589 tests: each invalid case above rejected; valid controls accepted; the checks also hold when decoding `Window` on its own.
- Cross-reference #1590 (`from`/`until` bounds) — the two together should leave no `Window` field combination that decodes but is dropped by the runtime parser for a format reason.

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode, verified this run against origin/main `e4abd8c375902c350dcaadfc08abd4d84360029a`.

body:
Parent: #1146

## Problem

Generating an image or a video from a text description means leaving OpenCode entirely: another app, another account, another key, then manually bringing the file back into the project. Media generation is provider-shaped — many backends, wildly different latencies and parameter surfaces — so it belongs behind the #1146 façade like everything else: ONE ingestion code path on common endpoints, providers converting results into the supported formats passing through as much as possible, and the provider/façade layer handling key registration and renewal. Just as importantly, a generated file is only useful if the user can *see* it where they work: the terminal when the protocol supports it, and natively in OpenChamber.

## Drew's ask (paraphrased)

Image/video generation: the user gives a text description and gets back a generated file. The file is displayed inline in OpenCode when the Kitty graphics protocol is available, otherwise delivered as a file on disk with a path. OpenChamber gains native viewing of photo/GIF/image/video.

## Expanded feature design (to be designed, not yet scoped for build)

1. **Façade endpoints.** Candidate shapes: OpenAI-compatible generation routes (e.g. `/v1/images/generations`-style, plus a video counterpart — video has no settled OpenAI shape, so the design must pick and document one) on the OpenCode server. Requests name a concrete provider/model ref (pass-through) or a route name resolved through the same selection machinery as chat. Provider parameters pass through as much as possible inside a normalized envelope (size, aspect, duration, seed, negative prompt where supported).
2. **Provider registry for generation backends**, mirroring the embeddings registry precedent (#1554): registered by name, config-gated, keys registered and renewed by the provider/façade layer; clients authenticate to the server once.
3. **Async generation jobs.** Image generation can take seconds-to-minutes; video, minutes-to-longer. Synchronous request/response is the wrong shape: submission returns a job handle, the client polls (or subscribes) for completion — the fleet's detached-job pattern (submit → handle → poll → collect). The design covers job state machine, where job state lives server-side, TTL/eviction for completed jobs and their outputs, cancellation, and failure envelopes that preserve the provider's error.
4. **Delivery + display in OpenCode.** On completion the file lands on disk at a real path (always — the path is the durable artifact and is what gets referenced in the session). Display: if the terminal supports the Kitty graphics protocol, render inline in the TUI; otherwise fall back to presenting the path (and opening externally where the client can). The design covers capability detection, image sizing/cells, GIF/animation behavior in-terminal, and video (poster frame inline + path, vs other options).
5. **OpenChamber native viewing.** A viewer component scope for photo/GIF/image/video: inline rendering in the session transcript, zoom/fullscreen, playback controls for video/GIF, and graceful handling of large files. The viewer consumes the same session attachment representation as OpenCode so a session moved between clients keeps its media intelligible.
6. **Formats.** Enumerate the supported output formats per media kind (PNG/JPEG/WebP, GIF, MP4/WebM at minimum as candidates), normalization vs pass-through of provider-native formats, and thumbnail/proxy generation for large outputs.
7. **Provenance + metadata.** Every generated file carries metadata: prompt, provider, model, parameters, job id, timestamp, and parent session/message. Where it lives (sidecar, embedded metadata, session record — design decides), and how it survives the file being copied out of the project.
8. **Session representation.** The generated file attaches to the session as a first-class part (like other attachments), so it can be referenced, re-displayed, and fed back into later turns (e.g. image-to-image follow-ups) without path archaeology.
9. **Accounting parity.** Generation calls through the façade land in the route_attempt ledger discipline like other façade traffic — generation is expensive, so per-provider cost/usage visibility matters from day one.

## Open questions

- Which generation providers are first-class candidates for image, and which for video? (The two sets barely overlap; does one registry serve both?)
- Sync-for-images / async-for-video split, or async uniformly behind one job contract?
- Content-policy divergence: providers reject different prompts — how are refusals surfaced so they are attributable to the provider, not mistaken for façade bugs?
- Where do generated files live by default (project dir, session dir, a media dir) and what naming/collision rules apply?
- Kitty graphics specifics: which terminal multiplexers pass the protocol through, and what is the degradation path under tmux/ssh?
- OpenChamber viewer: build native, or wrap a platform player? What are the size/streaming limits before a proxy transcode is needed?
- Rights/licensing metadata: do any candidate providers require attribution or restrict use, and should that ride in the provenance record?

## Acceptance shape

A design doc in the repo (`doc/`) covering: façade endpoint shapes for image and video, the async job contract, the registry + key handling, the OpenCode display story (Kitty inline vs path fallback), the OpenChamber viewer component scope, format support, and the provenance/metadata scheme. Reviewed and linked from #1146.

## Expansion path

From the accepted design, file implementation tickets per step: (1) façade generation routes + job machinery, (2) one ticket per provider backend (image first, video as its own phase if the design splits them), (3) OpenCode inline display (Kitty) + path fallback, (4) OpenChamber media viewer component, (5) provenance/metadata plumbing, (6) ledger parity + end-to-end parity tests per provider.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The design covers image/video generation behind the façade, including generated files delivered inline (Kitty graphics) and a non-Kitty fallback.
- [ ] Provider interface, size/format limits, and error mapping are specified.
- [ ] An implementation follow-up issue is filed if the design is adopted.

# fix(ci): script/gate-harness.test.ts runs in no workflow — the shared harness behind all three allowlist gates has no regression net

## Summary

`script/gate-harness.ts` is the shared harness the three allowlist gates (`check:proto-reads`, `check:bounded-http`, `check:numeric-boundaries`) were rebuilt on in #1526 (design #1525 phase 1, merged via PR #1586). Its unit suite, `script/gate-harness.test.ts` (10 tests: shared `scanSource` comment handling, `collect` hit-key POSIX paths, allowlist accounting including the duplicate-line and separator round-trip cases, `treesOnDisk`, and the three gates loading as declarations), is run by **no workflow**. It is the only one of the nine `script/*.test.ts` files without an explicit CI step.

## Evidence (verified this run against origin/main 57d2870e301ec26ac019383be8235ad3979a9c69, laptop probe tree)

- Per-file wiring scan — every sibling is named in `.github/workflows/test.yml`, `gate-harness.test.ts` is named nowhere (workflows, `package.json`, `turbo.json`, `bunfig.toml`, shell scripts all grepped):

  ```
  check-bounded-http.test.ts:    .github/workflows/test.yml
  check-doc-env-vars.test.ts:    .github/workflows/test.yml
  check-numeric-boundaries.test.ts: .github/workflows/test.yml
  check-proto-reads.test.ts:     .github/workflows/test.yml
  check-workflows.test.ts:       .github/workflows/test.yml
  gate-harness.test.ts:          (no match anywhere)
  main-broken-reconcile.test.ts: .github/workflows/test.yml, main-broken.yml
  mcpx-cleanup.test.ts:          .github/workflows/test.yml
  turbo-json.test.ts:            .github/workflows/test.yml
  ```

- The suite is green when run by hand, so this is a wiring gap, not a red test: `bun test gate-harness.test.ts` in `script/` at 57d2870e30 → **10 pass / 0 fail, 132 expect() calls**.
- `script/` is not a workspace, so turbo test never picks the file up, and the root bunfig test root blocks running tests from the repo root — the exact reason every sibling has an explicit `working-directory: script` step in test.yml (see the mcpx-cleanup step comment, test.yml ~line 159). The gate checks themselves run in test.yml, but they exercise the harness only against today's real trees; the harness's pinned edge cases (comment-skipping semantics gained by proto-reads in #1526, allowlist parse edge cases from #1394, temp-tree collection) are asserted only by this unwired suite.
- The file landed with the #1526 harness work (commits 0ae49914cb, f3829d16f2) without a step; the three gate-specific suites it complements each have one.

## Why it matters

The harness is now load-bearing for three gates at once — that was the point of #1526. A regression in shared scanning/allowlist logic (e.g. comment handling or hit-key construction) would silently change what all three gates catch, and the only tests that pin those shared behaviors run nowhere. This is the #1496/#1500 shape (a promised check that runs in no workflow, discovered by hand) one level down: #1527's planned registry covers gate *commands* (`check:*`/`lint:*` scripts), not script test files, so its meta-check as scoped would not catch this either.

## Acceptance criteria

- `.github/workflows/test.yml` gains an explicit step running `bun test gate-harness.test.ts` with `working-directory: script`, following the sibling steps' pattern and comment style.
- The step passes on main (suite verified green at 57d2870e30: 10 pass / 0 fail).
- No change to `gate-harness.ts`, the three gate scripts, their allowlists, or the existing gate/test steps.

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode (fleet role map: developing-today/code#2131; implementation #2152). Probe tree: laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-creator-20261104-0335` at origin/main 57d2870e30 (removed after the run).

body:
## Design: A gate must prove itself — one shared harness, coverage that cannot drift, and wiring that is itself gated

**Design doc:** `files/designs/opencode-gate-integrity-harness.md` in the goal workspace (keep-the-four-repos-healthy) — problem, evidence, alternatives, risks, and open questions in full. Grounded on main `3e483a8cafd816f4defe64cd71b1029249dc9e9f` (files read via the GitHub API; both sandbox clone attempts failed this run and were trashed).

### Problem

The repo's answer to its three biggest bug classes is a regression net — `check:proto-reads` (#865), `check:numeric-boundaries` (#995, #992 phase 3), `check:bounded-http` (#1129, #1127 phase 3) — and the nets have become a bug class of their own: **20+ filings about the gates themselves**, in four recurring shapes:

1. **Coverage by hand-maintained list.** Each gate hardcodes its scan trees; each expansion arrived one tree per issue — bounded-http: services #1256, script trees #1394, nested script trees #1425, `github/` still missing (#1436 open); numeric: server #1294, console+function #1302, services #1308, plugin-github #1318, remaining trees #1371, script trees still missing (#1517 open, 43 hits); proto-reads still scans only `packages/core/src` (#912, #1361, #1369 — 194 undispositioned reads — all open). Only one list in one gate ever got a drift guard (#1425); #1494 (open) verifies the `src` lists have none — a new package's first fetch or `Number(...)` lands unwatched.
2. **Gates that run nowhere, or can never run.** `lint:effect-patterns` is in no workflow and 32 violations red (#1496 open); `check.yml`'s `lint:changed` step is gated on `pull_request` in a push/dispatch-only workflow whose house policy forbids PR triggers — born dead (#1508 open); `packages/protocol`'s `check:generated` ran nowhere until #1500 was filed and hand-fixed.
3. **Copied machinery, divergent copies.** The three allowlist gates duplicate `scanSource`/`parseAllowlist`/`unlistedHits`/`staleEntries`/`collect` verbatim — and the copies drifted into bugs: numeric's `collect` still builds Windows-broken hit paths with `path.slice(...)`, the construction #1286/PR #1289 fixed in the other two (#1506 open; its `collect` is also unexported and untested); numeric's and proto's `parseAllowlist` mis-key hits containing ` :: ` (bounded-http's joins the middle fields, #1394); proto's `scanSource` doesn't skip comment-only lines, the others do; scanned extensions differ per gate (.ts / .ts+.tsx / +.astro).
4. **Allowlist drift reddening main** at least six times (#896, #1086, #1188, #1282, #1283, #1514 open) — the stale check is correct, but three copies of the accounting means three places for its fixes to miss.

Dedupe: `kind/design` here is #587/#800/#992/#1127/#1345 only — #992/#1127 *created* two of the nets and neither covers the nets' own integrity; the completed `check:`-in-title and "regression net" searches return only per-gate filings (two broader body searches timed out HTTP 408 this run and are noted as such in the design doc's run notes). ROADMAP.md's "CI and test health" area states the intent ("a main branch whose checks are green") with an **empty** items table — this design is that area's missing row (flagged for the maintainers; this job does not edit the roadmap).

### The contract (proposal)

A regression net is a promise with three parts, each checked by something other than the gate itself:

1. **One harness, gates are data.** The shared machinery — tree inventory, `collect` (POSIX hit keys, exported, on-disk tested once), `scanSource` (comment-skip), occurrence-aware allowlist accounting with the ` :: `-in-text parse — lives in one module under `script/`. Each gate becomes a declaration: patterns, tree kinds, allowlist path, remediation text. A machinery fix lands once; the missed-sibling shape (#1506) becomes impossible because there are no siblings.
2. **Coverage cannot drift.** Every gate states its scope as tree *kinds* over the shared on-disk inventory and fails when a tree of a claimed kind exists on disk outside its scope; exclusions are explicit and carry a reason. This is #1494 generalised from two lists to the family.
3. **Wiring is itself gated.** A registry of promised checks (name, command, owning workflow); a meta-check fails when a `check:*`/`lint:*` script exists but is unregistered, a registered gate appears in no workflow, or a registered gate's step is unreachable — its step-level `if:` names an event the workflow never triggers on (the #1508 shape, judged from parsed triggers the way `check:workflows` already parses them).

Unchanged: every gate's patterns, allowlists, dispositions, and the bug-class contracts (#992 values, #1127 semantics, #833 guard). The open per-tree expansions (#912/#1361/#1369/#1436/#1517) keep their disposition work — the harness makes each expansion a declaration change plus dispositions, and rule 2 guarantees the *next* tree cannot be missed silently.

### Phases

- **Phase 1 (filed as a sub-issue): the shared harness.** Extract the duplicated machinery; gates become declarations; byte-identical hit sets on current main. The #1506 POSIX-key fix rides along as the harness's single exported `collect` with the on-disk collect test — #1506's acceptance, satisfied by construction (noted on both issues; #1506 keeps its own lifecycle for its owner to close).
- **Phase 2 (adopted — existing #1494): coverage guards for the `src` lists**, exactly as #1494 specifies for bounded-http and numeric, landing as declaration-level changes on the harness; proto-reads gains the same scope statement for its single root (its *expansion* stays #912/#1361/#1369's). #1494 is linked as a sub-issue and keeps its own queue lifecycle (currently `queue/queued`).
- **Phase 3 (filed as a sub-issue): the gate registry + wiring meta-check** per rule 3. Its landing requires the two known wiring violations dispositioned by their own issues — #1508 (`lint:changed` on push, its stated fix) and #1496 (wire `lint:effect-patterns` after its 32 dispositions) — named as blockers in its body, not merged into it.

Open questions kept in the doc, not filed: meta-check inside `check:workflows` vs sibling `check:gates`; which per-package scripts beyond `check:generated` belong in the registry; whether proto-reads' eventual expansion (#1369) adopts derived scope wholesale; whether #1503's `permissions:` rule joins this umbrella (a policy-content question — left to #1503).

Alternatives (per-gate status quo; fully derived scope now; one mega-gate; external workflow linting) and why they lose are in the design doc.

🤖 Filed by the repo-design-architect job (opencode pass, 2026-11-03).
<!-- agent-note:v1 agent=repo-design-architect state=filed at=2026-11-03T14:04:47Z -->

## Acceptance criteria

- The design's three rules are each landed or explicitly dispositioned by a linked phase issue: (1) one shared harness for the allowlist gates (#1526), (2) coverage derived from the tree, not hand-maintained lists, with a drift guard, (3) a gate registry + wiring meta-check (#1527).
- Each phase issue carries its own acceptance criteria and is linked from here as a native sub-issue / blocked-by relation (protocol §11), not only as prose.
- When all phases land, a new package's first fetch / Number(...) / proto read is covered by the relevant gate with no list edit — demonstrated by a fixture package in the harness tests.

body:
## Finding

`script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts`'s `collect()` still builds each hit's repo-relative path with `path.slice(root.length + 1)` — the exact construction #1286 was filed against and PR #1289 removed from the two sibling gate collectors. On Windows, `join()` produces backslash paths, so every hit key comes out as `packages\core\src\...` and can never equal a forward-slash allowlist key: the gate reports every candidate as unlisted and every allowlist entry as stale, and exits 1. The gate is unusable on Windows, and no test can catch it — this collector is not exported and `script/check-numeric-boundaries.test.ts` has no on-disk collect test (the proto-reads fix in #1289 added exactly that test for its collector).

## Evidence

- PR #1235 (`ci(core): add check:numeric-boundaries regression net (#995)`, merged head `d53ccda5e7`) introduced the collector with the slice construction.
- Issue #1286 (closed): "regression-gate collectors build repo-relative paths with OS separators — bounded-http services test fails on Windows CI". PR #1289 fixed `script/check-bounded-http.ts` and `script/check-proto-reads.ts` to `relative(root, path).split(sep).join("/")`, exported proto-reads' `collect`, and added an on-disk collect test — but the numeric-boundaries collector, merged earlier the same day, was missed.
- Current main `9679be7a1d9abdaa6b107d02bffb53415bdee2a5`, `script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts:163`: `hits.push(...scanSource(path.slice(root.length + 1), readFileSync(path, "utf8")))` — and `collect` at :158 is not exported.
- Siblings on the same main: `script/check-bounded-http.ts:225` and `script/check-proto-reads.ts:101` both use `relative(root, path).split(sep).join("/")`. The other gate scripts (`check-doc-env-vars.ts`, `check-workflows.ts`) have no collector of this shape — numeric-boundaries is the only remaining slice-built collector.
- `script/check-numeric-boundaries.test.ts` on main covers `scanSource`, `SCAN_ROOTS`, `isScannedFile`, and allowlist accounting only — no `collect` test.

## Why it matters

The three gates are one family with one allowlist format; two were fixed for Windows and the third silently kept the defect. Anyone running `bun run check:numeric-boundaries` on Windows (or adding the on-disk collect test the siblings have) hits a wall of false unlisted/stale errors, and the divergence invites the next copy of the bug. This is the missed-sibling pattern the scan-coverage issues (#1294/#1302/#1318) keep finding in this gate family.

## Acceptance criteria

- `collect` in `script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` builds hit keys with `relative(root, path).split(sep).join("/")`, matching the sibling gates, and is exported for testing.
- An on-disk collect test mirroring the #1289 proto-reads test: walks a temp tree, asserts a hit is reported under its forward-slash repo-relative path, and non-scanned extensions are ignored.
- `bun run check:numeric-boundaries` still exits 0 on Linux with the same hit count; Linux hit sets are byte-identical before/after.

<!-- agent-note:v1 agent=pr-diff-review-b state=filed -->
Source: PR #1235 review (lane B, pr-diff-review-b), verified against current main above.

# fix(ci): check:bounded-http does not scan the github/ tree — the GitHub Action's token-exchange, attachment-download and token-revoke fetches have no deadline and read bodies unbounded

## Evidence (verified this run, two independent sources)

Verified on main `b34bc0e9e1f3` (GitHub API) and on the local clone at `595aa5b74c` before it was removed mid-run by an unrelated cleanup; both reads agree line-for-line.

- `script/check-bounded-http.ts` `SCAN_ROOTS` covers every `packages/*/src`, `services/*/src`, root `script/` and the per-package script trees (#1394) — but the top-level `github/` tree (the published opencode GitHub Action: `github/action.yml`, `github/package.json` `"module": "index.ts"`, `github/README.md`) is not a scan root, and `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` has **0** `github/` entries.
- Replicating the gate's own patterns (`fetch(`, `.text()/.json()/.arrayBuffer()` with no args) over `github/` gives **8 hits, all in `github/index.ts`, all undispositioned**:

| Line | Site | Problem |
|---|---|---|
| 377 | `fetch("https://api.opencode.ai/exchange_github_app_token_with_pat", …)` | no deadline/signal |
| 386 | `fetch("https://api.opencode.ai/exchange_github_app_token", …)` | no deadline/signal |
| 395 | `(await response.json())` (error branch) | unbounded body read |
| 399 | `(await response.json())` (token branch) | unbounded body read |
| 465 | `fetch(url, …)` downloading a commenter-supplied `github.com/user-attachments/…` URL | no deadline/signal |
| 485 | `Buffer.from(await res.arrayBuffer()).toString("base64")` | whole body buffered, then +33% base64, in runner memory |
| 508 | `fetch(\`${server.url}/event\`)` | long-lived event stream — needs an explicit allowlist disposition as an intentional exemption, not a deadline |
| 1063 | `fetch("https://api.github.com/installation/token", { method: "DELETE", … })` (token revoke at teardown) | no deadline; a stall hangs job exit |

- The attachment regexes at `github/index.ts:461-462` match both `user-attachments/assets/…` images and `user-attachments/files/…` file links, so line 465/485 can be fed a large non-image file by any commenter who can trigger the action; there is no `content-length` check and no cap before `arrayBuffer()`.
- Same escape class as #1256 (services/), #1394 (script trees) and #1425 (nested script trees): a tree the header claim does not enumerate escapes the regression net silently while the gate runs green. The numeric-boundaries and proto-reads gates also do not scan `github/` (2 `parseInt` hits at `github/index.ts:891` and `:1018`); this issue scopes the bounded-http gate, the others are noted for triage.

## Why it matters

This is the user-facing GitHub Action that runs in other people's CI on commenter-controlled input. A stalled token-exchange endpoint hangs the action until the workflow job timeout; an oversized attachment buffers whole (twice, with base64) in the runner; and because the gate does not scan the tree, none of this can regress-detect — the bounded-by-default contract (#1127) has a blind spot exactly where untrusted input enters.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `github/` is scanned by `check:bounded-http` (root added, or roots derived from the filesystem with a guard/test that fails when an on-disk production tree is unscanned), and the gate's header coverage claim matches reality.
- [ ] Every hit in `github/index.ts` is dispositioned in `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt`.
- [ ] Token-exchange fetches (377/386) carry a named deadline; their `.json()` reads (395/399) are byte-capped.
- [ ] The attachment download (465/485) carries a deadline and a byte cap enforced before buffering (declared-length pre-check plus a streaming cap, or equivalent), so an oversized attachment is rejected/skipped, not buffered whole.
- [ ] The token-revoke fetch (1063) carries a short named deadline so teardown cannot hang job exit.
- [ ] The `/event` fetch (508) is allowlisted with its long-lived-stream exemption stated, not given a deadline.
- [ ] `bun run script/check-bounded-http.ts` exits 0 with the increased root count; a test or guard covers the new root if roots become derived.

body:
Origin: Codex P2 review finding on PR #1384 (merged 2026-11-02 as f7b4c02dab), thread on packages/core/src/model-route.ts (line 541 at head 4794119cf5), left unresolved at merge. Verified still present on current main by queue task 6188 (lane A, 2026-11-02).

## Problem

When two pool members carry quota benches and a trusted reset is learned after those benches were created, `armBenchProbe` (packages/core/src/model-route.ts ~line 451) makes them probe-eligible at the reset without shortening their cooldowns — the existing half-open recovery path. But `quotaOut` (~line 546) / `poolQuotaExhausted` (~line 609) still count both leaves as quota-out until their original cooldowns expire, so the pool verdict stays exhausted and the resolver excludes every member, including the due probes, from both normal selection and the all-full last resort. A recovered pool can stay unavailable until the escalated cooldown expires (up to 24 hours), defeating the probe path.

## Fix direction (from the Codex finding)

Account for due probes when applying the pool exclusion: a leaf whose bench probe is due (`probeDueState`, ~line 459) should not count toward the pool-exhaustion threshold (or the exclusion should admit the due probe), while a claimed/outstanding probe and not-yet-due benches keep counting.

## Acceptance

- With two pool leaves quota-benched and a trusted reset learned, once the reset passes the pool is no longer excluded as a whole: the due probe leaf is selectable for its half-open probe.
- Before the reset, or while a probe is already claimed, the pool exclusion still applies.
- New regression test beside packages/core/test/model-route.test.ts pool-shaped tests demonstrating the due-probe case.
- packages/core model-route + model-resolver suites pass; typecheck clean.

Part of the #1014 PR3 follow-up set; does not reopen #1014's other routed packets.

## Acceptance criteria
- With two pool leaves quota-benched and a trusted reset learned, once the reset passes the pool is no longer excluded as a whole: the due-probe leaf is selectable for its half-open probe.
- Before the reset, or while a probe is already claimed, the pool exclusion still applies.
- A new regression test beside `packages/core/test/model-route.test.ts` pool-shaped tests demonstrates the due-probe case.
- packages/core model-route and model-resolver suites pass; typecheck is clean.
