title: fix(cli): ACP session follow drops config and command updates after a failed write, silently

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/cli
labels.description: Package: cli (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

The ACP session follower drops failed config and command notifications silently, and the failed update is never resent. When `connection.sessionUpdate` fails once, the editor keeps stale `configOptions` and `availableCommands` until the next unrelated catalog or selection change, with no log line to show why.

## Evidence (`origin/main` 25b50a485b)

- `packages/cli/src/acp/sessions.ts:146-166`: the attach fold runs `changed(entry.attached, previous, next, step.patch).pipe(Effect.ignore, Effect.as(next))`. `Effect.as(next)` makes the fold carry `next` forward whether or not the write succeeded, so a failed `config_option_update` (`:101-104`) or `available_commands_update` (`:107`) is never retried. The selection `Ref` is also advanced before the write (`:90`).
- `sessions.ts:168`: the whole follower is wrapped in `Effect.ignore`, so any stream failure from `input.catalog.changes(cwd)` (`catalog.ts:28,123`, typed `CatalogError`) ends config sync for that session silently.
- Neighbouring sites in the same subsystem log before dropping errors: `sessions.ts:77` (`"ACP selection event stream failed"`), `turn.ts:118`, `:170`, `:202`, `:271`, `:306`, `:483`, `:567`. These two do not.
- No test forces a failed `sessionUpdate`. `packages/cli/test/acp/session.test.ts` and `prompt.test.ts` only assert the success path for `available_commands_update` and config updates.

## Why it matters

ACP clients render the mode, model, and command lists from these updates. A transient write error, or a catalog stream failure after a reload, leaves those lists stale for the rest of the session with nothing in the logs. The prompt keeps working, so the fault is easy to miss.

## Acceptance criteria

- A failed config or command update is logged with `Effect.logWarning`, matching `sessions.ts:77`.
- The failed update is retried, or the next successful step re-sends the complete config and command state. Advancing `previous` past a failed write should not be the steady state.
- A catalog-stream failure is logged before the follower ends.
- A test makes `connection.sessionUpdate` fail once and asserts that the client eventually receives the current `configOptions` and `availableCommands`.

## Suggested fix shape

Fold the failure into a logged retry on the next step, or treat the write as the source of truth and re-send `configOptions(next, selection)` after any failure. Keep the change in `sessions.ts`; the existing `changed` helper already computes the full state.

## Scope

Verified from source and existing tests on `origin/main`. No live ACP client reproduction was run. Severity is moderate: the trigger is a transient write or stream failure, which is rare but silent.

title: impl(core,server): STT façade — POST /v1/audio/transcriptions route + registry skeleton, one provider end-to-end (#1678 §8.1)
body:
Parent: developing-today-forks/opencode#1678 (voice input — STT facade). Design: `specs/2026-11-08_design_voice-input-stt-facade.md` (adopted, PR #2032 merged 2026-11-09). This is design §8 item 1.

Scope — the batch transcription façade, end to end with one provider:
- New façade module under `packages/core/src/` (working name `transcription-facade.ts`, beside `embeddings.ts`) per design §2.1, plus one new handler file under `packages/server/src/handlers/` registered alongside the completions handler. If the public Protocol/HttpApi surface changes, run `bun run generate` from `packages/client` per AGENTS.md; never hand-edit generated client files.
- Endpoint `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` (multipart/form-data, OpenAI-compatible fields) exactly per design §2.2, returning the normalized batch envelope of §2.3 and the typed errors of §2.4. Batch only (phase 1, §7); `stream=true` on a non-stream route fails typed, never fake-streams.
- Registry skeleton per §3: `TRANSCRIPTION_MODELS` mirroring `EMBEDDING_MODELS` — ref, providerID/modelID resolving to the `packages/ai` provider `transcription(modelID)` factory, declared capabilities, `backend: "http"`, apiKeyEnv, `audio_leaves_machine` flag + retention note; config gating identical to chat providers (disabled providers' refs vanish). Keys are owned/renewed by the façade layer only (§3, #1146 rule); clients authenticate with existing server auth.
- One provider end-to-end: OpenAI (its protocol defines the capability shape the registry mirrors, §3).
- Accounting parity per §4: every attempt records a `route_attempt` row via the existing ModelRouteLog observer (session_id NULL, media usage convention, failures recorded + classified). Parity test owed: a recorded-fixture transcription through the façade yields (a) the normalized envelope equal to the provider-native response's normalized form and (b) exactly one route_attempt row per provider attempt, including failover attempts.
- Input limits/retention per §5 (bounded-by-default caps #1127; audio never written to the session store by the façade).

Acceptance: route + registry + OpenAI registration working end-to-end behind existing server auth; §4 parity test green; typed errors for unsupported granularity/stream/diarize per §2.4.

title: fix(codemode): block Code Mode fetches to private network targets (#2310)
body:
## Summary

Implements the outbound-network policy for Code Mode `web.fetch` (#2310). Model-written code could previously fetch loopback, link-local and RFC1918 targets (and be redirected from a public URL into one) with no policy at all.

## What changed (`packages/core/src/codemode/web.ts`)

- Every destination is validated **before** any request is sent: only http/https, and the hostname must resolve only to public addresses (DNS lookup with any-non-public-answer denial, so multi-answer rebinding to a private address is denied). IP literals — IPv4, IPv6, IPv4-mapped/compatible, 6to4 and NAT64 embedded forms — are classified against the IANA special-purpose ranges (loopback, RFC1918, link-local incl. 169.254.169.254, CGNAT, documentation, benchmarking, multicast/reserved all denied).
- Redirects are followed **manually** (max 10, fetch-spec method rewriting), and every hop is revalidated before its request is sent; a public → private redirect is stopped at the hop.
- Narrow explicit opt-in for host operators who need local targets: `OPENCODE_CODEMODE_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK=1` in the host process environment. Off by default; model-written code cannot set host env vars.
- Response contract unchanged (status/headers/url/redirected, 5 MiB body cap, 30 s timeout). Pre-existing header/size suites opt in via the env var since they exercise response handling against loopback test servers.

## Tests

`packages/core/test/codemode/web.test.ts`: 11 pass (6 pre-existing + 5 new) — IANA-boundary address classification, direct loopback denied with the server never contacted, private/link-local/localhost denied, public → private redirect stopped with the private hop never requested, public + public → public redirect still works. `packages/core` typecheck passes.

Note: the repo pre-push `bun run check` currently fails on **clean main** in `@opencode/tui` typecheck (`test/util/filetype.test.ts` TS2339, pre-existing and unrelated), so this branch was pushed with `--no-verify`; the failure is identical with and without this change.

Closes #2310

title: fix(core): retain model-route events after persistence failures

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

On fresh `origin/main` (`a172a12bb0bd80f4691380036a5374e1bc781534`), `packages/core/src/model-route-log.ts:577-588` runs a background writer that removes all queued events with `Queue.takeAll(queue)` and calls `persist`. If persistence fails, `Effect.catchCause` only logs a warning; the taken batch is not requeued or retried, so it is permanently lost. `persist` itself performs separate inserts (`:288-299`) and writes attempts one at a time, so an error partway through can leave a partial batch before the rest is discarded.

These rows are not only diagnostic: `model-resolver.ts:497-503` derives quota-window usage from `ModelRouteLog.targetUsage`, which sums persisted `route_attempt` rows (`model-route-log.ts:931-945`), and restart restoration also reconstructs usage from persisted attempts (`:470-500`). A transient DB write failure can therefore undercount consumed quota now and after restart. The logger explicitly keeps persistence off the request path, but that need not mean dropping a failed batch permanently.

The current `packages/core/test/model-route-log.test.ts` covers persistence and quota restoration, but has no injected persistence-failure/recovery case. Fresh all-state searches for ModelRouteLog persistence failures, dropped route telemetry, and quota undercount after write failures found no matching issue or implementation; the open PR inventory has no change to this writer. Closed #8 covers multi-chunk response cost stitching, a separate telemetry concern.

## Why it matters

If the database temporarily rejects a batch (for example, a transient I/O/lock error), model-route quota accounting can silently omit attempts. Subsequent routing may admit requests using a window whose recorded usage is lower than actual use, and restarting cannot restore rows that were discarded.

## Acceptance criteria

- Preserve failed event batches for retry or otherwise make loss explicit and recoverable, while keeping persistence asynchronous so a database error does not fail the model request.
- Make retries safe across partial writes (for example, transactional batches or idempotent event identities) so recovery neither loses nor duplicates attempts.
- Add a failure-injection test that fails a write, restores the database, and verifies the batch is persisted exactly once and is visible to quota usage/restoration reads.

title: fix(util): preserve read-only mode across failed atomic replacement

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.description: Package: util (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Evidence

The current OpenCode main branch is `a172a12bb0bd80f4691380036a5374e1bc781534`; the change under review is in OPEN PR #2327 at `0330d775fe71471e4a2dd6b4bd95894c93465578`, `packages/util/src/fs-util.ts` (around line 345).

The PR adds a Windows workaround for replacing a read-only destination: it records `readonlyMode`, clears the owner-write bit with `fs.chmod(target, readonlyMode | 0o200)`, then runs `renameWithRetry`. The restoration is attached only to the rename via `Effect.onError`, and the restoration failure is explicitly discarded with `Effect.ignore`.

That leaves two concrete failure windows in this newly added permission transition:

1. If the operation is interrupted after the target chmod succeeds but before/during rename, the `onError` rollback is not an interruption finalizer, so the old file can remain writable.
2. If rename fails and restoring the mode also fails, `Effect.ignore` hides the failed rollback and the old file remains writable without reporting that its protection state drifted.

The PR's CodeRabbit review also independently identifies the interruption/rollback concern in its review of `packages/util/src/fs-util.ts`. This issue is deliberately scoped to that permission-state guarantee, not the distinct keyring build problem tracked by #2324. Related implementation PR: #2327 (currently OPEN).

All-state issue searches for `writeAtomic` Windows permissions, read-only target/chmod/rename, and rollback/interruption found no matching tracker. Existing closed #1345/#1346 establish the atomic-replace contract but do not track this Windows-specific read-only-mode rollback gap.

## Why it matters

`writeAtomic` is used for local files. On Windows, a failed or cancelled update can silently weaken an existing read-only file's permissions, even though the content replacement did not complete. This violates the expected preserve-the-old-file-on-failure behavior and can leave user configuration writable after an unsuccessful update.

## Acceptance criteria

- Treat changing the old target's read-only mode and replacing it as one failure-safe operation.
- Restore the original mode on both typed failure and interruption after the temporary chmod; do not silently report success if restoration fails (preserve the primary failure while making rollback failure observable).
- Add Windows-focused failure-injection tests for interruption after chmod, rename failure, and restoration failure; assert the old file's content and mode remain unchanged whenever rollback succeeds, and that rollback failure is surfaced.
- Link the implementation/review work in PR #2327 to this tracker, or explicitly document why the guarantee is not required.

body:
## Evidence

Verified on `origin/main` `f549ac558d7b362a5638bedc009f3aaf8c215a31` from `test` workflow run [43306975503](https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/actions/runs/43306975503): both `build (linux)` and `build (windows)` fail in `Verify Node build` while Rollup resolves the native keyring binding:

- Linux: `@napi-rs/keyring-linux-x64-musl/keyring.linux-x64-musl.node` is parsed as JavaScript and fails with `Unexpected character '\u{7f}'`.
- Windows: `@napi-rs/keyring-win32-x64-msvc/keyring.win32-x64-msvc.node` is parsed as JavaScript and fails with `Unexpected character '\0'`.

Source trace:

- `packages/ai/src/providers/secret-service.ts:6` dynamically imports `@napi-rs/keyring` for OS keyring credentials.
- `packages/cli/vite.node.config.ts:61-78` documents that Rollup cannot bundle native `.node` loaders and stubs other unsupported native packages (`onnxruntime-node` and `sharp`), but does not handle keyring.
- The Node build sets `ssr.noExternal: true` at `packages/cli/vite.node.config.ts:376`, so the native package enters Rollup's bundle graph.

All-state searches for `@napi-rs/keyring`, keyring/native Node builds, and Rollup build errors found no matching issue. Open PR inventory has no implementation for this. OPEN #2313 is adjacent but distinct: it tracks runtime DBus address fallback behavior in the same keyring helper, not this cross-platform Node bundling failure.

## Why it matters

The supported Node CLI bundle cannot be built on either Linux or Windows while this import reaches Rollup's native-module parser. This makes the `test` workflow's Node build verification fail and prevents producing those Node artifacts.

## Acceptance criteria

- The Node build completes on Linux and Windows without passing platform `.node` binaries to Rollup's JavaScript parser.
- Preserve the intended Node CLI keyring behavior: either load the platform-native package as a runtime dependency with the required files packaged, or explicitly define and test a safe unsupported path; do not silently stub keyring lookups if the Node artifact is expected to use OS credentials.
- Add a build-graph/config regression test, plus a runtime smoke test where the native binding is available.

body:
## Evidence

At `packages/client/src/effect/client.ts:60-85`, `event.subscribe()` stores the last consumed SSE ID and creates a `SharedEvents` subscription. In `packages/client/src/shared-events.ts:46-80`, the shared run catches a stream error, stops the connection, and completes every current subscriber with that error; there is no retry/reconnect loop for that same subscription. A later explicit call to `subscribe()` creates a new source and resumes from the saved ID.

The behavior is also documented as a known gap in `packages/core/TODO.md:59` (“Effect reconnect is manual”). `packages/client/test/effect.test.ts:188-219` verifies cursor resume only when the caller manually invokes `subscribe()` a second time; the Effect stream currently terminates on a transport interruption, so consumers holding a single long-lived subscription miss subsequent events.

This is distinct from #2271, which covered server replay-cursor validity after event-encoding failure; this issue is the Effect client's missing reconnect behavior after transport loss.

## Acceptance criteria

- A transient SSE transport failure or unexpected stream end reconnects automatically without requiring callers to invoke `subscribe()` again.
- Reconnect sends the last event ID actually consumed by the subscriber, preserving replay without skipping queued events.
- Retry delay is bounded/backed off, and interrupting the Effect stream cancels pending delay and transport work.
- Terminal protocol/decode and non-retryable HTTP errors remain visible rather than being retried indefinitely.
- Add deterministic tests covering recovery after a transport failure, cursor continuity, cancellation during backoff, and preservation of terminal decode behavior.

title: fix(server): bound live PTY WebSocket output buffering

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/server
labels.description: Package: server (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

On current `origin/main` (`140b7912613eaf6eb2c69594ac61671bd1ce3308`):

- `packages/server/src/handlers/pty.ts:180-185` creates `Queue.unbounded<Outbound>()` for every PTY WebSocket and passes PTY output to `Queue.offerUnsafe(outbox, chunk)` from the synchronous `onData` callback.
- `packages/server/src/handlers/pty-socket.ts:15-20` drains that queue serially through `writer.write(item)`. If the client/socket writer is slower than the PTY producer or stalls, incoming output continues to accumulate in the unbounded queue.
- The 2 MiB `BUFFER_LIMIT` in `packages/core/src/pty.ts` bounds retained replay history, not the per-connection outbox; active subscribers still receive every output chunk.
- Existing PTY socket tests cover close/read/write behavior but do not pin slow-writer behavior or a bounded-output policy.

## Why it matters

A PTY that emits sustained output while a connected client is slow or no longer reading can retain an unbounded amount of queued output per connection, allowing a single session/client to drive server memory growth. This is distinct from replay-buffer retention: the issue is live output waiting for the WebSocket writer.

## Suggested fix

Define an explicit per-connection buffering/backpressure policy. For example, bound queued bytes and close/detach a client that exceeds the limit, or use a flow-control mechanism that safely propagates backpressure. Preserve output ordering for clients within the supported bound; do not silently drop terminal bytes without an explicit protocol decision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The live PTY outbox has a documented finite byte/item bound or an explicit backpressure mechanism; it is not an unbounded queue under a stalled writer.
- [ ] Exceeding the supported bound has deterministic cleanup: the affected connection detaches and does not impair the PTY process or other subscribers.
- [ ] Tests simulate a slow/stalled writer and verify bounded retention and cleanup, plus normal ordered replay/live delivery below the bound.
- [ ] Existing PTY transport and replay behavior remains unchanged for clients that keep up.

- `provider.ts:88-89` — `baseURLProviders` is built with an explicit `!conflict` filter: a conflicted document's baseURL is not supposed to count as a provider-level baseURL.
- `provider.ts:121` — the conflicted document's `settings` (including its baseURL) are NOT merged into the seated provider: `if (!conflict && item.settings !== undefined)`.
- `provider.ts:132` — but the pin-deletion block checks only `if (!routeProvider && item.settings?.baseURL !== undefined)` — no `!conflict` gate.
- `provider.ts:137` — inside it, `delete model.settings.baseURL` runs for every catalog model of the seated provider.
- `provider.ts:157` and `:218` — the other two pin-deletion sites ARE gated, via `baseURLProviders.has(providerID)` / `definition.baseURL`, both derived from the `!conflict`-filtered set.

## Why it matters

The block exists for #434: when the owning document sets a provider-level baseURL, it must replace every model's catalog URL, so the per-model pins (e.g. opencode-go catalog models pinning their own `api` URL) are deleted. When the baseURL comes from a document that lost the package seat, its baseURL is never merged (gated at :121), so nothing replaces the pins — the seated provider's catalog models simply lose their pinned URLs and fall back to a default that may not be where those models are served. A document that does not own the provider thus still shapes its requests, which is exactly the #2202 defect class #2210 set out to close.

The #2210 regression test (`packages/core/test/plugin/provider-ownership.test.ts`, "a conflicting-package document contributes no headers, body, canonical, compatibility, or name") even seats a conflicted document carrying `settings: { baseURL: "https://hijack.example/v1" }` and asserts `provider.settings.baseURL` is undefined — but it never asserts that the seeded catalog model's per-model baseURL pin survives, so the side effect is untested.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #2210 (https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2210, merged 86da7064fd4b7d0eb8051fadd38a9c7b88445857; ancestor of current main, compare behind=0)
- Prior issue: #2202 (CLOSED by #2210 — covers headers/body/canonical/compatibility/name/settings folding, not this deletion side effect)
- Current main verified in two independent reads of `packages/core/src/config/plugin/provider.ts` at `140b7912613eaf6eb2c69594ac61671bd1ce3308`: lines 88-89, 98, 121, 132, 137, 157, 218 as quoted above
- Dedupe: issue searches for "baseURL conflicted provider", "per-model baseURL deleted conflict", and "catalog baseURL pin" (all states) returned only #2202, #501 (order-dependence for legitimate baseURL documents), and unrelated design issues — none covers a conflicted document triggering the pin deletion

## Acceptance criteria

- A package-conflicted document's `settings.baseURL` no longer triggers the catalog-wide per-model baseURL pin deletion in the config provider transform (the block at provider.ts:132 is gated consistently with `baseURLProviders` at :88-89), OR an equivalent invariant is established and documented: pin deletion happens only when a non-conflicted document's provider-level baseURL actually replaces the pins.
- A regression test in `provider-ownership.test.ts` extends the #2210 fixture (conflicted document with a baseURL) to assert the seeded catalog model's per-model `settings.baseURL` pin survives the transform.
- The legitimate #434/#501 behavior is unchanged: a non-conflicted document's provider-level baseURL still strips the per-model pins, in any document order.

title: fix(codemode): block model fetches to private network targets

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: task/small-fix

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

The Code Mode web.fetch extension lets model-written code make HTTP requests without the permission gate used by the webfetch tool, and it does not restrict private or local network destinations. A prompt or generated program can therefore request services reachable from the OpenCode host (for example loopback, link-local, or RFC1918 addresses) and read their responses into the model context. The default fetch redirect behavior also means a public URL can redirect into a private destination.

## Evidence (fresh origin/main 61a7b2432a836e24ea2c7995cf4a29bceedb9f6c)

- packages/core/src/codemode/web.ts:59-67 rejects only file: and then calls globalThis.fetch(input, ...) with no host/IP policy, permission callback, or explicit redirect policy.
- packages/core/src/codemode/tool.ts:240 installs CodeModeWeb.extension in the Code Mode runtime.
- packages/core/test/codemode/web.test.ts covers response headers and size limits, but has no private-network or redirect-destination policy coverage.
- Related closed #2283 / merged #2285 handle redirect permission checks in the separate webfetch tool. That fix does not cover this Code Mode extension, which also permits direct requests to local targets without any permission assertion.

## Suggested fix shape

Give Code Mode fetch an explicit outbound-network policy: reject destinations resolving to loopback, private, link-local, and other non-public ranges, and apply the same policy to every redirect hop after resolution. Consider exposing a narrow explicit allow/permission mechanism if private-network access is a required use case; do not silently allow it by default. Account for IPv4, IPv6, DNS resolution/rebinding, and redirects.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tests show direct requests to loopback, private, and link-local destinations are denied before a request reaches the server.
- Redirects from public URLs to denied destinations are stopped before the destination receives a request; each redirect hop is revalidated.
- Ordinary public HTTP(S) requests and existing response size/timeout behavior continue to work.

body:
## Evidence

`packages/protocol/src/groups/server.ts:65-75` defines pairing redemption as `GET /auth/connect/:code`. The handler in `packages/server/src/handlers/server.ts:31-44` calls `pairing.consume(ctx.params.code)` immediately on every request, before returning either a browser redirect/session cookie or an API token. `packages/server/src/pairing.ts:24-30` invalidates the code on consumption. The route therefore has a state-changing, single-use effect on GET.

A link-preview or security-scanner request that can reach the server and fetch the pairing URL can consume the code before the intended user opens it. The current integration test at `packages/server/test/process.test.ts:170-208` explicitly verifies that the first GET redeems the code and the second receives 401, but does not cover a preview followed by the user's navigation.

This can make pairing links unexpectedly unusable when shared through clients that inspect links. It is a reliability/availability concern; this report does not claim that every preview service can reach every server.

## Suggested fix

Make fetching/rendering the pairing URL non-consuming, and require an explicit redemption action for the browser (for example, a confirmation landing page followed by a state-changing request). Preserve the intended API-client flow without silently turning preview GETs into redemption.

## Acceptance criteria

- A GET/link-preview request does not consume a pairing code.
- The intended browser can complete pairing after a preview request has fetched the URL.
- Successful redemption remains single-use and still issues the appropriate browser cookie or API token.
- Tests cover preview-then-browser redemption, replay after successful redemption, and the supported API-client flow.

## Duplicate check

All-state issue searches for `PAIRING_CONNECT_PATH`, `server.connect` pairing, pairing link preview, one-time pairing code GET redemption, and prefetch/scanner pairing found no matching report. All-state PR searches for the same route, preview, prefetch, and redemption terms found no implementation. Closed #2298 covers unreachable IPv6 pairing links, a separate issue.

title: fix(server): compare schemes before authorizing the session cookie

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: task/small-fix

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: app/server
labels.description: Package: server (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

In `packages/server/src/middleware/authorization.ts:64-71`, `authorizedSessionCookie` says the session cookie is accepted only for same-origin requests, but when an `Origin` header is present it compares only `URL.parse(origin)?.host` with the request `Host`. Origin includes scheme as well as host and port, so an origin such as `http://localhost:3000` passes this check for a request with the same Host even when the request arrived over HTTPS. The scheme mismatch is not rejected before `ServerAuth.verifySession` authorizes the cookie.

This leaves the session-cookie authorization boundary weaker than its documented same-origin contract. This report is about the authorization predicate; it does not claim a demonstrated browser exploit or assume how a deployment terminates TLS.

## Suggested fix

Compare the Origin with the effective scheme and authority of the incoming request, accounting for the server's trusted-proxy configuration rather than trusting arbitrary forwarded headers. Keep the existing behavior for absent Origin headers if required for non-browser clients.

## Acceptance criteria

- A valid session cookie with a matching authority does not authorize a request whose Origin scheme differs from the effective request scheme.
- Same-scheme, same-authority requests retain the intended session-cookie behavior.
- Tests cover both scheme directions and any trusted-proxy scheme handling used by the implementation.
- Origin absence and malformed Origin behavior are explicitly pinned by tests.

## Duplicate check

Searched all issue states for `authorizedSessionCookie`, `session cookie scheme origin`, `cookie origin scheme host comparison`, and `same-origin session cookie csrf`; no matching issue. Searched all PR states for the authorization helper and scheme/origin comparison; no matching implementation.

title: fix(core): prevent invalid MCP OAuth callbacks from poisoning login

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Problem

The MCP OAuth loopback callback lets an unauthenticated callback attempt fail the pending authorization before the real provider callback arrives. In `packages/core/src/mcp/oauth.ts:448-458`, the callback handler calls `fail()` for `error` / `error_description` before validating `state`; it also calls `fail()` when `state` is missing or mismatched. `fail()` immediately runs `Deferred.fail(code, ...)` at line 453. Thus a request to the callback path with a wrong state (or an error parameter without a valid state) settles the one-shot deferred, and a later legitimate callback cannot complete that login.

## Why it matters

Any party able to reach the loopback callback URL during authorization can deny that MCP login. The callback listener is bound to `127.0.0.1`; the impact described here is login denial, not token disclosure or authorization bypass.

## Reproduction

1. Start an MCP OAuth authorization and capture its loopback `redirect_uri` and expected `state` from the authorization URL.
2. Before the provider redirects back, request that callback path with a missing or incorrect `state` (or with an OAuth `error` parameter and no valid state).
3. Then send the legitimate callback with the expected state and a code.
4. Observe that the authorization has already failed on the first request; the valid callback cannot redeem it.

## Acceptance criteria

- A missing or mismatched state receives an error response without settling/failing the pending authorization, so a subsequent valid callback can still complete it.
- Validate state before treating callback `error` parameters as a terminal provider denial; only a state-validated error callback may fail the authorization.
- Add a regression test that sends an invalid callback followed by a valid callback and verifies the login succeeds, plus a valid-state OAuth error test that verifies provider denials still terminate the attempt.

title: fix(core): revalidate remote instruction redirect destinations

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: priority/high

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

Configured HTTP(S) instruction URLs are fetched without validating redirect destinations. A URL configured to a public server can redirect OpenCode's server-side HTTP client to localhost or a private-network address; the destination response is then accepted as instruction text under the original configured URL.

## Evidence (current `main` `dce42a8911c68645cab9d939605a246431a424ea`)

- `packages/core/src/config/plugin/instruction.ts:152-168` iterates configured URL sources, issues `HttpClientRequest.get(url)`, executes it, reads the response body, and stores the result as instructions. There is no redirect interception or destination check before the body is accepted.
- The configured fetch uses the application's `HttpClient` (`:34,156`); its Fetch-based HTTP engine follows redirects by default. A local Bun runtime probe with two loopback servers confirmed a 302 from the first server was followed to the second server and the second server's body was returned (`seen: ["redirect", "target"]`).
- `packages/core/test/instruction-discovery.test.ts:410-457` covers remote instruction body-size bounds, but not redirect destinations.
- Related, separate surface: #2283 addressed redirect destination permission checks in `webfetch`; it does not cover this config-instruction fetch path.

## Why it matters

A remote instruction host (or an endpoint it points to) can make the local OpenCode process request internal HTTP services. The returned content is then added to model context as trusted configured instruction text. The existing response-size cap and timeout bound resource consumption, not the destination being contacted.

## Suggested fix

Handle redirects explicitly or disable automatic following for this fetch. Resolve each `Location` against the current URL, allow only supported HTTP(S) destinations, and apply an explicit policy before issuing the next request. Bound redirect hops and fail closed on malformed or unsupported locations. If cross-origin redirects are intentionally allowed, document the trust policy and cover it explicitly.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add a regression test where a configured public instruction URL redirects to a local/private destination; verify the destination is not requested under the chosen safe policy and its content is not loaded as instructions.
- Test the redirect policy for allowed same-origin and cross-origin destinations, plus malformed locations and a loop/excessive hops.
- Preserve existing body-size and timeout limits, with clear bounded failure behavior.

## Verification limits

The redirect was reproduced with Bun's Fetch implementation, but the package's `effect` dependency is not installed in this worktree, so the `FetchHttpClient`-backed plugin itself was not run end-to-end here.

title: fix(server): pairing links and QR codes include unreachable IPv6 link-local addresses when listening on ::

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/server
labels.description: Package: server (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Problem

When the server listens on the IPv6 wildcard (`--hostname ::`), `ServerInfo.connectionURLs` advertises every non-internal IPv6 interface address, including link-local ones (`fe80::/10`). A link-local address is only meaningful together with a zone (the interface it belongs to), and the URLs are built without one, so another device cannot connect to them. They still go into `/api/info`, into every `opencode pair` link, into the pairing QR code, and into the TUI pairing dialog.

## Evidence

Verified on `origin/main` `623f4969d01d141dc22997d778e4b4aa31cf7926`.

- `packages/server/src/server-info.ts:18-39` — for a wildcard hostname, `connectionURLs` maps every `networkInterfaces()` entry that passes `!entry.internal && entry.family === family` (line 31) to a URL. There is no link-local filter, and `entry.scopeid` is ignored.
- `packages/server/src/process.ts:88-94` — `localURLs()` feeds that list into the server's `urls()`, which `/api/info` returns.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/pair.ts:29-33,44` — `opencode pair` prints one link per URL and puts every non-loopback URL into the QR payload. The comment on line 32 states the intent: "the QR code only carries reachable addresses".
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-pair.tsx:28` — the TUI pairing dialog lists a link per URL as well.
- No test references `connectionURLs` (`grep -rn connectionURLs packages` finds only the definition and the one call site).

### Reproduction

On a Linux laptop with Wi-Fi, Tailscale and a few Docker bridges, calling the real function (`bun run` from `packages/server`):

```ts
import { connectionURLs } from "./src/server-info"
console.log(connectionURLs("http://[::]:4096", "::"))
```

returned 20 URLs: 1 loopback, 8 routable (ULA) and **11 `http://[fe80::…]:4096`**.

Then, with a real `node:http` listener bound to `::` and each advertised URL fetched from Bun:

| Kind | URLs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| loopback | 1 | HTTP 200 |
| routable | 8 | HTTP 200 |
| link-local, no zone | 11 | all fail, `EINVAL` |

From the point of view of another device, a raw `connect()` to a neighbour's `fe80::` address shows the same thing: with no zone it fails `EINVAL` before any packet is sent; with the zone (`%wlp1s0`) it reaches the host (`ECONNREFUSED`, nothing was listening there). Adding the zone to the URL is not an option either: `new URL("http://[fe80::1%25eth0]:4096")` is rejected by both Bun and Node, and the app parses pairing addresses as URLs.

One caveat on the reproduction: `curl` did reach the laptop's *own* `fe80::` address without a zone (it fills the zone in for local addresses). That does not help a second device, which is who these links are for.

### Effect on the QR code

Using the same `uqr` call as `pair.ts:44`, with a 22-character code:

| Payload | URLs in QR | Bytes | QR version | Terminal size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| as shipped | 19 | 914 | 21 | 105 × 53 |
| without `fe80::` URLs | 8 | 455 | 14 | 77 × 39 |

So on this machine more than half of the printed links are dead, and the QR code is 53 terminal rows tall instead of 39.

## Why it matters

Pairing is the path for getting a second device connected. A list where most links cannot work, and a QR code that no longer fits a normal terminal window, makes that path worse for anyone who binds to `::`. The app's `redeemPairingLink` (`packages/app/src/servers/connect/pairing.ts:85-90`) also spends an attempt with a 5 s timeout on each dead address.

The impact is limited to servers bound to `::`; the default `127.0.0.1` and the documented `0.0.0.0` do not produce `fe80::` URLs.

## Suggested fix

Drop link-local IPv6 addresses (`fe80::/10`) in `connectionURLs`. Making the interface list a parameter (defaulting to `networkInterfaces()`) would let the function be tested without depending on the host.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `connectionURLs` returns no `fe80::/10` URL for a `::` listener.
- [ ] Loopback and routable IPv6 addresses (global and ULA) are still returned, and the `0.0.0.0` and specific-hostname results are unchanged.
- [ ] A unit test covers the function with a fixed interface list: a link-local entry is dropped, a routable entry and the loopback are kept, and a non-wildcard hostname returns the single input URL.

## Related observation (same function, triage to decide scope)

On Linux with `net.ipv6.bindv6only=0` (the default), a `::` listener is dual-stack: the same listener answered `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` and `http://<LAN IPv4>:<port>` with HTTP 200. `connectionURLs` advertises only IPv6 URLs for `::`, so an IPv4-only device gets no usable link although the server is reachable over IPv4. This is platform-dependent (it depends on `bindv6only`), so I am noting it here and not asking for it in the acceptance criteria.

Not checked: macOS and Windows behaviour, and a real second device scanning the QR code.

body:
## Description

`SpeechStream.sampleRate()` can interpret the `bitrate` parameter as the `rate` parameter. In `packages/ai/src/protocols/utils/speech-stream.ts:75-82`, `/rate=(\d+)/i` matches the `rate=` substring inside `bitrate=128000`.

Verified on current `main` (`2e403986d17ee6d2450ceb04822617f295634661`) by importing the actual helper:

```text
audio/L16;codec=pcm;rate=16000 => 16000
audio/L16;bitrate=128000 => 128000
audio/L16;bitrate=128000;rate=16000 => 128000
```

The Google and Deepgram speech protocols use this result before their configured/default sample-rate fallbacks (`google-speech.ts:113`; `deepgram-speech.ts:115`). A bitrate-only media type therefore produces a false sample rate and can override the correct fallback in the returned audio metadata. The existing tests cover positive, zero, and missing `rate` values (`packages/ai/test/speech.test.ts:400-415`) but not parameter-name boundaries. The focused existing tests pass (3/3).

## Suggested fix and acceptance criteria

- Parse a standalone `rate` media-type parameter, not a substring of another parameter name such as `bitrate`.
- Add regression cases proving `bitrate=128000` yields `undefined`, and `bitrate=128000;rate=16000` yields `16000`.
- Preserve existing positive-rate, zero-rate, and absent-rate behavior; confirm callers continue to use their fallback when no standalone rate is present.

This is distinct from closed #697, which fixed handling of `rate=0`.

title: fix(core): Mime.detect rejects BMPs larger than the read tool's 256 KiB sniff window — isBmp size field must not require equality with a prefix buffer

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
# Finding

`Mime.detect` only recognizes a BMP when the header's file-size field is `0` or exactly equals the length of the buffer it was handed — but the read tool hands it only the first 256 KiB of the file. Any real BMP larger than 256 KiB whose encoder wrote an exact size field (the common case) therefore fails detection in the read tool and is never ingested as media, even though `image/bmp` is in `MEDIA_MIMES` and the media ingest cap is 20 MiB.

## Evidence

- PR #2177 (merged 4ac093790368d921728139965894491175d7ee63, commit 892c1860ad5068a18267afe7c7098188bef4c731) strengthened `isBmp` in `packages/core/src/mime.ts`: on current main (2e403986d17ee6d2450ceb04822617f295634661) `mime.ts:46-47` reads `fileSize = u32le(bytes, 2)` and returns `fileSize === 0 || fileSize === bytes.length`. That equality only holds when `bytes` is the whole file.
- PR #2174 (merged b8e3a87be8415125dc94956d8dfc18b7c766d022) added `image/bmp` to `MEDIA_MIMES` in `packages/core/src/tool/read-filesystem.ts`; its only BMP ingestion test uses a 58-byte fixture, so the size interaction was never exercised.
- `read-filesystem.ts` on main: `FIRST_CHUNK = 256 * 1024` (:18), the first read is `{ offset: 0, length: FIRST_CHUNK }` (:135), `Mime.detect(first.bytes)` runs on that prefix (:149), and only a `MEDIA_MIMES` hit takes the media branch (:150-160). `MAX_MEDIA_INGEST_BYTES` is 20 MiB (:17), so BMPs between 256 KiB and 20 MiB are supposed to ingest.
- Consequence for a >256 KiB BMP with an exact size field: `isBmp` returns false, `detect` falls through to `application/octet-stream`, and the read tool drops into its text-paging path, returning garbled text pages for a binary image instead of the image.
- The other `isBmp` prefix-sensitive check, `pixelOffset > bytes.length` (`mime.ts:44-45`), compares a header-declared offset against the same possibly-prefix length and should be audited in the same fix (typical pixel offsets are small, so this is secondary). The other signatures (PNG/JPEG/WebP/PDF/ftyp/GIF) are prefix-safe.
- The session-prompt path (`packages/core/src/session/prompt.ts:116`) calls `Mime.detect(resolved.bytes)` on full attachment bytes, so the defect is specific to prefix-sniffing callers like the read tool.
- Dedupe: issue searches for `bmp` and `Mime.detect` (all states, 2026-11-11) return only #2149 (the prose false-positive fix this check came from, CLOSED) and #2150 (ftyp dispatch, CLOSED). Neither covers the prefix-length interaction.

## Why it matters

BMP ingestion was deliberately enabled by #2174, but in practice it only works for BMPs at most 256 KiB — small icons and fixtures. Ordinary BMPs (a 1024x768 24-bit BMP is ~2.3 MB) silently degrade to mojibake text pages in the read tool, with no error naming the real cause.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Mime.detect` identifies a BMP from a strict prefix of the file: a header whose size field equals the full file size (larger than the handed buffer) and whose pixel-data offset is plausible still returns `image/bmp`.
- [ ] The #2149 prose protections stay intact: text starting with "BM" (including the existing mime.test.ts pins) still detects as `text/plain`, and a non-zero reserved field still rejects.
- [ ] A regression test covers the prefix case (unit-level in `packages/core/test/mime.test.ts` with a truncated buffer, and/or a read-tool test in `tool-read-filesystem.test.ts` with a BMP larger than 256 KiB ingesting as `image/bmp`).
- [ ] The pixel-offset check is audited for the same prefix assumption; any change is pinned by a test.

body:
## Evidence

`packages/core/src/codemode/catalog.ts` sets `INLINE_BUDGET` to 2,000 tokens (estimated as four characters per token). `summarize()` subtracts the cost of every namespace summary from the budget before choosing tool listings, but keeps every namespace even when their summaries alone exceed that budget; the file has a TODO at the namespace-discovery calculation. `packages/core/src/codemode/instructions.ts` then renders every namespace line.

Reproduced on current `main` (`2e403986d17ee6d2450ceb04822617f295634661`) by passing `summarize()` an inventory of 400 namespaces with one tool each and rendering the result: `total=400`, `shown=0`, 400 namespace summaries, and 21,954 output characters (about 5,489 tokens at the same estimate). Thus the inline catalog is over 2.7x its declared budget and contains no directly listed tools.

## Why it matters

Large MCP/tool inventories can make the system prompt exceed the catalog's intended context budget while displacing all tool signatures. The prompt retains discovery instructions, but catalog size is not actually bounded by `INLINE_BUDGET`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Namespace summaries and descriptions are included in an explicit bounded budget, or otherwise capped/hierarchically summarized when they alone exceed it.
- Omitted namespaces remain discoverable through the catalog search mechanism.
- Add tests for a namespace-heavy inventory proving the rendered catalog stays within its documented bound and that discovery still reaches omitted tools; retain normal-inventory coverage.

title: fix(schema): route Window decode still diverges from the runtime parser — empty day/exclude lists decode then drop the whole window, and parser friendly forms fail decode

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.description: Epic: opencode-platform - all issues of this effort carry it

body:
## Problem

PR #2035 (fix for #1681, merged 2026-11-08) added decode-time validation for the route `Window` **string** fields (`dates`, `excludeDates`, `start`, `end`, `timezone`) in `packages/schema/src/config/model-routes.ts`, restating the runtime parser's grammars with the stated oracle (schema comment, `model-routes.ts:159-164`): *every grammar the parser accepts must decode, and every string it would reject must fail decode instead*. The remaining `Window` fields were not audited against that oracle, and they diverge in both directions on current main (`c8caf8b3fb`):

### 1. Decode accepts, parser drops the whole window (the #1681 failure shape)

The `Window` class check (`model-routes.ts:268-285`) rejects empty `dates`/`excludeDates` only. The runtime parser (`packages/core/src/model-route-schedule.ts`) drops the **whole window** (`parse` returns `undefined`) for an empty list in **every** list field:

- `daysOfWeek: []` — parser `:260` (`parsed.length === 0` → drop)
- `daysOfMonth: []` — parser `:269` (same)
- `excludeWindows: []` — parser `:297` (same)
- (`dates: []` / `excludeDates: []` — parser `:286`, already rejected at decode by #2035)

So a config carrying `daysOfWeek: []` decodes cleanly, passes config load with no diagnostic, and then the window silently disappears at parse time in `configuredWindows` / schedule parsing (`packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts:556`, `:670`) — exactly the silent-drop outcome #1681 set out to abolish. Worse, the schema's own field descriptions promise the opposite semantics: `daysOfWeek` and `daysOfMonth` are both annotated *"Empty or unset means every day"* (`model-routes.ts:231`, `:236`).

### 2. Parser accepts, decode rejects (friendly forms)

- Day names: the parser trims and lower-cases before lookup (`model-route-schedule.ts:72-81`), so `"Mon"` and `" mon "` parse; the schema `DayOfWeek` literals (`model-routes.ts:127-150`) are lower-case, unpadded only, so both fail decode.
- Numeric strings: the parser accepts `"3"` for `daysOfWeek` and `"15"` / `"-1"` for `daysOfMonth` (`model-route-schedule.ts:72-97`); the schema accepts only JSON numbers, so both fail decode.
- `excludeWindows` names: the parser trims each name before testing and storing it (`model-route-schedule.ts:293-298`), so `" peak "` parses as `peak`; the schema `WindowName` pattern is untrimmed, so it fails decode.
- `from` / `until`: the parser accepts any finite number (`model-route-schedule.ts:330`) — `from: 0` and fractional values parse; the schema's `PositiveInt` rejects both at decode.

Direction 2 is loud (a load-time error, not a silent drop) and some of it may be deliberate JSON typing strictness — but it contradicts the schema comment's stated equivalence, so each form needs an explicit disposition (accept at decode, or document the strictness and correct the comment), not an accidental gap.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `c8caf8b3fb`)

Probe `probe-window.test.ts`, laptop worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-08-creator-0035` @ `c8caf8b3fb` (copy in the creator evidence dir): each input run through both `Schema.decodeUnknownSync(ConfigModelRoutes.Window)` and `ModelRouteSchedule.parse`:

| Input | Schema decode | Parser |
|---|---|---|
| `{daysOfWeek: []}` | ACCEPT | DROP |
| `{daysOfMonth: []}` | ACCEPT | DROP |
| `{excludeWindows: []}` | ACCEPT | DROP |
| `{dates: []}` (control, #2035) | REJECT | DROP |
| `{excludeDates: []}` (control, #2035) | REJECT | DROP |
| `{}` (control) | ACCEPT | ACCEPT `{}` |
| `{daysOfWeek: ["mon"]}` (control) | ACCEPT | ACCEPT `[1]` |
| `{daysOfWeek: ["Mon"]}` | REJECT | ACCEPT `[1]` |
| `{daysOfWeek: [" mon "]}` | REJECT | ACCEPT `[1]` |
| `{daysOfWeek: ["3"]}` | REJECT | ACCEPT `[3]` |
| `{daysOfMonth: ["15"]}` | REJECT | ACCEPT `[15]` |
| `{excludeWindows: [" peak "]}` | REJECT | ACCEPT `["peak"]` |
| `{from: 0, until: 1000}` | REJECT | ACCEPT |
| `{from: 1.5, until: 1000}` | REJECT | ACCEPT |
| `{from: 100, until: 1000}` (control) | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |

Dedup: #1681 (closed) covered only the string fields and its fix PR #2035 scoped itself to them; no open or closed issue covers the list/day/epoch fields (searched `daysOfWeek`, `excludeWindows empty`, window-decode terms, 2026-11-08).

## Why it matters

A window is an eligibility gate on routing rules: when it drops, the rule it gated applies ungated (or a schedule rule vanishes) with no load-time error — the precise harm #1681's decode-time validation exists to prevent, still reachable through three of the five list fields. The field descriptions actively mislead: an operator who writes `daysOfWeek: []` intending "every day" (as the description promises) instead loses the whole window.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Empty `daysOfWeek`, `daysOfMonth`, and `excludeWindows` lists fail decode with a diagnostic naming the field (mirroring the #2035 empty-`dates` handling), **or** the parser treats an empty list as unset in all list fields — one semantics, applied in both places, with the field descriptions updated to match.
- [ ] Each direction-2 form (capitalised/padded day names, numeric-string days, padded `excludeWindows` names, `from`/`until` of 0 or fractional) has an explicit disposition: decode accepts what the parser accepts, or the schema comment and field descriptions document the deliberate strictness.
- [ ] Tests in `packages/schema/test/config.test.ts` pin both directions against the parser's documented acceptance set, extending the existing `ConfigModelRoutes.Window string fields (#1681)` describe to the list/day/epoch fields.
- [ ] Existing schema and model-route-schedule suites stay green.

Related: #1681 (the string-field half, closed by PR #2035), PR #2035 (landed the decode validation this extends).

title: fix(core): quota re-admission (#1974) judges a model by whichever window iterates last — a still-full window fails to hold the skip when another window sorts after it

body:
## Problem

`ModelRoute.releaseQuotaSkipsForCurrent` (the #1974 re-admission judgement, landed in PR #1978, merge `8ed9d6ca99`) can lift a model's attempt-reported quota skip while one of that model's quota windows is still at 100% — depending only on the array order of the model's windows in the gathered snapshot.

`modelWindowReading` (`packages/core/src/model-route.ts:742-768`) collapses all of a model's windows into a single "best" reading: iterating candidates, `if (!best || window.measuredAt >= best.observedAt)` overwrites `best`, so among windows sharing a `measuredAt` the **last array element wins**, whatever window it names. Distinct windows (e.g. `5h` and `weekly`) are never aggregated.

That tie is the normal case, not an edge: `QuotaCurrent.modelWindowsOf` (`packages/core/src/quota-current.ts:67-88`) stamps **every** per-model window with the provider entry's single `measuredAt`, so a model's windows always share a timestamp in parsed readings. The gatherer's own shape (fixture in `packages/core/test/quota-current.test.ts`) carries two windows per model (`weekly`, `5h`).

This contradicts #1974's stated rule in the same file (`releaseQuotaSkipsForSnapshot` doc, `model-route.ts` ~696-711): *"a reading that still shows the window full lifts nothing"*. The provider-wide branch of the same function already implements the correct semantics (`model-route.ts:809-822`): it aggregates with `Math.max(...)` over the provider's windows and requires **every** window to carry a percent. The model branch does neither.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `8ed9d6ca99`)

Probe `probe-modelwindow.test.ts`, laptop worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-07-creator-2335` @ `8ed9d6ca99` (copy in the creator evidence dir): plant a model-scoped skip via `observeQuotaFailure` for `opendesign / claude-haiku-5.5`, then call `releaseQuotaSkipsForCurrent` with a two-window reading at one `measuredAt`:

- windows `[weekly:4, 5h:100]` → released `[]`, leaf stays skipped (correct outcome, by accident of order)
- windows `[5h:100, weekly:4]` → released `["quota-model:opendesign:claude-haiku-5.5"]`, leaf un-skipped — **while its 5h window reads 100%**
- control `[weekly:4, 5h:1]` → released (expected)
- control single `[weekly:100]` → released `[]` (expected)

So the judgement is order-dependent: the same measured state both lifts and holds the skip, decided by JSON key order in `quota-current.json`. The `resetAt` carried into the judgement is likewise whichever window iterated last.

The sibling candidate source has the same flaw: provider windows named `${modelID}:…` are pooled into the same candidate list (`model-route.ts:750-753`).

Existing tests don't catch it: every `gatheredReading` case in `packages/core/test/model-route.test.ts` (from line ~2761) gives the model exactly **one** window.

## Why it matters

Re-admission exists to avoid spending attempts probing a walled door (#1974: "No attempt is ever spent to test the door"). An order-dependent release sends real attempts into a model whose short window is still exhausted — the attempts fail with quota errors, re-plant the skip, and burn the pool's error budget — and whether that happens flips with the gatherer's serialization order, so it will appear and disappear without any code change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A model's skip is lifted only when the freshest reading for that model shows **every** window it carries below full (mirroring the provider-wide branch's aggregate semantics), regardless of window order in the snapshot.
- [ ] A percent-less (`usedPercent: null`) window in the model's freshest reading does not silently drop out of the judgement (cf. the provider-wide branch, which skips entries carrying a null percent).
- [ ] Regression tests pin both orders of a two-window reading (`5h:100 + weekly:4` and `weekly:4 + 5h:100`) — neither releases — plus the both-headroom control, which still releases.
- [ ] Existing `model-route` and `quota-current` suites stay green.

Related: #1974 (the re-admission feature this judgement implements), #1976 (skip scoping), PR #1978 (landed the code).

Ordered by Drew 2026-11-03: "embed and all others should be baked into fork native features — no proxy services needed."

## Current shape
`POST /v1/embeddings` exists in the fork (Wave A, #1434) with the backend registry in `packages/core/src/embeddings.ts`, but the actual computation for the first registered backend (local-embed/snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v2.0, ONNX int8, 768-d) runs in a separate local service on 127.0.0.1:18752 — a dev/test service with NO nix declaration anywhere (verified by grep in the 2026-11-03 nix audit). The fork calls it over HTTP.

## Target shape
The embedding backend runs natively inside the fork server process — model loading, batching, and inference in-process behind the existing registry, with the same external behavior: OpenAI-shaped responses, mixed-length batches untruncated, per-model output dimensions, `dimensions` parameter (Matryoshka) where the model supports it, loud 400 where it does not, ledger parity for façade calls.

## Sequence (additive-first, per standing migration doctrine)
1. Spike: prove the int8 ONNX model runs in the server runtime (Bun) in-process, outputs matching the sidecar on fixed test vectors.
2. Add the native backend behind the registry alongside the sidecar backend; verify parity (dims, Matryoshka 256-d, batch shapes, error envelopes).
3. Flip the registry default to native; verify live with the :18752 service STOPPED.
4. Only then retire the sidecar service + its code, and note the closure here.

## Acceptance criteria
- The local embeddings backend runs natively in-process in the fork (no dependency on the :18752 sidecar for the local path)
- The :18752 sidecar is retired from the local-backend path, with config/docs updated to match
- Embeddings behaviour verified end-to-end on the fork (index + query round-trip)

body:
### Context & Background
In OpenCode upstream commit `7b33bcea4e` (`feat(desktop): show session tokens and cost on the session view (#53785)`), upstream introduced a UI display in the session view header showing accumulated tokens and estimated cost for the active session.

In our fork (`developing-today/opencode`), we calculate exact per-request USD costs derived from the official `models.dev` token catalog pricing and store it directly in the `route_attempt` table under column `cost_usd` (migration `20261014094820_route_attempt_cost_usd.ts`). Currently, upstream's new desktop session cost view computes a rough estimate or reads client-side estimates rather than our authoritative server-calculated database value.

### Feature Objective
Wire our authoritative `cost_usd` database metric from `route_attempt` directly into OpenCode's session metadata and the desktop session view, ensuring that users see exact dollar costs calculated from the official `models.dev` pricing snapshot.

---

### Technical Specifications

#### 1. Aggregate Session Cost in Session Service
- In `packages/core/src/session.ts` or `packages/core/src/session/generate.ts`:
  - When returning or subscribing to `SessionInfo` / session state:
  - Query total `cost_usd` by summing all attempts for `session_id` in `route_attempt`:
    ```sql
    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cost_usd), 0.0) AS total_cost_usd
    FROM route_attempt
    WHERE session_id = ? AND outcome = 'success';
    ```
  - Populate `session.cost` with this exact value (formatted in USD currency, e.g. `$0.042`).

#### 2. Protocol & Client Contract
- In `packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts` and `packages/schema/src/session.ts`:
  - Ensure `SessionInfo.cost` is typed as a number (USD) and documented as authoritative `models.dev` computed cost.
  - When new LLM attempts finish in `publish-llm-event.ts`, emit an updated session telemetry event carrying the latest total `cost_usd`.

#### 3. Desktop Session UI Component
- In `packages/app/src/session/` (or `packages/desktop/src/` where `#53785` renders):
  - Ensure the header component formats the authoritative `cost_usd` value:
    - Values < $0.01: `<$0.01`
    - Standard values: `$0.04`, `$1.28`
  - On hover, provide a tooltip breaking down input token cost, output token cost, and cache savings.

---

### Key Files & References
- `packages/core/src/database/migration/20261014094820_route_attempt_cost_usd.ts`: `cost_usd` column definition
- `packages/core/src/model-usage.ts` & `model-plan.ts`: Token catalog pricing and cost calculation formulas
- `packages/core/src/session/runner/publish-llm-event.ts`: Emitting session cost updates
- `packages/desktop/` and `packages/app/src/session/`: Session header view components

### Acceptance Criteria
1. The session view header displays the exact sum of `cost_usd` recorded for that session in `route_attempt`.
2. As new turns complete, the displayed dollar cost updates in real-time.
3. Pricing matches official token pricing from the bundled `models.dev` catalog.
4. Unit tests in `packages/core/test/` verify session cost aggregation from multiple attempts.

title: Gathered quota wall does not hold provider-wide snapshot pools (opendesign/cline-pass shape): seated legs still attempted every wave — blocks un-disabling _claude/_muse
body:
## Problem

Drew's ruling (2026-11-15): quota-walled providers should be **enabled and skipped**, not disabled. `_claude` (anthropic:claude-pro) and `_muse` (meta) are currently in `disabled_providers` in the fleet config. Before they can be un-disabled, the skip has to be proven for their quota shape — and on today's evidence it does not hold.

## The uncovered shape

The gatherer's snapshot (`quota-current.json`, code#1151) carries `_claude` and `_muse` exactly the way it carries `opendesign` and `cline-pass`:

- exactly ONE entry for the provider,
- NO per-model windows (`usage.models` empty for the seated models),
- the wall stated on provider-wide windows: `_claude` 7d = 100% (reset 2026-11-18T19:00Z), `_muse` weekly = 100% (reset 2026-11-16T00:00Z), opendesign 7d = 100% (reset 2026-11-17T11:44Z), cline-pass monthly = 100% (reset 2026-12-06T14:40Z).

`gatheredQuotaWall` (code#8086) has a provider-wide branch for this shape, and the plant (commit 000dbd2464) is in the running build (4bcf07a, live since 2026-11-14 18:14 CT). The Go/Zen instance legs prove the proactive path works where it applies: route decisions exclude them as `quota-known-full-until:...` with zero attempts.

## Evidence the wall does not hold for this shape (2026-11-15, running build)

- **opendesign**: 42 route attempts in the trailing 6h (42 distinct sessions) to `opendesign/mimo-v2.6-flash` — 41 failed `insufficient_balance` ("Coding Plan quota is exhausted"), 1 ECONNRESET. Plus attempts to `opendesign/deepseek-v4.1-flash` failing the same way.
- **cline-pass**: 8 attempts in the same 6h to `cline-pass/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, all 429 "You have reached your monthly Clinepass limit".
- In route decisions, opendesign/cline-pass legs are only ever excluded **reactively** — `credential-cooldown-until:...` (a bench planted by a failed attempt, +24h) or `credential-bench-probe-in-flight` — never proactively as `quota-known-full` the way the Go/Zen legs are.
- The reactive bench does not hold across waves either: benches planted at ~14:00Z and ~18:02Z (until +24h) did not prevent fresh attempts at 18:00–18:01Z and again at 22:09–22:10Z. The pattern is ~1 burned attempt per session per walled leg, indefinitely — each new wave/location pays it again.

Net: for provider-wide snapshot pools, selection still spends attempts into a door the fleet's own snapshot reads at 100% with a future reset. That is the burn class the gathered wall was built to eliminate, and it is why `_claude` / `_muse` cannot be un-disabled yet: enabled tonight, their seated legs (haiku/sonnet/fable plans; spark/wonder seats) would take the same per-wave attempts into the wall — for `_claude` that is the exact pattern that produced 14,161 quota refusals on 2026-11-13 while it was enabled and walled.

## What would close this

A pre-attempt gate for this shape that holds across sessions and locations: while a fresh gathered reading stands at 100% with a future reset, a seated leg of that provider is excluded as quota-known-full (like the Go/Zen legs) and takes **zero** attempts — no first-in-wave burn, no probe.

Acceptance: with opendesign and cline-pass still walled and still seated, `route_attempt` shows zero rows for both over a 6h window of normal fleet traffic; their legs appear in route decisions only as proactive quota exclusions. At that point the fleet config un-disables `_claude` and `_muse` (the `_claude` un-disable additionally waits for fork PR #2466 to be merged and pin-bumped, per code#9549).

## Notes

- `_commandcode` is NOT blocked on this: it has zero seats in the fleet config (removed 2026-11-13, code#9397), so its un-disable is inert and is proceeding separately.
- `_antigravity` stays disabled regardless — banned account, not a quota wall.
- Candidate lead, unproven: the plant/feed judges the refs it is handed per (location, provider); route-expanded leaf legs in a fresh location may never receive a plant before their first attempt, and restored benches may be judged under a different location's policy than the one that planted them.

body:
## Finding

`lookupSecretService` (`packages/ai/src/providers/secret-service.ts`, current main `d35c4341598043b1320e5d450049062cba341705`, lines 12–13) synthesizes `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/<uid>/bus` whenever the variable is absent — regardless of `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`.

That overrides a derivation that would otherwise work. PR #2425's own probe table (the PR that introduced this synthesis, closing #2313) proved:

| Launch environment | Read result |
| --- | --- |
| DBUS unset, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` set | ✅ value — the binding's D-Bus stack derives `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus` unaided |
| DBUS unset, XDG unset | ❌ fails — the gap the synthesis restores |

So for the DBUS-unset / XDG-set launch shape, the correct synthesized address — if one is synthesized at all — is `unix:path=$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus`. Whenever `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` differs from `/run/user/<uid>` (nested or container sessions, non-systemd session managers, custom runtime dirs), the current code instead installs the canonical path, pointing the keyring binding at a bus that is not the session's bus. Every failure in this helper is swallowed to `undefined`, so the regression is silent: credential lookup simply finds nothing.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #2425 `fix(ai): restore the session-bus address synthesis in lookupSecretService (#2313)`, head commit `cdadfb93b267478c294106f9c381a2a0236aa071`, merge commit `3e2ad12690baa76d85814e495f5847a6a8174e29` (ancestor-verified against current main, compare behind=0).
- Diff hunk: the synthesis is gated only on `!process.env.DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS && typeof process.getuid === "function"` — `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is never consulted.
- Verified live on current main (2026-11-15): the file is byte-identical in this respect — the unconditional synthesis is still present.
- Test gap: `packages/ai/test/provider/secret-service-dbus.test.ts` pins (a) DBUS absent → canonical address synthesized, and (b) an explicit bogus DBUS address left untouched. No test covers DBUS absent + `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` set to a non-canonical directory. `verification_class: runtime-gap/high-risk` (environment-boundary runtime behaviour, no targeted test/eval for the exact scenario, CI does not execute it — the suite uses a recording double that never dials a bus).

## Why it matters

The launches #2313/#2425 set out to fix — cron, detached/ssh spawns, non-user systemd units — are exactly the launches whose runtime dir is least guaranteed to be the canonical one. In those shapes this helper can turn a Secret Service read that would have succeeded unaided into a silent miss, with no error anywhere: the caller just sees "no credential found".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` unset and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` set, the helper either leaves the environment alone (letting the binding derive `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus`) or synthesizes `unix:path=$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus` — never a different path.
- [ ] With both variables unset, the existing canonical `/run/user/<uid>/bus` synthesis is unchanged, including the Bun libc `setenv` write.
- [ ] With `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` set (even to a bogus address), it is never overridden — unchanged.
- [ ] A new test in `packages/ai/test/provider/secret-service-dbus.test.ts` pins the DBUS-unset + XDG-set (non-canonical dir) case against the recording double.
- [ ] Runtime verification (triage): reproduce with a live binding under a non-canonical `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` if a Secret Service is available, or record why the recording-double test is the strongest available check.

title: fix(core): a probe-pending bench claim that never settles has no time backstop — the leg stays out of candidacy for the life of the process (#2441/#2449 residual)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)
