labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Finding

The half-open probe claims introduced for auth benches by PR #2441 (and extended to long retry-after benches and per-effort traffic scopes by PR #2449) have no time-based backstop. Once a probe-pending bench is claimed, the claim is cleared only by an explicit settle (`failed`/`completed`) or release (`releaseBenchProbe`). If any path ever misses both — an interrupted attempt fiber is the obvious candidate — the leg stays out of ordinary candidacy for the remaining life of the process: `probeDue` requires `probeClaimedAt === undefined`, and `recover()` can never clear the claim because it returns immediately when `cooldownUntil === 0`, which is exactly the probe-pending state's shape. Quota-bench claims do not have this failure mode: their bench cooldown keeps running, and when it lapses `recover()` clears the claim fields with it.

## Evidence

- PR #2441 (MERGED, merge `4bcf07ab5d36aebb1758f2f861f3e0090735d264`) — fix(core): half-open probes for auth benches (code#9950); PR #2449 (MERGED, merge `aa0c8be805f50c660dc792d655d0fac7715997c9`) — effort-scoped traffic benches, same claim machinery across four scopes.
- Verified on current main `c3247993265218b538a3a8ecc13149d7dcf8df13`, `packages/core/src/model-route.ts`: `recover()` (line ~528) begins `if (state.cooldownUntil === 0 || state.cooldownUntil > now) return`; `probeDueState` requires `state.probeClaimedAt === undefined`; `probeInFlight` (line ~925) reports a claim with no age check; `availability()` documents the design as "the probe, not a clock, ends the stop". A search of the file finds no claim TTL/age constant anywhere.
- Settle/release coverage is broad but enumerative: `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts` releases on the policy-failure path (lines 771-775) and for un-attempted hedge picks (lines 1072-1078); `packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts` releases on load failure (lines 1144-1147). Nothing reclaims a claim whose owner vanished mid-attempt (e.g. the step fiber is interrupted while the probe request is in flight — `packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts` holds no probe-claim handling at all).

## Runtime verification (verification_class: runtime-gap/high-risk) — REPRODUCED

- Commit tested: current main `c3247993265218b538a3a8ecc13149d7dcf8df13`, isolated worktree on the laptop (removed after; primary clone untouched).
- Command: `bun test test/probe-claim-ttl.test.ts` (packages/core, bun 1.4.4) — probe drives the real `ModelRoute`: auth-bench a target, let the bench expire into probe-pending, claim the probe, then never settle or release it.
- Result: 2 pass / 0 fail (18 expect() calls). The claimed scope still reports `probeInFlight === true`, `probeDue === false`, and availability reason "auth bench expired; half-open probe in flight" at +1h, +24h, and +30 days (synthetic clock), and a candidacy read (`cooldownUntil`, which invokes `recover()`) does not clear it. Control: a released claim makes the probe due again, as designed.

## Why it matters

Routing health is process-local and long-lived: one leaked claim silently removes a door (or one credential, or one effort leg) from every session's candidacy until the server restarts, with availability reporting a probe "in flight" that will never land. The failure is invisible precisely because the mechanism works as coded — there is no stale-claim state to alert on.

## Acceptance criteria

- A probe claim older than a bounded age (a named constant, sized well above any real attempt) is reclaimable: the scope becomes probe-due again (or the claim is cleared by a read, as `recover()` does for lapsed quota benches), at all four scopes (target, credential, traffic, traffic-credential).
- A regression test pins it: claim a probe-pending bench, advance past the claim bound without settling, assert the probe is due again; the existing auth-probe and rate-limit-bench tests keep passing.
- Alternatively, if the enumerative settle/release coverage is proven complete (including step-fiber interruption mid-attempt), record that proof on this issue and close it with the proof linked.

title: fix(server): PTY shutdown registry leaks a handle when attach fails outside the two caught tags or the connect handler is interrupted (#2430 residual)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/server
labels.description: Package: server (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Finding

PR #2430's graceful-shutdown registry for PTY websockets can leak a handle: the connect handler registers the socket with `trackPtySocket` *before* `pty.attach(...)` runs, but the only untrack is the `Effect.ensuring` attached to the later `runPtySocket(...)` call. Any failure or interruption between registration and `runPtySocket` — an attach error outside the two caught tags, or the handler fiber being interrupted while attach is in flight — leaves the handle in the module-level `ptySocketShutdownHandles` set for the life of the process.

## Evidence

- PR #2430 (MERGED, merge `7bd4089641a53ec13d0fd38309260ad94e9f106b`, head `d7d902768ac9f5bb65a6bbdcb7d74779cd99ae6e`) — fix(server): drain PTY websockets during graceful shutdown (#2284).
- Verified on current main `c3247993265218b538a3a8ecc13149d7dcf8df13`, `packages/server/src/handlers/pty.ts`: line 183 `trackPtySocket({...})` runs first; lines 187-202 `pty.attach(...)` is piped through `Effect.catchTags` for only `Pty.NotFoundError` and `Pty.ExitedError` — any other attach failure (or interruption) propagates out of the handler; the `Effect.ensuring(Effect.sync(untrackPtySocket))` is attached only to the `runPtySocket({...})` call that follows (line 211+), so it never runs on that path.
- Consequence, `packages/server/src/process.ts` (from the same PR): the leaked handle keeps `trackedPtySocketCount() > 0` forever, so every graceful shutdown offers a close frame into a dead outbox, waits the full `ptySocketDrainBound` (2s), logs "force-closing PTY sockets that did not drain", and terminates the dead outbox — and the count the drain (and `process.test.ts`) relies on is permanently wrong by the number of leaks.
- No test covers it: #2430's `process.test.ts` addition covers only the happy path (tracked socket closes deliberately with code 1001 during drain).

## Runtime verification (verification_class: runtime-gap/high-risk) — INCONCLUSIVE

Not reproduced this run: there is no seam to force a non-caught attach failure or a mid-attach interruption without modifying application code, and this run's one runtime-verification slot went to a higher-impact routing finding. The leak is established by code structure (registration scope vs ensuring scope, both quoted above); the acceptance criteria include the regression test that pins it.

## Why it matters

The registry is the shutdown drain's source of truth. A single leaked handle makes every subsequent shutdown pay the full PTY drain bound and emit a misleading force-close warning, masking real drain failures — and the leak is silent at the moment it happens, because the connect request itself has already failed for an unrelated reason.

## Acceptance criteria

- Registration is scoped so it cannot outlive the connect handler on any exit path (e.g. track after a successful attach, or wrap registration-to-`runPtySocket` in an acquire/ensuring that always untracks).
- A regression test covers a connect whose attach fails with an error outside the two caught tags (or whose handler is interrupted after registration): `trackedPtySocketCount()` returns to 0 and a later shutdown does not wait the PTY drain bound.
- The existing PTY drain test in `packages/server/test/process.test.ts` keeps passing.

title: fix(cli): Node SEA keyring adapter has no addon asset on darwin/win32 — AsyncEntry throws at first use (#2327)

body:
## Finding

PR #2327 (merged 25afb02d3352b260bfdda7b1c9a4f9379249d850; closes #2324) wired the native `@napi-rs/keyring` addon into the Node SEA bundle only for Linux targets. On darwin and win32 Node artifacts, any code path that constructs the keyring `AsyncEntry` throws `The Node artifact is missing its platform keyring addon` — the runtime adapter is in the bundle graph for every target, but no addon asset is ever extracted or pointed to for non-Linux targets.

## Evidence (all verified on current main 1e2537ba3280bbcbcfabcbcd2124c00bfbb5efba; PR #2327 merge confirmed an ancestor, compare behind=0)

- `packages/cli/src/node/target.ts:13-14` — `keyringAsset` is set only when `targetPlatform === "linux"` (`keyring/keyring.linux-${arch}-gnu.node`); darwin/win32 targets get `undefined`.
- `packages/cli/vite.node.config.ts:120-128` — the `opencode:keyring-runtime` adapter's `load()` throws when `OPENCODE_NODE_KEYRING_PATH` is unset; `:339` sets that env var in the SEA banner only when `input.target.keyringAsset` is truthy; `:158-161` requires the adapter in the bundle graph for ALL targets but only requires the asset for Linux.
- `packages/cli/script/node-assets.ts:38-42` — asset extraction happens only when `target.keyringAsset` is set, resolving `@napi-rs/keyring-linux-${arch}-gnu`.
- `packages/cli/script/build-node.ts:126-129` — the `AsyncEntry` smoke check runs only when `target.keyringAsset` is present, so non-Linux builds never exercise the path.

So the graph guard proves a keyring consumer is bundled for every platform, while the delivery mechanism exists for exactly one. `@napi-rs/keyring` ships darwin and win32 platform packages as well; those targets were simply not wired.

## Why it matters

Credential features backed by the OS keyring (Secret Service / Keychain / Credential Manager) work in the Bun build and in Linux Node artifacts, but hard-fail at first use in macOS/Windows Node artifacts with a build-configuration error the user cannot act on. It is a silent platform-parity gap: builds pass, smoke checks pass, and the failure only appears when a user actually touches a keyring-backed credential path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] darwin and win32 Node targets resolve and extract their platform keyring addon (`@napi-rs/keyring-darwin-*` / `@napi-rs/keyring-win32-*-msvc` or the correct platform package names) as a SEA asset, and the banner sets `OPENCODE_NODE_KEYRING_PATH` for them — OR an explicit, documented decision that Node artifacts on those platforms do not support keyring, with the adapter failing that way by design and the limitation recorded where #2324 was tracked.
- [ ] `build-node.ts`'s AsyncEntry smoke check (or an equivalent) runs for every target that claims keyring support.
- [ ] The bundle-graph guard asserts the asset exists for every target that claims keyring support, not only Linux.

Dedupe: issue searches for `keyring` (all states) return #2324 (the Linux bundle fix this PR landed, CLOSED) and #2313 (in-process Secret Service DBUS fallback, OPEN, different path) — nothing covers non-Linux Node-artifact keyring delivery.

title: fix(core): Copilot chat stream still emits tool-call events for chunks arriving after a stream error (#2312 residual)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Finding

PR #2312 fixed the flush path so a Copilot stream that has failed never flushes its *unfinished* tool calls, and made the error finish-reason sticky. But the transform still processes every chunk that arrives *after* the error normally: if a later chunk completes a tool call's JSON (or introduces a new tool call that is complete in one chunk), the transform enqueues a normal `tool-call` event for it — downstream of the `error` part the stream already reported. A single malformed SSE event does not end a real stream, so "error, then more chunks" is the ordinary shape of the failure #2311 was filed for, not an edge case.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #2312 (https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2312, merge commit `0f5561c21cb84465cefef3881fa1d6f8eaa43a4d`, confirmed an ancestor of current main, compare behind=0). Verified on current main `f80e767cb3f54418701db73e6a0fe5f3572b40fd` by reading `packages/core/src/github-copilot/chat/openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts` from main.
- On main: `hasStreamError` is set on a chunk parse/validation failure (:397) and on a provider error chunk (:411), and the sticky guard at :459 stops a later chunk's `finish_reason` from clearing the error state.
- The flush guard (:663-668) suppresses only the flush-time emission of unfinished tool calls.
- The transform-time emission sites have no `hasStreamError` check: a newly-seen tool call whose arguments are already parsable JSON is emitted as a `tool-call` event at :587, and an existing tool call completed by a later delta is emitted at :630. Text/reasoning deltas after an error are likewise still streamed. So the sequence partial-tool-call → malformed chunk → completing delta yields `[error, tool-call]` with finish reason `error`.
- Test gap in #2312: its three new tests end the stream after the error (a `[DONE]`, or a terminal chunk with an empty delta). No test sends a chunk that completes (or newly completes) a tool call after the error.

## Why it matters

- #2311's stated harm was downstream acting on tool calls from a failed stream; that harm survives for any tool call completed after the first bad chunk — the consumer receives an error *and* an executable tool call for the same response, and which one wins depends on the consumer.
- The sticky-finish fix in #2312's second commit shows later chunks were in scope; the tool-call emission path was left inconsistent with it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After a stream error (parse failure or provider error chunk), the transform emits no further `tool-call` events for that response — neither completions of in-flight calls nor new calls completed by post-error chunks.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/core/test/github-copilot/copilot-chat-model.test.ts`: (a) partial tool call, malformed chunk, then a delta completing the JSON → error part present, zero `tool-call` parts, finish reason `error`; (b) provider error chunk, then a new single-chunk complete tool call → zero `tool-call` parts.
- [ ] Clean-stream behavior is unchanged: tool calls completed before any error are still emitted, and the existing #2312 tests still pass.

body:
## Finding

PR #2264's membership gate in `SessionStep.attempt` returns before the hedge/escalation block whenever the attempt's model carries a membership stamp, so a capped primary is never hedged and never escalation-raced — and the hedge-slot helper written for exactly that composition is dead code on the only path that could use it for the primary.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #2264 (https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2264, merge commit `cab6bf481b231b3b734295fc9eec12f3f68be606`, confirmed an ancestor of current main, compare behind=0). Verified on current main `a7410110703b014b6a5437fa5f2ab9a4e46f2566` in two independent contents reads of `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts`.
- `step.ts:926-946` (on main): `const membership = input.model.membership; if (membership) { ... return yield* run(input).pipe(Effect.ensuring(release)) }` — every capped attempt exits through the single-request `run` path (or recurses to the fallback leg on gate refusal).
- `step.ts:948-975` (on main): the hedge block (give-up escalation via `ModelRoute.escalates`, `SessionHedge.race`, `hedgeAfterMs`) is reached only when `membership` is falsy. Its comment at `:958-961` says "the primary's slot was taken by the gate above; a hedge leg on the same account is a second concurrent request and meters separately" — but the gate above never ran on this path.
- `step.ts:975`: `yield* holdHedgeSlot(input.model)` is therefore a guaranteed no-op: `holdHedgeSlot` returns at once when `model.membership` is falsy (`:965`), which is exactly the condition for control to reach that line. Only `holdHedgeSlot(next)` for a capped hedge leg behind an uncapped primary (`:1002`) can ever fire.
- The PR body states the intended composition — "Hedge legs against a capped provider take their own slot and release it when the race settles" — and no test in #2264 exercises a capped primary on a route with `hedgeAfterMs` or an escalating target (the membership suites cover the gate, the accumulator, and the Generate façade, not step-level hedging).

## Why it matters

- The one provider that declares caps today is `opendesign` — the workhorse route's seat (#2253). Routes through it silently lose two standing latency/reliability behaviors: hedge racing after `hedgeAfterMs`, and immediate racing of a target that keeps giving up (`escalates`). Slow or hanging capped primaries now always wait for the single-request path's own timeouts.
- The dead call plus the comment that describes the unreachable flow make the code read as if the composition works; the next editor has no signal that capped primaries were excluded, deliberately or otherwise.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Either (a) a capped primary can hedge/escalate like an uncapped one — the gate's slot and the hedge legs' slots compose, with the primary's `holdHedgeSlot(input.model)` call reachable and metering the hedge leg as its comment describes — or (b) the exclusion is deliberate: the dead call is removed and the no-hedge-for-capped-primaries rule is documented at the gate with its reasoning.
- [ ] A test at the step/runner level pins whichever behavior is chosen: a capped primary on a route with `hedgeAfterMs` set (or an escalating target) demonstrably races a hedge leg holding its own membership slot, or demonstrably never races, per the documented rule.
- [ ] Gate behavior otherwise unchanged: bounded wait, silent failover on refusal, last-resort unmetered proceed when no fallback leg exists, and slot release on every exit.

## Shadow verdict (PoC)

Would-be verdict for PR #2264: **second-pass**.
- Ring 1 (the diff): the gate, the shared accumulator, and the tier-limit backstop are correct and heavily tested (seeded 5,000-step cap sweep, gate wait/failover/last-resort paths with injected clocks).
- Ring 2 (the whole work): checkable gap — the gate's early return silently removes hedging and give-up escalation for every capped primary, the hedge-slot composition the PR describes is unreachable for the primary, and `holdHedgeSlot(input.model)` is dead code; no test names a capped primary on a hedged route.
- Ring 3 (the goal): #2253's goal is that the opendesign account be usable up to its caps without session-visible tier-limit errors — not that the workhorse seat lose the router's standing latency behaviors; the trade-off, if wanted, is nowhere recorded as a decision.

title: fix(core): direct-model route attachment fallback has no last-resort pass — direct launches still die when every remaining target is cooling (#2265 residual)

body:
## Finding

The direct-model route attachment from PR #2265 builds its own `fallback()` closure that never runs the last-resort pass PR #2259 added to the routed fallback. A session launched on a bare provider/model whose containing route's remaining targets are all cooling (but not quota-dead) still dies on its first startup provider error — the exact #7073 case-(b) condition #2259 fixed for routed launches.

## Evidence

- Source PRs: #2265 (https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2265, merge commit `3dde5c3992966f5a8fc29ccf6f4db86cec739609`, confirmed an ancestor of current main, compare behind=0) and #2259 (https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2259, merge commit `f23d88c689ba2290258cea33cf6dcca0a1bc69d3`, ancestor of main, compare behind=0). Verified on current main `a7410110703b014b6a5437fa5f2ab9a4e46f2566` in two independent contents reads of `packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts`.
- Routed fallback (on main, `model-resolver.ts:861-895`): after `resolveRouteWithin` (ready-only) and `cascadeToParent` both come up empty, a "Last resort, last (#7073)" step re-runs `resolveRouteWithin(..., allowCooling=true, ..., allowQuotaDeadLastResort=false)` and seats the least-bad non-quota-dead target instead of refusing.
- Direct-attached fallback (on main, `model-resolver.ts:1341` `attachDirectRoute`; its `fallback` closure at `:1390-1422`): the chain is only `resolveRouteWithin(candidate, route, ..., allowCooling=false)` → `cascadeToParent(route, ...)` → fail-with-first-load-error / `undefined`. There is no last-resort step, and `cascadeToParent` (`:1249ff`) is itself ready-only (`allowCooling=false` at every hop).
- So the first fallback hop of a direct launch differs from a routed launch of the same route: when every untried target is cooling, the routed resolution's fallback seats one; the direct resolution's fallback returns `undefined` and the runner's failover cascade (gated on `model.routing`, the thing #2265 exists to provide) ends.
- Test gap in #2265: its single regression test ("attaches the containing route to a direct model so startup errors can fail over") uses only ready targets. #2259's walled-cascade tests (every remaining target benched, last resort seats one; quota-dead de-preferred) have no direct-launch counterpart.

## Why it matters

- #7073's incident condition was precisely "every untried target cooling" (a credential bench ~7.8h deep, another ~57s from recovery). Direct launches — cases (a)/(c) of the same issue — remain exposed to it even though both fix steps are merged.
- The divergence is invisible in the code's own terms: `attachDirectRoute`'s doc says its fallback "continues to parent routes exactly like a routed resolution's fallback", but the routed fallback's defining final step is missing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A direct resolution's `fallback()` ends with the same last-resort pass as the routed fallback: when no ready candidate remains in the route or its parents, it seats a cooling target that is not quota-dead in any scope, and still returns `undefined` when only quota-dead targets remain (#1806 clean stop).
- [ ] A regression test in `packages/core/test/model-resolver.test.ts` mirrors #2259's walled test for the direct path: direct model in a multi-target route, all other targets failure-benched (not quota), `fallback()` seats one of them; and a quota-dead-only variant returns `undefined`.
- [ ] Existing #2265 behavior is unchanged when a ready target exists: the direct target still serves first and the first ready route target serves on fallback.

## Shadow verdict (PoC)

Would-be verdict for PR #2265: **second-pass**.
- Ring 1 (the diff): the attachment itself is correct and tested for the ready-target case; the selected model still serves first and the direct target is seeded as tried.
- Ring 2 (the whole work): checkable gap — the direct fallback chain omits the last-resort pass its routed sibling gained in #2259 (same #7073 series), so the all-cooling condition that killed incident case (b) still ends a direct launch; no test covers a direct fallback with every remaining target cooling.
- Ring 3 (the goal): code#7073's goal is that startup provider errors fail over instead of killing lane sessions; two of its three named cases were direct launches, so the step-2 fix does not yet deliver the goal under the incident's own conditions.

body:
## Evidence

Verified against fresh `origin/main` at `e1d1a88bdd8f021f6b99bb62d5c04c03508451cf`. In `packages/core/src/session/runner/hedge.ts:31-51`, `startLeg` creates `Queue.unbounded<LLMEvent>()` and offers every event at line 39 before deciding whether it counts as output. The `OUTPUT` set at lines 8-19 excludes lifecycle events such as `step-start` and `step-finish`, so a leg can keep accumulating these while the hedge waits for output or the deadline. After a winner is selected, a fast producer can also outpace the consumer draining `Stream.fromQueue` (line 63). There is no byte or event-count bound.

`packages/core/test/session-hedge.test.ts:28-126` covers winner selection, replay, failure, and timeout, but has no stalled-consumer or sustained non-output-stream bound case. This is a source-verified memory robustness gap; I did not reproduce it against a live provider.

## Why it matters

A provider stream that emits many non-output events, or produces events faster than the selected stream is consumed, can grow a hedge leg queue without limit and exhaust process memory.

## Acceptance criteria

- Bound each leg's buffered event count and/or bytes while preserving event order and full replay within the supported limit.
- Define explicit overflow behavior that fails the affected leg/race; do not silently drop response events.
- Add deterministic tests for a sustained non-output stream and a slow consumer, including bounded-memory/overflow behavior and successful complete replay for an in-bound stream.

## Dedupe

Fresh all-state issue searches for `hedge`, `hedge event`, and `SessionHedge` found no matching item; #2223 (closed) concerns route_usage reporting for hedge winners, not queue capacity. OPEN #2330 is the client AI WebSocket inbound-frame queue, and OPEN #2335 is the route-telemetry persistence backlog; neither covers this per-leg stream queue. Fresh open-PR inventory and an open-PR search for `hedge` found no implementation of this change.

## Finding

`ModelRoute.plantGatheredQuotaWall` (from PR #2252) overwrites a standing attempt-reported model quota skip whenever the gathered snapshot shows a wall — flipping its `quotaSkipOrigin` from `"attempt"` to `"proactive"` and replacing its `until` and note — even though the function's own documentation states the opposite invariant.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #2252 (https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2252), merge commit `c43145b0f1f3f2bb53274626415224228c7209c5`, confirmed an ancestor of current main `a172a12bb0bd80f4691380036a5374e1bc781534` (compare behind=0).
- `packages/core/src/model-route.ts:929-930` (on main): "Attempt-reported records are another path's business (#1974): this plant neither lifts nor overwrites one."
- `packages/core/src/model-route.ts:939-951`: the wall branch computes `id = quotaModelSkipID(target)` and unconditionally calls `addAdjustment({ id, ..., until: wall.until, quotaSkipOrigin: "proactive", note: "quota exhausted (gathered snapshot); ..." })` — there is no check of the standing record's origin on this branch (the origin guard at `:953` covers only the lift branch).
- `packages/core/src/model-route.ts:3023-3025`: `addAdjustment` "Adds an adjustment, replacing one with the same id" — so the plant replaces the standing record in place.
- `packages/core/src/model-route.ts:2436-2443`: `observeQuotaFailure` plants the attempt-reported record under the **same** id (`quotaModelSkipID(target)`) with `quotaSkipOrigin: "attempt"` and `until` = the failure's stated reset (bounded by the gate).
- Trigger sequence is the production one: `packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts:579-580` (`refreshQuotaSkips`) runs `releaseQuotaSkipsForCurrent` then `plantGatheredQuotaWall` for every due target on each feed. On a full reading the release no-ops, then the plant replaces the attempt record.
- Test gap in #2252: the test named "the gathered plant never touches an attempt-reported skip" (packages/core/test/model-route.test.ts) exercises only a **headroom** reading, where `gatheredQuotaWall` returns undefined and the overwrite branch never runs. The wall-judged case against a standing attempt record is untested.

## Why it matters

- Provenance is load-bearing in this module: `releaseQuotaSkipsForSnapshot` (`model-route.ts:760ff`) only releases records `attemptQuotaSkip` recognises (`:728-731`: origin `"attempt"` or an "(attempt-reported)" note). After the flip, the plan-snapshot release path (`observeQuotaSnapshot`, `model-route.ts:2227`) no longer recognises the record at all; only the gathered plant's own lift branch (complete + fresh + headroom gathered reading) can remove it early.
- The attempt record's `until` — the reset the failing provider itself stated — is replaced by the gathered wall's `until` (the gatherer's window reset, or the fallback hold when it states none). The two need not agree, so a leg can be held longer or released earlier than the attempt evidence said, with the record's note/origin no longer showing which evidence governs it.
- This is exactly the class of silent cross-path interference #2254 later had to fix for feed stamps; the documented invariant is right, the wall branch just doesn't implement it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a record with id `quotaModelSkipID(target)` already stands with `quotaSkipOrigin: "attempt"`, `plantGatheredQuotaWall` leaves it untouched (no origin, `until`, or note change), matching its documented invariant — or the invariant is deliberately changed and the doc, the release-path consequences, and the tests are updated together with the reasoning recorded.
- [ ] A regression test in `packages/core/test/model-route.test.ts` covers the previously untested case: an attempt-reported skip standing + a gathered reading that judges a wall → the record remains attempt-origin with its original `until`.
- [ ] Existing gathered-wall behavior is unchanged for targets with no standing attempt record: a fresh 100% reading still plants a proactive wall pre-attempt, and a later complete headroom reading still lifts a proactive plant.

## Evidence (verified on `origin/main` `15ca2a204476646d25c2b4eda8ef45c2c6a899f1`)

The normal PTY connect handler upgrades the HTTP request at `packages/server/src/handlers/pty.ts:178` and immediately notes that graceful-shutdown socket tracking is not integrated (`:179`). It then waits on `runPtySocket` at `:205`, so the request remains active for the lifetime of the WebSocket. The client constructs this WebSocket in `packages/client/src/solid/pty.ts:24-40`.

`packages/server/src/process.ts:176-200` closes the listener, drains active requests only within configured grace periods, and warns when requests remain; the PTY handler does not register its upgraded socket with that lifecycle. Existing process shutdown tests cover ordinary HTTP requests (`packages/server/test/process.test.ts`) but not a live PTY WebSocket.

## Impact

A server restart with an attached terminal cannot perform a controlled PTY socket drain. The long-lived request can consume the request grace period and then be interrupted, dropping the terminal connection rather than closing it as part of the graceful shutdown lifecycle.

## Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- Register upgraded PTY sockets with the server shutdown lifecycle.
- During shutdown, send a deliberate WebSocket close and detach the PTY attachment, then wait only for a bounded drain before force-closing any remaining socket.
- Add a process-level regression test that keeps a PTY WebSocket open while shutdown begins and verifies the socket receives a controlled close and shutdown does not wait for the full request timeout.

# fix(script): raw-changelog still targets the upstream layout — the fork's packages never reach the changelog, and the default repo is anomalyco/opencode

## Summary

`script/raw-changelog.ts` — the script behind the `/changelog` command
(`.opencode/command/changelog.md:47` runs `bun script/raw-changelog.ts $ARGUMENTS`) —
was inherited from upstream and never adapted to this fork's package layout or
repo identity. Run in this repo today it produces an empty or wrong changelog
for the fork's own releases.

## Evidence (verified this run on the laptop primary @ e340f54ac284)

1. **Wrong default repo.** `script/raw-changelog.ts:25`:
   `const repo = process.env.GH_REPO ?? "anomalyco/opencode"`. Nothing in
   `.opencode/`, `script/release.ts`, `script/publish.ts`, or `package.json`
   sets `GH_REPO` (grep verified), so `latest()` (:53-58) reads the latest
   non-draft release of **anomalyco/opencode** and `diff()` (:60-74) compares
   upstream's commits — not this fork's.
2. **Pathspec names packages that do not exist here.** `commits()` (:122-123)
   filters `git log` to `packages/opencode packages/plugin packages/desktop
   packages/app sdks/vscode packages/extensions github`. In this fork
   `packages/opencode` and `packages/extensions` do not exist (ls verified);
   the living packages — `packages/core`, `packages/ai`, `packages/util`,
   `packages/cli`, `packages/tui`, `packages/server`, `packages/sdk`, … — are
   not in the pathspec at all.
3. **Measured effect.** Over `HEAD~50..HEAD` on current main (97 commits):
   the script's pathspec admits **0** commits; `packages/core` alone accounts
   for 16 and `packages/core` + `packages/ai` + `packages/util` for 55. The
   changelog input for any recent range is therefore empty ("No notable
   changes.") regardless of what actually shipped.
4. **Area mapping is old-layout only.** The per-file area assignment
   (:134-141) and the `sections` map (:35-44) only know the upstream prefixes
   (`packages/opencode/…` → core/tui, `packages/plugin/` → sdk, …). A file
   under `packages/sdk/`, `packages/core/`, `packages/cli/`, or
   `packages/tui/` matches no branch, so even a commit admitted by the
   pathspec (e.g. a mixed app+core commit) gets `areas.size === 0` for its
   fork-package files and is skipped or mis-sectioned.

## Why it matters

The `/changelog` command is the fork's release-notes path: its prompt
(`.opencode/command/changelog.md`) trusts the script's output as "already
filtered to the release-relevant packages". Today that filter silently drops
essentially everything the fork ships, and the release baseline comes from a
different repository. Release notes generated this way are wrong by omission
with no error surfaced.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The default repo is this fork (`developing-today-forks/opencode`), or
      the script fails loudly when `GH_REPO` is unset instead of silently
      reading upstream.
- [ ] The `git log` pathspec covers the fork's current packages (at minimum
      core, ai, util, cli, tui, server, sdk, app, desktop, plugin) and names
      no package that does not exist in this repo.
- [ ] The area/section mapping assigns every covered package to a section,
      including `packages/sdk` → SDK and `packages/tui` → TUI.
- [ ] A run over a recent range (e.g. the last 50 commits) on main lists
      real fork commits instead of "No notable changes."
- [ ] Existing section order and output format are preserved.

## Bug: repo-sweeper's daily stale-issue close always fails — close-issues.ts requires GITHUB_TOKEN, the workflow only provides GH_TOKEN

Found by queue triage task 11852 (lane opencode-a) while closing #1776; this is a distinct failure mode in the same workflow, filed separately per the one-failure-one-issue rule.

### Evidence (verified 2026-11-08)

- Run 42437029179 (schedule, 2026-11-08T02:05:36Z, head 373aad25) concluded **failure**. Failed step: `Close stale issues (daily, 02:00 UTC window)`. Log: `error: GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable is required` thrown from the closer script, exit code 1.
- `.github/workflows/repo-sweeper.yml`: the step (line ~168) runs `bun script/github/close-issues.ts` gated to schedule events in the 02:00 UTC hour, with no step-level env. The job-level env (lines 59-60) provides only `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`.
- `script/github/close-issues.ts:87-88`: `const token = process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN; if (!token) throw new Error("GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable is required")` — it never reads GH_TOKEN.

### Why it hides

The step self-skips outside the 02:00 UTC schedule window, so most repo-sweeper runs are green; the daily 02:00 UTC run is the one that executes the closer, and it fails every time the gate passes. Whether other closer scripts in script/github/ share the GITHUB_TOKEN-only read is part of the fix's audit scope.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The 02:00 UTC scheduled repo-sweeper run completes the `Close stale issues` step successfully (green run link as evidence), or the step's failure mode is an explicit error row rather than a job failure if the close itself is best-effort — pick one and record why.
- [ ] The token contract is consistent: either the workflow supplies the variable the script reads, or the script accepts the workflow's GH_TOKEN convention — one convention, applied to every script/github/ closer the sweeper invokes (audit close-prs and siblings for the same mismatch).
- [ ] A cheap guard exists so the mismatch cannot silently return (e.g. the script's required-env names are derived from / checked against the workflow env, or a test asserts the closer's env contract).

body:
## Observed defect: sessions stall in a loop of ~4-token no-message completions (claude-sonnet-5-5 via claude-code provider)

Observed twice on 2026-11-06 evening (CST), production server (fork build 08eca393d6d1), during the fleet feature wave on issue #1885:

- Session `ses_e5e4c6d3d7dffegQw6FgFK7K2u` (route `specialist`, provider `claude-code`, model `claude-sonnet-5-5`, variant high): after ~40 productive minutes it began emitting route attempts with `tokens_output = 4`, `assistant_message_id = NULL`, outcome `success`, recurring roughly every ~4 minutes (route_attempt ids 323432, 323500; tokens_input ~110k). No new session messages, no tool calls; a minder "Continue." prompt was accepted (HTTP 200) and also produced only a 4-token no-message attempt. Session was interrupted by the minder.
- Successor session `ses_e5e4c5f4065ffeGMJc7943Q5sG` (same route/model, fresh context, ~50k input tokens): three productive attempts, then the same 4-token no-message pattern and stall. Interrupted by the minder.
- Control group: two sessions on the `workhorse` route (DeepSeek) ran 60+ minutes the same evening with no such stall; the #1885 stream was relaunched on workhorse and proceeded normally.

Why it matters: a session in this state looks merely quiet — it burns a full-context attempt every few minutes and never progresses, and the retry/continuation machinery does not surface it as an error (outcome is recorded as `success`). It is adjacent to #1891 (serving-leaf invisibility) but distinct: the failure is in the attempt loop, not observability.

Suggested investigation: what a 4-token completion with no assistant message contains (stop reason?), why the loop keeps scheduling continuations after empty completions, and whether an empty-completion streak should trip the availability/cascade machinery (treat N consecutive no-message completions as a failed attempt and fail over).

Evidence: `route_attempt` rows for the two sessions above in the laptop server store (~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db), 2026-11-07T00:50Z–01:45Z.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A claude-code-provider session that receives a no-message ~4-token completion does not loop indefinitely: the loop is detected (repeated no-message completions) and the session surfaces an error or recovers instead of silently stalling
- [ ] Route-attempt records for the stall pattern are distinguishable from genuine short completions (a marker, outcome, or message-id invariant is enforced or logged)
- [ ] Regression coverage reproduces the observed pattern (successive 4-token, NULL-message attempts) against the session loop

title: fix(core): route failover traps sessions on a quota-walled member — sticky pin + fallback never re-draws the origin pool (89 sessions died 2026-11-05 while Luna served 3,149 successes in the same route)

body:
## Summary

On 2026-11-05 ~22:55–23:56Z, **89 queue-lane sessions died** on the Antigravity Claude/GPT quota wall ("Individual quota reached") even though their route (`workhorse`) had a healthy, serving member the whole time. In the same window, `workhorse-primary` chose `openai-plan/gpt-6-luna` **3,154 times** and `openai.main` logged **3,149 successes** through the workhorse route. The pools and the route work — sessions that *fresh-draw* rotate fine. Sessions that had already drawn the walling member were trapped: their sticky pin kept re-selecting it, and the failover walk never re-drew the untried healthy member of the origin pool, ending in `no-candidates`.

Drew's ruling when this was surfaced as "a wall": *unless every single plan is tapped out, a session dying on one pool's quota instead of auto-choosing another provider is an error in our stack.* It was not every plan: OpenAI plan was at ~87–90%, AG Gemini ~26–28%, DeepSeek API routes open, Mistral Vibe plan leg live.

## The error, identified

- Text: `Individual quota reached. Please upgrade your subscription to increase your limits. Resets in 81h35m49s.` — classified `AI.Error.RateLimit` by the AI layer.
- Source: provider **`antigravity-direct`**, model **`claude-sonnet-5-5`** (the Antigravity Claude/GPT bucket), drawn via `workhorse → workhorse-primary → sonnet-plan` (sonnet-plan's only live door; claude-code is disabled).
- Reset math checks out: first logged at 2026-11-05T23:24:33Z with "Resets in 81h35m49s" → **2026-11-09T09:00Z**, exactly the AG Claude/GPT bucket reset recorded in the route config on 2026-11-03.
- 591 occurrences in `opencode.log` that evening; 1,605 failed `route_attempt` rows against antigravity-direct in the 22:50–23:56Z window; 3,750 all-time for this error text.

## Evidence trail (laptop opencode.db, 2026-11-05)

Sessions `ses_e5e5213cb1dffehQZ9zzrdAcTU` (opencode lane #3026, created 22:55:00Z on route `workhorse`), `ses_e5e51f8557cffe9remJl4d8rtR`, `ses_e5e51ea9667ffd2MPFISZCgsXb` — all end `idle_outcome=failed`, cost 0.

Decision/attempt trace for the first session, first step:

1. `workhorse` (ordered) → `workhorse-primary` (round-robin) → `sonnet-plan` (round-robin) → **drawn** `antigravity-direct/claude-sonnet-5-5` → failure `RateLimit`, retryable=1.
2. Failover fired once: `workhorse` → `workhorse-ordered` → `deepseek-flash-plan` → drawn `mistral-plan/mistral-small-latest` → `mistral/mistral-small-latest` → failure **`QuotaExceeded`, retryable=0** (Mistral API pool had walled at 22:45Z). deepseek-flash-plan's other doors were legitimately out (cline-pass + opendesign pool-quota-exhausted, Go doors in credential cooldown).
3. Next resolution: `workhorse` → **`no-candidates`**. Exclusion detail lists `workhorse-primary` and `workhorse-ordered` as **`already-tried`**, and Luna's leaf excluded by two `credential-cooldown-until` reasons — while Luna's serving credential (`route_attempt.credential_id` for openai.main) had **no health rows at all** that evening and 4,765 successes on the day.
4. Every subsequent step repeats: `workhorse-primary` → **`sticky`** → `sonnet-plan` → **`sticky`** → AG → fail → `no-candidates`. ~10s cadence inside the runner, then ~4min claimant warm retries ("failed to warm session"), until drain failure. 763 `no-candidates` decisions across 74 sessions in the window.
5. Meanwhile `route_health` recorded **996 `cooldown-start` rows** for antigravity-direct (reason `retry-after`, until = +24h each) — the target kept being attempted while its own cooldown was active; each new failure just re-wrote the cooldown.

Current state: self-quieted by 2026-11-06 ~03:00Z (claimant stopped re-warming the dead sessions; fresh draws rotate to healthy members). The defect is latent — the AG bucket stays walled until 2026-11-09T09:00Z, and any session that sticks to a member whose pool walls mid-flight re-enters this trap.

## Narrowed candidate mechanisms (all in the resolution path)

1. **Sticky pin is not broken by quota failure / cooldown.** `packages/core/src/model-route.ts` — the sticky choice (chooser ~L2867, `stickyTarget` ~L1983) re-selects the session's pinned member on every step. Evidence says the pin survived both the target's quota failure and its recorded cooldown. Check what `steady()`/continuity validation actually consults (cooldown keyed by target+credential+location vs the AG target's credential-less attempts: AG `route_attempt.credential_id` is NULL for all 3,750 attempts).
2. **Failover `tried` set is scoped to the whole resolution tree, not the leaf.** In the step's failover resolution, both ancestor routes of the two attempted leaves were `already-tried`, so the walk could not re-enter `workhorse-primary` to draw its untried, healthy Luna leaf. `nextTarget` readiness is leaf-granular (`openLeaves`: ready && !tried per leaf, ~L2637), but the `tried` set accumulated during the chain (~L2964) appears to mark ancestor positions at each level (~L2758). Failover should exclude *leaves already attempted*, not *pools partially attempted*.
3. **A leaf's `unavailable` verdict may be judged by its worst credential.** Luna's leaf was excluded citing cooldowns of credentials that were not serving it (one already expired, one ~19h out — the quota-gated alternate credential cycles 30-min gates in `route_health`). A multi-credential leaf should be unavailable only when *every* credential is unavailable.
4. Secondary: **cooldown ignores the provider-stated reset.** AG said "Resets in 81h35m49s" (in the error body); the recorded cooldown was +24h. `model-route.ts` ~L465 caps cooldown at `quotaResetAt` only when a reset was extracted — the AG reset lives in message text and apparently is not extracted.
5. Secondary: **inconsistent quota classification.** The identical condition (pool exhausted) classifies as `RateLimit`/retryable=1 for Antigravity but `QuotaExceeded`/retryable=0 for Mistral. `retryable` drives the runner's same-target Retry outcome (`step.ts` `SessionRunnerRetry.isRetryable`), so AG failures invite ~10s same-target retries against an 81-hour wall. Quota-exhaustion should be uniformly failover-eligible and never same-target-retryable on a short cadence.

## Acceptance

- A session whose drawn member returns quota-exhausted is served by another eligible member of its route (same step or next step) whenever one exists — including a member of the *same* pool it just drew from.
- A quota failure breaks the session's sticky pin on the failed member; the member is not re-attempted while its quota/cooldown state says it is out.
- Regression test: two-member pool, wall member A mid-session, assert the session completes on member B without a `no-candidates` resolution.
- Related doctrine: #1014 (a declined retry cascades while eligible candidates remain), #1122, #587.

## Acceptance criteria
- When a drawn pool member returns a quota-wall RateLimit, failover re-draws untried healthy members of the origin pool before declaring no-candidates; a session is never stranded while any member of its route can serve.
- A sticky pin to a quota-walled member is released (or bypassed) on the wall, so pinned sessions fail over instead of re-selecting the walled member.
- A regression test reproduces the traced 2026-11-05 scenario (pinned session, walled drawn member, healthy untried member) and passes; route_attempt logging shows the healthy member being drawn.

## Finding

Three open PRs in this repo are superseded: the work each one carries already landed on main through a different PR, and both target issues are closed. Leaving them open invites a queue worker or PR shepherd to pick up duplicate work — or, worse, to merge a stale branch whose approach conflicts with the policy shape that actually landed.

## Evidence

**Effect-patterns set (target issue #1496, CLOSED 2026-11-04T02:36:54Z):**

- PR #1497 (open, head `effect-patterns-triage` @ 35a27a43df, base ae4b9776f8) — "fix(ci): disposition effect-patterns violations and wire scan into CI", triage of #1496.
- PR #1566 (open, head `queue/7181-1496-effect-patterns` @ 863e6cd586) — opened by the git-hygiene sweep from an unpushed laptop worktree; its head is literally a merge of PR #1497's head commit 35a27a43df, so the two PRs carry the same change.
- PR #1576 merged 2026-11-04T02:36:52Z ("fix(lint): disposition all 33 lint:effect-patterns violations and wire the scan into CI") and closed #1496. Verified on current main dddd6654b674: `.github/workflows/test.yml:153` runs `bun run lint:effect-patterns`.

**Workflow-permissions set (target issue #1503, CLOSED 2026-11-04T07:19:42Z):**

- PR #1504 (open, head `queue/6809-1503-permissions` @ ab20d93d70) — "Fixes #1503"; adds a `check:workflows` policy that accepts `permissions:` at workflow OR job level.
- PR #1594 merged ("feat(ci): add a permissions policy to check:workflows (#1503)") and closed #1503, implementing the stricter shape: a top-level `permissions:` mapping is required on every workflow. Verified on current main dddd6654b674: `script/check-workflows.ts:189-193` implements `require-top-level-permissions`. PR #1504's weaker job-level variant is subsumed by, and inconsistent with, the landed policy.

All three PRs carry no labels and no queue claim as of this filing (checked 2026-11-04).

## Why it matters

Stale open PRs are live hazards in this fleet: sweeps and shepherds treat open PRs as work waiting to happen. Merging #1504 now would add a second, weaker permissions policy alongside the landed one; merging #1497/#1566 would re-disposition 33 already-dispositioned lint violations from a stale base. Closing them with pointers to the landed PRs removes the trap at near-zero cost.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PR #1497 closed with a comment citing PR #1576 and issue #1496 as the landed disposition.
- [ ] PR #1566 closed with a comment citing PR #1576 (and noting it duplicates #1497's head commit 35a27a43df).
- [ ] PR #1504 closed with a comment citing PR #1594 and issue #1503 as the landed policy, noting the landed shape (top-level mapping) supersedes its job-level variant.
- [ ] No code changes; nothing is merged from any of the three branches.

Found by pr-diff-review lane B while reviewing PRs #1474–#1505 (2026-11-04 run).

body:
## Problem

`convertSchema` in `packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts` drops the JSON Schema `const` keyword entirely. A tool parameter pinned to a fixed value (`{ const: "fixed" }`) is sent upstream as an unconstrained schema (`{}`), so the model is free to supply anything.

## Evidence (verified this run on clean main `974ca6c76d`, laptop probe importing the real module)

`const` is absent from the field allowlist at `packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts:90-95`:

```ts
const SCHEMA_FIELDS = new Set([
  "type", "format", "title", "description", "nullable", "default", "enum",
  "example", "items", "prefixItems", "minItems", "maxItems", "minProperties",
  "maxProperties", "properties", "propertyOrdering", "required", "minLength",
  "maxLength", "pattern", "minimum", "maximum", "anyOf", "oneOf", "allOf", "not",
])
```

and `convertSchemaNode` skips any key outside the set, so the constraint vanishes. Probe output (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-03-creator2/probe.ts` on the laptop, module imported from main):

```
convertSchema({type:"object",properties:{kind:{const:"fixed"}}})
  -> {"properties":{"kind":{}},"type":"OBJECT"}
convertSchema({type:"object",properties:{kind:{type:"string",enum:["a","b"]}}})
  -> {"properties":{"kind":{"enum":["a","b"],"type":"STRING"}},"type":"OBJECT"}   // enum passes through fine
```

## Why it matters

The proto Schema has no `const` field, but it does carry `enum` (already in the allowlist and passed through verbatim, per the probe above), and a one-element `enum` is the faithful equivalent of `const` on both targets — Gemini's proto Schema and the Anthropic `input_schema` the door re-serializes for Claude models both accept `enum`. Fixed-value parameters are a real tool-schema pattern (discriminator fields, mode pins, version pins); today the pin silently disappears in the Antigravity door while working through other providers, so the same tool behaves differently depending on the route. Same silent-constraint-loss class as #1548 and #1550, in the same converter.

Scope note: the proto `enum` is string-valued, so this mapping is exact for string (and stringified scalar) consts; a non-string `const` disposition (stringify, or document the drop) should be chosen deliberately in the fix rather than left silent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A scalar `const` converts to the equivalent one-element `enum` (with the node's `type` preserved/derived consistently), for both Gemini and Anthropic targets.
- [ ] The chosen disposition for non-string `const` values is implemented and stated in a code comment (no silent drop).
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/antigravity.test.ts` covering a string `const` property and the non-string disposition.
- [ ] `bun test` in `packages/ai` green (1894 pass / 0 fail at main `974ca6c76d` before the change).

Related: #1548, #1550 (same converter, same class). Deduped against open and recently closed issues this run — no existing issue covers `const` handling in `convertSchema`.

title: fix(desktop): extension archive download has no timeout — size-capped pump in manager download() hangs forever on a stalled or slow-dripping server

body:
## Problem

The desktop extension manager's URL download bounds the archive's **size** carefully but never bounds **time**:

- `packages/desktop/src/main/extension/manager.ts:91` — `download(url)` calls Electron's `net.fetch(url)` with **no `signal`** and no deadline of any kind.
- `packages/desktop/src/main/extension/manager.ts:103-122` — the body is pumped chunk by chunk with a running size check against `archiveLimit` (100 MiB, `archive.ts:6`, plus the declared `content-length` pre-check at `:97-101`). The pump's only exits are stream end, stream error, or exceeding the size cap. A server that stalls after the headers — or slow-drips bytes under the cap (100 MiB at 1 KiB/s is ~29 hours; a full stall is forever) — keeps `reader.read()` pending indefinitely.

`install()` (`manager.ts:59-61`) awaits `download(source)` for a string source, and the entry point is the `ExtensionInstall` IPC handler (`packages/desktop/src/main/ipc-handlers/extensions.ts:58` → `host.ts:693-694`), so one stalled or slow-dripping extension URL hangs that install call in the desktop main process with no error, no cancellation, and no way for the user to learn what happened short of restarting the app.

## Verification (this run)

Line-level verification on main `42869cd3f7` (the #942 precedent): `net.fetch` at `manager.ts:91` receives no options object at all — no `signal` exists anywhere in `download()` — and the pump loop at `:103-122` contains no timer, deadline, or idle check; its exits are exactly `next.done`, a read error, and the size check. Dedup: `gh issue` search (all states) for the extension manager / archive download returns no issue covering this path; the nearest sibling, #1006 (SSH bootstrap fallback download), is a different package and path that had *neither* bound — this path has the size bound and is missing only the time bound.

## Why it matters

The size discipline in this function is the house pattern done right (declared-length pre-check + streaming cap, the same shape as #923/#1006's fixes) — which makes the missing time bound the one remaining way a remote server can hang a user-facing install forever. The URL is exactly the kind of thing a user pastes or an extension listing hands them. Other download/install paths in the fleet bound their time (the SSH bootstrap's primary path uses `curl --max-time 180`, #1006; the gui-extensions WSL health probe uses `AbortSignal.timeout(3000)`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `download()` carries a named overall deadline for the whole transfer (fetch + pump), sized for a 100 MiB archive on a slow-but-honest connection and stated in a comment; when it fires, the read is cancelled and the install fails with `ExtensionError("download", …)` (or a dedicated timeout error), not a hang.
- [ ] The deadline covers both phases: a response that never arrives (or stalls before the body) and a body that stalls or slow-drips mid-transfer both settle as the same download failure.
- [ ] Happy path unchanged: an archive under `archiveLimit` that completes in time installs exactly as today; the declared-length and streaming size checks behave exactly as today.
- [ ] A regression test pins the stalled-response and slow-drip behaviours (install rejects with the download error instead of pending forever), following the desktop package's existing extension test conventions (`lifecycle.test.ts` / archive tests; `net.fetch` may need an injectable seam, which is acceptable if kept minimal).
- [ ] Out of scope: the archive size limits and validation in `archive.ts`, the byte-source (non-URL) install path, and the SSH bootstrap download (#1006).

Filed by new-issue-creator-opencode, 2026-10-31 run. Cross-reference: #1006 (same missing-time-bound class in the SSH bootstrap fallback; different package and path).

title: Quota-aware session placement: filter by quota % and session type (root vs subsession)

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: New feature or capability request

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/l
labels.description: Large: multi-day or open-ended; expect staged check-ins

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

labels.name: epic/opencode-platform
labels.description: Epic: opencode-platform - all issues of this effort carry it

body:
## Problem

OpenCode routes sessions to providers/models without considering **how much quota is left** on a pool or **what kind of session** is being placed. In our fleet discipline (see the provider quota registry in developing-today/code), plan quotas are meant to be **used all the way to 100% and then stop** — never spilling into pay-as-you-go. But the *shape* of usage near the limit matters:

- A **subsession** (a subtask/subagent spawned inside a running session) is short and bounded. Near the limit, a pool is *ideal* subsession territory: the subsession can push the pool to 100% and then stop, without ever entering PAYG.
- A **root/primary session** is long-lived and open-ended. Starting a *new* root session on a pool that is already near its limit strands that session mid-work when the quota runs out.

Today there is no way to express that distinction, so placement is quota-blind.

## Desired behavior

Quota-aware placement filtering, driven by live quota percentage per pool and the session type:

1. **Subsession gate**: subsessions may be placed on a pool up to 100% of its plan quota. At 100% they stop — they must **never enter PAYG** (configurable, default: hard stop).
2. **Root session start gate**: new root/primary sessions are not *started* on a pool above a configurable threshold (default 85%). A root session already running on a pool may **continue until the quota runs out** — or stop exactly at the limit — configurable.
3. **Per-pool / per-model weights**: every rule carries an adjustable weight, and every rule can be individually **disabled** without removing its configuration.
4. All thresholds and behaviors are **configuration, not constants**: percentages, the PAYG stop, and the at-limit behavior for running root sessions are all settable per pool/provider.

## Config sketch

```yaml
quota:
  gates:
    rootSessionStartMaxPct: 85     # don't start new root sessions above this
    subsessionMaxPct: 100          # subsessions may burn to the limit
    subsessionAllowPayg: false     # hard stop before PAYG
    runningRootAtLimit: continue   # continue | stop-at-limit
  # each gate: { enabled: true, weight: 1.0, ... } — disable or re-weight per pool
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Placement decisions consult the current quota % for the candidate pool (using the existing quota sources; a stale read older than a configurable age is treated as unknown, not as headroom).
- [ ] A subsession request against a pool at 97% is admitted; at 100% it is refused/redirected and **no PAYG call is made**.
- [ ] A root session request against a pool above `rootSessionStartMaxPct` is redirected to the next eligible pool; a root session already running is unaffected until its configured at-limit behavior triggers.
- [ ] Setting any gate's `enabled: false` restores today's quota-blind behavior for that gate, verified by test.
- [ ] Weights change selection order among eligible pools, verified by test.
- [ ] Behavior is covered by unit tests for: below threshold, at threshold, at 100%, PAYG-stop, disabled gate.

## Context

Fleet rule (Drew, 2026-10-27): pools burn to 100%, then stop until reset or until a fresh read shows the quota has dropped off 100% (some providers reset early). Related: time-based weighting and native quota-driven reprioritization are filed as separate issues.

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

CodeRabbit raised this on PR #2466 and it was never addressed: when a claude-code renewal adopts another writer's rotated refresh token, single-flight ownership does not move with it. The renewal's pending operation stays registered under the original token's key, while its exchange now presents the adopted token. A concurrent load that reads the rotated credentials file computes its coordination key from the adopted token, finds neither the in-flight map nor the standing-renewal map under that key, and starts a second exchange of the same single-use refresh token within the same process — the concurrent-use hazard the single-flight maps exist to prevent (replaying a single-use token can revoke the token family).

- Source PR: #2466 — https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2466
- Review comment: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2466#discussion_r4577793172
- Reviewer: coderabbitai[bot], 2026-11-15T09:16:43Z (Major · Stability & Availability)
- Flagged location: `packages/ai/src/providers/claude-code-auth.ts:822`

## No-response evidence

- No replies on the review thread; the thread is unresolved (checked via GraphQL `reviewThreads` this run).
- The sibling finding on the same PR (adoption bound, comment 4577793169) was fixed pre-merge via issue #2467 / commit ad356786d2, and the PR's agent note (task 17356) covers only that bound fix — the ownership finding is not mentioned.
- Issue search found no tracker for the ownership finding; #2467 (closed) covers only the adoption-bound replay.

## Still live on current main

`packages/ai/src/providers/claude-code-auth.ts` (current main):

- `refreshCredential` (line 1049) keys coordination by the caller's snapshot token: ``const key = `${sources.configDir ?? ""}\^@${credential.refreshToken}` ``, and registers the attempt only under that key (line 1088, `inflightRefresh.set(key, attempt)`); `standingRenewals` is keyed the same way.
- `adoptStored` (line 836) replaces `currentRefreshToken = stored.refreshToken` inside `refreshAndPersist`, with no registration or join under the adopted token in either map.

So a load that starts from the rotated file (key = adopted token) cannot see the in-flight renewal that is about to exchange that very token.

## Acceptance criteria

- Before exchanging an adopted token, the renewal registers or joins the in-flight operation under the adopted token (and the same ownership rule applies to standing renewals), so concurrent loads share exactly one exchange of a single-use token, AND
- a regression test drives two concurrent loads across a rotation and asserts a single exchange of the adopted token; OR the finding is resolved by a documented decision recorded on this issue.

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

CodeRabbit raised this on PR #2464 (the #566 root-start placement PR) as an outside-diff review finding, and it was never addressed: when a session has no explicit model, the runner resolves the default model through `resolver.resolve(...)`, which carries no session context at all. The resolver therefore leaves `cascade.kind` undefined and skips the #566 root-start gate entirely — a new root session can start on a pool whose snapshot is at 90%, the exact start the gate exists to block. The explicit-model path in the same function does pass the session context (`resolveModel(selected, variant, session.id, requestTokens, session.parentID)`).

- Source PR: #2464 — https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2464
- Review: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2464#pullrequestreview-5909679260
- Reviewer: coderabbitai[bot], 2026-11-15T07:42:26Z (Major · Functional Correctness, outside diff range)
- Flagged location: `packages/core/src/session/runner/model.ts:109`

## No-response evidence

- The PR's thread replies and conversation notes address only the inline finding (snapshot staleness in `model-route.ts`, fixed in e6986dd0f7); nothing replies to, fixes, or tracks the default-model finding.
- Issue search (PR number; root-start/default-model keywords) found no existing tracker; parent feature #566 is closed.

## Still live on current main

- `packages/core/src/session/runner/model.ts:109` (current main): `const resolved = yield* resolver.resolve(undefined, requestTokens)` — no `session.id`/`session.parentID`.
- `packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts:1750` (current main): `resolve` ends in `resolveSelected(selected, target?.variant, undefined, requestTokens)` — `sessionID` hardcoded `undefined`, `parentID` dropped, so `cascade.kind` is undefined and `rootStartBlockFor` returns `undefined` (no gate) for every target.
- Contrast `model.ts:149` (current main): the explicit-model path passes `session.id` and `session.parentID` through `resolveModel`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Default-model resolution carries the session context (session id + parent id) into the resolver — e.g. the default model is selected first and resolved through the context-aware path — so the root-start gate judges new root sessions on the default route, AND
- a regression test shows a new root session whose default route target sits at a 90% snapshot is gated (blocked / placed elsewhere), with subsession behavior unchanged; OR the finding is resolved by a documented decision recorded on this issue.

title: fix(function): /feishu webhook has no request verification and relays message text to the Discord support channel

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

labels.description: Filed by pm-dispatch

body:
## Finding

The `/feishu` webhook in the function worker has no request verification. It logs the full inbound body, then relays any message text to the Discord support channel using the bot token. Anyone who can reach the URL can post to that channel.

## Evidence (verified in tree)

- `packages/function/src/api.ts:215-248` (`.post("/feishu")`): the handler parses the body as `{ challenge?, event?: { message?: {...} } }`. It has no verification-token check, no signature check, and no encryption-key handling. The only gate is `if (challenge) return c.json({ challenge })`, which echoes any value.
- `packages/function/src/api.ts:230`: `console.log(JSON.stringify(body, null, 2))` writes the full inbound payload, including the user's message and chat/thread IDs, to the worker log on every request.
- `packages/function/src/api.ts:243-246`: an accepted message is forwarded with `postDiscordSupportMessage({ channelId: Resource.DISCORD_SUPPORT_CHANNEL_ID.value, token: Resource.DISCORD_SUPPORT_BOT_TOKEN.value, ... })`, so the bot token is used on attacker-supplied content.
- `packages/function/src/api.ts:226-227`: `JSON.parse(content)` runs on a field the caller controls, with no try/catch. A malformed `content` throws and returns a 500 from the handler, not a clean 4xx.
- The only other Feishu reference is `packages/console/app/src/routes/feishu.ts`, which is a `redirect` to a Feishu chat link. It handles no webhook and does not gate `/feishu`.
- Repo search found no Feishu verification-token or signature helper in `packages/function/src`.

Caveat: I could not see the deployed worker config or whether Feishu's app-level verification is set up outside the repo. If a verification step exists in the Feishu console or a gateway in front of this worker, the finding narrows to the logging and the missing checks inside the worker. Please confirm before triage.

## Why it matters

A public endpoint that forwards arbitrary text into a support channel can be used for spam or impersonation of the bot. It also logs user message content at every request, which is a privacy and log-retention concern. A malformed body surfaces as a 500 rather than a rejection.

## Suggested fix shape

- Verify Feishu requests before any side effect: check the verification token (or the signature when encryption is enabled) against a configured secret, and reject mismatches with 401.
- Drop the unconditional `console.log` of the full body, or log only the event type and message ID.
- Wrap the inner `JSON.parse` so a malformed `content` returns a 400.
- Add a `packages/function` test for the reject and accept paths.

title: fix(function): share sync accepts unauthenticated writes once a share's secret is unset (after share_delete or before share_create)

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: app/function
labels.description: Package: function (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: source/dispatch
labels.description: Filed by pm-dispatch

body:
## Finding

`/share_sync` can publish content into a share whose secret is unset. This happens when the share was never created or was deleted, and the request omits `secret`. The unset stored secret and the omitted request secret are both `undefined`, so `assertSecret` passes.

## Evidence (verified in tree)

- `packages/function/src/api.ts:88-89`: `assertSecret(secret)` runs `if (secret !== (await this.getSecret())) throw`. There is no check that a secret exists. When the stored value is `undefined` and the request omits `secret`, `undefined !== undefined` is false, so the call passes.
- `packages/function/src/api.ts:152-165`: `/share_sync` reads `c.req.json<{ sessionID; secret; key; content }>()` with no runtime validation. A missing `secret` reaches `assertSecret` as `undefined`.
- `packages/function/src/api.ts:73-76`: `share()` is the only writer of `secret`. It returns early if a secret exists.
- `packages/function/src/api.ts:101-110`: `clear()` calls `this.ctx.storage.deleteAll()`, which removes `secret` and `sessionID`. So `/share_delete` (`:132-141`) leaves the shard in exactly the state the bypass needs.
- `packages/function/src/api.ts:48-54`: `publish()` checks `key` against `session/info/${sessionID}` etc. When `sessionID` is undefined, the accepted prefix is `session/info/undefined`, so the attacker can supply that literal. Keys are then written with `storage.put` (`:62`) and `Bucket.put` (`:57`).
- `packages/function/src/api.ts:78-86` and `/share_data` (`:166-190`): `getData()` returns every `session/*` entry, and `/share_data` builds the public `info` and `messages` from them. The `/s/<shortName>` share page reads this path.
- The DO is addressed only by `SyncServer.shortName(sessionID)`, the last 8 characters of the session ID (`:113-115`). Anyone who knows that short name can address the DO.

Tests: `packages/function/test` covers only `discord.test.ts` and `github.test.ts`. No test exercises `share_sync`, `share_delete`, or `assertSecret`.

Related but smaller: `assertSecret` and `/share_delete_admin` compare secrets with `!==`, which is not constant-time. Lower impact than the bypass.

## Why it matters

After an owner un-shares a session, or for a session that was never shared, an unauthenticated caller can write arbitrary `info` and `message` content that appears on the public share URL. That is content injection on a page users trust as their own session's share. It needs no credentials.

## Suggested fix shape

- In `assertSecret`, reject when the stored secret is missing, not only when it differs. Require `secret` to be a non-empty string at the boundary (`/share_sync`, `/share_delete`) and reject before any storage read.
- Compare secrets in constant time, for example with `crypto.subtle` or a fixed-length digest compare.
- Add a `packages/function` test that drives `/share_sync` against an un-shared and a deleted share, with and without `secret`, and asserts a 4xx with nothing stored.

body:
## Finding

PR #2551 bumped `nitro` past the Dependabot advisory range only in `packages/console/app`. The same advisory-affected version is still pinned by a second workspace app on current main.

## Evidence

- Issue #2548 (closed by PR #2551): Dependabot `security_update_not_possible` for nitro — advisory covers versions **< 3.0.260429-beta**, patched-versions empty; PR #2551 (merged, merge commit `28669eee40042ed722ec1b2c4f1fa02f4f7e5d53`, ancestor-verified against main `115283d60f9d78cbe6a3a4bdc4a790ac0e1eedb8`) bumped `packages/console/app` from `3.0.1-alpha.1` to `3.0.260429-beta` and regenerated `bun.lock`.
- On current main, `packages/stats/app/package.json` still declares `"nitro": "3.0.1-alpha.1"` (verified via contents API at main `115283d60f9d78cbe6a3a4bdc4a790ac0e1eedb8`), and the regenerated `bun.lock` in PR #2551's own diff retains the entry `"@opencode/stats-app/nitro": ["nitro@3.0.1-alpha.1", …]` — i.e. the fix's lockfile proves the second pin survived it.
- `3.0.1-alpha.1 < 3.0.260429-beta`, so the stats app remains inside the advisory range the console-app bump was filed to escape.

## Why it matters

A security-advisory fix that covers one of two identical pins leaves the exposure (and a future Dependabot `security_update_not_possible` failure for the stats directory) in place. This is the directly-related dependency update PR #2551 left undone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/stats/app/package.json` pins nitro at or past `3.0.260429-beta` (or an explicit, justified Dependabot ignore is recorded for this directory instead), with `bun.lock` regenerated so no workspace app resolves nitro < 3.0.260429-beta.
- [ ] `bun install` + the stats app's typecheck/test pass in the worktree used for the bump (same verification shape as PR #2551: install clean, package typecheck pass, package tests pass).
- [ ] A repo-wide grep of workspace `package.json` files shows no remaining `3.0.1-alpha.1` nitro pin.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #2551 (batch #2531–#2552, 2026-11-16). Dedupe: `gh search issues` for "nitro" returns only closed #2548 (console/app scope); "nitro stats" returns nothing.
