body:
## Finding

In `.github/workflows/nix-hashes.yml` on current main (`115283d60f9d78cbe6a3a4bdc4a790ac0e1eedb8`), the `compute-hash-darwin-fallback` job can never upload the hash it computes: its **Upload hash** step is still gated on the pre-split decide output that no longer exists in that job.

```yaml
# compute-hash-darwin-fallback job, line 216 on main:
      - name: Upload hash
        if: steps.decide.outputs.present == 'false'
```

## Evidence

- PR #2552 (merged, merge commit `160df11ac9acb68bcaa9bdcc1a8bfe176f15dbfc`, ancestor-verified against main via compare `behind_by: 0`) split the old fallback job in two: the decide step moved into the new `fallback-decide` job (ubuntu-24.04), where its step id is `decide` and its output was renamed `present` → `needed` (job output `needs.fallback-decide.outputs.needed`, lines 129–165 on main).
- The `compute-hash-darwin-fallback` job itself (lines 161ff) contains only Checkout, Setup Nix, Compute, and Upload steps — there is no step with id `decide` in that job, so `steps.decide.outputs.present` evaluates to an empty string, `'' == 'false'` is false, and the Upload step is always skipped.
- Consequence chain: fallback computes the `aarch64-darwin` hash → never uploads artifact `hash-aarch64-darwin` → `update-hashes` downloads `hash-*` artifacts, finds `hashes/hash-aarch64-darwin/hash.txt` missing, and exits 1 with "Missing hash for aarch64-darwin; refusing to commit a partial restamp" (the #2540 fail-closed guard). The recovery path #2552 was built to fix is still broken — it just fails later, after burning a macos-15 compute.
- Why it has not fired yet: the only post-#2552 nix-hashes run at filing time, run 43933347759 on the #2552 merge head, was all-green (fallback not needed, conclusion success). The bug only manifests on exactly the platform-cancelled-darwin-leg runs the fallback exists for (cf. runs 43895684693, 43920489996, 43924963639).

## Why it matters

The darwin-leg platform-cancellation failure mode has failed four main runs in this chain (#2539, #2544, #2547, and the #2549 follow-up). #2552's artifact-keyed decide is the right design, but with the upload gate dead, the next cancelled darwin leg will again leave `nix/hashes.json` unrestamped and the run red — after a wasted macOS compute.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The fallback job's Upload hash step no longer references `steps.decide.outputs.present` (the step runs unconditionally within the fallback job, or gates on a value that exists in that job); the uploaded artifact name stays `hash-aarch64-darwin`.
- [ ] A workflow-level check (YAML parse + a gate/step audit of `nix-hashes.yml`, or a simulated missing-primary-hash run) demonstrates: primary darwin artifact absent → fallback-decide sets `needed=true` → fallback computes → upload step executes → `update-hashes` finds all three platform hashes.
- [ ] The all-green path is unchanged: fallback-decide sets `needed=false`, no macos-15 runner is allocated, `update-hashes` proceeds on compute-hash success.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #2552 (batch #2531–#2552, 2026-11-16). Dedupe: `gh search issues` for "nix-hashes fallback upload decide" and "steps.decide" returned no existing issue; open nix-hashes issues are unrelated (#1876, #1825, #374).

title: fix(server): permission.saved.remove returns 204 for an unknown saved-permission ID — a remove against a stale or typoed ID looks like success

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/server
labels.description: Package: server (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Finding

`permission.saved.remove` (`DELETE /api/permission/saved/:id`) answers `204 No Content` for a saved-permission ID that does not exist. The core service has no not-found path at all: `PermissionSaved.remove` is a bare `DELETE ... WHERE id = ?` that succeeds on zero affected rows. A client that removes a stale, already-removed, or typoed saved-permission ID gets the same success response as a real removal.

### Evidence (on `origin/main` `160df11ac9`, verified in a read-only checkout)

**Core service** — `packages/core/src/permission/saved.ts:80-82` (interface `remove: (id) => Effect.Effect<void>` at :32):

```ts
const remove = Effect.fn("PermissionSaved.remove")(function* (id: ID) {
  yield* db.delete(PermissionTable).where(eq(PermissionTable.id, id)).run().pipe(Effect.orDie)
})
```

No row-count check and no error type, so the handler has nothing to map.

**Server handler** — `packages/server/src/handlers/permission.ts:99-104` (`saved.remove` at :102, `NoContent` at :103):

```ts
yield* saved.remove(ctx.params.id)
return HttpApiSchema.NoContent.make()
```

**Protocol** — `packages/protocol/src/groups/permission.ts:49-58` declares only `success: HttpApiSchema.NoContent`, with no `error:` entry.

**Same-class siblings already in the handler layer do the opposite.** Removes of a missing resource return 404 in these routes:

- `pty.remove` — `packages/server/src/handlers/pty.ts:106-115` maps `Pty.NotFoundError` to `PtyNotFoundError`; `packages/protocol/src/groups/pty.ts:87-91` declares `error: PtyNotFoundError`.
- `mcp.remove` / `mcp.connect` / `mcp.disconnect` — `packages/server/src/handlers/mcp.ts:8-9` (`notFound` helper) wraps each; `packages/protocol/src/groups/mcp.ts:42-47` declares `error: McpServerNotFoundError`.

This is a distinct endpoint and resource from the open same-class issues #2527 (credential), #2542 (shell.remove), #2543 (integration cancel), and #2553 (session inbox cancel). None of them covers the saved-permission route. No open or closed issue and no open PR mentions `permission.saved` / `PermissionSaved` (checked with `gh search` and `gh pr list`).

### Why it matters

- A client revoking a saved "always allow" grant cannot tell "removed" from "never existed or already gone". A typoed or stale ID reports success, which hides the client bug.
- It breaks the convention the server already follows for `pty.remove` and `mcp.remove`: a missing resource is a 404 on delete.
- The fix is small but crosses three layers (core error type, handler mapping, protocol `error:`), so it is easy to leave half-done unless tracked.

### Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- [ ] Core `PermissionSaved.remove` fails with a tagged `NotFoundError` when no row is deleted (check the affected-row count), instead of succeeding silently.
- [ ] Handler `permission.saved.remove` maps that error to a 404 `PermissionSavedNotFoundError` (or an existing not-found error type), mirroring `pty.remove` at `pty.ts:106-115`.
- [ ] Protocol `permission.saved.remove` declares the matching `error:` (mirroring `pty.remove` at `groups/pty.ts:87-91`).
- [ ] A test pins it: remove of an unknown saved-permission ID returns the not-found error, and remove of an existing ID still returns 204.
- [ ] `bun run generate` / the OpenAPI snapshot is updated in the same change (the route now declares an error response).

title: Auth-failure benches plant with until == plant time (zero-length), so entitlement-dead legs are re-dealt forever
body:
Found 2026-11-16 during the Claude re-admission repair (see #2554 for the sibling defect).

Evidence (route_attempt + route_note replay, laptop server DB, 2026-11-16 ~21:30Z): in 45 minutes, 99 `_commandcode` attempts: 97 failed Authentication/403, 1 QuotaExceeded, 1 Transport. The auth errors are entitlement deaths, not quota: `MODEL_NOT_IN_PLAN: GPT-6.1 Sol available in Max and above plans` and `The free Beam 1.0 tier has ended` (route workhorse; legs gpt-6.1-sol#medium and reflection/beam:free).

Why it loops: each auth failure plants a `cooldown-start` with reason `auth variant:…` whose `until` EQUALS its own plant time — a zero-length bench. The leg is eligible again instantly, workhorse deals it again, it fails auth again: 510 such cooldown-starts in 3 hours, plus 4 bench-probes. A death becomes a burn loop.

Expected: an auth/entitlement failure should bench the leg for a real duration (or mark it dead until a credential/plan change), never zero-length. At minimum, cooldown computation for the auth class must floor above zero and escalate on repeats, the way headerless-429 escalation already does for the rate-limit class.

Note: the gathered monthly wall on _commandcode (99.5%) is a separate verdict on other legs; these two legs are dead on plan entitlement regardless of quota.

title: Router never re-admits a provider after a provider-scoped attempt-reported quota skip when the gathered entry has no per-model reading keyed by model id (_claude idle ~2 days with a fresh 2% reading)
body:
## Symptom (live, 2026-11-16)

The anthropic pool (`_claude`) has received **zero pool-routed attempts since 2026-11-14 08:50Z**, despite the fleet gatherer reading it fresh and open (5h 1% / 7d 2% / Fable 0% at 21:15Z, credential renewed in-process at 20:08:27Z after the 19:15Z lapse, `claude -p` works). Every pool decision that includes a `_claude` leg excludes it with reason `quota-skip` (1,863 exclusions in one 30-min window). A server restart does not help. Claude is currently the fleet's only ample pool, so this idles real capacity.

## Standing record

Replaying `route_note` ops, the standing adjustment is:

- `quota:_claude` — provider-scoped, origin `attempt` (attempt-reported, corroborated), planted **2026-11-14T08:50:05Z** during that morning's genuine 429 cluster, `until` **2026-11-18T18:59:59Z** (the 7d reset the errors quoted). Never removed.
- `quota-model:_claude:claude-fable-5-2` — proactive, planted 2026-11-16T10:05:17Z when 7d was genuinely 100%, until 2026-11-18T19:00:00Z. Also still standing.

Drew reset the Anthropic window on 2026-11-16 (~14:04Z). The proactive gathered-gate path re-admitted on the fresh reading — it removed `quota-model:_claude:claude-haiku-5-5` at 14:01:31Z (`route_health` quota-readmitted rows) — but the attempt-origin provider record is outside that path's scope, and it kept every `_claude` leg skipped.

## Why the designed re-admission (#1974) cannot fire

`releaseQuotaSkipsForCurrent` (packages/core/src/model-route.ts, called from model-resolver.ts:587 on every resolution) begins:

1. `own = modelWindowReading(entries, providerID, target.id)`; `if (!own) return []`.
2. Only later does it reach the provider-standing branch that lifts a provider-wide skip on provider-wide headroom.

`modelWindowReading` finds a model's reading only via a models entry keyed by the **full model id** or windows named `<model-id>:<window>`. The gatherer's `_claude` entry in `quota-current.json` carries neither for any Claude model: its windows are named `5h` / `7d` / `Fable:7d` and its `usage.models` is keyed by the family nickname `Fable` only. So `own` is undefined for every `_claude` target, the function returns [] before the provider-wide branch, and **a provider-scoped attempt-reported skip on a provider whose gathered entry has this shape can never be lifted by readings — only by its `until`**, which defeats #1974's doctrine ("the reading governs, not the error").

The 30-day `QUOTA_GATE_MAX_MS` plant-time floor is not the blocker here (until − 30d is in October; fresh readings pass it). The blocker is purely the early return on a missing model-scoped reading.

## Suggested fix

In `releaseQuotaSkipsForCurrent`, when a provider-wide attempt-reported skip stands, evaluate provider-wide headroom (the existing `wide` computation) even when the target's own model reading is absent — the provider record's premise is provider-wide, so provider-wide evidence should be sufficient to judge it. Keep the model-record release gated on the model's own complete reading as today. Add a test with a gathered entry in the `_claude` shape (provider windows only + nickname-keyed models) proving the provider skip lifts on a fresh below-full reading.

## Operational workaround applied (2026-11-16 ~21:2xZ)

Operator remove records written to `route_note` in the server's own format (`{op:"remove", id}`) for `quota:_claude` and `quota-model:_claude:claude-fable-5-2`, then a server restart so restore replays them. No provider-stated Retry-After bench was touched (the lapse-window 429s were the OAuth token endpoint's, consumed by the renewal loop; `route_health` holds no `_claude` cooldown rows from the lapse).

title: fix(server): session inbox cancel swallows InboxConflictError — a cancel against an unknown or already-settled inboxID returns 204

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

body:
## Evidence
- Handler: `packages/server/src/handlers/session.ts:643-652` (`session.inbox.cancel`) catches `Session.InboxConflictError` with `() => Effect.void` and returns `HttpApiSchema.NoContent` unconditionally.
- Same-file sibling: `session.inbox.update` (`:653-663`, steer/queue on the same resource) routes through `pendingMutation` (`:89-97`), which maps the identical `Session.InboxConflictError` to a 409 `ConflictError`. Same core error, same resource, opposite HTTP answers.
- Core: `packages/core/src/session/inbox.ts:342-359` (`projectCancelled`) deletes the pending row `where (id, session_id, delivery in queue/steer)`; an unknown `inboxID`, an already-delivered/cancelled item, or an item owned by another session all yield `!deleted` → `LifecycleConflict`, which `mutatePending` (`packages/core/src/session/session.ts:167-182`) surfaces as `InboxConflictError` (after a `get(sessionID)` that only 404s the session, never the inbox item).
- The error contract is pinned at the core layer, not accidental: double-cancel → `InboxConflictError` (`packages/core/test/session-prompt.test.ts:1302-1303`), cross-session cancel → `InboxConflictError` (`packages/core/test/session-owned.test.ts:612-613`). No server test covers `session.inbox.cancel` (only inbox list/diff usages exist under `packages/server/test`), so the swallow is unpinned handler behavior.

## Why this is a defect
A cancel against a stale or typoed `inboxID` — or an inbox item belonging to another session — returns 204 and looks like a successful abort. The client cannot distinguish "pending input cancelled" from "nothing existed", and a wrong-session routing bug is masked. It is also inconsistent within the same resource: steer/queue 409 the same condition that cancel 204s. Same defect family as #2543 (integration cancel), #2542 (shell.remove), #2527 (credential) — those are scoped to other endpoints, so this is not a duplicate.

## Acceptance criteria / suggested fix
- `session.inbox.cancel` returns a non-2xx for a cancel that matched no pending inbox row: either map `InboxConflictError` to 409 `ConflictError` via the existing `pendingMutation` helper (one-line alignment with steer/queue), or add an existence check that answers 404 for an unknown `inboxID` while keeping the already-settled case at 409/204 per whatever cancel-idempotency the fleet decides (cf. #2543's idempotency note).
- Keep 204 for a cancel that actually removed a pending row.
- Add a handler-level test pinning the miss case (unknown inboxID → non-2xx), since none exists today.

title: fix(server): shell.remove returns 204 for a missing shell command — a remove against a stale or typoed ID looks like success

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/server
labels.description: Package: server (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Finding

`shell.remove` answers `204 No Content` for a shell ID that does not exist. The handler swallows the core service's `Shell.NotFoundError` and still returns success, so a client that removes a stale, already-reaped, or typoed command ID believes the removal happened.

### Evidence (on `origin/main` `d900497f15`)

**Server handler** — `packages/server/src/handlers/shell.ts:64-68` unconditionally returns 204:

```ts
"shell.remove",
Effect.fn(function* (ctx) {
  const shell = yield* Shell.Service
  yield* shell.remove(ctx.params.id).pipe(Effect.catchTag("Shell.NotFoundError", () => Effect.void))
  return HttpApiSchema.NoContent.make()
}),
```

**Core service** — `packages/core/src/shell.ts:209-211` fails `Shell.NotFoundError` for an unknown ID (via `require` at :190-194):

```ts
const remove = Effect.fn("Shell.remove")(function* (id: Shell.ID) {
  yield* require(id)
  yield* removeCommand(id)
})
```

**Same-file inconsistency** — the identical error is mapped to a 404 `ShellNotFoundError` by the sibling endpoints in the same handler file (`shell.get` :37-40, `shell.output` :54-57), and the protocol declares `error: ShellNotFoundError` for get (:44) and output (:60) but only `204` success for delete (`packages/protocol/src/groups/shell.ts:72-75`). So `GET /api/shell/:id` correctly 404s while `DELETE /api/shell/:id` for the same ID reports success.

Same defect class as #2527 (credential update/activate/remove 204-for-missing), different endpoint — that issue is credential-scoped and does not cover this path.

### Why it matters

- A client polling `remove` until a command disappears (or cleaning up after a reconnect) cannot distinguish "removed" from "never existed / already reaped" — silent success masks client bugs and stale-ID races.
- The sibling read endpoints already made the opposite contract choice (404), so clients reasonably expect 404 here too.

### Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- [ ] `shell.remove` maps `Shell.NotFoundError` to the protocol `ShellNotFoundError` (404), mirroring `shell.get`/`shell.output` in the same file.
- [ ] Protocol `shell.remove` endpoint declares `error: ShellNotFoundError`.
- [ ] A test pins it: remove of an unknown ID fails with `ShellNotFoundError` instead of 204 (same shape as the #2527 follow-up tests, if any).

title: fix(app): an aborted-while-queued request pins its slot and hangs the caller promise until an unrelated release

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/app
labels.description: Package: app (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`createRequestQueue` parks a request with no free slot in `waiting` with no abort listener, so aborting a queued request does not settle it: the entry stays in the queue and the caller's promise stays pending until some *other* request completes and `release()` happens to pop it.

## Evidence (origin/main `e7d5bb7354`)

- `packages/app/src/runtime/server/request-queue.ts:107-116` — `acquire()` pushes `{ entry, start }` into `waiting` and returns a promise that resolves only inside `start()`, which runs only when `release()` pops it. No `signal.addEventListener` exists on this path (the only abort wiring is line 137, attached after the request is sent).
- Probe against this checkout (`bun`, `limit: 1`): after `controller.abort()` on the queued second request, `queued()` is still `1` and the second promise is still pending; it rejects with `AbortError` only after the head request resolves and `release()` pops the dead entry. The dead request is never dispatched (`pending` shows only the head URL before and after).
- The existing test pins the leaky behavior: `packages/app/src/runtime/server/request-queue.test.ts:114-129` ("aborted requests leave the queue without being sent") resolves the head request *first* and only then expects the aborted promise to reject — i.e. the test encodes drain-on-release instead of settle-on-abort.
- While the dead entry sits in `waiting`, `queued()` counts it and the stall `watch()` (lines 63-79) keeps rescheduling every `stallMs` and can log a misleading "server thrashing detected" line for a request nobody is waiting on anymore.

## Why it matters

Abort sources on this path are real, not theoretical: palette/search cleanups (`packages/app/src/shell/commands/search.ts:14`, `palette.ts:240`), upload cancels (`composer/attachments/uploads.tsx:28`), websearch cancels (`session/requests/websearch.ts:52,67`). A cancelled navigation that queued behind a slow VCS/worktree request (which hold slots for seconds on large repos, lines 8-10) leaves a dangling caller promise plus a phantom queue entry until unrelated traffic drains it.

## Acceptance criteria / suggested fix

- In `acquire()`, attach a one-shot abort listener that removes the entry from `waiting` and rejects immediately (mirroring the already-aborted pre-check at lines 131-134).
- Update the "aborted requests leave the queue without being sent" test to assert the aborted promise settles *without* resolving the head request, and `queued()` drops back to 0.
- No change to the free-slot fast path or the sent-request abort forwarding (line 137).

title: fix(server): credential update/activate/remove return 204 for a missing credential — a failed revoke or activate looks like success

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: app/server
labels.description: Package: server (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Finding

`credential.update`, `credential.activate` and `credential.remove` answer `204 No Content` for a credential ID that does not exist. The handler returns success before the core service performs any existence check; the core service silently no-ops and the handler still returns 204.

### Evidence (on `origin/main` `e7d5bb7354053ca7aa09d6f370aee40d7f127503`)

**Server handler** — `packages/server/src/handlers/credential.ts:31-52`  
All three endpoints unconditionally return `HttpApiSchema.NoContent.make()` after the `yield* credential.*` call:

```ts
.handle(
  "credential.update",
  Effect.fn(function* (ctx) {
    const credential = yield* Credential.Service
    yield* credential.update(ctx.params.credentialID, { label: ctx.payload.label })
    return HttpApiSchema.NoContent.make()      // ← always 204
  }),
)
.handle(
  "credential.activate",
  Effect.fn(function* (ctx) {
    const credential = yield* Credential.Service
    yield* credential.activate(ctx.params.credentialID)
    return HttpApiSchema.NoContent.make()      // ← always 204
  }),
)
.handle(
  "credential.remove",
  Effect.fn(function* (ctx) {
    const credential = yield* Credential.Service
    yield* credential.remove(ctx.params.credentialID)
    return HttpApiSchema.NoContent.make()      // ← always 204
  }),
)
```

**Core service** — `packages/core/src/credential.ts`

- `update` (:235-238): looks up the row; if `!credential?.integrationID` logs `"credential_missing"` and returns.
- `activate` (transaction body, :180-183): `if (!credential?.integration_id) return` inside the transaction, then the outer function receives `undefined` and returns early at `:214 if (!removed) return`.
- `remove` (:273-276): `if (!credential) return` inside the transaction, then outer `:308 if (!removed) return`.

In every case the handler has already committed to `204 No Content` before the silent return.

**Protocol contract** — `packages/protocol/src/groups/credential.ts:33-71`  
Only `credential.create` declares an error (`ConflictError` 409). The other three declare `success: HttpApiSchema.NoContent` with no error alternative.

**Sibling surface for comparison** — `packages/server/src/handlers/project.ts` + `packages/protocol/src/errors.ts`  
`project.update` maps a missing row to `ProjectNotFoundError` (404). The error class exists in the protocol.

### Impact

- `DELETE /api/credential/<id>` (revoke) against an already-removed ID, a typoed ID, or an ID from a previous machine/database returns `204`. The operator or automation believes the credential was revoked; it was not.
- `POST /api/credential/<id>/activate` against a missing ID returns `204`. No credential is activated; the caller thinks one is.
- `PATCH /api/credential/<id>` against a missing ID returns `204`. The label update is a no-op; the caller thinks it succeeded.

Credentials hold secrets. Believing a revoke/activate succeeded when it did not is a security-relevant correctness failure.

### Related work

Open PR **#2498** (`feat(core): session-cookie credential kind…`) touches `credential.ts` and the protocol group but does not address the missing-ID 204 behavior. This issue should be cross-linked with that PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- `credential.update` of a missing ID returns a typed 404 error (e.g. `CredentialNotFoundError` or `NotFoundError` with `resource: "credential"`), not 204.
- `credential.activate` of a missing ID returns the same typed 404 error.
- `credential.remove` of a missing ID either:
  - returns the same typed 404 error, **or**
  - is deliberately documented as idempotent-204 with a protocol description update and a code comment; in that case update/activate must still error.
- Protocol error schema in `packages/protocol/src/groups/credential.ts` is updated to include the new error for update/activate/remove.
- Tests cover: nonexistent ID → declared status for all three endpoints; no `bus.publish(Event.Updated)` or `Event.Switched` is emitted on the miss.
- Existing credential tests stay green.

title: fix(core): accepting a stale plan suggestion checks the wrong step — positional applyCheck vs a "content-stable" suggestion id

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Finding

Two pieces of the suggest-first contract disagree about how a suggestion identifies its step:

1. `packages/core/src/execution-plan.ts:36-38` documents `Suggestion.id` as "Stable id for a step's content: dismiss/accept bookkeeping keys on it", but `suggestionID` (`:142-143`) hashes `step.index` together with the text, so the id changes whenever a step is inserted or removed above it.
2. The accept path is positional: `applyCheck` (`:203-204`) forwards `stepIndex` to `flip` (`:196-208`), which walks checklist lines and flips the nth match. Neither `line` nor `text` is re-checked, and `acceptSuggestion` (`packages/core/src/session/plan-suggestions.ts:78-81`) forwards the same `stepIndex`.

Nothing in the flow re-validates that the plan still looks the way it did when the suggestion was computed.

## Reproduction (on `origin/main` `e7d5bb7354053ca7aa09d6f370aee40d7f127503`)

```ts
import { ExecutionPlan } from "../packages/core/src/execution-plan.ts"
const plan = [
  "# Execution plan",
  "",
  "- [ ] 1. Scaffold API routes in `packages/web/server/routes.ts`",
  "- [ ] 2. Add session tests in packages/core/test/",
  "- [x] 3. Write the changelog entry",
  "- [ ] 4. Remove the legacy flag from `packages/core/src/flags.ts`",
].join("\n")
const [s] = ExecutionPlan.suggest(plan, { added: ["packages/web/server/routes.ts"], modified: [], deleted: [] })
const edited = plan.replace(
  "- [ ] 1. Scaffold API routes",
  "- [ ] 0. Verify the flaky integration test\n- [ ] 1. Scaffold API routes",
)
console.log(ExecutionPlan.applyCheck(edited, s))
```

Observed: the suggestion is `{"id":"plan-step-0-fa669f43","stepIndex":0,"line":2,"text":"1. Scaffold API routes in `packages/web/server/routes.ts`"}`. After prepending one step, `applyCheck` checks the prepended line:

```
- [x] 0. Verify the flaky integration test
- [ ] 1. Scaffold API routes in `packages/web/server/routes.ts`
```

The intended step stays unchecked; the control (unchanged plan) flips the right line. No error is returned either way.

## Why it matters

The suggestion is produced at the end of one turn (`packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts:1011`) and accepted later, possibly on a different turn — and the plan file is the artifact the agent edits while working. Any insertion, reordering, or deletion above the step silently retargets the accept onto a different checklist item, mutating the user's plan without a signal. This is engine and wiring merged this week (#2514, #2515/#2516) whose consumer is the OpenChamber Plans view, so the contract is being built against right now.

## Related observation (same module, separate fix — not in this issue's scope)

`parse` (`:94-108`) matches `- [ ]` lines inside fenced code blocks. A plan containing

````
```md
- [ ] <step text>
```
````

parses 3 steps with index 0 = `<step text>`, so the first real step's notice reads "Plan step 2" and a fenced example can itself be suggested and checked. Worth its own test/ticket; it is independent of the addressing fix below.

## Acceptance criteria

- Accepting a suggestion never flips a step other than the one the suggestion describes. Either resolve by a content-stable id and refuse (no write) when the plan no longer contains that step, or require that `suggestion.line` still carries the same step text before flipping; `applyUncheck` follows the same rule.
- `Suggestion.id` is content-stable as documented (drop `step.index` from the hash), or the doc comment is corrected and the id is renamed if positional identity is intended — the code and the contract must agree.
- Regression tests cover: (a) prepend a step between `suggest` and `applyCheck` → the intended step is checked or the call refuses, never the prepended one; (b) the same step text keeps the same id after an insertion above it; (c) the unchanged-plan accept still flips exactly one line (the existing test at `packages/core/test/execution-plan.test.ts:121`).
- Existing `execution-plan.test.ts` and `plan-suggestions.test.ts` stay green.

title: fix(server): persistent PTY connect sockets are never registered for the graceful-shutdown drain (#2284/#2454 covered only /api/pty)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/server
labels.description: Package: server (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Finding

The persistent-PTY connect handler never registers its upgraded WebSocket with the graceful-shutdown registry, so the server drain cannot close, flush, or force-close it. The legacy PTY handler does; only that handler was updated by #2284 and hardened by #2454.

## Evidence (verified on `origin/main` `e7d5bb7354053ca7aa09d6f370aee40d7f127503`)

- `packages/server/src/handlers/persistent-pty.ts:15` imports only `makePtyOutbox, runPtySocket` from `./pty-socket` — no tracking helper.
- `persistentPty.connect` (`:109`) opens the socket at `:124`, builds the outbox, and goes straight to `yield* runPtySocket({...})` at `:178`. There is no `trackPtySocket`/`withPtySocketTracked` call anywhere in the file.
- The registry is module-private and only entered through those helpers (`packages/server/src/handlers/pty-socket.ts:99-109`), so no other module can register on this handler's behalf.
- The drain consults nothing else: `packages/server/src/process.ts:185` calls `closeTrackedPtySockets()`, `:186-190` waits only while `trackedPtySocketCount() > 0`, and `:191` calls `terminateTrackedPtySockets()` — all three iterate the registry (`pty-socket.ts:128-133`). `bound.server.close()` cannot substitute: `pty-socket.ts:88-90` documents that an upgraded WebSocket outlives its HTTP request.
- The sibling handler shows the intended shape: `packages/server/src/handlers/pty.ts:186-189` wraps the whole attach + run section in `withPtySocketTracked`, with `close: () => void outbox.offer(new Socket.CloseEvent(1001, "server shutting down"))` and `terminate: outbox.shutdown`.
- The persistent handler predates the fix (`git log` first add `004b647311`, 2026-08-25; #2284 fix `4b92e98d9a`, 2026-11-11), so this is an unscoped route rather than a regression of #2430/#2454.

## Why it matters

A graceful restart with an attached persistent terminal skips the entire PTY stage of the drain: the client never receives the deliberate `1001 "server shutting down"` close the legacy route sends, queued outbox frames are not flushed before the process exits, `detach` is not reached through a closed socket, and the "force-closing PTY sockets that did not drain" warning cannot fire. The client sees an abrupt drop and cannot distinguish a restart from a crash. It also means the shutdown behaviour of the two PTY surfaces differs, and the existing regression test cannot see the difference because it only connects through `/api/pty/:id/connect`.

Persistent PTYs are the newer terminal surface and are explicitly restart-aware (`persistentPty.handoff`), so the close/detach path is exactly the part that should be deliberate.

## Coverage today

`packages/server/test/process.test.ts:446` ("closes an open PTY websocket deliberately during shutdown…") waits for `trackedPtySocketCount() === 1` after connecting through `/api/pty/${id}/connect` (`:476`), drains, and asserts close code `1001` and the count back at `0`. No persistent-PTY test asserts the count at all (`grep -n "trackedPtySocketCount" packages/` finds only `pty.ts`, `pty-socket.ts`, `process.ts`, `process.test.ts`, `pty-socket.test.ts`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `persistentPty.connect` wraps its attach + `runPtySocket` section in `withPtySocketTracked` (the #2454 scoped form, not a bare `trackPtySocket` + later `ensuring`), with `close` offering `new Socket.CloseEvent(1001, "server shutting down")` and `terminate` shutting the outbox down.
- A regression test opens a persistent terminal socket (see `openTerminalSocket` in `packages/server/test/persistent-pty.test.ts`), asserts `trackedPtySocketCount() === 1`, runs `server.drain(...)`, and asserts the socket closed with code `1001`, the count is back to `0`, and the drain finished well inside the grace period.
- Existing `pty-socket.test.ts` and `process.test.ts` shutdown tests keep passing.

title: fix(server): session.messages cursor drops type filter — following a filtered cursor with a different type silently mixes sequences

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/server
labels.description: Package: server (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Finding

`GET /api/session/:sessionID/message` cursors are not self-contained: they encode only `{id, order, direction}` while the `type` filter lives only in the query string. Following a filtered cursor with a different (or omitted) `type` silently applies an old anchor to a new filtered sequence, causing gaps or duplicates. The OpenAPI text says "passing the same type when following cursors", but the server never enforces it and the cursor carries nothing to enforce it with.

Contrast `session.list`, whose cursor preserves every filter field except `limit` (`withCursor` spreads `directory/project/subpath/search/parentID/order` plus anchor).

## Evidence (origin/main `99d219d283e0`)

- `packages/protocol/src/groups/message.ts:8-40` — `SessionMessagesQuery` has `limit` (capped 1..200), `order`, `cursor` (opaque string), `type` (10 literals). Cursor documented as "Do not combine with order" only; nothing binds cursor to `type`.
- `packages/server/src/handlers/message.ts:11-26` — `Cursor` struct is `{id, order, direction}`; `encode` stores only those three; `decode` restores only those three.
- `packages/server/src/handlers/message.ts:35-49` — handler decodes cursor for `order`+anchor but takes `type: ctx.query.type` fresh from the new request. No comparison against the type used to mint the cursor.
- `packages/core/src/session/store.ts:177-209` — `messages()` looks up the anchor by `(session_id, id)` only (`:182-189`, no type check), builds a `seq` boundary (`:192-196`), then applies the *new* `type` filter (`:204`). An anchor of type A paging under type B filters "after A's seq, of type B" — neither page's sequence.

Repro sketch (no fix in this task): page 1 `?type=user&limit=2` → `next` cursor for last user message U; page 2 `?cursor=<that>&type=assistant` (or omitted) returns assistants after U's seq, skipping assistants before U and duplicating none deterministically — a mixed sequence the client never asked for.

`limit` has the same drift (cursor drops it; next page falls back to default 50), but `type` is the correctness gap; `session.list` already preserves its filters (`packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts:84-94`, `packages/server/src/handlers/session.ts:102-139` spread `...query` into the cursor).

## Suggested fix

Make message cursors self-contained: encode `type` (and `limit`/`order`) into the cursor like `session.list` does, prefer the cursor's values on follow-up, and reject a request that combines a cursor with a conflicting explicit `type`/`order` with `InvalidCursorError`/`InvalidRequestError`. Alternatively validate the anchor row's type against the requested filter before paging.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Following a `type=user` cursor with `type=assistant` (or omitted vs explicit) is either rejected or yields the original filtered sequence, never a mixed one.
- [ ] Cursor stays opaque to clients; existing `order`-mismatch rejection (`message.ts:35-36`) still holds.
- [ ] Focused test pins filtered pagination across two pages with unchanged and changed `type`.

## Related

- #2483 (session.list uncapped limit) and #2484 (fs.find uncapped limit) — same pagination family, different endpoint/defect; this one is filter-binding, not a ceiling.
- PR #2488 (bounds session.list/fs.find) does not touch message cursors.

No code, PR, or queue task in this report.

title: fix(desktop): a failed write-behind flush is never rescheduled — one SQLITE_BUSY/IO error leaves drafts and window state unpersisted until an unrelated write or a clean quit

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/desktop
labels.description: Package: desktop (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

`createWriteBehind` requeues a failed batch but never schedules another flush. After one transient write error it relies on some *unrelated* future `set()` or a graceful quit to retry, so a single `SQLITE_BUSY` / disk-full / I/O error can leave desktop state and draft documents unpersisted for the rest of the process lifetime — and permanently lost on a crash, `kill -9`, or a quit that retries once and still fails.

## Where

- `packages/desktop/src/main/storage/write-behind.ts:12-30` — `flush()` clears/stores `timer = undefined` first (`:13-14`), then on a throw requeues the batch (`:25`) and reports through `onError` (`:27-28`) without re-arming a timer. The only places a timer is armed are `set()` (`:39`) and `flush()` itself.
- `packages/desktop/src/main/storage/write-behind.ts:45-48` — `close()` flushes once, then sets `closed = true`, so a batch requeued by that final failed flush can never be written again.
- `packages/desktop/src/main/storage/index.ts:24-26` — both stores are constructed with an `onError` that only logs (`logError("storage flush failed")`), so the `if (!input.onError) throw` escape hatch is never taken in production and the failure is fully swallowed.
- `packages/desktop/src/main/storage/index.ts:61-78` — `close()` closes the SQLite handle immediately after the two stores' single close-flush.
- Callers relying on the retry promise: `state.ts:32-44` (window/settings state) and `drafts.ts:50-77,80-84` (composer drafts + blob reference refresh), delay 250 ms and 500 ms.
- Reads consult `pending` before SQLite (`write-behind.ts:33-35`, `state.ts:55-60,76-84`, `drafts.ts:80-84`), so the renderer keeps being served the unpersisted values and nothing looks wrong.

The comment at `:23-24` states the intent explicitly — "Keep them queued so the next flush retries them" — but nothing guarantees a next flush.

## Trigger

1. The renderer saves a draft / window state; `set()` arms the timer.
2. The delayed `write()` throws. Realistic causes: `SQLITE_BUSY` (the connection sets no `busy_timeout` — `storage/database.ts:10-12` sets only `journal_mode`/`synchronous`/`temp_store` — so a second app instance or a long checkpoint raises it immediately), `SQLITE_FULL`, `SQLITE_IOERR`.
3. `flush()` requeues the batch, logs, and returns with no timer armed.
4. No further `set()` happens (user idle; e.g. they stop typing after the failure).
5. The app crashes, is force-quit, or quits while the error persists.

## Observed

Probe against the real module (`bun`, in-memory `write` that throws once, `delay: 10`):

```
after failed flush + 120ms: {"writes":1,"errors":1,"has":true,"get":1}
after another 200ms:        {"writes":1,"has":true}
after an unrelated set():   {"writes":2,"keys":["draft","other"]}
after close():              {"writes":2}
```

320 ms with a 10 ms delay produced no retry — the value is only served from `pending` — and it took an unrelated key's `set()` to trigger the retry. In the failing-at-quit case `close()` gives up after that same single attempt and `database.close()` follows (`index.ts:74-78`).

## Why it matters

The write-behind is the durability layer for composer drafts and desktop UI state. Today a transient database error converts a bounded retry into either an accidental later retry (if the user happens to type again) or silent data loss on any non-graceful exit, while every reader continues to report the value as saved. No test covers the error path at all — `write-behind.test.ts` exercises coalescing, `flush`, and `close` only.

## Acceptance criteria

- A failed `flush()` re-arms the timer (bounded/exponential backoff is fine) whenever `pending` is non-empty, so a transient error self-heals without needing another `set()`.
- No unbounded retry storm: back off (or cap attempts) and keep reporting through `onError`.
- `close()` attempts the remaining `pending` writes at least once more (or documents/returns a failure indicator) rather than silently dropping them before `database.close()`.
- New test in `packages/desktop/src/main/storage/write-behind.test.ts`: `write` throws on the first call and succeeds afterwards → a later flush happens and the batch is persisted, and `close()` after a failed flush still persists if the write recovers.
- Keys written after the failed attempt still take precedence (the existing `if (!pending.has(key))` rule is preserved).

## Related

- Same failure class in this package: #99 (transient rename failures with no retry), #1005 (in-place save destroys the previous version), #924/#998/#1067 (atomic-write family). Those are all about the write itself; this one is about the retry scheduler after a write throws.
- Found while reviewing `packages/desktop/src/main/storage/` on `origin/main` `99d219d283e0808b5b06ab364465ccf3d5545e21`.

title: fix(desktop): extension archive install trusts declared zip entry sizes — a 65 KB archive decompresses 64 MiB (1.07 GiB peak) before any cap applies

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

labels.name: status/done
labels.description: Work completed and verified

body:
## Problem

`readArchive` validates an extension archive using the **sizes the zip declares in its central directory**. Nothing verifies those sizes against the bytes actually produced, and the only actual-bytes check runs *after* every entry has been decompressed concurrently. A small archive that under-declares an entry's size is therefore decompressed in full first: a 65,583-byte `.ocdx` is accepted with a 67,109,888-byte `main.js` and a peak RSS of ~1.07 GiB, and a 125,617-byte archive decompresses 120 MiB before the `archiveLimit` rejection fires.

So the stated caps (`archiveLimit` 100 MiB, `entryLimit` 4,096, manifest 65 KiB) do not bound the work or memory the archive causes — they bound the numbers the archive claims.

## Evidence (origin/main `192f3fce43`)

- `packages/desktop/src/main/extension/archive.ts:30-33` — `entries.length > entryLimit` and `entries.reduce((total, entry) => total + entry.uncompressedSize, 0) > archiveLimit` both read the central directory's declared `uncompressedSize`.
- `archive.ts:42` — the manifest cap is `metadata.uncompressedSize > 65_536`, also declared, checked *before* `getData()` decompresses it.
- `archive.ts:52-63` — `Promise.all(entries.filter(...).map(... entry.getData(new Uint8ArrayWriter())))` decompresses every non-directory entry **at once**; the actual-bytes `tooLarge` check is line 62, after all of it has been materialised.
- `@zip.js/zip.js` `Uint8ArrayWriter` (`node_modules/@zip.js/zip.js/lib/core/io.js:527-551`) has no maximum: `init(initSize)` allocates the declared size and `writeUint8Array` grows by `previousArray.length + array.length`, so an under-declared entry (a) is not stopped at its declared size and (b) grows with repeated copy-out. `zip-reader.js:472` passes `uncompressedSize` only as that initial size; there is no post-inflate equality check.
- When the declared size is smaller than the payload, `getData()` also returns the writer's slack, so the output is not even exactly the payload: the accepted `main.js` above came back as 67,109,888 bytes for a 67,108,879-byte payload.
- No test covers `readArchive`: `packages/desktop/src/main/extension/` has `manager.test.ts`, `lifecycle.test.ts`, `storage.test.ts`, `assets.test.ts`, no `archive.test.ts`; the only archive test asserts `downloadArchive`'s `tooLarge` (`manager.test.ts:124-132`).

## Reproduction

```bash
cd packages/desktop
python3 - <<'PY'
import io, json, struct, zipfile
payload = b'const x = "' + b"a" * (64 << 20) + b'"\n//'
manifest = json.dumps({"schema": "opencode.gui-extension/1", "id": "bomb.test", "name": "Bomb",
    "version": "1.0.0", "renderer": "main.js", "main": "main.js",
    "imports": {"renderer": [], "main": []}}).encode()
buf = io.BytesIO()
with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
    z.writestr("manifest.json", manifest)
    z.writestr("main.js", payload)
data = bytearray(buf.getvalue())
i = 0
while (i := data.find(b"PK\x01\x02", i)) >= 0:          # central directory
    n = struct.unpack_from("<H", data, i + 28)[0]
    if data[i + 46 : i + 46 + n] == b"main.js":
        struct.pack_into("<I", data, i + 24, 1024)     # declare 1 KiB
    i += 4
i = 0
while (i := data.find(b"PK\x03\x04", i)) >= 0:          # local header
    n = struct.unpack_from("<H", data, i + 26)[0]
    if data[i + 30 : i + 30 + n] == b"main.js":
        struct.pack_into("<I", data, i + 22, 1024)
    i += 4
open("/tmp/bomb.ocdx", "wb").write(data)
print("archive bytes", len(data), "payload bytes", len(payload))
PY
/usr/bin/time -v bun -e 'import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { readArchive } from "./src/main/extension/archive.ts"
const t0 = performance.now()
try {
  const a = await readArchive(new Uint8Array(readFileSync("/tmp/bomb.ocdx")))
  console.log("accepted", a.files.map((f) => [f.path, f.data.byteLength]))
} catch (e) { console.log("rejected", e.code, e.message) }
console.log("ms", Math.round(performance.now() - t0), "rssMB", Math.round(process.memoryUsage().rss / 1048576))'
```

Measured on `192f3fce43`:

| archive | declared | decompressed | result | peak RSS | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 65,583 B (1 entry) | `main.js` 1,024 B (sum 1,169 B) | 67,109,888 B | **accepted**, install proceeds | 1,120,404 kB | 5.7 s |
| 125,617 B (24 entries) | 1,024 B each (sum 23,551 B) | 120 MiB total | `tooLarge` — after all 24 were decompressed | 655,780 kB | 0.85 s |

The 24-entry case is the one that scales: entries are inflated concurrently, and any number up to `entryLimit` (4,096) can each expand arbitrarily, so the peak is bounded only by the process's memory — not by `archiveLimit`.

## Why it matters

`archive.ts` exists to establish "reads and validates an extension archive before anything replaces a working installation", and the caps exist to make an untrusted or corrupt archive safe to try. Today the archive dictates the allocation: a ~65 KB developer-build install can spend ~1 GiB of RSS and 5+ s of CPU, and a multi-entry variant can inflate hundreds of MiB before the post-hoc `tooLarge`, which is exactly the OOM the check was meant to prevent. The same declared-vs-actual gap means an archive can install files larger than the documented 100 MiB envelope per entry (the sum check still catches the total, after the fact).

Reachability: `ExtensionInstall` is refused when `app.isPackaged` (`packages/desktop/src/main/ipc-handlers/extensions.ts:29-35`, `app.isPackaged` at :32), so this is the unpackaged/dev tool, not a packaged-build hole. It is still a robustness gap in the guard that is supposed to protect the running app from a bad archive, and the install path accepts a URL as well as a file (`packages/desktop/src/renderer/extensions.ts:72`), so the input need not be hand-picked.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decompression is bounded by actual bytes: an entry is rejected as soon as its real output exceeds its declared size (or a fixed per-entry cap), and the running total of real bytes is capped at `archiveLimit` *during* decompression — not after `Promise.all` completes.
- [ ] Entries are not all materialised concurrently; the archive budget is shared across the extraction (sequential, or bounded concurrency with a shared counter).
- [ ] The 64 MiB-under-declared fixture above is rejected as `tooLarge`/`invalidArchive` without the process allocating anywhere near the payload — peak RSS stays within a small multiple of `archiveLimit`, not of the payload.
- [ ] The manifest's 65 KiB cap is enforced on the actual decompressed bytes, not `metadata.uncompressedSize`.
- [ ] A regression test in `packages/desktop/src/main/extension/` builds a size-patched archive (declared 1 KiB, actual large) and asserts both the rejection code and that no more than the cap was decompressed; `readArchive` has no test file today.

## Notes

- Download-side bounds already exist and are tracked separately: #1091 (overall download deadline) and #2477 (`check:bounded-http` allowlist); this is the extraction half, which no existing issue covers (searched all issues for `archive`/`zip`/`ocdx`/`extension install`).
- Same declared-size-vs-actual-bytes family as #923 / #929 / #1071, and the same "cap needs to bound the work, not the claim" shape as #2483 / #2484 / #2486.

title: fix(server): bound shell output capture and shell.output page limit — unbounded file plus uncapped page risks disk exhaustion / OOM

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: task/small-fix

labels.name: status/parked

labels.name: queue/parked
labels.description: Queue task is parked (waiting on CI, time, or an event)

body:
## Problem

`shell.create` captures combined stdout/stderr to a file with no size cap, and `shell.output` pages it with no upper limit. One verbose / never-ending command (timeout `0` = disabled) can grow the capture file until the disk fills, and one `shell.output` request with a huge `limit` tries to materialise up to the whole file in a single `Buffer`.

## Evidence (origin/main `192f3fce43`)

- `packages/schema/src/shell.ts:63-74` — `CreateInput` has no `max_bytes`; `OutputInput.limit` is an unbounded `NonNegativeInt`.
- `packages/core/src/shell.ts:37-43,68-71` — `outputLimit()` explicitly has "no upper clamp" (callers page above the 64 KiB default, so it stays byte-identical); `0` clamps up to a 1-byte page.
- `packages/core/src/shell.ts:235-263` — `output()` does `Buffer.alloc(Math.min(limit, size - start))`; with an uncapped `limit` a single page allocates up to the whole capture file. `truncated` is hardcoded `false` (line 261) even though the schema carries the flag.
- `packages/core/src/shell.ts:387-397` — the spawn pump appends every chunk to the file and `command.size` with no max; retention is only count/time-based (`EXITED_LIMIT = 25`, `RETENTION = 7 days`, lines 30-33).
- `packages/core/src/shell.ts:63-66,452-459` — timeout `0` is the disabled sentinel, so the runaway case needs no special input.
- Contrast: VCS diff paths cap output at 10 MiB (`packages/core/src/vcs/patch.ts:22-23` `MAX_TOTAL_PATCH_BYTES`); shell capture has no equivalent.

## Why it matters

The route is location-scoped, but input is agent/model-driven: a faulty `yes`, verbose build/test loop, or `tail -f`-style command fills the server disk (affecting all projects/sessions on that host), and a single large `shell.output` page can OOM the server process. The existing `Output.truncated` flag gives a natural place to surface capping honestly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Captured shell output is bounded (cap + truncate/rotate), so one command cannot exhaust disk.
- [ ] `shell.output` page `limit` is clamped (schema and/or service) so one request cannot allocate the whole capture.
- [ ] `Output.truncated` reflects capping instead of always `false`.
- [ ] Documented defaults/limits; existing callers that legitimately page above 64 KiB (session shell 1 MiB, `result()` max_bytes) keep working via paging, not via one giant allocation.

## Notes

- Follows the same unbounded-`limit` family as #2483 (session.list) / #2484 (fs.find); this one covers the disk + single-allocation side rather than table/index scans.
- Checked open/all issues for `shell` — only #2478 (workflow interpolation) and #2266 (PATH/HOME) touch shell; no output-cap issue exists.

title: fix(server): bound session.list limit — PositiveInt with no ceiling loads entire table on one request

body:
## Problem

`GET /api/session` (and plugin `session.list`) accepts an unbounded `limit`. One request with `?limit=1000000` materializes that many session rows plus a grouped authoritative-usage rollup for the whole page — same unbounded-page DoS class as #2314/#2330/#2335, distinct site.

Messages are already capped at 200 and vcs branches at 100; sessions have no ceiling anywhere in the chain.

## Evidence

- HTTP schema has no max — `packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts:61`:
  ```ts
  limit: Schema.NumberFromString.pipe(Schema.decodeTo(PositiveInt), Schema.optional)
  ```
  vs messages capped 1..200 — `packages/protocol/src/groups/message.ts:9-11`:
  ```ts
  limit: Schema.optional(
    Schema.NumberFromString.check(Schema.isInt(), Schema.isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(1), Schema.isLessThanOrEqualTo(200)),
  )
  ```

- Handler passes it straight through — `packages/server/src/handlers/session.ts:111`:
  ```ts
  limit: ctx.query.limit ?? DefaultSessionsLimit, // 50
  ```

- Store explicitly documents no ceiling — `packages/core/src/session/store.ts:76-79`:
  ```ts
  // Unlike messages there is no ceiling (the HTTP surface applies none), so a finite limit is only
  // truncated to an integer and floored to 1 ...
  const listLimit = (limit: number): number | undefined => {
    if (!Number.isFinite(limit)) return undefined
    return Math.max(Math.trunc(limit), 1)
  }
  ```
  vs `messagesLimit` just above clamps to `[1,200]` mirroring the protocol.

- Plugin wrapper same gap — `packages/core/src/plugin/session-list.ts:39-45`:
  ```ts
  // Unlike `branchListLimit` there is no upper bound — the HTTP surface applies none,
  // so a positive integer passes through unchanged.
  export function sessionListLimit(limit?: number): number {
    return pageLimit(limit, { default: DEFAULT_SESSION_LIMIT })
  }
  ```

- Cost is per-row plus rollup — `packages/core/src/session/store.ts:164-171`: `query.limit(limit).all()` then `ModelRouteLog.authoritativeSessionUsage(db, ordered.map((row) => row.id))` over the whole page.

- Precedent caps in-repo: `branchListLimit` max 100 (`packages/core/src/plugin/vcs/branch-list.ts:14-22`), `branchLimit` max 100 (`packages/core/src/vcs.ts:46-49`), messages max 200.

## Why it matters

Any local client (or plugin) can force the server to load the entire sessions table in one page with one integer. On a long-lived instance with thousands of sessions this is a memory/CPU blowup from a single query param — inconsistent with every sibling list surface.

## Suggested fix / acceptance

- Cap the session-list page (e.g. `Math.min(limit, 200)` mirroring messages, or 100 mirroring branches — pick one and document it).
- Apply at all four layers: protocol schema (`SessionsQueryFields.limit`), handler default path, store `listLimit`, plugin `sessionListLimit` (pass `max` through existing `pageLimit` helper in `packages/core/src/util/number.ts:37-43`).
- Add/extend a unit test asserting `limit=1000000` clamps to the cap and `limit=0/-5/1.9/NaN` keeps current normalization.

title: fix(core): disposition bare Number() on regex-captured exclusion instant in model-resolver (check:numeric-boundaries red on main)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

body:
## Problem

`bun run check:numeric-boundaries` on current main reports one unlisted bare string→number conversion in `packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts`:

- `model-resolver.ts:1135` — `stated ? Number(stated[1]) : Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` inside the last-resort recheck instant computation.

`stated` is the result of `/until:(\d+)$/.exec(reason)`, so `stated[1]` is a regex capture constrained to one or more ASCII digits. `Number(...)` on a digit-only string cannot produce `NaN` and cannot truncate trailing garbage (there is no trailing garbage), so this conversion is safe by construction. But the gate's P-A sweep (`Number(`) flags every bare `Number(` call regardless of input provenance, so the site must be dispositioned before the gate goes green.

This is the only unlisted numeric-boundary candidate on main.

## Evidence

- File: `packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts`, inside `lastResortRecheckAt` computation (~line 1128-1140):
  ```ts
  const reason = unavailable.get(candidate)
  const stated = reason ? /until:(\d+)$/.exec(reason) : null
  const benchEnd = ModelRoute.cooldownUntil(target, now, locationDirectory)
  const skipEnd = ModelRoute.quotaSkipUntil(target, now, locationDirectory)
  const instant = Math.min(
    stated ? Number(stated[1]) : Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY,
    benchEnd > now ? benchEnd : Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY,
    skipEnd !== undefined && skipEnd > now ? skipEnd : Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY,
  )
  ```
- Gate: `bun run script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` reports `Unlisted numeric-boundary candidate at packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts:1135: stated ? Number(stated[1]) : Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY,`.
- Input provenance: `reason` is a string from `unavailable.get(candidate)` (a `Map` of target index → reason string), and the regex `/until:(\d+)$/` anchors the capture to trailing digits, so `stated[1]` is always a non-empty run of `[0-9]` when `stated` is non-null. `Number` of such a string is a finite integer (no `NaN`, no truncation, no `"" → 0`).

## Why it matters

This is the last unlisted numeric-boundary candidate on main. Until it is dispositioned, `check:numeric-boundaries` stays red, and the next scheduled test run files a fresh main-CI failure for it. The conversion itself is not a live `NaN`/truncation vector because the input is regex-constrained to digits, but it still needs an explicit disposition per the #992/#993 convention so the gate cannot silently rot and so future edits to the regex are reviewed against the conversion.

## Acceptance criteria

- `bun run script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` reports no unlisted candidate for `packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts:1135` (either converted through a shared primitive or a reasoned allowlist entry).
- `packages/core` typecheck clean.
- Model routing behaviour unchanged: last-resort recheck instant computation still yields the earliest re-admission moment among excluded/untried targets, and `Number.isFinite`/`instant <= now` guards still apply.
- No regression in model resolver tests.

## Suggested fix shape

Option A — convert through the shared primitives in `packages/core/src/util/number.ts` (#993). The capture is digit-only, so the appropriate primitive is the integer parse that rejects non-finite/non-integer results; if no primitive fits a digit-only string exactly, keep `Number` but wrap with an explicit guard and document why. (Check `packages/core/src/util/number.ts` exports before choosing; do not invent a primitive.)

Option B — add an allowlist entry to `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt`:
```
packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts :: stated ? Number(stated[1]) : Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY, :: safe by construction: stated[1] is the \d+ capture of /until:(\d+)$/ (anchored trailing digits), so Number() cannot yield NaN or truncate garbage here (#992)
```
(occurrence count is 1; the exact trimmed line must match the sweep output.)

Option B is the minimal change and matches the gate's "safe by construction with the reason" disposition; Option A is preferred only if a #993 primitive covers digit-only strings directly. Either unblocks the gate.

## Related

- Same class: #992 (design), #993 (phase 1 primitives), #995 (phase 3 net).
- Gate: `check:numeric-boundaries` (red on main).
- Sibling sites already dispositioned with `Number(...)` on regex-captured units/months: `packages/core/src/model-route-limits.ts` (`Number(amount) * UNITS[unit]`, `Number(dayFirst[...]`, …) and `packages/core/src/model-route-schedule.ts`.

title: fix(core): disposition unlisted proto-read candidate in model-route-match.ts (check:proto-reads red on main)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

body:
## Problem

`bun run check:proto-reads` on current main reports one unlisted prototype-chain read candidate in `packages/core/src/model-route-match.ts`:

- `model-route-match.ts:65` — `route[key] ?? []` inside `compile`'s `each` helper.

`key` is a closed union of `"include" | "exclude" | "contains" | "notContains"`, and `route` is a config-derived `Keys` object. None of those four names are `Object.prototype` members, so the prototype chain cannot supply a non-undefined value here — the read is safe by construction. But the gate's P-C sweep (`[...] ??`) flags every bracket read with a `??` fallback regardless of key provenance, so the site must be dispositioned before the gate goes green.

Until this is dispositioned, `check:proto-reads` stays red on main alongside the already-tracked candidates (#2476 render-card, #2472 model-routes, #2462 voice-input).

## Evidence

- File: `packages/core/src/model-route-match.ts`, `compile` function, `each` helper (~line 63-66):
  ```ts
  const each = (
    key: "include" | "exclude" | "contains" | "notContains",
    read: (text: string) => Result.Result<Predicate, string>,
  ) => (route[key] ?? []).flatMap((text, index) => keep([key, String(index)], read(text)))
  ```
- Gate: `bun run script/check-proto-reads.ts` reports `Unlisted prototype-chain read candidate at packages/core/src/model-route-match.ts:65: ) => (route[key] ?? []).flatMap(...)`.
- Caller: `packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts` (`ModelRouteMatch.compile(current, reference(...))`), where `current` is a config-derived `ConfigModelRoutes.Route`. `problems()` also calls `compile(route, () => undefined)` on raw routes.
- Key provenance: `key` is a compile-time string-literal union of four matching-key names; it is never a runtime-supplied or config-derived string, so none of the prototype-member names (`constructor`, `toString`, `__proto__`, …) can reach this read.

## Why it matters

This is the last untracked proto-read candidate: every other unlisted site is already tracked by an open issue (#2476, #2472, #2462). Leaving it unlisted keeps `check:proto-reads` red on main, so the next scheduled test run files a fresh main-CI failure for it. The read itself is not a live prototype-pollution vector because the key set is closed and none of its members are prototype members, but it still needs an explicit disposition per the #865 convention so the gate cannot silently rot.

## Acceptance criteria

- `bun run script/check-proto-reads.ts` reports no unlisted candidate for `packages/core/src/model-route-match.ts:65` (either guarded at the site or a reasoned allowlist entry).
- `packages/core` typecheck clean.
- `ModelRouteMatch.compile` behaviour unchanged for every valid route: include/exclude/contains/notContains arrays still compile identically, and malformed entries still surface as problems.
- No regression in model-route config loading (`packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts`).

## Suggested fix shape

Option A — guard at the site with `ownOr` (matches the #865 "blessed fix" direction), changing:
```ts
(route[key] ?? []).flatMap(...)
```
to
```ts
(ownOr(route, key, []) as readonly string[]).flatMap(...)
```
with `import { ownOr } from "../util/record.js"` (or the appropriate relative path), keeping `key`'s union type. This makes the own-property read explicit even though the key set is closed.

Option B — add an allowlist entry to `script/check-proto-reads.allowlist.txt`:
```
packages/core/src/model-route-match.ts :: ) => (route[key] ?? []).flatMap((text, index) => keep([key, String(index)], read(text))) :: safe by construction: key is a closed union of four literal matching-key names ("include"/"exclude"/"contains"/"notContains"), none of which are Object.prototype members, so the prototype chain cannot supply a non-undefined value here (#865)
```
(occurrence count is 1; the exact trimmed line must match the sweep output.)

Option A is preferred for consistency with #2472's direction; Option B is acceptable and matches #2476's render-card disposition style. Either unblocks the gate.

## Related

- Same class: #865, #916, #917, #2392, #2462 (voice-input), #2472 (model-routes weights), #2476 (render-card).
- Gate: `check:proto-reads` (red on main).

## Finding (pr-diff-review lane B)

PRs **#2470** and **#2471** are two open, mutually exclusive fixes for the *same* main CI failure — scheduled `test` workflow run [43703475593](https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/actions/runs/43703475593) on main `d35c4341598043b1320e5d450049062cba341705`, tracked as #2469. Both are still OPEN, and current main (`8e24d8c0d1fa73e43292d6ddcfaca24f888dde57`, verified this run) still carries the unguarded reads, so the failure #2469 tracks is still live. Only one of the two can land; the other will conflict on every shared file. They also **diverge semantically**, so this is a decision, not a coin flip:

| Surface | #2470 (head `6320e821735e`) | #2471 (head `8f09ca6a81be`) |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts:1058` weight lookup | Inline `Object.hasOwn`: an own key wins **even when its value is `undefined`** — the case-insensitive pool-name fallback no longer runs for an explicitly-undefined weight (behavior change vs main's `current.weights?.[key] ?? fallback`) | Shared `ownValue` util + `??` chain: preserves main's fall-through to the case-insensitive fallback when the exact-key value is `undefined` |
| `packages/core/src/model-route-match.ts:65` `route[key]` | No code change; scanner candidate dispositioned in `script/check-proto-reads.allowlist.txt` ("safe: fixed literal key list") | Code change to `ownValue(route, key)`; no allowlist entry needed |
| `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/voice-input.ts:86` | Inline `Object.hasOwn` + allowlist entry | `ownValue` from `@opencode/core/util/record` |
| `packages/ai/test/provider/secret-service-dbus.test.ts` (Windows failure) | Wraps **both** dbus tests in `describe.skipIf(process.platform !== "linux")` | Adds an early return to only the bogus-address test (the absent-address test already self-skips via `process.getuid`) |
| Tracking | Body states the tracking issue was "not located"; does **not** close #2469; pushed `--no-verify` | `Closes #2469` |
| Scanner result claimed | 293 candidates dispositioned | 291 candidates dispositioned |

Evidence: PR #2470 https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2470 (commit `6320e821735e8f90a4a25c6fe88bfcc081085950`), PR #2471 https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2471 (commit `8f09ca6a81bee582c9f96638a77b1831c2d25f9d`). Shared files: `model-routes.ts`, `voice-input.ts`, `secret-service-dbus.test.ts` (both), plus `model-route-match.ts` / `check-proto-reads.allowlist.txt` on one side each.

Sequencing note: open PR #2474 (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR session-bus synthesis, #2473) also rewrites `packages/ai/test/provider/secret-service-dbus.test.ts` (appends tests, extends `afterEach`). Whichever of #2470/#2471 survives will conflict with #2474 on that file; land them in an order that resolves the test-file conflict once.

## Why it matters

Main's scheduled test workflow is red (#2469) until one fix lands. Two live duplicates double review/CI surface, and if the wrong one merges first the other becomes a stale conflicting branch. The weight-lookup divergence is a real routing-behavior difference (explicit `undefined` weight vs case-insensitive fallback) that should be chosen deliberately, not by merge order.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exactly one of #2470 / #2471 is chosen as the survivor, with the weight-lookup semantics (own-undefined wins vs fall-through to case-insensitive fallback) decided and recorded on this issue.
- [ ] The survivor merges and closes #2469; the proto-read gate passes on main and the Windows `@opencode/ai` dbus test is green or Linux-scoped.
- [ ] The non-survivor is closed as superseded, naming the survivor.
- [ ] The survivor's landing is sequenced with #2474 so `secret-service-dbus.test.ts` conflicts are resolved exactly once.

title: fix(core): guard prototype-chain read on model route weights (weights?.[key] with config-derived pool id)

body:
## Summary

`packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts` (the `attach` helper inside `expandCollected`) reads a pool's weight via a bare bracket read on a config-derived key:

```ts
const weight =
  current.weights?.[key] ??
  (child.node === undefined
    ? undefined
    : Object.entries(current.weights ?? {}).find(
        ([name]) =>
          name.toLowerCase() === key.toLowerCase() ||
          name.toLowerCase().endsWith(`/${key.toLowerCase()}`),
      )?.[1])
```

`key` is a pool id / `providerID/modelID` / `door/id` string taken from the route config (not a closed union, not a numeric index). A bare `record[key]` walks the prototype chain, so a config that names a weight key `"constructor"`, `"toString"`, `"__proto__"`, etc. resolves to an inherited member (a function) instead of missing — and the `??` fallback never fires because inherited members are non-nullish. `weight` then becomes that function, propagates into `node.weights`, and corrupts weighted selection among pool members (NaN / non-finite weights, wrong autonomy/health decisions). The second branch already uses `Object.entries`, which is own-property only, so only the first branch is unguarded.

This is the same prototype-chain dictionary-read class audited in #865/#916/#917/#2392; the repo's `check-proto-reads` gate flags this exact site as an unlisted candidate.

## Evidence

- File: `packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts`, `attach` function (~line 1055-1066).
- Gate: `bun run script/check-proto-reads.ts` reports `Unlisted prototype-chain read candidate at packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts:1058: current.weights?.[key] ??`.
- Key provenance: `attach(..., \`${poolID}\`)`, `attach(..., \`${ref.providerID}/${ref.id}\`)`, `attach(..., \`${door}/${id}\`)`, `attach(..., leafKey)`, `attach(..., key)` — all config/route-derived strings, not constrained to own keys.
- Sibling sites already guard with `Object.hasOwn` / `ownValue`/`ownOr` (`packages/core/src/util/record.ts`), and the gate allowlist records those dispositions.

## Why it matters

Model route weights drive weighted selection among a pool's members and feed autonomy/health/failover decisions. A poisoned weight (inherited function) is non-nullish so the fallback never applies, and a function stored where a number is expected breaks arithmetic downstream (NaN propagation). Config is user-authored, so a hostile or accidental key name like `"constructor"` is reachable.

## Acceptance criteria

- The weight lookup reads `current.weights` only through an own-property guard (`ownValue`/`ownOr` from `packages/core/src/util/record.ts`, or an `Object.hasOwn` ternary at the site), matching the #865 pattern; the case-insensitive fallback branch is unchanged.
- `bun run script/check-proto-reads.ts` reports no unlisted candidate for this site (either guarded at the site or a reasoned allowlist entry).
- Regression: a route whose `weights` map has no own key but whose child id is a prototype member name (e.g. `"constructor"`) yields weight `1` (the fallback), not the inherited function; a normal own key still resolves to its configured weight.

## Related

- In-flight PRs already move this site to `Object.hasOwn`: #2470, #2471 (cross-linked both ways).
- Same class: #865, #916, #917, #2392, #2462 (voice-input).

## Suggested fix shape

```ts
const weight =
  ownValue(current.weights ?? {}, key) ??
  (child.node === undefined
    ? undefined
    : Object.entries(current.weights ?? {}).find(
        ([name]) =>
          name.toLowerCase() === key.toLowerCase() ||
          name.toLowerCase().endsWith(`/${key.toLowerCase()}`),
      )?.[1])
```
with `import { ownValue } from "../../util/record"` (adjust relative path). Keep the existing case-insensitive fallback for legitimate pool names that differ only in case.

title: fix(core): render-card quota wall stays latched when no card can be built — offeredWall is set before wallDirective is known and never cleared on the bare-error path (PR #2452 residual)

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
