body:
## Finding

In PR #2452 (the live render-card wiring for #2384 slices 2–3), a session's quota wall is latched before anyone knows whether a fallback card can actually be built, and the latch is never released when no card is built. `step.ts` calls `SessionRunnerRenderWiring.offerWall(sessionID, wall)` and returns `Outcome.QuotaWall` as soon as `offeredWall(sessionID) === undefined`; the runner's `QuotaWall` handler in `llm.ts` then computes `wallDirective(outcome.wall)` — which returns `undefined` when the plan store cannot supply the card's three actions (a cheap-tier walled model has no downgrade tier; a store with no other provider has no switch target; a throwing store read is caught and also yields `undefined`) — and ends the step with the original `StepFailedError`. But `offeredWall` stays set: `clearWall` is only called inside `applyToolResult` for a non-`none` render answer, and `clearSession` has no production caller in the PR (tests only). No card was ever shown, so no answer can ever settle the wall — every later quota wall in that session silently takes the bare-error ending, even after the plan store gains the missing provider or tier. The chooser path in the same module does this correctly: `chooserDirective` marks the session asked only after the tiers are known non-empty.

## Evidence

- PR #2452 (OPEN, head `9115c142a9754d07879ea6e710024d34472d92c3`, stacked on PR #2450) — core: wire the render-card seam into the live runner (#2384 slices 2-3). https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2452
- At that head: `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts` — the quota-wall block gates on `SessionRunnerRenderWiring.offeredWall(input.sessionID) === undefined`, then `offerWall(...)` and `return Outcome.QuotaWall({ wall, error })`.
- `packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts` — `QuotaWall` handler: `if (directive === undefined) return yield* new StepFailedError({ error: outcome.error })`, with no `clearWall` on that path (nor on the caught-throw path, which also yields `undefined`).
- `packages/core/src/session/runner/render-wiring.ts` — `wallDirective` returns `undefined` when `fallbackActionsFor` cannot derive all three actions; `clearWall` is called only in `applyToolResult` after a parsed non-`none` answer; the module's stated latch semantics are "a quota wall is offered at most once until a render answer settles it".
- The PR's tests cover the offered-wall gate and answer application, but no test covers a wall whose directive cannot be built followed by a second wall in the same session.
- Verified by code-structure reading of the PR head diff; not on current main (the PR is unmerged), so there is no main file:line to re-check — the finding is against the PR as written. No runtime verification was run for this finding (this run's one runtime verification was spent on the PR #2466 adoption-bound replay, reproduced on the laptop).

## Why it matters

The quota-fallback card is the user's only in-turn remedy when a quota wall ends a step. Sessions that hit their first wall while the plan store is thin — a single-provider store, or a walled cheap-tier model — permanently lose that remedy for the life of the session, with no log or state distinguishing "card offered and ignored" from "card could never be built". The failure is silent and sticky precisely in the least-configured setups the fallback is meant to rescue.

## Acceptance criteria

- A wall that produces no directive does not consume the latch: `offeredWall(sessionID)` is `undefined` after the `QuotaWall` handler falls back to `StepFailedError` (equivalently, the wall is only offered once a directive has been successfully built).
- A regression test pins it: a first quota wall with underivable fallback actions ends in the bare error and leaves no offered wall; after the plan store gains the missing action inputs, a second quota wall in the same session returns `Outcome.QuotaWall` again.
- The existing render-wiring and step suites (`session-runner-render-wiring`, seam suites) keep passing.
- Fix lands in PR #2452 before merge if it is still open; otherwise as a follow-on PR referencing this issue and #2384.

## Shadow verdict (PoC)

Stage A window already closed (summary on developing-today/code#2313, comment 6854418559) — no shadow verdict recorded.

title: fix(ai): claude-code renewal replays a rotated-out refresh token once the adoption bound (3) is exhausted — adoptStored silently stops adopting (PR #2466 residual)

labels.name: kind/security

labels.name: task/small-fix

labels.description: Package: ai (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Finding

PR #2466 makes a claude-code renewal re-read the shared credentials file before every exchange attempt and adopt another writer's rotation instead of replaying its snapshot token — but the adoption is capped at 3 (`adoptions < 3` in `adoptStored`), and when the cap is exhausted the renewal does not stop: `adoptStored` silently returns `undefined` and the loop goes on to present its current refresh token even though the file demonstrably holds a different, newer one. That is a replay of a rotated-out, single-use refresh token — the exact presentation the PR's own loop comment forbids ("Never present a rotated-out refresh token") and the theft-signal event that can revoke the whole token family (the 2026-11-13 death this PR sets out to prevent, code#9549). The same cap flaw hits the rejection path: once adoptions are exhausted, a grant rejection for a token another writer already replaced is believed terminal, because `adoptStored` can no longer change `currentRefreshToken`.

## Evidence

- PR #2466 (OPEN, head `b4dbe461ab91a5628c23f502147c6cc749e56376`) — fix(ai): claude-code renewal adopts another writer's rotation instead of replaying it (code#9549). https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2466
- `packages/ai/src/providers/claude-code-auth.ts` at that head, `refreshAndPersist`: `adoptStored` adopts the stored refresh token only while `stored.refreshToken !== currentRefreshToken && adoptions < 3`; past the cap it returns `undefined` without adopting, and the loop unconditionally calls `exchangeRefreshToken(effective, currentRefreshToken)`. The pre-attempt re-read has therefore *proven* the presented token is not the file's current token, and it is presented anyway.
- The PR's 4 new tests cover a single adoption each; no test drives a fourth rotation inside one renewal.

## Runtime verification (verification_class: runtime-gap/high-risk) — REPRODUCED

- Commit tested: PR #2466 head `b4dbe461ab91a5628c23f502147c6cc749e56376`, isolated worktree on the laptop (primary clone untouched, worktree removed after).
- Command: `bun test test/provider/probe-adopt-bound.test.ts` (packages/ai, bun 1.4.4) — a probe test in the PR's own harness shape: every exchange attempt is rate-limited (429, Retry-After 1, stubbed sleep) and another writer rotates the stored pair to a due pair before each retry.
- Result: 1 pass / 0 fail. Presented refresh tokens were `["ref-probe-0", "ref-probe-1", "ref-probe-2", "ref-probe-3", "ref-probe-3"]` — attempt 5 re-presented `ref-probe-3` while the file already held `ref-probe-4`. The exchange's own pre-write guard then threw (stored token differed and did not serve) and the renewal rejected to the standing retry — which, being a fresh `refreshAndPersist` with a fresh adoption budget, adopted `ref-probe-4` and landed, proving a retire-instead-of-replay fix shape works with the existing machinery.
- Probe kept at `hidden_files/pr-review-b-2026-11-15-0318-opencode/probe-adopt-bound.test.ts` (goal workspace).

## Why it matters

Replaying a rotated-out refresh token is treated by the provider as token theft and can revoke the entire token family, killing even the fresh pair another writer just persisted — the failure mode behind the 2026-11-13 login death (renewal landed 11:36Z, dead 401 by 13:00Z). PR #2466 is the fix that gates re-enabling the `_claude` door; a residual replay path that opens after only four cross-writer rotations during one renewal's rate-limit waits (each wait can last minutes, and the CLI plus every opencode process on the machine are writers) leaves the incident class alive in exactly the high-contention moments that produce rotations.

## Acceptance criteria

- When the adoption bound is reached and the file holds a refresh token different from the renewal's current one, the renewal presents nothing: it retires to the standing retry (fresh adoption budget) or fails with a dedicated exhausted-adoptions error — no exchange attempt is made with a token known not to be the file's current one. The rejection path follows the same rule (a rejection is not believed while the file holds a different token).
- A regression test in `packages/ai/test/provider/claude-code-auth.test.ts` drives at least four rotations inside one renewal and asserts every presented refresh token is the file's current token at the moment it is presented (no token is ever presented twice after a rotation).
- The PR's 4 adoption tests and the full `claude-code-auth.test.ts` file keep passing; `packages/ai` typecheck clean.
- Fix lands in PR #2466 before merge if it is still open; otherwise as a follow-on PR referencing this issue.

## Shadow verdict (PoC)

Stage A window already closed (summary on developing-today/code#2313, comment 6854418559) — no shadow verdict recorded.

title: fix(server): bound and validate persistent-pty connect attachment_id

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary
`GET /api/experimental/persistent-pty/:ptyID/connect` reads `attachment_id` directly from the query string without length or format validation, then uses it as the attachment identity, echoes it back to the client in the `attached` frame, and forwards it to the persistent PTY service/daemon.

## Evidence (origin/main `3065d29f62`, 2026-11-15)

`packages/server/src/handlers/persistent-pty.ts`
```ts
119: const cursor = Number(url.searchParams.get("cursor") ?? "0")
120: const role = url.searchParams.get("role") === "observer" ? "observer" : "controller"
121: const framedInput = url.searchParams.get("input_protocol") === "1"
122: const attachmentID = url.searchParams.get("attachment_id") ?? crypto.randomUUID()
123: if (!Number.isSafeInteger(cursor) || cursor < 0) return HttpServerResponse.empty({ status: 400 })
...
131:   .attach(ctx.params.ptyID, {
132:     cursor,
133:     attachmentID,
134:     role,
...
157: void outbox.offer(
158:   JSON.stringify({
159:     type: "attached",
160:     attachmentID,
...
```

Other connect query params are constrained here (`cursor` validated, `role`/`input_protocol`/`takeover` normalized to known values), but `attachment_id` is accepted verbatim as any string.

The API/schema also treat it as an unconstrained string:
- `packages/protocol/src/groups/persistent-pty.ts:119-121` declares `attachment_id` as a query parameter with `schema: { type: "string" }`.
- `packages/schema/src/persistent-pty.ts:37` defines `UpdateInput.attachmentID` as `optional(Schema.String)` (no max length/format).
- Core/daemon protocol carry it as a string (`packages/core/src/persistent-pty/index.ts` passes `attachment_id` in write/resize/control/input/attach requests; `packages/core/src/persistent-pty/daemon.ts` models attached/controller events with string attachment ids).

By contrast, when omitted the server generates a bounded UUID (`crypto.randomUUID()`), and the regular PTY connect endpoint does not accept a client-supplied attachment identifier.

## Why it matters
A client can supply an arbitrarily large `attachment_id` value. That value is:
- serialized into the `attached` JSON control frame sent back over the socket,
- passed into `attach`/`control`/`input` operations and daemon messages,
- potentially retained as attachment/controller identity state.

This makes the endpoint susceptible to avoidable memory/CPU pressure and oversized protocol frames from untrusted or buggy clients. Experimental APIs should still bound client-controlled identifiers consistently with the rest of the endpoint's input validation.

## Suggested fix / acceptance criteria
- [ ] Bound/validate `attachment_id` on persistent PTY connect (and consider aligning `PersistentPty.UpdateInput.attachmentID`): reject or ignore values that are empty/too long or contain unexpected characters (e.g. cap length to a small fixed maximum such as 128, and/or require a safe token/UUID-like format).
- [ ] On invalid `attachment_id`, fail the request with a clear 4xx (or fall back to a server-generated id) rather than forwarding it unchanged.
- [ ] Add a regression test showing an oversized/invalid `attachment_id` is rejected or normalized and is never echoed/forwarded verbatim.
- [ ] Document the accepted `attachment_id` shape in protocol/schema/openapi if a format/limit is imposed.

body:
## Finding

Open PR #2436 ("fix(ci): repair failed test workflow checks") is half-superseded and needs a disposition. Its transcription-facade half — replacing aliased `configure` imports to satisfy the `no-import-alias` lint rule — was landed by merged PR #2438 in a different shape, and the facade has since been rewritten again by merged PR #2431. Its other half — Linux platform guards for the secret-service DBus tests — has not landed anywhere and still fixes a real test-gate mismatch. Left open, the PR invites a stale rebase that re-litigates a settled approach; closed without salvage, the DBus test fix is lost.

## Evidence

- PR #2436 (OPEN, head `510d6c5827c02d670b54d6735eb40d002df49a96`): two files — `packages/core/src/transcription-facade.ts` (lazy `PROVIDER_MODULES` map replacing all five static `configure` imports, including OpenAI's) and `packages/ai/test/provider/secret-service-dbus.test.ts` (platform guards).
- PR #2438 (MERGED, merge `88a2f1dd29552a604cee59b08bebdd29c887dae1`, closes #2437): the same lint fix landed as top-level `await import(...)` for the four aliased providers, keeping OpenAI's static import and `PROVIDER_FACTORIES`. Verified on current main `c3247993265218b538a3a8ecc13149d7dcf8df13`: `packages/core/src/transcription-facade.ts` lines 556-559 are #2438's eager dynamic imports, and `PROVIDER_FACTORIES` is in use at lines 660/733 — the region #2436 rewrites no longer exists in its form.
- PR #2431 (MERGED, merge `18d688bc8ee3e09934857cde817beaf59b3b04ce`) further changed the same file (streaming `transcribeStream`), so #2436's facade half is two changes stale.
- The DBus half is not on main: `packages/ai/test/provider/secret-service-dbus.test.ts` at main still guards the synthesis test with `if (typeof process.getuid !== "function") return` and leaves the bogus-address test unguarded. `process.getuid` exists on macOS, so the first test runs (and fails against the implementation's Linux gate) on non-Linux runners, per #2436's own checklist note. #2436's change — `process.platform !== "linux"` guards on both tests — is the unlanded remainder.

## Why it matters

An open, stale, half-duplicated PR costs every future triage pass a re-derivation of this disposition, and its still-valid test fix protects the Windows/macOS basic-unit legs the PR was created to repair. One decision ends both costs.

## Acceptance criteria

- PR #2436 is dispositioned exactly one way: (a) rebased onto current main keeping ONLY the `secret-service-dbus.test.ts` platform-guard change, retitled to match, and merged; or (b) closed as superseded-by-#2438 for the facade half, with the DBus guard change refiled as a fresh small PR/issue and linked from the close comment.
- Either way, the DBus platform guards land (or a linked follow-up exists that will land them): both secret-service tests skip on non-Linux and run on Linux.
- Note for the triager (context, not a requirement): #2438's merged shape loads all four provider modules eagerly at facade module load via top-level await; #2436's lazy map avoided that. If that tradeoff is worth revisiting, file it separately — do not hold this disposition on it.

title: fix(deps): Dependabot security PRs #2414/#2415/#2416 bump astro to 7.4.7 package.json-only — no bun.lock, split across three directories; lock-rescue and consolidate before merge (recurrence of #196/#480)

body:
## Finding

Three open Dependabot **security** PRs bump astro to 7.4.7 in three different packages, each changing `package.json` only — no `bun.lock` — so none of them can land as-is without desyncing the workspace lockfile. This is a recurrence of #196 / #480: security updates for directories not covered by an npm-ecosystem entry in `dependabot.yml` arrive package.json-only, while the root `bun.lock` covers every workspace package. The three PRs should be lock-rescued and consolidated (or individually rescued) as one shepherded set before any of them merges.

## The PRs

- PR #2414 — astro 7.2.8 → 7.4.7 in `/packages/posts` (OPEN, head `3ea6580e81535b5150151c5383b49c6cd5a51c08`)
- PR #2415 — astro 7.3.3 → 7.4.7 in `/services/www` (OPEN, head `1ebc9eb1ee05a476092b74d0cff633c4f8b90e2f`)
- PR #2416 — astro 5.7.13 → 7.4.7 in `/packages/web` (OPEN, head `1179c5ed1e95475da9f2d55878d3041643324205`)

## Evidence

- Each PR's diff is exactly one file, `package.json`, +1/−1; none touches `bun.lock` (verified from the PR file lists).
- On current main `18d688bc8ee3e09934857cde817beaf59b3b04ce`, root `bun.lock` still pins the old astro per package (posts 7.2.8, www 7.3.3, web 5.7.13). Merging any of the three leaves manifest and lockfile disagreeing, and `bun install --frozen-lockfile` fails — the exact failure the header comment in `.github/dependabot.yml` records for #196.
- `.github/dependabot.yml`: version updates run under the root bun entry and regenerate `bun.lock`; security updates arrive as npm_and_yarn jobs scoped to the manifest's directory, and the only npm entry covers `/packages/core`. `packages/posts`, `services/www`, and `packages/web` are uncovered — the #480 gap, still open for these directories.
- All three PRs show MERGEABLE/CLEAN with only a CodeRabbit check — no install/CI gate ran on them, so nothing flags the desync before merge.
- PR #2416 is not a routine patch bump: `packages/web` jumps two majors (5.7.13 → 7.4.7), so it needs a real build verification, not just a lock regeneration. (The lockfile's `@astrojs/cloudflare` 14.1.4 already declares a peer of `astro ^7.0.0`, which web's current 5.7.13 does not satisfy.)
- The 7.4.7 line these PRs carry includes security-relevant fixes (astro's own changelog in the PR bodies shows the undici v8 [SECURITY] update), so leaving the set stranded leaves the fix unlanded.

## Why it matters

Three security updates sit unmergeable in their delivered form; if any is merged naively, the next frozen-lockfile install breaks for every developer and CI job. The fleet has rescued this exact shape repeatedly (#196, #257, #480, #1375) — the durable pattern is one shepherded lock-rescue, not three independent merges.

## Acceptance criteria

- astro is at 7.4.7 in `packages/posts`, `services/www`, and `packages/web` with `package.json` and the root `bun.lock` moving together; `bun install --frozen-lockfile` passes on the result.
- Build/check passes for all three packages on astro 7.4.7 — explicitly including `packages/web`'s 5→7 major jump; any major-bump breakage found is fixed in the rescue or filed as its own issue, not silently dropped.
- The three PRs are each closed with a pointer to the rescuing change (superseded-by note if consolidated into one PR; merged note if rescued in place).
- No other package's pinned versions change in the rescue beyond what the astro move requires.

title: fix(ai): antigravity const lowering misses non-string enums — a numeric/boolean const that IS a declared enum member is not narrowed, the pin is silently dropped (#2423 residual)

body:
## Finding

PR #2423's const lowering in the antigravity schema converter silently drops the pin when the declared `enum` is numeric or boolean: the membership test compares the stringified const against the verbatim (unstringified) enum members, so a const that IS a member of its declared enum is treated as a non-member and the enum is left untouched — the fixed-value constraint is lost on the antigravity door.

## Evidence

- PR #2423 (MERGED, merge `f566b4e4f1255fbfb58893f9ead52df2dd883805`, head `1c2d84610d6073265b2197e817b28fa961cb98fb`) — fix(ai): antigravity convertSchema lowers const to a one-element enum (#1557).
- `packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts`, `convertSchemaNode` const block (unchanged on current main `18d688bc8ee3e09934857cde817beaf59b3b04ce`):
  - `enum` rides the allowlist verbatim (`SCHEMA_VALUE_KEYS` / `out[key] = value`), so a JSON Schema enum `[1, 2]` stays numeric in `out.enum`.
  - The const block computes `const value = String(pinned)` and tests `out.enum.includes(value)` — `"1"` is never an element of `[1, 2]`, and `"true"` is never an element of `[true, false]`.
  - Result: `convertSchema({ type: "integer", enum: [1, 2], const: 1 })` yields `{ type: "INTEGER", enum: [1, 2] }` — no narrowing — instead of the intended `{ type: "INTEGER", enum: ["1"] }`. Same for boolean enums.
- The regression test added by #2423 covers enum narrowing only for a string enum (`{ type: "string", enum: ["a", "b"], const: "b" }`), which is the one case where the verbatim and stringified forms coincide.
- The const-outside-the-enum disposition (leave the enum untouched) is the deliberate, issue-prescribed behavior for a genuine non-member — this finding is only about members misread as non-members because of the type mismatch.

## Why it matters

A tool parameter declared `{ enum: [1, 2], const: 1 }` (or the boolean equivalent) is a fixed-value parameter; on every other door the const constrains it, and #1557/#2423 set out to preserve exactly that on antigravity. With the pin dropped, the model may legitimately pick the other enum value and the tool receives input its schema forbids — the same unconstrained-parameter failure #1557 reported, surviving in the enum-carrying shape.

## Acceptance criteria

- A numeric or boolean const that is a member of the declared enum (membership judged on the stringified members, matching how scalar consts ride the string-valued proto enum) narrows the enum to the one-element pin, e.g. `enum: [1, 2], const: 1` → `enum: ["1"]`.
- Regression tests cover integer-enum and boolean-enum narrowing; the existing string-enum narrowing and non-scalar-const drop tests keep passing.
- A const genuinely outside the declared enum keeps the documented disposition (enum untouched), pinned by a test so the two cases are distinguishable.

body:
## Finding

The TUI voice-input submit path from PR #2420 has no working in-flight guard: invoking `/voice-send` a second time while a transcription is still submitting calls the STT façade a second time for the same audio, and on success the transcript is inserted into the composer twice.

## Evidence

- PR #2420 (MERGED, merge `93af5bf8eaf1db2b95f5e3c69108154e0f1614bd`, head `4bede2ccb01a48f1a9236cf66800efc7c236884c`) — feat(tui): voice input — attach + mic capture + review + composer insertion (#2387).
- `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/voice-input.ts` — `VoiceInputMachine.beginSubmit()`: when the state is already `submitting`, it returns the current snapshot unchanged — `{ state: "submitting", audio }` — indistinguishable from a fresh reviewing→submitting transition.
- `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx` — `voiceSubmit()`: the only guard is on that returned snapshot (`if (snapshot.state !== "submitting" || !snapshot.audio) return`), so a second invocation while in flight passes the guard and proceeds to `submitVoiceTranscription(...)` again; each success path calls `input.insertText(result.text)`.
- Verified still present on current main `18d688bc8ee3e09934857cde817beaf59b3b04ce`: `beginSubmit` and the `voiceSubmit` guard are unchanged, and the streaming branch added by #2431 sits behind the same guard, so both the batch and streaming paths are affected.
- No test covers it: `packages/tui/test/component/voice-input.test.ts` exercises `beginSubmit()` from `reviewing` and from `error` only, never while already `submitting`.

## Runtime verification (verification_class: runtime-gap/high-risk) — REPRODUCED

- Commit tested: exact PR head `4bede2ccb01a48f1a9236cf66800efc7c236884c`, isolated worktree on the laptop (removed after; primary clone untouched).
- Command: `bun test test/component/probe-voice-double-submit.test.ts` (packages/tui, bun 1.4.4) — probe replicates the composer's `voiceSubmit` guard composition verbatim against the real `VoiceInputMachine`, with a counting fake façade call.
- Result: 1 pass / 1 fail as predicted — the pass pins that a second `beginSubmit()` while submitting returns an indistinguishable submitting snapshot with audio; the fail shows two concurrent composer submits both proceed: `facadeCalls: 2` where exactly 1 is correct.

## Why it matters

A double `/voice-send` (easy while a slow transcription is in flight — the status line still shows the audio held and the command stays enabled) spends a second paid provider transcription for the same clip and inserts the transcript text twice into the draft, silently corrupting what the user then sends. The state machine was built specifically to make the submit step singular (§6.2: "submitting calls the façade once").

## Acceptance criteria

- A second submit attempt while a transcription is in flight is a no-op: exactly one façade call per reviewed audio, on both the batch and streaming paths.
- The guard is distinguishable at the machine/caller boundary (e.g. `beginSubmit` reports already-in-flight, or the caller tracks the transition), not just a snapshot state check.
- A regression test covers submit-while-submitting (two concurrent submits → one façade call, one insertion).
- Existing `packages/tui` voice-input tests keep passing.

title: fix(core): Form.ask timeout cancels a shared (joined) form — a joiner's timer aborts the owner's pending question

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Summary

`Form.ask` supports joining an already-pending form when `dedupePending` is set (#1883): a second, identical ask reuses the original form instead of creating a second question. The bounded-wait timeout (#1883) is supposed to cancel **this ask's own** form when its timer fires.

But the timeout branch is built unconditionally:

```ts
const timedOut = Effect.sleep(timeout).pipe(
  Effect.andThen(
    cancel(form.id, { message: ... }).pipe(Effect.ignore),   // <-- runs for joiners too
  ),
  Effect.andThen(Deferred.await(entry.deferred)),
)
```

`cancel(form.id)` settles the **shared** deferred, so a joiner whose timer fires first cancels the form the original asker owns. The original asker's pending question is aborted by a stranger's timeout, and the owner's `awaited` resolves with the joiner's timeout message.

This contradicts the in-code invariant documented two lines above:

> A joined ask does not own the form: interrupting it must not cancel the original asker's pending question.

That invariant is enforced for `Effect.interrupt` (the `onInterrupt` hook is only attached when `!existing`), but **not** for the timeout path.

## Evidence

File: `packages/core/src/form.ts`, function `Form.ask`, lines 178–198 (commit 1e2537ba32).

- `existing` (line 168) is the joined form, present only for a deduped ask.
- `awaited` (lines 182–184) correctly skips the `onInterrupt` cancel for a joiner.
- `timedOut` (lines 191–198) calls `cancel(form.id, ...)` regardless of `existing`, settling the shared deferred.

Reachability is latent today: the sole opt-in caller (the `question` tool) uses a uniform 10-minute timeout, and a joiner's timer starts later, so the owner's usually fires first. But any caller that passes differing timeouts (or a shorter one on a resume) lets a joiner cancel the owner's question. The fix is a one-line guard, matching the existing `onInterrupt` guard.

## Why it matters

- A joiner can abort another session's pending question, leaving the owner with a spurious "timed out" terminal state and no answer.
- It makes the timeout option unsafe to combine with `dedupePending`, which is exactly the resume-after-forced-error shape #1883 exists to support.

## Suggested fix shape

Guard the cancel on ownership, mirroring the `onInterrupt` guard:

```ts
const timedOut = Effect.sleep(timeout).pipe(
  Effect.andThen(
    existing
      ? Effect.void
      : cancel(form.id, { message: options?.timeoutMessage ?? "Form timed out without being answered" }).pipe(Effect.ignore),
  ),
  Effect.andThen(Deferred.await(entry.deferred)),
)
```

A joiner that times out then waits for the shared form to settle (via the owner's own timeout or a reply) instead of cancelling it. Update the comment on lines 187–190 to note the cancel is owner-only.

## Acceptance criteria

- A joined (`dedupePending`) ask with a timeout never calls `cancel` on the shared form; the original asker's pending question survives the joiner's timeout.
- Add a regression test in `packages/core/test/form.test.ts` that forks two deduped asks with different timeouts on the same form and asserts the shorter-timeout joiner resolving does not settle/cancel the owner's form (owner remains pending until its own timeout or a reply).
- Existing `Form ask bounds (#1883)` tests still pass.

## Out of scope

- Changing the timeout default or the dedupe matching predicate.
- Making a joiner return independently without waiting for the shared deferred (would change the ask's return contract).

## Summary

`packages/core` typecheck fails on a clean checkout of main (d9d67a785568bc681516c33222835255ede944b2), which makes the husky pre-push hook (turbo typecheck) reject **every** push touching the repo from a cold worktree — including changes whose own files typecheck clean.

Pristine detached worktree at d9d67a7855 + `bun install`, then in `packages/core`: `bun run typecheck` (`tsgo -b tsconfig.json tsconfig.tests.json`) reports exactly 4 errors, all in one file:

- `test/session-step.test.ts(3198,102)`: error TS2345
- `test/session-step.test.ts(3262,104)`: error TS2345
- `test/session-step.test.ts(3293,84)`: error TS2345
- `test/session-step.test.ts(3323,58)`: error TS2345

All four are the same shape: `Argument of type '() => Effect.Effect<void, unknown, unknown>' is not assignable to parameter of type 'Body<void, unknown, LLMClientService | Scope | Service | ...>'` — a test lambda's Effect carries `unknown` requirements where the harness `Body` type expects the session services.

The same 4 errors reproduce identically in a second worktree carrying an unrelated change (model-route/model-resolver), whose touched files add no type errors — the failure is pre-existing at base, not change-caused. On the long-lived primary clone the hook passes only because turbo replays a cached `@opencode/core:typecheck` success.

Any cold-worktree push is blocked by the pre-push hook until this is fixed; workers either stall or push with `--no-verify` (task 16740's PR does, with this issue as the record).

body:
## Finding

PR #2390 added the STT door (`POST /v1/audio/transcriptions`) with a 25 MiB upload cap, but the cap is only checked **after** the server handler has buffered the entire request body in memory. An oversized body is fully ingested before it can be rejected, so the cap does not bound memory on this route.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #2390 (merged, merge commit `25b50a485b00490618a669ce7582264bc668d0a6`), verified still present on current main `7bd4089641a53ec13d0fd38309260ad94e9f106b`.
- `packages/server/src/handlers/transcriptions.ts:37` (current main): `const body = yield* ctx.request.arrayBuffer.pipe(...)` — the whole request body is read with no size limit, no `content-length` pre-check, and no streaming byte counter.
- The body is then copied again through `new Response(body, ...).formData()` (same file, ~:40-42), and the file part is copied again via `value.arrayBuffer()` (:58).
- The 25 MiB cap lives in `packages/core/src/transcription-facade.ts` (`parseTranscriptionRequest`: `file.bytes.length > registration.maxUploadBytes` → 413 `audio_too_large`, registration `maxUploadBytes: 25 * MIB`). It can only run after the handler has already materialized the full body and the parsed file bytes.
- The façade's own parse tests (oversize → 413) exercise the post-buffer check only; no test posts a body larger than the cap through the HTTP handler.

## Why it matters

A client (or a buggy/malicious caller of the local server) can send a multipart body far larger than 25 MiB — hundreds of MiB or more — and the server will allocate it (multiple times: raw buffer, form parse, file bytes) before the typed 413 ever fires. That defeats the stated §5.2 purpose of the cap ("never silently unlimited") and is a memory-exhaustion surface on a brand-new route, of exactly the kind this repo has been closing elsewhere (bounded reads, `readJsonBody` byte caps, bounded WebSocket queues in #2378).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The transcriptions handler rejects an over-cap body **while reading**: a declared `content-length` above the cap is refused up front, and a streamed/chunked body is cut off at the cap with the same typed 413 `audio_too_large` envelope — without materializing the full body.
- [ ] The bound used is the resolved registration's `maxUploadBytes` (plus a small, named multipart-overhead allowance), not a second hard-coded number that can drift from the façade's cap.
- [ ] A server-level test posts a body larger than the cap through the HTTP handler and asserts the 413 envelope; a test with an under-cap body still transcribes normally.
- [ ] Behaviour for non-multipart and unparseable bodies is unchanged (400 `invalid_audio`).

---
Filed by pr-diff-review lane B (issue #1336 charter): PR-diff review of #2390. Cross-checked against current main before filing; dedupe searches (`transcriptions arrayBuffer`, `audio_too_large bound`) returned no covering issue.

body:
## Summary

In `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts`, `hedgeSlots` are acquired during `SessionHedge.race` (via `holdHedgeSlot(next)` at line 1002) and at line 975 (`holdHedgeSlot(input.model)`), but are only released inside `run(...).pipe(Effect.ensuring(...))` at lines 1067–1071.

If `SessionHedge.race` is interrupted or fails before `run(...)` is entered (for example, when a user cancels/aborts the session while waiting for the first token from either leg), `Effect.ensuring` on `run(...)` never executes and every slot in `hedgeSlots` is permanently leaked.

## Evidence

- `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts:962-975`: `hedgeSlots` is initialized and `holdHedgeSlot(input.model)` runs before `SessionHedge.race`.
- `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts:1002`: inside `SessionHedge.race({ start: ... })`, `Effect.tap(() => holdHedgeSlot(next))` acquires a membership slot for the hedge leg and pushes it onto `hedgeSlots`.
- `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts:1061-1072`: `hedgeSlots` is only released in `run(...).pipe(Effect.ensuring(...))`.
- `packages/core/src/model-route-membership.ts:71-88`: `tryAcquire` checks `state.inFlight >= limits.concurrent`.

## Why it matters

Each leaked slot permanently keeps `inFlight` incremented in `ModelRouteMembership` for the lifetime of the process. Once `inFlight` reaches `limits.concurrent`, all subsequent requests to that membership account stall for `waitMs` (5s) and fail over.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Wrap `holdHedgeSlot(input.model)`, `SessionHedge.race(...)`, and `run(...)` together in `Effect.ensuring` (or `Effect.acquireUseRelease` / `Scope`) so `hedgeSlots` are released on every exit path, including interruption or failure during `SessionHedge.race`.
- [ ] Add a unit test in `packages/core/test/session/` that interrupts `SessionStep.attempt` while `SessionHedge.race` is pending with a capped hedge target and asserts `ModelRouteMembership.accountSnapshot(...).inFlight === 0`.

## Related

- Distinct from #2383 (which tracks `holdHedgeSlot(input.model)` being unreachable for capped primaries).

title: fix(ci): check.yml is disabled_manually — the only typecheck job cannot run, so clean-main breakage is caught only by the pre-push hook

labels.name: kind/ci

labels.name: task/ci-investigation

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: app/script
labels.description: Package: script (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s

body:
## Evidence

Fresh `gh workflow list --all` on `developing-today-forks/opencode` (2026-11-13) reports:

```
check   disabled_manually   379524501
```

A manual dispatch is refused outright, so the workflow's only declared trigger cannot be exercised at all:

```
$ gh workflow run check.yml --repo developing-today-forks/opencode --ref main
could not create workflow dispatch event: HTTP 422: Cannot trigger a 'workflow_dispatch' on a disabled workflow
```

`check.yml` is the **only** place typecheck runs:

- `.github/workflows/check.yml:8-9` — `on:` / `  workflow_dispatch:` (dispatch-only)
- `.github/workflows/check.yml:21` — job `basic typecheck`
- `.github/workflows/check.yml:35` — `run: bun run check`
- `package.json:28` — `"check": "bun run lint && bun run typecheck"`; `package.json:27` — `"typecheck": "bun turbo typecheck --concurrency=3"`

No **active** workflow runs typecheck:

- `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs `bun turbo test` and `bun turbo build` only — a grep for `typecheck` in `test.yml` returns nothing, and `turbo.json`'s `build` task depends only on `transit`.
- `.github/workflows/deploy-changelog.yml`, `deploy-files.yml` and `deploy-update.yml` do run `bun typecheck`, but all three are themselves `disabled_manually`.

Since the push triggers were removed (#1635), `check` has run **zero** times: its last run was 2026-11-03 (`push`, run `41555628031`), and every run in its history predates that.

The policy still treats `check` as a live tier:

- `.github/ci-policy.md:53` — `basic typecheck` (workflow `check`) listed as a tier check on a `main` run
- `.github/ci-policy.md:68-69` — `check` is "the basic tier's core; **manual dispatch only** (`workflow_dispatch`)"
- `.github/ci-policy.md:85-92` — the release **main-gate** is `test`, `check`, `nix-eval`: "for the exact SHA being published, the latest completed run of each on branch `main` must have conclusion `success` … a failed, cancelled, or **missing** conclusion refuses the publish (fail-closed)"
- `.github/workflows/main-broken.yml:24` — `workflows: ["test", "check", "nix-eval"]`

This is the same defect class as **closed #2322** (`test` was found `disabled_manually` on 2026-11-12, re-enabled the same day, and a backstop guard was added at `.github/ci-policy.md:161`). That guard checks `test` only; `check`, `nix-eval` and `storybook` are all still `disabled_manually` today.

## Why it matters

The only remaining net for typecheck is each developer's local pre-push hook: `.husky/pre-push:20` runs `bun run check`, which blocks **every** branch when `main` is red. Clean-main typecheck breakage therefore accumulates with no CI signal and is discovered only at push time:

- **#2195 (OPEN)** — `prompt-family.test.ts` fails typecheck on main; its own title says it "blocks pre-push for every branch"
- **#2400 (OPEN)** — `filetype.test.ts` fails typecheck on main (`injections` / `injectionMapping` missing on the query union)
- recently closed #2355; historical #447, #659, #1177, #1489

Because `main-broken.yml` watches `check`, a disabled `check` also means the remediation chain can never file a typecheck breakage: typecheck is invisible to automation, while the other watched workflow (`test`) is not.

Secondary (latent) consequence: the release main-gate requires a completed `success` run of `check` and `nix-eval` on the SHA; both are `disabled_manually`, so their conclusion is always "missing", which the gate treats as fail-closed — any publish therefore needs `MAIN_GATE_OVERRIDE=1`, making the hotfix override the routine path. (The publish workflows are themselves `disabled_manually` in this fork today, so this is latent, not currently observed.)

## Suggested fix shape

1. Re-enable the workflow (`gh workflow enable check`) and dispatch a verification run on `main`.
2. Extend the #2322 backstop guard in `.github/ci-policy.md` (and the repo-health sweep check it names) from `test` alone to every dispatch-only tier workflow that must be runnable — at least `check` and `nix-eval`, and `storybook` — so a disabled validation workflow cannot silently remove a tier again.
3. If `check` is deliberately intended to stay disabled, record the decision and its replacement typecheck net in `ci-policy.md` first (the #2322 rule for `test`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `gh workflow list --all` reports `check` as `active`, and a dispatched run on `main` reaches the `basic typecheck` job.
- [ ] The `ci-policy.md` backstop guard covers `check` (and the other dispatch-only tier workflows), not just `test`.
- [ ] A typecheck regression on `main` is surfaced by CI rather than only by the local pre-push hook.

body:
## Agent-side slices of the interactive tier chooser + quota fallback card (split from developing-today-forks/openchamber#14)

OpenChamber issue #14 asks for an interactive model tier chooser (`/route`) and a live 429/quota fallback card, both rendered via `render.page` with `awaitAnswer`. Slice 1 landed in the OpenChamber repo: the card helpers (`buildTierChooserCard` / `buildQuotaFallbackCard` in `packages/web/server/lib/openchamber-control/tier-chooser-card.js`, PR #717) and the full `render.page` `awaitAnswer` protocol (`createPageAnswers` in `render-page.js`, the `openchamber_render` tool in `agent-tool/runtime.js`, `packages/ui/src/lib/renderPageAnswer.ts`).

The remaining slices cannot be implemented from the OpenChamber repo (verified twice: task 7021 blocked analysis 2026-11-03, and a fresh re-check on 2026-11-13 against openchamber main `ed6927594`):

- **Slice 2 (chooser trigger):** `pageAnswers.wait` is called only from the agent-tool action path (`render-page.js:184`) — a wait exists only while an agent tool call is in flight. Wiring the chooser therefore belongs to the agent runtime: when routing is bare/ambiguous (or the user runs `/route`), the agent calls `openchamber_render` with the helper's HTML and `awaitAnswer: true`, then applies the submitted `{ tier, model }` to the session's routing. The routing application point is this repo's routing modules (`packages/core/src/model-plan.ts`, `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/route-usage.ts`).
- **Slice 3 (429 fallback):** a grep of the OpenChamber web server finds no provider-turn seam (only GitHub API rate limits and notification throttling) — the provider turn is owned by this repo's runtime. The 429/quota-exceeded path during agent execution is where `buildQuotaFallbackCard` must be rendered and the submitted fallback (switch provider/tier, or wait for the known reset) applied, resuming in the same turn.

## Acceptance

- [ ] On a bare/ambiguous routing decision, the agent renders the tier chooser through `openchamber_render` (`render.page`, `awaitAnswer: true`) using the OpenChamber helper's card HTML, and the submitted `{ tier, model }` is applied to session routing.
- [ ] On a provider 429/quota-exceeded during execution, the agent renders the quota fallback card the same way and applies the submitted fallback in the same turn; typing in chat instead aborts the wait (`RENDER_PAGE_CLOSED_IN_CHAT_NOTE`) and the turn continues from the user's text.
- [ ] Tests cover the trigger and the answer application in this repo's routing/tool test suites.

Filed by queue lane any-b (task 7021 re-scope, 2026-11-13). The OpenChamber-side remainder, if Drew prefers it, is the alternative recorded on openchamber#14: permit a composer-registered page wait (client-supplied `callId`) in the OpenChamber server protocol.

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
## Evidence

Verified on current GitHub `main` (`c96e77b4b892022962855ec1f00a696a8453cb27`). In `packages/core/src/model-route-log.ts:577-586`, the layer creates `Queue.unbounded<Event>()`, offers every event with `Queue.offerUnsafe`, then runs one consumer that drains with `Queue.takeAll` and awaits `persist` before taking the next batch. `persist` writes attempts sequentially (`:288-299`). There is no queue capacity, producer backpressure, or bounded spill path.

While a database write is slow or stalled, producers continue to offer events and the sole consumer cannot drain the queue, so pending telemetry memory grows with event rate and stall duration. Current `packages/core/test/model-route-log.test.ts` covers asynchronous persistence and usage/restoration behavior, but has no stalled-writer or queue-growth-bound test.

## Why it matters

Route telemetry records decisions and attempts used by quota accounting and restoration. Keeping writes off the model-request path is useful, but an unbounded in-memory backlog turns a slow database into potentially unbounded process memory growth. The upcoming retry path can keep the single consumer occupied longer while new events continue to arrive.

## Related work and dedupe

OPEN #2331 and OPEN PR #2334 address retaining a batch after persistence errors (including partial-write safety); they do not bound pending events while the writer is slow or retrying. PR #2334 still uses `Queue.unbounded` and a single awaited consumer. This issue is the separate backlog-capacity problem; coordinate the writer changes with #2331/#2334. OPEN #2330 concerns the AI WebSocket inbound-frame queue, a different subsystem. Fresh all-state issue searches for this backlog/queue-bound gap found no matching issue, and the open PR search found only the related #2334.

## Acceptance criteria

- Bound in-memory pending telemetry while preserving asynchronous recording off the model-request path.
- Define and document an explicit, observable overflow policy (or a bounded durable spill strategy); avoid silent unbounded growth.
- Add a deterministic gated/stalled-writer test that offers events beyond the bound and verifies the memory/backlog limit and the chosen overflow behavior; verify normal writes still drain in order after the gate opens.
- Keep the failure-retry and partial-write guarantees in #2331/#2334 intact when bounding the queue.

body:
## Evidence

On fresh `origin/main` (`a172a12bb0bd80f4691380036a5374e1bc781534`), `packages/ai/src/route/transport/websocket.ts:232-257` states the socket callback cannot be paused and creates an unbounded Effect queue. It checks only each individual message against `MAX_FRAME_BYTES` (16 MiB at `:36,236-237`) and then offers it without any cumulative byte/item accounting (`:255-257`). A slow or stalled `messages` consumer therefore lets queued frames accumulate for the lifetime of the connection; the per-frame ceiling does not bound aggregate memory.

Reproduced against the actual `fromWebSocket` implementation in `packages/ai`: created a fake open `EventTarget` socket, opened the connection without consuming `connection.messages`, then synchronously dispatched 2,048 distinct 16 KiB text frames (32 MiB total). The queue accepted all frames; Node/Bun process measurements increased by ~27 MiB heap and ~57 MiB RSS. Existing tests cover WebSocket errors, close behavior, metadata, and consumer flow, but do not pin a cumulative inbound-queue bound or slow-consumer overflow behavior. The source comment's >1,000-frame burst explains why the implementation needs a deliberate finite burst allowance, not why aggregate memory should remain unbounded.

## Why it matters

A provider or configured WebSocket endpoint that produces frames faster than the protocol consumer can process can grow process memory without limit, potentially stalling or terminating the OpenCode process. This is distinct from the server-side PTY output outbox tracked by #2320: this is the client-side AI WebSocket transport's inbound frame queue.

## Acceptance criteria

- Bound total queued inbound WebSocket bytes (and, if needed, item count) independently of the per-frame 16 MiB maximum.
- On overflow, fail the stream and close/clean up the socket explicitly; do not silently drop protocol frames. Preserve the documented synchronous burst behavior within the chosen bound.
- Add deterministic tests for a stalled consumer, exact-boundary acceptance, overflow failure/close, and a >1,000-small-frame burst that remains within the supported allowance.

title: fix(server): bound JSON request bodies before buffering

body:
## Evidence

- `packages/server/src/handlers/completions.ts:48-57` reads `ctx.request.text()` into a complete string before JSON parsing or request validation. The same module uses `ctx.request.json` for the `/v1/messages` handlers (around lines 284 and 315).

- Thus a very large or chunked request is fully buffered before the endpoint can reject it as malformed/invalid. Concurrent requests can multiply that memory use and exhaust the OpenCode server process.

This is a separate surface from closed #1954, which capped the single DigitalOcean OAuth callback POST; it did not add a general inbound limit to the HTTP API.

## Suggested fix

Enforce a documented byte cap at the request-stream boundary before `text()` / `json()` materialization for JSON API routes, including the completion and messages façades. Return a deterministic 413 and stop consuming an oversized body; do not rely only on `Content-Length`, since chunked requests have no declared size. Keep the raw-body pass-through semantics for accepted completion requests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Oversized bodies are rejected before being fully buffered, for both declared-length and chunked requests.
- [ ] The limit applies consistently to the Node server and `ServerFetch.make` handler.
- [ ] Focused tests pin the 413 response and show ordinary completion/messages requests remain unchanged.

## Evidence

On current `origin/main` (`2e403986d17ee6d2450ceb04822617f295634661`), `packages/plugin-browser/src/files.ts:8-16` resolves each caller-supplied path against the project directory and opens the result directly. `resolve(directory, input)` allows both absolute paths to override the project directory and `..` paths to escape it; there is no containment check or `FileAccess` authorization in this path.

`packages/plugin-browser/src/tools.ts:24-29` invokes this read for both `files.upload` and `files.drop`, then sends the returned bytes to the connected browser at :29. The RPC schema accepts caller-provided paths at `packages/plugin-browser/src/rpc.ts:339-347`.

Reproduction: with the browser tool available, call `browser.files.upload` or `browser.files.drop` with a selected `tabID` and `paths: ["/etc/hostname"]` (or a readable path outside the project). The server resolves and opens that file, then transfers its bytes to the selected page. I reproduced the same `resolve` + `open` behavior in Node; running the package-level Effect probe was blocked because this checkout lacks the `effect` dependency. Existing `packages/plugin-browser/test/tools.test.ts` has no upload/drop path-scope or authorization case.

This is distinct from #2286: that issue covers the core read tool's symlink authorization path; browser uploads bypass `FileAccess` entirely through `BrowserFiles.read`.

## Why it matters

A browser-tool call can disclose any file readable by the OpenCode server process, including files outside the project, to a page selected by the caller. Browser permission does not scope the supplied filesystem paths.

## Acceptance criteria

- Upload and drop paths are checked against the applicable filesystem authorization boundary before any bytes are read.
- Absolute paths and traversal outside an authorized root are rejected or require the appropriate external-directory approval; symlink targets cannot bypass that decision.
- Add regression tests for an in-project file, an absolute outside path, `..` traversal, and an in-project symlink to an outside file.

body:
## Evidence

`packages/core/src/file-access.ts:94-103` resolves the requested path lexically and decides whether it is internal with `FSUtil.contains`. An internal path returns without an `externalDirectory` authorization target. `authorizeRead()` then asserts only the lexical `read` resource at `:149-159`.

The read tool passes `target.absolute` to `reader.read()` at `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/read.ts:49-56`; the filesystem read follows symlinks. A symlink located inside the workspace can therefore point outside it while the authorization path remains classified as internal.

Reproduction shape: create `workspace/secret.txt` as a symlink to `outside/secret.txt`, deny or ask for `external_directory`, and request a read of `secret.txt`. The path check considers it internal, while normal filesystem resolution reads the outside file. A local filesystem probe confirmed the lexical path is under the workspace, `realpath` is outside it, and reading the lexical path returns the outside file's contents. Existing `packages/core/test/file-access-path.test.ts` exercises lexical paths but has no symlink containment case.

## Why it matters

The external-directory permission is an approval boundary for workspace tools. A workspace symlink can expose files outside the workspace without triggering that approval, including when the external path would otherwise be denied or require user approval.

## Acceptance criteria

- A read through an in-workspace symlink to an outside file is rejected or requires the appropriate `external_directory` approval before the outside contents are read.
- Add regression coverage for both an external-target symlink and an in-workspace-target symlink, preserving intended internal access.
- Ensure the authorization decision and the filesystem operation cannot be trivially separated by changing a symlink between checking and use; document the chosen symlink policy for paths that do not yet exist.

title: fix(server): compare Basic-auth passwords in constant time

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

body:
## Evidence

`packages/server/src/auth.ts:33-36` accepts the configured server password with a direct JavaScript string equality check (`password === config.password.value`). This is the Basic-auth credential path used by requests to a password-protected server. The adjacent signed-session path uses `timingSafeEqual` in `verifySession`, so the two accepted credential forms have different comparison behavior.

An attacker able to make repeated requests to a reachable password-protected server can potentially use comparison timing to test password prefixes. No timing reproduction was run; the finding is based on the direct comparison in the active authorization path.

## Suggested fix

Use a constant-time comparison for the configured password, handling unequal lengths safely (for example, compare fixed-size digests or otherwise ensure `timingSafeEqual` receives equal-length buffers). Keep username matching and session-token verification semantics unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- Basic-auth password comparison does not use ordinary string equality on the secret.
- Correct passwords remain accepted; wrong passwords, including same-length and different-length values, are rejected.
- Existing session token verification, password rotation revocation, and unauthorized response behavior remain unchanged.
- Add focused tests for the comparison helper and retain the existing server auth tests.

title: fix(server): reject weak validators for If-Range requests

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

body:
## Evidence
On main at 4ddc98738fbeb4de80091c80a4bc0b44611334fd, `packages/server/src/handlers/fs.ts:69-72` emits a weak `W/"size-mtime"` ETag. `matchesIfRange` at lines 119-126 strips the weak prefix from both the request and current ETag, then treats equal values as a match. Lines 82-96 consequently return `206 Partial Content` for a `Range` request with `If-Range: W/"..."` (or its stripped strong-looking equivalent), instead of ignoring the range.

If-Range entity tags require strong comparison (RFC 9110 §13.1.5); a weak entity tag cannot match. A client resuming a changed file could combine bytes from different versions if its size and timestamp happen to match. This is distinct from #1646, which concerned invalid Range handling in the separate files worker.

## Acceptance criteria
- Entity-tag If-Range comparisons use strong comparison; a weak request or current validator does not match and a valid Range request gets the full `200` response.
- Preserve ordinary Range requests without If-Range and the existing date-validator behavior, and add regression coverage for weak and strong-looking request tags against the weak emitted ETag.

Triage queue: not enqueued by this improvement-issue creator run; the standing coverage reconciliation can enqueue it.

title: Quota-aware walling: bench providers whose binding window is <1% and failing with quota errors

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: New feature or capability request

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

labels.name: epic/opencode-platform
labels.description: Epic: opencode-platform - all issues of this effort carry it

body:
## Doctrine (Drew, 2026-11-10)

Providers are never put in `disabled_providers` for quota reasons. The fork owns walling: it has the measured quota (the same read the gatherer publishes) and it sees every failure. A provider whose binding window is nearly gone **and** is failing must be treated as walled by the router itself.

Drew's words: "you don't put models to disabled — the opencode fork should know the quota and see the failures and figure out that it's below 1pct and failing every time or has a quota related error". And on the concrete case: "$0.05 left is walled, nothing will run."

## Today's evidence (2026-11-10, live reads)

- Command Code monthly measures **99.513% used ($9.95 / $10 — $0.05 left)**; its 5h reads 0/3, weekly 64.6%.
- The quota read still reports the provider state as **"ok"**; it is not in `disabled_providers` (removed 2026-11-06 on Drew's order, in reliance on the availability system).
- Its seats remain live in the plan pools (deepseek-flash-plan weight 1, deepseek-pro-plan weight 0.5), so sessions can still be routed onto a pool that cannot pay for a real call.
- #1828's availability state machine benches on a classified quota/balance failure and releases on measured increase — but the bench decision does not use the measured quota level itself: at <1% remaining the router keeps offering the seats until failures accumulate, one dribbling session at a time.

## Expected behavior

1. The route layer consumes the measured quota per provider (binding window = the window that actually gates calls, e.g. monthly for Command Code).
2. When the binding window measures **<1% remaining** AND the provider is returning quota-class errors (or failing every attempt), the provider is **walled immediately**: benched, seats not offered, no further attempts dribbled into it.
3. Rejoin is the existing measured-increase path (window reset or balance increase re-admits automatically) — never a config edit, never `disabled_providers`.
4. The wall state is visible in the route/quota surfaces as walled-below-1%, distinct from a generic error bench, so reports stop describing a dead pool as "ok / not walled".

## Acceptance

- With a provider at <1% on its binding window and quota-class failures present, route decisions show it walled with zero new attempts routed to it.
- A measured increase on the binding window re-admits it with no config change.
- Command Code today would read as walled under this rule ($0.05 of $10 left).

title: Router: model the opendesign membership caps (10 concurrent, 100/min) — wait briefly, then fall to the next leg

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: epic/opencode-platform
labels.description: Epic: opencode-platform - all issues of this effort carry it

body:
## Problem

The Open Design account (served through the `opendesign` provider; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is the seat the workhorse route draws on) has hard membership caps the router does not model:

- **10 concurrent** requests
- **100 requests/minute**

On 2026-11-10 ~19:00–19:20Z the workhorse route drew heavily on this account and the caps burst: **1,365 route attempts** in the laptop router's attempt ledger failed with `[code=tier_limit_exceeded] membership concurrency limit exceeded: 11/10` / `membership rpm limit exceeded: 101/100`, and **55 of 62 fleet sessions errored** in a single orchestration pass. The error is session-visible today, so a per-account cap turns into a fleet-wide wall.

## Directive (Drew, 2026-11-10, with his clarification the same day)

Integrate the limit into the fork's router so the account is used up to its caps and never past them:

1. **The config lands on the provider**: the caps (10 concurrent, 100/minute) are declared on the `opendesign` provider definition — not per route, not per leaf, not per model.
2. **One shared accumulator across all uses**: a single counter set for the provider. Every request that lands on `opendesign` — any route, any model it serves, any session — draws from the same concurrency count and the same per-minute window, because it is one membership account. (The retired sibling IDs design-code / code-design / open-design all pointed at this same account/proxy; if any alias is ever re-enabled it must share this same accumulator, keyed on the account, not the provider-ID string.)
3. **Short wait when appropriate**: when a cap is momentarily hit and a slot frees (or the window/reset lands) within a short bounded wait, wait for the slot instead of failing.
4. **Fall back to the next leg**: when the wait would exceed the bound, fail over to the next leg in the route silently — the session must never see `tier_limit_exceeded` from this provider.
5. **Backstop from the upstream error**: if a `tier_limit_exceeded` still arrives (races, other clients), parse its reset time and hold the provider out of rotation until then (extends the provider-availability rules: rate limit → stop until retry-after).

## Acceptance

- A burst of >10 concurrent / >100-per-minute draws on `opendesign` — spread across multiple routes and models — produces **zero session-visible** `tier_limit_exceeded` errors; the attempt ledger shows waits/failovers instead, and the shared accumulator never exceeds 10 in-flight / 100 starts per minute.
- Caps are declared once, on the provider definition; the accumulator is keyed to the account so aliases share it.
- Tests cover: shared concurrency cap across routes, shared per-minute window across models, short-wait path taken when a slot frees in time, failover path taken when it does not.

title: test(core): tool-schema meta-validation inventory is hand-maintained with no completeness check — a new built-in tool escapes #1668 validation silently (#1674 follow-up)

body:
## Finding

The draft-2020-12 meta-validation added by PR #1674 (closing #1668) validates only a **hand-maintained mirror list** of built-in tools, and nothing checks that list for completeness — so the next built-in tool added to the registry silently escapes the exact validation #1668 asked for, with the suite staying green.

- `packages/core/test/tool-schema.test.ts:35-68` (current main): `builtinInputs` is a literal array of 33 `{ name, input }` entries, hand-imported from the tool plugin modules. The meta-validation test at `tool-schema.test.ts:587` loops over exactly this array and nothing else.
- The tools themselves are registered on at least two independent surfaces, neither of which the test reads: the `PluginInternal` `pre` list in `packages/core/src/plugin/internal.ts` (PatchTool, EditTool, GlobTool, GrepTool, OpenCodeTools, McpResourceTools, MessagingTools, QuestionTool, ReadTool, ShellTool, PtyTool, McpxTool, SkillTool, SubagentTool, WebFetchTool, WebSearchTool, WriteTool, PlanInfoPlugin, …) and `ConfigModelRoutesPlugin`'s editor registrations in `packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts:88-91` (`RouteUsageTool.add`, `RouteAdjustTool.add`, `RouteStatsTool.add`).
- The list is already visibly a freehand copy rather than a derivation: its label for the mcpx observe tool is `"opencode_mcpx_observe"` (tool-schema.test.ts:45) while the tool registers as `"mcpx_observe"` (`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/mcpx.ts`). Harmless today — the label only feeds the synthetic `definition()` name and Ajv error text — but it proves nothing mechanical ties the list to the registry it claims to inventory.
- Contrast with the standard this repo set for itself the same week: the gate registry from #1527 / PR #1670 fails CI when a gate script exists but is unregistered (`unregistered-gate` in `script/gate-harness.ts`). The tool-schema inventory has no equivalent rule in either direction.

I verified the list is complete *today* (33 entries; counts per plugin match the `draft.add` registrations in `opencode.ts` — 6 tools, `mcpx.ts` — 5, `mcp-resource.ts` — 2, `messaging.ts` — 3, plus the single-input plugins and the three route tools). The defect is structural: completeness is asserted by hand, so it decays silently on the next tool.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1674 — "test(core): meta-validate built-in tool schemas", merged, merge commit `a92341f2e05b77a98b86e165affe076579566ba5` (head `b5bca31dfa99756a8cdfee605b207a046f4c68c4`). It closed #1668 ("meta-validate **every** built-in tool schema…"). To make the schemas reachable it exported named inputs (`ListInput`/`ReadInput`, `ExecInput`/`DiscoverInput`/`ObserveInput`/`ProjectInput`/`RetractInput`, `WorktreeListInput`) and enumerated them in the test — the enumeration step is the unguarded part.
- Current main `2d11e0f649436d6c4d20a64ce13fd7e0501bdd96` (verified twice via the commits API): `builtinInputs` at `packages/core/test/tool-schema.test.ts:35`, test at `:587`; registration surfaces at `packages/core/src/plugin/internal.ts` (`pre` list) and `packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts:88-91` — no cross-reference from the test to either.
- Dedupe: searched open + closed issues for "tool-schema inventory", "meta-validate built-in", "convertSchema"-adjacent test terms (2026-11-06). #1668 is CLOSED by the source PR (this is a follow-up on its implementation's durability, not a re-file); nothing asks for a completeness check on the inventory.

## Why it matters

#1668 exists because an invalid built-in schema reached the Anthropic door unnamed (#1550). The meta-validation is the regression net for that class. A net whose coverage list is maintained by memory fails in the worst way — silently, on exactly the new-tool change most likely to introduce a fresh invalid schema, while the test name ("built-in tool input schemas satisfy the official draft 2020-12 meta-schema") keeps claiming full coverage.

## Acceptance criteria

- The suite fails when a built-in tool is registered (on either surface above — the `PluginInternal` tool plugins or the model-routes editor tools) without a corresponding meta-validated entry, and passes on current main with the existing 33.
- The mechanism is mechanical, not a second hand-list: e.g. derive the inventory from the registered plugins/tools, or assert the hand list equals a registry-derived set of tool names/inputs. (If full derivation is impractical for the editor-registered route tools, a registry-derived check for the `PluginInternal` surface plus a pinned count/names assertion for the route tools is acceptable — say which in the change.)
- The existing meta-validation behavior is unchanged: every currently listed schema still goes through `definition()` + Ajv 2020-12 validation + the Anthropic-target `convertSchema` exercise.
- A negative control demonstrates the new check: adding (temporarily) a tool registration or removing one inventory entry turns the suite red.

title: [priority: very high] bug: subsession `question` call stalls child AND foreground parent silently — no notification, and retry machinery re-asks the identical question

body:
## Finding

When a subsession (child) session calls the `question` tool, the child blocks — and a parent waiting on a foreground `subagent` call blocks with it — **indefinitely and silently**. Nothing notifies the parent: no message in the parent's transcript, no form on the parent session (`GET /api/session/<parent>/form` → `[]`). The form waits on the *child* session for an external actor (UI or API client) that, in a detached tree, may never come.

## Workshop evidence

Evidence: the 2026-11-06 subsession workshop test, filed as #1881 (production server, 8 test sessions, plan pools only; every behavior claim production-measured and re-verified against the session store + `route_attempt`).

- The question child's `question` call ("Which color?", options Red/Blue) sat in `status=running` for **10+ minutes**; the parent's foreground `subagent` call blocked the whole time; zero notification anywhere.
- Left alone, the stall **degrades into a loop**: ~25 minutes later the call ended in `status=error`; session-retry machinery resumed both sessions; the child received its task re-delivered as a fresh user message and **re-asked the identical question** (stall #2), while the parent relaunched the child via the `sessionID` continuation path. Unanswered, this burns turns producing nothing.
- An external answer unblocks instantly (see #1881 Q6): `POST /api/session/<child>/form/<id>/reply` → 204, child completed, parent relayed the result. The machinery to answer exists — the failure is that nobody is told there is a question.

## Desired behavior (minimum)

- A pending `question` form in a child session must be **surfaced to its parent session** (and/or produce an observable event the parent/orchestrator can act on) — never a silent stall of the foreground chain.
- The question call must have a **bounded lifetime**: on timeout it resolves with a visible, handleable cancellation/timeout result instead of an opaque error that retry machinery treats as a fresh task.
- Retry/resume must **not re-ask an identical unanswered question** without an answer or an explicit escalation (dedupe identical pending questions across resume).

## Related

- Question escalation to the parent (parent answers, passes up the stack): filed separately as a feature.
- API launch mode that disables `question` entirely: filed separately as a feature.

## Acceptance sketch

- Repro of the workshop scenario: child asks via `question`, parent foreground-waits → parent is observably notified within seconds, or the call resolves by timeout with a handleable result.
- After a forced error + session resume, the child does not re-issue the identical question.
- Regression tests name their oracle: session-store state + form endpoints before/after.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproducing the workshop scenario (child session calls `question`, parent foreground-waits on a subagent call) observably notifies the parent within seconds, or the question call resolves by a bounded timeout with a visible, handleable result.
- [ ] After a forced error and session resume, the child does not re-issue an identical unanswered question.
- [ ] Regression tests cover both behaviors and name their oracle (session-store state and form endpoints before/after, per the issue's acceptance sketch).
- [ ] No silent indefinite stall remains: a pending question in a detached tree is always either surfaced, timed out, or escalated.

body:
## Audit follow-up — antigravity + vibe credential paths spawn `secret-tool`; antigravity refresh requires the `agy` binary

Source: 2026-11-06 provider audit (Audit B: binary-required providers). The wire-only doctrine ("no provider the fleet uses requires a local binary") does **not** hold on the credential path for the two keyring-based doors. Whole-tree check: `grep -rnE "child_process|Bun.spawn|execa"` over `packages/ai/src/{providers,protocols,route}` returns exactly two files — these two.

### `antigravity-direct` (source id `antigravity`) — hard dependency

Inference is wire (`POST daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal:streamGenerateContent`). The credential path is not:

- `antigravity-auth.ts:103-111`: every credential load dynamically imports `node:child_process` and `execFile`s `secret-tool lookup service gemini username antigravity` (15s timeout). `findSecretTool()` searches `$SECRET_TOOL_PATH`, `$PATH`, `/nix/store/*libsecret*/bin/secret-tool` and **throws `secret-tool not found`** — no non-binary credential tier (static override aside).
- Token refresh requires the `agy` **binary file**: `findAgyBinary()` probes `$AGY_BIN`, `~/.gemini/bin/agy`, `/run/current-system/sw/bin/agy`; `binaryIntel()` reads its bytes to extract GOCSPX OAuth client-secret candidates; `refresh()` fails hard (`could not extract OAuth client secret from agy binary`) when absent. A still-valid token works without it; an expired one cannot be refreshed. (The binary is read, never executed; the CLI also owns writing the keyring credential.)
- Same pattern in the quota layer: `quota/providers/antigravity.ts:124` also `execFile`s `secret-tool` (graceful `null` there).

### `vibe-direct` (source id `vibe`) — fallback tier that is the deployed tier

Inference is wire (MistralChat route, `api.mistral.ai/v1`); no vibe subprocess exists. But `vibe.ts:133` wires `VibeAuth.vibeAuth`, whose tier-4 resolution (`vibe-auth.ts:105-118`) `execFile`s `secret-tool lookup`. It is nominally a fallback (env → `~/.vibe/.env` → keyring, failures fall through) — **except** the fleet config deliberately keeps `MISTRAL_API_KEY` out of the server env (#1653) so the deployed door falls through to the keyring sign-in key: in actual fleet use, the credential is obtained by spawning `secret-tool`.

### Desired end state

Credential resolution that reads what the one-time CLI sign-in provisioned **without spawning a helper binary** — e.g. read the keyring via a Secret Service D-Bus library binding instead of the `secret-tool` subprocess, or make a file/env tier the deployed default with the keyring tier removed. `claude-code` / `commandcode` already prove the read-in-place pattern (file read only, zero spawns). For antigravity refresh, the agy-binary byte-extraction should be replaced by a provisioned client-secret source (vaulted at sign-in time) so refresh survives the CLI's absence.

Related: `muse-direct`'s layer-2 dependency (its local muse-proxy spawns the Muse CLI) is tracked with the proxy decommission pass in developing-today/code, not here.

## Acceptance criteria
- The credential paths for the antigravity and vibe providers no longer hard-require a local binary (`secret-tool` / `agy`) without a documented fallback tier, OR the wire-only doctrine is amended in writing to name these two credential-path exceptions explicitly.
- On a host without `secret-tool`, a credential load for each affected provider either succeeds via the fallback tier or fails with an error that names the missing binary and the supported alternatives (no opaque throw).
- Regression coverage exists for the no-binary path (simulated missing `secret-tool`) for both providers.
