body:
## Provider naming & ownership convention — design (Drew directive 2026-11-06)

Drew: *"any other alignments for the providers as a whole. if there's a cleaner structure like direct/ or leading _ or _.provider or something. if we know it's ours then we don't need to say direct."*

This issue is the design home for the provider-id convention. It broadens #1817 (claude-code → claude-direct) — **no renames are executed here**; Drew rules on the convention first, then the rename map below is applied as one coordinated pass.

### Principle

A provider id should say **whose it is**. "-direct" describes a mechanism (wire emulation); if the id itself marks fleet ownership, the mechanism suffix is noise. Official upstream ids are never renamed.

### Inventory (verified 2026-11-06: fork `packages/ai/src/providers/` + fleet config `developing-today/code .opencode/opencode.jsonc`)

**OURS — fleet-built, fork source (header comments state the direct-provider pattern verbatim):**

| Config id (runtime) | Source id (`ProviderID.make`) | Package | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claude-code` | `claude-code` | `providers/claude-code.ts` | wire emulation of the Claude Code CLI (#6117) |
| `antigravity-direct` | `antigravity` | `providers/antigravity.ts` | config id ≠ source id — the split this convention ends |
| `vibe-direct` | `vibe` | `providers/vibe.ts` | config id ≠ source id, same split |
| `commandcode` | `commandcode` | `providers/commandcode.ts` | quota registry spells it `command-code` — second split |
| `meta` (native pkg) | `meta` | `providers/meta.ts` | ⚠️ config id `meta` currently binds `@ai-sdk/openai` → api.meta.ai instead — which "meta" is canonical must be settled before any rename (see map) |

**OURS — fleet-configured doors (no fork code; official SDK packages + our config):**

| Config id | Binding | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `muse-direct` | `@ai-sdk/openai` → local muse-proxy `127.0.0.1:18747` | fleet-created id; fronts a local proxy (infra fate tracked by the decommission pass, not this issue) |
| `opendesign` | `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` → amr-link.open-design.ai | names a third-party service |
| `cline-pass` | `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` | names a third-party service |

**OFFICIAL — upstream, used as-is, ids untouchable:** the rest of `packages/ai/src/providers/` (`anthropic`, `openai`, `mistral`, `deepseek`, `google`, `groq`, `openrouter`, `xai`, `zai`, … 45 source ids total). Fleet-used today include `openai`, `mistral`, `deepseek`; `groq`/`openrouter` are defined but disabled. A separate audit (running in parallel) verifies no fleet edits live inside official provider files and that no used provider spawns a binary.

**RETIRED ids (definitions retained, disabled, per the switchboard rule):** `antigravity-ls`, `antigravity-agy`. Plus catalog tombstones in `disabled_providers` (`google`, `google-vertex`, `cloudflare-ai-gateway`, `cloudflare-workers-ai`, `github-copilot`) whose definitions are deleted but whose entries must stay.

**Quota-layer ids** (`packages/ai/src/quota/providers/`): `antigravity`, `claude` (serves provider `claude-code`), `cline-pass`, `codex` (the OpenAI plan pool), `command-code`, `deepseek`, `groq`, `meta`, `mistral`, `opencode-go`, `opendesign`, `openrouter`, `turso`. Two of these already disagree with their provider ids (`claude`, `command-code`) — the convention pass should unify them via the alias mechanism, not leave a third naming layer.

### Constraints (why most shapes fail)

- The provider id is the **first segment of every leaf string** `provider/model` in routes, sessions, and config. **An id containing `/` is mechanically impossible** — the parser splits on the first slash. This kills the `direct/` namespace shape outright.
- Ids are keys in: config provider blocks, `disabled_providers`, route leaves, `session_message`/`route_health` rows, the quota registry (ids + aliases), the pm-stack quota gatherer, logs and dashboards. A rename is a coordinated config + registry change; historical DB rows keep the old id (they are history, not pointers).
- Id grammar in the wild is lowercase words + dashes (`zai-coding-plan`). Any marker must survive JSON keys, URLs, shell, and SQL unchanged.

### Candidate evaluation

| Shape | Example | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Slash namespace | `direct/claude` | **Impossible** — slash is the leaf separator |
| Mechanism prefix | `direct-claude` | Says "direct", not "ours" — the thing Drew wants to drop |
| Leading underscore | `_claude` | Legal, sorts first, clearly non-catalog; but reads as *private/internal* in most ecosystems and looks like a temporary hack in logs/URLs |
| `.provider` suffix | `claude.provider` | Dots already occur in **model** ids (`claude-haiku-5.5`), so leaf strings get harder to eyeball; and it says "is a provider" (everything here is), not "ours" |
| `_.` compound | `_.claude` | Stacks both oddities; same private connotation |
| **Ownership prefix `dt-`** | `dt-claude` | **Recommended.** Short, dash-grammar native, unmistakably ours (developing-today), collision with any future upstream id is essentially impossible, the whole family sorts/groups together everywhere ids are listed |

Fallback if Drew prefers plain English over the org mark: `ours-` (same mechanics, one syllable longer, slightly more generic if configs are ever shared).

### Rename map (under the recommended `dt-` convention)

| Current | Proposed | Touches |
|---|---|---|
| `claude-code` | `dt-claude` | source id, config block, 4+ leaves, quota id `claude` becomes an alias of `dt-claude` |
| `antigravity-direct` / `antigravity` | `dt-antigravity` | config + source ids **converge**; leaves; quota id follows |
| `vibe-direct` / `vibe` | `dt-vibe` | config + source converge; mistral-plan membership |
| `commandcode` | `dt-commandcode` | source + config; quota `command-code` becomes alias — spelling split closed |
| `meta` (native pkg) | `dt-meta` | ⚠️ sequence AFTER deciding canonical "meta": today config `meta` = SDK door to api.meta.ai while the native package is unused by that block. Rename must not silently rebind the config door |
| `muse-direct` | `dt-muse` | config id only (door definition unchanged) |
| `opendesign`, `cline-pass` | **unchanged** (proposal) | fleet-configured but they name third-party services, like `openrouter`; mark them only if Drew wants every fleet-config id badged |
| `antigravity-ls`, `antigravity-agy` | unchanged | retired + disabled; renaming dead definitions is churn with zero runtime effect |
| all official ids | unchanged | by the principle above |

### Migration notes

1. Order: fork first (source `ProviderID.make` + quota registry, keeping old ids as quota **aliases** for continuity), then the code-repo config (provider blocks, `disabled_providers`, every route leaf), then deploy + server restart, verified via `GET /api/provider`.
2. The config file's deployed copies must stay byte-identical through the change (single repo edit + normal deploy; regenerate the runtime overlay as part of the same pass — the overlay staleness bit us on 2026-11-06).
3. Historical `session_message` / `route_health` rows keep old ids; dashboards should treat the rename map as the join key for pre/post comparisons.
4. Docs/comments that narrate the old ids get a dated rename note, not a rewrite of history.
5. One PR per repo, merge commits only; the whole map lands atomically enough that no route ever names a non-existent provider (config and fork deploy together, or config ships with both ids defined for one release window if sequencing demands it).

### Related workstreams (not this issue)

- Audit: fleet edits inside official provider files (report + follow-ups).
- Audit: binary-required providers among those the fleet uses (wire-only doctrine check).
- Proxy-infra decommission: the retired proxy lineage (`bin/*-proxy.mjs` family, :18749/:18751 units) across opencode / openchamber / code.

Drew rules on: (a) `dt-` vs `ours-` vs another marker; (b) whether fleet-configured service doors (`opendesign`, `cline-pass`) get badged; (c) canonical "meta" before its rename line is scheduled.

## Acceptance criteria
- A single provider naming & ownership convention is recorded as decided on this issue (the marker scheme for fleet-built providers, and the rule that official upstream ids are never renamed).
- A complete rename map (config id, source id, package) for every fleet-built provider is attached to this issue before any rename executes.
- Renames, when executed, land as one coordinated pass across the fork and the fleet config in developing-today/code, with a compat/migration note for stored route-health and session rows keyed by old ids.

body:
Parent: #1146

## Problem

OpenCode has no voice input: a user who wants to speak a prompt must leave the tool, transcribe elsewhere, and paste text back. Speech-to-text is a provider-shaped problem — multiple STT providers with different formats, pricing, and streaming behavior — which is exactly what the #1146 façade pattern is for: ONE ingestion code path on a common endpoint, providers converting results into the supported format passing through as much as possible, and the provider/façade layer handling key registration and renewal, so no client ever holds a transcription provider's key.

## Drew's ask (paraphrased)

Voice in OpenCode: a user submits audio inside OpenCode and gets a transcript back (speech-to-text).

## Expanded feature design (to be designed, not yet scoped for build)

1. **Façade endpoint.** Candidate shape: an OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions`-style route on the OpenCode server, following the façade rule from #1146 — the request names a concrete provider/model ref (pass-through) or a route name resolved through the same selection machinery as chat traffic. Response passes through as much provider detail as possible (segments, word timings, language detection, confidence) inside a normalized envelope, rather than flattening to bare text.
2. **Provider registry for STT backends**, mirroring the embeddings registry precedent (#1554): backends registered by name, config-gated (`disabled_providers`-style), keys registered and renewed by the provider/façade layer — clients authenticate to the server once with existing server auth.
3. **Input modes.** (a) File input: an existing audio file attached/submitted in the session. (b) Recorded input: capture from the microphone inside OpenCode (TUI) and OpenChamber, with clear recording state, cancel, and a review-before-send step. The design covers format/codec acceptance, size/duration caps (per the bounded-by-default contract, #1127), and what happens to the audio after transcription (retention vs discard — default discard should be considered).
4. **Streaming partial transcripts.** Providers that support streaming return partial hypotheses; the design covers how partials stream through the façade (SSE shape consistent with the chat façades' streaming translation) and how the client renders an updating transcript without committing partial text to the session prematurely.
5. **How the transcript lands in the session.** Candidate shapes: transcript inserted into the composer for editing before send (default candidate — voice as an input method, not an auto-send), transcript attached as a message part with provenance (provider, model, duration), or both. Editing-before-send matters: STT errors in code identifiers are common, so the design should treat the raw transcript as draft input unless the user opts into direct submit.
6. **Accounting parity.** Transcription calls through the façade land in the route_attempt ledger discipline like other façade traffic, so usage/quota accounting is uniform.
7. **Client scope.** OpenCode TUI: record/attach affordance, waveform/recording indicator, transcript insertion. OpenChamber: equivalent capture using its own media permissions path. Shared behavior (endpoint, envelope, error shapes) is defined once by the façade design; clients differ only in capture/rendering.

## Open questions

- Which STT providers are first-class candidates (hosted APIs vs local/on-device models, e.g. a Whisper-class local backend baked into the fork like the embeddings direction in #1554)?
- What is the streaming-partial contract — do we normalize provider partial formats into one event grammar, and what fidelity is lost?
- Language handling: auto-detect vs explicit hint vs per-session setting?
- Diarization / speaker labels: in scope for the envelope even if no first provider supplies them?
- Maximum audio length and the chunking story for long recordings (meetings vs prompts are different products — is long-form in scope or explicitly out)?
- Privacy posture: which providers retain submitted audio, and does the registry need a per-backend "audio leaves the machine" flag surfaced in config?

## Acceptance shape

A design doc in the repo (`doc/`) covering: the façade endpoint + envelope, the STT registry shape and key handling, file vs recorded input flows for OpenCode and OpenChamber, the streaming-partial contract, and the transcript-into-session UX decision. Reviewed and linked from #1146.

## Expansion path

From the accepted design, file implementation tickets per step: (1) façade transcriptions route + registry skeleton, (2) one ticket per STT backend, (3) OpenCode TUI capture + transcript insertion, (4) OpenChamber capture + insertion, (5) streaming partials (may be its own phase after batch transcription ships), (6) ledger parity + parity tests against provider-native responses.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The design covers speech-to-text providers behind the façade (request/response shape aligned to the /v1/audio/transcriptions model).
- [ ] Streaming vs batch expectations and provider error mapping are specified.
- [ ] An implementation follow-up issue is filed if the design is adopted.

`bin/commandcode-proxy.mjs` (developing-today/code), port 18748, `commandcode-proxy.service` active/running. Front: `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/models`. Backend: CommandCode CLI with resident ACP sessions (conversations map to ACP threads — warm-door state, §9.2).

The hosted CommandCode API rejects the current plan; the CLI is the ONLY working route. Backend retirement for this door is blocked on a plan/API change, not on façade work. This issue is therefore FRONT-only: callers repoint to the façade for shape/selection, while the provider backend continues to reach the CLI — explicitly, not by accident. body:
**Decision for Drew (one line):** approve the delivery mechanism — one versioned `std` namespace, evaluated program-side inside the confined interpreter (not scattered globals, not import syntax in the interpreter) — for the Code Mode helper library you adopted on code#607 / #765?

## Summary

#765 records Drew's decisions (from developing-today/code#607): adopt an opt-in import map for scripts, keep arbitrary remote imports allowed by default, and adopt a small standard helper library for Code Mode `execute`. It does not specify a mechanism. This design is the mechanism, grounded in the interpreter as it exists on current main:

- **Extensions can't host the library.** `packages/codemode/src/extension.ts` exposes host functions as globals across a copy-only boundary ("values crossing in either direction are converted, never shared… Extension calls are not tool calls"). `mapLimit`/`retry` need to drive *program* callbacks with interpreter semantics (cooperative timeout, the 10,000 pending-promise cap in `packages/codemode/src/interpreter/limits.ts`); program `Value`s don't cross that boundary as callables. The only extension wired today is `fetch` (`packages/core/src/codemode/web.ts`); runtime assembly is `packages/core/src/codemode/tool.ts` (`CodeMode.make({ tools, extensions: [CodeModeWeb.extension], hooks })`).
- **Proposal:** `CodeMode.make` gains a `libraries` option — a named, versioned library whose source is JavaScript in the interpreter's supported subset, evaluated in the program scope and bound to one frozen global: `std`, with `std.version` readable and the version printed in the Code Mode instructions (`packages/core/src/codemode/instructions.ts`). Additive-only within a major version. Diagnostic source locations must not shift.
- **v1 surface:** `bind` (default arguments for a tool callable or a whole namespace), `chunk`, `uniqBy`, `keyBy`, `pick`, `omit` (phase 1); one host primitive — a capped `sleep` extension, wrapped as `std.sleep` — plus `mapLimit`, `retry`, `withTimeout` (phase 2). `withTimeout` bounds waiting, **not** execution: it cannot cancel an admitted tool call, and the instructions listing must say so.
- **Import maps stay out of the interpreter.** Confinement is its purpose; a map for a language with no imports is a no-op. The import-map half lands in mcpx's Deno launcher (developing-today/code) under #765 as the set's origin — see the set remainder below. The design doc (§5) specifies the contract: no map = behaviour unchanged; open mode (default) pins mapped specifiers and allows the rest; closed mode (opt-in) refuses unmapped remote specifiers; the launcher never resolves/installs packages itself.

Full design: `files/designs/opencode-codemode-stdlib.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace (problem, evidence, alternatives — host extension globals, interpreter imports, mcpx-projected helpers, invisible prelude — risks, open questions).

## Phased breakdown

1. **Phase 1 — library mechanism + pure helpers** (filed as a sub-issue of this issue, enqueued): `libraries` option in `@opencode/codemode`, std v1.0.0 pure set, core wiring, instructions listing, tests, `interpreter-support.md` entries.
2. **Phase 2 — `sleep` primitive + async helpers** (filed as a sub-issue, enqueued): capped `sleep` extension + `std.sleep`/`mapLimit`/`retry`/`withTimeout` with the semantics above.
3. **Phase 3 — SET REMAINDER (not filed from this pass):** mcpx import maps in developing-today/code, implementing the design doc §5 contract under #765 as origin. Owed repo: developing-today/code. Pick it up from #765 / this issue — do not re-file it as a fresh per-repo issue.

## Links

- Implements the mechanism for #765 (decisions: developing-today/code#607)
- Grounding: `packages/codemode/src/extension.ts`, `packages/codemode/src/interpreter/limits.ts`, `packages/codemode/interpreter-support.md`, `packages/core/src/codemode/tool.ts`, `packages/core/src/codemode/web.ts`, `packages/core/src/codemode/instructions.ts`
- Register: `files/potential-projects.md`, design "Code Mode's missing standard library" (keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace)
- Note: `ROADMAP.md` has no Code Mode row although the fork maintains the interpreter — flagged in the design doc as a gap for a future roadmap pass.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Drew's decision on the delivery mechanism (one versioned `std` namespace evaluated program-side) is recorded on this issue — approve, amend, or reject.
- [ ] Phase 1 (sub-issue): `libraries` option in `@opencode/codemode`, std v1.0.0 pure helpers, core wiring, instructions listing naming `std.version`, tests, and `interpreter-support.md` entries — diagnostic source locations unchanged.
- [ ] Phase 2 (sub-issue): capped `sleep` host primitive wrapped as `std.sleep`, plus `mapLimit`/`retry`/`withTimeout` with the documented semantics (withTimeout bounds waiting, not execution, and the instructions say so).
- [ ] Phase 3 set remainder stays tracked under developing-today/code#765 (mcpx import-map contract, design doc §5) — it is not re-filed as a fresh per-repo issue, and this issue's closing comment names its disposition.

body:
## Origin

Implementation issue for the decisions recorded on developing-today/code#607 (Drew, 2026-10-28). Drew's placement ruling: this work is done **here, in OpenCode 2** — 'fix it in OpenCode 2. Handle code mode. Do all of those things.'

## Decisions being implemented (from code#607)

1. **Import maps / pinned imports: ADOPT, opt-in.** Scripts (mcpx-style Deno runs and Code Mode) can declare an import map that pins exact versions (e.g. `jsr:@std/async@1`, `npm:p-limit@6`) so runs are reproducible and an operator can see and limit what loads. No map configured = behavior unchanged.
2. **Arbitrary remote imports: KEEP ALLOWED by default.** Only a configured import map may close the set ('only these may load'). Do not flip the global default — it would break existing unpinned scripts.
3. **Code Mode helper library: ADOPT (Drew overruled the defer recommendation).** The `execute` interpreter cannot import at all (`import()` unsupported, no `setTimeout`, no `Deno`; only `fetch`), so common helpers are rewritten inline in every script. Provide a small standard library for Code Mode, covering at least:
   - binding default arguments to a tool namespace (e.g. a fixed `aws_profile`)
   - `chunk`, `uniqBy`, `keyBy`, `pick` / `omit`
   - `mapLimit` / bounded concurrency, `retry` with backoff, `withTimeout`
   
   Per code#607's 'not proposing' list: do NOT bake libraries in as unversioned globals, and do NOT make the runtime detect/install packages — Deno already caches on first import where imports exist.

## Notes

- Default permission profile is NOT part of this issue: Drew ruled it stays `all` (current default); the existing `readnet` profile stays available as an opt-in. Recorded on code#607.
- mcpx lives in both developing-today/code and dezren39/nix (cross-repo set rule): if a piece of Q1 turns out to belong in mcpx's launcher rather than here, file it as part of this same set with this issue as origin — do not let the set split silently.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A script run with an import map configured resolves the pinned versions; a script importing an unmapped remote package behaves as the map's mode specifies (allowed, or refused in closed mode) — demonstrated by a test or a documented manual run.
- [ ] With no import map configured, existing scripts run exactly as today (arbitrary imports allowed).
- [ ] Code Mode `execute` can use the helper library (chunk/keyBy/mapLimit/retry/withTimeout etc.) without inline rewrites — demonstrated by a test or documented manual run.
- [ ] Docs updated (agents.mdx / runtimes docs) describing the import map config and the Code Mode helpers.

body:
**Decision needed (one line):** Adopt the shared-contract design — one derived `QuotaSnapshot` signal, gates filter candidates before weighting, the burn-rate controller writes only through the existing tuner `Adjustment` channel — or keep #566/#567/#568 as three independent features with separate quota reads and config?

<!-- decision above is why this carries user/review; the rest routes through normal fleet triage -->

## Summary

Three features filed the same day — #566 (quota-aware session placement), #567 (time-based weighting), #568 (native quota intelligence / burn-rate controller) — each presuppose a **quota signal** and a **shared weight model** that none of them defines, and each sketches a different config surface to do it. This design is the missing contract: (1) a `QuotaSnapshot` value derived from data the fork already owns (`ModelPlan` windows + `windowReport()` usage), with one staleness rule where unknown/stale is never treated as headroom; (2) a layering rule — gates (#566) *filter* candidates before weighting, weights rank survivors through the existing `weightOf` layers, the controller (#568) writes only expiring `Adjustment`s like the tuner already does, and credential failover (#6) stays orthogonal inside an attempt; (3) per-layer weight attribution in the decision log so "why is this model ranked here?" is answerable for all three.

This extends — does not duplicate — the existing thread: #566, #567, #568, #6 stay as the implementation vehicles for phases 3–5. It also closes a roadmap gap: `ROADMAP.md` → "Routing, cost and plans" lists #6–#10 but has no row for #566/#567/#568. Full design doc: `files/designs/opencode-quota-signal-routing.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace (registered in `files/potential-projects.md`).

## Current state (evidence)

- `packages/core/src/model-route.ts` → `weightOf()` already composes layers in order: scheduled `WeightRule`s (time windows incl. `from`/`until` — most of #567's mechanism exists) → user `prefer` overrides → learned tuner adjustments (non-`fixed` routes only) → quota **demotion**, a binary `DEMOTED_FACTOR = 0.01` after quota errors (`quotaCooldownMs: 900_000`). Quota enters selection only as this reactive demotion.
- Quota knowledge is reporting-only: `packages/core/src/model-plan.ts` holds plans + `QuotaWindow`s; `packages/core/src/model-usage.ts` → `windowReport()` derives `percent` / `remaining` / `resetRule` from recorded usage. The selection path never reads it.
- `packages/core/src/model-route-tuning.ts` → `suggest()` already produces expiring, id-replaced `Adjustment`s (`auto:` ids) installed via `setAdjustments`/`addAdjustment`, gated by the route's `autonomy` level — the channel the controller should reuse.
- The decision log records final effective weights per candidate but not which layer produced them, so neither #567's inspection acceptance nor #568's audit acceptance can be met from the log today.
- The three issues' own words: #566 "using the existing quota sources; a stale read… is treated as unknown"; #567 "should share the weight model"; #568 "should adjust the same weight model they use rather than inventing a parallel one" — followed by three incompatible config sketches (`quota.gates.*`, `schedules:`/`boosts:`, a controller ladder), none matching the code's actual config shapes.

## Proposal (point of view)

- **One snapshot, one staleness rule.** `QuotaSnapshot { planID, window, providerID, percent|null, remaining|null, resetAt|null, observedAt, stale }`, derived purely from `ModelPlan` + `windowReport()` in v1 — no external polling. `percent === null` or `stale` ⇒ unknown: never headroom, never a wall; each consumer's configured fallback applies (gates default to admit = today's behaviour).
- **Gates filter, weights rank.** #566's gates run as a candidate filter in `nextTarget` before weighting — a refusal, not a weight of 0 — so the decision log can say "refused" and sticky/continuity logic can't resurrect a gated target. The fleet rule (burn to 100%, then stop, never PAYG) is a refusal and is modelled as one.
- **The controller is a second adjustment producer**, beside the tuner, with its own id prefix, expiring adjustments, observe mode = compute + log without installing, act mode gated per-route by the existing `autonomy` levels. The more restrictive adjustment wins on collision; both are logged.
- **Per-layer attribution** in the `decision` detail: weight after each layer (`base`, `scheduled`, `prefer`, `adjustment`, `demotion`) plus gate verdicts — one inspection feature serving #567 and #568.
- **#6 stays orthogonal**: credential failover inside an attempt on a selected target; it neither reads snapshots nor writes weights.
- Alternatives that lose, with reasons, are in the design doc: per-feature quota reads/config; external polling first; gates-as-weights; a new controller weight layer above `weightOf`.

## Phased breakdown

1. **Phase 1 — `QuotaSnapshot` derivation + staleness contract.** Pure module over `ModelPlan` + `windowReport()` data; unknown/stale rules; unit tests (missing limit, missing `windowHours`, stale observation, threshold boundaries). No selection behaviour change. *(Filed as a sub-issue of this design issue and enqueued.)*
2. **Phase 2 — Per-layer weight attribution in the decision log.** Traced weight computation; traced weights must equal `weightOf` weights; surfaced via existing route-review tooling. No behaviour change. *(Filed as a sub-issue of this design issue and enqueued.)*
3. **Phase 3 — Quota gates on the snapshot.** The existing #566, re-scoped onto this contract once the decision lands. *(Not re-filed — #566 is the vehicle.)*
4. **Phase 4 — Controller as adjustment producer.** The existing #568; its telemetry acceptance is narrowed by Phase 1. *(Not re-filed.)*
5. **Phase 5 — #567 close-out.** Verify `WeightRule` windows/boosts against #567's acceptance; inspection surface on Phase 2's attribution; retire its separate config sketch. *(Not re-filed.)*

## Open questions (in the design doc, deliberately not filed as issues)

- Which reset rules can yield a concrete `resetAt`, and does the controller need it, or is percent + remaining enough?
- Per-credential quota dimension once #6 lands, or is provider-level percent the right gate granularity?
- Snapshot max-age default (the wider fleet uses a ≤60-minute quota read for placement decisions).

## Non-goals

- No PAYG routing, ever (inherited from #566/#568 and the fleet pool rule).
- No change to `ModelRouteSchedule` semantics.
- No cross-repo quota sync with developing-today/code's provider-quota registry in v1.

## Related

- #566, #567, #568, #6 (the features this contract serves), #550 (windowReport omits windows without `windowHours` — snapshot must surface those as unknown)
- Files: `packages/core/src/model-route.ts` (`weightOf`, `nextTarget`), `packages/core/src/model-route-tuning.ts`, `packages/core/src/model-plan.ts`, `packages/core/src/model-usage.ts` (`windowReport`), `ROADMAP.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The decision in the first line is recorded on this issue (adopt the shared contract, or keep the three features independent), with the decider named.
- [ ] If adopted: Phases 1–2 land as their sub-issues specify, and #566/#567/#568 are re-scoped onto the contract (snapshot + layering) in their bodies.
- [ ] If not adopted: the rationale is recorded here and the three issues' "shared weight model" expectations are removed or replaced, so the thread does not stay dangling.
- [ ] No code changes land under this design issue itself.

body:
Observed 2026-10-25 on the sandbox (standalone `opencode serve`, v2.0.30+e7baa0d from this fork, installed via the code repo flake):

## Symptom
Sessions on the `meta` provider (Muse Wonder, `@ai-sdk/openai` against https://api.meta.ai/v1) never produce output: the turn sits in state `running` indefinitely, the assistant message stays empty, and session token counters stay at zero. Interrupt works. Reproduced across two sandbox reboots and with a scratch serve instance (minimal env) on a second port, so it is not the systemd unit's environment or experimental flags.

## What works (same machine, same minute)
- Sessions on the `openai` provider through the same server: answer normally with real token counts.
- The Meta API called directly with curl using the same API key and the same egress proxy (http://hatch-egress-proxy:3128): non-streaming returns 200; streaming returns chunks immediately (`pong` in ~5s).
- Sessions on the `meta` provider through the OpenChamber-embedded build of the same rev on the laptop: answer normally (content-verified repeatedly on 2026-10-25).

## Config facts
- Provider block: `"meta": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai", "options": { "baseURL": "https://api.meta.ai/v1" }, models: muse-wonder-1.0 / muse-spark-1.3 / muse-spark-1.1 }`.
- Server process env has NO META_API_KEY override; auth.json holds the key (sha256 prefix 6b1ea8ee, verified working via curl above).
- Sandbox egress is proxy-only; the server env carries HTTP(S)_PROXY like other working clients.

## Suspicion
Something in the standalone serve path (Bun fetch through the CONNECT proxy to api.meta.ai, or the AI SDK stream handling for this endpoint) stalls where the embedded build and curl do not. No error is surfaced in the session or the server journal — the turn simply never yields a token.

Workaround in use: run meta-pool sessions against the laptop's embedded server instead of the sandbox standalone serve.

## Acceptance criteria

- A standalone `opencode serve` from this fork completes a turn on the `meta` provider: tokens stream, the assistant message is non-empty, and session token counters advance.
- The hang is root-caused to a named layer (proxy/CONNECT handling, Bun fetch, or AI SDK stream handling for api.meta.ai) with evidence, not just bypassed.
- A regression check or documented repro script exists that would catch a recurrence (standalone serve + meta provider smoke turn).
- No regression on other providers through the same standalone server (e.g. the `openai` provider still answers normally).

body:
## Problem

Settings written for a pool's own model under `providers["opencode-route"].models.<pool>` (for example `disabled: true`, which the routing-config skill gives as the way to hide a model, or `name` and `limit`) do not hold for pools.

From reading the code; not reproduced in a test yet:

- `ConfigProviderPlugin` runs its provider transform before `ConfigModelRoutesPlugin` (`packages/core/src/plugin/internal.ts`, the `post` list). For a configured provider it calls `providers.update(providerID, ...)` (`packages/core/src/config/plugin/provider.ts`, about line 62), and the provider editor creates a missing record on update (`entry` in `packages/core/src/provider.ts`, about lines 363-370). The routes provider transform then finds `opencode-route` already present and returns at once (`if (providers.get(ModelRoute.PROVIDER_ID)) return`, `packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts` line 67 on main), so no pool built in the provider transform is created. This is on main.
- In #233, pools that use the new matching or effort keys are built in a model transform that runs after the provider plugin's model transform, which applies the per-model overrides. `editor.update(ModelRoute.PROVIDER_ID, id, (model) => Object.assign(model, info))` (`model-routes.ts` about line 143 in #233) then writes the whole route model over them, `enabled` included, so `disabled: true` does not hide such a pool.

Raised by Copilot in review of #233.

## Direction

Alias settings need to apply after the pool model is built, while concrete model overrides (configured variants, limits) still apply before the pools read them. One way: the provider plugin skips `opencode-route` models, and the routes plugin applies their configured overrides after it builds them, in both transforms. A test should configure `providers["opencode-route"].models.<pool>.disabled` for a pool built in each transform.



## Acceptance criteria

- Settings under `providers["opencode-route"].models.<pool>` (e.g. `disabled: true`, `name`, `limit`) hold for pools built in the provider transform AND for pools built in the model transform.
- A test configures `providers["opencode-route"].models.<pool>.disabled` for a pool built in each transform and asserts the pool stays hidden; concrete per-model overrides (variants, limits) still apply before the pools read them.

body:
## Finding

PR #233 (https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/233, head d92970ddfb) adds pattern-based pool membership (`include` / `contains` / `match`) and, commendably, a diagnostic for almost every other way a pool setting can be silently dropped: a malformed pattern skips the pool with a diagnostic, an unknown key is reported as "omitted unknown setting", a bad schedule leaves a config warning, a declared level no model can run is logged, and a pool pinned at a level it does not declare "adds nothing, and says so".

One silent drop is left: **a pool whose matching keys select no models at all produces no diagnostic.**

- In `expand()` (`packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts:537-556` on the PR branch), the `selects` loop simply places nothing when no catalog entry passes the predicate (typo'd pattern, a provider that is not connected, an `exclude`/`notContains` that removes everything the include matched). No entry is added to `diagnostics` — contrast the diagnostics pushed at lines 344, 390 and 425 for the level/pin/unknown-pool cases.
- The transforms then erase the pool without a word: the model transform does `if (leaves.length === 0) return editor.remove(ModelRoute.PROVIDER_ID, id)` (line 141), and a pool that also has `targets` keeps its targets while its `include`/`contains`/`match` silently adds nothing.

So a one-character typo (`*luno*` for `*luna*`), or a provider that failed to connect, makes a pool vanish from the picker — or quietly run without the models its author intended — with nothing in the log, in exactly the way this PR set out to eliminate for schedules and unknown keys.

## Evidence

- PR: developing-today/opencode#233, head `d92970ddfb42e48cf390c2ef78d931a2dc63619a` (OPEN at time of filing).
- `packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts:537-556` — the selects loop in `collect()`; no diagnostic on zero placements.
- `packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts:141` — model transform removes an empty pool silently; line 102 does the same in the provider transform.
- The PR's own tests pin diagnostics for the neighbouring cases and none for this one: `packages/core/test/model-routes-matching.test.ts` expects `"pool small declares level ultra, but none of its models can run it, so it is not offered"` and `"pool low-only is pinned at level max, which it does not declare, so it adds nothing"`, but no test expands a pool whose `include`/`contains`/`match` selects nothing and asserts what is reported.
- Deduped: no open or closed issue in this repo mentions a diagnostic for a pool matching no models (searched "pool matched no models", "include matches nothing", "model route diagnostic"). The two follow-ups the PR body already filed, #236 (transform-created models) and #237 (pinned nested pool remaps), are different findings.

## Why it matters

Pattern pools are the PR's headline feature, and their failure mode is otherwise invisible: the pool is absent (or smaller than configured) and the only symptom is a model the user expected never being offered. The PR establishes the principle that a routing setting must never be dropped without a word; this is the remaining place that principle is not applied.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a pool's matching keys (`include` / `contains` / `match`, after `exclude` / `notContains`) add no models during expansion, a model-route diagnostic naming the pool (and ideally which key(s) selected nothing) is emitted through the existing `report()` path in `packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts`, so it is logged once while it lasts and again if it recurs after clearing.
- [ ] A pool that has targets and whose matching keys add nothing is also diagnosed (the pool surviving on its targets must not hide the dead key).
- [ ] New tests in `packages/core/test/model-routes-matching.test.ts` (or the expand tests) cover: an `include` pattern that matches nothing, a `match` expression that selects nothing, and an `exclude` that empties an otherwise-matching `include` — each asserting the diagnostic; and a matching pool that selects at least one model asserts no such diagnostic.
- [ ] Fix in PR #233 itself or in a follow-up referencing this issue; either is acceptable, but the behaviour should not ship silently.

body:
## Problem

Route pools need models that the model picker doesn't need to show. Today there are two states for a model under a provider: enabled (listed in the picker) and disabled. Open question, to verify first: **when a model is disabled in the provider config, is it also removed from route pool selection?** If yes, there is currently no way to keep a model routable while keeping it out of the picker's way — the picker fills up with pool-only models nobody should pick by hand.

## Proposal

### 1. `disable` keeps working exactly as it does today

No behavior change to the existing disabled state, whatever the verification above finds.

### 2. New `hide` state for models

A hidden model:

- Does **not** appear in the model picker list.
- **Does** appear in the picker when the search text is the model's **exact full name** (typed completely). Partial matches do not reveal it.
- Remains fully selectable by route pools.

### 3. Wildcards in route pools and in the picker search

- Route pool selectors accept wildcard patterns (e.g. `*flash*`, `deepseek/*`).
- The model picker search box accepts wildcards too, with the same matching. This changes nothing for anyone who never types a `*` — the character has no meaning in model names today, so existing searches are unaffected. Anyone who does type one discovers it does something.

### 4. Matching rule (slashes)

Patterns match against model names as follows:

- If the pattern **contains a forward slash**, it is matched against the full `provider/model` name — and, in route pools, against route pool names that contain slashes.
- If the pattern **contains no slash**, it is treated as `*/<pattern>`: the pattern applies to the model segment under any provider.

A hidden model is revealed/selected only when something names it specifically: the exact-name search above, an explicit route entry, or a wildcard pattern that matches it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Verified and documented: whether a provider-disabled model can still be selected by a route pool today.
- [ ] A model can be hidden: absent from the picker list, present on exact-full-name search, routable throughout.
- [ ] Route pool selectors accept wildcards per the slash rule above.
- [ ] Picker search accepts wildcards with identical matching semantics.
- [ ] Searches containing no `*` behave byte-for-byte as before.

Filed as a task for pickup — design/implementation intentionally left to whoever takes it.

body:
## Question

What does `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_FILEWATCHER` actually cost at runtime, and is it better or worse than the default watcher? We currently ship `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLE_FILEWATCHER=1` in user config (large trees everywhere); this issue tracks replacing gut feel with measurements.

## Background

- Default watcher: watches the project tree — powers live external-edit awareness, @-mention freshness, snapshot/revert accuracy, live file tree, LSP refresh. (Diffs themselves are git-based and work regardless.)
- Experimental watcher: watches the **entire directory tree**, not just the project. The desktop app enables it by default.
- Suspected costs on very large trees: inotify watch count, event churn, CPU/IO, memory — especially with node_modules-scale subtrees, .git, and huge monorepos.

## Benchmarks needed (this is the deliverable)

Design and run benchmarks that answer, for default vs experimental vs disabled:

1. Idle CPU and RSS on trees of increasing size (1k / 50k / 500k files), including a tree with node_modules and a large .git.
2. Event latency: time from an external file edit to the session/UI reflecting it.
3. Behavior at the inotify watch limit (`fs.inotify.max_user_watches`): graceful degradation or silent staleness?
4. Cost under churn: bulk operations (git checkout of a big branch, codegen, package install) — event storm handling, CPU spike, dropped events.
5. Network filesystems and containers: where OS notifications don't exist or lie.
6. Battery/laptop impact on a real workstation over a workday (subjective + sampled CPU).

## What to test exactly

- Correctness parity: does experimental catch edits the default misses (outside-project files), and does either miss edits the other catches?
- Whether experimental is *more performant* anywhere (batching, native recursive watch) or purely broader in scope.

## Outcome wanted

A table of measured results + a recommendation per environment class (laptop / desktop / server / container) for which watcher setting to ship, so the config flags stop being guesses.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A benchmark harness exists that runs default vs experimental vs disabled watcher over at least three tree sizes (incl. node_modules-scale and a large .git) and records idle CPU/RSS and edit-to-reflection latency.
- [ ] Behaviour at the inotify watch limit is measured and recorded (graceful degradation vs silent staleness).
- [ ] Results are posted on this issue as a table, with a per-environment-class recommendation (laptop / desktop / server / container) for which watcher setting to ship.
- [ ] The user-config `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLE_FILEWATCHER=1` gut-feel default is either confirmed by the data or changed per the recommendation.

body:
### Context & Background
In OpenCode upstream commit `81d57087a4` (`feat(session-ui): summarize each turn's changed files (#55064)`), OpenCode added automated detection and summarization of all files added, modified, or deleted within each turn.

In our fork ecosystem, agents generate structured execution plans with checklist items (`- [ ] 1. Scaffold API routes`, `- [ ] 2. Update UI component`) via `/plan` or the `plan-tracking` skill, which are displayed in OpenChamber's Project Knowledge Plans view. Currently, agents must manually read their plan markdown file and edit the checkboxes (`- [x]`) by invoking file tools. If an agent forgets to update the checklist after editing files, the plan's progress indicator remains stale.

### Feature Objective
Automatically update and infer plan step completion using turn file change summaries:
When an agent turn concludes with file changes matching the files or scopes referenced in a plan step, automatically suggest or check off the corresponding plan step in Project Knowledge (`openchamber_knowledge` / `.openchamber/plans/`), keeping plan progress continuously accurate.

---

### Technical Specifications

#### 1. Turn File Changes Event & Hook
- Upstream emits turn change summaries in `packages/core/src/session/` / `packages/session-ui/`.
- In `packages/core/src/session/subagent-completion.ts` or post-turn hooks in `packages/core/src/plugin/supervisor.ts`:
  - Extract the list of files touched in the turn: `{ added: string[], modified: string[], deleted: string[] }`.

#### 2. Plan Step Scope Matcher in `plan-tracking`
- In `packages/core/src/plugin/skill/plan-tracking.md` and related plan parsing helpers:
  - If a plan step specifies target files or directories (e.g. `Implement routes in packages/web/server/routes.js` or `Add tests in packages/core/test/`):
  - When all referenced files for that step have been modified/created in recent turns:
    - Automatically check off the step (`- [x]`) in the active plan file or mark it as completed.
    - If the plan is stored via `openchamber_knowledge`, invoke `knowledge.save(kind: 'plan', ...)` with the updated checklist markdown.

#### 3. Agent Confirmation & Notification
- When a step is automatically checked off:
  - Include a lightweight notice in the turn timeline (e.g., `Plan step 2 checked off: Implement routes`).
  - Allow the user or agent to uncheck or adjust if the step was only partially completed.

---

### Key Files & References
- `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts`: Turn completion, diff detection
- `packages/core/src/plugin/skill/plan-tracking.md`: Agent plan tracking workflow instructions
- `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/plan-info.ts`: Plan information and update tool
- OpenChamber Project Knowledge plans: `packages/web/server/lib/openchamber-control/project-knowledge.js`

### Acceptance Criteria
1. The system extracts file modification summaries at the end of each turn.
2. When modified files satisfy the targets of a plan step, the step is marked complete (`- [x]`) in the plan markdown file.
3. OpenChamber's Project Knowledge Plans tab reflects the updated step completion count (e.g. `3/5 Done`).
4. Unit tests in `packages/core/test/` verify automated step matching against simulated file changes.

title: fix(server): instructions-entry endpoints never validate the session — the declared SessionNotFoundError is unreachable (put 500s on a dead session; remove returns 204 for unknown session/key)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: source/queue-worker
labels.description: Filed or worked by the queue/worker pilot

labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/server
labels.description: Package: server (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

The API contract declares `SessionNotFoundError` for all three experimental instructions-entry endpoints, but the handler group is the only session-scoped group that never checks the session, so the declared 404 is unreachable:

- **Contract:** `packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts:662-719` lists `SessionNotFoundError` in the error set for `session.instructions.entry.list` (:668), `.put` (:688) and `.remove` (:708).
- **Handlers:** `packages/server/src/handlers/session.ts:662-684` calls `instructions.list/put/remove` with no session-existence check and no `Effect.catchTag("Session.NotFoundError", ...)` — every neighboring session.* handler does map it (e.g. `session.get` at :266-273, and `session.generate` at :686-698 does the same check directly below this group).
- **put → 500, not 404:** `packages/core/src/session/instruction-entry.ts:134-156` inserts rows for `session_id: input.sessionID` with no session validation. The table has a foreign key to the session table (`packages/core/src/session/sql.ts:152-155`) and the database enforces it (`PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`, `packages/core/src/database/database.ts:48`), so an unknown sessionID throws inside `.run().pipe(Effect.orDie)` and surfaces as an internal 500, not the declared 404.
- **remove → 204 on any input:** `instruction-entry.ts:158-171` is an UPDATE that matches no rows for an unknown sessionID (or a key that was never attached) and resolves void, so the handler returns 204 — indistinguishable from a successful removal. Same "stale or typoed ID looks like success" class as the fixed #2556 / #2542 and the open #2543.
- **list → 200 `data: []`** for an unknown session, although the contract declares `SessionNotFoundError`.
- **Tests:** `packages/server/test/fetch.test.ts:40-49` asserts only the unknown-*location* 404 on the entries route; no test covers unknown-session or unknown-key behavior for any of the three endpoints.

Observed-by-reading call shapes against a stale/typoed `ses_…` id:
- `PUT /api/experimental/session/ses_unknown/instructions/entries/some-key` → 500 internal (FK violation die)
- `DELETE /api/experimental/session/ses_unknown/instructions/entries/some-key` → 204 NoContent
- `GET /api/experimental/session/ses_unknown/instructions/entries` → 200 `{data: []}`

## Why it matters

A client that attached durable context entries and then reuses a stale or mistyped session ID (e.g. after `session.remove`, which cascade-deletes the entries) gets three mutually wrong answers: a raw 500 that masks a plain not-found, a success 204 that did nothing, and an empty list that looks like "no entries were ever attached". The declared contract already promises a 404; the implementation just never delivers it, and nothing pins the behavior in tests.

## Suggested fix shape

Resolve the session first in all three handlers and map `Session.NotFoundError` → 404, mirroring the `session.generate` check at `packages/server/src/handlers/session.ts:686-698`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `list`, `put` and `remove` against an unknown sessionID all return 404 `SessionNotFoundError`, matching the declared error sets in `packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts:662-719`.
- [ ] `put` no longer surfaces an internal 500 (FK violation) for an unknown session.
- [ ] `remove` of a key that was never attached is either 404 or a deliberate, documented idempotent 204 — decided and pinned by a test (fleet precedent: #2556 chose 404 for `permission.saved.remove`).
- [ ] Regression tests cover unknown-session for all three endpoints and the unknown-key `remove` decision; `fetch.test.ts`-style coverage is sufficient.

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

CodeRabbit raised this on PR #2450 and it was never addressed: `parseRenderAnswer` returns a `chat` answer for every `{ answered: false }` result, without checking `reason`. An answer such as `{ answered: false, reason: "timeout" }` — or one with `reason` absent — enters the chat branch, so the runner proceeds as if the user answered in chat (with the closed-in-chat note) although no chat answer was supplied. The parser's own documented contract says only `{ answered: false, reason: "chat" }` is a chat answer and that an unanswered page is `none`, never a guess.

- Source PR: #2450 — https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2450
- Review comment: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2450#discussion_r4575255981
- Reviewer: coderabbitai[bot], 2026-11-14T19:10:52Z (Minor · Functional Correctness)
- Flagged location: `packages/core/src/session/runner/render-card.ts:298`

## No-response evidence

- No replies on the review thread; the thread is unresolved (checked via GraphQL `reviewThreads` this run).
- No fix commit after the comment: the branch is unchanged on current main. The PR's merge-time agent notes disposition only the automated-review gate, not this finding.
- Issue search (PR number, file, function) found no existing tracker.

## Still live on current main

`packages/core/src/session/runner/render-card.ts` (current main, lines 302–304):

```ts
if (answer.answered === false) {
  return { type: "chat", note: typeof data?.note === "string" ? data.note : RENDER_PAGE_CLOSED_IN_CHAT_NOTE }
}
```

No `reason` check, while the doc comment directly above the function (lines 285–289) specifies the `reason: "chat"` shape and `none` for anything else.

## Acceptance criteria

- The unanswered branch returns `chat` only when `reason === "chat"` and returns `none` for other unanswered results (including absent `reason`), with a regression test covering the timeout/absent-reason cases; OR the finding is resolved by a documented decision recorded on this issue.

body:
## Summary

A v1-dialect config variant spelled with an `options` bag -- e.g. `"variants": { "high": { "options": { "thinkingConfig": { "thinkingLevel": "high" } } } }` -- migrates to variant settings `{ options: { thinkingConfig: ... } }`, and nothing on the native request path ever unwraps that bag. The variant resolves, is selectable, and carries the settings in every dump -- and sends nothing on the wire. Only effort spellings survive, because `Provider.nativeSettings` happens to hoist them.

## Evidence (fork main 746cce4d27)

- `packages/core/src/v1/config/migrate.ts` (`migrateModel`): the variant value is passed through `split()` whole, so the migrated variant settings keep the nested `options` key. Model-level options are instead passed as the bag contents -- the two paths are inconsistent.
- `packages/core/src/provider.ts` (`nativeSettings`, #2203): hoists only `reasoningEffort` / `reasoning_effort` out of `options`; every other key stays nested. Pinned by `packages/core/test/provider.test.ts` ("preserves unrelated settings and nested options": `options.temperature` stays nested).
- `packages/core/src/aisdk-native.ts` (`options()` translator): for non-Bedrock/OpenRouter packages the settings pass through with the nested bag untouched.
- `packages/ai/src/protocols/gemini.ts`: the provider-options schema is `{ cachedContent, safetySettings, serviceTier, thinkingConfig }` -- no `options` field, and the lenient decode drops unknown keys, so the request goes out with no `thinkingConfig` at all (provider default thinking).
- The catalog spelling is flat and works: `packages/core/src/variant.ts` (gemini protocol) resolves effort variants to `settings: { thinkingConfig: { includeThoughts: true, thinkingLevel } }`; see `packages/core/test/variant.test.ts:531`.

## Real-world instance

developing-today/code PR #10622 (merged 2026-11-16) defined five `google.*` alias providers whose hand-written variants used exactly this shape. A resolved dump through the fork plugin pipeline (ModelsDevPlugin + ProviderInstancePlugin + ConfigProviderPlugin) shows the seated models carrying `settings: { options: { thinkingConfig } }` -- the plans pinned top efforts that would never have bound on the wire. Those aliases are being slimmed to catalog inheritance (`instanceOf`) separately; this issue is about the silent-inert trap itself, which any v1-dialect config can still fall into.

## Suggested directions (not prescriptive)

- Hoist the whole v1 `options` bag in `nativeSettings` for native packages, or
- make the v1 migration unwrap variant options the way it unwraps model options, or
- at minimum, warn at config load when a native-package variant`s settings contain a nested `options` key whose contents no consumer will read.

title: fix(server): route-overrides POST returns 200 for an already-expired override that save() silently drops (PR #2496)

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/normal

body:
## Finding (from PR diff review of PR #2496)

PR #2496 adds `POST /api/route/overrides` and promises: an entry core's parse would drop "is rejected with `InvalidRequestError` and nothing is stored — the API never writes an override routing would silently ignore."

That promise has a hole for an **already-expired** override (`until` in the past):

- Core's `ModelRouteOverrides.parse` (`packages/core/src/model-route-overrides.ts`, at PR head `226fc85b2342`) keeps an entry whose `until` is any finite number — there is no past/expiry check in parse.
- The new handler (`packages/server/src/handlers/route.ts`) validates only via parse: `parsed.find((entry) => entry.id === ctx.payload.id)` succeeds for an expired entry, so no `InvalidRequestError` is raised.
- `ModelRouteOverrides.add` → `save()` then silently filters it out: `overrides.filter((item) => item.until === undefined || item.until > now)`.
- The handler returns HTTP 200 with the list now in force — which does not contain the posted override. A client (the OpenChamber consolidation in #2491 is the intended caller) cannot distinguish "stored" from "silently dropped" except by re-scanning the returned list for its own ID.

This is distinct from closed issue #535 (save dropping expired *scheduled* overrides inside core); this is the new API surface returning success for a store that never happened.

## Evidence

- PR #2496, head `226fc85b2342fa82eda8f500b2708a80c8fe1faf`, diff of `packages/server/src/handlers/route.ts` (validation = parse + find-by-id only) and `packages/server/test/route.test.ts` (covers happy path + no-provider/model malformed case; no expired-`until` case).
- Core source at the same head, verified via `gh api .../contents/packages/core/src/model-route-overrides.ts?ref=226fc85b...`: `parse` has no expiry check; `save` filters `until > now`.

## Why it matters

The consolidation (#2491) moves OpenChamber's route-rules writes onto this API. A silent 200-without-store turns a client bug or a clock-skewed `until` into a routing instruction that quietly never takes effect — the exact "silently ignored" failure mode the PR set out to eliminate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `POST /api/route/overrides` with `until <= now` is rejected with `InvalidRequestError` (400), consistent with the malformed-entry behaviour, OR the handler verifies the posted ID is present in the list it returns and errors otherwise.
- [ ] A regression test in `packages/server/test/route.test.ts` posts an expired override and asserts the rejection (and that nothing was stored).
- [ ] Existing route tests still pass.

title: fix(core): route-overrides add/remove overwrite the store with [] when the file is corrupt — every override is erased

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator

labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

`ModelRouteOverrides.add` and `remove` build their replacement list from `current()`. `current()` returns `[]` for a malformed or truncated `route-overrides.json` (`packages/core/src/model-route-overrides.ts:197-200`). `save()` then writes the file back with only the new item, so one bad byte erases every override the user had and overwrites the corrupt file. The plan store does the opposite: `readStore` in `packages/core/src/model-plan.ts:116-126` throws on malformed JSON "so a bad write cannot silently erase the user's plans". The route-overrides writer has no such guard.

## Evidence

- `model-route-overrides.ts:306-307`: `add = (item, now) => save([...current().filter(...), item], now)`; `remove` at `:311-316` is the same shape.
- `model-route-overrides.ts:197-200`: `try { list = parse(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8"))) } catch { list = [] }`.
- `model-route-overrides.ts:240-262`: `save` writes whatever list it is given, atomically, with no check against the prior file contents.
- `model-route-overrides.ts:53-99`: `parse` also drops single invalid entries silently. A well-formed file with one entry the parser rejects loses that entry on the next unrelated `add`, too.

Repro, run in a scratch worktree at `origin/main` `cd29e5bc05b8` (`packages/core`, `bun test`, temporary test file removed afterwards):

1. `setFilePath(file)`; `add({id:"keep-me", ...})`. `current()` lists `keep-me`.
2. Overwrite the file with a truncated `{"version":1,"overrides":[{"id":"keep-me"`. This is what a crash mid-edit, a bad hand edit, or a partial sync leaves behind.
3. `add({id:"new", ...})`. The file now contains only `"new"`. `keep-me` is gone and the corrupt bytes are gone with it.

Observed after step 3: `{"version":1,"overrides":[{"id":"new", ...}]}`.

Dedupe: the open and recently closed searches found #924 (atomic write, fixed), #2605 (cache staleness), #570/#669/#536/#662 (parse-level drops), #535/#2503 (expiry on save), and #1263 (preserved branch for #924). None covers writing over a corrupt or unparseable store. No open PR touches `model-route-overrides.ts`.

## Why it matters

Route overrides are user instructions to the router, such as "avoid this provider until Friday" or "prefer that model". Losing them silently means routing reverts to defaults with no error. The same user action, `add`, is the one that destroys the data, so the user has no signal that anything went wrong.

## Suggested fix shape

- Make the write path refuse to proceed when the existing file is present but unparseable: read it strictly, and if it fails, throw (as `readStore` does) rather than writing. Keep the read-only `current()` tolerant so routing never stops.
- Alternatively, on a corrupt existing file, move it aside to `route-overrides.json.corrupt-<ts>` before writing, and log it.
- Make `parse` report dropped entries (count or log) so that a silent drop on write is visible.

## Acceptance criteria

- A test writes a truncated `route-overrides.json`, calls `add` (and separately `remove`), and asserts that either the call throws and leaves the bytes unchanged, or the corrupt bytes are preserved in a sibling file. The current behaviour (overwrite) must fail the test.
- A test asserts that `current()` on the same corrupt file still returns `[]` (keeps the existing read-tolerance test at `packages/core/test/model-route-overrides.test.ts:171`).
- The `parse`-drops-an-invalid-entry case is covered by a test that asserts the drop is observable and not silently erased by a subsequent `add`.

title: fix(core): shell output reads silently succeed empty when a capture file disappears
body:
## Problem

When a shell command's capture file disappears for any reason other than the retention sweep, reads of its output silently succeed empty:

- `packages/core/src/shell.ts` `readRange` resolves a read-stream error as a zero-byte page (`stream.on("error", () => resolve(buffer.subarray(0, 0)))`).
- For a spawned command, `captureOf` reports the in-memory `command.size` without touching the file, so `Shell.output()` returns successful empty pages against a nonzero size — the caller cannot distinguish "the capture is gone" from "the command produced no output".

Missing capture data must not be silently represented as a successful empty read.

## Origin

Split from #2673 criterion 4, per Lane NG's prepared design recorded there (comment 7095545226): the retention fix (PR #2758, merge `116368c274ff`) removed the primary disappearance cause — the hourly sweep unlinking live captures — but other disappearance causes remain possible (external deletion, a remove/teardown race), and the read path's silent-empty behaviour is a separable defect with its own fix shape.

## Evidence (main `116368c274ff`, post-#2758)

- `readRange` in `packages/core/src/shell.ts`: any stream error resolves as an empty buffer.
- `captureOf` spawned branch: returns `{ size: command.size, truncated: command.truncated }` from memory alone; `output()` then pages `readRange(command.info.file, ...)` and formats whatever comes back, including the error-swallowed empty page.
- The daemon branch of `captureOf` already treats a missing file explicitly (`stat` failure → size 0), so the spawned branch's behaviour is the inconsistent one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reading output for a command whose capture file is missing does not return a successful empty page indistinguishable from a genuinely empty capture; the disappearance is surfaced (an error, or an explicit marker consistent with the existing truncated/capped notices in `result`/`output`).
- [ ] Regression coverage: a capture that disappears before or during a read reports the disappearance instead of empty success; a genuinely empty capture still reads as a successful empty page.
- [ ] The existing shell and output suites stay green (`shell-cleanup`, `shell-retention`, `shell`, `tool-shell` families).

## Related

- #2673 — the retention sweep deleting live captures (fixed by PR #2758); this issue is its criterion 4, split out rather than bundled.

title: fix(tui): do not treat JSONL read failures as an empty store

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: effort/xs

body:
## Evidence

`packages/tui/src/prompt/jsonl.ts:47-51` catches every `readText(input.file)` failure and substitutes `""`, parses that as an empty store, then runs the caller's update and atomically writes the result back to the same path. The prompt history, prompt stash, and frecency providers all use this helper. A transient or permission-related read failure can therefore turn an ordinary append/update into replacement of the existing persisted store with only the new/current in-memory entries. `read()` at line 34 has the same error-to-empty behavior, so startup can also silently present an empty store.

This is distinct from closed #2528, which fixed cross-process rewrites dropping concurrent appends. That fix added the lock and fresh read, but a failed fresh read is still treated as an empty valid store.

## Why it matters

Prompt history and stashed prompts can be irrecoverably discarded by a transient filesystem error. Frecency history can similarly be overwritten or loaded as empty. This also masks an I/O failure as a valid empty store, making recovery and diagnosis difficult.

## Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- Treat `ENOENT` as an empty new store where appropriate, but propagate or otherwise safely handle read errors that do not mean the file is absent; do not rewrite the file from an assumed-empty snapshot.
- Ensure a failed startup read does not replace a populated in-memory store with empty data.
- Add tests for a read failure followed by an update, asserting the existing file is not replaced, plus a normal missing-file case that still initializes successfully.
- Keep the multi-process locking and atomic-write guarantees from #2528.

## Reproduction shape

Use a populated JSONL file in a directory that remains writable while the file itself is unreadable to the process. Trigger a normal history/stash update. The current `update` path treats the read failure as an empty list and attempts to publish a replacement rather than refusing the update. A controlled injected read failure would also exercise the same branch deterministically.

title: fix(core): fs.read streams the path by name after its confinement check — a post-check symlink swap serves outside-root bytes

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: app/server
labels.description: Package: server (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Evidence

`packages/core/src/filesystem.ts:163-180` (`FileSystem.read`): `resolve()` canonicalizes + enforces root containment, `fs.stat(target.real)` checks type, then it returns a lazy `stream` closure capturing `target.real` — a path string, not an open handle:

```ts
stream: (options) => fs.stream(target.real, options),
```

`packages/server/src/handlers/fs.ts:147` consumes that stream at response time (`serveFile` → `file.stream(...)`). Effect platform `stream(path)` opens by name when the stream runs, so the file is re-opened by name after the check.

`packages/protocol/src/groups/fs.ts`: `fs.read` is documented as confined ("Stream one file relative to the requested location"); `fs.watch` says "Paths follow read confinement" (and its check calls `fs.read`). Contrast `fs.write`, which is explicitly documented as NOT confined (#2502). A read escaping the root contradicts the documented contract.

Same defect class as the just-merged plugin-browser upload fix (`a5166c551d`, which binds the read to the checked object via re-canonicalize + dev/ino compare). The core read path never got the same treatment.

## Repro (deterministic, verified on origin/main bcc17298c7)

Temporary bun test against the real `FileSystem.node` layer (removed afterwards):

1. Write `doc.txt` (inside location) and `secret.txt` (outside location).
2. `service.read({ path: "doc.txt" })` → passes containment.
3. `rm doc.txt && symlink(secret, doc.txt)` before consuming the stream.
4. `Stream.mkUint8Array(file.stream())` → returns `"outside-secret"`.

No timing luck involved: the swap sits squarely in the check/use window that the lazy stream leaves open.

## Why it matters

Any concurrent project-dir writer (agent command, background task, second session) can redirect a confined `fs.read` response — or the `fs.watch` existence check built on it — to outside-root bytes served to the HTTP client. The window is larger than the plugin-browser one: the stream opens at response-streaming time, not immediately after the check.

## Suggested fix shape

Bind the stream to the checked object, mirroring `BrowserFiles.read` after `a5166c551d`: open the handle inside `FileSystem.read`, fstat it, refuse on dev/ino mismatch (and non-regular files), and stream from the handle (or re-verify identity at stream-open). Cover `fs.watch`'s check path with the same hardened check.

## Acceptance

- Post-check symlink swap (file replaced between `read()` returning and stream consumption) is refused before any bytes are served; no outside-root bytes cross `fs.read`.
- Regression test places the swap deterministically between check and stream consumption (same seam style as the plugin-browser `openFile` tests).
- `fs.watch` confinement check shares the hardened path.

title: fix(cli-rs): api-types generator emits literal-enum variant named Self (Rust keyword) — MessagingChainInputDepth does not compile
body:
## Summary

`bun run generate` in `packages/cli-rs` cannot complete on current main even after the optional-and-nullable number gap (opencode#2733) is fixed: the Rust type generator emits a literal-enum variant named `Self` for the `MessagingChainInput.depth` literal `"self"`, and `Self` is a Rust keyword that no `r#` prefix can save, so the generated `opencode-api-types` crate does not compile:

```
error: expected identifier, found keyword `Self`
     --> crates/api-types/src/type_macros.rs:84:15
     ::: crates/api-types/src/types.rs (literal_enum! { MessagingChainInputDepth { Self => "self", ... } })
error[E0425]: cannot find type `MessagingChainInputDepth` in this scope
```

## Cause

`script/rust/types.ts` builds variant names with `pascal()` and never keyword-checks the result. `pascal("self")` is `Self`. The codebase's own convention for the lowercase form already exists in `snake()`: `self`/`super`/`crate`/`_` gain a trailing underscore because they cannot be raw identifiers.

## Fix shape

Map the PascalCase `Self` to `Self_` wherever a literal value becomes a variant or tag name (`literals()`, `tagged()`, `staticTag()`, `tagModule()`), leaving the wire string unchanged (`Self_ => "self"`). The wire format is unaffected; only the Rust variant name changes.

Found by Lane TO while fixing opencode#2733; the fix rides that PR since #2733's acceptance (`bun run generate` completes) is blocked on it.

title: fix(plugin-github): authorizeRead should return the canonical path for an existing target (#2641 follow-up)
body:
## Follow-up to #2641 (optional step 3, not covered by the landed fix)

PR #2720 closed #2641: `packages/plugin-github/src/files.ts` now classifies by canonical location, consistent with `packages/core/src/file-access.ts`. One optional step from #2641 was not taken:

**`authorizeRead` should hand back the canonical path for an existing target.** Core's `FileAccess.authorizeRead` does this so the file that was authorized is the file that is read. The plugin's `authorizeRead` returns the `resolve()` target unchanged, so for an internal target reached through an in-project symlink, `GitHubShared.readable()` returns the lexical (symlink) path. If the symlink is swapped between authorization and the caller's read, the read can be redirected to a different file than the one classified and approved — a narrow TOCTOU window of the same class #2641 fixed for classification.

## Proposed change

In `files.ts` `authorizeRead`, after the permission asserts: if the target exists, return `{ ...target, absolute: <canonical path> }`; otherwise return the target unchanged. Add a regression test: an in-project symlink to another in-project file is authorized on its lexical resource, and the returned `absolute` is the canonical target file.

Acceptance criteria (from #2641) are already met without this; it is a hardening refinement, filed separately per the single-implementation rule after the #2641 claim collision (Lanes SK/SM, 2026-11-23).

title: test(ui): bun test JSX transform emits an undefined jsx identifier for component files — packages/ui cannot host render tests
body:
## Problem

`packages/ui` cannot host a component render test: any test that imports a `.tsx` component fails before it runs.

The test preload (`packages/ui/test/solid-jsx.ts`) registers a Bun plugin that transpiles every `[jt]sx` file with `Bun.Transpiler` using `jsx: "react-jsx"` and `jsxImportSource: "solid-js/h"`. With the repo's Bun (1.4.4), that transform emits calls to a hashed jsx identifier (observed: `jsx_w77yafs4`) that is never defined or imported in the output, so the module throws at runtime:

```
ReferenceError: jsx_w77yafs4 is not defined
  at LineCommentEditor (packages/ui/src/data-display/line-comment/line-comment.tsx)
```

Reproduced from #2710's work: a `bun test` file importing `LineCommentEditor` from `./line-comment` and rendering it under happy-dom (with `--conditions=browser`, per the note in `packages/session-ui/src/timeline/placement-reactivity.test.ts`) fails with that error inside the component module itself. Running the preload's exact transpiler settings over `line-comment.tsx` directly shows the dangling `jsx_w77yafs4` references in the output.

Pure `.ts` modules (e.g. the line-comment `machine.ts`) transform fine, which is why the existing suite — state machines and other logic only — never hits this. There is currently not one DOM-render component test under `packages/ui/src`.

## Impact

Component-level behaviour in `@opencode/ui` (rendered ARIA semantics, DOM structure, event wiring) cannot be pinned by tests in the package that owns the components; verification has to fall back to view-model seams or the app package's browser harness.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `bun test` file under `packages/ui/src` can import a `.tsx` component, render it into happy-dom, and assert on the resulting DOM.
- The existing `bun test src` suite in `packages/ui` still passes unchanged.
