title: fix(server): job.cancel returns 204 for unknown job IDs — a typoed or stale ID looks like a successful abort

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/server
labels.description: Package: server (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

- `packages/core/src/job.ts:177`: `cancel` is typed `Effect<Info | undefined>`.
- `packages/core/src/job.ts:555-594` (`cancelInternal`): unknown `id` hits `if (!job) return [{}, jobs]` (:561), so `result.info` is `undefined` and the cancel resolves to `undefined`.
- `packages/server/src/handlers/job.ts:25-27` (`JobHandler.cancel`): `yield* jobs.cancel(id)` discards the `Info | undefined` return — miss and hit both fall through to the endpoint's `NoContent` success.
- `packages/protocol/src/groups/job.ts:45-47`: `job.cancel` declares success `NoContent` with **no error cases**, so an unknown ID answers 204 exactly like a real abort.
- No `JobNotFound`-style error exists anywhere (contrast the many `…NotFoundError` classes in `packages/protocol/src/errors.ts`), and no test pins the unknown-ID behavior.

## Why this is a defect

A cancel against a typoed, wrong-session, or already-GC'd job ID returns 204 and is indistinguishable from a successful abort — the same defect class as #2543 (integration oauth/command cancel), but on the experimental background-job endpoint, which #2543 does not cover. It also masks client routing bugs: nothing tells the caller the job never existed. Precedent for the stricter posture already exists in-repo: `packages/server/test/session-inbox-cancel.test.ts:6` pins that `session.inbox.cancel` maps an unknown inbox item to a conflict instead of an empty success.

Note the endpoint description already documents "Cancelling a job that already finished does nothing" — idempotent 204 for a *known, settled* job is intended and must be kept. Only the *unknown-ID* case should change. Complication: `completeBackground` (:648-661) deletes consumed entries from the in-memory map, so a recently finished-and-consumed job is currently indistinguishable from a never-existed one at the handler layer.

## Acceptance criteria / suggested fix

- `POST /api/experimental/job/:id/cancel` returns 404 (new `JobNotFoundError` in `packages/protocol/src/errors.ts`, wired into the endpoint's error list, handler `mapError`, and `openapi.json`/generated clients) when the ID matches no live-tracked job.
- Keep 204 for a known but already-settled job (idempotent cancel, per the documented description) — e.g. consult the persisted background-job row/tombstone where the in-memory entry is gone, or document that consumed IDs 404 and update callers.
- Update the fire-and-forget callers to tolerate the not-found case: `packages/tui/src/routes/session/composer/scripts-tab.tsx:115`, `packages/tui/src/routes/session/composer/subagents-tab.tsx:201`, `packages/app/src/session/requests/model.ts:304` (`cancelJob`), plus the shared `job.cancel` wiring in `packages/server/src/handlers/persistent-pty.ts:46`.
- Add a server test mirroring `session-inbox-cancel.test.ts`: unknown job ID -> 404, known running job -> 204, known settled job -> 204.

title: fix(a11y): expose line-comment mention list as a listbox
body:
## Problem

The @-mention autocomplete in both line-comment editors renders its popup as a plain `div` of plain `button`s, with the active item marked only by `data-active`. The textarea has no `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, or `aria-activedescendant`.

- v2 (`packages/ui/src/data-display/line-comment/line-comment.tsx`, lines 350-407): textarea at 350-378 carries only `aria-label`; the mention list at 380-407 is a role-less `div`, items at 387-394 are role-less `button`s with `data-active` instead of `aria-selected`.
- v1 (`packages/session-ui/src/components/line-comment.tsx`, lines 339-404): same shape — textarea at 339-375, role-less mention list at 376-404, `data-active` on plain buttons.

Meanwhile the shared editor machine (`packages/ui/src/data-display/line-comment/machine.ts`, `navigation()` + `textareaKey()`) moves an active item with ArrowUp/ArrowDown (and Ctrl+n/p) and exposes it as `activeMentionPath` in `viewLineCommentEditor()`. So keyboard users can change the highlighted item, but assistive technology gets no announcement that a listbox is open, how many options it has, or which option is active.

## Verification

Parsed both render blocks for ARIA wiring — neither contains `listbox`, `option`, `aria-selected`, `aria-activedescendant`, or `aria-expanded`:

```
line-comment.tsx (ui)        | listbox: False | option: False | aria-selected: False | activedescendant: False | aria-expanded: False
line-comment.tsx (session-ui)| listbox: False | option: False | aria-selected: False | activedescendant: False | aria-expanded: False
```

The machine test (`packages/ui/src/data-display/line-comment/machine.test.ts`) covers state transitions only, so nothing pins the rendered semantics.

## Acceptance criteria

title: fix(core/server): session.permission.create asks leak — no timeout, no cap, orphans survive session.remove

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
## Summary

`Permission.ask` entries created via `session.permission.create` live in an in-memory `pending` map with no timeout, no cap, and no cleanup when the owning session is removed. Orphaned requests stay listed as pending until the location shuts down, and `session.permission.get` / `reply` keep serving them after the session is gone.

## Evidence

- `packages/core/src/permission.ts:284-301` — `create()` inserts into `pending` with a fresh `Deferred`, publishes `permission.asked`, and returns. No timeout, no expiry, no size cap.
- `packages/core/src/permission.ts:303-309` — `ask()` calls `create()` when the evaluated effect is `ask` and returns immediately. Unlike `assert()` (`packages/core/src/permission.ts:327-340`, which deletes the entry in `Effect.ensuring` after the await settles), the `ask()` path has no awaiter and therefore no cleanup path except `reply()` or full service `close()`.
- `packages/core/src/permission.ts:180-193` — the only bulk cleanup is `close`, run on location shutdown (`packages/core/src/location-lifecycle.ts:63`). Nothing runs on session removal.
- `packages/core/src/session.ts:592-608` — `Session.remove` interrupts execution, cancels jobs, closes transport, clears environments, publishes `SessionEvent.Deleted`, and removes the bus, but never touches `Permission` pending entries.
- `packages/server/src/handlers/permission.ts:21-29` — `requireOwnedRequest` (used by `session.permission.get` at `:70-75` and `session.permission.reply` at `:77-85`) only checks `permission.get(requestID)` and `request.sessionID === sessionID`. It never checks the session still exists, so a deleted session's orphaned request is still retrievable/repliable. By contrast `session.permission.list` (`:60-68`) resolves the session first via `sessionInfo`, so list 404s while get still 200s — inconsistent.

## Repro

1. Create a session `S`.
2. `POST /api/session/S/permission` with an action/resources pair that evaluates to `ask` (e.g. an unlisted action). Repeat N times without replying.
3. `GET /api/session/S/permission` grows by N each time; nothing expires.
4. `DELETE` (session.remove) `S`.
5. `GET /api/session/S/permission/:requestID` still returns the orphaned request from the in-memory map, while `GET /api/session/S/permission` (list) fails session lookup. The orphans persist until the location scope shuts down.

Effect: any API client can grow the location-scoped `pending` map unboundedly, spam the approval UI with requests that outlive their session, and leave `permission.request.list` polluted with dead-session rows.

## Impact

- Unbounded in-memory growth per location (one entry + one never-awaited `Deferred` per unanswered `ask`).
- Stale approval prompts for sessions that no longer exist; inconsistent get-vs-list behavior after delete.
- Tool-run `assert()` waiters are interruptible via `execution.interrupt`, but API-created `ask()` entries have no owner fiber to interrupt, so they are the ones that leak.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ask()`-created pending entries have a bounded lifetime (timeout/expiry) and/or are purged when the owning session is removed.
- [ ] `session.permission.get` / `reply` validate the owning session still exists (consistent with `list`), or orphaned entries are deleted on `Session.remove` so the question is moot.
- [ ] Repeated unanswered `session.permission.create` calls cannot grow memory without bound (cap, TTL, or backpressure).

## Notes

- Distinct from #2619 (Form.ask join timeout): this is the Permission service's `ask()` path, not Form. No open `permission` issue covers pending expiry/orphans (checked `gh issue list --state open`; matches were only closed or unrelated).

title: feat(desktop): recover window bootstrap over IPC when the argv bootstrap is missing
body:
## Problem

#2695 hardened the desktop preload so a window started without a `--opencode-window=` bootstrap argument no longer crashes before `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld`: the preload exposes a minimal bridge (empty snapshot, undefined `windowID`/`bootstrap`) and the renderer asks over IPC for what the IPC contract can answer (first-launch state, per-namespace storage reads).

The degraded window still has **no window id**, so window-scoped state cannot be seeded or persisted for it: the renderer's window state falls back to an empty id (no restored route, no window snapshot), and anything keyed by the real window id is unavailable until the window is recreated normally.

## Proposed slice

Add a main-side IPC channel that answers the bootstrap for the calling webContents:

- Main keeps a window registry (`register(win, id)` in `packages/desktop/src/main/windows/index.ts`); a handler can resolve `event.sender` → `BrowserWindow.fromWebContents` → the registered app-level window id, then answer with the existing `windowBootstrap(id)` from `main/windows/bootstrap.ts`.
- The preload, when `windowBootstrapFromArguments` returns undefined, invokes that channel and exposes the recovered bootstrap (and fetches the snapshot with the recovered id) instead of the minimal bridge.
- Renderer contract stays as widened by #2695 (`getWindowID()` / `getWindowBootstrap()` may be undefined only if the channel also fails).

## Acceptance

- A window whose preload starts with a missing/malformed bootstrap argument recovers its real window id and bootstrap over IPC; its storage snapshot is fetched with the recovered id.
- The channel answers only for registered windows (unknown sender → undefined, renderer stays in the #2695 degraded mode).
- Tests cover: recovery happy path, unknown-sender refusal, and the preload falling back to the minimal bridge when the channel errors.

Two test files in `services/legacy/test/` target modules and routes that no longer exist on main (`7403b84a0d`), so the legacy package's `bun test` suite cannot pass as written:

title: feat(core): replace timed shell/command handoff with durable admission

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: New feature or capability request

labels.name: task/triage

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

body:
## Problem

The composer serializes prompts, shell requests, and server-command requests through one per-session send chain, but shell/command requests do not have durable admission. In `packages/client/src/solid/data.ts:317-333,1987-2012`, the chain releases a long-running request after a fixed 250 ms even if its HTTP response has not arrived. The source comment documents why this is needed: a prompt can be waiting on a browser-attachment gate, while `!shell` or `/command` must not overtake it. This makes ordering depend on a timing heuristic, not on the server's admission order, and keeps the request open while work runs.

The server-side split is visible in `packages/core/src/session/session.ts:254-297,322-340`: prompts and compactions enter `SessionInbox` and wake execution, while shell starts a fiber and joins until the process exits; `packages/core/src/session/command.ts:11-38` executes a command (which may run shell and then prompt) inline. The client TODO at `data.ts:317-333` already identifies durable admission and event-driven completion as the way to remove the workaround.

## Proposed improvement

Give shell and server-command operations durable, idempotent admission into the session's ordered work stream. Return from the HTTP request once admitted, then report start/progress/completion or failure through session events. Preserve ordering against prompts and compactions without a fixed `SEQUENCE_HANDOFF_MS` delay, and define how retries, cancellation, and restart recovery behave.

## Acceptance checks

- A delayed or disconnected client request cannot make a later prompt, command, or shell overtake an already accepted operation.
- The client can reconcile an admitted operation and its terminal result from durable state/events without keeping the POST open for the whole execution.
- Tests cover gated preparation, delayed admission beyond 250 ms, duplicate admission IDs, and operation completion/failure; retain existing shell/command behavior and output.

title: session record carries no route_usage: claim stamps cannot name the serving leaf (server-side remainder of #1891)
body:
## Gap: session records carry no `route_usage` — claim stamps can't name the serving leaf

**Found by:** Lane GT (archer) reconciliation of developing-today/code#1340 criterion 1, 2026-11-23. Fresh production measurement + code read; this is the server-side remainder of #1891 (closed: the route_usage tool readout exists) and of developing-today/code#9408 (closed: the fleet-queue client now prefers `route_usage.lastServing` when a session record carries it).

### Evidence

- The fleet-queue client's stamp derivation (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client/support.rs`, `session_model_stamp`) reads `route_usage.lastServing` from the session record when present, and deliberately stamps **nothing** for routed sessions when it is absent — recording the declared route alias (`opencode-route/workhorse`) would permanently mislabel the claim. Its own comment records: "The deployed server's session records today carry no route_usage field at all — verified 2026-11-14".
- Fresh measurement of the production queue DB (Turso `fleet-queue`, window 2026-11-22T00:00Z → 2026-11-23T06:05Z, 315 completions, status=done):
  - `claim_variant` non-null: **0 / 315** (and 0 / 21 tasks in `claimed` state at measure time)
  - `claim_model` non-null: 116 / 315 — 114 are the by-design `muse-lane` marker for non-session actors, 1 is `opencode-route`/`workhorse` (the route alias itself), 1 is a real leaf (`_openai.main`/`gpt-6-luna`)
  - completion-telemetry `effort` non-null: **0 / 315** (it derives from claim_variant / the session leaf's variant — both empty)
  - completion-telemetry `model` non-null: 109 / 315, of which 108 are the `muse-lane` pseudo-model

### Ask

Surface the serving-leaf readout on the session record itself: `GET /api/session/<id>` (and the enveloped `data` shape) should carry `route_usage.lastServing` with `providerID` + `modelID` + `variant` — the same shape the route_usage tool already produces (#1891) — updated as the serving leaf changes, so a claim made mid-session stamps the leaf that is actually serving at claim time.

### Why it matters

developing-today/code#1340 (meta-reviewer) criterion 1 — per-pool/per-effort outcome tables from real fleet data — stays unmeetable until routed session claims stamp a real serving leaf and variant. The client side is done and waiting on this record shape; no fleet-queue change is needed once the field lands (the derivation prefers it automatically, and a present-but-unparseable readout stamps nothing rather than falling back to the alias).

title: fix(desktop): harden window-bootstrap parsing in preload — missing/malformed argv throws before contextBridge
body:
## Problem

`windowBootstrapFromArguments` (`packages/desktop/src/shared/window-bootstrap.ts:16-22`) throws on every abnormal input, and its only production caller is the preload entry (`packages/desktop/src/preload/index.ts:19`), which runs **before** `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld`. Any throw there leaves the renderer without `window.electron` (no `windowID`, no storage snapshot) — a broken shell instead of a degraded one. The file header even says `Undefined means "ask over IPC"`, but the implementation has no undefined path: it throws `Error("Window bootstrap argument not found")` when the arg is absent.

## Evidence (verified on `origin/main` b8de4520)

Replicated the exact function logic under node:

| argv | result |
|---|---|
| `["electron"]` (arg missing) | `THROWS Error: Window bootstrap argument not found` |
| `--opencode-window=%E0%A4%A` (truncated UTF-8) | `THROWS URIError: URI malformed` (`decodeURIComponent`) |
| `--opencode-window=%ZZ` (bad escape) | `THROWS URIError: URI malformed` |
| `--opencode-window=42` / `null` (valid JSON scalar) | returns `42` / `null` cast as `WindowBootstrap` — then `bootstrap.id` is `undefined` and `windowDataFile(undefined)` (`packages/desktop/src/shared/ipc-transport.ts:40-42`) throws `TypeError` on `.replace` |

So three throw classes (missing / malformed-encoding / valid-JSON-wrong-shape), all uncaught in the preload, all fatal to renderer setup. The existing test (`window-bootstrap.test.ts:10`) even locks in the throwing behavior for the missing-arg case.

Reachability: argv is normally written by main (`main/windows/bootstrap.ts:20-22`), but a second-instance handoff, dev harness, or any future caller that opens a window without the arg hits the crash path with no fallback.

## Suggested fix

- Return `undefined` (per the header contract) instead of throwing when the arg is absent or unparseable, and validate the parsed shape (`typeof parsed === "object"`, non-null, `typeof id === "string"`) before casting.
- In `preload/index.ts`, handle `undefined` by exposing a minimal bridge and letting the renderer take its existing ask-over-IPC path for the snapshot.

## Ruled out as duplicates

Searched open/recent issues and open PRs for `bootstrap`, `preload`, `contextBridge`, `argv` — no matches (only unrelated #2517 via the word "Windows"). Related #2659 covers rejected renderer `loadURL` promises, a different failure point.

title: fix(ai/quota): antigravity wrong-client reclassification is dead code — refresh outcome drops status and OAuth error code
body:
## Defect

In `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/antigravity.ts`, the wrong-client reclassification can never fire:

- `refreshAccessToken` builds `RefreshOutcome` as `{ ok: true, accessToken, status: 200 }` on success and `{ ok: false, error: message }` on failure — the HTTP status is **never set on failure**.
- `AntigravityAuth.refresh` (`packages/ai/src/providers/antigravity-auth.ts`) fails with plain `Error`s whose messages are `token endpoint rejected refresh (HTTP <status>)` or the client-secret-not-configured text — the OAuth error code (`unauthorized_client`) from the token endpoint's response body is never parsed or propagated.
- `isWrongClientRejection` requires `result.error === "unauthorized_client"` **and** `result.status === 400 || 401` — neither can ever hold, so the rule "every candidate came from the credential store and every refresh was a confirmed wrong-client rejection → report Not configured" is dead code.

## Effect

A credential-store `google` login issued by another client (e.g. a Gemini CLI OAuth sign-in) sits in a permanent `configured: true` / "Failed to refresh Antigravity token" state instead of the canonical module's "Not configured". The openchamber module classifies this correctly (`refreshGoogleAccessToken` returns `{ status, error }` and its `isWrongClientRejection` works); the fork's port lost the classification on the way over.

Found during developing-today/code#2490's keyring-unification slice (developing-today-forks/openchamber#2513), where the same classification matrix was re-verified surface by surface.

## Fix shape

Carry the token endpoint's HTTP status and OAuth error code through `AntigravityAuth.refresh`'s failure (parse the response body's `error` field, as the canonical module's exchange does) into `RefreshOutcome`, so the existing `isWrongClientRejection` rule works as written. Add provider tests: store-origin candidate + `unauthorized_client` @400 → `configured: false` "Not configured"; store-origin + `invalid_grant` → refresh-failure state kept; keyring/file-origin + `unauthorized_client` → refresh-failure state kept (Antigravity-issued by construction).

title: fix(gui-extensions): SSH remote-CLI discovery picks the lexically-last cached beta, not the newest (0.0.0-beta-9 wins over beta-10)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

The SSH remote-CLI discovery script picks a cached managed beta by glob order, not by version. The loop in `RemoteCli.discoverScript` keeps the **last** match of `"$HOME"/.opencode/desktop-ssh/0.0.0-beta-*/opencode`. Shell globs sort lexically, so once two betas are cached the older one wins: `0.0.0-beta-9` is chosen over `0.0.0-beta-10`, and `0.0.0-beta-2` over `0.0.0-beta-10`. Nothing removes old staged betas, so the inversion persists until the lexically-larger directory is deleted by hand.

## Evidence

- `packages/gui-plugins/src/ssh/remote-cli.ts:30-36` (origin/main `ce615977a2`): the cache branch loops over `"$HOME"/<dir>/<prefix>*/opencode` and assigns `cli="$binary"` on every executable match, so the final assignment wins.
- `packages/gui-plugins/src/ssh/bootstrap.ts:19-20`: this is the SSH `discoverScript` that uses `fromPath: true` plus `cache: { directory: ".opencode/desktop-ssh", prefix: "0.0.0-beta-" }`.
- `packages/gui-plugins/src/ssh/bootstrap.ts:164`: the discovered path is run as `"$cli" service status` (through `registrationScript`), and `parseRegistration` output decides whether a registered service is reused (`registered.version === input.version`) or a fresh install and start is attempted.
- Reproduction, with the generated loop reproduced verbatim (`sh`, empty `PATH`, fake executables): with `~/.opencode/desktop-ssh/0.0.0-beta-9/opencode` and `~/.opencode/desktop-ssh/0.0.0-beta-10/opencode` present, the script prints `.../0.0.0-beta-9/opencode`.
- No existing test covers more than one cached beta: `packages/gui-plugins/src/ssh/remote-cli.test.ts:237-260` (fake staged CLI) and `bootstrap.test.ts:40` (`2.0.0` only).
- Dedupe: fresh searches of open and closed issues (`beta`, `discover`, `desktop-ssh`, `lexical`) and of open and merged PRs found only the closed banner and WSL framing work (#265, #290, #334, #340, #345), the SSH download caps (#1006, #1281, #1307), and PR #270 and #346. None addresses cache ordering.

## Why it matters

`latestBeta()` keeps moving forward (`0.0.0-beta-N`) and each install stages a new directory, so this configuration becomes common over time. Discovery then probes status through an older CLI than the one just installed. The concrete user-visible effect depends on whether the older binary's `service status` is compatible with the running service; I have not verified that, so the claim here is limited to the wrong binary being selected and used for the status read. The fix is cheap and removes a silent version skew.

## Suggested fix

Select the cached binary with the highest version, not the last glob match (for example by sorting the matches with `sort -V` before choosing, or by preferring the version the installer last staged). Keep the existing `-x` check and quoting.

## Acceptance criteria

- With `0.0.0-beta-9` and `0.0.0-beta-10` cached, discovery prints the `beta-10` path. Also cover `beta-2` vs `beta-10`.
- A regression test in `packages/gui-plugins/src/ssh/remote-cli.test.ts` runs the real `discoverScript` through `sh`, following the existing fake-CLI harness at lines 237-260.
- The existing single-cache and no-cache cases keep their output.

Filed by improvement-issue-creator (lane B). Scratch worktree cleanup is recorded in the sweep log.

title: fix(core): continuation bypasses per-target context ceilings

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

Per-target context ceilings are still bypassed when a routed turn continues on a pre-resolved fallback after output has started.

- `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts:1035-1045` resolves `ContinueOn` by calling the current member's `routing.fallback()` after output has started.
- `packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts:329-336,449-456` keeps that resolved member as `continueOn` and passes it into the next `context.load`.
- `packages/core/src/session/context.ts:201-219` returns immediately when `chosen` is supplied. The history-size estimate and sized resolution used by the ordinary path are below that return at `:221-307`.

So the next member is used as-is without comparing the continued request size against its per-target context ceiling. The following automatic compaction may reduce the request when enabled, but this is not equivalent to context-aware route selection: with auto-compaction disabled, a too-small fallback can receive an oversized continuation even when a later route member has enough context. That can turn an otherwise recoverable continuation into another context-overflow failure.

## Relationship to prior work

This is a follow-up to closed #891 / merged #898, which thread request sizing through initial session-context resolution. #891's ordinary `SessionContext.load(selection)` path is present on current `main`; this report is specifically the early-return path for an already chosen `ContinueOn` member. Searches for `ContinueOn`, continuation context ceilings, `requestTokens`, and open PRs found no distinct tracked follow-up or implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Continue-on-fallback resolution accounts for the active history size when applying per-target context ceilings.
- [ ] A continuation skips an over-limit member when a later eligible member can serve it, without retrying an already-served route member or mishandling probe claims.
- [ ] Tests cover the continuation path and preserve the existing initial-turn behavior; unknown-size behavior remains non-filtering.

title: fix(core): retain shell capture files while commands are running

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage

labels.name: source/creator

labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

The hourly shell-output retention sweep can unlink the capture file for a command that is still running. Once the file is removed, the open write stream may keep writing to an unlinked inode while `Shell.output()` reads by pathname; the reader converts the missing-file error into a zero-byte page, silently losing the command's captured output.

## Evidence (fresh `origin/main` `e86346cd26fa4dd030909be97142d20f920f9ca9`)

- `packages/core/src/shell.ts:139-162` enumerates every `sh_*.out` capture across projects and passes all paths to `FileRetention.cleanup` with `RETENTION` (7 days), without checking whether a file belongs to a running command.
- `packages/core/src/shell.ts:165-167` runs this cleanup hourly. The active `commands` map is local to the location-scoped service (`:189`), while the cleanup node is global (`:169-173`), so the sweep currently has no active-command exclusion.
- `packages/core/src/shell.ts:409-421` registers a running command and opens its capture with `createWriteStream`. The output pump (`:423-442`) stops writing after the 10 MiB cap, so even a still-running capped command's file mtime can age past retention.
- `packages/core/src/file-retention.ts:11-19` removes any file older than the cutoff based only on mtime; it does not account for an open writer or running command.
- `packages/core/src/shell.ts:254-275` reads output by pathname and resolves stream errors as zero bytes. After cleanup unlinks a live capture, callers can therefore receive empty output instead of an error or their captured bytes.

A direct regression scenario is to start a command that writes output and remains running, backdate its `.out` mtime beyond seven days, then invoke `Shell.cleanup()`: the path is eligible for deletion while the command remains registered as `running`. On POSIX filesystems, subsequent writes through the still-open stream do not recreate that pathname.

The existing `packages/core/test/shell-cleanup.test.ts` only verifies pruning expired orphan files across projects and preserving recent/unrelated files; it does not cover an active writer. I attempted `bun test test/shell-cleanup.test.ts` in the fresh scratch checkout, but it could not start because dependencies are not installed there (`Cannot find package 'effect'`).

## Why it matters

Long-lived or quiet shell commands (including dev servers/watchers) may outlive the seven-day cutoff without writing, and output-capped processes stop refreshing their capture mtime. The hourly sweep can then make all previously captured output—and any later output—unreadable while the process still runs. This breaks the shell service's output/read contract and can hide command results from sessions and tools.

## Suggested fix

Make retention cleanup aware of live capture files (for example, share a reliable active-file registry with the global sweep or use an equivalent lease/marker design). Continue pruning expired files left behind by exited commands or prior process runs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Periodic cleanup does not unlink a capture file while its command is running, including a quiet command and a command whose capture reached the output cap.
- [ ] Regression coverage starts a live shell command, ages its capture past the retention cutoff, runs cleanup, and verifies the path and captured output remain readable until the command terminates.
- [ ] Expired orphan captures from exited commands or prior process runs are still removed; the existing cross-project cleanup test remains green.
- [ ] Missing capture data is not silently represented as a successful empty read if a separate disappearance occurs.

## Related

- CLOSED #2486 capped shell output size and `shell.output` page allocation. This report is distinct: it covers the retention sweep deleting a still-active command's capture file.

title: Pin a preferred pool member per session while keeping pool failover
body:
## Problem

In a model pool (`opencode-route/<id>`) there is no way to say "use this pool member for this session" and keep the pool's failover. OpenChamber's current-model menu (developing-today-forks/openchamber#2466) can only do it with `session.switchModel` to the member's concrete model, which takes the session out of the pool: no failover, no cooldown handling, until the user picks "Return to pool". Route overrides (`route-overrides.json`) apply to every session, so they can't express a per-session choice either.

## What we want

A per-session preferred target inside a pool:

- The session stays on `opencode-route/<id>`.
- OpenCode uses the chosen member for every request while it is healthy (not benched, not over budget, not quota-demoted, not skipped by an `avoid` override, still in the pool).
- When that member errors (timeout, quota, cooldown, refused), the request fails over to the pool's other members exactly as today, and the failover shows in the route log like any other.
- Once the chosen member is healthy again, later requests return to it (same as "continuity" returning to the origin target today), unless the user cleared or changed the choice.
- Clearing the choice returns the session to normal pool selection.

## Rough shape

- Store the choice per session and route next to the existing sticky state (`sessionTarget` / continuity in `packages/core/src/model-route.ts`), or as a session field so it survives a restart. Decide which and document it.
- Apply it in the walk before the round-robin/weighted draw and the ordered rank: the chosen leaf goes first when it is in the available set; otherwise the normal order applies.
- Expose it over the API, e.g. `POST /api/session/:id/route-target` with `{ routeID, target: "provider/model#variant" | null }`, plus the current value on the session or in `route_usage` so clients can show it.
- Respect timing: a change made during a running turn applies from the next model request (the runner already reloads context per step).

## Tests

- Chosen member is used while healthy, for round-robin, weighted and ordered pools.
- Chosen member benched or erroring: the request goes to the next member; after the bench ends, requests return to the chosen member.
- A chosen member that left the pool, or is skipped by an `avoid` override, is ignored.
- Clearing restores normal selection; other sessions on the same pool are unaffected.

## Follow-up in OpenChamber

Switch the current-model menu (`CurrentModelIndicator` / `lib/routing/poolMemberPick.ts`) to the new call so a pick no longer leaves the pool, drop the "direct pick stops pool failover" notice, and show the chosen member on the current-model line.

title: fix(core): reconcile file mutations interrupted before tool settlement

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

body:
## Problem

A process interruption can leave a file mutation applied without a settled tool result in the session history. This is a crash-consistency gap between filesystem side effects and durable tool execution state, not a request for general file undo (Git-backed snapshots and `session.revert` already exist).

In `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts`, a local tool call is published before `executeTool` runs (around lines 535-547); after execution, its output is truncated and then passed to `publisher.toolExecution` (lines 544-549). `packages/core/src/file-mutation.ts` performs the write at lines 111-123 and explicitly leaves crash recovery/idempotency between `Tool.Called` and durable settlement as a TODO at line 158.

If the process exits after the filesystem write but before `publisher.toolExecution`/`publisher.failTool` completes, the file has changed while the session contains an unsettled tool call. The next session resume or retry has no explicit reconciliation protocol for that partially completed side effect.

## Requested work

Define and implement a recovery/idempotency contract for file-mutating tool calls across interruption between mutation and durable settlement. Reconcile interrupted calls on resume (or use another documented strategy) so the session history and filesystem do not silently disagree, and avoid blindly repeating a non-idempotent partial operation.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add a deterministic test that interrupts execution after a file mutation has taken effect but before its tool result is durably settled.
- On recovery/resume, the tool call is reconciled according to a documented outcome; it is not left indefinitely ambiguous and the mutation is not blindly duplicated.
- Cover both successful recovery and an operation that fails before changing the file, preserving existing `session.revert` behavior.
- Update or remove the crash-recovery TODO in `packages/core/src/file-mutation.ts` once the contract is implemented.

## Evidence

- `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts`: tool-call publication precedes execution, and `publisher.toolExecution` / `publisher.failTool` follow execution.
- `packages/core/src/file-mutation.ts:111-123`: filesystem write occurs before the mutation returns; `:158` names the crash-recovery/idempotency gap.
- Existing snapshots and undo cover reverting completed changes, but do not by themselves settle a tool call interrupted between its side effect and result publication.

Dedupe: fresh all-state searches for durable settlement and interrupted/idempotent tool mutation returned no matching issue; open/closed PR search found no implementation.

body:
## Evidence

On `origin/main` (`b70580bbee83c4f5773e733b4859ff6afd8ea1d9`), `packages/ai/src/protocols/commandcode.ts:401-412` lowers each historical tool result to a Command Code `tool-result` whose `output` is always `{ type: "text", value: ProviderShared.toolResultText(part) }`. The Command Code wire type has only this text output shape here; the internal result discriminator (`text` vs `error`) is discarded. In `packages/ai/src/protocols/shared.ts:311-325`, `toolResultText` serializes error values as ordinary text/JSON, with no error marker. Thus a failed operation and a successful result with the same text become identical in subsequent Command Code request history.

The existing history test in `packages/ai/test/provider/commandcode.test.ts:147-188` covers only a successful tool result. The shared error-marker fix #2226 explicitly left Command Code unchanged (PR #2661 body) and its acceptance/tests cover OpenAI Chat/Responses, Mistral, and Antigravity only. Related provider-specific history issues #2663 (Cohere) and #2664 (Gemini) do not cover Command Code.

A targeted `bun test test/provider/commandcode.test.ts` was attempted from `packages/ai` on this checkout; it cannot execute because the worktree lacks the `effect` package. The gap is directly evidenced by the lowering and serializer above; no source changes were made.

## Impact

After a failed tool call, Command Code receives ordinary-looking output in the next request and can treat the operation as successful, impairing recovery and creating inconsistent tool behavior relative to the adapters fixed in #2226.

## Acceptance criteria

- Preserve failed-tool status in Command Code request history using a representation supported by its text-only tool-result wire shape (prefer the stable `[tool_error] ` marker already introduced for text-only adapters in #2226).
- Add a Command Code protocol regression test that compares an error result and a successful result with the same text and proves they remain distinguishable on the wire.
- Keep successful text and JSON tool-result lowering unchanged.

title: fix(protocol): openapi.json stale on main — route-overrides API, instruction-entry 404 and inbox-cancel 409 missing; check:generated red
body:
## Summary

`packages/protocol/openapi.json` on `origin/main` (dfb64702a1) is stale. `bun run check:generated` (`packages/protocol/script/generate-openapi.ts --check`) fails there, so the drift gate is red on main. The committed document is missing:

- the whole `/api/route/overrides` surface (list, add, remove) from #2496 (merged in `015f1aaced`);
- the `InstructionEntryNotFoundError` 404 shape for `DELETE /api/experimental/session/{sessionID}/instructions/entries/{key}` from `4afde072b0` (#2656), which still documents only `SessionNotFoundError | LocationNotFoundError`;
- the 409 `ConflictError` response and the updated description for the inbox cancel route, from a merged change that did not regenerate the document.

The `services/www/openapi.json` and `services/www/public/openapi.json` copies are derived from the protocol document and are stale in the same way (`grep route/overrides` finds nothing).

## Evidence

- Scratch worktree of `origin/main` at `dfb64702a1cd7b23d29b751c4191b909fd58094c`, `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, then `bun run script/generate-openapi.ts --check` in `packages/protocol`: exit 1, "Generated OpenAPI document is stale. Run `bun run generate` from packages/protocol."
- Regenerating gives a 367-line insertion and 2-line deletion diff against the committed `openapi.json`; the three hunks above account for it.
- `4afde072b0` changed `packages/protocol/src/errors.ts` and `packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts` and did not touch `openapi.json`.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs `check:generated`, so main's CI is expected to report this.

## Why it matters

Any client generated from `openapi.json`, and the www API docs, will miss the route-overrides API that OpenChamber is being consolidated onto (#2491), and will mis-document the instruction-entry 404. The drift gate exists to catch exactly this, and it is currently red on main.

This is a recurrence: closed #1560, #1498, #1593, #1610, #829 and #660 are the same class. The fix is a regeneration, and it should not be repeated per merge.

## Acceptance criteria

- `bun run check:generated` passes in `packages/protocol` on a fresh checkout of main.
- `packages/protocol/openapi.json` contains `/api/route/overrides` (get/post/delete) and `InstructionEntryNotFoundErrorEncoded` in the instruction-entry remove 404.
- The `services/www` copies (`openapi.json` and `public/openapi.json`) are regenerated from it, and their own staleness check passes.
- The fix regenerates; it does not hand-edit the document.

## Suggested fix shape

Run `bun run generate` in `packages/protocol`, then the www copy script, and commit the regenerated output in one PR. Optionally, a follow-up can make the merge path re-run the check on protocol-touching PRs, so a change to `packages/protocol/src/**` cannot land without the regenerated document.

No open PR covers this (`gh pr list --search openapi`; #2517 touches gate allowlists only, not `openapi.json`).

title: fix(desktop): handle rejected renderer loadURL promises

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
## Problem

`packages/desktop/src/main/windows/scheme.ts:11-20` calls `void win.loadURL(...)` in both development and packaged mode. Electron's `BrowserWindow.loadURL()` returns a promise that rejects when navigation fails; `void` does not handle that rejection. The desktop main process has no `unhandledRejection` handler (the CLI has one, but desktop does not), so under the runtime's default unhandled-rejection behavior a renderer navigation failure can terminate the main process. A Node reproduction with the same unhandled rejected-promise shape exits with code 1.

There is an additional first-window timing gap: `createEarlyWindow()` calls `loadWindow()` in `windows/early.ts:92`, while `wireWindowRecovery()` is only attached later in `windows/index.ts:174` after the main bundle is imported. A fast initial navigation failure can therefore also precede the `did-fail-load` recovery listeners. Later windows attach recovery before calling `loadWindow`, but the returned promise is still unhandled.

## Why it matters

A transient renderer/protocol startup failure should be reported and recovered by the existing window recovery flow, not unexpectedly crash the whole desktop main process and all windows.

## Suggested fix

Handle the `loadURL()` promise at the shared `loadWindow()` boundary. Preserve the existing recovery behavior, and ensure early-window load failures are logged or surfaced even before the normal recovery listeners are installed; do not simply swallow the failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- Both dev-server and packaged-protocol `loadURL()` rejections are handled.
- A rejected initial early-window navigation does not become an unhandled rejection or terminate the main process.
- Failures remain observable and use the existing recovery UX where possible.
- Add focused tests for rejection in both URL branches and for the early-window timing path.

title: fix(ai): honor tool indexes when streamed IDs collide
body:
## Problem

`toolIndexByID` in `packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts` can select the wrong tool-call slot when a gateway reuses one tool-call ID at different indexes. It searches `{ ...pendingTools, ...tools }` and returns the first matching ID; integer-like object keys iterate in ascending order, so this is the lowest index, not necessarily the index on the incoming delta. The caller then prefers this match over the delta's explicit `tool.index`.

For example, with calls at indexes 0 and 1 both carrying `id: "call_0"`, a continuation `{ id: "call_0", index: 1 }` resolves to index 0. Its arguments can be appended to the wrong call. The existing occupied-index guard does not help because the ID match is already defined.

This is conditional on a gateway reusing IDs; the isolated helper reproduction confirms the misrouting, but this report does not claim that IDs are reused by every or any particular provider.

## Suggested direction

Use the stated index when it identifies a compatible slot, and make conflicting ID/index matches explicit rather than silently routing to the first ID match. Add regression coverage for duplicate IDs at distinct indexes and for pending/committed entries.

Related: #1708 tracks custom-provider tool-call support; PR #2260 handles a different case where an index is reused with a new ID.

title: fix(ai): guard unguarded `new URL(result.url)` in `isSessionExpiredStatus` — a non-empty malformed final URL throws (inconsistent with guarded `teamIdOf`)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

body:
## Problem

`isSessionExpiredStatus` in `packages/ai/src/quota/cdp.ts` ends with an unguarded `new URL(result.url)`:

```ts
export const isSessionExpiredStatus = (result: CdpFetchResult): boolean => {
  if (result.status === 401 || result.status === 403) return true
  if (!result.url) return false
  // Redirects to login pages land on an exact auth/login path segment.
  // Resource names (for example, `login-history`) and query values are not pages.
  return new URL(result.url).pathname
    .split("/")
    .some((segment) => segment.toLowerCase() === "auth" || segment.toLowerCase() === "login")
}
```

`CdpFetchResult.url` is the final URL string returned by the in-page `fetch(...).url` (a browser CDP response). The empty-string case is already handled, but any other value that is not a valid absolute URL — a relative path, a `data:`/`about:` blob, a malformed or truncated string, a value with stray whitespace or an unencoded character — makes `new URL(...)` throw a `TypeError: Invalid URL`. The helper is not wrapped in try/catch, so the throw propagates.

Both callers invoke it inside a `try { ... } catch` that classifies any thrown error as `cdp-unavailable` / a portal failure rather than as a data read:

- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/meta.ts:406` — `if (quotaResult && isSessionExpiredStatus(quotaResult))` → sets `portalFailure = { failureClass: "session-expired", ... }` and falls through to the key-endpoint cross-check; a throw instead aborts the whole portal block into the outer `catch` as `cdp-unavailable`.
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/mistral.ts:165` — same shape; a throw turns a single malformed final URL into "portal read failed" / `cdp-unavailable` instead of a normal HTTP classification.

So the defect is not a crash (the outer catches save it) but a **misclassification**: a quota read whose final URL happens to be non-parseable is reported as `cdp-unavailable` (browser unreachable) rather than as the HTTP outcome it actually was, and the good data / correct failure class is lost. This is inconsistent with the established, guarded pattern in the same file's neighbourhood: `teamIdOf` (meta.ts:61-69, fixed in #1931) wraps `new URL(pageUrl)` in try/catch and falls through to the default on an unparseable page URL, with a comment noting "An empty or unparseable page URL names no team". `isSessionExpiredStatus` was not given the same guard when it was rewritten for #2166 (segment-based matching).

## Evidence (verified this run on main `e437f09da3`)

- `new URL("not a url")` → `TypeError: Invalid URL` (Node/`bun`).
- `new URL("")` is already covered by the `if (!result.url) return false` guard; the gap is specifically non-empty, non-parseable strings.
- `isSessionExpiredStatus` at `cdp.ts:333-341` has no try/catch around `new URL(result.url)`.
- `teamIdOf` at `meta.ts:61-69` is the in-repo precedent for the guarded parse.

Probe cases (direct calls to the exported helper, `packages/ai/test/cdp.test.ts` style):

- `{ status: 200, url: "not a url" }` → throws `TypeError` (should return `false`).
- `{ status: 200, url: "https://admin.example/api/quota" }` → `false` (control, must stay `false`).
- `{ status: 401, url: "not a url" }` → `true` (status check precedes URL parse, already safe).

## Why it matters

The final URL comes from an untrusted browser response and is not validated anywhere upstream (`CdpFetchResult.url` is typed `string` and populated straight from `r.url`). A provider rename, a redirect through a relative/`about:` URL, or a browser that reports a truncated URL can flip a healthy quota read into a spurious `cdp-unavailable` ("browser unreachable") classification, which is the wrong failure class and misleads both the UI and any retry/health logic keyed on `cdp-unavailable`. The guard is cheap and makes the helper total over its input domain, matching `teamIdOf`.

## Suggested fix

Wrap the parse in try/catch returning `false` on failure, mirroring `teamIdOf`:

```ts
export const isSessionExpiredStatus = (result: CdpFetchResult): boolean => {
  if (result.status === 401 || result.status === 403) return true
  if (!result.url) return false
  try {
    return new URL(result.url).pathname
      .split("/")
      .some((segment) => segment.toLowerCase() === "auth" || segment.toLowerCase() === "login")
  } catch {
    // A final URL that does not parse names no login page; the HTTP status
    // (already checked above) is the only signal available.
    return false
  }
}
```

No change to the segment-based matching semantics introduced by #2166, to the `cdp-unavailable` classification, or to per-path result shapes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `isSessionExpiredStatus` never throws for any string input; a non-parseable non-empty `url` returns `false` (unless status is 401/403).
- [ ] The intended detections still classify as expired: 401, 403, and a landed-on login/auth page URL (redirect case), each pinned by a test.
- [ ] New unit tests cover the malformed-URL case (`{ status: 200, url: "not a url" }` → `false`) plus the existing #2166 probe cases (no regression).
- [ ] Meta and Mistral quota suites stay green; no change to `cdp-unavailable` classification or per-path result shapes.

## Relevant files

- `packages/ai/src/quota/cdp.ts` — defect site (`isSessionExpiredStatus`, lines ~333-341).
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/meta.ts` — caller; guarded `teamIdOf` (#1931) is the established pattern.
- `packages/ai/src/quota/providers/mistral.ts` — other caller.
- `packages/ai/test/cdp.test.ts` — existing tests for `isSessionExpiredStatus` (#2166).

title: fix(console): console-signup reads its inbound JSON body unbounded before validation — no size cap on POST /api/console-signup
body:
## Evidence

The Console signup route reads its inbound JSON body with no size cap, before any validation runs:

- `packages/console/app/src/routes/api/console-signup.ts:7` — the SolidStart `POST /api/console-signup` handler passes `event.request` straight through.
- `packages/console/app/src/lib/console-signup.ts:10` — `const data: unknown = await request.json().catch(() => null)` — no `content-length` precheck, no capped reader. The whole body is buffered and parsed before `consoleAccountSchema.safeParse` ever sees it.

This is the last uncapped inbound JSON parse in the console/function surface:

- The same file's *response* side got the bounded treatment in #1158: `packages/console/app/src/lib/console-account.ts:19-38` (`CONSOLE_ACCOUNT_LOOKUP_MAX_BYTES = 64 KiB`, content-length precheck + streaming read that cancels on over-cap), with a comment noting the schema keeps a valid payload under 1 KiB.
- Every neighboring inbound body already has a cap: enterprise contact form (#2635), newsletter multipart (#2634), the function-package share/admin/token routes (#2648), `/share_sync` (#2626), `/feishu` (#2603). This route was missed by that sweep.

## Why it matters

`POST /api/console-signup` is deployed in the console app and gated only by the shared `CONSOLE_CRM_TOKEN` bearer (timing-safe compare at `console-signup.ts:6-8`). The capping family has consistently treated token-gated routes as in scope (#2648's `share_delete_admin`, #2632's admin routes): a leaked or rotated-out CRM token, or a compromised/buggy caller service, can stream an arbitrarily large or endless body that `request.json()` buffers whole in the server worker — memory exhaustion and DoS of the console app before the zod validation (which caps `id` at 255 chars and would reject it) ever runs. The failure is silent: the request simply never completes.

## Suggested fix shape

Mirror the existing in-repo pattern (`readCappedLookupJson` in `console-account.ts`):

1. Add `CONSOLE_SIGNUP_MAX_BYTES` (a valid payload is < 1 KiB by schema construction; 16 KiB is generous) in `console-signup.ts`.
2. Content-length precheck → reject over-cap with 413 before reading; otherwise stream-read the body, cancelling the stream as soon as the running byte count exceeds the cap, and return 413.
3. Then parse and zod-validate as today. The local dev path (`packages/console/app/script/dev-enterprise.ts:56`) calls the same handler, so it inherits the cap with no extra work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An oversized body with a declared `content-length` above the cap returns 413 without the body being read.
- [ ] An oversized body with no/lying `content-length` is rejected 413 mid-stream (the underlying stream is cancelled), never fully buffered.
- [ ] Valid small payloads, invalid JSON, and schema-invalid payloads behave exactly as today (200 / 400 / 400).
- [ ] The request never reaches `syncConsoleAccount`/Salesforce unless the body was under the cap.
- [ ] Unit test in `console-signup.test.ts` covering the declared-over-cap and streamed-over-cap paths.

title: fix(console): bound Honeycomb webhook payload before parsing and logging
body:
## Evidence

`packages/console/app/src/routes/honeycomb/webhook.ts:82-84` parses the authenticated request with `request.json()` and immediately logs both the object and a pretty-printed serialization. The Zod schema at lines 14-35 accepts an unbounded array of groups and unbounded `key`/`value` strings. There is no declared-length check or streaming byte limit before parsing. A sufficiently large valid webhook body is therefore fully buffered, parsed, and expanded into logs; logging duplicates the payload and pretty-printing adds further amplification.

This is distinct from #2650, which bounds the *outbound Discord content* after parsing and does not bound or suppress the incoming payload/logging.

## Why it matters

An oversized webhook can consume memory and produce disproportionately large server logs before the outbound Discord limit is applied. The route requires the webhook token, but that does not bound a misconfigured or compromised sender or protect the process/log pipeline from large accepted requests.

## Acceptance criteria

- Enforce a finite request-body byte cap before JSON parsing, including chunked requests without `Content-Length`; reject over-limit input with 413.
- Avoid logging the full untrusted payload; log bounded metadata or a redacted/truncated representation.
- Add tests for oversized declared and streamed bodies, and for bounded logging behavior.
- Keep the existing #2650 Discord content-length handling and webhook authentication behavior.

body:
## Problem

The Honeycomb webhook relay builds one Discord `content` string from every alert group, with no limit on group count or `group[].value` length. Discord documents webhook `content` as up to 2,000 characters ([Execute Webhook](https://discord.com/developers/docs/resources/webhook#execute-webhook)). When the generated content exceeds that limit, Discord rejects the POST and this route returns 502, so the alert is not relayed in that attempt.

## Evidence

- `packages/console/app/src/routes/honeycomb/webhook.ts:24-31` accepts an unbounded array of groups and unbounded string values.
- `packages/console/app/src/routes/honeycomb/webhook.ts:40-68` maps every group into a line and joins all lines into one `content` value without truncation or splitting.
- `packages/console/app/src/routes/honeycomb/webhook.ts:104-107` maps any non-2xx Discord response to 502.
- A source-faithful construction using 20 groups with 123-character values produced a 2,816-character `content` string; the current schema accepts that shape.

The existing Honeycomb timeout fix (#1126 / merged PR #1135) handles a stalled Discord endpoint, not a content-size rejection.

## Requested improvement

Keep generated alert content within Discord's documented limit, preferably by splitting large alerts into bounded messages or by truncating with a clear indication and preserving the alert URL/role mention. Ensure any multi-message strategy has an explicit failure policy so partial delivery is observable.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add regression coverage for oversized group/value payloads.
- No outgoing webhook `content` exceeds Discord's documented 2,000-character limit.
- Normal-sized alerts retain their current content and mention behavior.
- Oversized alerts are handled deterministically and do not get treated as successfully delivered when all useful alert details were dropped.

title: fix(function): cap remaining JSON POST request bodies before parsing (share_create, share_delete, share_delete_admin, exchange_github_app_token_with_pat, /api/share)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Finding

Several Cloudflare Function JSON POST routes still call `c.req.json()` with no request-body cap, so an unauthenticated (or pre-authentication) caller can make the Worker buffer and parse an arbitrarily large payload before any validation or secret check runs. Two siblings already track this pattern — #2603 (`/feishu`) and #2626 (`/share_sync`) — but the remaining routes below are not tracked, and #2626's acceptance criteria only *suggests* applying the same bounded-body helper to them. This issue makes that concrete per route so the function has one consistent request-size policy.

## Evidence (verified on main `16e1c7cb833927bea6b9c393c0aebec834c70211`)

`packages/function/src/api.ts`:

- Line 124 `.post("/share_create", ...)`: line 125 `const body = await c.req.json<{ sessionID: string }>()` — parses the full body before deriving `sessionID` and calling `stub.share`; no `Content-Length` pre-check or streaming cap.
- Line 136 `.post("/share_delete", ...)`: line 137 `const body = await c.req.json<{ sessionID: string; secret: string }>()` — parses before the `secret` type check (line 140) and `stub.assertSecret` (line 143).
- Line 147 `.post("/share_delete_admin", ...)`: line 148 `const body = await c.req.json<{ sessionShortName: string; adminSecret: string }>()` — parses before the `adminSecret !== Resource.ADMIN_SECRET.value` check (line 151), so the admin secret is only compared after the whole body is materialized.
- Line 350 `.post("/exchange_github_app_token_with_pat", ...)`: line 351 `const body = await c.req.json<{ owner: string; repo: string }>()` — parses `owner`/`repo` (lines 352-353) before the `Authorization` header check and permission verification inside the `try` (line 355+).

`packages/function/src/share.ts` (V1 compatibility host):

- Line 164 `.post("/api/share", ...)`: line 165 `const body = await c.req.json<{ sessionID: string }>()` — materializes the entire body even though only `body.sessionID.slice(-8)` (line 166) is used; the route is externally reachable and keeps working for legacy clients.

None of these routes (nor the function package generally) performs a `Content-Length` pre-check or streaming byte cap — `grep` for `content-length`/`contentLength`/`maxBody`/`bodyLimit` in `packages/function/src/` only matches an unrelated response header read in `discord.ts`.

## Why it matters

- `/share_create`, `/share_delete`, `/share_delete_admin` and `/api/share` are externally reachable share endpoints; `/share_delete_admin` additionally gates on `ADMIN_SECRET`. Parsing first means an attacker can force unbounded memory/CPU work before any credential check, and (for `/share_delete`) before `assertSecret`.
- `/exchange_github_app_token_with_pat` reads its body before validating the bearer token, so the PAT-gated path can be driven to allocate memory with no valid credential.
- `/api/share` (V1 compat) exists solely to keep old clients working and stores nothing, but still buffers the whole request.
- Repeated oversized unauthenticated requests can exhaust Worker memory/CPU; this complements (does not duplicate) #2603 and #2626, which track the same gap for `/feishu` and `/share_sync`.

## Suggested fix

Introduce one shared bounded-body helper for the function package (mirroring the declared-length pre-check + streaming cutoff shape used by the server's `readBoundedJsonBody` in `packages/server/src/handlers/completions.ts`, #2314) and apply it to every JSON POST route in `packages/function/src/api.ts` and `packages/function/src/share.ts`. Reject oversize declared `Content-Length` up front and cut off chunked bodies the moment the streamed total crosses the cap, returning a deterministic 413 before parsing, Durable Object calls, R2 writes, or secret comparison. Choose and document a per-route (or single) limit appropriate to each payload (share payloads are small; the token-exchange body is tiny).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `/share_create`, `/share_delete`, `/share_delete_admin`, `/exchange_github_app_token_with_pat` and `/api/share` each enforce a documented maximum request size before `c.req.json()` parsing.
- [ ] Declared `Content-Length` over the limit is refused before body consumption (no parse, no Durable Object/R2/secret side effect).
- [ ] Chunked / unknown-length bodies are stopped at the byte cap before full buffering/parsing and answered 413.
- [ ] Oversized requests return 413 and do not invoke `stub.share`/`assertSecret`/`clear`/`publish`, the Octokit/GitHub flow, or the Discord relay.
- [ ] Valid (in-limit) requests for all five routes continue to behave as before, including V1 `/api/share` clients.
- [ ] Tests cover oversized declared-length, chunked/unknown-length overflow, and a normal in-limit request for each route (or a shared helper test plus per-route wiring tests).
- [ ] The function has one consistent request-size policy; `/feishu` (#2603) and `/share_sync` (#2626) remain the trackers for their own routes and are not duplicated here.

Distinct from #2603 (Feishu webhook) and #2626 (share_sync) and #2314 (server JSON routes).

body:
## Evidence

In `packages/plugin-browser/src/files.ts:27-33`, `BrowserFiles.read` resolves a caller path, awaits `realpath(candidate)`, checks that the returned path is under the project root, then separately awaits `open(real, "r")`. The verified path is therefore not tied to the object that is opened: replacing the resolved in-project directory entry with a symlink after `realpath` but before `open` makes `open(real)` follow the new symlink outside the project.

Reproduced the filesystem ordering directly with Node's `node:fs/promises`: resolve an in-project file with `realpath`, unlink it, replace it with a symlink to an outside file, then `open` the previously verified pathname. The read returned the outside file's `outside-secret` contents. The source has the same two separate awaited operations in that order.

Both `files.upload` and `files.drop` invoke `BrowserFiles.read` and send its returned bytes to the selected browser page (`packages/plugin-browser/src/tools.ts`). #2289 established the project-directory authorization boundary and closed the ordinary traversal/symlink escape; it does not make the checked object stable across this check/open race. OPEN #2645 addresses byte-limit enforcement on the same read path, not path containment across replacement. Fresh all-state searches for `realpath/open/symlink upload`, `TOCTOU symlink filesystem`, and `race plugin-browser path`, plus open-PR search for `plugin-browser symlink realpath`, found no tracker or implementation for this race.

## Why it matters

A concurrent writer able to replace an upload path in the project can race the check and cause the server to read and transfer a file outside the authorized project directory. The path boundary is explicitly intended to prevent browser uploads from reading outside the project.

## Acceptance criteria

- Bind the containment decision to the opened filesystem object, or otherwise detect and reject a path replacement before reading any bytes.
- Ensure an in-project file remains readable and outside-project targets remain rejected for both upload and drop.
- Add a deterministic regression test that replaces the path between canonicalization and open (for example through an injected filesystem seam), and assert that outside-file bytes are never returned.
- Keep the byte-limit behavior tracked separately under #2645.

body:
## Problem

The GitHub attachment upload checks a local file size with `stat()` and rejects files over the image/video limit, but later reads the file with unbounded `fs.readFile()`. The authorization check and repository API request occur between the size check and the read (`packages/plugin-github/src/explore.ts`, `readLocal`/`readBytes` and upload flow around lines 629-651, 1445-1455). If the file grows or is replaced after `stat()`, the tool can read and upload more than the declared 10 MiB image or 100 MiB video limit, allocating the full contents in memory first. The response also reports the earlier stat size, not the actual bytes read.

## Expected

Enforce the configured limit during the read itself (or use an equivalent opened-file/fstat and bounded-read strategy), reject if the file exceeds it or its contents are inconsistent with the authorized size, and report the actual uploaded byte count.

## Acceptance criteria

- A file that grows after the initial size check cannot cause a read/upload beyond the image/video byte cap.
- Validation and authorization metadata correspond to the bytes actually uploaded.
- Tests cover growth/replacement between stat and read, as well as normal image/video boundary behavior.

body:
## Evidence

In `packages/plugin-browser/src/files.ts:33-46`, each upload/drop path is opened, checked with `file.stat()`, and then read with `file.readFile()` (to EOF). The per-file `stat.size` check is only a pre-read snapshot, so a file that grows after the stat can exceed `Browser.MAX_FILE_BYTES` during the read. The aggregate check at `:53-56` occurs only after `Promise.all` has fully read every file.

`packages/plugin-browser/src/rpc.ts:338-348` allows up to eight paths for both `files.upload` and `files.drop`, while their documented limit is 5 MiB total. Thus eight individually 5 MiB files are all materialized concurrently (up to 40 MiB of file bytes, before object/copy overhead) and only then rejected. A concurrent file growth can also bypass the per-file stat guard because `readFile()` has no byte limit.

This is distinct from #2289, which addressed authorization/containment of uploaded paths, and #2644, which addresses whole-file reads in the core local filesystem driver. This finding is limited to the plugin-browser upload/drop transfer cap.

## Why it matters

The tool advertises a 5 MiB total transfer limit, but rejected calls can still allocate substantially more memory, and a changing file can exceed even the per-file limit before rejection. Concurrent tool calls amplify the transient memory use in the OpenCode server.

## Acceptance criteria

- Enforce the aggregate byte budget before or during reads, not after all file contents have been materialized.
- Bound bytes actually read from each open file so file growth after `stat()` cannot bypass the 5 MiB per-file ceiling.
- Keep both `files.upload` and `files.drop` at the documented 5 MiB total limit and preserve useful errors for oversized inputs.
- Add tests proving an over-total multi-file request is rejected without reading every payload, and that a file growing after metadata inspection cannot cause an oversized read.

body:
## Evidence

In `packages/core/src/environment/local.ts`, `makeLocalDriver().read` first stats the target, but the no-range branch then calls `fs.readFile(value)` without checking `info.size` or enforcing a byte ceiling (around lines 21–27). The same driver does use a bounded allocation for ranged reads.

This is reachable from ordinary file mutation tools: `FileMutation.readText` in `packages/core/src/file-mutation.ts` calls `files.read(target)` with no range, and edit/patch/write use that helper to read existing content before building previews or applying a change (for example `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/edit.ts:247` and `write.ts:73`). A very large existing file can therefore be fully materialized in the local OpenCode process, sometimes more than once during a mutation.

There is already a contrasting bound in `packages/core/src/environment/exec-defaults.ts`: whole-file process-backed reads are collected with `MAX_DATA_BYTES = 64 * 1024 * 1024`, and the Files contract documents that larger whole-file reads fail. The local driver has no corresponding limit, so behavior depends on the selected environment driver.

## Why it matters

A large file encountered by a normal edit/write/patch operation can consume memory proportional to its full size and contribute to an OpenCode process OOM. The caller's intent to make a small edit does not constrain the size of the pre-existing file.

## Acceptance criteria

- Whole-file reads through the local driver have a documented, enforced upper bound consistent with the Files contract, or are changed to a bounded/streaming strategy where callers need larger files.
- Ranged reads remain usable for files above that bound.
- Add a regression proving an oversized whole-file read fails with the typed `Environment.Failed` result without allocating the full file; cover the boundary and a successful ranged read on the same file.
- Confirm edit/write/patch surface the bounded failure as a normal tool error rather than crashing the process.

title: fix(core): a dead mcpx daemon is never re-spawned in a live session — the daemonEnsured latch never re-arms and projected tools fail outright
