labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

`ensureDaemon()` runs once per process at plugin init (`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/mcpx.ts:437`) and sets the module-level `daemonEnsured = true` on **every** exit path (`:311`, latch set at `:334`, `:343`, `:352`, `:380`, `:386`). After the daemon dies mid-session — idle exit, crash, or supervisor restart — nothing in the process ever re-probes or re-spawns it: every later `ensureDaemon()` returns immediately, and the only `/v1/reload` call site is inside that dead code path.

The default lifecycle guarantees the condition: a daemon opencode spawns gets `--daemon-idle-exit 1h` by default (`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/mcpx.ts:139-149`, the #14 leak fix), so any opencode session that outlives one idle hour loses its daemon **by design**, with no in-process recovery story.

## Evidence (reproduced on origin/main f8522013c5)

Stub-daemon repro using the real `mcpx.ts` module (same pattern as `packages/core/test/mcpx-daemon-client.test.ts`: `MCPX_DAEMON_ENDPOINT` pointing at a local HTTP daemon, plus a recording fake `OPENCODE_MCPX_BIN`):

```
step1 health hits after first ensureDaemon: 1
step1 spawn attempts: none
step3 second ensureDaemon returned in 0 ms
step3 additional health probes during second ensureDaemon: 0
step3 spawn attempts after daemon death: none
step4 /v1/call error name: DaemonUnreachableError | DaemonUnreachableError
```

- First `ensureDaemon()` probes health once and latches.
- After the daemon is closed, a second `ensureDaemon()` performs **zero** health probes and **zero** spawns.
- A projected-tool-style call (`/v1/call`) then fails with `DaemonUnreachableError`.

Asymmetric impact within one session:

- `mcpx_exec` degrades to the CLI fallback on `DaemonUnreachableError` (`mcpx.ts:506-516`) — the only tool with a fallback.
- Projected tools have **no** CLI fallback: their execute calls `callDaemon("/v1/call", "POST", ...)` directly (`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/mcpx-projection.ts:261-267`), wrapped by `failureOf` into a `ToolFailure`. A projected tool stays broken for the rest of the process.
- `mcpx_project` fails the same way (`projectTools` → `/v1/tools`, `mcpx.ts:645-652`), and `autoProjectFromScript` silently yields nothing.
- `ensureServerReady` (secrets gate) also runs through the dead daemon, so even the path before the call fails.

## Why it matters

- Long-lived sessions (this fleet's norm) silently lose every projected tool — browser automation, database tools, everything — until the process restarts or an `mcpx_exec` CLI fallback happens to resurrect the daemon as a side effect.
- The failure surfaces as a raw "fetch failed"/unreachable `ToolFailure` on an individual projected tool, which looks like a per-tool or per-server outage, not a dead daemon; nothing names the actual cause.
- The reload path (config/binary hot reload, `mcpx.ts:331-333`) is also dead once the latch is set.

## Suggested fix shape

- **Re-arm on unreachable:** when `callDaemon` throws `DaemonUnreachableError` (the one class that means "the daemon never received the request" — see the comment at `mcpx.ts:246-248`), reset `daemonEnsured`, run `ensureDaemon()` once, then retry the call. Bound the recovery (e.g. at most one re-ensure per N seconds) so a genuinely missing mcpx does not spawn a stampede; respect the existing gates (`daemonAutostartEnabled`, `mcpxDaemonAutostart`, owner-tagged spawn args) — same code path, just allowed to run again.
- Alternatively/additionally: replace the permanent latch with a lazy or periodic cheap health re-probe (e.g. re-ensure when the last successful health check is older than some interval) before projected-tool calls.

## Acceptance criteria

- Regression test (stub daemon, existing test pattern): first ensure succeeds → daemon dies → a projected-tool-style `/v1/call` (or second `ensureDaemon()`) re-probes health, spawns (fake mcpx records the attempt), and the call succeeds once the daemon answers again.
- A daemon that stays dead does not loop: recovery is bounded (single attempt / backoff), and the failure still surfaces promptly.
- `mcpx_exec` CLI fallback semantics unchanged — `DaemonTimeoutError` must still NOT fall back or replay.
- No startup-cost regression: a healthy daemon is not re-probed on every tool call.

## Related (dedupe checked)

- Closed #14 (daemon leak / idle exit), #134 (autostart=false race), #55 / #79 (idle-exit validation), #1023 (daemon client bounds) — adjacent, none covers mid-session death recovery.
- All-state issue search for `ensureDaemon`, `daemonEnsured`, daemon respawn/restart/dies/death/unreachable: no match. Open PR search (`mcpx`, `daemon`): no implementing PR (#2546 is an unrelated quota fix).
- This is the lead the 2026-11-18T12:01Z creator-B pass deferred pending a repro; this run supplied the repro (stub-daemon script, no source changes).

title: fix(plugin-github): classify local paths by canonical location — in-project symlinks to outside files skip external_directory approval

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
## Problem

The built-in GitHub plugin (`packages/plugin-github`) classifies local paths lexically, so an in-project symlink that points outside the project is treated as an internal file. The read then follows the symlink. No `external_directory` approval is raised, and the file's contents go to GitHub.

This is the same class as #2286 ("symlinked workspace paths bypass external-directory approval"). #2595 fixed it for `packages/core/src/file-access.ts` by classifying on the canonical (realpath) location. The plugin-github guard was not included in that fix. #2289/#2606 covered plugin-browser uploads only.

## Evidence

- `packages/plugin-github/src/files.ts`, `resolve` (~lines 40-60): `path.resolve(directory, expanded)` followed by `inside(directory, absolute)` / `inside(project, absolute)`. No `realpath` call. A symlink inside the project resolves to an internal target, so `external` is never set and `authorizeExternal` returns without asking.
- `files.ts`, `authorizeRead`: asserts only the `read` permission on the lexical `target.resource` (in-project path).
- `packages/plugin-github/src/shared.ts:208-209`, `readable()`: returns `target.absolute`, which callers then open by that path, so the OS follows the symlink.
- Callers that read the file contents after `readable()`:
  - `access.ts` ~450: deploy-key `from_file` → `readFile(file, "utf8")`, then sent to GitHub as the key text.
  - `release.ts` ~116-130: release assets and attachments → `stat(resolved)` and the upload reads the file by path.
  - `explore.ts` ~1437: upload path → `readLocal(file)` and then upload.
  - Also `automation.ts:74`, `settings.ts:621`.
- Core reference for the fix: `packages/core/src/file-access.ts` ~lines 93-158 canonicalizes the target (and the project and location roots) before `contains` checks.

## Impact

With a repo-committed symlink such as `assets/logo.png -> /home/user/.ssh/id_ed25519` or `key.pub -> /etc/...`, an agent using these GitHub tools can read and publish a file outside the project. The `external_directory` prompt that should appear does not. The user approves what looks like an in-project read.

## Proposed fix

1. In `files.ts` `resolve`, compute the canonical path with realpath (through the existing nearest-ancestor logic in `file-access.ts`, or a shared helper) before the `inside` checks. Use the canonical path for classification and for `external`. Keep `absolute` as the path the caller opens, so reads match the approved target.
2. Add a regression test in `packages/plugin-github/src/files.test.ts` (or the nearest existing files test): an in-project symlink to a file in a temp directory outside the project must trigger `external_directory` for the canonical directory. It must not be treated as internal.
3. Optionally, have `readable()` return the canonical path so the file opened is exactly the approved one (closes the TOCTOU window between authorize and read).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `files.ts` classifies by canonical location, consistent with `file-access.ts` (#2286 / #2595).
- [ ] A regression test with an in-project symlink to an outside file fails before the fix and passes after it.
- [ ] Non-symlink in-project and external-path behaviour is unchanged (existing `files` / `actions` tests stay green).

## Notes

Searched open and closed issues for `symlink`, `plugin-github`, `external_directory`, and `realpath` before filing. No existing issue covers the plugin-github guard. Open PRs checked at filing time: none touch `packages/plugin-github/src/files.ts`.

title: fix(console): salesforceRequest reads its Salesforce JSON response unbounded before parsing

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.description: Package: console (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Problem

`salesforceRequest()` in `packages/console/app/src/lib/salesforce.ts` returns the parsed body of every successful Salesforce response through an uncapped read:

- `salesforce.ts:206-218`: `const response = await fetch(...)`, then, after the status and 204 checks, `return response.json()`. The request carries `AbortSignal.timeout(8000)` (line 214), so the call is bounded in time but not in bytes.

The rest of the file already enforces a 1 MiB cap on Salesforce responses: `SALESFORCE_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` (line 12), `readCappedBody` (lines 15-42, declared `content-length` check plus a per-chunk count with reader cancel on overflow) and `readCappedBodyText` (line 44). The login and lead legs (#1097, lines ~99-127 and ~189-199) read through them. The `salesforceRequest` read was left out.

The gap is reachable from the public enterprise/console signup path: `packages/console/app/src/lib/console-signup.ts:14` calls `syncConsoleAccount(account.data, client ?? (await salesforceRequest()))`, and `syncConsoleAccount` (`salesforce.ts:223+`) issues read/query requests through this function. Its JSON body is therefore parsed without a byte limit.

The bounded-http gate records this read as an open remainder rather than a bounded site: `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` line 99 (`salesforce.ts :: return response.json()`) says "the body read itself is uncapped — remaining surface ... under design #1127". #1127 is CLOSED, so no live issue owns this site. Searches (all states) for `salesforce` and for `bounded by default`/`remaining surface`/`direct response body` found #1097 (login/lead timeouts, closed), #1607 (numeric-boundary disposition of the #1097 content-length parse, closed) and #1127/#1129 (closed design and gate). No open issue or PR covers this read.

## Impact

Low. Salesforce is a trusted upstream, so this is a missing guard against an oversized or misbehaving response rather than a practical exploit: an unexpectedly large response (a broad query or an upstream fault) is buffered whole into memory while the signup request waits. It is the one uncapped body read left in the file that otherwise follows the repo's bounded-by-default contract.

## Suggested fix

- Replace `return response.json()` with a capped read, for example `return JSON.parse(await readCappedBodyText(response))`. Keep the existing `status === 204` early return, which runs before the read, so no-body responses still return `null`.
- Re-disposition `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` line 99 as "bounded at the site" (naming `readCappedBodyText`), so the gate matches the code.

## Acceptance criteria

- `salesforceRequest()` never buffers more than `SALESFORCE_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`: a response with a declared `content-length` above the cap, or a body whose streamed size exceeds it, rejects with the existing "Salesforce response exceeded" error and cancels the body.
- A test in `packages/console/app/src/lib/salesforce.test.ts` covers the oversized case through `salesforceRequest()` (for example a query returning more than 1 MiB), and a regular JSON response and a 204 response still parse as before.
- `check:bounded-http` passes with the updated allowlist disposition for `salesforce.ts:218`.

## Repo

Origin: `developing-today-forks/opencode`. Single affected repo; no other repo carries this site.
Evidence checked on origin/main `f8522013c5`.

## Evidence

On `devtoday/main` (`fa677f8172`), `packages/function/src/api.ts` imports `timingSafeEqual` and uses it for the Feishu verification token at about line 253, but the share-secret check in `SyncServer.assertSecret` (around lines 88–94) uses `secret !== stored`. The admin secret authorizes clearing any shared session, and the share secret protects sync/delete operations. These comparisons can exit at the first differing character rather than comparing in constant time. This is a hardening gap; no practical remote timing exploit is claimed, especially for random secrets over network endpoints. The repository has already adopted constant-time comparison for Basic auth (#2281 / PR #2597) and Feishu verification (#2564 / PR #2599), but these Function secret checks remain uncovered.

## Suggested fix

Use a shared constant-time comparison helper for both checks, including safe handling of unequal lengths (for example, compare fixed-length digests as the Feishu handler already does). Keep missing-secret rejection fail-closed.

## Acceptance criteria

- Both share and admin secret comparisons avoid ordinary early-exit string equality.
- Missing/empty secrets and incorrect secrets are rejected; correct secrets are accepted.
- Add tests covering the share and admin checks, including a wrong secret with a different length.
- Existing function-package tests pass.

body:
## Evidence

- `packages/console/app/src/lib/enterprise.ts:100` in `handleEnterpriseRequest`: `const body = (await request.json()) as EnterpriseFormData` runs before any size check. There is no `Content-Length` check and no byte cap on the stream.
- `packages/console/app/src/routes/api/enterprise.ts` exposes this as a public `POST` with no auth, so any client can send an arbitrarily large body to the handler.
- Existing trackers cover only the outbound side (#1111 EmailOctopus response body, #1143 SES timeout, #1158 CRM lookup body). None covers the inbound request body read.

## Why it matters

The whole body is buffered and parsed before validation, including the honeypot check. A large POST spends memory and CPU in the console worker on an unauthenticated route. Other console inputs already use a declared-length plus streamed cap (`CONSOLE_ACCOUNT_LOOKUP_MAX_BYTES` in `console-account.ts`), so this path is the inconsistent one.

## Fix shape

- Reject requests whose declared `Content-Length` exceeds a fixed limit (for example 64 KiB) with 413 before reading.
- Read the body through a byte-counting stream so chunked requests without a length are also capped at the same limit.
- Add a test in `packages/console/app/src/lib/enterprise.test.ts` that sends an oversized body and expects 413, plus one that a normal form still succeeds.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Oversized declared length returns 413 without calling `request.json()`.
- [ ] Oversized chunked body (no `Content-Length`) returns 413.
- [ ] Normal-size form submission behaves as before.
- [ ] Test added in `enterprise.test.ts` and passing.

body:
## Summary

The public `POST /api/newsletter` handler in `packages/stats/app` buffers the entire inbound multipart/form body with `formData()` before any size check. Nothing caps the bytes. Every other inbound body read on the public surfaces was bounded in the same class of work (#2314, #2433, #2626, #2632), and stats itself caps its own outbound reads, so this route is the inconsistent one.

## Evidence (origin/main `2c7a113cc6`)

- `packages/stats/app/src/routes/api/newsletter.ts:8-11`: the only guard is a `content-type` header check (`multipart/form-data` or urlencoded). It does not look at `content-length`.
- `packages/stats/app/src/routes/api/newsletter.ts:13`: `const form = await event.request.formData()` reads and parses the whole body, unbounded, before the email field is checked.
- The route is unauthenticated. Its test builds the request as `https://stats.opencode.ai/api/newsletter`.
- Precedents in the same package: `packages/stats/app/src/routes/stats-shell.tsx:28-50` (GitHub stars: declared-length check plus streamed byte accounting against `GITHUB_STARS_MAX_BYTES`), and `packages/stats/core/src/domain/catalog-response.ts:2,18` (`CATALOG_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`).
- `packages/stats/app/src/routes/api/newsletter.test.ts` covers the 5s timeout, the 502 path and the stalled upstream. It has no oversized-body case.
- Related but distinct: #1111 (closed) fixed the outbound EmailOctopus fetch (timeout and error-body cap). It did not bound the inbound form read.

## Why it matters

Anyone on the internet can POST an arbitrarily large multipart body to a public route, and the worker will buffer the whole thing before rejecting it. The email field is only needed to be a short string. This is the same resource-exhaustion shape the fleet has filed for `/share_sync` (#2626) and the update service publish path (#2632).

## Suggested fix

- Reject when `content-length` is over a small ceiling (for example 8 KiB, which is generous for one email field) before reading.
- When the length is absent or wrong, stream the body with a running byte count and cancel at the ceiling, following the `stats-shell.tsx` pattern.
- Add a test in `newsletter.test.ts` that sends an oversized body and asserts a 413 (or 400) with no upstream `fetch` call.

## Acceptance criteria

- An oversized `POST /api/newsletter` is rejected before `formData()` runs, with no call to the EmailOctopus `fetch`.
- A normal subscription still returns 200 with the existing timeout signal.
- The new test fails on current main and passes after the fix.

body:
## What

services/update reads request bodies on three routes with no size bound in application code:

- `src/index.ts:422` `publishArtifact()` — after `verifyGitHub(request)` (line 423; Bearer JWT pinned to `anomalyco/opencode`'s `publish.yml` via the remote JWKS), `await request.json().catch(() => undefined)` (line 425) reads the whole body before `parseArtifact()`/`parseKey()` regex-validate channel/name/distribution/version. `metadata` is arbitrary `unknown` JSON and is stored verbatim (`JSON.stringify`, `activate()` lines 484-509, D1 `artifact` table).
- `src/index.ts:448` `markArtifact()` — `await request.formData()` (line 451) after `validMutation()` (line 634; Origin check only when an `Origin` header is present).
- `src/index.ts:264` `configureRollout()` — `await request.formData()` (line 267), same `validMutation()`.

Routes: `/api/publish`, `/admin/activate`, `/admin/minimum`, `/admin/rollout` (`fetch()`, lines 71-77). No Content-Length check, streaming cap, or cap constant exists anywhere under `services/update`.

## Why it matters

The publish path is authenticated (GitHub Actions OIDC JWT; `validGitHubClaims` pins repository/workflow/ref, lines 558-599), so this is an application-level guard gap rather than an unauthenticated flood: an accepted request can buffer and parse without bound, and `metadata` flows into D1 and admin/API responses unchanged. The auth/validation are otherwise careful (token pinning, regex identifiers, version format checks), which makes the missing size bound an inconsistency, not an unaddressed surface.

Note that `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt:205` already dispositions this exact read as "inbound request body read (authenticated publish handler), not an outbound response body" — that gate covers outbound response bodies, so it neither bounds this nor can catch a regression here.

## In-tree precedent

`services/changelog/src/index.ts:21-54` already solves the sibling shape: named constant (`CHANGELOG_MAX_BYTES`) + declared-Content-Length check + reader loop with per-chunk accounting and cancel-on-cap, documented as "The 5s fetch deadline bounds duration, not bytes, so the body is read through the capped reader below (#1250, the #1158 duration-not-bytes pattern)".

## Acceptance

- One shared bounded-body read used by all body-reading routes above (declared Content-Length over cap → 413 + cancel; streamed body over the cap → cancel + 413), or a documented, owned decision for the surface.
- Cap as a named constant with headroom rationale, mirroring the changelog pattern.
- Tests: over-cap body rejected (both declared-length and chunked/no-Content-Length shapes if the bun:test harness allows), in-cap behavior unchanged. `services/update/test/index.test.ts` currently has 6 tests, all lookup/D1-cache/retry paths; none touch publish/admin request-body parsing.

title: fix(function): share_delete leaves persisted R2 session objects behind

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/function
labels.description: Package: function (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

On current `main` (`2c7a113cc6023529582039fb877a8a4c85abafa5`), `packages/function/src/api.ts` writes every published share object under `share/${key}.json` (`SyncServer.publish`, lines 47–62). For a session info key, the actual R2 key is `share/session/info/<sessionID>.json`; message and part keys likewise begin `share/session/message/` and `share/session/part/`.

`SyncServer.clear` (lines 104–114), called by both authenticated `/share_delete` and `/share_delete_admin`, instead lists `session/message/${sessionID}/` (missing the `share/` prefix), deletes `session/info/${sessionID}` (also missing `share/` and the `.json` suffix), never lists/deletes `session/part/` objects, and processes only one `Bucket.list` result with `limit: 1000` without following a truncated cursor. The function then clears Durable Object storage and returns success, leaving the persisted R2 share data behind. `packages/function/test/share.test.ts` mocks `Bucket.list` as always empty and does not assert R2 cleanup after a successful sync/delete.

Fresh issue searches found no open tracker for share deletion/R2 cleanup; the only related open issue is #2626, which concerns bounding `/share_sync` request bodies. No open PR matched `share_delete`.

## Why it matters

Users and admins are told a share was deleted, but persisted copies of session info, messages, and parts can remain in R2. This is both a data-retention/privacy failure and unbounded stale-object accumulation; the current test double hides the problem.

## Acceptance criteria

- Delete all R2 objects belonging to the session using the same canonical key prefix used by `publish` (`share/session/...`).
- Include info, message, and part objects, and paginate through every `Bucket.list` result until no cursor/truncation remains (including sessions with more than 1,000 objects).
- Add tests with an R2 bucket fake that honors prefixes and pagination; verify successful user and admin deletion leave no session objects, while preserving objects for other sessions.
- Keep the Durable Object storage clear and secret invalidation behavior covered by existing tests.

title: fix(ci): auto-format rewrites gate-allowlisted lines — a Prettier pass turns check:numeric-boundaries red on main with a stale entry and an unlisted candidate

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: kind/ci
labels.description: CI/CD pipelines, workflows, and build automation

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: area/ci
labels.description: CI, workflows, and build infrastructure

labels.name: app/script
labels.description: Package: script (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

`auto-format` (#2453, `.github/workflows/auto-format.yml`) commits Prettier output straight to `main` and never runs the allowlist gates. The three allowlist gates (`check:numeric-boundaries`, `check:bounded-http`, `check:proto-reads`) key every disposition on the **exact trimmed source line** (`script/gate-harness.ts` — `hitKey = file :: text`). So whenever Prettier joins a wrapped `if (...)\n  return ...` onto one line, a *correctly dispositioned* site silently becomes two failures at once: an unlisted candidate (new single-line text) and a stale entry (old two-line text). Nothing catches it, because a push made with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` triggers no downstream workflow and `test.yml` is only `workflow_dispatch` + a nightly cron.

Verified on `main` (`4674a6f447`, `bun run check:numeric-boundaries`, bun 1.4.4):

```
Unlisted numeric-boundary candidate at packages/core/src/form.ts:534:
  if (monthFirst) return [Number(monthFirst[3]), MONTH_NUMBERS[monthFirst[1].toLowerCase()], Number(monthFirst[2])]
Unlisted numeric-boundary candidate at packages/server/src/handlers/completions.ts:79:
  const declaredLength = Number(Option.getOrElse(Headers.get(request.headers, "content-length"), () => ""))
Stale allowlist entry (the line no longer matches a sweep pattern): packages/core/src/form.ts :: return [Number(monthFirst[3]), MONTH_NUMBERS[monthFirst[1].toLowerCase()], Number(monthFirst[2])]
error: script "check:numeric-boundaries" exited with code 1
```

## Reproduction of the drift (not a code bug — a formatting bug in the disposition record)

```
$ git show 72cab5557d -- packages/core/src/form.ts | sed -n '/monthFirst/,+2p'
-  if (monthFirst)
-    return [Number(monthFirst[3]), MONTH_NUMBERS[monthFirst[1].toLowerCase()], Number(monthFirst[2])]
+  if (monthFirst) return [Number(monthFirst[3]), MONTH_NUMBERS[monthFirst[1].toLowerCase()], Number(monthFirst[2])]
```

`72cab5557d` is `github-actions[bot]`, 2026-11-17T04:35:35Z, subject `style(auto-format): auto-format on main`. Before it, `main` had the two-line form and `script/check-numeric-boundaries.allowlist.txt:22` matched it:

```
packages/core/src/form.ts :: return [Number(monthFirst[3]), MONTH_NUMBERS[monthFirst[1].toLowerCase()], Number(monthFirst[2])] :: pre-existing bare conversion inventoried as ...
```

After it, the key matches nothing (stale) and the new joined line is unlisted. The same commit collapsed four more wrapped `if` bodies in the same file (lines ~338, 375, 443, and the `monthFirst` case above) — none of those carry a `Number(` so only this one flipped the gate.

The bot commit is also the last change to `packages/server/src/handlers/completions.ts` (`72cab5557d` shows as that file's newest commit), while the offending `Number(content-length)` at line 79 is from `93f430d7af` (`fix(server): bound JSON request bodies before buffering (#2314)`, PR #2596). That site never got a disposition and the merge that introduced it was not gated — `test.yml` has no `pull_request` trigger (`#1401`) and its only scheduled run is `0 3 * * *`.

## Why this is not already covered

- **#2587** (OPEN) covers `transcriptions.ts:59` only, one other `Number(content-length)` from the same #2433/#2314 wave.
- **#2518** / **#2537** / **#2522** / **PR #2517** cover the `check:bounded-http` drift from run 43849921062 (`extension/manager.ts`, `voice-input.ts`) — none of them touch `packages/core/src/form.ts` or `completions.ts:79`. Confirmed with `gh pr diff 2517 | grep -E 'form\.ts|completions\.ts'` → no matches, and `PR #2517`'s branch (`green-main-unit-ci`) still carries the pre-format `transcriptions.ts` line and no `completions.ts` disposition at all.
- The historical gate-drift issues (#1514, #1540, #1606, #1655, #1660, #2405) each fixed one round of *content* drift. None addressed the mechanism, and none was caused by the formatter (the workflow landed 2026-11-17, #2453/#2602).

So the class of failure — "the formatter rewrites a dispositioned line and the disposition key dies with it" — has no tracker, and it will recur on every auto-format pass that touches a gated line.

## What to change (suggested; the fix decision is yours)

1. **Make auto-format prove itself.** After `bunx prettier --write`, run the three gates on the working tree before committing. If a gate that passed at `origin/main` now fails, fail the pass (or open a follow-up issue) instead of pushing a red `main`. The workflow already has the full checkout and bun available (`.github/workflows/auto-format.yml` steps 1–3).
2. **Do not dispose on the formatter's mercy for joinable statements.** Either make the keys formatter-stable (normalize whitespace in `hitKey`, e.g. collapse internal runs of whitespace in the trimmed text, so `if (x)\n  return Y` and `if (x) return Y` are one key), or add a `// prettier-ignore` immediately above each allowlisted multi-line site. The normalized-key option also closes the same trap for `check:bounded-http` and `check:proto-reads`, which share `script/gate-harness.ts`.
3. **Disposition the two live sites** now, so `main` is green while (1)/(2) land: delete the stale `form.ts` two-line entry (line 22), add `packages/core/src/form.ts :: if (monthFirst) return [Number(monthFirst[3]), MONTH_NUMBERS[monthFirst[1].toLowerCase()], Number(monthFirst[2])]` with its existing baseline disposition text, and add `packages/server/src/handlers/completions.ts :: const declaredLength = Number(Option.getOrElse(Headers.get(request.headers, "content-length"), () => ""))` with a safe-by-construction reason of the same shape already used for `transcriptions.ts` — absent header → `0`, malformed → `NaN`, and the `Number.isFinite` guard before the cap comparison.

Note for (3): `transcriptions.ts:59` is deliberately left out — that is #2587's scope.

body:
## Evidence

`packages/function/src/api.ts:157-169` handles the public `POST /share_sync` route by calling `await c.req.json()` at line 158 before checking the share secret with `stub.assertSecret(body.secret)` at line 168. There is no declared-length check or streaming byte limit. An unauthenticated caller can therefore make the Worker buffer and parse an arbitrarily large JSON payload before the request is rejected. For authorized requests, `content` is then serialized again in `SyncServer.publish` (`api.ts:47-62`) and stored in both R2 and Durable Object storage, increasing the memory and storage impact.

The current route tests in `packages/function/test/share.test.ts:102-127` verify that missing/old secrets cannot write, but do not cover oversized bodies. The related closed #2563 fixed the missing-secret authorization bypass; this is a separate resource-exhaustion gap, and closed #2314 adds a bound only to the OpenCode server handlers, not this Cloudflare Function.

## Why it matters

`/share_sync` is externally reachable and performs expensive body parsing before authentication. Repeated large unauthenticated requests can consume Worker memory/CPU without a valid share secret. A secret holder can also submit a very large `content` that is serialized and persisted twice.

## Acceptance criteria

- Enforce a documented maximum request size before JSON parsing on `/share_sync`; enforce it while streaming too, so chunked requests without a trustworthy `Content-Length` cannot bypass it.
- Reject oversize requests with a clear 413 response before calling the Durable Object or writing to R2.
- Add tests for oversized valid JSON with no secret, chunked/unknown-length overflow, and a normal authorized sync that still succeeds.
- Consider applying the same bounded-body helper to the other JSON POST routes in `packages/function/src/api.ts` so the function has one consistent request-size policy.

title: fix(core): parseRenderAnswer classifies fallback answers without current provider/tier context — a wait for the exhausted provider becomes a switch to it (PR #2450 review finding)

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

CodeRabbit raised this on PR #2450 and it was never addressed: `parseRenderAnswer` accepts being called without its context argument, and then misclassifies quota-fallback answers. For a wait action naming the currently exhausted provider/tier — e.g. `{ action: "fallback", provider: "anthropic", tier: "standard" }` — a context-free call returns `kind: "switch"`, because the wait/switch distinction is computed by comparing the payload against `context.currentProvider`/`currentTier`. `applyQuotaFallback` then produces a switch to the exhausted provider/tier instead of a wait. The payload carries no action kind, so the parser cannot infer the selection without complete context.

- Source PR: #2450 — https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2450
- Review comment: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2450#discussion_r4575255985
- Reviewer: coderabbitai[bot], 2026-11-14T19:10:52Z (Minor · Functional Correctness)
- Flagged location: `packages/core/src/session/runner/render-card.ts:304`

## No-response evidence

- No replies on the review thread; the thread is unresolved (checked via GraphQL `reviewThreads` this run).
- No fix commit after the comment: the fallback branch is unchanged on current main. The PR's merge-time agent notes disposition only the automated-review gate, not this finding.
- Issue search (PR number, file, function) found no existing tracker.

## Still live on current main

`packages/core/src/session/runner/render-card.ts` (current main, lines 291–310): the signature keeps `context?` optional, and the fallback branch computes

```ts
const kind =
  context?.currentProvider === answer.provider && context?.currentTier === answer.tier ? "wait" : "switch"
```

so with `context` omitted the answer is always classified `switch` whenever provider/tier are well-formed.

## Acceptance criteria

- Fallback answers are not classified as a switch when current provider/tier context is missing — complete context is required for fallback parsing, or the parser returns `none` when it is incomplete — AND
- a regression case covers calling `parseRenderAnswer` without context (asserting `applyQuotaFallback` does not switch to the exhausted provider/tier), while wait-vs-switch behavior with complete context is preserved; OR the finding is resolved by a documented decision recorded on this issue.

title: fix(core): joined Form.ask silently ignores its own timeout — a deduped ask can pend past its deadline, indefinitely when the owner set none

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: queue/queued
labels.description: Has a queued task in the Supabase agent queue

labels.name: app/core
labels.description: Package: core (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Finding

PR #2582 (fix for #2445) made a joined (deduped) `Form.ask` timeout stop cancelling the shared form — but as implemented, the joined ask's own `timeout` is silently unhonored entirely: the joiner keeps waiting on the shared deferred past its own deadline, and if the owning ask set no timeout and nobody replies, the joiner pends indefinitely despite explicitly passing a bounded wait.

## Evidence

- PR: #2582 — https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2582 (merged 2026-11-17T01:38:50Z, merge commit 3f19c9a495e0)
- Current main `c53fd4768cba`, `packages/core/src/form.ts:194-206` (verbatim at review time):

```ts
const timedOut = Effect.sleep(timeout).pipe(
  Effect.andThen(
    existing
      ? Effect.void
      : cancel(form.id, { ... }).pipe(Effect.ignore),
  ),
  Effect.andThen(Deferred.await(entry.deferred)),
)
return yield* restore(awaited.pipe(Effect.race(timedOut)))
```

For a joined ask (`existing` set), once its timer fires `timedOut` degenerates to `Deferred.await(entry.deferred)` — the same deferred `awaited` already waits on — so the race can only settle when the form itself settles (reply, owner cancel, or the owner's own timeout). The owner's timeout is optional: at `form.ts:185-186`, an owner with `timeout === undefined` returns `restore(awaited)` directly, so a joined ask against such a form has no bound at all.

- The PR's own test (`packages/core/test/form.test.ts`, "a joined ask timeout does not cancel the pending form it joined") gives the owner a 10-minute timeout and settles the form by reply; it never asserts the joiner resolves at (or near) its own 1-minute deadline.

## Why it matters

Callers pass `timeout` to bound how long they block on a user answer (#1883's bounded wait exists precisely because "a pending form's cache entry never expires"). A deduped re-ask — the session-resume path dedupe was built for — can now block far beyond its stated bound, or forever, with no signal that its deadline was ignored.

## Acceptance criteria

- A joined ask resolves at its own timeout with a terminal/timeout outcome visible to that caller, WITHOUT cancelling or otherwise settling the shared form for the owner and other joiners.
- A test pins it: owner with no timeout (or a much longer one), joiner with a short timeout — the joiner resolves at its deadline while the form stays `pending` and a later reply still answers the owner.
- The existing #2445 test (joiner timeout does not cancel the shared form) still passes.

---

title: compaction fails on short sessions: 'Compaction produced no summary' / 'Compaction summary reached the output token limit' (9 fleet sessions, 2026-11-17)
body:
Compaction fails on short workhorse sessions, failing the session. Nine fleet sessions hit `compaction.failed` between 03:15 and 03:53 CST on 2026-11-17, with two distinct error strings.

**Error strings (verbatim, from `session_message` `compaction.failed` rows):**
- `Compaction produced no summary`
- `Compaction summary reached the output token limit`

**Evidence (session ids, route `opencode-route/workhorse`):**
- `ses_e5e175641e7ffe6JFOJ07OZqj0` (Main CI failure — fix trigger 02:40): "produced no summary", 16 assistant messages, failed 03:29
- `ses_e5e172ee193ffe3NPbduqzjdJn` (Plans Space freshness keeper): "output token limit", **4 assistant messages**, failed 03:31
- `ses_e5e173622c6ffeu3hzRR8to4Lh` (Improvement issue creator 03:15): "produced no summary", 9 assistant messages, failed 03:31
- `ses_e5e17317f8fffeA1O366PNHkwO` (Fleet conductor 03:20): "output token limit", 8 assistant messages, failed 03:33
- `ses_e5e17519af0ffej1CMnurGE4iC` (Improvement issue creator 02:45): "produced no summary", 26 assistant messages, recorded a compaction failure but finished `succeeded` at 03:36
- `ses_e5e17287c46ffe1dYy8TibSTRk` (Main CI failure 03:30): "output token limit", 13 assistant messages, finished `succeeded` at 03:53
- `ses_e5e1756443cfferRgIWOneGKYr` (Fleet conductor 02:40): "output token limit", 20 assistant messages, failed 03:47
- plus two more sessions in the same window with the same `compaction.failed` row

The "output token limit" cases are the suspicious part: a 4-message session should not reach a compaction output cap, which points at the compaction request/summary budget rather than real context size.

**Not a duplicate:** searched open and closed issues in developing-today-forks/opencode for `compaction.failed`, "Compaction produced no summary", "output token limit" and "compaction"; the nearest, #2277 (preserve compaction-hook edits) and #559 (context cap bypassed for compaction), are different defects. Searched developing-today/code too; no match.

**Acceptance test:** a session with a short transcript (under 10 assistant messages) that triggers compaction completes with a non-empty summary and no `compaction.failed` row. Add a regression test that compaction on a short workhorse transcript returns a summary within the output budget, and that an empty summary is reported as an error rather than silently failing the session.

title: fix(core): route-overrides cache keyed on mtime alone serves a stale list after a same-tick external rewrite

labels.name: effort/s

body:
## Summary

`ModelRouteOverrides.current()` caches the parsed override list keyed only on `fs.statSync(file).mtimeMs` (`packages/core/src/model-route-overrides.ts:172-187`, cache hit check at `:180`, on `origin/main` `dd67190b6f`). `save()` replaces the file by renaming a freshly written temp file over it (`:219-247`, rename at `:237`), so an external writer (OpenChamber reads the same file, per the comment at `:160-161`) can land a complete new file whose `mtimeMs` equals the one the cache was filled from. The reader then keeps returning the old list. The in-process `save()` clears `cache` (`:247`), so only an external rewrite is affected, and it stays stale until the next write that changes the mtime.

## Evidence

Reproduced against the real module (`bun`, `packages/core/src/model-route-overrides.ts` on `dd67190b6f`, `setFilePath` to a scratch file):

1. write file with override `a<i>`, call `current()` (cache filled, mtime M)
2. (gap G) write a complete new file with override `b<i>` to a temp path and `rename` it over the store, as `save()` does
3. `current()` returns `a<i>`, not `b<i>`

| gap G between step 1 and step 2 | stale results (of 200) |
|---|---|
| 0 ms | 181 |
| 2 ms | 0 |
| 5 ms | 0 |
| 20 ms | 0 |

On this ext4 mount two back-to-back writes share an `mtimeMs` in roughly a third of trials, so the window is the timestamp tick, not a fixed time. Staleness is not reset by a later read of the same file; only the next mtime change clears it.

Related but distinct: #924 (closed) made the store writes atomic and noted that a truncated body was cached against mtime. That fix removes the partial-read case; the complete-file same-tick case above is still open in the current code.

## Why it matters

Routing silently applies an `avoid`/`prefer`/`allow-over-budget` set that the user (or OpenChamber) has already replaced or removed. The window is narrow (two writers within one timestamp tick), so this is a robustness gap rather than a hot path, but the failure is silent and persists until the next write.

## Suggested fix

Key the cache on more than mtime, for example `(dev, ino, size, mtimeMs)` from `statSync`. `save()` always replaces the file with a new inode, so inode and size change on every write even when the mtime does not.

## Acceptance criteria

- After an external atomic replace that leaves the mtime unchanged (use `fs.utimesSync` to restore the old mtime after the rewrite, which makes the test deterministic), `current()` returns the new list.
- A regression test in the existing route-overrides test file covers that case.
- No behavior change for the normal path (cache still avoids re-parsing an unchanged file).

## Dedupe

All-state searches for `route-overrides`, `mtime`, `route overrides cache` returned #924 (closed, write atomicity, cache mentioned only for the truncated-body case), #924's related write-side issues (#998, #1005, #977), and the open route-overrides API slice #2494 / PR #2496 (protocol/server files, does not touch the cache). No open issue or PR covers the reader cache key.

Filed by improvement-issue-creator-b (probe: `bun` script using the real module; reproduced in a scratch directory, not in the fleet repo).

body:
## Finding

The public Feishu webhook buffers and parses the entire request before it can inspect the verification token, and there is no byte limit on this function route. An oversized (or chunked) unauthenticated request can therefore consume worker memory/CPU in JSON parsing before it is rejected.

## Evidence (verified on main `72cab5557d554682e1e5ffe2a201727f122b6a3f`)

- `packages/function/src/api.ts`, `.post("/feishu")`: `body = await c.req.json()` reads/parses the body before the `FEISHU_VERIFICATION_TOKEN` check.
- The route has no `Content-Length` pre-check or streaming byte cap before JSON parsing.
- The merged #2564 fix adds token verification and malformed-JSON handling, but still parses the full body first; its tests cover malformed and null bodies, not oversized bodies.
- The server-side JSON cap in #2314 is in `packages/server` and does not cover this Cloudflare function route.

## Suggested fix

Bound the `/feishu` request stream before materializing JSON. Reject an over-limit `Content-Length` early and enforce the same cap while reading chunked bodies; return a deterministic 413 without parsing or relaying. Choose/document an appropriate webhook limit and cover both declared-length and chunked oversized requests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Oversized declared-length bodies are refused before body consumption.
- [ ] Chunked bodies are stopped at the byte cap before full buffering/parsing.
- [ ] Both paths return 413 and do not relay to Discord; valid verification challenges and event requests continue to work.

Distinct from #2564 (request verification and logging) and #2314 (server JSON routes).

title: fix(server): disposition bare Number() on content-length header in transcriptions handler (check:numeric-boundaries)

body:
## Problem

`bun run script/check-numeric-boundaries.ts` on current main reports one unlisted bare string→number conversion in `packages/server/src/handlers/transcriptions.ts`:

- `transcriptions.ts:59` — `const declaredLength = Number(Option.getOrElse(Headers.get(ctx.request.headers, "content-length"), () => ""))`

The value is a raw `content-length` header string (or `""` when absent). `Number("")` is 0 and a non-numeric header yields `NaN`; the next line guards with `Number.isFinite(declaredLength) && declaredLength > bodyLimit`, so a `NaN` falls through to the streamed cutoff rather than disabling the size check. Whether that makes the conversion safe-by-usage or whether it should convert through a guarded parse is a disposition decision for the handler's owner — this issue exists so the site is tracked explicitly instead of silently keeping the gate red.

## Evidence

- Gate output (2026-11-17, main after the #2482 disposition): `Unlisted numeric-boundary candidate at packages/server/src/handlers/transcriptions.ts:59`.

## Acceptance criteria

title: fix(server): bound vcs.status changed-file results — every untracked path is statted and returned
body:
## Summary

`GET /api/vcs/status` has no result limit or pagination. On a location with many changed/untracked files, one request collects and sorts every status row, stats every untracked file, and serializes the entire array. The 10 MB patch budget in the VCS diff path does not apply to this endpoint.

## Evidence (origin/main `ad33dc7f9ad7`)

- `packages/protocol/src/groups/vcs.ts`: `vcs.status` accepts only `LocationQuery` and declares `Array(Vcs.FileStatus)`; unlike `vcs.branch.list`, there is no `limit`.
- `packages/server/src/handlers/vcs.ts`: the handler calls `vcs.status()` without bounds.
- `packages/core/src/vcs.ts`: decodes the full array and copies all rows (`status` service implementation); no cap or pagination.
- `packages/core/src/plugin/vcs/git.ts`: `status()` collects Git status and stats, sorts the complete list, and runs `Effect.forEach` over every item, including per-file stats for untracked entries.
- Repro: in a temporary Git repository with 2,500 untracked files, `git status --porcelain=v1 -z` emitted 2,500 entries (55,000 bytes). The service path has no truncation between that provider result and the HTTP response.
- `MAX_TOTAL_PATCH_BYTES` in `packages/core/src/vcs/patch.ts` is applied only by `diff`; it does not bound status rows.

## Why it matters

Generated output, dependency trees, or bulk file operations can make a single VCS status request do work and allocate/serialize output proportional to every changed path. This can stall a local server/UI and inflate responses even when each file is small.

## Suggested fix shape

Add a bounded page/limit contract for `vcs.status` (or an explicit capped response with continuation/truncation metadata), and ensure the Git adapter does not stat and serialize rows beyond that bound. Preserve a way for clients to discover that more results exist.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The status API has a documented, enforced maximum result/page size.
- [ ] The Git status path avoids per-file stat work for rows outside the returned page.
- [ ] A test with more changed files than the cap proves the response remains bounded and indicates additional results.
- [ ] Existing ordinary working-copy status behavior remains unchanged.

title: fix(config): an alias cycle is silently ignored — the config loads clean and the session fails with an unrelated model-unavailable error

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

body:
## Summary

An alias cycle in the \`aliases\` config (e.g. \`"a/x" -> "a/y"\`, \`"a/y" -> "a/x"\`) is detected by \`ModelAlias.resolve\`, which throws \`AliasCycleError\`. Three call sites catch that error with an empty \`catch {}\` and fall back to the unresolved reference. The result is that a broken alias configuration produces no diagnostic at config load, and at session time the user sees a generic "model unavailable" error for the raw ref with no mention of the cycle.

## Evidence (origin/main \`b59523b7c0\`)

- \`packages/schema/src/model-alias.ts:81\` throws \`AliasCycleError\` (also \`AliasMaxDepthError\` at :199 and "Invalid model reference" throws).
- Empty catch fallbacks on the same error:
  - \`packages/core/src/config/normalize.ts:636-642\` (\`resolveModelString\`) returns the raw model string on any error.
  - \`packages/core/src/config/normalize.ts:846-854\` (\`diagnoseSelection\`): catches, leaves \`modelStr\` as the raw value, and then runs the shape regex \`/^[^/#]+\/[^#]+$/\`. A cyclic ref like \`a/x\` passes that regex, so **no diagnostic is emitted** for a broken alias.
  - \`packages/core/src/session/runner/model.ts:127-133\` (session runner): after the catch, \`target\` stays \`a/x\`; \`catalog.find\` misses and the user gets \`ModelUnavailableError { providerID: "a", modelID: "x" }\`.
  - \`packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts:1698-1704\` and \`packages/core/src/session/context.ts:220-226\`: same fallthrough.
- Probe (bun, schema module standalone): \`resolve({models:{"a/x":"a/y","a/y":"a/x"}}, "a/x")\` throws \`AliasCycleError: Cycle detected in alias resolution: a/x\`; the caller-style \`try/catch {}\` fallthrough returns \`a/x\`.
- Existing tests: \`packages/core/test/model-alias.test.ts:113-122\` pins the throw at the schema function only. No test covers the config-load diagnostic or the session-level message. Searches of open and closed issues for \`AliasCycleError\`, "alias resolution catch", and "alias cycle config diagnostic" return only #399 (max-depth off-by-one, closed), so this is untracked.

## Why it matters

A user who writes a self-referential or two-step alias gets no signal where the mistake is. The error names the wrong thing (a provider/model that may well exist), and \`opencode\` config validation reports the file as clean. This is the same class as the closed #411/#407/#406 schema fixes, which turned silently-accepted alias targets into errors; cycles were not covered by that series.

## Suggested fix shape

1. In \`diagnoseSelection\` and \`resolveModelString\`, catch only the expected alias errors (\`AliasCycleError\`, \`AliasMaxDepthError\`) and push a \`Diagnostic\` at the config path naming the cycle chain. Let other errors keep the fallthrough.
2. In the session runner and resolver, when \`resolve\` throws \`AliasCycleError\`, surface the cycle in the \`ModelUnavailableError\` detail (or a dedicated error) instead of silently using the raw ref.
3. Tests: a config with a two-step alias cycle emits a diagnostic at load; the session path reports the cycle, not a generic unavailable; a valid alias chain is unchanged.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Alias cycle in config produces a diagnostic naming the cycle.
- [ ] Runtime error for a cycled ref names the cycle.
- [ ] Non-cycle alias errors keep the existing fallthrough behavior.
- [ ] Tests added in \`packages/core/test/model-alias.test.ts\` or \`config/config.test.ts\`.

Filed by improvement-issue-creator-b (lane B). Source: fleet creator run 2026-11-17.

## Evidence

- PR #2546 diff: `fetchAllQuota` now wraps each leg in `withQuotaLegDeadline` (60s) inside a try/catch that pushes a `buildResult({ ok: false, failureClass: "leg-timeout" | "leg-error", … })` row and continues the loop. Before the PR, a throwing leg aborted the whole run; a hanging leg froze it (the 2026-11-16 locked-gnome-keyring incident in the PR body).
- The PR's three new tests in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` test only the helper `withQuotaLegDeadline` in isolation (settles in time / never-settling promise rejects with `QuotaLegDeadlineError` / rejection propagates unchanged). None call `fetchAllQuota`.
- The pre-existing `fetchAllQuota` tests in the same file (e.g. `fullListingEmitsEveryConfiguredProviderAndCredential`, at head `2a3b7f6a84bf`) cover the *probe*-failure path from `listConfiguredQuotaProvidersDetailed` — a different code path that never reaches the new try/catch around `fetchQuotaForProviderInstances`.
- So a regression that removed or mis-wired the catch (e.g. wrong `failureClass` mapping, or the loop aborting on first error) would pass the full suite: the helper tests would stay green while the incident behaviour returned.

## Why it matters

The PR exists because one wedged leg froze every fleet quota read for hours. The integration behaviour — one bad leg becomes an error row, the other providers' results still land — is the entire point of the change, and it is the part with no test.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test in `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` drives `fetchAllQuota` with a provider leg that never settles (or throws) and asserts: the run resolves, that provider appears exactly once with `ok: false` and `failureClass` `leg-timeout` (resp. `leg-error`), and at least one other configured provider's results are present and unaffected.
- [ ] The test uses a short injected deadline (the helper already accepts `deadlineMs`) so the suite does not wait 60s.
- [ ] Existing quota tests keep passing (`bun test test/quota.test.ts` in `packages/ai`: 219 pass at PR head per the PR body, plus the new test).

## Runtime verification

Inconclusive (not executed): injecting a hanging/throwing provider leg into `fetchAllQuota` requires a test harness change (the provider registry is static), and modifying application code for verification is out of bounds for the review job. The gap itself is verified statically: full test-file inventory at PR head `2a3b7f6a84bf` (2,999 lines) contains `leg-timeout`/`QuotaLegDeadlineError` only in the three helper tests. The acceptance test above, once written by the triage worker, is the runtime verification.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #2546 (batch #2531–#2552, 2026-11-16). Dedupe: `gh search issues` for quota leg deadline / fetchAllQuota returned no existing issue covering this test gap.

title: fix(ai): partial-json trims truncated numbers only for lowercase 'e' — [1E] silently drops the entry, top-level 1E throws

body:
## Summary

`parseNum` in `packages/ai/src/protocols/utils/partial-json.ts` trims a truncated number to its mantissa only when the exponent marker is lowercase `e`. A truncated uppercase `E` is not trimmed, so the same streamed value parses differently depending on the case of the exponent marker. Inside an array the entry is silently dropped; at the top level the parse throws.

## Evidence

Source (main `115283d60f`, file identical to `origin/main`):

- `partial-json.ts:267-275`: the `Allow.NUM` fallback computes `token.lastIndexOf("e")` and retries `decodeJson` on the prefix only for lowercase `e`.
- `partial-json.ts:251`: the top-level (`index === 0`) fallback has the same lowercase-only search.

Probe, run against the real module with `Allow.ALL` on main `115283d60f` (`bun test`, temporary file removed afterwards):

| input | result |
|---|---|
| `1e` | `1` |
| `[1e]` | `[1]` |
| `1E` | throws `SchemaError(Expected a valid JSON string)` |
| `[1E]` | `[]` (the `1` is silently lost) |
| `-1E` | throws `SchemaError` |
| `[-1e]` | `[-1]` |
| `[1E5]` (complete) | `[100000]` |

Lowercase and uppercase truncations are both valid JSON prefixes (`1e`/`1E` are prefixes of `1e5`/`1E5`), so the two spellings should behave the same.

## Why it matters

Tool-argument streaming runs through this parser. A model that emits an uppercase exponent (`E`) and is cut off mid-exponent gets a truncated argument that loses the value, or fails the whole parse. The lowercase path was fixed in #2213 (closed) and now recovers, so the two cases diverge.

This is the uppercase residual of #2213, which was scoped to lowercase `e`. Frequency is low.

## Acceptance criteria

- `[1E]`, `{"a":1E}` and top-level `1E` recover to the mantissa as the lowercase forms do, with the same `Allow.NUM` gating.
- Negative mantissas (`-1E`, `[-1E]`) match `-1e`.
- Regression tests pin both the array and top-level cases, and a control confirming `1E5` complete values are unchanged.

## Suggested fix shape

Search for the exponent marker with both cases, for example `Math.max(token.lastIndexOf("e"), token.lastIndexOf("E"))` in the nested path and the same in the top-level path. Keep the `exponent > 0` guard.

body:
## Evidence
- Handler: `packages/server/src/handlers/integration.ts:190-199` (`integration.oauth.cancel`) and `:256-264` (`integration.command.cancel`) return `HttpApiSchema.NoContent` unconditionally with no existence check.
- Contrast in the same file: `integration.oauth.status` (`:124-150`) and `integration.command.status` (`:228-253`) map a miss to `IntegrationAttemptNotFoundError`, and `integration.oauth.complete` (`:152-188`) maps `Integration.AttemptNotFound` to `IntegrationAttemptNotFoundError`.
- Core: `packages/core/src/integration.ts:856-866` (`oauth.cancel`) and `:885-895` (`command.cancel`) do `SynchronizedRef.modify(...)` returning `undefined` for unknown `attemptID`, wrong `integrationID`, non-`pending` status, or `persisting`, then `if (attempt) close scope` — all miss cases resolve to void, so the handler answers 204.

## Why this is a defect
A cancel against a stale or typoed `attemptID` (or an attempt belonging to another integration) returns 204 and looks like a successful abort. The client cannot distinguish "auth flow aborted" from "nothing existed", and a wrong-`integrationID` routing bug is masked. It is also inconsistent within the same resource: `status`/`complete` 404 the same ID that `cancel` 204s.

## Acceptance criteria / suggested fix
- `integration.oauth.cancel` and `integration.command.cancel` return `IntegrationAttemptNotFoundError` (404, matching `status`/`complete`) when no attempt matches `{integrationID, attemptID}`.
- Keep cancel idempotent for a matched but already-settled attempt (204) — only the unknown/wrong-integration case should 404, mirroring the `status` lookup (`attempt.integrationID !== input.integrationID` -> not found).
- Suggested: do a read-through lookup like `status` before/instead of the blind modify, or surface the `modify -> undefined + absent` case as `AttemptNotFoundError`; add a handler `mapError` to `IntegrationAttemptNotFoundError` as `status` does.

| File | PR #2517 | PR #2522 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/voice-input.ts` | Bounds only the response **body** read (`voiceResponseBody` via `readBoundedResponseText`, 1 MiB); the `fetch` itself still carries **no deadline/signal**, so a façade that never sends headers still hangs the submission | Bounds the fetch with a deadline signal (`VOICE_REQUEST_DEADLINE_MS = 120_000`), a per-frame idle bound for streaming (`VOICE_STREAM_IDLE_MS`), **and** the body reads (refuse 1 MiB / excerpt 64 KiB) |
| `packages/codemode/test/libraries.test.ts` | Keeps the std.sleep test on **real timers**, inflating the request to 500 ms and relaxing the segment-count assertion | Rewrites the same test on a **fake clock** (`vi.useFakeTimers` + `setSystemTime`), asserting the exact segmentation `[35, 25, 15, 5]`, and splits `withTimeout` into its own exact-deadline test |
| `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` | Re-dispositions the same stale `packages/desktop/src/main/extension/manager.ts` entry (different wording) | Same entry, different wording |

Both PRs state the same root cause in their bodies: #2517 — "Two independent failures in that one run" (run 43849921062), tracked via #2477 / #2482, refs #2462; #2522 — "Fixes the two failures in main-CI run 43849921062 (#2518)".

### Why it matters

Main's `test` gate is red (issues #2518, #2477, #2482, #2462 all OPEN). Two divergent fixes racing for the same gate invites a conflicted second merge, a half-applied voice bound (body bounded but header phase unbounded, if #2517's voice half wins), or a real-timer sleep test that stays load-sensitive (if #2517's test half wins). One combined PR keeps exactly one approach per surface.

title: fix(tui): a second TUI's prompt history/stash/frecency entries are silently erased — unlocked whole-file rewrites race the append path

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: priority/normal

labels.name: app/tui

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Finding

Three machine-global JSONL stores under the TUI state directory are read-modify-rewritten with no lock, while the same files are also appended to. When two `opencode` processes run (two terminals, a reload plus the old process, a TUI plus a `serve`-driven session), the rewriting instance writes back its stale in-memory snapshot and the other instance's appended entries are gone from disk — with no error anywhere.

### Evidence (on `origin/main` `e7d5bb7354053ca7aa09d6f370aee40d7f127503`)

`packages/tui/src/util/persistence.ts`:
- `writeText` (:13-16) is a plain `writeFile` — truncate + write, no temp file, no lock.
- `appendText` (:18-21) is a plain `appendFile` — no lock.
- The package already has `writeJsonAtomic` (:49) and `Flock.withLock` is already used by `context/storage.tsx:72` and `model-preference.ts:116`, so the correct pattern exists in-tree.

The three stores use `writeText` for every whole-file rewrite and `appendText` for the fast path:

| file | rewrite sites | append site |
|---|---|---|
| `prompt/history.tsx` | `:100` startup self-heal, `:136` trim | `:139` |
| `prompt/stash.tsx` | `:45` startup self-heal, `:68` trim, `:77` `pop`, `:86` `remove` | `:71` |
| `prompt/frecency.tsx` | `:65` startup self-heal, `:81` trim | `:74` |

`paths.state` is the machine-global XDG state dir (`packages/util/src/global.ts`), not per-project, so the files are shared by every TUI on the box. There is no singleton guard and no lock around any of these mutations.

The startup "self-heal" is the widest window: the file is read, parsed, then rewritten from the parsed snapshot. Any append that lands between the read and the rewrite is discarded — the read/write pair is not atomic with respect to other processes.

### Reproduction

Probe (two instances modeled against the real module logic, run from `packages/tui`):

```ts
// A and B each load the file; B appends; A rewrites from its own snapshot
// S1: stash pop on A after B's push      → B's entry absent from disk
// S2: history trim on A after B's append → B's entry absent from disk
// S3: A startup self-heal after B append → B's entry absent from disk
```

Observed on `e7d5bb7354`:

```
FAIL S1 stash pop keeps other instance's push: on disk after A pop: 0 x from-B, 49 entries
FAIL S2 history trim keeps other instance's append: on disk after A trim: 0 x from-B, 50 entries
FAIL S3 startup self-heal keeps append in its read/write window: on disk after A startup: 0 x from-B, 1 entries
```

(A fourth probe asserting the rewrite never leaves a truncated file while a reader reads passes for small payloads; the defect here is the lost update, not torn writes. `writeText` can still tear on large payloads, which the atomic-write precedent would also fix.)

### Why it matters

- A stashed prompt is an explicit "keep this for later". `pop` returns the entry to the caller and rewrites the file from that process's snapshot; another instance's push is lost, so the stash silently under-reports what exists.
- Prompt history and frecency quietly lose entries; frecency loss degrades completion ordering with no signal.
- All of it is silent: every call site has `.catch(() => {})`, and a lost entry is indistinguishable from one that was never written.

The sibling implementations in the same package (`context/storage.tsx`, `model-preference.ts`) already take `Flock.withLock` and write `writeJsonAtomic`; `Flock.setGlobal({ state })` is wired at startup, so the lock root is available.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every mutating operation on these three files (append, trim, pop, remove, startup self-heal) runs under one lock per file and re-reads the file inside the lock before writing, so no entry written by another process is dropped; or compaction/self-heal becomes lock-guarded while appends stay append-only.
- Whole-file rewrites use an atomic write (`writeJsonAtomic`/temp+rename), not bare `writeText`.
- A regression test drives two writers against the same file through the real mutate paths and asserts every append from either writer survives; existing `packages/tui/test/prompt/jsonl.test.ts` and `history-provider.test.tsx` stay green.

title: route(core): the gathered provider wall never gates an Authentication-dead provider — _commandcode took 545 attempts across 95 sessions in one wave, 412 with no failover

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/small-fix

body:
## What happened

In yesterday's `_commandcode` seating, a single 08:41:01Z–10:30:03Z wave burned **545 route attempts across 95 sessions** on legs that could not succeed. Every attempt on the provider was dealt by the planner, made, and lost:

| model | attempts | sessions | window |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_commandcode/reflection/beam:free` | 420 | 95 | 08:41:01Z – 10:30:03Z |
| `_commandcode/gpt-6.1-sol` | 102 | 49 | 09:13:40Z – 10:06:50Z |
| `_commandcode/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | 21 | 1 | 10:05:49Z – 10:06:55Z |
| `_commandcode/meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` | 2 | 2 | 09:13:39Z – 09:45:00Z |

Outcomes: 520 × `failure/Authentication`, 23 × `failure/QuotaExceeded`, 2 × `timeout/Transport`. **412 of the 545 have `failed_over_to IS NULL`** — the planner spent the attempt and the session got nothing. The provider's own message is terminal, not retryable:

```
The free Beam 1.0 tier has ended. Run /model and pick another model to keep going.
https://commandcode.ai/models
```

(route DB `route_attempt`, 3h window ending 11:39Z; no `_commandcode` attempt has been recorded since 10:30:03Z.)

## Why the wall did not idle the legs

The legs were re-seated deliberately, on the stated promise that the fork's gathered provider-wide quota wall would skip them before any attempt:

> 2026-11-15 (Drew, direct order): the `_commandcode` door is RESTORED below, exactly as seated before the 2026-11-13 removal — the fork's gathered provider-wide quota wall (opencode#2479, merged today) now skips a walled provider's legs before any attempt, so a spent door idles instead of burning.
> — `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc:2569`

The running server is `opencode-2.0.30+5b65c2a`, and `82f089daff` (#2479) is an ancestor of it, so the wall shipped. But the wall is **quota-keyed only**:

- `observeGatheredProviderWall` (`packages/core/src/model-route.ts:1425`) gates a provider only from a `QuotaCurrent.ProviderReading`, and only when `QuotaSnapshot.isKnownFull(...)` is true (`:1477`-ish, the `gated: true` branch).
- A provider whose every attempt returns a terminal `Authentication`/tier-ended error emits **no quota reading at all**. `entries.length === 0` → `return undefined` (`:1257` region). The provider therefore never becomes `gated`, and every draw of the door is dealt again.

So the wall is silent exactly for the failure class that is most obviously permanent.

## Why this is not #8048 or #1014

Both are prior art for the same class on a different path, and both are closed:

- **#8048** (route-proxy) — `demotedPairs()` counted only `quota`/`RateLimit`; fixed to include `Authentication`. That fix lives in `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs`, which is **not the path serving these sessions**: no route-proxy process was running; the attempts come from the in-server planner.
- **#1014** (core+openchamber) — "repeated errors of ANY class remove a model from rotation for escalating time". That is the right stance; the gathered-wall path above does not implement it for a non-quota terminal error.
- **developing-today/code#10128** — the housekeeping flip that formally walls the Command Code monthly window. Its body asserts "no route can currently deal this door a leaf (all doors removed #9397), so nothing in flight changes." The live ledger contradicts that: the door was re-seated on 2026-11-15 and is being dealt constantly.

## Proposal

Give the gathered wall a hard-failure arm, mirroring #8048's rule:

1. Track consecutive `Authentication` (non-retryable provider-terminal) failures per provider, shared by the planner.
2. When a provider reaches N ≥ 3 consecutive hard failures with 0 successes in the window, mark it `gated` for the same escalating backoff the quota wall uses, and log `provider:<id> hard-failure-gated`.
3. Clear only on a live success (the #9397 re-seat condition), never on elapsed time alone.

## Acceptance

- Replaying the dead leg through a 95-session draw yields **at most 1 attempt per session** (the first, which records the gate), not 5.7, and no session ends with `failed_over_to IS NULL` on that leg.
- `route_attempt` for the walled provider shows a burst of ≤ (sessions) rows, then zero, with no further attempts until a live success.

## Evidence

```sql
select model_id, count(*), count(distinct session_id), min(time_started), max(time_started)
from route_attempt
where provider_id like '%commandcode%' and time_started > (unixepoch('now')-3*3600)*1000
group by 1;

select count(*) from route_attempt
where provider_id like '%commandcode%' and time_started > (unixepoch('now')-3*3600)*1000
  and failed_over_to is null;   -- 412
```

Seats to be revisited once the arm exists: `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc:2699`, `:2777`, `:3069`, `:3115`, `:3248`.

title: fix(server): bound fs.list directory listing — no limit param, full materialize+sort per request

labels.name: status/blocked

labels.name: queue/blocked

body:
## Summary
`GET /api/fs/list` has no `limit` parameter and materializes the full child list on every request: the handler passes the query straight through, the service reads all directory entries into memory, maps them, and sorts the whole array before responding.

A single request against a directory with very many direct children (build output, cache/data dirs, large checkouts) therefore loads, sorts (`localeCompare`), and serializes the entire listing in one go. Sibling surface `fs.find` already takes a caller limit (tracked for its missing ceiling in #2484 / #2488); `fs.list` is worse — it cannot be paged at all.

## Evidence (origin/main `6aaca789a1`)
- Protocol: `packages/protocol/src/groups/fs.ts:9-14` — `ListQuery` carries only `path`; `fs.list` endpoint at `:49-51` returns `Array(FileSystem.Entry)` with no limit/offset. Contrast `FindQuery` (`:20-25`) which at least carries `limit`.
- Handler: `packages/server/src/handlers/fs.ts:27-36` — passes `ctx.query` straight to `fs.list`, no bound.
- Service: `packages/core/src/filesystem.ts:176-207` — `list` does `readDirectoryEntries(directory)` (full `DirEntry[]`), then `flatMap` + full `.sort()` in memory before returning. No limit, no truncation.
- Primitive: `packages/util/src/fs-util.ts:67,108-119` — `readDirectoryEntries` itself returns the whole array.

## Why it matters
- One cheap GET can force the server to allocate/sort/serialize an arbitrarily large listing — disk-adjacent DoS in the same family as #2483 (session.list), #2484/#2488 (fs.find), #2486 (shell output).
- No client workaround: without a limit/offset or truncation flag the only way to list a huge directory is to swallow it whole.
- `fs.list` explicitly reaches outside the location directory (parents/siblings), so the caller can point it at system dirs with large fan-out.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `fs.list` accepts an optional page size (e.g. `limit`, default ~100 like `find`, ceiling consistent with #2488's decision) and either paginates (cursor/offset) or returns a documented truncation signal.
- [ ] The service enforces the bound before/at materialization (not map-everything-then-slice only), so a huge directory cannot OOM the server.
- [ ] OpenAPI description documents the bound/truncation so clients page instead of retrying.
- [ ] Regression test: listing a directory with more entries than the ceiling returns the bounded page without loading the full sorted array (or asserts the cap).

## Related (distinct, not duplicates)
- #2484 / #2488 — `fs.find` limit with no ceiling (different endpoint; `find` at least has a limit param).
- #2483 — `session.list` limit with no ceiling (different surface).
- #2486 — shell output capture/page (different surface).
- #2502 — `fs.write` body/path (write path, not list).

title: fix(server): credential.create fallback response bypasses the session-cookie redaction added in PR #2498

labels.description: Package: server (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Finding (from PR diff review of PR #2498)

PR #2498 establishes the posture "the generic credential read path never discloses the cookie" and implements it by mapping server responses through `Credential.redactedValue` in `entries()` (`packages/server/src/handlers/credential.ts`).

The `credential.create` handler has a fallback that bypasses that mapping:

```ts
const entry = entries(yield* credential.list(created.integrationID)).find((item) => item.id === created.id)
return { data: entry ?? { ...created, active: false } }
```

`created` is the raw `Credential.Info` returned by `Credential.Service.create` — its `value` is the **unredacted** value. If the `find` ever misses (any future change to `list()` filtering/decoding, a row `stored()` drops, a race), creating a `session-cookie` credential returns the full cookie in the create response — silently defeating the PR's central guarantee on exactly the path that first receives the secret. The fallback also spreads a Schema class instance, losing the `entries()` shape guarantees (ordering/active semantics).

Verified at PR head `6fd4ff19e41086c6a5d6e6bafa7694fd9750b8f9` via the diff and via `gh api .../contents/packages/server/src/handlers/credential.ts?ref=6fd4ff1...` (full handler source). In today's code the `find` normally succeeds (`list()` returns the created row), so this is a latent bypass, not a demonstrated live leak — but a non-disclosure guarantee should not rest on a fallback that returns the raw secret.

## Why it matters

Session cookies are provider session credentials (parent issue #2490, code#5060). The redaction was added precisely so generic readers never receive the cookie; a raw-value fallback in the same handler is the kind of path that leaks it later, after a routine refactor of `list()`, with no test watching it — `credential.test.ts` covers `redactedValue` in isolation, and no server test asserts the create response for a session-cookie credential.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The `credential.create` fallback can never return an unredacted value: apply `Credential.redactedValue` to the fallback (or construct the fallback through `entries([created])`), so every value leaving this handler passes the same mapping.
- [ ] A server-level test creates a session-cookie credential and asserts the response body does not contain the cookie string (covering both the found-entry and fallback shapes, e.g. by unit-testing the response construction).
- [ ] Existing credential/integration tests still pass.

## Directive

Drew's ruling (chat, 2026-11-16 00:12 CST), folding into the #2491 consolidation: "make an appropriate surface then to view route attempts etc" — nobody should need to open the database file to see route attempts.

## Symptom / evidence

OpenCode core owns the `route_attempt` ledger (and `route_decision`) in `opencode.db`, written by `packages/core/src/model-route-log.ts`. But there is no server surface over it, so every consumer reads the SQLite file directly:

1. **OpenChamber's routing telemetry** — `packages/web/server/lib/routing/model-route-stats.js` (openchamber fork) resolves the db path itself (`OPENCODE_DB` or the data dir), opens it read-only (`openRouteDb`), and runs its own aggregate SQL over `route_attempt` / `route_decision`.
2. **The PM-stack aggregator's quota analytics** — `pm-stack/aggregator/src/analytics-store.ts` (developing-today/code) computes all route_attempt-derived inputs (burn, models, efforts, legs, coverage) with SQL `FROM route_attempt` against `opencode.db` read-only; its view labels the source "route_attempt ledger (opencode.db), read-only".

Direct file readers couple both consumers to the ledger's physical schema, bypass the server entirely, and break the moment the storage engine or schema moves — which is now a live question (#2492, the TursoDB evaluation: a non-stock-SQLite engine makes direct file reads by outside tools fail outright).

## Scope

1. A read API in the OpenCode server over the route_attempt ledger: recent attempts with the filters both readers actually use (time window, provider, model, session), plus the aggregate shapes they compute today (per provider/model attempt + token totals, error breakdowns, coverage) — derived from the two readers' real queries, not invented.
2. A view where the codebase's patterns support one (the server already serves operator surfaces; follow the existing pattern rather than inventing a new one).
3. Re-point both current direct readers at the API: OpenChamber's `model-route-stats.js` and the aggregator's `analytics-store.ts` stop opening `opencode.db`.

## Acceptance

- Both current direct readers run against the API with no direct `opencode.db` access, and their outputs (OpenChamber route stats; aggregator burn/models/legs analytics) are unchanged in shape and totals for the same ledger window.
- No remaining code path outside the OpenCode server opens `opencode.db` to read route attempts (the server's own internals excepted).
- The API is read-only: it exposes attempts and aggregates, never prompts/responses (the ledger stores none) and never credentials.

## Refs

- developing-today-forks/opencode#2491 (consolidation epic; this is part of slice 1, routing)
- developing-today-forks/opencode#2492 (TursoDB spike — direct file reads are a migration blocker this surface removes)
- developing-today-forks/opencode#2494 / PR #2496 (route-overrides API — the sibling surface landed first)
- developing-today/code#5060 (the original ruling)
