title: fix(server): bound fs.find limit — PositiveInt with no ceiling materializes the whole file index on one request

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: app/server
labels.description: Package: server (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

`GET /api/fs/find` takes a client-controlled `limit` with no server-side ceiling:

- `packages/protocol/src/groups/fs.ts:28` — `FindQuery.limit` is `Schema.NumberFromString.pipe(Schema.decodeTo(PositiveInt), Schema.optional)`; no max, mirroring the unbounded shape that #2483 filed for `session.list`.
- `packages/server/src/handlers/fs.ts:41-47` — the `fs.find` handler passes `ctx.query` straight into `FileSystem.Service.find` with no clamp.
- `packages/core/src/filesystem/search.ts:39` (ripgrep backend, served via `filesystem.ts:157` `find: search.find`) — `fuzzysort.go(input.query, items, { limit: input.limit ?? 50 })`. The scored index holds up to the ripgrep scan cap at `:72` (100_000 entries, or `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` for VCS locations), so `limit=2147483647` retains, maps, and JSON-serializes up to the entire location index in one response instead of the default 50-entry page.
- `packages/core/src/filesystem/search.ts:142` (fff backend) — same raw value feeds the native index as `pageSize: input.limit ?? 50`, so both find paths are affected.

## Why it matters

Any HTTP client (or a misbehaving TUI/plugin caller) can turn a 50-entry fuzzy-find page into a full-index dump with one query param. Sibling surfaces already cap this class: session message list is capped 1..200, branch lists go through `branchListLimit` (max 100), and #2483 tracks the same defect for `session.list`. `fs.find` is the remaining uncapped list-style endpoint.

## Acceptance criteria / suggested fix

- Cap the find limit server-side (e.g. a shared page-size helper mirroring `branchListLimit`'s [1, max] shape); keep the default page at 50.
- Apply the cap at one choke point so both backends (ripgrep/fuzzysort `limit` and fff `pageSize`) are covered.
- Regression test: requesting an oversized `limit` returns the capped page, not the whole index; default (absent limit) behavior unchanged.

Related: #2483 (session.list, same defect class, different endpoint/layer).

title: fix(ci): review workflow interpolates untrusted PR title/body into shell command

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: area/ci
labels.description: CI, workflows, and build infrastructure

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

In `.github/workflows/review.yml` (current `main`, e.g. lines 66-110 in the checked-out workflow):

- Line 66 sets `PR_TITLE` from API-fetched PR data: `PR_TITLE: ${{ steps.pr-details.outputs.title }}`.
- Line 75 reads the PR body into a shell variable: `PR_BODY=$(jq -r .body pr_data.json)`.
- Lines 76-110 pass a single double-quoted argument to `opencode run ...` that expands both values inside bash double quotes:
  - `${PR_TITLE}` is interpolated in the prompt text (line 76: `"A new pull request has been created: '${PR_TITLE}'"`).
  - `$PR_BODY` is interpolated into the `<pr-description>` block (lines 84-86).

Because the `run` step executes in bash and these untrusted values are expanded inside a double-quoted shell string, command substitution (`$(...)`, backticks) and other shell metacharacters in a PR title or body can execute arbitrary commands in the runner.

## Why it matters

The workflow runs with repository secrets and elevated token permissions (`OPENCODE_API_KEY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` with `pull-requests: write`, per lines 69-74 and job permissions lines 31-33). Although triggering requires `issue_comment` `/review` from an `OWNER`/`MEMBER` (lines 26-29), the PR title/body remain controlled by the PR author (including external contributors), so a trusted maintainer invoking review on an untrusted PR can unintentionally execute attacker-controlled shell content in CI.

## Suggested fix shape

- Treat PR title/body as untrusted data: do not interpolate them directly into shell command strings.
- Pass them via environment variables and consume them without shell re-expansion (e.g. let the invoked tool read from env/files/stdin), or write them to temp files and reference file contents safely with proper quoting/heredocs that prevent command substitution.
- Keep the generated prompt construction robust to quotes, newlines, and `$`/backtick characters so the content is forwarded as data, not interpreted by the shell.

title: fix(ci): check:bounded-http stale allowlist for desktop extension download after #2422 leaves gate red on main

labels.name: kind/ci
labels.description: CI/CD pipelines, workflows, and build automation

labels.name: task/pr-shepherd
labels.description: Queue packet kind: shepherd an open PR or PR set to merge

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`bun run check:bounded-http` is red on current `main` (`b043483b35c7`, 2026-11-15) because the desktop extension archive download fix (#1091, merged via PR #2422 / commit `b683d9663e`) changed the fetch site but did not update its bounded-http allowlist disposition.

On `origin/main`:

- `packages/desktop/src/main/extension/manager.ts` now performs the bounded download through `electronFetch`:
  - `packages/desktop/src/main/extension/manager.ts:109-113` defines `electronFetch` as `async (url, init) => { const { net } = await import("electron"); return net.fetch(url, init) }` and passes it into `downloadArchive` (used by `install()` when source is a URL).
  - `packages/desktop/src/main/extension/manager.ts:101-107,115+` documents and enforces `EXTENSION_DOWNLOAD_DEADLINE_MS = 300_000` covering fetch + pump together via an `AbortController`/deadline signal (`#1091`), so the `net.fetch(url, init)` call is bounded at the site by that deadline signal.
- `script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt:148` still contains the pre-fix, now-stale entry:
  - `packages/desktop/src/main/extension/manager.ts :: const response = await net.fetch(url).catch((error) => { :: Electron net.fetch (Chromium network stack) with no signal in the call options — remaining surface in this inventory under design #1127`

The gate header states: "An entry whose line no longer matches is stale and fails the gate." The scanner now flags the new `return net.fetch(url, init)` site as an unlisted bounded-http candidate while the old allowlist entry is stale, so `check:bounded-http` cannot pass until the allowlist is updated to reflect the bounded implementation.

## Why it matters

`check:bounded-http` is the regression net for unbounded outbound calls (#1129 / design #1127). A stale disposition left behind by a fix keeps the gate red on `main`, hiding new unbounded-call regressions behind known breakage and creating noise for every run that depends on the gate.

## Evidence

- `origin/main`: `b043483b35c7df60f346164fdf352782090dbeea` (`chore(core): refresh bundled models.dev snapshot`, 2026-11-15T18:28:13Z)
- Fix present on main: `git show origin/main:packages/desktop/src/main/extension/manager.ts` contains `EXTENSION_DOWNLOAD_DEADLINE_MS = 300_000`, `electronFetch` passing `init` (signal) to `net.fetch(url, init)`, and `downloadArchive` (lines ~89-120+).
- Stale allowlist on main: `git show origin/main:script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt` line 148 is the old `const response = await net.fetch(url).catch((error) => {` entry with "no signal in the call options — remaining surface..." disposition.
- Running `bun run script/check-bounded-http.ts` from a clean checkout of `origin/main` reports `Unlisted bounded-http candidate at packages/desktop/src/main/extension/manager.ts:112: return net.fetch(url, init)` and `Stale allowlist entry (the line no longer matches a sweep pattern): packages/desktop/src/main/extension/manager.ts :: const response = await net.fetch(url).catch((error) => {` and exits non-zero.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replace the stale `packages/desktop/src/main/extension/manager.ts` allowlist entry with a disposition matching the current bounded `electronFetch`/`net.fetch(url, init)` site (or otherwise disposition the site so the gate reflects reality): note that the call is bounded at the site by the download deadline signal (`EXTENSION_DOWNLOAD_DEADLINE_MS`, overall fetch+pump abort) per #1091/#2422.
- [ ] `bun run script/check-bounded-http.ts` passes on `main` for this site (no stale manager.ts entry; no unlisted manager.ts candidate). If other currently-tracked unlisted candidates remain (e.g. #2462 / tui voice-input), this issue does not require fixing them, but the manager.ts regression introduced by #2422 must be resolved.
- [ ] No behavior change to extension downloads; the existing deadline/size-cap behavior and tests remain intact.

title: fix(tui): voice input missing guards — unguarded prototype-chain read on extension and unbounded HTTP fetch/response reads

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/tui
labels.description: Package: tui (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

body:
## Summary

The TUI voice-input module (`packages/tui/src/component/prompt/voice-input.ts`) ships three unguarded
sites that the repo's own gates (`script/check-proto-reads.ts`, `script/check-bounded-http.ts`) flag as
unlisted candidates. They are the same defect classes already fixed elsewhere in the STT path
(`#865`/`#2392` own-value guard in `packages/core/src/transcription-facade.ts`,
`#1127`/`#1129` bounded-http, `#2314`/`#2433` body caps), but the client side was never brought
along. The server-side transcription façade already guards `EXTENSION_MEDIA_TYPES` with `ownValue`;
the TUI helper does not.

## Evidence

### 1. Unguarded prototype-chain read on a filename-derived key
`packages/tui/src/component/prompt/voice-input.ts:86`
```ts
const extension = name.split(".").pop()?.toLowerCase()
return (extension ? EXTENSION_MEDIA_TYPES[extension] : undefined) ?? ""
```
`extension` comes from a user-selected filename (not a closed union). A file named `foo.constructor`
resolves `EXTENSION_MEDIA_TYPES["constructor"]` to the inherited `Object.prototype.constructor`
function, which is truthy, so the `?? ""` fallback never fires and `voiceMediaType` returns a
function instead of a string. The server-side façade already uses `ownValue(EXTENSION_MEDIA_TYPES,
extension)` for exactly this reason (`#865`/`#2392`).

Gate: `bun run check:proto-reads` reports
`Unlisted prototype-chain read candidate at packages/tui/src/component/prompt/voice-input.ts:86`.

### 2. Unbounded outbound fetch (no deadline signal)
`packages/tui/src/component/prompt/voice-input.ts:328` (batch) and `:460` (streaming):
```ts
response = await doFetch(endpoint, { method: "POST", headers: { ...input.headers }, body: form })
```
Neither call passes an `AbortSignal`/deadline. A façade that accepts the connection but never
responds hangs the composer's `submitting` state indefinitely. The repo's bounded-http doctrine
(`#1127`, `deadlineSignal` in `@opencode/util/http-body`) requires every outbound call to carry a
deadline. `ExtensionFetch` in `packages/desktop/src/main/extension/manager.ts` shows the established
pattern (deadline race + abort).

Gate: `bun run check:bounded-http` reports
`Unlisted bounded-http candidate at packages/tui/src/component/prompt/voice-input.ts:334` and `:467`.

### 3. Unbounded response body reads
`packages/tui/src/component/prompt/voice-input.ts:334` and `:467`:
```ts
const body: unknown = await response.json().catch(() => undefined)
```
`Response.json()` buffers the entire body with no cap. A hostile/buggy façade can OOM the TUI.
The bounded readers `readExcerptResponseText`/`readBoundedResponseText` in
`@opencode/util/http-body` exist for exactly this case (excerpt semantics for diagnostics).

## Why it matters

- Prototype-pollution-class misclassification of media type from a crafted filename (same class as
  the audited `#865` fix), inconsistent between server and client surfaces.
- A hanging/unresponsive transcription façade permanently stalls the voice-submit flow with no
  timeout or cancellation path.
- Unbounded body buffering is an OOM/DoS vector against the TUI.

## Acceptance criteria

- `voiceMediaType` uses `ownValue(EXTENSION_MEDIA_TYPES, extension)` (import from
  `@opencode/core/util/record` or a TUI-local equivalent) so prototype members miss.
- Both `submitVoiceTranscription` and `submitVoiceTranscriptionStream` pass a deadline signal into
  `doFetch` (e.g. `AbortSignal.timeout(...)` or `deadlineSignal(caller, timeoutMs)` with a caller-
  supplied/constant ceiling), and abort on timeout.
- Response bodies are read through `readExcerptResponseText` (for the error-path diagnostics) or
  `readBoundedResponseText` (for the success path) from `@opencode/util/http-body` instead of
  `response.json()`, with a byte cap.
- `bun run check:proto-reads` and `bun run check:bounded-http` report no unlisted candidates for
  `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/voice-input.ts`.
- Existing `packages/tui/test/component/voice-input.test.ts` still passes; add regression coverage
  for a `constructor`/`toString` filename extension and a (stubbed) hanging fetch.

## Out of scope

- The desktop extension manager fetch at `packages/desktop/src/main/extension/manager.ts:112` is
  already bounded via its `init.signal` (the gate hit there is an allowlist-staleness artifact of the
  `#1091` refactor, not a missing guard).
- The `model-routes.ts`/`model-route-match.ts` proto-read hits are on closed key sets and are
  tracked separately if at all.

Impact: the AGENTS.md workflow for public Protocol/HttpApi changes ("run `bun run generate` from packages/client; never hand-edit generated client files") cannot be followed — e.g. the new `completions.transcriptions` endpoint from #2385 cannot be generated into the client until this is fixed. The server-side API works; only client generation is blocked.

Ask: fix the Config.ModelRoutes schema representation the generator chokes on (or the generator's handling of it) so `bun run generate` completes on main; then regenerate so pending protocol additions land in the client.

body:
## Defect: quota gates are credential-scoped and family-blind — one family's wall silences its sibling family on the same credential

**Live evidence (2026-11-07):** `_antigravity` (provider id in telemetry: `antigravity-direct`) — the Gemini family sat at **4% weekly used, OPEN** (reset 2026-11-13T23:43Z) with live seats (`gemini-flash-plan` is a pool of ONE in the `speed` route; argon-plan; sonnet/opus fallback), yet recorded **zero attempts for ~26h** (last 2026-11-07 01:52:52Z).

Mechanism, all three layers verified in `opencode.db` + fork source:

1. **Provider skip is family-blind by construction.** When the Claude/GPT family exhausted (weekly 100%), `observeQuotaFailure` (credential-less path, `packages/core/src/model-route.ts`) planted ONE durable adjustment `quota:antigravity-direct` with `match: "antigravity-direct/"`, `until` = the Claude family's stated reset **2026-11-09T09:00:22Z**. The match is a provider-prefix substring (`model-resolver.ts`: `ModelRoute.skipped` → reason `user-skip`): it matches Gemini targets identically. There is no per-model-family dimension on provider-scope skips.
2. **Credential gate state is credential-scoped, not family-scoped.** The Antigravity credential's gate/cooldown state (route_health rows: thousands of `cooldown-start` for the credential, incl. `gemini-3.8-flash` targets benched with `quota retry-after` + `quota-gated … quota-known-full` against **the Claude window's reset**) is restored at every server start by `restoreCooldownsFrom` (`model-route-log.ts`, 24h replay window). The 2026-11-07 21:04 CST restart re-armed the Gemini targets' benches from the Nov 6 Claude-family exhaustion.
3. **The last Gemini decision on record** (2026-11-07 01:52:52Z, `gemini-flash-plan`) already shows the shape: the pool-of-one's only candidate present in weights yet `excluded: cooldown-until:…` — after which the route stopped producing served attempts entirely.

So: the Gemini family is healthy, its quota is open, and it is unroutable until the Claude/GPT reset (Nov 9 09:00Z) — because every gate dimension the router has (provider skip, credential gate, credential cooldown restore) is scoped at provider-or-credential granularity, never at the model-family/quota-window granularity the provider's own quota actually has (the quota gatherer already reports the two families as separate windows: Gemini 4% vs Claude+GPT 100%).

## Ask

- Scope quota gates to the quota window/family they were derived from: a gate derived from family A's exhaustion must not exclude family B targets on the same credential/provider. Concretely: provider skips from `observeQuotaFailure` should carry the model(s) that reported exhaustion (match `provider/model` prefix), falling back to provider scope only when the report is genuinely provider-wide; credential restore should not re-arm benches on targets of a different family than the one whose window the bench's reset belongs to.
- Until then, the finest config-level remedy is none: the skip is one durable record with a provider-prefix match; there is no supported way to exempt one family from it.

Related: #1974 (same staleness class, different mechanism — bench evidence vs lapsed gates in the pool verdict).

## Acceptance criteria

- Quota adjustments are scoped per model family: a wall in one family (e.g. Claude) cannot skip routes of a sibling family (e.g. Gemini) sharing the credential/provider prefix.
- A regression test proves a provider-prefix quota adjustment for one family leaves sibling-family targets attemptable.
- After the fix, live telemetry shows the under-quota family recording attempts again (the Antigravity Gemini case in the issue: 4% used, zero attempts for ~26h).
- Single-family skip behaviour is otherwise unchanged (same-family exhaustion still skips, with the family's own reset).
